prs.title: fix(core): commit a staged revert before running a session command
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #62138

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

After `/undo`, a revert stays staged on the session. `Session.prompt` commits a staged revert before admitting new work, but `SessionCommand.execute` did not, so a command sent after an undo — such as `/goal <objective>` — queued its kickoff behind the staged revert. The kickoff goes through `session.synthetic`, which stays held in the inbox while a revert is staged, so the goal showed as active but never ran. Committing after the command would be too late: the commit deletes inbox items after the revert point, including the kickoff itself.

This commits a staged revert at the start of `SessionCommand.execute`, before the command runs, mirroring `Session.prompt`. `Session.command` now provides its `Bus` to `SessionCommand.execute` for the commit, the same way the prompt path provides services to its preparation step. No feature flag: this fixes existing behavior.

### Test report

- New regression test in `packages/core/test/plugin/goal.test.ts`: "runs a goal commanded after an undo staged a revert" — two prompts finish, a revert is staged at the first prompt, then the `goal` command runs. Before this change the revert was still staged after the command and the goal never ran; after it, the revert is committed, the reviewer is asked once, and the goal completes.

prs.title: feat(app): add a session media panel behind the session_media flag
prs.body:
## Summary

Adds a **Media** tab to the session side panel that lists the images, videos and links shared in a session, by you or the agent, so you can find a screenshot or a link without scrolling the conversation. It covers the whole session, not just the messages the timeline has loaded.

- **Media:** images and videos you attached or pasted, images the agent read or wrote by path, and images tools returned, such as browser screenshots. Shown as gallery cards grouped by day.
- **Gallery viewer:** clicking an image opens the existing zoomable viewer as a gallery over the tab's images. Previous/next buttons and a "3 / 12" counter sit in its control bar, and ← / → step while the image isn't zoomed in (mirrored in right-to-left layouts). Images whose files are gone stay as "Couldn't load" cards but are skipped by the viewer.
- **Links:** web addresses in your messages and the agent's replies, pages the agent fetched, and web search results, each listed once. They're grouped by site, or by repository for GitHub. Issues and pull requests show as `#123` chips, and other pages as title chips. Hovering a chip shows the full title, the address, who shared it and when. Clicking opens the in-app browser, or the system browser when that isn't available. Icons work like the timeline's links: GitHub's mark, a public site's favicon, and a globe for private hosts such as `localhost`, which are never sent to the favicon service.
- **Search:** a search button opens a field under the filters that matches link titles and addresses and image names and paths. While searching, the panel keeps reading older history so it finds items not listed yet.
- **Filters:** Media / Links, and an Everyone / You / Agent dropdown for who shared it. Both are saved per session, so they stay the same when you switch tabs or restart the app.
- **Loading:** older history loads as you scroll to the end of the list. Thumbnails load as they scroll into view.

## Implementation

**Server:** a built-in plugin, `packages/core/src/plugin/media.ts`, registered next to `goal`. It serves an `experimental.media` RPC whose `list` method reads a page of a session's messages from the database, newest first, and returns only the images, videos and links in them, plus a cursor for the next page. Pages never include file bytes. The extraction is in `media/collect.ts`, with tests in `packages/core/test/plugin/media.test.ts`. The RPC definition and item schemas are in `packages/schema/src/session-media.ts`.

**App:** the built-in GUI plugin in `packages/gui-plugins/src/media/`.
- `history.ts` pages the RPC: 200 messages on the first read, 200 more each time older history is needed, and the 50 newest whenever the timeline's last message changes (a new message, a tool finishing, a reply ending). It doesn't read message contents from the timeline or make the timeline load older history.
- `source.ts` loads each card's bytes once it's visible: stored media through `experimental.media.get`, files by path through `file.read`, and inline bytes from their message.
- `link-groups.ts` groups the links, with tests. `links.tsx` renders the groups.

`ImagePreview` (`packages/ui`) gains two optional props, `position` and `onStep`, for stepping through a set. It now remembers which origin it hid, so stepping to another image shows the thumbnail it left. Existing callers pass neither prop and behave as before.

## Feature flag

Guarded by the new `session_media` flag in `packages/schema/src/config/flag.ts`. It is on in local and dev builds and off in releases. When the flag is off, the server doesn't register the RPC, and the app closes the tab and hides the + menu item and the "Open media" command.

The app reads the flag from the session directory's config the same way Core resolves it: `experimental.session_media`, then `experimental.all_flags`, then the build channel. It can't see `OPENCODE_FLAGS`, which only the server reads.

## Not included

- Clicking an item can't jump to the message it came from yet, because the plugin SDK has no way to scroll the conversation to a message.
- An image whose bytes are inline in a message (a pasted image, a tool screenshot) loads that whole message to show its thumbnail.
- The panel is hidden on narrow screens.

## Testing

- `bun run check` passes, plus `bun test src/media` in `packages/gui-plugins`, the media plugin tests in `packages/core`, and the image tests in `packages/ui`.
- Called the RPC on a dev server running against a copy of a real database: paging with the cursor reaches the start of a session, a pasted image and agent screenshots come back as references without bytes, those references load from their messages, an unknown session returns an empty page, and an out-of-range page size is rejected.
- The redesigned links, search and saved filters have not been checked in a running app yet.

prs.title: fix(core): recover stale snapshot repositories
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #59751

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

`Git.repo.create` builds a temporary repository and renames it onto the store path. It handles a successful rename and a target that already has `HEAD`, but not a target that exists without `HEAD`. The reporter's case was a stray empty `git init` in a directory opencode snapshotted. Against such a target every later rename fails with `ENOTEMPTY`, which a test that builds that state by hand reproduces. The failed repository fiber is also cached for the location, so the error replays until reload even after the stale directory is removed by hand.

This removes a target without `HEAD` and retries the rename once, and invalidates the cached fiber when repository initialization fails so the next capture retries. A valid store from a concurrent creator is still adopted, and successful initialization stays cached. The existing uninterruptible join is unchanged, so a caller's cancellation still leaves the shared attempt running.

### What this does not change

The TUI prompt path, the capture engine below `Git.repo.create`, the packing schedule, and the public API. It also does not repair a database that was already damaged before this fix.

### How did you verify your code works?

Added tests for a stale store without `HEAD` and for a create that fails once then succeeds on the next capture. Both fail without their fix: with `dev`'s `git.ts`, the stale-store test fails with `ENOTEMPTY` and no `HEAD`; with `dev`'s `snapshot.ts`, the retry test fails at the second capture with `undefined`. Restoring this branch's sources makes both pass.

On Debian 13/WSL2 with Bun 1.4.4, `cd packages/core && bun test test/git.test.ts test/snapshot.test.ts` passes (34 tests), and `bun run check` passes (lint and typecheck).

### Limitations

The tests drive `Git.repo.create` and `Snapshot.capture` directly rather than the TUI prompt, so they stand in for that path instead of repeating it. The interruption behavior of the cache change is not separately tested; that join is unchanged from before this PR.

### AI assistance

I used AI assistance to investigate this issue and draft the change. I reviewed the diff, ran the tests and checks above, and am accountable for the code in this PR.

prs.title: fix(core): size compaction output limit to room left by shortened requests
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #62185

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Fixes an issue where automatic conversation compaction throttles the summary request's output token limit to the compaction trigger buffer (e.g. 13,107 tokens on a 256k window with a 5% buffer) even when older exchanges were omitted or shortened into a small transcript leaving hundreds of thousands of tokens of free context room. When the summary output reaches that artificial ceiling, compaction fails with `Compaction summary reached the output token limit` (#62185).

1. `prepare` sizes the initial request options leaving room for `budget` (the trigger ceiling, e.g. `window - buffer`). When the unchanged transcript fits, `requests[0].maxTokens` correctly reflects that ceiling.
2. However, when the transcript exceeds the ceiling, `flattenAndDropOldest` shortens the transcript by dropping older exchanges and flattening history to text, or `shrink.history` drops the retained tail. Previously, the shortened request retained `prepared.request.maxTokens` (the trigger buffer size, e.g. 13,107).
3. `fitOutput` then took `Math.min(request.maxTokens, ...)`, which locked `maxTokens` at 13,107 and prevented it from expanding to the model's actual allowed output limit, despite hundreds of thousands of tokens of headroom left by the shortened prompt.
4. Sized the output limit on shortened requests (`flattenAndDropOldest` and `shrink.history`) to `SessionModelRequest.outputLimit(context.model.limit)` so `fitOutput` dynamically scales `maxTokens` to the actual remaining context window headroom up to the model's catalog output limit.

### How did you verify your code works?

- Added `compaction sizes output limit to room left by a shortened request` in `packages/core/test/session-compaction.test.ts`. Verified that without this fix, the test reproduces the issue with `Expected: 32000, Received: 13107`, and with this fix it passes cleanly.
- Verified all 40 tests in `packages/core/test/session-compaction.test.ts` pass (40 pass, 0 fail).
- Verified adjacent compaction suites (`test/session-native-compaction.test.ts`, `test/session-compaction-transport.test.ts`, `test/session-compact.test.ts`, `test/config/compaction.test.ts`).
- Verified clean types with `bun typecheck` (2,012 files across 2 projects clean) and `tsc -b tsconfig.json tsconfig.tests.json`.

prs.title: fix(plugin): only call function return values when tearing down a plugin
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #57719

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

A plugin's `setup()` runs as JavaScript, so it may return anything. The teardown that runs when the previous plugin generation is released only checked the returned value for truthiness and then called it:

```ts
(cleanup) => (cleanup ? Effect.promise(() => Promise.resolve(cleanup())) : Effect.void)
```

A plugin whose `setup()` returns an object therefore hits `cleanup()` and the reload dies with `TypeError: o is not a function`, which surfaces as `opencode reload` failing against the background service.

Only a real function counts as a cleanup callback now, so a plugin that returns something else is simply left without a teardown hook.

This is a different layer from #57096: that PR isolates a cleanup that *throws* so one plugin cannot abort the whole activation, while this one avoids calling a value that was never a cleanup function in the first place. The two are complementary — a plugin can still return a well-formed cleanup that throws, and #57096 covers that.

### How did you verify your code works?

- New regression test in `packages/core/test/plugin/supervisor-reload.test.ts` loads a local plugin whose `setup()` returns an object, then triggers a reload and asserts the new generation replaces the old one instead of the reload dying. Red/green checked: the previous truthiness check fails that case, the fix passes it.

prs.title: fix(core): settle the turn instead of interrupting it when the user dismisses a prompt
prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #62277

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

### What does this PR do?

Dismissing a `question` prompt or declining a permission prompt left the session **claimed as if a run were still live**. The decline fibers surface in `runner/step.ts`, which answered them with a bare `Effect.interrupt`. That interrupt carries no `interruptionReason`, so the execution layer's `terminal()` classified it as a shutdown-style stop — and shutdown deliberately keeps the write-ahead claim alive so a dead process can resume its turn on restart. The claim never released, no idle state was recorded, and anything treating the claim as "running" skipped the session until the user prompted again.

A dismissal or decline is the user ending the turn, not a crash. The tool part already records it (`failedTool` with "The user dismissed this question" / "The user declined this tool call"), so the step now settles as a normal completion (`needsContinuation: false`) — the same shape the location-shutdown branch already returns. The execution claim releases and the session returns to idle. Location shutdown keeps its own branch and semantics.

### How did you verify your code works?

- The two runner scenarios that pinned the old interrupt behavior ("interrupts runner continuation when a question is cancelled" and "...on a decline after settling an ordinary tool error") now assert a **successful** settle plus a released claim: `SessionTable.time_suspended` is `NULL` after the turn, and the dismissed tool part still records the aborted outcome.
- `bun test test/session-runner.test.ts` is 245/245 passing.
- `bun test test/plugin/permission-assert.test.ts test/plugin/promise-tool.test.ts test/plugin/module.test.ts test/session-compact.test.ts` adds 17/17 (permission/question adjacent surfaces).
- `bun typecheck` clean (1,898 files across 2 projects).

prs.body:
### Issue for this PR

Closes #57641

### Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Refactor / code improvement
- [ ] Documentation

### What does this PR do?

Opening a large session family hydrates permissions and forms for every child. Each empty response invalidated whole-family scans in the session view, tab attention state and terminal status, making startup quadratic.

Memoize each child's request list and keep empty results stable. Reuse the aggregation in the session view and tracked tabs. Real requests still appear, update and disappear in family order; closed tabs release their computations. This does not skip permission/form fetches or change approval behavior.

### Current validation (November 7)

The targeted hydration regression also passes 10 consecutive runs. No feature flag is needed for this bug fix. Hosted checks on the synchronized commit are pending.

prs.title: fix(session-ui): keep a URL's own closing bracket when linking plain text
prs.body:
**Links in plain text keep a closing bracket that belongs to the URL.**
A link like `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_(planet)` used to point at `…/Mercury_(planet`, with the `)` left outside the link. Brackets that wrap the whole URL, like `(see https://…).`, are still left out.

❌ **Before**
1. A URL is found in a message.
2. ❌ Every trailing `)` and `]` is stripped as punctuation, even when the URL opened that bracket itself.

✅ **After**
1. A URL is found in a message.
2. Trailing `,.;:!?` are stripped as before; a trailing `)` or `]` is stripped only when the URL has no matching opener for it.

```diff
- href = url without trailing ),.;:!?]
+ href = url without trailing ,.;:!? and without unmatched ) or ]
```

📊 **Proof**

| Text | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_(planet)` | ❌ `…Mercury_(planet` | ✅ `…Mercury_(planet)` |
| `(see https://…/Mercury_(planet)).` | ❌ `…Mercury_(planet` | ✅ `…Mercury_(planet)`, `).` stays text |
| `https://example.com/list[0]` | ❌ `…list[0` | ✅ `…list[0]` |

The new test fails without the change; 4 pass with it.

👀 **Read:** `link-segments.ts`, the trailing-character loop. It counts openers and closers in what's left of the URL before dropping each closer. The rest is routine.

prs.title: fix(core): keep trailing blank lines and CRLF endings when applying a patch
prs.body:
**Editing a file with the patch tool no longer deletes its trailing blank line or turns its Windows (CRLF) line endings into a mix of CRLF and LF.**
Both bugs were in the step that applies a patch's hunks to the file's current text. Files that end in a single newline and use LF throughout are not affected.

❌ **Before**
1. A file ends in a blank line (`line 1\nline 2\n\n`); a patch changes `line 2`.
2. ❌ The result is `line 1\nLINE 2\n`: the blank line is gone. A hunk that *adds* a blank line at the end is dropped the same way.
3. A file uses CRLF on every line (`a\r\nb\r\nc\r\n`); a patch changes `b`.
4. ❌ Every line the hunk writes, including the context lines it echoes back, comes out with LF, so the file ends up with mixed endings.

✅ **After**
1. The final newline is always restored on its own, so blank lines at the end that the patch didn't touch stay, and a blank line a hunk adds is kept.
2. When every line in the file ends in CRLF, the lines a hunk writes get CRLF back. Files with mixed endings are left exactly as they were.

```diff
  apply hunks to lines
- if last line != "": add final newline   # an existing trailing "" swallowed it
+ if every line in the file ended in CRLF: put "\r" back on lines that lack it
+ always add the final newline
```

📊 **Proof**

| The patch… | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| changes a line in a file ending in a blank line | ❌ blank line deleted | ✅ kept |
| adds a blank line at the end of a file | ❌ dropped | ✅ kept |
| changes a line in an all-CRLF file | ❌ edited lines become LF | ✅ stay CRLF |
| changes a line in a mixed-ending file | ✅ left as is | ✅ left as is |

Both new tests in `patch.test.ts` fail on `dev` and pass here.

👀 **Read:** the end of `derive` in `packages/util/src/patch.ts`. The final newline is now added unconditionally; that's safe because the split at the top already removed the real terminator, and after the CRLF pass the last line is never empty. This differs on purpose from upstream apply_patch, which has the same conditional. The rest is routine.

prs.title: fix(core): watch symlinked config file targets
prs.body:
# fix(core): watch symlinked config file targets

## Problem

A global `opencode.json` that is a symlink into a dotfiles repository never
reloads when its target is edited. Existing locations keep the stale document,
so changes such as `model` are ignored until a location is recreated or the
service restarts. New sessions in the affected location keep using the old
default (in this case a free fallback model) despite `opencode.json` naming a
different model.

## Why it happens

`ConfigDiscovery.discover` resolves symlinks when loading files
(`FSUtil.resolve` uses `realPath`), but `ConfigWatch.plan` only receives the
configured directory. The global config directory is watched recursively;
edits to a symlink target outside that directory produce no inotify event
under the watched path, so `Config.reload` never runs.

The load path itself is correct: any other config watch event reloads the
symlinked file's new contents. The missing piece is only the trigger.

## Reproduction (OpenCode v2.2.5, Linux)

Setup:

```sh
ln -s ~/.dotfiles/opencode/opencode.json ~/.config/opencode/opencode.json
# opencode.json contains:
#   "model": "opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash#high"
```

A location that was loaded before the target edit:

```sh
opencode api get '/api/config?location[directory]=<project>'
# global opencode.json document: model: None

opencode api get '/api/model/default?location[directory]=<project>'
# opencode / iceman-free
```

A location created after the edit resolves the same file correctly:

```sh
opencode api get '/api/model/default?location[directory]=<fresh-location>'
# opencode-go / deepseek-v4.1-flash
```

Triggering any watch event inside the global config directory fixes the stale
location without editing the config file:

```sh
touch ~/.config/opencode/.config-reload-probe && rm ~/.config/opencode/.config-reload-probe

opencode api get '/api/model/default?location[directory]=<project>'
# opencode-go / deepseek-v4.1-flash
```

Service log corroborates: the target was edited at
`2026-11-07T00:53:26+01:00`, the last `config.updated` event for the project
location was `2026-11-06T23:49:51Z`, and the active watchers were
`~/.config/opencode` (directory) plus individual instruction files, never the
resolved dotfiles target.

## Fix

- `ConfigDiscovery.Sources` gains `targets`: resolved paths of present config
  files (global and project direct files).
- `ConfigWatch.plan` includes those targets. The existing parent-watch logic
  turns an out-of-root target into an `entries` watch on its real parent, and
  targets already covered by a watched root are deduplicated.

## Tests

```sh
cd packages/core
bun test test/config/watch.test.ts test/config/discovery.test.ts
# 8 pass, 0 fail

bun test test/config/reload.test.ts
# 13 pass, 0 fail

bun typecheck
# No type errors in 2,012 files across 2 projects
```

New coverage:

- discovery resolves a symlinked global config to its target path
- the watch plan adds an `entries` watch on the target's real parent
- a target inside an already watched root does not add a duplicate watch

## Notes

This is a core config-reload bug, not a mini-client bug. `opencode mini`
surfaced it because the stale location defaulted new sessions to the free
fallback model.

prs.title: fix(tui): skip malformed frecency entries when loading
prs.body:
**File autocomplete skips broken entries in its recently-opened list instead of keeping them forever.**
The TUI remembers which files you open to rank autocomplete. A saved line that is valid JSON but has no path, or a count or timestamp that isn't a number, was loaded anyway, scored as `NaN`, and written back on the next save. Prompt history and the stash already check each entry; this list didn't.

❌ **Before**
1. The list is read from disk, line by line.
2. ❌ Any line that parses as JSON is kept, even `{"frequency":3,"lastOpen":1}` with no path.
3. ❌ The cleanup rewrite saves it back, so it never goes away.

✅ **After**
1. The list is read from disk, line by line.
2. A line is kept only if it has a non-empty path and numeric count and timestamp.
3. The cleanup rewrite drops the rest.

```diff
- entry = JSON.parse(line) as FrecencyEntry
+ entry = valid path && finite frequency && finite lastOpen ? parsed : skip
```

📊 **Proof**

| Saved line | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| no `path` | ❌ kept | ✅ skipped |
| `path: ""` or `path: 7` | ❌ kept | ✅ skipped |
| `frequency: "3"` or missing | ❌ kept | ✅ skipped |
| valid entry | ✅ kept | ✅ kept |

The new test fails without the change; 3 pass with it. Only a hand-edited or older state file can hold such lines.

👀 **Read:** `prompt/frecency.tsx`, the new per-entry check; it mirrors the one prompt history uses. The rest is routine.

prs.title: fix(core): name a missing local plugin path instead of failing with ENOENT
prs.body:
**A configured local plugin whose folder is missing now fails with an error that names the path.**
If a local plugin path in config was misspelled or deleted, loading it crashed on a raw `ENOENT`, and the plugin list only said "Plugin failed to load" with no path. Plugins that exist load as before.

❌ **Before**
1. Config lists a local plugin at `./plugins/my-plugn` (a typo).
2. Loading checks whether the path is a file and the check throws `ENOENT`.
3. ❌ The plugin shows "Plugin failed to load", with no hint which path is wrong.

✅ **After**
1. Same config.
2. A missing path is treated like a folder with no server entrypoint.
3. The load fails with `Plugin entrypoint not found: <path>`.

```diff
- local && stat(target).isFile()            // throws ENOENT if target is gone
+ local && stat(target).then(isFile, false) // missing -> look for an entrypoint -> "not found: <path>"
```

📊 **Proof**

| Configured local path | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| missing folder | ❌ raw `ENOENT`, no path shown | ✅ `Plugin entrypoint not found: <path>` |
| existing folder or file | ✅ loads | ✅ loads |

The new test fails without the change; 10 pass.

👀 **Read:** `packages/core/src/plugin/module.ts`, the `standalone` check. Swallowing the `stat` error is deliberate: the entrypoint check right after it reports the missing path. The rest is routine.

prs.title: fix(core): batch instruction blob writes and reads under the Durable Object parameter limit
prs.body:
**Sessions with many instruction entries no longer fail on the Durable Object server.**
A session saves its instruction values (one per instruction entry, such as each `api/*` entry) in a single database statement. Durable Object SQLite accepts at most 100 values per statement, so a session with more than 50 entries failed every turn. Local SQLite has a much higher limit and was not affected.

❌ **Before**
1. A session has around 50 or more instruction entries.
2. Saving them builds one insert with 2 values per entry.
3. ❌ Durable Object SQLite rejects it ("too many SQL variables: 300"), and the turn fails.

✅ **After**
1. The insert is split into batches that stay under the limit, the same way other inserts in the runtime already are.
2. Reading the values back is split into batches under the same limit.

```diff
- insert all blob rows in one statement
- read blobs with IN lists of 500 hashes
+ for each batch from DatabaseBatch.insertBatches: insert batch
+ read blobs in DatabaseBatch.batches (under 100 params each)
```

📊 **Proof**

| Session with 150 instruction values, on Durable Object SQLite | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Save and render instructions | ❌ "too many SQL variables: 300" | ✅ all 150 render |

The new test runs on the Durable Object SQLite fixture, fails on `dev`, and passes here.

👀 **Read:** `insertBlobs` and `loadBlobs` in `packages/core/src/session/instruction-state.ts`. Both just switch to the shared batching helpers. The rest is routine.

prs.title: fix(core): allow `changes: false` beside another shell check predicate
prs.body:
**A scheduled shell check can now set `changes: false` next to `is` or `matches`.**
A shell check picks at most one way to decide if it passed: `is`, `matches` or `changes`. Saving the check counted `changes: false` as a choice, while running it already treats `false` as "not set".

❌ **Before**
1. A schedule's check is `{ run: "echo hi", is: "hi", changes: false }`.
2. ❌ Creating it fails with "Choose at most one of is, matches or changes", even though `changes` is turned off.

✅ **After**
1. The same check is accepted and runs as an `is` check.
2. `changes: true` next to `is` is still rejected.

```diff
- predicates = count(is set, matches set, changes set)
+ predicates = count(is set, matches set, changes == true)
```

📊 **Proof**

| Check | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `is: "hi", changes: false` | ❌ rejected | ✅ accepted |
| `is: "hi", changes: true` | ✅ rejected | ✅ rejected |

The new test fails on `dev` and passes here.

**Code Mode search finds a namespace written as `tools.slack` even when an MCP server is named `tools`.**
Search results show every path with a `tools.` prefix, so callers often repeat it in `namespace`. Search dropped that prefix only while no tool path started with `tools.`, so adding a server named `tools` silently broke scoped search for every other server. Nothing changes when no server is named `tools`.

❌ **Before**
1. Connect two MCP servers, `tools` and `slack`.
2. Run `search({ namespace: "tools.slack" })`.
3. ❌ It returns no results, because the prefix is kept and no path starts with `tools.slack`.

✅ **After**
1. Same setup and call.
2. `tools.slack` names nothing as written, so the prefix is dropped and `slack` is searched.
3. It returns `tools.slack.read`. `namespace: "tools.tools"` and the query `tools.tools.ping` still find the `tools` server.

```diff
- drop a "tools." prefix only if no tool path starts with "tools."
+ drop a "tools." prefix only if the written name matches no namespace or tool
```

📊 **Proof**

| Call (servers `tools` and `slack`) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `namespace: "tools.slack"` | ❌ nothing | ✅ `tools.slack.read` |
| `namespace: "tools.tools"` | ✅ `tools.tools.ping` | ✅ `tools.tools.ping` |
| `query: "tools.tools.ping"` | ✅ `tools.tools.ping` | ✅ `tools.tools.ping` |

The new test fails without the change; 34 pass in both engines.

👀 **Read:** `packages/codemode/src/tool-runtime.ts`, the `names`/`unprefixed` helpers at the top of the search tool: a literal match always wins over dropping the prefix. The rest is routine.

<sub>🔍 Found in a code audit · no user reports</sub>

<details><summary>Checks run</summary>

- `bun test test/tool-paths.test.ts` (packages/codemode): 34 pass
- `CODEMODE_ENGINE=vm bun test test/tool-paths.test.ts`: 34 pass
- `bun turbo typecheck` (pre-push): pass

</details>

releases.name: v2.2.6
releases.body:
### Highlights

- **Shared MCP Connections**: Turn on pooling for an MCP server to share one connection across projects with the same setup, so you run fewer processes and start faster. ([#61185](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61185))
- **GUI Plugin Themes and New Slots**: GUI plugins can now add color themes, render or add actions to code blocks, and use native settings and menu components. ([#61485](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61485), [#61533](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61533), [#61527](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61527), [#61509](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61509))
- **Mobile Composer Dock**: On phones and tablets, composer actions now sit in a touch dock above the keyboard with larger buttons. ([#61773](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61773))
- **Scripted Runs in Worktrees**: Run `opencode run -w` to start the session in a new git worktree, or `--worktree=<name>` to name it. ([#60712](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/60712))
- **Automatically Archived Runs**: Add `--archived` to `opencode run` to keep scripted and CI sessions out of your inbox and session lists. ([#61270](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61270))

### Core

#### Improvements

- Added opt-in MCP connection sharing through `pool: true`. ([#61185](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61185))
- Added `opencode run --archived`, which creates the session already archived so scripted and CI runs stay out of the inbox, home, and session lists. Archived sessions are also hidden from the TUI session list and skipped by `--continue`. ([#61270](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61270))
- Added `opencode run --worktree` (`-w`), which starts the session in a new git worktree. Use `--worktree=<name>` to choose the worktree name. It cannot be combined with `--continue` or `--session`. ([#60712](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/60712))
- Added provider- and model-specific session warming settings, including an `interval: "auto"` mode based on cache TTL. ([#60025](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/60025), [#60969](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/60969))
- Added the `websearch.use` policy action and switches for enabling all feature flags with `OPENCODE_FLAGS=all` or `experimental.all_flags`. ([#61557](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61557), [#61826](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61826))
- Added an experimental bytecode VM for Code Mode. It is off by default; turn it on with `experimental.codemode_vm: true` or `OPENCODE_FLAGS=codemode_vm`. ([#62358](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62358))
- Added support for Microsoft Store installations of PowerShell 7 on Windows. ([#61952](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61952))
- Added Azure Messages support for Foundry Claude models. ([#60934](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/60934))

#### Bug fixes

- `opencode run` now waits for the background shell commands, subagents, and image jobs that its prompt started, then lets the model respond to their results before it exits. While it waits, it prints `waiting for N background job(s)` (a `background_wait` event with `--format json`). There is no time limit: a job that never exits, such as a dev server or file watcher, keeps the run open until you press Ctrl+C or send SIGTERM, so set a timeout on CI jobs. ([#60699](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/60699), [#61911](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61911))
- Reworked noninteractive `opencode run` execution so arguments, cancellation, compiled WebSocket upgrades, and service shutdown complete reliably. SIGTERM now cancels the session and its background jobs and exits with code 143. ([#61911](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61911), [#61721](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61721), [#61518](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61518), [#61564](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61564))
- Serve file reads and media from the server API as sandboxed downloads, and refuse cross-site browser navigations and requests from disallowed origins to `/api/*`, so a file in your project cannot run scripts on the server's origin. ([#62422](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62422))
- Webfetch and Code Mode `fetch` now reject URLs that contain credentials and ignore the `#fragment` when matching permission rules, and Code Mode `fetch` checks every redirect against your webfetch rules. ([#60502](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/60502), [#61701](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61701), [#62373](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62373))
- Ask for `external_directory` permission before `session_move` leaves the current project. ([#62204](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62204))
- Wait up to 2 seconds for MCP servers that are still connecting before a model call, so tools from servers that connect quickly reach the first prompt and `opencode run`. Also expand `~` in local MCP working directories, handle legacy stdio servers, and send `logo_uri` during dynamic registration. ([#60490](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/60490), [#61496](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61496), [#61817](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61817), [#59031](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59031))
- Time out OpenCode Console config requests after 5 seconds, so startup no longer hangs when the Console accepts the connection but never answers. ([#62404](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62404))
- Retry provider requests while their host is unreachable and recover prematurely ended Cohere streams. ([#61880](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61880), [#61184](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61184))
- Keep legacy custom providers whose models set only part of `limit`, such as only `limit.context`, instead of dropping the whole provider without an error. Thanks @Tarquinen. ([#62240](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62240))
- `opencode acp` now removes a session that a client creates with `session/new` and closes without prompting, so IDE integrations no longer leave empty sessions behind. ([#62189](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62189))
- Prevent repeated zsh `q` flags from freezing shell permission scanning. Thanks @yangguan-xue. ([#60791](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/60791))
- Allow npm upgrade install scripts again. Thanks @renatomoselli. ([#51554](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/51554))

### TUI

#### Improvements

- Added **Scroll on send** in Settings. Choose **Keep** (`session.submit_scroll: "keep"`) to retain your reading position after submitting a prompt. ([#61460](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61460))

#### Bug fixes

- Allow Ctrl+Z to suspend OpenCode while a form or dialog is open. ([#62118](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62118))
- Keep focus on an open dialog when a question arrives and contain plugin dialogs that throw during rendering. ([#60365](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/60365), [#62110](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62110))
- Show an error when Ctrl+V cannot read the clipboard. Thanks @jimmyallinai. ([#61094](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61094))
- Prevent session titles containing newlines from crashing the TUI. Thanks @vishalshekhar. ([#57523](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/57523))
- Improved message spacing and prevented older history from flashing while scrolling. ([#62104](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62104), [#59236](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59236))
- Jump to the first or last message with Home, End, and Ctrl+G in subagent sessions. Thanks @ricky9408. ([#60817](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/60817))
- Keypad Home, End, Page Up, and Page Down now navigate the transcript like the main keys in terminals that use the kitty keyboard protocol. Thanks @argszero. ([#59770](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/59770))
- `opencode mini` now uses the agent colors from your config. Thanks @ferdinandyb. ([#62067](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62067))
- Return to the `/mcp` list after signing in to an MCP server, with that server still selected. Thanks @Tarquinen. ([#62245](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62245))
- Allow favoriting models with Ctrl+F in `/models` when they come from a provider declared in config or an add-on instead of a saved connection. Thanks @Tarquinen. ([#62244](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62244))

### Desktop

#### Improvements

- Added a mobile composer dock for touch devices, with 44px action targets and predictable multiline input. ([#61773](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61773))
- Added close-other-tabs and close-tabs-after actions to the tab menu. ([#61631](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61631))
- Added unread-session grouping in Inbox and failed-run indicators on tabs. ([#61691](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61691), [#62077](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62077))
- MCP sign-in now accepts a pasted redirect URL when automatic redirection is unavailable. ([#61706](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61706))
- Markdown file previews now display frontmatter as a properties list. ([#60333](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/60333))
- The command palette shows a date instead of "Xd ago" for sessions 7 or more days old. Hover the time to see the full date and time. ([#62314](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62314))
- Prompt history now keeps up to 200 prompts. Past the newest 100, only prompts without attachments are kept. ([#62313](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62313))

#### Bug fixes

- Improved prompt submission and timeline behavior during loading, reconnects, retries, scrolling, compaction, and optimistic delivery. ([#62025](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62025), [#62037](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62037), [#61932](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61932), [#62151](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62151))
- Surface loading and offline failures in review previews, file search, details, Word pages, and review diffs instead of showing empty or clean results. ([#62114](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62114), [#61862](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61862))
- Fixed provider connection, MCP sign-in, settings, and plugin loading flows that could become stuck after failures. ([#62102](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62102), [#61917](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61917), [#61580](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61580))
- Preserve drafts, focus, caret position, queued prompts, and selected terminal tabs across failed or concurrent transitions. ([#61579](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61579), [#61969](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61969), [#61852](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61852))
- Restart plugins after failed update handoffs and recover the renderer, storage, event stream, and background-service connection from transient failures. ([#61649](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61649), [#61908](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61908), [#61804](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61804), [#61748](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61748))
- Corrected V2 file labels and mention syntax. Thanks @velmet and @cheapredwine. ([#55677](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/55677), [#60737](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/60737))
- Attach only the `@mentions` in a line comment that match an existing file or folder, so a comment such as `Check @here` no longer fails the send. Render partial diffs in the review pane when it shows all lines, instead of a blank pane. Thanks @Tarquinen. ([#62242](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62242), [#62241](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62241))
- Keep pasted images sendable after the clipboard tool deletes its temporary file. Thanks @lfscqk67. ([#62057](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62057))
- While an input method is composing text, Escape, Enter, and Tab go to the input method instead of stopping the agent or picking a suggestion. ([#62318](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62318))
- Fixed padding in the WSL distribution picker, the position of worktree and branch labels in Home search results, and the selected ring on the Interface layout setting. Thanks @inuyume. ([#53676](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/53676), [#62317](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62317), [#62309](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/62309))

### SDK

#### Improvements

- Added `client.experimental.job.list()` and its Effect equivalent for listing background shell, subagent, and image jobs, with session, descendant, kind, and status filters. ([#60698](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/60698))
- Server embedders can provide a custom `fetch` implementation for OpenCode HTTP, model, web, and remote MCP traffic. ([#61582](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61582))

### Extensions

issues.title: openai: ChatGPT sign-in still uses 272K for GPT-6.1 Sol despite 500K account catalog
issues.body:
### What happened?

With `openai` authenticated through **Sign in with ChatGPT**, Pi 1.3.0 reports a 272K context window for `gpt-6.1-sol`, although the same account's live model catalog reports a 500K default. This gives Pi a smaller context/compaction budget than the server advertises.

An authenticated `GET https://api.openai.com/v1/models` using the stored `openai` OAuth access token returned HTTP 200 and:

```json
{"slug":"gpt-6.1-sol","context_window":500000,"max_context_window":872000}
```

This is an account-specific catalog check, not an inference test above 272K. [OpenAI's documentation](https://developers.openai.com/siwc/token-sharing-open-source/models-and-inference) directs this sign-in flow to use `/v1/models` for the account's current catalog.

Related: #10840 and commit 5712b134e corrected `openai-codex` to 500K, but left `openai` at 272K. The static short-context pricing cap also applies when `openai` uses subscription OAuth, not an API key.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Sign in to `openai` through Sign in with ChatGPT.
2. Run `pi -ne --no-mcp --list-models gpt-6.1-sol`:

```text
provider  model        context  max-out  thinking  images
openai    gpt-6.1-sol  272K     128K     yes       yes
```

3. With the same OAuth access token, query `GET https://api.openai.com/v1/models` and inspect the entry whose `slug` is `gpt-6.1-sol`. The tested account returns `context_window: 500000`.

### Expected behavior

For ChatGPT subscription authentication, use the account's advertised default context window (500K here), rather than inheriting the API-key pricing cap. This report does not request a blanket change to API-key defaults or use of the separate 872K maximum.

### Version

1.3.0

issues.title: Avoid pinning completed ! command output below a streaming conversation

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

When running `!` shell commands during an agent response, the output stays at the bottom of the visible area and reduces the space available for the conversation. Related: #3657 (reported for `!!` on 0.70.2). Reported on pi 1.5.0 on macOS; extension-free reproduction with `pi -ne` has not yet been verified.

### Why?

A long command result can obscure ongoing work, especially in a small terminal. The collapsed bash preview can still use up to 20 visual lines.

### How? (optional)

Keep live output visible while a command runs, then move completed results into the normal scrollable transcript in the correct order, or provide a way to dismiss/collapse the pending view without deleting the result or changing model context. `handleBashCommand` currently places streaming-session commands in `pendingMessagesContainer`; preserve existing session ordering and `!` versus `!!` context semantics. Test streaming and idle cases, multiple commands, and long output.

issues.title: Preserve hard line breaks and soft-wrap semantics for accurate TUI selection copy

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

I would like pi-tui to preserve line-boundary semantics through rendering and copying, so mouse selection can join soft wraps introduced by viewport width while retaining hard line breaks from the source content.
#506 describes this symptom, and #7721 attempted to track soft wraps with invisible markers. I understand the compatibility and risk concern raised when that PR was closed: custom components would also need to understand and propagate those markers.
I would therefore like to suggest a different direction: optional semantic selection metadata kept separate from display strings. Built-in components such as `Text` and `Markdown` could provide it, while components without it would naturally retain the current copy behavior. This could solve the hard-break/soft-wrap problem without requiring existing custom components to understand hidden markers.

### Why?

I can reproduce this in Kitty, Alacritty, and Ghostty: copying a response wrapped because of viewport width inserts extra newlines into the clipboard. This does not appear to be specific to one terminal.
The distinction still exists inside `wrapTextWithAnsi()`: it first separates source newlines, then creates visual wraps with `wrapSingleLine()`. However, it ultimately returns only `string[]`, so that boundary information is lost. Fullscreen selection copy later reconstructs the result with:
```ts
const text = lines.join("\n");
```
Every visual row therefore becomes a hard line break. `/copy` preserves the original full assistant message, but cannot copy an arbitrary mouse selection. The public extension API also has no access to transcript selection coordinates or the built-in copy reconstruction path.

### How?

One possible design is optional selection information associated with each visual line, for example:
```ts
interface SelectionLineProjection {
  text: string;
  joinerToPrevious?: string;
  selectableColumns?: { start: number; end: number };
}
```
The joiner could preserve a real `"\n"`, omitted whitespace, or `""` for a continuous soft wrap such as a long token or CJK text. Layout, clipping, and scrolling would propagate this sidecar without interpreting it, and fullscreen selection copy would use it to reconstruct selected text. Lines without a projection would fall back to the existing visual-row behavior.

issues.title: codemode: preserve nested Error messages in allSettled output and returned values
issues.body:
## Problem

Codemode preserves a nested tool rejection as an Error in the VM, but its output serialization drops the Error's non-enumerable name/message. Consequently `text(await Promise.allSettled(...))`, console output, and the returned result can show `reason: {}` instead of actionable guidance.

Observed with installed Pi / pi-codemode 1.0.4 on macOS, also reproduced against toolkit development dependency 0.99.1.

## Minimal reproduction

Provide a sandbox tool `read` whose execute function throws `new Error("Example actionable read failure")`, then execute:

```javascript
const results = await Promise.allSettled([tools.read({path: "missing.txt"})]);
text(results);
text(results[0].reason.message);
return results;
```

Actual output:

```text
[{"status":"rejected","reason":{}}]
Example actionable read failure
```

The returned value likewise contains `reason: {}`. The message exists in the VM, as the second output proves; it is lost during nested output serialization.

## Expected

Codemode's output serializers should preserve a safe diagnostic representation of nested Errors, e.g. `{name: "Error", message: "Example actionable read failure"}`. Preserve other supported diagnostic fields where appropriate without serializing secrets or unbounded stacks. Handle nested errors in arrays/objects, mixed allSettled results, console output, and returned values consistently.

A serializer-owned Error-aware replacer is preferable to rewriting arbitrary user source, changing Error.prototype, or replacing frozen globals. Explicit user calls to `JSON.stringify` still have normal JavaScript semantics unless the user supplies a replacer; this report concerns codemode's own output/return serialization boundaries.

## Context

Originally observed with an economy-mode rejection in RAHUL1115/pi-toolkit#1: an assistant spent another read round trip just to recover the missing message. Toolkit is addressing normal oversized reads by reducing the requested line limit before native execution, but generic/native errors and exceptionally oversized first lines still need actionable serialization. We deliberately removed a source-rewriting workaround because of its coupling to VM internals.

Related toolkit issue: https://github.com/RAHUL1115/pi-toolkit/issues/1

issues.title: codemode: console.log prints NaN and Infinity as null

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

In codemode, `console.log` prints `NaN` and `Infinity` as `null`. A script like `console.log("avg", total / count)` with `count === 0` shows the model `avg null`, so it reasons about a value that isn't there. `text(0 / 0)` in the same script correctly prints `NaN`, so the two output paths disagree. `throw NaN` is also reported with message `null`.

Cause: `format()` in `packages/codemode/src/runtime/prelude-source.ts` sends every non-string, non-Error value through `JSON.stringify`, which returns `"null"` for NaN and Infinity.

### Steps to reproduce

Run this codemode script:

```js
console.log("avg", 0 / 0, 1 / 0);
text(0 / 0);
```

issues.title: bash temp-file stream errors still crash the whole process on 1.0.4 (ENOSPC on a full /tmp, EACCES)
issues.body:
## What happened?

pi 1.0.4 died mid-run with an uncaught `ENOSPC: no space left on device, write` (`~/.pi/agent/crashes.json`: `kind: "uncaught_exception"`, `2026-10-07T02:46:22.281Z`, Linux aarch64). The session log stops at the previous event — the in-flight run was lost, with no tool error and no truncated result.

Context: `/tmp` is a 16 GiB / 1 M-inode tmpfs on this machine; concurrent agent runs had filled it with scratch while the root filesystem had 130 GiB free. Output past `DEFAULT_MAX_BYTES` opens a temp file in `tmpdir()`, so any temp-write failure (full disk, inode exhaustion, permissions) takes down the whole process instead of failing the tool.

Same bug as #9827 (auto-closed, labeled `no-action`; tc3oliver's EACCES repro is in the comments); same class: #2512/#2513, #5667, #7237 (all closed). Still present on main as of `eb326d2`: `ensureTempFile` opens the stream with no `error` listener at [bash-executor.ts#L62-L70](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/eb326d265ae0b88489a6d10319307780df827cdf/packages/coding-agent/src/core/bash-executor.ts#L62-L70) and [output-accumulator.ts#L245-L256](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/eb326d265ae0b88489a6d10319307780df827cdf/packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/output-accumulator.ts#L245-L256); [output-files.ts#L31-L34](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/eb326d265ae0b88489a6d10319307780df827cdf/packages/coding-agent/src/utils/output-files.ts#L31-L34) adds none. Filing again because it still reproduces on the current release and no released version has the fix; close it if the `no-action` call on #9827 stands.

## Steps to reproduce

1.0.4, no extensions, no model call (core API only, so no extension can be involved):

```sh
mkdir ro && chmod 500 ro
TMPDIR=$PWD/ro node --input-type=module -e '
import { createBashTool } from "@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent";
await createBashTool(process.cwd()).execute("t", { command: "seq 1 300000" }, undefined, () => {});'
```

Result: `throw er; // Unhandled 'error' event` — `EACCES: permission denied, open '…/pi-bash-<hex>.log'`, exit 1. A full disk (ENOSPC) hits the same path — consistent with the real-world crash above (the crash record carries no stack, so that link is inference from the code, not proof).

## Expected behavior

The temp-file failure should degrade gracefully: drop `fullOutputPath` and return the truncated in-memory output (or at worst fail the tool) instead of killing the process.

## Version

1.0.4 (latest release), main @ `eb326d2`. Linux aarch64 (Asahi M1 Pro). PR #9800 has a fix with regression tests for this path (auto-closed, unapproved).

issues.title: openai-codex: onResponse never fires on the WebSocket transport, so x-codex-* usage headers are lost

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

`openai-codex-responses` only calls `options.onResponse` on its SSE path (`api/openai-codex-responses.js`, after the fetch). The WebSocket path (`processWebSocketStream`) never calls it, and the default transport is `"auto"`, which uses WebSocket whenever there's a session id.

So in practice `after_provider_response` / `onResponse` never fires for Codex, and the `x-codex-primary-*`, `x-codex-secondary-*`, and `x-codex-credits-*` usage headers aren't visible anywhere. We read them to show the ChatGPT plan's 5-hour/weekly usage and whether requests are drawing on credits; with WebSocket they only appear on the occasional request that falls back to SSE.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Pass an `onResponse` that logs headers to `models.stream(...)` for an `openai-codex` model with a `sessionId` (pi-durable conversations always set one).
2. Send a few turns: `onResponse` isn't called.
3. Repeat with `transport: "sse"`: it's called on every request with the `x-codex-*` headers.

### Expected behavior

Some way to get the response metadata on the WebSocket transport: call `onResponse` with the upgrade response's status and headers, or with the usage/rate-limit info when the server sends it over the socket.

### Version

pi-ai 1.5.0

issues.title: grep: a glob with a folder in it silently matches nothing unless path is the cwd

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
### What happened?

grep's `glob` doesn't say what it's relative to, and in practice it's anchored to the process cwd, not to `path`. So `{ path: "repo", glob: "migrations/main/*.js" }` returns "No matches found" even though `repo/migrations/main/a.js` exists.

That's ripgrep's design (it roots `--glob` at its own cwd, `OverrideBuilder::new(&state.cwd)` in hiargs.rs), and `grep.ts` spawns rg without a cwd, so the anchor is a folder the model never sees. Meanwhile grep prints results relative to `path` (`migrations/main/a.js` in the example), so a glob written in that same frame finds nothing. `find` already handles this case, it prefixes `**/` to path globs.

It bit us in agents: the model got a false "no matches", decided the file didn't exist and gave up. The empty result looks exactly like a real negative.

I'd like to implement the fix myself, it's a three-line change plus a test.

### Steps to reproduce

```sh
mkdir -p /tmp/g/repo/migrations/main && echo hello > /tmp/g/repo/migrations/main/a.js
cd /tmp/g
rg -l --glob 'migrations/main/*.js' hello repo        # nothing
cd repo && rg -l --glob 'migrations/main/*.js' hello . # ./migrations/main/a.js
```

Same through the tool: from `/tmp/g`, `grep` with `path: "repo"`, `glob: "migrations/main/*.js"`, `pattern: "hello"` returns "No matches found". With `glob: "**/migrations/main/*.js"` it finds `migrations/main/a.js`.

### Expected behavior

The glob is relative to `path`, the same frame grep prints its results in, so it finds `a.js`.

Two ways to get there, either works for me:

1. Anchor the glob to `path`: spawn rg with `cwd` set to the search dir and search `.` instead of the absolute path, then resolve rg's relative paths against `searchPath` in `formatPath`. Searching `.` matters: rg resolves its cwd through symlinks, so only setting `cwd` still misses on paths like macOS `/tmp`. I patched it into 1.5.0's dist and the call above finds `a.js` (relative, absolute and symlinked `path`), a decoy at `repo/nested/migrations/main/b.js` correctly stays out, and output for every other case is unchanged.
2. If anchoring to the cwd is intended, say so in the `glob` description (folder globs need a leading `**/`) or prefix it like `find` does.

### Version

1.5.0

issues.title: Add a horizontal layout option for extension select menus

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What do you want to change?

Extension select menus always render their options as a vertical list. I want an optional horizontal layout that puts the choices on a single row, for menus with two to four short options.

Two levels, if both make sense to you:

- an `orientation` entry on `ExtensionSelectorOptions`, so a single call can pick the layout
- a global `selectOrientation` setting, `"vertical"` by default and `"horizontal"` as the other value, so a user can set it once

### Why?

A vertical list of three short choices takes six lines plus borders, and in fullscreen on a wide terminal it is a narrow column in a large empty area. A permission prompt with "Allow", "Allow for session", "Deny" would read fine on one line.

The bigger part is keys. The selector only handles `tui.select.up` and `tui.select.down` today, so horizontal navigation needs configurable left/right keybindings under `tui.select.*`. That is the piece I am least sure belongs in core.

### How? (optional)

`ExtensionSelectorComponent` takes an `orientation` option and, in horizontal mode, renders the options in one `Text` row with the selected entry using the same selection colors. `handleInput` matches the new left/right keybindings, added with defaults to `DEFAULT_APP_KEYBINDINGS` rather than hardcoded.

It should fall back to vertical when the row would overflow the terminal width or when the list is long, since the component windows at ten rows today and labels can be long.

Longer term, `tui.select.prev`/`tui.select.next` may be the better abstraction: the layout picks the physical keys, so a new layout needs no new bindings. That is a rename of existing ones, so your call whether it belongs here.

Scope question: the component is used by extension `select` menus, the Radius `/login` selector, and the bug report form. A global setting changes all three, which may be more than you want. The per-call option alone would cover extensions.

3. Read the file back: bytes are now `61 0d 0a 62 0d 0a 43` (`a\r\nb\r\nC`). Line 2's `\n` (`0a`) became `\r\n` (`0d 0a`) even though only `c` was replaced.

issues.title: Resume restores stale thinking level after /tree navigation
openai-completions sends tools: [] when there's tool history in the transcript, LiteLLM/vLLM backends 400 on it
issues.body:
Running pi 1.5.0 with a custom provider (`api: "openai-completions"`, baseUrl is a LiteLLM gateway in front of hosted vLLM).

Every request that has no tools but whose transcript contains tool calls/results gets `params.tools = []` in the body, and the gateway rejects it:

```
400: litellm.BadRequestError: Hosted_vllmException -
{"error":{"message":"`tools` must not be an empty array. Either provide at least one
tool or omit the field entirely. (parameter=tools)"...}}
```

This is `packages/ai/src/api/openai-completions.ts`, ~L852 on current main:

```ts
} else if (hasToolHistory(context.messages)) {
    // Anthropic (via LiteLLM/proxy) requires tools param when conversation has tool_calls/tool_results
    params.tools = [];
}
```

Checked directly against the gateway:

| Request | Result |
|---|---|
| `tools: []` | 400, error above |
| field omitted | 200 |
| field omitted, messages carry tool_calls + tool role | 200 |
| non-empty tools | 200 |

So at least for this backend, omitting the field is enough - the empty array is the only failing shape. The `[]` workaround for Anthropic-behind-LiteLLM setups is applied to every openai-completions endpoint unconditionally, and there's currently no way to opt out.

Not proposing a fix - an AI-drafted patch here would be nonsense anyway, and it's a maintainer call what the right approach is.

issues.title: pi-durable 1.5.0: tasks get stuck in waiting or completing

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: untriaged
labels.description: This issue has been auto closed and has not been triaged

issues.body:
### What happened?

In pi-durable 1.5.0, tasks can get stuck in `waiting` or `completing` even after all their dependencies or children have finished. I reproduced both with plain tasks and `MemoryStorage` by using the `Storage.publishing` hook to control when commits get published.

Both seem to be race conditions where cleanup from an earlier pass removes a newer notification:

1. Suppose W is waiting on its last dependency M. M's terminal commit has been stored but hasn't published yet, so planning still sees M as running and puts W in `plan.dropped`. The callback then pauses at `await #region(...)`. Meanwhile, M publishes, adds W to the `#runnable` set and requests another drain. But when the callback resumes, it removes W from `#runnable`, so the next pass misses it.

2. Suppose P is `completing` and still has a running child M. An earlier check saw M was still running and consumed P's pending check. A later pass starts planning with an empty `#finalizeChecks`. While it's awaiting, M publishes and queues P for another check, but the old pass then clears the entire set. P stays stuck in `completing`, and idle waits never resolve.

I think we can fix this by synchronously swapping out the pending set for a fresh one before the planning await. That way, any new notifications arriving during planning go into the new set and can't be erased by the older pass.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use `MemoryStorage` and `Storage.publishing` to delay a child’s terminal publication.
2. **Waiting case:** publish after reservation planning marks the waiter `dropped`, but before its removal from `#runnable`.
3. **Completing case:** publish after an empty finalization plan, but before `#finalizeChecks.clear()`.
4. Observe the task remains stuck in `waiting` or `completing` accordingly.

I can attach a repro bundle (written by codex) if helpful but it should be relatively straightforward to reproduce or just reason about this directly. LMK.

### Expected behavior

_No response_

### Version

_No response_

issues.body:
## What happened?

Running a `!` or `!!` command while the agent is streaming puts the output box in the pending-messages area. Pressing `ctrl+o` toggles the global state (the status line shows "Tool output: expanded/collapsed"), but the box in the pending area never expands — even though it still shows "(ctrl+o to expand)". Cause (from reading dist 1.5.0): `handleBashCommand` adds the `BashExecutionComponent` to `pendingMessagesContainer` when `session.isStreaming` is true, but `setToolsExpanded` only iterates `loadedResourcesContainer` and `chatContainer`. `flushPendingBashComponents()` (which moves it into chat) only runs when a message is submitted while idle.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Send a prompt that keeps the agent streaming for a while
2. While it streams, run `!!seq 1 60`
3. Once the command finishes, press `ctrl+o`
4. The output box stays collapsed, still shows "(ctrl+o to expand)"
5. Send any normal message (e.g. `ok`), then press `ctrl+o` — now it expands

## Expected behavior

`ctrl+o` should expand/collapse `!`/`!!` output regardless of whether the command ran while the agent was streaming.

## Version

1.5.0

issues.title: openai-completions: duplicate tool-call stream index silently concatenates two tool calls' arguments

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
### What happened?

When an OpenAI-compatible provider reuses the same `tool_calls[].index` for two different tool calls (distinct ids, distinct arguments), pi-ai silently concatenates both calls' argument streams into one tool call. The arguments end up as two JSON objects glued together:

```json
{"command":"echo AAA"}{"command":"echo BBB"}
```

and downstream `JSON.parse` fails with:

```
MALFORMED_RESPONSE: Tool call "bash": Unexpected non-whitespace character after JSON at position 98
```

No error is raised at parse time — the second call is just absorbed into the first block.

### Steps to reproduce

Stream these chunks from a mock/replayed OpenAI-compatible endpoint (both calls share `index: 0`):

```js
{ choices: [{ delta: { tool_calls: [{ index: 0, id: "call_A", type: "function", function: { name: "bash", arguments: '{"command": "echo AAA"}' } }] }, finish_reason: null }] }
{ choices: [{ delta: { tool_calls: [{ index: 0, id: "call_B", type: "function", function: { name: "bash", arguments: '{"command": "echo BBB"}' } }] }, finish_reason: null }] }
{ choices: [{ delta: {}, finish_reason: "tool_calls" }] }
```

Result: one toolCall block with the concatenated arguments above.

Root cause: in `packages/ai/src/api/openai-completions.ts`, `ensureToolCallBlock` resolves the target block by stream index first, then by tool-call id, with no check that the two keys agree — so the second call matches the first call's block via the index key.

### Expected behavior

Two independent toolCall blocks (`bash` / `{"command": "echo AAA"}` and `bash` / `{"command": "echo BBB"}`). I have a fix ready (collision guard in `ensureToolCallBlock`: on key disagreement where the delta starts a new call — carries a function name — start a fresh block; this preserves the existing mid-stream id-mutation coalescing behavior tested in `openai-completions-tool-choice.test.ts`) plus a regression test, and can submit a PR if approved.

### Version

pi-ai 1.5.0 (observed via dsh headless against a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint; also reproduced with a mock stream against the repo's test harness)

### What do you want to change?

## Issue

`deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` is available through QwenCloud but is missing from the Pi `qw` provider's model list.

```bash
pi --list-models deepseek
```

```text
provider  model            context  max-out  thinking  images
qw        deepseek-v4-pro  1M       384K     yes       no
```

I was able to use the missing model by registering a separate custom provider, but additional API compatibility and long-context issues required workarounds.

## 1. Missing Model — models.json

Creating `~/.pi/agent/models.json` with a separate provider ID (`qwen-custom`) resolves the model registration issue.

Using the existing `qw` provider ID did not expose the additional model.

```json
{
  "providers": {
    "qwen-custom": {
      "baseUrl": "https://token-plan.maas.qwencloudapi.com/compatible-mode/v1",
      "api": "openai-completions",
      "apiKey": "$QWENCLOUD_API_KEY",
      "models": [
        {
          "id": "deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017",
          "name": "DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017",
          "reasoning": true,
          "input": ["text", "image"],
          "contextWindow": 1000000,
          "maxTokens": 384000,
          "compat": {
            "supportsDeveloperRole": false
          }
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

The `supportsDeveloperRole: false` setting is necessary to resolve:

```text
Error: 400: developer is not one of
['system', 'assistant', 'user', 'tool', 'function']
```

## 2. Long-Context Issue — settings.json

During extended coding sessions, the API may return:

```text
Error: 400: data_inspection_failed
Input text data may contain inappropriate content.
```

A fresh session works normally, and running `/compact` resolves the error in the affected session.

To preserve the 1M context window while triggering compaction earlier, the following configuration can be used in `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`:

```json
{
  "compaction": {
    "enabled": true,
    "modelOverrides": {
      "qwen-custom/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017": {
        "reserveTokens": 100000
      }
    }
  }
}
```

This targets compaction around 900K tokens instead of the default threshold near 984K.

The early-compaction configuration is a proposed workaround; its effectiveness against `data_inspection_failed` has not yet been verified.

## Suggested Improvements

- Include `deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` in the QwenCloud provider's model catalog.
- Apply the appropriate API compatibility settings automatically, particularly `supportsDeveloperRole: false`.
- Consider earlier automatic compaction or a `/compact` recovery suggestion when long-context requests encounter `data_inspection_failed`.

**Result:** The model works successfully with the custom provider and compatibility configuration. Manual `/compact` also restores affected long-running sessions.

### Why?

The QwenCloud provider does not currently expose `deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017` in its model catalog, preventing users from selecting the model directly in Pi.

Manual configuration is required to address three issues:

1. **Missing model registration:** The model must be added through a separate custom provider in `models.json`.
2. **API incompatibility:** The QwenCloud endpoint rejects the `developer` role, requiring `supportsDeveloperRole: false`.
3. **Long-context failures:** Extended sessions may return `data_inspection_failed`, which can be resolved by manually running `/compact`.

Adding native support for this model, including appropriate compatibility settings and improved long-context handling, would eliminate the need for these manual workarounds.

### How? (optional)

_No response_

labels.name: no-action
labels.description: This issue has been rejected after triage

issues.body:
**What happened?**

I'm writing a viewer for pi session files, and it can't read them: the fourth line of every session is a `type: "message"` entry whose `message.role` is `system`, so the reader stops with `Unknown message role: system` and shows nothing at all.

```json
{"type":"message","id":"2b87aefe","timestamp":"2026-11-06T14:22:18.912Z",
 "message":{"role":"system","content":"",
            "sections":{"preamble":"You are a coding assistant…","tools":"<tools>…","rules":"<rules>…","docs":"…","project_context":"…","skills":"…","cwd":"…","mcp_servers":"…"},
            "timestamp":1793974938909,"toolsAdded":[{"name":"read","description":"…","parameters":{…}}, …]}}
```

Two things make this awkward on the reading side:

- `system` isn't in the role set a transcript otherwise has (`user` / `assistant` / `tool`), so anything that switches on role throws and gives up on the whole file.
- `content` is an empty string. The text is in `sections`, and the full tool schemas are repeated in `toolsAdded`, so a reader that skips system messages — or renders `content` — shows nothing where the session header should be.

Happens in every session I have, e.g. `~/.pi/agent/sessions/--Users-…--/2026-11-06T14-22-06-063Z_<uuid>.jsonl`, line 4 (after `session`, `model_change`, `thinking_level_change`). Not extension-related; reproduces with `pi -ne`.

**Steps to reproduce**

1. `pi` in any repo, send one prompt, quit.
2. Open the session `.jsonl`.
3. First `type: "message"` line: `message.role == "system"`, `message.content == ""`, prompt text under `message.sections`.

**Expected behavior**

Any of these would be fine:

- the system prompt becomes its own entry type (`type: "system"` or `"system_prompt"`), so "the messages" keep meaning user / assistant / tool;
- or `message.content` carries the joined text, with `sections` kept as the structured extra;
- or, at minimum, the session format documentation says consumers must ignore `role: "system"` message entries and that `content` can be empty.

As it is, every reader has to know about `sections` and special-case the role; ones that don't just fail on the file.

**Version:** 1.5.0 (npm `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`, macOS)
