issues.title: durable: per-conversation compaction policy
issues.body:
Observed on `@earendil-works/pi-durable` 1.5.0. Related: #10942 (per-model compaction settings, closed), which this extends with a per-conversation layer.

## Problem

`CompactionPolicy` (`enabled`, `reserveTokens`, `keepRecentTokens`, `backgroundTokens`) can only be set harness-wide
(`HarnessSettings.compaction`) or per model (`modelOverrides`). A host that runs many conversations in one Harness
cannot give one conversation its own thresholds or switch its automatic compaction off.

Our case (mehos, a web panel over one Harness per process): the owner wants "auto-compaction off for this session"
and, later, different thresholds for a long research session than for a short chat. Today we can only:

- switch a session off with a `beforeCompact` hook that returns `{ decline: true }` (works, but the compaction task
  has already been created and the hook runs once per attempt; thresholds stay global), and
- change the global value through a `settings.compaction` getter (works, since settings are read at every use).

Neither gives per-conversation thresholds. `AgentChange` has no compaction field, and `compactionPolicy(settings, model)`
(compaction.js) does not take the conversation.

## Proposal

Add a per-conversation layer, resolved after the model override:

```ts
type AgentChange = {
  // ...existing fields
  /** Overrides CompactionPolicy for this conversation, field by field; null clears it. */
  compaction?: Partial<CompactionPolicy> | null;
};
```

- Stored in `AgentDoc` like `thinkingLevel`/`maxTurns`, so it is durable, versioned with the agent state, and copied
  by fork/subagent the same way other agent fields are.
- Resolution order, field by field: conversation `agent.compaction` > `modelOverrides[provider/model]` > harness-wide
  policy > defaults. `compactionPolicy(settings, ref, agent)` gets the agent as a third argument.
- All threshold checks (generation preparation, background trigger, overflow recovery) use the resolved policy, so
  `enabled: false` skips threshold and overflow compaction before a task is created. Manual `compact()` still ignores
  `enabled`, as today.

## Alternative (smaller)

Let `HarnessSettings.compaction` be a function of the conversation: `compaction: CompactionPolicy | ((id: ConversationId) => CompactionPolicy)`.
No storage change, the host owns persistence. Less durable (policy is not part of the conversation), but trivial to add.

## Why not just hooks

`beforeCompact` runs after range selection and cannot lower or raise thresholds, only decline a compaction that was
already due. It also cannot stop background compaction from being scheduled.

## Compatibility

Additive: no field means today's behaviour. Happy to send a PR if the direction is acceptable.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): prevent uncaught AbortError when local file or session reads abort
prs.body:
## Problem

When an `AbortSignal` aborts while a `read` tool call is opening or statting a local file (for example when a `codemode` script returns with an unawaited `tools.read(...)` call still in flight and `Execution.finish()` aborts pending call controllers), `pi` crashes and exits with an uncaught `AbortError`:

```
pi exiting due to uncaughtException:
AbortError: The operation was aborted
    at stream.<computed>.AbortError.cause (node:internal/streams/add-abort-signal:47:22)
    at module.exports.addAbortSignalNoValidate (node:internal/streams/add-abort-signal:53:5)
    at addAbortSignal (node:internal/streams/add-abort-signal:38:25)
    at ReadStream.Readable (node:internal/streams/readable:376:7)
    at new ReadStream (node:internal/fs/streams:257:3)
    at FileHandle.createReadStream (node:internal/fs/promises:414:12)
    at Object.readLocalFileChunks (packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/read.ts:84)
    at async selectLinesFromStream (packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/read.ts)
```

## Root cause

1. **`packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/read.ts` (`readLocalFileChunks`):**
   `handle.createReadStream({ end, signal, autoClose: false })` passes `signal` to `new ReadStream`, which calls Node's `addAbortSignalNoValidate(signal, stream)` synchronously in the constructor. If `signal` aborted while `detectImageMimeType`, `fsOpen`, or `handle.stat()` was resolving (or if `selectLinesFromStream` exits its `for await` loop early on abort), `stream.destroy(new AbortError(...))` queues `emitErrorNT` on `process.nextTick` with no `'error'` listener attached on the `ReadStream`, raising `uncaughtException`.

2. **`packages/coding-agent/src/core/session-manager.ts` (`buildSessionInfo`):**
   `createReadStream(filePath, { encoding: "utf8", signal })` has the same `addAbortSignal` hazard on early exit: when the first parsed entry is not `"session"` and `buildSessionInfo` returns `null` early on a file larger than one 64 KiB chunk, `for await` closes `readline` (removing `readline`'s `'error'` listener) without destroying `stream`. A subsequent `signal.abort()` destroys the still-open `ReadStream` with `AbortError` and no listener attached.

## Fix

- Replace `handle.createReadStream({ end, signal, autoClose: false })` in `readLocalFileChunks` with direct 64 KiB `handle.read(buffer, 0, buffer.length, null)` reads guarded by `signal?.throwIfAborted()`, keeping `handle.close()` in `finally` and returning early if `signal` aborted during `detectImageMimeType`. Non-empty regular files still stop at their initial `stats.size` so growing files terminate, and zero-size or special files (such as `/proc`) still read until EOF.
- Remove `signal` from `createReadStream` in `buildSessionInfo`, keep an `'error'` listener attached on `stream`, wire an explicit abort listener (`rl.close(); stream.destroy()`), check `signal?.throwIfAborted()` around `stat` and `for await`, and always clean up both `rl` and `stream` in `finally`.

## Verification

- `packages/coding-agent/test/read-streaming.test.ts`: staggered real-file `createReadTool` aborts across `open`/`stat` (reproduced 15 uncaught `AbortError`s before the fix; 0 after) and unawaited `CodemodeSandbox` `tools.read` calls cancelled on script return (`0` `uncaughtException` / `unhandledRejection`).
- `packages/coding-agent/test/session-manager/file-operations.test.ts`: `SessionManager.list` early-returning on a >64 KiB non-session `.jsonl` file followed by `controller.abort()` (reproduced 1 uncaught `AbortError` before the fix; 0 after).
- `packages/codemode/test/sandbox.test.ts`: late async rejection from an unawaited tool call aborted on script return across `worker`, `inline`, and `remote` backends (`0` `unhandledRejection` / `uncaughtException`).
- `npm run check` and touched Vitest suites pass.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): match grep globs relative to path
prs.body:
The grep tool's `glob` was matched from the folder pi was started in, not from `path`. A glob with a folder in it found nothing when `path` was a different folder.

Example: pi runs in `/tmp/g`, and `/tmp/g/repo/migrations/main/a.js` contains `hello`.

| Call | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `path: "repo", glob: "migrations/main/*.js"` | `No matches found` | `migrations/main/a.js:1: hello` |
| `path: "repo", glob: "**/migrations/main/*.js"` | `migrations/main/a.js:1: hello` | same |
| `path: "repo", glob: "*.js"` | works | same |

The empty result looks like a real negative, so the model concludes the file does not exist. Grep prints results relative to `path` (`migrations/main/a.js`), which is the form the failing glob used.

**Cause:** ripgrep always matches `--glob` from its own working directory and has no option to change that. `grep.ts` started rg without `cwd`, so it inherited pi's.

**Fix:** for directory searches, start rg with `cwd: searchPath` and search `.`, then resolve rg's `./…` output paths against `searchPath` in `formatPath`. The output format is unchanged. The glob is now anchored at `path`: a lookalike at `repo/nested/migrations/main/b.js` does not match `migrations/main/*.js`, and `**/migrations/main/*.js` still matches both.

Searching `.` instead of the absolute path is needed for symlinks. rg takes its working directory from the OS, which returns the real path (`/tmp/real/repo`), but it builds found paths from the search argument as given (`/tmp/link/repo/...`). Those don't share a prefix, so the glob would miss again (macOS `/tmp` is a symlink). With `.`, the found paths are already relative.

Single-file searches are unchanged: rg cannot start inside a file, and it ignores `--glob` for files named directly.

A leading `./` in the glob (`./src/*.ts`, `!./dist/**`) is now dropped, because rg never matches it.

The `glob` description now says the glob is relative to `path`, and that a pattern without `/` matches file names at any depth.

Alternatives considered:
- Prefix `**/` to globs that contain `/`, as `find` does: a one-line change, but it also matches nested lookalike folders (#10418).
- Rewrite the glob to an absolute one: rg reads a leading `/` as anchored at its working directory, not at the filesystem root. It would also need glob escaping of folder names, special handling for basename globs, and Windows drive handling.

**Behavior change:** a glob written relative to pi's cwd while `path` points elsewhere no longer matches. That only worked by accident and contradicted the output format.

**Testing**
- New regression test in `test/tools.test.ts` with a plain and a symlinked `path`: an anchored folder glob, the nested lookalike, `**/`, `./` and `!./`. It fails on main with `No matches found`.
- `test/tools.test.ts` passes (111 tests), and `npm run check` passes.
- Windows: ran the built tool with Windows Node and `rg.exe` on `C:`, covering relative, absolute and junction `path`, `**/`, `./`, `!./`, no glob, and a single file. All gave the expected output with `/` separators.

fixes #11807
fixes #10998

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): wait for image resize worker to terminate
prs.body:
`resizeImageInWorker` starts a new worker thread for each image. Its `finally` block called `void worker.terminate()`, so `resizeImage()` returned before the worker had stopped. When images are read one after another, the next worker can then start while the previous one is still shutting down. On macOS arm64 with Node 24.16 this overlap was reported to abort the whole process with SIGABRT, with the stack inside `node::worker::Worker::Run` during startup.

This change awaits `worker.terminate()`, so each resize returns only after its worker has stopped. It still ignores errors from `terminate()`. The cost is the worker's shutdown time on each resize.

Limitation: this only helps resizes that run one after another. Parallel tool calls can still run several resize workers at once.

## Testing

- Added `test/image-resize-worker-teardown.test.ts`. It replaces `Worker` with a fake whose `terminate()` stays pending, and checks that `resizeImage()` does not resolve until termination finishes. The test fails without the fix (`expected true to be false`) and passes with it.
- Passing: the existing image tests (`image-processing`, `image-resize-callers`, `image-process`, `tool-result-images`).
- `npm run check` failed, but only on type errors in `packages/ai/test` (`cache-retention`, `max-thinking`, `supports-xhigh`) about model IDs; no error points at files in this change. Lint reported nothing.
- I could not reproduce the SIGABRT itself on Linux with Node 24.22, using the reporter's worker-churn reproducer (800+ rounds), so the crash fix is not confirmed. The reporter saw the abort go away with this exact change on macOS with Node 24.16.

Fixes #10695

Requested by @petrroll

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): edit refuses files that are not valid UTF-8
prs.body:
The edit tool decodes a file as UTF-8 and writes it back as UTF-8. A file that is not valid UTF-8 has every byte it cannot decode replaced with U+FFFD, and the tool still reports success. This affects UTF-16 files and files in legacy encodings such as Windows-1252 or GBK.

Example from #10349: a GBK `config.py` with a Chinese comment and `TIMEOUT = 30`. Editing `TIMEOUT = 30` to `TIMEOUT = 60` returns "Successfully replaced 1 block(s)". The comment is now garbled and the file grew from 36 to 52 bytes.

This PR makes the edit tool refuse such files instead:

```
Could not edit file: config.py. It is not valid UTF-8 (for example UTF-16, or a legacy encoding such as Windows-1252 or GBK). The edit tool only writes UTF-8, so editing it would corrupt it. The file was left unchanged. To change it, use a shell command that keeps its encoding.
```

The file is decoded with `new TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: true, ignoreBOM: true })` instead of `buffer.toString("utf-8")`. For valid UTF-8 the result is the same string, and a UTF-8 byte order mark is kept as before. Invalid UTF-8, which includes any file starting with a UTF-16 byte order mark, throws and is refused. The TUI preview (`computeEditsDiff`) uses the same check, so it shows the error instead of a diff.

This does not try to support other encodings. Per the discussion in #5797, guessing encodings is unreliable and models expect UTF-8. Refusing the edit is the narrowest fix for the silent corruption, as #10349 proposed. #11811 is the alternative that edits UTF-16 and ASCII ranges of legacy-encoded files; this PR is the smaller option.

**Behavior change:** edits to files that are not valid UTF-8 now fail with the error above instead of succeeding and corrupting the file. The `read` tool is unchanged.

**Testing**
- New `test/edit-tool-non-utf8.test.ts`:
  - Windows-1252, GBK, UTF-16LE and UTF-16BE files are refused with the message, the file bytes are unchanged, and the preview returns the same error. This fails on main.
  - A UTF-8 file with a byte order mark still edits and keeps the mark. This passes on main too.
- `test/tools.test.ts`, the other `test/edit-tool-*.test.ts` files, `test/edit-diff-window.test.ts` and the UTF-8 BOM regression test pass, 129 tests in total.
- `npm run check` passes.

fixes #10349

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): edit keeps line endings of untouched lines, diffs only around changes
prs.body:
The edit tool rewrote the line endings of lines it did not touch. It could also fail after the file was already written, for example by running out of memory while diffing a large file. Encoding handling (non-UTF-8, UTF-16) was split out into a separate PR.

## Line endings (#8544)

**Problem.** The edit tool looked for the first line ending in the file, normalized the whole file to LF for matching, and wrote the whole file back with that one ending:

```
a\nb\r\nX = 1\r\n   edit X = 1 -> X = 2   =>  a\nb\nX = 2\n    (both CRLF became LF)
a\r\nb\nc           edit c -> C           =>  a\r\nb\r\nC     (the LF became CRLF)
a\rb\nX = 1\n       edit X = 1 -> X = 2   =>  a\nb\nX = 2\n    (untouched lone CR became LF)
```

**Solution.** Matching still runs on the LF-normalized text, so matching itself is unchanged: exact and fuzzy matching, multiple edits, duplicates, overlaps and error messages. `applyEditsToNormalizedContent` now also returns the replacements it applied. `applyReplacementsToOriginal` maps each replacement back to the original text and splices it in there. Normalizing only shortens CRLF to LF, so the original offset is the normalized offset plus the number of CRLFs before it. A range that covers a normalized LF therefore covers the whole CRLF. Text outside the replaced ranges keeps its bytes.

Line breaks in the new text use the line ending of the line where the replaced range starts. For an unterminated last line, they use the ending of the line before. A lone CR is used only in files with no LF at all (classic Mac files). Elsewhere a lone CR is more likely a control character inside a line.

Fuzzy matches still rewrite the whole lines they touch, as before. They now return those lines as one replacement instead of rebuilding the file, so lines outside the replacement keep their endings.

A kept CR and an LF can meet at a splice seam and would then merge into one CRLF line break. For example, in `a\rb\nc` the edit `b -> \nB` would write `a\r\nB\nc` (normalized `a\nB\nc`) while the diff shows `a\n\nB\nc`. Deleting `b` would write `a\r\nc` while the diff shows `a\n\nc`. Whenever a piece ending in CR is followed by a piece starting with LF, an LF is added at the seam. This turns the CR into a CRLF of its own, so the written file normalizes to exactly the content the diff and patch describe. No kept byte is changed or removed; the one added byte sits where the replaced text was. For a pure deletion between a lone CR and an LF there is no other way to keep both line breaks. Writing the merged bytes and diffing them instead would silently join two lines the model meant to keep apart.

Pure LF and pure CRLF files produce the same output as before. For files without any CR, the normalized result is written directly, as before.

## Diff before writing, only around the changes

**Problem.** `execute` wrote the file and then ran `generateDiffString` and `generateUnifiedPatch`. Each diffs the whole file with jsdiff, which takes roughly 10 to 15 times the file size in memory, however small the change. A two-line edit of a 50 MB file crashed with `--max-old-space-size=256` after the new content was already on disk, and took about 4 s with the default heap. The TUI preview (`computeEditsDiff`) diffed the whole file again.

**Solution.**
- The diff and patch are computed before the file is written, so a failure there leaves the file unchanged.
- The edit tool and the preview use a new internal `generateEditDiff`. The replacement positions are known, so it diffs only a window around each replacement: the replaced lines plus 32 unchanged lines on each side, with overlapping windows merged. jsdiff still does the diffing; the window results are renumbered to file line numbers. The display diff uses the same formatter as `generateDiffString` (extracted into `formatDisplayDiff`), and the patch is jsdiff's `structuredPatch` hunks shifted and written with `formatPatch`, as `createTwoFilesPatch` does.
- `details.diff`, `details.patch` and `firstChangedLine` have the same format and content as before for every file size. The one possible difference: in runs of repeated lines, jsdiff may align a change differently within a window than over the whole file. The patch still applies and describes the same edit.
- The exported `generateDiffString` and `generateUnifiedPatch` are unchanged.
- The model-visible result is unchanged.

## Behavior differences

  - fuzzy match widening in a mixed file

prs.title: fix(ai): translate sampling reasoning_effort through thinkingLevelMap
prs.body:
## Problem

`samplingParams.reasoning_effort` is applied **after** the `thinkingLevelMap`
translation (`Object.assign(params, samplingParams)` is the last step of
`buildParams`), so a config-level literal bypasses the map and reaches the wire
as typed.

That makes an "advertised but unsupported" level unrecoverable for callers. Measured
against SGLang serving `moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1`:

| request | result |
|---|---|
| `reasoning_effort: "low"` | 200 |
| `reasoning_effort: "high"` | 200 |
| `reasoning_effort: "max"` | 200 |
| `reasoning_effort: "medium"` | **HTTP 500** — `Unsupported thinking_effort='medium'; supported values are ['high','low','max']` |

The server's own validation enum *lists* `medium` (`none, minimal, low, medium,
high, xhigh, ultra, max`; `ultra` is also a 400), so the value passes the API
schema and dies in the chat template.

A model that correctly declares `thinkingLevelMap: { medium: "high", ... }` still
sends `medium` if any sampling literal names it, because sampling params win. The
only workaround for the caller was to not configure `reasoning_effort` at all.

## Change

Translate a `reasoning_effort` literal through `thinkingLevelMap` when it names a
thinking level, and drop the key when the model marks that level unsupported
(`null`). The map becomes authoritative again.

- Non-level values (e.g. `"thorough"`, numbers) are untouched.
- Request-supplied sampling params keep their normal precedence.
- Models without a `thinkingLevelMap` behave exactly as before.

## Tests

`packages/ai/test/sampling-reasoning-effort-map.test.ts` covers: medium→high
translation, `null` dropping the key, non-level values preserved, no-map models
unchanged, and request params still overriding non-effort sampling keys.

## Compatibility

Strictly narrower than before: an effort literal that names a level now resolves
through the map the caller already wrote. Nothing that previously produced a
*working* request changes its outcome, because before this change the map was
simply ignored for that key.

prs.title: fix(ai): omit empty tools array for tool history on openai-completions
prs.body:
## Problem

`openai-completions` sends `"tools": []` whenever a request has no tools but the transcript contains tool calls or tool results. vLLM 0.20+ rejects this ([vllm#39780](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/39780)), directly or behind LiteLLM:

```
400: `tools` must not be an empty array. Either provide at least one tool or omit the field entirely.
```

Trace: session uses tools -> all tools disabled (or SDK call without tools) -> next request has `tools: []` -> 400 on every request. There was no way to opt out.

The empty array came from #150 (2024), a workaround for LiteLLM raising `Anthropic doesn't support tool calling without tools= param specified`. Current LiteLLM adds a dummy tool itself for Anthropic in that case (`litellm/llms/anthropic/chat/transformation.py`).

The OpenAI spec defines `tools` as an optional array, so omitting it is valid. vLLM issue #39741 reports that OpenAI also rejects `tools: []` with `empty_array`; not verified here.

## Change

- Omit `tools` by default when there are no tools.
- New `compat.requiresToolsWithToolHistory` (default `false`) restores `"tools": []` for proxies that need it, such as older LiteLLM versions in front of Anthropic.
- Regenerated `models.schema.json` and `models-configuration.md`.
- Tests: default omits the field (#11843), the compat flag sends `[]`.

## Risk

Setups that relied on the implicit `[]`: older LiteLLM with Anthropic, and possibly OpenRouter Claude models (the only built-in Claude models on `openai-completions`). Not verified against OpenRouter; those users can set the flag.

Fixes #11843

prs.title: fix(tui): draw fullscreen Kitty images after the rows they cover on every terminal
prs.body:
Closes #11835

## Problem

In Orca, fullscreen inline images show only their first row; regular mode shows them in full.

Orca renders Kitty graphics with xterm.js's image addon, which stores an image as tiles in the cells it covers. WezTerm does the same. For a 5-row image, `TuiAltScreen` wrote:

```
row 1: move, clear line, image sequence   -> image covers rows 1-5
row 2: move, clear line, ""               -> erases image row 2
...
row 5: move, clear line, ""               -> erases image row 5
```

Regular mode clears the covered rows first and draws the image last, so it was unaffected. Fullscreen already had that ordering, plus a redraw when a covered row changes, but only for WezTerm (#10319).

## Fix

Use the draw-images-last path and the covered-row redraw for every Kitty terminal instead of only WezTerm. Cost is bounded by the viewport (the visible rows and the images in view, re-placed from the uploaded copy without retransmitting), not by scrollback.

## Testing

- Headless repro with Orca's exact `@xterm/xterm@6.1.0-beta.336` + `@xterm/addon-image@0.10.0-beta.331` and Orca's patches applied, counting image tiles per row: before, fullscreen kept tiles only in the first image row; after, all rows.
- Real terminals (WSLg screenshots), with initial render, a write to a covered row, scrolling, and a cropped image:

| Terminal | Old interleaved output | Draw images last |
|---|---|---|
| Ghostty 1.3.1 | correct | correct |
| Kitty (latest) | correct | correct |
| herdr 0.9.5 in Ghostty | correct | correct |
| WezTerm nightly 20260117 | first row only | correct |

- Regression tests in `packages/tui/test/tui-alt-screen.test.ts` no longer depend on terminal env vars. `tui-alt-screen.test.ts` passes, and `npm run check` is clean.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): run shutdown cleanup when the Windows console closes
prs.body:
## Problem

pi listens for SIGHUP only on POSIX (`process.platform !== "win32"` in interactive, print and RPC mode). The check came with the first SIGHUP handler (5d440b055, #3212), and neither the commit nor the issue mentions Windows.

On Windows, Node never emits SIGTERM (`TerminateProcess` cannot be caught), but libuv does emit SIGHUP when the console window or terminal tab is closed (`CTRL_CLOSE_EVENT`). Windows then ends the process about 5 s later (measured 4.8-5.1 s). With no SIGHUP listener, closing the window ran no `session_shutdown` and killed no process trees:

```
pi in a conhost window, bash tool running `bash -c "sleep 300"`, close the window
before: pi exits at once, no session_shutdown, ping/sleep.exe + bash.exe keep running
```

Libuv's job object kills the bash process Node spawned, but not what bash started.

Enabling SIGHUP alone was not enough. On Windows, `killTrackedDetachedChildren()` started an asynchronous `taskkill /F /T` per pid, and the shutdown paths call `process.exit` right after it. pi's exit kills the shell (libuv's job), and `taskkill /T` walks parent pids, so it no longer finds the shell's descendants. Killing a shell and exiting at once left `sleep.exe` + bash 6 out of 6 times.

## Solution

- Interactive, print and RPC mode listen for SIGHUP on all platforms.
- On Windows, `killTrackedDetachedChildren()` runs one `taskkill /F /T /PID a /PID b ...` and waits for it (`spawnSync`, 2 s timeout, well below the ~5 s Windows allows after a close). `windowsHide` gives taskkill its own hidden console, so it does not receive the closing console's close event. This also fixes the same race on the dead-terminal and crash exit paths, which already call it.
- Normal quit in interactive mode (Ctrl+D, `/quit`) and RPC `shutdown()` call `killTrackedDetachedChildren()` after `dispose()`. `dispose()` only starts the asynchronous kill of a running user `!` command or RPC `bash` command, which had the same race: quitting while `!ping -n 3000 127.0.0.1` ran left `ping.exe` and two `bash.exe` on Windows (before and after enabling SIGHUP). Agent bash tool commands were not affected, since dispose waits for the aborted tool.
- `docs/extensions.md` notes that on Windows `session_shutdown` has about 5 s after a console close.

## Testing

Windows 11 x64, Git Bash, built pi started in a new `conhost.exe` or `wt.exe -w new` window by a PowerShell script, with a test extension whose fake model runs one bash tool call and which logs `session_shutdown`. The window was closed by posting `WM_CLOSE` to the console window; Ctrl+D and `/quit` were typed with `WriteConsoleInput`.

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| conhost close, print / RPC | exit 1 after ~20 ms, no `session_shutdown`, ping + 2 bash left | exit 129 after 270-370 ms, `session_shutdown` runs, nothing left |
| conhost close, interactive | same | exit 0 after 390-600 ms, nothing left |
| Windows Terminal window close, all 3 modes | same as conhost | same as conhost |
| `session_shutdown` hook taking 3 s | - | completes, exit at ~3.3 s |
| `session_shutdown` hook taking 8 s | - | Windows kills pi at 5.03 s (`0xC000013A`); processes already gone, since the kill runs before `session_shutdown` |
| Ctrl+D / `/quit` while a `!` command runs; RPC stdin EOF while a `bash` command runs | command left running | nothing left |

- Writes to the closed console do not throw or hang (no EPIPE); interactive runs reached the normal exit path.
- The waited taskkill takes 190-330 ms, only when a command is running; otherwise `killTrackedDetachedChildren()` returns at once.
- Linux (WSL), real pi: SIGHUP exits 129, SIGTERM 143, both run `session_shutdown` and leave nothing; RPC stdin EOF exits 0. Same before and after.
- New tests: SIGHUP on win32 in `print-mode.test.ts` (fails without the change), the single waited taskkill and unchanged POSIX behaviour in `shell-kill-process-tree.test.ts`, kill after dispose on RPC stdin EOF in `rpc-prompt-response-semantics.test.ts` (fails without the change). These and `bash-close-hang-windows` pass.
- `npm run check`: clean apart from `check:install-lock:coding-agent`, which fails on Windows on unmodified `main` too (the generator orders the `chalk` entry differently); the steps after it pass.

## Notes

- `taskkill /T` still misses processes whose parent already exited, for example `sleep` in `bash -c "sleep 300; echo x"`, `sleep 300 | cat` or `sleep 300 &` in Git Bash. This is the gap #11854 closes with a job object. #11854 touches the same signal handlers and `killTrackedDetachedChildren()`; whichever lands second needs a rebase.
- Not tested: closing a single tab of a Windows Terminal window with several tabs (same close event, only whole windows were closed).

prs.body:
If you ran `!` or `!!` while the agent was streaming, the output box went into the pending-messages area. `setToolsExpanded` only updated the loaded-resources and chat containers, so ctrl+o changed the global state but not that box. The box stayed collapsed, still showing "(ctrl+o to expand)", until a later idle submit moved it into the chat.

This change:
- adds `pendingMessagesContainer` to the containers `setToolsExpanded` updates;
- calls `setExpanded(this.toolOutputExpanded)` on new `!`/`!!` output components in both paths of `handleBashCommand`. Before, they always started collapsed, even when tool output was expanded.

- `npm run check` passes.

  - Before: running `!!seq 1 60` during streaming and pressing ctrl+o showed "Tool output: expanded", but the box still said `... 41 more lines (ctrl+o to expand)`.
  - After: the box expands and collapses with ctrl+o while the agent is still working.
  - A second `!!` command run while expanded starts expanded.

Fixes #11875

Requested by @petrroll

**Follow-up commit (related bugs in the same pending-area code):**
- `updatePendingMessagesDisplay()` cleared the pending area whenever a steering or follow-up message was queued or delivered. That hid `!`/`!!` output still waiting to move to the chat, so ctrl+o could not reach it, and it came back on the next submit with an old expand state. The pending area now rebuilds with those boxes first, then the queued messages.
- Pending `!`/`!!` output now moves into the chat on `agent_settled`, when the session records the deferred bash results. Before, it waited for the next idle submit.
- `renderCurrentSessionState()` now drops pending bash boxes. Before, a box could carry over into the next session's chat after `/new`, `/resume` or `/fork`.
- Tests in `test/interactive-mode-status.test.ts` cover ctrl+o in the pending area, queued-message updates and the move on settle. All three fail without the fix.

prs.title: fix(tui): keep out-of-band stderr from corrupting the fullscreen display
prs.body:
## Problem

In fullscreen mode, `/new` can leave the previous session on screen: old user input stays visible below the "New session started" banner and model-scope warnings print over the interface, so the new session looks like it still contains old messages. Reported in #11264 and reproduced there with extensions disabled.

## Root cause

1. `TuiAltScreen` renders by diffing each frame against the previous one and writes only changed rows. Bytes any other writer leaves on the terminal are invisible to that model and persist until a full repaint.
2. Every session switch re-creates the runtime, which re-resolves the model scope; `resolveModelScope` warned the "No models match pattern ..." diagnostic straight to stderr — out-of-band, exactly as the renderer redraws.

The reporter's evidence isolates stderr as the trigger: with stderr to `/dev/null` the stale input cleared in 2/2 trials; with normal stderr it persisted 2/2.

## Fix

Three parts:

1. **Alt-screen stderr guard (`packages/tui`).** While the alt screen is active, `TuiAltScreen` diverts `process.stderr.write` to an opt-in `onStderrLine` sink: line-buffered, ANSI-stripped, empty lines dropped, write callbacks invoked and `true` returned. The original write is restored in `beforeTerminalStop`, which every stop path runs (including fatal ones), so crash output on the restored main screen stays raw. While the guard is active, no stderr byte can land on the terminal behind the diff renderer.

2. **In-band warning rendering (`packages/coding-agent`).** Both `createInteractiveTui` call sites (initial mount and the fullscreen remount) pass a sink that strips the doubled `Warning: ` prefix and renders the line via `showWarning`, so diverted output appears as chat content instead of baking into the display.

3. **Model-scope diagnostics through the runtime channel.** The guard alone wasn't enough: `renderCurrentSessionState()` clears the chat container after the diverted `/new` warning lands, so it was silently swallowed. `main.ts` now collects the diagnostics from `resolveModelScopeWithDiagnostics` into the runtime's diagnostics set, and interactive-mode renders the fresh runtime's diagnostics in the rebind hook — the one point that fires after a session switch clears the transcript — so the warning stays visible below the banner. Non-interactive modes keep printing via `reportDiagnostics`; the raw-warn `resolveModelScope` variant is removed (no production callers remained).

Scope note: stderr only. stdout is owned by the TUI; a runaway stderr writer now produces in-chat lines rather than display corruption, mirroring regular-mode scrollback.

## Tests

- `packages/tui/test/stderr-guard.test.ts` — 8 pins: diversion while active (intercepted bytes never reach the terminal stream), restore-on-stop, partial-write buffering, ANSI strip + empty-line drop, Uint8Array decode, trailing-line flush, write-callback semantics, no-op without the option.
- `packages/coding-agent/test/model-resolver.test.ts` — pins diagnostics collection; the raw-print pin is removed with the retired function.
- Same-surface tmux reproduction of the reported scenario (fullscreen, unmatched `enabledModels` pattern, extensions disabled): before the fix the warning is baked into the editor interior and stale input persists; after, it renders as an in-chat line above "New session started" with no stale pixels, in both normal-stderr and stderr-suppressed arms.

Fixes #11264

AI disclosure: this fix and its description were developed with AI assistance (pi coding agent) under human
direction and review.

prs.title: openai-completions: split tool-call blocks when stream index and tool-call id disagree
prs.body:
Fixes #11881

## Root cause

`ensureToolCallBlock` in `packages/ai/src/api/openai-completions.ts` resolves the target block for a streamed tool-call delta by stream `index` first, then by tool-call `id`. When an OpenAI-compatible provider violates the streaming contract and reuses the same `index` for two different tool calls (distinct ids, distinct arguments), the second call's argument fragments are silently appended to the first call's block, producing concatenated arguments like:

```json
{"command":"echo AAA"}{"command":"echo BBB"}
```

Downstream `JSON.parse` then fails with `Unexpected non-whitespace character after JSON at position N` (observed against pi-ai 1.5.0 with a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint replayed via dsh headless).

## Fix

Collision guard in `ensureToolCallBlock`: after a block is matched via either key (index or id), verify the other key agrees; on disagreement — and only when the delta actually starts a new call, i.e. it carries a function name — discard the match (`block = undefined`) so a fresh block is created for the second call. An `indexMismatch` check against the block's recorded stream index covers the mirror case (a delta whose index disagrees with the block it matched by id).

The "carries a function name" condition is load-bearing: some providers (e.g. Kimi) mutate the tool-call id mid-stream on continuation deltas that carry no name; those fragments belong to the same call and must keep coalescing by stable stream index. The pre-existing regression tests for that behavior (`coalesces tool call deltas by stable index when provider mutates ids mid-stream`, `accumulates mixed content, reasoning, and parallel tool call deltas independently`) pass unchanged.

## Test

New regression test `packages/ai/test/openai-completions-duplicate-tool-call-index.test.ts` feeds a mock stream in which two tool calls (`call_A`/`call_B`, both `bash`) illegally share `index: 0`, and asserts **two** independent toolCall blocks with arguments `{command: "echo AAA"}` / `{command: "echo BBB"}` (2 `toolcall_start` / 2 `toolcall_end` events).

Local run (vitest 4.1.12, packages/ai):

```
 Test Files  11 passed (11)
      Tests  131 passed (131)
```

covering the new file plus the existing openai-completions family (empty-tools, tool-choice incl. the id-mutation coalescing tests, azure-openai-completions, cache-control-format, prompt-cache, reasoning-details, retry, raw-stop-reason, vllm-priority, thinking-token-budget) — zero regressions.

prs.title: fix(coding-agent): keep apostrophes in prompt template arguments
prs.body:
`parseCommandArgs` started a quoted section at every `'` or `"`, even in the middle of a word, and dropped the quote character. As a result, `/ask why doesn't the user's cache work` reached the model as `why doesnt the users cache work`. With a single apostrophe, everything after it became one argument, so `$1`/`$2` were wrong. Backslash-escaped quotes were not supported either: `"quoted \"text\""` gave `quoted \text\`.

What the change does:
- A quote only opens a quoted argument at the start of an argument. Apostrophes inside words such as `doesn't` and `user's` stay as text.
- If a quote has no closing match, the parser goes back to the quote, keeps it as text, and parses the rest of the input normally. For example, `'tis the season` gives `'tis`, `the`, `season`.
- Inside a quoted argument, a backslash before that argument's quote character gives a literal quote: `"quoted \"text\""` gives `quoted "text"`, and `'it\'s here'` gives `it's here`. All other backslashes are kept as typed, so paths such as `"C:\dir\file"` and `'\\server\share'` don't change.
- `"..."`, `'...'`, `""` and `''` arguments behave as before.

One edge case: a quoted argument that ends in a backslash, such as `"C:\dir\"`, now reads the final `\"` as an escaped quote. The quote then never closes, so the whole argument is kept literally, quotes included.

The prompt templates doc and the changelog describe the new behavior.

Testing:
- Added tests in `packages/coding-agent/test/prompt-templates.test.ts` for apostrophes inside words, quotes with no closing match, and escaped quotes (including paths that keep their backslashes). The existing escaped-quote test now expects `quoted "text"`. All 96 tests in the file pass.
- `npm run check` passes.
- Before: `parseCommandArgs("why doesn't the user's cache work")` → `["why","doesnt the users","cache","work"]`. After: `["why","doesn't","the","user's","cache","work"]`.

Fixes #11861

Requested by @davidbrai

issues.title: fix(managed-agent): resident external workspace bindings have no shipped retirement/recovery entry point

labels.name: priority/P2
labels.description: Medium - Moderately impactful, noticeable problem

labels.name: status/blocked
labels.description: Blocked by external dependency

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working as expected

issues.body:
## Summary

The resident external-workspace recovery/retirement/EPHEMERAL entry points added by #16023 have no production caller, and the stop/close paths for a shared binding all refuse. A deployment that enables `provisioner=external-workspace` with `bound-session-isolation-class=workspace` — a combination #16023 newly validates as legal — can create a Session but can never CLOSE it: the operation ends in a permanent `409` with no shipped route to finish the retirement it demands.

Deferred from #16023 (round 4) under the AGENTS.md review-scope rule. **Interaction with R3-3:** #16023's R3-3 fix enables external workspace provisioning, so this lifetime gap must be closed before workspace sharing is production-ready.

Review thread: https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16023#discussion_r4496692291 (finding R1-21).

## Problem

`retire`, `resume`, `listCandidates`, `requireSnapshot`, `recoverSnapshot` and `ensureEphemeralRegistered` are constructed only by tests; `external-terminal-retirement-enabled` appears nowhere but its annotation (it is absent from `configuration-descriptions.json`, which documents 438 sibling keys). Meanwhile the stop/close paths for a shared binding all refuse: `completeStoppedSessionRelease`, `requireDrainMembers` and `canStopExternalDrained` answer `409` for the shared class. So nothing reachable can stop or close a resident binding.

## Evidence

- `packages/managed-agent-server/persistence/src/main/java/com/alibaba/qwen/code/managedagent/persistence/ExternalWorkspaceRetirementService.java:30` — retirement entry point, test-only construction.
- Tree-wide grep for `ExternalWorkspaceRetirement` returns this file and its test; grep for `external-terminal-retirement-enabled` returns only the annotation; `ExternalWorkspaceRecoveryService` and `ExternalWorkspaceRegistrationService` have the same shape (test-only construction).

## Impact

A legal configuration can create but never close a Session (permanent `409`, resource leak). Blocks the resident-binding lifetime model that #16023's workspace sharing depends on.

## Suggested fix

Give the retirement/recovery path a shipped, operator-gated entry point (and document the property in `configuration-descriptions.json`), or drop the files and land them with their callers — and until then keep the durable non-shared drain available so a Session can still be closed.

**Constraint the fix must keep:** `HarnessOwnership.sharesRuntimeSessions` keys on the isolation class plus the managed context and capability digest, so any "let durable ones drain" fix must branch on `RegisteredExternalStorage.ephemeral()` rather than on the isolation class.

## Acceptance criterion

An end-to-end case that enables the workspace-isolated external profile, creates and closes a Session, and asserts it reaches `CLOSED` (or that a documented operator call finishes the retirement) — no test drives `CLOSE` on a shared binding today.

issues.title: fix(managed-agent): EPHEMERAL workspace registration skips cross-tenant host-path exclusivity

labels.name: priority/P1
labels.description: High priority issue

labels.name: status/blocked
labels.description: Blocked by external dependency

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working as expected

labels.name: category/security
labels.description: Security and privacy

issues.body:
## Summary

`registerEphemeralWorkspace` does not enforce the cross-tenant host-path exclusivity check that `registerExternalStorage` enforces. A second registration can claim a host directory another tenant already owns, in both directions (external→ephemeral and ephemeral→external), binding the same host path under two different owners with no coordination.

Deferred from #16023 (round 4) under the AGENTS.md review-scope rule: the EPHEMERAL registration path has **no production caller** today (`parseStorage` admits only `EXTERNAL`), so this is unreachable in the shipped surface and is tracked here as a security hardening follow-up rather than blocking the PR. It must be closed before any caller enables EPHEMERAL registration.

Review thread: https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16023#discussion_r4496692280 (finding R3-6).

## Problem

The ephemeral document is decoded with `aliasPath == mountRoot`, so it claims a host path exactly as an external registration does. Register tenant A externally at `/aliases/one`, then:

```
registerEphemeralWorkspace("B", "k2",
    new EphemeralWorkspaceRegistration("provider", "ws", "/aliases/one", 1))
```

The alias key is tenant-hashed, `ma_workspace` and `ma_runtime_binding` are empty for B, and no path comparison exists, so the row is inserted and two Workspaces bind the same host directory under different owners. One tenant's writes and deletes land in the other's tree with no coordination, and `physical_key` differs by construction so nothing downstream detects it. The reverse order is equally open because the exclusivity scan reads only `storage_kind = 'EXTERNAL'`, which #16023 starts producing EPHEMERAL rows alongside.

## Evidence

- `packages/managed-agent-server/persistence/src/main/java/com/alibaba/qwen/code/managedagent/persistence/ExternalStorageRegistrationStore.java:138` — `registerEphemeralWorkspace` has neither the path scan nor the global lock.
- `ExternalStorageRegistrationTest.conflictsNeverRebindAliasesPhysicalOwnersOrIdempotencyKeys` pins the invariant for the external path (a different tenant registering `/aliases/one` must get `alias_conflict`); the ephemeral method has no equivalent.

## Impact

Cross-tenant data exposure / corruption (one tenant's writes and deletes land in another tenant's host tree). Unreachable today because no production code path registers EPHEMERAL storage; becomes live the moment a caller is wired.

## Suggested fix

Apply the same path-exclusivity rule to `registration.mountRoot()` before the inserts in `registerEphemeralWorkspace`, and widen the existing scan to `storage_kind IN ('EXTERNAL','EPHEMERAL')` so the external direction sees ephemeral claims too.

**Constraint the fix must keep:** the cross-tenant scan is serialized by a deliberate global lock row (`WorkspaceStorageKindGuard.lockDomain(jdbc, "external-storage-registration/1", 10)`), while the ephemeral path takes only the per-tenant lock; a cross-tenant scan added there must take the same global lock.

## Acceptance criterion

A new case registering an external alias then asserting the ephemeral registration for another tenant throws `409 alias_conflict`, plus the reverse order — both red without the guard.

issues.title: Aux-model selectors persist a NUL-separated baseUrl that every public surface emits verbatim

labels.name: priority/P2
labels.description: Medium - Moderately impactful, noticeable problem

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working as expected

labels.name: category/configuration
labels.description: Configuration management

labels.name: category/security
labels.description: Security and privacy

labels.name: scope/model-switching
labels.description: Model selection and switching

labels.name: scope/credential-security
labels.description: Credential security

issues.body:
## Summary

Five settings keys persist a model selector in the form `authType:<id>\0<baseUrl>`: `visionModel`, `imageModel`, `advisorModel`, and — as of #12773 — `fastModel` / `compactionModel`. When a provider `baseUrl` embeds userinfo (`https://user:sk-...@host/v1`), that suffix **is a credential**. There is no single owner of this format: each surface that reads one of these settings decides for itself whether to strip, display, or publish the suffix, and most publish it verbatim.

This was found while reviewing #12773 (fix for #12760). That PR made `fastModel` join the class; four review rounds then grew per-site scrubs for `fastModel` only, which covered 2 of the 4 aux branches in the same dialog handlers and left the class open. Those scrubs were removed again in [`a240767`](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/12773/commits/a240767784f68687a5d4ccf968c2184a7f1d38f6) — the class belongs in one central change, which is what this issue is for.

## Verified egress surfaces (all on `main` @ `5deddb722b`)

Every one of these was read off `origin/main`, not off the review thread:

1. **Daemon settings route** — `publicValue` redacts `mcpServers` and nothing else (`packages/cli/src/serve/routes/workspace-settings.ts:196-197`). `WEB_SHELL_SETTINGS` contains `imageModel` and `advisorModel` (`:59-65`), so both are served to the Web Shell verbatim.
2. **Daemon providers-status payload** — `fastModelId` (`packages/cli/src/serve/workspace-providers-status.ts:142-145`) and `visionModelId` (`:146-149`) are emitted verbatim, in the same `current` object whose neighbouring `baseUrl` field *is* scrubbed.
3. **ACP status payload** — `const fastModelId = this.settings.merged?.fastModel || undefined` (`packages/cli/src/acp-integration/acpAgent.ts:8308`), emitted at `:8322`. `readCoreSettingValues` likewise returns core setting values unchanged, and `fastModel` is one of them (schema entry `:1544`).
4. **`/system` extended info** — `packages/cli/src/ui/systemInfo.ts:237`.
5. **`/settings` dialog row** — `fastModel` and `visionModel` are in `isSubDialogSetting` (`packages/cli/src/ui/components/SettingsDialog.tsx:1275-1279`) and the row renders `displayValue = String(effectiveCurrentValue)` (`:1303`), i.e. the raw NUL-bearing string.
6. **`/model --vision` / `--image` readback** — `formatVisionModelSettingForDisplay` returns `` `${parsed.selector} (${parsed.baseUrl})` `` with the URL unsanitized (`packages/cli/src/ui/commands/modelCommand.ts:114-121`, called at `:720` and `:936`), so a userinfo-bearing URL is echoed to the terminal.
7. **Workspace-scope writes** — the picker writes the selector at whatever scope `getPersistScopeForModelSelection` resolves to, with no sanitizing on any aux branch. At `Workspace` scope that file is `<project>/.qwen/settings.json`, which teams commit. A project that declares its own `modelProviders` resolves to Workspace without the user picking a scope.
8. **Startup advisor-validation error → stderr** — `resolveAdvisorModel` reads `settings.advisorModel` raw, applying only `.trim()` (`packages/cli/src/config/config.ts:1240`), and `validateCliAdvisorModel` interpolates that raw value into the failure message (`formatUnavailableAdvisorModelMessage`, `:1255`: `` `Advisor model '${modelName}' is not configured.` ``), which is thrown as a `FatalConfigError` (`:1279`) and written to stderr by the startup error handler. `checkAdvisorModelAvailability` hand-rolls its own `modelName.indexOf('\0')` split (`packages/cli/src/config/advisor-model.ts:83`). The advisor pin is persisted at `SettingScope.User` while the provider entry usually is not, so running `qwen` in any other workspace makes the model unavailable and puts the credential — plus a literal NUL byte — into terminal scrollback, a CI job log or `2>err.txt`, on a path where the CLI has already failed and the user is reading that output. Found while reviewing #12862 (round 4, R4-1); neither file is in that PR's diff, which is why it is recorded here rather than fixed there.

## The format itself has no owner

- **Writers disagree on the empty suffix.** `packages/cli/src/serve/model-configuration.ts:178` persists `` `${authType}:${model.id}\0` `` (empty suffix) when the entry declares no `baseUrl`, while `:189` / `:196` persist a real one.
- **Readers disagree on what an empty suffix means.** `packages/core/src/utils/modelId.ts` drops everything after the NUL; `packages/core/src/agents/forkedAgent.ts:259-263` turns an empty suffix into `null`; `splitModelBaseUrl` in `packages/core/src/core/baseLlmClient.ts:48-57` turns it into `undefined`. Those three values are not interchangeable downstream — `null` and `undefined` take different branches in `getModel` (`packages/core/src/models/modelRegistry.ts:395-402`) and in the forked-runtime guard (`packages/core/src/models/content-generator-config.ts:222-231`).
- **Declared vs effective baseUrl.** The registry exposes both: `baseUrl` is the effective URL (`config.baseUrl || getDefaultBaseUrl(authType)`, `modelRegistry.ts:467`) and `registryBaseUrl` is the declared one (`:468`). Registry keys and the forked-runtime guard compare the *declared* value; the picker and `serve/model-configuration.ts` persist the *effective* one. Concrete consequence on `main`: the daemon's provider-delete scrub compares the persisted endpoint against the deleted entry's configured `baseUrl` (`packages/cli/src/serve/routes/workspace-models.ts:332`), so a dangling pin written for an entry that declared no `baseUrl` is not cleared. #12773 translates effective → declared at the `getFastModel()` / `getCompactionModel()` boundary for this reason; the divergence itself is still there for the other three keys.
- **Two publishability predicates with opposite failure modes**, in the same file: `sanitizeProviderBaseUrl` returns its input unchanged when the string has no `scheme://` prefix (`packages/cli/src/utils/acpModelUtils.ts:179-182`), so scheme-less and protocol-relative userinfo shapes pass through; `publicProviderBaseUrl` (`:17-25`) is fail-closed and strips userinfo, query and hash. Callers pick between them ad hoc.

## Suggested shape

One module owning the aux-selector format — encode, decode, display, and a single fail-closed "is this URL publishable" predicate — and then each egress site calls it instead of hand-rolling a `split('\0')`. That closes items 1-8 with one decision rather than eight, and makes the empty-suffix and declared-vs-effective questions answerable in one place.

Worth deciding explicitly while doing it: whether the *persisted* value should be the declared `baseUrl` (registry identity, what the guard and the delete-scrub compare) rather than the effective one. That single choice removes the divergence in the third bullet instead of translating around it at each consumer.

## Reproduction

No credentials needed to see the shape; the credential case only needs a provider `baseUrl` with userinfo. `\^@` below is the JSON escape for the NUL separator the format uses:

```jsonc
// ~/.qwen/settings.json
{ "visionModel": "openai:some-model\^@https://user:sk-secret@host/v1" }
```

Then read it back through any surface above — e.g. `GET /workspace/settings` from the daemon, or `/model --vision` with no argument in the CLI, which prints `openai:some-model (https://user:sk-secret@host/v1)`.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

`visionModel` / `imageModel` / `advisorModel`（以及 #12773 之后的 `fastModel` / `compactionModel`）都以 `authType:<id>\0<baseUrl>` 持久化。当 provider 的 `baseUrl` 带 userinfo 时，这个后缀就是凭据。这个格式没有统一归属：每个读到它的面自行决定剥离、显示还是原样对外，而大多数是原样对外。

上面 8 个出口面全部是在 `main`（`5deddb722b`）上逐个读代码核实的，不是从评审线程抄的；第 8 条（启动期 advisor 校验失败信息 → stderr）是 2026-09-29 复查 #12862 第 4 轮 R4-1 时补录并重新核实的：`resolveAdvisorModel` 只 `.trim()` 就原样读 `settings.advisorModel`（`config.ts:1240`），`formatUnavailableAdvisorModelMessage`（`:1255`）把这个原值插进报错文案并抛成 `FatalConfigError`（`:1279`），而 `advisor-model.ts:83` 自己手写 `indexOf('\0')` 拆分——advisor pin 存在 User scope、provider 条目通常不在，于是在别的 workspace 里跑 `qwen` 就会把凭据连同一个字面 NUL 字节送进终端回滚缓冲、CI 日志或 `2>err.txt`。另外三处结构性问题也已核实：写者对「空后缀」不一致（`serve/model-configuration.ts:178`）、读者对空后缀的语义不一致（`null` vs `undefined` vs 丢弃，下游分支不同）、以及「声明 baseUrl vs 有效 baseUrl」的错位（注册表 key 和 fork 运行时校验比的是声明值，而持久化写的是有效值；`workspace-models.ts:332` 的删除清理因此会漏掉悬空的 pin）。

建议的修法是一个模块统管这个格式的编解码、显示与「可否对外」判定，各出口面调用它，而不是各自 `split('\0')`。顺带值得明确决定：持久化值是否应该改成「声明的 baseUrl」——这一个选择就能消掉第三处错位，而不必在每个消费方各翻译一次。

这个 issue 从 #12773 拆出来：那个 PR 修的是 #12760 的持久化不对称，评审四轮里长出的逐站点清洗只覆盖 4 个 aux 分支中的 2 个，已在 `a240767` 删除。

</details>

<!-- autofix-deferred pr=12975 -->

Verified review findings from PR #12975 by wenshao whose fixes lie outside that PR's footprint, deferred by the autofix loop for follow-up. cc @wenshao. issues.title: feat(core): continuable subagents — follow-up messages to sub-sessions and failed background agents
issues.body:
## Proposal

Make a subagent a conversation the orchestrator can return to, not a one-shot
function call. Two concrete gaps share one theme — in both, the continuation
machinery already exists on the other side of the boundary and only the
model-facing surface is missing:

1. **Sub-sessions (daemon)**: `create_sub_session` returns a `sessionId`, but
   no tool accepts it. Every follow-up must spawn a fresh sub-session and
   re-pay the context warm-up, while the daemon already continues any session
   by id.
2. **Background agents (classic)**: `send_message` continues `completed` and
   `paused` agents — but a `failed` agent is permanently rejected, even though
   its transcript and recorded error persist on disk and the transcript-revival
   path that would restore it already exists.

Codex CLI treats both cases as continuable; this proposal brings the same
shape to qwen-code by exposing existing capability rather than adding new
machinery.

## Motivation

**Sub-sessions.** The spawner result hands the model an addressable handle
(`sessionId`) with no operation that consumes it. Asking one more question
about a sub-session's work today means either a brand-new sub-session (all
context restated, prior conversation lost) or pulling the whole thread back
into the parent's context. Yet the sub-session is a first-class persisted
session — parent lineage is recorded into its transcript — and the daemon's
`continueSession` is already exercised by HTTP routes. The gap is purely the
tool layer.

**Failed agents.** The terminal handling is asymmetric: `completed` agents can
be continued twice over (resident runtime, else transcript revival), `paused`
agents resume, but `failed` agents are rejected outright — their transcript,
which shows exactly where the run went wrong, stays on disk and unreachable.
The orchestrator's only recourse is a fresh agent that starts blind to the
failure. Continuing a failed agent from its transcript, with the recorded
`lastError` injected as context, is the same revival machinery already used
for non-resident completed agents.

## Current state (anchors)

**Sub-sessions:**

- Tool parameter surface (`packages/core/src/tools/create-sub-session.ts:43-48`):
  `prompt`, `completion`, `model`, `name` — no session id, no continuation form.
- Spawner contract (`packages/core/src/config/config.ts:2470-2501`):
  `SubSessionSpawnRequest` carries only the four fields above; the result
  returns `sessionId` — the handle exists, the operation does not.
- Lifecycle (`packages/cli/src/serve/create-sub-session.ts:34-35`): the
  sub-session is fire-and-forget — not kept resident, idle-reaped once done;
  its transcript persists.
- Server-side continuation already exists:
  `StandaloneSessionService.continueSession`
  (`packages/cli/src/serve/conversations/standalone-session-service.ts:1101`),
  used by the HTTP session routes.

**Background agents:**

- Terminal dispatch (`packages/core/src/tools/send-message.ts`): `paused` →
  resume (line 281); `completed` → resident continue, else transcript revival
  (lines 307-348); **any other status — including `failed` — is rejected**
  (lines 350-358, "Cannot send messages to stopped tasks").
- Failure evidence persists: the meta sidecar is patched to `status: 'failed'`
  with `lastError` recorded
  (`packages/core/src/agents/background-agent-resume.ts:1424-1434`).
- Revival machinery exists: `recoverTranscript` rebuilds history from the
  JSONL, replays it into a fresh runtime, appends to the same transcript with
  a `resumeCount` increment (background-agent-resume.ts:341-424, 1100-1149);
  `reviveCompletedBackgroundAgent` (line 713) is the completed-status entry
  point.
- Existing blocklist preserved by any change:
  `continuationBlockedReason` (external executors, container isolation) is
  stored in the registry and checked before continuation
  (send-message.ts:270-279).

## Proposed shape

- **Slice 1 — continuable sub-sessions**: give the model a follow-up path that
  continues an existing sub-session by id through the daemon's existing
  `continueSession` path, instead of always spawning fresh. Exact surface is
  open question 1; either way the spawner contract gains a continuation form
  and the tool description tells the model when to reuse a session.
- **Slice 2 — continue failed background agents**: extend the terminal
  dispatch in `send_message` so a `failed` entry routes through the existing
  transcript-revival path (resident continuation does not apply — no live
  runtime after failure), with the recorded `lastError` injected into the
  continuation context so the agent resumes knowing how it failed. The
  `continuationBlockedReason` guard, eviction cap, and `resumeCount`
  accounting all carry over unchanged.
- Slices are independent; either can land first.

## Non-goals

- Foreground subagents stay one-shot — the deliberate skip rule
  (background-agent-resume.ts:508-512, foreground sidecars are never exposed
  as continuable) is not revisited here.
- No `--resume` picker exposure of subagent transcripts — they live under
  `subagents/`, not the session store's `chats/`, by design.
- No new persistence format; transcripts and meta sidecars as-is.
- No hosted/web-shell surface in this slice.
- No change to the Live Voice automatic follow-up path.

## Open questions

1. Slice 1 surface: a `session_id` parameter on `create_sub_session` (one
   tool, two modes) vs a sibling `continue_sub_session` tool (one mode per
   tool). Tool-count discipline vs schema ergonomics — maintainers' call.
2. Slice 2 semantics: the follow-up message as the next instruction with
   `lastError` appended as context (consistent with the existing revival
   prompt shape), vs a dedicated "retry the original instruction" form.
3. Follow-up arriving while a `completion: 'sent'` sub-session is still
   mid-turn: queue it or reject until idle?
4. Should a continuation surface in the parent transcript as a linked entry,
   the way spawn results do today?

<details><summary>中文说明</summary>

## 提案

让子代理成为编排方可回访的"对话"，而非一次性的函数调用。两个具体缺口同属一个主题——两边都是续跑机制已经存在于边界另一侧、只缺面向模型的入口：

1. 子会话（daemon）：create_sub_session 返回 sessionId，却没有任何工具能消费它；每次追问都必须新开子会话、重付上下文预热，而 daemon 本已支持按 id 续跑任意会话。
2. 经典后台代理：send_message 可以续跑 completed 与 paused，但 failed 被永久拒绝——即使其转录与记录的错误都在磁盘上、能恢复它的转录复活路径也已存在。

Codex CLI 对两种情形都允许续跑；本提案通过暴露既有能力（而非新增机制）把同样的形态带给 qwen-code。

## 动机

子会话侧：spawner 结果把一个可寻址的句柄（sessionId）交给模型，却没有消费它的操作。对子会话的工作多问一个问题，今天要么全新开一个（上下文全部重述、先前对话丢失），要么把整条线索拉回父会话上下文。而子会本是第一等的持久化会话——父系血缘已写入其转录——daemon 的 continueSession 也已被 HTTP 路由使用。缺口纯在工具层。

失败代理侧：终态处理不对称——completed 两条路可续（常驻运行时、否则转录复活），paused 可恢复，failed 直接拒绝；记录了失败位置的转录留在盘上却不可达，编排方只能换一个对失败一无所知的新代理。让 failed 经由既有转录复活路径续跑、把记录的 lastError 注入续跑上下文，用的正是非驻留 completed 代理今天已在用的机制。

## 现状锚点

子会话侧：工具参数面（create-sub-session.ts:43-48）只有 prompt/completion/model/name，无会话 id；spawner 契约（config.ts:2470-2501）请求仅此四字段、结果却返回 sessionId——句柄存在、操作不存在；生命周期（serve/create-sub-session.ts:34-35）fire-and-forget，不驻留、空闲即回收、转录持久；服务端续跑已存在（standalone-session-service.ts:1101 continueSession，HTTP 会话路由在用）。

后台代理侧：终态分发（send-message.ts）paused→恢复（281）、completed→常驻续跑/转录复活（307-348）、其余状态含 failed 一律拒绝（350-358）；失败证据持久——meta 侧car被打成 status:'failed' 并记录 lastError（background-agent-resume.ts:1424-1434）；复活机制已备——recoverTranscript 重建历史、重放进新运行时、同一转录追加并递增 resumeCount（同文件 341-424、1100-1149），reviveCompletedBackgroundAgent（713）是 completed 状态的入口；continuationBlockedReason（外部执行器、容器隔离）先于续跑检查（send-message.ts:270-279），任何改动都保留该封锁。

## 形态

切片 1——可续跑子会话：给模型一条按 id 续跑既有子会话的路径，走 daemon 既有 continueSession，而不是总是新开。确切入口形态见待定问题 1；无论哪种，spawner 契约增加续跑形态，工具描述告诉模型何时复用会话。切片 2——续跑失败的后台代理：扩展 send_message 终态分发，failed 条目走既有转录复活路径（常驻续跑不适用——失败后无存活运行时），并把记录的 lastError 注入续跑上下文，让代理带着"如何失败的"恢复。continuationBlockedReason 守卫、逐出上限、resumeCount 记账全部原样保留。两切片相互独立，可分别落地。

## 非目标

前台子代理保持一次性——刻意的跳过规则（background-agent-resume.ts:508-512，前台侧car永不暴露为可续跑）不在本提案重议；不把子代理转录暴露进 --resume 选择器（它们按设计位于 subagents/ 而非会话库 chats/）；无新持久化格式，转录与 meta 侧car照旧；本切片不含 hosted/web-shell 面；不改 Live Voice 自动跟进路径。

## 待定问题

1. 切片 1 入口：create_sub_session 加 session_id 参数（一个工具两种模式），还是独立的 continue_sub_session 工具（一工具一模式）——工具数量纪律与 schema 工效之间，由维护者定。
2. 切片 2 语义：跟进消息作为下一条指令、lastError 附加上下文（与现有复活提示形态一致），还是专门的"重试原始指令"形态。
3. completion:'sent' 的子会话仍在回合中时跟进到达：排队，还是拒绝直到空闲？
4. 续跑是否应在父转录中像今天的 spawn 结果那样显示为链接条目？

</details>

issues.body:
## Context

PR #16404 fixes live stacked-skill overflow reporting. Its final repair delivers the warning to QQ without losing it after streaming or duplicating it across deferred sends. After five review rounds, the remaining non-blocking suggestions are recorded here rather than expanding that correctness fix.

## Follow-up decisions

- Structured stdout: headless currently writes the warning to stderr in all output modes. Decide whether JSON/stream-JSON should also expose a structured notice, and define its schema and compatibility before changing the contract.
- Consumer regression coverage: add a focused headless sink test that verifies warning visibility, unchanged successful exit behavior, and uncontaminated JSON stdout. Parser tests and historical runtime evidence exist; the stderr sink currently lacks a dedicated retained test.
- Transcript replay: decide whether this transient pre-turn warning should be recorded and replayed. Live ACP delivery is implemented; replay is not part of the current contract.
- Warning wording: consider consolidating the identical message used by the two interactive surfaces and the non-interactive producer when one of those paths next changes. This is maintenance work, not a blocker.

Each item needs its own bounded justification; this issue is not a request to implement all four together or redesign channel delivery. References: #16396 and the [round-five review](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16404#pullrequestreview-5796286447).

issues.title: Isolate external PR CI with disposable runners
issues.body: External pull requests can run contributor-controlled CI scripts. Reusing self-hosted runners risks exposing host credentials or leaving files and processes behind for later jobs. We need isolated, disposable execution for these jobs, including a safe way to access models when required.

issues.title: feat(cli): /memory show — print the combined memory the session actually carries

labels.name: priority/P3
labels.description: Low - Minor, cosmetic, nice-to-fix issues

labels.name: type/feature-request
labels.description: New feature or enhancement request

labels.name: category/cli

labels.description: Memory and context management

labels.name: roadmap/terminal-ux
labels.description: Roadmap: Terminal UX and UI

issues.body:
## Proposal

Add a `show` subcommand to the existing `/memory` slash command that prints,
in the terminal, the combined memory content the current session carries
(hierarchical QWEN.md context files + the auto-memory prompt + the auto-memory
context). Today a user can manage memory from several surfaces but can never
simply *see* what is loaded. Gemini CLI's `/memory show` established this UX;
this brings parity with a change confined to `packages/cli/src/**`.

## Motivation

Every memory-editing surface has a verification blind spot:

- `/memory` opens a dialog of toggles and "open in editor" affordances — it
  renders no content.
- `/context` reports per-file token counts, not content.
- The `search-memory` tool is model-facing; the user transcript shows a
  one-line summary.
- `MemoryManager.getStatus` (per-topic entry counts) has no CLI caller.

So the loop "edit QWEN.md, run `/remember`, or migrate team memory → confirm
what the model now sees" requires an external-editor roundtrip. The content to
show is already well-defined: it is exactly what the system prompt assembles —
`getUserMemory()` as `contextFiles` and `getAutoMemoryPrompt()` as the
`autoMemory` layer — so showing that same combined view also closes a trust
gap ("is my edit actually loaded?") without introducing a second definition
of "memory".

## Current state (anchors)

- `/memory` dispatch (`packages/cli/src/ui/commands/memoryCommand.ts:19-30`):
  no args → open the memory dialog; any argument other than `migrate-team` →
  usage error. There is no `subCommands` array and no `show`.
- **The implementation already exists, unwired.**
  `createShowMemoryAction` (`packages/cli/src/ui/hooks/useShowMemoryCommand.ts:15-81`)
  builds the combined view from `config.getUserMemory()` +
  `config.getAutoMemoryPrompt()` + `config.getAutoMemoryContext?.()`
  (lines 32-40), reports the loaded context-file count (lines 41, 52-62), and
  prints the combined content in a markdown fence (lines 64-69), with an
  explicit empty-state message otherwise. Its only references repo-wide are
  its own test file and `dist/` artifacts — no production caller.
- What the model receives: `packages/core/src/core/client.ts:2241`
  (`contextFiles: this.config.getUserMemory()`) and `:2258`
  (`autoMemory: this.config.getAutoMemoryPrompt()`), assembled by
  `assembleSystemPrompt`. The command would print the same three inputs.
- `/context` memory detail is counts only:
  `packages/cli/src/ui/commands/contextCommand.ts:476-493`.
- Docs describe the panel UX without content display:
  `docs/users/features/memory.md:227-238`.

## Proposed shape

- Extend the `/memory` action: `/memory show` runs the show-memory behavior;
  update `argumentHint` to `[show|migrate-team]` and the usage error string
  accordingly.
- Wire through the existing `createShowMemoryAction` (or an inline equivalent
  with identical behavior driven by `CommandContext`) so command and hook
  cannot drift; its existing tests define the output contract.
- Output contract (already implemented): one INFO message with the loaded-file
  count, one INFO message with the combined content in a markdown fence, or
  the empty-state message when nothing is loaded. New user-visible strings go
  through i18n like the rest of the command.
- Docs: add `/memory show` to the command list in
  `docs/users/features/memory.md`.
- No `packages/core/src/**` change; the gate zone is untouched.

## Non-goals

- No editing or management from this command — the dialog plus `/remember`,
  `/forget`, `/dream` already own those.
- No new truncation/sizing logic in this slice (open question 2).
- No headless flag (`--memory-show`) — the command is interactive-only today;
  a non-interactive surface can follow if there is demand.

## Open questions

1. Reuse `createShowMemoryAction` as-is vs inline its logic into the command
   action via `CommandContext`. Either way the behavior should stay identical
   to the hook's existing tests.
2. Very large combined memory: print in full (default — it is what the model
   receives) or cap with a pointer to `/context` for sizes?
3. Should the count notice name the actual context files (from
   `settings.merged.context?.fileName`) instead of a bare count?

<details><summary>中文说明</summary>

## 提案

给现有 `/memory` 斜杠命令增加 `show` 子命令，在终端直接打印当前会话实际携带的组合记忆内容（分层 QWEN.md 上下文文件 + auto-memory prompt + auto-memory 上下文）。今天用户可以从多个入口管理记忆，却没有任何方式直接"看到"已加载的内容。Gemini CLI 的 `/memory show` 已确立这个交互；本提案以仅限 `packages/cli/src/**` 的改动补齐对齐。

## 动机

所有记忆编辑入口都有验证盲区：/memory 打开的是开关与"在编辑器中打开"的对话框，不渲染内容；/context 只报 token 数；search-memory 工具面向模型，用户转录只有一行摘要；MemoryManager.getStatus 没有任何 CLI 调用者。于是"编辑 QWEN.md / 执行 /remember / 迁移团队记忆 → 确认模型现在看到什么"这个循环必须绕道外部编辑器。而要展示的内容早有精确定义：就是系统提示装配的同一组输入（getUserMemory 作为 contextFiles、getAutoMemoryPrompt 作为 autoMemory 层），展示同一组合视图同时关闭一个信任缺口（"我的修改真的加载了吗？"），不引入"记忆"的第二套定义。

## 现状锚点

/memory 分发（memoryCommand.ts:19-30）：无参数→打开对话框；migrate-team 之外的任何参数→用法错误；无 subCommands、无 show。实现已存在但未接线：createShowMemoryAction（useShowMemoryCommand.ts:15-81）从 getUserMemory + getAutoMemoryPrompt + getAutoMemoryContext 构建组合视图（32-40 行）、报告已加载上下文文件数（41、52-62 行）、以 markdown 代码块打印组合内容（64-69 行），空态有明确消息；全仓引用只有它自己的测试文件和 dist 产物，没有生产调用者。模型接收侧：client.ts:2241（contextFiles）与 :2258（autoMemory）。/context 只有计数（contextCommand.ts:476-493）。文档描述的面板 UX 不含内容展示（docs/users/features/memory.md:227-238）。

## 形态

扩展 /memory action：/memory show 执行展示行为；argumentHint 改为 [show|migrate-team]，用法错误串同步更新。通过现有 createShowMemoryAction 接线（或经 CommandContext 内联等价实现），命令与 hook 不漂移，其现有测试即输出契约。输出契约（已实现）：一条 INFO 报文件数、一条 INFO 以 markdown 代码块展示组合内容，或空态消息；新增用户可见字符串走 i18n。文档补 /memory show 条目。不改 packages/core/src/**。

## 非目标

本命令不做编辑/管理（对话框与 /remember、/forget、/dream 已负责）；本切片不做截断/计量逻辑（待定问题 2）；不做 headless 旗标（--memory-show），有需求再跟进。

## 待定问题

1. 原样复用 createShowMemoryAction，还是经 CommandContext 内联进命令 action——无论哪种，行为都应与 hook 现有测试完全一致。
2. 组合记忆很大时：完整打印（默认，因为这就是模型收到的），还是截断并指向 /context 查看体量？
3. 计数提示是否应列出实际上下文文件名（settings.merged.context?.fileName）而非只报数量？

</details>

issues.title: feat(web-shell): expose Channel delivery targets in Scheduled Tasks

labels.name: status/needs-triage
labels.description: Issue needs to be triaged and labeled

labels.name: type/feature-request
labels.description: New feature or enhancement request

issues.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Add an optional Channel delivery target selector to the Scheduled Tasks create/edit form in the `qwen serve` Web Shell, and show the saved destination on the task card or details view.

The daemon already supports persisting a delivery target and sending a successfully completed scheduled run's final response through the configured Channel. This request exposes that existing capability in the Web UI.

**Expected behavior / acceptance criteria**

1. Users can leave delivery off, or explicitly choose a configured Channel instance and a supported user/chat destination in the task's workspace. Reuse the existing observed-contacts API for destination suggestions where available; show enough identity information to distinguish similarly named targets.
2. Creating or editing a task submits the existing `delivery` contract. Users can change the destination, reopen the form with the saved selection intact, and explicitly remove delivery (`delivery: null` on update). Editing unrelated fields preserves an existing destination, including one no longer returned by contact discovery.
3. The task card or details view shows whether delivery is configured and its destination. Configuring a Channel alone does not opt tasks into sending messages.
4. Respect the daemon's `channel_delivery` capability and existing session-mode restrictions. Delivery is supported for `persistent` tasks; explain that `per_run` tasks do not support it. Switching modes must not silently discard the destination or change the user's chosen mode.
5. Keep destination discovery and task mutations scoped to the selected workspace. Workspace changes must not retain or submit a destination selected from another workspace. Loading failures, no configured Channels, and unavailable targets should be understandable without silently clearing saved configuration. Observed contacts are discovery suggestions, not a new authorization requirement.
6. Include focused UI/browser coverage for create, edit, clear, saved-target round-trip, workspace changes, capability gating, and the `per_run` restriction. Existing tasks without delivery retain their behavior.

Use the existing API shape:

```json
{
  "delivery": {
    "kind": "channel",
    "target": {
      "channelName": "my-dingtalk",
      "type": "chat",
      "id": "<platform-chat-id>"
    }
  }
}
```

### Why is this needed?

A user can configure a Channel and create a recurring task entirely in the Web Shell, but cannot connect the two there. For example, scheduling a daily project summary and having its final response sent to a DingTalk group currently requires a separate daemon API request to add `delivery`.

The same gap makes destinations configured through the API invisible in the task form. A selector and saved-target display would make the existing backend feature discoverable and manageable without manual REST calls or instructions asking the model to send the result itself.

### Additional context

Source review of `main` at `3d9988abc25e526b6bcb8aaf866787025fab473c` confirms the gap:

- [Web form submission](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/3d9988abc25e526b6bcb8aaf866787025fab473c/packages/web-shell/client/components/dialogs/ScheduledTasksDialog.tsx#L1252) does not expose or submit a delivery selection.
- [Task creation](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/3d9988abc25e526b6bcb8aaf866787025fab473c/packages/cli/src/serve/routes/scheduled-tasks.ts#L1111) already accepts delivery and rejects the unsupported `per_run` combination; [task updates](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/3d9988abc25e526b6bcb8aaf866787025fab473c/packages/cli/src/serve/routes/scheduled-tasks.ts#L1535) support setting and clearing it.

This is a focused UI follow-up to the backend delivered in #7387 / #7388, related to the earlier request #7152. PR #7153 briefly implemented a selector and then removed it while narrowing scope; it was ultimately closed without merging. Its [scope-trimming design](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/2d299cba5cee4ee5ac406a7adccce73c62659bcc/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-18-daemon-scheduled-channel-delivery-design.md#L203) explicitly says:

> Web Shell destination UI already added on the feature branch is removed from this minimal change and can be proposed separately against the final API.

Keep this change on the final, existing API. Generic outbound webhook Channels, durable delivery retries/outboxes, failure alerts, and delivery support for `per_run` are separate features. The UI should describe the existing successful-final-response delivery behavior without promising guaranteed receipt.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

希望在 Web 定时任务的创建、编辑表单中增加可选的 Channel 投递目标选择器，并在任务卡或详情中显示已保存目标。复用 daemon 已有的 `delivery` 能力，支持设置、修改、清除和回显，让用户无需手工调用 REST API，就能将定时任务结果发往指定用户或群。

本次聚焦 Web UI：遵守 workspace 隔离、`channel_delivery` 能力开关及 `persistent` / `per_run` 限制；保留通过 API 配置的已有目标，联系人发现仅提供候选。任意 webhook、持久化重试、失败告警和 `per_run` 投递支持不在本次范围内。旧设计已明确允许针对最终 API 单独提出这项 UI 补齐。

</details>
