prs.title: fix(core): read the recent window of an over-cap session transcript
prs.body:
## What this PR does

A session transcript larger than the 256 MiB index cap is no longer refused. The reader indexes the last 256 MiB of it, starting at the first complete line, and reports where that window starts as a history gap with a new reason, `transcript_window`, so it can be told apart from history that was actually lost. The lines before the window are still parsed, without a full prefix index, so ownership and completeness checks cover the whole file and the session-level state a resumed session needs is restored even when it was recorded before the window: the first record (project check and start time), the session source and parent session, the last valid model, approval and workflow mode, the sources snapshot, the attribution snapshot and the last assistant model. The turn index now returns gaps too, and the CLI and ACP replay show a separate notice for a window cut: the earlier conversation was not loaded because the session is too large to restore in full.

A record written as several lines with one uuid that starts before the window is restored in full when the complete logical record fits within 256 MiB. Its turn and daemon prompt identities, navigation/display rules and parent relationship are rebuilt from the true first fragment, including when the final fragment has no visible text. The retained prefix state and prefix fragment references share a separate 256 MiB source-byte budget, and replaced settings release their retained bytes. Oversized logical records or retained prefixes receive the existing controlled size refusal. The scan never reads a physical line past the cap, and the first record is kept as metadata only unless it is also one of the settings above.

The index still refuses, with the same `transcript_too_large`, when no line starts within the window, when the window holds no conversation, when a prefix line or a complete logical record is longer than the cap, when the retained prefix exceeds its budget, or when the log is Managed.

## Why it's needed

#13113: a long-lived session that crosses 256 MiB becomes unopenable. All three reader APIs throw before reading a line, and a daemon restore answers `413 transcript_too_large`. A reported scheduled-task controller reached 280 MB in 20 days through ordinary growth (tool results, compression, telemetry, assistant messages), so fixing the snapshot write amplification alone would not keep such sessions under the cap. Today the only recovery is editing the JSONL by hand.

This follows the read-side direction discussed on the issue, which the affected operator confirmed is acceptable for their sessions as long as the restore says it is partial.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Create a transcript larger than 256 MiB in a workspace's `chats` directory (the scripts below generate one), start `qwen serve` in that workspace and call `POST /session/<id>/load` with `{"historyPageSize": 20}`.
2. Before this change the response is `413 transcript_too_large`. After it, the load succeeds, `GET /session/<id>/turn-index` returns a gap with `reason: "transcript_window"`, and the transcript page starting at that gap's child shows "Earlier conversation was not loaded…" rather than the storage-loss notice.
3. Unit tests: `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/services/session-transcript-reader.test.ts` (the `over-cap transcripts` block uses a test-only cap), and `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/ui/utils/resumeHistoryUtils.test.ts`.

4. Restore a bounded logical record whose first fragment is before the window and whose final fragment is empty or contains only a PDF attachment. Its original text and turn identity should remain present, including in the turn index.
5. Restore a record whose individual lines fit the limit but whose complete logical record exceeds it. Expect the existing `413 transcript_too_large`, rather than a partial record or a call-stack failure.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Verified independently on Ubuntu 24.04, Node 22.23.4, with the real 256 MiB cap unless a test-only cap is explicitly noted. All transcripts were synthetic; daemon checks used isolated HOME/runtime state, explicit loopback binding and no model inference.

| Scenario | Observed result on this revision |
| --- | --- |
| Ordinary 293,613,272-byte transcript | Load, turn index, transcript and boundary page all return 200; source metadata is retained; the boundary shows the window notice rather than a storage-loss notice |
| 283,226,963-byte reader fixture with a bounded two-part current record | Both parts, turn 42, original prompt/daemon identities and the corresponding turn-index row are retained |
| 283,223,178-byte daemon fixture with identity only on the first fragment and an empty final fragment | Load and turn index return 200; the original prompt row and first-fragment text remain visible |
| Original 342,640,968-byte / 150,000-prefix-fragment counterexample | Controlled `SessionTranscriptTooLargeError`; no `RangeError` |
| Three 96 MiB fragments forming one over-budget logical record | Reader refuses it intentionally; actual daemon load returns 413 with `code=transcript_too_large` |
| Small fixtures using a test-only 8 KiB cap | Cross-record prefix accumulation is bounded; ordinary partial history remains readable |

Eight independent reader checks and three actual daemon HTTP checks passed. The nine new reader regression cases cover text/empty/PDF tails, display suppression, first-fragment parent and gap classification, aggregate and cumulative limits, and budget release after settings are replaced. The failure cases were exercised against the unfixed implementations to establish that they catch the defects.

Final-source validation passed: complete root build and bundle; all-workspace and integration TypeScript checks; **792 core + 111 CLI + 165 ACP bridge tests (1,068 total)**; ESLint with zero warnings on the changed TypeScript files; Prettier and bilingual design-reference checks. Root typecheck used `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=6144`, matching the repository build budget: the 8 GiB host's default approximately 2 GiB compiler heap had been exhausted in unchanged CLI code. No assertions were weakened or failures suppressed. This is focused Linux acceptance evidence, not a full monorepo test-suite or hosted-CI result.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ not tested |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ Ubuntu 24.04, Node 22.23.4 |

### Environment (optional)

Built with the pinned pnpm 11.24.0 and frozen lockfile, `npm run build` and `npm run bundle`. Root typecheck used the same 6 GiB compiler heap budget as build. The daemon checks used isolated `HOME`/runtime state, a fake API key and a closed loopback model endpoint.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: this changes the contract set by the [selective session restore design](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/main/docs/design/2026-08-08-selective-session-restore.md), which made a cold restore over 256 MiB fail with 413. That limit was introduced as an intentional compatibility change requiring maintainer approval, and this revision needs the same. The prefix is still parsed, so opening a very large transcript takes time proportional to its size. State from before the window is limited to the kinds listed above; earlier UI telemetry, goal records, artifacts and file history are not restored, and turns before the window cannot be rewind targets. Settings recorded only before the window are taken in file order, because the prefix has no chain to walk; `rewindRecording` re-appends the current model, approval mode and workflow mode after its marker, so for those the last one in file order is the active one, while the last assistant model and the attribution snapshot can come from a branch abandoned before the window.
- Not validated / out of scope: macOS and Windows; Web Shell UI rendering (checked through the daemon routes it calls); writer-side growth, retention and the snapshot delta codec; a configurable cap. Fork is unchanged: it does not use the index and already copies the whole file, so the earlier sketch's idea of refusing fork from a windowed session turned out unnecessary.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none for transcripts under the cap. `HistoryGap.reason`, `TranscriptReplayGapInput.reason` and `SessionTranscriptTurnIndexPage.gaps` are optional additions. A client that relied on 413 for over-cap sessions now gets a partial restore instead.

Design: [English](https://github.com/Sumire-no-kai/qwen-code/blob/98907c83e781b771be7ccdbe28d9c9b309fb85d2/docs/design/2026-11-07-transcript-index-window.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/Sumire-no-kai/qwen-code/blob/98907c83e781b771be7ccdbe28d9c9b309fb85d2/docs/design/2026-11-07-transcript-index-window.zh-CN.md). Open questions for maintainers: whether windowing should replace the 413 by default or sit behind a setting, and whether the configurable cap the operator asked for as a stopgap is still wanted.

## Linked Issues

Refs #13113. This addresses the read-side refusal only; the snapshot write amplification and retention in that issue are separate.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 的改动

大于 256 MiB 索引上限的会话记录不再被拒绝。读取器从第一个完整行开始，索引其最后 256 MiB，并把窗口起点报告为带新原因 `transcript_window` 的历史缺口，以便与真正丢失的历史区分。窗口之前的行仍会被解析，但不建立完整的前缀索引，因此所有者与完整性校验覆盖整个文件；即使会话级状态记录在窗口之前，续接会话所需的状态也会恢复：第一条记录（项目校验与起始时间）、会话来源与父会话、最后一条有效的模型、审批模式和工作流模式、来源快照、归因快照，以及最后一条助手记录的模型。turn index 现在也返回缺口；CLI 和 ACP 回放对窗口截断显示单独的提示：会话过大，无法完整恢复，因此更早的会话记录未加载。

以同一 uuid 写成多行、且从窗口之前开始的记录，在完整逻辑记录不超过 256 MiB 时会完整恢复，并从真正的首分片重建回合身份、daemon prompt 身份、导航与展示规则和父节点关系，即使尾分片没有可见文字也不例外。保留的前缀状态和前缀分片引用共享一份独立的 256 MiB 源字节预算；设置被替换时会释放旧值占用。完整逻辑记录或保留前缀超额时，使用现有的受控大小错误拒绝。扫描绝不会读超过上限的物理行；第一条记录除非同时也是上面的某项设置，否则只保留元数据。

以下情况索引仍以相同的 `transcript_too_large` 拒绝：窗口内没有任何行首、窗口内没有会话记录、前缀物理行或完整逻辑记录超过上限、保留前缀超过预算，或日志是 Managed 会话。

## 为什么需要

#13113：长期运行的会话一旦超过 256 MiB 就无法打开。三个读取接口在读取任何一行之前就抛错，守护进程恢复返回 `413 transcript_too_large`。有一个已报告的定时任务控制会话通过正常增长（工具结果、压缩、遥测、助手消息）在 20 天内达到 280 MB，因此仅修复快照写放大无法让这类会话保持在上限以内。目前唯一的恢复方式是手工编辑 JSONL。

这沿用了 issue 中讨论的读取侧方向；受影响的使用者已确认，只要恢复结果标明是部分恢复，对其会话就可以接受。

## 审阅者测试计划

### 如何验证

1. 在某个工作区的 `chats` 目录中创建大于 256 MiB 的会话记录（下方脚本可生成），在该工作区启动 `qwen serve`，并以 `{"historyPageSize": 20}` 调用 `POST /session/<id>/load`。
2. 改动前响应为 `413 transcript_too_large`。改动后加载成功，`GET /session/<id>/turn-index` 返回带 `reason: "transcript_window"` 的缺口，从该缺口子记录开始的会话记录分页显示 "Earlier conversation was not loaded…"，而不是存储丢失提示。
3. 单元测试：`cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/services/session-transcript-reader.test.ts`（`over-cap transcripts` 部分使用仅供测试的上限），以及 `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/ui/utils/resumeHistoryUtils.test.ts`。

4. 恢复一条完整大小在预算内、首分片位于窗口前、尾分片为空或仅含 PDF 附件的逻辑记录。原始文字和回合身份应保留，turn index 中也应存在该回合。
5. 恢复一条各物理行都在上限内、但完整逻辑记录超过上限的记录。预期返回现有的 `413 transcript_too_large`，而不是半条记录或调用栈异常。

### 证据（改动前后）

在 Ubuntu 24.04、Node 22.23.4 上独立验证；除明确注明的仅供测试上限外，均使用真实的 256 MiB 上限。所有会话数据都是合成的；daemon 检查使用隔离 HOME/runtime、显式回环监听，不调用模型。

| 场景 | 本版实测结果 |
| --- | --- |
| 293,613,272 字节的普通会话记录 | 加载、turn index、会话分页和边界页均返回 200；来源元数据保留；边界显示窗口提示而非存储丢失提示 |
| 283,226,963 字节的 reader 夹具，当前逻辑记录只有两小段 | 两段正文、第 42 回合、原始 prompt/daemon 身份及对应 turn-index 行均保留 |
| 283,223,178 字节的 daemon 夹具，身份仅在首片且尾片为空 | 加载和 turn index 均返回 200；原始回合行和首分片文字仍可见 |
| 原 342,640,968 字节、15 万个前缀分片的反例 | 受控返回 `SessionTranscriptTooLargeError`，不再出现 `RangeError` |
| 三个 96 MiB 分片组成一条超预算逻辑记录 | reader 按边界要求拒绝；实际 daemon 加载返回 413，明确 `code=transcript_too_large` |
| 使用仅供测试的 8 KiB 上限的小夹具 | 跨记录的前缀累计大小有界；普通部分历史仍可读 |

8 项独立 reader 检查和 3 项真实 daemon HTTP 检查全部通过。新增的 9 项 reader 回归覆盖有文字、空和 PDF 尾片，展示抑制，首分片父节点与缺口分类，逻辑记录与累计预算，以及设置被替换后释放预算。失败场景已在未修复实现上运行，确认测试能击中缺陷。

最终源码验证通过：完整根目录 build 和 bundle；所有 workspace 和 integration 的 TypeScript 检查；**core 792 项 + CLI 111 项 + ACP bridge 165 项（共 1,068 项）**；改动 TypeScript 文件的 ESLint 零警告；Prettier 和双语设计引用检查。根目录 typecheck 使用 `NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=6144`，与仓库 build 的预算一致；8 GiB 主机的默认约 2 GiB 编译堆曾在未改动的 CLI 代码中耗尽。没有削弱断言或压制失败。这是定向 Linux 验收证据，不代表全仓测试套件或托管 CI 结论。

### 测试平台

|     操作系统     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ 未测试 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未测试 |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ Ubuntu 24.04，Node 22.23.4 |

### 环境（可选）

使用仓库锁定的 pnpm 11.24.0 和冻结锁文件、`npm run build` 与 `npm run bundle` 构建。根目录 typecheck 使用与 build 相同的 6 GiB 编译堆预算。守护进程检查使用隔离的 `HOME`/runtime、假 API 密钥和一个未开放的回环模型端点。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：这改变了[选择性会话恢复设计](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/main/docs/design/2026-08-08-selective-session-restore.md)设定的契约，即超过 256 MiB 的冷恢复以 413 失败。该限制作为需要维护者批准的有意兼容性变更引入，本次修订同样需要批准。前缀仍需解析，因此打开很大的会话记录所需时间与其大小成正比。窗口之前的状态只恢复上面列出的几类；更早的 UI 遥测、目标记录、Artifact 和文件历史不会恢复，窗口之前的轮次也不能作为 rewind 目标。只在窗口之前记录的设置按文件顺序选取，因为前缀没有活动链可以遍历；`rewindRecording` 会在其标记之后重新追加当前的模型、审批模式和工作流模式，因此这几项按文件顺序的最后一条就是活动的那条，而最后一条助手记录的模型和归因快照可能来自窗口之前被放弃的分支。
- 未验证 / 不在范围内：macOS 和 Windows；Web Shell 界面渲染（通过其调用的守护进程路由检查）；写入侧增长、保留策略和快照增量编码；可配置上限。Fork 保持不变：它不使用索引，本来就会复制整个文件，因此早先方案中拒绝从窗口化会话 fork 的想法并无必要。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：上限以内的会话记录没有变化。`HistoryGap.reason`、`TranscriptReplayGapInput.reason` 和 `SessionTranscriptTurnIndexPage.gaps` 是可选新增字段。依赖 413 判断超限会话的客户端，现在会得到部分恢复结果。

设计文档：[English](https://github.com/Sumire-no-kai/qwen-code/blob/98907c83e781b771be7ccdbe28d9c9b309fb85d2/docs/design/2026-11-07-transcript-index-window.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/Sumire-no-kai/qwen-code/blob/98907c83e781b771be7ccdbe28d9c9b309fb85d2/docs/design/2026-11-07-transcript-index-window.zh-CN.md)。待维护者决定的问题：窗口化是否应默认取代 413，还是放在设置开关之后；使用者曾请求的可配置上限临时手段是否仍需要。

## 关联 Issue

Refs #13113。这里只处理读取侧的拒绝；该 issue 中的快照写放大与保留策略另行处理。

</details>

prs.title: fix(managed-agent): prove A3 rewritten command recovery without Hook rerun
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Completes the remaining A3 rewritten-input / Hook-no-rerun half of the G3 Step 3 recovery matrix. It proves that a command input rewritten by a Hook is treated as a new, independently approved step rather than inheriting the previous step's Allow; that completed Hook occurrences and completed command steps replay durable results after restart without physical re-execution; and that an outer skill expanding into two command steps survives a crash between the steps while preserving the second Action's identity and deadline. It adds a packaged failover arm, durable evidence collection, focused regression witnesses, and synchronized English/Chinese design documentation.

## Why it's needed

Issue #14481 tracks recovery gaps where restart could reuse an approval for a different final command input, rerun already-completed Hooks or command effects, or lose the identity of a later command step. These behaviors are safety- and correctness-critical for managed command execution: a rewritten input must not ride on a stale Allow, and durable receipts must be the source of truth for replay. This change closes the A3 gap with real packaged evidence rather than only unit-level assertions.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the new packaged command-rewrite failover arm in the managed-agent harness. The expected observation is a three-generation sequence: generation 1 waits for the first command approval; generation 2 allows the first step, completes it and its PostToolUse occurrence, then crashes when the second approval is requested; generation 3 replays the first step and completed Hook occurrences from durable results without physical rerun, preserves the second Action's ID, creation time, expiry, and input reference, and requires a separate Allow for the second step. The final evidence must show two distinct Actions, one physical execution for each command stage and each completed Hook occurrence, settled command receipts, recorded model traffic, a completed relief Turn, terminal count 2, and reliable close. A focused TypeScript regression can be run with `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/serve/hosted-command-step-hook-recovery.test.ts`. The merged branch passes local TypeScript build/typecheck and contract/meta suites; full Java and Hosted CI gates are pending on this PR.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — non-UI recovery and evidence changes. A separate PR comment contains the packaged run report, evidence hashes, local gate results, and CI-pending caveats.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Local macOS TypeScript tests, build, and typecheck; real packaged managed-agent harness on Linux with Temurin 21, MySQL 8.4, registered storage, and delegated cgroup. Acceptance remains pending until the required CI gates pass on the merged revision.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: Recovery now distinguishes extension-owned Hook/command replay from native approval continuation; incorrect gating could either re-execute durable effects or block legitimate recovery. The added packaged arm and regression witnesses pin both sides.
- Not validated / out of scope: Full post-merge Java/Hosted CI suites are not yet green. Local full ESLint was OOM-limited on this host, so lint was run partitioned with generated build outputs ignored. R2 remains out of scope.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: No public API migration. Action ID validation now accepts the command-step Action grammar alongside the legacy tool approval grammar; stored development catalogs should follow the module's baseline schema policy.

Design documentation: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/fix/14481-a3-rewritten-hook/docs/design/2026-11-01-hosted-a3-rewritten-hook.md) / [中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/fix/14481-a3-rewritten-hook/docs/design/2026-11-01-hosted-a3-rewritten-hook.zh-CN.md). Both versions are complete and synchronized, including decisions, constraints, acceptance criteria, and follow-up work.

## Linked Issues

Refs #14481 (G3 Step 3 A3 rewritten-input / Hook-no-rerun recovery). This PR does not auto-close the tracker.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

完成 G3 Step 3 恢复矩阵中剩余的 A3「改写输入 / Hook 不重跑」半边。它证明：被 Hook 改写后的命令输入会作为新的、需要独立批准的步骤处理，而不是继承上一步的 Allow；已完成的 Hook occurrence 和已完成的命令步骤在重启后通过持久化结果重放，不会物理重跑；外层 skill 展开成两个命令步骤时，在两步之间崩溃仍能保留第二个 Action 的身份和截止时间。它新增了一个打包故障支路、持久化证据采集、聚焦回归见证，以及同步的英文/中文设计文档。

## 为什么需要它

Issue #14481 跟踪了一些恢复缺口：重启后可能把批准复用于不同的最终命令输入、重跑已经完成的 Hook 或命令副作用，或者丢失后续命令步骤的身份。这些行为对受管命令执行的安全性和正确性至关重要：改写后的输入不能搭上旧的 Allow，持久化回执必须作为重放的唯一事实来源。这个变更用真实打包证据关闭 A3 缺口，而不仅依赖单元级断言。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

在 managed-agent harness 中运行新增的打包 command-rewrite 故障支路。预期观察到三代序列：第 1 代等待第一个命令批准；第 2 代允许第一步，完成第一步及其 PostToolUse occurrence，然后在请求第二个批准时崩溃；第 3 代从持久化结果重放第一步和已完成 Hook occurrence，不物理重跑，保留第二个 Action 的 ID、创建时间、过期时间和输入引用，并要求对第二步单独 Allow。最终证据必须显示两个不同 Action、每个命令阶段和每个已完成 Hook occurrence 各一次物理执行、已落定的命令回执、记录的模型流量、完成的 relief Turn、terminal count 2，以及可靠 close。聚焦 TypeScript 回归可通过 `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/serve/hosted-command-step-hook-recovery.test.ts` 运行。合并后的分支已通过本地 TypeScript build/typecheck 和契约/元测试套件；完整 Java 和 Hosted CI 门禁仍待本 PR 触发。

### 证据（Before & After）

N/A — 非 UI 的恢复与证据变更。单独的 PR 评论包含打包运行报告、证据哈希、本地门禁结果和 CI 待通过说明。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### 环境（可选）

本地 macOS TypeScript 测试、构建和类型检查；Linux 上的真实打包 managed-agent harness，使用 Temurin 21、MySQL 8.4、注册存储和委托 cgroup。在所需 CI 门禁于合并修订上通过之前，验收仍为 pending。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：恢复逻辑现在区分扩展拥有的 Hook/命令重放与原生批准 continuation；错误门控可能导致重跑持久化副作用，或阻塞合法恢复。新增打包支路和回归见证钉住了两侧。
- 未验证 / 范围外：合并后的完整 Java/Hosted CI 套件尚未变绿。本机完整 ESLint 受 OOM 限制，因此 lint 采用分区运行并忽略生成构建产物。R2 仍不在范围内。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无公共 API 迁移。Action ID 校验现在在旧版工具批准语法之外接受命令步骤 Action 语法；已存储的开发目录应遵循模块的基线 schema 策略。

设计文档：[英文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/fix/14481-a3-rewritten-hook/docs/design/2026-11-01-hosted-a3-rewritten-hook.md) / [中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/fix/14481-a3-rewritten-hook/docs/design/2026-11-01-hosted-a3-rewritten-hook.zh-CN.md)。两个版本完整同步，包括决策、约束、验收标准和后续工作。

## 关联 Issue

Refs #14481（G3 Step 3 A3 改写输入 / Hook 不重跑恢复）。本 PR 不自动关闭该跟踪 Issue。

</details>

prs.title: feat(web-shell): offer a details side task from pending AskUser questions
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds an "Ask for details" action to the pending Ask User Question panel in the Web Shell. The action opens a side task whose first prompt is prefilled with a snapshot of the pending question and its options (including multi-select semantics), plus instructions to explain the background, each option's meaning, differences, impact and risks, and a recommendation — without answering the question for the user or touching the main session. The explanation is delivered as a self-contained single-file HTML written in controlled, ASD-STE100-style sentences in the UI language, saved under the agent's scratch directory (`.qwen/tmp/`), and opens in the existing right-panel HTML preview. The pending question stays pending; the user returns to the main view to answer or ignore it. There is one details side task per pending question: repeat clicks focus the existing tab instead of provisioning duplicates. The action appears only in the main view when the daemon advertises the side-task capability, the same scope as `/btw side`, and the panel's action row wraps so every button stays reachable on narrow viewports.

## Why it's needed

While an Ask User question is pending, the Web Shell hides the main composer and the btw shortcut ignores the pending-approval state. A user who does not understand the options has no way to ask for clarification: the only available moves are answering blindly, typing a free-text answer, or ignoring the question. This PR gives that user a clarification path that reuses the existing side-task infrastructure (a child session with inherited parent context, file tools, and the HTML artifact preview), so the main conversation is neither polluted nor unblocked by the explanation.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Run a daemon that advertises `session_side_task` and open the Web Shell in a workspace session.
2. Make the agent call `ask_user_question` (for example, ask it to consult you on a two-option decision about a file in the workspace).
3. While the question is pending, confirm the new "Ask for details" button sits in the panel's action row, left of Ignore, and that the main composer stays hidden.
4. Click it. Expected: a side-task tab opens in the right panel and immediately starts working on a prefilled prompt that contains the question text, the option labels/descriptions, the controlled-language HTML instructions, and the `.qwen/tmp/` output target. The pending question must remain pending. Clicking again focuses the same tab — no second child session is created.
5. Wait for the side task's first turn. Expected: it writes a self-contained HTML explainer under `.qwen/tmp/`; the file appears as a turn-output card in the side-task chat and renders in the right-panel preview (review panel → Preview).
6. Return to the main view and answer or ignore the question as usual. Expected: the answer flow is unchanged; the side task neither submits the permission nor sends a prompt to the main session.
7. Without the capability (or in split-view/embedded panes), the panel is unchanged. Keyboard behavior on the panel (digits, arrows, Enter, Esc, Ctrl+Enter) is unchanged; the new button is outside the option group and registers no shortcuts.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: the pending panel offers only Submit / Ignore / Previous / Next and a free-text "Other" input; the composer is hidden, so `/btw side` is unreachable at exactly the moment the user needs clarification.

After (real daemon + real model + headless Chromium, Linux):

![Pending Ask User panel with the new Ask for details button](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/ask-user-details/01-ask-panel-with-details.png)

![Side task opened with the prefilled explanation prompt; the question stays pending](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/ask-user-details/02b-still-pending-after-open.png)

![HTML explainer rendered in the right-panel preview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/ask-user-details/03d-html-preview-rendered.png)

![Answer submitted through the unchanged main flow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/ask-user-details/04-answer-submitted.png)

Dark/light mock-daemon captures (zh-CN UI) from the visuals suite: `client/e2e/visuals/output/screenshots/ask-user-details-{panel,side-task}-{dark,light}.png`.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Real `qwen serve` daemon 0.26.8 (workspace session, real model) + vite dev Web Shell + headless Chromium driven over CDP; unit tests via vitest (jsdom); visuals via Playwright in the repo's local image.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the prefilled prompt shapes the side task's behavior. It instructs the side task to verify facts before claiming them, mark unverified items, and never answer for the user; the side task is a separate session, so the pending permission can only be resolved from the main panel regardless.
- Not validated / out of scope: no details action in split-view panes or inside side-task panes (same scope as `/btw side`, which is main-view-only); the explanation language follows the UI language (en/zh-CN; ru falls back to en through the existing i18n fallback); macOS/Windows not tested locally.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. New optional component prop, new i18n keys, and a new pure formatter; no daemon, protocol, or settings changes.

Design documents: [English](docs/design/2026-11-06-ask-user-details-side-task.md) | [简体中文](docs/design/2026-11-06-ask-user-details-side-task.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

None.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

在 Web Shell 待答的 Ask User Question 面板上新增「问细节」动作。点击后打开一个侧边任务，其首条提示词预填了待答问题与选项的快照（含多选语义），并要求解释问题背景、每个选项的含义、差异、影响与风险，以及给出建议——不替用户作答，也不改动主会话。解释以 ASD-STE100 受控句式、按 UI 语言写成自包含单文件 HTML，保存到 agent 临时目录（`.qwen/tmp/`），用现有右侧面板 HTML 预览打开。待答问题保持待答；用户回到主视图作答或忽略。每个待答问题只有一个细节侧边任务：重复点击聚焦已有 tab，不会重复创建。该动作仅在 daemon 声明侧边任务能力时出现在主视图，与 `/btw side` 的作用域一致；面板操作行可换行，窄视口下每个按钮都保持可达。

## 为什么需要

Ask User 问题待答时，Web Shell 会隐藏主输入框，btw 快捷键也会忽略待审批状态。不理解选项的用户没有任何追问途径：只能盲选、输入自由文本答案或忽略问题。本 PR 复用现有侧边任务基础设施（继承父会话上下文的子会话、文件工具、HTML 产物预览），给这样的用户一条澄清路径，主对话既不被污染，也不会被解释过程解除阻塞。

## 评审验证计划

### 如何验证

1. 运行声明 `session_side_task` 的 daemon，在工作区会话中打开 Web Shell。
2. 让 agent 调用 `ask_user_question`（例如就工作区中某个文件的二选一决策征求你的意见）。
3. 问题待答时，确认面板操作行出现「问细节」按钮（位于忽略左侧），主输入框仍隐藏。
4. 点击。预期：右侧面板打开侧边任务 tab，立即开始处理预填提示词，其中包含问题文本、选项 label/description、受控句式 HTML 指令与 `.qwen/tmp/` 输出目标。待答问题必须保持待答。再次点击聚焦同一 tab——不会创建第二个子会话。
5. 等待侧边任务首轮完成。预期：在 `.qwen/tmp/` 下写出自包含 HTML 解释；文件以回合产物卡片出现在侧边任务聊天中，并可在右侧面板预览（review 面板 → Preview）渲染。
6. 回到主视图，照常作答或忽略。预期：作答流程不变；侧边任务不会提交权限，也不会向主会话发送提示词。
7. 无该能力（或 split view/嵌入式面板）时，面板保持不变。面板键盘行为（数字、方向键、Enter、Esc、Ctrl+Enter）不变；新按钮在选项组之外，不注册快捷键。

### 证据（前后对照）

改动前：待答面板只有 提交 / 忽略 / 上一题 / 下一题 与「其他」自由输入；输入框被隐藏，用户最需要澄清的时刻恰恰无法使用 `/btw side`。

改动后（真实 daemon + 真实模型 + headless Chromium，Linux）：

![待答 Ask User 面板与新增的问细节按钮](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/ask-user-details/01-ask-panel-with-details.png)

![侧边任务带着预填解释提示词打开；问题保持待答](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/ask-user-details/02b-still-pending-after-open.png)

![HTML 解释在右侧面板预览中渲染](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/ask-user-details/03d-html-preview-rendered.png)

![通过不变的主流程提交答案](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/ask-user-details/04-answer-submitted.png)

视觉套件的暗/亮双主题 mock daemon 截图（zh-CN UI）：`client/e2e/visuals/output/screenshots/ask-user-details-{panel,side-task}-{dark,light}.png`。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### 环境

真实 `qwen serve` daemon 0.26.8（工作区会话、真实模型）+ vite dev Web Shell + CDP 驱动的 headless Chromium；单测走 vitest（jsdom）；视觉走仓库本地 Playwright 镜像。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险/取舍：预填提示词塑造侧边任务的行为。提示词要求先核实事实再下结论、标注未核实项、绝不替用户作答；侧边任务是独立会话，待答权限无论如何只能从主面板解析。
- 未验证/范围外：split view 面板与侧边任务面板内不提供问细节入口（与 `/btw side` 一致，后者也只在主视图可用）；解释语言跟随 UI 语言（en/zh-CN；ru 经现有 i18n 回退落到 en）；macOS/Windows 未本地测试。
- 破坏性变更/迁移说明：无。新增可选组件 prop、新 i18n 键与一个纯格式化函数；不改 daemon、协议或设置。

设计文档：[English](docs/design/2026-11-06-ask-user-details-side-task.md) | [简体中文](docs/design/2026-11-06-ask-user-details-side-task.zh-CN.md)

prs.title: feat(channels): add GitHub repository event filter with allowlist and blocklist
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds a repository event filter to the GitHub channel with two explicit modes — allowlist (process only the listed repositories) and blocklist (process all except the listed ones) — and surfaces it in the Web Shell channel editor as a first-class "Repository Filter" control. The filter runs where notifications enter the channel, before any reason filtering; skipped notifications are recorded in the channel event timeline as `repo_filter` rows (capped per poll, with one collapsed count row) and never hold the poll cursor. The editor shows the repository list only while a mode is active, accepts pasted repository or PR URLs (shortened to `owner/repo` on save, including `.git`, query, and fragment suffixes), rejects URLs under known non-repository GitHub areas (`orgs/`, `apps/`, `settings/`, `trending/`, …) instead of silently shortening them — the area list is best-effort and documented as such — and validates entries against the same rules the daemon enforces at save time. One shared validator serves the runtime and the save path, and a parity table binds the editor mirror to the plugin's own descriptor so the two cannot drift.

## Why it's needed

The GitHub channel processed notifications from every repository the authenticated account can see. The only repository-level control was the group access allowlist, which cannot express "everything except these noisy repositories" and hides a plain event filter behind access-policy machinery (group gates, sender policies, per-repository overrides). In the Web Shell editor that allowlist lived under Group Policy → Allowlist → Allowed repositories, which made "filter events by repository" unintuitive to configure. Operators now get a dedicated, self-explanatory filter with both whitelist and blacklist semantics, independent of who is allowed to talk to the channel.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Open Settings → Channels → GitHub in the Web Shell. Repository Filter defaults to Off and no repository list is rendered. Choosing Allowlist or Blocklist reveals the Filtered Repositories list; saving with an active mode and an empty list is refused inline ("List at least one repository, or set Repository Filter to Off."); switching back to Off retires the message, hides the list, and saves.
- Paste `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/pull/123` into the list and save: the stored config carries `owner/repo`, lowercased and deduplicated. Pasting a non-repository URL such as `https://github.com/orgs/community` is rejected with the owner/repo format message instead of being shortened to a nonexistent repository.
- Configure a blocklist naming one repository against a running channel: notifications from that repository are skipped and appear as `repo_filter` rows in the channel event timeline, while other repositories keep flowing and the poll cursor advances. An allowlist with the same list flips exactly this. The daemon also refuses an active mode with an empty list at the API level (HTTP 400 with the validator message).
- Regression: an existing channel without the new keys behaves exactly as before (the select shows Off); a list stored while the mode is Off is ignored by the runtime and preserved verbatim on unrelated saves.

### Evidence (Before & After)

This is a new control, so there is no "before" — the pairs below show the default Off state and an active Blocklist configuration, in light and dark themes, captured by the visuals suite against the real plugin descriptor.

| Off (default) | Blocklist active |
| --- | --- |
| ![Repository filter off, light](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/github-repo-filter/01-repo-filter-off-light.png) | ![Repository filter blocklist, light](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/github-repo-filter/02-repo-filter-blocklist-light.png) |
| ![Repository filter off, dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/github-repo-filter/03-repo-filter-off-dark.png) | ![Repository filter blocklist, dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wenshao/qwen-code/assets/github-repo-filter/04-repo-filter-blocklist-dark.png) |

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Bundled daemon (`npm run build && npm run bundle`) against a local GitHub-compatible HTTP stub with two repositories and two channels (one per mode); Playwright visuals suite in a local Chromium container; vitest unit suites for the github channel package, the Web Shell channels components, and the CLI channel registry/store/routes.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the filter composes with the group access policy — when both restrict repositories, only the intersection is processed. The field description and the user guide state this explicitly.
- Not validated / out of scope: every incoming notification is filtered, including notifications about PRs bound to a live session; only their PR state watch events bypass the filter (documented). Other channels, the group gate, and the shared group-policy type are untouched.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. Two new optional config keys; the default Off preserves existing behavior, and channels without the keys are unaffected.

prs.title: fix(core): keep Write deny rules when quoting hides the async operator
prs.body:
## Linked Issues

Fixes #12246.

## What

`cd .qwen ; cd 'x\'';echo ' & echo {} > settings.json` with `deny: ["Write(.qwen/settings.json)"]` evaluated to `allow` and overwrote the protected file with no prompt. The second `cd` is backgrounded by the real ` & ` (bash reads `'x\''` + `';echo '` as one concatenated argument), but the permission splitter read a `;` between the two quote fragments, treated the `cd` as foreground, moved the effective cwd, and the write resolved to the wrong path — so the deny rule never saw it.

Verified live against bash: the payload above really does write `.qwen/settings.json`.

## Root cause

The two backslash readings disagree on where the operators are: the escape-everywhere reading sees a `;` inside what bash treats as one quoted word. A boundary only one reading sees cannot be allowed to decide a `cd`'s foreground/background effect on its own, and mixing both readings' boundaries into one split invents phantom `cd` targets no shell produces.

## Fix

Built on top of #11765's dual-reading splitter:

- `splitCompoundCommandSegmentsForReading(command, reading)` exposes one reading's split next to the union default (rule-parser). The union split stays the default for boundary discovery.
- `extractShellOperationsAcrossCommand` walks each self-consistent reading separately when a backslash is present and merges the operation sets (deduped); for cwd attribution the walker needs each reading's own split, since the union's mixed boundaries would attribute writes to phantom cwds. The permission layer aggregates to the most restrictive verdict, so a boundary only one reading sees can no longer move a write away from the protected path.
- `isDynamicShellPath` also escalates `cd` targets carrying shell metacharacters (`;|&><`), which can only be quoting artifacts of a split.

## Reviewer Test Plan

Verify the original payload with a deny rule for `.qwen/settings.json`. The permission decision must be `deny`, and the extracted write must resolve under the first `cd` target rather than the repository root or a directory invented by the quote split. Repeat with the plain-quote control and confirm it remains denied.

Verify ordinary comment prose containing an apostrophe or unmatched double quote. A following newline must remain a command boundary, and a protected write on the next line must still be denied. Also verify the upstream redirect cases: redirects on static, dynamic, and backgrounded directory changes must be reported from the directory where that segment starts.

## Merged main

`7b9dceca4e` merges `main` through `7b4b353750` and clears the conflict GitHub reported. The one real conflict was in `shell-semantics.ts`, and it was architectural rather than textual: upstream #15681 rewrote the redirect tokenizer to track which characters were typed unquoted and to treat `2>&1` / `>&-` as descriptor operations, while this branch already carries per-character bare/quoted state on each `ShellToken`. Both answer the same question, with two representations.

I kept the `ShellToken` representation and ported upstream's descriptor semantics onto it, since it already has the quoting detail upstream needed `fdRedirects`/`fdCloses` out-params for:

- `redirectTargetFile` decides what a target names. A bare `&` followed by a number or `-` is a descriptor and opens nothing, `/dev/null` and the `/dev/tcp`/`/dev/udp` pseudo-devices open nothing, and anything else names a file without the `&`. An unquoted `-` after a bare `&` is a close, so the redirect token keeps the whole `&-word`; a quoted or escaped `-` is part of the name and is reported without the flag check that would drop it.
- `pushToken` walks an `>&-` chain in a loop, so a long one cannot overflow the stack, and only the first redirect keeps the whole word.
- A bare `&` inside a word is what makes the two readings of `2">"&1` disagree, so that shape still reports the literal `&1` write. A fully quoted word (`cd '>y'`) has no bare syntax and stays an operand, which this branch's R3-1 rows pin.

Nothing in #12246 is superseded by #15681; they are different bugs that met in the same tokenizer.

## Tested

| OS | Result |
| --- | --- |
| macOS arm64 | `7b9dceca4e`: `packages/core/src/permissions` 1501/1501 across 16 files, which is upstream's fd-duplication rows and this branch's R3/R7/R9 rows together; `tsc --noEmit -p packages/core` clean; eslint clean on the touched file |

Wider `packages/core` on this merge is 40293 passed with 6 failures in unrelated subsystems: packaging asset counts, a memory recall scan timing ceiling, git commit tracking, a pull refusal message, the Anthropic user-agent identity and an omni preset path that resolves outside the repo. None of them import `permissions/shell-semantics`, and I did not re-baseline them against `main`.

The earlier head `b381c0628d` was 1394/1394 on the permissions suite before upstream's tokenizer landed.

### R8-4 follow-up (`d32bf4c060`)

Ordinary comment prose no longer supplies quote state to the compound-command scanner on backslash-free commands. The existing comment preprocessing blanks quote characters without moving any bytes, so `cd .qwen # don't` still ends at its newline and the following write resolves to `/repo/.qwen/settings.json`. Backslash-bearing commands retain the existing conservative dual-reading merge.

Both the apostrophe and unmatched-double-quote variants were red at `7b9dceca4e`: the operation was attributed to `/repo/settings.json`, and PermissionManager returned `allow` despite `Write(.qwen/settings.json)` being denied. Both now pass at the operation and permission layers. The complete two permission files are 947/947, core `typecheck` and `build` pass, and Prettier plus touched-file ESLint are clean. An intermediate version that also changed backslash-bearing comments broke three existing conservative-merge tests; the final scope preserves all three without changing their expectations.

### Current main merge (`d9e3982a72`)

Merged `main` through `478c2f87ab` with a normal merge commit, without rebase or force-push. Upstream #16129 now carries redirect results with directory resolution. The conflict resolution keeps that contract on this branch's quote-aware token representation: comment and process-substitution handling, operand counting, dynamic-directory escalation, starting-directory redirect attribution, and `/dev/fd` filtering all remain in the same path. Commands unrelated to directory changes do not pay for a second redirect parse.

Validation on this merged head:

- The two permission suites pass 961/961: 653 permission-manager tests and 308 shell-semantics tests. This includes the upstream #16129 redirect cases and this branch's comment-quote regressions together.
- Core `tsc --noEmit`, Prettier, and touched-file ESLint pass.
- The full PR diff received two clean review passes after the final formatting change. Existing review threads and their explicitly deferred items are not being marked resolved by this merge.
- A local build was not run on this merged head because the host had about 11 GiB free, below the 15 GiB workspace build floor. Hosted build and CI are still required and are not claimed green here.

## Risk & Scope

Core permission path, small scope. The dual-reading evaluation only engages when the command contains a backslash; backslash-free commands retain that path except for neutralizing quote characters inside real comment text. The three `echo 'a\' # ...` comment rows settle at `ask` (fail-closed), matching upstream's existing expectation for the ambiguous shape.

## Out of scope

- Converging the two segmentations themselves (#11882 umbrella).
- No changes to the `Write` rule matcher or deny syntax.

## Affiliation

Individual contributor (not affiliated with Moonshot AI).

prs.title: fix(core): settle background shell status files left running by a dead CLI
prs.body:
## What this PR does

When a session is taken over, either by a process that starts on a resumed session or by switching to another session inside a running CLI, the status sidecars of its background shells are checked. A sidecar that still says `running` while the process it recorded no longer exists is rewritten to `status: "unknown"`, keeping every other field. The shell tool's guidance now lists `unknown` and tells the model it means the session that started the process ended without recording how it finished.

A sidecar whose process is still alive keeps `running`, and the Config watches that process for as long as it holds the session: once it exits, the sidecar is settled the same way, so a command that finishes after the resume does not stay `running` either. Switching to another session or shutting down stops the watch. Sidecars without a pid, other statuses and unreadable files are left alone, and a Config with an execution environment, whose shells may run elsewhere, skips the check.

## Why it's needed

#15800: the sidecar has a single writer, the CLI that started the shell. The child is spawned detached and outlives a CLI that is killed or crashes, so its sidecar stays `running` forever and a resumed session reads a finished command as still running. In the reported run the model concluded it was "just an async status-update lag". `writeStatusFile()` already records the child pid so such a sidecar "can still be cross-checked", but nothing performed the check. Handling SIGHUP in headless mode (#15823) narrows the window, but no write-side change covers SIGKILL or a crash, so this fixes the read side, as the triage suggested.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Start a headless run whose model calls `run_shell_command` with `is_background: true` and a command that takes a few seconds, then kill the CLI (SIGKILL, or SIGHUP to its process group) while the command runs.
2. Wait for the command to finish. The sidecar under `~/.qwen/tmp/<project>/background-shells/<session>/` still says `running` and its pid is gone.
3. Resume the session headless (`-p … --resume <session>`). Before this change the sidecar still says `running`; after it, it says `unknown` with the original `id`, `command`, `cwd`, `startTime` and `pid`.
4. Unit tests: `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/services/backgroundShellRegistry.test.ts src/config/config.test.ts`.

### Evidence (Before & After)

On Ubuntu 24.04.4 (AWS), Node 22.23.4, the bundled CLI driven by the repo's fake OpenAI server, with an isolated `HOME` and a fake key:

| How the CLI ended | Sidecar after `--resume`, before | Sidecar after `--resume`, after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SIGKILL, command then finished | `running`, pid gone | `unknown`, `id`/`command`/`cwd`/`startTime`/`pid` kept |
| SIGHUP to the process group, command then finished | `running`, pid gone | `unknown`, fields kept |
| SIGKILL, resumed while the command still ran, session left before it ended | — | `running`, unchanged |
| SIGKILL, resumed while the command still ran, session still open when it ended | `running` | `unknown` within that session, about a second after the command ended |

Checks on the same host: prettier, eslint (`--max-warnings 0`) and core `tsc --noEmit` on the changed files; the core suites `backgroundShellRegistry`, `config`, `shell` and `process-liveness` (1530 tests) pass. Mutation checks, each turning a new test red: ignoring whether the pid is alive; settling any status; dropping the original fields; not settling at initialization; settling the session already in use; a watcher that never settles; a watcher that ignores liveness; not watching survivors at takeover; keeping the old watch on a switch; keeping the watch on shutdown. A real-child test covers the full sequence (alive at takeover, exits later, no second takeover) and fails when the watcher is removed. The change is confined to core, so the repo-wide typecheck was not run.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ not tested |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ Ubuntu 24.04, Node 22.23.4 |

### Environment (optional)

Built with the pinned pnpm 11.24.0, `npm run build` and `npm run bundle`.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the new persisted value. I asked on the issue whether maintainers prefer `unknown` or `failed` with an `error`; this PR uses `unknown` because `failed` would claim an outcome nobody observed, and switching is a one-line change. A reused pid looks alive, so such a sidecar stays `running`, today's behaviour. Writers without a session lease (TUI, headless CLI) running on one session at the same time could race with an owner that is about to record a result; two concurrent writers on one session are already unsupported.
- Not validated / out of scope: macOS and Windows; write-side handling of signals (#15823); recording outcomes after the fact.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: a sidecar can now read `unknown`. Sidecars written by older versions are settled the same way.

Design: [English](https://github.com/Sumire-no-kai/qwen-code/blob/c9c981dd616dc46e2dee370668c3b932d5d1bedc/docs/design/2026-11-07-orphaned-shell-status.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/Sumire-no-kai/qwen-code/blob/c9c981dd616dc46e2dee370668c3b932d5d1bedc/docs/design/2026-11-07-orphaned-shell-status.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

Fixes #15800

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 的改动

当一个会话被接管时——无论是进程在已恢复的会话上启动，还是运行中的 CLI 切换到另一个会话——都会检查其后台 shell 的状态文件。仍为 `running`、但所记录进程已不存在的状态文件，会被改写为 `status: "unknown"`，其余字段全部保留。shell 工具的引导文字现在列出 `unknown`，并告诉模型其含义：启动该进程的会话结束时没有记录进程是如何结束的。

进程仍存活的状态文件保持 `running`，并且只要 Config 仍持有该会话，就会持续监视该进程：进程一结束就用同样方式收尾，因此恢复之后才结束的命令也不会停在 `running`。切换到其他会话或关闭时停止监视。没有 pid 的状态文件、其他状态以及无法读取的文件保持不动；带有执行环境的 Config（其 shell 可能运行在别处）会跳过检查。

## 为什么需要

#15800：状态文件只有一个写入方，即启动 shell 的 CLI。子进程以分离方式启动，会比被杀或崩溃的 CLI 活得更久，因此其状态文件永远停在 `running`，恢复的会话会把已结束的命令读成仍在运行。在报告的运行中，模型得出的结论是"只是异步状态更新延迟"。`writeStatusFile()` 已经记录子进程 pid，使这类状态文件"仍可交叉核对"，但没有代码执行这项核对。在 headless 模式下处理 SIGHUP（#15823）能缩小窗口，但写入侧的改动覆盖不了 SIGKILL 或崩溃，因此本 PR 按 triage 的建议修复读取侧。

## 审阅者测试计划

### 如何验证

1. 启动一次 headless 运行，让模型以 `is_background: true` 调用 `run_shell_command` 执行一个需要几秒的命令，在命令运行期间结束 CLI（SIGKILL，或向其进程组发送 SIGHUP）。
2. 等命令结束。`~/.qwen/tmp/<project>/background-shells/<session>/` 下的状态文件仍为 `running`，且其 pid 已不存在。
3. 以 headless 方式恢复该会话（`-p … --resume <session>`）。改动前状态文件仍为 `running`；改动后变为 `unknown`，并保留原有的 `id`、`command`、`cwd`、`startTime` 和 `pid`。
4. 单元测试：`cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/services/backgroundShellRegistry.test.ts src/config/config.test.ts`。

### 证据（改动前后）

在 Ubuntu 24.04.4（AWS）、Node 22.23.4 上，用仓库的模拟 OpenAI 服务驱动打包后的 CLI，使用隔离的 `HOME` 和假密钥：

| CLI 如何结束 | `--resume` 后的状态文件（改动前） | `--resume` 后的状态文件（改动后） |
| --- | --- | --- |
| SIGKILL，随后命令结束 | `running`，pid 已不存在 | `unknown`，保留 `id`/`command`/`cwd`/`startTime`/`pid` |
| 向进程组发送 SIGHUP，随后命令结束 | `running`，pid 已不存在 | `unknown`，保留原字段 |
| SIGKILL，命令仍在运行时恢复，命令结束前离开会话 | — | `running`，未改动 |
| SIGKILL，命令仍在运行时恢复，命令结束时会话仍开着 | `running` | 在该会话内变为 `unknown`，约在命令结束 1 秒后 |

同一主机上的检查：对改动文件运行 prettier、eslint（`--max-warnings 0`）和 core 的 `tsc --noEmit`；core 的 `backgroundShellRegistry`、`config`、`shell` 和 `process-liveness` 测试（1530 个）全部通过。变异检查（每项都会让新测试失败）：不检查 pid 是否存活；任何状态都收尾；丢弃原有字段；初始化时不收尾；对正在使用的会话也收尾；监视器从不收尾；监视器忽略存活状态；接管时不监视仍存活的进程；切换会话时保留旧监视；关闭时保留监视。一条使用真实子进程的测试覆盖完整时序（接管时存活、之后退出、没有第二次接管），去掉监视器后该测试失败。改动只在 core，未运行整仓 typecheck。

### 测试平台

|     操作系统     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ 未测试 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未测试 |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ Ubuntu 24.04，Node 22.23.4 |

### 环境（可选）

使用仓库锁定的 pnpm 11.24.0、`npm run build` 和 `npm run bundle` 构建。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：新的持久化取值。我在 issue 中询问过维护者倾向 `unknown` 还是 `failed` 加 `error`；本 PR 使用 `unknown`，因为 `failed` 会声称一个无人观察到的结果，而改用 `failed` 只需改一行。被复用的 pid 看起来仍存活，这类状态文件保持 `running`，即今天的行为。不获取会话租约的写入方（TUI、headless CLI）若同时运行在同一会话上，可能与即将记录结果的持有者竞争；同一会话上两个并发写入方本身就不受支持。
- 未验证 / 不在范围内：macOS 和 Windows；写入侧的信号处理（#15823）；事后补记结果。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：状态文件现在可能为 `unknown`。旧版本写入的状态文件按同样方式收尾。

设计文档：[English](https://github.com/Sumire-no-kai/qwen-code/blob/c9c981dd616dc46e2dee370668c3b932d5d1bedc/docs/design/2026-11-07-orphaned-shell-status.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/Sumire-no-kai/qwen-code/blob/c9c981dd616dc46e2dee370668c3b932d5d1bedc/docs/design/2026-11-07-orphaned-shell-status.zh-CN.md)

prs.title: fix(cli): forward the folder-trust store into the container sandbox
prs.body:
## What this PR does

When Qwen Code re-executes itself inside a Docker or Podman sandbox, it now forwards a custom folder-trust store path into the container, translating it with the same helper the MCP and hook approval stores already use. Without the forward, the containerized process falls back to its own `QWEN_HOME`, which may not contain the trust decision, so a workspace the host trusted is treated as untrusted and its project hooks and settings are withheld.

## Why it's needed

The v0.26.8 release failed at `Integration Tests (Docker)`. The same failure is tracked in #16322 and reproduces on every recent main commit, including the release SHA and its successor: the two ACP tool-hook cases fail only in the `sandbox:docker` lane, while the same tests pass in `sandbox:none`. The ACP fixtures start the CLI with a scratch `QWEN_HOME` and rely on the rig's `QWEN_CODE_TRUSTED_FOLDERS_PATH` override for the workspace grant. Because the sandbox launcher did not forward that override, the container looked in the scratch home, found no `trustedFolders.json`, and withheld the hooks; both cases then observed zero hook invocations. The same forwarding is under review separately in #16390.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

On Linux with Docker available, run `QWEN_SANDBOX=docker npx vitest run --root ./integration-tests cli/tool-hook-context.test.ts cli/tool-hook-updated-input.test.ts`. Before this change the two ACP cases fail with an empty `hookHits()` array while the other twelve cases pass; after it, all fourteen pass. For the path plumbing, run `npx vitest run src/serve/sandbox.test.ts src/serve/process-env-guard.test.ts` in `packages/cli`.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — non-UI change. The deterministic before/after is the two ACP cases above; the `sandbox:docker` lane only runs on main pushes.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

The autofix sandbox has no Docker daemon, so the `QWEN_SANDBOX=docker` lane could not run locally. The sandbox unit suite and the same two integration files in host mode passed.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: if the custom trust store lives outside the directories the container mounts, it remains unreadable there and trust stays fail-closed — the same behavior as before this change.
- Not validated / out of scope: the Linux Docker E2E lane itself; CI is the verification vehicle.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. When the override is unset, no argument is added.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #16397
Refs #16322

prs.title: feat(cli): open Agent View with the Left arrow and make the roster work on Windows
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Makes Agent View usable end to end and adds a Claude Code style entry point: with `experimental.agentView` enabled, pressing Left on an empty prompt sends the current session to the background and opens a full-screen roster of every background session.

The roster groups sessions into Pinned, Needs input, Working, Completed and Failed. Each row shows the session title (its rename title, otherwise its first prompt), a one-line summary of the last turn written by the model, the latest bound PR, and the age. From the roster, Space peeks at a session and can send it a reply without leaving, Enter attaches to the full session, Left on the attached session's empty prompt comes back, Up/Down/PgUp/PgDn move the selection, Ctrl+T pins, Ctrl+R renames, and Ctrl+X stops (a second Ctrl+X removes). Typing a prompt in the roster starts a new background session. `/background` (alias `/bg`) does the same as the Left key, and `qwen agents` opens the roster directly.

This builds on the Agent View stack by @ZijianZhang989: the supervisor, PTY workers and lifecycle are already on `main`, and the roster UI and command surface come from the open #7802 and #7803, ported onto current `main` with the existing `qwen agents join` subcommand kept. On top of that it wires what was missing for the merged backend to run, and fixes what broke on Windows:

- The CLI now handles the internal supervisor and PTY host launch flags (gated on the env the spawner sets, so a prompt that mentions a flag cannot trigger them). Before this the supervisor child exited on an unknown argument.
- Workers send `ready`, report idle and start their heartbeat at startup, so adopting a session no longer times out.
- The terminal is handed to the roster by the relaunch supervisor. A nested synchronous spawn from the exiting session does not work on Windows: the blocked parent keeps reading console input and the roster never sees a key. The session now only tells the supervisor which workspace to open; the supervisor runs its own CLI. Without a relaunch supervisor (Linux, where the process is replaced in place) the existing spawn path is used.
- Attaching repaints the worker the same way wake/SIGCONT does. In terminal-buffer mode the old redraw wrote nothing, so an attached session stayed blank until the first key.
- On Windows the exiting session clears the console title, and Node 22's libuv aborts when the next process reads an empty title (`Assertion failed: process_title`). The supervisor sets a title before starting the roster.
- `/background` uses the same submission-scoped idle check as `/restore` and `/logout`; the general idle flag reads busy while any slash command runs, so it always refused.

Design doc: [English](docs/design/2026-11-06-agent-view-left-arrow-roster.md) / [简体中文](docs/design/2026-11-06-agent-view-left-arrow-roster.zh-CN.md). E2E test plan: `.qwen/e2e-tests/2026-11-06-agent-view-left-arrow-roster.md`.

## Why it's needed

The Agent View backend has been on `main` for months but no released build can reach it, and the roster PRs no longer apply. People running several sessions at once have no way to see which one is working, which one is waiting on them, and which one is done without switching terminals. Claude Code's agent view solves this with one key; this brings the same workflow to Qwen Code, behind the existing experimental flag.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Set `"experimental": { "agentView": true }` in `~/.qwen/settings.json` and start `qwen` in a scratch folder.
2. Ask for a haiku and wait for the reply, then press Left on the empty prompt. The roster opens with the session under Completed, titled by your prompt, with a one-line summary.
3. Press Space, type a follow-up and press Enter. The row goes to Working and back to Completed with a new summary, without leaving the roster.
4. Press Space to close the peek, then Enter. The full session paints immediately. Press Left on its empty prompt to return.
5. Type a task in the roster prompt and press Enter to start a new background session; rename one with a name plus Ctrl+R, pin with Ctrl+T, stop with Ctrl+X and remove with a second Ctrl+X.
6. With the flag off, Left behaves exactly as before.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: Left on an empty prompt does nothing, `/background` does not exist, and starting an Agent View session fails because the supervisor never starts.

After, captured from a real pseudo-terminal against a live model (Windows):

```
  Tips: Try /insight to generate personalized insights from your chat history.

0 awaiting input - 0 working - 2 completed - 0 failed

Pinned
> * Write a haiku about fence pos… Wrote a haiku about fence posts 38s

Completed
  * List the files here.           Found one file README.md in the workspace 26s

Pinned.

──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
> describe a task for a new session
──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
enter to open · space to reply · ctrl+x to delete ·
```

Peek with a reply in flight (Linux, WSL Debian 13):

```
Working
> * Write a haiku about fence pos… Standing through the years. 25s

╭─────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ Write a haiku about fence posts. 25s                │
│ Standing through the years.                         │
│ Waiting for response: Now one about gates.          │
│ waiting for response · space to close · ctrl+x to … │
╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

Pinned and renamed, with a PR bound to the session (Windows):

```
Pinned
> * Fence haiku          Wrote a haiku about fence posts standing guard #221 1m
Completed
  . Write a 600 word story about … The gate remains. It swings. … 59s
```

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ✅   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Windows 11: source build on Node 24, and the `win-x64` standalone package on its bundled Node 22. Linux: WSL Debian 13 on Node 22, source build. Both driven through a pseudo-terminal (node-pty plus a headless xterm) against an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Unit tests: the ported roster, command and backend suites plus new tests for the Left binding, the `/background` idle exception, the relaunch roster handoff, PgUp/PgDn, the Failed group and the summary cleaner; 1,600+ related tests pass. On Windows, five existing relaunch tests (process replacement and POSIX supervisor signals) fail with or without this change.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: everything is behind `experimental.agentView` (default off). With it on, each finished turn in a background session makes one extra model request for the summary (fast model when configured); it is best effort and falls back to the last output line.
- Not validated / out of scope: macOS was not run locally (CI covers it). Backgrounding mid-turn is refused rather than supported, since adoption restarts the session in a supervisor-owned PTY. The OpenTUI renderer reports that detaching is unsupported. `qwen --bg` and the managed-resume guard from #7802 are left for a follow-up. Needs input was not exercised end to end because the runs used YOLO approval mode. Pressing Ctrl+X in the first seconds while a newly dispatched worker is starting can record it as failed instead of stopped.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. `qwen agents` without a subcommand now opens the roster (or lists sessions when not on a TTY); `qwen agents join` is unchanged.

## Linked Issues

Builds on #7802 and #7803.

prs.title: fix(cli): scrub advisor selector from startup errors
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The startup error for an unavailable Advisor model now renders the configured aux-model selector through the existing credential-safe display formatter. A selector such as `openai:missing-advisor\0https://user:sk-secret@gw.example/v1` is shown as `openai:missing-advisor (https://gw.example/v1)` instead of writing the userinfo credential and a literal NUL byte to stderr.

The raw selector is still passed unchanged to Advisor availability and routing checks; only the human-readable failure message is scrubbed.

## Why it's needed

Issue #12856 tracks the surfaces that emitted NUL-separated aux-model selectors verbatim. The earlier merged fix covered the daemon, ACP, settings, system-info and model-readback paths, but left the startup Advisor-validation failure open because the stored selector is also the routing key.

When an Advisor pin exists at User scope but its provider entry does not exist in the current workspace, startup fails with that selector interpolated into a `FatalConfigError`. The critical-error handler writes the message to stderr, placing a live credential in terminal scrollback, CI logs or redirected error files precisely when the user is inspecting the failure.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Configure `advisorModel` with a missing model name and an `https://user:sk-secret@host/v1` registry base URL, then start the CLI in a workspace where that provider is unavailable. Expected: startup still fails with the Advisor configuration error, but the model line shows the selector and scrubbed endpoint without userinfo or a raw NUL; the raw selector still determines which configured models count as available.
2. Repeat with an ordinary selector such as `missing-advisor`. Expected: the existing error text is unchanged.
3. Repeat with an non-http suffix or a value that cannot be parsed as a selector. Expected: the display helper drops the unpublishable suffix rather than echoing it.

### Evidence (Before & After)

The regression test drives the real `loadCliConfig` startup path and captures the resulting `FatalConfigError`. It asserts that the message contains the scrubbed model label and does not contain `sk-secret` or a NUL byte.

The current execution constraint did not permit local tests, build, typecheck or formatting commands, so these checks were not run locally and no passing result is claimed.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit-test path only; no live provider or model request is involved.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the rendered label can differ from the persisted selector, but this is deliberate and matches every other aux-selector display surface. The routing value itself is not transformed.
- Not validated / out of scope: local tests, build, typecheck and formatting were not run. The remaining startup-handshake work discussed in #12856 is unrelated; this PR covers only the deferred Advisor stderr surface.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. Persisted settings keep their current format.

## Linked Issues

Refs #12856. This closes the deferred startup-error surface, while the issue remains the tracking point for any remaining class-wide format decisions.

prs.title: feat(desktop): persist Web Shell catalogs across restarts
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The desktop client now keeps the Web Shell's saved daemon connections and workspace-host catalog across restarts. Both catalogs live in the desktop shell's settings file and are read through a small allowlisted IPC surface gated to the runtime origin. The browser Web Shell keeps its existing storage behavior.

## Why it's needed

The desktop shell serves the Web Shell from a bundled daemon on an ephemeral loopback port. WebView2 scopes storage by origin, so the catalogs written by one launch were unreachable on the next and users had to re-add their connections every time. This is Part 1 of #14947; credential persistence is deliberately separate.

The live restart check also found that the workspace-host catalog would record the page's own ephemeral origin once persistence existed, adding one stale host per launch. This change skips the page origin **in the desktop shell**, where that origin really is ephemeral; the sidebar still adds it in-session. The browser keeps saving it, because there the saved entry is the local group's offline snapshot.

Hydration also re-pushes a `localStorage` mirror that differs from the native copy instead of deleting it: within one launch every change is mirrored while hydration clears the mirror, so a differing copy can only be newer than a native write that never landed.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Launch the desktop shell from this branch and add a daemon connection under Settings → Connections.
2. Restart the app. It comes back on a new loopback port, and the saved connection is still listed; Settings → Connections shows it.
3. Click × next to the connection. It disappears from the list and from `desktop-state.json`.
4. Restart twice and confirm `qwen-workspace-hosts` does not grow a `127.0.0.1:<port>` entry per launch.

Expected: the connection catalog survives restarts; the workspace-host catalog contains remote hosts only. Before this change the connection list was empty after every restart.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: after a restart the saved list was empty because both catalogs lived in origin-scoped `localStorage`.

After: a Windows debug build from this branch, with an isolated app identifier, wrote a catalog, restarted, came back on a different port, and read the catalog back; Settings → Connections showed the saved host. The same run reproduced the per-launch workspace-host growth and then verified its fix. The unit and integration checks below pass.

An independent A/B run on macOS confirmed the same on head `8a220bc4d`: five launches on rotating ports, catalogs intact after each restart, base arm empty after the first one, and the browser arm still writing the page origin to `localStorage`.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ✅   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

The macOS row reflects what the author ran; the independent run above covers the restart flow on that platform, not the full PR scope.

### Environment

Local Tauri debug build with an isolated app identifier and profile; bundled runtime built from this branch.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the catalogs now live in `desktop-state.json`. The file is plaintext, so it must stay free of credentials; it stores addresses and workspace identities only.
- Not validated / out of scope: Linux live restart checks. The full repository typecheck OOMs in `packages/cli` on this Windows machine; the `web-shell` package typecheck passes. Credential persistence, a stable shell origin, and an automated desktop E2E remain out of scope.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. Browser behavior is unchanged. Migration reads only the current origin's `localStorage`; older launches cannot be recovered.

## Design docs

- [English](https://github.com/BigDaddy1337/qwen-code/blob/feat/desktop-shell-state/docs/design/2026-10-25-desktop-shell-state.md)
- [简体中文](https://github.com/BigDaddy1337/qwen-code/blob/feat/desktop-shell-state/docs/design/2026-10-25-desktop-shell-state.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

References #14947.

<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

桌面客户端现在会在重启后保留 Web Shell 的已保存 daemon 连接和工作区主机目录。两个目录都保存在桌面外壳的设置文件中，并通过一层小而带白名单、按运行时 origin 校验的 IPC 读取。浏览器 Web Shell 保持原有存储行为。

## 为什么需要

桌面外壳由内置 daemon 在临时回环端口上提供 Web Shell。WebView2 按 origin 隔离存储，因此一次启动写入的目录在下一次启动时无法读取，用户每次都要重新添加连接。这是 #14947 的第一部分；凭据持久化刻意分开处理。

实机重启检查还发现：一旦目录开始持久化，工作区主机目录会记录页面自身的临时 origin，每次启动都追加一个过期主机。本次改动在**桌面外壳中**跳过页面 origin——那里的 origin 确实是临时的；侧边栏仍会在会话内加入它。浏览器则继续保存它，因为在浏览器中该条目是本地分组的离线快照。

水合时，与原生副本不同的 `localStorage` 镜像会被回推而不是删除：一次启动内每次变更都会写镜像，而水合会清空镜像，因此不同的副本只可能比“从未真正落地”的原生写入更新。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

1. 从本分支启动桌面外壳，在 Settings → Connections 中添加一个 daemon 连接。
2. 重启应用。应用会以新的回环端口回来，已保存连接仍在列表中；Settings → Connections 能看到它。
3. 点击连接旁的 ×。它会从列表和 `desktop-state.json` 中消失。
4. 连续重启两次，确认 `qwen-workspace-hosts` 不会每次启动都增加一个 `127.0.0.1:<port>` 条目。

预期：连接目录能跨重启存活；工作区主机目录只包含远程主机。改动前，每次重启后连接列表都是空的。

### 证据（修改前后）

修改前：重启后已保存列表为空，因为两个目录都存放在按 origin 隔离的 `localStorage` 中。

修改后：在 Windows 上使用本分支的 debug 构建和隔离的应用 identifier，写入目录、重启、以不同端口回来并读回目录；Settings → Connections 显示了已保存主机。同一次实跑先复现了每次启动累积工作区主机的问题，随后验证了修复。下面的单元与集成检查均通过。

一次独立的 macOS A/B 实跑在 head `8a220bc4d` 上确认了同样的结果：五次启动、端口轮换，每次重启后目录都完好；base 臂第一次重启后即为空；浏览器臂仍把页面 origin 写入 `localStorage`。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ⚠️  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ✅  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ⚠️  |

macOS 一行反映的是作者本人的验证；上述独立实跑覆盖的是该平台的重启流程，而非本 PR 的全部范围。

### 环境

本地 Tauri debug 构建，使用隔离的应用 identifier 与配置目录；运行时由本分支构建。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险与取舍：目录现在位于 `desktop-state.json`。该文件是明文，因此必须保持不含凭据；其中只存地址和工作区标识。
- 未验证 / 超出范围：Linux 的实机重启检查。在这台 Windows 机器上，完整仓库的 typecheck 会在 `packages/cli` 中 OOM；`web-shell` 包的 typecheck 通过。凭据持久化、稳定外壳 origin 与自动化的桌面端到端测试仍超出范围。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。浏览器行为不变。迁移只读取当前 origin 的 `localStorage`；更早的启动无法恢复。

## 设计文档

- [English](https://github.com/BigDaddy1337/qwen-code/blob/feat/desktop-shell-state/docs/design/2026-10-25-desktop-shell-state.md)
- [简体中文](https://github.com/BigDaddy1337/qwen-code/blob/feat/desktop-shell-state/docs/design/2026-10-25-desktop-shell-state.zh-CN.md)

## 关联 Issue

引用 #14947。

prs.title: test(serve): cover the workspace_runtime_stop boot-time conjunction
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds one test to `packages/cli/src/serve/server.test.ts` that exercises the boot-time computation behind the `workspace_runtime_stop` capability, instead of injecting the resulting toggle. The positive arm mounts the real serve app with every dependency the gate needs and asserts the capability is advertised; the negative arm removes exactly one required dependency and asserts it is not.

## Why it's needed

`runtimeStopReady` in `packages/cli/src/serve/server.ts` is a five-way conjunction: `deps.managedChildProcesses`, `deps.workspaceRuntimeRemoval`, a live ACP HTTP handle, `deps.manageScheduledTaskSessions`, and a managed runtime whose bridge implements `stopWorkspaceRuntime` / `getRuntimeStopCompletion` / `getRuntimeStopSnapshot`. Both read points (`workspaceRuntimeStopAvailable` in the capabilities toggles and the stop route's `available`) are derived from it.

Nothing exercised that computation. `workspaceRuntimeStopAvailable` appeared in the suite only as a directly injected value in the conditional-features drift test, and `runtimeStopReady` had zero hits in the test file — so if any one leg regressed (say the registry predicate stopped checking a method, or a dependency stopped being passed), the capability would silently stop being advertised while the suite stayed green.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

The new test is `advertises workspace runtime stop only with the full managed stop wiring`, placed in the existing `GET /capabilities` block right after the current-session scheduling test.

- Positive arm: mount the app with `managedChildProcesses`, `workspaceRuntimeRemoval`, `manageScheduledTaskSessions`, and a registry built from `createWorkspaceRegistry` + `makeWorkspaceRuntimeForTest` whose bridge carries all three stop methods. `GET /capabilities` must contain `workspace_runtime_stop`.
- Negative arm: destructure `manageScheduledTaskSessions` out of the same deps and mount again. The same route must not contain the capability.

The test never references `workspaceRuntimeStopAvailable` — the label has to come through the production conjunction, which is what makes the assertion load-bearing.

Mutation probe (whole assignment `runtimeStopReady = false` in `server.ts`, no other change):

```
$ npx vitest run --config <tmp> src/serve/server.test.ts -t 'advertises workspace runtime stop only with the full managed stop wiring'
 FAIL  src/serve/server.test.ts > createServeApp > GET /capabilities > advertises workspace runtime stop only with the full managed stop wiring
AssertionError: expected [ 'health', 'daemon_status', …(144) ] to include 'workspace_runtime_stop'
 Tests  1 failed | 1445 skipped (1446)
RC=1

$ npx vitest run --config <tmp> src/serve/server.test.ts -t 'honors every entry in CONDITIONAL_SERVE_FEATURES'
 ✓ src/serve/server.test.ts (1446 tests | 1445 skipped) 39ms
 Tests  1 passed | 1445 skipped (1446)
RC=0
```

The injected-toggle drift test stays green under the same mutation, confirming the new test is the only one with teeth on this gate. Restoring `server.ts` from a byte-identical backup (sha256 `1b6fc425cb37…`) puts the new test back to green (RC=0).

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — test-only change, no user-visible surface.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Linux, `packages/cli` vitest 3.2.7 against `origin/main` 7cb46d9fed. Workspace packages were not built in this worktree, so the run used a temporary config that bypassed the fresh-checkout global setup and aliased the unbuilt `@qwen-code/channel-*` packages to their sources; the config was deleted afterwards and is not part of the diff. Full `server.test.ts` also ran: 1438 passed, 7 failed, and all 7 failures reproduce on the unmodified baseline in this environment (5 need `git init -b`, which local git 2.19.1 lacks; 2 export-HTML tests return 500 without the built export template).

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the negative arm removes only one of the five legs, so it pins "at least one leg is load-bearing" rather than each leg individually. The whole-assignment mutation probe covers the conjunction as a unit.
- Not validated / out of scope: no attempt to cover the per-leg branching of the registry predicate (three method checks) or the `runtimeStopsClosing` half of the read points; that is beyond this finding.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Part of #12563 — does not close it.
