prs.title: fix(core): replay the persisted startup prelude on resume
prs.body:
## What this PR does

A resumed session now replays the exact startup prelude it originally sent instead of rebuilding it from the current date, directory tree, git snapshot, MCP instructions, skills, and deferred-tool list. The prelude is persisted as a system record when a session starts or rebuilds it, recovery keeps the latest record and places it as the first API-history entry, and a session that already has the saved prelude no longer builds a second one.

This keeps the first user message byte-identical across resume, so an implicit prefix cache can reuse the conversation history instead of stopping at the system prompt.

## Why it's needed

When a session is resumed, the client rebuilds the startup prelude in front of the saved turns. The rebuilt prelude contains fresh workspace data, so the first user message differs from the one the previous process sent. With vLLM-style implicit prefix caching, the reusable prefix ends at that first difference.

A reported 417k-token conversation reused only about 14k tokens of KV cache and recomputed about 186k tokens, producing a 126-second time to first token. The stored transcript's first user record is the real prompt; it has no startup prelude, so a resumed process had nothing to replay.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the focused regression tests; all should pass on the branch:

```bash
cd packages/core
npx vitest run src/core/environmentContext.test.ts -t "reuses a stored startup prelude"
npx vitest run src/services/session-api-history.test.ts -t "startup context replay"
npx vitest run src/core/client.test.ts -t "records a generated startup prelude"
```

To see the regression, temporarily remove the saved-prelude reuse and the startup-context recovery branch (or stash the implementation) and rerun the same tests. Before the fix, the first test rebuilds a fresh prelude in front of the saved turns and the second drops the saved prelude entirely; both fail.

For a real session, start a new conversation with the branch and `--openai-logging`, complete a few turns, exit, and resume. The first request's `messages[0]` should be identical to the pre-resume request's first message, and the provider's cached-token count should include the conversation history rather than only the system prompt.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — this is a core session-recovery change with unit-level evidence.

Before the fix, the two focused tests failed:

```
environmentContext: reuses a stored startup prelude -> 1 failed
session-api-history: startup context replay -> 1 failed
```

After the fix, they pass. Full local runs:

```
client.test.ts                      624 passed
environmentContext.test.ts          116 passed
session-api-history.test.ts          63 passed
chatRecordingService.test.ts        191 passed
session-transcript-reader.test.ts   152 passed
transcript-records validation        48 passed
ACP targeted test                     1 passed
```

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| --- | --- |
| macOS | ⚠️ not tested |
| Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
| Linux | ✅ tested (Node 26.8.1, packages/core vitest) |

### Environment

Local Node 26.8.1 with `npx vitest` from `packages/core`; core `tsc --noEmit`, Prettier, and ESLint pass. The full CLI build and a live vLLM prefix-cache run were not executed in this environment.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the saved prelude keeps the original date and git/MCP/skills snapshot. Date freshness still comes from the existing history-derived tail reminder. The git snapshot is intentionally frozen at session start; the model can run `git status` for current state.
- Not validated / out of scope: full CLI build and live vLLM E2E; divergence caused by changes in the system prompt or tool declarations is a separate part of the broader context-immutability issue. Managed-session journals that cannot carry the new record fall back to rebuilding the prelude.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: sessions recorded before this change have no saved prelude. Their first resume rebuilds once and records the new prelude; later resumes can reuse it. No configuration or migration is required.

## Linked Issues

Part of #14215. Related: #8277, #14246, #16362.

## Design docs

- [English design](https://github.com/MikeWang0316tw/qwen-code/blob/fix/resume-startup-prelude-cache/docs/design/2026-11-06-resume-startup-prelude-cache.md)
- [Chinese design](https://github.com/MikeWang0316tw/qwen-code/blob/fix/resume-startup-prelude-cache/docs/design/2026-11-06-resume-startup-prelude-cache.zh-CN.md)

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做什么

resume 后的 session 现在会重播它当初送出的同一份 startup prelude，而不是用当下的日期、目录树、git snapshot、MCP instructions、skills 与 deferred-tool 清单重新建一份。session 开始或重建 prelude 时会把它写成 system record；还原时保留最新的一笔，放到 API history 的第一个 entry；已经有存档 prelude 的 session 不会再建第二份。

这让 resume 后的第一个 user message 与原本 request 完全一致，implicit prefix cache 才能重用整段对话历史，而不是只重用到 system prompt。

## 为什么需要

实际回报的 417k-token 对话只重用了约 14k tokens 的 KV cache，其余约 186k tokens 重算，TTFT 126 秒。存下来的 transcript 第一笔 user record 是真正的 prompt，没有 startup prelude，所以 resume 的 process 无从重播。

## Reviewer Test Plan

### 如何验证

跑三个 focused regression tests；在 branch 上都应通过：

```bash

npx vitest run src/core/environmentContext.test.ts -t "reuses a stored startup prelude"
```

用真实 session 验证时，用这个 branch 开一个新对话并加上 `--openai-logging`，完成几轮后离开再 resume。第一个 request 的 `messages[0]` 应与 resume 前的第一个 message 完全相同，provider 的 cached-token 数量应包含对话历史，而不是只有 system prompt。

### 证据（修正前后）

N/A — 这是 core session-recovery 变更，以 unit-level 证据为主。

修正前，两个 focused tests 失败：

```
environmentContext: reuses a stored startup prelude -> 1 failed
session-api-history: startup context replay -> 1 failed
```

修正后通过。完整本地测试：

```
client.test.ts                      624 passed
environmentContext.test.ts          116 passed
session-api-history.test.ts          63 passed
chatRecordingService.test.ts        191 passed
session-transcript-reader.test.ts   152 passed
transcript-records validation        48 passed
ACP targeted test                     1 passed
```

### 测试环境

| OS | 状态 |
| --- | --- |
| macOS | ⚠️ 未测试 |
| Windows | ⚠️ 未测试 |
| Linux | ✅ 已测试（Node 26.8.1，packages/core vitest） |

### 环境

本地 Node 26.8.1，从 `packages/core` 跑 `npx vitest`；core 的 `tsc --noEmit`、Prettier、ESLint 都通过。此环境没有跑完整 CLI build 与 live vLLM prefix-cache 测试。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险／取舍：存下来的 prelude 会保留原始的日期与 git/MCP/skills 快照。日期新鲜度仍由既有的 history-derived tail reminder 负责；git snapshot 刻意冻结在 session 开始时，模型可自行跑 `git status` 取得目前状态。
- 尚未验证／超出范围：完整 CLI build 与 live vLLM E2E；若 divergence 来自 system prompt 或 tool declarations，属于更大的 context-immutability 问题，不在这个 PR。Managed session 的 journal 若无法携带新 record，会退回重建 prelude。
- Breaking changes／migration：在此变更之前建立的 session 没有存档 prelude。它们第一次 resume 会重建一次并记录新的 prelude，之后的 resume 才可重用。不需要设置或 migration。

Part of #14215。Related: #8277、#14246、#16362。

prs.title: refactor(runtime-broker): extract binding provisioning from RuntimeBrokerService
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Moves the Runtime binding lifecycle out of the Runtime Broker service into a dedicated package-private collaborator, following the same pattern as the existing execution dispatcher, reconciler, recovery and cancellation classes. The moved code covers durable provisioning and attestation, the bounded reconciliation loop, lost-binding cleanup and reclaim, and the trusted maintenance recovery path, together with their deadline and step-timeout helpers and private result types.

This is a pure move: no logic, ordering, timeout or lease handling changes. The service now delegates binding acquisition, recovery, the operation deadline, step-timeout mapping and attestation checks to the collaborator. The provision failure handler is now owned by the collaborator, which also removes the constructor-time method reference cycle in the service. The binding renewal helper stays in the service because the drain path also uses it; the collaborator receives its constructor as a factory, so every renewal behaves exactly as before.

The service shrinks from 4174 to 2943 lines. This is the third step of the managed agent server cleanup series, after #16485 and #16486.

The class-size ratchet records the extracted class at 1326 lines and tightens the service and global ceilings to 2943 and 3328 lines, so later changes cannot silently undo the split.

## Why it's needed

The Runtime Broker service was the largest class in the module, and the binding lifecycle made up about a quarter of it while depending only on itself and the operation claim. Keeping it inline made the service hard to navigate and review, and it mixed binding provisioning with Session, execution and drain concerns. Isolating it gives the binding lifecycle a clear boundary and makes later changes to recovery smaller and easier to review.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Confirm that the full unit/H2 suite, Checkstyle and SpotBugs pass in CI, along with the Hosted and fault profiles that exercise Runtime recovery. When reviewing the diff, check that the removed service code and the new class body match line for line, except for visibility on the five members the service still calls, the renewal factory call, and the constructor wiring.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A, refactor with no user-visible change.

Local results on the PR revision, using JDK 21 and Maven 3.9.9 with an isolated repository:

- Runtime Broker module install, including the bound Checkstyle and SpotBugs gates: passed, 0 Checkstyle violations and 0 SpotBugs bugs.
- Focused suites `RuntimeBrokerServiceTest`, `DurableRuntimeRecoveryTest`, `RuntimeRecoveryTest`, `RuntimeMaintenanceRecoveryTest`, `ManagedContextRecoveryTest`, `RuntimeHarnessDrainTest`, `TakeoverReconciliationTest`, `ManagedRuntimeCapacityTest` and `Issue13183RegressionTest`: 390 tests run, 0 failures, 0 errors, 0 skipped.
- A line-multiset comparison of the removed service code against the new class body showed no differences beyond the intended visibility, factory and delegation edits.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Focused Maven unit/H2 tests only; no MySQL or Hosted process run locally.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: recovery and lease code is sensitive to ordering. The change is a verbatim move, and renewals still go through the same inner class, so ordering and claim handling are unchanged.
- Not validated / out of scope: the full unit/H2 suite, MySQL integration and the Hosted/fault profiles were not run locally and are left to CI. The other large classes and the inline fully qualified names are left for later PRs.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. All moved types are package-private.

## Linked Issues

Follows #16485 and #16486.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

把 Runtime binding 的生命周期逻辑从 Runtime Broker service 中移出，放到一个独立的包级私有协作类中，做法与现有的 execution dispatcher、reconciler、recovery 和 cancellation 类一致。移出的代码包括：持久化 provisioning 与 attestation、有界的 reconciliation 循环、丢失 binding 的清理与回收、可信的维护恢复路径，以及与之配套的截止时间、单步超时辅助方法和私有结果类型。

这是纯粹的代码搬移，没有修改任何逻辑、执行顺序、超时或租约处理。service 现在把 binding 获取、恢复、操作截止时间、单步超时映射和 attestation 校验委托给新的协作类。provision 失败处理器改由协作类持有，这也消除了 service 构造函数中的方法引用循环。binding 续租辅助类仍留在 service 中，因为 drain 路径也在使用它；协作类以工厂方式拿到它的构造函数，因此每次续租的行为都与之前完全相同。

service 从 4174 行缩减到 2943 行。这是 managed agent server 清理系列的第三步，承接 #16485 和 #16486。

类大小门禁把新拆出的类登记为 1326 行，并把 service 和全局上限分别收紧到 2943 和 3328 行，防止后续改动悄悄撤销本次拆分的收益。

## 为什么需要

Runtime Broker service 是该模块中最大的类，binding 生命周期约占其四分之一，而且只依赖自身和操作 claim。把它留在 service 内部，使 service 难以阅读和评审，也把 binding provisioning 与 Session、execution、drain 等职责混在了一起。把它独立出来，可以给 binding 生命周期一个清晰的边界，也让以后对恢复逻辑的修改更小、更容易评审。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

确认 CI 中完整的单元测试 / H2 测试、Checkstyle 和 SpotBugs 都通过，同时覆盖 Runtime 恢复的 Hosted 和故障测试档位也通过。评审 diff 时，可以核对从 service 删除的代码与新类的方法体是否逐行一致；预期的差异只有三类：service 仍在调用的五个成员的可见性、续租工厂调用，以及构造函数中的装配代码。

prs.title: feat(ci): add disposable external PR runners
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Add an opt-in pool of disposable GitHub Actions runners. A host manager creates one just-in-time runner per container, removes the container and its network after a job, and replenishes the slot only after cleanup. When enabled, selected external fork PR build, test, lint, and no-credential integration jobs use the new pool.

## Why it's needed

External PR jobs can execute contributor-controlled scripts. A fresh runner container per job prevents the next job from inheriting the previous job's workspace and processes.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Check that the runner routing remains unchanged with the new variable unset, that the global hosted and kill-switch overrides win, and that the opt-in selects the expected architecture only for untrusted fork PRs. Check that completed, failed and timed-out runners are removed before a slot is replenished and that cleanup failures block replenishment.

The focused routing and manager tests passed. On an ARM64 Hangzhou host, ten disposable runners simultaneously registered with a private test repository and ran ten no-secret smoke jobs successfully. All ten containers, networks and runner registrations were removed afterward. A repository-scoped temporary relay authenticated the GitHub API calls; the GitHub App token exchange was simulated.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — CI infrastructure change.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| --- | --- |
| macOS | Focused tests and formatting passed; full build and typecheck blocked by missing workspace dependencies and build outputs. |
| Windows | Not tested. |
| Linux ARM64 | Ten-runner controlled GitHub Actions smoke passed. |

## Risk & Scope

- Docker shares the host kernel; the new route stays disabled by default. A dedicated host, verified network restrictions, and runner-group access policies are required before enabling it for untrusted PRs.
- Full repository CI on the new image, real GitHub App authentication, and model-proxy integration have not been validated or enabled.
- Roll back new routing by unsetting or disabling `EXTERNAL_PR_EPHEMERAL_RUNNER_ENABLED`; already queued jobs may need cancellation and rerun.

## Linked Issues

Related to #16514. This PR delivers the disposable runner lifecycle, not the complete untrusted-PR security boundary.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 变更内容

新增默认关闭的一次性 GitHub Actions runner 池。宿主机管理服务为每个容器创建一个即时 runner，任务完成后删除容器和网络，清理成功后补充槽位。启用后，选定的外部 fork PR 构建、测试、lint 和无凭证集成任务使用新池。

## 变更原因

外部 PR 可以执行贡献者控制的脚本。每个 job 使用全新容器可避免后续任务继承先前任务的工作区和进程。

## 测试计划

确认新变量未设置时原路由不变，全局 hosted 选择和关闭开关优先；启用后只有非可信 fork PR 选择对应架构的新池。确认完成、失败及超时的 runner 清理后才补充槽位，清理失败阻止补充。

路由与管理服务专项测试通过。在杭州 ARM64 机器上，十个一次性 runner 同时注册到私有测试仓库，十个无密钥 smoke job 全部成功；随后十个容器、网络和 runner 注册均已回收。GitHub API 通过限定仓库的临时代理认证，GitHub App 换取令牌过程为模拟。

前后截图：不适用，属于 CI 基础设施变更。macOS 上专项测试和格式检查通过；完整 build 和 typecheck 被缺失的工作区依赖及构建产物阻塞。Windows 未测试。Linux ARM64 上十 runner 的受控 GitHub Actions smoke 通过。

## 风险与范围

- Docker 共享宿主机内核，新路由默认关闭。用于非可信 PR 前，需要专用主机、验证过的网络限制和 runner group 访问策略。
- 新镜像上的完整仓库 CI、真实 GitHub App 认证和模型代理集成尚未验证或启用。
- 取消设置或关闭 `EXTERNAL_PR_EPHEMERAL_RUNNER_ENABLED` 可回滚新路由；已排队任务可能需要取消并重新运行。

## 关联 Issue

关联 #16514。本 PR 提供一次性 runner 生命周期，不代表已完成外部 PR 的完整安全隔离。

</details>


### Dispatch boundary — rollout blocked

A PR can modify its own workflow YAML and replace `runs-on`; this opt-in selector does not prevent it from requesting other persistent runners available to the repository. Repository-scoped runner groups alone do not separate trusted and untrusted revisions. Keep the new route disabled until dispatch is enforced outside PR-controlled YAML, or sensitive runners are removed from this repository’s reach. See #16514 for the rollout gates.

prs.title: fix(core): bind the LSP hot-reload callback and align the LSP guide with current behavior
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Updates the LSP guide to describe current configuration, workspace trust, timeout, sandbox, server-selection, diagnostics, and document-synchronization behavior. It also corrects the model-facing usage guidance so `character` is documented as optional and defaults to the first column.

It also binds the LSP hot-reload callback to its `Config` receiver so `.lsp.json` edits reconcile at runtime (requested in review), with a regression test that fails on the unbound call.

## Why it's needed

The existing guide contains several statements that no longer match the implementation. In particular, it implies that project configuration can bypass workspace trust, that one server is always used per operation, that startup timeouts cover initialization, and that saving an already-open document refreshes the server. These mismatches can lead users and the model to rely on behavior the current LSP integration does not provide.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Compare the guide's configuration and limitations sections with the current LSP configuration loader, server manager, connection factory, native service, and tool schema. Confirm that project configuration cannot opt out of the trust check, the default-disabled folder-trust layer is described separately, diagnostics are pull-only, multi-server aggregation is limited to the named operations, and `character` is optional with a tested first-column default. Run `cd packages/core && npx vitest run src/tools/lsp.test.ts`; all 79 tests should pass.

- Run `cd packages/cli && npx vitest run src/llm.test.tsx`; all 112 tests should pass.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — documentation and model-facing tool guidance only.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Node.js 24 with the repository's authoritative `npm ci` install. The focused LSP suite passed 79/79, and formatting, lint, both builds, and typecheck passed. A mutation of the omitted-character default from column 1 to column 2 makes the new regression test fail. The exhaustive workspace test stage was also run; unrelated CLI/core tests that write to the sandboxed home directory, open file watchers, or depend on tight parallel timing failed in this restricted environment, while the focused LSP suite and the remaining workspace packages passed.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: Documentation can drift again as the experimental LSP implementation evolves.
- Not validated / out of scope: Adding push diagnostics, synchronizing saved documents, changing initialization timeout behavior, and updating downstream translated documentation are separate implementation or publishing concerns.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: None.

## Linked Issues

Refs #11418. The source guide corrections are complete; the published Chinese page lives in a separate documentation-site repository and still requires downstream coordination.

This change was prepared with AI assistance and independently reviewed against the current implementation.

prs.title: fix(ci): route the review/resolve permission gate to the ECS pool
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Routes the write-permission gate that fronts every `@qwen-code /review` and `@qwen-code /resolve` command onto the self-hosted ECS runner pool when the trigger is a comment or a manual dispatch. Previously these two triggers always fell back to GitHub-hosted runners; the gate now uses the idle persistent pool the same way the autofix router and scan already do. The fork isolation for events that carry a pull-request payload, the hosted fallback, and the ECS kill switch are all unchanged. The conflict-resolution agent and the credentialed publish step deliberately stay on hosted runners; this change only removes the wait at the gate.

## Why it's needed

The gate's runner routing keyed off a pull-request payload field that comment and dispatch events do not carry, so every interactive command fell through to the hosted pool regardless of how idle the self-hosted pool was. Because the gate is a hard prerequisite, nothing downstream even enters the queue until it finishes. On a congested hosted queue this stalled commands for hours: on PR #15286 the four-second gate waited 3h10m (run 42201221971, created 10:15:08Z, gate started 13:25:52Z) while the ECS pool sat idle, and the queued resolution was eventually cancelled without ever running. The gate is an API-only job — it reads the triggering principal from event metadata and calls one read permission API; it runs no agent, checks out nothing, and processes no pull-request content — so it is safe on the persistent pool, exactly like the autofix router/scan steps that already route payload-less events there (the scan loads a bot PAT; the router uses only the read-only github.token).

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

- Confirm the routing change only affects comment and dispatch triggers: PR-payload events keep the same-repo/fork behavior, and the hosted fallback plus the `MAINTAINER_ECS_RUNNER_DISABLED` kill switch still force hosted. The design doc has the full before/after event table.
- Run the pinning meta-test: `npx vitest run --config ./scripts/tests/vitest.config.ts scripts/tests/qwen-pr-review-workflow.test.js -t "runner routing"` → 2 passed. Mutation witness: reverting the gate's runner expression to the old same-repo-only form makes the new test fail (verified locally); restoring it passes.
- Full suites pass: `qwen-pr-review-workflow.test.js` (271 tests) and `qwen-resolve-workflow.test.js` (55 tests).
- After merge, a fresh `@qwen-code /resolve` on a same-repo PR should show the gate job landing on an `ecs-qwen` runner instead of queueing on `ubuntu-latest`.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — CI routing change, no UI.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ not tested |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ tested |

### Environment (optional)

Local vitest (`scripts/tests` suite) on Linux; no sandbox needed (YAML + meta-test only).

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the gate loads a bot PAT on the persistent pool. This is the same exposure already accepted for the autofix scan (which loads a bot PAT on the same pool; the router uses only the read-only github.token), and the gate is strictly lighter (one read API, no checkout). The structural close for PAT-bearing steps on the shared pool is tracked in the runner-isolation design; this does not regress it.
- Not validated / out of scope: the resolution agent and the publish step still run on hosted, so a saturated hosted pool can still delay them — this removes the gate wait only. Moving the agent to ECS behind a working docker sandbox (with dry-run evidence) is a separate experiment, explicitly not decided here.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. Behavior changes only for comment/dispatch triggers; reversible via the existing ECS kill switch.

Design doc: [English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/fix/review-authorize-ecs-routing/docs/design/review-authorize-ecs-routing.md) | [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/fix/review-authorize-ecs-routing/docs/design/review-authorize-ecs-routing.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

Motivated by the stalled resolution on #15286 (referenced, not closed). Related: the runner-isolation design for PAT-bearing steps on the shared pool.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

把守在每一条 `@qwen-code /review` 与 `@qwen-code /resolve` 命令前面的写权限门，在触发器是评论或手动 dispatch 时路由到自建 ECS runner 池。此前这两类触发器总是回落到 GitHub 托管 runner；现在该门像 autofix 的 router 与 scan 一样使用空闲的持久池。对携带 pull-request 载荷的事件的 fork 隔离、托管回落、以及 ECS 开关全都保持不变。解冲突 agent 与携带凭据的 publish 步骤仍有意留在托管 runner 上；本改动只消除门口的等待。

## 为什么需要

该门的 runner 路由依赖一个评论与 dispatch 事件并不携带的 pull-request 载荷字段，因此每一条交互命令都回落到托管池，无论自建池多空闲。由于该门是硬前置，它不结束，下游连队列都进不了。在拥堵的托管队列上这会把命令卡死数小时：PR #15286 上这个只需四秒的门等了 3 小时 10 分（run 42201221971，创建于 10:15:08Z，门于 13:25:52Z 启动），而 ECS 池当时是空闲的，排队中的解冲突最终被取消、从未运行。该门是一个纯 API job——它从事件元数据读出触发主体并调用一个只读权限 API；不跑 agent、不 checkout、不处理任何 pull-request 内容——因此在持久池上是安全的，恰如早已把无载荷事件路由到那里的 autofix router/scan 步骤（scan 加载 bot PAT；router 只用只读的 github.token）。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

- 确认路由改动只影响评论与 dispatch 触发器：PR 载荷事件保持同仓/fork 行为，托管回落与 `MAINTAINER_ECS_RUNNER_DISABLED` 开关仍能强制托管。设计文档有完整的改动前后事件对照表。
- 运行 pin 住路由的 meta-test：`npx vitest run --config ./scripts/tests/vitest.config.ts scripts/tests/qwen-pr-review-workflow.test.js -t "runner routing"` → 2 通过。变异见证：把该门的 runner 表达式还原为旧的同仓唯一形式会使新测试失败（已在本机验证）；恢复后通过。
- 完整套件通过：`qwen-pr-review-workflow.test.js`（271 个测试）与 `qwen-resolve-workflow.test.js`（55 个测试）。
- 合并后，在同仓 PR 上发一条新的 `@qwen-code /resolve`，应能看到门 job 落在 `ecs-qwen` runner 上，而不是在 `ubuntu-latest` 上排队。

### 证据（改动前后）

N/A —— CI 路由改动，无 UI。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ⚠️ 未测试 |
| 🪟 Windows | ⚠️ 未测试 |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ 已测试 |

### 环境（可选）

本机 Linux 上的 vitest（`scripts/tests` 套件）；无需沙箱（仅 YAML + meta-test）。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或权衡：该门在持久池上加载一个 bot PAT。这与 autofix scan 已被接受的暴露相同（它在同一池上加载 bot PAT；router 只用只读的 github.token），且该门严格更轻（一个只读 API、无 checkout）。共享池上携带 PAT 步骤的结构性收口在 runner-isolation 设计中跟踪；本改动不使其倒退。
- 未验证 / 范围外：解冲突 agent 与 publish 步骤仍在托管上运行，因此饱和的托管池仍可能延迟它们——本改动只消除门口等待。把 agent 搬到一个可用的 docker 沙箱之后的 ECS（需 dry-run 证据）是独立实验，此处明确不作决定。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。行为仅对评论/dispatch 触发器变化；可通过既有 ECS 开关回退。

设计文档：[English](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/fix/review-authorize-ecs-routing/docs/design/review-authorize-ecs-routing.md) | [简体中文](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/blob/fix/review-authorize-ecs-routing/docs/design/review-authorize-ecs-routing.zh-CN.md)

## 关联 Issue

由 #15286 上停滞的解冲突促成（引用，非关闭）。相关：共享池上携带 PAT 步骤的 runner-isolation 设计。

</details>

prs.title: fix(ci): keep sdk-java resolver bookkeeping and in-house jars out of the host cache (#15281)
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The job-local Maven repository that the sdk-java suites resolve from no longer shares mutable inodes with the host cache:

- Every seed site drops `maven-metadata-local.xml` together with the other resolver bookkeeping names (`_remote.repositories`, `resolver-status.properties`, `*.lastUpdated`, `*.tmp`), so the unlocked Maven runs cannot rewrite a host-cache file through a seeded hardlink.
- The locked write-back removes every in-house fixed-release coordinate from the host cache (the `qwen-managed-agent-*` modules are purged by glob, tracking #15871's module split), prunes them at any depth rather than only at the repository root, publishes only job-produced files (the same five names stay job-local), and downgrades a failed cache-directory creation to a warning instead of reddening a green suite.
- The self-hosted Managed Agent Checkstyle leg resolves the SDK from the job-local repository the suite installed it into.
- The release builder's seed copies into the job-local repository instead of nesting a second `repository/` inside it, and drops the same bookkeeping names.
- The workflow meta-tests pin the five exclusions at every seed and both prunes, the write-back's children and their fd 9 closure, the host-side removal, the warning path, and the Checkstyle repository.

## Why it's needed

Moving Maven above the per-host lock is only safe while the job-local repository has no inode in common with the host cache. Maven's resolver rewrites its bookkeeping files in place, and the suites `install` fixed-release in-house artifacts: seeded as hardlinks, they let an unlocked run mutate state that every sibling job on the host reads.

Correction to the earlier description: the lock-scope change itself ("only the write-back takes the lock") landed through #15128 and #15254 and is already on main. #15274 remains open with overlapping cache and deferred-status changes. This PR is the cache-isolation half that makes that scope safe, and it is judged on that, not on the lock wait from #15281.

Reconciliation on 2026-10-31: merged main `812a8c7ccb` and reconciled with #15871's split of the Managed Agent server into nine Maven modules. The seed drops, the write-back prunes and the host-cache purge now cover the full in-house coordinate set; the purge globs `qwen-managed-agent-*` so a future module rename cannot leave a stale host copy behind. All four unique behaviors are retained: the host-cache purge, the seed nesting fix, the self-hosted Checkstyle repository, and the reference-release seed isolation. When #15274 lands, this branch reconciles against its delivered code again.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Open the `SDK Java (fast) / ubuntu-latest / Java 21` job of a PR that touches a managed-agent path. The self-hosted step should show the `cp -aln` seed and all three Maven invocations before any `Waiting for the sdk-java host lock` line; the lock wait should appear only at the cache write-back, and the write-back should remove the in-house coordinates before copying. Grep the job-local repository for `maven-metadata-local.xml` after the suite: it should hold only job-produced files.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before: a seeded `maven-metadata-local.xml` and a seeded `qwencode-sdk` jar were the same inode as the host cache, so the unlocked `mvn install` changed the host file (same inode, SHA and mtime both moved). After: the host file is byte- and mtime-identical while the job-local copy is still written, the write-back publishes zero bookkeeping files and never the in-house coordinates, and the host cache loses the pre-PR in-house trees. N/A for UI.

### Tested on

|     OS     |                       Status                        |
| :--------: | :-------------------------------------------------: |
|  🍏 macOS  | ✅ meta-tests (367 passed, 11 Linux-only skipped), shell probes, Prettier |
| 🪟 Windows |                   ⚠️ not tested                    |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ CI is authoritative for the Linux-only behavioral legs; earlier heads ran the full meta-tests there |

### Environment (optional)

Meta-tests at head `28eedc0e1a` (macOS): `scripts/tests/sdk-java-workflow.test.js`, `scripts/tests/workflow-size.test.js`, `scripts/tests/sdk-java-lock.test.js` — 367 passed, 11 skipped (the Linux-only behavioral legs run in CI). Local shell probes confirmed the nine-coordinate any-depth prune, the five-name exclusion and the glob host purge. No JDK 21 / Maven locally, so the real Java suite is left to CI.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a cold host pays the seed cost once, and the write-back is best-effort and capped at 300 seconds, matching the MariaDB lane. The write-back also deletes pre-existing in-house copies from the host cache — intended, because they are the stale fixed-release jars the in-house prune exists to stop publishing.
- Not validated / out of scope: the real ECS pool and its ticketed lock queue; the full JDK 21 Maven suite; the MySQL / MariaDB integration lanes; the hosted legs.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

Design documents: [English](docs/design/2026-10-20-sdk-java-fair-lock-queue.md) | [简体中文](docs/design/2026-10-20-sdk-java-fair-lock-queue.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

Related to #15281 (the lock-scope change landed through #15128 and #15254; this PR closes the cache-isolation gap that the smaller lock scope depends on).

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

sdk-java 套件解析所使用的 job 本地 Maven 仓库，不再与宿主缓存共享可写 inode：

- 每个播种站点在删除其他解析器记账文件（`_remote.repositories`、`resolver-status.properties`、`*.lastUpdated`、`*.tmp`）的同时也删除 `maven-metadata-local.xml`，因此不持锁的 Maven 运行无法穿透播种的硬链接改写宿主缓存。
- 持锁的写回会在宿主缓存中删除全部内部固定发布坐标（`qwen-managed-agent-*` 各模块以 glob 清理，跟随 #15871 的模块拆分），按任意深度 prune 而不只匹配仓库根，只发布本 job 产生的文件（同样五个名字留在 job 本地），并把缓存目录创建失败降级为警告，而不是让绿色套件变红。
- self-hosted 的 Managed Agent Checkstyle leg 从套件安装到的 job 本地仓库解析 SDK。
- 发布构建的播种改为向 job 本地仓库内复制，而不是在其中再嵌套一个 `repository/`，并删除同样的记账文件。
- 工作流元测试钉住每个播种点与两处 prune 的五个排除名、写回子进程及其 fd 9 关闭、宿主侧删除、警告路径，以及 Checkstyle 的仓库。

## 为什么需要

把 Maven 移到池级锁之外，只有在 job 本地仓库与宿主缓存没有共同 inode 时才是安全的。Maven 解析器会原地重写记账文件，而套件会 `install` 固定发布坐标的内部构件：一旦以硬链接播种，它们会让不持锁的运行改写同宿主上所有兄弟 job 都读取的状态。

对早先描述的更正：持锁范围的改动本身（“只有写回取锁”）已通过 #15128 和 #15254 落地并在 main 上。#15274 仍然开放，其中缓存和延后状态处理的改动与本 PR 有重叠。本 PR 是让该范围安全成立的缓存隔离部分，评审应以这一点为准，而不是 #15281 的锁等待。

2026-10-31 对齐：合入 main `812a8c7ccb`，并与 #15871 将 Managed Agent server 拆分为九个 Maven 模块的改动对齐。播种删除、写回 prune 与宿主缓存清理现在覆盖完整的内部坐标集合；清理以 glob 匹配 `qwen-managed-agent-*`，未来模块改名也不会遗留过期的宿主副本。四项独有行为全部保留：宿主缓存清理、播种嵌套修复、self-hosted Checkstyle 仓库选择、reference-release 播种隔离。#15274 合入后，本分支会再按其实际交付的代码对齐一次。

## Reviewer 测试计划

### 如何验证

打开一个触及 managed-agent 路径的 PR 的 `SDK Java (fast) / ubuntu-latest / Java 21` job。self-hosted step 应先出现 `cp -aln` 播种和三次 Maven 调用，之后才可能出现 `Waiting for the sdk-java host lock`；锁等待只应出现在缓存写回处，且写回会先删除内部坐标再复制。套件结束后在 job 本地仓库里 grep `maven-metadata-local.xml`，应当只剩本 job 产生的文件。

### 证据（Before & After）

Before：播种出的 `maven-metadata-local.xml` 与 `qwencode-sdk` jar 与宿主缓存是同一 inode，不持锁的 `mvn install` 会改写宿主文件（inode 相同，SHA 与 mtime 都变化）。After：宿主文件字节与 mtime 完全不变，同时 job 本地副本仍被写入；写回不发布任何记账文件、也从不发布内部坐标；宿主缓存中遗留的内部目录被删除。UI 不适用。

### 测试环境

head `28eedc0e1a` 上的元测试（macOS）：`scripts/tests/sdk-java-workflow.test.js`、`scripts/tests/workflow-size.test.js`、`scripts/tests/sdk-java-lock.test.js` —— 367 通过、11 跳过（Linux 专属行为测试交给 CI）。本机 shell 探针实测了九坐标任意深度 prune、五名排除与 glob 宿主清理。本机没有 JDK 21 / Maven，真实 Java 套件交给 CI。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险与取舍：冷宿主要付一次播种成本；写回是尽力而为且上限 300 秒，与 MariaDB 通道一致。写回还会删除宿主缓存中遗留的内部坐标副本——这是有意为之，因为它们正是内部坐标 prune 要阻止继续发布的过期固定发布 jar。
- 未验证 / 范围外：真实 ECS 池及其票据化锁队列；完整 JDK 21 Maven 套件；MySQL / MariaDB 集成通道；hosted leg。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。

## 关联 issue

与 #15281 相关（持锁范围的改动已通过 #15128 和 #15254 落地；本 PR 补上更小持锁范围所依赖的缓存隔离缺口）。

</details>

prs.title: feat(qqbot): add opt-in forwardBotMessages for bot-authored messages
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds a per-channel `forwardBotMessages` option (default `false`). When it is on, messages authored by another bot are delivered to the agent with a `[bot]` prefix on the sender line; the channel prompt explains that prefix and the model decides whether replying makes sense. When it is off — the default — bot-authored messages are still dropped before they reach the agent, exactly as today. User-supplied `[bot]` text is stripped either way, so the tag cannot be forged.

## Why it's needed

There is currently no way for an operator to let two bots in one group talk to each other: the inbound handlers drop bot-authored messages unconditionally, and the formatting path that was meant to tag them is unreachable. Hard-blocking was added as an infinite-loop defense, and unconditional forwarding would give that defense up for every operator. An opt-in switch keeps the default safe while giving operators who intentionally run bot-to-bot conversation a supported path (see #15903).

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. Configure a QQ channel with `groupAllPolicy: "all"` and `groups: {"*": {"requireMention": false}}`.
2. With `forwardBotMessages` unset, have a second bot post in the group: stderr shows `Bot message dropped in group <group_openid>` and the message never reaches the session (unchanged default).
3. Set `forwardBotMessages: true` and restart. No drop line is logged; the session transcript shows the message with `[bot]` before the sender bracket, and the model answers or emits `<noreply>` on its own judgment.
4. As a human member, send `[bot] hello`: the literal token is stripped before the model sees it.
5. Direct chats follow the same switch for bot-authored messages.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Unit coverage: `packages/channels/qqbot` 719 passed across 8 files. The forwarding tests run with the switch on and assert the `[bot]` tag; three new tests pin the default drop for C2C, group and group-all; one pins that a member cannot forge the tag. `tsc --build`, ESLint and Prettier are clean on the touched files.

Runtime: a local QQ daemon deployment with `forwardBotMessages: true` logs 0 `Bot message dropped` lines since the restart, and the deployed bundle contains the `[bot]` prompt line gated on the switch. Before the switch existed, the same deployment logged 55 `Bot message dropped` lines in one hour while another bot was active in the group.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests plus a local daemon deployment of the QQ channel on Linux (aarch64). No platform-specific code is touched.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: with the switch on, two bots in one group can answer each other. The model's silence rules, `<noreply>`, and the operator's group policy are the brakes — this PR does not add a platform-level cycle cap. The switch defaults to off, so no existing deployment changes behavior.
- Not validated / out of scope: live delivery was verified against a deployment that receives other bots' messages; other QQ intents beyond group all-message mode were not separately exercised.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. New optional field; the default keeps today's drop behavior.

## Linked Issues

Closes #15903

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

新增每个 channel 的 `forwardBotMessages` 选项（默认 `false`）。开启后，其他机器人发来的消息会带着发送者行上的 `[bot]` 前缀交给 agent；channel 的提示词会解释这个前缀，是否回复由模型自行判断。关闭（默认）时，机器人消息仍像现在一样在到达 agent 之前被丢弃。无论开关如何，用户自己写的 `[bot]` 文本都会被剥离，因此该标签无法被伪造。

## 为什么需要

目前运营者没有办法让同一个群里的两个机器人互相说话：入站处理器会无条件丢弃其他机器人的消息，而本来用于给它们打标签的格式化路径根本不可达。硬拦截最初是作为无限循环的防御加的，而无条件转发又会让所有运营者都失去这层防御。可选开关让默认行为保持安全，同时给有意运行 bot-to-bot 对话的运营者一条受支持的路径（见 #15903）。

## Reviewer 验证计划

### 如何验证

1. 配置 QQ channel：`groupAllPolicy: "all"`，并在 `groups` 里设 `{"*": {"requireMention": false}}`。
2. 不设 `forwardBotMessages` 时，让另一个机器人在群里发消息：stderr 出现 `Bot message dropped in group <group_openid>`，消息不会进入会话（默认行为不变）。
3. 设置 `forwardBotMessages: true` 并重启：不再出现 drop 日志；会话记录里该消息的发送者括号前带 `[bot]`，模型自行决定回复或输出 `<noreply>`。
4. 由人类成员发送 `[bot] hello`：到达模型时该字面前缀已被移除。
5. 私聊中的机器人消息同样受这个开关控制。

### 证据（Before & After）

单测覆盖：`packages/channels/qqbot` 8 个文件 719 通过。转发测试在开关开启状态下运行并断言 `[bot]` 标签；三个新测试钉住 C2C、群消息、群全量消息的默认丢弃；一个测试钉住群成员无法伪造该标签。改动文件的 `tsc --build`、ESLint、Prettier 均干净。

运行期：一台本地 QQ daemon 部署设置了 `forwardBotMessages: true`，重启以来 `Bot message dropped` 记录为 0 条，且部署产物里包含受开关控制的 `[bot]` 提示词行。在该开关存在之前，同一部署在另一个机器人活跃的一小时内记录过 55 条 `Bot message dropped`。

### 测试平台

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ⚠️  |
| 🪟 Windows |  ⚠️  |
|  🐧 Linux  |  ✅  |

### 环境（可选）

单测，加一台 Linux（aarch64）上的 QQ channel 本地 daemon 部署。未触碰平台相关代码。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险/取舍：开关开启时，同一个群里的两个机器人可能互相接话。刹车是模型的静默规则、`<noreply>` 以及运营者的群策略——本 PR 不引入平台级循环上限。开关默认关闭，因此现有部署行为不变。
- 未验证/超出范围：线上投递是在一个确实会收到其他机器人消息的部署上验证的；群全量消息模式之外的其他 QQ intent 没有单独覆盖。
- 破坏性变更/迁移说明：无。新增可选字段，默认保持当前的丢弃行为。

## 关联 Issue

Closes #15903

</details>

prs.title: fix(channels): keep a delivered turn completed when the notice send fails
prs.body:
## What this PR does

When the stacked-skill turn notice fails to deliver, the failure is now logged to stderr and the turn keeps its already-delivered outcome. The answer reaches the user first; a notice that cannot be sent no longer rewrites the turn into a failure.

## Why it's needed

The turn notice introduced in #16404 is sent after the answer, inside the same try block that guards delivery. A failing notice send bubbles into the catch that emits `failed` with `phase: 'delivery'` and rethrows, so `handleInbound` rejects and an already-delivered turn is rewritten as failed — even though the user did receive the answer. This violates the invariant written right below the delivery code: once delivery started, the turn's outcome is fixed. The path is reachable with transient errors: the QQ send throws `DeliveryError('RATE_LIMITED')` immediately on HTTP 429 by design (no retry), and the notice send goes through the same route. This was flagged during the review of #16404 and recorded as a follow-up item in #16441.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

The regression test reproduces the exact failure shape by making only the notice send throw (the answer send passes through):

1. `cd packages/channels/base && npx vitest run src/ChannelBase.test.ts -t 'keeps the turn completed when notice delivery fails'`
2. Without the production fix, the test fails: `Error: secret notice detail` bubbles out of `handleInbound` after the answer was delivered.
3. With the fix, the test passes: the turn emits `completed` (no `failed`), the sent messages contain only the answer, the error detail never appears in any user-visible message, and the failure is logged to stderr.
4. Full file for regressions: `npx vitest run src/ChannelBase.test.ts` → 795 passed.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before (test run against the unfixed code):

```
FAIL  src/ChannelBase.test.ts > ChannelBase > response delivery > keeps the turn completed when notice delivery fails
Error: secret notice detail
 ❯ src/ChannelBase.ts:7671:24   (the notice sendResponseMessage)
Tests  1 failed | 794 skipped (795)
```

After:

```
Tests  1 passed | 794 skipped (795)   (targeted test)
Tests  795 passed (795)               (full ChannelBase.test.ts)
```

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests only (`npx vitest run` inside `packages/channels/base` on macOS, Node 22); `npx eslint` and `npx tsc --noEmit` clean on both changed files.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: a failing notice is now dropped with only a stderr log. Deliberate: the notice is advisory, the answer is already delivered, and the alternative breaks the turn outcome for a message the user can do nothing about.
- Not validated / out of scope: the notice prefix-stripping logic, the notice content contract, and adapter-level 429 handling are untouched.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Refs #16441 (the recorded follow-up item this closes out). The regression was introduced by #16404.

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

当叠加技能（stacked-skill）的轮次提示（turn notice）投递失败时，现在只把失败写进 stderr 日志，轮次保持其已投递的结果。答案先送达用户；发不出去的提示不再把整个轮次改判为失败。

## 为什么需要

#16404 引入的轮次提示在答案之后发送，且位于守护投递的同一个 try 块内。提示发送一旦抛错，就会冒泡进 catch 分支：emit `failed`（`phase: 'delivery'`）并 rethrow，导致 `handleInbound` reject——一个已经送达答案的轮次被改判为失败，尽管用户其实已经收到了答案。这违反了紧挨着投递代码写下的不变量：一旦投递开始，轮次结果即固定。该路径可被瞬态错误命中：QQ 发送在 HTTP 429 时按设计立即抛 `DeliveryError('RATE_LIMITED')`（不重试），而提示发送走的正是同一条路径。此问题在 #16404 评审期间被发现，并作为后续事项记录在 #16441。

## 评审测试计划

### 如何验证

回归测试精确复现该失败形状：只让提示发送抛错（答案发送正常通过）：

1. `cd packages/channels/base && npx vitest run src/ChannelBase.test.ts -t 'keeps the turn completed when notice delivery fails'`
2. 不带生产端修复时，测试失败：`Error: secret notice detail` 在答案已送达后从 `handleInbound` 冒泡而出。
3. 带上修复后，测试通过：轮次 emit `completed`（无 `failed`）、已发送消息只含答案、错误细节不出现在任何用户可见通道、失败被记录到 stderr。
4. 全文件回归：`npx vitest run src/ChannelBase.test.ts` → 795 通过。

### 证据（修复前 & 修复后）

修复前（在未修复代码上运行该测试）：

```
FAIL  src/ChannelBase.test.ts > ChannelBase > response delivery > keeps the turn completed when notice delivery fails
Error: secret notice detail
 ❯ src/ChannelBase.ts:7671:24   （提示的 sendResponseMessage）
Tests  1 failed | 794 skipped (795)
```

修复后：

```
Tests  1 passed | 794 skipped (795)   （定向测试）
Tests  795 passed (795)               （ChannelBase.test.ts 全文件）
```

### 测试环境

|     操作系统     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

仅单元测试（macOS、Node 22，在 `packages/channels/base` 内 `npx vitest run`）；两个改动文件的 `npx eslint` 与 `npx tsc --noEmit` 均干净。

## 风险与范围

prs.title: fix(ci): recreate git metadata before the publish-triage checkout
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Closes a workspace-reuse gap in the `publish-triage` job and states its safety argument accurately. The job holds the triage lane's write PAT and may land on the persistent ECS pool, but it was the only job reaching `actions/checkout` on that pool without recreating the workspace `.git` first — an earlier agent run owned that workspace and could have planted git hooks/config that checkout's git commands would execute in the credential-bearing job. This adds the same `Recreate runner Git metadata` step the `triage`/`tmux-testing`/`verify` jobs run before their checkouts, and adds `publish-triage` to the `qwen-runner-checkout-workflow.test.js` matrix that behaviorally executes the step (broken-shallow recovery, symlinked `.git` not followed, idempotence). The job's header comment is rewritten to name the controls instead of certifying safety: it no longer claims "it is safe there" or "sole writer" (the triage job's reaction and lifecycle host steps also write with the PAT); it now says this job is the only path from the agent's drafts to GitHub. The design document pair is updated in both languages.

## Why it's needed

Found by the patrol closeout on this PR's first revision (yiliang114), which checked the rewritten comment's claims against the file instead of taking them on trust: the pool-safety claim was not backed by the workspace precautions the sibling jobs take, and the "sole writer" claim was factually false. The first is a real execution path for planted git metadata in the one job that holds the write PAT, introduced with `publish-triage` in #16468; the fix belongs here rather than in wording alone.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

1. In `.github/workflows/qwen-triage.yml`, confirm `publish-triage` now runs `Recreate runner Git metadata` (gated on `runner.environment == 'self-hosted'`, `rm -rf -- "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/.git"`) after the ownership restore and immediately before `Checkout the triage publisher scripts` — the same shape as the `triage` job's pair of steps.
2. Run `PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH" npx vitest run --config ./scripts/tests/vitest.config.ts scripts/tests/qwen-runner-checkout-workflow.test.js` — the new `qwen-triage / publish-triage` entry executes the step against a broken shallow boundary and a symlinked `.git` (17 entries total). Removal witness: deleting the step turns exactly that entry red (verified, byte-level restore).
3. Read the reworded header: no safety certification, no "sole writer"; the parenthetical acknowledges the triage job's own PAT-writing host steps.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — no user-visible surface. Local checks on `278a61e93e`: runner-checkout + workflow-size suites 255 passed / 1 skipped, `.github/scripts/qwen-triage-workflow.test.mjs` 130/130, CI budget holds (no job/timeout delta), YAML parses, prettier clean.

|  🍏 macOS  | N/A |
| 🪟 Windows | N/A |
|  🐧 Linux  | ✅ tested |

### Environment (optional)

N/A (static + behavioral shell tests only).

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the recreate step deletes the workspace `.git` on self-hosted runners before the sparse checkout re-creates it — identical to the three sibling jobs' long-standing behavior; hosted runs skip the step.
- Not validated / out of scope: the live publish-path observation checklist from #16468 continues unchanged; `publish-tmux` needs no such step (it never checks out).
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Follow-up to the patrol closeout on this PR and to #16468 (merged as `dd4515ca27`), which introduced `publish-triage`.

<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做什么

关闭 `publish-triage` job 的 workspace 复用缺口，并准确陈述其安全论据。该 job 持有 triage lane 的 write PAT 且可能落在持久 ECS 池上，但它是池上唯一不先重建 workspace `.git` 就执行 `actions/checkout` 的 job——早前的 agent run 拥有过该 workspace，可能种下 git hooks/config，被 checkout 的 git 命令在这个持凭据的 job 里执行。本 PR 补上与 `triage`/`tmux-testing`/`verify` job checkout 前相同的 `Recreate runner Git metadata` 步骤，并把 `publish-triage` 加入行为级执行该步骤的 `qwen-runner-checkout-workflow.test.js` 矩阵（broken-shallow 恢复、不跟随符号链接 `.git`、幂等）。job 头部注释改为列举控制而非认证安全：不再声称「it is safe there」与「sole writer」（triage job 的 reaction 与 lifecycle 宿主步骤也用 PAT 写入），改为「该 job 是 agent drafts 到达 GitHub 的唯一路径」。设计文档对双语同步更新。

prs.title: fix(ci): report main CI runs a job timeout cancelled
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The main-CI failure tracker now also reports a run GitHub concluded `cancelled`, after separating a job-timeout cancellation from a concurrency supersede by the job annotation. A timed-out run gets rerun whole instead of one-for-one, and the report names the cancelled job and step and says why the run ended.

## Why it's needed

The gate in `main-ci-failure-issue.yml` only admitted `conclusion == 'failure'`. A job that hits its `timeout-minutes` cap caps the whole run as cancelled with no failing job anywhere in it, so that class of breakage produced no report at all — which is how the E2E `sandbox:docker` shard sat red for weeks (#16214). Roughly half of that day's main E2E runs ended cancelled and only the failure-conclusion ones were ever looked at.

The two ways a run ends cancelled need opposite treatment. A concurrency supersede is replaced by the run that cancelled it and owns nothing, so reporting it would file an issue per supersede. A timeout is a real breakage whose only trace is this event. The job annotation tells them apart: only a timeout carries "The job has exceeded the maximum execution time". Reads fail open like every other one in that step, and the repeating dedupe marker bounds a misclassified supersede to one comment.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Run the two touched suites:

```
npx vitest run scripts/tests/main-ci-failure-issue-workflow.test.js
node --test .github/scripts/ci/main-failure-signature.test.mjs
```

Then confirm the classification against a run that actually timed out. Run 41743539611 is the one this issue was split from: its `E2E Test (Linux) - sandbox:docker - shard 1/1` job was cancelled at 01:14 after the full 60 minutes.

```
gh api "repos/QwenLM/qwen-code/check-runs/<id>/annotations" --jq '.[].message'
```

Expected: `The job has exceeded the maximum execution time of 1h0m0s`, which is what `cancellation_kind=timeout` selects on. A cancelled run without that annotation (a supersede) selects `superseded=true` and reports nothing.

### Evidence (Before & After)

N/A — CI workflow change, not user-visible.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   N/A  |
|  🐧 Linux  |   N/A  |

### Environment (optional)

N/A — unit tests only; no workflow run was executed.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the annotation read is one API call per cancelled job, bounded by the cancelled jobs in that run. A cancelled run whose annotations cannot be read is reported rather than dropped — a misclassified supersede costs one comment, a dropped timeout costs the regression, which is the direction the existing fail-open reads already take. A timed-out run's whole-run rerun counts as attempt 2 and the next repeat as attempt 3, so an occurrence spends two full matrix reruns before the first report files; that is deliberate, and it is what lets a lane that died on a transient stall clear itself without a human.
- Not validated / out of scope: the workflow itself was not executed end to end. The annotation classification was verified against real cancelled runs through the same commands the step runs, but the rerun, dispatch gates and issue rendering were exercised only by the suite's stubs.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #16272

<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 这个 PR 做了什么

主 CI 失败追踪现在也会上报 GitHub 结论为 `cancelled` 的运行，并通过 job annotation 区分「超时取消」与「并发取消」。超时的运行改为整轮重跑而不是只重跑失败 job；报告会写明被取消的 job 和步骤，并说明运行为什么结束。

## 为什么需要

`main-ci-failure-issue.yml` 的门条件只接受 `conclusion == 'failure'`。job 撞到 `timeout-minutes` 上限时，整个运行会被标记为 cancelled，而其中没有任何失败的 job，于是这一类故障完全不会产生报告——E2E 的 `sandbox:docker` shard 就是这样红了数周（#16214）。当天 main 上的 E2E 运行约有一半以 cancelled 结束，而只有结论为 failure 的那些被看过。

两种 cancelled 需要相反的处理方式。并发取消会被取消它的那次运行取代、本身不拥有结果，上报它等于每取消一次就开一个 issue；超时则是真实故障，这个事件是它唯一的痕迹。两者的区别在 job annotation 上：只有超时带有 "The job has exceeded the maximum execution time"。读取失败时按开放处理，与该步骤其它读取一致；重复的 dedupe marker 会把误判为超时的并发取消收敛到一条评论。

## 审阅者验证方式

跑两个受影响的测试套件：

```
npx vitest run scripts/tests/main-ci-failure-issue-workflow.test.js
node --test .github/scripts/ci/main-ci-failure-signature.test.mjs
```

再用真实超时的运行确认分类。run 41743539611 就是这个 issue 拆分来源：它的 `E2E Test (Linux) - sandbox:docker - shard 1/1` 跑满 60 分钟后于 01:14 被取消。

```
gh api "repos/QwenLM/qwen-code/check-runs/<id>/annotations" --jq '.[].message'
```

预期输出 `The job has exceeded the maximum execution time of 1h0m0s`，这正是 `cancellation_kind=timeout` 的判据。不带该 annotation 的 cancelled 运行（并发取消）会得到 `superseded=true`，不上报。

### 证据（前后对比）

N/A —— CI workflow 改动，非用户可见。

### 测试环境

|     OS     | 状态 |
| :--------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS  |  ✅  |
| 🪟 Windows |  N/A |
|  🐧 Linux  |  N/A |

### 环境（可选）

N/A —— 仅单元测试，未实际执行 workflow。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险：annotation 读取按被取消的 job 数量增加 API 调用，上限由该运行的 cancelled job 数决定。读不到 annotation 的 cancelled 运行会选择上报而不是丢弃——误判的并发取消只多一条评论，漏掉的超时则丢掉整个回归，这与此处既有读取的 fail-open 方向一致。超时运行的整轮重跑算作新的运行，因此重复超时会转而 filing 而不是无限重跑，这是有意为之。
- 未验证 / 超出范围：workflow 未端到端执行。annotation 分类用与步骤相同的命令对真实 cancelled 运行验证过，但重跑、调度门和 issue 渲染只由测试套件的桩覆盖。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。

## 关联 issue

Fixes #16272

</details>

prs.title: fix(core): name the model and setting in media refusals
prs.body:
## What this PR does

When a model cannot accept an image, audio, or video file, Qwen Code refuses it with a message the model then reads. That message named neither the model nor the setting behind the refusal, and it read identically whether the input modalities were guessed from the model name or declared by the user. In both cases it ended by pointing at skills, which is the wrong direction when the real cause is a configuration value.

The refusal now leads with the model id and states how the modalities were resolved. A value inferred from the model name tells the caller to declare `generationConfig.modalities` on the provider entry. A value the user declared points at where it was declared instead. The rest of the guidance — that `read_file` cannot process the file either, and the skills fallback — is unchanged, as is the separate PDF wording that suggests installing the document-skills extension.

## Why it's needed

Reported in #16178. A provider-backed model with image input configured was refused, and the message sent the reporter down a resize-image path; the setting had been right all along and the resolved route genuinely had no image modality. The message was accurate about the state but not actionable, because the one fact that would have separated "you configured this wrong" from "we guessed wrong from the name" was already computed and then discarded.

The resolved configuration already tracks where each field came from, so the distinction costs no new resolution logic. The source kind is carried on the request context for the API-time path; the read_file path reads it directly. It is deliberately withheld when the generator is serving a model other than the configuration's primary one, so a sub-agent or side query cannot inherit the primary model's attribution and report a setting the user never set for it.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Configure an OpenAI-compatible provider entry whose model id matches no known family pattern, without `generationConfig.modalities`, then ask the agent to read a PNG. The refusal should name that model id and say the modalities were inferred from the model name, with the exact JSON key to add.

Then add `"modalities": { "image": true }` to that entry and repeat: the image is read instead of refused, which confirms the advice points at the field that actually decides the outcome.

A model whose id does match a known vision pattern, with image modality left on, should still read images normally — the new text only replaces a refusal.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before and after are the text the model receives. Captured from the real read_file path and the real request-building pipeline, with a 1x1 PNG on disk and modalities resolving empty:

Before (both cases identical):

```
[Unsupported image file: "image.png". This model does not support image input. The read_file tool cannot process this type of file either. ...]
```

After, modalities guessed from the model name:

```
[Unsupported image file: "image.png". Model 'my-custom-openai-id' does not support image input: its input modalities were inferred from the model name. Declare "generationConfig": { "modalities": { "image": true } } on this provider entry to enable it. The read_file tool cannot process this type of file either. ...]
```

After, modalities declared on the provider entry without image:

```
[Unsupported image file: "image.png". Model 'my-custom-openai-id' does not support image input: this provider entry's "generationConfig.modalities" is set without image. Check it and re-select the model with /model. The read_file tool cannot process this type of file either. ...]
```

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ⚠️   |
| 🪟 Windows |   N/A  |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ✅   |

Unit tests, type checking, lint, and formatting were all run inside a `node:22-bookworm` Linux container against the merged base. The macOS column is ⚠️ rather than ✅: the same suite also passes there, but the bundle build needed for the full CLI integration harness does not complete on this machine's container filesystem, so the end-to-end evidence above was produced from the source-level pipeline rather than a bundled CLI run. Nothing in this change is platform-specific.

### Environment (optional)

Unit tests and type checking in a Linux container; no sandbox, no live model endpoint.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the refusal text is what the model reads, so changed wording can shift model behaviour around file handling. The leading clause keeps the substring previous assertions and any model familiarity rely on, and the advice is additive.
- Not validated / out of scope: the reporter's original observation that the setting appeared to need a restart is not addressed here. The modalities are re-resolved on auth refresh and on `/model`, so the hint says "re-select the model with /model" rather than claiming a restart is required; whether their hot-reload path was misbehaving is a separate question left open on the issue.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. The new request-context field is optional and nothing else reads the message text.

## Linked Issues

Fixes #16178


<details>
<summary>中文说明</summary>

## 本 PR 做了什么

当某个模型无法接受图片、音频或视频文件时，Qwen Code 会拒绝它，并给出一条由模型读取的说明。这条说明既没有点名模型，也没有指出拒绝背后的设置，而且无论输入模态是从模型名推断出来的、还是用户显式声明的，读起来都一模一样。两种情况下它还都以指向 skills 收尾，而当真正的原因是某个配置值时，这个方向是错的。

现在这条拒绝信息以模型 id 开头，并说明模态是如何解析出来的。从模型名推断出的值会提示调用方在 provider 条目上声明 `generationConfig.modalities`；用户显式声明的值则改为指出它声明在哪里。其余指引——`read_file` 同样无法处理该文件，以及 skills 兜底——保持不变；PDF 的单独措辞（建议安装 document-skills 扩展）也不变。

## 为什么需要

见 #16178。一个配置了图片输入的 provider 模型被拒绝，而这条信息把报告者引向了一条「压缩图片」的路径；其实那个设置一直是对的，解析出的路由确实没有图片模态。这条信息对状态的描述是准确的，但不可操作，因为那个本可以区分「你配置错了」和「我们从名字猜错了」的关键事实早已被算出，却又被丢弃了。

解析后的配置本就记录了每个字段来自哪里，因此这个区分不需要新的解析逻辑。来源种类会随请求上下文带到 API 时路径上；read_file 路径则直接读取它。当生成器服务的不是配置中的主模型时，它会刻意被 withhold，这样某个子代理或侧查询就不会继承主模型的归因，去报告一个用户从没为它设过的设置。

## 审阅者验证方式

### 如何验证

配置一个 OpenAI 兼容的 provider 条目，其模型 id 不匹配任何已知的家族模式，且不写 `generationConfig.modalities`，然后让代理读取一个 PNG。拒绝信息应当点名该模型 id，说明模态是从模型名推断的，并给出要添加的确切 JSON 键。

接着给该条目加上 `"modalities": { "image": true }` 再重复一次：图片会被读取而不是被拒绝，这就确认了提示指向的是真正决定结果的字段。

一个 id 确实匹配已知视觉模式的模型，在图态保持开启时，应当仍然正常读取图片——新文案只替换拒绝信息。

### 证据（修改前后）

修改前后指的都是模型收到的文本。取自真实的 read_file 路径与真实的请求构建流水线，磁盘上放一张 1x1 的 PNG，模态解析为空：

修改前（两种情况完全相同）：

```
[Unsupported image file: "image.png". This model does not support image input. The read_file tool cannot process this type of file either. ...]
```

修改后，模态从模型名推断：

```
[Unsupported image file: "image.png". Model 'my-custom-openai-id' does not support image input: its input modalities were inferred from the model name. Declare "generationConfig": { "modalities": { "image": true } } on this provider entry to enable it. The read_file tool cannot process this type of file either. ...]
```

修改后，provider 条目声明了模态但不含图片：

```
[Unsupported image file: "image.png". Model 'my-custom-openai-id' does not support image input: this provider entry's "generationConfig.modalities" is set without image. Check it and re-select the model with /model. The read_file tool cannot process this type of file either. ...]
```

### 测试环境

|    操作系统    | 状态 |
| :------------: | :--: |
|  🍏 macOS      |  ⚠️  |
| 🪟 Windows     |  N/A |
|  🐧 Linux      |  ✅  |

单元测试、类型检查、lint 与格式化都在 `node:22-bookworm` Linux 容器中对合并后的基线运行。macOS 一栏是 ⚠️ 而非 ✅：同一套测试在该平台也通过，但完整 CLI 集成测试所需的 bundle 构建在本机的容器文件系统上无法完成，因此上面的端到端证据来自源码级流水线，而不是打包后的 CLI 运行。本改动没有任何平台相关的部分。

### 环境（可选）

Linux 容器中的单元测试与类型检查；无 sandbox，无真实模型端点。

## 风险与范围

- 主要风险或取舍：拒绝文案是模型读取的内容，措辞变化可能影响模型在文件处理上的行为。开头子句保留了既有断言和模型熟悉度所依赖的子串，新增建议是追加式的。
- 未验证 / 超出范围：报告者最初的观察——该设置似乎需要重启——没有在本 PR 中处理。模态会在鉴权刷新与 `/model` 时重新解析，因此提示说的是「用 /model 重新选择模型」，而不是声称需要重启；他们的热重载路径是否异常是另一个问题，留在 issue 中。
- 破坏性变更 / 迁移说明：无。新增的请求上下文字段是可选的，也没有其他地方读取消息文本。

## 关联 issue

Fixes #16178

prs.title: feat(web-shell): surface task Q&A activity above the composer
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Adds a waiting card to the main Web Shell composer. A compact heatmap button at the end of the streaming status row opens a card whose primary purpose is to surface the current task's Q&A activity over time. The activity view is a fixed 44-week daily calendar (44 columns × 7 rows) where columns are Monday-to-Sunday weeks and each cell is one local day; the calendar ends with the current week, future days are empty placeholders, cell color shows that day's Q&A count, month labels sit below the grid, hovering a day shows its date and count, and clicking a populated day scrolls the transcript to the first Q&A of that day and highlights the message. An Activity / Usage switch shows the task's total, input, output, cached and context tokens instead of a credits balance. The header, tab row, body and footer keep a fixed frame across the activity, usage, intro and game views, so switching does not resize the card. When the configuration-gated waiting games entry is enabled, a white square with a dark gamepad icon appears after five seconds on a random cold day; clicking it starts horizontal Tetris or Snake at random, with a QWEN CODE pixel intro first (Tetris blocks fly to the right edge and settle into the random start cluster, while Snake keeps its intro static). Best scores and the sound preference stay in `localStorage`. The card closes when the turn ends, renders only on the main composer, and is hidden on coarse-pointer devices. The activity and token summaries are framework-free (`utils/waitingActivity.ts`), as are the Tetris (`utils/waitingMinigame.ts`) and Snake (`utils/waitingSnake.ts`) engines.

### Configuration

The activity and usage views are always available. The game entry is off by default and can be enabled with any of: `?waitingGames=1` on the Web Shell URL (`?waitingGames=0` forces it off), `localStorage['qwen-code-web-shell-waiting-games'] = '1'`, or a host-injected `window.__QWEN_CODE_WAITING_GAMES__ = true`. Without that configuration, the gamepad entry and all game controls stay out of the card.

## Why it's needed

A long turn currently shows only a spinner, elapsed time, token count and a rotating phrase. The card gives the wait a useful reading state (Q&A activity and token usage) and a way back into the transcript, without leaving the conversation or hijacking typing. The game is an optional waiting-time extra behind configuration, not the default experience.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Open the Web Shell, send a prompt, and look for the heatmap button at the end of the streaming status row. Clicking it opens the activity calendar; hover a populated day to see its date and count, click one to jump to that day's first Q&A, switch to Usage to see the token breakdown, and confirm the card frame does not resize between views. With the game configuration enabled, wait five seconds for the gamepad square on a cold day, click it to play the intro and then Tetris or Snake, and confirm Escape (or the card's collapse control) closes the card. End the turn and the card disappears. From `packages/web-shell`:

```sh
../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run client/utils/waitingActivity.test.ts client/utils/waitingSnake.test.ts client/utils/waitingMinigame.test.ts client/utils/waitingGamesConfig.test.ts client/components/WaitingMinigame.test.tsx client/i18n.test.ts
# 71 passed

../../node_modules/.bin/vitest run client/App.test.tsx
# 1363 passed

../../node_modules/.bin/tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit
../../node_modules/.bin/playwright test --config playwright.config.ts --project=chromium client/e2e/waiting-minigame.spec.ts
# 5 passed
```

ESLint and Prettier pass for the changed files. A local UI harness needs no daemon: run `npm run dev -- --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5173` and open `http://127.0.0.1:5173/e2e/waiting-minigame-harness.html`. The harness provides synthetic daily activity and token data, theme and language switches, a `Games: off/on` toggle (off by default, matching the product), an entry-delay toggle and a `Next game` selector for Tetris/Snake.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before (base `main`): the composer status row shows only the spinner, phrase, elapsed time, token count and cancel hint, with no waiting card or entry point. After (this revision): a heatmap button at the end of the row opens the activity calendar, the usage view, and the optional game views below.

| Activity heatmap with hover details | QWEN CODE intro |
| --- | --- |
| ![Activity](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/samuelhsin/qwen-code/feat/dac-waiting-minigame/docs/design/waiting-minigame/waiting-minigame-heatmap-tooltip.png) | ![Intro](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/samuelhsin/qwen-code/feat/dac-waiting-minigame/docs/design/waiting-minigame/waiting-minigame-intro.png) |

| Blocks flying to the right cluster | Settled start cluster |
| --- | --- |
| ![Flight](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/samuelhsin/qwen-code/feat/dac-waiting-minigame/docs/design/waiting-minigame/waiting-minigame-flight.png) | ![Landed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/samuelhsin/qwen-code/feat/dac-waiting-minigame/docs/design/waiting-minigame/waiting-minigame-landed.png) |

| Tetris | Snake with an apple |
| --- | --- |
| ![Tetris](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/samuelhsin/qwen-code/feat/dac-waiting-minigame/docs/design/waiting-minigame/waiting-minigame-board.png) | ![Snake](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/samuelhsin/qwen-code/feat/dac-waiting-minigame/docs/design/waiting-minigame/waiting-minigame-snake.png) |

| Token usage (sample) | Dark theme, Chinese heatmap |
| --- | --- |
| ![Usage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/samuelhsin/qwen-code/feat/dac-waiting-minigame/docs/design/waiting-minigame/waiting-minigame-tokens.png) | ![Dark Chinese](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/samuelhsin/qwen-code/feat/dac-waiting-minigame/docs/design/waiting-minigame/waiting-minigame-dark-zh-heatmap.png) |

| Configured game entry on a cold day |
| --- |
| ![Game entry](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/samuelhsin/qwen-code/feat/dac-waiting-minigame/docs/design/waiting-minigame/waiting-minigame-game-entry.png) |

The activity, usage and dark-theme screenshots use the local harness sample data with the game entry off. The game-entry frame uses the local harness with `?waitingGames=1`. The intro and game frames use the Chromium E2E (`packages/web-shell/client/e2e/waiting-minigame.spec.ts`) with the game entry enabled.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   N/A  |
|  🐧 Linux  |   N/A  |

### Environment (optional)

Local macOS run through `npm run dev` in `packages/web-shell` with the browser harness and the Playwright mock daemon (no real backend); CI covers Linux.

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the card expands in normal flow inside the composer footer, so opening it temporarily resizes the transcript instead of overlaying it; the game entry is off by default and only renders behind explicit configuration, so third-party hosts must opt in.
- Not validated / out of scope: split and side-task panes, touch controls, a real daemon beyond the mock harness, Firefox/WebKit, Android WebView, sound output, and per-commit attribution are not covered by this round; an intermittent ~36 px composer shift when starting a game was observed in external verification and the root cause is not isolated; the host-level opt-out for third-party hosts remains an open design-doc question.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: none. No new dependencies, and no daemon route, transcript, telemetry or host prop changes beyond the optional configuration reads; best scores and the sound preference keep their existing `localStorage` keys.

Design notes: [English](https://github.com/samuelhsin/qwen-code/blob/feat/dac-waiting-minigame/docs/design/2026-11-01-web-shell-waiting-minigame.md) · [简体中文](https://github.com/samuelhsin/qwen-code/blob/feat/dac-waiting-minigame/docs/design/2026-11-01-web-shell-waiting-minigame.zh-CN.md)

## Linked Issues

Closes #16036.

* feat(web-shell): add a waiting minigame to the composer

Show a dismissible horizontal-Tetris strip above the main composer while a
prompt is streaming. The game closes when the turn ends, ignores editor
keyboard targets, and stays out of split panes and coarse-pointer devices.

Add engine and component tests, EN/ZH copy, design docs with page
screenshots, and a Chromium E2E scenario.

Refs #16036

* docs(web-shell): point the waiting minigame design at the committed E2E spec

* fix(web-shell): move the waiting minigame trigger into the status line

Replace the full-width waiting strip with a compact gamepad button at the
end of the streaming status row. The main composer now owns the open
state, and the board mounts above the status row only while open.

Keep the game's window keydown listener stable through a ref so rerenders
cannot drop the Escape that collapses the board, and update the component
tests, E2E scenario, screenshots, and both design docs.

* fix(web-shell): keep the waiting minigame scoped and recoverable

Pause and resume correctly after the tab is hidden, scope game keys to
the focused card so Escape no longer arms stream cancellation, let
focused buttons keep Space, restore the sound toggle, and keep the
board grid out of the aria-hidden wrapper that also held the overlays.

* fix(web-shell): keep the waiting minigame recoverable and scoped

Resume gravity after the tab becomes visible again, create the audio
context when sound is enabled, let the card's own buttons keep
Space/Enter, leave Escape to open dialogs, and keep the restart button
out of the aria-hidden board. The main composer now lets the open game
own Escape so the first press collapses it without arming stream cancel.

* feat(web-shell): add a waiting card with activity, usage and games

Open a waiting card from the streaming status button. The card starts on the
task's 44-bucket Q&A activity heatmap, switches to token usage instead of a
credits balance, and places a Qwen mark that opens a Tetris/Snake picker.
Games share the 44x7 grid and offer back-to-activity and switch-game actions.

Add the activity and Snake engines, component and E2E coverage, a local
harness with sample data, and design docs with page screenshots.

Refs #16036

* feat(web-shell): refine waiting card activity and game intros

Add hover details and click-to-locate to the activity heatmap, start a
random game from a delayed cold-cell Qwen entry, and play a QWEN CODE
intro that flies the blocks into the Tetris start cluster. Snake keeps
its intro static, eats an apple emoji, and starts at a slower speed.

* feat(web-shell): show task activity in a daily calendar

Replace the task-span buckets with a fixed 44-week day calendar, including
month labels, per-day hover details, click-to-locate and a stable card frame
across activity, usage, intro and game views. Gate the Qwen game entry behind
the waiting games configuration so the activity card stays the default
experience.

* fix(web-shell): show a gamepad icon on the configured game entry

Replace the Qwen brand mark in the calendar's game entry with a gamepad
icon, remove the now-unused Qwen logo component, and let the local harness
read the waiting games config so ?waitingGames=1 opens the preview with the
entry visible. Game screenshots and docs now describe the gamepad mark.

* fix(web-shell): read cached tokens from the connection fallback

The usage card falls back to the connection's token usage before any
assistant usage frame arrives, but the fallback read the message-level
cachedTokens field while the connection object carries cachedReadTokens.
Accept both names and pin the connection shape in the unit test.

* fix(web-shell): keep the game entry hit area inside its cell

Give the calendar game entry a positioning context so its forgiving hit
area stays bounded when prefers-reduced-motion disables the intro
animation and removes the transform that used to establish it. Cover the
reduced-motion path with an E2E that hovers and clicks a day while the
entry is visible.

Also reuse one Intl formatter pair per locale, format task token totals
above 1M as M, and drop the unused no-activity copy.

prs.title: fix(core): bound the project directory name to one path component
prs.body:
## What this PR does

The directory a project's sessions are stored under is derived by flattening the whole absolute project path into a single path component. That flattening only replaces non-alphanumeric characters, so it never shortens anything: for a project path deep enough to flatten past the filesystem's per-component limit, the resulting directory can never be created.

A session directory that cannot be created fails quietly. The command still exits successfully with a normal result and a session id, but no transcript is written; listing sessions from the same directory then fails with `ENAMETOOLONG`. A working directory the host filesystem accepts is enough to reach this state — every individual component of the reproduction path is only 50 characters.

This bounds the generated identifier to a single component: identifiers that already fit keep their existing spelling byte for byte, so no current session moves, and only an identifier that would not fit is shortened to a readable prefix plus part of the project path's hash. The hash keeps two long paths from colliding on the shared prefix and keeps the name stable across runs.

## Why it's needed

Session recording, listing, and resuming are core user-visible behavior, and today they break for a valid working directory with no in-product recovery path. The existing temp-directory layout already avoids this by keying on the project hash; the sessions directory did not.

This is a focused fix rather than a design change: it does not introduce a new identifier format for short paths, so nothing needs migrating, and it does not claim to repair sessions whose directories were already never created.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

Reproduce the original failure on a filesystem with a 255-byte component limit (any APFS/ext4/NTFS host):

1. Build a directory whose components are all individually valid but whose flattened path exceeds 255 bytes, e.g. five 50-character components under a temp root.
2. Confirm the identifier the storage layer generates for it, then try to create that directory — it fails with `File name too long` (errno 63).
3. With this change, the generated directory name is at most 255 bytes, is created successfully, and a transcript written into it can be listed back.

The added unit tests pin the same properties without touching the disk: a short project keeps its existing identifier unchanged, an over-long one is bounded to 255 bytes, contains the hash suffix, retains a readable prefix, is stable across calls, and two different long paths resolve to different directories.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Original failure observed on macOS while validating this change:

```
path bytes: 268
old identifier bytes: 268
old-style mkdir FAILED: OSError 63 File name too long
new identifier bytes: 255
new-style listing: ['probe.jsonl']
```

Red-then-green for the new bound test: with the original `getProjectDir()`, the test fails with `expected 319 to be less than or equal to 255`; with the change it passes.

### Tested on

|     OS     | Status |
| :--------: | :----: |
|  🍏 macOS  |   ✅   |
| 🪟 Windows |   ⚠️   |
|  🐧 Linux  |   ⚠️   |

## Test plan

- `npx vitest run src/config/storage.test.ts src/services/sessionService.test.ts` — 373 passed.
- `npx vitest run src/memory/ src/services/chatRecordingService.test.ts` — passed; one recall-latency timing test flaked under the combined run and passes on its own.
- `npx prettier --check` and `npx eslint` on the changed files — clean.
- `npx tsc -p packages/core/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — no errors in the changed files; the run reports pre-existing errors in unrelated files under this worktree's shared dependency tree.
- Not run: the full monorepo build, integration suites, and the Windows/Linux filesystem limits from this host.

Fixes #15412
