prs.title: feat(managed-agent): enable external workspace execution
prs.body:
## What this PR does

Builds the external Workspace execution slice on top of the materialization prerequisite in #15654. The branch now includes live `hosted-workspace-external-files/1` admission, bounded and single-query Workspace discovery, authoritative registration checks, stable lifecycle refusal classification, and receipt-backed release for external Runtime bindings. The separate materialization operation still creates metadata only; it does not allocate storage or start a worker.

This revision closes the remaining review gaps in that execution slice: registration decode failures, including field-type failures, now resolve to a permanent `409 workspace_unavailable`; a malformed registration disables only its own Workspace during batch discovery; saved-provider shutdown is classified as retryable `503`; attachment actor lookup fails closed on zero, multiple, or null rows; and external lifecycle authorization preserves the exact permanent fence response.

## Why it's needed

#15512 needs a durable link from registered external storage to a Workspace that can be discovered and used safely. A Session must not become executable through a partially wired path, and one corrupt storage row must not hide every healthy Workspace on the page. The same branch also needs terminal close and recovery paths to distinguish permanent identity failures from provider availability failures.

## Reviewer Test Plan

### How to verify

On an isolated fresh catalog, register external storage using the loopback operator credential, materialize its alias with an owner, and verify that only the owner can discover it. Exercise Session creation after the external-files gates and a Harness lifecycle capability are available. Confirm that prompts can run, file tools remain within the external profile, and close/recovery uses the receipt-backed ownership transition without destroying a shared placement.

For the query and failure paths, corrupt one registration and confirm only that Workspace loses Session-creation eligibility while another Workspace remains visible. Confirm that an admission attempt against the corrupted Workspace returns `409 workspace_unavailable` with `retryable=false`. Shut down the saved external provider during drain-capability checks and confirm a retryable `503`. Submit a non-current lifecycle authority to the external attachment path and confirm `409 workspace_lifecycle_claim_fenced` with `retryable=false`.

### Evidence (Before & After)

Before this revision, a field-type error while decoding an opaque-persisted registration could escape as a mapper failure, batch discovery could fail as a whole when one row was malformed, and a shut-down saved provider was conflated with a permanent binding conflict. The candidate maps these cases explicitly, uses one registration batch read rather than per-row JDBC work inside a mapper, and keeps external lifecycle fences non-retryable.

Earlier evidence in this stack covered materialization, registration replay, and isolated MySQL validation. The newest commit was checked statically and through the repository's CI gates; no local test, build, or typecheck was run under the requested execution policy.

### Tested on

| OS | Status |
| :--- | :---: |
| macOS | ✅ static review and `git diff --check`; no heavy local execution |
| Windows | ⚠️ not tested |
| Linux | ✅ repository CI for the branch; the new head is checked again after push |

## Risk & Scope

- Main risk or tradeoff: the authenticated operator delegates the Workspace owner. That field is a grant target, not authenticated user identity. Existing operator and tenant checks remain required.
- Batch discovery now fails closed per malformed storage row instead of failing the whole Workspace page. A failed SQL read remains a retryable provider-unavailable verdict.
- `workspace_lifecycle_claim_fenced` remains permanent. Do not reinterpret a stale or non-current authority as a transient outage.
- Full external Hosted shell/capture, attachment widening beyond the current profile, and the Resident shared-worker behavior remain outside this PR. #16023 carries the Resident and EPHEMERAL layers.
- Breaking changes / migration notes: the preceding stack extends the shared V1 catalog under the repository's pre-release fresh-catalog policy. No V2 migration is introduced here.

Design: [English](docs/design/2026-10-25-external-hosted-workspace.md) · [简体中文](docs/design/2026-10-25-external-hosted-workspace.zh-CN.md).

## Linked Issues

Part of #15512. Related prerequisite: #15654. The Resident shared-worker increment is stacked in #16023 and must not merge before this PR.

releases.name: Release v0.26.9
releases.body:
<!-- qwen-release-notes:v2 -->

## Highlights

_See the complete change list below._

## Breaking Changes

No known breaking changes.

## Skill installation and activation

Skill ZIP uploads, daemon APIs, TypeScript SDK support, bulk activation, and recovery protections make installing and managing Skills more reliable.

- Adds PUT /skills/activation and setUserSkillsActivation to enable or disable 1-100 user Skills in one request, with saved preferences and propagation status. ([#16186](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16186))
- Prepares Skill installation for larger archives by adding disk-based ZIP handling and recovery-backup protection to the installer. ([#16421](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16421))
- Adds daemon API routes for installing large Skill ZIPs by upload or host file path and querying installation receipts after failures. ([#16422](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16422))
- Adds TypeScript SDK support for installing Skill ZIPs from File, Blob, bytes, or host path, with attempt IDs and receipt lookup. ([#16423](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16423))
- WebShell can now upload Skill ZIP archives from the Skills page, show daemon limits, and check uncertain installation results. ([#16424](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16424))

## Web Shell sessions and composer

Web Shell session titles, Add menu polish, draft preservation, batch deletion, and listSessions pagination fixes improve everyday session management.

- Keeps Web Shell sidebar session titles visible when a transcript is rebuilt, preventing session names from disappearing. ([#16299](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16299))
- Polishes the Web Shell composer Add menu with consistent icons, labels, descriptions, spacing, and improved accessibility for actions and Plan state. ([#16181](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16181))
  ![Main menu](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/d37bb0579f3c6b212c2a18d76acc59af920279fb/composer-menu-16155/before-dark.png)
  ![Updated production-package menu](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ytahdn/qwen-code/d37bb0579f3c6b212c2a18d76acc59af920279fb/composer-menu-16155/after-dark.png)
- WebShell now preserves unsent drafts when ArrowUp or ArrowDown moves through wrapped prompt lines before history navigation. ([#14909](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14909))
- web-shell: batch session deletions at the route limit ([#14637](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14637))
  ![Before bulk deletion](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jianyx1/qwen-code/82199691bd3c0e8908df82bbaf5d38a98fb44143/before.png)
  ![After bulk deletion](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jianyx1/qwen-code/82199691bd3c0e8908df82bbaf5d38a98fb44143/after.png)
- listSessions pagination no longer skips sessions when multiple session files share the same modification time. ([#16024](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16024))

## Managed agents and sessions

Managed agent automation, durable questions, activation renewals, writer recovery, and history caching improve hosted session reliability and speed.

- managed-agent: support durable structured user questions ([#16433](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16433))
- managed-agent: enable automation by default ([#16448](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16448))
- Managed agent activation renewals now locate the activation lease more efficiently, reducing renewal lookup overhead. ([#16336](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16336))
- Improves managed-agent performance by removing tenant guard locks from native journal snapshot publication. ([#16410](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16410))
- Managed Session history rebuilds now cache message bodies per process, reducing repeated reads and improving performance for hosted turns. ([#16337](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16337))
- HTTP Managed Session writer recovery now keeps a live in-flight renewal grant instead of unnecessarily re-acquiring the writer. ([#16287](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16287))

## GitHub PR automation

Sandboxed /verify can read PR review threads, /autofix-pr refusals expose machine-readable codes, and GitHub inbound recovery retries failed reads.

- The sandboxed /verify round can now see PR review threads, including resolved and outdated threads, so reviewer findings are available during verification. ([#16300](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16300))
- /autofix-pr helper refusals now include a machine-readable refused code and next step on stderr, making failures easier to handle. ([#16238](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16238))
- GitHub inbound recovery now retries after a failed read instead of stopping, so recovered tasks run once the task store becomes readable. ([#16402](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16402))

## Model and provider support

Image input fixes for Llama, LLaVA, Pixtral, Mistral Small, and Qwen VL models plus OCI Generative AI documentation broaden provider coverage.

- Enables image input for Llama 3.2 Vision, Llama 4, LLaVA, Pixtral, and Mistral Small 3.1 and 3.2 models. ([#16311](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16311))
- core: accept images for Qwen VL models under their Ollama names ([#16309](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16309))
- providers: document OCI Generative AI under OpenAI-compatible providers ([#16345](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16345))

## Channels and messaging

QQ proactive delivery and richer Channel event timeline recording improve active group messaging, delivery tracking, and scan health visibility.

- Enables QQ proactive delivery so loop messages, webhook tasks, background responses, and daemon sends can be sent as active group messages. ([#15635](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15635))
- Channel event timeline now records private bound-session deliveries, undelivered events, and scan health outcomes. ([#16237](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16237))

## CLI and terminal status

Interactive CLI reports working, blocked, done, or error status via OSC 7501, while experimental.unifiedAgentLoop helps Ink TUI finish tool batches.

- The interactive CLI now reports working, blocked, done, or error status to terminals using OSC 7501 with app=qwen-code. ([#16407](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16407))
- With experimental.unifiedAgentLoop enabled, Ink TUI turns await their shared tool batch so tool continuations complete within the turn. ([#16385](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16385))

## Daemon, runtime, and account recovery

Faster SSH registration and MCP startup, reduced tool-execution locking, bounded daemon replay memory, and subscription recovery improve platform stability.

- SSH registration settlement and Session worktree preparation are less serialized, allowing more concurrent Runtime work and faster workspace preparation. ([#16386](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16386))
- Loads MCP client Google auth providers on demand to reduce startup load while keeping configured server behavior unchanged. ([#16242](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16242))
- Improves ordinary session tool execution performance by reducing unnecessary locking during admission and dispatch. ([#16415](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16415))
- Daemon command and skill replay now limits snapshot memory with an 8 MiB per-session ring, configurable via --event-ring-max-bytes. ([#16413](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16413))
- subscription: isolate activation and restore sign-in recovery ([#16453](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16453))

## Other Changes

- Internal test coverage for renewal recovery and writer seal handling was hardened without changing production behavior. ([#14482](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14482))
- Consolidates Web Shell sidebar test scaffolding onto a shared sidebarHarness without changing user-visible behavior. ([#16016](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16016))
- Adds a design proposal for moving PR state transition detection from GitHub channel polling to the daemon PR refresh timer. ([#16246](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16246))
- Shortens the stale PR policy to mark pull requests stale after 30 inactive days and close them after 14 more days, with a larger sweep budget. ([#16435](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16435))
- Fixes release Docker integration builds to use the same apt-mirror probe as E2E builds, improving mirror selection and cache reliability. ([#16278](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16278))
- The no-AK integration gate now runs on the self-hosted ECS pool for every pull request, including untrusted forks. ([#16132](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16132))
- test(managed-agent): cover pending sibling approval holds ([#15994](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/15994))
- ci: build the PR tree once and shorten the required path ([#16450](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16450))
  ![Screenshot from pull request 16450](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a78d1c35-4957-416a-92aa-e3c642125344)
  ![Screenshot from pull request 16450](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/51886ce5-eee8-422e-9a96-03e524b77bbf)

---

## 中文摘要

### Skill 安装与激活

Skill ZIP 上传、daemon API、TypeScript SDK 支持、批量激活与恢复备份保护，让 Skill 安装和管理更可靠。

- 新增 PUT /skills/activation 与 setUserSkillsActivation，可一次启用或禁用 1-100 个用户 Skill，并返回保存与传播状态。 ([#16186](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16186))
- 为大型 Skill 压缩包安装做准备，在安装器中加入从磁盘读取 ZIP 的能力与恢复备份保护。 ([#16421](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16421))
- 新增守护进程 API，可通过上传或主机文件路径安装大型 Skill ZIP，并在失败后查询安装回执。 ([#16422](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16422))
- TypeScript SDK 支持通过 File、Blob、字节或主机路径安装 Skill ZIP，并提供尝试 ID 与回执查询。 ([#16423](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16423))
- WebShell 现在可从 Skills 页面上传 Skill ZIP，显示守护进程限制，并查询不确定的安装结果。 ([#16424](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16424))

### Web Shell 会话与输入

Web Shell 会话标题、Add 菜单细节、草稿保留、批量删除与 listSessions 分页修复改进日常会话管理。

- 当 transcript 重建时保留 Web Shell 会话列表标题，避免会话名称丢失。 ([#16299](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16299))
- 优化 Web Shell 作曲器 Add 菜单的图标、标签、描述、间距，并改进无障碍展示与 Plan 状态指示。 ([#16181](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16181))
- WebShell 现在在 ArrowUp 或 ArrowDown 浏览换行提示行时保留未发送草稿。 ([#14909](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14909))
- web-shell: batch session deletions at the route limit ([#14637](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/14637))
- listSessions 分页在多个会话文件修改时间相同时不再跳过会话。 ([#16024](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16024))

### Managed agent 与会话

Managed agent 自动化、持久用户问题、activation 续期、writer 恢复与历史缓存提升托管会话的可靠性与性能。

- managed-agent: support durable structured user questions ([#16433](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16433))
- managed-agent: enable automation by default ([#16448](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16448))
- Managed agent 激活续期现在能更高效定位 activation lease，降低查询开销。 ([#16336](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16336))
- 通过移除 native journal 快照发布中的 tenant 守卫锁，提升 managed-agent 性能。 ([#16410](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16410))
- Managed Session 历史重建现在按进程缓存消息正文，减少重复读取并提升性能。 ([#16337](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16337))
- HTTP Managed Session 写入方恢复现在会保留有效的在途续期授权，避免不必要重新获取。 ([#16287](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16287))

### GitHub PR 自动化

沙箱 /verify 可读取 PR review threads，/autofix-pr 拒绝输出机器可读代码，GitHub 入站恢复在读取失败后重试。

- 沙箱 /verify 轮次现在可读取 PR review threads，包括已解决和过期讨论，便于验证时参考评审意见。 ([#16300](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16300))
- /autofix-pr 助手拒绝时会在 stderr 输出 refused 代码和 next 步骤，便于自动处理。 ([#16238](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16238))
- GitHub 入站恢复在读取失败后会继续重试，任务存储可读后已恢复任务将运行。 ([#16402](https://github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code/pull/16402))

Llama、LLaVA、Pixtral、Mistral Small 与 Qwen VL 图像输入修复，以及 OCI Generative AI 文档扩展 provider 覆盖。

交互式 CLI 通过 OSC 7501 报告 working、blocked、done 或 error 状态，experimental.unifiedAgentLoop 帮助 Ink TUI 完成工具批处理。

SSH 注册、MCP 启动、工具执行锁与 daemon 回放内存限制优化，以及 subscription 恢复改进平台稳定性。

issues.body:
<!-- cw-0103-acceptance-current -->
## Release acceptance — November 2, 2026 (UTC)

**stall guards implemented; original long-run incident open.**

Verified: Phase watchdog/timeouts/durable diagnostics and queued-message recovery are landed. A controlled reasoning stall produced a visible record in2.303s and preserved queued follow-up. Settlement uses event_sent instead of claiming user-visible delivery.

Remaining: Original hours-long ZAI/tool-heavy silent freeze was never reproduced; scoped fixture does not prove that incident resolved.

Next action: Capture the original-condition phase/request/thread trace and queued-message outcome on an authorized real-provider long task, or an independent reproducible counterexample.

Source checkpoint: [canonical main ee30f0e5](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/ee30f0e5f585081bf36ef6f9f8b41e98698b6e2c). This is an implementation/qualification checkpoint; 0.10.3 is unpublished. Earlier status entries below are historical.
<!-- /cw-0103-acceptance-current -->

## Body

```markdown
### Environment

- codewhale 0.9.13 (Rust TUI), linux x86_64
- provider: zai, model: GLM-5.3-Flash
- posture: Ask / workspace-write

### Summary

During long, tool-heavy runs the engine stops producing model output mid-turn.
Everything the user types afterwards is persisted into the session journal but
never answered. The stall is completely silent: no ERROR/WARN in the TUI log,
no crash entry, the spinner just keeps absorbing input.

This happened twice in two independent sessions on consecutive days.

### Steps to reproduce (observed, not deterministic)

1. Run an interactive session with a long skill-driven task that issues many
   bash tool calls (session A), or a multi-turn task with tool approval
   round-trips (session B).
2. Mid-run, the model stops emitting output (session B stalled right after an
   assistant thinking block, before any text/tool output).
3. Send follow-up user messages. They are accepted and persisted.
4. No reply ever arrives; force-quit is the only way out.

### Observed evidence (timestamps UTC)

Session A `a69916b2…` (2026-09-14):

- TUI log `tui-2026-09-14-2784622.log` ends at `10:51:38` with
  `engine.turn completion settled status=Completed delivered=true`.
- The session demonstrably continued for hours after that line and stalled
  later. The entire stall window produced **zero** additional log lines —
  the freeze is invisible to the log.
- Journal tail contains three consecutive `user` entries with no assistant
  response after them (a Chinese follow-up question, `"hello?"`, and a
  `/feedback bug` draft request).
- On-disk session JSON is structurally intact: 95 journal entries, valid
  `leaf_id` pointing at an existing entry, undamaged parent chain.

Session B `53b16822…` (2026-09-15):

- Assistant emitted a thinking block, then stalled before any text or tool
  output. A later `"继续"` (continue) user message also got no response.
- On force-quit, the TUI logged **two** pending turns at the same moment:

  ```
  2026-09-15T03:27:48.318072Z  INFO engine.turn: engine turn completion settled status=Interrupted delivered=true
  2026-09-15T03:27:48.548725Z  INFO engine.turn: engine turn completion settled status=Interrupted delivered=true
  ```

  Note `delivered=true` even though the user received no model output for
  either turn — the flag does not mean the user saw anything.

- `~/.codewhale/crashes/` is empty in both cases.

### Expected

- A stalled provider stream should be subject to a read/response timeout and
  surface a visible error in the UI.
- Queued user messages during a stalled turn should be rejected or reported,
  not silently absorbed.
- `delivered=true` on an Interrupted turn should not be recorded when nothing
  was ever rendered to the user.

### Impact

Long tasks can absorb follow-up messages indefinitely with zero feedback. The
user cannot distinguish "still working" from "dead" and must force-quit, which
then triggers the separate resume bug (filed separately).

### Hypothesis (unconfirmed)

No network-layer logs are available, so the transport-side root cause is
unknown. Suspected: a zai streaming hang with no read timeout in the harness.
Regardless of the transport cause, the missing stall detection and the silent
absorption of user messages are harness-side gaps.

---
Sanitized log excerpts: see `attachment-issue-1-logs.en.md`.
```

[attachment-issue-1-logs.en.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32222431/attachment-issue-1-logs.en.md)

<!-- cw-0103-acceptance-current -->
## Release acceptance — November 2, 2026 (UTC)

**source and macOS journey repaired; final Windows acceptance open.**

Verified: Canonical2cef4ce03d binds selected range rollback to owned invocation UUIDs and acknowledged durable rewind.117 existing checks and14macOS ordinary-terminal scenario modes passed, including progress frames, stale-label refusal, hashes and restart. Earlier native Windows single-turn/API range receipts remain scoped to their binaries.

Remaining: Exact frozen-candidate ordinary Windows multi-turn terminal/package evidence is absent; macOS PTY does not replace it. Native x64/build14393 remain platform gates.

Next action: Use a headless Windows ordinary-terminal/ConPTY journey or independent tester on the exact release binary; no more blocking on repeated guest login attempts.

Source checkpoint: [canonical main ee30f0e5](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/ee30f0e5f585081bf36ef6f9f8b41e98698b6e2c). This is an implementation/qualification checkpoint; 0.10.3 is unpublished. Earlier status entries below are historical.
<!-- /cw-0103-acceptance-current -->

### Before you start

- [X] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. 我已搜索过现有 issue。

### What happened? 发生了什么？

When executing the `/undo` command, the TUI indicates that the file changes have been reverted, but the conversation content has not been undone. After multiple retries, I no longer know how many changes have actually been reverted.

```
Note /undo reverted workspace files to snapshot 'tool:d163e0b8-6551-45ae-8b18-c7edc71562be' (ed67db74)

Note Restored 3 file(s) to snapshot 'tool:d163e0b8-6551-45ae-8b18-c7edc71562be' (ed67db74):
▏    recreated dev/_lines.py
▏    recreated dev/_regen.py
▏    modified skills/lesson-plan-json/SKILL.md
```

### Steps to reproduce 复现步骤

Execute the `/undo` command after the task is completed.

### Codewhale version 版本

0.10.1

### Where did it happen? 在哪里出现？

TUI (terminal interface)

### Operating system 操作系统

Windows

### How did you get Codewhale? 获取方式

Scoop / Nix / Docker / other package

### Provider and model 提供商和模型

Deepseek-v4.1-flash

### Terminal and shell 终端

Windows Terminal

### codewhale doctor (optional)

```text
```

### Logs, screenshots, anything else (optional)

*No response*

Ubuntu 24.04.2 ARM64 production CLI and a terminal at frozen source 1ce833117d plus the October 31 qualified inputs reproduced a durable undo gap. A single real turn read, changed one file and created another. /undo restored both files and reported conversation removal, but the saved active path still contained the original human prompt and assistant final after 20 seconds. Claiming crates/tui/src/tui/ui/session_state.rs, the undo action in ui/apply.rs and Engine session persistence/rewind paths as traced. Verify a fresh resume and preserve audit branches, snapshots and failed-save reporting. Original Windows/Scoop report remains separately open.

A separate fresh process reopened the old human request and assistant reply after /undo, although both workspace files stayed restored. The file rollback path mutated local history then dispatched ordinary SyncSession, which skipped the existing RewindConversation acknowledgement and durable save. A local correction defers that UI mutation to the same acknowledged and persisted route used by conversation-only undo. The Ubuntu baseline and traced file writes are in linux-package/{resume-undo,undo-traced}.json. Native correction validation pending.

The Ubuntu ARM64 production executable with the durable /undo repair passed actual PTY + fresh-process verification. An edited file was restored, a created file removed and an unrelated file preserved. The active transcript went from eight entries to zero, with eight retained in the recovery branch. A second undo reported nothing to undo. Five existing portable command cases passed. Both focused TUI unit-binary builds stopped at explicit disk guards before running those assertions. The verified runtime patch is backed up locally and pending the focused TUI tests. Windows and range/progress criteria remain open.

The durable file-plus-conversation rewind landed on Engine main af3e9e36326a67c2c720c56b252c5f85495274f9. The founder approved four specific compiler caches. After recovery of 21.1 GiB, a 1,554-input recheck matched the Ubuntu candidate. The focused native TUI run passed 47 of 50 initially. # ACP regression in 0.10.1: `sandbox_mode` / `ask` from config ignored again — Paseo ACP sessions run sandboxed and approval-gated

## Summary

The ACP posture bug from [#6310](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6310>) (fixed in the 0.10.0 nightlies and verified in Paseo) is back in stable **0.10.1**: sessions launched via `codewhale serve --acp` ignore `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"` and `ask = "never"` from `~/.codewhale/config.toml`, and run with the OS sandbox on, network off, and approval gates firing on every shell call.

## Environment

* codewhale **0.10.1** (build `fead51eeea0f`), macOS (Apple Silicon)
* Launched as an ACP provider for the Paseo app (verified: multiple `codewhale serve --acp` processes owned by Paseo)
* `~/.codewhale/config.toml`:

  ```toml
  approval_policy = "suggest"
  sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"
  ask = "never"
  ```

## Observed (live session, 2026-10-15)

* `CODEWHALE_SANDBOX=seatbelt` is set in the session environment → the OS sandbox is applied despite `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"`.
* `python3 -c 'import socket; s=socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX); s.bind("/tmp/x.sock")'` → `PermissionError: [Errno 1] Operation not permitted` — the exact [#6310](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6310>) signature; this breaks Node test runners and Playwright webServer.
* `ps` → `operation not permitted` (can't even list processes).
* Network is blocked: `curl -sI https://example.com` returns nothing (`000`).
* Every shell call still hits the typed-ask gate and requires a manual approval in the client UI, even though `ask = "never"`. (`gh` could not even read its own config at `~/.config/gh/hosts.yml` — EPERM — until the shell was escalated.)
* The policy engine itself agrees these should be skipped: `codewhale sandbox check --ask never 'ls -la /tmp'` → `{"allow": true, "requires_approval": false}`. So the disconnect is between the policy engine and the posture actually applied to live ACP sessions.

## Difference vs the original [#6310](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6310>) report

* Writes to `/tmp` now succeed (in 0.9.13 they were EPERM), but AF_UNIX socket creation is still blocked — the one thing Playwright/Node runners need.
* Approval prompts now reach the Paseo UI and can be approved manually (in 0.9.13 they were auto-denied). Still: `ask = "never"` should not gate at all.

## Suspected relation

[#6473](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6473>) (Full Access now requires per-session confirmation) combined with [#6310](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6310>)'s fix ("makes Full Access discoverable **without letting a client select it**") leaves the ACP path with no way to enter Full Access at all. `sandbox_mode = "danger-full-access"` is effectively dead config for Paseo users, and every real workflow — network, sockets, process listing, CLI tools like `gh` — breaks. If per-session confirmation is the intended mechanism, the ACP client needs a way to request/confirm it. Until then this is a regression from the verified-working 0.10.0 nightly.

## Ask

1. Restore config-derived posture for ACP sessions when the client does not pin one, or
2. Expose a Full Access selection/confirmation path to ACP clients (Paseo), or
3. At minimum, honor `ask = "never"` so gated commands skip instead of prompting.

Happy to provide full transcripts or run a nightly/repro build. Greetings from Colombia 🇨🇴

Current 0.10.3 qualification is exercising the shipping ACP stdio entry, the reporter's exact approval settings, CLI opt-in forms, a stricter read-only floor, and local-only socket effects on macOS. No Paseo or Windows result is inferred. Source ownership remains in crates/tui/src/acp_server.rs, its runtime adapter, and the Engine's existing approval/sandbox authority.

Seven macOS source-candidate ACP stdio scenarios passed (binary codewhale-hq/codewhale-app#334 03fcb66028f5aefc7252f99c0357638deb39b008bb8cc421e2c0645299a71e27). The reported suggest/danger-full-access/ask-never config advertised Ask and rejected client-side escalation. A terminal-capable client saw one permission request, denied it and produced no effect. Explicit post-serve --full-access bound a Unix socket and reached a loopback HTTP server with no prompt. Global/post-serve --yolo, config yolo=true, a stricter Plan floor and rejection of approval_policy=never behaved as specified. Ports, provider responses, workspace and account state were local fixtures. Published macOS 0.10.2 independently passed the Ask vs Full Access socket comparison. Paseo and native Windows acceptance remain open.

<!-- /cw-0103-acceptance-current -->

People must be able to remove Codewhale reliably, whichever supported route installed it. This is a required 0.10.3 acceptance item requested by the founder.

Current source already contains removal instructions and a Windows NSIS uninstaller, so this ticket is about completing and proving the whole uninstall journey. It does not assume that every existing uninstall path is broken.

Source baseline: main `916d3227e8`.

* [Install guide: uninstalling](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/blob/916d3227e8/docs/INSTALL.md#L864>) currently relies on manual binary deletion/package-manager commands and separate data removal.
* [Windows NSIS uninstaller](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/blob/916d3227e8/scripts/installer/codewhale.nsi#L142>) removes owned binaries, launcher, shortcut, registry entries and its PATH entry; this is existing implementation, not proof that every distribution is qualified.

## Acceptance for 0.10.3

- [ ] Give users a discoverable, supported uninstall path for direct shell/manual installs, npm, Cargo, Homebrew, Windows PowerShell/direct installs, NSIS, WinGet and Scoop. Package-managed copies use their package manager's removal mechanism.
- [ ] Remove the installation's owned executables and aliases (`codewhale`/`codew`), bundled extension-host artifacts, launchers, shortcuts, completion files and exact product-owned PATH/shell integration. Respect custom install directories and ownership/symlink boundaries; preserve shared runtimes and unrelated files.
- [ ] Preserve user configuration, credentials, sessions and workspace content by default. Any optional data purge must clearly list its scope and require an explicit choice; normal uninstall must not search broadly and delete matching directories.
- [ ] Inventory any product-installed background/startup integration and handle it by verified ownership. Report running-process, permission and partial-removal failures rather than saying uninstall succeeded.
- [ ] Handle multiple installation methods/copies: if another `codewhale` or `codew` remains on PATH, identify it and explain the remaining removal step. Repeated uninstall is safe, and reinstall works afterward.
- [ ] Record isolated install → use/help/version → uninstall → absence/leftover check → reinstall receipts for each supported route/platform, using existing checks where applicable. Validate retained data and unrelated sentinel files. Mark unavailable platform evidence explicitly; documentation alone does not qualify the flow.
- [ ] Update the install guide, package/installer guidance, help/discoverability and CHANGELOG. If a new command/flag is introduced, update its feature registry row in the same slice.

Target release: **0.10.3**, before the candidate freeze. Track execution with the existing 0.10.3 scope packet (codewhale-hq/codewhale-app#3279).

Verification must use disposable prefixes/environments; do not uninstall the founder's active installation or remove their data. This issue authorizes no release, publication, paid VM/provider use or destructive host cleanup.

issues.body:
## Summary
`codewhale auth chatgpt` completes the browser sign-in, but then fails with:

```
error: ChatGPT token signature or identity claims failed verification
```

`codewhale auth status --provider openai-codex` afterwards still reports `active source: missing`.

## Environment
- CodeWhale 0.10.2 (ff466b2ed0bf), installed via `npm i -g codewhale` (latest on npm)
- Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300, Git Bash, Node via nvm4w
- No proxy / custom CA env vars

## Steps
1. `codewhale auth chatgpt`
2. Sign in on auth.openai.com in the browser (callback to `http://127.0.0.1:1455/auth/callback`)
3. Terminal prints the error above; no grant is stored.

## Checks already done
- Clock skew vs auth.openai.com is ~15 s
- `https://auth.openai.com/.well-known/jwks.json` and `openid-configuration` are reachable (HTTP 200)
- The error string appears to cover several failure paths in the binary (unknown/invalid verification key, audience mismatch with the registration, missing `chatgpt_account_id`/subject), so it is unclear which one is hit.

## Request
Please make the error say which check failed (signature / audience / identity claim), or document the account/plan requirements for `auth chatgpt`.

### Engine local-catalog slice landed — 2026-10-28

Engine main `7c49574a6b` probes unknown Ollama tag capabilities with bounded concurrency, publishes an authoritative catalog only when the probe is complete, and fences automatic adoption against superseded discovery and changed endpoints. Four focused existing checks passed on the shared frozen Engine source; the local discovery checks used synthetic loopback fixtures. Desktop installed-model discovery and a real Ollama interaction have not been requalified with the current app and Engine. The issue remains open; no live-model or release proof is claimed.

## What a new user hits

Fresh desktop app (QA bundle codewhale-app `40766826`, bundled Engine 0.10.2, isolated `HOME`/`CODEWHALE_HOME`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME`), with Ollama running two tags: `qwen3:4b` (chat) and `nomic-embed-text:latest` (embedding).

1. Composer → **Choose a model** → the **Ollama** chip shows *Ready*; the Model list offers only **Default**.
2. Send "Reply with exactly: DESKTOP-QA-OK" → `Invalid request (400): "nomic-embed-text:latest" does not support chat`, card "Couldn't finish: this model can't chat. Pick another model."
3. **Choose model** again: the list still shows only `nomic-embed-text:latest`; `qwen3:4b` is not offered. The user has to know to expand **More** and type `qwen3:4b` into *Model ID* → **Use** (Return in that field does nothing).

So on the desktop, "Default" for Ollama resolves to an embedding model, and installed chat models are not listed. The TUI on main picks `qwen3:4b` from the same Ollama, using `choose_chat_tag` (`crates/tui/src/client/ollama_catalog.rs`, capability `completion`), so the desktop/app-server default path appears to bypass that rule.

Expected: the Ollama default is a chat-capable tag, and the model list shows the installed chat tags from `/api/tags`.

Not yet rechecked against current codewhale-app main + main Engine (build slots were busy); the 0.10.3 desktop bundles a newer Engine.

Evidence: `CW/artifacts/qa-20261027/jD1-desktop-default-embed-model.jpg`.

A clean-source Engine build matching `bd9d4422ed` was made on macOS (all 4,160 source inputs rehashed unchanged; binary digest `3eb1b93a0614f519c18e0f88811d805f4a0e035f8f2f874ed668b47ba6eebe7f`). In an isolated product home and workspace, with outbound network sandboxed to localhost, the actual local Ollama daemon exposed `qwen3:4b` for completion and `nomic-embed-text:latest` for embedding. Runtime API refresh returned only `qwen3:4b`; switching with no model selected it and persisted it, a new thread used it, and a tiny local turn completed successfully. Receipt: `CW/artifacts/7116-local-ollama-2/receipt.json`. The first harness start failed because its Unix socket path exceeded macOS limits; the shorter retry passed. This is Engine/runtime proof, not current desktop picker or installed-app proof, and the original cause remains unconfirmed. The native `/api/tags` plus `/api/show` refresh requires complete capabilities and filters for completion; an incomplete native refresh retains its prior roster. The narrow guard will prevent the generic verification response from overwriting the native roster. This is source-derived, not a reproduced desktop report; previously contaminated caches and installed desktop behavior remain open.

The installed picker did list the sole chat tag and excluded the embedding tag, and the selected model completed a real turn. The repaired cold TUI picked qwen3:4b, excluded nomic-embed-text, answered 9+7 with 16 and persisted it. issues.body:
<!-- cw-0103-acceptance-current -->
## Release acceptance — November 2, 2026 (UTC)

**source fixes landed; incident evidence open.**

Verified: Automatic-off recovery guard 7b54e7f572 and original PR #7180 merge 00226bbfbb8 retain exact ancestry; 42 focused checks and repeated-input macOS PTY cover that specific defect. Source also emits reroot/resume/compaction lifecycle records.

Remaining: The reported long-session Windows seam is not reproduced. Root-count alone includes preserved alternate branches and does not prove the actual prepared request omitted distinct authored turns.

Next action: Capture sanitized before/after journal plus prepared model request, route/window/usage and compaction-state ledger at the seam; qualify retained ancestry and visible seam behavior.

Source checkpoint: [canonical main ee30f0e5](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/ee30f0e5f585081bf36ef6f9f8b41e98698b6e2c). This is an implementation/qualification checkpoint; 0.10.3 is unpublished. Earlier status entries below are historical.
<!-- /cw-0103-acceptance-current -->

## Landed setting fix — 2026-10-29

Engine main/origin commit 7b54e7f5724daa88ed29b6479f8ea0b7cf353b0c fixes the concrete automatic-off bypass. Preflight/provider overflow recovery now refuses before summary/start/replacement when compaction is disabled, retains original messages and records an actionable typed refusal through the existing audit/error owners. Both overflow paths preserve the recovery failure's actual cause; cancellation takes priority after the awaited recovery. Explicit manual compaction remains available.

Local proof: initial libtest compile and137focused compaction/error/Engine checks passed. After the final model-step cancellation guard, libtest recompiled and69affected Engine/recovery/cancellation checks passed; unchanged pure-check evidence is retained. The renamed existing emergency fixture covers disabled-but-compactable and enabled-but-unnecessary history, zero model calls/attempts, unchanged messages and one typed refusal. Format, boundary, blocking budget569sites169files, dead-code164, changelog/facts and diff checks pass. No new test functions/comments. Exact receipts: artifacts/codex-0103-resume-20261029/compaction-off-landing-verification.json. Source files are released, not held for another build.

Keep this issue and public Engine7142 open. The setting bypass is established and repaired, but it does not explain every reported Windows seam or complete the remaining lifecycle/continuity acceptance. A read-only local Mac journal inspection did not reproduce the reported multi-root shape; that does not prove no context loss or disprove the reporter's sample. No real-provider, hosted CI, Windows/installed/device or release proof is claimed.

---

## Summary

A session's live `messages` window can be re-rooted partway through a conversation. When
that happens, every `journal` entry before the new root becomes unreachable to the model
while the on-disk journal keeps it in full. The window stays internally consistent — it
equals its own new branch exactly — so nothing looks truncated from the inside.

Three things are missing at the moment it happens:

* **no summary entry at the seam.** The new root is a bare `kind: "message"` with
  `parent_id: null`; the entry immediately before it is an ordinary turn on the branch
  that was just abandoned. Real compaction leaves a condensed account of what it replaced.
  This leaves a copy and a hole.
* **no marker in the interface.** No banner, no notice, no error.
* **no session-lifecycle event in** `audit.log`**.** In 8,792 events across five event types,
  every one is `tool.approval.*` or `tool.gate.decision`. Nothing announces that the model's
  working context was replaced.

`settings.toml` has `auto_compact = false` and `auto_compact_threshold_percent = 80.0`
throughout. If this is compaction, the setting is not describing what the runtime does.

## Environment

* `codewhale --version`: **0.10.2 (ff466b2ed0bf)** — verified against the binary
* OS: Windows 11 (10.0.26200), PowerShell 5.1
* Model: `deepseek-v4-pro` (provider `deepseek`)
* Install: npm global; `~/.codewhale/{config,settings,permissions}.toml`, no `[compaction]`
  block and no `retained_user_message_tokens` in `config.toml`
* Reproduces on **0.10.1 and 0.10.2**

## What it looks like

Dump of four consecutive documents from this host. `entries` = `journal.entries`;
`window` = `len(messages)`; `root` = the journal index the live branch starts at.

```
created (UTC)        window  entries  root   coverage
2026-10-28T13:08:15     944      986     1      99.9%   <- intact (benign doubled opening)
2026-10-28T15:24:44     632     1639   987      39.8%   <- re-rooted
2026-10-29T07:11:22     403      473    50      89.4%   <- re-rooted
2026-10-29T08:20:46      61      325   259      20.3%   <- re-rooted (this one, mid-report)
```

The seam itself, from `2026-10-29T07:11:22`:

```
[48] kind=message  role=assistant  parent_id=Y     3970 chars
[49] kind=message  role=user       parent_id=Y     1362 chars
[50] kind=message  role=user       parent_id=NONE  2054 chars   <- window begins here
[51] kind=message  role=assistant  parent_id=Y      360 chars
```

Prose for scale: the `journal` for that session holds 473 entries; the model could see 403
of them. The boot turn, including the whole startup sequence, was gone from the window and
present on disk.

## Prevalence on this host, and an onset date

87 session documents were parsed structurally. `journal` + `leaf_id` on this host arrives
between 11 and 12 Aug 2026 (before that, documents carry `artifacts` and no journal, so this
signature cannot exist and cannot be tested — that period is **untestable, not clean**).

| period | sessions | shape |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 12 Aug – 17 Oct 2026 | 47 | one branch root, window == journal, 100% reachable |
| 18 Oct – 29 Oct 2026 | 40 | two or three roots; **15 re-rooted mid-session** |

The onset boundary is narrow: `…d6832ea3` (17 Oct 18:33:49Z) is clean at 113/113;
`…021a7d6a` (18 Oct 01:46:51Z) is the first re-root at 962 window / 1045 entries.

Across the 15 mid-session re-roots, the root lands at journal indices 8, 20, 30, 50, 67, 97,
160, 259, 295, 347, 367, 472, 733, 987. Post-re-root coverage ranges from **14.1%** to
89.4%; combined unreachable entries **3,909**.

**In 0 of 87 sessions is the window shorter than its own branch.** This is not truncation —
the window is always a complete branch. The branch is simply no longer the session.

## Reproduction

No special configuration; it appears on ordinary long sessions. A read-only probe against
any session document:

```python
import json, hashlib

doc = json.load(open(PATH, encoding="utf-8"))
msgs, entries = doc["messages"], doc["journal"]["entries"]

by_id = {e["id"]: i for i, e in enumerate(entries) if e.get("id")}
chain, seen, cur = [], set(), len(entries) - 1
while cur is not None and cur not in seen:
    seen.add(cur); chain.append(cur)
    cur = by_id.get(entries[cur].get("parent_id"))

root = min(chain)
print("window", len(msgs), "branch", len(chain),
      "root", root, "coverage %.1f%%" % (100 * (len(entries) - root) / len(entries)))
```

* `window == branch` and `root <= 1` → healthy (a root at 1 is the benign doubled opening;
  do not flag it — see *What I got wrong*, below).
* `root > 1` → the window re-rooted mid-session. `root` entries are unreachable.

To inspect a seam, print `entries[root-2 : root+2]` and check for anything summary-shaped.
On this host there is never one.

## How this differs from the nearby open reports

* [#6842](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/6842>) (journal has no bound; compaction retires live messages but keeps superseded
  versions in RAM) names the same underlying machinery and is about **memory growth**. This
  report is about **model visibility**: the earlier turns were not merely retained
  redundantly, they became unreachable while the record survived. Different harm, possibly
  the same call site.
* #7133 (automatic compression at \~40% against an 80% setting) is the closest
  behavioural neighbour and may share a cause — it reports the *threshold* being wrong,
  where this reports a *silent re-root with no summary*. Worth triaging together.
* #7095 (history lost, labelled v0.10.3) is a different fault: there the record does not
  survive because the last save did not flush. Here every byte survives and is correct, and
  only the window is replaced.

## What I am asking for

In order of value, and each is independently useful:

1. **Emit a session-lifecycle event.** `session.opened`, `session.window.rerooted`,
   `session.compacted`, `session.resumed` — with both sizes and a reason, into `audit.log`
   beside the existing `tool.*` events. This is the smallest change and it converts an
   unexplained amnesia into a dated, attributable event. It is worth having **even if the**
   **re-root turns out to be intended**, so please do not let the other two asks gate it.
2. **Honour** `auto_compact = false`**, or rename it.** A setting that says compaction is off
   while the window is replaced is worse than no setting: it is a claim the operator can
   rely on and cannot verify.
3. **If a window re-root is intended, summarise at the seam.** A bounded, visible,
   summarised compaction is a feature. An unannounced re-root that leaves a bare copy of an
   existing message is a data-visibility defect.

## What I have not established, and will not guess at

**The trigger.** Observed re-roots span 78 to 1639 journal entries, 11 to 1437 window
messages, and roughly 1.3 MB to 5 MB of document. That spread is inconsistent with a single
simple threshold, and two documents is not a sample. It could be turn count, cumulative
tokens, document size, wall clock, or a path that only runs on resume.

**Whether it is intended.** [#5262](<https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/issues/5262>) (closed, shipped v0.9.5) specifies an append-only journal
forest where branching "only moves the leaf — it never rewrites history", so multiple roots
are expected by that design and a re-root is legal in that model. What is not
design-legible is doing it silently, mid-session, with no summary, while
`auto_compact = false`.

## What I got wrong on the way here

Recorded because it is the reason this report is careful, and because a maintainer deserves
to know which tests have already failed.

My first pass used a **positional** test — does `messages[0]` start where `journal.entries[0]`
starts — and produced two confident wrong answers in one morning: first "41 of 93 sessions
lost turns", then, over-correcting, "nothing was lost at all". The positional test fires on
the benign doubled opening, which is why I checked a session minutes old and never restarted
before trusting any number here. The figures above come from a **membership** test: walk the
branch by `parent_id` and ask whether the window can reach every entry its own session wrote.

If this report is wrong, it is wrong in the direction of under-claiming: 15 measured re-roots
on one host, with the mechanism named and the unknowns listed.

---

*Reproduction and evidence kept locally. Happy to provide sanitised session documents or run*
*any probe upstream asks for.*

October 31 continuation. Codex is reviewing contributor PR codewhale-hq/Codewhale#7180 and the #7178 bare/stamped history reproducer against the current Engine. Claimed paths are crates/runtime/src/session_tree.rs, crates/models/src/turn_classify.rs, crates/engine/src/session_manager.rs and the TUI send/snapshot paths as needed. Verify preservation of authored text, turn authority, sibling history and single-send behavior. The related Windows incident remains open until its own acceptance is established.

The contributor head c80c16c14a on original Engine PR codewhale-hq/Codewhale#7180 has 42 focused checks and a macOS PTY receipt. Two deliberate identical submissions yielded two requests and two answers on one intact active path. GitHub's base-branch policy blocked a normal merge. The Windows incident and the wider session window investigation remain open.

Original contributor PR codewhale-hq/Codewhale#7180 merged normally as 00226bbfbb8e421e93dfcf9730f48413aeb10385. Its final head 0079c86058849dfba17105948a28e3084cb432ba resolved only release-note conflicts. The verified Rust changes retain stable patch ID b6620900da6e16abc104326d2061fdd5776b10a0. The live macOS repeated-input receipt and 42 focused tests cover the specific journal defect. Issue #7178 remains open for Windows acceptance, and this wider re-root report retains its separate recovery gates.

## Release acceptance — November 2, 2026 (UTC)

**source fixes landed; incident evidence open.**

Verified: Accepted-route window/provenance da026a2436 and persisted historical receipt de99f0530a are landed. Five Ubuntu fresh-process journeys passed. Matched Windows controls compacted after 801k against the configured 800k threshold.

<!-- /cw-0103-acceptance-current -->

Canonical Engine commit da026a2436a27ac7eb75edc63fb2ba5ba78010d6 landed the accepted-route window and its source across planning, compaction, client limits, the model picker and same-route SetModel. Its recorded 113 focused checks include the alternate-model regression that failed in the October 29 handoff. The current save/restore path persists the Auto provider, model and reasoning receipt. It still lacks the historical context-window value and source in SavedAutoRouteReceipt. Original Windows behavior and final platform qualification remain open. Earlier candidate logs below are historical.

## Handoff — 2026-10-29

At the founder's request for a new takeover, the sixth candidate test build was intentionally interrupted before tests; there is no sixth-run result. Its exact 2,759-input inventory matches `CW/artifacts/engine-codex-takeover-20261029/context-receipt-candidate-sixth-freeze.json`, its log is `context-receipt-candidate-sixth.log`, and the 41-file dirty candidate is backed up as `CW/backups/codewhale-context-window-20261029/context-receipt-sixth-candidate.patch`. Current Engine `main` and `origin/main` were both `6a08f03124` at handoff. The fifth run had 93/94 passes and the alternate-model client regression detailed below; the subsequent correction is unverified. The candidate's idle SetModel can also discard an installed receipt even when model and limits are unchanged, and restored Auto sessions do not retain an exact historical window receipt. Reconcile these paths, review the complete diff, and rerun appropriate existing checks before landing. The original Windows report is still unproved; leave this issue In Progress.

## Restore and protocol limits — 2026-10-29

Read-only review found that saved Auto-route history does not persist the newly tracked context-window receipt. Restoring such a session may therefore fall back to reconstructing a window for the historical model without its exact historical provider/endpoint budget. Idle `SetModel` also does not carry the paired source across the protocol boundary. Neither path is covered by the accepted-turn candidate's 93 passing local checks; both remain open. A targeted rerun of the alternate-model metadata-freezing correction is compiling on `context-receipt-candidate-sixth-freeze.json`; no result yet.

## Focused candidate result — 2026-10-29

On frozen Engine `6a08f03124` plus 41 dirty files, 93/94 focused cases passed after a 20-minute local test build; all 2,759 input hashes matched. The planner reproduction, session projection, route-switch, pressure, tool-output and budget cases passed. Existing `alternate_declared_model_freezes_wire_limits_and_price` failed: the candidate mistakenly replaced a client-frozen output limit of 32 with a later config value of 512. The candidate is being corrected to derive alternate-route receipts from the client's frozen declarations and window overrides; this correction is not yet verified. The temporary planner reproduction was removed after its result. Evidence: `CW/artifacts/engine-codex-takeover-20261029/context-receipt-candidate-fifth.log` and `context-receipt-candidate-fifth-freeze.json`. Original Windows report, idle SetModel/protocol handoff, and final release acceptance remain open.

## Candidate transition review — 2026-10-29

The fourth frozen compile ended before tests on an unused helper in the temporary planner reproduction; `context-receipt-candidate-fourth.log` records the failure. Codex removed that temporary-only lint problem and is including `crates/tui/src/tui/ui/event_loop.rs` and the existing Engine route-install case in `crates/tui/src/core/engine/tests/test_cases_02.rs`. The candidate now also includes `crates/tui/src/core/engine/preview.rs` so preview output planning uses the same resolved window; it is still uncommitted and unverified. The first candidate compile found two type/ownership errors; the corrected second frozen compile completed with an unused-helper lint error before tests. @Hmbown 
More of an FYI background information than a bug - but it does impact reliability and prompted an idea

I use a 'save session' command to a personalised context transfer as an adjunct to codewhale does.  The agent was cut off while executing that command and it was impacted.

Details follow - from the new agents view on the other side of an Emergency Compaction

It has also prompted a though that I will expand on later. Perhaps we can avoid (by design) the need for emergency context compaction.

In essence, the agent is most effective when the context buffer is nearly full - lots of relevant recent experience to call on.  /new destroys that and the agent only has its training to rely on. Emergency compact does much better by transferring context to the new agent.

But perhaps instead of codewhale directly doing the compaction (keep that for true emergencies) ...the agent could be given a tool to allow it to selectively prune its context..
. 
As long as the agent is given the state of the context buffer and the config parameters at each turn,  it could  then prune some of its older context by calling that tools if the parameters require it - but let the agent choose the scope of the context to prune

That should leave an agent with a ongoing mildly varying (almost full) context buffer and not suffer the  drastic interruption that /compact implies. Continuity rather than disruption





# Emergency compaction — the impact on the `save session` task

**Recorded:** 2026-09-29, by the session that resumed after the compaction.
**Subject:** the emergency context compaction that interrupted the `save session` command, and what it
cost the agent's ability to complete that task accurately.
**Evidence class:** every number and path below was measured with a tool after the compaction, from the
live filesystem and the runtime's own stores. Statements that come from the compaction's summary rather
than from a measurement are marked **[reported]**. Statements that could not be explained are marked
**[unresolved]** rather than given a cause.

---

## 1. What happened, in short

The user issued `save session`. That turn began, produced **3,908 characters of reasoning and nothing
else**, and was cut off by an emergency compaction before it called a single tool. The compaction took a
2.5 MB snapshot of the transcript, wrote an 8,608-byte relay summary, and handed that summary to a resumed
turn — the one that wrote this file.

The consequence for accuracy is not that facts were lost. It is that **the only continuity between the
two turns was a model-written summary of a transcript that no longer exists**. Everything inherited from
it had to be re-measured before it could be written down; and of the four claims that failed that
re-measurement, none was a small detail. What cost the agent its accuracy was not the gap in the
transcript but the confidence of the summary that filled it.

Cost, measured: roughly ten gathering calls across three full-state probes, plus the re-measurement that
the four failures forced. The delivered file is `workbench-development/context-transfer-2026-09-29-11:36:26.md`
(24,229 bytes, 339 lines), written between 11:36:26 and 11:36:55, about three minutes after the resume.

---

## 2. The event, as far as it is observable

No tool records the compaction itself. What follows is the trace it left, and the timestamps agree to
within half a minute.

- **Snapshot** — `~/.codewhale/sessions/cc61cccd-9a41-4e00-ac24-6240e53d72a9/artifacts/context-transfer-4cf0b914-6eba-41da-b993-987d1e769a4a.json`,
  2,540,963 bytes, written **11:33:08**.
- **Relay summary** — the `.md` beside it, 8,608 bytes, written **11:33:38**. Its first line is
  *"Another language model started to solve this problem and produced a summary of its thinking process…"*
  — and that is the text that appears in the resumed session's transcript as a user-role message.
- **Resumed turn** — its first tool call ran at **11:33:08**, its second at **11:33:41**. The compaction's
  two writes therefore straddle the resume: the resolver handover and the disk write overlap by seconds.
- **The interrupted turn** — one assistant message, index `msg[57]` in both stores, 3,908 characters of
  reasoning, **no tool calls**. Its closing lines are *"Let me gather facts first."*, then a blank line,
  then *"Let me run."* — so it died in the act of starting, not in the act of writing.
- **Nothing partial was left behind** — verified, not assumed: the project root's newest transfer before
  the resumed one is `context-transfer-2026-09-29-04:40:48.md` (14,845 bytes), and nothing in the project
  root has a modification time between 11:25 and 11:36 except the file the resumed turn wrote.

**This was not the session's first compaction.** The session `cc61cccd-9a41-4e00-ac24-6240e53d72a9` was
created **2026-08-30**, and its `artifacts/` directory holds **46** compaction relays dated from
2026-09-15 onward — including **two today** (04:47 and 11:33). The transfer files at the project root are
a separate, user-facing series written on request; the relays are the runtime's own. So the content of
the delivered transfer file inherits from a chain of summaries, even though the *file* has exactly one
compaction hop behind it.

---

## 3. What was lost, and what was not

**Lost:** the agent's side of the transcript for every turn before the compaction boundary. The live log
and the checkpoint both retain assistant reasoning only from `msg[57]` onward — the interrupted turn's
block and the resumed turn's segments. Everything the agent reasoned in the earlier turns of this session
was replaced by summary text.

**Not lost — the user's own words.** All **57** of this session's user turns survive verbatim in the
stores — `msg[0]` through `msg[56]`, every one of them. (The 58th user-role message is the compaction
relay itself, at `msg[59]`.) Every instruction, every correction — "No point
referencing line numbers", "try to avoid using invented shorthand", "Option B", "deploy this to a514" —
is checkable word for word. The asymmetry is exact and worth stating plainly: **the compaction destroyed
the agent's reasoning and preserved the user's instructions.**

**Recoverable, and where:** the interrupted turn's own 3,908 characters survive in both stores, and the
resumed turn's reasoning survives in the checkpoint. The fuller record is the checkpoint beside the log —
`~/.codewhale/sessions/checkpoints/cc61cccd-9a41-4e00-ac24-6240e53d72a9.json` (22.7 MB, rewritten as the
session turns) — which carries more messages and more reasoning segments than the live log at any moment:

- live log, first sampled early in the resumed turn: **61 messages, 1 assistant block, 3,908 chars**.
- live log, sampled at the end of the resumed turn: **118 messages, 30 assistant blocks**.
- checkpoint, sampled at the end of the resumed turn: **125 messages, 33 assistant blocks**.

So the stores do retain reasoning — progressively, and only from the last boundary. The live log simply
lags within a turn, which is what made the first sample look like an empty store.

---

## 4. Impacts on the ability to complete the task accurately

### 4.1 Continuity arrived as a summary, and the summary was the only record

The resumed turn began with no transcript of the interrupted turn — no tool results, no partial
deliverable, no working memory. The provenance chain for the file it produced is: **full transcript
(dropped) → relay summary → delivered transfer file.** Each hop is lossy, neither is checkable against
its source, and the second hop was written by an agent that had itself only the summary. The practical
effect: the deliverable could be made *true* only by re-measuring the world, never by trusting its input.

### 4.2 The reasoning behind every decision was unavailable — only its conclusion survived

The summary states outcomes: decision 3 is Option B; the composer is PHP; the headline figures are read
from each site's rendered report; the report links were dropped. It does not carry the argument for any of
them. For conclusions that rest on a chain — *why* the five headline figures cannot come from the data
file, for instance — the resumed turn could restate the conclusion with the summary's own one-line
justification and nothing more. It could not re-derive it, and could not tell whether the justification was
the real one. **Errors of fact were catchable; errors of reasoning were not.**

### 4.3 Four claims failed on contact with live state

All four were completion claims — the class of statement a summary compresses hardest and asserts most
confidently. Each was found by measuring, not by reading:

1. **"The `debian/changelog` quirk is now recorded in `docs/code-quirks.md`."** Measured false. That file's
   newest entries are dated **2026-09-27**; it contains **no** 2026-09-28 or 2026-09-29 entry at all — so
   neither the build quirk nor any of the four composer defects reached the quirks backlog, though the
   project rule requires the append in the turn each is found. The summary reported a diligence that had
   not happened. **[Reported, then refuted by measurement.]**
2. **The `.buildinfo.new`.** The summary and the user's own screenshot disagreed with each other; live
   state resolves neither: the file is absent from `~/Documents`, from `/tmp`, and from a full-depth search
   beneath `~/Documents`, and no command in the resumed turn removed it. **[Unresolved — recorded as
   observed.]**
3. **The reasoning-retention measurement.** The summary's figure — 599 messages, 225 thinking blocks,
   845,169 characters — matches **neither** store. Measured: the live log began the resumed turn with 61
   messages and one 3,908-character block, and the checkpoint with 109 messages and 25 blocks. **[Reported,
   then refuted.]**
4. **Where the `.deb` goes.** The summary's "published" implied the parent directory; the build script
   publishes it with `mv` to `workbench-linux/website/workbench-linux.sentuny.com/dl/`, where it verifies
   at 31,402,694 bytes dated 11:28. This one the resumed turn could settle by reading the code. **[Reported,
   then corrected.]**

Three of the four were caught only because the resumed turn re-measured the world rather than describing
it. Had it written the file first and verified afterwards, all four would have been written down as fact.

### 4.4 A measurement that could not be reconciled at all

The 599/225/845,169 figure cannot be reproduced from either store now, and no third store was found. The
resumed turn recorded the divergence as a divergence, inside the outstanding-questions section of the
delivered file, rather than choosing a number. That is the honest handling — but it leaves the record
with a figure that is known to be wrong and is not known to be replaced by a right one.

### 4.5 The boundary between the two turns was destroyed — including my ability to audit the loss

The resumed turn could not tell, from the stores alone, whose reasoning the one retained block was. It
reasoned about it, concluded it was the resumed turn's own (streamed live), and **wrote that conclusion
into the delivered transfer file** — where it is wrong. The block at `msg[57]` is the *interrupted* turn's;
its closing lines ("Let me gather facts first.", then "Let me run.") show it died before its first tool call.
The live log was simply lagging in persisting the resumed turn's own segments.

So the compaction did not merely remove information; it removed the *marker* by which the loss could be
measured. Reconstructing the boundary took several probes of two stores and their timestamps. One
reconstruction was committed to paper before it was checked, and it was false. This is the sharpest form
of the impact: **a summary that does not date itself makes its own errors unattributable.**

### 4.6 No partial artefact existed to inspect or salvage

A real hazard for a task whose deliverable *is* a file is a half-written file that reads as complete. It
did not materialise here: the interrupted turn made no tool calls, wrote nothing, and the project root's
previous transfer file is untouched at 04:40:48. The resumed turn verified that instead of assuming it.

### 4.7 The session's own subject was demonstrated by its own ending

The session opened with the user noticing that the previous turn's reasoning cannot be reviewed after the
fact, and it closed with the agent's reasoning being destroyed mid-task by the machinery that keeps the
context window. Both are the same mechanism seen from two sides. The delivered transfer file records the
first; this document records the second.

---

## 5. What the resumed turn had to re-establish before it could write anything

Every one of these was measured after the resume; none was inherited as fact.

- The three deployed files' **md5 sums against the box** — `acd494130580eba918449a48badd706d`
  (`/etc/draff.yaml`), `a0f074b5128f2d36d61ef142297ecbcc` (`/opt/draff/compose-daily-report.php`),
  `1a9333e314a47bfe2545fb628498b548` (`/opt/draff/run-daily.sh`) — all three matching the repos.
- The **cron line** (`35 1 * * * /opt/draff/run-daily.sh >> /var/log/draff.log 2>&1`) and the last line in
  `/var/log/draff.log` (04:25:34, the old `draff` job), which is what proves the composer has never run in
  production.
- **PHP 8.3.6** on the box.
- The **test suite, re-run live**: 14 passed, 0 failed; message 119,836 bytes; longest line 657 bytes;
  195 bar rows; 11 plain tables; three download detail blocks.
- **Seven repositories' branch and dirty state**, and the one commit since the previous transfer
  (`779354c`).
- The **plan document**: 882 lines, decision 3 settled as Option B, the nineteen categories listed, the
  Revisions section present.
- `~/Documents` **free of build artefacts at any depth**, and the `.deb` present in the website's `dl/`.
- The **session stores' own shape** — which is what turned a hidden risk into a recorded one.

**What could not be re-measured, and is therefore inherited in the delivered file:** that the four
composer defects were each "fixed and proved" (only their *consequences* were re-measured — the clean test
suite, the line-length distribution, the `-f` sender in the source, the Postfix log line); the user's own
in-conversation confirmation that the email "looks good"; the account of the earlier over-broad cleanup
that deleted three `/tmp` artefacts; and every statement about *why* a decision was taken. These are
written in the delivered file as they were reported, and they carry the summary's authority rather than a
measurement's.

---

## 6. Defects this event exposed in the delivered file

Both are corrections the resumed turn found *after* writing the transfer file. Neither has been applied —
an edit needs the user's word.

1. **A mis-attribution in the `### Session Log` section.** It says the live log's single retained
   `thinking` block is *"the current turn's reasoning, streamed as it is produced."* Measured after the
   fact, that block is `msg[57]`, the **interrupted** turn's reasoning — and the claim's second half is
   wrong too: the live log does retain assistant reasoning, from the compaction boundary onward, and now
   holds 30 such blocks.
2. **A pointer that understates the record.** The section directs a future reader to the live log, which
   at any moment is the *thinner* of the two stores. A fresh session following the delivered pointer would
   conclude that reasoning is barely retained and stop looking — the opposite of the truth. The checkpoint
   beside it, and the 46 relays in the session's `artifacts/` directory, are the fuller record.

---

## 7. Structural risks for future `save session` turns, and proposed mitigations

Recorded as proposals; none is implemented.

1. **A summary's completion claims are its least trustworthy content.** They are the most compressed and
   the most confidently asserted. A relay should mark each claim as *verified by tool* or *reported*, and
   the resumed turn must treat everything unmarked as a hypothesis to test. Here the four failures were
   all of this class.
2. **A summary must date and delimit itself.** Without a statement of which turns it covers and when it
   was taken, the boundary is unreconstructable and its own errors become unattributable (§4.5). The
   compaction's own artifacts do carry timestamps; the relay text does not.
3. **Write the deliverable early, then verify.** The interrupted turn gathered facts in no particular
   order and died with nothing on disk. Even a first-pass skeleton on disk would have made the resume
   cheap and the loss small. This is compatible with authoring the document in full — it changes the
   order, not the authorship.
4. **Layer the pointers.** A transfer file's research section should name the live log, the checkpoint and
   the compaction relays, and say which is fuller — otherwise the next session reads the thinnest one and
   believes it.
5. **Record the provenance depth in the file itself.** The delivered transfer file has one compaction hop
   behind it, but its content inherits a chain of 46 relays. A reader cannot tell the difference, and
   should be able to.
6. **State the boundary index.** `msg[57]` is where retained reasoning begins. One line in the research
   section would tell the next session exactly which turns' reasoning is gone and need not be hunted for.

---

## Appendix A — measurements cited

```
session id                 cc61cccd-9a41-4e00-ac24-6240e53d72a9
session created            2026-08-30
compaction relays in store 46, dated 2026-09-15 .. 2026-09-29 (two today: 04:47, 11:33)
snapshot (11:33 compaction)  artifacts/context-transfer-4cf0b914-….json  2,540,963 bytes  11:33:08
relay summary (same event)   artifacts/context-transfer-4cf0b914-….md       8,608 bytes  11:33:38
interrupted turn             msg[57], assistant, 3,908 chars of reasoning, no tool calls
resumed turn first tool call 11:33:08      second tool call 11:33:41
live log, early in resume    61 messages (60 user, 1 assistant), 1 thinking block (3,908)
live log, end of resume     118 messages (88 user, 30 assistant), 30 thinking blocks
checkpoint, end of resume   125 messages (92 user, 33 assistant), 33 thinking blocks
delivered transfer file      workbench-development/context-transfer-2026-09-29-11:36:26.md
                             24,229 bytes, 339 lines, written 11:36:26–11:36:55
previous transfer file       context-transfer-2026-09-29-04:40:48.md  14,845 bytes (untouched)
user turns retained         57 verbatim (msg[0] .. msg[56]); the 58th user-role message is the relay
```

## Appendix B — the interrupted turn's surviving reasoning

Recoverable in full from both stores at `msg[57]`. Opening, verbatim:

> The user says "save session". Per AGENTS.md, that means: generate a context-transfer file at the pro…
>
> **Execute this instruction exactly as written. Do not optimise, streamline, or deviate.**
>
> Steps:
> 1. Get the current date/time for the filename.
> …

Closing, verbatim:

> Let me gather facts first.
>
> Let me run.

Those closing lines are the whole proof that the turn produced nothing: it was about to gather, and the
compaction arrived first.

## Appendix C — how to re-derive any of this

```bash
# the two stores, and which is fuller
ls -t ~/.codewhale/sessions/*.json | head -1
ls -l ~/.codewhale/sessions/checkpoints/

# every compaction relay this session has had, with dates
ls -lt ~/.codewhale/sessions/<id>/artifacts/context-transfer-*.md

# the retained turns, roles and reasoning blocks, without reading 22 MB into a viewer
python3 -c "
import json,collections
d=json.load(open('<store>.json'))
print(len(d['messages']), dict(collections.Counter(m.get('role') for m in d['messages'])))"
```

Corrective release and exact-candidate qualification. Release scope approved November 5, 2026.

Keep history/undo and compaction continuity, login/model selection, worker durability and safe retries, bounded input/output, runtime responsiveness, and supported installation/client qualification here. Use release-blocker for the unresolved repair/qualification gates. Broad refactors, optional features, full historical audit sweeps and unqualified optimization claims move to the later planning milestones. This replaces the previous all-refactors-for-0.10.3 umbrella scope; unfinished requirements are deferred, not completed or discarded. Confirmed release-critical defects must not be hidden by a future umbrella target.

The uncommitted Pager batch is excluded.

Engine bundled source is retired. Current CU source SHA5765a460b3ff1d7b27f54cb860a3a9d88f3cf74e is separate from Engine. Carrying source: [d9015df5b8](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/d9015df5b8a85c0ea1d0d4e295832410ae44da95), [6ae6cb4433](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/6ae6cb44331b43e6b25bbf9c5c88414953f77eb0).

- **T01-08 — retired original path:** The old computer meter implementation is deleted by carrying34bf6568f2; do not invent a current Engine meter fix. Carrying source: [51b1451512](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/51b1451512c05e52cb883af3d62a86f155efad6b).
- **U02-03 — source complete:** dispatch resolves the existing echoed_user_turn_cell instead of inserting a second user row. Carrying source: [0d9a74a6d9](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/0d9a74a6d9906567c1cafc246a4041511442a1d5).

A retained read-only Nov1binding receipt confirms DRAFT_CLAIM_LOCK on all then-active deployed versions; this is not deployment of current main. Carrying source: [ccc0009881](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/ccc00098818cdc6df34a3b04497b6869415bd308), [82723e9606](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/82723e96060791b4e369eac94b9ab7c8dd29db78), [639d8003fd](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/639d8003fd88d22b19e6ae49e3ca8ebbb6f418e1).
- **W02-05 — source complete local qualified:** Both formerly open source gaps are fixed: runFactsDrift requires existing named lease before fetch, saveDraft holds per-identity claim through resolution/read/write and receipt. Carrying source: [e7bee48a3c](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/e7bee48a3ce97c1b28c9bf4b3e1d0d3052a66598), [c4a31ba850](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/c4a31ba85007ae00795ee3722be6cee35e38ff54).

- **O02-11 — explicit policy downgrade candidate:** deny.toml retains multiple-versions=warn with explicit founder-approval ratchet and version-pinned skip entries; three skip-tree roots remain name-only. Dependency-version policy is not operation replay. Preserve the policy; root can record an out-of-class downgrade and keep any enforcement decision in its existing dependency owner. Carrying source: [460819e86f](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/Codewhale/commit/460819e86f2596eaad5dd2f68f4620e72f7a1599).

**Next action:** Update the existing issue body with the landed W02/source retirements and scoped evidence. Finish/decide T02-07 and resolve the exact U05 unseen-worker case; record T05-07/O02-11 class ownership rather than silently dropping them.
