> Source: static audit of `main@384439634`. Candidates are static and not reproduced — confirm each before changing code.
> Template: agent-task (agent-ready, `docs/ISSUE_TRIAGE.md`). Labels: `bug`, `agent-ready`.

## Goal / Why
Tool calls, MCP calls, HTTP turns, bridge messages, and forge actions are retried or replayed on ambiguous failure without an `operation_key`/CAS. When a request times out or the connection drops the operation may already have been applied, so the retry applies it a second time. Duplicate side effects range from noisy (a double comment) to costly (double billing, divergent remote state, a duplicate PR). The fix is an operation key (or compare-and-swap) on every side-effecting call on the retry path, so replay can detect an already-applied operation.

Confirmed static findings in this class: **20** (reassessed severity noted per line).

## Scope / Plan
1. Re-read each candidate below at the cited `file:line` on current `main`; drop anything already fixed or misread.
2. Introduce an operation key (or CAS) for every side-effecting call on the retry path; make replay detect an already-applied operation.
3. Add the smallest regression/gate that would catch a re-introduction (focused test, budget script, or grep guard).

## Key files
- `crates/tui/src/core/engine/turn_loop.rs`
- `crates/tui/plugins/computer-use/src/app-socket.mjs`
- `crates/tui/plugins/computer-use/src/backends/darwin-accessibility.m`
- `crates/tui/src/computer_meter.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/cloud_dispatch.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/mcp.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/tui/widgets/agent_card.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/fleet/store.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/plugins/marketplace/parsers/codewhale.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/llm_client/mod.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/tui/control_socket.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/runtime_api.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/runtime_mobile.html`
- `crates/tui/src/runtime_threads.rs`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every listed candidate is either fixed with a test, or downgraded with a written reason in the PR.
- [ ] No new instance of this class is introduced (guarded by the test/budget).
- [ ] Existing behavior for unrelated paths is unchanged.

## Verification
```sh
cargo check -p codewhale-tui
cargo test  -p codewhale-tui --lib
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo deny check bans advisories   # if cargo-deny is installed; see .github/workflows/cargo-deny.yml
( cd pet && npm run check )
( cd web && npm run check )
```

## Out of scope
- Findings that belong to another systemic class or to the localized backlog.
- Re-architecture beyond the listed sites.

## Related existing work (do not duplicate)
#5199 (stack R5), #6252 (sticky route binding), #6096 (session-export slice)

## Candidate findings (20)
- [ ] **CU01-07** · CU01 — Computer-use · `crates/tui/plugins/computer-use/src/app-socket.mjs:64` — timeout/cancel after dispatch returns cancelled without `outcome_unknown`, encouraging duplicate action.  
  _audit severity: high; reassessed: major_

  _audit severity: high; reassessed: major_
- [ ] **T01-08** · T01 — TUI entry, process lifecycle, support · `crates/tui/src/computer_meter.rs:474` — meter interval can cross expiry, replay digest checks only a subset of fields.  
  _audit severity: high; reassessed: major_
- [ ] **T06-01** · T06 — Remote control, MCP, OAuth, cloud dispatch · `crates/tui/src/cloud_dispatch.rs:291` — cancel/phase-save race resurrects a canceled job; fixed shared `.tmp` races writers.  
  _audit severity: high; reassessed: major_
- [ ] **T06-03** · T06 — Remote control, MCP, OAuth, cloud dispatch · `crates/tui/src/mcp.rs:4932` — ambiguous failed `tools/call` automatically replayed without idempotency.  
  _audit severity: high; reassessed: major_
- [ ] **U05-04** · U05 — Work surface, widgets, agent cards/panels · `crates/tui/src/tui/widgets/agent_card.rs:574` — delayed mailbox event after terminal reopens delegate/fanout and duplicates counts.  
  _audit severity: high; reassessed: major_
- [ ] **C02-04** · C02 — TUI engine and turn loop · `crates/tui/src/core/engine/turn_loop.rs:1443` — reasoning-only retry nudge visible to model but absent from session log; needs durable runtime event/replay.  
  _audit severity: major; reassessed: major_
- [ ] **C02-14** · C02 — TUI engine and turn loop · `crates/tui/src/core/engine/turn_loop.rs:2906` — tool admission does not bound cardinality/batch and duplicate IDs before side effects.  
  _audit severity: major; reassessed: major_
- [ ] **F01-04** · F01 — Fleet and plugins · `crates/tui/src/fleet/store.rs:290`, `crates/tui/src/plugins/marketplace/parsers/codewhale.rs:161` — schema/identity validation is incomplete; unbounded control-containing values and duplicate names are preserved.  
  _audit severity: major; reassessed: major_
- [ ] **T02-07** · T02 — Model HTTP/SSE clients · `crates/tui/src/llm_client/mod.rs:1246` — ambiguous POST transport failures are retried without idempotency, creating duplicate billing/side effects.

- [ ] **U02-03** · U02 — Event loop, dispatch/apply · `crates/tui/src/tui/ui/dispatch.rs:91` — hook-replaced queued message remains echoed, then a duplicate User history cell is added.  
  _audit severity: major; reassessed: major_

> Template: agent-task (agent-ready, `docs/ISSUE_TRIAGE.md`). Labels: `bug`, `agent-ready`.

## Goal / Why
State, session, ledger, goal, and job records are written with non-unique temp names, without fsync, or as multi-step commits. A crash, power loss, or a second writer can then leave a truncated file or a half-applied batch that later code reads as valid — losing claims, decisions, or session history, or reviving deleted records. The fix is one atomic durable-write contract per record set: unique temp name, fsync, rename, and batch/transaction semantics for multi-file commits. Non-atomic Windows replacement and mirror-write ordering belong to the same contract.

Confirmed static findings in this class: **8** (reassessed severity noted per line).

## Scope / Plan
1. Re-read each candidate below at the cited `file:line` on current `main`; drop anything already fixed or misread.
2. One owner for atomic durable writes: unique temp file, fsync, rename, and batch/transaction semantics per record set.
3. Add the smallest regression/gate that would catch a re-introduction (focused test, budget script, or grep guard).

Network responses, files, child pipes, and artifact reads are consumed with `.text()`/`read_to_string`/`read_to_end` (or a growing buffer) before any size bound. > Source: static audit of `main@384439634`. Candidates are static and not reproduced — confirm each before changing code.

## Goal / Why
Filesystem, subprocess, git, secret-store, and tempfile work is executed synchronously inside `async` call chains (engine tasks, tool handlers, UI event loop, runtime API). Parking a Tokio worker stalls every task sharing that runtime: the TUI stops responding to input, unrelated tools and streaming freeze, and cancellation/timeouts are delayed. Repository convention #6149 requires `tokio::fs`/`tokio::process` or `spawn_blocking`, and `scripts/check-blocking-calls-budget.py` ratchets the unprotected-site count precisely to stop this class from creeping back. Each site below must move to async IO, `spawn_blocking`, or a dedicated thread without raising that budget.

Confirmed static findings in this class: **9** (reassessed severity noted per line).

1. Re-read each candidate below at the cited `file:line` on current `main`; drop anything already fixed or misread.
2. Move each listed site to `tokio` async IO, `spawn_blocking`, or a dedicated thread; do not raise the blocking-calls budget.
3. Add the smallest regression/gate that would catch a re-introduction (focused test, budget script, or grep guard).

Parent: #7235

## Problem

The first native DSH host and UI slice landed in `b0b2b9a335` (Engine), `f190bf19` (app) and `e923d11f` (platform), but it is not full DSH parity:

- reviewed dependency closure and `engines.dsh`/`dsh.bundle.platforms` admission are in place;
- a UI-only `dsh.client` bundle stages its source and one desktop/web slot host renders a bounded adapter;
- web production has a host route but no live local Engine transport, so it only works with a fixture;
- lifecycle events, most slots and plugin CSS/images/fonts are still missing.

## Scope

- Project DSH lifecycle events from the Engine into the host: at minimum `tools/result`, session/turn boundaries and child `agent/created`; keep the five authority-bearing events refused.
- Preserve the reviewed dependency closure on Node and Bun; add pnpm-style directory-symlink dependency trees only with hash checks.
- Expand the shared slot vocabulary beyond `customize.plugins.detail` (composer, settings, sidebar/right rail, tool card and conversation nodes) with owner props, order/priority, disposal and locale/theme scope.
- Serve plugin CSS, images and fonts under the sandbox CSP; support relative assets and multi-chunk/lazy client entries.
- Live web Engine transport for plugin UI (blocked by #7236) and mobile is separate.
- Keep the refused authority surface: no `llm`, `approval`, credentials, raw fs/subprocess, `runtimeLoop`, session writes or a second loader.

## Acceptance

- A published-style DSH bundle with its own dependency tree runs on Node and Bun.
- A lifecycle observer receives one redacted event per relevant tool/turn boundary.
- A real `dsh.client` bundle renders in desktop and web from a live Engine.
- The refused services remain refused and the host still fails closed on escape/incompatible input.

issues.title: Proxy credentials can reach the log file when HTTP(S)_PROXY is malformed

labels.name: area:tui
labels.description: Terminal UI behavior, rendering, or interaction

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP servers, tools, OAuth and the mcp CLI

issues.body:
## What happened?

`redact_proxy_userinfo` in `crates/net/src/proxy.rs` returns its input unchanged when the string has no `://`. One caller passes a raw environment value rather than a parsed `Url`, so when the configured proxy is malformed and carries credentials, the password is written to the log file in clear text.

The branch is the malformed-`HTTP(S)_PROXY` warning in `configured_mcp_proxy`:

```rust
let Some(normalized) = normalized else {
    tracing::warn!(target: "mcp", proxy = %redact_proxy_userinfo(&proxy_url), "ignoring malformed HTTP(S)_PROXY URL");
    return Ok(None);
};
```

`proxy_url` is the raw `read_environment(key)` value, never parsed at that point. The other three call sites pass `reqwest::Url` values (`url.as_str()`, `target.configured`), which always carry a scheme, so they are fine.

`tracing::warn!` goes to `~/.codewhale/logs/tui-YYYY-MM-DD-PID.log` and is kept for the retention window, so the value persists on disk.

## Steps to reproduce

Feed the redaction function the strings that actually reach that branch (checked against `0.10.3`):

```text
input                                      Url::parse   http:// prefix   logged
http://user:pass@proxy.example:8080        ok           ok               -
user:pass@proxy.example:8080               fail         ok               -
user:pass@ho st:8080                       fail         fail             LEAKS
user:pass@proxy.example:port-not-a-number  fail         fail             LEAKS
user:pass@[::1:8080                        fail         fail             LEAKS
user:pass@                                 fail         fail             LEAKS
```

A row that fails both parses reaches the warning; `logged` is what the warning would write. The four rows marked `LEAKS` come through with the password intact, because none of them contains `://` and the function bails out before redacting.

End to end:

1. Export a malformed proxy carrying credentials, e.g. `HTTPS_PROXY='placeholder-user:placeholder-pass@proxy.example:not-a-port'`.
2. Start the TUI with an MCP server configured, so `configured_mcp_proxy` runs.
3. Search the current `~/.codewhale/logs/tui-*.log` for `placeholder-pass`.

It appears in clear text.

## Expected

Either redact the value or drop it from the message. "Ignoring a malformed HTTP(S)_PROXY URL" already identifies the problem, and the operator knows what they exported.

A fix that keeps the diagnostic: when there is no `://`, locate the last `@` before any `/`, `?` or `#` and replace everything before it with `***@`, mirroring the schemed branch. The existing table in `proxy::tests::redact_proxy_userinfo_strips_password` can take the four unschemed inputs above as regression cases.

## Version and configuration

`0.10.3` source. The early return predates the loopback-proxy work in #7231; that PR tightened the function's doc comment to say unschemed input is not redacted, but did not change this branch's behaviour.

## Where did it happen?

MCP — the warning fires from `configured_mcp_proxy`, which the MCP HTTP client calls per request.

## A note on classification

I am filing this as a bug rather than a private advisory on purpose, and I would rather be explicit than quiet about it: there is no attacker and no remote path here. It needs the user to put a plaintext password in `HTTPS_PROXY` *and* malform the URL, and that password is already readable by same-user processes through the environment. What changes is that it lands in a file that people paste into issues. One step short of what `SECURITY.md` calls a credential leak.

I could not open a private advisory either — creating one needs `admin` on the repository, and outside contributors do not have it (`permissions.admin == false`). If you read this as a security report rather than a bug, close this and I will follow whatever channel you prefer.

## Attribution

🤖 Generated by SpikeBot 000(CodeWhale-LOCAL)

issues.title: Remove the workspace-wide sub-agent coordination flock: one stale session leaves every new session read-only and repeating "Failed to clean up sub-agents"

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:tui
labels.description: Terminal UI behavior, rendering, or interaction

labels.name: os:macos
labels.description: macOS-specific behaviour

labels.name: area:core
labels.description: Engine core: turn loop, agent loop, runtime

labels.name: area:state
labels.description: Sessions, persistence and the state store

issues.body:
### Before you start

- [x] I searched existing issues and this is not a duplicate. 我已搜索过现有 issue。 Related (closed): #7042, #5036.

### What happened? 发生了什么？

New TUI sessions in one workspace show this on every sub-agent sidebar refresh:

```
Warn Failed to clean up sub-agents: Runtime coordination was opened without its writer lock; stop and restart this Runtime process after the other session exits
```

Restarting does not help. Every new session's TUI log shows why:

```
WARN subagent: delegated store admission failed; writable state remains refused error=another Codewhale process (pid 69066) owns delegated coordination for <workspace>: Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 35)
WARN subagent: this session cannot append to the shared coordination ledger error=Runtime coordination was opened without its writer lock; stop and restart this Runtime process after the other session exits
```

- **The named holder is wrong.** PID 69066 does not exist. No acquirer writes its PID into `subagents.v1.lock`. The file's content dates from August, so the diagnostic names a dead process.
- **The real holder** was a `codew` started six days earlier and suspended since then (`STAT T`, no TTY, parent launchd). It held two fds on `<workspace>/.codewhale/state/subagents.v1.lock`.
- **Why it blocks everything:** the workspace still had a legacy `subagents.v1.json` file and no `subagents.v3.json`. So every new session attempts the v1→v3 cutover, and the cutover requires the lock **exclusively**. One forgotten process blocks the cutover indefinitely, and every new session in the folder runs with sub-agent state read-only.

Expected: one stale process does not degrade every other session in the folder. If something does block, the message names the actual blocker and says what to do, once.

### Steps to reproduce 复现步骤

1. Use a workspace that still has `.codewhale/state/subagents.v1.json` and no `subagents.v3.json`. Start any Codewhale session there and leave it running or suspended (Ctrl+Z).
2. Start a current-build session in the same workspace.
3. Open the sub-agent sidebar. The warning repeats on each refresh where cleanup is due. The log names whatever PID is in the lock file, not the holder.

### Codewhale version 版本

codewhale 0.10.3 (d214a969012f)

### Where did it happen? 在哪里出现？

TUI (terminal interface)

### Operating system 操作系统

macOS

### How did you get Codewhale? 获取方式

Built from a git checkout

### Provider and model 提供商和模型

deepseek / deepseek-flash (does not matter)

### Terminal and shell 终端

_No response_

### codewhale doctor (optional)

_No response_

### Logs, screenshots, anything else (optional)

**Mechanism** (on `main` at `d214a9690`):

1. `ensure_subagent_store_cutover` (`crates/engine/src/tools/subagent/mod.rs:13710`) calls `CoordinationProcessLock::acquire(root, true)` (exclusive) whenever the v1 tombstone is missing. Any other live session fails it, even one holding the lock shared or sitting suspended.
2. On that failure, `with_state_path` and `require_coordination_process_lock` (`mod.rs:6070-6105`) set `coordination_snapshot_read_only = true` for the life of the process. Nothing retries when the holder leaves. `ensure_coordination_process_lock` (`mod.rs:6110`) then returns the "restart" error forever.
3. `Op::ListSubAgents` (`crates/engine/src/core/engine.rs:4110-4135`) runs cleanup on each refresh where cleanup is due and sends a user-visible error every time. The result is repeated warnings that never name the blocker.
4. The holder PID is read from the lock file's content (`mod.rs:4037-4050`), which no acquirer writes.

**Proposal: remove the workspace-wide process flock.**

The v3 store already handles its own concurrency:

- a bounded, per-operation `subagents.v3.transaction.lock` (`acquire_store_transaction`, `mod.rs:13638`);
- per-writer boot leases, `subagents.v3.writer.<boot>.lock` (`mod.rs:13910`).

`docs/architecture/delegated-coordination.md` (§ "Legacy cutover and recovery") already says two things: the retained `subagents.v1.json` directory is what stops an old publisher from overwriting state, and concurrent old binaries are not a supported coordination domain. So:

- Run the v1→v3 cutover under the transaction lock only.
- Delete `CoordinationProcessLock`, `coordination_process_lock[_required]`, `coordination_exclusive` and `coordination_snapshot_read_only`. They have 66 references in `subagent/mod.rs` and 40 in `subagent/tests.rs`.
- Decide whether the single-host policy of `codewhale serve` and the runtime API (#7042's exclusive constructor) still needs anything the store leases do not cover. Keep it only if it does, and state why.
- Keep working: #5036 (isolated worktree builders) and #7042 (several resumed sessions in one folder). Update the architecture doc in the same change.

If full removal is rejected, the minimum fix is:

- Retry store admission once the holder exits, instead of staying read-only for the life of the process.
- Report a cleanup or admission failure once, naming the real holder and the remedy, rather than on every sidebar refresh.
- Write the PID on acquire, or stop claiming to know it.

**Workaround:** end the stale process (`kill -CONT <pid>; kill <pid>` for a suspended one), then start a new session.

milestone.title: v0.11
milestone.description:
Planned architecture release. Reuse this existing milestone rather than creating a competing v0.11.0 bucket.

Scope approved November 5, 2026: gix read-path adoption, coarse host/crate decomposition, completion of the command-contract frontier, typed Responses profiles and tool projection, embedder capability contracts, incremental context-folding/model-invoked compaction, and optional independent goal verification.

Complete every admitted consumer of a migration, retain a single turn loop/request authority, and qualify platform, cancellation and recovery behavior. Existing PRs and historical completed work stay attached. No due date or publication commitment.

issues.body:
<!-- status-at-0.10.1 -->
> **Status at 0.10.1** (re-triaged 2026-10-08): not started. Filed against v0.9.3 (filed 2026-08-02 for the v0.9.4 milestone).
>
> **What remains**
> - Introduce one typed Responses dialect policy (as data, per the 2026-08-07 overlay) covering store/include, instructions vs system item, sampling fields, max_output_tokens, reasoning shape and replay for the three live dialects: OpenAI Codex, DeepSeek, Concentrate
> - Refactor crates/tui/src/client/responses.rs (`build_responses_body_for_provider` and the input-replay builder near :815) to read that policy instead of ProviderKind checks
> - Add JSON-in / expected-wire-out golden fixtures for request bodies and SSE (split function-call args, usage, malformed/out-of-order events) runnable offline
> - Document how to add a new profile and its fixtures
>
> **Checked in the 0.10.1 source**
> - No `ResponsesDialectProfile` or equivalent type at the tag: `git grep -il 'ResponsesDialect\|responses_dialect' v0.10.1` matches only crates/tui/src/integrations/dsh/tests.rs
> - `build_responses_body_for_provider` still takes a ProviderKind and branches on it: crates/tui/src/client/responses.rs:45-58 (signature, `is_deepseek`, `is_concentrate`), :64, :72, :75, :109, :118, :127
> - Input replay also branches on provider identity: crates/tui/src/client/responses.rs:815, :903, :913, :930, :987
> - A third hard-coded Responses dialect (Concentrate) was added since filing, so the branch count grew: crates/tui/src/client/responses.rs:51-58
> - No language-neutral fixture harness for Responses: the tag has only Rust unit tests in crates/tui/src/client/responses/tests.rs; crates/tui/src/conformance/ holds events/golden/hooks/mcp/prompt/sse/stream_json and nothing for the Responses dialect
> - No commit in v0.9.3..v0.10.1 references #5093 (`git log --grep '#5093'` empty)

---

## Problem

The Responses bridge already covers substantial request construction, streaming, tool calls, and usage handling, but provider-specific branches are embedded in the adapter and exercised as individual cases. Adding custom Responses routes without a table-driven dialect contract would make regressions likely in tool loops, reasoning, caching, and normalized usage.

v0.9.4 needs a typed dialect-policy seam backed by deterministic conformance fixtures. Both built-in and custom Responses routes should share one normalized runtime contract while declaring their wire differences explicitly.

## Current evidence

- `crates/tui/src/client/responses.rs` owns Responses request construction, SSE event parsing, function-call assembly, and usage extraction.
- `build_responses_body_for_provider` currently receives an `ApiProvider` and contains provider-specific request branches.
- `crates/tui/src/client.rs::prepare_outbound_request` is the shared no-I/O preparation seam used by execution and request preview.
- `crates/tui/src/client/prepared.rs` provides a typed prepared-request boundary suitable for snapshot and contract tests.
- #3019 and #3084 established the reliability and provider-adapter baselines that this work should preserve.

## Scope

1. Introduce an internal typed `ResponsesDialectProfile` (name may vary) that owns declared differences in:
   - endpoint and header policy
   - stateful versus stateless turns
   - reasoning field shape
   - supported sampling and output-token fields
   - `store` and `include` behavior
   - input replay requirements
   - supported server-side capabilities
2. Refactor request preparation to consume the profile instead of scattering provider identity checks through body construction. Provider identity may select a profile; it must not implicitly grant unrelated capabilities.
3. Add a table-driven conformance harness covering at least the standard and stateless/plain-reasoning profiles.
4. Cover outbound request fixtures for:
   - instructions/system input and exact model identity
   - function tools and schema sanitation
   - parallel tool-call policy
   - function-call outputs and multi-turn replay
   - reasoning configuration and reasoning summaries
   - stateful/stateless `store` and `include` behavior
5. Cover SSE fixtures for:
   - text and reasoning deltas
   - split function-call arguments
   - completion and usage events
   - unknown, malformed, duplicated, and out-of-order events
   - UTF-8 boundaries, idle timeout, retry, and terminal errors
6. Verify normalized usage and cache accounting for input, output, reasoning, cache hits, cache misses, and cache writes. Do not fabricate cost when a route has no known SKU.
7. Add a deterministic error matrix:
   - invalid profile/configuration fails before network
   - 400/401/403 errors fail fast with sanitized diagnostics
   - 429/5xx behavior follows the declared retry policy
8. Document how to add a new typed profile and its fixtures.

Tests must use loopback or in-process fixtures only; no live provider traffic.

## Key files

- `crates/tui/src/client/responses.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/client.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/client/prepared.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/models.rs`
- `crates/tui/src/client/cost_status.rs`
- Existing cache-guard and provider-native-search tests where capability gating intersects the profile

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Standard and stateless/plain-reasoning profiles pass the same normalized transcript and tool-loop contract wherever the capability is supported.
- [ ] Unsupported features fail before network access with an error naming the selected profile and capability.
- [ ] Production execution and request preview use the same profile-derived prepared request.
- [ ] Function-call argument fragments assemble correctly across event boundaries and never emit a partial tool call.
- [ ] Unknown or malformed events produce deterministic, sanitized behavior without hiding terminal provider errors.
- [ ] Reasoning, token, and cache usage survive normalization without double counting.
- [ ] Cost remains unknown unless the exact route/model SKU is registered.
- [ ] Fixture snapshots contain no credentials or account identifiers.
- [ ] The full harness runs offline and documents how another profile is added.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
- `cargo test -p codewhale-tui client::responses`
- `cargo test -p codewhale-tui client::prepared`
- `cargo test -p codewhale-tui cache_guard`
- `cargo clippy -p codewhale-tui --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- Confirm all fixtures are deterministic and require no provider credentials.

## Out of scope

- Live provider certification
- A user-programmable adapter language
- New provider authentication flows
- Default enablement of server-side tools
- Pricing additions without a verified SKU

## Related

- Parent architecture issue: #5092
- Responses reliability baseline: #3019
- Provider descriptor and adapter baseline: #3084

## Triage note

Milestone: **v0.9.4**. This is the adapter-extraction and offline proof slice for the parent architecture issue.

prs.title: fix(net): go direct when a local proxy disappears
prs.body:
## What and why

reqwest snapshots `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` / `ALL_PROXY` when a client is built, and Codewhale builds its engine HTTP clients once per session. A session started behind a local proxy (Clash, v2rayN, sing-box on `127.0.0.1:…`) therefore kept dialing that port after the proxy was closed: every request failed with a connect error, including requests to providers that need no proxy at all, and the only recovery was restarting Codewhale.

`codewhale_net::proxy::install_loopback_proxy()` installs a `reqwest::Proxy::custom` route for ambient **loopback** proxies:

- `no_proxy()` runs first, so the custom route is the only proxy source. `no_proxy()` clears every proxy registered before it, so the order matters: a request the callback declines cannot fall back to the address reqwest read when the client was built.
- A background thread probes each configured loopback proxy on its own port. While a port refuses connections, requests that would use it go direct; when it answers again, proxy routing resumes. A live `HTTP_PROXY` therefore does not keep a dead `HTTPS_PROXY` in the path.
- Only a definite `ECONNREFUSED` from every resolved address moves a proxy to direct. A timeout, an fd limit or a resolver failure leaves the previous state alone: routing a session direct on that evidence would put traffic on a network path the operator deliberately avoided.
- While the port answers, routing is unchanged: `ALL_PROXY` / `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` precedence, `NO_PROXY`, proxy credentials, and the existing socks5 → socks5h remote-DNS handling. A portless socks proxy defaults to 1080, as reqwest does, instead of silently disabling the fallback.
- IPv6 and IPv4-mapped IPv6 loopback proxies are watched too: `Url::host_str` keeps the brackets, so the address is unwrapped before it is matched and probed.
- Remote proxies are deliberately not watched. A configuration mixing a local and a remote proxy watches the local one and routes through the remote one exactly as before. An unreachable remote proxy is a network outage to report, not a boundary to route around.
- `CODEWHALE_LOCAL_PROXY_FALLBACK=0` restores the previous behaviour.

`crates/engine/src/lib.rs` gains one `platform_client_builder()`, and every engine client that used to call `codewhale_release::tls::reqwest_client_builder()` directly now starts there — the model client and the API-key verification probe, models, the HTTP/1.1 fallback, vision, web search, web run, finance, the dev-server readiness probe, the MCP registry, `models.dev` and the profile constitution check. The TUI balance poll and the app-server relay install the same route. Half-fixing this was worse than not fixing it: a session where the model works and every tool fails reads as a tool bug. Reviewed plugin remotes and guarded fetches keep their own no-proxy builder on purpose.

Two details worth calling out because they decided the design:

- **Windows needs about two seconds to report a refused loopback connection.** `TcpStream::connect_timeout` with a 300 ms bound returns `TimedOut` and never sees the refusal, so the fallback would never engage on the platform the report came from. The probe bound is 4 s.
- **`HTTPS_PROXY` does not proxy `http://` destinations.** That is reqwest's semantics and this change preserves it, which is why the end-to-end test configures `ALL_PROXY`.

Known limitations, stated in the code and the docs: reachability is a TCP connect rather than a proxy handshake, so a process that holds the port without forwarding traffic still counts as up; detection takes a few seconds, so a request issued in that gap can still fail once; and going direct leaves from the machine's own address. Not covered: `doctor`'s search probe, the Runtime API runtime-info probe, `cloud-facts` refreshes and the sandbox client.

## Issue

No-Issue: reported from a local session that lost its proxy mid-run; no tracking issue exists.

## How I tested it

`cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes, `cargo clippy -p codewhale-net --lib --no-deps --all-targets` is clean, and `cargo check -p codewhale-engine -p codewhale-app-server -p codewhale-tui --lib` finishes.

`cargo test -p codewhale-net --lib proxy` → `test result: ok. 32 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 39 filtered out`, and `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` → `test result: ok. 2 passed`. The end-to-end case uses a real `reqwest::Client`: with the proxy port closed the request fails, after one probe it reaches a local target server and returns `200`. Other cases cover a refused port switching to direct, a returning port switching back, per-proxy isolation (live http, dead https), `ALL_PROXY` / `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` precedence, `HTTPS_PROXY` leaving http targets direct, IPv6 and IPv4-mapped loopback, a portless socks default, remote and mixed configurations, `NO_PROXY` whitespace and `*`, credentials surviving the route, and the install order.

End-to-end on Windows against the real API (no key configured, so a `401` proves the request reached it) with a throwaway harness that built the same client and installed the fallback:

- `HTTPS_PROXY=http://127.0.0.1:<closed port>` → `ok status=401 Unauthorized` (went direct).
- Proxy answering at startup, killed mid-session, same client requested again after the probe → first request went through the stub proxy and failed there, second returned `ok status=401 Unauthorized`.
- `NO_PROXY=api.deepseek.com` with a live stub proxy → `ok status=401 Unauthorized` (went direct).

Not run locally: the interactive TUI against a real Clash/v2rayN session, and the full workspace suite (left to CI).

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main`
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [x] If this adds or changes a user-facing feature, I updated its docs and its row in `docs/features.toml` — `local-proxy-fallback`, documented in `docs/INSTALL.md` and listed in `docs/CONFIGURATION.md`

## Attribution

🤖 Generated by SpikeBot 000(CodeWhale-LOCAL)

Bumps [codewhale-hq/Codewhale](https://github.com/codewhale-hq/codewhale) from b92540d882b8e7c66389aa35e5fa0c3c178fe4ce to b0b2b9a335cc1d24abe8a087189bed080d1cc3db.
Changelog

Sourced from codewhale-hq/Codewhale's changelog.

Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

[Unreleased]

[0.10.3] - 2026-11-06

This is the Codewhale v0.10.3 source candidate. It is not a published release until the matching tag, packages, checksums, and release assets exist.

Added

  • Present final files: the read-only present tool takes 1–32 existing workspace files, streams their SHA-256 and byte counts, and returns an auditable handoff receipt without copying, moving or uploading them. It is eager in Act/Operate and Plan; the present-handoff feature is experimental, and there is no dedicated app card yet.

  • Truthful background jobs: shell job snapshots and completion events now carry the exact start time, a typed termination cause (producer, killed, timed_out, unknown) and whether the producer reported it. A killed job is no longer indistinguishable from a failed one, and the bash guidance tells the model to collect or cancel live jobs before a final answer.

  • /export writes HTML and JSON: /export file report.html saves a self-contained page (light and dark, no scripts, a strict content-security policy, tool calls collapsed) and report.json a versioned, typed-block envelope. --format md|html|json overrides the extension, and --no-tools drops tool calls and results from the conversation. /export file with no path now writes an auto-named codewhale-<title>-<timestamp> file under <codewhale home>/exports and reports the format, line count and redactions; ~ expands and quotes keep a path with spaces together. --force, --no-tools and --format are accepted in any position. HTML and JSON are file-only; the clipboard and /export turn remain Markdown.

  • Tencent HY4: the stable tencent/hy4 model is available through OpenRouter with its published multimodal, tool, reasoning and context metadata. /provider tencent adds the direct TokenHub route with hy4 and TENCENT_API_KEY; direct availability and prices remain separate from OpenRouter, and preview/HY3 selections are preserved.

  • WeCom steers a running turn (#7211): a WeCom message sent while a turn is running is forwarded to the Runtime's steer endpoint instead of being dropped with the busy notice, which remains the fallback when the steer is rejected. Thanks @​gaord.

  • WeCom accepts media and voice (#7212): the WeCom bridge downloads image, video and file messages into WECOM_MEDIA_DIR (default <workspace>/media) under a sanitized name and replies with the saved name, size and path; a failed download tells the sender the link expires after about five minutes. Voice messages use WeCom's transcription as the prompt, and other message types get an explicit answer instead of a blanket refusal. Thanks @​gaord.

  • Pinned local thread controls (preview): initialized App Server clients can list retained loaded Engines with cursor paging and rename the canonical thread through thread/loaded/list and thread/name/set. Saved but unloaded threads stay out of the loaded list; existing aliases remain available. Full-tool turns and subscription parity remain unfinished.

  • Local whale voice (preview): the host can edit its private, revision-checked SOUL.md through the Runtime API. The Engine captures it for the next turn within the existing instruction budget and records its source; invalid private files refuse the turn with a terminal failure.

  • MCP tool approval rules (preview): exact tool names in the global server configuration can use Always, Ask or Off across workspaces. Off wins, server edits invalidate the prior grant, and required Computer Use consent and nested-program approval remain in place.

  • Attested watch-turn ingress (preview): a configured Runtime master bearer can admit typed schedule or pull-request receipts through the existing thread and turn owner, with exact operation replay and read-only recovery lookup. This supplies the Native ingress prerequisite; it does not qualify the complete continuous-operation workflow.

  • Goal continuations send the objective once per live conversation window. Later passes show the current goal state, estimated conversation input and the applicable compaction setting. Full notes stay available through get_goal. Thanks @​7jrxt42BxFZo4iAnN4CX for measuring the repeated text and identifying the misleading token figure (#7172).

  • Composition on the first request: execute_tools accepts a bounded named batch from the current MCP catalog, with argument names from its allowed members and the same nested gate as a JavaScript program. Exact tool-name searches work with regex anchors. Stream receipts hash the executable in the background; CODEWHALE_TIMING=1 reports phase durations. (CW-7649)

Each message is masked whole for credential shapes and currently configured secrets before it is searched or paged, and codewhale sessions scrub-secrets now also rewrites those snapshots. A /fork cannot read the archive its handoff note refers to, and a bare secret

prs.title: chore(deps): bump similar from 3.2.0 to 3.2.1
prs.body:
Bumps [similar](https://github.com/mitsuhiko/similar) from 3.2.0 to 3.2.1.
Changelog

Sourced from similar's changelog.

3.2.1

  • Improved real-world diffing performance substantially without changing the produced diffs. On a corpus of real source file revisions, line diffs run about 4x faster with Algorithm::Myers, 5x faster with Algorithm::Histogram, and 2.5x faster with Algorithm::Patience; word diffs run about 2x faster. This comes from a faster line tokenizer, a SipHash-1-3 content hash that consumes whole words (randomly keyed with std), cheaper integer-keyed lookup tables, hashing only the changed middle of Myers line diffs, flat occurrence tables in Histogram, and a gap buffer in the compaction pass that was quadratic on diffs with many ops. Allocation counts and peak memory dropped as well; in particular one sided and heavily unbalanced inputs no longer build index structures proportional to the larger side for Algorithm::Hunt, Algorithm::Histogram, and Algorithm::Patience.
  • Fixed Algorithm::Histogram overflowing the stack on inputs with many scattered changes. Pending ranges are now tracked on the heap, so stack usage no longer grows with the number of anchors. #105
  • Fixed TextMerge::labels writing carriage returns and newlines verbatim into conflict markers, which let a label add lines to the output that looked like merged content. Line terminators in labels are now replaced with spaces. #101
Commits
  • 71d4831 chore(release): prepare 3.2.1
  • b61e6c3 test(histogram): skip small stack tests on WASI
  • a4ee936 fix(histogram): track pending ranges on the heap
  • 96993d9 docs: add runnable example output gallery (#104)
  • 1c64280 docs(changelog): describe diff performance and memory improvements
  • a3da6ec perf(compact): use a gap buffer for large operation lists
  • ce3a403 perf(histogram): reuse indexes and bound unbalanced input allocations
  • 2bcae2f perf(myers): skip unchanged hashing and unused split bookkeeping
  • 5a5aa8d perf(text): accelerate line and word tokenization
  • 80bc240 perf(hash): accelerate content hashing and integer lookups

prs.title: feat(tasks): pause the task wall clock for answerable human waits
prs.body:
## What and why

Upstream's turn layer already treats human waits as outside the budget — `crates/runtime/src/turn_budget.rs`: "the budget bounds what the agent spends on its own, not how long a person takes to answer." #6118 already suspends the task idle watchdog while an approval is pending. The durable task wall clock, however, still bounds a run parked on its own prompt — task_manager's #6118 note records that bound deliberately ("`0` waits indefinitely by configuration; the wall deadline still bounds the run"). For an automation run with no operator at the keyboard, that bound interrupts the run at the wall deadline, withdrawing the pending approval on the host's behalf (`ApprovalOutcome::Cancelled` — a withdrawal, not a denial) and discarding the run.

This pauses the durable task wall clock while a prompt on the run itself awaits a decision — deliberately relaxing that documented bound, and only where a decision surface can actually answer:

- `TaskManagerConfig::human_waits_answerable` (default **false** — TUI-managed tasks behave exactly as today). The app-server runtime API opts in: its tasks are answerable via `POST /v1/approvals/{id}` and `submit_user_input`.
- While a prompt is pending, the wall deadline moves with each closed window (preserving #5898's crossed-first attribution — a crossing before a window still terminalizes `WallTimeout` at the moved deadline). A 24h aggregate fail-safe cap (`human_wait_cap`, new `human_wait_timeout` terminal reason) bounds the exclusion across the whole task, and Cancel/Shutdown classification outranks a spent cap so a canceled task is never mislabeled.
- Parked decision polling backs off 200ms → 2s; a decision wakes it immediately.
- Idle handling composes with #6118 (unchanged): a window close restarts the idle budget fresh.

`[approval] timeout_seconds` is unchanged and remains the lever for bounding the wait on the human's side; this changes only the task supervisor's accounting. The feature row `thread-scheduled-turns` in docs/features.toml is updated (its `api` surface is where the opt-in lives).

## Issue

No-Issue: extends the documented turn-layer human-wait philosophy to the durable task layer; complements #6118 (unchanged).

## How I tested it

- Red-on-base evidence via mutation runs recorded in the commit (raw wall clock, cap hoisted above cancel/shutdown, aggregate arm removed, gate removed, server flag off — each flips a named test).
- Targeted suites: `human_wait`/`execution_guard` filters → 21 passed, 0 failed (two new ordering/attribution pins included: cancel outranks a spent **parked** cap; `WallTimeout` attribution at the moved deadline); task_manager module → 101 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored; app-server `server_task` pins → 2 passed; `cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` → 2 passed.
- Zero-regression pin: an unanswerable (default) surface still wall-times out through a prompt, asserting no window is armed.
- Honest limits: the `run_http_server` call-site hop is not test-pinned (pinning it requires booting the server); the two runtime_api pins cover the builder and executor-forward hops.

## Checklist

- [x] One focused change, started from current `main` (no need to rebase when `main` moves)
- [x] `cargo fmt --all` passes, and tests cover new or changed behavior
- [x] User-facing feature: docs/RUNTIME_API.md updated and the `thread-scheduled-turns` row in docs/features.toml updated (`cargo test -p codewhale-tui --test feature_registry` passes)

prs.title: feat: add bounded HTTP rate-limit recovery
prs.body:
HTTP 429 currently shares the short ordinary transport retry allowance, so a temporary provider limit can abort a request before capacity recovers. This change gives native HTTP calls an independent, validated recovery policy: 20 total attempts including the first, a 600-second recovery budget, and exponential equal jitter from a 5-second base to a 60-second local ceiling, while preserving server minima.

Known quota windows and minima that do not fit the recovery window stop automatic short retries. Typed errors distinguish a provider rejection from admission without dispatch, retain quota/account guidance and the original reset advice, and make no claim that the transport saved a checkpoint. Shared provider pauses and automatic rate-retry sleeps are bounded at one hour. The public total-timeout budget is rechecked before another attempt, including after time spent in callbacks.

Native MiniMax/Zai JSON error inspection has a 32 MiB size limit and the caller's first-byte/idle deadlines. Complete normalized refusals settle the original HTTP attempt; uncertain reads or parse results retain unknown outcomes. Both ordinary and isolated senders use the same rules. Ordinary transport retries retain successful-recovery receipts. Unknown 503/499 inference outcomes are never automatically replayed.

The configuration reference explains the separate `[retry.rate_limit]` fields, validation ranges and interaction with legacy retry settings. `retry.enabled = false` disables this HTTP retry loop; the existing safe pre-dispatch HTTP/1.1 fallback within stream opening remains possible.

This is a transport-only contribution. Existing stream recovery, task continuation and host checkpoint lifecycle remain caller-owned. It adds no task scheduler, persisted checkpoint, host UI protocol or shared task-operation budget across outer retries.

No-Issue: Contributor-proposed transport recovery improvement; no existing issue is being closed.

## Main integration

Follow-up commit: [`43a80ea`](https://github.com/Pinvou/CodeWhale/commit/43a80ea0a56d3865e9344cf4d2a8c94b2c9676a1).

Merged upstream main at `13760312`. The Responses conflict retains the precise unknown-outcome test names, main's exact one-attempt checks and the typed 503/499 assertions. Accepted upstream usage-ledger fixes are inherited from main; no separate unrelated CI repair is added to this contribution.

## Validation

Windows, rustc 1.99.1, locked dependencies; combined with upstream `13760312`.

- Engine `rate_limit` filter: 37 passed, including all four ordinary/isolated sender and quota/billing settlement cases, bounded native reads, long hints and child pause behavior.
- Responses unknown-outcome checks: 2 passed; scoped retry recovery/exhaustion: 2 passed. Long-minimum refusal, Engine receipts, child classification, concurrent observation scopes, worker wall budget and native reservation/projection: 1 passed each. These selections cover 47 distinct Engine tests from the candidate source tree.
- A separate local probe of the public `with_retry` API passed: after a real monotonic-clock callback barrier crossed a 1-second budget, the fixed code made one attempt and retained the original typed 503. Removing the guard made two attempts. Removing native refusal settlement separately in each sender failed the original `OutcomeUnknown` versus `Rejected` assertion. All three negative controls failed for the expected reason; the fixed production bytes were restored before the positive runs.
- Original candidate Runtime retry-status tests: 7 passed. Full workspace formatting, version consistency, staged whitespace and dead-code budget checks passed.

The Engine runs used an isolated candidate-source copy with test-only native case tracing/selection and the local deadline probe. Production source and the lockfile match the submitted candidate. Runtime and scoped Clippy use the original source tree. No test-only probe or selector is included in the PR.

Clippy on the original candidate is **not reported as fully passing**. The strict invocation stopped on the unchanged Windows UTF-16 decoder's `chunks_exact_to_as_chunks` lint. A diagnostic continuation allowing that lint exposed the existing sandbox `ReadDenial` size lint and two non-Unix plugin-GC permission lints.

Primary-crate checks used `--no-deps --lib --tests --all-features --locked` with the three CI lint allowances, so dependency lints could not mask the changed crates. Engine library and unit targets each reported the same two existing Windows lint sites: pointer alignment in `extension_host/windows.rs` and the conservative tail return in `mcp.rs`. Runtime completed with the additional, explicitly recorded UTF-16 decoder lint allowance. The affected types, platform conditions and callers were checked against main; these findings are unrelated to this contribution. No source or lint-budget changes were added to address them, and no global error-size exemption was used.

The unchanged blocking-call checker exits 1 on Windows because its backslash path keys do not match the POSIX budget keys. A diagnostic comparison of its complete measurements with normalized path keys found no excess (641 sites in 173 files). This is not an official checker pass or a Linux result; neither the checker nor its budget was changed in this PR. Historical results from older trees are not current-head results.

No live-provider traffic, non-Windows native run, whole-workspace test run, packaged artifact or full host restart/continuation workflow is claimed. External review and applicable current-head CI remain merge prerequisites.

issues.body:
## Bug type

Behavior bug (source-verified; microphone reproduction still pending).

## Summary

When Voice Wake is set to start Talk Mode on macOS, the configured trigger-to-session routing rule is skipped, so Talk can use the active native chat or main session instead.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a Voice Wake trigger to target a non-main session with `voicewake.routing`.
2. Enable **Trigger Talk Mode** on the macOS app and invoke that trigger.
3. Inspect the resulting Talk session target.

Source trace on current `main` (`94c0f0d5`): `VoiceWakeRuntime.beginCapture` calls `setTalkEnabled(true)` without passing the recognized trigger. Native Talk selects `WebChatManager.shared.activeSessionKey` or main in `TalkModeRuntime.sendAndSpeak`; realtime Talk independently selects the active chat or bootstrap main in `TalkModeRuntime.makeRealtimeRelaySession`. Neither path consults Voice Wake routing. This is a source-level reproduction, not a claim that a physical microphone run was completed.

## Expected behavior

Wake-started Talk uses the session selected by the matched Gateway Voice Wake routing rule for the whole conversation, including follow-ups.

## Actual behavior

The configured rule is not consulted by wake-started Talk. One-shot Voice Wake forwarding does apply it through the Gateway agent-turn path.

## Environment

- OpenClaw: behavior exists in installed `2026.9.7` and current `main` source at `94c0f0d5`.
- OS: macOS 26+ Voice Wake path.
- Install method: macOS app connected to a Gateway.
- Model and provider/routing chain: not relevant to session selection.

## Impact

A wake command can enter an unrelated conversation context when a user has configured a dedicated voice session. Frequency: every wake-started Talk activation using an explicit routing rule in the source path; live acoustic frequency has not yet been measured.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Summary

On Android/Termux, `openclaw gateway run` and `openclaw doctor --lint` fail with `SQLite read-only worker failed while creating its private snapshot: permission denied (EACCES)`. The read-only snapshot is published with a hard link (`fs.linkSync` in `@openclaw/fs-safe` [`src/publish-copy-stage.ts:40`](https://github.com/openclaw/fs-safe/blob/50fd5171eecc127f9609fa72153cd0aa121dbc95/src/publish-copy-stage.ts#L40)), and Android denies hard links to every app, in private and shared storage alike. Termux maintainers: "Android restricts creating hardlinks, no matter if it is private (termux's filesystem) or shared... All termux packages are patched to avoid using hardlinks" ([termux/termux-packages#21167](https://github.com/termux/termux-packages/issues/21167)).

This is the next blocker after #167623 (fixed by #167719): once the database is no longer refused as "generation changed", Termux stops here.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Android 15 (API 35) arm64 emulator, Termux v0.118.3 (GitHub release), `pkg install nodejs` (v26.4.0).
2. Install the build from #167719 (or any build that passes database admission on Android).
3. Run `openclaw gateway run --allow-unconfigured` or `openclaw doctor --lint` with an existing `~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite`.

### Expected behavior

The read-only worker creates its private snapshot and the Gateway/Doctor continue, or fall back to a publication method Android allows.

### Actual behavior

```text
[openclaw] Reason: Cannot read shared state for discovery: ~/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite. Retry after the current state operation completes. Error: SQLite read-only worker failed while creating its private snapshot: permission denied (EACCES); snapshot staging root ~/.cache/openclaw/openclaw-sqlite-readonly-v2-L030Lo: check filesystem health and write permissions or set XDG_CACHE_HOME to a writable filesystem (code=EACCES)
```

The suggested `XDG_CACHE_HOME` change cannot help: the restriction applies to every app-writable location.

Probe in the same Termux session (Node v26.4.0, `~/.cache/openclaw`):

```text
writeFile ok | chmod 600 ok | link (hard link) EACCES | copyFile ok | copyFile FICLONE ok | rename dir ok | sqlite open+write ok | sqlite readonly ok
```

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.9 plus #167719 (d37860c); released 2026.9.9 fails earlier with #167623.

### Operating system

Android 15 (API 35, arm64 emulator), Termux v0.118.3

### Install method

npm global install inside Termux

### Model

Not applicable (local state admission; no model call)

### Provider / routing chain

Not applicable

### Additional information

`@openclaw/fs-safe` already falls back when `RENAME_NOREPLACE` is unsupported (openclaw/fs-safe#843, openclaw/fs-safe#838, openclaw/fs-safe#876). A comparable fallback when `link()` is refused on Android may be the narrowest repair, but it changes a no-replace publication primitive, so I'm reporting it before proposing code.

issues.body:
### Summary

A single model request that runs longer than the cache TTL makes client-side `cache-ttl` pruning trim the tool results of the run that is still using them. We would like a way to protect the current run, and/or a TTL that follows the provider's actual prompt-cache retention.

### Problem to solve

Since #140713, the pruning clock is the start of the last successful model request. That is right for a cache whose lifetime is refreshed when it is read. It has a side effect inside tool loops: a single request that generates for longer than the TTL opens the TTL gate for the very next request of the same loop. Examples are composing a large `write` or `exec` argument, or reasoning for minutes. Its own output often pushes usage past 30% as well. Every tool result older than the third-to-last assistant message is then trimmed if it is over 4,000 characters, or cleared at 50%+ usage.

In a tool loop, "the last three assistant messages" is the last three tool calls, not the current user turn. So the results being pruned are frequently the ones the agent is in the middle of using.

On OpenAI models the premise behind a 5-minute TTL (that the cache is cold by then, so trimming is free) does not hold in our data. The prompt cache usually still hits at 5–10 minute gaps. Pruning in that band therefore costs cache reads instead of saving cache writes.

### Proposed solution

This is a product decision, so we list options. Any one would help.

1. **Per-provider (or per-model) TTL.** For example, a provider hook or a `contextPruning.ttl` keyed by provider, so OpenAI can use a longer TTL than Anthropic's 5 minutes. Today `contextPruning` exists only at `agents.defaults`.
2. **Opt-in protection of the current run.** For example, `contextPruning.protectCurrentRun: true`, which never prunes tool results produced after the user message that started the active run. It trades cache cost for task integrity, and it only matters when a single request exceeded the TTL.
3. **Per-agent `contextPruning` settings at least.** Agents that read heavily and then compose could then run with a longer TTL, without changing the whole fleet.

### Alternatives considered

- **Raising the global TTL.** We moved from 5m to 10m. It removes the cases we observed, but it is fleet-wide, and any request longer than 10 minutes still triggers the same behavior.
- **Prompt rules for incremental persistence and re-reading after a trim.** We added these. They have to live in every skill that reads and then composes, and they do not help an agent that has not seen them.
- **Turning pruning off.** That loses the benefit on long idle-gap sessions, where pruning is useful.

### Impact

- **Affected:** agents that read many or large files and then compose a large output in one response: audits, report and wiki compilation, long syntheses. Most visible on providers whose cache outlives the TTL.
- **Severity:** silent quality loss or lost work. The agent continues on excerpts or discards what it produced (see the companion issue for the notice side).
- **Frequency** (our deployment, 2 weeks, about 4.2k sessions): 28 pruning rounds.
  - 15 inside the run that produced the trimmed results. For the 13 with trajectory data, the request before the pruning request ran 303–464 s, produced 6k–28k output tokens, and ended normally with `stop=toolUse`.
  - 2 of those were hard-clears inside the running turn, of 22 and 38 results.
  - The other 13 were turn-boundary rounds after idle gaps or subagent settle wakes, the case pruning is designed for.
- **Consequence:** re-runs and degraded results. In one case a complete 177/177 output was overwritten with 14 items.

### Evidence/examples

OpenAI prompt-cache hit ratio (cacheRead / prompt tokens, prompts over 20k tokens) by gap between consecutive request starts in one session:

| gap | pruned in between | n | median hit |
|---|---|---|---|
| < 60 s | no | 34,925 | 0.972 |
| 60–300 s | no | 1,965 | 0.941 |
| 300–600 s | no | 215 | 0.749 |
| 300–600 s | yes | 14 | 0.253 |
| 600–1,800 s | no | 145 | 0.000 |

Related: #140713 (per-request clock, merged), #137021, #58284 (turn-based pruning request, closed), PR #96383 (proposed a 30-minute TTL for OpenAI, closed unmerged).

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

Companion issue, about making the trim notice say that it is pruning and that the source can be re-read: #167786.

issues.body:
Any registered `before_agent_finalize` handler makes every embedded run hold its assistant output until the final answer (the hold is decided from `hookRunner.hasHooks("before_agent_finalize")` with no context, `prepareEmbeddedAttemptStream`; docs/concepts/streaming.md says so). That is the right contract for a handler that may revise what a person is about to read (#92382). But a plugin that only needs to revise scheduled runs (a heartbeat's or a cron job's final answer before it is delivered) has no way to say so. Registering it freezes every interactive chat on the gateway: the Control UI shows nothing until the whole reply lands.

Repro, on a stock gateway with nothing else loaded (2026.9.6 and 2026.9.9; the 2026.10.1-beta.2 code path reads the same): a plugin whose `register` adds `api.on("before_agent_finalize", () => undefined)` (enabled with `plugins.entries.<id>.hooks.allowConversationAccess: true`, as docs/cli/plugins/list.md requires), and a scripted model streaming a 12-chunk reply. A client subscribed with `sessions.messages.subscribe`, as the Control UI is, receives 12 `chat` deltas without the plugin and ONE delta carrying the whole reply, at its end, with it (2026.9.6: 12 deltas from 2.3 s to 5.1 s vs 1 at 5.1 s; 2026.9.9: 12 from 1.5 s to 4.3 s vs 1 at 4.6 s). The same plugin with the `api.on` line removed streams all 12, so the hook, not the plugin load, causes the hold.

Proposal:
1. Accept `eligibleTriggers` (`cron`, `heartbeat`, `user`) on `before_agent_finalize`, enforced by the host before invocation, exactly as it is for `before_agent_reply`.
2. Decide the hold per attempt from the handlers eligible for that attempt's trigger: `hasHooks("before_agent_finalize", { trigger: attempt.trigger })` (the `ctx` form `hasHooks` already supports through `isHookContextEligible`). A user turn with no eligible handler then streams as if none were registered. A scheduled run keeps today's contract.
3. Optionally, for the "observe or wait, never revise" case (a handler that only holds the turn's end until something it started has settled), a registration flag such as `mayRevise: false` that runs the handler without holding output. This is the "preview mode" suggested on #92382, and we would use it too.

Two related gaps on the scheduled-result path, which are why a finalize handler is the only place left to fix a scheduled run's answer:
- A `current`-session cron result is committed with `commitBackgroundResultToSession` → `persistSessionTranscriptTurn` and runs no plugin hook (dist/run-delivery.runtime-BsyGE_KF.mjs:42-168 on 2026.9.6; `run-delivery.runtime-C4Cgxa0F.mjs:39` on 2026.9.9). Yet docs/automation/cron-jobs/delivery.md says it is committed "through the canonical transcript writer", and docs/plugins/hooks/tool-policy.md says `before_message_write` operates on OpenClaw-owned transcript writes. Measured: with a `before_message_write` handler that rewrites assistant text, a tool-less job's DeepSeek DSML markup and a reasoning-plus-token answer were both committed unchanged. Running `before_message_write` on that commit, or a dedicated scheduled-result hook, would close it.
- The silent-reply handling there (`normalizeSilentReplyText`, dist/delivery-dispatch-policy-Cf7nqpRg.mjs:29-47, used at dist/run-delivery.runtime-BsyGE_KF.mjs:1043-1045) treats reasoning that ends in a bare `NO_REPLY` as silent. Measured: not delivered. It misses the same ending followed by punctuation or markdown: "... Appropriate response: NO_REPLY." was delivered whole. The trailing pattern (`getSilentTrailingRegex`, dist/tokens-BTKQYTUd.mjs) allows leading `*` but nothing after the token. Tolerating trailing `.`, `!`, `*`, backticks or quotes after the final token would match what models actually write. (Related, on the heartbeat path: #138229.)

issues.body:
### Summary

For self-hosted OpenAI-compatible backends (vLLM, llama.cpp, LM Studio, etc.) configured as a custom provider with `api: "openai-completions"`, there is currently no native way to keep tool-heavy scheduled turns inside the context budget:

1. `agents.defaults.contextPruning.mode: "cache-ttl"` is not eligible for these providers (eligibility covers Anthropic/Google, plugins, and since 2026.9.6 official OpenAI routes / opted-in OpenAI proxies). A custom `openai-completions` provider id never gets the `openclaw.cache-ttl` marker, so old tool results are never pruned. Related but different: #159089 (custom id with `openai-responses`, closed) and #95840 (official OpenAI, closed).
2. The number of mid-turn overflow recovery attempts is fixed in code (3). #150513 (2026.9.6) renews the allowance after successful progress, which helps; it would still be useful to make the allowance configurable (e.g. `compaction.midTurnPrecheck.maxRecoveryAttempts`) for operators running small-context local models.

### Use case

Scheduled isolated agent turns doing web research on a local model with ~98k `contextTokens`. Each research round adds two or three ~10–16k-char tool results; the turn compacts mid-turn, then refills within a few rounds, and fails once the recovery allowance is used up. The local backend has no prompt cache cost model, so pruning stale tool results (or truncating them to a short placeholder) after they have been consumed would be safe and would keep these turns well inside the budget.

### Proposal

- Let `contextPruning` be enabled explicitly for a custom provider/model, e.g. `models.providers.<id>.models[].compat.contextPruning: true` (or `compat.supportsPromptCacheKey`-style opt-in), independent of prompt-cache semantics — for local backends the goal is context size, not cache economics. A non-TTL mode (prune tool results older than N tool turns) would fit local models even better.
- Expose the mid-turn recovery allowance as config, keeping the current value as default.

### Environment

OpenClaw 2026.9.5, Linux, Docker gateway; provider `api: openai-completions` → vLLM (Qwen3.8 27B FP8, 131k window, `contextTokens 98304`); `compaction.mode: safeguard`, `midTurnPrecheck.enabled: true`.

Related: #101929 (tool-result token over-estimation), #9986 (fallback on context overflow).

issues.body:
### Summary
On Windows, when a fresh restart has already been scheduled (e.g. after a model-provider `Apply`, or after another deferred/rollback restart), `openclaw gateway restart` returns a **deferred** result and exits 0 immediately:

```
gateway restart -> safe restart requested; will restart momentarily (async)
```

The actual restart then happens later, on a schedule, up to minutes afterwards. During that window the Scheduled Task stays in state `Running` while the old worker keeps serving — and if the old worker was already gone, the task is `Running` but **not serving** (`/healthz` refused) until the deferred restart triggers.

### Why it matters
Operational tooling (maintenance scripts, model-apply hooks, supervisors) has exactly two signals: the `restart` command's exit code (0 = "requested") and `/healthz`. With async deferral:

1. `restart` exits 0 **before** anything restarts → "I restarted" reports success that hasn't happened yet.
2. `/healthz` can go down for minutes while the task is still `Running` — a supervisor that only checks the task state sees "Running" and does nothing for the whole window.
3. On 2026-10-09 both of our machines were left in "task `Running` but not serving" for ~3–5 min after this path, recoverable only by manual `schtasks /End` + `schtasks /Run`.

### Expected behavior
- CLI detects the pending restart and surfaces it: e.g. `gateway restart` reports `restart deferred; current pid <pid> still serving` and exits non-zero (or `gateway restart --wait` that blocks until the **new** pid serves `/healthz`), and/or
- `gateway status --json` exposes a `pendingRestart: { scheduledAt, reason }` field, and/or
- the gateway exposes a state distinct from "the process is up": `/healthz` already does this ("live" via app-level checks), but the task-state/supervisor contract should expose it so external watchers can stop treating `Running` as "serving".

### Repro
1. Windows, task `OpenClaw Gateway` running.
2. Arrange a scheduled restart (e.g. model `Apply` that changes `models.providers`, or `gateway restart` while one is already deferred).
3. `openclaw gateway restart` → deferred announcement, exit 0.
4. Watch: task state `Running`, but `/healthz` refused until the deferred restart fires (minutes later).

### Environment
OpenClaw 2026.9.9, Windows 11 Pro, Node 24.x, gateway via Windows Scheduled Task with `--task-supervisor`.

issues.body:
### Summary

Make the cache-TTL soft-trim notice say that it is context pruning, and that the original tool result is unchanged and can be fetched again. The image marker already says this.

### Problem to solve

On 2026.9.9, client-side `cache-ttl` pruning projects an older text tool result as:

```
<first 1500 chars>
...
<last 1500 chars>

[Tool result trimmed: kept first 1500 chars and last 1500 chars of N chars.]
```

To the model this reads as "the tool returned a truncated result". It cannot tell that its own context was shortened later, nor that the full text was in its context a few requests earlier. The image counterpart is unambiguous: `[image removed during context pruning]`. The hard-clear default `[Old tool result content cleared]` has the same ambiguity, although that one can be overridden with `hardClear.placeholder`. The soft-trim text cannot be overridden.

How this cost us a complete result, in a real run (one turn, one session):

1. The agent read 7 files whole, 12k–32k characters each, and noted in its plan that it had read all the items in them.
2. In one request it composed the complete output from those reads: 177 of 177 items, written to a file in an 84.5k-character `write` call. The request ran 331 s.
3. The next request pruned 16 older tool results (soft), because the TTL had elapsed since the start of the previous request and usage was 35%.
4. The agent saw the notice, logged an "integrity correction: the returns were truncated by the runtime", and marked the 7 files as not read. It then overwrote its complete output with only the 14 items whose text sat inside the kept head and tail windows.

Nothing told the agent that its earlier work had been done on whole text, or that it could simply read the files again.

The session-pruning docs describe the soft-trim as "first and last 1,500 characters with `...` in between" and do not mention the appended line.

### Proposed solution

- Make the soft-trim marker self-describing and actionable, for example:
  `[Context pruning: this older tool result was shortened to its first 1500 and last 1500 of N chars to save context. The original output is unchanged; run the tool again if you need the full text.]`
- Give the hard-clear default placeholder the same two facts: it was pruning, and the tool can be re-run.
- Document the exact strings on the session-pruning page.

### Alternatives considered

- **Tell every agent in its prompt that a trim line means context pruning.** We did this, but it has to be repeated in every agent and skill, and the agent still has to map a generic "trimmed" line to it.
- **`hardClear.placeholder`.** It covers only the hard-clear case, not the soft trim, which is what most rounds produce.

### Impact

- **Affected:** any agent with `contextPruning.mode: "cache-ttl"` that reads large tool results and keeps working on them across a long request or an idle gap.
- **Severity:** silent quality loss. The agent discards or downgrades correct work, or treats excerpts as complete results, and no error surfaces.
- **Frequency:** intermittent. In our deployment: 28 pruning rounds in 2 weeks across about 4.2k sessions. 15 of them trimmed results produced inside the run that was still using them.
- **Consequence:** lost work and re-runs (in the case above, a second full run), or conclusions drawn from excerpts.

### Evidence/examples

- The marker text: `softPruneCacheTtlToolResult` in `dist/tool-result-truncation-*.mjs` (2026.9.9), next to `CACHE_TTL_IMAGE_MARKER = "[image removed during context pruning]"`.
- The run above: the pruning round is visible as an `openclaw.cache-ttl` custom transcript entry with 16 `soft` keys. The transcript still holds the whole results, and the first output survives as the arguments of the overwritten `write` call.
- Related: #140713 (per-request TTL clock in tool loops), #137021 (sticky projections).

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

Companion issue on the trigger side, where one long request prunes the same run's results: #167787.

issues.body:
### Summary

`workboard lifecycle sync failed: Error: UNIQUE constraint failed: workboard_card_attempts.id` fires on every sweep (about once a minute) once two cards' executions fall back to the **same session key** as their attempt id. The sweep aborts part-way, so every card after the colliding one stops being reconciled too.

Seen on 2026.9.8; the same code is on `main` today (`extensions/workboard/src/store.ts:171`, `store-card-helpers.ts:76`, `sqlite-store-schema.ts:124-125`).

### Cause (source at v2026.9.8)

1. The lifecycle sweep builds an association with no `runId` (`lifecycle-sync.ts` ~359-365 fills only `expectedRunId` and `sessionKey`).
2. `lifecycleExecution()` (`store.ts:170-189`) sets `runId = params.association.runId ?? existing?.runId`. For a card with **no execution yet** this is `undefined`. It does not fall back to the card's own `run_id`, even when the card has one.
3. `syncExecutionAttemptMetadata` (`store-card-helpers.ts:76`) then keys the attempt as `execution.runId ?? execution.sessionKey ?? execution.id`, i.e. the bare session key, e.g. `agent:main:main` or `agent:main:discord:channel:<id>`.
4. `insertChildren` (`sqlite-store-write.ts` ~32-46) deletes only **this card's** attempt rows before inserting, but `workboard_card_attempts.id` is a **table-wide** `PRIMARY KEY` (`sqlite-store-schema.ts:124-125`). If another card already holds an attempt with that session-key id, the insert throws.
5. `syncWorkboardLifecycleSessions` stops at the throw; `lifecycle-sync.ts` ~537-539 logs the error. Next sweep, same card, same throw.

Any two cards admitted from the same session (e.g. two auto-admitted cards from one channel, or a card plus a skill-review card on the main session) can collide.

### Repro (minimal)

1. Two unarchived cards, A and B, both with `execution_run_id = NULL` and both resolving to the same `sessionKey`.
2. Card A already has an attempt row whose id is that session key (it got there through the same fallback).
3. Card B has no execution. The next lifecycle sweep → `UNIQUE constraint failed: workboard_card_attempts.id`, every minute.

Workaround: archive the card being inserted (archived cards are skipped by `syncLifecycle`, `needsWorkboardLifecycleReconciliation` and `syncWorkboardLifecycleSessions`). Archiving the *holder* does not help, because archived cards keep their attempt rows.

### Suggested fix

Either (or both):
- `store.ts` `lifecycleExecution`: `const runId = params.association.runId ?? existing?.runId ?? cardRunId(params.card);`
- Scope attempt ids per card (`PRIMARY KEY (card_id, id)`), or never use a bare session key as an attempt id (prefix it with the card id), so two cards cannot collide by construction.

### Environment

OpenClaw 2026.9.8 (fc23bc8), Docker, Linux x86_64, bundled workboard plugin, Discord + Telegram channels, codex app-server harness.
