issues.body:
### Summary

After an npm update 2026.9.7 -> 2026.9.8 (core now 2026.9.9), one plugin's deferred data/settings migration never converges:

    Plugin "signal" data/settings upgrade is unfinished: Package convergence must wait until the updating parent releases its install records.

The warning has persisted for 6 days across every documented recovery path:

- two independent-shell passes (gateway stopped) of "openclaw update repair" followed by "openclaw doctor --fix"
- three "openclaw triage" runs (2026-10-08 20:08, 20:15, 21:07 local); no coding agent is installed on the host, so triage could only collect diagnostics

"openclaw update status" now also reports:

    Package recovery | managed handoff lease database identity changed

The gateway runs and serves normally; all four external plugins (ollama, deepseek, llama-cpp, signal) report the new version and are enabled; "openclaw plugins doctor" passes. The functional residue is the pending settings/data migration plus ~800 MB of retained rollback artifacts.

### Environment

- Linux (Debian 13), kernel 6.12.x, x64
- Node v26.10.0, npm global install, channel stable
- Core: 2026.9.9 (bcfc888); previous 2026.9.8 (fc23bc8), before that 2026.9.7 (c074824)
- systemd --user unit: openclaw-gateway.service (Restart=always)
- No coding agent installed (none of the triage agents)

### Concrete lead: the handoff lease database identity changed

The update transaction descriptor in

    ~/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/.openclaw.package-activation-ca2889ddfcaa5aded37892b5.control/operation.sqlite

records:

    authority.databasePath     = /tmp/openclaw/managed-update-handoffs.sqlite
    authority.databaseIdentity = "2069:30"        (dev:ino)

On disk today:

    /tmp/openclaw/managed-update-handoffs.sqlite   dev=2069 ino=3070

The current inode no longer matches the recorded identity - which is exactly what "managed handoff lease database identity changed" reports. The lease database lives under /tmp (a real ext4 mount on this host), so /tmp cleanup or recreation invalidates the recorded identity, leaving the publication transaction unable to reconcile and, in turn, the deferred plugin migration unable to converge.

### Timeline (America/Martinique)

- 2026-10-02 22:44: update.run accepted (9.7 -> 9.8); handoff started; gateway restarted 23:23.
- 2026-10-02 23:24 and 23:25: two update-failure records, reason "service-revalidation-failed". The "openclaw doctor" step exited 1 with "OpenClaw state at ... is undergoing offline maintenance; retry when it finishes"; "package-backup-retention" exited 1 with "Installation recovery is unverified"; recovery reported serviceRestartSafe: false.
- 2026-10-03 19:14: first maintenance pass from an independent shell (gateway stopped). "openclaw update status" then reported "OpenClaw updated to 2026.9.8", but the plugin warning remained.
- 2026-10-03 19:22: second pass ("openclaw update repair" then "openclaw doctor --fix"). Unchanged.
- 2026-10-08 20:08 / 20:15 / 21:07: three "openclaw triage" runs. Still unchanged; new failure records repeat "Installation recovery is unverified".
- 2026-10-08 21:23: core updated to 2026.9.9. Same warning still reported.

### Retained artifacts

    ~/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/.openclaw.package-activation-ca2889ddfcaa5aded37892b5           (735 MB; previous/ holds the full 2026.9.7 tree)
    ~/.npm-global/lib/node_modules/.openclaw.package-activation-ca2889ddfcaa5aded37892b5.control   (64 MB; operation.sqlite + recovery.mjs)

operation.sqlite, table package_activation: slot 1, revision 14, phase "publication-complete";
publications_json = [{"name":"openclaw","identity":"2070:3674353"}];
intent_json = null.

### Questions

1. What exactly must release the "install records" so the deferred migration can converge?
2. Is the manager's handoff lease database under /tmp expected to survive /tmp cleanup and reboots, or should its identity be re-anchored durably? Here the recorded identity (2069:30) no longer matches the on-disk inode (2069:3070).
3. Should a changed lease-database identity be repairable through "openclaw update repair" / "openclaw doctor --fix"? Neither cleared it on this host, and triage (diagnostics only) did not either.
4. Is it safe to leave this state - gateway healthy, plugin enabled and working, data preserved - or does the pending settings migration risk future breakage?

### Related

- #161921 - same "data/settings upgrade is unfinished" deadlock (macOS, plugins stuck on the previous release)
- #166554 - 9.7 -> 9.8 unfinished migration gating every recovery path (macOS, codex/ClawHub)
- #164986 - 9.8 repair finalize failures

issues.body:
> Agent-written on behalf of the reporter · model: claude-opus-5-5 · filed with the reporter's approval

## Summary

After a config hot reload of an `agents.entries.<id>` change, the plugin **setup inventory** was retired but several callers kept using it. For about 1.5 hours, until a Gateway restart, they failed with `Plugin <id> setup inventory has retired` / `Plugin inventory has retired; begin a new plugin operation.` A later plugin enable (`plugins.entries.workboard`) hot reload did not clear it either. Only a restart did.

This is the same error family as #144291 (in-flight turns aborted by config hot reload) and #155881 (exec auto-review reusing a retired inventory). Here the callers are different, and the stale state **persisted** rather than affecting only in-flight work. Per the note in #155881 that fixing one caller does not cover others, I'm filing it separately. Close as a duplicate if it's already covered.

## Environment

- OpenClaw **2026.9.6 (eb377ac)**, npm global install, Linux x64 (Ubuntu kernel 6.8), Node v26.8.1
- Single Gateway, systemd `--user` unit
- Config at the time contained an **unresolved** env SecretRef at `models.providers.deepseek.apiKey` (provider `deepseek` was `SECRETS_DEGRADED`, state `cold`). This may be relevant: one of the persistently failing paths is the deepseek setup inventory.

## Timeline (2026-10-08, America/New_York)

```
13:30:24 [reload] config change detected; evaluating reload (agents.entries.code-orchestrator)
13:30:57 [secrets] [SECRETS_DEGRADED] cold provider:deepseek: secret reference was not found.
13:30:57 [agents/subagent-registry] subagent notification store retirement has no current task owner runId=…   (x2)
13:31:02 [reload] config hot reload applied (agents.entries.code-orchestrator)
13:35:04 [plugins/setup-registry] plugin setup [browser] setup-entry-load-failed: setup entry failed to load from …/dist/extensions/browser/setup-api.js: Plugin browser setup inventory has retired
         (same for [canvas], [elevenlabs], [xai]; repeats every few minutes, 11 rounds through 14:13)
13:59:34 [reload] config hot reload applied (plugins.entries.workboard, plugins.allow)   <- did not clear it
14:01:49 [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=session:agent:main:setup-inference:incognito-probe-setup-inference-… error="Plugin inventory has retired; begin a new plugin operation."
14:22:06 [agents/prepared-model-runtime] auth-triggered model runtime refresh failed: Error: Plugin deepseek setup inventory has retired   (x6 in 7 s)
14:22:26 [warn] Subagent completion direct announce failed for run …: Plugin deepseek setup inventory has retired
14:30:09 [ws] ⇄ res ✗ chat.metadata errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=Error: Plugin deepseek setup inventory has retired
14:51:59 [agents/subagent-registry] subagent_ended hook failed (best-effort) phase=plugin-runtime err="Plugin inventory has retired; begin a new plugin operation."
14:51:59 [agents/subagent-registry] context-engine onSubagentEnded failed (best-effort) err="Plugin inventory has retired; begin a new plugin operation."
15:06    removed the unresolved deepseek apiKey ref, Gateway restart -> no further "has retired" lines
```

89 `has retired` log lines in total, from 23 distinct minutes between 13:35 and ~14:52.

## Affected callers (all distinct from #144291 / #155881)

- `plugins/setup-registry` setup-entry loads (browser, canvas, elevenlabs, xai)
- `setup-inference` probe lane (the `openclaw` system-expert tool path)
- `agents/prepared-model-runtime` auth-triggered refresh
- subagent completion direct announce (completion was lost to the requester)
- `chat.metadata` WS method (returned `UNAVAILABLE` to the Control UI)
- `subagent_ended` hook and context-engine `onSubagentEnded`

## Expected

When the setup inventory is retired by a hot reload, later callers should start a new plugin operation / inventory generation rather than keep the retired handle. A degraded or unavailable provider secret should not leave that provider's setup inventory permanently retired for the life of the process.

## Actual

Retired setup inventory handles persisted across subsequent hot reloads. Unrelated surfaces (chat metadata, subagent announce, system-expert inference) failed until a full Gateway restart.

## Reproduction

NOT a confirmed minimal repro. The observed sequence was: config contains an unresolved provider SecretRef → `openclaw config set agents.entries.<new-id>…` (hot reload) → setup-registry errors begin ~4 minutes later and persist. I have not retried it, because the hot reload also retired in-flight subagent runs on a production Gateway.

issues.body:
### Summary

Allow an embedding host to supply an acquisition transport for the existing
native web_fetch tool through normal core tool assembly, while retaining
native extraction, output formatting, and untrusted-content handling.

This is an extension request, not a vulnerability report.

### Problem to solve

A host may need to route page acquisition through its own trusted network or
policy boundary before any outbound request occurs.

The inspected implementation performs direct guarded acquisition before
provider fallback. A fallback provider therefore cannot enforce admission
before the initial request.

Same-name plugin replacement also does not provide a clean solution:
core assembly constructs web_fetch before plugin resolution, duplicate names
are rejected, and disabling native fetch affects both construction and execution.


### Proposed solution

Expose an optional host acquisition transport through ordinary core tool
assembly. Keep the API narrow and follow existing extension conventions.

The contract should:
- Supply the exact normalized URL, request options, cancellation, applicable
  limits, and host-established invocation context where needed.
- Never derive trusted context from model-controlled tool arguments.
- Use the selected transport exclusively: refusal or failure must not fall
  back to direct HTTP or another provider.
- Preserve user enable/disable and tool-deny settings, including supported
  runtime configuration changes.
- Clearly assign responsibility for SSRF, redirects, headers/credentials,
  response-size limits, and cancellation.
- Define cache partitioning and reuse, including whether cache hits bypass
  acquisition, without accidental cross-context reuse or unnecessary refetching.

Keep native extraction, truncation, output presentation, and untrusted-content
wrapping. Preserve current behavior when no host transport is configured.

### Alternatives considered

- Provider registration: fallback occurs after direct acquisition.
- Same-name plugin replacement: conflicts with core construction and complicates
  preservation of user settings.
- A differently named tool: leaves native web_fetch behavior unchanged.
- Global network interception: depends on transport internals and can miss
  dispatcher-specific paths.

### Impact

Embedding hosts could reuse native page-reading behavior rather than maintain
replacement tools or transport interception patches. This would be opt-in,
with existing standalone behavior and user controls preserved.

### Evidence/examples

Inspected on 2026-10-08:

- Native fetch:
  https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/dc203b5e486d3b931face78556019797dbe3f376/src/agents/tools/web-fetch.ts
- Core assembly:
  https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/dc203b5e486d3b931face78556019797dbe3f376/src/agents/openclaw-tools.ts
- Core assembly types:
  https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/dc203b5e486d3b931face78556019797dbe3f376/src/agents/openclaw-tools.types.ts
- Plugin resolution:
  https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/dc203b5e486d3b931face78556019797dbe3f376/src/plugins/tools.ts

Release v2026.9.9 was also inspected; no sufficient host-supplied acquisition
transport seam was found.

Regression coverage should exercise actual core assembly, unchanged default
behavior, exclusive host acquisition, refusal without fallback, user disable/
deny preservation, native output processing, and cache/network-safety contracts.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Yes, I plan to implement this myself

### Additional information

This requests a generic acquisition extension point—not organization-specific
policy logic in OpenClaw core.

### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On Windows MSIX 2026.9.900.0, enabling the managed Codex plugin causes repeated Gateway readiness timeouts and severe main-thread event-loop starvation, with symbolized samples showing filesystem metadata/path work.

### Steps to reproduce

Observed on the preserved installation; not yet reproduced from a clean install.
1. Stop the supervisor-owned Gateway and back up the isolated account’s existing ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json, preserving state and credentials.
2. Edit the existing JSON flags: plugins.entries.codex.enabled=true and plugins.entries.acpx.enabled=false; retain other settings. The comparison used configuration edits, not repeated plugin installs.
3. Start through clawctl gateway-service start --json, using the packaged Node and native-redirect preload.
4. Probe HTTP readiness and observe sustained Gateway CPU and readiness timeouts. The existing WPR trace captured a Codex-enabled stall.

### Expected behavior

Gateway should reach HTTP /readyz 200 with ready=true and remain responsive. On this same installation, Codex off/ACPX off reached that state in about 2.5 minutes; Codex off/managed ACPX on also reached readiness, albeit slowly. No known-good Codex-enabled MSIX version has been established.

### Actual behavior

Codex on/ACPX off: repeated readiness timeouts and severe main-thread starvation. One startup reached the HTTP-listening stage after 2132 seconds, without a verified healthy readiness response before stopping. A heartbeat reported elapsed=2052244ms (~34 minutes); this does not prove a single uninterrupted synchronous block.

Comparison results:
- Codex off, ACPX off: healthy in about 2.5 minutes.
- Codex off, managed ACPX on: healthy after about 9 minutes; repeat 19:05:37–19:16:09 BST took 10 minutes 32 seconds. Subsequent /readyz: ready=true, failing=[], eventLoop.degraded=false.
- Codex on, ACPX on: an earlier attempt remained unresponsive for about 15 minutes before stopping.

ACPX also shows slow startup; a shared cause with Codex is not established.

### OpenClaw version

MSIX 2026.9.900.0; payload and managed Codex/ACPX plugins 2026.9.9; managed Codex CLI 0.160.0

### Operating system

Windows, build 26300.9550, display version 26H2; x64 packaged Node 24.21.0

### Install method

Windows MSIX; supervisor-managed isolated account; clawctl gateway-service start --json; packaged Node with native-redirect preload

### Model

Startup failure precedes Gateway inference; gpt-6-astra passed independent managed Codex inference.

### Provider / routing chain

Intended: Gateway → managed Codex app-server → OpenAI via ChatGPT login; Gateway integration remains unverified.

### Additional provider/model setup details

Independent managed Codex authentication, model discovery and real Astra inference succeeded using ChatGPT login, without an API key. Direct ACPX-to-authenticated-Cursor requests also succeeded. Neither proves Gateway-owned runtime health. Credentials were preserved.

### Logs

```shell
2026-10-08, BST:
15:43:30: eventLoopDelayP99Ms=64592.3, eventLoopDelayMaxMs=64592.3, eventLoopUtilization=1; SQLite lock-wait failure and slow transaction hold.
18:15:30: liveness heartbeat elapsed=2052244ms.

Earlier ACPX-related reload preparation failed with EPERM while linking WindowsApps/app into plugin-captures; generation 2 replacement was not applied. Fresh junction tests later succeeded.
Codex installation linked its OpenClaw peer dependency successfully, then lost core:plugin-lifecycle/global about 6.5 minutes later. Registration was published; complete lifecycle success is not established. Lease loss is not a proven cause of startup starvation.

Full redacted surrounding excerpts are included in the evidence section.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Symbolized existing WPR trace: Gateway PID 10056, main thread TID 11436, relative interval 2–25 seconds. 22,964.4459ms sampled CPU weight in 23 seconds.

Node executable and PDB GUID c4ea0e3a-70ff-9635-4c4c-44205044422e, age 1, match exactly. Native symbols resolved without an override. Unresolved leaf weight: 8.43%; anonymous caller sequences remain.

A 1400.5638ms inclusive prefix shows V8 microtasks → unresolved callers → node::fs::LStat → uv_fs_lstat → uv__fs_work → fs__stat_impl_from_path. This is evidence for that path, not attribution of the entire interval. Kernel stacks show path lookup/filter/NTFS work; no filter defect is established. JavaScript callers and queried paths remain unknown.

The two reviewed reports are included in full below because the browser attachment picker failed. Raw ETL remains local.

issues.body:
**Reporting Agent**: Qwen Code CLI (session `.openclaw-30`, ref `306fca`)
**Session ID**: 306fca
**Component**: gateway / update activation / supervisor restart handoff
**Severity**: High

### Description

On this host the Gateway performs a **full-process restart roughly every 40 minutes**, each one a
graceful drain that costs in-flight work, and the only recorded reason for them is a
`gateway_restart_handoff` row that **expired four days ago** and names a build that is not running.

### Environment

- XPS15-9520, WSL2; user unit `openclaw-gateway.service` (TimeoutStopSec=330, KillMode=mixed)
- OpenClaw **2026.10.1-beta.1** (`6830fe7` — CLI and on-disk package agree)
- Times below are BST.

### Reproducible steps

1. Run the Gateway on this channel and leave it running.
2. `journalctl --user -u openclaw-gateway.service` shows a stop/start pair recurring every ~40 min.
3. Immediately before a stop, **two transient scopes are active at once**:
   `openclaw-update-220384b5-…scope` (1min 17.940s CPU, 1.6G peak) and
   `openclaw-update-74146498-…scope` (1min 17.871s CPU, 1.2G peak).
4. At each shutdown the gateway logs a slow-SQLite operation
   `operation=gateway.restart-intent.clear` against `openclaw.sqlite`.

Observed 2026-10-08: start 10:12:22 · stop 10:54:10 → start 10:59:39 · stop 11:38:36 → start 11:44:06.

### Expected behaviour

Either the Gateway does not restart when no update has been activated, or every restart states its
true reason; and the handoff/intent tables hold no expired rows.

### Actual behaviour

Restarts recur without a stated live reason, and the reason presented is stale and wrong. Read from
`state/openclaw.sqlite` on this host:

- `gateway_restart_handoff` holds **exactly one row**, `handoff_key=current`,
  `created_at=1791153205656`, `expires_at=1791153265656` (**+60 s**), with
  `reason = gateway.installation_replaced: Installation replaced: running 2026.9.7 build
  2026.9.7-release-c074824a27c9-2026-09-29T23-33-45.013Z; on-disk runtime chunks unavailable`,
  `supervisor_mode=systemd`, `restart_kind=full-process`, `source=unknown`. It expired on
  **2026-10-04** and is four days stale, yet being the only row it reads as the current reason.
- `gateway_restart_intent` is **empty (0 rows)** between restarts, so an intent is written and
  cleared within each restart.

### Questions

1. Is a full-process restart on every update activation intended, and is a ~40-minute cadence
   expected on this channel? Two concurrent `openclaw-update-*.scope` units in the same minute look
   like a de-duplication gap.
2. Is there a setting governing restart-activation cadence, or `supervisor_mode=systemd`?
3. Should an expired `gateway_restart_handoff` row be reaped rather than left as the last recorded
   reason? It currently misleads anyone diagnosing a restart.

### Suggested fix

- Reap expired handoff/intent rows (or key `current` to the live intent), so the presented reason is
  never a stale row.
- De-duplicate concurrent update-activation scopes.
- Report the drain's cost alongside the restart — the ~314 s budget and the queue sizes — rather
  than only in the journal.

### Note on the caller

No systemd user timer and no crontab entry invokes `openclaw update` on this box. Its automations
store (`state/openclaw.sqlite` -> `cron_jobs`) contains a job named **`gateway-restart-watch`**,
which is the likeliest caller; I have not yet read that job's definition, so this is a lead rather
than a finding.

### Logs / Stack Trace

<details>
<summary>Click to expand</summary>

```
[gateway] draining active work before stop with timeout 314587ms:
  queueSize=4 pendingReplies=2 embeddedRuns=1 agentRuns=1 sessionAdmissions=5 rootRequests=5 cronRuns=1
  client calls fail "unavailable during gateway restart": agent.identity.get, sessions.describe, workboard.cards.list
operation=gateway.restart-intent.clear (openclaw.sqlite)   <- slow SQLite op at shutdown

transient scopes immediately before the 10:54 stop:
openclaw-update-220384b5-…scope: Consumed 1min 17.940s CPU time, 1.6G memory peak
openclaw-update-74146498-…scope: Consumed 1min 17.871s CPU time, 1.2G memory peak

gateway_restart_handoff.current:
  reason = gateway.installation_replaced: Installation replaced: running 2026.9.7 build
           2026.9.7-release-c074824a27c9-2026-09-29T23-33-45.013Z; on-disk runtime chunks unavailable
  supervisor_mode=systemd  restart_kind=full-process  source=unknown
  created 2026-10-04 23:33:25 BST   expires 2026-10-04 23:34:25 BST
```

</details>

### Related

Searched before filing; the closest existing reports are cited rather than duplicated:

- **#154840** (open) — WSL2/systemd gateway restart loop after `gateway.restart` (EADDRINUSE): same
  platform and supervisor, different trigger.
- **#152863** (open) — feature: a public external-supervisor graceful stop handshake.
- **#110237** (closed) — doctor upgrade vs fractional restart-handoff timestamps: the same handoff table.
- **#160875** (closed) — `readGatewayRestartIntentPayloadSync` dropping the restart intent on a
  state-DB read failure: the same intent path.
- **#144094** (open) — macOS launchd crash-loop with `[admission] closed: restart drain`: the drain is
  shared, the trigger is not.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.9.8, a `claude-cli` live session that has already written a final assistant message (`stop_reason=end_turn`, no tool in flight) never logs a completed `cli turn`. Exactly 600 seconds later the no-output watchdog kills the process, the gateway reports `Embedded agent failed before reply`, and the finished reply is not saved.

### Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO for a short deterministic repro. Observed five times on one gateway on 2026-10-05. The detailed case:

1. OpenClaw 2026.9.8 `(fc23bc8)`, Claude Code 2.1.289, runtime `claude-cli`, model `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`. `agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds` is 7200, so the fresh no-output watchdog cap is 600000 ms.
2. Dashboard session `febaa037-1447-4b5f-b6ba-e015ebeedbf0` (`agent:main:dashboard:543ceef8-0508-471a-aa4a-07c03378cded`), Claude CLI session `bf75d5f6-79b2-4bc2-a1fe-e16fe827a674`, run `35374ebb-50ce-4975-b9a7-f3ff9b25ea73`.
3. The turn runs and uses tools. The last tool call is a Bash invocation whose `tool_result` is written at `2026-10-06T03:00:06.809Z`.
4. At `2026-10-06T03:00:27.870Z` the Claude session JSONL records the last event before the kill: `type=assistant`, `stop_reason=end_turn`, 2797 characters of text, no tool call.
5. The gateway's last progress for this run is `model_call:stream_progress` at that same instant. The first stalled-session diagnostic is `2026-10-05T23:02:42-04:00` with `lastProgressAge=135s`.
6. At `2026-10-05T23:10:28-04:00`, 600.1 seconds after that assistant event, the watchdog fires. There is no `cli turn: ... durationMs=` completion line for this run.

The same JSONL-to-watchdog gap happened on four other `claude-cli` sessions the same day. In each one the event immediately before the 600-second silence is `assistant` / `end_turn` with text, and the tool call before that already has its `tool_result`.

### Expected behavior

A finished assistant message should be the turn's reply. `extensions/anthropic/cli.runtime.ts` says the completed answer can be delivered through the normal reply hooks without waiting on child work. `docs/gateway/cli-backends.md`, as cited by #158626, says the same. Here no child work was outstanding: the last tool result was already in the transcript. The Control UI had already streamed the answer. That answer should be persisted, and the turn should not be reported as `Embedded agent failed before reply`.

### Actual behavior

The runner does not complete the turn on `stop_reason=end_turn`. `executeClaudeCli` calls `completeTurn` only when a `result` event arrives (`extensions/anthropic/cli.runtime.ts`), and `execute-plugin.ts` leaves `terminalResult` at `"none"` until a non-interim `result` event. After the final assistant text, no further CLI progress is logged. 600 seconds later:

```
2026-10-05T23:10:28.326-04:00 [agent/cli-backend] cli watchdog timeout: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 session=bf75d5f6-79b2-4bc2-a1fe-e16fe827a674 noOutputTimeoutMs=600000 pid=node
2026-10-05T23:10:28.579-04:00 [agent/cli-backend] cli terminal failure: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 durationMs=2195259 runId=35374ebb-50ce-4975-b9a7-f3ff9b25ea73 error=CLI produced no output for 600s and was terminated.
2026-10-05T23:10:28.647-04:00 Embedded agent failed before reply: CLI produced no output for 600s and was terminated.
2026-10-05T23:10:28.666-04:00 [gateway] terminal session persistence failed session=agent:main:dashboard:543ceef8-0508-471a-aa4a-07c03378cded run=35374ebb-50ce-4975-b9a7-f3ff9b25ea73 error=Error: operator model execution authority is no longer active
2026-10-05T23:10:28.670-04:00 [diagnostic] message processed: channel=webchat ... sessionId=febaa037-1447-4b5f-b6ba-e015ebeedbf0 ... outcome=error duration=2195689ms
```

The OpenClaw session transcript for `febaa037` contains the user message that started run `35374ebb` and does not contain the assistant reply. The session status is `timeout`. The Control UI showed the streamed answer, then the banner `CLI produced no output for 600s and was terminated.`, and marked the in-progress task row Failed.

This gateway did not kill quiet in-flight tools at 600 seconds. On the same day a Bash tool with no output from `2026-10-05T18:47:01Z` to `2026-10-05T18:57:02Z` (601 seconds) completed normally, and an Agent tool was quiet for 691 seconds (`18:29:38Z` to `18:41:09Z`) without a watchdog kill.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.8 (fc23bc8)

### Operating system

macOS 26.6.2, Darwin arm64, Node v26.10.0

### Install method

npm global (`/opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/openclaw`)

### Model

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 and anthropic/claude-opus-4-8, both with `agentRuntime.id` `claude-cli`

### Provider / routing chain

OpenClaw gateway -> claude-cli live session (`liveSession: claude-stdio`) -> local `claude` 2.1.289

### Additional provider/model setup details

`agents.defaults.timeoutSeconds` is 7200. The bundled Claude backend does not set `reliability.watchdog`, so an explicit run timeout selects the fresh profile (`noOutputTimeoutRatio` 0.8, `maxMs` 600000). That is why these resumed sessions die at 600 seconds of silence rather than the 180-second resume cap.

Channels observed: webchat dashboard and Slack direct threads.

### Logs

Five watchdog kills on 2026-10-05. `silence_s` is the gap from the last timestamped Claude session JSONL event to the watchdog log. That last event is `assistant` / `stop_reason=end_turn` with text and no tool call. The prior tool call already has a `tool_result`.

| kill (EDT) | CLI session | model | last JSONL event (UTC) | text chars | silence_s | run durationMs | channel |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 14:56:09 | 3729c35c-a272-46b6-a047-a82e1da1f59a | claude-opus-4-8 | 2026-10-05T18:46:08.686Z | 2187 | 600.3 | 1616905 | slack |
| 15:09:59 | 5a97d166-865c-43d6-bb52-2391cb58148b | claude-opus-5-5 | 2026-10-05T18:59:58.449Z | 1798 | 600.6 | 2304790 | slack |
| 17:07:27 | 7e4b22ef-f6a0-4a85-8069-cd118e554251 | claude-opus-4-8 | 2026-10-05T20:57:27.281Z | 1949 | 599.7 | 2196176 | slack |
| 18:54:30 | b8800e19-d1ca-4e9e-bb53-2abc2a4da4d2 | claude-opus-5-5 | 2026-10-05T22:44:30.085Z | 2716 | 599.9 | 7013916 | webchat |
| 23:10:28 | bf75d5f6-79b2-4bc2-a1fe-e16fe827a674 | claude-opus-5-5 | 2026-10-06T03:00:27.870Z | 2797 | 600.1 | 2195259 | webchat |

Matching gateway lines for the other four, same shape as the 23:10 case:

```
2026-10-05T14:56:09.122-04:00 cli watchdog timeout: ... session=3729c35c-a272-46b6-a047-a82e1da1f59a noOutputTimeoutMs=600000
2026-10-05T14:56:09.377-04:00 cli terminal failure: ... durationMs=1616905 runId=8a247595-be9b-4f2b-837e-67420ce60a5e error=CLI produced no output for 600s and was terminated.
2026-10-05T14:56:09.466-04:00 Embedded agent failed before reply: CLI produced no output for 600s and was terminated.

2026-10-05T15:09:58.866-04:00 cli watchdog timeout: ... session=5a97d166-865c-43d6-bb52-2391cb58148b noOutputTimeoutMs=600000
2026-10-05T15:09:59.119-04:00 cli terminal failure: ... durationMs=2304790 runId=a7919706-3270-4849-a47c-bbbe7c18eb20 error=CLI produced no output for 600s and was terminated.
2026-10-05T15:09:59.206-04:00 Embedded agent failed before reply: CLI produced no output for 600s and was terminated.

2026-10-05T17:07:27.604-04:00 cli watchdog timeout: ... session=7e4b22ef-f6a0-4a85-8069-cd118e554251 noOutputTimeoutMs=600000
2026-10-05T17:07:27.855-04:00 cli terminal failure: ... durationMs=2196176 runId=013a4917-3dff-40a5-92a9-095637a593ef error=CLI produced no output for 600s and was terminated.
2026-10-05T17:07:27.909-04:00 Embedded agent failed before reply: CLI produced no output for 600s and was terminated.

2026-10-05T18:54:30.507-04:00 cli watchdog timeout: ... session=b8800e19-d1ca-4e9e-bb53-2abc2a4da4d2 noOutputTimeoutMs=600000
2026-10-05T18:54:30.762-04:00 cli terminal failure: ... durationMs=7013916 runId=dc580b07-17bb-411c-b556-abff598f89de error=CLI produced no output for 600s and was terminated.
2026-10-05T18:54:30.848-04:00 Embedded agent failed before reply: CLI produced no output for 600s and was terminated.
```

Stalled diagnostic for the detailed run, first sample:

```
2026-10-05T23:02:42.553-04:00 [diagnostic] stalled session: sessionId=febaa037-1447-4b5f-b6ba-e015ebeedbf0 ... state=processing age=135s queueDepth=0 reason=active_work_without_progress classification=stalled_agent_run activeWorkKind=embedded_run lastProgress=model_call:stream_progress lastProgressAge=135s
```

`135s` before `23:02:42` is `23:00:27` EDT, which is `2026-10-06T03:00:27Z`, the JSONL `end_turn` timestamp.

The Claude session JSONL does not contain the stdout `result` frames. What is directly observed is that the JSONL stops on `end_turn`, the gateway records no later CLI progress, and it never logs a successful `cli turn` before the watchdog.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Control UI for session `febaa037-1447-4b5f-b6ba-e015ebeedbf0`: the final assistant text is on screen, then a banner `CLI produced no output for 600s and was terminated.` The task row for that turn is shown as Failed.

Code on current `main` (unchanged in this path since #161260, which is already in 2026.9.8; `extensions/anthropic/cli.runtime.ts` has no later commit, including in `v2026.10.1-beta.1`):

- `extensions/anthropic/cli.runtime.ts`: `completesTurn` is computed only inside `if (message.type === "result")`. A result is marked `openclaw_interim_result` while background task ids are pending. `completeTurn` runs only when `completesTurn` is true.
- `src/agents/cli-runner/execute-plugin.ts`: the stream loop sets `terminalResult` only for a `result` event whose `openclaw_interim_result` is not true. Any other event calls `watchdog.noteOutput()`. The iterator does not end on an assistant `end_turn`.
- `src/agents/cli-runner/no-output-timeout-policy.ts`: with no active tool, background task, or compaction, silence past `noOutputTimeoutMs` becomes `CLI produced no output for ${seconds}s and was terminated.`

### Impact and severity

Affected: this gateway's `claude-cli` dashboard and Slack direct sessions on 2026.9.8.

Severity: blocks the turn. The user sees a failure banner after the answer was already streamed, and the reply is not stored in the OpenClaw transcript. Tool side effects from earlier in the turn remain.

Frequency: 5 of 5 `claude-cli` no-output watchdog kills recorded on this gateway on 2026-10-05 followed this pattern (last JSONL event is `end_turn` with text, then 599.7–600.6 seconds of no CLI progress).

Consequence: a finished turn is reported as `outcome=error`. One of those also logged `terminal session persistence failed` because the operator model execution authority was no longer active.

### Additional information

Related, but not the same observation:

- #157647 is a watchdog kill while a foreground Bash command was backgrounded and the continuation was still in progress. The quiet in-flight Bash and Agent spans above were not killed at 600 seconds.
- #158626 is a finished answer not delivered while a native background agent is still running.
- #164696 is a live-session reply held until the next inbound message. That report does not include the 600-second watchdog or `failed before reply`.

issues.body:
## Summary

Telegram message delivery intermittently fails for extended periods due to a session-admission race condition, even though the gateway reports healthy (HTTP 200) throughout. Recovery via restart is temporary (holds ~70-90 minutes before recurring); clearing the stuck ingress queue is the only safe mitigation found, and it is not a fix.

## Environment

- OpenClaw version: v2026.9.7 (upgraded from v2026.6.11 on 3-4 Oct 2026)
- Platform: macOS, Apple Silicon (M4 Pro)
- Channel: Telegram (direct chat)

## Observed behaviour

Starting shortly after a clean gateway boot, inbound Telegram messages continued to be received (logged normally, growing queue), but no replies were sent. Gateway process CPU pegged at 100-250% with `agent/embedded tool-search: cataloged N tools` log lines repeating every few minutes, but no agent-turn completion and no outbound send. Restarting the gateway temporarily resolved it, but the symptom recurred within minutes to ~90 minutes each time, independent of the restart.

## Root cause (traced from source)

In `dist/worker/sqlite-store.worker.mjs`, inbound messages are queued per `lane_key` in the `channel_ingress_events` table. Each retry calls `admitUserTurn`, which re-reads the live `session_nodes` entry for the resolved session key and compares it against an "expected session state" snapshot captured when the message was first queued (function `sessionMatchesExpectedTranscriptTurn` / `buildRestartRecoveryExpectedState`, inside `createReplyRestartRecoveryClaimController`).

The comparison checks a cluster of fields beyond `sessionId`: `status`, `abortedLastRun`, `activeWriterRunId`, `lifecycleRevision`, `mainRestartRecovery.cycleId`/`revision`, and several `restartRecovery*` fields. If any of these drift between queue-time and commit-time, admission is rejected with:

```
Error: session changed before durable user-turn admission
```

In our case this was happening on effectively every retry for the live session (`agent:main:direct:<user>`), whose `snapshot_revision` was incrementing normally (confirmed via `session_nodes.entry_json`) — i.e., not corruption, but a legitimate field (most likely `activeWriterRunId` or `lifecycleRevision`) drifting between the time a message is queued and the time its retry attempts to commit. Only one gateway process was confirmed running throughout (no duplicate/zombie process racing on the same DB), so this appears to be either an internal race in the admission logic itself, or a legitimate concurrent writer (cron/heartbeat touching the same session key) that the admission check doesn't account for when comparing against a stale baseline captured potentially hours earlier for long-queued retries.

## Reproduction / mitigation notes

- Marking the stuck `channel_ingress_events` rows as `failed` (not deleting payloads) and restarting temporarily restores delivery, but new stuck entries accumulate again after ~70-90 minutes.
- A separate, unrelated session row for the same chat (`agent:main:telegram:direct:<id>`, stuck at `snapshot_revision=0`, `delivery.kind: "none"`) was investigated as a possible cause and ruled out — deleting it had no effect on recurrence, confirming the live/relevant session key is `agent:main:direct:<user>`, not that vestigial duplicate.
- **Caution for anyone else attempting a DB-level fix:** directly editing a single field (e.g. `snapshot_revision`) on a `session_nodes` row in isolation, without updating the corresponding `entry_json` consistently, triggers the canonical-validation worker to treat the row as internally inconsistent and causes a hard crash-restart loop (`session-sqlite reclamation worker retired reason=failure kind=canonical-validation`, repeating every 10-15s). This was hit once during diagnosis and required a full restore from backup to resolve.

## Expected behaviour

Transient admission-state drift during a long retry window should not cause indefinite, silent delivery failure. At minimum, a stale "expected state" baseline for long-queued retries should be refreshed/invalidated rather than rejected forever, and/or admission failures should surface a visible error/log signal distinguishable from "all healthy" rather than failing silently with no outbound reply and no obvious log marker at the point of failure.

## Impact

Full loss of Telegram responsiveness for a live, healthy-looking gateway, recurring every ~70-90 minutes, for several hours on 8 Oct 2026, until mitigated by manual queue-clearing. No data loss (all backups/quarantine actions preserved, nothing deleted).

issues.body:
## Summary

On OpenClaw **2026.9.6**, agent runs that end through the exec-backgrounding / yield path never execute the settlement block that commits their durable turn advancement. The `context_engine_turn_outbox` row stays at `state='admitted'` with `attempt_count=0` (never attempted), and is silently discarded by `recoverContextEngineTurnOutbox` at the next turn start. Context engines that rely on turn advancement for accounting (e.g. lossless-claw's `afterTurn`) therefore silently stop updating their ledger for **every turn that backgrounds an exec** — which is nearly every real agent turn. No warning is logged.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.9.6 (Homebrew, macOS arm64, launchd gateway)
- `plugins.slots.contextEngine = "lossless-claw"` (v1.1.0)
- Channels: Feishu (websocket) + Telegram

## Production symptom

- 62 outbox rows accumulated over ~2 days since the 9.6 upgrade, **all** `state='admitted'`, **all** `attempt_count=0`. Owners: cron sessions, subagents, internal-effects runs, and the latest turn of live chat sessions.
- Per-conversation `conversation_compaction_maintenance` / `conversation_compaction_telemetry` (lossless-claw tables) frozen at their last values for all chat conversations. Only tool-free sessions (active-memory subagents, single model call) keep updating — their advancements settle fine.
- Gateway log has **zero** `durable turn advancement is blocked` / settlement warnings — the settlement code path simply does not run for these turns.

## Repro (sandbox, deterministic)

Fake Feishu channel + fake model (same 9.6 build, gateway started from a probe-instrumented copy of dist):

1. **Plain DM turn** (single model call): settlement runs — probe at the `canAdvanceContextEngineTurn` call site shows `accepted=true`; outbox row is created, committed, delivered and deleted; the engine's telemetry row updates the same second (timestamp match to the second).
2. **Turn whose model issues exec calls that background** (e.g. 6 × `sleep 45`, exceeding the yield window): the settlement block **never executes** (probe produces no output for the run); a new outbox row is left stuck at `state='admitted'`; telemetry does not update.

Same conversation, two turn shapes, one settles and one does not — so it is not about conversation age, channel transport, or engine capabilities (`turnAdvancementIdempotency: "atomic-idempotent-v1"` and `commitTurn` are declared and work in case 1).

## Expected

The turn advancement created at run start should be settled (accepted → committed → delivered) when the run finishes through the backgrounding/completion-turn path — or the `turnAttempt` reference should survive continuations so the final settlement commits it.

## Relation to #163566

Related subsystem, different failure: #163566 describes rows stuck as `session-rebound` with loud `durable turn advancement is blocked` warnings and CPU burn after an update repair. Here rows are stuck at `admitted` with **no warnings at all**, triggered by ordinary exec-backgrounding turns, on a clean install with no repair history.

## Details

- State machine observed: `admitted` (enqueue at turn start) → `accepted` → `ready` (commit with messages) → delivered → deleted. Stuck rows never leave `admitted`.
- `recoverContextEngineTurnOutbox` discards `admitted` rows at the next turn start for the same session, which makes the loss silent and keeps only the final turn's row visible for live sessions.
- Compaction drains that trigger on live stored-context size still work; only the advancement-driven accounting path is dead.

issues.body:
### Summary

Make ordinary `ask_user` questions recoverable across Gateway restarts, with durable answer settlement and an explicit continuation after the original turn has ended.

### Problem to solve

A person may need hours or days to answer an agent's question. Reconnecting to a live Gateway and recovering the question after the Gateway process has gone away are different contracts. The latter needs durable ownership of the question and the work owed after an answer; extending a timer or preserving a rendered card is insufficient.

At inspected main `57dd17b4ea39b5f5d87db9faabaa2f0b10fa83f4`, `QuestionManager` describes itself as process-local, keeps entries and waiters in memory, and clears them on reset. The ordinary `ask_user` tool waits on `question.waitAnswer`; its timeout is currently clamped to 30-3600 seconds. There is already answer-commit machinery, including `resolveWithCommit` and unknown-write-outcome handling. This proposal must preserve and build on that machinery, not replace it with a weaker acknowledgement.

This is a feature/design request based on source inspection, not a claim of a newly reproduced current-main runtime regression. It is scoped initially to ordinary, non-secret `ask_user` questions. Secret-entry, MCP forms, and harness-owned questions must retain their existing ownership and authority unless explicitly included by design review.

### Proposed solution

Keep one native owner of question truth and the obligation to continue. The desired user flow is: ask a question, finish the asking turn, restart the Gateway, restore the actionable question with its original deadline, accept an authorized answer, and admit a new turn with that explicit answer context.

1. Persist the question's immutable definition, exact session/conversation identity, requester/caller and delivery context, absolute deadline, terminal outcome, and continuation obligation through the existing SQLite worker/storage APIs. The exact schema and owner require review. Do not create a parallel file store or reconstruct response authority from display history alone.
2. Publish an actionable question only after its durable registration succeeds. Yield the asking turn after registration without launching later tools in the same batch. A continuation is a new turn, not restoration of private in-flight model reasoning.
3. Make settlement first-answer-wins and retry-safe. A successful durable acknowledgement must follow commit, including when another turn occupies the session. Reconcile a lost ACK or unknown commit outcome through canonical readback; do not invite blind resubmission or acknowledge only from memory.
4. Admit owed continuations through the native session controller/queue. Coordinate with #160745 and #163058; avoid a second busy-session poller or independently scheduled retry loop. Revalidate the exact conversation generation and current authority at admission, not just before an asynchronous RPC call.
5. Define recovery for each crash boundary: before registration, before/after decision commit, before/after continuation admission, and during execution/delivery. Require one terminal decision and no duplicate admitted work for the same obligation. Do not promise exactly-once external effects after an interrupted model/tool run; ambiguous execution must have an explicit recovery or user-visible interrupted outcome.
6. Preserve original caller and delivery provenance through the new turn. Native provenance supplies correlation, not a new authorization grant. Recheck authorization when settling and continuing; reset, deletion, or revoked authority must not resurrect old work.
7. Agree on user semantics for Skip, expiry, ordinary newer messages, unavailable presentation, and blocked/interrupted continuation. A newer unrelated message must not be invented as an answer. Do not silently inherit downstream policy choices for these cases.
8. Define long-deadline capability and rollout behavior for existing clients. A six-day pending question within a seven-day lifetime is a concrete acceptance target, subject to owner agreement; changing the default or sending longer deadlines to incompatible clients is not assumed.

### Alternatives considered

- Longer tool timeout: retains the live waiter and still does not survive process loss.
- Reconnect/list recovery alone: useful for a live owner, not durable reconstruction after restart.
- True suspended-turn checkpoint/resume: a possible future direction, but a substantially different runtime contract; not required for an explicit new continuation turn.
- Plugin-owned question database and scheduler: would duplicate the native question validation, authority, session admission, and reset lifecycle. Prefer native ownership or a maintainer-approved extension contract that preserves a single owner.
- Transcript-tail reconstruction: can lose pending questions to compaction or scan limits and is not a substitute for reviewed canonical state ownership.

### Impact

Affected: ordinary human-input workflows across web and supported channels where the user returns after a restart/update or after a long absence.

Consequence: without a durable question and continuation obligation, the user must restate the decision/task or may see an old card whose original waiter cannot resume. This blocks unattended multi-day workflows. No measured current-main incident frequency is claimed.

### Evidence/examples

Source inspected at `57dd17b4ea39b5f5d87db9faabaa2f0b10fa83f4`:

- [Question lifecycle, requester authority, answer commit, and reset](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/57dd17b4ea39b5f5d87db9faabaa2f0b10fa83f4/src/gateway/question-manager.ts).
- [Ordinary ask_user registration and live answer wait](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/57dd17b4ea39b5f5d87db9faabaa2f0b10fa83f4/src/agents/tools/ask-user-tool.ts).
- [Existing timeout bounds](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/57dd17b4ea39b5f5d87db9faabaa2f0b10fa83f4/src/agents/tools/ask-user-tool-normalization.ts).

Related work, not complete replacements:

- #160745: proposed durable session mailbox; storage and recovery coordination.
- #163058: completion/yield continuations through session admission with original requester provenance.
- #163060: messages refused as question answers should remain ordinary inputs where authorized.
- #162241, case 2: waiting ask_user turn evicted by a per-chat cap; a related symptom, not proof of this full restart contract.
- #149247: channel question delivery after a yielded continuation; does not itself establish multi-day question durability.

Required implementation evidence:

- Real Gateway process restart restores the same pending question and absolute deadline; compaction and large histories do not erase canonical question state.
- Answer while the session is idle and while it is busy; crash immediately after successful ACK; read back the same committed outcome.
- Concurrent devices, duplicate answers, lost ACK, and unknown commit outcome preserve one terminal decision.
- Restart before admission and interruption during continuation produce the explicitly agreed replay/interruption outcome; no claim of exactly-once side effects based only on a dedupe key.
- Reset/delete and admission races cannot dispatch into a replacement conversation; authority and caller binding are revalidated.
- Old-client compatibility, expired questions, six-day questions, Skip, and newer-message behavior have executable coverage.
- An assembled web path and at least one supported channel prove presentation, answer settlement, continuation delivery, and terminal receipt. Preserve sibling harness/secret-question behavior.
- Storage migration, retention, deletion, upgrade/rollback, and worker write cost are reviewed and tested.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

Maybe, with maintainer guidance.

We intend to contribute implementation and regression coverage once the ownership, storage, and public behavior are accepted. Implementation ownership is not assigned by this issue.

### Additional information

Please review the durability/authority boundary, continuation admission integration, client compatibility, and storage/retention design before production implementation. This follows the repository's [material storage-change review checkpoint](https://docs.openclaw.ai/reference/database-schemas/storage-changes#review-checkpoint-for-material-changes).

Suggested delivery: one behavior-complete PR for agreed durable registration, settlement, and native continuation recovery; a separate follow-up for longer deadlines/client presentation if that requires independent compatibility work. Split a generic admission/provenance prerequisite only if maintainer review identifies a separately useful API. Keep tests with the behavior they prove.

The issue does not require consumer-specific policy endpoints, organizational rollout flags, or channel-specific authorization exceptions in core. Evidence should be source, tests, and bounded reproducible proof; no agent transcript is needed.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On OpenClaw 2026.9.6, two image_generate jobs successfully saved PNG artifacts but failed to deliver them to the originating Weixin direct chat; completion handoff timed out while recovery logged retired state-owner errors.

### Steps to reproduce

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO

### Expected behavior

The documented async image-generation contract says completed media is delivered to the requester, with idempotent direct fallback when the wake fails or the session is inactive: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/main/docs/tools/image-generation.md . A saved successful generation should remain recoverable for delivery without generating the image again.

### Actual behavior

Two independent jobs in one ordinary Weixin direct-chat session completed generation but neither image reached the requester. Both task_runs rows show status=succeeded, progress_summary="Generated 1 image", and terminal_outcome=blocked with a required-completion delivery timeout. Completion entries initially remained pending and repeatedly logged retired state-owner scheduling errors. A read-only inspection after a gateway restart found both entries failed while both PNG files still existed. No evidence of a Weixin upload attempt/rejection was found in the inspected logs.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.6 (eb377ac); installed package version rechecked on 2026-10-08

### Operating system

Linux Docker container on Synology NAS; exact distribution/version not recorded

### Install method

AlphaClaw-managed Docker; globally installed OpenClaw package. Incident occurred before subsequent document-runtime dependency additions; image-generation code was not patched.

### Model

gpt-6-astra via native Codex harness; image generation: gpt-image-2

### Provider / routing chain

Weixin direct chat -> openclaw-weixin -> OpenClaw Gateway -> native Codex harness -> image_generate -> OpenAI image provider -> detached completion/session-delivery queue -> original Weixin chat

### Additional provider/model setup details

_No response_

### Logs

```shell
Sanitized evidence; task/queue IDs and artifact names replaced with stable aliases.

For both tasks:
status=succeeded
progress_summary="Generated 1 image"
terminal_outcome=blocked
delivery_status=not_applicable (silent task ledger; not evidence of successful delivery)
terminal_summary="Required completion delivery failed before reaching the requester: cron continuation did not become ready before the handoff deadline. Retained generated media: Attachments: 1 ..."

Same-queue recovery error during the incident:
"cannot schedule ... for a retired state owner: OpenClaw state database read admission changed"

2026-10-08 read-only recheck after gateway restart:
queue A: status=failed, retry_count=1, last_error=null
queue B: status=failed, retry_count=0, last_error=null
artifact A: exists=true, bytes=1612842
artifact B: exists=true, bytes=1468164

Installed media-generate-background-shared bundle defines MEDIA_GENERATION_COMPLETION_HANDOFF_TIMEOUT_MS=120000; wakeMediaGenerationTaskCompletionWithRetry throws the recorded deadline error while outcome.status remains pending.
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Observed timeline on 2026-10-07, UTC+8 (not a deterministic clean-install reproduction):
1. 16:30:49: first image task submitted from a normal Weixin direct chat.
2. Approximately 16:32:26: generated PNG entered completion queue with one structured image attachment.
3. 16:34:26: handoff deadline expired.
4. 16:34:52: user asked for the image; image_generate action=status returned no active task. The agent submitted another generation instead of recovering the saved result.
5. 16:35:14: second task submitted; approximately 16:36:38 its PNG entered the completion queue.
6. 16:38:38: second handoff deadline expired.
7. Initial DB inspection: both executions succeeded, both terminal outcomes blocked, both completion entries pending. Later inspection on 2026-10-08: both queue entries failed, artifacts still present.

Queue payload inspection showed the original channel delivery context and expectedMediaUrls/expectedMediaAttachments were present. Private recipient identifiers and raw conversation content are omitted.

### Impact and severity

Affected: one observed Weixin direct-chat agent session. Severity: blocks generated-image delivery to the requester. Frequency: 2/2 observed generation jobs in this incident; broader frequency is unknown. Consequence: both usable PNG artifacts were retained locally but not delivered, and the follow-up produced an additional generation job rather than recovering the first result.

### Additional information

Related: #86034 (closed as implemented). This report supplies a later-version Weixin/Codex-harness case with matching queue recovery errors, retained artifacts, and failed delivery entries. It is not evidence that the earlier missing-target repair is absent: requester routing and media attachment metadata were present here. Whether this is the same root cause or a distinct lifecycle defect is unconfirmed.

No last-known-good version or current-main reproduction is available. The event that retired the state owner has not been isolated; please do not treat the observed chat sequence as a guaranteed reproducer. No user cron job was involved despite the timeout wording.

The active-only status lookup is documented behavior, but it hid the completed/blocked result from the follow-up and contributed to duplicate generation. This is supporting impact context, not a separate asserted status-API bug.

Suggested investigation, not a proven fix: verify session-delivery recovery reacquires a live state owner after read-admission changes, and verify timed-out completion can recover the saved attachment idempotently without requiring a new generation.

issues.body:
### Summary
A Workboard nudge that arrives while the board's automation job is still running is logged as `workboard automation nudge skipped for board <board>: job <job> already-running` and discarded; no follow-up run happens when the active run finishes, so the handoff waits for the next scheduled run.

### Problem to solve
We use a board automation as the review step for worker handoffs: when a worker releases a card to `review`, the nudge (#125170, #156130) starts the automation, which reviews, integrates and reports. A common loop is that the review finds a small defect, dispatches a follow-up on the same card and then spends several more minutes writing its report (our runs take 8–18 minutes). If the worker finishes the follow-up during those minutes, its handoff nudge hits `already-running` and is dropped. In our case the follow-up took about one minute (dispatched 19:30, finished 19:31), the automation run ended at 19:34, and the card stayed in `review` until an operator ran the job by hand at 20:26. The next scheduled run would have been the next morning.

This is by design today: `automation-nudge.ts` calls `enqueueRun(jobId, "if-enabled")` and on `ran: false` only logs a warning, and both the docs and the code comment say the automation's schedule remains the backstop. That is a reasonable guarantee, but with a daily schedule the backstop is many hours late, exactly in the short fix loops where the nudge matters most. Stream schedules already keep one bounded pending batch while a payload runs; Workboard nudges do not. (A second event inside the 60-second per-board debounce window is also dropped silently, without a log line; that was not the cause here, but the same mechanism would cover it.)

### Proposed solution
- When `enqueueRun` returns `reason: "already-running"` (the result already distinguishes it from `disabled`, `ownerless` and `invalid-spec`), mark the board as dirty in the nudge service's own state and request exactly one follow-up `if-enabled` run after the active run completes — trailing-edge coalescing: many events during a run, one run afterwards. Cron-origin sessions stay suppressed, so the follow-up cannot self-trigger, and card state is untouched.
- The cron service already has a wait-for-settlement primitive for `on-exit` schedules (`waitForRunSettlement`, used by `runOnExit`); the nudge path could reuse it instead of adding a new queue.
- Alternatively, let the cron service keep one pending manual run for jobs that are already running, like the pending batch for stream schedules.

### Alternatives considered
An `every` schedule (10 minutes) with a `trigger.script` condition that compares the latest worker attempt `endedAt` on `review`/`blocked` cards with the job's `lastRunAtMs` and fires only when a handoff arrived after the last run started. This works without model calls and is what we run now, but every operator has to write it, and it adds up to one schedule interval of latency. Before that we used an external watcher that grepped the Gateway log for `already-running`.

### Impact
- Affected: boards whose automation job reviews or orchestrates worker handoffs.
- Severity: a finished handoff waits for the next scheduled run (hours with a daily schedule).
- Frequency: whenever a worker finishes while the automation is still running — typical for short follow-up fixes dispatched by the review itself.
- Consequence: stalled cards and manual operator triggers.

### Evidence/examples
```text
19:16:31 [plugins] workboard automation nudge requested for board <board>: job <job> run manual:<job>:…
19:30:34 [ws] workboard.cards.dispatchWithOptions            (review dispatches the follow-up)
19:31:30 [plugins] workboard automation nudge skipped for board <board>: job <job> already-running
```
`openclaw cron runs`: the run started 19:16:31 finished 19:34:03 (status ok); no further run until a manual `openclaw cron run` at 20:26; `nextRunAt` was the next morning.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?
No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information
OpenClaw 2026.9.8 (fc23bc8) and 2026.9.9 (`extensions/workboard/src/automation-nudge.ts` unchanged on `main` since #156130), macOS 26.6.2 arm64, npm global install, single Gateway. Related: #156130, #125170, #116360.

No

### Summary

On an install that already has an OpenRouter OAuth sign-in, running the OpenRouter OAuth sign-in again (`openclaw.setup.auth.start` with `authChoice: "openrouter-oauth"`) succeeds at OpenRouter and saves the new key, but only as an inactive replacement. The wizard session ends in `status: "error"` with "Credentials saved; default unchanged…", and every agent keeps the old key.

The error's own suggestion, choosing the saved sign-in, doesn't work. `openclaw.setup.activate.start` with `kind: "saved-auth:<profileId>"` fails the same way, so on 2026.9.7 the new key cannot be put into use. Separately, that activation would change the default model to `openrouter/auto`, because the saved credential's `setup.modelRef` is `openrouter/auto`, even when the agents are deliberately on a specific OpenRouter model.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Fresh install. Sign in with OpenRouter OAuth through the gateway: `openclaw.setup.auth.start` `{ sessionId, authChoice: "openrouter-oauth", agentId: "main" }`, then `wizard.next` until done, approving at OpenRouter.
2. Set the default model to a specific OpenRouter model, e.g. `openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-4.8`. Make one or two agents on it. Replies work.
3. Run the same OpenRouter OAuth sign-in again (step 1), approving again at OpenRouter. OpenRouter issues a new key.
4. `models.authStatus` for any agent now lists two OpenRouter profiles:
   - the first, `openrouter:setup-<uuid-1>`, `status: "static"` (in use);
   - the new one, `openrouter:setup-<uuid-2>`, `status: "missing"`, `reasonCode: "setup_inactive"`, `displayName: "Saved sign-in (inactive)"`.
5. Send a message to any agent: the request to OpenRouter carries the old key.
6. Try to activate the saved sign-in: `openclaw.setup.activate.start` `{ sessionId, kind: "saved-auth:" + encodeURIComponent("openrouter:setup-<uuid-2>"), agentId: "main" }`, then `wizard.next`.

### Expected behavior

Signing in to OpenRouter again on an install that already uses OpenRouter should put the new key into use for the agents that use OpenRouter (the old key is likely deleted or used up, which is often why people sign in again). One of these would do:

- the OpenRouter OAuth re-login verifies the new key against the current default model and activates it, without changing the default model; or
- `openclaw.setup.activate` with `saved-auth:<id>` honours the `modelRef` it is given (or the agent's current model) instead of the method's starter model, verifies, and activates without changing the model.

The plugin's own note says "Re-run OpenRouter OAuth to rotate that key", which is what people expect to happen.

### Actual behavior

Step 3's wizard session ends with:

```
{"done":true,"status":"error","error":"Credentials saved; default unchanged. The candidate route does not match the selected provider, model, and credential. Review model runtime policy and retry. Choose the saved sign-in in Model Setup to retry without signing in again.","activationRejection":{"disposition":"rejected-before-promotion","status":"unavailable"}}
```

Step 6 ends immediately with the same error and `{"disposition":"rejected-before-promotion","status":"unavailable"}`. The new profile stays `setup.replacement: true`, and the agents keep the old key.

The first sign-in on a fresh install also ends with this error (the key is saved, and is usable only because it is the only one). We saw the same message with a real OpenRouter key on 2026-10-01, so it doesn't seem specific to our test setup.

**Where it seems to come from (reading dist):**

- `src/system-agent/setup-inference-activate.ts`, `verifyAndActivateCandidate`: `route.modelLabel !== staged.modelRef` (or the pinned auth profile differs) returns "The candidate route does not match…".
- `stageSavedAuthCandidate` uses `saved.modelRef` (`openrouter/auto`, the OpenRouter method's starter model) and ignores the `modelRef` passed to `openclaw.setup.activate`. The route that is actually resolved doesn't match it.
- If the route did match, `createSystemAgentModelSelectionUpdater({ model: staged.modelRef, authProfileId })` would set the agent's model to `openrouter/auto`. That would replace the model the person chose.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.7 (c074824)

### Operating system

Linux (Debian 13), gateway run as a systemd user service, Node 24

### Model

openrouter/anthropic/claude-opus-4.8 (the default the agents use); the saved sign-in's starter model is openrouter/auto

### Provider / routing chain

OpenRouter via OpenClaw's OpenRouter OAuth sign-in (openrouter-oauth), direct

### Additional information

Workaround we use: A small command job, with no model calls, that runs as the gateway user. It uses the plugin SDK (`updateAuthProfileStoreWithLock`) to do what `activateSavedSetupCredential` does: it deletes `setup` from the new profile and marks the old one inactive. The gateway then restarts so its auth runtime reads the store again; `models.authRefresh` alone wasn't enough, and requests kept the old key for a while. After a verification reply, the old profile is removed (`removeProviderAuthProfilesWithLock`). We'd rather not keep this.

Searched first (2026-10-08): "candidate route does not match" (0 results), "default unchanged", "saved-auth", "openrouter oauth inactive" — none about this.

issues.body:
## Summary

In restricted native Codex execution, the read-only CLI command `openclaw config get tools.exec` exits with a SQLite read-only worker `spawnSync ... EPERM` error. An operator-side isolation probe shows that a Node child can actually run successfully (`status=0`, expected version in stdout) while `spawnSync` also returns `error.code=EPERM` when stdin is piped.

This issue tracks the downstream OpenClaw failure and the upstream reports. It does not establish a broken host configuration or a verified production fix.

## Environment

- Fedora 44
- Node.js v26.8.1
- OpenClaw Core and `@openclaw/codex`: 2026.9.9
- Also observed with OpenClaw 2026.9.8
- Restricted native Codex execution
- The version of the Codex binary actually launched was not independently measured; it must not be inferred from the plugin version.

## Reproduction and actual behavior

Inside the affected native Codex execution context:

```sh
XDG_CACHE_HOME=/tmp openclaw config get tools.exec
```

Exit code: **1**. Sanitized diagnostic (paths replaced with placeholders):

```text
OpenClaw config could not be read: <config>/openclaw.json
- <root>: read failed: Error: SQLite read-only worker failed to start:
  spawnSync <runtime>/bin/node EPERM
```

An earlier `Unsafe fallback OpenClaw temp dir` error was resolved by passing `XDG_CACHE_HOME=/tmp`. It is separate from the remaining worker failure. Direct selective JSON reading of the configuration succeeded; this does not provide evidence of a defective host configuration.

## Expected behavior

The read-only configuration command should succeed where its required operations are permitted. If the execution environment prevents reliable worker communication, report that limitation accurately rather than implying that the child necessarily never started. Preserve error checking and existing security boundaries.

## Operator-confirmed isolation in the affected native context

| Invocation / stdio | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Direct Node invocation | Success |
| `spawnSync(Node, ["--version"])`, default pipes | `status=0`, `errorCode=EPERM`, expected Node version in stdout |
| `stdio: "ignore"` | Success, no EPERM |
| `stdio: "inherit"` | Success, no EPERM |
| Only stdin piped | EPERM |
| Only stdout piped | No EPERM |
| Only stderr piped | No EPERM |
| `["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"]` | No EPERM |

These are channel-isolation observations, not proof of the exact denied sandbox syscall. The successful child execution above refers to the isolation probe, not a successful full OpenClaw worker/CLI run.

## Separate controlled launcher/SQLite test — different evidence scope

In another restricted Codex execution environment, the synchronous launcher from the integrity-checked published OpenClaw 2026.9.9 npm package was tested in isolation with controlled dependencies and a disposable SQLite fixture:

| Variant | Result inside that restricted environment |
| --- | --- |
| Original launcher | EPERM |
| Ignore stdin | No EPERM, but empty captured stdout |
| Ignore stdin and emit fixture output synchronously using `fs.writeSync` | Success |

With the same Node version outside that environment, all variants succeeded.

**Important limitation:** the additional empty-stdout symptom was confirmed in this separate controlled test, not in the operator's OpenClaw-native context. No complete patched OpenClaw worker or CLI invocation was successfully tested. No production patches were installed. Synchronous fixture output is diagnostic evidence, not a production-ready fix.

## Inspected 2026.9.9 code

Published bundle: `dist/sqlite-readonly-worker-01V3ktP_.mjs`, function `runSqliteReadOnlyWorkerSync()`.

- Uses `spawnSync` with stdin piped by default.
- Checks `result.error` before `result.status`; a successful child status therefore does not rescue the command when an error is also present.
- The worker receives its inputs through arguments in `sync` mode.
- The one-shot worker emits its result with `process.stdout.write`.
- Other worker modes, particularly `reclaim`, use stdin. A blanket stdio change across all workers would be inappropriate.

## Upstream tracking

Our reproductions and their limitations are recorded here:

- stdin-pipe / EPERM observation: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/41175#issuecomment-6074712802
- Separate controlled empty-output observation: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/18473#issuecomment-6074712964

## Requested assessment

Please assess whether a narrowly scoped compatibility measure for the synchronous, argument-fed worker path is appropriate, or whether a more informative diagnostic can distinguish launcher/transport errors from actual child startup failure while upstream work is tracked.

Ignoring `result.error`, disabling the sandbox, or recommending broadly elevated permissions is not a proposed solution. Any compatibility change would need full-worker and CLI verification in the affected native context, including reliable result capture, and must preserve stdin-dependent modes such as `reclaim`.

No configuration/environment dumps, secrets, account details, hostnames, private paths, or database contents are included. No production changes, repairs, or restarts were performed for this report.

issues.body:
> **Update 2026-11-06 (live repro on current main `e29577b7d7d`):** the original "host dispatch resolved to undefined" framing below was wrong (see the 2026-10-10 comments: every recorded occurrence was guest code reading `<nested result>.value.aggregated`). The remaining bug is the title: an ordinary guest exception is still reported as `code: "internal_error"`, the same code used for genuine host/runtime failures, and the 3-strike turn-abort text carries no guest cause.
>
> Lab run on `e29577b7d7d` (`createCatalogCodeModeHarness`, a fake exec tool returning `{status, exitCode, aggregated}`), both executors:
>
> | guest code | node | quickjs |
> |---|---|---|
> | `const r = await fake_exec({...}); return r.aggregated;` (control) | `completed`, `"hi"` | `completed`, `"hi"` |
> | `... return r.value.aggregated;` | `internal_error`, `failurePhase: "guest"`, `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'aggregated')` | `internal_error`, `guest`, `TypeError: cannot read property 'aggregated' of undefined` |
> | `await tools.fake_exec({...})` | `internal_error`, `guest`, `ReferenceError: tools is not defined` | `internal_error`, `guest`, same |
>
> Source owners unchanged: `formatGuestFailure()` in `src/agents/code-mode-node.worker.ts` returns `bridgeCode ?? "internal_error"` (only `require/module/process is not defined` maps to `invalid_input`); `REPEATED_TOOL_ERROR_MESSAGE` in `packages/agent-core/src/errors.ts` has no phase or guest cause. #172850 (merged 2026-10-15) moved guest exceptions to warning-level diagnostics but kept the result code. No open PR changes either.

---

### Bug type
Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
A Code Mode `exec()` call inside a guest script can fail with `code: "internal_error"` and an empty `output`, leaving `exec()`'s resolved value `undefined`; a guest script that reads `r.aggregated` off that result then crashes with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'aggregated')`, losing the whole cell's work.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Run OpenClaw 2026.9.8 with Code Mode engaged, `exec`/`wait` visible as the only top-level tools (`visibleTools: ["exec","wait"]`).
2. From guest code, call `const r = await exec({ command: "<any shell command>" }); return r.aggregated;` (this is the ordinary, documented pattern for reading a completed exec's combined output).
3. On an internal dispatch failure, the host returns `{"status":"failed","code":"internal_error","failurePhase":"guest","bridgeDispatchStarted":true,"replaySafe":false,"output":[],...}` for the *outer* code-mode cell, not for the `exec()` call itself — the guest's `r` binds to `undefined` instead of an exec result object.
4. The guest script's own `r.aggregated` dereference throws, and the thrown error is what actually reaches the model: `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'aggregated')\n    at openclaw-code-mode:user.js:<line>:<col>`.

### Expected behavior
Either `exec()` never resolves to `undefined` on an internal host-side dispatch failure (it should reject or resolve to an object carrying `status`/`code`/`error`, matching its documented shape), or the host-level `internal_error` surfaces directly to the model as the cell's own failure before the guest script gets a chance to dereference a property on it. The model should see one clear, actionable error, not a second-order `TypeError` from its own code.

### Actual behavior
Observed verbatim, twice, in the forge agent's session store (`agent:forge:subagent:*` windows, `openclaw-agent.sqlite`, `transcript_events`), both as `isError:true` `exec` toolResults:
```
{"status":"failed","code":"internal_error","failurePhase":"guest","bridgeDispatchStarted":true,"replaySafe":false,"telemetry":{"catalogSize":52,"sources":{"openclaw":47,"mcp":5,"client":0},"counterScope":"<redacted>","searchCount":0,"describeCount":0,"callCount":27,"visibleTools":["exec","wait"]},"output":[],"error":"TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'aggregated')\n    at openclaw-code-mode:user.js:6:83"}
```
```
{"status":"failed","code":"internal_error","failurePhase":"guest","bridgeDispatchStarted":true,"replaySafe":false,"telemetry":{...,"callCount":29,"visibleTools":["exec","wait"]},"output":[],"error":"TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'aggregated')\n    at openclaw-code-mode:user.js:3:16"}
```
Both samples show `failurePhase: "guest"` and `bridgeDispatchStarted: true`, i.e. the bridge did dispatch into the guest sandbox, but something upstream of the guest's own `exec()` await resolved to `undefined` rather than an exec-result object, and the guest's dereference of `.aggregated` is what the harness recorded as the cell's terminal error.

### OpenClaw version
2026.9.8 (fc23bc8)

### Operating system
Linux (CT 112, Proxmox LXC), Debian-based

### Install method
npm global (`openclaw` CLI)

### Model
anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 (and anthropic/claude-sonnet-5 subagents); not model-specific — the dereference happens in the guest JS sandbox, not model output

### Provider / routing chain
openclaw -> anthropic (direct, Claude Code/Max auth), Code Mode engaged

### Logs
```
22 occurrences of exact string "TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'aggregated')" counted from forge-agent spawned-job transcript_events (isError:true exec toolResults), 2026-10-02 through 2026-10-08 (7 days), across 150 subagent session windows / 12,199 toolResult events scanned.
```

### Impact and severity
Affected: any Code Mode session where guest code reads `r.aggregated` after `await exec(...)` (the documented, common pattern).
Severity: Blocks workflow — the cell aborts with a confusing secondary TypeError instead of a clear host-side failure reason, and the guest script's actual work in that cell is lost.
Frequency: ~22 occurrences/week on one fleet of 5-10 agents running Code Mode continuously; not reproduced as a clean minimal repro in this report (see Additional information).
Consequence: wasted cells/turns, confusing error text surfaced to the model in place of the real host failure, extra retries.

### Additional information
NOT_ENOUGH_INFO on a minimal, deterministic repro: the two occurrences observed both show `failurePhase: "guest"` with `bridgeDispatchStarted: true` but empty `output`, which is consistent with the internal exec dispatch failing after entering the guest sandbox but before the exec() promise resolved with data — the exact trigger (host-side timeout race, bridge serialization fault, or a specific exec option) could not be isolated from the available evidence. Reporting the production-observed failure signature as-is rather than guessing at root cause, per this template's instruction not to speculate beyond the evidence.
