issues.body:
### Summary

Let operators pass an explicit vocabulary to Scribe v2 through the bundled ElevenLabs batch transcription provider using the existing `providerOptions.elevenlabs` configuration.

### Problem to solve

When transcribing recordings containing product names or specialized terms, an operator may want to supply a specific list of recognition hints. A [LiveKit developer requested this integration control](https://community.livekit.io/t/keyterms-missing-in-elevenlabs-scribe-v2-tts-plugin/408) on February 27, 2026, and supplied an implementation for that product. This is an external demand signal; applying the task to OpenClaw's recorded-audio workflow is an inference, not a report that this person uses OpenClaw.

OpenClaw already transcribes audio through Scribe v2. Its [current ElevenLabs implementation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts) reads only `no_verbatim`, `tag_audio_events`, and `diarize` from provider options. A configured `keyterms` array reaches the provider request context but never enters the multipart request. The [provider documentation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/docs/providers/elevenlabs.md#provider-options) explicitly limits support to those three fields.

The missing capability is selecting the terms used by Scribe's recognition-bias mechanism within this native transcription path. This does not promise correct spelling for every recording or a general improvement in accuracy.

### Proposed solution

Support one additional, opt-in provider option, `keyterms: string[]`, for `scribe_v2` batch transcription. Reuse current provider-scoped configuration and merge precedence; no new top-level configuration or tool is needed. For example:

```json
{
  "tools": {
    "media": {
      "models": [{
        "provider": "elevenlabs",
        "model": "scribe_v2",
        "capabilities": ["audio"]
      }],
      "audio": {
        "enabled": true,
        "providerOptions": {
          "elevenlabs": {
            "keyterms": ["OpenClaw", "Acme Research", "PostgreSQL"]
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Serialize the list as repeated multipart `keyterms` fields, following the provider's array contract and [official SDK request construction](https://github.com/elevenlabs/elevenlabs-python/blob/f5d53e09e35717523435cee238ac5cc7f51966fb/src/elevenlabs/speech_to_text/raw_client.py#L177). Preserve each term's spelling and Unicode content; do not comma-join the list or encode it as one JSON string. Keep all option fields before the original file, preserving its filename, MIME type, and bytes; the shared multipart builder documents this ordering for streaming parsers. Keep array assembly provider-local rather than widening the shared scalar helper. A model-entry list replaces the audio-default list, as existing options already do. An empty list clears inherited terms; an absent or empty effective list sends no keyterms.

Keep this an explicit allowlisted addition. Preserve dedicated fields, existing scalar options, authentication, guarded HTTP transport, cancellation, and the synchronous transcript-text result. Reject an incompatible option shape or unsupported model rather than silently applying a different control. Surface provider validation errors through the existing error/fallback handling without truncating terms silently.

Document the option and its extra provider charge before users choose it. The [current API reference](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/speech-to-text/convert) currently permits up to 1,000 terms, requires each term to have fewer than 50 characters and at most five normalized words, and specifies disallowed characters. It adds a 20% surcharge; more than 100 terms also impose a minimum billable duration of 20 seconds per request. The provider remains authoritative for validation and future billing changes. No vocabulary is inferred from conversation history or sent by default.

### Alternatives considered

- **Explicit transcription prompt:** OpenClaw already forwards a configured prompt as context. It may help some tasks, but the current ElevenLabs API reference does not specify it as equivalent to structured `keyterms`. Preserve existing prompt behavior; this proposal does not claim it is useless.
- **Deepgram:** OpenClaw supports repeatable Deepgram keyterms after [#176781](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176781). Switching providers is valid. This proposal retains the selected ElevenLabs account and model.
- **Official ElevenLabs skill or SDK, a CLI transcription model, or a custom provider plugin:** These can perform vocabulary-guided transcription outside the bundled adapter. The [official skill reference](https://github.com/elevenlabs/skills/blob/9a1a4b7fbb6ca02fbdc7f44f2271e6c829d0f421/speech-to-text/references/transcription-options.md) includes keyterms. These are real alternatives; native support avoids maintaining a separate transcription script or provider registration for one additional input.
- **Correct text afterward:** This can repair known spelling errors but does not give the recognizer a selected term list. An uncertain correction can also change meaning.

### Impact

- Affected users/systems/channels: Operators using bundled ElevenLabs transcription for recorded audio with specialized vocabulary. The affected OpenClaw population is unknown.
- Severity/urgency: The requested recognition control is unavailable in that adapter; ordinary transcription remains usable. No production outage or measured urgency is established.
- Frequency: A configured list would apply to matching transcription requests. Actual usage frequency is unknown.
- Practical consequences: Operators must accept transcription without that control, correct text, switch providers, or maintain another integration. Time savings and accuracy gains have not been measured. Enabling keyterms can increase provider charges.

### Evidence/examples

- [Original integration request and follow-up](https://community.livekit.io/t/keyterms-missing-in-elevenlabs-scribe-v2-tts-plugin/408); [LiveKit implementation #4967](https://github.com/livekit/agents/pull/4967). These concern the same author and task, not two independent users.
- [Official keyterm guide](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-api/guides/how-to/speech-to-text/batch/keyterm-prompting) describes vocabulary biasing and distinguishes batch and realtime inputs.
- [Current options schema](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/src/config/zod-schema.core.ts#L627), [runner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/src/media-understanding/runner.entries.ts#L86), and [registered provider](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e8764a3fa59ccd28e66902d6bc86548c20ae3560/extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts#L22) establish the input path and missing mapping.
- [#177975](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177975) already implemented three scalar options. This request adds a vocabulary input; it does not reopen that repaired bug or propose unrestricted forwarding.

Verification was static against the pinned main revision. No installed Gateway, live ElevenLabs transcription, or recognition-quality comparison was run for this proposal.

### Do you plan to open a PR for this?

No, proposing the idea only

### Additional information

The implementation owner is `extensions/elevenlabs/index.ts`; its former standalone media-understanding module was consolidated into registration. Suggested work is provider-local array serialization and validation, focused registered-provider coverage, and documentation. Public `AudioTranscriptionRequest.query` already accepts string arrays. A new SDK contract, provider manager, dictionary store, or model-facing tool is unnecessary.

Preserve the existing media authorization, HTTP guards, and cancellation behavior applicable to the caller at dispatch; this option does not introduce a new universal execution context. A vocabulary does not authorize a transcription request. Keep terms out of diagnostic logs; they may contain names absent from the audio. No retention or permission change is requested.

Non-goals: Realtime/Voice Call/Google Meet transcription, TTS pronunciation dictionaries, vocabulary management, speaker-label output, asynchronous webhooks, redaction, multichannel results, unrestricted form overrides, or guaranteed accuracy. No implementer has committed.

Acceptance criteria:

- With an isolated configuration selecting `elevenlabs/scribe_v2`, native recorded-audio transcription sends two configured terms as separate multipart fields alongside one unchanged audio file, and returns the transcript through the existing path.
- Capture the actual HTTP body from the shipped transcription entry point, not only a helper call. Verify model-entry replacement of defaults, an empty list clearing defaults, and unchanged requests without a list.
- Existing scalar `false` values and dedicated model/language/prompt fields retain their behavior. Other providers do not receive the ElevenLabs vocabulary; unsupported response-changing keys remain excluded.
- An incompatible scalar value or unsupported model does not silently send an unconditioned Scribe request. Provider-side term rejection surfaces without truncation. With an actual cancellation-capable execution context, cancellation before dispatch prevents a request.
- In an authorized live check, submit a synthetic name-bearing recording with a valid small vocabulary and confirm provider acceptance and native transcript return. Recognition output is observational evidence, not a promise that every supplied term appears.

issues.body:
## Summary

**At least 28** failures on stable **2026.10.5**; child effects unproved; no fix.

```text
service child cleanup identity lost: Error: Direct shared-state reader requires current integrity admission
```

## Environment

- Ubuntu **24.04.5 LTS**, Linux x64 **6.8.0-147-generic**.
- Node.js **24.21.0**.
- Stock npm OpenClaw **2026.10.5 (1b58cb9)**, managed user Gateway service.
- Official `v2026.10.5` tag resolves to commit
  `1b58cb9a1b4f4353e1add63c8506db4d890962e8`.
- No locally patched core files were carried into this stable update.
- No deliberate concurrent schema mutation, forced workflow, restart,
  database repair, integrity bypass or child replay was used to reproduce it.
  The triggering operation was an already occurring ordinary scheduled turn.

## Actual Evidence And Timing

Original native event clocks, UTC:

| Evidence | Observed value |
| --- | --- |
| Host-exec request event | 2026-10-19T19:05:14.174Z |
| Native error result event | 2026-10-19T19:05:15.134Z; `isError:true` |
| Event-clock difference | 960 ms; not measured child runtime |
| Admitted helper stdout | None returned |
| Child start/exit/reap/cleanup receipt | None returned; lifecycle unknown |
| Repetition count | At least twenty-eight unique ordinary native-exec failures, including intervening successful ordinary turns |

Opaque SHA-256 digests of the retained canonical events (no event payloads
or identifiers are published):

### Subsequent Ordinary Observation: Did Not Recur

  `71b87546c13fb672d52fa4a8351e939a5e38e7e59056a77b6f57ded597e6d488`.
- Admitted result: 2026-10-19T19:34:49.693Z, `isError:false`, `ok:true`,
  event digest
  `5f6fb687db628e2c9d9ccb80141195c0c5226716dd392155740503c9a63275b6`.
- The owning turn then genuinely persisted its question and source attempts,
  validated the written plan successfully, completed normal delivery/release
  and reached native terminal at 19:36:16.953Z. At 19:36:43Z the read-only
  handoff check found no matching runtime processes or active OAuth leases.

Intervening independent success required no core patch or restart; it neither repaired nor replayed the earlier unknown child outcome.

### Recurrence On A Different Local Read

A subsequent untouched ordinary turn returned the same full error on a
different local Python command that reads retained JSON research context:

- Request event: 2026-10-19T20:03:25.112Z, digest
  `e9b1da906778bf797fd8fc53bf117112a83053f26dc9aa253eb84005504cfa61`.
- Error result: 2026-10-19T20:03:25.751Z, `isError:true`, digest
  `70720e276fc1c900f1d3a01c94001c691ad8b1d89f045bde0c6b012965916bd5`.
- Event-clock difference: 639ms, not measured child runtime. Again, no helper
  stdout or child start/terminal receipt was admitted; actual child outcome
  remains unknown.

The turn continued using independent retained facts and fresh provider observations, without a same-reference retry, deliberate invalidation, core change, restart or forced workflow. That continuation does not prove the rejected child's outcome.

The local helper is a pure structural preparation operation: its relevant
branch imports no SQLite/OpenClaw state, Node runtime, claim or database
reader. A separate direct local structural invocation succeeds. That control
does **not** exercise native service-child admission and is not a repaired
native-exec result.

The owning workflow retained the failed preparation/persistence disposition;
it did not obtain completed question registration or attempt persistence
through this rejected call. The turn later completed its mandatory reporting
and bookkeeping. Those later technical flags do not prove the rejected exec
operation healthy, its persistence completed or any financial action cleared.

## Installed Source Boundary, Not A Captured Stack

Package-relative locations in this exact installed build:

- `dist/openclaw-state-db-read-connection-BVtgeFmS.mjs:97`:
  `prepareOpenClawStateDirectReader` rejects if the integrity revision differs
  from its epoch, or an existing-schema context lacks integrity/proof.
- `dist/exec-approvals-store-B7WwLRrI.mjs:218`:
  `prepareExecApprovalsCurrentRead(context)` prepares this direct reader;
  its returned guard independently rechecks admission and reads current policy.
- `dist/plugin-node-host-YOtba4hi.mjs:102`:
  plugin-exec authorization captures the worker context and prepares that
  current-policy reader. The approvals store has another authorization
  settlement caller; this error alone does not select between them.
- `dist/child-DMrKblk4.mjs:702`:
  service-child `loseIdentity` wraps its message as
  `service child cleanup identity lost: ...`.

The retained tool error is **not a JavaScript stack**. It does not reveal the
exact caller branch, concurrent writer, integrity epoch/revision/proof values,
schema operation, or ordering relative to process spawn. The source matches
identify a boundary to investigate, not a proven root cause or proof that
Python itself accessed shared state.

Exact installed artifact SHA-256s:

```text

```

## ClawSweeper Follow-Up

The [review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/177656#issuecomment-6275795871)
requests an isolated failing native stable case, payload-free admission and
child-lifecycle diagnostics, and the same case on pinned main. **These behavioral
proof requests remain unfulfilled.** No repair PR or incident-matched fix is claimed.

Source inspection confirms that merged [PR #169584](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/169584),
commit `d502f1aac87aee6c99c92a8a667810a2fefa4d88`, replaces the
[stable direct-reader policy preparation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/1b58cb9a1b4f4353e1add63c8506db4d890962e8/src/infra/exec-approvals-store.ts#L148)
with a [worker-prepared current-policy owner](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d502f1aac87aee6c99c92a8a667810a2fefa4d88/src/infra/exec-approvals-store.ts#L286).
The changed path is a relevant candidate, not proof it resolves this incident.
Its separately reported synthetic allow/revocation evidence is not this case.

Inspected suites, an inconclusive bounded attempt and successful native controls
are recorded below, not a failure repro or suite verdict. Consumer/invalidator,
integrity values and child outcome remain unknown. Keep open; do not duplicate
existing repairs, manufacture revocation, patch/restart core or replay unknown work.

## Existing Repair And Duplicate Check

[PR #167486](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/167486) already fixes
redundant schema initialization invalidating prepared exec integrity proof.
Its merge `5a0baa04e5bbe68767a9691497324c47c1ba3f96` is an ancestor of this
installed stable commit; GitHub compare reports behind=0. Its existing
real-worker/native-printf proof is useful prior work. This observation does
**not** establish that the same schema producer ran or regressed, nor justify
reimplementing that repair.

Distinct related boundaries, not duplicate evidence:

- [#176353](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/176353), fixed by
  [#176413](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/176413), concerns
  `Exec approval policy is unavailable or changing before execution`
  during Allow Once approval bookkeeping. This report has a different exact
  integrity error and no observed Allow Once trigger.
- [#161171](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/161171) concerns
  session-accessor prepared-admission tests, not this observed exec guard.
- [#161439](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/161439) tracks
  shared-state responsiveness. No event-loop/SQL-wait attribution was captured
  for the 960-ms event interval here; this is not evidence of its historical
  ordinary-workload stall.
- [#139887](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/139887) concerns a
  macOS EPERM process-group cleanup observation, not Linux integrity admission.

Read-only repository searches for the exact full error, `Direct shared-state
reader`, `prepareExecApprovalsCurrentRead`, and related integrity/exec-approval
terms found the merged repair above but no issue tracking this exact new
stable-release observation. Search results are not proof that no duplicate
exists; please consolidate under an existing exact owner if appropriate.

## Reproduction Status And Proposed Minimal Isolation

**No deterministic failing stable/main case or before/after repair proof exists.**
Use a credential-free Linux/Node24 scratch fixture and actual native consumer:

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/exec-approvals-schema-admission.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Existing #167486 first-read/profile/provenance/bound-approval/audit and reopen
cases are starting points; the older-checkout attempt below timed out without
a verdict. A harmless native request may use
`python3 -c 'import json; print(json.dumps({"ok": True}))'`; direct Python is
not equivalent. Expand only from an observed failure.

Capture payload-free consumer, captured/current revision+epoch/proof, generation,
invalidating writer/committed outcome and ordered launch/exit/reap/cleanup.
Authorized execution must settle once; genuine authority changes must deny.
Unknown outcomes, blind replay and integrity bypass are not repair evidence.

## Evidence Ledger / Remaining Gaps

Supplied: pinned stable environment, canonical timings/digests, artifacts and repair/duplicate checks. At least28 distinct failures are retained. Positive controls and later ordinary success are not failing reproductions or fixes. The failing consumer, admission invalidator, child lifecycle, matched-main regression and repaired exactly-once/real-revocation behavior remain unproved.

## Further Ordinary Recurrence (2026-10-19)

An untouched later ordinary turn returned the identical full native exec error
twice more, bringing the retained total at that observation to four unique native errors:

| Local operation | Request UTC / SHA-256 | Error UTC / SHA-256 | Event-clock gap |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Read retained JSON context | `23:03:56.178Z` / `46c2b8ec08da558a09fd3ac7a438e4cf6f3aed7d52198670ec35241bc8716311` | `23:03:56.772Z` / `e9bedb11159fbb0bca1ba35381f05870205dd9e496142e34f50dfd7b5bc9d1e2` | 594 ms |
| Local finalization wrapper | `23:04:58.141Z` / `5ab1aabe66e4fa3547a9a1da9fad21d6af70bed2bbcdcdb72ec38925d0bb2ef6` | `23:04:58.660Z` / `0b33c2bce5dd057ab1e15ab6dd5d9b69e37bcb63d764ec7b7122ad1885e19b25` | 519 ms |

Both matched canonical results are `isError:true` with the quoted wrapped error. Intervals are event-clock spacing, not child runtimes. Neither admitted stdout/terminal proof; child effects remain unknown. Wrapper echoes are excluded and neither uncertain command was replayed.

The owning turn later reached a separate real finalizer result: exit 1 for a
missing new-candidate row. Canonical save, delivery, status and release completed,
while three technical verification checks were false. This establishes degraded
workflow completion, but does not establish that either native integrity failure
caused the independent candidate-registration failure. No Python decimal error,
broker failure, trade execution or financial clearance is inferred.

At this dated follow-up, latest stable was still `2026.10.5`; no core patch/update, Gateway restart or production/approval-data edit was used.

### Isolated Investigation Status

Exact installed boundaries were rechecked; consumer/invalidator and child outcome
remain unknown. Successful controls do not fulfill the failing-case requests above.

### Executed Stable Native Positive Controls

**Real environment tested:** the unmodified installed `2026.10.5` artifacts on
Linux / Node `v24.21.0`. A fresh process inherited only an explicit small `env -i`
environment: executable search path and scratch `HOME`, `TMPDIR`,
`OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`. No production configuration,
state, provider credentials, Gateway connection or listening port was used.

**Exact behavior exercised:** stock database bootstrap seeded a synthetic
`full` / `off` policy in scratch state; the stock provenance worker primed its
ordinary feature schema; stock asynchronous database close completed. Two
scenarios then reopened that scratch database and used stock
`captureOpenClawStateWorkerContext` + `prepareExecApprovalsCurrentRead`:

1. Baseline after reopen.
2. An ordinary `listAgentProvenance()` worker read after reader preparation and
   before native launch.

Each scenario invoked the installed process supervisor's native
`anchored-shell` owner with the harmless command
`printf 'isolated-native-ok\n'` and its `required-all` cleanup owner. A fixture
guard called the actual prepared policy reader at every stock supervisor guard
callback and asserted the synthetic policy remained `full` / `off`. The fixture
did not invoke the full model/tool transport, plugin-exec policy consumer or
approval-settlement consumer; it exercises their implicated reader boundary with
a real native service child, not their complete authorization flow.

**Observed result, without a patch:** both real native calls returned exit 0
with exactly the expected stdout; each made six current-policy reader checks,
and both native scope cleanup joins completed. Captured epoch and current
revision were both `0` throughout; actual proof was present and unchanged.
The captured context's `existingSchemaPath` was absent. No diagnostic fields
were modified, no schema was dropped and no revocation was manufactured.

```text

provenance-after-preparation: checks=6, exitCode=0, expectedStdout=true, scope-cleanup-joined

```

Both scenarios and the enclosing process were joined; no control child was left
running. These hashes identify retained controls, not an attached reproducible
failing fixture.

Successful isolated stock-native controls only: no failing repro, production child-outcome proof, incident-matched main comparison or main deployment/test.

### Fifth Ordinary Occurrence: First Cycle Command

The next untouched scheduled turn failed on its first cycle-admission command,
before any broker/provider call. At that observation the retained total was

- Request event: `2026-10-19T23:32:13.679Z`, SHA-256

This occurrence independently blocks admission before the earlier candidate-registration defect. Caller, invalidator and spawn order remain unknown. First-feature scratch exploration produced no result and is excluded; subsequent inspection found no scratch/native-control processes. Outstanding proof requests remain open.

### Sixth Unique Canonical Recurrence: Local Contract Read

Additional ordinary recurrence on unmodified stable2026.10.5, 2026-10-20; not a fix.

The directly recorded native `exec` request was a read-only local file operation:

A plain local workflow-contract file read, not a database operation.

The working directory was the configured agent workspace. No host override was supplied. This command did not request any broker action, network operation, credential change, or state repair.

Recurrence only: isolated failing, matched-candidate and genuine-revocation proof remain absent. Privacy exclusions below apply.

## Seventh Ordinary Recurrence: 2026-10-20T01:04Z

Sanitized evidence for the existing issue #177656. This is an observation of an ordinary scheduled cycle, not an injected reproduction or a claim that the issue has been fixed.

### Environment And Pinned Code

- Installed package version, read directly from package.json: **OpenClaw 2026.10.5 stable**.
- package.json SHA-256: `44c4e2ed880440392d10224f0fec7c4f5ad59d93008827586e2acb038a5a21ee`.

### Observed Chronology

1. Ordinary scheduled native turn began at **2026-10-20T01:02:13.461Z**, using the existing native OpenAI/Codex path and unchanged auth/runtime owner.
2. At **01:04:49.411Z**, a native `exec` tool call requested a bounded read-only Python helper that indexes retained local venue proposals. Shape only: `{command: <fixed Python helper plus symbol argument>, workdir: <existing workflow directory>, title: <source lookup description>}`. Command payload, symbol, private paths and identifiers are intentionally omitted.
3. At **01:04:50.391Z**, the corresponding native runtime `tool.result` recorded `success: false`. Exact error:

   Same exact wrapped error quoted in Summary.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

In the native iOS chat, markdown tables are hard to read on a small iPhone, for three reasons:

1. **Columns don't wrap.** A two-column table with medium-length cells doesn't fit the width. Column 1 stays on one line and takes over half the width, and the last column gets cut off at the screen edge.
2. **No scroll cue.** Nothing shows the table can scroll sideways, so the clipped text looks lost.
3. **Smaller text.** Table text renders noticeably smaller than the paragraph and list text around it in the same reply. Raising the text size doesn't close that gap.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On an iPhone, ask the agent for a 2-column table where column 1 has entries like `Canola oil (ideally cold-pressed)` and column 2 has short phrases like `Sautéing, roasting, drizzling`.
2. View the reply in the iOS app.

### Expected behavior

- Cells wrap so the table fits the available width, at least for text columns.
- If a table really is too wide to fit, a visible cue (scroll indicator or edge fade) shows there's more to the right.
- Table text uses the same size as the body text of the reply.

### Actual behavior

- Column 1 stays on one line, and column 2 is clipped mid-word ("Sautéing, roasting, driz", "Baking, stir-fries, all-pu").
- There's no scroll indicator.
- Table text is clearly smaller than the paragraphs and bullet list right below it.

### OpenClaw version

2026.10.3 (59cb447), iOS app 2026.10.70

### Operating system

iOS 27.2, iPhone 15; gateway on Ubuntu (VPS)

### Install method

iOS app from the App Store; gateway via npm

### Model

N/A (client-side rendering). The reply came from claude-opus-5-5

### Provider / routing chain

N/A (client-side rendering), Anthropic API direct

### Additional information

Possibly related: `ChatMarkdownTableView` in `apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawChatUI/ChatMarkdownBlockViews.swift` uses `ScrollView(.horizontal, showsIndicators: false)`, which would explain the missing cue. I haven't confirmed why the cells don't wrap or why the table font is smaller.

For comparison, Poe's iOS app also scrolls wide tables, but its table text matches the body size and stays readable. Screenshots to follow in a comment.

issues.body:
After using the iOS app, Settings feels visually disconnected from chat—more like a separate web interface inside the app. Screenshots make this easier to explain.

## 1. Simplify the navigation hierarchy

Settings has a fixed native **Settings / Gateway** toolbar, then another **Settings** heading inside the page. In Appearance, a second **Back / Appearance** row appears beneath that toolbar.

When scrolling, the inner title and back control disappear while the outer Settings toolbar stays. This makes the navigation feel like two stacked interfaces.

Captured screens supporting this feedback (attachments pending): Settings top, Settings scrolled, Appearance top, and Appearance scrolled.

## 2. Bring chat and Settings into one visual system

The typography, spacing, contrast, and controls feel noticeably different between chat and Settings. To my eye, the Settings screens feel dated and dense compared with the rest of the app.

A more consistent type scale, clearer secondary text, and coordinated navigation would help. This isn’t necessarily a request for a full native rewrite.

Captured screens supporting this feedback (attachments pending): empty chat and Appearance UI.

## 3. Explain which settings affect this phone versus the Gateway

“This Control UI client” is implementation language. As a phone user, I want to understand:

- Does this change only this iPhone?
- Does it affect my other devices?
- Does it change the agent or Gateway?

The Appearance description says preferences are for “this Control UI client,” while theme and language descriptions say they sync through the Gateway. The scope is hard to follow.

Labels such as **Prefs**, **steer / queue**, and the `ui.seamColor` explanation could also use clearer, user-facing wording.

Captured screens supporting this feedback (attachments pending): Appearance top and Appearance UI.

## 4. Bring session filtering to iOS

On web and macOS, I can filter the session list. On iOS, that filtering isn’t available, making it harder to find the conversation I want as the list grows.

Please bring the same filtering options to iOS, adapted for the smaller screen.

## Maintainer direction

**Would a focused design proposal be welcome before a PR?** Happy to help test changes and provide more screenshots.

## Screenshot context

These are app-only crops captured from the installed iOS app on November 6, 2026 (Pacific). They show the current installed experience, not a proposed redesign. The installed source revision is unknown; this is product feedback rather than a claim that every point reproduces on current `main`. Session filtering is user-reported; the captured screenshots cover chat and Settings.

## Screenshots

Six app-only screenshots have been captured, but the CLI attachment upload was rejected because the posting account lacks repository write access. Screenshots still need to be attached through the GitHub web interface.

issues.body:
**Version:** 2026.9.4 (3a9d69d), official container image, Linux arm64, self-hosted.

**Symptom:** `view_image` on a HEIC file logs

```
view_image failed: Image processor unavailable for jpeg encoding; tried: photon, imagemagick, graphicsmagick, ffmpeg
```

Each failed call leaves roughly 250–400 MB of gateway RSS that is not released while idle (JS heap stays ~450–500 MB; the growth is off-heap).

**Repro:** one subagent on a vision-capable model calls `view_image` on six copies of a 2.7 MB, 4032×3024 iPhone HEIC. Gateway memory goes ~1.0 GB → ~3.0 GB peak, ~2.4 GB retained 2+ minutes after the run ends.

**Expected:** a failed conversion releases its buffers; ideally the failure is detected before the image is decoded.

**Workaround:** install ImageMagick with HEIC support in the container. The same test then ends at ~0.66 GB with all images converted.

**Possibly related:** #131492.

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
A long-lived orchestration conversation reported that automated continuation turns could neither spawn a replacement subagent nor dispatch follow-up work, while a subsequent human-triggered turn could. A fresh isolated scheduled-run control successfully spawned a child, so this is NOT a blanket inability to spawn from cron.

Related: #187535, #175062, #178812.

### Steps to reproduce
Observed workflow, not yet a deterministic minimal reproduction:
1. In a long-lived Control UI conversation using Claude CLI, authorize an agent to supervise child sessions and finish their work unattended.
2. Let supervisor/completion notifications continue that conversation without a fresh human message.
3. Have the continuation send follow-up work to an existing child or spawn a replacement child.
4. Compare the result after a fresh human message in the same conversation.

Historical session evidence reports the two errors below around 07:25 UTC+08 on November 7, followed by successful dispatch around 07:55 after a human message. These errors were recovered from the assistant's subsequent explanation, NOT independently recovered raw tool results. The assistant explicitly corrected an earlier “all night” claim: the identified interruption was about 30 minutes. Exact attribution between supervisor wake, child completion, and queued follow-up remains unproven.

### Expected behavior
Previously authorized orchestration should retain the bounded, revalidated authority and Gateway custody required to continue it, or fail at admission with a supported recovery path. A fresh human message should not be needed merely to reconnect an otherwise-authorized continuation to its Gateway. A fresh isolated scheduled-run control below demonstrates that scheduled execution can legitimately spawn a child.

### Actual behavior
Historical reported errors:
```text
sessions_send: Followup completion requires in-process caller custody.
sessions_spawn: Requester provenance requires trusted in-process Gateway dispatch.
```
The work was resumed following a human-triggered turn. This does not establish that all automated turns fail.

### OpenClaw version
2026.11.1, running Gateway commit b9d3e55ad90c4547308718feb5ef5f6f4d6a8d36

### Operating system
macOS 26.6.1 (25G76)

### Install method
Git checkout, local Gateway

### Model
Affected historical conversation: anthropic/claude-sonnet-5-5 through Claude CLI. Fresh isolated scheduled control: anthropic/claude-opus-5-5 through Claude CLI.

### Provider / routing chain
OpenClaw Gateway → Claude CLI → Anthropic

### Logs
Fresh diagnostic scheduled at 2026-11-07 03:42:15 UTC, isolated agentTurn, creator tool cap ["*"], timeout120s, delivery none:
- Scheduler receipt: status ok, completionStatus succeeded, duration28421ms.
- Probe reported sessions_spawn accepted; agents_wait returned status done with exact child output WAKE_AUTHORITY_CHILD_OK (4.4s).
- Probe reported automations add was not exposed in its scheduled tool schema; no timer was created and no bypass was attempted.
- The one-shot disappeared from the current inventory after completion; its recorded outcome was recovered with `openclaw automations runs --id <probe-id> --limit 1`. Visible-session history for its run key was unavailable afterward. Thus the control is supported by the recorded run summary, not an independently inspected child transcript.

Focused existing tests on the running checkout, single worker:
```text
node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run   src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-spawn-gateway.test.ts   src/agents/tools/in-process-gateway.test.ts   src/agents/tools/cron-tool.management.test.ts   src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.model-routing-authority.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
Test Files 4 passed (4)
Tests 61 passed (61)
```
These are existing boundary tests, NOT a new reproducer of the failing continuation lifecycle. No production patch, rebuild, restart, or credential substitution was made.

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence
Code paths matching the historical error strings at the reported commit:
- `src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-spawn-gateway.ts`: refuses requester-bearing agent dispatch without trusted in-process Gateway context.
- `src/agents/tools/in-process-gateway.ts`: refuses requester provenance on transport fallback.
- `src/agents/tools/sessions-send-followup-custody.ts`: throws when captureOperatorToolGatewayContinuationContext returns no custody.

These identify refusal conditions, not the lifecycle step that lost the binding. Please preserve those checks rather than relaxing them globally.

### Impact and severity
Blocks unattended recovery of child work in the observed conversation until a human sends another message. Two different dispatch operations were reported refused in that episode. Frequency across other continuation paths is unknown; a fresh isolated scheduled control succeeded.

### Additional information
Please compare the admitted Gateway resolver, requester provenance, and continuation custody across supervisor/session-target wakes, child-result announcements, exec-completion continuations, and fresh user turns. Include a regression test across turn termination and resumption, not just direct helper invocation.

Two adjacent symptoms are deliberately excluded from the claimed bug:
- Fresh timer creation from a scheduled turn is explicitly self-scoped away in `src/agents/tools/cron-tool.ts` and `src/gateway/tool-resolution-authority.ts`. Own-job next_check is the supported continuation mechanism when admitted. Changing that policy is distinct from repairing lost dispatch custody.
- “Automation has no recorded inference account” is an inference-binding refusal, not evidence of missing tool authority. Related account-following request: #193855.

No claim that the failing lifecycle has been deterministically reproduced, or that a particular source patch fixes it.

issues.body:
## Summary

After upgrading to 2026.11.1, every scheduled heartbeat run finishes its patrol but the final `heartbeat_respond` tool call is rejected by the gateway: `heartbeat_respond is only accepted during a heartbeat run`. The gateway then treats the run as failed and delivers a "⚠️ Heartbeat Respond failed" alert to the owner DM every heartbeat interval.

## Environment

- OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (4ffdd20), macOS 15.6.1 arm64, gateway via launchd
- `agents.defaults.heartbeat`:
```json
{
  "every": "4h",
  "timeoutSeconds": 180,
  "lightContext": true,
  "isolatedSession": true
}
```
- heartbeat target was the default (`owner`)

## Timeline

- Gateway upgraded to 2026.11.1 and restarted Nov 6 19:21 (+08)
- First scheduled heartbeat fire after upgrade (Nov 7 07:30:15 +08) and the next (11:30:13 +08) both failed with the same signature. No such failures exist in logs before the upgrade (earlier heartbeat errors were model FailoverError, different signature).

## Log evidence

```
2026-11-07T07:30:15.498+08:00 [auto-reply/agent-turn-timing] agent turn milestone runId=c3055e74-22fe-47bb-8945-e19994d9a308 sessionId=f3d1a099-0384-40d7-aa53-287b35e8e3ca sessionKey=agent:main:main:heartbeat milestone=tool_execution_started totalMs=16074
2026-11-07T07:30:15.503+08:00 [tools] heartbeat_respond failed: heartbeat_respond is only accepted during a heartbeat run raw_params={"notify":false,"outcome":"no_change","summary":"Heartbeat todo list empty; nothing needs attention."}
2026-11-07T11:30:13.357+08:00 [auto-reply/agent-turn-timing] agent turn milestone runId=99099b6f-838f-4fc4-8ed0-326f8bdcb395 sessionId=cda125e1-62d9-45e4-bf83-bff0b48d3e8a sessionKey=agent:main:main:heartbeat milestone=tool_execution_started totalMs=13772
2026-11-07T11:30:13.362+08:00 [tools] heartbeat_respond failed: heartbeat_respond is only accepted during a heartbeat run raw_params={"notify":false,"outcome":"no_change","summary":"Heartbeat patrol clean: no active exec sessions, no subagents, no media tasks, no interrupted inputs; scratch shows no pending items."}
```

The patrol itself runs fine (the model executes its checks and produces a no_change summary); only the result-recording call is rejected.

## Observed behavior

- Owner DM receives, every 4h: the one-time "First heartbeat alert" explainer plus "⚠️ Heartbeat Respond failed"
- Heartbeat outcome is never recorded

## Workaround

`openclaw config set agents.defaults.heartbeat.target "none"` — stops the DM alerts; patrol keeps running, failures stay internal.

## Suspected cause

A 2026.11.1 regression in how the heartbeat-run identity is propagated to the tool policy layer: for scheduled isolated-session heartbeat turns (sessionKey `agent:main:main:heartbeat`), the validator no longer recognizes the run as a heartbeat run, so it rejects the very tool the heartbeat turn is supposed to end with.

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug / observability gap

### Summary
In one Control UI conversation, an owner turn was admitted with Gateway-wide automation management. About 50 seconds later, the next owner turn from the same profile and client was admitted **without** it (`automations list` returned only the conversation's own jobs). The persisted metadata for the two turns is identical. The inputs that decide `chat.send` cron-creator admission are neither persisted nor logged, so the cause can't be found after the fact, and the owner can't tell why management disappeared.

Related: #146870 (separate `runs` gap, seen in turn A below) and #168823 (scope loss after subagent completion; does not match here, because the subagent settle arrived after the loss).

### Steps to reproduce
Intermittent; no deterministic repro yet. Observed sequence on one Core Router dashboard conversation:

| turn | persisted origin | entitlement | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | owner profile, `openclaw-control-ui`/webchat, no provenance, not steer/spawn | yes | `list` = full inventory |
| B (~50 s after A finished) | identical | **no** | `list` = caller scope (2 jobs); prompt-cache diagnostic reports the "Tooling" section changed |
| C | identical | no | caller scope |

### Expected behavior
Either the next authenticated owner turn from a Control UI admin connection is entitled again, or the refusal is attributable: a log, audit field, or user-visible reason saying which admission condition failed.

### Actual behavior
Management silently drops to caller scope. Repeating the request in the conversation doesn't restore it, and no log line explains why.

Ruled out on the affected gateway:
- An earlier scheduled continuation that targeted the same conversation. It terminated `succeeded`, and its one-shot job was deleted after the run.
- A leftover `cronRunContinuation` marker on the conversation entry. There is none, and turn A came after that continuation and was entitled.
- A gateway restart, or a Control UI build-mismatch reload.
- Device scopes. Every paired Control UI device has `operator.admin`.

Remaining unrecorded inputs to `resolveGatewayChatCronCreatorAuthorityAdmission` / `resolveDirectOperatorAuthority`:
- the connection's `internal.controlUiAdmin` / effective scopes. These are set at connect time and can be narrowed per connection by `applyConnectionScopeCap` or a remote-ingress principal.
- the client-supplied `reconnectResumeRequested`
- `turnKind`
- `isSystemGenerated`

Proposed instrumentation: one sanitized record per `chat.send` admission (for example, fields on the `agent.run.started` audit event) containing:
- `clientId`, `authMethod`
- booleans: `isLocalClient`, `controlUiAdmin`, `hasAdminScope`, `remoteIngress`, `reconnectResume`
- `turnKind`, input provenance kind, `hasRestoredCronContinuation`
- decision (`entitled` | `caller-scoped`) and the first failing condition

The record holds no tokens or content.

Regression tests worth adding:
- Restricted turns stay caller-scoped:
  - scheduled/internal provenance
  - steer
  - `spawnedBy`
  - `reconnectResume`
  - no admin scope
  - capped remote ingress
- After a run completes (including NO_REPLY), throws, times out, or is aborted, its grants are refused **and** the next fresh admitted human turn is entitled again.

### OpenClaw version
2026.11.1 (ee336e0)

### Operating system
macOS 26 (Mac mini, native gateway)

### Install method
npm global (Homebrew Node)

### Model
openai/gpt-6.1-sol (agent primary)

### Provider / routing chain
openclaw-native-codex-responses

### Logs
Gateway logs at the default level contain only prompt-cache WARN lines for these runs, with no admission or connection events. That absence is the issue.

issues.body:
### Bug type
Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker
No

### Summary
On Vertex AI, `gemini-2.5-flash` abandons structured function calling for an entire turn and emits a malformed `print(default_api.<tool>(...))` text call whenever any tool in the request's declared tool list has a JSON Schema parameter named after a Python hard keyword (e.g. `in`, `from`) — even for tool calls unrelated to the offending tool.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Configure a `google-vertex` model provider pointing at `gemini-2.5-flash`, authenticated via a service account (ADC).
2. Enable the `coding` tool profile (or otherwise ensure the built-in `automations` tool, which has an `in` parameter for its `next_check` action, is in the declared tool list alongside other tools).
3. Ask the agent to use any tool, e.g. `read` a file: `openclaw agent exec "Use the read tool to read <file> and tell me its first line."` (fresh session/state dir to avoid conversation-history confounds).
4. Observe the run fails with `MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL: print(default_api.read(path='...'))`, even though the `read` tool's own schema has nothing wrong with it.

Isolated further with a minimal reproduction: I captured the exact request OpenClaw sent (system instruction, 35 function declarations from the `coding` profile, thinking config) and replayed it directly against the Vertex `generateContent` endpoint via curl, then bisected the 35 tool declarations. Removing or renaming the single `in` property on the built-in `automations` tool's schema was sufficient to flip the result from `MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL` to a correct, structured `functionCall` part — with every other property of every other tool held constant. The built-in `memory_get` tool has the same latent issue with a `from` property.

### Expected behavior
The agent should always call `read` (or any other unrelated tool) with a normal structured function call, since the `automations` tool's schema is well-formed JSON Schema and the `read` tool's schema has no keyword collisions.

### Actual behavior
The turn fails with `Google generation stopped (MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL): Malformed function call: print(default_api.read(path='...'))`, reproducible on the first attempt of a fresh session, deterministically, whenever the `automations` (or `memory_get`) tool is present in the declared tool list alongside the tool actually being called.

### OpenClaw version
2026.8.1

### Operating system
macOS (Darwin 25.5.0)

### Install method
npm global

### Model
google-vertex/gemini-2.5-flash

### Provider / routing chain
openclaw -> google-vertex (Vertex AI, service-account ADC) -> gemini-2.5-flash

### Additional provider/model setup details
Standard `google-vertex` provider config (`models.providers.google-vertex`) with the model added via the `coding` tools profile (`tools.profile: "coding"`). No custom `models.providers.google-vertex.request` overrides. Reproduced with `thinkingConfig.thinkingBudget: 8192` and also with thinking disabled — thinking config is not required to trigger it.

### Logs
```
[provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response provider=google-vertex api=google-vertex model=gemini-2.5-flash status=200 elapsedMs=1660 dispatcher=new contentType=text/event-stream
[agent/embedded] embedded run agent end: runId=<redacted> isError=true model=gemini-2.5-flash provider=google-vertex error=LLM request failed. rawError=Google generation stopped (MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL): Malformed function call: print(default_api.read(path='<redacted>'))
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence
Minimal curl-level bisection (auth/project/model/tools redacted; full 35-tool `coding`-profile declaration set otherwise unchanged), run against the real Vertex `generateContent` endpoint:

| Change from the real captured OpenClaw request | `finishReason` |
| --- | --- |
| (unmodified, full request as captured) | `MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL` |
| Remove `generationConfig.thinkingConfig` | `MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL` |
| Remove `systemInstruction` | `MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL` |
| Keep only the `read` tool declaration (drop the other 34) | `STOP` (correct `functionCall`) |
| Keep all 35 tools, but rename `automations`'s `in` property to `in_` | `STOP` (correct `functionCall`) |
| Keep all 35 tools, remove only `automations`'s `in` property | `STOP` (correct `functionCall`) |

Per-property removal on the `automations` tool's ~16 top-level schema properties showed exactly one property, `in`, was necessary and sufficient to trigger the failure; every other property (including deeply nested ones) could be removed without fixing it, and removing `in` alone fixed it regardless of what else was present.

### Impact and severity
- Affected: any `google-vertex`/Gemini agent using the `coding` (or `full`) tool profile, since the built-in `automations` tool ships with an `in` parameter and `memory_get` ships with a `from` parameter.
- Severity: High — blocks essentially all tool use for the affected model/profile combination, not just the two named tools, since the malformed-call failure applies to the whole turn's tool-calling attempt.
- Frequency: Deterministic, 100% reproduction rate across every fresh-session test I ran (curl-level and through the actual `openclaw agent exec` CLI).
- Consequence: Any tool call attempted while `automations` or `memory_get` is in the declared tool set fails with `MALFORMED_FUNCTION_CALL` instead of succeeding.

### Additional information
Root cause: Gemini's function-calling implementation appears to render tool signatures internally as Python `def name(param, ...)` declarations for at least this model/transport combination. A JSON Schema property named after a Python hard keyword (`in`, `from`, etc.) produces an invalid Python signature, and the model falls back to emitting a Python-`print()`-style pseudo call as plain text instead of a real function-call part, for the entire turn — not just the tool with the offending property.

I have a fix + tests ready and will open a PR against this issue.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Crash (process/app exits or hangs)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

On the 2026.8.1-beta.3 train, with the iMessage plugin (`@openclaw/imessage`, local Messages.app via `imsg`, not `remoteHost`), a single inbound photo from an allowlisted contact makes the Gateway process spin (~80 % CPU, sustained), the HTTP health probe stops answering, and log output freezes. Restarting the Gateway does not recover: durable ingress rescans the still-pending inbound message on boot and the Gateway wedges again immediately, so the install stays down for every channel. Setting `channels.imessage.includeAttachments: false` did **not** prevent the re-wedge. Rolling the core back to 2026.7.1-2 (bundled iMessage channel) cleared it; the same photo ingests normally there.

### Steps to reproduce

1. macOS Mac mini (Apple silicon), OpenClaw `2026.8.1-beta.3` installed with `openclaw update --channel beta --yes` (plugin sync moved the official plugins to the same beta train), `@openclaw/imessage` from that train, brew `imsg` 0.14.1 (`steipete/tap`), Node 26.
2. `channels.imessage`: `enabled: true`, `dmPolicy: allowlist` with a few numbers, `includeAttachments: true`, `mediaMaxMb: 25`. Debug logging was enabled at the time.
3. From an allowlisted iPhone, send one 3–4 MB JPEG (a normal camera photo) to the bot's iMessage account, with or without text.
4. Watch the Gateway process: CPU climbs to ~80 % and stays there; `curl` to the Gateway health endpoint stops returning; the gateway log stops advancing.
5. `openclaw gateway restart` (or reboot). The Gateway comes up and wedges again within seconds, before any turn runs — the pending inbound message is picked up again by durable ingress.
6. Set `channels.imessage.includeAttachments: false`, restart → same re-wedge.
7. `openclaw update --channel stable --tag 2026.7.1-2 --yes` (bundled iMessage channel) → Gateway healthy, the same photo is ingested and readable by the agent.

Text-only messages in the same chats were processed normally before the wedge. Earlier the same day the persisted echo cache also dropped three inbound photo messages as echoes (#126814); that is a separate symptom and only mentioned for context.

### Expected behavior

- Attachment ingest should be bounded and off the event loop: a large or slow attachment must never make the whole Gateway unresponsive.
- A message whose attachment fails to ingest should be surfaced explicitly (placeholder + log) and not be retried in a way that blocks boot; durable-ingress replay of a poison message should be bounded (retry budget, then quarantine), so a restart always recovers.
- `includeAttachments: false` should skip attachment ingest entirely, including on replay.

### Actual behavior

Sustained ~80 % CPU spin in the Gateway process, health endpoint dead, log frozen, all channels down; restarts re-wedge on the same pending message; `includeAttachments: false` has no effect; only a core rollback to the bundled channel recovers.

### OpenClaw version

2026.8.1-beta.3 (rolled back to 2026.7.1-2 the same day, 2026-08-28)

### Operating system

macOS 26.6 on Apple silicon (Mac mini)

### Install method

npm global (`openclaw update`)

### Model

Not model-related. Agents run `oauth-bridge/claude-*` (a local OpenAI-compatible proxy in front of the Claude Code CLI).

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> local OpenAI-compatible bridge (127.0.0.1) -> Claude Code CLI. The wedge happens during inbound ingest, before any model call.

### Additional provider/model setup details

n/a

### Logs

Not retained, unfortunately: the install was rolled back within hours and the daily log rotated. Symptoms above are from live observation (`top`, health probe, tail of the gateway log). I can reproduce this in a staging window on the current stable release train if you tell me what to capture (debug log sections, `openclaw doctor` output, a CPU sample of the Gateway process, the pending-message row from the ingress store).

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

None retained. Related but distinct: #135860 (remote-host attachment materialization; this report is a local Messages.app setup) and #126814 (echo cache dropping inbound photos, same day).

### Impact and severity

- Affected: the whole Gateway (all channels), triggered through iMessage.
- Severity: blocks workflow, message loss — the operator's photo messages were lost and the assistant was down until a manual rollback.
- Frequency: always, on that day, for every inbound photo of that size; persisted across restarts.
- Consequence: forced rollback to 2026.7.1-2; we are still holding on that version until this and #126814 are fixed.

issues.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

With auto-TTS enabled (`tts.auto=always`) and an agent running on the Codex app-server runtime (OpenAI ChatGPT-subscription models), the terminal assistant transcript entry persisted to the Control UI webchat history is `Audio reply` plus an audio block; the model's real final answer text is never persisted, so later turns lose the answer from context. Reproduced 18 times since 2026-09-07 on one agent; confirmed by reading stored transcript entries. Zero occurrences on native (non-Codex-mirrored) runtimes with the same TTS config.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a channel/session for webchat with `tts.mode=final` (default), `tts.auto=always` (`/tts on`), TTS provider Microsoft.
2. Run an agent whose runtime is the Codex app-server (OpenAI ChatGPT-subscription model), so transcript entries carry `__openclaw.mirrorOrigin=codex-app-server`.
3. Send a prompt and let the run finish with a short final answer (observed with 214 output tokens, well under the ~1500-char auto-summary threshold, so summarization is not a factor).
4. Read the persisted terminal assistant transcript entry for that run in the Control UI chat history (`agent:<id>:dashboard:*` session).

### Expected behavior

The terminal transcript entry should contain the model's actual final answer text (optionally alongside the TTS audio block), the same as it does for non-Codex-mirrored runtimes with identical TTS config, and the same as Telegram (which defers/merges the final text via `captionedFinalText`).

### Actual behavior

The stored terminal transcript entry has content `[{"type":"text","text":"Audio reply"}]` plus `openclawDelivery.mediaUrls` pointing at the synthesized TTS audio file. The literal placeholder string "Audio reply" is what's visible in the UI and in later-turn context — never the model's real answer. Example sanitized stored entry:

```json
{
  "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "Audio reply" }],
  "openclawDelivery": { "mediaUrls": ["<state-dir>/media/tool-speech-synthesis/voice---<uuid>.mp3"] },
  "__openclaw": { "runTerminal": true, "mirrorOrigin": "codex-app-server" },
  "usage": { "output": 214 }
}
```

No `openclawTtsSupplement` marker is present on the stored entry.

### OpenClaw version

2026.9.2 (also present in 2026.9.3 — verified same code path in the published tarball)

### Operating system

Linux (Debian 12 host, systemd-managed gateway service)

### Install method

npm global (`openclaw` package under `node_modules/openclaw`)

### Model

OpenAI ChatGPT-subscription model via the Codex app-server runtime

### Provider / routing chain

openclaw -> Codex app-server (OpenAI ChatGPT subscription) -> microsoft (TTS provider, for the audio leg only)

### Additional provider/model setup details

`tts.mode=final` (default), `channels.<channel>.tts.auto=always` (persisted via `/tts on`), TTS provider `microsoft`. Any agent whose runtime is the Codex app-server reproduces this; native (non-mirrored) runtimes with the identical TTS config do not.

### Logs

n/a — no error is logged; this is a silent persistence defect. Evidence is the stored transcript content shown above (redacted).

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

Store query over one agent's Control UI transcript history since 2026-09-07 found 18 terminal assistant entries with `content[0].text == "Audio reply"`, all carrying `__openclaw.mirrorOrigin=codex-app-server`, none carrying an `openclawTtsSupplement` marker, and zero such entries for runs on native (non-mirrored) runtimes with the same TTS config in the same window.

Code-level cause (identical in 2026.9.2 and 2026.9.3 dist):

- `src/tts/captioned-final.ts`: `shouldDeferFinalTtsText` returns true only for channels advertising `captionedFinalText` — currently only Telegram. Webchat is not in that set.
- For webchat, the final-dispatch path (`dispatch-from-config.finalize`, region "accumulated block TTS") sends a media-only supplement payload via `markReplyPayloadAsTtsSupplement({ mediaUrl, spokenText, ... }, text, { visibleTextAlreadyDelivered: true })`.
- In `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-send-reply-dispatch.ts`, the final-append path that uses `useTranscriptMirrorOwner` (taken for the Codex mirror) calls `appendAssistantTranscriptMessage` with that media-only payload.
- `buildWebchatAssistantMessageFromReplyPayloads` synthesizes the literal text `Audio reply` because `payload.text` is empty.
- `buildMediaOnlyTtsSupplementTranscriptMarker` does not produce an `openclawTtsSupplement` marker on the stored entry in this path, so `chat-display-projection.history` has nothing to merge the audio back into the real text entry with, and the Codex mirror never separately persists the final text.

### Impact and severity

Affected: any webchat/Control UI agent running on the Codex app-server runtime with auto-TTS enabled (`tts.auto=always`, any provider).
Severity: blocks workflow — the model's real final answer is permanently lost from the persisted transcript and from later-turn context; it is not a cosmetic UI issue.
Frequency: 18/18 observed terminal entries meeting the precondition (Codex mirror + auto-TTS) over the sampled window; 0 on native runtimes with the same TTS config.
Consequence: operators/agents reading transcript history see only "Audio reply" and cannot recover the answer text; downstream turns reasoning over prior context lose the assistant's prior answer entirely.

### Additional information

Root cause is scoped to webchat's final-dispatch handling for mirrored runtimes (`useTranscriptMirrorOwner`), not to auto-TTS or the Codex app-server individually — each works correctly in isolation. Likely fix direction: either extend `shouldDeferFinalTtsText` to also cover the mirrored-transcript case regardless of channel `captionedFinalText` support, or have `buildMediaOnlyTtsSupplementTranscriptMarker` always emit an `openclawTtsSupplement` marker for the mirrored-append path so `chat-display-projection.history` can merge the real text back in.

OpenClaw 2026.7.1 (2d2ddc4), Node 22.23.2 (`node:sqlite`), Linux aarch64, running inside an NVIDIA NemoClaw 0.0.123 sandbox as user `sandbox`.
`memory.search` provider `ollama-mem` (custom provider, api `ollama`) — the provider is *unavailable* (no plugin serves it; gateway logs the
FTS-only fallback). `sqlite-vec` is not installed in this runtime.

## Reproduction
```
$ openclaw memory status --json     # works, creates the DB
  dbPath /sandbox/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite, files 0, chunks 0, dirty true, provider ollama-mem, providerState pending
$ openclaw memory index --force --verbose
Memory Index (main)
Provider: ollama-mem (requested: ollama-mem)
Sources: memory (MEMORY.md + $OPENCLAW_HOME/.openclaw/workspace/memory/*.md)
[memory] sync: indexing memory files          <- debug log: {"files":0,"needsFullReindex":true,"batch":false,"concurrency":1}
Memory index failed (main): unable to open database file   <- ~10 ms later
```
Same result after deleting the database (a fresh one is created), after removing `openclaw-agent.sqlite.reindex-lock.sqlite`, after a gateway restart,
and with `workspace/memory/` present or absent.

What works from the same user in the same directory (so it is not permissions, `/tmp`, or the temp-file name):
```
$ node -e '
const {DatabaseSync}=require("node:sqlite"); const crypto=require("crypto");
const db="/sandbox/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite";
const tmp=db+".memory-reindex-"+crypto.randomUUID();           // the tempDbPath runInPlaceReindex uses
const t=new DatabaseSync(tmp,{allowExtension:true}); t.exec("PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000"); t.exec("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL"); t.exec("create table x(a)"); t.close();
const m=new DatabaseSync(db,{allowExtension:true}); m.exec("ATTACH DATABASE \x27"+tmp+"\x27 AS memory_reindex"); m.exec("DETACH DATABASE memory_reindex"); m.close();
console.log("temp db + attach ok")'
temp db + attach ok
```
Directory: `drwx------ sandbox sandbox /sandbox/.openclaw/agents/main/agent`; `/tmp` writable; `TMPDIR` unset; disk 3.4 TB free.

## Expected
A full reindex on an empty memory set with an unavailable embedding provider should either build an FTS-only index or report *why* the
provider prevents it — not `SQLITE_CANTOPEN`. Suspects: the provider-unavailable path or the sqlite-vec load path inside `runInPlaceReindex`
opening a path that does not exist; the error message hides which file failed.

## Ask
Surface the failing path in the error (`unable to open database file: <path>`), and make the FTS-only full reindex succeed when the embedding
provider is unavailable / sqlite-vec is missing.

issues.body:
﻿## Summary

OpenClaw compaction currently rebuilds the summarization request with a different system/user prompt instead of preserving the final prompt prefix used by the live foreground turn.

For local OpenAI-compatible backends that keep KV/prefix cache (llama.cpp, vLLM APC, etc.), this makes compaction start from token 0 with `cached_tokens=0`, even when the entire live conversation prefix is already resident in KV cache.

This is related to, but distinct from, #110564. That issue focuses on avoiding forced map-reduce when a single pass fits. The problem here is that even a single-pass compaction request can still miss the cache if OpenClaw rewrites the live prompt prefix.

## Environment

- OpenClaw: `2026.9.2 (3928bad)`
- Provider: self-hosted OpenAI-compatible `local-llm`
- Backend: llama.cpp behind llama-swap
- Model: Ornith 1.5 35B A3B, 262144-token context
- Endpoint: `/v1/chat/completions`
- Tools in live request: 52

## Observed behavior before patch

A normal foreground request and the immediately following compaction request used the same model and the same 52 tool definitions, but the message prefix differed.

Example capture:

```text
Foreground request:
  input_tokens: 31,543
  cached_tokens: 0
  messages: [system, user]
  tools: 52
  tool_choice: auto

Compaction request:
  input_tokens: 31,585
  cached_tokens: 0
  messages: [system, user, assistant, user]
  tools: 52
  tool_choice: none
```

The tool schema hash was identical, but the first two message hashes differed.

The live foreground system prompt contained runtime shaping such as:

```text
<!-- openclaw:attempt:STABLE -->
...
```

and other final runtime additions (surface/session/channel/capability context). The compaction path rebuilt its own prompt without exactly preserving those final bytes. The user message also differed because normal foreground shaping had already added the runtime timestamp, while the compaction reconstruction used the pre-shaped message.

Result: llama.cpp could not reuse the resident KV prefix and reported `cached_tokens=0`.

On a real 205,015-token session, staged compaction generated several cold summarization calls (for example ~31K, 16K, 33K, 15K prompt chunks), each with no useful foreground-prefix reuse.

## Minimal A/B proof outside OpenClaw

Using the exact same ~48K-token prefix twice against the same llama.cpp backend:

1. First request: full prefix, `cached_tokens=0`.
2. Second request: keep the prefix byte-for-byte identical and only append a final compaction instruction.

Result:

```text
First request:
  input_tokens: 48,023
  cached_tokens: 0
  duration: ~12.1 s

Second request:
  cached_tokens: 48,019
  new input tokens: 34
  duration: ~2.38 s
```

So the backend itself is fully capable of reusing the live KV for compaction. The cache miss comes from request shaping in OpenClaw.

## Verified local patch

I tested a transport-level prototype that keeps a transient per-session snapshot of the **final payload actually sent to the model** after OpenClaw's normal request shaping.

For a compaction request marked as cache-aware, the transport reuses the stored `messages + tools` prefix and appends only the compaction-specific suffix. Compaction keeps its own output settings (`tool_choice=none`, compaction max tokens, normal compaction reasoning settings).

The snapshot is in-memory only; if there is no compatible snapshot, normal compaction behavior remains the fallback.

### Production verification

Fresh session after gateway restart:

```text
Foreground warm request:
  input_tokens: 31,530
  cached_tokens: 0

Immediate compaction:
  cached_tokens: 31,613
  new input tokens: 538
  duration: ~8.1 s
```

The foreground and compaction captures were checked directly:

```text
first-two-messages SHA256: MATCH
52-tool payload SHA256:    MATCH
```

The compaction request still used its normal compaction settings:

```text
reasoning_effort: low
max_tokens: 16000
tool_choice: none
```

After compaction, a normal follow-up request in the same session correctly recalled an identifier from the pre-compaction turn and itself reported:

```text
cacheRead: 31,460
new input: 597
```

So the cache-aware path preserved both session continuity and subsequent prefix reuse.

## Suggested upstream design

The important part is not the exact prototype implementation, but the invariant:

> A compaction request should preserve the already-sent foreground prompt prefix byte-for-byte whenever possible, and add the summarization instruction as a suffix.

Possible implementation approaches:

1. Capture the final shaped foreground payload per session at the transport boundary and reuse that prefix for compaction.
2. Or expose/reuse the exact post-shaping system/messages representation from the foreground runner instead of reconstructing it in the compaction runner.
3. Keep the current staged/chunked compaction as a fallback when a single cache-aware request would exceed the context window or when no compatible live-prefix snapshot exists.

A transport-boundary snapshot was the most reliable prototype in my testing because it automatically includes timestamps, `STABLE/DYNAMIC` markers, surface/channel context, tool ordering, and future prompt-shaping changes without duplicating those rules in the compaction code.

## Why this matters

For local long-context models, prefill is often the dominant cost of compaction. Re-reading tens or hundreds of thousands of tokens that are already in KV cache is unnecessary work. Preserving the live prefix turns compaction from another cold long-context prefill into mostly summary generation plus a small suffix prefill.

This should also complement #110564: single-pass compaction gives the largest benefit when the single pass is constructed as a true extension of the live cached prefix rather than as a separately reconstructed summarization prompt.

---

Behavior and timings above were captured on a real deployment; the patch was validated end-to-end with llama-swap/llama.cpp activity captures.

issues.body:
## Status 2026-10-26: reply to `clawsweeper:needs-live-repro`

**Live reproduction.** Every number in this report comes from production traffic: 949 wire-captured `POST /v1/messages` on `2026.8.1` (comment of 2026-09-10), the 2026-09-12 incident on a WhatsApp-facing agent (comment of 2026-09-21) and the fleet-wide 01/09→12/09 measurement (comment of 2026-09-27). This install runs the npm release (`openclaw@2026.9.8`), so it cannot produce a run on current `main`. Source on `main` @ `6cd627de53` (2026-10-26) still carries both constructions:

- Item 1: `src/agents/agent-command-local.ts:72` keeps `senderIsOwner: params.opts.senderIsOwner ?? true,`; the deny side is `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-tool-authority.ts:136` (`senderIsOwner === false ? { deny: [...GATEWAY_OWNER_ONLY_CORE_TOOLS] }`). #182585 (merged 2026-10-25, `201127429a0`) added `src/agents/scheduled-owner-tool-guard.ts`, which rechecks a scheduled requester's owner bit before each owner-only call. It leaves the `?? true` default of the `agent --deliver` path as it was; its effect on the tool list a cron turn submits has not been measured here.
- Item 2: `buildInboundMetaSystemPrompt` (`src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.ts:332`) is still built per message, from `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run-context.ts:237` and from `src/agents/command/session-preparation.ts:417`.
- Installed `2026.9.8`: `dist/agent-command-*.mjs:905`, same `?? true` expression.

**Correction to section 1 below.** The gate is `senderIsOwner`, threaded per message (2026-09-09 comment). The `embedded ? [] : [...]` description in section 1 is wrong; the cost numbers stand.

The latest review names an owner decision on the boundary between a session-stable prompt and live tool authority. That call is a maintainer's, and nothing further is reproducible from this side.

---

Measured on 2026.9.2 across a seven-agent fleet, 06/09→09/09: 103 sessions, 4,373 API calls,
**254 prefix rewrites costing 21.31M cache-write tokens** out of 52.06M written in total.
Anthropic caches on `tools → system → messages`, so each of those rewrites re-charges the whole
message history of a live session.

Method: `logs/cache-trace.jsonl` — `stream:context.systemDigest` (sha256 of the whole system prompt)
and `cache:state.options.snapshot.toolNames` (the tool list actually submitted) — joined with
`transcript_events.usage.cacheWrite` from every agent database. Query in
`workspace-arthur/scripts/cache-attribution.py`.

Two of the five are already closed locally by configuration; they are reported because the design
that produced them is still there.

## 1. The tool set depends on the entry path, inside one session (8.43M, 40%)

The owner tools (`gateway`, `sessions`, `terminal`, `openclaw`, `computer`, `portal`, `nodes`,
`mobile_ui`, `whatsapp_login`, `conversations_*`) are built by `embedded ? [] : [...]` in the tool
builder (`openclaw-tools-*.js`, `createOpenClawDelegateToolsForRun`). A session reached from Discord
or the Control UI submits 46 tools; the same session reached by `openclaw agent --deliver`, by cron
or by heartbeat submits 58. In one Discord session over three days: 63 calls with them, 212 without.

Every flip rewrites the prefix. **Proposal:** the submitted tool set should be a property of the
session, not of the message that woke it.

**Worked around locally** by denying the 12 tools for that agent, which levels the two paths to a
byte-identical list. That is levelling *down* — levelling up is not expressible, because on the
embedded path the tools are never constructed and `alsoAllow` cannot resurrect them.

## 2. `### Message Context` is built per message, and its channel flaps (1.68M, 8%)

`buildInboundMetaSystemPrompt` (`inbound-meta-*.js:358`) is called once per message from
`get-reply-*.js:4099` and its payload is derived from the message, not the session. On a turn that
originates from another agent's `sessions_send`, `resolveInboundChannel` returns `webchat` for one
message and nothing for the next, for the same source session — 17:42 `webchat`, 17:43 `unknown`,
17:43 `webchat`, all from `agent:enzo:main`.

When the channel does not resolve, `response_format` disappears with it, because
`resolveInboundFormattingHints` keys off the same value. So a single unresolved field drags the
channel plugin's whole formatting-hints block out of the system prompt: the deltas are ±142 bytes
and ±1.1k–1.4k bytes, alternating.

No configuration gates any of this. **Proposal:** resolve the channel once per session, or omit the
field rather than emitting a value that alternates.

## 3. Isolated finalization sends a new system prompt with the whole history (0.69M, 3%)

When a turn settles after a tool call without a final answer, `embedded-agent-*.js:6825` logs
`settled post-tool turn lacked a final answer … running isolated finalization` and re-runs with a
finalization prompt of its own. "Isolated" describes the prompt, not the conversation: the call
carries the full message history under a different system prompt, which is the worst case for the
cache. 23 events in three days across 22 sessions and three providers; in the two large sessions it
cost 288k and 271k tokens each. The gateway's own line above it reads
`cache read dropped 1014609 -> 366633 … no tracked cache input change`.

**Proposal:** reuse the system prompt of the run being finalized, since the history is already reused.

## 4. The cache observer digests only `stablePrefix`

`diagnostics.cacheTrace` records a digest of the stable prefix, so every finding above was invisible
to it: the tool list and the per-message system additions both change *after* that boundary. We only
got the attribution after computing our own digest over the whole system prompt. One-line change,
and it is the reason this took a week.

## 5. A failed MCP server silently removes its tools, with no notice to the model

While `recall-api` was down for maintenance, `bundle-mcp` failed to start the server on each turn
(`failed to start server "recall_<agent>" … ECONNREFUSED`) and **omitted its 19 tools from the
prompt** — no retry, no last-known set. 37 of 594 turns.

The cache cost (0.64M) is the smaller half. The larger one is that every agent ran without any memory
tool and **was not told**: nothing in the prompt says a tool set was truncated, so the model answers
as if the capability never existed.

## Minor: `github_identity_status` is gated on `!== undefined`

`createGitHubIdentityStatusTool` is included when `githubPublicationAvailable !== undefined`, while
its sibling `github_publish` uses `=== true`. The probe
(`github-publication-availability-*.js:48`) never returns `undefined` — it ends in `catch { return
false }` — so `undefined` only means "an entry path did not thread the field", and the tool appears
and disappears with the path. 17 rewrites, 1.91M, until we denied it.


Happy to split any of these into their own issue — they share a measurement, not a cause.
