prs.title: fix(gateway): surface retriable work-start rejections as 409 conflicts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When an OpenAI-compatible request (`/v1/responses`, `/v1/chat/completions`) targets a session that changed while starting work, the gateway rejects the run with `SessionWorkStartChangedError` / `SessionWorkStartInvalidatedError`. Both mean "resubmit the same request", but `resolveOpenAiCompatError` had no branch for them, so clients saw a generic HTTP 500 / `response.failed` with `type: "api_error"`, `message: "internal error"`. A web client sending a second message while the first reply is still running shows a hard failure and cannot tell a retriable coordination conflict from a real server fault. Closes #192465.

This maps both work-start rejections to `409` carrying the error's stable `code` (`SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED` / `SESSION_WORK_START_INVALIDATED`), `type: "invalid_request_error"`, and the original message (which ends in "Retry."), following the archived-session precedent from #170029. `isSessionWorkStartInvalidatedError` also recognizes duck-typed `code` carriers, so these errors still map after crossing a worker or serialization boundary. The shared `resolveOpenAiCompatError` also serves `/v1/embeddings`.

The Responses adapters used to rebuild the failed response from `error.type`, so both conflicts still arrived as `invalid_request_error` — over SSE and in the non-streaming JSON body — and streaming clients could not tell them apart from other invalid requests. Both adapters now prefer the mapped `error.code` when present, which is what the Chat Completions envelope already returns, and both wire formats are covered by the new case.

## Evidence

- Red first, mapper: the two new cases in the "OpenAI-compatible agent error envelopes" suite (`src/gateway/openai-compatible-agent-run.test.ts`) failed before the change with the envelope resolving to `500` / `api_error` (`2 failed | 24 passed`).
- Green after, mapper: `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/gateway/openai-compatible-agent-run.test.ts` → `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, 26/26 tests including both conflict cases.
- Red first, wire envelopes (`42c27ddec`): `keeps the work-start conflict code on the failed response (stream=false|true)` in `src/gateway/openresponses-http.test.ts` failed on `c7f8f572e` — the failed response carried `invalid_request_error` instead of `SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED` (`2 failed | 60 skipped` when filtered to the new cases).
- Green after: the same filtered run is `2 passed`, and the two files together are `3 failed | 85 passed`. The 3 failures are the pre-existing `…admitted until its deferred SSE terminal is written` timing cases: they fail identically with `src/gateway/openresponses-http.ts` reverted to `e25fdc28`, so they are not caused by this patch.
- The existing `decimal_above_max_value` streaming case now asserts the preserved provider code rather than the collapsed `invalid_request_error`; that is the same adapter change, exercised through the existing `STREAM_FAILURE_CASES` table.
- `./node_modules/.bin/oxlint` on the touched gateway files → `0 warnings and 0 errors`; `node scripts/run-format.mts --check` → all formatted.
- `config/test-lines-allocations/openai-compat-work-start-conflict.txt` is set to `50`, the measured net test-line growth of this PR (`51` added, `1` removed across the two changed test files), so `check-test-lines-ratchet` no longer credits more than was added.
- The `run-oxlint` / `run-tsgo` wrapper failures on this checkout are the known local `@openclaw/fs-safe` version mismatch (`overwriteFileHandleWithAuthority`, `DirectoryMode`, `dirMode` string-vs-number) in files this PR does not touch; neither touched file produces any diagnostic.

Related: #170029, #127195.

prs.title: fix(tools): accept an explicit optional: false in read arguments
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`read` declares `optional` as `Type.Literal(true)` (`src/agents/sessions/tools/tool-schemas.ts:95`), so a model that spells the flag out as `false` gets its call rejected before the tool runs:

```
Validation failed for tool "read":
  - optional: must be equal to constant
```

That is what #189440 reports: `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` via OpenRouter emits `{"path": "...", "optional": false}` on roughly one in three cron turns. The model then re-sends the same `read` without the field, so the cost is a wasted round trip per occurrence — and any caller that keeps sending `false` never gets the file.

The flag is a switch, not an enum. `read.ts:499` only branches on `optional !== true`, so `false` and an omitted field already mean the same thing (a missing path throws). The schema was the only thing rejecting the value; the tool's behavior never needed to change.

This widens the input schema to `Type.Boolean()` and leaves the runtime path untouched:

- `optional: true` → missing paths still return the structured `not_found` result (`read.ts:504-512`).
- `optional: false` or omitted → a missing path still throws.
- `readToolOutputSchema` keeps `optional: Type.Literal(true)`, since the `not_found` output only ever carries `true`.

Advertised schemas change shape for providers that canonicalize literals: Gemini compatibility used to publish `enum: ["true"]` for this property (`agent-tools-parameter-schema.ts:102-103` turns `const` into a single-value enum) and now publishes `type: "boolean"`. `src/agents/tool-search-runtime.test.ts:261` pinned the old shape and is updated with it.

Closes #189440

## Evidence

Red, on the unchanged implementation — `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/agents/sessions/tools/read.test.ts`:

```
 ×  agents-support  src/agents/sessions/tools/read.test.ts > read tool > accepts an explicit optional: false as a required read 9ms
   → Validation failed for tool "read":
  - optional: must be equal to constant
```

The new case runs the real `readToolInputSchema` through `validateToolArguments` (the same validator the agent loop uses), then executes the returned arguments against a temp file:

```ts
const args = validateToolArguments(
  { name: "read", description: "", parameters: readToolInputSchema },
  { type: "toolCall", id: "read-optional-false", name: "read", arguments: { path: "notes.txt", optional: false } },
);
expect(args.optional).toBe(false);
expect(textContent(await executeRead(tool, args))).toBe("present");
await expect(executeRead(tool, { path: "missing.txt", optional: false })).rejects.toThrow();
```

Green, after the change — same command:

```
 ×  agents-support  src/agents/sessions/tools/read.test.ts > read tool > keeps terminal modules cold until rendering in a headless session 195ms
      Tests  1 failed | 31 passed | 1 skipped (33)
```

The remaining failure is not related to this change: that case spawns a subprocess that imports an absolute Windows path as an ESM URL, which the Node loader rejects before any of this code runs:

```
Error [ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME]: Only URLs with a scheme in: file, data, and node are supported by the default ESM loader.
On Windows, absolute paths must be valid file:// URLs. Received protocol 'd:'
```

Validation on the pushed head:

```
node scripts/test-projects.mts src/agents/sessions/tools/read.test.ts     → 31 passed, 1 pre-existing Windows ESM failure
node scripts/test-projects.mts src/agents/tool-search-runtime.test.ts     → 46 passed (46)
./node_modules/.bin/oxlint <changed files>                               → 0 warnings, 0 errors
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json                          → 6 pre-existing errors, none in the changed files (stale @openclaw/fs-safe in this checkout)
node scripts/run-format.mts --check                                      → all files formatted
```

`scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` aborts in this checkout at its extension-package boundary preparation step (`Boundary preparation failed (1). If deps changed, run pnpm install.`), a local dependency-state failure unrelated to these files, so the vendored `oxlint` binary was used directly.

Test-line allocation for the 19 added test lines is in `config/test-lines-allocations/read-explicit-optional-false.txt`.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The project picker can open with only a search icon, requiring another click before users can find a project. Even when search is visible, keyboard focus can remain on the picker trigger.

## User Impact

Opening the project picker shows and focuses search immediately, including empty and small catalogs. Reopening the picker restores focused search, even after explicitly collapsing it. Users can start typing without another click.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the catalog-size threshold for the initial search state and focus lazily mounted search inputs when autofocus is requested. Native popover autofocus handles retained inputs on reopening; no extra document listener is needed. Keep explicit collapse available within the current opening and reset it when the picker closes.

## Evidence

- Chromium regression reproduced the original hidden-search state before the fix.
- All 9 project/GitHub browser-flow tests passed, including immediate typing, empty-query reopening, collapsed-search reopening, and query preservation.
- All 67 tests across 8 adjacent UI files passed.
- UI typecheck, changed-file formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Targeted lint completed with one pre-existing `solid/reactivity` warning in the unchanged keydown handler.
- The pinned-base bundle-performance comparison passed after removing redundant focus handling: startup JS unchanged, chat/new boot JS +15 bytes gzip versus the original base.

### After

prs.title: fix(sessions): replay a queued follow-up across an interposed command exchange
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A follow-up message queued while a run is active is dropped when `/stop` is used. The dispatcher mirrors the stop's
command exchange into the transcript, and the queued follow-up's replay admission then resolves the **command row** as
the current turn, refuses with `Persisted user turn changed before replay admission`, and the message is never answered.

Reproduced with the reporter's fixture (`extensions`-free, real session manager + real transcript): on `main` the queued
follow-up ends with `0` model calls and that error; with this change it is answered.

## Why This Change Was Made

`src/agents/sessions/session-manager-current-turn.ts` decides which transcript entries the current-turn walk may step
over. It already treats context metadata, compaction markers and runtime/system custom messages as traversable because
they are not model-facing turns. A delivered command exchange is the same kind of row — a transcript mirror of the
dispatcher's reply — but it was not listed, so the walk stopped on it.

The fix marks rows whose `idempotencyKey` is `command-input:*` or `command-reply:*` as traversable. Nothing else changes:
real user turns still stop the walk, and the admission still requires the prepared user message to match exactly.

## User Impact

A queued follow-up survives `/stop`: it is persisted once and gets answered instead of silently disappearing behind a
generic "couldn't finish this reply". Commands that are not mirrored (`/new` etc. still write their exchange the same
way) behave the same, and no transcript bytes change.

## Evidence

Reporter's fixture, run with `node scripts/test-projects.mts <file>`:

| case | base | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| no interposed write (control) | answered | answered |
| Workshop notice interposed (control, #181473) | answered | answered |
| **`/stop` exchange interposed** | `Persisted user turn changed before replay admission`, 0 model calls | 1 model call, `FOLLOWUP_ANSWERED` |

- Base: `2 failed | 4 passed` (both reader modes fail on the interposed case). Fixed: `6 passed`.
- Neighbours: `attempt-session-replay.test.ts` 61 passed; `session-manager-bounded.test.ts` 28 passed;
  `session-manager-async-entries.test.ts` 9 passed.
- `oxlint`: 0 warnings, 0 errors. The new test file carries an allocation in
  `config/test-lines-allocations/stop-exchange-replay-admission.txt`.

## Scope

One production file (the traversal predicate), the reporter's regression test registered next to
`attempt-session-replay.test.ts` in `test/vitest/vitest.database-worker-core-paths.mjs`, and the allocation file.

## AI Assistance

This PR was prepared with AI assistance from the issue report and its attached fixture; the author reviewed the change
and its evidence.

prs.title: fix: agents stay unavailable after temporary startup overload
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes agents remaining unavailable after a Gateway restart when temporary worker overload interrupts database preparation.

## User Impact

Sessions and workboard requests recover when capacity returns within the existing startup retry budget. If contention persists, the diagnostic tells the operator to retry admission by restarting the Gateway after competing work settles, without incorrectly recommending `openclaw doctor --fix`. There is no new configuration or schema change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Startup previously retried overload during opening but not migration, and raw task-pool overload also missed opening and runtime-publication retry classification. One shared predicate now covers deletion checks, open/foreground integrity, migration, and publication. Unknown write settlement, corruption, mixed cleanup errors, invalid schemas, and lost ownership remain terminal. Deferred preflight keeps its original refusal and recovery guidance.

Retries remain bounded to four attempts; exhaustion does not advertise automatic retry when no recovery task remains. Background full verification already treats overload as incomplete verification rather than corruption, so its admission policy is unchanged. Earlier reconnect shedding is a separate follow-up: custom-store discovery can compete with startup, but blanket gating would also block admitted siblings and read-ready agents.

Related: #173994. This is separate from #186748's wrapped SQLite-lock classification and cron-maintenance changes.

## Evidence

- Exact-base regression at `2ab781210c6f2cf90c92043e6bfc2cb6283a4bce`: seven new cases fail, including migration `WorkerTaskError("overloaded")` refusing the agent after one attempt; 21 existing/control cases pass. Tests exercise real admission-state transitions with a fixed journal transport.
- Final startup-owner suite: 29 passing cases. Together with Gateway preparation, real Gateway lifecycle, and sibling integrity/preflight coverage, 115 focused cases pass. The final five-file run passed 102 cases in 269.00 s; the unchanged 13-case lifecycle file passed in the preceding run.
- Chromium production-build proof: seven passing cases across startup backoff and the HTTP post-deploy session admission handoff (109.16 s command wall). No browser-runtime module imports changed.
- `pnpm check:changed --base 2ab781210c6f2cf90c92043e6bfc2cb6283a4bce`: all gates pass except changelog attribution, which reproduces with identical 20 findings on the exact base. Introduced by `266a7aa0fe69e2b5fe6445c4ceb1e15b5360c957` (#194364); this is a main regression, not a new failure from this change. Final benchmark-script typecheck and scoped lint also pass.
- Isolated Codex autoreview, local candidate against the base above, P0–P2: scoped-clean. Its first pass found an unknown-settlement envelope that could be retried; the existing outcome classifier now rejects it and an owner regression covers it.
- Production delta: **+11 lines** (+77/−66). The small growth preserves preflight recovery guidance and excludes unknown settlement while replacing per-step contention policy. Tests: +53 lines with a dedicated regression allocation; benchmark tooling is counted separately.

Measurement acceptance rule (set before sampling): on a populated synthetic ~35-GiB database with 10,000 sessions, one rejected migration attempt must recover to admitted state on attempt two while preserving the session count. Use five counterbalanced baseline/candidate pairs, separate no-overload controls and allocation runs, plus A/A controls. Report the existing backoff and successful recovery cost; this is not a latency optimization. No-overload latency, CPU, and allocations must be assessed against the control spread.

Paired measurements are running on a populated 35.035-GiB synthetic database (10,000 sessions and 629,544 transcript events). This draft will receive the final timing, CPU, allocation, and A/A results before being marked ready.

Limitations: owner-boundary measurements on synthetic local APFS data do not reproduce production btrfs, a workspace-tree scan, a full reconnect flood, or a live model turn. The owner does not scan workspace files. No production state was copied or modified.

prs.title: fix(codex): zombie processes accumulate when app-server transports close on Linux
prs.body:
Related: #97616

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes part of the zombie-reaping umbrella: Codex app-server close kills observed descendants by exact PID and treats a defunct (`Z`) process as terminated, but a zombie only clears when its parent consumes the exit status with waitpid. Descendants killed during close (hook relays, shells) can therefore linger as defunct children after the tracked root exits. In deployments where the gateway is PID 1 or the adoption point (fly.toml, Docker entrypoint overrides that drop tini), those zombies are adopted by the gateway and never waited, accumulating over hours into the hundreds and thousands reported in #97616 until the runtime degrades (spawn EAGAIN, uv_thread_create failures, connector silence).

## User Impact

User impact: long-running Linux gateways that repeatedly start and stop Codex app-servers now consume the exit statuses of the descendants their close path killed, so those defunct children stop accumulating. Deployments with a reaping PID 1 (tini, docker --init) are unaffected either way, and non-Linux platforms see no change.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `terminateCodexAppServerDescendants` now returns the exact descendant identities it proved and killed.
- Transport close schedules `scheduleAdoptedDescendantReapAfterRootExit`, an identity-scoped sibling of the group-scoped reaper landed in #139548. After the tracked root exits it reaps only retained PIDs that are zombies parented to the current process, guarded by their `<bootId>:<startTicks>` procfs identity against PID reuse. It never waits the tracked root (libuv owns that status), never waitpids unscoped PIDs, and installs no signal handlers, preserving the spawner-owned scoped-reaper design this umbrella established (the gateway-wide SIGCHLD approach from #97731 stays rejected).
- Contained descendants may not share the root's process group (hook relays can lead their own groups), which is why the existing PGID-scoped reaper cannot see them.
- When containment cannot prove identities, the force-kill fallback group-kills the root's group, so close also schedules the existing group-scoped reaper for that path, with the hosted-gateway attached topology reported correctly.
- Both reaping helpers are exposed through `openclaw/plugin-sdk/process-runtime` so the extension reaches them through the supported boundary, with a docs paragraph in the SDK runtime guide. SDK direction: ClawSweeper recommended accepting these focused exports as narrow shared cleanup contracts; final public-API signoff belongs to the area owner.

## Evidence

Real behavior proof runs through the changed production boundary (containment to transport close to scheduled reaper) with real adopted descendants across process groups, and demonstrates base failure versus head success with the same test file.

**Real-process regression:** `extensions/codex/src/app-server/transport.close-reaping.process.test.ts`. A Linux subreaper harness (mirroring gateway-as-PID-1 adoption) spawns a fixture app-server root whose holders and relays span independent and shared process groups, closes it through the real `closeCodexAppServerTransportAndWait` boundary, then observes /proc from outside the fixture tree. It asserts the close result is `{ exited: true, cleanup: "closed" }` (containment actually ran), the tracked root completed with exit code 0, every retained descendant fully left /proc, no run-owned zombie stays parented to the harness, and an unrelated process outside the tree keeps running. A red control first proves the observer detects an intentionally leaked adopted zombie that no close owns, then reaps it through the exported scheduler. Unconditional teardown terminates, joins, and reaps every task-owned fixture process on success and failure alike, so a failing run cannot leak processes or adopted zombies into later tests. This replaces the earlier mocked scheduling test per review feedback.

**Base failure (merge base `bd23988e`, same test file overlaid), Debian Linux, real processes:**

```text
FAIL ... > transport close consumes adopted descendants across process groups
AssertionError: holder-independent pid 1095 still present: {"state":"Z","ppid":1029,"startTicks":"23486"}: expected { state: 'Z', ppid: 1029, …(1) } to be undefined
```

The descendant killed by containment survives real transport close as a zombie parented to the harness (pid 1029), which is the reported leak shape. The control also fails on base because the exported scheduler does not exist there.

**Head success (`8429c35c`):** the regression passes in GitHub CI Linux (changed-extensions bundle shard, both tests green) and passed 3 consecutive local Debian runs:

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  2 passed (2)   x3 local runs, plus CI
```

Both tests pass: the contained close returns `closed`, the root exits 0, and all four descendants (independent and shared groups) are fully gone from /proc, with the unrelated process alive. The red control confirms the green is not vacuous: the same observer does flag a stuck adopted zombie when one is planted, and forced failing runs on the merge base leave no live fixture processes behind.

Unit coverage for the reaper itself stays in `src/process/scoped-child-reaper.test.ts` (19 passed: reaps only identity-matching adopted zombies after root exit, skips PID reuse under a new start identity, never waits the tracked root, retains live descendants until they become adopted zombies, stops at its deadline, no work on darwin/win32, single registration per child, no scheduling without usable identities).

Validation: **CI fully green on `8429c35c`** (all 30 checks, including the `check-test-types` extensions-test lane after satisfying its test typecheck, and the security/boundary scans). Locally: `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions`, `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`, targeted oxlint and `oxfmt --check`, and the three extension import-boundary checks pass. One earlier CI round hit an unrelated `crabbox-managed-binary` 120 s acquisition timeout on a loaded 2-vCPU runner; the touched codex and process tests passed in that same round and the retry is green. prs.title: fix(gateway): prevent stalls from oversized workspace reconciliation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a large worker workspace result can stall the Gateway main thread during local reconciliation and repeatedly fail recovery without a durable rejected outcome.

## User Impact

Oversized unapplied results now fail visibly with exclusion/splitting guidance and a preserved recovery reference. Local agents can correct retained files and checkpoint again; automatic settlement leaves the rejected result parked. Accepted receipts and rollback journals remain recoverable. No configuration or database schema change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Conflict retention scanned every conflict for each applied path, causing quadratic main-thread work and transient string allocation. One ancestor set preserves the same conflict result with linear path processing. Patch creation, tree preparation, rollback-pack hashing, and recovery diff collection use the existing Git worker and transfer owned buffers.

Historical unapplied results now receive publication's 50,000 changed-path admission limit before materialization, alongside existing byte limits. Local rejection is recorded by the database owner in the existing checkpoint receipt; cloud recovery retires only an unaccepted, durably staged result without a mutation journal. Disposable local output should be moved to checkout-root `.openclaw/tmp/` or removed before a new explicit checkpoint; `.gitignore` alone does not exclude already admitted local sandbox files.

Release-note context: keep the Gateway responsive while reconciling large worker workspaces, report oversized results once with repair guidance, and preserve rejected work for recovery.

## Evidence

Production-shaped synthetic btrfs proof uses real Git and `applyStagedWorkerWorkspace`: 20,000 changed files / 491.52 MB with a controlled concurrent writer, producing exactly the same 20,000 conflicts before and after. Five runs per arm, including A/A controls:

| Measurement | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median wall time | 35.261 s | 27.704 s |
| Median main-thread CPU | 9.168 s | 0.527 s |
| Maximum heartbeat gap | 7,917.8 ms | 52.84 ms |
| Sampled main-thread allocation | 8.15 GB | 143 MB |

A 65,000-file / 1.10 GB synthetic result rejects at the apply owner in 0.995 ms, with an 11.05 ms maximum heartbeat gap and actionable error. CPU profiles locate the baseline stall in the nested conflict scan. After the existing worker idle GC runs, retained RSS is approximately 3% higher, while main live heap is approximately 1% lower. Patch-only generation did not reproduce the spin; these measurements demonstrate the owner defect, not the duration or exact stack of an uncaptured production incident.

Final lifecycle suites: 95 passed (two platform/environment skips); checkpoint store/manifest/CAS consumers: 39 passed; patch/recovery/worker siblings: 37 passed (one macOS broker skip, covered on the Linux rig). The new admission, durable quarantine, and terminal recovery regressions all fail on exact parent `2ab781210c6f`. Codex autoreview is scoped-clean at P0–P2.

`pnpm check:changed` is still running. Its changelog attribution gate fails identically on exact parent `2ab781210c6f` with 20 historical bot-thanks entries. This main regression was introduced by `266a7aa0fe69` (#194364), which added forbidden handles without updating historical records. No affected check or changelog source is changed here. Build and exact-head CI outcomes will be recorded before landing.

prs.title: fix(whisper): fail transcription when the API returns an HTTP error
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the bundled transcription helper reporting success and saving an API error as a transcript when the server responds with HTTP 401, 429 or 500 in JSON-output or Whisper text-output mode.

## User Impact

Callers receive a nonzero exit status and an HTTP error on stderr instead of a misleading output-file success message. Successful text and JSON responses keep their existing behavior. This does not change the existing output-file lifecycle: a failed direct-output request can still leave an empty output file.

## Why This Change Was Made

Enable curl's established `--fail` behavior at the shared HTTP request. The script's existing `set -e` then stops processing before the final success-path output. No new dependency, retry policy or response parser is introduced.

This is an HTTP failure-handling fix, the same general class as recently merged external contributions #194150 (ooiuuii, merged by obviyus on November 6) and #193234 (1052326311, merged by steipete on November 5).

## Evidence

Base `bd3d7a65e1c1c6c481ad8a5101aeb3bfdac52bc9`; candidate `87ed855b3fed4aab9ef32b72cbd8bd5f52418550`.

Ran the complete shell entrypoint with **real curl 7.61.1**, a valid synthetic WAV and a loopback HTTP server through the existing `OPENAI_BASE_URL` override. The peer consumes the multipart upload and returns controlled HTTP responses. No curl stub or direct helper call was used. This proves the script's actual HTTP failure behavior; it does **not** claim live OpenAI/model transcription. The fake API key and all files are task-private, inside secretless offline Docker capped at 256 MiB and 0.5 CPU.

| Mode / server response | Base | Candidate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--model whisper-1`, HTTP 200 | Exit 0, text transcript and output path | Same |
| `--json`, HTTP 200 | Exit 0, JSON transcript and output path | Same |
| Either mode, HTTP 401 / 429 / 500 (six cases) | Exit 0; prints output path; saves API error JSON | Exit 22; stdout empty; stderr identifies HTTP status; API error is not saved as transcript |

The committed regression also uses real curl and a private HTTP server, testing 200/401/429/500 through the full `--json` command. All three error subcases fail on the base; all four cases pass on the candidate in **0.219 s**. It requires no extra Python package, uses no sleeps, and terminates/reaps its server in `finally`. The existing skills pytest lane discovers the file. This single owner-level regression covers success and HTTP failures without adding a fake curl implementation.

Focused `bash -n`, Ruff lint/format and `git diff --check` passed. Simplification retained one production-line replacement (+1/-1) and 66 Python test lines; no shared baseline/allocation changes. Python files are outside the JS/TS test-line ratchet patterns. No full local suite, large install or core build was run: the affected helper is shipped shell code with no compilation step. Hosted CI results will be added when available.

Independent agent static review of the full base/candidate diff passed with no actionable findings; canonical diff SHA-256 `42e15f6c0d87da0f1a9b845a75ab7e420b1e0b3a39322a8a14ba934ba5827fe7`. This was a delegated code review, not an autoreview tool run; the reviewer inspected retained runtime evidence without rerunning it.

<details>
<summary>Replay the committed regression against both scripts</summary>

Requires Bash, curl and POSIX Python 3.10+. Run without shell `set -e` so the expected baseline failure does not skip the candidate:

```bash
for revision in bd3d7a65e1c1c6c481ad8a5101aeb3bfdac52bc9 87ed855b3fed4aab9ef32b72cbd8bd5f52418550; do
  case_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
  git show "$revision:skills/openai-whisper-api/scripts/transcribe.sh" > "$case_dir/transcribe.sh"
  git show 87ed855b3fed4aab9ef32b72cbd8bd5f52418550:skills/openai-whisper-api/scripts/test_transcribe.py > "$case_dir/test_transcribe.py"
  python3 "$case_dir/test_transcribe.py"
  rm -rf -- "$case_dir"
done
```

The server is local and synthetic; no provider account, real credential or model request is needed.

</details>

prs.title: fix(doctor): repair legacy shallow project clone history
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated history downloads in legacy shallow partial managed project clones by giving operators a supported migration through `openclaw doctor --fix`.

## User Impact

Doctor can fetch complete history while retaining `blob:none`, existing objects, and reflogs. Busy clones are skipped immediately; failed or incomplete fetches are reported per clone and can be retried. Ordinary Doctor remains read-only. Fetches run at lower priority with a 30-minute timeout and require access to `origin`.

Doctor does not repack, prune, or expire reflogs. At 1,000 or more packs it suggests a separate bounded operator repack under the same checkout lifecycle lease. Existing disk usage is not automatically reclaimed. Update-time Doctor continues to defer this standalone check.

## Why This Change Was Made

The current clone producer already creates full-history clones, so it needs no change. The old diagnostic only printed commands to remove partial-clone settings, refetch objects, and run an unbounded repack. This replaces that manual path with the existing project checkout lifecycle owner (`waitMs: 0`), preserves filtering, and removes three inspection subprocesses. No schema, config option, or cache is added. Production LOC is **−10**; test LOC is **−18**.

Git can return success when `origin` is itself shallow without removing the client's shallow boundary. The migration explicitly reports that incomplete outcome instead of claiming success.

## Evidence

- Real-Git local-bare fixtures cover read-only detection, full-history/partial/shallow/missing repositories, lease contention, failed-origin retry, shallow-origin incomplete repair, actual Doctor contribution dispatch, idempotence, preserved HEAD/reflog/filter, ignored user-managed shallow workspaces, and current producer full-history behavior.
- Regression fails on parent `2ab781210c6f2cf90c92043e6bfc2cb6283a4bce`: Doctor repair leaves `--is-shallow-repository=true`. It passes with the fix. The focused migration/update-scope/lint-isolation run passed **26 tests**; the final migration suite passed all five tests again (22.99 s runner wall time). Hosted CI timing is pending.
- `pnpm check:changed --staged` ran all checks. Typechecks, lint, formatting, repository/database guards, and all dead-export scans passed. The stale-mock baseline was shrunk by exactly the two deleted mock factories and its guard was rerun. The remaining failure is inherited changelog attribution: 20 violations reproduced from exact parent `2ab781210c6f2cf90c92043e6bfc2cb6283a4bce`, introduced as that failure set by #194364 (`266a7aa0fe69`). Its predecessor has a different 26-credit failure set; this is a main regression needing follow-up, not ignored noise. No release-owned records were changed. The final two documentation summaries passed their formatting check.
- Codex autoreview of the production, test, and documentation changes against `2ab781210c6f2cf90c92043e6bfc2cb6283a4bce`: scoped-clean at P0–P2, no actionable findings.

Bounded diagnostic measurements used a synthetic 62,000-file / 1.143 GB checkout with 61 commits, five interleaved samples and five A/A pairs on local APFS/Git 2.56. Read-only owner median wall time changed **21.831 → 1.949 ms**, Node CPU **7.570 → 2.276 ms**, and sampled JS allocation **1,482,456 → 190,152 bytes**; A/A baseline wall medians were **27.046/27.136 ms**. The migration restored **1 → 61 commits** in 625.466 ms median; native Git used 610 ms CPU and 133.9 MB peak RSS.

The local file-origin fixture did **not** reproduce whole-history download amplification during lazy blob reads: both shapes added one 136-byte promisor pack despite noop negotiation. These measurements prove migration behavior and reduced inspection work, not quantified production download savings. Btrfs and native total allocation were not measured. The owner does not read agent session databases, so no large agent database was fabricated. Measurements used external diagnostic scripts, not committed benchmark infrastructure; no full performance gate is claimed. No production host was accessed.

prs.title: fix(ui): keep plugin credential drafts out of IME commits
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Pressing Enter to confirm an IME candidate (Chinese, Japanese, Korean input) in the plugin credential secret input could save the literal draft before the user actually submitted it. Two paths were affected:

1. A keydown with `isComposing: true` (or `keyCode 229`) reached the `onKeyDown` handler and committed the draft.
2. WebKit can deliver the committing Enter after `compositionend` with both composition flags cleared; that Enter also committed the draft.

## User Impact

Users entering credential literals in the Plugins page with an IME (most CJK users) could have their partially-typed secret committed and sent to the Gateway mid-composition, before they pressed Enter to actually submit. The draft is stored as a literal credential value, so this both surprises the user and can persist an unintended value.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared IME guard (`ui/src/lib/ime.ts`) already covers the browser toolbar, command palette, and chat composer. The plugin credential editor was the remaining secret input handling Enter without that protection. This applies the same contract so a composing Enter is ignored and only a genuine submit (non-composing Enter, blur, or Save) commits the draft.

## Evidence

Two regression tests added in `ui/src/pages/plugins/credential-editor.browser.test.tsx`, both red on the base and green with this fix:

- `does not commit the literal draft while IME composition is in progress` — dispatches a `keydown` Enter with `isComposing: true`; asserts `onCommit` is not called.
- `does not commit the literal draft from a WebKit composing Enter after compositionend` — dispatches `compositionend` then a committing Enter; asserts `onCommit` is not called.

Red (base, 2 failed):
```
× does not commit the literal draft while IME composition is in progress
× does not commit the literal draft from a WebKit composing Enter after compositionend
```

Green (fix, 2 passed):
```
✓ does not commit the literal draft while IME composition is in progress
✓ does not commit the literal draft from a WebKit composing Enter after compositionend
```

Run: `node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config ui/vitest.config.ts --project browser ui/src/pages/plugins/credential-editor.browser.test.tsx -t "IME composition|WebKit composing"`

Lint: `oxlint --config .oxlintrc.json ui/src/pages/plugins/credential-editor.tsx ui/src/pages/plugins/credential-editor.browser.test.tsx` → 0 errors, 0 warnings. Format: `oxfmt --check` clean.

## Merge Danger

Low. The change is additive: it only skips the Enter-commit path while IME composition is active and clears the composition marker on focus-out. Non-IME Enter submission, blur commit, and Save are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(agents): retract running deferred dispatcher when nested target starts
prs.body:
Fixes #194168

## What Problem This Solves

Discord progress mode with `toolProgress: true` renders **two identical rows** for each deferred tool call while it runs: one for the `dispatch_action` dispatcher and one for its nested target. Both rows share the same label and `running` status at the same time, even though the transcript records a single execution. This fix retracts the dispatcher row as soon as its nested target starts, so the live draft shows exactly one row per tool call. Independent tool calls with identical labels remain separate.

## Problem

With Discord progress mode and `toolProgress: true`, a deferred tool call dispatched through `dispatch_action` renders as **two identical rows** in the live draft while it runs: one for the dispatcher and one for its nested target. Both rows show the same label and the same `running` status at the same time.

The transcript shows each tool call executed exactly once.

## Root cause

`dispatch_action` is a pure forwarding wrapper. It publishes its own visible prepared item (`tool:<dispatcher-call-id>`) when it starts, and its nested target (`tool_call:<parent>:<name>:<seq>`, `parentToolCallId` = dispatcher id) publishes a second visible item with an identical label. The existing wrapper suppression (`resolveCompletedActivityWrappers` / `finalizeToolActivity`) only collapses a completed wrapper **at run termination**, so while the target is still running both rows stay on the draft.

## Fix

Represent a deferred dispatcher and its nested target as one live operation at the producer (`src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.start.ts`):

- When a nested target starts (`lifecycleProvenance: "nested"`), look up its parent dispatcher from the tracked tool starts.
- If the parent is a `dispatch_action` wrapper that is still visible, retract its row by emitting an `update` item event with `hideFromChannelProgress: true` (the channel progress compositor clears the row by item id).
- Persist `hideFromChannelProgress` on the parent's start record so the dispatcher's terminal event stays hidden too — the run-termination collapse in `finalizeToolActivity` is unchanged.

A `dispatch_action` that fails to dispatch (no nested target) keeps its own visible row with the error, so no information is lost. Independent tool calls with identical labels stay separate because they have no parent/child relationship.

## Evidence

### Regression (fails on base, passes with fix)

New test `retracts a running deferred dispatcher once its nested target starts` in `src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.tool-result-ordering.test.ts`:

- On base: the dispatcher receives no retraction update → assertion `expected [] to have a length of 1` fails.
- With fix: the dispatcher receives exactly one `phase: "update"` item event with `hideFromChannelProgress: true`, and the nested target's own start row stays visible.

```
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  14 passed (14)
```

### Related suites (all pass)

- `src/infra/agent-activity-events.test.ts` — 25 passed
- `src/channels/progress-draft-compositor.test.ts` — 59 passed
- `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.draft-preview.rest.test.ts` — 16 passed

### CI-equivalent checks

- `oxlint --type-aware --deny=warn` — clean
- `node scripts/run-format.mts --check` — clean
- `check-test-lines-ratchet` — pass (new test lines covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/issue-194168-deferred-dispatcher.txt`, 45)
- `check-test-mock-exports --prune` — 6387 → 6387, no new violations
- typecheck on changed files — 0 errors

## What was not tested

No live Discord round trip was run in this environment. The regression exercises the producer event stream (`handleToolExecutionStart`), which is the source both channels and the Control UI consume; the Discord draft-preview test suite confirms the retraction path (`hideFromChannelProgress` + item id) is honored by the compositor.

prs.title: fix: memory plugin hooks skip CLI-backed turns because they get no memory audience
prs.body:
Fixes #194453

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: memory plugins skip auto-recall and auto-retain on every turn that runs through a CLI backend such as `claude-cli`, because the turn's plugin hooks receive no memory audience.

## User Impact

User impact: memory plugins that read `ctx.memoryAudience` in `before_prompt_build`, `llm_input`, `llm_output`, `before_agent_run` or `agent_end` now recall and retain on CLI-backed turns the same way they already do on embedded turns. Plugins that do not use the audience see no change.

## Why This Change Was Made

CLI turns resolved a memory audience only for the loopback MCP grant (#173927), so MCP memory tools had one but the turn's hooks did not. The CLI runner now resolves the turn's host-minted audience once during preparation, with the same resolver the grant used, and passes it to every turn hook. The grant reuses that resolution for its own session, so the turn takes one set of leases. The audience carries the same currency guard as on embedded turns, and its leases are released at run end, after the grant is revoked, or immediately if preparation fails.

Like embedded turns, a hook that is still running after the run ends (for example an asynchronous `agent_end` on a channel turn) sees `assertMemoryAudienceCurrent()` throw "released". That matches the documented rule that an audience is invalidated when the run that owns it ends.

## Evidence

- Red on main 5e4684a1d8b, green on this branch (macOS, `pnpm test <file>`):
  - `src/agents/cli-runner.memory-audience.test.ts` (new): the CLI turn's `llm_input` and `agent_end` hooks receive the host-minted audience, and their guard turns stale when the session lineage changes. Main: 1 failed, 1 passed. Branch: 2 passed.
  - `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.test.ts`: the prompt-build hook, the prepared turn and the grant share one audience, the grant is revoked before the leases are released, and a preparation failure releases the leases once. Main: 2 failed. Branch: 113 passed.
- Branch only, all passing: `cli-runner/mcp-memory-audience` (3), `harness/hook-context` (1), `cli-runner.interrupted-partial-output` (8), `embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-memory-audience` (3).
- `pnpm check:changed`: every lane passes except `changelog attributions`. That lane fails on existing entries in `CHANGELOG/2026.6.8.md` and `CHANGELOG/2026.7.1.md`; this branch does not touch them.
- One existing test changed: "hands the admitted turn's memory audience to the CLI grant..." used a frozen literal audience. Prompt-build hooks now get that audience too, and they reject audiences the host did not mint, so the test now uses a minted one (`withChildAudience`). Its original assertions are unchanged, and it now also checks the hook context and the revoke-before-release order.
- `prepare.ts` stays within the line-cap ratchet. The resolution and the prompt-build hook context move to `cli-runner/prepare-hook-context.ts`.

- Live claude-cli turn, branch vs base (macOS, loopback Gateway with isolated state, model `claude-cli/claude-sonnet-4-6`, one operator-created session via `sessions.create`, then `openclaw agent --session-key <key>`). A probe plugin owns the memory slot (stub native provider) and records what `before_prompt_build` and `agent_end` receive:

  ```
  base 5e4684a1d8b:
  {"hook":"before_prompt_build","audienceKind":null,"audienceAgentId":null,"guard":"absent"}
  {"hook":"agent_end","audienceKind":null,"audienceAgentId":null,"guard":"absent"}
  branch 942dfab0df7:
  {"hook":"before_prompt_build","audienceKind":"owner-private","audienceAgentId":"main","guard":"current"}
  {"hook":"agent_end","audienceKind":"owner-private","audienceAgentId":"main","guard":"current"}
  ```

  Both runs: `agent_exit=0`, gateway log `cli turn: provider=claude-cli`. Session keys and tokens redacted. A first attempt sent the turn to `agent:main:main`, which has no durable chat type, so it gets no audience on any runtime; the run above uses an operator-created root.

Not tested yet: recall and retention through a real memory provider on a claude-cli turn, and provider-effect checks for conversation, mismatched-session and released audiences (in progress); hosted CI; channel-delivered turns (Telegram, Discord and so on) end to end, including the asynchronous `agent_end` path; CLI backends other than `claude-cli`.

Related: [maintainer-nerfed role-assignment report](https://discord.com/channels/1456350064065904867/1568036361880207371/1568474450226057237).

## What Problem This Solves

Clarifies that an administrator can delegate a GitHub role preassignment directly, without first fetching the public profile and unnecessarily tainting the turn.

## User Impact

The setup-tool description now tells the agent to pass the supplied login or profile URL and requested role directly. Documentation distinguishes saving a pre-login mapping from a person actually signing in with a verified GitHub identity. No authorization, taint, or role-resolution checks change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing configuration owner already validates preassignments locally and role resolution matches them against verified GitHub identity. The narrow change documents that supported path instead of adding a taint exception or a new assignment mechanism.

## Evidence

- Existing role-policy, configuration, and authority tests passed, including invalid mappings, verified-identity matching, revoked authority, and taint after tool preparation. Documentation link audit passed.
- After the description change, all 23 delegation, authority-preparation, and prompt-prefix stability checks passed across three files (251.45 seconds wall time across two Vitest shards, including cold compilation). Targeted type-aware lint, formatting, and git diff --check passed.
- Baseline reached the real custodian without a tainted-turn rejection. OpenRouter then returned HTTP 402 (insufficient available credits given in-flight requests); the run ended in error and no requested mapping was saved. This is not a reproduction of the original defect or red-to-green proof. The initial fixture attempt failed before inference on an incorrect role-field assertion, which was corrected to read users.list.

prs.title: improve(ui): open Channels without loading Chat
prs.body:
Channels currently downloads Chat’s transcript dependencies through a native Checkbox used by the closed pairing dialog. Keeping that unchanged control in the existing deferred UI chunk removes the Chat edge from the route. The initial view also waits for its first status result, so connected rows do not arrive below an already-visible Add channel control. Cached refreshes and failed-read retries retain their content.

## Performance proof

The 990-observation performance run used matched complete production builds at base `36a1c58e91dd9ae991edd76f9ccbfdcd056c5fa0` and head `48fa2a66752092fb9cf494d09084d37c40bfdc24`. The final branch merges current main `e814c50ed66c1c3849e596e32324c22100034f1c`; its only Channels integration change was import ordering around main’s IconButton change. Test readiness repairs wait for the lazy effort slider, asynchronous transcript end-follow, and full command-palette scrollbar styles before their existing assertions. Main now supplies the independently landed keyboard-tooltip repair and 44px composer touch-target correction (#194419); the merge takes both versions verbatim. Those repairs have left this PR’s diff. The Channels feature, its chunking and settled rendering are unchanged. Screenshots are retained from the previous integration; the newer shared menu and Logs changes do not change the captured Channels states. The feature behavior and chunking remain identical. Complete matched builds and final screenshots were refreshed after integration; the performance run is reused with that disclosed source delta. All ten native plugin UIs were built; all nine feature-eligible distributions ship. Synthetic fixtures isolate renderer and transport cost; these are not live Gateway/provider latency claims. The committed engines harness runs one observation at a time, with 20 rotated base/head/base triplets per cell and A/A controls. Localhost and 100 ms HTTP/inbound-Gateway latency are separate.

Five fewer JavaScript requests and **1,696,290 fewer decoded JS bytes** load during the first Channels navigation after `/new`. One CSS request disappears. Chromium RTT completed target assets fall 48→42 and the HTTP/1 six-connection lower bound falls 8→7; observed JS request-start clusters stay 2→2. The lower bound is not dependency depth. No new code-coverage claim is made.

| Engine / network | First visit base → head, median/p95 ms | Warm return base → head, median/p95 ms |
|---|---:|---:|
| chromium / localhost | 99.80/101.50 → 96.20/97.90 | 27.70/29.50 → 28.10/29.70 |
| chromium / rtt-100ms | 991.45/995.10 → 878.50/895.10 | 27.25/29.30 → 27.10/28.50 |
| webkit / localhost | 196.00/209.00 → 153.00/163.00 | 32.00/35.00 → 32.00/34.00 |

| firefox / rtt-100ms | 996.00/1001.00 → 890.00/897.00 | 29.50/34.00 → 31.00/34.00 |

First-visit RTT medians improve **11.39% Chromium, 13.97% WebKit, 10.64% Firefox**; every first-visit p95 improves. Chromium first-visit task CPU improves 7.90% locally and 7.25% at RTT.

The initial Firefox warm result and WebKit RTT tail required ten additional rotated pairs with A/A. Firefox confirmation: local 31/34→30.5/35 ms (A/A 30.5/38), RTT 32/38→30.5/36 (A/A 31/34). Pooled 30-pair Firefox local is 29.5/34→31/36 (A/A 28.5/38): the +5.08% pooled median is borderline, but the independent confirmation improves 1.61% and its tail is within A/A variation. Pooled Firefox RTT is 30/37→31/35. WebKit confirmation holds 32 ms median and improves p95 35→34; pooled p95 is 35→36 ms. Both original and confirmation results are retained; this is acceptance under the ten-additional-pairs rule, not a claim that every sample improved.

| First native detail open (localhost, 20 triplets) | Application base → head, median/p95 ms | A/A median/p95 ms |

All 990 timing observations passed behaviorally (720 initial navigation, 180 first action, 90 targeted confirmation). First action uses the browser-local input-to-last-commit interval; the harness does not admit action steps under nonlocal profiles, so it is measured only at localhost. Host one-minute load ranges: navigation 2.85–13.50, action 3.55–5.52, targeted confirmation 3.28–5.01. No browser or build matrix overlapped another.

## Final complete-build bytes — no cap increase

The coordinator accepted the earlier +176 B whole-Chat served-gzip / +160 B normalized-gzip trade (raw −170 B); New Session was −131 B served. After integrating main, both complete Control UI builds include the previously built native plugin distributions (their source is unchanged). The candidate now shrinks both whole surfaces. The former cap edit is removed: **no budget changes remain**.

| Whole route surface | Raw bytes (base → head) | Served gzip (base → head) | Normalized gzip (base → head) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Chat | 4,974,664 → 4,974,488 (−176) | 1,431,004 → 1,430,692 (−312) | 1,422,989 → 1,422,911 (−78) |
| New Session | 3,196,639 → 3,196,480 (−159) | 901,998 → 901,892 (−106) | 896,715 → 896,689 (−26) |

Startup remains **89,940 B normalized JS**, three JS requests and one CSS request, identical to the refreshed base. Existing absolute largest-chunk, Chat and New Session limits are exceeded on that base; candidate growth is evaluated against it and is not hidden by a ceiling increase. Nine feature-eligible native plugin distributions ship.

## Correctness and review

| Proof | Result |
|---|---|
| UI typecheck, targeted lint | Passed for the exact runtime source |

The current test-line budget has 70 lines of headroom; no allocation is added. The complete touched `view.tsx` module retains 14 memos. No signal, effect, listener, query, lifecycle or lazy owner is added. The existing domain owner still controls reads and errors.

## Screenshots

Inspected synthetic data only, with no masks or injected styles. Both Channels-entry and first-action Chromium CLS are zero at all three widths. Whole-document CLS includes earlier New Session boot variation, also seen in A/A; that variation is retained and not attributed to this route. ## CI repairs and current landing state

Initial CI run 42326746072 exposed a one-line test budget overage and an ambiguous keyboard-tooltip locator. The repair keeps every assertion while shortening repeated DOM queries, removes the allocation, and selects the status tooltip by its accessible name. Focused Channels status tests (4/4), keyboard E2E (1/1), and UI typecheck passed.

Replacement run 42329533795 passed every Control UI E2E shard, including keyboard and Goal replacement. It failed changed-file import formatting and five UI assertions. Every failed assertion passed on the latest completed scheduled main run 42324053721, so none is called inherited from that comparison. Current main supplies the landed annotations, mobile Review menu and Agents-memory assertion repairs. The remaining effort-picker test pressed Tab after the native popover opened while its lazy slider was still absent; it now waits for the visible slider, preserving every focus/Escape assertion. That complete browser test file passes9/9. Independent review found no actionable issue in either repair.

The original auto request was confirmed retired before replacement. The final branch uses native explicit replacement-head recovery after fresh review/preparation and CI; no direct GitHub merge or re-armed cancelled auto request is used. Final repaired head is `b396e315cc80757944a1ce032001b2972899351a`; fresh full CI is pending. Complete-build bytes above remain from3a146 (subsequent changes are test-only readiness waits). The previous head could not start CI because main had landed two overlapping repairs. Merging main resolved those conflicts by retaining main’s code exactly; no empty push or CI rerun was used. Fresh independent P0–P2 review is scoped-clean, the UI typecheck passes, and complete builds pass the strict base-relative budget check with zero violations. The latest scheduled main never reached WebKit, so no inherited-failure exception is claimed. Local base and head passed the file, but that was not Linux proof. The test now waits for the final non-prepared row and actual end before stopping. prs.title: fix(plugins): suspend unused install snapshot publication
prs.body:
Related: #187350. Follow-up to #189624.

## What Problem This Solves

Managed plugin installs publish persistent source snapshots that startup does not consume, adding filesystem work and disk usage without a reader.

## User Impact

Installs and updates stop publishing those unused snapshots. They still capture unexecuted source and record content/dependency-closure digests so a future reader can qualify lazy publication. Runtime startup continues to use fresh captures.

## Why This Change Was Made

Suspend the install-time publication pass until a startup reader meets its security and performance gate. Keep the existing snapshot format, installed-index owner, rollback retention, reader custody, and retirement machinery for artifacts already created by main/nightly builds. No eager replacement or extra data deletion is introduced.

Current published stable tags v2026.10.10/v2026.11.1 and beta v2026.11.5-beta.1 exclude the original publisher commit and implementation paths. This changes no release artifact or fs-safe pin.

## Evidence

The failing-first install-boundary regression observed two publication calls for two preparations; the suspended path must make zero while retaining matching content/closure digests and never evaluating plugin code. Existing artifact tests cover final-reader retirement and interrupted publication cleanup. All 35 focused install/artifact cases pass under the pinned runtime, including last-reader retirement, interrupted staging, owner changes, token replacement, and tamper rejection. Core and plugin-test type checks, scoped lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Independent P0–P2 review found no actionable issues. The change removes 41 net production lines with zero net test growth. The two real-install persistence cases also pass after replacing their old eager-publication expectations; they verify stable digests, normalized integrity, no snapshot artifacts/candidates, and no plugin execution across reinstall. The cached integration run took 18.1 s overall (7.6 s test execution); the initial CI run took 14.9 s for this file. Exact-head CI will be recorded before landing.

The first CI head exposed exactly two stale persistence-test expectations that still required eager snapshots. They were reproduced locally and corrected to the new suspension contract; no production behavior was changed in that repair. Independent P0–P2 review of the repair is clean.

prs.title: improve(android): benchmark selected Material icons
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Android release builds process the full Material Icons Extended library even though the phone app and tests import only 98 of its icons.

## User Impact

This is a nonpublishing performance experiment. **Do not merge.** No appearance changes are intended, and no build will be uploaded to Play or Firebase.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep Material Icons Core and copy only the exact existing Extended vector implementations into app-owned packages (97 shared production icons and one third-party-only production icon). Geometry, mirroring, vector names, lazy initialization, screen layout, and accessibility descriptions stay unchanged. Packages/private cache names adopt repository conventions; original copyright headers, modification notices, provenance, and Apache license are retained.

The full Extended AAR contains 11,105 classes and 85,390,331 uncompressed class bytes (81.4 MiB). The selected upstream Kotlin sources total about 233 KiB before repository formatting. These counts identify avoidable build input; they do not establish a speedup.

Temporary benchmark tooling on this branch will not land. A focused production PR will be prepared only if this experiment qualifies; otherwise this PR will be closed with the measured results.

## Evidence

- 42 focused Play Debug tests passed with no skips, including native Compose rendering of all 128 imported icons (Core + Extended), component rendering, tool icon selection, command palette, settings toggles, and packaged license notices.
- Both LTR and RTL captures are byte-identical before/after. Source comparison also confirms all 98 upstream vector implementations after reversing the documented package/cache-name/formatting changes.
- `:app:ktlintFormat` passed. `:app:compileThirdPartyDebugKotlin` passed; release runtime dependency tree contains Core 1.7.8 and no Extended dependency.
- Codex AutoReview of the complete local candidate against baseline `e814c50ed66c1c3849e596e32324c22100034f1c`: scoped-clean at P2 after repairing and reproducing the third-party source-set finding. Candidate source commit is patch-identical to the reviewed snapshot. Temporary workload independently reviewed against candidate `8bcd08ef217b0350a0d85207243aa2e9fd21a68b`: scoped-clean at P2. Workflow/actionlint, targeted contract test, syntax, lint, formatting, and whitespace checks passed.
- Baseline: `e814c50ed66c1c3849e596e32324c22100034f1c`. Candidate source: `8bcd08ef217b0350a0d85207243aa2e9fd21a68b`.

### Preregistered workload and acceptance (before dispatch)

One fresh `blacksmith-8vcpu-ubuntu-2404` runner; five serial alternating-order baseline/candidate pairs (AB, BA, AB, BA, AB). Both use the production 3-GiB Parallel GC, eight Gradle worker leases, `--no-parallel`, and serial Tooling API model execution. Before measurement, build and verify each variant once to hydrate one common dependency snapshot; these two preparation builds are excluded from results. Each measured sample restores pristine source/task outputs to the same build path, that identical warm snapshot, and fresh JVMs. Node dependency inputs, build identity, source-commit metadata, and disposable signing identity stay identical. No release environment, store credentials, Firebase credentials, OpenAI credentials, upload steps, or shared cache writes.

Committed command:

```sh
node scripts/bench-android-selected-icons.mjs \
  --source candidate --candidate selected-icons-source \
  --output .build/android-selected-icons
```

Each sample runs signing preflight, `:wear:bundleRelease :app:bundlePlayRelease`, and two `jarsigner` checks. Collect Gradle profiles/task outcomes, AAB sizes, 1-Hz aggregate Java RSS/CPU and host pressure/OOM counters.

Keep only if all of the following hold:

- Bundle median improves by **at least 5% and 5 seconds**, with **at least 4/5 pair wins**.
- No regression in bundle p95/max, complete preflight/build/signature median, median Java CPU, or maximum aggregate Java RSS.
- All ten builds and twenty signatures pass, complete task/outcome/actionable coverage matches, and zero OOM kills occur.
- A measured regression of 20% or more in any performance/resource metric prevents shipping; resource tradeoffs require explicit acceptance.

Five-sample p95 uses the observed maximum. Collection success is reported as `collected`, with acceptance pending offline analysis. No result is declared qualified from one run or one sample.

### Initial setup failure and preparation repair

Run 42336846577 stopped before any build or measured sample: no production Gradle cache matched the manifest hash on this candidate. No comparison data was collected. The workload now performs one unmeasured build/verification of each frozen source revision, stops their JVMs, and takes a common dependency snapshot. All ten measured samples still start from pristine source/task outputs and that same snapshot. No shared cache is saved, and the acceptance rule is unchanged. This measures the warm-dependency case; it does not claim first-build download savings.

### Collector correction

Run 42337212577 successfully built and verified both preparation variants and the first measured baseline. It then stopped on a collector mistake: aggregate `bundle` lifecycle tasks have no actions and correctly report `Did No Work`. The retained profile confirms 163 task rows, 149 actionable tasks (146 executed, 3 up-to-date), and fresh Kotlin/R8/package/sign work. The corrected guard requires the actual package/sign tasks to execute, preserving complete task/outcome equality and signature checks. No performance comparison is claimed from that incomplete run. The acceptance rule is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(media): keep images on separately registered provider routes
prs.body:
Closes #192434

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes images being sent through the wrong provider when a separately registered provider uses a historical media alias, and retained image tools continuing with a removed credential after logout. The follow-up repair preserves valid provider-scoped migration and inherited shared-credential recovery.

## User Impact

Declared providers keep their own routing and credentials. Retained tools refuse removed or replaced stored credentials without cancelling unrelated valid work. Unclaimed legacy aliases, explicit standalone model choices and intentional local no-auth behavior remain unchanged. No configuration migration is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing provider-identity, captured-generation and physical credential-authority owners. Selected-provider/config context now reaches credential preparation and migration checks, preserving [PR #143310](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/143310)'s scoped migration contract. Valid producer-owned inheritance can recover a derived store without overriding a readable local credential or using retained credential bytes as authority.

The credential-read operation was moved with its existing reader injected to satisfy the source-size ratchet. No new state store, global revision fence or blanket logout abort. Current main `e814c50e` is integrated without rewriting the existing PR history; independent recovery, extraction and integration reviews are linked in the evidence with their actual scopes and resolved findings.

## Evidence

- **Current source `a0be996609f0b1c4f8a23ab7f2ab5883efbe79fa`:** [immutable main-integration evidence](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/8c1ab5514caf953253b48bba7731c13b0416bebe/credential-recovery-a0be9966/README.md). Exact source tree, all 40 changed-file hashes, commands, original/export hashes, reviews, package binding and observed results are included.
- **Targeted checks:** 202 tests across 12 affected files passed on `93e40061e`; the only subsequent source change is an erased type-import correction. Exact `a0be9966` passes production/auth-test typechecks, scoped production/test lint, changed-TypeScript formatting and the test-size ratchet.
- **Installed product-boundary proof:** canonical public package build and tar integrity passed; 17,161 installed dist/launcher files match the tar. Both model-only and native-handler positive controls send the correct synthetic key and image. Live logout removes the API-key profile without blanket-aborting the retained run; live inventory confirms removal. Both retained tools then refuse with zero post-logout HTTP. Final runtime proof: exit 0, 204.88s.
- **Adverse evidence retained:** the earlier e33d revoked-credential transmission, prior failed/limited attempts and [9db evidence](https://github.com/jason-allen-oneal/openclaw/blob/9bc423d06dba9d58d83545be955bb5f88d635780/credential-repair-9db22c6c/credential-repair-evidence.md) remain intact. This addendum also retains the dependency-containment refusal, an overbroad local filename assertion, and the first runtime readiness timeout; none is relabeled as a passing attempt. The corrected readiness driver uses the maintained default retry count with unchanged revocation assertions.
- **Build advisories:** the UI performance step uses maintained `--report-only` behavior and reports three gzip size overruns. Exact values are linked; they are not passing size targets, no limits were raised, and separate baseline attribution was not established.
- **Explicit limits:** synthetic loopback receivers, not live Gemini/OAuth. Separate fresh-after-logout calls send an image using `custom-local` and receive 401; zero I/O applies only to retained revoked tools. Earlier generation-overlap and install/upgrade sweeps remain prior-head evidence, not new runs. Hosted checks and current-head review are tracked separately; local proof does not claim hosted acceptance.

No production installation, deployment or merge. Maintainer edits remain enabled. Exact-head maintainer security approval remains required separately.

prs.title: fix(node): reconnect after OpenClaw ID server rotation
prs.body:
Related: #193993, #193982

## What Problem This Solves

Saved OpenClaw ID nodes keep dialing the server key from enrollment, so an honest Gateway key rotation cannot be discovered on reconnect.

## User Impact

Nodes refresh and verify current signed server authority and membership before connecting, retire an active connection when its server key changes, and preserve learned trust across restart and refused re-enrollment. Verified node removal stops the host with a rejoin instruction.

Preview targets without an explicit Discovery origin must rejoin. Pairing assumes the invitation remains secret; the six-digit comparison does not protect against a stolen invitation combined with control of pairing delivery. Existing freshness/v1 bounded-replay limits remain.

## Why This Change Was Made

Enrollment and reconnect share one bounded, node-signed Discovery client and descriptor verifier. The canonical SQLite writer retains the strongest binding pin, membership order, and binding-retirement facts without overwriting unrelated node settings. Persistence completes before dialing; failed persistence stops further attempts. Periodic authority refresh continues during active traffic.

This is one repair commit on top of `openclaw-517/node-join`, not a replacement for the draft feature stack.

## Evidence

- Original source failed the real Unix bridge regressions (8 failed, 4 passed), the protocol retirement regression (1 failed, 8 passed), and the SQLite stale-startup regression. The repair passed all 106 focused tests, including 21 SQLite config tests and four native Gateway integration tests. All 18 affected connection/bridge/native Gateway tests passed again after final corrections.
- Isolated Linux arm64 execution used the real native addon, production Unix bridge, signed loopback Discovery, and a task-local relay. HTTP 200 moved from server A to B after signed rotation; active A closed; restart refused replayed or missing evidence; previously learned retirement evidence survived a newer-order snapshot. Native callback persistence and real SQLite durability were proved separately.
- Changed-file lint, core types, all selected changed-test type graphs, formatting, diff checks, and the test-line budget passed. The +668 LF allocation covers the new bridge, lifecycle, enrollment, protocol, and SQLite regression coverage; the shared scalar is unchanged.
- A qualified local ClawSweeper runtime was unavailable. Local autoreview (OpenAI/Codex, `gpt-6.1-sol`, high, P0–P2) completed against the change snapshot based on `b7abc8d1cb76e3a5ffba12c1a3f4dca6bf74b81f` with no actionable findings after three initial findings were repaired. Subsequent changes only consolidated stop checks, completed worker fixture fields, typed a test spy, and clarified documentation; affected checks passed again. Final head: `b697e1b192249307525a33970a8d3fc5df8b466a`.
- Broad CI remains in progress and is not green. Current failed jobs and their attribution are recorded below; no checks were rerun or bypassed.
- [Hosted build and artifact checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42338938864/job/128302514029) passed using main's trusted harness with `target_ref=b697e1b192249307525a33970a8d3fc5df8b466a`; the job log confirms that exact checkout. prs.title: fix(tmux): honor zero-padded decimal wait timeouts
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The bundled tmux text-wait helper accepts digit-only seconds, but Bash interprets leading zeroes as octal: `08` and `09` error, while `010` waits eight seconds instead of ten.

## User Impact

Zero-padded timeout values use the documented decimal duration. Default timeout, zero, validation, polling and diagnostics remain unchanged. No new configuration or dependency.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add an explicit `10#` radix at the existing deadline calculation. The original commit by @zhangguiping-xydt is preserved. The existing help already documents integer seconds and needs no change.

## Evidence

Exact head: `9ab45d03b6c56ed8d74568e609aec344b68349cb`, compared with main `49e8b5d2b5a7ca23d26fc60776be522140c027b9`.

[Observed elapsed-time table and raw diagnostic excerpts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194449#issuecomment-6702365732).

The published real-tmux packaged-script proof records actual wall-clock waits in secretless Linux Docker using a private pane, real capture, real clocks and sleeps. Each script is extracted from its npm tarball; no mocked tmux, clock or sleep. Shell helpers need no compilation/core build, so packaging uses `npm pack --ignore-scripts`. Main rejects `08`/`09` and interprets `010` as eight; the candidate interprets them as eight, nine and ten seconds. Ordinary `5`, `0`, invalid input, and already-present text with zero/default timeout retain their behavior. `bash -n` passes.

The added 37-line mocked Python clock test is replaced by the published real-runtime regression evidence, following the same maintainer-approved approach as #194434. Net test lines **0**; production **+1/−1**, no allocation.

## Merge Risk

Two-way door: reverting fully restores previous arithmetic; no persisted state or API migration. Blast radius is deadline calculation in the bundled tmux text-wait script for digit-only timeout arguments.
