prs.title: fix(plugins): cancel interrupted marketplace list reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An acknowledged interrupt during the read-only `openclaw plugins marketplace list <source>` does not cancel the pending marketplace source read. When the source is a git/GitHub URL, the read is a `git clone` that stays open until the process is forced down, and an uncancelled late result can still reach the renderer. This is the invocation-interrupt class repaired for ClawHub package searches in #194076, and for inference in #192896 and #193893.

Precedent: #194076（同形状：read-only CLI 网络读 + invocation signal 转发；本 PR 换点位到 git-clone 泳道）

## Why This Change Was Made

#194076 forwarded the invocation signal through the ClawHub HTTP adapters (`fetchWithSsrFGuard` already declared `signal`). The marketplace list git-clone path was not covered: `runPluginMarketplaceListCommand` passed no signal into `listMarketplacePlugins` / `loadMarketplace` / `cloneMarketplaceRepo` / `acquireGitSource`, so the underlying `git clone` never saw cancellation even though `runCommandWithTimeout` already declares `signal`.

This PR preserves the established behavior: `runPluginMarketplaceListCommand` now checks the invocation signal before dispatch and before publishing a result, and forwards it through the existing chain into `acquireGitSource`, whose `run` closure passes it to `runCommandWithTimeout`. The parameter stays optional, so install callers (`installPluginFromMarketplace`, git-install, source-install) keep their existing behavior. No new validator, option, config, retry policy, lifetime owner, or schema.

Production LOC is `+17/-0`.

Classification: `behavior-completing`

## User Impact

Interrupting `openclaw plugins marketplace list <git-or-https-source>` inside a managed async-work scope now aborts the pending clone and suppresses the late result/output, instead of printing the marketplace after Ctrl+C. Uninterrupted listings, local path sources, and install flows are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Exact-head proof receipt

- Product head SHA: `02e423602de`
- Current-main RED baseline: `8662f3bf78dc7d644d207c8afb6f2f8b8f5750b0`
- Production entry: `runPluginMarketplaceListCommand` in `src/cli/plugins-marketplace-list-command.ts`
- Canonical owner exercised: `listMarketplacePlugins` in `src/plugins/marketplace.ts`, `acquireGitSource` in `src/infra/git-source.ts`
- Decision surface: the interruption signal forwarded from the CLI into the git-clone read path
- Recorder/readback boundary: captured CLI output / JSON write for a late marketplace result after the signal fires
- Acceptance RED: on pristine current-main, the same `AsyncWorkScope` scenario prints the late marketplace result (`writeJson`) after `beginClose()`; both cancel cases fail.
- Acceptance GREEN: on this head, both cancel cases emit no output, no JSON, no error, no exit; all 16 marketplace suite tests pass.
- Legal controls: uninterrupted json/text listing still prints the marketplace; existing marketplace/git-source suites (39 tests) pass unchanged.
- Cleanup and limitations: every run used isolated temp state; no production Gateway, session, channel, token, or config was touched.
- Format and ratchet: the cancellation regressions were merged into the existing marketplace command suite (oxfmt-clean), and the justified +18 test lines are offset by a scoped test-lines allocation.

### Real Git child-process cancellation (RED -> GREEN)

The signal-forwarding contract is proven against a **real `git clone` subprocess**, not a mock. A local TCP listener that accepts but never responds (`git://127.0.0.1:<port>/repo.git`) holds a real `git clone` open; `acquireGitSource` calls the real `runCommandWithTimeout` and the real `git` binary. The CLI-side `AsyncWorkScope` owns the forwarded signal.

| Build | Interrupt | Returned after | Comment |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| RED (no signal passed) | — | **8041 ms** (timeout 8000) | clone hangs until `runCommandWithTimeout` force-kills it |
| GREEN (signal forwarded) | `beginClose()` | **11 ms** | git child process cancelled immediately; no late output |

Timing is monotonic wall time from start; both runs share the identical hanging source, temp output dir, and `git` binary. The RED run proves the pre-fix behavior waits out the whole timeout; the GREEN run proves the forwarded signal reaches and cancels the live git child process. No external network, credentials, or non-local services are involved.

### Shipped CLI real-PTY proof (independent build)

A **shipped `openclaw.mjs`** was independently built from this head (Node 24.22.1, tsdown runtime build) and driven through a **real controlling PTY** with a **real `git clone`** against a local slow git source (`http://127.0.0.1:19428/repo.git`, a TCP listener that accepts but never responds, so the clone stays pending). SIGINT is delivered as the terminal VINTR byte; the same slow source, temp HOME/profile, and `git` binary are used for every run.

| Build | SIGINT | Settled after | Observable behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| RED (base, no signal) | VINTR | **1.6 s** | Bare `^C`; the process is hard-killed by the signal with **no cleanup notice and no cancellation of the in-flight clone**. Without SIGINT the clone stays pending past the `runCommandWithTimeout` window (>15 s, only the timeout force-kill settles it). |
| GREEN (this head, signal forwarded) | VINTR | **3.2 s** | `^CCommand interrupted by SIGINT. Waiting for cleanup before exiting.` then `{"ok":false,"error":{"type":"cli_error","message":"Plugin CLI invocation is closed"}}`; the live `git clone` child process is cancelled (zero git processes remain) and no marketplace JSON is emitted. |

The RED run proves the interrupted in-flight Git read is not cancelled on the base (either hard-killed with no settlement, or left pending to the timeout), and the GREEN run proves the forwarded invocation signal reaches the real `git clone` subprocess and cancels it with a clean settlement. No mocks are imported into the CLI; the built binary, the child git process, and the terminal are all real.


### Inspectable RED -> GREEN terminal trace (command suite)

`vitest run --config vitest.config.ts src/cli/plugins-cli.marketplace-entries.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.

```text
RED (pristine main, production code without signal):
  × plugins marketplace list > cancels the marketplace list read: before
  × plugins marketplace list > cancels the marketplace list read: result
  Tests  2 failed | 14 passed (16)

GREEN (this head):
  ✓ plugins marketplace list > cancels the marketplace list read: before
  ✓ plugins marketplace list > cancels the marketplace list read: result
  Tests  16 passed (16)
```

### Test consolidation (review feedback)

The first revision added a standalone `src/cli/plugins-marketplace-list-command.test.ts` with two new closed mock factories and 108 test lines. Per review, that file is removed and the cancellation regressions are consolidated into the existing `src/cli/plugins-cli.marketplace-entries.test.ts` marketplace command suite, whose mocks were already grandfathered:

- `pnpm check:test-mock-exports` — passes (no new first-party mock factories; the file is deleted).
- `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` — net test-line **-87** (remove 108, add 21), well under ceiling.
- The standalone json/text/registration cases duplicated coverage already present in the marketplace suite; only the two cancellation cases are added.

### Verification

- `src/cli/plugins-cli.marketplace-entries.test.ts` — 16 passed (head), 2 failed / 14 passed (pristine base)
- `src/plugins/marketplace.test.ts` + `src/plugins/marketplace.sources.test.ts` + `src/infra/git-source.test.ts` — 39 passed (no regression)
- `pnpm check:test-mock-exports` + `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` — pass
- `git diff --check`
- Not tested: a live `node openclaw.mjs` PTY run against a remote git URL on this host (network read; the terminal-recording form of this proof was supplied by the maintainer for the sibling #194076/#193893); the signal-forwarding contract is proven here at the live git-child boundary and at the CLI output-suppression boundary.

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: `+17/-0`
- Test LOC: `+21/-108` (net -87)
- Existing-solutions preflight: reuses `getAsyncWorkSignal` (already exported for CLI commands) and the already-declared `signal` on `runCommandWithTimeout`; no new abstraction.
- Config/default, protocol/schema, authorization, storage, migration, upgrade impact: none. Optional parameter; all existing callers unchanged.

prs.title: feat(streaming): allow a separate command progress limit
prs.body:
Closes #157614

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot keep raw shell commands compact while allowing longer human-readable progress lines: both currently share one character limit.

## User Impact

Adds optional `streaming.progress.commandMaxLineChars`, for example:

```json5
progress: {
  toolProgress: true,
  commandText: "raw",
  maxLineChars: 400,
  commandMaxLineChars: 100,
}
```

Omitting the new key preserves existing behavior. It neither enables raw command text nor changes default visibility. Native Telegram/Slack labels and status presentation retain their existing limits; the override bounds command detail there. Platform-wide message limits still apply. This is presentation control, not redaction.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing command-bearing classification now survives progress-line snapshots so shared text, native Telegram live/adopted cards, and Slack cards/task chunks can use the same optional setting without guessing from displayed prose.

No new SDK exports, model calls, shell parser, migration, or default changes. Pure progress config readers move into the existing config-reader module, Telegram live/adopted rendering share account-option resolution, and Slack title deduplication is isolated as a pure render helper. Canonical UI hints describe the new field as a display-only limit rather than a privacy boundary. Existing oversized-file ratchets stay green without exemptions.

Direct boundary probes also cover Telegram plain/rich rendering, Slack card/native updates, nested account inheritance, Unicode-safe compaction, invalid schema values, and the extracted Slack title helper.

- Existing fixture extension only; no new sleeps, polling implementation, Gateway boot, or external credentials.
- The deterministic pre-PR wrapper passes on frozen base `ef54f6720460` at exact signed head `27eb8524489a` (merge tree `d9fd44e5aa7a`), including core and extension source/test typechecks, changed-file lint/format, dead-export scan, generated metadata/docs, SDK boundaries, and repository ratchets.

prs.title: fix(xai): restore subscription-backed X search
prs.body:
Related: #147728, #165654. Related implementation: #179944.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes native X search failing with Grok subscription OAuth because its Responses request loses the selected auth mode, uses the public API by default, and omits the subscription client headers.

## User Impact

OAuth-backed X search and the sibling native Responses tools select the subscription endpoint and required client identity. Explicit API-key and custom-proxy requests keep their route. A failed subscription refresh cannot silently retry with a configured paid API key. Searches that previously recovered by switching to that paid key will now fail on the subscription route instead.

**Live subscription acceptance is still unverified.** This candidate has not been installed on a live gateway; all external HTTP in the regression tests is simulated. No merge or deployment is requested.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the selected credential's mode through the existing host auth resolver instead of inferring it from token bytes or unrelated configuration. Keep the old string callback source-compatible, and bind both callbacks to the existing plugin/operation lifetime before and after asynchronous resolution.

Share xAI's proxy-only header policy between streaming and Responses tools, using the observed Grok CLI compatibility floor of `1.0.13` rather than OpenClaw's release version. Preserve configured-key precedence, secret-reference refusal, cancellation, citations and auth-separated caches.

#179944 addresses related streaming/utility/probe compatibility. This change adds native X/Responses tool routing and selected-auth propagation; it does not copy that PR's utility, probe or billing changes.

## Evidence

Current head: `63d340e0765eb545a55b16ca6a579a1cecc655fa`; tested base: `941b949f8c72566fd3b5ff9583418a36e08a2253`.

- Observed native `x_search` on OpenClaw `2026.10.10` fail with HTTP 426: Grok CLI version `none`, minimum `1.0.13`. Before production edits, the real X tool plus simulated external HTTP reproduced missing-header HTTP 426 and default-route HTTP 401; API-key/custom-proxy controls passed.
- 177 focused tests passed on the repair; an additional 1,117 plugin/gateway/lifecycle tests passed, including actual loopback recovery, native grant/revoke and OAuth tool exposure.
- The final follow-up changes only a test fixture to parse captured requests with `Request`. Its 51-test owner suite and targeted lint pass. [The follow-up diff](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/compare/2ac16ea992423e8669e5283cd084a1132e5d011c...63d340e0765eb545a55b16ca6a579a1cecc655fa) leaves production files unchanged.
- Complete build passes on the current head: `pnpm build` (354.7s). The built CLI reports `OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (63d340e)`; the built public `callGatewayFromCli` export loads successfully.
- Core and xAI type checks, targeted lint, format parity and the test-lines ratchet pass. The task-owned allocation covers regression boundaries without changing the shared ceiling.
- Independent source review found and verified repair of a refresh-to-paid-key path. Comprehensive exact-head P3 review returned zero findings for this base/head (request `req-20261107T042433Z-6459216126`, epoch 2). That review inspected the supplied diff; it did not execute runtime tests. [CI42338493997](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42338493997) passes on this head.

The tests prove request assembly and local authority/lifecycle behavior, not account-specific acceptance. A maintainer with a configured subscription can supply the remaining live X result and citations.

Key regression sources: [X subscription transport](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/63d340e0765eb545a55b16ca6a579a1cecc655fa/extensions/xai/x-search-subscription.test.ts), [registered tool transport](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/63d340e0765eb545a55b16ca6a579a1cecc655fa/extensions/xai/index.test.ts), and [retained auth callback lifetime](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/63d340e0765eb545a55b16ca6a579a1cecc655fa/src/plugins/tool-factory-context.test.ts).


**Maintainer decision requested:** accept the additive `resolveAuthForProvider` tool-context capability and the intentional retirement of paid-key recovery after a rejected subscription request. [The current hosted review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194445#issuecomment-6702364892) found no definite introduced bug and recommends accepting that boundary, while keeping merge blocked for owner acceptance and proof.

**Remaining proof:** the registered tool must reject a retired plugin/operation at the final credential-bearing HTTP effect; a live Gateway subscription X-search call must return an answer and citations; fresh/upgrade routing controls must preserve existing settings and credentials. Callback-lifetime and simulated HTTP tests do not substitute for those checks. No live gateway installation or credentialed acceptance run was performed.

prs.title: fix(android): say when a chat file is outside the allowlist
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Android chat keeps the curated attachment allowlist from #110941, but a `.csv` is rejected when the provider reports `text/comma-separated-values`, and a file outside the list disappears with no usable next step.

Fixes #190979.

## User Impact

PDF, Office, CSV, Markdown, and media attachments still attach. JSON, ZIP, YAML, XML, and plain text still do not. Picking one of those now shows "This file type isn't supported. Choose a PDF, Office, CSV, Markdown, or media file." A CSV labeled `text/comma-separated-values`, or a generic `application/octet-stream` whose name ends in an allowlisted extension such as `.csv` or `.pdf`, is admitted as that type. A `.json` name is not. Extra supported files past the eight-file cap stay a limit omission, not a type rejection.

## Why This Change Was Made

#110941 added this allowlist on purpose and did not accept blanket `application/*`. This change keeps that set. The picker is unfiltered only so a rejected file can be chosen and explained. Admission is still the allowlist, plus aliases and generic filenames that already name a listed type.

## Evidence

- `:app:testPlayDebugUnitTest` `ShareLaunchTest`: passed. Ten JPEGs still drop two for the cap with `unsupportedAttachmentCount == 0`. A JSON share drops one and sets `unsupportedAttachmentCount == 1`.
- `:app:ktlintMainSourceSetCheck` and `:app:ktlintTestSourceSetCheck`: passed.
- API 34 emulator. Before this branch, the Files picker could select PDF and Markdown only. JSON, CSV (`text/comma-separated-values`), YAML, plain text, XML, and ZIP were not selectable.

![Before: filtered Downloads picker](https://github.com/saariuslystoned/openclaw/raw/4c6120aff13bfac53b53e1eb57ddd06429620638/apps/android/proof/191316/before-filtered-picker.png)

- Same emulator, Play debug build of this head:
  - System share sheet, `sample.txt` (`text/plain`): the app shows the notice and does not stage the file.
  - System share sheet, `sample.csv` (`text/comma-separated-values`): the app stages `sample.csv`.
  - In-app picker, `octet.csv` (provider `application/octet-stream`): the app stages it. The share sheet does not list the app for `application/octet-stream`; the manifest filter is unchanged.
  - In-app picker, `sample.json`: the notice. `sample.csv`: staged. Crops are the composer only.

![Share sheet rejects plain text](https://github.com/saariuslystoned/openclaw/raw/4c6120aff13bfac53b53e1eb57ddd06429620638/apps/android/proof/191316/share-txt-rejected.png)

![Share sheet stages CSV](https://github.com/saariuslystoned/openclaw/raw/4c6120aff13bfac53b53e1eb57ddd06429620638/apps/android/proof/191316/share-csv-staged.png)

![Picker stages octet-stream CSV](https://github.com/saariuslystoned/openclaw/raw/4c6120aff13bfac53b53e1eb57ddd06429620638/apps/android/proof/191316/picker-octet-csv.png)

![Unsupported JSON notice](https://github.com/saariuslystoned/openclaw/raw/4c6120aff13bfac53b53e1eb57ddd06429620638/apps/android/proof/191316/unsupported-notice.png)

![CSV staged after the JSON notice](https://github.com/saariuslystoned/openclaw/raw/4c6120aff13bfac53b53e1eb57ddd06429620638/apps/android/proof/191316/csv-admitted.png)

## Decision still with a maintainer

The review asked whether the picker should show every file while admission stays curated. This PR does that, and leaves broader document types on #190979. The new screenshots do not decide that.

prs.title: fix(android): start a new chat while a response is still running
prs.body:
Closes #191339

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Android New does nothing while the open chat is still responding, and a later attempt can fail with "Parent session is still active."

## User Impact

User impact: New on Android starts another chat without waiting for the current response, keeps the previous chat's model, thinking, and Fast Mode, and leaves that response running.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sidebar New button was refused in the app whenever a local run was pending, and the gateway treated that same create as a parent reset while the parent still had active work. Ordinary New now stays a parallel child: it still names the open chat as its parent so settings are inherited, and it does not run the parent reset hooks or stop the original response. An explicit worktree start still waits. Forks of an active parent stay refused.

## Evidence

Regressions failed on the pre-fix tree, then passed after the repair.

- Gateway, before: `sessions.create` with `succeedsParent: false` while the parent response was running returned `UNAVAILABLE` / `Parent session main is still active; try again in a moment.`
- Android, before: `startNewChatSucceedsWhileRunPending` failed because New returned false and never called `sessions.create`. The worktree wait still held.
- After: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.sessions.create.lifecycle.test.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.create.forks.test.ts` — 39 passed. The lifecycle test checks inherited provider, model, thinking, and Fast Mode, an unchanged parent session id, the parent run still in phase `running`, and no parent reset hooks.
- After: Android `ChatControllerCommandControlsTest`, `ChatControllerReconnectRestoreTest`, and `ChatControllerOutboxTest` passed. `:app:ktlintCheck` passed. Line-cap ratchet OK.

Fold proof on this head, after the proof gateway was rebuilt from `b8211519e3b14a91fbd1223b5393328fc2bee538`. The installed debug APK matches that build (`80f1d3f315ba148eb48169b643de714e3ce59ac7e9a3f9558fbfdfa2509ab093`). An earlier install was overwritten by a different debug APK and still showed the wait banner; the shots below are from the reinstalled matching APK. The gateway address in the sidebar is covered.

1. Stop is showing, 2 seconds into "List twenty harbor birds slowly one name per line." Model chip is Gemini 3.8 Flash.

![Stop visible during the original reply](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/saariuslystoned/9ef714b6a4cde33c6b287080430603dc/raw/93ee65f997bb973d0e00e200a2a63f56b38ddd91/08-birds-running.png)

2. Sidebar New, tapped while that Stop control was up. A separate "New chat" opens on the same model. The banner is the existing "Could not refresh models" notice, not "Wait for the current response to finish."

![New chat opened during the run](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/saariuslystoned/9ef714b6a4cde33c6b287080430603dc/raw/93ee65f997bb973d0e00e200a2a63f56b38ddd91/09-new-while-stop.png)

3. Back on the original thread, the bird list is complete and readable. The composer is idle again, still on Gemini 3.8 Flash. An earlier New in the same session was also used: that chat answered "docked" to "Reply with the single word docked."

![Original reply completed after New](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/saariuslystoned/9ef714b6a4cde33c6b287080430603dc/raw/93ee65f997bb973d0e00e200a2a63f56b38ddd91/10-original-after.png)

The shot is the local-pending case: New while Stop is on screen, against the patched gateway, with the original model run finishing afterward. A separate moment where the phone had already dropped its pending indicator while the gateway run was still active was not staged on its own.

Related: #192203

## What Problem This Solves

The native iOS main conversation appears to disappear after switching chats because Sessions and All Sessions omit it, while its existing shortcut is named Home.

## User Impact

- The current agent's existing conversation is recognizable as **Main Session** in Pages, Sessions, All Sessions, Overview, and current-session accessibility text.
- Both sidebar shortcuts share selection while Main Session is open; selecting another chat or page clears that selection.
- History and session identity are reused. Existing main-session delete, archive, and snooze protections remain in place.
- The optional blue selection redesign is deliberately excluded.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the shared session projection and alias resolver rather than creating a second conversation or changing session lifecycle policy. All Sessions includes the resolved current-agent main row; Overview still keeps its main shortcut separate from recent conversations. Native localization artifacts and the iOS navigation documentation are updated.

Related work was checked: #191729 changes New Chat creation, #167173 concerns group controls, and #165515 concerns last-chat restoration and voice routing. This change does not replace those behaviors.

## Evidence

### Adopted contribution and source checks

prs.title: docs(imessage): document the probe timeout option
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`channels.imessage.probeTimeoutMs` bounds how long OpenClaw waits for `imsg` in the monitor and action checks that gate the private API bridge, and it is the knob an SSH-wrapped `cliPath` setup needs when a slow round trip makes a healthy bridge look broken. A grep for `probeTimeoutMs` across `docs/` returns nothing, while `docs/channels/imessage/private-api.md` walks readers through exactly those checks.

- Problem: the timeout behind the monitor's startup readiness probe, the cached private-API check that gates actions, and the `watch.subscribe` request is undocumented, including its default — and nothing tells readers that the `openclaw channels status --probe` command on the same page budgets itself instead.
- Solution: state the field, its `10000` ms default, the three checks it covers, when to raise it, that it can be set per account, and that the status command's own `--timeout <ms>` takes precedence over it.
- What changed: `docs/channels/imessage/private-api.md` (2 lines).
- What did NOT change: no code or behavior changes; documentation only.

## Why This Change Was Made

The page already explains what the probe reports and how the cached capability check gates actions, so the timeout that decides whether either of them succeeds belongs in the same place rather than in a config reference the reader has to leave the page for. Because step 4 of that same section tells the reader to run `openclaw channels status --probe`, the paragraph also names the knob that command actually uses, so the two timeouts cannot be confused. `probeTimeoutMs` sits in the account base that both the channel root and `channels.imessage.accounts.<id>` reuse, so the paragraph names both scopes instead of implying a global-only key. The `imsg rpc` label keeps its own separate `timeoutMs: 30_000` in the monitor, so this text deliberately does not claim to cover general RPC calls.

## User Impact

Users on a remote or SSH-wrapped Messages Mac can discover and raise the probe budget instead of reading `probe.ts`, and can tell that a bridge that answers slower than `10000` ms is expected to report unhealthy rather than actually being down. No behavior changes.

## Evidence

**Schema** — `extensions/imessage/src/config-schema.ts:95` declares the field, and `:75` puts it inside `IMessageAccountSchemaBase`, which `:120` extends for the channel root and `:124` reuses for each `accounts.<id>` entry:

```typescript
probeTimeoutMs: z.number().int().positive().optional(),
```

**Runtime type** — positive integer, milliseconds; no enum leaf to track.

**Default** — `extensions/imessage/src/constants.ts:1` is the value each documented call site falls back to:

```typescript
export const DEFAULT_IMESSAGE_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000;
```

The documented checks all resolve through that constant: `extensions/imessage/src/probe.ts:259` (`timeoutMs ?? cfg?.channels?.imessage?.probeTimeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_IMESSAGE_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS`), `extensions/imessage/src/monitor/monitor-provider.ts:260`, and `extensions/imessage/src/actions.ts:310`. ## What Problem This Solves

The configuration reference table in `docs/channels/tlon.md` lists the keys a Tlon section accepts — `enabled`, `ship`, `url`, `code` and the rest — but omits `configWrites`, the gate that decides whether the channel may apply `/config set` and `/config unset` requests arriving from chat. - Problem: `channels.tlon.configWrites` is missing from the Tlon configuration reference.
- Solution: document the key, its enabled-by-default behavior, the commands it gates, and the per-account inheritance.
- What changed: `docs/channels/tlon.md` (1 line).

## Why This Change Was Made

The key is live configuration: `tlonCommonConfigFields` declares it and both `TlonAccountSchema` and `TlonConfigSchema` spread that same shape, so `channels.tlon.configWrites` and `channels.tlon.accounts.<ship>.configWrites` are accepted, and the shared config-write policy consults the key for every channel-originated write. ```

prs.title: fix(macos): Gateway status stays "Using existing gateway" after the Gateway exits
prs.body:
Closes #190148

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after the Gateway the Mac app attached to exits, the app keeps showing "Using existing gateway" (or "Running") and never starts a Gateway. Transport recovery skips the start path while the status still names a Gateway.

## User Impact

User impact: when a Terminal-run or launchd Gateway exits, the next connection recovery notices the empty port. The app then starts its own Gateway, or reports the real failure, instead of keeping the stale status.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both recovery drivers (the control channel and the Gateway connection) call `setActive(true, source: .recovery)`. That reaches `startIfNeeded`, which returns for `.running` and `.attachedExisting` without checking anything.

Recovery now re-checks the port first whenever the status names a Gateway the app does not host as its own child:
- If something is still listening, nothing changes.
- If the port is empty, the stale status is cleared and the normal start path runs. The existing ownership rules still decide what happens; for example, an externally managed installation is still refused rather than taken over.

The check runs as the start task, so concurrent recoveries and `waitForStartupAttempt` callers see one decision. App-hosted children are unaffected; their supervisor's events still own their status.

Related: an inconclusive `lsof` currently reads as an empty port (#190152). This path inherits that until #190152 is fixed.

## Evidence

New test `transport recovery restarts only after the attached Gateway leaves its port` in `GatewayProcessManagerTests`, with two cases:
- **Port empty:** the status must leave `.attachedExisting` and a new start must begin.
- **Listener still present:** the status must stay the same and nothing restarts.

I ran it locally with `swift test --skip-build`, with a private `HOME`, `TMPDIR`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`:

| Code | Suites | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `main` (63e1079af) | `GatewayProcessManagerTests` (91 tests) | The port-empty case fails both checks: the status stays `.attachedExisting`, and no new start begins. |
| This PR | `GatewayProcessManagerTests`, `ControlChannelHeartbeatTests`, `GatewayConnectionControlTests` (139 tests) | Both new cases pass. |

Also:
- `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests` succeeds.
- `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos`, `scripts/format-swift.sh macos` and `git diff --check` are clean.

Pre-existing failure: `restart waits for an in-progress disable` fails at its `uninstall` expectation on this machine, both on `main` and with this PR, in all 3 runs on its own. It is unrelated to this change.

**Real-behavior proof (shipped macOS app + real Gateway):**

Setup:
- A Gateway built from this checkout ran with `openclaw gateway run --port 18789`.
- The debug app ran with `--background-only --attach-only`. Both used the default profile inside a throwaway `HOME`/`CFFIXED_USER_HOME` with its own Keychain.
- The app attached and reported `primary.connection.state = connected` to `ws://127.0.0.1:18789`.
- I then sent the Gateway SIGINT (Ctrl-C) and captured the app's `ai.openclaw` log for 60 s.
- `--attach-only` keeps the app from installing a launchd service, so the restarted start path stops at `gateway launchd enable skipped (disable marker set)`. That line shows the stale status was dropped and startup was decided again.

| App build | Control recoveries | Failed reconnects | Start-path (`gateway.process`) lines |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `main` (63e1079af) | 1 | 12 | **0**: the status stays "Using existing gateway" |
| This PR | 1 | 19 | **1**, 2.1 s after shutdown |

<details><summary>App log with this PR (de-duplicated)</summary>

```
14:14:35.488 [control] control channel state -> degraded: gateway shutdown
14:14:35.490 [control] control channel recovery starting mode=local reason=gateway shutdown
14:14:35.993 [control] control channel state -> degraded: connect failed: connect to gateway @ ws://127.0.0.1:18789: Could not connect to the server.
14:14:37.528 [control] control channel recovery failed connect failed: connect to gateway @ ws://127.0.0.1:18789: Could not connect to the server.
14:14:37.636 [gateway.process] gateway launchd enable skipped (disable marker set)
14:14:38.045 [control] control channel state -> degraded: Cannot reach gateway at localhost:18789; check that the gateway is running.
```
</details>

<details><summary>App log on main (same window, de-duplicated)</summary>

```
14:09:30.093 [control] control channel state -> degraded: gateway shutdown
14:09:30.094 [control] control channel recovery starting mode=local reason=gateway shutdown
14:09:30.622 [gateway] gateway ws connect failed connect to gateway @ ws://127.0.0.1:18789: Could not connect to the server.
14:09:33.675 [control] control channel recovery failed connect failed: connect to gateway @ ws://127.0.0.1:18789: Could not connect to the server.
14:09:34.180 [control] control channel state -> degraded: Cannot reach gateway at localhost:18789; check that the gateway is running.
(no gateway.process lines for the rest of the 60 s; reconnects keep failing)
```
</details>

A named profile was not usable for this run: profiles only attach to their own launchd-managed Gateway (`profileAllowsExistingGatewayAttachment`).

prs.title: fix(apple): Gateway stays disconnected after a network drop during the device-token retry
prs.body:
Closes #190150

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Apple apps stop reconnecting ("Gateway token is out of date") when the network drops during the one device-token retry the Gateway grants after rejecting a rotated shared token.

## User Impact

User impact: after a Wi-Fi handoff or timeout during that retry, the app reconnects on its own with its still-valid paired device token, without a restart or re-pairing.

## Why This Change Was Made

The channel marked the granted retry as used while it built the connect request. A transport failure before the Gateway answered therefore left the retry spent, and later attempts sent only the stale shared token until reconnect paused.

The retry now stays pending until the Gateway answers the connect request:
- A scope-suppressed retry is still dropped up front.
- A Gateway rejection of the device token still pauses reconnect, as before.
- The 250 ms fast retry now applies only to the rejection that grants the retry. An outage during a pending retry keeps the normal exponential backoff instead of retrying four times a second.

This touches the same catch block as #191424, which clears a rejected device token that was the only credential. The two changes are independent.

## Evidence

New regression test `transport loss during the device-token retry keeps the stored device token for recovery` in `GatewayChannelDeviceTokenRetryTests`. It runs twice: once where the connect send fails, and once where the socket is lost before the connect response.
- A fake Gateway rejects the rotated shared token with `canRetryWithDeviceToken`, drops the first device-token retry, and accepts only the stored device token.
- The test asserts that the same channel then connects with the device token, and that the backoff after the drop is above the 250 ms fast path.

I ran `GatewayChannelDeviceTokenRetryTests|GatewayChannelConnectTests` (20 tests) three times with `swift test --skip-build`, with a private `HOME`, `TMPDIR`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`:

| Code | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `main` (63e1079af) | Fails 4 checks, the same 2 in both cases: `connected`, and the recovery connect carries `deviceToken`. |
| Channel change only, old backoff | Recovers, but fails the backoff check in both cases: the drop got the 250 ms fast retry. |
| This PR | 20/20 pass. |

Also:
- `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests` succeeds.
- `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos`, `scripts/format-swift.sh macos`, SwiftLint and SwiftFormat on the three changed files, and `git diff --check` are all clean.

**Real-behavior proof (shipped macOS app + real Gateway):**

Setup:
- A Gateway built from this checkout ran with shared token T1, in its own state directory.
- The debug macOS app ran in remote/direct mode against `ws://127.0.0.1:18791`, holding its own copy of T1. It used a throwaway `HOME`/`CFFIXED_USER_HOME` with its own Keychain.
- Port 18791 is a small loopback proxy in front of the Gateway (loopback stays a trusted retry endpoint).
- The Gateway auto-approved the app's device pairing, so the app held valid device tokens.

Steps:
1. Rotate the Gateway's shared token to T2 and restart it. The app still holds T1.
2. The proxy drops the first connect request that carries `deviceToken` (only within 0.8 s of the first drop), before the Gateway sees it. This simulates a network drop during the granted retry.
3. Capture the app's `ai.openclaw` log and `openclaw-mac status` for about 80 s.

| App build | After the dropped device-token retry | Primary connection about 80 s later |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `main` (63e1079af) | Later attempts send only the stale shared token; `gateway reconnect paused for non-recoverable auth failure … gateway token mismatch` | `connecting` (stuck on "Gateway token mismatch") |
| This PR | The next attempt, about 4 s later (normal backoff), carries the device token again; `control channel state -> connected` | `connected` |

<details><summary>This PR: proxy and app log</summary>

```
proxy 14:22:19.793 connect auth=shared-token -> forwarded            (rejected: token mismatch, canRetryWithDeviceToken)
```

prs.title: fix(macos): key Agent Events rows by globally unique id
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves The macOS Agent Events window (`Debug → Open Agent Events…`) keys its rows by `ControlAgentEvent.seq`, but `seq` is a per-run counter the Gateway restarts at 1 for every run (`src/infra/agent-events.ts`). The window buffers up to 400 events spanning many runs, so ids 1, 2, 3… repeat. SwiftUI treats duplicate identifiers as the same element, so rows from different runs are reused and earlier runs lose theirs. The type already exposes a globally unique `id` (`"\(runId)-\(seq)"`). Fixes #187608. ## Why This Change Was Made `apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/AgentEventsWindow.swift:21` passes `id: \.id` instead of `id: \.seq` to `ForEach`. That is the only production change, and it is what the issue's Expected section names. The store, the event type, and the Gateway's sequence allocation stay untouched: per-run `seq` is correct for ordering events inside one run. The regression test renders the shipped window instead of asserting model properties. `AgentEventsWindowRowIdentityTests.keeps one row per run when sequence numbers overlap` hosts `AgentEventsWindow` in an `NSHostingView`, seeds `AgentEventStore.shared` with `run-a` (`seq=1`), lets that row render, then starts `run-b` at `seq=1` while the window is open and reads the rows back from the AppKit accessibility tree. It requires one row per run, so it fails on `id: \.seq` and passes on `id: \.id`, without asserting SwiftUI type names or other implementation details. ## User Impact Opening the debug Agent Events window after more than one agent run shows a stable, correctly attributed list: every row keeps its own identity instead of sharing one with an unrelated run. The window is debug-only, so no default user flow changes, and there is no config, storage, or protocol change. ## Evidence **Shipped app, end to end.** `scripts/package-mac-app.sh` built `dist/OpenClaw.app` from this branch on `macos-latest` (ad-hoc, debug), the app attached to a local Gateway running the `stub` model (`--attach-only`), `openclaw.debugPaneEnabled` was on, and the status menu was driven through the accessibility API: `Debug → Open Agent Events…`. Two agent turns then ran through the CLI while that window stayed open (`events-a`, then `events-b`, each restarting `seq` at 1). Reading the window's accessibility tree back after both turns: | build | runs the shipped window lists | rows | | --- | --- | --- | | `main`, `id: \.seq` | 1 — `b867f318-ae6f-4cb6-bb7a-21d21bc0252f`; the earlier run is gone | 7 | | this PR, `id: \.id` | 2 — `eceeb8df-752d-4cdd-97a5-bfab967d1956` (newer) and `4031cd64-7664-4589-816d-fd94c145b61c` (earlier) | 5 + 7 | Runs ([workflow](https://github.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-macos-proof/blob/main/.github/workflows/shipped-app-v17.yml)): [head](https://github.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-macos-proof/actions/runs/41233068505), [base](https://github.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-macos-proof/actions/runs/41233075151). Each run asserts its own expectation from the live window: head requires exactly two distinct run ids in the tree and fails unless the captured screenshots between them also show both runs; base requires exactly one, so it only goes green while the bug is present. The entry point, in the shipped status menu: ![shipped status menu: Debug → Open Agent Events…](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-macos-proof/main/media/188827/shipped-app-status-menu.png) this PR — the window as it opens, listing the newer run: ![this PR: newest run in the shipped window](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-macos-proof/main/media/188827/shipped-app-head-newest-run.png) this PR — the same window after scrolling the list to the bottom: the earlier run's rows are still there, each under its own run id: ![this PR: earlier run still listed after scrolling](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-macos-proof/main/media/188827/shipped-app-head-earlier-run-after-scroll.png) `main` — same two turns, same window: one run only, and scrolling past it lands on empty space because the earlier run was never rendered: ![main: a single run in the shipped window](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-macos-proof/main/media/188827/shipped-app-base-single-run.png)
Accessibility text read back from the live window (full dumps: base, head) `main`, `id: \.seq` — 7 rows, one run: ``` WINDOW=Agent Events AXStaticText :: Agent Events AXStaticText :: run b867f318-ae6f-4cb6-bb7a-21d21bc0252f AXStaticText :: run b867f318-ae6f-4cb6-bb7a-21d21bc0252f … ``` this PR, `id: \.id` — 12 rows across two runs: ``` WINDOW=Agent Events AXStaticText :: Agent Events AXStaticText :: run eceeb8df-752d-4cdd-97a5-bfab967d1956 … AXStaticText :: run 4031cd64-7664-4589-816d-fd94c145b61c … ```
**Real rendering on macOS (in-process harness).** The `agent-rows-proof.yml` workflow on `macos-latest` builds the package, boots the shipped `AgentEventsWindow` in a real `NSHostingView` with the real `AgentEventStore`, reads the AppKit accessibility tree, and records the window bitmap. Two runs append one event each (`seq=1` for both), then four each: | build | rows the window renders (AX text) | SwiftUI runtime diagnostics | | --- | --- | --- | | `main`, `id: \.seq` | `run-a=0 run-b=1`, then `run-a=0 run-b=4` — every run-a row is gone | `ForEach<…, Int, EventRow>: the ID N occurs multiple times within the collection, this will give undefined results!` | | this PR, `id: \.id` | `run-a=1 run-b=1`, then `run-a=4 run-b=4` | none | Runs: [head](https://github.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-macos-proof/actions/runs/41160831946), [base](https://github.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-macos-proof/actions/runs/41160838178). Bitmaps with one event per run: `main` — the run-b event replaced the run-a row, so the window still renders a single row: ![before: seq-keyed rows, one row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-macos-proof/main/media/188827/agent-events-before-seq-key.png) this PR — both rows stay, each attributed to its own run: ![after: id-keyed rows, two rows](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-macos-proof/main/media/188827/agent-events-after-unique-id.png) **Committed regression.** The same rendered-row check is committed as `AgentEventsWindowRowIdentityTests.keeps one row per run when sequence numbers overlap` in `AgentEventStoreTests.swift`, so reverting the key makes `swift test --filter AgentEventsWindowRowIdentityTests` fail in `OpenClawIPCTests`. The macOS Swift shard runs on main pushes rather than ordinary PRs, so the committed test was executed through the same package workflow on `macos-latest` in both modes: [base](https://github.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-macos-proof/actions/runs/41197202500) with `id: \.seq` fails (`rows → ["run-b"]`, 5.5s), [head](https://github.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-macos-proof/actions/runs/41197195509) with `id: \.id` passes (0.4s), one row per run each time. Upstream encodes the per-run reset in its own tests: `src/infra/agent-events.test.ts:144` expects `[1, 2, 1, 1]` across a reset. Reproduced on latest `main` at `6d015738872`: `AgentEventsWindow.swift:21` still reads `id: \.seq`, and `ControlAgentEvent.id` is still `"\(runId)-\(seq)"` (`ControlChannel.swift:18-21`).

prs.title: fix(ios): refuse an invalid custom header name before it looks saved
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On iOS, Gateway Settings, Custom Headers, a name such as `X Client ID` can be added with no warning. The new row appears and the fields clear. After leaving the screen and opening it again, the row is gone. A name such as `X-Client-ID` stays.

Storage already drops a name that is not one HTTP token. The editor treated that drop as a successful add.

## Evidence

The Custom Headers editor uses `GatewayCustomHeaders.isValidName`. Add Header stays disabled for a bad name, the footer explains the token rule, and the draft stays on screen. A valid name is stored by the Add Header button and is still listed after leaving the screen and opening it again.

The shots below are from that walk on the iPhone 17 simulator (iOS 27.2), head `a032553fd3c1bccca9df8981b59308ecd4ff2604`. The test opens Gateway settings, types `headers.example.com` into Host, opens Custom Headers, types `X Client ID` and a value, then replaces the name with `X-Client-ID` and taps Add Header.

Invalid name, draft kept, Add Header disabled:

![Invalid header name stays in the field with the token explanation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SebTardif/openclaw/proof/193595-header-shots/proof/invalid-name-kept.png)

Valid name after leaving the editor and opening it again:

![Saved X-Client-ID is still listed after the editor is opened again](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/SebTardif/openclaw/proof/193595-header-shots/proof/valid-name-reopened.png)

```console
$ xcodebuild test -project apps/ios/OpenClaw.xcodeproj -scheme OpenClawUITests \
    -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,id=9CFD7CAB-3B71-45D1-90F9-EF3B770C0ABE' \
    -only-testing:OpenClawUITests/OpenClawSnapshotUITests/testCustomHeaderInvalidNameStaysAndValidNameSurvivesReopen
Test Case '-[OpenClawUITests.OpenClawSnapshotUITests testCustomHeaderInvalidNameStaysAndValidNameSurvivesReopen]' passed (53.147 seconds).
** TEST SUCCEEDED **
```

The same interaction and assertion sequence was run again on the base and on this head. That run used an iPhone 17 simulator, iOS 27.0, Xcode 27.2, Light mode, and a separate XCTest runner bound to the laboratory Debug bundle.

Base `1bf13d4df5c1` fails `XCTAssertFalse(add.isEnabled)` after `X Client ID` is entered. Add Header stays enabled. The run took 40.064 seconds.

Before, the invalid name still enables Add Header:

![Before: invalid name still enables Add Header](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0ab4b498-4222-4b85-816b-e96f006489c9)

Head `a032553fd3c1bccca9df8981b59308ecd4ff2604` passes. The invalid name stays in the draft, Add Header is disabled with the explanation, and `X-Client-ID` is still listed after leaving the editor and opening it again. The run took 52.153 seconds.

After, the invalid name is rejected and kept:

![After: invalid name is rejected and retained](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/746c7131-d694-44a9-b863-74018bebef00)

Valid header after leaving and reopening:

![Valid header after leaving and reopening](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/09c03a8a-f399-42d9-a44e-580ccb1fa2d4)

The four existing `GatewayCustomHeadersTests` passed in a dependency-free Swift package, using the unchanged test file and the shared production file. Both app builds passed. The synthetic header was removed through the UI, and it was absent after the editor was opened again.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** An invalid custom header name is refused in the editor instead of appearing as a saved row that disappears on the next visit. A valid name remains after the editor is opened again.
- **Real environment tested:** iPhone 17 simulator, iOS 27.2, Xcode 27, macOS, worktree `/tmp/oc-193490` at `a032553fd3c1bccca9df8981b59308ecd4ff2604`. The base comparison used an iPhone 17 simulator, iOS 27.0, Xcode 27.2, Light mode, base `1bf13d4df5c1`, and the same head.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `xcodebuild test -project apps/ios/OpenClaw.xcodeproj -scheme OpenClawUITests -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,id=9CFD7CAB-3B71-45D1-90F9-EF3B770C0ABE' -only-testing:OpenClawUITests/OpenClawSnapshotUITests/testCustomHeaderInvalidNameStaysAndValidNameSurvivesReopen`. The base comparison used that same native sequence on base `1bf13d4df5c1` and on this head.
- **Evidence after fix:** The invalid shot shows `X Client ID` still in the name field and the footer "Header names cannot include spaces or other characters outside a single HTTP token." There is no saved Headers section. The second shot, after Add Header and reopening the screen, shows `X-Client-ID` under Headers and an empty draft. The base shot shows Add Header still enabled for `X Client ID`. The later head shots show that name kept with Add Header disabled, then `X-Client-ID` still listed after reopen.
- **Observed result after fix:** Typing the invalid name left Add Header disabled and kept the draft. Tapping Add Header for `X-Client-ID` stored that header, and it was still listed after leaving the editor and opening it again. On the base build, the same invalid name left Add Header enabled.
- **What was not tested:** A physical iPhone, and the next gateway connection sending the stored header. The value is a secure field, so the shots do not show it.

## Summary

Closes #193490

## Why This Change Was Made

## Evidence

This includes the URL-provider cases that remain platform-specific failures on macOS.

Only TestBundlePath changed to an identical copy inside the task-owned simulator fixture app; every bundle file SHA-256 matches, and source, test assertions, SDK runner variables and selection are unchanged. No global permissions or configuration changes. This is native simulator test execution, not a workaround to product assertions.
- Production extension UI: one passing test on a dedicated iPhone 17 / iOS 27.0 simulator with only the task app and synthetic share fixture. Asserted the exact imported Python, local editing, then Cancel. Built/installed extension arm64 UUID matches `5F5627B4-5EFA-3837-BCBC-D38B5AEACD54`. No content sent externally.
- Screenshot artifacts inspected: `before-draft` (illustrative older preflight build with identical base composer source) and `after-draft` (final production build). Exact base regression is Foundation/source proof; the screenshots are not claimed as exact iOS binary A/B. The sanitized images are embedded below.

Focused macOS test run: 1.45s wall / 0.001s test time; CI duration unavailable. Added regression cases cover meaningful text corruption with actual providers; production line count is unchanged. No dependencies or migration required.

Validated source: `e0114329e8fa75b0bfff0761816a4df44a26975b`; base `10951e196f81bf113bb73b562fa76948e3852509`. Independent parent-agent source review accepted the newline-preserving fix and regression controls before local commit.

prs.title: fix(android): hide misleading empty message below sidebar sessions
prs.body:
Closes #185678

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Android sidebar says “No sessions” beneath populated chat sessions when the separate session catalog is empty.

## User Impact

Pinned and recent sessions no longer appear alongside a contradictory empty-state message. Loading indicators, errors, and empty messages inside named sections are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Remove the redundant, unlabelled catalog-empty message. Extend the existing rendered-sidebar test instead of adding another fixture. Production change: three deleted lines; test change: one assertion.

## Evidence

- **Installed-app proof:** Built and installed the base APK (`5b144096c76`) and fixed APK (`406bee2bdf8`) on an isolated Android API 36 ARM64 emulator. Paired the app through manual setup with a real, isolated Gateway. With Pinned expanded and Recent collapsed, the base shows “Pinned sidebar proof” followed by “No sessions”; updating to the fixed APK preserves the session and removes the contradictory message. Both screenshots show the connected Gateway as Ready. Only the loopback endpoint label is redacted.
- **CLI/Gateway proof:** Real `health`, `sessions.create`, `sessions.patch`, `sessions.list`, `sessions.catalog.list`, and `node.list` calls passed. prs.title: fix: Android chat inputs do not capitalize sentence starts
prs.body:
Closes #194320

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the native Android app's chat composer ignores Gboard's sentence auto-capitalization, so messages start lowercase even when the user has auto-capitalization enabled — unlike Signal/Telegram/WhatsApp and unlike the web Control UI.

## User Impact

Android users get automatic sentence-start capitalization in the chat composer and in the question free-text answer field, matching every mainstream messaging app. No behavior change for other fields.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both prose inputs set no `keyboardOptions` (or `KeyboardOptions.Default`), and Compose's default is `capitalization = KeyboardCapitalization.Unspecified` — the IME receives no `textCapSentences` hint, so Gboard never capitalizes. This adds `KeyboardOptions(capitalization = KeyboardCapitalization.Sentences)` to the two chat prose inputs. Intentionally untouched: the emoji custom-reaction field (capitalization would be noise), secret/URI question fields (already set deliberately), and the model-picker search box (not prose). Attribute-only change, no logic touched.

## Evidence

- Before recording + frame from the issue: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/194320#issuecomment (Gboard auto-capitalization ON; typing `why don't you auto capitalize?!` stays all-lowercase in the shipped 2026.10.90 app).
- Root cause verified against androidx source: `KeyboardOptions` default `capitalization = KeyboardCapitalization.Unspecified` (compose/foundation `KeyboardOptions.kt`).
- Gap noted: no after-recording yet — building a debug APK requires the Android SDK, which isn't available in this agent environment. Happy to have the reporter sideload a CI-built debug APK and record the after-state, or a maintainer with a local build can verify in seconds.

prs.title: chore: investigate Windows node exec pending in Code Mode (#176315)
prs.body:
Related: #176315

> **Investigation placeholder — intentionally draft, not ready for review or merge.** No implementation patch exists yet. The root cause and current-main reproduction remain unproven; no native Windows before/after result or passing regression is claimed.

## What Problem This Solves

A Windows-node command submitted through Code Mode can remain pending without returning native output, an exit status, or an actionable failure, even when discovery and native Codex session listing succeed.

## User Impact

The intended outcome is for remote Windows commands to return their actual output and exit status, or a truthful denial, timeout, cancellation, or unknown-outcome result. There is no delivered behavior change yet. Authorization and unknown-outcome safeguards must remain intact; uncertain requests must not be replayed automatically.

## Why This Change Was Made

Issue #176315 reports this failure with a Linux Gateway and native Windows node running OpenClaw 2026.10.4. The failing owner has not been identified, so this draft deliberately does not propose a speculative repair.

The next step is one bounded, harmless absolute-path `codex.exe --version` probe in an isolated paired environment, using normal supported approvals. Correlate the Code Mode bridge request with exec entry, preparation, approval disposition, node invocation, native process completion, terminal-result acceptance, and Code Mode continuation. Only then select the smallest fix at the responsible boundary.

## Evidence

**Completed investigation — source analysis, not native execution:**

- Read the report and complete comments, traced the execution and result-return owners, and compared release `383c124cc32f` with inspected main `76985e4c31c4`.
- The release sets `bridgeDispatchStarted` before `runBridgeRequest`; it does not establish that exec or a Windows process started. [Release source](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/383c124cc32ffee3f8e56f549b88da94d269a4af/src/agents/code-mode-state.ts#L570-L573).
- Last confirmed incident boundary: an outstanding Code Mode `bridge:callValue`. First unconfirmed boundary: entry into the nested exec implementation and node-target resolution. Later execution and return stages remain unconfirmed for that request.
- Compared #168523 (headless approval delivery), #104798 (bare-name allowlist precheck), PR #166140 (open at the October 29 inspection) (Windows shell-wrapper policy), and merged PRs #175949 and #128440 (Code Mode lifecycle repairs). Similar symptoms do not establish a shared cause or prove that this report is fixed.

**Required before this can become an implementation PR:**

- [ ] Verify actual Gateway/node builds, Node versions, transport, capabilities, and effective approval policy in the isolated test environment.
- [ ] Capture the bounded native Windows failure and its first stalled boundary; reconcile the request before any control or retry.
- [ ] Compare the equivalent supported direct node-exec path with Code Mode, keeping policy and command equivalent.
- [ ] Add a regression that fails on the base and passes with the owner-correct repair.
- [ ] Capture native Windows before/after stdout and exit delivery; verify relevant denial, error, cancellation, and disconnect cases.
- [ ] Complete targeted tests, typecheck, lint/format, and independent review; replace this draft's pending statements with exact results.

Native Windows access and an isolated paired Gateway were unavailable in the investigating session. No implementation tests were run, and no production service, approval policy, or unrelated session was changed.

Reported by @ceo633 in [#176315](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/176315).

- Implementation and verification: pending; no implementation session or patch exists yet.

prs.title: feat(plugin-sdk): publish access-policy revisions for retained rechecks
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Repeated operator-authority revalidation enters the access-policy plugin runtime even when its decision inputs have not changed.

## User Impact

Plugins may opt into revision-published caching for explicitly classified non-effect rechecks. Existing plugins and every unclassified `assertCurrent()` caller retain live checks. Credential use, tools/commands, external effects, and publications continue through the live/default path.

**Security tradeoff and review request:** this trusts an opting-in plugin to publish every dependency change and declare a truthful validity bound. Assertions with untracked mutable invocation inputs must not opt in. Request independent review from **@openclaw/openclaw-secops** before merge. This PR is for maintainer review; do not merge without that review.

## Why This Change Was Made

The plugin publishes revisions through an optional SDK subscription; reading a revision does not enter plugin runtime scope. The operator-access-policy owner holds one allow slot per captured authority. Cache hits require the same plugin publication, registry, ambient request scope, and an unexpired deadline; profile/config changes also replace the retained-grant slot. Unknown revision, callback errors, retirement, and expiry force a live check. Weak request-scope references avoid retaining completed request graphs. No denial is cached.

`assertCurrentForEffect()` and parameterless `assertCurrent()` stay live. Rechecks require explicit propagation; copying an authority and replacing its live guard cannot silently inherit the old cached path. The visitor plugin publishes grant changes and supplies the grant's actual expiry, so delayed timer execution cannot extend access.

| Site | Classification | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Admitted operator `readCurrentRoleFacts` | Recheck, only with explicit owner opt-in | Reads retained role facts; performs no effect |
| Gateway/channel/recovery `retain` | Recheck | Acquires lifetime custody; later effects revalidate live |
| Channel/recovery source-change notifications | Recheck | Revalidates retained work without performing effects |
| Recovered role reads | Recheck | Preserves the exact live recovery claim and identity/config guards |
| Default assertions, effect entry, recovery `assertPolicyCurrent` | Live | Preserves execution/publication and unclassified callers |
| HTTP/WS access checks and tool/command callers | Live | Existing parameterless path is unchanged |

Follow-ups after #182066: classification in `lane-controller.ts`, `run-attempt-dispatch.ts`, harness `host-capability.ts`, `host-trajectory.ts`, `tool-authority.runtime.ts`, and `tools/gateway-caller-context.ts`. Those callers remain live in this PR; none of their files is modified.

Production LOC delta is **+318** (+453 / -135, excluding tests, test support, and docs). It grows because the approved contract requires plugin publication and validity, generation/error fencing, bounded cache storage, and a purpose split while preserving live effect checks. There is no new config option, schema, durable state, TTL heuristic, or Gateway-generated policy revision.

## Evidence

- Baseline recovered-owner work-count regression: 183 plugin assertions for 60 role reads and three live effects; failed the expected count of three. Candidate: three after warming the allow (-180, -98.36%). This is an owner fixture, not a measured whole cron scheduler/model turn.
- Initial complete focused run: 126 tests passed across seven files, including revision/expiry/error/retirement, principal and ambient-scope isolation, copied claim guards, recovery, managed plugin registration, and visitor lifecycle.
- Core typecheck and the export-collision guard passed. Both required import-closure files passed (22 tests); the final affected recovery/visitor rerun passed (39 + 11 tests). Changed-file core and extension lint passed.
- Independent subagent review (autoreview route unavailable): no actionable P0/P1/P2 findings after resolving ambient-scope contract ambiguity, including a final review of publication and fixture lifecycle cleanup. The configured helper rejected its provider route before inference; configuration was not changed.
- Owner allocation campaign: predeclared five paired samples per scenario, fixed work, synchronized warm starts, swapped interleaved CPUs, shared guard. Results pending quiet-slot admission. No GC/promotion/latency claim from the sampled allocation pass.

Production signal after deployment: fewer access-policy plugin assertions and plugin-scope allocation during retained role reads, with unchanged live effect counts and immediate revocation/expiry enforcement. Whole-Gateway latency, promotion, and the remaining unclassified assertion family are not established by this owner proof.

<details>
<summary>Focused validation files</summary>

- `src/plugins/gateway-access-policy-registration.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/operator-access-policy.github-login.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/operator-run-authority.worker.test.ts`
- `src/gateway/operator-run-recovery.test.ts`
- `src/agents/admitted-run-context.test.ts`
- `extensions/visitor-access/index.test.ts`
- `extensions/visitor-access/src/visitors.authority.test.ts`
- `test/scripts/eager-import-closure.test.ts`
- `test/scripts/pr-wrapper-source-closure.test.ts`

Commands: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <focused files> --maxWorkers=1`, changed-file `oxfmt`/`scripts/run-oxlint.mjs`, `pnpm tsgo:core`, and `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-export-name-collisions.mts`.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Reproducible owner probe adapter (applied identically to baseline and candidate)</summary>

The existing `scripts/perf/operator-authority-measure.ts` stays unchanged in this PR. This task-local adapter supplies an opting-in synthetic policy and 20 role reads before each live effect. Run its generated script with the existing harness flags (`--scenario recovery-source --iterations 2000 --warmup 200`), adding `--recheck-turn` for retained-work samples; omit that flag for the live-effect control. Use separate synthetic state, the shared quiet-slot lock and guard, synchronized `--start-at`, and swapped interleaved CPUs.

```python
from pathlib import Path
p = Path('scripts/perf/operator-authority-measure.ts')
s = p.read_text()
s = s.replace('    iterations: { type: "string", default: "20000" },', '    "recheck-turn": { type: "boolean", default: false },\n    iterations: { type: "string", default: "20000" },')
s = s.replace('  signal: controller.signal,\n  assertCurrent()', '  signal: controller.signal,\n  recheckValidUntil: Infinity,\n  assertCurrent()')
s = s.replace('registerGatewayAccessPolicy({\n  authorize', 'registerGatewayAccessPolicy({\n  subscribeRevision(publish) { publish("synthetic-policy-1"); return () => {}; },\n  authorize')
s = s.replace('      counts.recoverySource++;\n      authority.assertCurrent();', '''      counts.recoverySource++;
      if (values["recheck-turn"]) {
        for (let read = 0; read < 20; read++) {
          assert(authority.readCurrentRoleFacts);
          authority.readCurrentRoleFacts();
        }
      }
      authority.assertCurrent();''')
s = s.replace('    includeCollected: true,', '    includeCollected: true,\n    roleReadsPerWork: values["recheck-turn"] ? 20 : 0,\n    effectsPerWork: 1,')
assert 'roleReadsPerWork' in s and 'subscribeRevision(publish)' in s
Path('scripts/perf/buf7-authority-adapter.ts').write_text(s)
```

</details>

## CI attribution

The first-head changed-plan PDF-tool failure is inherited from the newest scheduled main run (created 2026-10-24 07:31:48Z), head `068022e6e8df38c35d39cc5dadff40e8f58eac2d`: [main job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40074498223/job/120815064175), [PR job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40075489577/job/120818124451). Both fail `src/agents/tools/pdf-tool.test.ts:397:35`, “reports omitted images for a text-only model and supplies Codex instructions,” with byte-identical assertion annotations after removing terminal color codes. No CI rerun was requested.

The first-head requester E2E failure was a stale assertion after main's [#182285](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182285), commit `5d47168b9170d92c45aeb82cd7680719f211b89a`: preparation capacity is released on Gateway acceptance, not model settlement. The scheduled main inventory does not include this E2E, so no matching scheduled-main claim is made for it. The test-only correction now proves three accepted restored model turns remain open, an ordinary probe progresses, and no duplicate restored wake appears. The existing registry preparation-bound test retains the separate two-slot admission invariant. No product behavior changes for this repair. A local focused replay was stopped when its wrapper attempted a broad runtime build. Changed-file format/lint and independent review passed; CI provides the E2E execution proof.

Current review head: `1bee4229b915d54887926748f44fb081bc8849ec`. The second commit only updates the stale requester E2E to main’s documented acceptance lifetime; the policy implementation is unchanged. SecOps review remains requested.

## Final-head CI

Head `1bee4229b915d54887926748f44fb081bc8849ec`: 70 checks passed. The repaired requester E2E passed in [checks-node-changed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40077034541/job/120822761202). The only failed test shard is the [PDF-tool assertion](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40077034541/job/120822761177), whose annotation is byte-identical to the [newest scheduled main failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40074498223/job/120815064175). The aggregate CI gate is red because of that inherited failure. No rerun was requested to chase green.

Owner allocation measurements are still waiting for the shared quiet slot; no measured sample has started. This PR must remain unmerged pending the required SecOps review and the lead’s decision on the remaining measurement gap.

prs.title: feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage
prs.body:
feat(audit): record observed runtime skill usage

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can emit skill-usage diagnostics while an agent reads or invokes a skill, but that observed runtime signal is not available through the durable audit surface. Operators therefore cannot inspect which skills were actually used during a run from the audit CLI/API.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first revision inferred skill selection from prompt text after attempt completion. Review correctly called that out as the wrong boundary: prompt inference is not proof of skill use and it also risked perturbing the embedded attempt-result contract.

This revision records only observed runtime skill usage from the existing `before_tool_call` skill-usage boundary:

- Skill read/command activation is detected where `recordRunSkillUsage()` already emits runtime diagnostics.
- A metadata-only `skill_selection` audit event is emitted with `selectionSource: "observed_runtime"` and `selectionConfidence: "observed"`.
- No prompt text, tool arguments, tool output, or skill file contents are persisted.
- `skill_selection` is persisted outside run-start deduplication so it is not dropped after `agent.run.started`.
- Legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only; the versioned `audit.activity.list` surface exposes skill-selection records.
- `completeEmbeddedAttemptResult()` is restored to the production calling contract, preserving the existing truncated-stream/tool recovery behavior.

## User Impact

- `openclaw audit --kind skill_selection` can show observed skill usage for a run through the activity-list API.
- Existing `audit.list` clients keep their shipped run/tool event shape and do not receive the new record kind.
- Operators get a durable metadata trail for actual skill usage without sensitive prompt or file-content capture.

## Evidence

Current-head validation after merging `upstream/main` and removing the unrelated `USER.md` bootstrap policy change:

```bash
pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm protocol:check:swift
pnpm db:kysely:check
pnpm lint:kysely
pnpm check:architecture
pnpm test src/agents/workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts src/audit/audit-events.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.test.ts
```

Results:

- `pnpm tsgo:core` passed.
- `pnpm protocol:check:swift` passed after regenerating `GatewayModels.swift`.
- `pnpm db:kysely:check` passed after regenerating `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts`.
- `pnpm lint:kysely` passed after moving ordinary companion-table insert/read/prune queries to the sync Kysely owner.
- `pnpm check:architecture` passed, including generated Kysely verification, Kysely guardrails, and database-first legacy-store guard.
- Targeted Vitest run passed 4 shards in 22.13s.
- `audit-events.test.ts`: 54 tests passed, including companion-table storage, bounded retention, and observed runtime projection.
- `server-methods/audit.test.ts`: 34 tests passed, including explicit `skill_selection`/`observed` activity access and V1-compatible unfiltered activity.
- `audit.test.ts`: 7 protocol schema tests passed, including activity schema discrimination.
- `workspace.bootstrap-privacy.test.ts`: 9 tests passed; shared sessions now drop only root `MEMORY.md`, leaving `USER.md` behavior unchanged.
- `pnpm exec oxlint src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` passed. A full local `pnpm lint:core` was started but manually stopped after 6+ minutes with no diagnostic output; CI remains the authoritative full core-lint signal.

Published-release upgrade, older-reader, and candidate-reopen proof:

- the published `v2026.9.4` tag at `3a9d69db3` created a fresh state database and wrote legacy `agent_run` sequence `1`.
- candidate head `7d74807a5` opened that exact database, preserved the legacy row, created the additive `audit_skill_selection_events` table, and wrote observed `debug-toolkit` sequence `2`.
- `v2026.9.4` then reopened the candidate-used database without migration or schema errors, ignored the additive table, and wrote a second legacy `agent_run` at shared sequence `3`.
- the candidate reopened the same database and returned sequences `[3, 2, 1]`, including both legacy rows and the retained skill-selection row.
- physical SQLite readback reported `integrity_check: ok`, `user_version: 17`, `audit_events: 2`, and `audit_skill_selection_events: 1`.
- this proves published release → candidate upgrade → published older-reader open/use → candidate reopen while preserving the legacy table, additive companion, and shared sequence allocation.

## Changed Files

- `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.ts` — observed-only metadata marker.
- `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.wrapper.ts` — emits `skill_selection` from the existing observed skill-usage boundary.
- `src/audit/agent-event-audit.ts` — projects observed-only skill-selection records and routes them outside run-start deduplication.
- `src/audit/audit-event-store.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-store.skill-selection-storage.ts` / `src/audit/audit-event-types.ts` — durable store/types for observed skill-selection metadata, with ordinary companion-table access through Kysely.
- `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` — generated Kysely declarations for the companion table.
- `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.ts` — exposes skill-selection through `audit.activity.list` while preserving legacy `audit.list`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit-activity.ts` — versioned activity schema includes `skill_selection`.
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/audit.ts` — legacy audit schema stays run/tool-only.
- `src/commands/audit.ts` — CLI uses the activity surface and renders selected skill metadata.
- `docs/gateway/audit.md` / `docs/gateway/config-observability.md` / `docs/cli/audit.md` — document the approved metadata fields, default-on collection, 30-day retention, separate 100,000-row cap, compatibility behavior, and explicit CLI filters.

## Test Plan

1. Verify observed skill reads/commands emit `skill_selection` audit events.
2. Verify `skill_selection` persists between run start and terminal events.
3. Verify `audit.activity.list` and CLI expose skill-selection records.
4. Verify legacy `audit.list` remains run/tool-only.
5. Verify attempt-result recovery tests still pass.
6. Verify existing SQLite state opens, creates the companion table, preserves old activity rows, and reopens with skill-selection rows intact.


## Review findings addressed (2026-10-10)

All five ClawSweeper code findings are fixed on this head:

- **Distinguishable skill identities** — the lossy hyphen sanitizer is replaced by an injective dash-escape encoding (`-` doubles to `--`, other unsafe bytes become `-hh-` hex), so `Daily Brief` persists as `Daily-20-Brief`, distinct from `Daily-Brief` → `Daily--Brief` (and `_helper` stays distinct from `helper`). The audit projector accepts the encoding. Boundary coverage in `src/skills/runtime-skill-selection.test.ts`.
- **Admission-owned schema setup** — the canonical schema admission owns `audit_skill_selection_events` (`src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql`); additive DDL now runs at most once per connection and only for pre-admission databases, instead of on every insert and prune tick.
- **Bounded write overhead** — per-connection row-count cache mirrors the canonical ledger pattern: one `COUNT(*)` per connection lifetime, advanced by inserts and maintenance deletes, invalidated on rollback.
- **Restart guidance** — `docs/gateway/audit.md` now states the recorder re-reads `logging.audit.enabled` on every event, so disabling stops new rows immediately.
- **Protocol type ownership** — `AuditActivitySkillSelectionV1` is derived from the canonical schema properties via `SchemaContract` (same pattern as adjacent variants), restoring wire-required attribution to typed consumers.

## Production-path proof

Throwaway script (not committed) driving production code on a temp state DB — marker encoder → recorder projector → production SQLite writer → `audit.activity.list` Gateway handler:

```
encoded identities: Daily-20-Brief vs Daily--Brief
projected inputs: 1 kind: skill_selection
writer stored: skill_selection Daily-20-Brief
gateway response: {"events":[{"schemaVersion":1,"sequence":1,"eventId":"<uuid>","sourceSequence":1,"occurredAt":<ts>,"redaction":"metadata_only","kind":"skill_selection","agentId":"main","sessionKey":"agent:main:<session>","sessionId":"session-<id>","runId":"run-proof-1","action":"skill.selection.observed","status":"observed","eventType":"skill_selection","actor":{"type":"agent","id":"main"},"selectedSkill":"Daily-20-Brief"}]}
worker rows: 1 first toolName: Daily-20-Brief
PROOF OK: gateway output matches the observed skill invocation
```

Tool-invocation → emission coverage lives in `src/agents/agent-tools.skill-selection-audit.e2e.test.ts`; recorder → DB → filtered readback in `src/audit/audit-events.skill-selection-hidden.test.ts`; handler shaping in `src/gateway/server-methods/audit.test.ts`.


## Round 2 (rev.199 follow-up)

Three further findings from review rev.199 are fixed on this head:

- **Token-built identities** — the encoder appends complete encoding tokens only while they fit the 128-char bound (reserving the `x-` flag prefix up front), so truncation can never cut inside an escape and valid suffixes survive (`skill-a` vs `skill-b` regression covered).
- **Single-owner expiry accounting** — the deleter returns the removed count without touching the warm cache; insert-prune and maintenance ticks each adjust exactly once, with a warm-cache expiry-to-overflow regression test (exact cap trim to 99,976 rows).
- **Tool-boundary assertion** — the wrapper e2e expects the encoded `demo--skill` identity while the run-usage receipt keeps the original `demo-skill` name.
