prs.title: feat(ios): add a Talk microphone mute button
prs.body:
Related: #187722

## What Problem This Solves

iOS Talk has no microphone mute button separate from ending the conversation.

## User Impact

Adds a microphone toggle to the Talk activity strip. Works across native speech recognition, Gateway relay, and WebRTC, retaining mute across Talk restarts within the app run.

The UI follow-up uses the composer's scaled 17-point medium SF Symbol styling and retains a 44-point hit target. A crossed-out mic is gray when input is on and orange when muted. The collapsed strip is about 48 points tall at normal text size. Idle muted realtime Talk displays **Connected (Realtime)** above **Microphone muted**; thinking, speaking, connecting, and error statuses remain visible. VoiceOver continues to announce the action and microphone state. While Talk is active, the composer's dictation/voice-note microphone is hidden and returns after Talk ends. Mute stays exclusively in the Talk activity strip, not in the dictation button's position.

**Ready for review.** The requester has verified pre-mute word preservation on an iPhone. Returned kit v3 now verifies the Apple build, all 373 selected iOS tests, and all 21 selected shared-package tests for the repaired candidate matching `c22355b8f89a`. Actual normal-size UI screenshots and the requester’s lifecycle recording are now attached below. Remaining physical audio/lifecycle cases, large-text layout, and pre-change baseline comparison are not established by this recording. The confirmed conflict with `main` was resolved in `417349df1cf48b407eb3c31cd11abdfc0251b622`, integrating base `0499ce287bb8c7b41a1db0cebcd57084e62c0c21`. GitHub now reports the branch mergeable. Current-head CI is green (38 passed, 52 skipped/neutral, no failures or pending checks at the November 6 check). The requester has also posted current-head targeted simulator red/green results and base/head normal and accessibility3 strip renders, summarized below. Earlier Mac-kit results remain evidence for their explicitly identified candidate.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ports the Android feature from @davelutztx in #187722, using the existing iOS Talk manager and transport owners. No new configuration, permissions, dependencies, or protocol changes. Shared control defaults leave existing macOS callers unchanged.

Android reference checked on November 5, 2026: still open at `3d852cea86599dcabc6df2f97dababf59ed842bc`.

**Native finalization repair:** [Android feedback](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187722#issuecomment-6547128842) and the [iPhone report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192648#issuecomment-6627385033) showed that immediate recognizer cancellation discards pre-mute trailing words. Native continuous Talk now closes the audio tap/engine immediately and calls `endAudio()`, retaining that recognition generation until a usable final result or a two-second fallback. Errors, empty finals, and the deadline use the latest nonempty partial; settlement submits once and retires old callbacks. Quick unmute/re-mute cannot replace the draining recognizer. End Talk/session teardown cancels it, and gateway replacement invalidates its transcript owner. Realtime mute and accepted reply playback paths are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Layout issue also observed without the mute button — November 6

**Requester comparison result:** the requester reproduced the intermittent issue with and without the mute button in **the same chats containing very long messages**, and reports **no apparent worsening with this PR**. This is the requester's comparative device observation; it was not independently executed in this session.

This supports treating the overlap as a pre-existing long-message layout problem, **not an observed mute-button regression or exacerbation**. It remains a separate investigation, not a blocker specific to this PR on the available evidence. The earlier blanket merge hold is withdrawn. No layout repair or root cause is claimed, and other review and validation requirements are unchanged.

<details>
<summary>Original observation and related investigation</summary>

The supplied recording and four screenshots show lost reading position and newer user/assistant bubbles overlapping older assistant content. The overlap is visible even after the Talk card disappears. No message-role or persisted-transcript corruption has been established.

![Real iPhone screenshot: newer chat bubbles overlap an older assistant response](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9b46564f-ae0c-403a-a419-ea7bc374dd7c)

This inspected crop removes model metadata and unrelated surrounding UI; originals are retained unchanged. Seven transcript layout/identity/rendering files are byte-identical to base `0499ce287bb8`. That source comparison alone did not prove baseline behavior; the requester’s subsequent device comparison is the additional evidence.

[PR #192232](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192232) addresses related lazy-height instability causing blank transcripts. It remains an investigation lead, not a verified repair for this overlap. No code from it has been imported, no layout repair is claimed, and no broad device/provider test matrix is requested.

</details>

### Conflict-only integration — November 5

- Published head: `417349df1cf48b407eb3c31cd11abdfc0251b622`; verified ancestry includes main `0499ce287bb8c7b41a1db0cebcd57084e62c0c21`.
- The sole manual conflict was the demo fixture helper extraction: main independently made the same extraction with different helper names. Kept main's names and verified the complete fixture file matches that main revision byte-for-byte. The fixture and shared initializer build repairs are now already upstream, reducing the PR-relative diff to 13 files.
- Native mute manager/regressions, WebRTC mute, relay mute, and Talk-strip UI are byte-identical to the earlier Apple-tested candidate. All 13 PR-relative files plus the two upstream build-repair files were verified against the published head.
- `pnpm native:i18n:verify` passed (4,637 entries, no drift); base-relative staged whitespace check passed. Fresh full-candidate Auto Review against the integrated base: P0-only, scoped-clean, no findings. No Apple code was executed in this Linux session; these checks do not replace current-head Apple integration validation.
- [Latest completed ClawSweeper verdict](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192648#issuecomment-6626345064) covers current head `417349df1cf4`: overall Gold, patch quality Diamond, no actionable findings, ready for maintainer review, and no before-merge items listed. It notes remaining declared device-proof gaps separately; this rating is advisory. The targeted source-hunk red/green report and requester device evidence are retained below.
- Current-head CI is green as observed November 6: 38 passed, 52 skipped/neutral, no failures/pending checks. This includes iOS screenshot/evidence and Periphery build jobs; the dedicated iOS build matrix is skipped, so this is not a claim that every Apple test suite ran in CI. No merge has been submitted.

- Native repair published at `1c6c79a5005b25713a0bd02abae9990dbd4365f7`; the three repair files were verified byte-for-byte against the reviewed workspace matching the locally supplied patch.
- **Requester device report, November 4:** tested the supplied native-finalization repair locally and confirmed that words spoken before mute are no longer cut off. This is a manual result for the supplied local patch. Kit v2 subsequently exposed build blockers; kit v3 confirms the build repairs and automated regressions pass, as detailed below.
- `git diff --check` and staged whitespace check: passed.
- `pnpm native:i18n:baseline` added the source-owned UI wording entries; `pnpm native:i18n:verify` passed (4,549 entries, no inventory drift).
- Fresh Auto Review of the complete local candidate against `18516599b1d417fee621b2fd2ceda21107bc038a`: **P0-only**, scoped-clean, no findings. This does not certify Swift compilation or Apple runtime behavior.
- Separate source-only lifecycle review of the finalization changes and tests: no unresolved concrete issues after preserving the latest partial on empty finals and adding automatic-unmute-resume cases. This was an excerpt-based audit, not executed proof.
- Author simplification pass: finalization stays in the existing Talk manager, reuses its recognition and transcript-processing generations, and splits input shutdown from recognizer retirement. The added bounded pending state prevents pre-mute word loss without a second capture manager or configuration option.
- Added gateway-boundary regressions in `TalkMicrophoneMuteTests`: final results with/without an earlier partial; error/timeout/empty-final fallback; exactly-once send; quick unmute/re-mute, including no-word automatic resume; stale callbacks; End Talk/session replacement. They exercise actual `GatewayNodeSession` `chat.send` framing with synthetic recognition callbacks and a terminal-aborted acknowledgement to stop at the submission boundary. **Passed on the requester's Mac in kit v3:** all seven regression definitions, including their parameterized cases. This is fixed-candidate green execution; automated red-on-base execution was not performed.
- [Requester device results at `7e0def937e73`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192648#issuecomment-6627385033): iOS app build passed; 27 tests in three iOS suites passed; xAI Gateway relay and OpenAI WebRTC mute/unmute worked on an iPhone. Native recognition lost a word spoken before mute. These are **prior-head results**, not proof of the native finalization repair or revised UI.
- The same report found the shared OpenClawKit test target blocked by a pre-existing `ChatViewModelTests.swift` initializer mismatch, so shared relay tests did not run on that host.
- Apple compilation and automated Swift tests were run on the requester's Mac, not in this Linux session. The returned xcresult summary/tree and Swift XML/logs were independently inspected here. Actual current UI screenshots from the requester's recording are now attached below. Remaining physical lifecycle/input/playback cases still need verification; the silent recording does not establish audio behavior. Chat mockups and render-smoke tests remain separate from runtime screenshot evidence.

### Additional requester evidence on integrated head — November 5–6

All reports below name head `417349df1cf4` and base `0499ce287bb8`.

- [Simulator red/green report](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192648#issuecomment-6667982238): on Xcode 27.2, the requester reports **red** after reverting only finalization, muted-recognition, and relay-silence source hunks while retaining the tests: 7 mute tests with 21 issues, and 10 relay tests with 3 issues. **Green** on unchanged PR head: 18 tests across `TalkMicrophoneMuteTests` and `TalkGatewaySpeechClientTests`, plus 10 shared relay tests, all passing. Reported mute-suite time: 721 seconds. This is targeted regression sensitivity, **not a literal plain-base test run**. These are attributed results from the comment; raw xcresult/log bundles for this new run were not supplied to this session.
- [Base/head normal and accessibility3 strip renders](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192648#issuecomment-6669395455): publicly accessible immutable images were downloaded; normal and large-text active/muted examples and large-text connecting were inspected. They show real SwiftUI `ImageRenderer` output from a fixed 393-point test fixture at 3x, not full-app screenshots. Head adds the expected gray/orange crossed microphone and muted wording. At accessibility3 the muted text wraps mid-word (`Micropho / ne muted`); status/transcript text is also constrained. Treat the real chat's large-text layout as unverified, not accepted based on this fixture.
- [Requester's evidence mapping and remaining device checks](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192648#issuecomment-6669410988): simulator assertions cover finalization, fallback, exactly-once submission, Talk-session restart, quick toggles, and teardown. Audible playback and physical-device lifecycle/large-text verification are still pending. The earlier successful native trailing-word device report remains valid and should not be discarded.

**Restart contract clarification:** mute is retained across Talk stop/start and reconnect within the same app run. It is intentionally not persisted across quitting and relaunching the app. A full-app relaunch retaining mute is therefore **not** an acceptance requirement for this PR; the relevant retention check is restarting Talk without terminating the app.

### Requester real-device lifecycle recording — November 5

The requester supplied a 36-second iPhone recording and explicitly authorized use of the test-chat screen. These are **actual device screenshots, not mockups**. The recording does not display a build commit, so this is requester-supplied visual evidence, separate from the hash-verified kit v3 test run.

![iOS Talk lifecycle: active at 00:04, muted at 00:14, unmuted at 00:22, and ended at 00:34](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c3f306d3-3bb9-48a0-84e0-4b23fce03bbc)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/271983e6-399c-4788-b066-920970c21f33

Observed in the recording:
- **00:04:** Listening (Realtime), gray crossed-out microphone in the Talk card, and no composer dictation microphone.
- **00:14:** Connected (Realtime), orange crossed-out microphone and Microphone muted label. The Talk controls remain present and the agent reply appears in chat.
- **00:22:** Unmuted; Listening (Realtime) and the gray mute action return.
- **00:34:** Talk ended; the Talk card is gone and the composer dictation microphone is visible again.
- A stop/restart segment is also present. It is not independently counted as proof of mute retention or capture exclusion because the recording does not expose touch events or microphone input.

Publication edits only: the composer model label is covered, the final iOS Control Center transition is omitted (published clip is 34.5 seconds), and the silent audio track and file metadata are removed. Test-chat text and Talk controls are unchanged. The original recording is retained locally unchanged. Its audio track contains no audible signal; this evidence does **not** prove TTS continuity or post-mute speech exclusion. Normal-size current UI is covered; large-text layout and a pre-change baseline comparison are not established by this clip.

### Returned Mac kit v3 results — November 5

**Apple build and both selected test groups passed. No rerun is needed for the collector's summary error.**

Returned archive: `talk-mute-results-20261105T034708Z-0712fe.zip`, SHA-256 `1fb79eeebf7d716ca593c263e4939da1230e34f6cd28980ba55a78909edf715e`. This was the pinned `1c6c79a5005b25713a0bd02abae9990dbd4365f7` base plus bundled build-repair SHA-256 `f0c863e5a3c1ffa1b379908840c256d7ef54f77fb9febc1c5f41c21e813a8684`, not a bare-base run. The six manifest source hashes match the reviewed files published at `c22355b8f89a6abb0ebce72dd0eced45cecb0b93` and remained unchanged during the run.

Environment: Xcode 27.2, Apple Swift 6.4.2, macOS 27.2 arm64, isolated iPhone 17 Pro simulator on iOS 26.5. Caller-selected Node 26.12.1 and repository-pinned pnpm 12.15.0 passed preflight. The created simulator was deleted successfully.

| Check | Result | Reported wall time |
| --- | --- | --- |
| iOS `build-for-testing`, including strict lint | Passed, exit 0 | 568.084 s |
| iOS `test-without-building` | 373 tests passed; 0 failures, skips, or expected failures | 777.116 s |
| Shared `swift test` | 21 tests in 3 suites passed; 0 failures or skips | 174.464 s, including build |

iOS xcresult records 373 test definitions / 429 parameterized invocations. All eight requested suites and all seven required mute regression definitions are present and passed:

- `TalkMicrophoneMuteTests`: 7
- `TalkGatewaySpeechClientTests`: 11
- `TalkModeManagerTests`: 51
- `TalkRealtimeVoiceSessionCleanupTests`: 7
- `NodeAppModelInvokeTests`: 258
- `SwiftUIRenderSmokeTests`: 13
- `OpenClawTypographyTests`: 22
- `LocalFixtureChatTransportTests`: 4

The shared XML and console output independently confirm `RealtimeTalkRelaySessionAudioInputTests`, `ChatTalkControlTests`, and `ChatHistoryCoalescingTests` all passed. This includes relay silence while muted, queued-audio retirement, and preservation of capture/reply playback in the test harness.

**Collector-only defect:** kit v3's top-level summary says `shared: results_unverified` / `attention_required` because it looked only for `shared-results.xml`; Swift emitted `shared-results-swift-testing.xml`. That actual report is present in the returned archive with 21 passing cases and no failures/skips, and the command exited 0. The local collector now reads framework-suffixed reports as well. Its regression reproduces the false warning on shipped v3 and passes after the fix; the original returned ZIP is preserved unchanged. This correction does not alter or rerun the app tests.

The native regression fixtures took approximately 2 minutes for final-result submission and 1 minute 20 seconds each for fallback and quick-toggle groups; these are measured automated harness times, not a physical speech-finalization latency claim. The two-second native finalization deadline remains unchanged. Apple tests are green, but this run does not establish red-on-base automation, physical speech exclusion/playback across every transport, or screenshot acceptance.

#### Earlier v2 blockers — repaired and superseded by v3

Kit v2 reached both builds but executed no tests: strict lint rejected two raw-orange uses in `ChatTalkActivityViews.swift` and the unchanged 210-line demo seed function; shared compilation rejected the old route-lease initializer in `ChatHistoryCoalescingTests`.

The follow-up at `c22355b8f89a` uses existing warning/muted theme tokens, extracts two demo branches unchanged, and updates the routing-test initializer/closure signatures. No lint gate or assertion was disabled; native microphone-finalization code and tests were unchanged. Kit v3's successful build and tests above now verify these repairs on Apple tools.

### Local device test

Check out this PR, follow `apps/ios/README.md` for signing/build setup, run `pnpm ios:gen`, and build/run `apps/ios/OpenClaw.xcodeproj` on an iPhone.

- Mute/unmute while an answer plays; verify playback and accepted work continue.
- Speak while muted, then unmute; verify muted speech is not replayed.
- Native regression: say **five four**, mute, then say **three two**. Exactly one request should contain **five four**, excluding speech after mute. Also try muting before the first partial appears, quick unmute/re-mute, and End Talk during finalization.
- Restart Talk while muted, then test standalone push-to-talk after ending Talk.
- Verify the composer mic disappears during Talk and returns after End Talk; mute stays in the Talk card.
- Check the control at normal and large text sizes; capture real before/after screenshots.

The selected automated iOS and shared suites have passed in kit v3; no repeat is requested for unchanged source. The checklist above remains the physical-device acceptance scope.

## Android maintainer handoff (#187722)

The same native lifecycle correction applies to Android: stop new input and ask `SpeechRecognizer.stopListening()` to finalize, rather than snapshotting the current partial and immediately canceling/destroying the recognizer. Preserve the original recognition/session identity until `onResults`, or a bounded `onError`/deadline fallback to the latest partial; settle once before retiring that identity. Muted/draining callbacks must not restart capture or interrupt playback. Quick toggles and End Talk/session replacement must not leak old speech into a new capture or conversation.

The **five four → mute → three two** regression should send only **five four**, once. Also cover a final with no earlier partial, error/timeout fallback, duplicate finals, quick toggles, and teardown. iOS's two-second deadline is an implementation choice to validate on-device, not a prescribed Android timeout. This note is retained here for the Android author/maintainers; no Android code or metadata was changed.

prs.title: fix: exec refuses every command once lost launches fill the spawn broker
prs.body:
Related: #177656

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: every exec fails with `Spawn broker request capacity exceeded` until the Gateway restarts, once enough commands have been lost between their launch grant and the broker's ownership receipt.

## User Impact

User impact: a command the Gateway loses after granting its launch no longer leaves a slot behind in the spawn broker, so a long-running Gateway keeps running exec instead of refusing every command after about 256 such losses.

## Why This Change Was Made

When the service-child relay fails a command after the host has granted its launch, but before the broker's `owned` receipt arrives, the host retires the request at `owned`. The broker then transfers that command's pipes. The host's branch for requests it no longer tracks answered each transfer with `pipe-received` only. The broker forgets an owned command only once every transferred fd is drained (`forget()` in `worker.ts`), so that entry stayed in its owned map for the life of the Gateway and counted toward the cap.

The untracked-pipe branch now also sends `output-drained` with an error for that fd. That is the same acknowledgement `BrokerChild.attachPipe` already sends for tracked requests. The helper is in `pipe.ts` because `host.ts` is at its 700-line cap.

This is the leak in [KarolAdamiec's heap readings on #177656](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/177656#issuecomment-6629331547): one `owned` entry with `openPipes=1` left per post-launch identity loss, until the broker hit 256 and exec was dead for about 9 h. The host-side `nativeInitiated` path from [an earlier comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/177656#issuecomment-6546377246) does not leak on main: the worker answers `launch allowed:false` with an `error` frame, which clears it.

## Evidence

- **Regression test** (`host-transport-retirement.test.ts`): drives prepare -> launch -> relay loss -> `owned` -> `pipe` through the existing synthetic broker fixture. On main `24401ee0555d` it fails with `expected undefined to match object { type: 'output-drained', ... }`; with this change it passes. No timers: one `setImmediate` turn after `pipe-received`.
- **Suites**, macOS arm64, Node 26.13.0: `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/process/spawn-broker/ src/process/supervisor/` gives 449 passed, 16 skipped (Linux-only cases), 0 failed. These ran under Node because the default Bun runtime skips the broker's real command transport.
- **`node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base 24401ee0555d`**: line cap, oxlint, format, core typecheck and the other ratchets pass. Three gates fail, and they fail identically on unmodified `24401ee0555d`:
  - the mock-export ratchet on two `ui/src` tests;
  - TS1117 in `ui/src/i18n/locales/en-terminal.ts`;
  - two unused exports, `QUALIFIED_PACKAGE_SMOKE_LANES` and `sessionStopCopyKey`.
- **Test cost:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/process/spawn-broker/host-transport-retirement.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` takes 23.3 s wall for the whole file (18 tests, mostly startup). The new test runs in 1-2 ms.
- **Our two Mac mini Gateways** (logs, read-only):
  - Before #169584/#167739, cleanup identity loss was frequent. On a 10.5/10.6-based build, mac-mini logged 9-14 `[process/supervisor] spawn failed ... cleanup identity lost` a day (83 over 10-24..10-30, 458 agent turns).
  - That trigger is gone on 10.10 code: 0 spawn failures of any kind from 2026-10-31 07:30Z to now, over 405 agent turns, on 10.10-beta.4/beta.5-based builds.
  - Identity loss still happens there for other reasons: two `service child cleanup identity lost: anchor channel closed without a matching closing receipt` on 2026-11-02, on the beta.5-based build.
  - Neither host has reached the 256 cap, because both restart for deploys every few days, so they do not show the leak itself.

Not covered: I did not reproduce the full chain with a real relay losing identity inside that window, and I did not run on Linux. The test pins the host's half of the protocol, the half that was missing.

prs.title: feat(ios): browse and preview files shared in a conversation
prs.body:
Closes #192890. ## What Problem This Solves Returning to files shared in an iOS conversation requires finding their original messages; Workspace Files lists the agent's working directory instead. ## User Impact Users can open **Artifacts** beside Chat actions, find files by name or type, preview text/images/PDFs, and save or share originals while keeping their conversation and draft intact. This includes cataloged assistant files and canonical user uploads. Recovering uploaded documents requires the Gateway change in this PR; older Gateways retain their existing catalog coverage. This is an online collection, not an offline archive or a browser of arbitrary paths mentioned in chat. ## Why This Change Was Made The native app can reuse the conversation catalog already used by the web client. The toolbar entry makes conversation content accessible separately from configuration and workspace browsing. The proposed entry point is the Artifacts tray button shown below; scope and use cases are described in #192890. The iOS collection uses existing list/download contracts, captured conversation/Gateway identity, and the existing temporary-file owner. Text is rendered literally; images use the existing decoder and PDFs use PDFKit. Unsupported previews remain exportable when downloading is supported. The preview retains its rendered content rather than the original download buffer; Share reacquires the file under current authorization. Preview limits are smaller than the existing 100 MiB document-download limit. A real picker upload revealed that the full catalog omitted canonical inbound media facts. The Gateway commit projects those facts through the existing artifact owner and media store, preserving current session authorization, transcript membership, grant expiry, and byte-integrity checks. It adds no RPC, filesystem index, dependency, schema migration, or model tool. Internal custody locations stay out of public summaries. Builds on the workspace browser (#100767), native attachment downloads (#155195), and web Files browsing (#176329). ## Evidence Original, unannotated Light-mode captures from iPhone 17 Simulator / iOS 27.0, Xcode 27.1. Synthetic files; working native Debug screens, not App Store screenshots. Before/after use the same conversation and assistant file.
Before: individual message downloadAfter: direct collection entry
Assistant files and actual uploadsUploaded file preview and Share
- **Baseline:** upstream `4a43644e7a7b` downloaded the original 197-byte assistant file from its message. Chat controls had no collection; Workspace Files showed its separate workspace scope. - **Real upload and export:** picker → send → app relaunch/history → collection → preview → Share → Save to Files passed against an isolated TLS Gateway. The saved file matched the input byte for byte, a nonempty draft stayed intact, the export survived dismissal, and the temporary file was removed. An upload created before the Gateway fix also became retrievable. Another conversation could not download it. - **Native proof:** 78 focused native tests, 9 shared tests, and the connected collection UI flow passed. The UI flow covers duplicate names, search, filters, text/PDF preview, system sharing, and draft preservation. Duplicate catalog IDs have a regression that fails before the repair. - **Gateway proof:** 78 tests passed, including `operator.sessions.read`, foreign-session denial, revocation, removed transcript membership, changed bytes, size limits, missing files, and isolated media roots. The original projection fails inbound discovery; the fix passes with the same dependency pins. Empty media slots also fail before the final guard and pass afterward. - **Local checks/review:** native and Gateway builds, focused typecheck/lint/format, native source-inventory verification, and the test-line budget passed. Independent local source reviews found duplicate identities, an internal-locator leak, empty-slot projection, and an offline-demo control with no action; each was corrected before submission. The new native regression failed with `invalidSource` before the repair; the corrected route preserves TLS pinning, byte limits, current-connection checks, and the artifact grant's MIME/disposition checks. The CI failure in `artifacts.images.test.ts` was an obsolete expectation that the unfiltered catalog excluded inbound uploads. Its explicit eight-item expectation now matches this feature while preserving the Activity gallery's pagination, path preference, unsupported-path and bounded-read checks. The same failing test passed after the change: 15/15; 12.616 s test time (47.93 s runner time including preparation). **Inspectable authority proof:** the existing HTTPS test now starts the production Gateway with isolated state, temporary TLS identity, synthetic canonical inbound media, and separate authenticated WSS clients. No authorization function or HTTP handler is mocked. The inbound record is seeded through existing media/transcript owners; the earlier native picker/export run proves ingestion separately. | Operation | Observed final effect | | --- | --- | | Reader with `operator.read` requests the upload grant, then HTTPS GET | HTTP 200; 51 bytes; SHA-256 identical to the expected file | | Client without `operator.read` requests that artifact | RPC rejected: `missing scope: operator.read`; no grant issued | | HTTPS GET without a valid grant | HTTP 404; exactly `Not Found` (9 error bytes, zero upload bytes) | | Administrator calls `device.token.revoke` for the original reader; reuse the **same original URL** | HTTP 404; exactly `Not Found` (9 error bytes, zero upload bytes) | Expected and received SHA-256: `d7efd3d8685b1cafc7abea4f55450ba775f2d1655e458d17957edd3daa622830`. The HTTP route uses a capability URL, not an additional reader identity on each GET. The forbidden-client case proves denied grant issuance and denial without a valid grant; it does not claim that a second holder of a live bearer URL is independently authenticated. Personal instructions saved in Profile settings do not reach agent requests in managed worktree sessions.

## What Problem This Solves After an Android **Files → Load more** request fails, a successful retry loads the remaining files but leaves “Files unavailable / Could not load this folder.” visible. ## Why This Change Was Made Clear the directory screen's prior error after a successful listing, alongside the existing entries/total update. Failed and pending retries retain their error and loaded rows. This follows the screen's existing full-reload recovery behavior; pagination, protocol, and storage are unchanged. ## User Impact Recovered pagination displays the loaded files without a stale failure message. Both standard thirdPartyDebug APKs and external instrumentation APKs were built from the exact baseline/candidate checkouts. Runtime BuildConfig.GIT_COMMIT, APK hashes, source identity and clean tracked source were verified. - **Native differential:** ordinary launcher → setup-code onboarding → Overview → Files → 251-file folder. Initial real page of 250 → one controlled page failure → successful retry returning the final file. Exactly three listing events on one connection, default limit omitted, no refresh or first-page reload. The baseline reproduces the stale error; the patched APK removes it. The native runner uses only normal UI actions; its source is on a separate fork proof ref, outside this PR diff. - **Team-metal regression:** final cleaned LEGACY/default-graphics Compose/RPC unit test is RED unpatched, GREEN patched (one UI test); all three existing parser tests and scoped repository ktlint pass. This additional unit scenario covers two failed retries and a held retry before recovery. - **Independent review:** exact claude-opus-5-5, high reasoning, clean on the final product patch and final proof-runner changes. Structured final reports are in the proof archives. - **Upstream CI:** tracked separately on this PR's current head. The fork native proof supplements the upstream required-check gate. ### Inspected native before/after Both images were taken after the final page loaded and the driver returned to the folder header and first row. | Baseline APK: stale error remains | Fixed APK: error cleared | | --- | --- | | | | [Native final-page capture: file-250.txt loaded, Load more absent](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/627e1343-75ca-4bd4-8887-5bacc286a6ab). For fixes, describe the user-visible symptom and trigger: fix: task list fails to load when user has no environments Avoid implementation details such as: fix: add null check to task query **MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers can help update the branch when needed. -->

Closes #194414

## What Problem This Solves

The Workboard CLI reference tells readers to run `openclaw gateway restart` after `openclaw plugins enable workboard`, but enabling a plugin already applies to a running Gateway. The stale restart step contradicts the plugin guides and can make readers restart a Gateway that did not need one.

## User Impact

Docs-only change: readers of the Workboard CLI page no longer restart the Gateway after enabling the plugin, and the page now matches how plugin enablement actually behaves.

## Why This Change Was Made

`openclaw plugins enable` applies each change through the running local Gateway and saves the change for the next Gateway start when it is offline (see docs/cli/plugins/install.md, Enable installed plugins). The Workboard and Memory Wiki plugin pages already state that enablement applies to a running Gateway automatically, so this removes the leftover restart step and points at the shared Apply changes and inspect section.

## Evidence

- Docs-only change. `git diff --check` passes.
- Contradiction verified across docs/cli/workboard.md, docs/cli/plugins/install.md, docs/plugins/manage-plugins.md, and docs/plugins/workboard.md before editing.
- Diff: one file changed, one stale line removed, one clarifying note added.

prs.title: feat(sessions): add creator-only and named-audience confidentiality
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

I made it so my own team can have a) top level sessions reserved for only few people b) personal-only sessions for every employee c) sesions visible for everyone like now, still supporting current draft/suggest/readonly/shared modes.

My team shares one OpenClaw server. We need three simple choices for each conversation:

1. **Personal:** only its creator can use it (besides administrators acting under their existing server privileges). The product goal is that every registered member can start their own private session.
2. **For a small group:** the creator chooses the specific registered people who can join. Everyone else must not find the conversation, open its history, receive its updates or access its media.
3. **Open to the server:** everyone with the required server and agent permissions can access it. “Open” does not mean available anonymously on the internet.

Today, **Draft**, **Shared**, **Suggest** and **Read-only** describe how a session appears or how people collaborate; they are not a reliable answer to **who may see it**. This PR adds that separate access choice, so a private conversation stays private even if the people in it work together. It checks the audience consistently when a session is found, read, changed or streamed, including its media.

**Scope:** This PR provides the access rules and lets authorized creators/admins choose an exact audience. It does not add a one-click invitation interface, and it currently does not give members session-creation rights beyond their existing server role. The all-registered-members creation requirement still needs verification against role policy; do not read this PR as proof that it is already met. Old sessions with no access setting keep their previous behavior; new sessions receive an access setting.

## Published revision

Head: `21320336f4d447ef22e8a0efd005bbbd01e86dca`; tree: `65af164abf5475c3561a4e339bde87548916375e`; parent: `24a38dcce87c2755444360a58ee7024699b40089`. The latest commit is a fast-forward update to the existing PR, not a separate packaging PR.

For sessions saved before ACL metadata existed, absent ACL preserves the prior access behavior. Selected older sessions can be explicitly assigned a specific audience; new sessions receive ACL. Draft defaults are unchanged. An unrelated plugin-packaging hunk and its 111-line test were removed from this revision; the packaging paths match pinned upstream `938a72d4`.

## Evidence

Source-level checks run November 6, 2026:

On the exact newest published source tree before its commit was pushed, 82 unique selected source cases passed, including real synthetic standalone attachment HTTP routes, prior media routes and negative ACL/revocation checks. Format, lint, typechecks, mock exports and the exact pinned-main test-line ratchet also passed (slack 0). Scoped independent review found no confirmed P0–P2 in the incremental standalone-media repair; this is not maintainer approval. The retained audience-revocation test, part of `src/gateway/chat-goal-created-authority.e2e.test.ts`, demonstrated the pre-fix history count growing 7→8; with the fix it stayed 7→7 with byte-identical canonical stored history, zero stale content/events, and one authorized error notice. The source-test reports and sanitized traces are retained with the local qualification receipt; reviewers can rerun the test from the PR source. These assertions use a synthetic Gateway and scripted external provider I/O, **not** employees or production data.

The preceding revision `edbd79e` had 92 selected local PASS, with real image-policy red/green source HTTP traces attached in the PR. Those results do not replace new-head acceptance or a binary-upgrade test.

**New P1 source-policy image fix:** ClawSweeper found that the image-byte filter preferred a request-start config snapshot even when a live config accessor existed. A source-policy reload removing an audience member during an awaited read could serve revoked avatar or workspace-icon bytes. Reproduction on the previous code served image bytes in 4/4 config-revocation cases; with the new source repair, the same cases deny bytes and ETag, while permitted controls still pass. The shared filter now evaluates live source policy at final authorization for both consumers. These are source HTTP tests, not a shipped binary or human QA. ClawSweeper reviewed `edbd79e` with zero actionable findings and acknowledged the P1 fix, but still required legacy compatibility proof and maintainer decisions. ClawSweeper reviewed `24a38dc` and found one further P2 regression in old standalone Draft attachments; that regression is addressed by the new `2132033` source change, which needs its own verdict.

**Legacy no-ACL read preservation:** Earlier source changed direct access to an existing Draft without ACL from the pinned-base behavior to null when roles were absent. The new patch restores legacy direct `sessions.describe`, `sessions.get`, `sessions.preview` and `chat.history` while still hiding Draft from discovery and retaining denial when roles are enabled or explicit ACL/source restrictions apply. Five actual pre-fix HTTP assertions failed as expected; all nine targeted HTTP assertions passed on the fixed candidate, alongside negative role/ACL/source checks. This is source behavior, not the shipped UI or a binary migration.

**Legacy standalone media preservation:** ClawSweeper found that an authenticated, roleless reader with existing operator.read could no longer fetch a Draft attachment when the saved session had no ACL. A real source HTTP reproduction returned 404 on the previous code; the new code restores the prior 200 response only for that no-ACL case. Named-role or explicitly restricted ACL/source sessions remain denied, including revocation while a file opens. The exact red/green execution report and original sanitized HTTP traces are attached in the new-head PR comment. These are source checks, not shipped-binary upgrade proof.

The three rendered source-fixture summary images remain removed; they were not UI screenshots. The following **are actual captures of the isolated notebook Gateway interface** with synthetic admin/Alice/Bob, an Authelia test setup and mock model. They show the intended final behavior: admin sees five test sessions; Alice sees her own personal session and group A (not group B); Bob sees his own personal session and group B (not group A). Direct access to the other person's group displays a generic unavailable page. These screenshots come from the earlier source head `1e24780af60565fe149020634460945992fefeb6`. They illustrate the acceptance target but do **not** certify the current `2132033` binary or production. The new head still needs its own UI/upgrade acceptance.

**Visible sessions — synthetic admin 5, Alice 2, Bob 2:**
![Real notebook Gateway UI: synthetic admin, Alice and Bob session lists](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dankarization/openclaw-pr-proofs/66aa8b4a68b7f3d09378318901243790d4fcfded/187836-qa-20261104/qa-187836-1e24780-visibility.png)

**Alice: group A opens; group B is unavailable:**
![Real notebook Gateway UI: Alice can read group A, not group B](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dankarization/openclaw-pr-proofs/66aa8b4a68b7f3d09378318901243790d4fcfded/187836-qa-20261104/qa-187836-1e24780-alice-history.png)

**Bob: group B opens; group A is unavailable:**
![Real notebook Gateway UI: Bob can read group B, not group A](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dankarization/openclaw-pr-proofs/66aa8b4a68b7f3d09378318901243790d4fcfded/187836-qa-20261104/qa-187836-1e24780-bob-history.png)

## Remaining review and release gates

- Required hosted CI and independent maintainer security approval must be evaluated on the **new head**. A local source PASS is neither a hosted green check nor approval.
- The PR still reports a conflict against moving `main`. Resolve it deliberately for landing and rerun affected checks; do not assume the pinned-base result covers future main.
- A built artifact, product UI check and latest-stable binary upgrade/data-preservation test have **not** been completed. The notebook's local SSD currently has ~15 GB free, below the 50 GB heavy-build guard, so no heavy build or install was started there.

No production Gateway, real employee ACL or live sessions were changed.

## What Problem This Solves

Android Talk users need to pause microphone input without ending the conversation or interrupting the assistant's work and response audio.

## User Impact

A separate, accessible microphone button beside End Talk lets users mute and unmute input while keeping the call, accepted work, and reply audio active. Mute remains set across Talk restarts in the app process until explicitly unmuted; standalone push-to-talk still works after ending Talk.

Realtime mute sends silence while the recording session stays open, so Android's microphone indicator may remain visible. Native Talk finishes already-recognized words before pausing recognition. No new permission, configuration, dependency, protocol, or release-version change is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ending Talk and muting reply playback are different operations from muting input. Keep input mute owned by `TalkModeManager` and expose that state through the existing runtime/view model to the actual ChatScreen control. Reuse the capture ownership lock to retire native recognition and keep queued microphone audio from crossing a mute/unmute toggle at socket enqueue. Preserve upstream detach/abort behavior.

The patch excludes selected-chat routing, Health Connect, SMS, version bumps, and the unrelated chat-metadata warning repair. It adds no parallel capture manager: the necessary growth is one input state plus audio-frame invalidation and the control/proof. Production Kotlin delta: +132/-20; tests: +253/-1; README: +1.

## Evidence

- Built and tested against pinned main `6c672d42f2dec42b7917f34dfe5ae8157b9b0abb`; Initial Kotlin test/review head `750c924b8ec5e95018239108fd9f85382d936a7c`; current head `3d852cea86599dcabc6df2f97dababf59ed842bc` adds only the generated source inventory entries described below.
- `:app:ktlintCheck` passed. `:app:testThirdPartyDebugUnitTest` passed **121 tests**, zero failures/errors/skips: all 118 `TalkModeManagerTest` cases and three targeted `ChatComposerLayoutTest` cases covering the real toggle, accessible state, and 320dp/French/large-font controls. Gradle build/check wall time: **4m 11s**; recorded suite times: **17.745s** and **12.297s**, respectively. These are Kotlin/Gradle suites, not `pnpm test` suites. The completed updated-head CI result is summarized below.
- Transport checks exercise microphone PCM replacement with silence, a read spanning a toggle, and queued audio waiting at the actual socket enqueue. Native/relay checks preserve admitted work and playback; push-to-talk checks cover muted admission and standalone use after Talk ends.
- The requester initially liked the feature during real voice use on the custom 2026.10.7 phone build, but subsequently reported that muting seemed to silence assistant playback as well. That observation is not yet reproduced or attributed; do not treat output preservation as accepted device proof. Source inspection confirms separate microphone and speaker controls, but does not establish what happened on that phone. This current-main port has not separately been installed on a device; do not treat the synthetic screenshots as live audio proof.
- Fresh independent Codex read-only review of the final mute-only snapshot against the pinned base found no actionable likely/high-impact findings. CLI AutoReview was attempted but unavailable because OpenAI returned HTTP 401; it is **not** counted as a passing AutoReview. `git diff --check` passed. Full Android framework/resource lint and broad hosted CI are not claimed passing.

### CI localization correction

The initial [CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40892555492) passed Android third-party, Play, Wear, both native-accessibility jobs, and Kotlin style. Its one underlying failure was `native-i18n`: the source extraction inventory omitted the five new mute strings. `openclaw/ci-gate` reflected that failure.

Reproduced the same inventory failure locally before the repair. Ran `pnpm native:i18n:baseline`, which added exactly five generator-owned entries to `apps/.i18n/native-source.json`. `pnpm native:i18n:verify` now passes, including Android and Apple source safety checks; `pnpm android:i18n:gen` regenerates the Android lookup/resources with the new labels. Kotlin source and tests are unchanged, so the earlier focused test and independent review evidence remains scoped to that unchanged code. The [updated-head native-i18n job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40899576510/job/123538746357) now passes on GitHub for `3d852cea86599dcabc6df2f97dababf59ed842bc`; that run is now complete. Android third-party and Wear tests, ktlint, both native-accessibility jobs, and native-i18n passed. The [`android-test-play` job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40899576510/job/123538748350) exceeded its 20-minute unit-test limit, which failed `openclaw/ci-gate`. No failing assertion was established in the inspected log, and the empty failure-classification table does not establish an inherited failure. The timeout remains under investigation; no blind CI rerun was requested.

Translated dictionaries and derived locale metadata remain owned by the serialized post-merge locale refresh ([publication policy](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/6c672d42f2dec42b7917f34dfe5ae8157b9b0abb/.agents/skills/openclaw-pr-maintainer/references/landing.md#open-or-update-the-pr)); this correction commits the source-owned inventory, not hand-edited translations. The new labels can use English fallback until that refresh.

### Current-head phone testing artifact and CI follow-up — October 30

An [unofficial contributor test APK](https://github.com/davelutztx/openclaw/releases/tag/pr-187722-phone-test-3d852cea8659) is available from the exact
clean head `3d852cea86599dcabc6df2f97dababf59ed842bc`. The download page includes the APK SHA-256,
signature/build manifest, and [route-specific test instructions](https://github.com/davelutztx/openclaw/releases/download/pr-187722-phone-test-3d852cea8659/TESTING.md).
It is phone-only `thirdPartyDebug` (`ai.openclaw.app.debug`), not an official
release; no private Health/Samsung/selected-chat/lock-screen patches or version
source changes are included. No device installation was performed.
The unchanged upstream version label is `2026.8.2-debug`; identify
the artifact by commit and SHA-256, not the version label.

The new local build also passed **121 focused Play tests**, zero failures/errors/skips
(118 TalkModeManager cases and three ChatComposerLayout cases), with artifact
signature, CRC, manifest, compiled mute setters, and exact commit/timestamp
verified. This does not replace full hosted CI or physical audio proof.

**Physical acceptance remains pending.** The [current review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187722#issuecomment-6500004345)
found no actionable code findings but requires a device recording or redacted
runtime trace for **both native and realtime** mute/unmute during active answers,
showing suppressed new input, uninterrupted audio, and completed accepted work.
The testing packet includes that exact scope and a result template. The maintainer
decision on the feature's control, silence-based realtime behavior, and mute
lifetime also remains open. No new review was requested without that proof.

**CI investigation:** the [timed-out Play job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40899576510/job/123538748350)
left about **9m50s** after launching the app test JVM, whereas the
[previous passing Play job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40892555492/job/123513827300)
needed **10m32s** and passed 3,658 tests. Those heads differ only in the five
localization inventory entries, not Android code/tests/Gradle/CI. Current-head
third-party CI passed 3,776 tests in about 9m19s after test JVM launch.
This strongly supports inadequate whole-job headroom; failed-only logging and
skipped timeout reports mean an individual stall is not ruled out. The
[full findings](https://github.com/davelutztx/openclaw/releases/download/pr-187722-phone-test-3d852cea8659/CI-NOTES.md) propose a **test-play-only 30-minute
budget** while preserving all other budgets, followed by one result on the changed
head. Current upstream main still uses 20 minutes for this job. **No workflow
edit, blind CI rerun, inherited-failure classification, or green-gate claim was made.**

### Remaining before merge

- Supply runtime evidence on this current-main Android port for native and realtime mute/unmute during an active answer, including input suppression and continued playback. The older custom-build user report and synthetic UI captures do not establish that evidence.
- Obtain the maintainer product decision on the separate input control, silence-based realtime mute, and mute lifetime across Talk restarts. The author's requested feature and phone acceptance are not represented as upstream maintainer approval.

### Synthetic ChatScreen captures

The images below come from the real ChatScreen Robolectric fixture at 320dp, not a mock-drawn control or a live provider call. They demonstrate the control/status and layout only.

prs.title: feat(tui): add screen reader mode
prs.body:
Closes #9637

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the TUI is hard to use with a screen reader (NVDA, JAWS) because it repaints animated spinners, colors, borders, scrolling lists and inline cards that a reader announces over and over or not at all.

## User Impact

User impact: people who use a screen reader can run `openclaw tui --screen-reader` (or set `ui.tui.screenReader: true`) and get a TUI that speaks each thing once, in order.

Nothing changes for anyone who does not turn it on. There is no environment variable, no new default, no migration and no breaking change. The new config key is optional and schema-validated.

## What changes in screen reader mode

- Launch prints "Screen reader mode on" before the TUI draws.
- The status row is static text. One line and at most one bell per status change ("Working", "Done in 12s", "Status: error"). Startup is not announced as a run.
- Replies appear one finished terminal row at a time and a row you heard is never repainted: the last, still-growing row is held back until another row starts or the reply ends. The labels `You:`, `Assistant:`, `System:` and `Tool x: [running]/[ok]/[failed]` replace color cues. Output is colorless.
- The composer line starts with `$`, borders are dropped, and the real cursor is shown.
- Pickers and settings lists keep rows byte-identical while you arrow. Only the cursor moves to the selected row, the scroll window stays still (screen reader mode only; the default pickers keep their centered window), and overlays cover whole rows so chat text is not read alongside the options. Name and description are joined once instead of read twice.
- `ask_user` questions follow the selected option with the cursor. The expiry is a fixed clock time that changes once, to "under 30 seconds left", instead of a countdown that ticks every second.
- `/btw` answers open in a closable overlay (Esc/Enter closes, `c` copies) instead of an inline card. An answer taller than the terminal scrolls with the arrow and Page Up/Page Down keys. "Asking side question" is announced on send, and a failure line appears after 60 seconds with no answer, and "btw ended without an answer." is announced when a run finishes empty.

Docs: `docs/web/tui.md`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The activation flag is the single switch. `tui-a11y.ts` owns it, and the status, label, selection and overlay code read it from there. The status row moved from `tui.ts` into `tui-status-line.ts` with the same behavior, so screen reader mode can swap the animated loader for static text without a second owner. The `/btw` state moved to `tui-btw-overlay.ts` for the same reason. `tui.ts` shrank.

Pickers and the question prompt are wrapped by a `SelectionCursor` instead of being rewritten, so one place decides where the reader's cursor sits. The `/btw` overlay places its own cursor, because its answer text can contain lines that start with an arrow.

## Review follow-up

Addressed the ClawSweeper findings on `377f239b4d3`:

- **Terminal safety (P1):** plain-mode messages now go through `sanitizeTerminalControlsAndBinary`, the same sanitizer the markdown path uses, so erase-screen and OSC 52 sequences in assistant text are stripped. This keeps the hardening from #118998. Regression test: `markdown-message.test.ts`.
- **Picker scrolling (P2):** the stable window is now opt-in. `SearchableSelectList` and `FilterableSelectList` keep their original centered window unless screen reader mode turns `stableWindow` on, so default TUI behavior is unchanged. This preserves the picker behavior from #1271. Tests cover both modes.
- **Long `/btw` answers (P2):** the overlay windows the answer to the terminal height and scrolls it; the question and controls stay visible.
- **Empty side-question result (P2):** a run that ends without an answer is announced once instead of going silent.
- **Question cursor (P2):** `QuestionPrompt` now places the cursor on its own selected row in screen reader mode, so an option description that starts with an arrow can no longer take the cursor. `SelectionCursor` no longer infers selection from `›`.
- **Merge conflict:** merged current upstream `main`; the only conflicts were the generated config baseline files, which were regenerated.
- **Data compatibility:** no stored data or schema changed. The only addition is the optional `ui.tui.screenReader` boolean. Configs without `ui.tui` validate exactly as before, so an upgrade from the latest stable keeps existing settings; the schema tests cover valid and invalid `ui.tui` payloads and an existing `ui` config without `ui.tui`.

## Review follow-up (round 2)

Addressed the ClawSweeper findings on `f91d2c1400d`:

- **Literal text (P2):** plain-mode messages are no longer rewritten. Sentence ends used to become line breaks, which split code and quoted strings (`print("Hello! world")`). Now the text is shown exactly as sent; while streaming, only the part up to the last finished sentence or line break is shown, so a reader still hears whole sentences. Regression test: `chat-log-screen-reader.test.ts` ("shows literal text unchanged").
- **Picker metadata (P2):** `SelectionCursor` no longer drops a column whose text ends the label; it only joins the columns with a comma. An agent `my-default` now keeps its `default` tag. The check for a model name that only restates its id moved to the owner of the rows, `modelSelectItems`: a name is hidden when it matches the id ignoring case and punctuation (`DeepSeek V4.1 Flash` vs `deepseek-v4.1-flash`). This also applies outside screen reader mode, where the same name was shown twice. Regression tests: `selection-cursor.test.ts`, `selectors.test.ts`.
- **Cursor after copy (P2):** scrolling the `/btw` overlay clears the "Copied to clipboard." notice, so the cursor returns to the visible answer. Regression test: `btw-overlay.test.ts`.
- **Data compatibility:** added a schema test that an existing `ui` config without the `tui` block (`seamColor`, `prefs`) validates and loads unchanged.

Each regression test fails on `f91d2c1400d` and passes with the fix. At the new head: `pnpm tsgo:core` passes, oxfmt is clean, oxlint passes on the changed files, and `src/tui` runs 1120 passing tests with the same 5 Windows-only failures as before (`tui-autocomplete`, no `fd`; `tui-launch`, POSIX fixture path).

## Review follow-up (round 3)

Addressed the ClawSweeper findings on `b5899812f59`:

- **Announced rows stay stable (P2):** round 2 showed everything up to the last sentence end, so a second sentence joining the same wrapped row rewrote that row and the renderer re-emitted the first sentence. Streaming now holds back the last wrapped row (`StreamingText` in `markdown-message.ts`); rows already shown never change, and the text is still shown exactly as sent. Regression test: `chat-log-screen-reader.test.ts` ("holds the last wrapped row and never rewrites an announced one").
- **Delivered answer is not "empty" (P2):** both backends send `chat.side_result` and then a message-free `chat` final. `handleBtwEvent` now passes the run id to `showResult`, which marks the run answered, so the empty final no longer announces "btw ended without an answer." after a delivered answer. A final with no answer still announces. Regression test: `tui-btw-overlay.test.ts`.
- **Behavior proof:** see "Terminal capture" below.

## Review follow-up (round 4)

Addressed the ClawSweeper findings on `a7858707729`:

- **No full redraw when a run ends (P2):** lifecycle end/error, `chat.final` and the run coordinator call `requestRender(true)`, which makes pi-tui forget what it drew and print the whole transcript again. In screen reader mode the event handlers now get a renderer that drops the force flag (`noForcedRender` in `tui-a11y.ts`, applied where `tui.ts` builds the event handlers). pi-tui still does a full redraw by itself when the viewport needs it (resize, changed rows above the viewport). Forced redraws for session switch and history reload are unchanged, and default mode is unchanged. Test: `tui-a11y.test.ts` ("drops the force flag so finished runs keep differential rendering"). The terminal capture below shows each prompt printed once after its reply finishes (steps 2-3).
- **Merge conflict:** merged current `main`. The only conflicts were the generated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.*` files: took `main`, ran `pnpm config:docs:gen`, and `pnpm config:docs:check` passes. `main` moved again with the same generated-file conflict; merged it at `f656018eeb2` and again at `f55c2d707ce` the same way; `pnpm tsgo:core` passes at both. The last merge changed no `src/tui` files.
- Checks: at `a1a99985e4b` oxlint and the format check are clean on the changed files and the `tui-a11y`, `tui-event-handlers` and `tui` tests pass (170 tests); after the merge (`1abfb17303d`) `pnpm tsgo:core` passes. Full `src/tui` suite at `f656018eeb2`: 1137 of 1142 tests passed; the 5 failures are in tests this PR does not change (3 in `tui-autocomplete.test.ts`: no `fd` on this machine; 2 existing standalone-launch cases in `tui-launch.test.ts`: POSIX `file:///` fixture path on Windows).

## Review follow-up (round 5)

Addressed the ClawSweeper finding on `f55c2d707ce`:

- **Test typecheck (P2):** `noForcedRender` returned an inferred `{ requestRender: () => void }`, so the test's `requestRender(true)` failed TS2554 in the commands test-type project. The function now declares its optional-force contract (`RenderRequester`, `requestRender(force?: boolean)`) as both its parameter and return type, so the wrapper keeps the same method shape the event handlers call. The same CI run also flagged an uncommented `as StreamingText` cast in `markdown-message.ts` (assertion-safety ratchet); it is now an `instanceof` guard.
- Checks: CI passed on `6fc656c585c`. On the new head, the format check is clean, the commands test-type project and `pnpm tsgo:core` pass, and `tui-a11y.test.ts` passes.

## Review follow-up (round 6)

Addressed the ClawSweeper findings on `7e9e2f5a3c2` in `cb43662cc86`, plus the same kind of text guessing elsewhere in the screen reader layer:

- **Selection cue only in its column (P2):** `SelectionCursor` treats only a `→ ` in column 0 as the selection cue (every picker draws it there) and blanks it only on the selected row. A session titled "→ Deploy" keeps its arrow and no longer pulls the cursor away from the session Enter would pick. Test runs through the real session picker (`buildSessionChoices` + `FilterableSelectList`).
- **Composer scroll borders (P3):** in screen reader mode a row starting with `─` is a border (text and suggestion rows start with the two padding columns). Scroll borders become plain words ("3 more lines above", "1 more line below") instead of being dropped, so a reader still learns a draft has hidden lines, and the `$ ` marker goes on the first text row. When a very narrow terminal cuts the count off, the row says "more lines above". Tests cover a 10-line draft at 24 rows and a 10-column terminal.
- **No more decoration guessing:** the session and model pickers leave out their position counter and divider themselves in screen reader mode (`stableWindow`), so `SelectionCursor` no longer deletes rows that only look like a counter or a rule (a label "3/4", a "───" detail line).
- **Commas only on option rows:** column padding becomes a comma only on the option rows around the selection, split at the column the rows share, so titles, details, hints and a double space inside a label keep their text.
- **Autocomplete:** while the `/` suggestion list is open, the cursor parks on the selected suggestion so a reader follows it.
- Checks at `cb43662cc86`: full `src/tui` suite 1143 of 1148 pass (the same 5 Windows-only failures as before: 3 in `tui-autocomplete.test.ts`, no `fd`; 2 standalone-launch cases in `tui-launch.test.ts`, POSIX `file:///` fixture). Format and oxlint clean on the changed files; `pnpm tsgo:core` and the `commands` and `other` test-type projects pass; line-cap, assertion-safety, max-lines, mock-export, timeout-race and test-lines ratchets pass (6301287 of 6302000).
- The terminal capture below predates this change: picker steps 12-19 still show the counter and divider.

## Review follow-up (round 7)

Addressed the ClawSweeper finding on `cb43662cc86` in `27facddea56`:

- **Hidden-line notices fit the terminal width (P2):** the composer's "N more lines above/below" notice now wraps to the render width (`wrapTextWithAnsi`), so a 10-column terminal shows "more lines" / "above" on two rows instead of one 16-column row that pi-tui rejects. Every word stays, so a reader still hears the direction and the count. The narrow-terminal test now asserts the wrapped rows and that every rendered row fits the width, instead of expecting the overwide string.
- Checks at `27facddea56`: `custom-editor.test.ts` 13 of 13 pass; format and oxlint clean on the changed files; `pnpm tsgo:core` and the `commands` test-type project pass; line-cap, assertion-safety and test-lines ratchets pass (6301289 of 6302000).
- Merged main `9a5581b4ce2` in `44d4d592649` (conflicts only in `config/test-lines-baseline.txt` and `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`: took main, reran `pnpm config:docs:gen`). After the merge the test-lines total is 6302722 against main’s 6302000 ceiling, so the ceiling is now 6303000 with a one-line justification in the file (this PR adds about 1,100 test lines; main’s reserve is about 450). On the merged tree `pnpm tsgo:core` and the `commands` test-type project pass, and the line-cap ratchet passes against main.

## Terminal capture

Shipped CLI built from `1abfb17303d`, `openclaw tui --local --screen-reader`, real model (`opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`), isolated state directory (deleted afterwards), real Windows terminal (ConPTY), 110x32. A driver typed each step; the app's own stdout was recorded before ConPTY touched it. After every step the driver counts how many times the app has printed the first two `You:` rows; a count above 1 means the transcript was printed again. Credentials and personal data were checked for and not present.

- The PTY test `src/tui/tui-screen-reader-pty.e2e.test.ts` passes 2/2 under WSL. It does not run on native Windows.
- End-to-end run: an isolated Gateway (throwaway state directory, loopback port) with a real model (`opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`), and `openclaw tui --screen-reader` connected to it. One message produced: "Screen reader mode on", `You:` and `Assistant:` labels, the status lines Working, waiting, running, streaming and "Done in 22s", the reply sentence by sentence, and one bell at completion. No per-second status lines appeared.
- Tested by hand: Real NVDA use on Windows Terminal, confirmed.
- The end-to-end run used piped output, succeeded.

## Accepted limits

- Closing an overlay (the `/btw` answer, the model picker) prints the chat again (capture steps 9 and 16). This looks like pi-tui's own full redraw when the rows padded under an overlay are removed; not yet checked whether default mode does the same.
- While streaming, the last wrapped row is hidden until another row starts or the reply ends, so a short reply appears when it finishes and a reader hears a full row (about a line) at a time.
- Resizing the terminal prints the whole chat again (capture step 27): pi-tui does a full redraw on every width change, in every mode.
- A same-session history reload keeps an open `/btw` answer, but a session switch closes it.
- Onboarding wizard accessibility is out of scope.
- CI runs  the full `lint:core`.
- Not run: the SQLite worker ratchet (`rg` missing locally).
