prs.title: fix(agents): Claude CLI turns hit output limits on discarded stream frames
prs.body:
Related: #153545, #184352, #186085, #166127, #159930, #111382 This PR no longer adds environment overrides. The earlier revision restored output-limit tuning that #111382 removed; it is replaced here by an accounting repair inside the existing fixed limits, the direction the first review recommended. No limit, setting or environment variable changes. ## What Problem This Solves Claude stream frames the parser throws away (thinking signatures, empty thinking progress ticks, block and message stops, message deltas) are charged their full raw size against the 8 MiB output budget, and every one counts toward the 20,000-line limit. In long tool-heavy `claude-cli` turns that framing alone stops the turn with `CLI JSONL output exceeded 8388608 characters` and loses the final reply. This change charges those frames a fixed allowance. Other record types are charged as before. ## User Impact On the 1,980-step tool loop below, current `main` stops the turn after step 1,744 and returns no reply; with this change the same loop completes all 1,980 steps and replies `DONE`. Per tool round the charge drops from about 4,700 to 3,590 characters, so a `claude-cli` turn fits about 30 percent more tool calls before the unchanged limits apply. ## Why This Change Was Made `chargeClaudeStreamJsonLine` charges each Claude stream-json line its raw length unless a narrower rule applies: #153545 charges text, thinking and tool-input deltas their payload plus 32 characters (#186085 extended it to frames carrying `api_message_id`), and #184352 charges discarded child messages a fixed 64. Five `stream_event` kinds have no rule, although the parser reads at most one small field from them: | Frame | What the parser reads | Typical raw size | | --- | --- | --- | | `signature_delta` | nothing (`cli-output-events.ts:491`: "opaque continuation material") | about 2 KB, up to 21 KB | | `thinking_delta` with empty `thinking` (progress tick) | `estimated_tokens` (`cli-output-events.ts:483`) | 343 | | `content_block_stop` | `index` (`cli-output-events.ts:330`, `:467`) | 243 | | `message_stop` | the event type (`cli-output-stream.ts:524`) | 227 | | `message_delta` | nothing (`src/` has no reader of `message_delta`; `readCliUsage` reads top-level `usage`, not `event.usage`) | 740 | The charge only feeds the budget; it never changes what the parser reads or emits. `measureClaudeStreamControlFrame` (new, beside the partial-frame helper) charges a matching frame 32 characters, plus the `estimated_tokens` field for progress ticks and any wire whitespace around the JSON: - Progress ticks and stop frames have closed, bounded shapes, so like partial frames they no longer count toward the 20,000-line limit. Each costs at least 33 characters with its newline, so the 8 MiB budget still caps them at about 254,000 per turn. Progress ticks still reach `onThinkingProgress` once per frame. - Signature and message deltas carry discarded content of any size, so they keep counting as ordinary lines, and at most 8 KiB of each line goes uncharged; anything beyond that is charged. A turn may therefore parse up to 20,000 such lines of 8 KiB (about 156 MiB) where the budget used to stop near 8 MiB. That is acceptable because the content is discarded, not retained, and the line and single-line limits still bound the work; a test drives such lines until the line limit trips. - The envelope check that #186085 added for partial frames (allowed top-level keys, `api_message_id` at most 64 characters, `thinking_display` at most 32, valid block index) moves into `readBoundedStreamEvent` and is shared by both helpers instead of duplicated. `thinking_display` is accepted only on progress ticks. - An unknown key at any level, oversized or non-string metadata, a non-numeric estimate, thinking text, an empty signature or an invalid index keeps full accounting, as does any key a future Claude Code release adds until it is reviewed. `message_start` and `content_block_start` stay fully charged because they feed parser state. #166127 (tool results) and #159930 (Edit/Write file echoes) discount other record types and do not overlap. ## Evidence **Real behavior proof (shipped entry point).** One `openclaw agent exec` turn per build through the bundled `claude-cli` backend, built from `main` (67c3c3abfa6) and from this PR at 21fe91648a317548ac92b8b278f8a6986979264e (the follow-up commit changes only tests and the test-lines allocation, so the production code exercised is the code under review). macOS, Node 24, Claude Code 2.1.296, `claude-haiku-5-5`, `--thinking low`, each run with its own temporary `OPENCLAW_HOME` and this config: ```json { "agents": { "defaults": { "model": "anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5", "models": { "anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5": { "agentRuntime": { "id": "claude-cli" } } }, "timeoutSeconds": 7200 } } } ``` Prompt: run `echo step-K` with the `exec` tool for K = 1 to 1,980, one call per message, then reply `DONE`. Each round is one tiny tool call, so most of the stream is per-message framing (message start, block start and stop, message delta, message stop, snapshots and tool results), the shape of a long tool loop. | Build | Exit | Result | Tool calls | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `main` 67c3c3abfa6 | 1 | `CLI JSONL output exceeded 8388608 characters` after step 1,744, no reply (2,174 s) | 1,746 (incl. `ToolSearch` and the cancelled step 1,745) | | this PR 21fe91648a3 | 0 | `ok`, final `DONE` (2,882 s) | 1,982: 1,980 steps, `ToolSearch`, 1 rejected first guess | The `main` run stops after step 1,744: the parser refuses the stream mid-turn, the in-flight call is cancelled and no reply is returned. In the head run the model first called a bare `exec` (rejected: the tool was not loaded yet), loaded `mcp__openclaw__exec` with `ToolSearch`, then ran all 1,980 steps; that rejected first guess is the single tool failure and the two extra calls. The working directory holds only the prompt after both runs. A pass-through wrapper on `PATH` copied Claude Code's stdout to a file in both runs, because the gateway does not log the stream of a failed turn. Replaying each file through `chargeClaudeStreamJsonLine` from both builds, fed the way the live transport feeds the parser (it consumes control messages first): | Stream | `main` accounting | this PR accounting | | --- | --- | --- | | `main` run (25,659 lines) | 8,392,097 chars, trips at line 25,649 (the gateway stopped within 10 lines of it) | 6,442,638 (77%), 12,254 ordinary lines | | head run, completed (26,847 lines) | 9,312,559 (111%), would trip at line 24,101 | 7,103,109 (85%), 13,912 ordinary lines | On the completed stream that is about 4,700 characters per tool round on `main` and 3,590 with this change.
main 67c3c3abfa6: redacted output ``` $ openclaw agent exec --config openclaw.json --cwd work --message-file work/prompt.txt --thinking low --timeout 7200 --json { "ok": false, "status": "error", "final": "", "payloads": [], "model": null, "provider": null, "sessionId": "", "error": { "message": "CLI JSONL output exceeded 8388608 characters; refusing to parse output.", "kind": "exception" } } --- stderr (filtered) --- [agent/cli-backend] cli session history refused across auth boundary: reason=auth-unknown [agent/cli-backend] cli live session start: provider=claude-cli model=claude-haiku-5-5 activeSessions=1 [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=cli:claude-cli:owner: durationMs=2166285 error="CLI JSONL output exceeded 8388608 characters; refusing to parse output." errorName=FailoverError [agent/cli-backend] cli terminal failure: provider=claude-cli model=claude-haiku-5-5 durationMs=2166902 runId= error=CLI JSONL output exceeded 8388608 characters; refusing to parse output. [model-fallback/decision] model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed requested=anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5 candidate=anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5 reason=format next=none [state/agent-db] agent database clean-close receipt: written; agent=main CLI JSONL output exceeded 8388608 characters; refusing to parse output. exit 1 (elapsed 2174s) --- Claude Code stdout (1980-step prompt) --- tool_use blocks: 1746; tool results: 1748; last echoed step: step-1744 ```
this PR 21fe91648a3: redacted output ``` $ openclaw agent exec --config openclaw.json --cwd work --message-file work/prompt.txt --thinking low --timeout 7200 --json { "ok": true, "status": "ok", "final": "DONE", "payloads": [ { "text": "DONE", "mediaUrl": null } ], "usage": { "input": 2, "output": 4, "cacheRead": 42888, "cacheWrite": 93, "cacheWrite1h": 93 }, "toolSummary": { "calls": 1982, "tools": [ "exec", "ToolSearch", "mcp__openclaw__exec" ], "failures": 1 }, "model": "claude-haiku-5-5", "provider": "anthropic", "sessionId": "" } --- stderr (filtered) --- [agent/cli-backend] cli session history refused across auth boundary: reason=auth-unknown [agent/cli-backend] cli live session start: provider=claude-cli model=claude-haiku-5-5 activeSessions=1 [state/agent-db] agent database clean-close receipt: written; agent=main [agent/cli-backend] cli turn: provider=claude-cli model=claude-haiku-5-5 durationMs=2873510 outBytes=4 outHash= [state/agent-db] agent database clean-close receipt: written; agent=main exit 0 (elapsed 2882s) --- Claude Code stdout (1980-step prompt) --- tool_use blocks: 1982; tool results: 1984; last echoed step: step-1980 ```
Redaction replaced run and session ids, hashes and temporary paths, and dropped repeated skill-loading lines. This run shape exercises stop frames and message deltas; it has almost no thinking, so the signature and progress-tick savings show in the captured-stream breakdown below. **Charge breakdown on captured streams.** Each line fed through `chargeClaudeStreamJsonLine` from `main` (67c3c3abfa6) and from this PR, applying the real limits: | Capture | `main` | this PR | | --- | --- | --- | | 41,071 real records, Claude Code 2.1.310 (694 completed gateway turns) | 12,316,948 chars, 12,697 lines | 9,639,274, 9,099 | | One complete real turn, Claude Code 2.1.296 (Haiku, thinking, 8 tools) | 469,353, 130 | 444,427, 88 | | Four failed production turns (41 to 73 minutes, 283 to 448 tool calls), rebuilt from their transcripts (estimates) | 5.09 to 5.43 MB (61 to 65%) | 4.14 to 4.37 MB (49 to 52%) | The four production turns failed on `main` before #186085 at 109 to 114 percent of the budget; #186085 brings them to 61 to 65 percent, and this change takes off another 0.95 to 1.06 MB each. **Tests and checks** (macOS, Node 24). The RED and mutation runs were done at 11b83ab6550; the code and test changes in this PR are byte-identical at the current head (only the docs paragraph was rewrapped around a `main` edit). Everything else was rerun at the current head ff03f752ae4 (this branch merged with `main` 638a1851e7e), from a fresh clone: - `src/agents/cli-output-control-frames.test.ts` (new): 45 passed. Covers the Claude Code 2.1.296 shape of each frame kind (exact charge and line accounting), wire padding, index-less and child-attributed frames, the 8 KiB allowance (at, just over, far over, with padding), every metadata cap at its limit, and full accounting for each rejected shape above. It also checks that progress ticks and tool starts still reach the parser callbacks, that 20,001 progress or stop frames complete, that signature and message deltas at the allowance stop on the 20,001st line, and that progress, block-stop and message-stop floods hit the 8 MiB budget at the computed frame. - RED: with only `cli-output-stream-limits.ts` reverted to `main`, 26 fail and 19 pass. 21 single-site mutations of the production file (zero charges, dropped or moved metadata caps, `thinking_display` anywhere, unknown event or delta keys, no padding, empty signatures, no index check, skipping the shared envelope check, no overflow charge, larger allowance, line-count flips, no estimate charge): 20 fail at least one test. The survivor removes the `thinking === ""` guard on progress ticks; it is equivalent today because the #186085 partial-frame rule charges any thinking delta with text first, and the guard stays so the control-frame rule never discounts thinking text on its own. - All 12 `src/agents/cli-output*.test.ts` files: 284 passed. `src/agents/cli-runner/` (74 files): 911 passed. - `cli-output-partial-messages.test.ts` drops its empty-thinking-progress and signature-delta rows, which expected full accounting for the frames this PR now discounts; the new suite covers both shapes with their new charges. The net test growth (264 lines) is recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/claude-stream-control-frames.txt`; `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base 638a1851e7e` (6,556,625 lines, ceiling 6,556,696) and `git diff --check` pass. - The lanes that were red on fe88e02d1ed now pass: `pnpm tsgo:prod`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm tsgo:scripts`, `pnpm check:test-types`, `pnpm tsgo:core:test`, and `pnpm check:baseline-ratchets --base 638a1851e7e` (all 9 ratchets ok). - `pnpm check:changed --base 638a1851e7e` passes every step (including lint, format, dead-export scan, and core typecheck) except `changelog attributions`, which flags 20 existing `Thanks @...` lines in `CHANGELOG/*.md`. This PR touches no changelog file, and the check prints the same output on `main` 638a1851e7e. - Why fe88e02d1ed was red: CI tested it merged with `main` f2c27f09ea5. Every failure came from that base and shows up the same on `main` 7c2ff8f775a (the merge base at that point) with no changes from this PR. The type lanes all failed on one error in a file this PR does not touch: `ui/src/components/browser/browser-panel-render.tsx(149,11): error TS2322`, fixed on `main` by #192868. The ratchet lane failed on `test-lines`: `over by: 191`. `main` alone was over by the same 191 lines, and #192905 reconciled them; this PR's own +264 is covered by its allocation. prs.title: fix(oc-path): keep file I/O failures inside the documented CLI error envelope
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw path` documents that JSON mode reports path/file errors as one object — `{ ok: false, error: { type: "cli_error", code, message } }` — and that file errors exit `2` (`docs/cli/path.md`, exit-code table). Only the domain checks honoured that contract. Two file-system calls sat outside any error boundary:

- `loadOcPathFile` awaited `fs.open(...)` **before** its `try`, so `ENOENT` / `EACCES` / `EISDIR` / `EMFILE` escaped from every verb that loads a file (`resolve`, `find`, `set`, `emit`).
- `set` awaited `fs.writeFile(...)` with no guard, so `ENOSPC` / `EACCES` escaped there.

Users got the generic failure envelope instead: exit `1`, no domain `code`, and in human mode only a bare `ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '…'` line with no `OC_PATH_` identifier.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both boundaries now report through the module's existing `emitError` owner, which already produced the documented envelope for the domain errors, and set `process.exitCode = 2`:

- read side → `OC_PATH_FILE_UNREADABLE`
- write side → `OC_PATH_WRITE_FAILED`

The parse calls (`parseJsonc` / `parseJsonl` / `parseYaml` / `parseMd`) stay outside the new `catch`, so parse errors keep their current propagation and are never relabelled as I/O failures. The existing domain codes (`OC_PATH_FILE_NOT_REGULAR`, `OC_PATH_INPUT_TOO_LARGE` / `OC_JSONC_INPUT_TOO_LARGE`, `OC_PATH_INPUT_NOT_UTF8`) are untouched. No new abstraction, no new option, no change to the write mechanism.

Docs: the exit-2 row, the JSON-envelope paragraph, and the `set` exit note now name both codes. Tests: four cases folded into the existing `resolve` and `set` suites. To stay under the 1000-line `max-lines` cap, the quoted-literal `it.each` case moved verbatim into `cli.quoted-literals.test-support.ts` and is registered from the same suite; `config/test-lines-allocations/oc-path-cli-fs-error-envelope.txt` carries the 70-line test budget.

## User Impact

A missing or unreadable file, or an unwritable target, now fails exactly like every other `openclaw path` error: one JSON object carrying `error.code` in JSON mode, `CODE: reason` on stderr in human mode, and exit `2`. Scripts that branch on `error.code` can finally tell an I/O failure apart from a parse error or a refused pattern, and human-mode output names the file and the cause instead of only the raw `errno` string.

## Evidence

Real CLI, final head, run from the worktree with an isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and the `oc-path` plugin enabled (`openclaw path` is disabled by default). "before" is `origin/main` with the same command and workspace.

| # | Command | before (`origin/main`) | after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `path resolve oc://does-not-exist.md/heading --human` | exit `1`; stderr `ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '…'` (no code) | exit `2`; stderr `OC_PATH_FILE_UNREADABLE: failed to read …/does-not-exist.md: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '…'` |
| 2 | same, `--json` | exit `1`; `{"ok":false,"error":{"type":"cli_error","message":"ENOENT: …"}}` — no `code` | exit `2`; `{"ok":false,"error":{"type":"cli_error","code":"OC_PATH_FILE_UNREADABLE","message":"failed to read …: ENOENT: …"}}` |
| 3 | `path set oc://note.md/[frontmatter]/title changed --json` on a `chmod 444` file | exit `1`; no `code` | exit `2`; `{"ok":false,"error":{"type":"cli_error","code":"OC_PATH_WRITE_FAILED","message":"failed to write …/note.md: EACCES: permission denied, open '…'"}}`; file sha256 unchanged |
| 4 | control: `path resolve oc://x/../y --json` | exit `2` + domain `code` | exit `2` + same domain `code` (no regression) |

Regression tests are red on the base and green with the fix — on `origin/main` the two new cases fail as thrown `ENOENT` / `EACCES` because the helpers rethrow non-`CommanderError` values, which is exactly the unhandled escape this PR closes.

```
vitest run extensions/oc-path/src/cli.test.ts
  Tests  81 passed | 4 failed (85)
```

The 4 failures are pre-existing on `origin/main` in this environment: they shell out to `patch`, which is absent (`spawnSync patch ENOENT`).

```
check-test-lines-ratchet:  Test lines OK: 6556082; ceiling: 6556091; slack: 9.
check-line-cap-ratchet:    OK (3 changed source files; no new violations or growth)
oxlint (changed files):    0 warnings, 0 errors
tsc -p (oc-path only):     0 errors
```

Collision check on today's open-PR snapshot: `#172164` also edits `extensions/oc-path/src/cli.test.ts` but in a different region (wildcard array-path coverage, `@@1004`) and does not cover this bug; `#193166` is rewriting the same `docs/cli/path.md` exit-code paragraph, so one of the two will need a trivial rebase. No open PR touches `extensions/oc-path/src/cli.ts`.

Note: because the write test target is `chmod 444`, the write never starts and the bytes stay intact. This PR does not change `fs.writeFile`'s truncate-then-write behaviour, so a mid-write failure can still lose the old content; that is a separate atomic-write concern.

Review follow-up (`c71d080e0`): the write-denial case now skips privileged runners, using the same guard as `src/memory/root-memory-files.test.ts` (`process.getuid?.() !== 0`), because a DAC-override runner ignores the `0o444` mode. Both diagnostics also end with the next step, and the write one states explicitly that a partway failure may leave the file incomplete rather than implying the old bytes survived.

prs.title: fix(macos): keep Apple Event permission probes off the cooperative thread pool
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On 2026.9.3 the macOS app periodically goes dead while still running: the paired node shows **offline** in the Gateway dashboard although the Mac is on and the TCP session to the Gateway is still ESTABLISHED (32 KB of unread bytes sitting in the receive queue), the menu bar item stops opening its menu, and the process ignores SIGTERM (needs SIGKILL). It "fixes itself" only when the app is relaunched.

## Root cause

`AppleEventPermissionProbe.state` runs the blocking `AEDeterminePermissionToAutomateTarget` in `Task.detached`, which schedules onto the Swift cooperative thread pool. The call blocks until Terminal answers the Apple Event handshake (and, when `askUserIfNeeded`, until the user answers tccd). `MacNodeModeCoordinator` re-probes permissions on every refresh trigger (`UserDefaults.didChangeNotification`, config change, permissions change, app activation, reconnect probe), so a slow Terminal under system load lets probes stack up.

A 3 s `sample` of the wedged process showed **all 16 cooperative threads** parked here, main thread idle:

```
DispatchQueue_18: com.apple.root.user-initiated-qos.cooperative
  closure #1 in AppleEventPermissionProbe.state(askUserIfNeeded:)
    AppleEventPermissionProbe.determineTerminalPermission(askUserIfNeeded:)
      AEDeterminePermissionToAutomateTarget
        _dispatch_semaphore_wait_slow
          semaphore_wait_trap
```

Terminal automation was already **granted** in TCC (`kTCCServiceAppleEvents ai.openclaw.mac → com.apple.Terminal = 2`), so this was not a pending prompt. Once the pool is exhausted nothing async in the app can run, including the gateway websocket receive and the status item, and any continuation the AE reply needs can never be scheduled.

## Fix

- Run the blocking probe on a dedicated `DispatchQueue` (concurrent, so a prompt is never queued behind a hung passive check), bridged with a `CheckedContinuation`, so it never pins a cooperative thread.
- Single-flight concurrent callers per `askUserIfNeeded` value through a small actor (`AppleEventPermissionProbeCoordinator`), so at most one probe blocks at a time regardless of how many refreshes fire.
- Bound passive (non-prompting) probes with a 10 s timeout that surfaces as `.failed(errAETimeout)` → capability `.unknown`, instead of hanging the caller. Prompting probes keep waiting on the user.

No change to call sites; `AppleEventPermissionProbe.live` and `TerminalAutomationPermission` keep their API.

## Evidence

- `concurrent passive checks share one blocking probe`: 32 concurrent passive `state` calls → exactly one `determine` call, all callers get the result.
- `a hung passive probe times out instead of blocking callers`: a `determine` that never returns yields `.failed(errAETimeout)` in ~200 ms with a 200 ms timeout.
- `interactive prompts are never timed out`.
- Existing suite unchanged and green (12/12).
- Live observation, 2026-09-09: reproduced twice on the same Mac (2026.9.3 release build). Both times `netstat -anv -p tcp` showed the OpenClaw-owned socket to the Gateway ESTABLISHED with 32,778 and 52,617 bytes in Recv-Q, and `sample <pid> 2` showed 16 and 17 frames in `AEDeterminePermissionToAutomateTarget`. The second occurrence started within 60 s of a Gateway restart, i.e. on the reconnect refresh path. `pkill -9` + relaunch cleared it each time.

`swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests` ✅, `scripts/format-swift.sh macos` ✅, `scripts/lint-swift.sh macos` ✅ (Xcode 26.6 / Swift 6.3.3).

## Review follow-up (revision 3)

Both P2 findings are addressed:

- **Retain the in-flight operation after a caller times out.** The coordinator now keeps the operation in `inFlight` until the native call actually returns. Caller deadlines are measured from the operation's start, so once the deadline has passed later passive callers answer `errAETimeout` immediately and never enqueue a second native call. When the target replies, the tracked operation drains and the next probe runs fresh. Covered by the new test `timed-out callers never enqueue a second native call behind the hung one` (second caller answers in < 150 ms with `callCount == 1`, operation still in flight; after release the next probe runs and `callCount == 2`).
- **Synchronize overlapping callers before releasing the test probe.** The concurrency test now waits until all 32 callers are parked on the coordinator (`waiterCount == 32`) before releasing, and `BlockingProbeGate.release()` opens the gate permanently so every native call a test started completes during cleanup.

The probe queue is concurrent so an interactive prompt is never queued behind a hung passive check.

## After-fix native proof

Debug build of this branch on a second Mac (macOS 26.4.1, Xcode 26.6), run in a throwaway app profile pointed at a remote Gateway URL that refuses connections (so every reconnect attempt builds a manifest and evaluates permissions). Terminal.app, the Apple Event target, was frozen with `SIGSTOP` so the probe could not get a reply, then resumed with `SIGCONT`. The passive probe returned `noErr` on this host: its TCC database already holds an allowed `kTCCServiceAppleEvents` row for bundle id `ai.openclaw.mac` → `com.apple.Terminal`, which the debug build shares, so recovery shows as a normal `returned 0`.

| Phase | `sample` probe frames | Cooperative-pool frames in the probe | `openclaw-mac status` (control socket) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline | 0 | 0 | ok |
| Terminal frozen, 55 s | 1, on `DispatchQueue: ai.openclaw.apple-event-permission (concurrent)` | 0 | ok |
| Terminal resumed, 50 s later | 0 | 0 | ok |

Unified log (`ai.openclaw`/`AppleEventPermissionProbe`), timestamps relative to the freeze:

```
-27 s  I  probe ask=false returned 0 after 0.172922083 seconds
-19 s  I  probe ask=false returned 0 after 0.033881875 seconds
-10 s  I  probe ask=false returned 0 after 0.208797417 seconds
  0 s     Terminal.app frozen (SIGSTOP)
+17 s  E  probe ask=false timed out after 10.0 seconds; operation retained
+58 s     Terminal.app resumed (SIGCONT)
+58 s  I  probe ask=false returned 0 after 50.992712958 seconds
+66 s  I  probe ask=false returned 0 after 0.032903625 seconds
+97 s  I  probe ask=false returned 0 after 0.137408166 seconds
```

No second native call started while the first was hung (the only lines between the freeze and the resume are the single timeout), the retained call returned as soon as Terminal answered, and the probes after it ran fresh.

The app answered its control socket throughout, kept exactly one blocked thread (on the private queue, never the cooperative pool), released it when Terminal answered, and quit within 1 s of `SIGTERM` afterwards. On the release build the same condition ends with 13 to 17 cooperative threads blocked, a dead status menu, and `SIGTERM` ignored (openclaw/openclaw#146030).

Filtered test run (`swift test --filter AppleEventPermissionTests`, private HOME, throwaway profile, `--skip-build`): 13 tests, 0 failures. Full native suite left to the `macos-swift` CI job per `apps/macos/AGENTS.md`.

### Signed-bundle run (signing provenance)

The run above used the bare SwiftPM debug binary (ad-hoc signed). Repeated on the same Mac with a full `scripts/package-mac-app.sh` bundle of head `621a4a4d8`, signed through `scripts/codesign-mac-app.sh` with a real Apple Development certificate and kept at the fixed path the permissions guide asks for (`<checkout>/dist/OpenClaw.app`). Provenance, identity details redacted:

```
Identifier=ai.openclaw.mac.debug
Format=app bundle with Mach-O thin (arm64)
CodeDirectory v=20500 flags=0x10000(runtime)
Authority=Apple Development: <redacted>
Authority=Apple Worldwide Developer Relations Certification Authority
Authority=Apple Root CA
TeamIdentifier=<redacted, set>
Sealed Resources version=2 rules=13 files=42384
codesign --verify --deep --strict: OK
```

`ai.openclaw.mac.debug` has no Automation grant on this Mac, so the passive probe's real answer is `-1744` (`errAEEventWouldRequireUserConsent`), returned without a prompt once Terminal answers. Same procedure (throwaway profile, refusing Gateway URL, Terminal `SIGSTOP` for 55 s, then `SIGCONT`):

| Phase | `sample` probe frames | Cooperative-pool frames in the probe | `openclaw-mac status` (control socket) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline | 0 | 0 | ok |
| Terminal frozen, 55 s | 1, on the private queue | 0 | ok |
| Terminal resumed, 50 s later | 0 | 0 | ok |

```
-28 s  I  probe ask=false returned -1744 after 0.207445334 seconds
  0 s     Terminal.app frozen (SIGSTOP)
+14 s  E  probe ask=false timed out after 10.0 seconds; operation retained
+58 s     Terminal.app resumed (SIGCONT)
+58 s  I  probe ask=false returned -1744 after 54.768811875 seconds
```

One blocked native call, no second call queued behind it, bounded caller wait, control socket answering throughout, the retained call returning the moment Terminal resumed, and the app quitting within 1 s of `SIGTERM` afterwards.

## Release note

Fix the macOS app wedging (node offline while TCP alive, menu bar item unresponsive, ignores SIGTERM) when concurrent Terminal Automation permission probes exhausted the Swift cooperative thread pool.

Diagnosed and written with Claude Code: https://claude.ai/code/session_014TmTvgdhcL7bPCwg3f8B6G
Review follow-up, after-fix proof, and this revision: https://claude.ai/code/session_01RW45HgmUaFSiM4DSZGrVSp

prs.title: fix(memory): promotion stalls when MEMORY.md is near its budget and holds consolidation sections (#163900)
prs.body:
## Current-head verification (November 7, 2026)

Head 09541c5c3e9e0e05131805a7dcdfe96b7ec8aa02 merges main 80795a82a614193bdf9f6bb3b98104d4ee94350a without rewriting contributor ancestry. The PR-only diff remains the same three files: docs/concepts/dreaming.md and two memory-core budget files.

At this head, all four budget, promotion, consolidation, and project-consolidation suites passed (131 tests); extension and extension-test typechecks, targeted formatting, pnpm build, and independent P0-P2 review passed.

Changed-file checks passed 30 of 31 gates. The only local failure is changelog-attributions on unchanged upstream release-owned entries; this PR changes no changelog. The local test-line ratchet now passes: 6,556,664 lines versus a 6,556,684 ceiling, with 20 lines of slack. No allocation or baseline was changed by this PR. The previous head failed hosted test-line CI by 75 lines; current-head hosted checks-fast-baseline-ratchets and openclaw/ci-gate passed with no failed required checks. The production-flow proof below remains historical, not a new native run.

Related: #163900

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Dreaming and `openclaw memory promote --apply` stop adding durable memories near the `MEMORY.md` budget when the existing generated sections were written by deep consolidation.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Summary

Use the existing bounded compactor for both promotion and consolidation output, while preserving handwritten content.

### Root Cause

`extensions/memory-core/src/memory-budget.ts:isGeneratedPromotionBlock` previously recognized only promotion headings and promotion markers. The consolidation writer emits `## Consolidated Memory (...)` and can put a lineage marker before the promotion marker, so its generated sections were always preserved.

### Changes

- Recognize both generated section headings and the consolidation writer's optional lineage marker.
- Require each deletion-qualifying marker line to be exactly one HTML comment.
- Preserve the existing oldest-first order, prior-entry loss bound, and caller-owned final budget check.

## User Impact

Promotion can reclaim an eligible old consolidation section instead of deferring every new memory. Sections containing handwritten text, annotated markers, or an orphaned lineage marker remain intact.

## Evidence

### Current integration: November 1, 2026

Head `7914a956c8d38ced31bb113454fc2284297cbfa5` merges main `c97faa7ae259970cd1ca953ad0783efaa94c2118` without rewriting contributor ancestry. The resolution preserves main's single-comment promotion-marker predicate and current bootstrap-budget handling, plus this PR's consolidation heading and lineage recognition. The main-relative change remains three files.

### Distinction from #164089

#164089 landed as `49600b5cf8f3f387e5f8b90c7654c712432e8f71` and closed #163900. It repairs handwritten comments attached to promotion markers, but does not recognize consolidation headings or lineage markers. This PR incorporates that repair rather than duplicating it.

A fresh isolated probe of the actual production compaction owner at main `c97faa7ae259970cd1ca953ad0783efaa94c2118`, with four lineage-bearing consolidation sections and a 0.25 prior-entry loss allowance, confirms the remaining distinction:

```text
main:       droppedDates=[]; next section does not fit
integrated: droppedDates=["2026-09-01"]; next section fits
handwritten fact preserved=true
annotated consolidation section preserved=true
```

That probe is supporting production-owner evidence, not a new built-CLI or live Dreaming capture.

### Real Behavior Proof

The original built-CLI before/after captures below are retained historical evidence of the parser repair, not new executions on the integration head.

On macOS arm64 with isolated state, a 9,768-byte `MEMORY.md` contained 265 handwritten lines and four consolidation sections, each with a plain and lineage-tracked entry. The same `memory rem-backfill --stage-short-term` and `memory promote --apply` commands produced:

| Observation | Main `350e91cf765` | Repaired parser |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Promotion | Deferred: `MEMORY.md budget exceeded (10254 > 10000 chars)` | `appended=1` |
| Resulting file | 9,768 bytes, unchanged | 9,142 bytes |
| Oldest eligible section | Retained | Reclaimed within the 0.25 loss bound |
| Handwritten lines retained | 265 | 265 |

The subsequent built-CLI inline-note comparison used a 9,748-byte file with 130 handwritten lines and five consolidation sections. On `5f70c6640ef`, promotion deleted the annotated oldest section and its note. On repaired head `314ca9f748a`, it preserved that section byte for byte, reclaimed the next clean section, retained all 130 handwritten lines, and still reported `appended=1`.

### Test (supporting)

On the integrated tree, Node 24.22.1 and the pinned repository tools:

- The four compaction, promotion, consolidation, and project-consolidation suites pass: 131 tests; 47.17 seconds total wall time.
- Extension production and extension test typechecks pass.
- Targeted typed lint, formatting of all three changed files, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Fresh independent P0-P2 review of the complete main-relative patch reports no actionable findings.
- The original heading/lineage and inline-note regressions were red before their respective repairs.

At current head 09541c5c3e9, the full changed-file run completed: 30 of 31 gates passed, with only inherited changelog attributions failing. The local test-line ratchet passed with 20 lines of slack. Earlier head 7914a956c8d hosted CI was green and ClawSweeper accepted the real behavior proof; neither historical outcome is claimed as current-head CI, whose test-line ratchet and ci-gate both passed.

## Risk

Compaction can remove only fully generated sections within the existing entry-loss bound. Handwritten text and annotated or orphaned markers keep their entire section ineligible for deletion. No schema, persisted format, configuration option, or retention policy changes.

## Changelog

Release-note context: Dreaming promotion no longer stalls on eligible consolidation-written sections near the memory budget. Release-owned changelog files are unchanged.

## Notes

AI-assisted: yes. Current-head local checks and the independent review are scoped above; built-CLI proof belongs to the identified earlier heads, and current-head hosted test-line ratchet and ci-gate both passed. Configurable budgets, partial-batch admission, and deferral observability remain outside this repair.

prs.title: perf(android): evaluate release task parallelism
prs.body:
## Experiment

Measure whether enabling Gradle cross-project task execution improves Android phone/Wear release builds. The measured baseline reports `parallelProjectExecution=false` and eight worker leases. Independent work may overlap with `--parallel`; R8 already uses threads, so contention and peak memory are measured rather than assuming a speedup. Production configuration remains unchanged during this draft experiment.

The committed workload reuses the ten-build heap experiment at `7a764c59c5f8bbd9a0c5eafa401c3afcb54c347e`, adapted to vary only `--no-parallel` versus `--parallel`. Both variants retain the 3 GiB heap, Parallel GC, fixed version/codes/timestamp, signing validation, lint, R8, Wear and phone bundle tasks, and two signature checks. Tooling API parallelism is explicitly disabled for both, leaving this comparison about CLI task execution. No tasks or release checks are removed.

The temporary diagnostic operation uses the same `blacksmith-8vcpu-ubuntu-2404` release runner and frozen source `5e4684a1d8b031bd3eae670502d0b5470af213db`. It has read-only repository permissions, no release environment or real signing credentials, and no Play/Firebase upload. Its disposable benchmark key cannot authorize a real release. Dependency caching is restore-only; task-output caching is disabled.

## Acceptance rule, recorded before dispatch

Five serial pairs on one runner, in AB, BA, AB, BA, AB order. Before every sample restore identical pristine source and dependency snapshots at the same paths and stop previous Gradle/Kotlin JVMs. Report medians, nearest-rank p95/max, spread, pair wins, sampled Java CPU and aggregate RSS, available host memory/load, and OOM counters. Dependency cache is warm; task outputs and JVMs are fresh for each sample.

A candidate qualifies only with:

- At least 5% and five seconds lower median bundle time, winning at least four of five pairs.
- No regression in bundle p95, complete signing-preflight/build/signature median, median sampled Java CPU, or maximum aggregate Java RSS; no OOM.
- All ten builds and twenty individual signature checks passing with identical complete task/outcome inventories, unchanged eight-worker limit, and actual serial/parallel execution settings confirmed from Gradle logs.
- No 20% regression in any measured performance cell. A resource tradeoff is not implicitly accepted.

If this fails, close the experiment without changing production. If it qualifies, remove the temporary workflow operation/job, benchmark script, and test-option changes; replace them with the focused production change and documentation, complete review, mark ready, and watch CI. Do not merge this PR. Android Internal validation follows a separately approved merge.

## Result: rejected; production unchanged

[Nonpublishing benchmark run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42332355609) collected all ten samples successfully in 29m20s. Workload commit: `3efe29686d1981a1f60f4be5af62169f9739dd57`; frozen source: `5e4684a1d8b031bd3eae670502d0b5470af213db`. The runner reported eight available CPUs and 30.95 GiB RAM. The `android-release-gradle-parallel-42332355609` artifact retains root/sample receipts, build and signature logs, complete Gradle profiles, and one-second resource samples for seven days. The reproducible workload remains committed on this experiment branch.

All ten builds and twenty individual bundle signature checks passed. Each build had the same 163 task/outcome rows and `149 actionable tasks: 146 executed, 3 up-to-date`. Actual daemon commands retained 3 GiB and Parallel GC. Both preflight and bundle logs confirmed eight worker leases, Tooling API parallelism disabled, and the intended serial or parallel task-execution mode. Every sample recorded zero change in the host kernel OOM-kill counter. The cgroup counters remained unavailable. No OOM errors were found in the logs. Nothing was uploaded to Play or Firebase.

| Metric | Serial median | Parallel median | Serial p95/max | Parallel p95/max |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Bundle build | 131.611 s | 138.779 s | 173.197 s | 166.777 s |
| Signing preflight + build + signature checks | 138.953 s | 146.226 s | 182.333 s | 175.884 s |
| Java CPU | 797.480 CPU-s | 900.110 CPU-s | 1097.210 CPU-s | 1091.140 CPU-s |
| Aggregate Java peak RSS per sample | 6.740 GiB | 6.768 GiB | 6.875 GiB | 6.796 GiB |
| Minimum available host RAM per sample | 23.145 GiB | 23.141 GiB | 23.227 GiB | 23.479 GiB |
| Host CPU busy per sample | 74.441 % | 78.510 % | 76.973 % | 79.026 % |

Five samples per variant; nearest-rank p95 is the maximum at this sample count. Bundle ranges: 128.291–173.197s serial and 128.807–166.777s parallel. Complete-workload ranges: 135.265–182.333s and 135.446–175.884s. Resource sampling covers signing preflight through final signature verification. Java CPU is sampled aggregate process CPU time; memory is sampled aggregate Java RSS.

| Pair | Order | Serial bundle | Parallel bundle | Parallel saving |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 01 | serial → parallel | 131.611s | 128.807s | +2.804s (+2.13%) |
| 02 | parallel → serial | 173.197s | 166.777s | +6.420s (+3.71%) |
| 03 | serial → parallel | 164.017s | 151.872s | +12.145s (+7.40%) |
| 04 | parallel → serial | 129.065s | 132.137s | -3.073s (-2.38%) |
| 05 | serial → parallel | 128.291s | 138.779s | -10.488s (-8.18%) |

Parallel execution fails the preregistered rule: median bundle time increases **7.168s (5.45%)**, complete-workload median increases **7.274s (5.23%)**, median Java CPU increases **12.87%**, and it wins only **three of five pairs**. Tail time improves and maximum sampled RSS decreases 1.15%, but those improvements do not satisfy the speed, consistency, complete-workload, and CPU requirements. The wide timing spread is retained; no samples were discarded or replaced. This result does not establish that parallel execution is always slower, but it provides no qualifying improvement for this release workload.

The task profiles show longer median durations for the main phone R8 task (57.317 → 62.270s), phone lint analysis (47.164 → 49.212s), and phone Kotlin compilation (45.121 → 48.984s). Wear Kotlin compilation rises 9.949 → 12.492s (+25.6%). These task durations can overlap and are not additive wall time. The profiles and increased CPU are consistent with added contention; they do not independently prove its cause.

## Preparation proof and final state

JavaScript syntax, targeted scripts lint, formatting, whitespace, workflow lint/security checks, and the focused manual/exact-SHA/secretless diagnostic contract passed. Independent AutoReview at P0–P2 is scoped-clean after fixing ambiguous root collection-status wording. The workflow reports collection complete with performance acceptance pending offline analysis; this table records that analysis and its rejected verdict.

Hosted Workflow Sanity passed. All current draft-PR checks are terminal with no failures; broad CI was skipped for this draft. No production setting is changed, and this PR will not merge. The temporary workflow operation, benchmark script, and test-option changes remain only on the closed experiment branch.

Simplification pass: the experiment reused the prior committed harness and existing manual diagnostic workflow. No ongoing benchmark service, runner fanout, cache writer, or production build policy was added.

prs.title: fix(templates): avoid descriptor exhaustion with many workspace sources
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw templates validate` and `build` reject a valid project containing many tiny workspace files when its file count exceeds the process descriptor limit.

## User Impact

User impact: projects within the existing file-size and aggregate byte limits can validate and build without raising the system's open-file limit.

## Why This Change Was Made

Release each source handle after the metadata preflight, then read each file through the existing bounded safe-reader owner. The aggregate preflight still happens before reading contents; per-file/actual aggregate limits, hardlink and symlink checks, source ordering and digest inputs are retained. This trades a second sequential open per source for bounded descriptor usage.

## Evidence

Real CLI comparison on base `fc7f037d6b97f3156f50437e5bcd06332dfd2343` and the fix, using identical generated project bytes in separate isolated directories:

| Actual CLI invocation | Base | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Validate 16 sources, `ulimit -n 1024` | succeeds | succeeds |
| Validate 1,100 sources, `ulimit -n 4096` | succeeds | succeeds |
| Validate 1,100 sources, `ulimit -n 1024` | fails: `workspace_source_invalid` at source 1005 | succeeds |
| Build 1,100 sources, `ulimit -n 1024` | not separately replayed | succeeds; 1,102 archive entries and all 1,100 source files byte-verified |

<details>
<summary>Reproduction through the shipped CLI</summary>

After preparing the repository CLI build with `pnpm openclaw templates --help`, create the fixture with Node:

```js
// Save as make-project.mjs, then: node make-project.mjs /tmp/template-many
import { mkdir, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { join } from 'node:path';
const project = process.argv[2];
await mkdir(join(project, 'files'), { recursive: true });
await writeFile(join(project, 'package.json'), JSON.stringify({
  name: 'many-files', version: '1.0.0', openclaw: { template: 'CLAW.md' },
}));
const files = [];
for (let i = 0; i < 1100; i++) {
  const source = `files/source-${String(i).padStart(4, '0')}.txt`;
  await writeFile(join(project, source), `Reference ${i}\n`);
  files.push({ source, path: `reference/source-${i}.txt` });
}
await writeFile(join(project, 'CLAW.md'), `---\n${JSON.stringify({
  schemaVersion: 1, agent: { id: 'reader-agent' }, workspace: { files },
})}\n---\nReference assistant.\n`);
```

```sh
(ulimit -n 4096; pnpm openclaw templates validate /tmp/template-many --json)
(ulimit -n 1024; pnpm openclaw templates validate /tmp/template-many --json)
(ulimit -n 1024; pnpm openclaw templates build /tmp/template-many --out /tmp/template-many.tgz --json)
```

</details>

The committed process regression sets a real 128-descriptor limit: a 16-source control builds successfully, then the same child process builds 160 sources and verifies 162 archive entries. It fails on the base and passes with this fix. Reader, schema, project and descriptor regressions: 90 passed, 1 skipped. The new test has its own exact 81 LF allocation; the descriptor assertion takes ~1.7 s, while cold runtime-worker compilation dominates the ~231 s focused run. The POSIX limit test skips Windows; Windows runtime behavior and a full declaration build were not replayed locally. Targeted type-aware lint, the official templates typecheck shard, formatter Node/Bun parity and the test-line ratchet pass. Full PR CI provides the broad check.

### Captured CLI output

Actual CLI JSON excerpts, with the large manifest/archive file lists omitted and temporary fixture roots replaced by `/proof/base` and `/proof/fixed`.

Before (pinned base):

```text
$ (ulimit -n 1024; pnpm openclaw templates validate /proof/base/project --json)
exit 0
{
  "schemaVersion": "openclaw.templateProject.v1",
  "stability": "experimental",
  "ok": true,
  "root": "/proof/base/project",
  "source": {
    "kind": "package",
    "name": "many-files",
    "version": "1.0.0",
    "packageRoot": "/proof/base/project",
    "manifestPath": "/proof/base/project/CLAW.md",

  },

}
$ (ulimit -n 4096; pnpm openclaw templates validate /proof/base/project --json)
```

prs.title: feat(channels): add dead-letter deletion commands
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #145870.

Operators can inspect and resubmit failed channel ingress events but cannot intentionally discard an unrecoverable dead letter. This adds `channels dead-letters delete <event-id>` and account-scoped `channels dead-letters purge`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Deletion runs through the current shared-state ingress worker and its transaction/commit admission. Commands snapshot failure identity before confirmation; deletion compares event ID, update time, receive time, and attempt count, retaining events resubmitted or changed afterward. Statements use bounded batches of portable field comparisons within one transaction, avoiding SQLite parameter limits and SQLite-only JSON comparisons. The public Plugin SDK queue contract remains unchanged.

## User Impact

Both commands require interactive confirmation unless `--force` is supplied, and support `--json`. Active and completed events and other channel/accounts are preserved. Physical discard removes the failed row and its queue-level duplicate barrier, permitting later delivery with the same event ID to be accepted again.

## Evidence

- Focused queue, authority, pruning, health, command, and CLI tests: 79 tests passed across 7 files.
- Regression coverage verifies worker execution, cached health invalidation, transaction/commit authority revocation, replacement failure preservation, and a 40,001-entry selection.
- `pnpm build` passed with supported Node 24.22.1.
- Real isolated-state `pnpm openclaw` flow passed: non-interactive deletion refused without `--force`; single delete returned `deleted: true`; purge deleted the remaining one failed event; another account retained its failure. Follow-up queue verification retained the pending event, recognized the completed event, and accepted replay of the deleted ID.
- Core, all core-test, and extension-test typecheck graphs passed (the latter after correcting the SDK fixture return contract); changed-file lint, format, SDK/plugin boundaries, dialect guard, and line caps passed.
- `pnpm docs:check-links`: 15,845 links checked, zero broken links.
- Fresh independent source review found two issues (SDK parameter typing and PostgreSQL query compatibility); both were fixed and the follow-up review reported no P0–P2 findings. The `autoreview` CLI itself could not produce a verdict because its reviewer authentication failed.
- `git diff --check upstream/main` passed.
- The dead-export guard reports 5 script, 14 production, and 10 full-tree findings. The exact same command on detached `main@7a1d72c4410` reports identical findings in every section; no finding was introduced by this PR. This inherited failure is reported rather than suppressed.
- The previous failed daemon install/update and timeout tests are fixed by main commits `7471ac64552` (#147398) and `65b5a3ecae5` (#147117), both included by the conflict-resolution merge.

## CI Failure Attribution

The first updated-head run [39940436145](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39940436145) tested merge `e2f42b9a2c3c` against main `55477abbbb5066644339e44c56974e7ab0e8c754`. Its extension-test typecheck failure was introduced by the inferred SDK fixture return type and is fixed by `3073642b6a3`; the full extension-test type graph now passes locally. Final-head CI [39942306239](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39942306239) completed: `check-test-types` and the remaining selected checks passed; the three inherited test failures below remain red, along with the aggregate gate. Its merge base advanced to `3b153699457f`; the only main changes since the reproduced baseline are release-workflow settings and an unrelated Gateway test, leaving all three failing paths unchanged.

All three remaining test failures were reproduced independently on clean, unmodified main `55477abbbb50`, with supported Node 24 and its own installed dependencies:

| Failed job | Baseline reproduction |
| --- | --- |
| `checks-node-compact-small-3` | `test/vitest-scoped-config.test.ts`: watch discovery lists a nonexistent `attempt-prompt-submit.steering.test.ts`; same 1,734-entry result and failed inclusion assertion. |

prs.title: feat(plugins): let plugins gate the final model provider request
prs.body:
## Summary

### High Level TLDR

Plugins can add context and gate a run before the prompt is built, but nothing lets a plugin see or change the exact request body that is about to go to the model provider. This adds `before_model_request`, an awaited, fail-closed policy hook on the embedded runner's provider transport. A handler gets the final provider payload plus a detached copy of the model-facing history (with host sender metadata) and can return a replacement payload, for example with untrusted text withheld or quarantined, or with credentials (API keys, tokens, passwords, private keys) that leaked into tool output or context redacted before they leave the Gateway. If a handler throws or times out, the request is not sent.

**CLI runtimes too.** CLI-backed runtimes such as `claude-cli` own their provider requests, so the hook now also runs where OpenClaw hands text to the CLI: once per CLI turn dispatch and once per input steered into a live CLI turn. There the event has `runtime: "cli"` and `payload: { prompt, prependContext?, appendContext? }`, and `messages` ends with the current user row including its input `provenance`. Before this, a subagent completion from an untrusted agent reached a CLI-backed agent as the prompt itself and no plugin could screen or withhold it.

**Compaction too.** Compaction resends older history to a model, so a value a plugin redacted on a turn could still leave in a compaction summary request. Embedded compaction requests (the summary call and server-side compaction) now pass the same gate, marked `requestKind: "compaction"` (turns are `"turn"`). The hook still only changes the outgoing request, never stored history; the docs now say so and point redaction of stored content at `tool_result_persist` / `before_message_write`.

The hook is **opt-in**: it is off by default for every plugin, bundled ones included, and only runs after the operator sets `plugins.entries.<id>.hooks.allowModelRequest: true`. Without that, the registration is ignored and the Gateway logs one startup warning naming the key to flip.

### What Problem This Solves

A prompt-injection scanner or data-loss policy plugin cannot enforce anything on the bytes that actually reach the model. `before_prompt_build` and `before_agent_run` run before provider `onPayload` transforms, tool-loop follow-up calls, and transport retries, and `llm_input` is observe-only. Content added after those hooks (tool results in later loop iterations, provider/config payload rewrites) never passes through a policy gate.

### User Impact

Plugin authors can register `api.on("before_model_request", handler)` to inspect, rewrite, or withhold the final embedded provider request, once the operator opts that plugin in with `plugins.entries.<id>.hooks.allowModelRequest: true`. Nothing changes for installs with no handler registered: the transformer returns the payload as-is without copying messages or awaiting anything.

### Why This Change Was Made

- **Owner:** `wrapStreamFnWithProviderPromptState` already owns the post-`onPayload` request body (it hashes it for context-retry admission). The gate runs there, right after provider `onPayload` transforms. For transports that use host request encoding, it runs at encode time instead, including encode-only retries. The replacement is what gets hashed, recorded, encoded, and sent, so retry admission and the wire bytes agree.
- **Hook runner:** registered as a modifying hook. Handlers run in priority order and each sees the previous replacement. Added to the runner's `fail-closed` policy set (like `before_agent_run` / `before_channel_ingress`) with a 10 s default timeout. An aborted turn rechecks its signal after the hook, so it cannot send late.
- **Tool surface, model, and Access program are fixed:** a replacement may rewrite content but not `tools`, `tool_choice`, `toolConfig`, `functions`, `function_call`, `model`, or `access_programs` (top level or under `config`). These fields are snapshotted in their JSON wire form before any handler runs and compared against the effective payload on every return path, so an in-place edit to `event.payload` (including one followed by returning nothing) fails the request just like a changed replacement. Tool, provider-hosted tool, model, and Access-program authorization (for example code-mode `web_search` filtering, or the admitted `cyber` program) is settled before this hook, and hosted tools have no later local gate.
- **Authority after the await:** the gate rechecks the run's abort signal right after the handler. The existing managed-fetch egress guard (`withGuardedFetchBeforeRequest`) still revalidates access-program authority at HTTP egress, after the hook has finished.
- **Context:** the hook gets the same agent hook context as other embedded hooks (`buildEmbeddedAgentHookContext`: agent, session, run, channel and sender fields) plus `modelProviderId` / `modelId`.
- **Explicit opt-in:** new config key `plugins.entries.<id>.hooks.allowModelRequest` (boolean, default off for all origins, unlike `allowConversationAccess`, which bundled plugins get by default). `registerTypedHook` checks it first: when it is not `true`, the registration is dropped with one registry warning, `typed hook "before_model_request" ignored: it is off by default; set plugins.entries.<id>.hooks.allowModelRequest=true to enable it`. The Gateway startup diagnostics logger (`server-plugin-bootstrap.ts`) prints it, and `openclaw plugins inspect <id>` lists it. Registration is the single owner of typed hooks, so an ignored handler never reaches the runner and the transport fast path (`hasHooks`) stays free. Schema (Zod, strict boolean), normalization, help text, label, and the generated config baseline are updated. No global switch: per-plugin opt-in already means nothing runs unless an operator turns it on, and `plugins.entries.<id>.enabled` or removing the key turns it off.
- **Permissions:** the opt-in does not replace the existing gates. Metadata sets `conversationAccess: true` and `promptInjection: true`, so non-bundled plugins need `allowConversationAccess`, and `allowPromptModification: false` blocks registration, same as `before_prompt_build`. Added to the harness `WORKSPACE_EFFECT_HOOKS` list with the other in-turn agent callbacks.
- **Typing:** `PluginHookBeforeModelRequestEvent` / `Result` are added to the typed handler map, so `api.on` infers them. They live in a leaf `src/plugins/hook-model.types.ts` (no import back into `hook-types.ts`, so there is no cycle). That file also holds the model hook metadata, and `hook-model.ts` holds the model hook runner bindings, so `hook-types.ts` and `hooks.ts` do not grow past their line caps. `llm_input` / `llm_output` incognito suppression is unchanged.
- **CLI runtimes:** the CLI owns its wire request and tool loop, so the gate sits at the last text OpenClaw controls. `executePreparedCliRun` runs it after history reseed, resume context and plugin input text transforms, before image paths, node placement and process start (including each recovery retry), and rechecks run currency after the await. `createSteeredCliMessageInjection` runs it before input enters a live plugin-owned turn (the path a subagent completion takes into a busy session), with the steered row (provenance included) last in `messages`. The gate is built per run in `runPreparedCliAgentOwned` (`src/agents/cli-runner/model-request-hook.ts`) and carried on `PreparedCliRunContext.beforeModelRequest`; it is absent for isolated completions, control operations such as compaction, and CLI side questions, which already skip turn hooks. A replacement may rewrite text only: anything but `{ prompt: string, prependContext?: string, appendContext?: string }` fails the dispatch, as do a throw or timeout (CLI not started; steered input refused). The system prompt, images and the CLI's own tool results are out of scope. The event gains `runtime: "embedded" | "cli"` on both paths.
- **Compaction:** every embedded compaction model call (the safeguard/default summary via `summarizeCompactionHistory` -> `generateSummary`, and `attemptServerEndpointCompaction`) runs on the compaction session's own `streamFn`, which `prepareCompactionSessionAgent` builds and which previously had no gate. The gate is now installed there with `wrapStreamFnWithProviderPromptState` + `createModelRequestTransformer(context, "compaction")`, at the same depth as on a turn: right after stream resolution, inside the provider text transforms and `applyExtraParamsToAgent` wrappers, so it sees the final shaped payload and also gates encode-only transports. Hook context: agent, session key/id, workspace, message provider, trigger, `modelProviderId` / `modelId`, `contextTokenBudget`. Fail-closed as on turns: a throw or timeout fails that compaction request. The event gains `requestKind: "turn" | "compaction"` (CLI dispatch and steered input are `"turn"`); documented as extensible, unknown kinds should be treated as turns.
- **Stored history is out of scope by design:** the hook gates bytes leaving the Gateway; `messages` stays a detached copy. Keeping a secret out of the transcript (and so out of every later request) is the job of the existing write-time hooks `tool_result_persist` and `before_message_write`; docs now state this next to the scope list and in the security page.
- **Docs:** `docs/plugins/hooks/prompt-and-session.md#final-model-request-policy`, plus catalog, timeout, permission, and "choose a hook" rows; `docs/gateway/security/prompt-injection.md#screening-the-final-model-request` covers request and credential screening with a config and redacting-handler example.

<details>
<summary>Security considerations</summary>

- This is a strong hook: a registered handler sees full conversation content and can replace the provider request. It needs the explicit `allowModelRequest` opt-in plus the same two registration permissions as `before_prompt_build`. Trusted plugins only.
- A handler cannot change the tool surface (see above), so prompt-modification permission cannot restore a denied provider-hosted tool such as `web_search`.
- Fail-closed by design: a crashing or hanging scanner blocks the model call instead of silently sending unscanned content. A plugin that wants outage passthrough must catch its own errors and return nothing (documented).
- `messages` is a `structuredClone`, so handlers cannot mutate session history through the event. Sender trust must come from host metadata (`__openclaw.senderIsOwner`), not message text (documented).
- Still runs for incognito sessions, as other policy hooks do. `llm_input` / `llm_output` observations stay suppressed there.
- Embedded compaction requests are gated (`requestKind: "compaction"`). With `agents.defaults.compaction.mode: "default"` explicitly set, the agent session's own in-turn compaction can also run; it uses the turn's already-gated `streamFn`, so it is gated but reported as `requestKind: "turn"`. The shipped default (`safeguard`) disables that path.
- Not covered (documented): tool results a CLI reads inside its own loop, CLI side questions, isolated completions and control operations, external harnesses such as Codex, compaction a CLI runtime runs itself, custom transports that bypass both `onPayload` and host encoding, and provider-hosted tool results that never return to the client.

</details>

### Real behavior proof

Provider-I/O proof: the real embedded transport owner (`prepareEmbeddedAttemptTransport`) runs with the real OpenAI Responses transport, and the transport host's model fetch is replaced by a local capture, so the assertions run on the exact HTTP request body. A `before_model_request` handler is registered:

```
pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/provider-prompt-state.test.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/model-request-hook.test.ts \
  src/plugins/hooks.before-model-request.test.ts \
  test/embedded-agent-attempt-stream-transport.test.ts

 ✓ hooks.before-model-request.test.ts > awaits replacements in priority order
 ✓ hooks.before-model-request.test.ts > does not send the original when a policy hook fails
 ✓ model-request-hook.test.ts > dispatches final payload with detached provenance and the correct session
 ✓ model-request-hook.test.ts > leaves the request intact when the plugin is absent
 ✓ provider-prompt-state.test.ts > final model request gate > awaits one gate after provider transforms (encoded=false)
 ✓ provider-prompt-state.test.ts > final model request gate > awaits one gate after provider transforms (encoded=true)
 ✓ provider-prompt-state.test.ts > final model request gate > gates encode-only retries and stops an aborted request after the gate
 ✓ embedded-agent-attempt-stream-transport.test.ts > sends the before_model_request replacement with run context
 ✓ embedded-agent-attempt-stream-transport.test.ts > gates the final OpenAI Responses request at provider I/O (withhold)
 ✓ embedded-agent-attempt-stream-transport.test.ts > gates the final OpenAI Responses request at provider I/O (hosted-tool)
 ✓ embedded-agent-attempt-stream-transport.test.ts > gates the final OpenAI Responses request at provider I/O (throw)
 ✓ model-request-hook.test.ts > rejects replacements that change the provider tool surface
```

Observed at provider I/O: with `withhold`, the HTTP body carries `[withheld]` and not the original user text. With `hosted-tool`, a replacement that appends `{ type: "web_search" }` ends the turn with `must not change the provider tool surface` and no HTTP request is made. With `throw`, the turn errors with the handler's failure and no HTTP request is made. In-process: order is provider `onPayload` → gate → send, the handler's replacement is the body that is hashed and sent, encode-only retries are gated each time, an abort after the gate prevents the send, a throwing handler rejects the request, and edits to `event.messages` do not reach the session.

Red checks: with the tool-surface check disabled, the `hosted-tool` case fails (`expected 'stop' to be 'error'`). With the transport wiring removed (base `attempt-stream-settle.ts`), the transport test fails with `expected { input: [ 'outside' ] } to deeply equal { input: [ 'withheld' ] }`. The other new tests fail on base because the hook and its runner method do not exist. The protected-field snapshot (head `8687f8c`) adds `model-request-hook.test.ts` cases for an in-place `tools.push({ type: "web_search" })` with and without a returned payload, and for replacements that change `model` or `access_programs.cyber`; with the previous comparison (post-handler, replacement-only, tools only) both new cases fail, and with the snapshot they pass. The real OpenAI Responses transport test (`test/embedded-agent-attempt-stream-transport.test.ts`, "gates the final OpenAI Responses request at provider I/O") adds `in-place-tool` (handler pushes `web_search` onto `event.payload.tools` and returns nothing) and `model` (replacement sets `model: "other-model"`) modes: both end with `stopReason: "error"` and zero captured fetches; against the previous hook implementation both fail with `expected 'stop' to be 'error'` (the request was sent).

CLI proof through the real CLI runner (`runPreparedCliAgent` → `executePreparedCliRun` → process supervisor, with the real hook runner and a registered `before_model_request` handler; the supervisor spawn is captured so assertions run on the exact argv the CLI would get):

```
pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/cli-runner.model-request-hook.test.ts

 ✓ screens the CLI turn once and sends the replacement prompt
 ✓ leaves the CLI prompt alone when no plugin is allowed the hook
 ✓ does not start the CLI when the hook times out
 ✓ does not start the CLI when the hook returns a non-text payload
 ✓ screens input steered into a live CLI turn
```

Observed: the handler runs once per turn with `runtime: "cli"`, the original prompt, the current user row carrying `provenance: { kind: "inter_session", sourceSessionKey: "agent:<untrusted>:subagent:..." }`, and context with `agentId`, `sessionKey`, `modelProviderId`, `modelId`; the spawned argv carries `[held]` and not the original handback text. With no registered handler the argv carries the original prompt. A 20 ms hook timeout or a `{ prompt: 1 }` replacement rejects the run and the CLI is never spawned. Steered input: the injection receives the replacement text and context, not the original. Red check: with `src/agents/cli-runner.ts` at the previous head, the turn, timeout and malformed-payload cases fail (hook never called, CLI spawned with the original text).

Opt-in proof on a real Gateway built from this branch (isolated state dir, loopback port, no model credentials, no model calls), with a local plugin whose `register` only calls `api.on("before_model_request", ...)` and `allowConversationAccess: true`:

```
# hooks: { allowConversationAccess: true }   (allowModelRequest unset)
openclaw gateway run --allow-unconfigured --port <free> --bind loopback --auth none
[gateway] [plugins] typed hook "before_model_request" ignored: it is off by default; set plugins.entries.model-request.hooks.allowModelRequest=true to enable it (plugin=model-request, source=<plugin>/index.cjs)
[gateway] http server listening (2 plugins: memory-core, model-request; 4.4s)

# hooks: { allowConversationAccess: true, allowModelRequest: true }
[gateway] http server listening (2 plugins: memory-core, model-request; 3.4s)      (no warning)

openclaw plugins inspect model-request --runtime --json
  off: typedHooks [] , diagnostics ["typed hook \"before_model_request\" ignored: ... allowModelRequest=true to enable it"]
  on:  typedHooks ["before_model_request"], diagnostics []

# hooks: { allowModelRequest: "yes" }
OpenClaw config is invalid
  - plugins.entries.model-request.hooks.allowModelRequest: Invalid input: expected boolean, received string (allowed: true, false)
```

Opt-in unit proof (`src/plugins/loader-model-request-permission.test-support.ts`, run through `loader.test.ts` with the real loader): unset and `false` register nothing and emit exactly one warning naming the key; `true` registers the hook; `true` without `allowConversationAccess` is still blocked by the conversation-access gate; `true` with `allowPromptModification: false` is still blocked by the prompt gate. Red check: forcing the resolver to allow always fails the `unset` and `false` cases. Schema and normalization: `config-misc.test.ts` accepts `true` and rejects the string `"true"`; `config-state.test.ts` keeps a boolean and drops a non-boolean.

Live proof with a real Gateway, a real model, and a scanner plugin registered on this hook is not in this PR. Also not shown: Access revocation or account reassignment while a handler is awaited (this PR does not change `prepareEmbeddedAccessProgramGuard`), and a latest-stable upgrade run; the only config addition is the new optional boolean `allowModelRequest`, so existing plugin entries load unchanged. It will follow on a deployment running this branch.

Compaction gate proof (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/compaction-session-agent.test.ts`, real `prepareCompactionSessionAgent`, real hook runner, mocked transport + a payload-shaping wrapper standing in for `applyExtraParamsToAgent`): a handler receives `requestKind: "compaction"`, the session hook context, and the payload *after* provider/config shaping (`{ input: "API_TOKEN=fixture-value", shaped: true }`), and the transport sends its replacement (`API_TOKEN=[REDACTED]`); with no handler the payload is sent unchanged. Red check: removing the new wrapper from `prepareCompactionSessionAgent` fails the first case (handler never called, secret sent). `model-request-hook.test.ts` asserts `requestKind` defaults to `"turn"` and passes `"compaction"` through.

### What was not tested

- No live Gateway run with a real provider in this PR (see above). The opt-in gate was proven on a real Gateway startup without model calls.
- `openclaw doctor` does not show the opt-in warning: doctor does not load plugin runtimes for this check, and the same is true for the existing conversation-access registration warnings. Startup logs and `plugins inspect` do show it.
- The timeout path was not exercised directly. It uses the shared modifying-hook timeout plus the fail-closed policy, and the thrown-error path is tested.
- Locally, `src/agents/harness/` suites that spawn supervised child processes failed with `service child cleanup identity lost: native owner closed without kernel descendant extinction`. The same suites fail the same way on the base commit, so it is a local process-supervision environment limit, not this change. CI is the reference for them.
- CLI: the turn path is proven with a `codex-cli`-shaped arg backend; the `claude-cli` plugin-owned transport consumes the same gated `prompt` / `promptContext` values and its steering path is covered by the steered-input test, but no claude-cli process ran in tests. Live claude-cli proof follows on deployment.
- Locally, `src/agents/cli-runner/bundle-mcp*.test.ts` (MCP config projection) and `execute-plugin.steering.test.ts` fail; `bundle-mcp.test.ts` and `execute-plugin.steering.test.ts` fail the same way on the previous head (`57b5ec1`), so they are a local environment limit, not this change. CI is the reference.
- Compaction: no live compaction against a real provider with a scanner plugin. The gate placement relative to provider/config wrappers is proven with a stand-in wrapper, not each provider's real `onPayload`.
- Not measured: no before/after benchmark. With no handler registered the added work is one `hasHooks` lookup per provider request. With a handler, cost is one `structuredClone` of the history plus the handler's own time.

## Verification

- Targeted + hook suites: 5 files, 102 tests pass (`provider-prompt-state`, `model-request-hook`, `hooks.before-model-request`, `embedded-agent-attempt-stream-transport`, `hooks.phase-hooks`).
- Adjacent suites: `src/plugins/hooks.phase-hooks.test.ts`, `attempt-session-runtime-prepare.test.ts`, `model-request-body.test.ts` pass.
- `tsgo` core and core-test / root-test shards: clean.
- `oxlint` on changed files: clean. Formatter: applied. Line-cap, madge import-cycle, import-cycle, and assertion SAFETY ratchets: pass.
- Opt-in suites: `loader.test.ts` (198 tests), `config-state.test.ts`, `config-misc.test.ts`, `schema.tiers.test.ts`, plus the hook suites above, all pass. `pnpm tsgo:core` clean; `oxlint` and `oxfmt` clean on changed files; `pnpm config:docs:check` OK after `pnpm config:docs:gen`; base config schema check OK.
- Test-lines ratchet: `config/test-lines-allocations/before-model-request.txt` allocates the 563 added test lines (289 for the hook, 44 for the opt-in gate, 47 for the protected-field snapshot cases, 183 for CLI runtimes), since this is a new hook with its own tests.
- CLI extension (head `dc1267b`): `src/agents/cli-runner` suites (1006 pass; only the pre-existing local failures above), `cli-runner.model-request-hook`, `hooks.before-model-request`, embedded `model-request-hook`, `reply-tool-authority.worker` pass. `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:test:src`, `tsgo:test:root` clean; `oxlint` (incl. max-lines) and `oxfmt` clean on changed files; import-cycle and madge checks 0 cycles; `config:docs:check` OK after `config:docs:gen`; `format:docs:check` clean. Autoreview (Claude engine, P0-P1) on the CLI delta: scoped-clean.


- Compaction follow-up (head `deac31b`): 29 compaction/hook suites, 317 tests pass (`compact*`, `compaction*`, `cli-runner.model-request-hook`, `hooks.before-model-request`, `model-request-hook`, new `compaction-session-agent`). `tsgo:core` and core-test shards clean; `oxlint` / `oxfmt` clean on changed files; line-cap, max-lines, import-cycle and madge checks pass; `format:docs:check` clean; test-lines allocation raised to 682 (+119 for the compaction gate tests). Autoreview (Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, standard tier, P0-P1) on the compaction delta: scoped-clean.
- Docs: `pnpm format:docs:check` and `pnpm check:docs` (markdownlint, MDX, link audit, config examples) pass with the prompt-injection screening section.
