prs.title: fix(agents): forward hook-stamped _meta on bundle-mcp tool calls
prs.body:
Related: #151413

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a plugin's hook-authored identity stamp never reaches MCP servers on bundle-mcp tool calls — and both mechanisms attempted so far mis-assigned trust in the request-metadata lane.

Hooks (e.g. Brayer's `harness/agent/session` stamp) rewrite tool params, but JSON-RPC `_meta` lives *beside* `arguments`; the executor forwarded params verbatim as `arguments`, so servers saw no request-level identity (the last open seam of the #151413 identity transport). Revision 1 inferred trust by diffing hook input against executing params — value equality cannot establish authorship, and a whole changed object carries preserved model fields into the trusted lane — while also hoisting (deleting) the `_meta` argument. The execute-factory extraction also snapshotted `disposal` at factory creation — retained forms never observed run end — and tested a restriction-map *entry* instead of the map.

## User Impact

Hooks now publish identity through an explicit result field: `before_tool_call` may return `requestMeta`, which invocation owners forward as request-level `_meta` on every bundle-mcp path (embedded agent runs, client tool definitions, gateway `/tools/invoke`). Authorship is the hook's declaration, never a value comparison: params `_meta` is never promoted, never deleted, and never diffed — model-supplied `_meta` stays an ordinary argument, and a hook stamp equal to the caller's value still ships. Servers consuming the identity lane (Brayer's `resolveIdentity`) read it first. Retained MCP form callbacks still reject with `MCP run has ended` on run end; an App view absent from an established restriction map keeps its explicit empty grant.

## Why This Change Was Made

Revision 2 required an owner decision: *should `before_tool_call` expose an explicit request-metadata result instead of inferring trusted metadata from parameter differences?* **Decision: yes.** The direction is the contributor owner's decision recorded here; the resulting public `requestMeta` contract itself awaits a recorded OpenClaw maintainer sign-off (requested in the review thread — CODEOWNERS owners of `src/plugins` / `src/agents`). `PluginHookBeforeToolCallResult` gains an optional `requestMeta`; the host shallow-merges it per key across hooks (later hooks win; deliberately not covered by the approval params lock — the operator reviews params and approval text, never this transport lane), threads it through `HookOutcome`, approval grants and deferred-approval round-trips, and each invocation owner binds it for exactly its own execution through the existing async scope. Trusted tool policies share the same contract: `runTrustedToolPolicies` now accumulates `requestMeta` with the identical per-key merge — kept for metadata-only decisions (previously returned `undefined`, dropping the stamp) and alongside `requireApproval` (previously discarded). The bundle-mcp execute factory forwards it as `runtime.callTool(..., { _meta })` and passes `arguments` through untouched — `hoistHookMeta` is gone. P1 (mixed-origin promotion), P2 (equal-stamp delivery) and the security item (trusted-lane provenance) are resolved by construction: only the declared field enters the request lane, and value content never decides. The contract and merge semantics are documented in `docs/plugins/hooks/tool-policy.md`; the motivating plugin is updated in igorjpimenta/brayer#46 (`requestMeta: { brayer }`, flat-arg and `params._meta` mirrors retained for engines predating the hoist).

Lifecycle repairs from revision 1 are retained: disposal reads through the materializer's live closure, and an explicit empty App grant stays distinct from a never-bound restriction map.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — current head `44186ae`

Isolated OpenClaw profile, real model (`opencode-go-responses/muse-spark-1.3-contributor`), real Brayer MCP service (igorjpimenta/brayer `b3aaf57`, isolated store). The consumer reports the identity channel and request-`_meta` keys on every accepted call:

```text
brayer: brayer_order_create from openclaw:main:agent:main:main via=meta metaKeys=brayer
```

Six accepted calls, every one `via=meta metaKeys=brayer`:

| # | Path | Case | Consumer-side result |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Gateway `/tools/invoke` | legitimate — args carry **no** identity | order created; `via=meta` proves the request lane delivered it |
| 2 | Gateway | mixed-origin/forged args (`brayer_agent:mallory`, `brayer_session:forged-ctx`, args `_meta.revision:7`) | order created with **real** identity; `metaKeys=brayer` — no `revision` in the trusted lane, forged args ignored |
| 3 | Gateway | equal-stamp — args replay the exact real stamp | `via=meta` — delivery preserved despite value equality (P2) |
| 4 | Agent turn, real model | legitimate — prompt forbids identity fields | reply is the order id; 4th `via=meta metaKeys=brayer` line |
| 5 | Agent turn, real model | instructed to pass forged fields | model stripped them itself; order created `via=meta` (wire-level forged case is #2) |
| 6 | Gateway, Brayer plugin disabled | forbidden / retired stamp source | `{"error":"brayer: agent and session must be stamped on the call"}`; consumer log 4→4, orders 5→5 — refused before the handler ran |

**Revocation during awaited preparation.** A call parked on a pending approval (receipt `plugin:7c5fc598…` / `plugin:ecd741ab…` captured via `approvals pending --json`), then `config unset mcp.servers.brayer` landed mid-await:

```text
[reload] config hot reload applied (..., mcp.servers.brayer)
request handler failed: Error: Approval requester authority changed
⇄ res ✗ plugin.approval.waitDecision ... errorCode=UNAVAILABLE errorMessage=Error: Approval requester authority changed
[agents/tools] plugin approval gateway request failed; blocking tool call
```

The operator grant arrived afterwards (`"status":"allowed"`), yet the call still returned `{"ok":false,"error":{"type":"tool_call_blocked","message":"Plugin approval required (gateway unavailable)","requiresApproval":true}}`; consumer log 4→4, orders 5→5 — rejected before the consuming service's effect. A post-restore call succeeds (`via=meta`), proving state heals.

Command shapes and log excerpts are redacted: gateway token shown as `$GATEWAY_TOKEN`, loopback addresses as `<loopback>`, host paths shortened; no keys, tokens, or non-public endpoints appear in any quoted line.

### Automated coverage at the production invocation boundary

Per revision 2's test finding, the comparison-helper unit table is deleted. `src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-executes.test.ts` now proves forwarding, mixed-origin non-promotion, and equal-stamp delivery through the real chain — policy → wrapper → bundle-mcp factory — with only the hook runner stubbed, plus trusted-policy `requestMeta` forwarding through invocation and MCP dispatch for both metadata-only and approval-bearing decisions (embedded approval broker resolves the grant). `src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.trusted-approval.test.ts` proves the policy-level halves: a metadata-only trusted decision returns `requestMeta`, and an approval-bearing decision keeps it through the grant. `src/plugins/hooks.before-tool-call.test.ts` covers the new per-key merge (later hooks win; a stamp contributed after an approval request survives). Per revision 3's test finding, the ALS helper tests are trimmed to nested shadowing and scope restoration — direct publish / undefined-publish / outside-store assertions are already covered at the invocation boundary.

### CI and gates on `9c19c5241`

Local gates on a true merge tree of this branch and current `main`, using CI's base (`pull_request.base.sha`): mock-exports, assertion-safety, max-lines, timeout-race, line-cap, wrapper-shadowing, deprecated-api-usage, import-cycles and knip all green; `pnpm tsgo:core` and every core test shard green (the ui type error visible against this branch's stale base alone is byte-identical to `fb530875` and fixed on `main` by #192868; CI evaluates the merge tree). The test-lines allocation is set to 430 — exactly this PR's measured net test delta against current `main` (credit == delta, the policy maximum).

**Known repo-wide test-lines condition (resolved):** while this PR was in review, `main` itself carried inherited test-ratchet debt — over its own ceiling with `net delta: 0`, introduced by #191508 / `d46a50ff8` (merged 2026-11-06 16:03 UTC, test additions without an allocation record; slack was 13 immediately before). The ratchet deliberately does not forgive inherited debt (credit may not exceed this change's own delta), so no allocation could cover it — every PR with positive net test growth failed `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` by exactly the inherited amount (this PR reported `over by: 49; net delta: +430` — delta exactly equal to its allocation of 430, zero uncovered growth; #192862 showed the same red). `main` has since been reconciled (slack 94 at `5e4684a1d`, verified with the ratchet on a clean main checkout and on this branch merged with current `main`), and this PR's refreshed CI (merge re-created on reopen) is green: `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` passes, 72 checks green, 0 failures. This PR never raised the shared scalar (policy: scalar raises are review-owned).

The line-cap growth guard forced two message-prescribed sibling extractions — `hook-before-tool-call-merge.ts` (the before_tool_call result chain) and `tools-invoke-upload-request.ts` (a leaf predicate). Local affected suites (trusted-policy, before-tool-call e2e/integration/decision, executes, ALS): all green.

### Scope

Publish sites are the three boundaries that run `before_tool_call` and then execute tools — `agent-tools.before-tool-call.wrapper.ts`, `agent-tool-definition-adapter.ts`, `gateway/tools-invoke-shared.ts` — consumed in `agent-bundle-mcp-executes.ts`. The MCP loopback HTTP handlers run hooks for gateway-scoped tools only; no bundle-mcp factory is in that path.

**Delta vs merge base `fb530875`:** 21 files, +803 / −208 — `f9f467d` original transport fix, `d794099` lifecycle repairs, `c539c75` ratchet bookkeeping, `83b3ddc` explicit `requestMeta` contract with threading and boundary tests plus the `hook-before-tool-call-merge` extraction, `44186ae` the `tools-invoke-upload-request` extraction, `9c19c52` trusted-policy `requestMeta` accumulation (review-3 P2) with regression tests, ALS test trim, and allocation set to the measured delta.

prs.title: fix(searxng): web_search reports "no results" when SearXNG's engines are unresponsive
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: SearXNG can return no results because upstream engines timed out or were rate-limited. OpenClaw treated that as a successful empty search and cached it for 15 minutes, so identical searches remained empty after recovery.

## User Impact

Zero results plus `unresponsive_engines` now produces the existing generic provider error instead of a cached empty answer. The next search can reach recovered engines. Partial results and genuinely empty responses remain cacheable, and successful results retain their existing TTL.

## Why This Change Was Made

Read SearXNG's failed-engine metadata alongside the existing shared native result codec. After the existing general-category retry, throw only when results are empty and engines failed, before the cache write. Engine/reason detail stays in the internal error; the tool-facing message remains the existing provider error. No config, API, permission, timeout or cache-policy change.

Retains @geekforlife's original commit. Current main is integrated and its shared native request/result codecs are preserved; no duplicate local result parser is restored. The regression is consolidated into the existing response-error test, and fixture setup is simplified without removing assertions: tests +5/-5 (net 0), no allocation; production +34/-5, docs +4.

## Evidence

[Exact-head shipped Gateway before/after proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190619#issuecomment-6701612882).

Main twice and candidate twice: real built Gateway `web_search` via `/tools/invoke`, with a local SearXNG HTTP fixture and the same live cache owner throughout each ref. Main keeps serving cached empty results after recovery. Candidate returns the existing generic error after `news`→`general`, reaches the recovered endpoint on the second call, returns the real result and caches it on the third. Partial-result and genuine-empty controls remain cached exactly as before. No clock manipulation or real provider credentials.

Committed regression fails on main and passes on candidate. All three SearXNG suites: 21 passed; changed-file format/lint pass. Earlier direct-runtime proof is superseded by the shipped Gateway evidence.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door: reverting restores the old failed-engine empty-result caching; no persistent migration or new contract. Blast radius is SearXNG responses with zero results and failed engines after category fallback. Genuine empty, partial-result and successful-cache controls protect neighboring behavior; other search providers are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(ui): paint channels save failures with the indicator failure class
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Channels config save feedback still applies `settings-save-indicator--danger`, but that modifier no longer has any CSS rule after the settings save-indicator contract cutover (#191354 removed it). Conflict, save-error, and not-saved text therefore renders in the default color instead of the danger color the canonical indicator uses.

## User Impact

When a channel Save fails, hits a hash conflict, or is cut short, the explanatory line under the dialog looks like neutral status text. Operators can miss that the save did not land and may assume the config was written.

## Why

The canonical `openclaw-settings-save-indicator` paints failures with `settings-save-indicator__failure` (`color: var(--danger)` on the text span) and no longer defines `--danger`. Channels' `ChannelConfigFeedback` was left behind as an incomplete cutover: it still writes the orphan modifier on the container, so the stylesheet never colors the message. Interrupted notices intentionally stay uncolored and keep that distinction.

## Evidence

**Running Control UI (mock Gateway) before/after** — computed colors from the built Channels dialog:

| State | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Conflict | span neutral `rgb(53, 53, 53)`, orphan `--danger` present | span `rgb(185, 28, 28)` + `settings-save-indicator__failure`; Reload/Overwrite stay neutral `rgb(53, 53, 53)` |
| Save error | span neutral `rgb(53, 53, 53)`, orphan `--danger` present | span `rgb(185, 28, 28)` + `settings-save-indicator__failure` |
| Interrupted | neutral `rgb(53, 53, 53)`, no failure class | neutral `rgb(53, 53, 53)`, no failure class (unchanged) |

**Conflict** — before / after:

| ![conflict before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/channels-failure-color/proof-channels/conflict-before.png) | ![conflict after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/channels-failure-color/proof-channels/conflict-after.png) |
|---|---|

**Save error** — before / after:

| ![error before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/channels-failure-color/proof-channels/error-before.png) | ![error after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/channels-failure-color/proof-channels/error-after.png) |
|---|---|

**Interrupted** — before / after (must stay neutral):

| ![interrupted before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/channels-failure-color/proof-channels/interrupted-before.png) | ![interrupted after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/channels-failure-color/proof-channels/interrupted-after.png) |
|---|---|

Raw JSON facts (span class + computed color + button colors): `proof-channels/*.json` on branch [`proof/channels-failure-color`](https://github.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/tree/proof/channels-failure-color/proof-channels).

Capture path: mock Control UI e2e (same harness as `channels-explicit-save.e2e.test.ts`) against the built Control UI; Chromium headless; `animations: "disabled"`; clip = feedback region. Before run used base `view.config.tsx` markup; after run used this PR head `a1154311b52`. No phone numbers, API keys, or non-public endpoints in fixtures (synthetic bot token placeholders only).

**Unit red/green:** with base markup + new assertions, 4 tests fail; with the fix, **53 passed** (`channels-page.save.test.ts` + `view.test.tsx`).

**Ratchet:** `check:test-lines-ratchet.mts --base 01a5e160dab` → `Test lines OK: 6515022; ceiling: 6515041; slack: 19`.

**Occupancy:** `gh api search/issues` for the orphan class / `__failure` + channels → `total_count: 0` (open and closed).

## Merge Danger

- Visual only: channels save/conflict/error text gains `var(--danger)`; interrupted notices stay default-colored. Buttons in the conflict row keep `.btn` colors (the failure class is on the message span, not the container).
- No schema, gateway, or i18n string changes. Depends on existing `settings-save-indicator__failure` in `settings.css` (shared with the canonical indicator).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes narrow-screen RTL composer overflow when goal, mention, and reply contexts are stacked.

## User Impact

Context dismiss buttons retain their 44px touch targets inside the composer, with the same visible 28px buttons and dismissal behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared IconButton migration in #194140 increased the button from 24px to 28px but retained its 10px invisible extension on each side. That made the target 48px wide. Reducing the extension to 8px restores the original 44px target without moving the icon, changing strip sizing, or clipping the control.

Total CSS324,776→324,777B gzip (1B variance), raw CSS−1B. Strict base/head comparison has no violations; existing base JS cap overages are unchanged. |

prs.title: fix(ios): mount Control UI pages under the advertised base path
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/191177

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the iOS app's embedded Control UI pages (the Settings tab's Dashboard, session Dashboards, Terminal and Desktop) show the Gateway's "Not Found" when the Gateway serves the Control UI under `gateway.controlUi.basePath` and the app is connected by discovery or by host and port, a connection URL without a path.

## User Impact

User impact: iOS users with a Control UI base path can use those pages without re-pairing by QR code. Connections whose URL already has a path (setup codes since https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/161620) keep it.

## Why This Change Was Made

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185141 made the Gateway advertise its Control UI mount in hello-ok (`controlUiBasePath`) and made macOS use it: the connection URL's path wins when it has one, else the advertised mount. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/190199 proposes the same rule for Android. On iOS, `AuthenticatedControlUI.pageURL`, which builds the URL for every embedded page, used only the connection URL's path, and the operator session dropped the hello-ok field.

This change applies the same rule at the same owners:
- `GatewayNodeSession` admits `controlUiBasePath` from hello-ok next to the methods, scopes and limits it already keeps for the current route, and clears it on disconnect.
- `NodeAppModel` copies it onto the active connect config before it marks the operator connected, because the pages build their URL when they appear on that flag. The field stays out of the connection and WebView identity inputs (`controlUIInputs`, `hasSameConnectionInputs`): it is learned after connect, and putting it there would replace the WebViews and their bridges on every connect.
- `AuthenticatedControlUI.pageURL` uses it, percent-encoded, when the connection URL has no path. All seven callers follow without edits. The native bridge checks that trust a page's origin (`ControlUINativeGatewayAuthHandler.isAvailable`, `IOSDeviceSettingsBridge.isTrustedSource`) derive from the same URL, so they narrow to the mount too, and the chat source preview (`IOSSourceResourceLoader`, through `nativeControlPageURL`) resolves resources under it.

Accepted edge case: a page opened before the operator hello arrives, or kept open while the Gateway changes its mount, keeps its old URL until it is opened again. The Settings Dashboard is not affected: it appears only once the operator is connected, which happens after the mount is stored.

Size against the merge base `23194454398`: production +29/−1 in 4 files, tests +70/−3 in the existing `SessionDashboardScreenTests` and `GatewayNodeSessionTests` suites.

## Evidence

Tested on a real iPhone (iOS 26.7.1) with the iOS app built without and with the fix, against an isolated Gateway (own state, no channels, placeholder token) with `gateway.controlUi.basePath: "/gateway"`. The same UI script ran on both sides: launch with onboarding reset, connect from **Settings → Gateway** by host and port only with the token, relaunch on the Settings tab, and read the embedded page.

The device builds carry one extra proof-only commit on both sides, which this PR does not include. Current main's iOS app needs the iOS 27.1 SDK (`\.toolbarVerticalEdge` in `apps/ios/Sources/Design/ChatProTab.swift`, from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/187045), which the Xcode 26.6 that built the Before app lacks. An older base does not help here, because every commit with the hello-ok field from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185141 also needs that SDK. The screenshot and recording are from the first After run, an earlier build of this fix on main `eb4881915a0` with the SDK commit, made with Xcode 26.6; the re-run on this PR's head gave the same three results and the same settings page under `/gateway/`.

prs.title: fix(matrix): message bursts become separate turns despite messages.inbound debounce
prs.body:
Closes #165823 Related: #161505 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: Matrix turns every line of a quick text burst into separate agent turns, even when `messages.inbound.debounceMs` or `byChannel.matrix` is configured. ## User Impact With `messages.inbound.byChannel.matrix` (or the global `debounceMs`) set, a burst of Matrix messages from one sender gets one reply. The Matrix default stays 0, so nothing is delayed unless the operator opts in. ## Why This Change Was Made Rebuilt on the durable Matrix ingress (the earlier head targeted the replay-claim API that main has since removed). It follows the Mattermost fan-in debouncer from #166499: - Ingress `dispatch` hands each event and its claim lifecycle to a room-keyed `createChannelInboundDebouncer` and returns `{ kind: "deferred" }`. `canAppend` only merges contiguous text from the same sender and thread root, and `serializeImmediate` keeps everything in room order, so a burst never jumps ahead of another sender's message. - A flush fans the batched claims into one lifecycle (`fanInChannelIngressLifecycles`). Adopting the merged turn completes every claim; a gated turn settles them; a handler failure fails each claim so the drain's retry policy applies; shutdown or an aborted claim cancels them back to the queue. - The merged event keeps the latest event id (reply threading), joins bodies with newlines, keeps each event's HTML in `formatted_body` (escaped plain text otherwise, joined with `
`) so the handler's matrix.to pill check still validates mentions, and merges `m.mentions`. - Media, voice notes, edits, real replies (not thread fallbacks), the bot's own events, and control commands dispatch alone. Command bypass strips the mention prefix the way the handler does (bot MXID, room display name, every agent's mention patterns), so `@Bot: /stop` is never delayed. Prefix lookup is async, so it is chained per room. - Pre-startup history and E2EE decryption are now handled by ingress before delivery, so the old pre-startup predicate and repeat-emit filter are gone. - Monitor shutdown closes the debouncer with task admission: pending batches and late deliveries return to the durable queue instead of being dropped. - The delay is read from live config.
Test-only changes - `index.test-helpers.ts`: the fake ingress passes a full claim lifecycle and records it; the fake runtime gains a `messagesConfig` knob and a `mock-isolation` note (`config/test-mock-exports-baseline.txt` drops that entry). - `index.test.ts`: handler failures and late post-shutdown events are now asserted on the claim lifecycle (`onFailed` / `onCancelled`) rather than as a rejected delivery; the shutdown-order test waits for the handler to start before aborting.
## Evidence - Original defect: the new `index.test.ts` case "merges a Matrix text burst when messages.inbound.byChannel.matrix is set" fails with `index.ts` reverted to main (handler called 2 times, no batching) and passes with the fix. - `inbound-debounce.test.ts` (16 tests): merge on latest event, single adoption per claim, gated-turn settle, failure fans out `onFailed`, immediate dispatch for edits/replies/commands (MXID, display-name pill, mention pattern)/images, arrival order under async prefix lookup, room order across senders and threads, HTML and mention merge, own messages, shutdown cancellation. - `index.test.ts`: burst merge through the monitor wiring and a debounce delay committed after startup. - Local gates on this head: `pnpm test:extension matrix` pass; `pnpm check:changed --base upstream/main` typecheck-all, format, mock-export ratchet, dead-export scan, plugin boundaries pass; oxlint on `extensions/matrix` clean; `pnpm format:docs:check` clean. - Earlier live run (2026.9.8 Gateway, previous implementation, `byChannel.matrix: 3000`): a five-line Element burst produced one user-triggered agent turn. Not re-run on this head.

prs.title: feat(control-ui): show worker lifecycle and telemetry
prs.body:
Closes #163982

## What Problem This Solves

The Systems page hides worker lifecycle history, can leave a reclaimed worker shown as `Attached` until reload, and does not connect live dedicated workers to the CPU, memory, and disk telemetry their enrolled nodes already report.

## User Impact

Operators can distinguish active workers from recent destroyed or failed workers, inspect lifecycle/provider/profile/lease/error details, see terminal state changes without reloading, and troubleshoot or right-size live dedicated workers from the same resource graphs used for base systems.

Workers without dedicated node telemetry show an explicit not-reported state. Shared-host workers do not expose whole-host statistics as if those measurements belonged to one worker.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Systems inventory now retains terminal worker records, groups active and historical workers separately, and refreshes canonical `environments.list` data when durable `sessions.changed` events or worker placement changes arrive.

For dedicated workers, the Gateway additionally projects the enrolled node identity. The Systems inventory joins that exact identity to `node.list`, reuses the existing host-stat history and graphs, and continues polling while the worker is selected. No provider shell probe, SSH command, or second telemetry poller is introduced.

## Evidence

### October27 identification repair

Short worker IDs now remain visible beside lifecycle status. [Exact-head regression results and before/after screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/163995#issuecomment-6456168501). This fixes the same-profile identification finding; history-policy acceptance and main integration remain pending.

### Earlier lifecycle and telemetry evidence

The following results document earlier tested revisions; they are not a new full-suite or live-runtime qualification of the October27 head.

Live Apple Container lifecycle, captured from the same Systems page without a reload:

**Before reclaim — worker is Attached**

![Systems sidebar showing an attached worker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff22cbbe-35d0-4d25-a08c-6799626eb040)

**After reclaim — worker moved to Recent worker history as Destroyed**

![Systems sidebar showing the reclaimed worker as destroyed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ee681765-dd7b-4cad-adf6-0708837275eb)

- Live transition observed in about one second and repeated twice without reloading.
- Disposable live telemetry proof: an Apple Container worker reached `ready`, published a dedicated node identity, and reported Linux host stats with 5 CPUs, load averages, 4.26 GB memory capacity, and 541.13 GB disk capacity through `node.list`. The worker was reclaimed; provider and Apple Container inventories were empty afterward.
- Focused validation:
  - Gateway environment projection: 20/20 pass.
  - Gateway protocol schema: 22/22 pass.
  - Systems telemetry/UI: 36/36 pass, including distinct session and telemetry-node names.
  - Changed-file formatting and lint: pass.
  - Core and UI typechecks: pass.
  - Production Control UI build: pass.
- Earlier branch-wide validation:
  - `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base origin/main`: pass (335.15 s).
  - `pnpm test:changed`: 20,926 pass / 3 skip; one unrelated `shell-viewport.test.ts` RAF-coalescing assertion failed under the full parallel lane, then passed 3/3 isolated reruns (11/11 each).
  - Upstream `control-ui-performance`: pass. The local check showed a nondeterministic gzip edge 24–30 B over the 373,454 B startup limit while raw startup JS stayed exactly 1,208,683 B with and without the Systems reconciliation helper, confirming this patch does not change the startup asset set.
  - Repo autoreview helper was attempted but unavailable because its local Codex credential returned HTTP 401; no review verdict was produced.

The two older `Destroying` rows visible in the screenshots predate this worker and are a separate provider-history cleanup issue.

prs.title: chore(codex): test warm claim settlement and scope revocation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

**Tests-only regression coverage; no runtime source change or production fix in this PR.** The proof target here is that a failed owner leaves no orphan native-thread claim and a later attempt can reuse that thread.

A Codex-backed conversation can reject the next turn as “claimed by active work” after failed ownership settlement, even though the failed attempt is no longer running. The existing cleanup lacks targeted coverage at the warm-claim cleanup and monitor-setup revocation seams.

Related: karmaterminal/openclaw#1431 (the queue-behind-*genuinely active* work request is separate and remains open).

## User Impact

No production behavior changes. These tests protect the existing claim-release behavior against regressions that could strand subsequent Codex attempts.

## Why This Change Was Made

Inject a lease-settlement failure after proving warm claim transfer (without a cold resume), and separately revoke session binding authority during monitor setup. Assert cleanup clears each claim and the same native thread can be claimed by a follow-up attempt. The latter is **scope revocation, not a simulated binding-store lease expiry**. The tests complement the existing lifecycle cleanup; they do not implement queueing behind active work.

## Evidence

- Based on upstream `main` `6ba6ad224ae` (2026-10-25); two Codex app-server test files only.
- Focused Codex app-server suites: 2 files, 21/21 tests passed on upstream base.
- Exact PR head 14bf56f9ea33: [GitHub Actions changed-extensions-config](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40253224772/job/121349722824) ran both changed test files, 21/21 passed. Its log includes the warm lifecycle injected-failure test and the monitor-failure binding-scope revocation test; the latter asserts a completed follow-up turn on the same native thread with the claim cleared. [CI gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40253224772/job/121351049271) passed. These are fixture-driven in-repo assertions, **not** a shipped Gateway/CLI lease-loss trace.
- Extension test typecheck, targeted format and lint pass; line-cap ratchet passes against `upstream/main` for the two changed files. (The default local ratchet base is `origin/main`, a divergent fork, and falsely flags unrelated upstream files.)
- No live service change or end-to-end field reproduction claimed.

**Follow-up proof correction (2026-10-27):** A Claude source review found the monitor case calls `releaseBindingAuthority()` (binding scope, not simulated lease expiry); the warm case now asserts ownership is held at the injected settlement fault and no cold `thread/resume` occurs before it. Updated head `71d416664521dc5f51bf3e6ac2a435786f91f07c`: focused Vitest 21/21, extension-test tsgo, targeted oxfmt/oxlint and diff check passed locally. Hosted CI is pending; no live lease-expiry or production fix is claimed.

prs.title: fix(telegram): route bound conversations when agent selection is ambiguous
prs.body:
Closes #159334

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Telegram conversation with an active session binding fails with `AgentSelectionRequiredError` on a multi-agent install that has no channel-wide Telegram route, so its messages are never processed.

## User Impact

User impact: runtime-bound Telegram conversations reach their bound agent regardless of how many agents are configured. Conversations without a binding, or whose binding names no agent, keep today's behavior — including still requiring an explicit channel owner. A binding revoked or replaced while a message is being routed no longer leaves the former owner selected.

## Why This Change Was Made

`prepareTelegramConversationRoute` asked ordinary agent selection for a route before looking at the binding, and ordinary selection refuses an ambiguous roster. It now selects the base route inside the SDK's `resolveRuntimeConversationBindingRouteAsync({ resolveRoute })` (and `inspectRuntimeConversationBindingRoute({ inspection, resolveRoute })` for route-owner inspection): the binding owner's canonically classified `boundAgentId` arrives before ordinary selection, and when it is set the base route is derived from session-only config with that agent as the default. This is the shared binding-owner selection Slack, Discord and iMessage use, so Telegram no longer re-implements the session-key/metadata classification. Topic overrides, configured bindings, and the runtime-binding step that follows are unchanged.

### Binding changes during resolution (review follow-up)

An earlier revision chose the agent from a synchronous binding read and then let `resolveRuntimeConversationBindingRouteAsync` read the binding again after an `await`, so a binding revoked in between could leave the former owner selected; that revision guarded it with a re-prepare/retry loop.

Since merging current `main` (`4ee4606`), agent selection runs inside the `resolveRoute` callback of the single awaited inspection, so the agent and the binding facts come from the same read. There is no second read to diverge from, and the retry loop is gone. The same applies to `prepareTelegramConversationRouteInspection` (new on `main`), whose `resolve(inspection)` now selects the agent from the inspection it is handed. `inspectTelegramConversationRouteAsync` shares the inbound path with `touchBinding: false`.

## Evidence

New cases in `conversation-route-owner.test.ts`, all on a two-agent config with no route bindings:

- inbound `resolveTelegramConversationRoute` selects the bound agent and session, reports `runtime-bound`, and touches the binding once;
- `inspectTelegramConversationRouteAsync` selects the bound agent without touching liveness;
- a sentinel `global` session with `metadata.agentId` selects that agent;
- a binding that names no agent still rejects with `AGENT_SELECTION_REQUIRED`;
- a binding revoked just before the awaited inspection rejects with `AGENT_SELECTION_REQUIRED` instead of routing to the former owner;
- a binding replaced just before the awaited inspection routes to the new owner and its new binding.

Negative controls: with `main`'s `conversation-route.ts` (`4ee4606`), 4 of these 6 fail with `AGENT_SELECTION_REQUIRED` (the bound-agent, inspection, sentinel-metadata and replacement cases); the no-agent and revocation cases pass there, as intended, since both assert that rejection.

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/conversation-route-owner.test.ts
19 passed (19)
$ pnpm test extensions/telegram
passed 63 Vitest shards
$ pnpm tsgo:extensions && pnpm tsgo:extensions:test
0 errors
```

Focused regression cost: `pnpm test extensions/telegram/src/conversation-route-owner.test.ts` — 19 tests, 16.4 s Vitest duration / 20.8 s wall time locally. `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check` and the assertion SAFETY ratchet are clean on the changed files. The test fixture uses `agents.entries` (the authored shape since `agents.list` was retired on `main`).

**Live Telegram proof:** not included. The `telegram-e2e-userbot` harness needs Convex-leased team credentials, which I don't have as an outside contributor. The evidence above is unit-level through the real binding-routing SDK with a test adapter.

AI-assisted. I reviewed the change and ran the tests and negative controls above locally.

prs.title: fix(agents): apply provider authHeader on simple completions
prs.body:
[AI-assisted]

## What Problem

For a provider configured with `authHeader: true`, agent turns send `Authorization: Bearer <key>` but **simple completions** (utility-model helpers such as conversation labels) do not. A gateway that only accepts a Bearer token rejects every helper call with `401`, while turns on the same provider and the same key return `200`.

From the report, the same model behaves differently by path: with Sonnet 4.6 as the utility model, cron turns pinned to Sonnet 4.6 succeed through the gateway while Sonnet *helper* calls get `401`.

## Why This Change Was Made

`applyAuthHeaderOverride` (`src/agents/model-auth-model.ts`) is the function that injects the canonical `Authorization: Bearer <apiKey>` header for `authHeader` providers. On main it is called from `run-attempt-dispatch.ts`, `prepared-compaction-runtime.ts`, and `decision-inference.ts` — but not from `prepareSimpleCompletionModel`.

That path instead only ran `applySecretRefHeaderSentinels`:

```ts
const model = applySecretRefHeaderSentinels(
  applyLocalNoAuthHeaderOverride(resolvedModel, resolvedAuth),
  params.cfg,
);
```

so the request carried only the SDK's vendor header (`x-api-key` for `anthropic-messages`) and never the Bearer token the gateway requires.

The fix is to use the same helper the turn path uses. `applyAuthHeaderOverride` already applies the secret-ref sentinels internally (it starts with `const sentinelModel = applySecretRefHeaderSentinels(model, cfg)`), so this is a drop-in replacement rather than an extra pass, and the helper path now picks up the provider's `authHeader` preference through the one owner that defines it:

```ts
const model = applyAuthHeaderOverride(
  applyLocalNoAuthHeaderOverride(resolvedModel, resolvedAuth),
  resolvedAuth,
  params.cfg,
);
```

Existing guards are preserved because they live in `applyAuthHeaderOverride` itself: no override without a real (non-sentinel) `apiKey`, no override when the provider does not set `authHeader`, and no clobbering of an already-prepared request auth (`requestAuth.mode !== "provider-default"`). The pre-existing `Authorization` strip keeps the header from being comma-joined.

## User Impact

Utility-model helper calls authenticate the same way as agent turns on `authHeader` providers, so conversation labels, compaction helpers, and the other simple-completion callers stop returning `401` behind a Bearer-only gateway. Providers without `authHeader` are unaffected, as is any path that prepared explicit request auth.

## Evidence

Two cases in `src/agents/simple-completion-runtime.test.ts`: the reported `authHeader: true` provider, and a control without `authHeader` that must not gain an `Authorization` header.

**Red on base** (implementation stashed, tests applied):

```text
 ×  agents-core  src/agents/simple-completion-runtime.test.ts > prepareSimpleCompletionModel > applies the provider authHeader bearer on the simple-completion path 563ms

prs.title: feat(talk): forward talk.speechLocale to realtime input transcription
prs.body:
Fixes #176044

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: realtime Talk input transcription guesses the language per utterance and mishears short phrases ("Yes" → "Ja.", "make the change" → "Make a deal.") when the operator has configured `talk.speechLocale`, because the OpenAI browser session builders never forward that locale to `audio.input.transcription.language`.

## User Impact

User impact: operators who set `talk.speechLocale` now get the same transcription language hint on Control UI/browser realtime Talk sessions that Android already derives from the same setting, so short utterances transcribe in the configured language instead of being auto-detected. Unset, malformed, and unknown locale values behave exactly as before (provider autodetect), and the native/relay paths are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildOpenAIRealtimeGaSessionPolicy` already accepts a `language` parameter and the relay/bridge path already forwards one; only the two browser session builders in `realtime-voice-provider-factory.ts` omitted it. This change resolves the ISO 639-1 component from `talk.speechLocale` once per `createBrowserSession` call and passes it to both builders — no new config option, no SDK/type surface change, no behavior change when the setting is unset. Locale handling mirrors the existing `resolveCallTranscriptionLanguage` precedent in `extensions/voice-call` (PR #190703): BCP-47 → ISO-639-1 via `Intl.Locale`, validated with `Intl.DisplayNames`, underscore form normalized the way the Android Talk config parser does.

## Evidence

**Base** `ab4074fb57e344ccf9ee3ae4f370b6642db374e4` → **Candidate** `447c588446762d9260b0bd1d7628cc0961b9bf65` (branch `fix/openai-talk-speech-locale-transcription`).

Red/green proof — new parameterized cases run against both refs (secretless, Node v24.22.1):

| Case (`talk.speechLocale`) | Expected `transcription.language` | Base | Candidate |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cs-CZ` (GA branch) | `cs` | ❌ red | ✅ green |
| `de_DE` (GA branch, underscore form) | `de` | ❌ red | ✅ green |
| `en` (GA branch) | `en` | ❌ red | ✅ green |
| `xx` (GA branch, unknown) | absent | ✅ | ✅ |
| unset (GA branch) | absent | ✅ | ✅ |
| `cs-CZ` (WebRTC branch) | `cs` | ❌ red | ✅ green |
| `en_US` (WebRTC branch) | `en` | ❌ red | ✅ green |
| `xx` / unset (WebRTC branch) | absent | ✅ | ✅ |

On base: 5 positive cases fail (missing `language`), all negative cases pass — confirming the defect and that the unset path is behaviorally unchanged by the fix. With the candidate: **64/64 tests pass** across the two touched test files.

Checks (all run in the isolated worktree on the pinned toolchain):

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/openai/realtime-voice-bridge-connection.test.ts \
  extensions/openai/realtime-voice-browser-auth.test.ts   → 64 passed, exit 0
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/openai         → 1178 passed, 1 failed (see gap)
node scripts/run-format.mts --check <3 files>             → clean
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs <3 files>                     → exit 0
node scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base <base>   → OK, slack 24
pnpm markdownlint-cli2 <2 docs files>                     → 0 issues
node scripts/format-docs.mts --check                      → clean
tsc -p tsconfig.extensions.json --noEmit                  → 18 errors, byte-identical with and without
                                                             this change (all in unrelated files:
                                                             codex/line/vault/policy…; tsgo binary
                                                             cannot run on this host's glibc 2.28,
                                                             tsc used as the supported alternative)
```

**Shipped Gateway diagnostic recording (both GA routes + unset control):** ran the shipped build (`dist/index.js` at `447c588446762d9260b0bd1d7628cc0961b9bf65`) as a real Gateway with `OPENCLAW_DEBUG_PROXY_ENABLED=1` and an isolated state dir, drove both GA session routes over the Gateway WebSocket API (`talk.client.create` → client-owned `client_secrets` POST; `talk.client.create` with `capabilities:["gateway-control-v1"]` → SDP offer redemption → Gateway `realtime/calls` multipart POST), and read the Gateway's built-in `capture_events` store. Environment note: this runner's DNS cannot reach `api.openai.com` directly, so the Gateway runs with the shipped inherited-routing marker `OPENCLAW_PROXY_ACTIVE=1`; both routes completed real TLS requests and OpenAI answered `403 unsupported_country_region_territory` (region block on this runner) — the captured request payloads are what this proof inspects. `Authorization` headers are auto-redacted by the capture store; payloads contain no API keys, IPs, or phone numbers.

| Leg | Route (captured outbound request) | `session.audio.input.transcription` |
|---|---|---|
| `speechLocale: "cs-CZ"` | A — Gateway-controlled GA → `POST /v1/realtime/calls` (multipart, 3794 B) | `{"model":"gpt-4o-mini-transcribe","language":"cs"}` ✅ |
| `speechLocale: "cs-CZ"` | B — client-owned → `POST /v1/realtime/client_secrets` (JSON, 3172 B) | `{"model":"gpt-4o-mini-transcribe","language":"cs"}` ✅ |
| unset (control) | A — `POST /v1/realtime/calls` (3778 B) | `{"model":"gpt-4o-mini-transcribe"}` — no `language` key ✅ |
| unset (control) | B — `POST /v1/realtime/client_secrets` (3156 B) | `{"model":"gpt-4o-mini-transcribe"}` — no `language` key ✅ |

The set/control byte deltas (−16 B each route) are exactly the `,"language":"cs"` fragment, confirming the forwarding is opt-in and the unset payload is otherwise unchanged.

Whole-PR delta: production +26/-0 (`extensions/openai/realtime-voice-provider-factory.ts`), tests +65/-0, docs +26/-25 (one sentence in 2 files + mechanical table re-alignment), test-lines allocation +4.

**Gaps / not claimed:** `extensions/openai/embedding-batch.test.ts > bounds batch output file content…` fails with `fetch failed` in this environment — reproduced identically on clean base with this change stashed, so it is pre-existing/environmental (local `createServer` + fetch), not caused by this PR. The shipped-Gateway recording proves the outbound session payloads on both GA routes but no live OpenAI realtime session was established — this runner's region is blocked by OpenAI (`403 unsupported_country_region_territory`), so no media flowed and no transcription-accuracy claim is made; the proof shows only that the configured language hint is now present in the session payload. No Windows or Azure-path coverage (browser sessions reject Azure endpoints before this code).

## Compatibility and Merge Risk

Two-way door: reverting restores the previous payload (no `language` key) without migrations or persisted-state changes. Blast radius is `createBrowserSession` in the OpenAI realtime provider — the two browser session payload builders; GPT-Live/quicksilver sessions, native bridges, relay sessions, Google/Azure realtime, and the dictation transcription provider are untouched. Unchanged when `talk.speechLocale` is unset (default): the resolved value is `undefined` and the key is omitted, byte-identical payloads to base.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Discord `channel-edit` reports success without changing forum or media thread tags when `appliedTags` is provided.

The action schema already exposes `appliedTags`, but the Discord channel-edit parser, payload type, and REST adapter did not carry it to Discord's `applied_tags` field. This change wires the value through and deliberately preserves an explicit empty array so callers can clear every tag.

prs.title: fix(exec): dollar amounts in agent messages are corrupted when exec text uses $<digit> in double quotes
prs.body:
Closes #179890

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: dollar amounts in agent-sent messages are silently corrupted ("$900" becomes "00") when an `exec` command passes the text in double quotes.

## User Impact

User impact: exec commands that would deliver a corrupted dollar amount are refused before they run. The refusal shows the text as written next to what the shell would deliver, and how to fix it (single quotes, `\$`, or a quoted heredoc), so the agent retries correctly instead of sending the wrong amount to a customer. It can be disabled with `OPENCLAW_EXEC_DOLLAR_GUARD=off`.

**Open question for maintainers:** this is default-on and uses an environment switch. If you'd prefer it opt-in, or shipped as a plugin on the existing `before_tool_call` hook instead of in core, I'm happy to rework it that way. Tell me which shape you want.

## Why This Change Was Made

`runBeforeToolCallHook` checks `exec` command text for a `$<digit>` that the shell would expand, before any plugin or approval policy runs. Codex-native shell commands reach the same policy through the PreToolUse native hook relay. Relay planning now counts the guard as a before-tool-call policy and keeps `exec` in the PreToolUse matcher, so native commands are covered even with no other policy installed.

The scanner is deliberately conservative. It only flags an expansion it can show would be empty:
- It honours single quotes, `\$`, `$'...'`, quoted heredoc delimiters, `${...}`, `$((...))` and comments.
- It recurses into `$(...)`, including substitutions inside unquoted heredoc bodies, with their own quoting.
- It ignores `$0` (the shell or script name) unless it reads as money (`$0.50`).
- It stays out of commands that define functions or set positional parameters (`set --`, `shift`, `getopts`), where `$1.00` may be intended.
- It fails open on anything it cannot parse.

Code-mode `exec` (JavaScript) is excluded.

## Evidence

- `src/agents/shell-dollar-expansion-guard.test.ts` (35 tests): the hazard shapes, every safe quoting form, `$0`, populated positional parameters, heredoc command substitution, `bash -lc` unwrapping, fail-open, and the `runBeforeToolCallHook` veto, allow and disable cases. The `$0`, positional-parameter and heredoc-substitution cases fail on the previous revision and pass now.
- `src/agents/harness/native-hook-relay.dollar-guard.test.ts` (6 tests): Codex `Bash` and `exec_command` are denied and single-quoted amounts pass. Relay planning enables PreToolUse for `exec` with no other policy and keeps it in a relay scoped to other tools; these planning cases fail without the relay change.
- The existing `agent-tools.before-tool-call*` and `native-hook-relay*` unit suites pass. `native-hook-relay.participants` and `native-hook-relay.remote-http` fail identically on `main` without this change in my environment.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, oxlint and oxfmt are clean.
- Replayed against 391 unique `$`-bearing exec commands from a production deployment: 18 were flagged, all genuine expansion bugs, with no false positives.
- Still to add: a gateway trace of a real agent refusing and retrying. I'll attach it before asking for re-review.

prs.title: fix(test): avoid repeated release fixture compiler starts
prs.body:
Related: #186423

## What Problem This Solves

Release checklist tests repeatedly start Node to strip identical fixture programs for each scenario.

## User Impact

No product behavior change. This removes repeated test setup while retaining every scenario, fresh sandbox, real fixture repository, mock, assertion and cleanup path.

## Why This Change Was Made

Prepare each of six fixed programs lazily at the test-file owner using Node's existing strip-only helper and vm.Script. Reuse compiled code only; each evaluation still creates a fresh VM context. The two singleton checklist programs stay unchanged. Filtered-out programs do no preparation. Selected Node, warning suppression and parser isolation remain unchanged under both Node and Bun.

Production: 0 lines changed. Tests: net -6 lines. No new helper, runtime option, retry, timeout, mock or weakened assertion.

## Evidence

Initial compiled-Script variant, exact head e0295c1056c4bf6c3386118abb096abdc31ee765: **HOLD**. Actual stripping children fell 58 -> 8; every complete run retained the same ordered 149 passing cases. Node26.12.1 and pinned Bun1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1 both passed; each representative filtered run passed its one selected case and started zero stripping children. Type-aware lint, formatting and independent source reviews passed for this head.

Five serial interleaved baseline/candidate pairs; one count-instrumented warm-up per revision excluded. Timed runs used the original, uninstrumented Node helper. Values are median / nearest-rank p95 [min, max]:

| Metric | Baseline | Initial candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Wall seconds | 17.720 / 18.990 [12.960, 18.990] | 12.840 / 14.130 [10.910, 14.130] |
| Body seconds | 13.545 / 14.836 [9.957, 14.836] | 9.156 / 11.080 [8.406, 11.080] |
| User CPU seconds | 8.720 / 9.800 [7.160, 9.800] | 5.920 / 6.150 [4.720, 6.150] |
| System CPU seconds | 4.670 / 5.000 [3.380, 5.000] | 3.530 / 3.820 [2.910, 3.820] |
| Peak RSS MiB | 479.281 / 484.438 [454.531, 484.438] | 482.531 / 483.422 [477.375, 483.422] |

Median wall improved 27.5%, but median RSS increased 0.7%; the recorded rule is not met. Load averages during timed samples ranged 14.439-22.557 (one minute). The count-only probe explicitly preloaded actual selected-Node parser children; an initial failed probe was discarded because test isolation clears inherited NODE_OPTIONS.

A strings-only alternative restores baseline VM compilation while retaining one-time stripping, but its natural formatted change adds nine ratcheted test lines. Independent source review found no honest removable setup within these two files; it is not being forced past the existing ceiling. That uncommitted alternative was discarded. The retained compiled-Script head remains on performance hold; this draft is not ready to merge.

Acceptance rule, recorded before the first benchmark: run the two complete files in their original case order with supported Node26.12.1 on the same qualified macOS checkout, serial maxWorkers=1, five interleaved baseline/candidate pairs after one excluded warm-up per revision. Measure actual stripping children separately, require identical ordered case names/results, and report wall/body time, user/sys CPU, peak RSS, median/p95 and host load. Counts must be58 -> 8; wall/body/CPU/RSS must hold or improve; record a regression as a hold. Keep cold preparation separate from steady comparisons. Also run complete-file Bun parity and representative filtered checks to prove unused programs stay unprepared.

Any future changed candidate needs fresh source review, full runtime parity and a prospective baseline/candidate comparison; these timings qualify only the retained head.

No Windows, hosted-minute or billed-cost saving is claimed.

prs.title: fix(agents): a quota-class failure should prefer the model chain over a same-profile auth rotation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On a quota-class provider failure (HTTP 429 with a usage/plan-limit body), the embedded agent rotates the auth profile and re-runs the **same** model before the configured model-fallback chain is consulted. When the provider has exactly one usable profile - or when the rotation re-selects the profile that just failed - that rotation is a no-op: it spends a provider attempt against the same exhausted plan and delays the chain that could have recovered the run.

The `rate_limit` path already has a rotation cap that escalates to the model chain (`MAX_RATE_LIMIT_PROFILE_ROTATIONS`), and the `overloaded` path escalates through `overloadProfileRotationLimit`. What is missing is the rule that **a rotation which lands on the same profile is not a rotation at all**.

## User Impact

A quota-class failure now advances the model chain in the same failure instead of burning an attempt on the exhausted profile first. A run that has a working fallback chain configured recovers on the first quota error rather than the second.

## Why This Change Was Made

`advanceAuthProfileCandidate` advances by **index** over the prepared auth attempts. When two prepared attempts carry the same profile id (an OAuth attempt and an inline attempt for the same profile, or two routes for one profile), the "rotation" re-selects the profile that just failed and still reports success. The caller then retries the same model against the same exhausted plan.

The fix keeps profile rotation useful whenever it can actually change the credentials:

- The rotation is reported as a rotation only when the active profile changes.
- When the rotation re-selects the failed profile and a model chain is configured, the controller reports "no rotation", so the failover policy resolves to `fallback_model` and the chain advances immediately.
- Without a configured chain the existing same-profile retry is preserved, so a single-model deployment loses nothing.

Scope notes:

- The `overloaded` path is untouched.
- The session/request model-pin contract (#151980) is untouched; this change is about auth profiles, not model pins.
- The failed profile is still marked in cooldown exactly as before; only the decision to *retry* the same profile changes.

Related: #141115 (a 429 must consult the chain - this PR is the ordering half of that class), #151980 (session model pins stay strict; this change touches auth profiles, not model pins), #186418 (the request-level ladder half, carried by #186420).

## Evidence

Focused test run on this branch (rebased onto main at `fdeb8f7e`):

    node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-embedded-agent-run.config.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/failover-retry-controller.test.ts
    -> Test Files  1 passed (1), Tests  42 passed (42)

New coverage in `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/failover-retry-controller.test.ts`:

- a quota-class rotation that re-selects the failed profile reports no rotation, so the caller advances the model chain;
- a quota-class rotation that moves to a different profile still reports a rotation and still counts toward the rotation cap;
- without a configured model chain the same-profile rotation still retries, so single-model deployments keep their existing recovery.

One existing fixture was updated: "waits for the provider floor before exhausting recovery and rotating credentials" used an `advanceAttemptAuthProfile` stub that returned `true` without moving the active profile. A successful rotation moves the active profile, so the stub now does the same; the assertions are unchanged.

prs.title: fix: keep OpenClaw ID snapshots refreshing after restart
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes periodic OpenClaw ID snapshot publication stopping after a Gateway restart republishes a snapshot within the same timestamp second.

## User Impact

The Gateway resumes regular snapshot refresh after Discovery rejects a duplicate timestamp, so browser access does not later lose freshness evidence because the refresh timer stopped. The refused attempt still appears as failed; this change does not claim remote acceptance or add immediate retries for a lagging snapshot sequence.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discovery requires a newer `issued_at` when the snapshot sequence is unchanged. A `stale_snapshot` response previously left startup without a refresh timer. The existing publication owner now rearms its regular refresh for that response, covering scheduled and direct publication paths while preserving lifecycle stop behavior and other error handling.

No new scheduler, state, configuration, dependency, or migration is introduced. The regression adds exactly 47 test lines; its per-change allocation records the service restart boundary proof. The production delta is +11/-9 lines, including comments and log correction.

## Evidence

- New service regression fails on the original source: a same-second restart is refused and no later idle publication occurs. Six existing service cases pass on that base.
- Fixed owner/sibling suites: 37 passed across `service.publication-refresh.test.ts`, `publication-retry.test.ts`, and `publisher.test.ts`, also independently repeated.
- The new regression anchors the clock, preserves failed status without an accepted receipt or immediate retry, then observes a newer accepted snapshot and the next refresh deadline.
- Targeted Gateway typecheck, lint, formatting, whitespace, and test-line ratchet pass.
- Exact-head [CI run 42329848576](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42329848576) completed successfully on `6b9bd4130a65312e558ddd821dcbe0a9bbd9945d`; `openclaw/ci-gate` is successful. Draft-era skipped checks are not counted as test proof.
- Independent source review: no remaining P0–P2 findings.
- Canonical Codex autoreview of the committed change against `7ab0143fc2288251377d0b355b1c78a30c1b55ac`: `scoped-clean`, no P0–P2 findings. Static review; it did not execute project tests.
- Isolated interoperability proof passed using the production publisher, retry owner and Discovery client against the actual Discovery Worker/D1: startup, same-second restart refusal followed by idle refresh, outage/retry recovery, membership publication, and server-key rotation without a membership change. This is composed module proof with synthetic identity and shortened scheduler dependencies, not a full deployed Gateway process. No live service was changed or deployed.

Simplification retained one predicate in the existing publication wrapper and one service-boundary regression.

## What Problem This Solves

Prepares the regression starting point for long SMS failing on Samsung/Optus when Android's carrier-aware message division throws a phone-state permission error.

## User Impact

**Draft handoff only: no production fix or user-visible behavior change yet.** This PR contains unfinished regression scaffolding for RoboClaw to continue. It is not ready to merge.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reproduction calls the production SMS sender with a carrier-divider shadow that throws `SecurityException("getGroupIdLevel1")`. Cases cover long GSM text, Unicode, GSM extension characters, and a surrogate boundary, with permission and successful-platform-division controls.

Existing work: #166334 by @Minhal128 and #159558. Their branches are untouched. Recheck both before implementing or reusing code and preserve contributor credit where applicable. The reviewed concern with #166334 is that 67 Unicode units plus a four-character non-EMS page indicator can exceed the 70-unit single-message limit.

- Establish a genuine failing reproduction; correct the draft fixture if needed.
- Implement the smallest fallback in the existing SMS owner. Keep normal platform segmentation and permission enforcement intact.

- Run the focused third-party Android test, formatting/lint, and applicable build checks. Obtain Samsung/Optus or equivalent framework-path evidence before claiming real-device delivery.

Related: #177312

## What Problem This Solves

The plugin management guide gives operators an incomplete description of recovery when a reload fails after services and channels begin stopping.

## User Impact

Operators reading the guide can see that automatic recovery may also follow a failure while draining admitted work or waiting for service shutdown, before replacement registration begins.

## Why This Change Was Made

The recovery sentence currently names only registration and pre-publication activation failures. It now describes the broader boundary already used by the implementation and the SDK runtime guide: once services and channels begin stopping, a failure before publication can trigger fresh registration of the captured previous code and configuration.

prs.title: fix(apple): dead Gateway sockets stay "connected" for up to two minutes when keepalive pongs stop
prs.body:
Closes #194219

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the iOS and macOS apps keep showing a Gateway connection as live for 60 to 120 seconds after the socket stops answering, when nothing changes on the local network (weak cellular signal, a NAT or proxy silently dropping the flow).

## User Impact

User impact: a socket that misses two keepalive pongs in a row, with no other traffic arriving, is dropped and reconnected, so the app notices a dead link within about 35 to 50 seconds. Before, this took 60 to 120 seconds on macOS and in background node sessions, and about 45 to 63 seconds in the foreground iOS app. A single late pong, or a slow link that is still delivering data, keeps the connection.

## Why This Change Was Made

`GatewayChannelActor` already pings every 15 seconds with a 10 second pong deadline, but it threw the result away. The only remaining detectors were the tick watchdog, which checks every 2x the tick interval (60 to 120 seconds with the default 30 second tick), and the network path probe from #168024, which only runs after a path change. On iOS the foreground health monitor helps (about 45 to 63 seconds), but macOS and background node sessions only had the ticks.

The keepalive loop now counts consecutive ping failures for its socket. A successful pong resets the count. So does any inbound frame received while the ping was outstanding: on a slow link a pong can queue behind a large server-to-client payload, and a socket that is still delivering data is alive. The receive path keeps a frame counter for this, and the keepalive compares it before and after each ping. At two misses it retires the socket through the same `transitionToDisconnected(shouldReconnect: true)` path the network path probe uses, with the same guards: the connection generation must still be current, reconnect must not be paused for an auth failure, and the channel must not be shutting down. Pending requests on that socket fail with "gateway socket unresponsive to keepalive pings".

Accepted edge case: an idle link that is alive but so slow that two pongs in a row take longer than 10 seconds, with no inbound frames in between, now reconnects. That is the same pong deadline the keepalive already used, and the reconnect goes through the normal backoff.

A DEBUG-only `testKeepaliveSleep` seam drives the loop in tests. It is separate from `testRecoverySleep` because the path recovery fixture makes that one return immediately, which would make the keepalive loop spin and change existing ping counts.

## Evidence

### Real Gateway proof

The shipped `GatewayChannelActor` connected to a real `openclaw gateway run` built from base `cb73e59f935`: loopback only, token auth, an isolated state directory, channels and Bonjour off. The client is a device-less operator using the shared token (`client=openclaw-ios mode=ui role=operator`), with the production timers (15 s keepalive, 10 s pong deadline, the Gateway's 30 s tick) and no network path updates. 35 s after hello the proof test froze the Gateway process with SIGSTOP. The TCP connection stays open, but the Gateway answers no pongs and sends no ticks. When the client reported its disconnect, the test resumed the Gateway with SIGCONT so the replacement handshake reached the same Gateway. Harness: [`rig/real-gateway.diff`](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/6c0e892c75edfd369da89a85c34a3864a1910578/rig/real-gateway.diff) and [`rig/real-gateway.sh`](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/6c0e892c75edfd369da89a85c34a3864a1910578/rig/real-gateway.sh) (proof only, not in this PR; the linked script is the hosted-runner variant, and the local runs used the same steps with local paths and the byte-identical `real-gateway.diff`). Trees: base + harness `46b4a414220`, head `1c4b421973d` + harness `11ed46dc9ae`. Xcode 27.2 (27B52), Swift 6.4.2, Node 24.22.2, macOS 27.2.

| | Base `cb73e59f935` | Head `1c4b421973d` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Gateway frozen (SIGSTOP) | t=37.29 s | t=36.68 s |
| Client retires the socket | t=124.56 s, `gateway tick missed; reconnecting` | t=82.58 s, `gateway socket unresponsive to keepalive pings` |
| Time frozen before the client noticed | 87.3 s | 45.9 s (enough for two unanswered keepalive pings plus the 10 s pong deadline) |
| Replacement hello from the real Gateway | t=125.24 s, generation 2 | t=83.24 s, generation 2 |
| Gateway log on resume | "process was frozen ~81855ms", then EPIPE on the old connection, new `client connected` | "main-thread stall: elapsedMs=43719", new `client connected` |

The test passes on both trees, because it only checks that a replacement connection arrives within 180 s. The difference is the disconnect reason and the timing.

<details><summary>Client and Gateway output (copied from the saved logs; token, hostname and home paths redacted)</summary>

```

The fixture sends Gateway ticks every 30 s, then about 35 s after hello goes silent: it keeps reading and records every ping, but sends no pongs, ticks or other frames. The same harness ran on base + harness (tree `112f483ceee`) and on head + harness (tree `5d06ec3ad73`), Xcode 27.2 (27B52), Swift 6.4.2, macOS 27.2. | Time from silence to retirement | 87.8 s | 47.0 s |
| Replacement hello | t=125.21 s, generation 2 | t=84.71 s, generation 2 |

In both runs the fixture decoded a second Gateway `connect` frame on a new connection (`replacement connect frame decoded=true`). On base the socket kept looking connected through three unanswered pings until the tick watchdog fired; on head it was retired about 10.5 s after the second unanswered ping, which is the pong deadline. While pongs are missing, pings are about 26 s apart: the 15 s keepalive sleep plus the 10 s pong deadline.

Three tests in `GatewayNetworkPathRecoveryTests`, driven by the injected keepalive sleep and held pongs on the fake socket (no real time):

- `a keepalive miss between healthy pongs keeps the socket`: miss, healthy pong, miss leaves the same socket and connection generation.
- `inbound frames during missed pongs keep a busy socket`: three pings in a row miss their pongs, but a response frame arrives while each one is outstanding; the socket and connection generation are kept.

prs.title: chore(android): prepare WebSocket backlog recovery regression
prs.body:
Related: #127406

## What Problem This Solves

Prepares a production-listener regression for Android retaining an unbounded WebSocket backlog and delaying disconnect/reconnect behind accepted frames.

## User Impact

**Draft handoff only: no production fix or user-visible behavior change yet.** This PR contains unfinished regression scaffolding for RoboClaw to continue. It is not ready to merge.

## Why This Change Was Made

The regression blocks the existing message pump, queues a connect response containing an issued token, fills candidate count/UTF-8-byte budgets, and exercises explicit overload closure. It aims to preserve accepted connect-token persistence and a single terminal callback while rejecting subsequent work.

Current production still uses `Channel.UNLIMITED`. The adjacent merged #135878 intentionally excluded this issue. The scaffold assumes candidate limits of 256 retained frames, 25 MiB per frame, and 50 MiB total; the byte sizes align with current Gateway payload/send-buffer constants, but the final Android policy and recovery semantics still need review. Counter-field assertions are provisional and must follow the final implementation or be replaced with observable proof.

### RoboClaw handoff

- Run and validate the failing production-listener reproduction before editing production code.
- Add atomic per-socket count and UTF-8-byte admission accounting with exact reservation release, including failure/retirement paths.
- On overload, visibly retire/close the physical socket and use normal reconnect recovery. Do not silently drop protocol frames or replay writes with unknown outcomes.
- Preserve FIFO handling and persistence of an already accepted one-time connect token. Do not force-cancel accepted side effects merely to shorten teardown.
- Validate disconnect/replacement, budget reuse, repeated overflow, and normal event/response ordering. Distinguish a finite backlog from a guarantee that an arbitrary blocking handler returns.
- Complete focused Android tests/build/lint, independent review, and update evidence before marking ready.

## Evidence

- Starting source: `7ab0143fc22` from current main; unlimited admission confirmed by source inspection.
- Independent source inspection of the initial test scaffold and `git diff --check`: completed.
- Focused Gradle attempts were started, but no verified result is included. No passing build/test, established red/green result, production repair, or device proof is claimed.
- Focused command: `cd apps/android && ./gradlew :app:testThirdPartyDebugUnitTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.gateway.GatewaySessionReconnectTest.inboundOverloadClosesOnceAndDrainsTheAcceptedConnectToken --no-daemon --max-workers=2`.
- Initial publication is intentionally test-only at the requester's request for an early maintainer handoff; the linked issue is not closed by this draft.

prs.title: fix(skills): skill picker titles skills from embedded boilerplate headings
prs.body:
Closes #184724

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: skills that embed a shared boilerplate section in their SKILL.md body all render that section's heading as their title in the composer skill picker, so distinct skills can appear with identical labels.

## User Impact

User impact: a skill's picker title now comes from a heading that opens the skill's own body — the SKILL.md convention — instead of the first `#` heading found anywhere in the body. Skills that embed a shared reference section keep distinct labels. This changes title selection for skills whose first heading follows introductory prose; that policy requires maintainer review.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveSkillDisplayName` matched the first ATX `#` heading anywhere in the body (`/m` flag) and used the frontmatter `name` only when the body had no heading at all. The Agent Skills spec treats frontmatter `name` as the skill identity, and a heading buried in the body is ordinary prose that often belongs to embedded shared content — in the reporter's install, the embedded spec's `# AI-First Note Rules` heading sits at the end of 47 of 49 skills and titles all of them.

The display title now requires the heading to open the body (after leading blank lines). Later headings fall back to the skill's identity: the frontmatter `name`, then the humanized directory name. Skills whose body starts with their own title — including every bundled and custodian skill and the pinned library flow, which asserts heading-derived display titles for such skills — keep the exact display they have today. Anchoring to the body opening preserves the deliberate heading-title design (the library flow's "keeps the heading separate from the selected command identity" behavior) while removing the boilerplate pollution the issue reports.

## Evidence

- New unit tests in `src/skills/loading/skill-materializer.test.ts`. Against unpatched `origin/main`, exactly the boilerplate case fails (title came out as "AI-First Note Rules" from the embedded section at the end of the body); with the fix all four cases pass: boilerplate heading ignored ("Obsidian Save" from the frontmatter name), body-opening heading kept ("Short Description"), title heading after leading blank lines kept, and the humanized fallback without any heading.
- Every existing assertion is unchanged: `skills.test.ts` heading-derived display, `library/service.test.ts` "keeps the heading separate from the selected command identity" (heading case still renders "Friendly Title"), and the bundled/custodian skills whose bodies open with their titles.
- `pnpm test` passes on all suites exercising the materializer and its consumers: `src/skills/loading/`, `src/skills/library/`, `src/skills/discovery/`, skills runtime resources, embedded agent runner skill-runtime suites, and the CLI live session registry. The one red file, `workspace-skill-sync.runtime.test.ts` ("preserving unchanged destinations"), fails identically on unpatched `origin/main` on this machine (macOS temp-dir ENOENT) and is untouched by this PR.
- `pnpm check:changed`: typecheck core, typecheck core tests, lint, formatting, and the guard lanes pass. The only red lane is the pre-existing `deadcode` unused-export scan, which flags three exports in files this PR does not touch (`src/infra/sqlite-worker-operation-settlement.ts`, `src/boards/board-store.fixtures.test-support.ts`, `src/commands/cleanup-command.test-support.ts`); no path owned by this PR appears in its output.


**Follow-up:** Leading blank lines are now skipped without stripping indentation from the first content line, so an indented code block is not treated as a title. The new regression failed on the prior PR head and passed with this change. The materializer and library suites passed (28 tests); targeted lint, formatting and core typecheck passed. The full changed check was stopped before completion. The isolated autoreview completed on the full PR branch with an available account model and reported no actionable P0–P2 findings. Real Gateway picker proof and the title-precedence decision remain outstanding.
