prs.title: fix(ios): preserve blocked shares for native chat import
prs.body:
## Ready for review — technical CI succeeded; administrative label exception

Head `6c3149153a6c2aa4d54f53af4cbdf388703c561d`; exact tree `810841b4656eaa0fbb2521628a69336ff9ccfc0e`; direct parent `bb03e49471a91c17c6d261a541c0747f9990da96`. Accepted reconciliation base remains `7302f00ac3eea8d12f84b3591fb451564a7fed7e`. Full scope: **19 files +1292/−73**, no authored workflow delta. Ready for review is not merge-ready or merge authorization.

## Behavior preserved

Save complete original share text/bytes; manually open OpenClaw; explicitly review/import into the intended Gateway/agent/chat’s empty composer. No automatic send, unrelated draft overwrite, parallel upload pipeline or app-private database relocation. Current destination/session/composer authority is revalidated after awaited preparation, and complete staging precedes saved-copy deletion. Existing native attachment budgets and attachment-pinned active-config/focus/restoration ownership remain authoritative.

The protected SQLite inbox retains its approved 48-hour expiry, 50-share/50-attachment and 48-MiB aggregate limits, with 128-KiB text/share. Failed import/cancelled review retains it; explicit discard, expiry on access and successful staging clean up. Displayed expiry remains a localized absolute date/time, with unchanged actual expiry enforcement. Both typography tests/all seven assertions and canonical maintained MAIN fixture1102 remain intact.

## New native CI root and reviewed repair

After the earlier formatter hotfix, [bb03 native screenshot build](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42182648139/job/127776109746) reached **SwiftLint** and failed there before tests. The immutable CI checkout4cf7c932… and CI-base8a186ad7… lint configurations/pins/wrapper match published source; the affected checkout modules match bb03. This is not evidence of an additional compiler/runtime defect.

This follow-up changes **three shared files +71/−23**: attachment parameters/arguments are laid out one per line without token/operand/API changes; the inbox reader rejects invalid stored text; one narrow actual-SQLite regression is added. SQL, user messages, filenames, format placeholders, schema, permissions, durability and retention are unchanged. No rule/config/pin/suppression or budget edits.

### UTF-8 integrity boundary

Swift String producers bind valid UTF-8 with explicit byte counts, preserving empty strings, Unicode and embedded NULs. Every selected metadata TEXT column is STRICT NOT NULL; no-row handling is unchanged. SQLite can nevertheless contain malformed TEXT. The private reader now uses failable `String(bytes:encoding:.utf8)` and throws the existing `SharedDraftError.unavailable` instead of silently replacing bytes with U+FFFD or returning an empty error fallback. Already-throwing destination/pending/materialize APIs propagate that error to existing UI catches. No row is silently skipped/deleted and no attachment cleanup is added; materialization unwinds before discard.

The new Swift Testing regression injects malformed SQLite TEXT, expects the typed storage error, restores text, and verifies the same row ID/target survives. **Authored, not executed with Swift locally.** Supplemental Python/SQLite confirms the corruption fixture and strict-vs-lossy decode behavior only—not execution of the Swift owner. Existing valid embedded-NUL/Unicode round-trip assertions are preserved.

## Current bounded local proof

Official checksum-verified **SwiftLint0.65.1** Linux static asset: canonical `scripts/lint-swift.sh ios` reproduced17 violations and now exits0 with0/516. **Coverage is partial:** the official Linux route cannot run SourceKit-dependent `custom_rules`, `literal_expression_end_indentation` or `statement_position`; this local result does not independently establish native Mac rule parity. The configured native formatter/linter/compiler path subsequently completed in successful iOS test builds; no independent rule-by-rule Mac parity audit was performed. The dynamic variant’s newer-library requirement was not bypassed by host changes.

Canonical **SwiftFormat0.63.1** iOS entry remains green,0/516. Required native-source verify and actual source admission pass with `strict_native_i18n=false`; **67 Node tests/three source/i18n consumer files pass**, not native SharedKit execution. Accepted-base test-line/line-cap/assertion-safety/mock-export, docs format/list and whitespace pass. Fresh whole19-file LOCAL P0–P3 review against commit7302f00… is scoped-clean. Local style parsers/static review are not Swift compilation or full CI proof.

Native source plus stable-ID inventory only is shipped; serialized locale automation owns translated dictionaries/platform catalogs. The168 genuine values remain private/deferred and not expert-linguistically validated. No translated dictionary, generated catalog or inventory changes accompany this repair.

## Observed native CI — terminal at 2026-11-06 08:38:24 UTC

For source head `6c314915…`, actual CI preparation used merge checkout `a8b22f647c2c7857011e2b22eb4311532fbf50e9`, parents `5bd69e0a3365a3095df1d34576a6885de6fdf5d3` + `6c3149153a6c2aa4d54f53af4cbdf388703c561d`. These are CI-composition results, not a bare-head execution claim.

- [iOS Periphery build job127787287100](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42186181607/job/127787287100): success; **TEST BUILD SUCCEEDED at08:34:26 UTC**. Configured formatter/lint/compiler phases completed without the prior errors. Periphery workflow:8 jobs,7 success/1 skip/0 fail.
- [Release screenshot UI job127787635311](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42186181515/job/127787635311): success; **4 selected tests,0 failures,70.214s**. Images remain **uninspected**. Execution CI:49 jobs,20 success/29 skip/0 fail.
- CI dispatch42186181518:1 success/1 skip. Complete workflow inventory: **14 workflows,7 success/6 skipped/1 administrative failure/0 active**. Skips are not passing test executions.

### Administrative exception — not all workflows green

[Label job127786943161 / run42186178740](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42186178740/job/127786943161) failed parsing `.github/labeler.yml`: YAMLException, duplicate key `extensions: deep-research` at613:2. That job checked out `5bd69e0a…`; the key occurs at554 and613, file SHA-256 `8170eea60bbb0559789fe6579ede8f6915051787a29355f825af0b3bc5681a93`.

The PR source6c314915 and accepted base7302f00 labeler files are byte-identical, SHA-256 `c9cf99fdac0fa801aa3553a261111be8510d39e174c199904944597505de296b`, with that key once at609. This is an attributed shared job-configuration parse failure outside PR-authored changes, **not token, permission, rate or native-code failure**. Follow-up: maintainers should reconcile the labeler configuration actually selected by that job. No shared config/workflow repair or rerun was attempted here, and no claim is made about unqueried current-default-main state.

## Proof limits retained

The new25-line malformed-UTF8 SQLite regression is authored but **not observed executing** in these jobs. Local67 Node passes are not native SharedKit test execution; Linux static lint still has the three documented SourceKit skips. Successful iOS test-build and four selected release UI cases do not establish all-native acceptance, actual Photos/Files Share→save→reopen→original-chat import, complete-byte/FIFO/live-authority behavior, live Gateway/no-auto-send, standalone normal app+embedded-Watch qualification, compatibility/upgrade, exact-case red/green, or inspected before/after screenshot evidence. Those boundaries remain unproven here.

[Historical23-pass simulator evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191527#issuecomment-6606246736) and [recovered source artifact](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191527#issuecomment-6608874552) remain scoped to older focused source—not the new regression or broad native execution. Runner-local results were not independently replayed, and historical generated-input identity was not established. Prior aggregate Process/sidebar failures are not erased or promoted to current broad-package passes. No manual CI dispatch/rerun, CW request, Ready flip or merge.

prs.title: improve(ci): skip unnecessary boundary-test parsing
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The required extension boundary guard parses every tracked core test source on each applicable CI run, including files that cannot contain an extension import.

## User Impact

Reduces work in the mandatory CI guard without changing test selection, isolation, or boundary coverage. Part of the maintainer-directed adaptive-CI cost reduction work.

## Why This Change Was Made

Screen source text before invoking the existing AST parser. Every source containing `extensions` or a backslash still receives full parsing, including escaped module paths. All sources are still read; the existing import rules remain authoritative. Literal and escaped imports have regression coverage.

## Evidence

- Frozen base `266a7aa0fe69e2b5fe6445c4ceb1e15b5360c957`: 14,444 scanned sources; 6,225 still require parsing, avoiding 8,219 parses (56.9%).
- Full focused suite: 13 tests passed. Targeted lint, format, and `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.root.other.json` typecheck passed.
- One same-machine warm-cache pair through `scripts/run-vitest.mjs`: guard body 6.003s → 3.480s; total invocation 11.762s → 8.743s. This is local evidence, not a measured Blacksmith billing saving; cache preparation and timing noise remain in total wall time.
- Local ClawSweeper committed-range review: base `266a7aa0fe69e2b5fe6445c4ceb1e15b5360c957`, head `ce4fc367fbba25b60e413fc950204bdc756bbc98`; complete, no actionable correctness or security findings.
- Production lines: unchanged. Test lines: net +21; matching allocation +21.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Share failing against a Gateway that native chat can reach using approved TLS trust or custom service headers. Reconnect OpenClaw after upgrading or changing headers to refresh Share access. Browser Access still requires the main app; Share retains its separate identity and cannot approve certificates.

**Ready for review: source reconciliation is complete and the bounded Ready-triggered workflow set is terminal (6 success, 5 skipped; no failures or active runs, observed 2026-11-06 07:03 UTC). This is not merge-ready or native acceptance, and no merge is authorized.**

## Source and Ownership

Published head: `c39b33bf4501aa9f490e2468db9ec860981dc34f`. Exact reviewed tree: `ba2be1abd4784d3f6feb38ecd958870255c91318`. Accepted main/review base: `9c8db2d231b57a70c68ff71c6fbdcdd8f511fe27`. Feature delta: **11 files, +206/−18**, zero workflow delta against that base.

The existing shared Keychain/TLS owners carry explicit approved pins and service headers, bind credentials to exact Gateway identity and URL, recheck current authority before upgrade, disable redirects/ambient credentials, and retire saved Share access when host transport authority changes. No admission/result, extraction/handoff, configuration, or protocol-version change is included.

Raw commit headers and the fetched graph verify prior PR head `9df2fbc9d585f534c49e2c646e59736e8f1e2ecc` and accepted main as ancestors. Publication commit `c39b33b…` follows integration `9e8d57e…`, whose parents are `587996e…` and accepted main. All six newly published task-owned commits retain required human credit.

Canonical fixture blob `1102d368ac888322b162bf494d1a3cd9489fdb63` exactly matches upstream; the old private-helper repair is superseded. Current focused-session and active-config authority owners are preserved.

Native localization follows the same-base source-owner contract: **source strings plus stable-ID inventory only**. The 21 translated dictionaries and iOS catalog were restored to accepted-base versions; prepared genuine translations remain private for the serialized locale owner. No manual generated rows, policy waiver, paid translation, or English fallback masquerading as translation was used.

## Evidence

### Fresh checks

- Actual 11-path source-admission predicate passes; `strict_native_i18n=false`. Required final-tree `native:i18n:verify` passes with **4,633 entries**. Earlier aggregate strict-check success concerned a temporary generated tree, not this final source packet.

- Exact-base whitespace and test-line ratchet pass: **6,527,544 ≤ 6,527,571**. Line-cap reports zero counted changed source files. Generic formatting passes for one supported file; native-state schema v39 and relevant docs MDX checks pass.
- Fresh canonical **one-pass LOCAL P0–P3 whole-candidate review**, exact accepted commit: `scoped-clean`, no findings. Receipt SHA-256: `649ab74d41c3ab47c942e9855de0a039b354ed4cff6f3e8200c0530c42a482de`. Static review is not native execution.

### Reused/qualified inputs

Root physical dependencies were reused only after multidocument-lock comparison: changes affect `extensions/deep-research` and `extensions/rerank` importers only; root importer, packages, snapshots, global settings, manifest, and workspace policy are unchanged. Node 24.20.0 and declared pnpm 12.15.0 were used. No reinstall, dependency-pin, or guard change was necessary.

All retained feature blobs and current header/TLS owner contracts are unchanged from the prior reviewed source-only packet. The old hypothetical TOFU-pin finding remains separately declined: direct iOS policies disable TOFU; rotation installs an explicit reviewed fingerprint. The fresh review found no reachable defect; no future TOFU support or extra pinning policy is claimed.

### Ready-triggered hosted evidence

At **2026-11-06 07:03 UTC**, the bounded parent-observed workflow set for head `c39b33bf4501aa9f490e2468db9ec860981dc34f` was terminal: **11 workflows = 6 success + 5 skipped, 0 failures, 0 active**. These bounded counts are not a claim that every optional check executed.

The parent directly inspected [job 127754476751](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42175913680/job/127754476751), verified its head and success, and observed **`TEST BUILD SUCCEEDED` at 06:58:39 UTC**. This metadata update's narrower job reread was unavailable; it does not replace the parent's inspected receipt.

prs.title: improve(chat): stop rebuilding every reply's source cards when a transcript message arrives
prs.body:
Closes #193862
Related: #193741

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the iOS and macOS chat rebuilds the source cards of every cited reply in the session each time a message is added to the transcript or history reloads, so long researched sessions spend milliseconds of main-thread time per update.

## User Impact

User impact: long chat sessions with cited answers do much less main-thread work while an agent turn runs and when history refreshes; the source cards shown are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ChatSourcePreviewProjector` already kept each message's parsed links and result fields, but still rebuilt cards for every cited reply on every call. It now keeps each reply's cards and rebuilds them only when one of their inputs changed: the reply itself, an earlier message of the same run, the ids of those earlier messages (a removal, insert or reorder), or the source context. Those are all the inputs of the card builder. Rendered titles and excerpts are still shared between replies in one cache, as before, and are kept only for the cited replies that remain. A first projection does the same dictionary work as before: each rendered value is looked up and stored once, and each reply also records the values it used in a plain array. The shared cache is only rebuilt when a reply that had cards is rebuilt or removed; otherwise new values are merged into it.

Why a cache (rather than deleting the work): the cards are needed and the projection runs from `messages.didSet`, which sees the full transcript each time. The per-message cache this extends already exists; this adds the per-reply result to it, keyed on the same inputs. The change adds no API, no initializer parameter and no test-only hook; the test drives the existing `project(_:context:)`.

## Evidence

The proof below comes from the shipped iOS app (`apps/ios`, built from source) on an iOS simulator, driven through its demo chat transport so that appends, history refreshes and source-context refreshes all go through the normal view model path. Base and head ran interleaved in one job, and three runs repeat it. A shorter macOS run follows it. The measured head is `98e6cbaee3d`; the final commit `8f03742d568` only rewraps one call in `ChatSourcePreviews.swift` for the pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.1 lint, so production source is unchanged from the measured tree except formatting.

- **Projector work:** card builds per persisted message drop from 83 to 0 (84 to 1 for a cited reply), and per history refresh from 87 to 0. A context refresh drops from 174 builds to 87. The card output is identical on every sample.
- **Cold load:** no regression detected. On iOS the call that builds all 80 replies is 0.5 to 2.1% slower on head across the three runs (medians of 6 samples), much smaller than the spread between samples (run 3: base 115.7 to 187.7 ms, head 131.7 to 208.4 ms). On macOS, 30 pooled interleaved rounds gave 55.2 ms on base and 55.1 ms on head (-0.2%, sign test p = 0.86). An earlier +20.3% macOS figure came from 7 single samples and does not reproduce. A cost of about 2 ms on a fresh view in an already warm process cannot be ruled out.
- **Context refresh:** median per call is lower on head in all three iOS runs, but p95 per call is higher on head in two of them; head does half the card builds per refresh. Details under Gaps.
- **Frames:** display-link hitches move in both directions between runs, so this PR claims less main-thread work per update, not a frame-rate change.

### Native runtime proof

#### Shipped iOS app on an iOS simulator

The shipped iOS app (`apps/ios`, built from source) ran on an iOS simulator. Base and head were measured interleaved on one simulator in one GitHub Actions job on a fork. The runs used no secrets.

- **Runs:** three runs of the same steps and code, all green (in run 3, the base round 1 XCUITest exited 65 on a screenshot timeout; its script had finished and its counts and digests are included):
  - Run 3: https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/42196768586. This is the main run; its measurement job is https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/42196768586/job/127827857051.
  - Run 1: https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/42179860919
  - Run 2: https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/42187968212
- **Artifacts (per run):**
  - `chatui-perf-proof-p2-ios` holds `summary.md`, `counts.json`, per-sample probe logs and screenshots (`samples/<side>-<round>/`), XCUITest logs, `environment.txt` and `load.txt` (runner load average). Run 3 adds the redacted trace in `timeline/<side>-<round>.json` and the os_signpost stream.
  - `ios-build-base` and `ios-build-head` hold the built apps, the applied scratch diffs and the build logs.
- **Toolchain:**
  - Xcode 26.6 (17F113) on GitHub-hosted `macos-26` runners: macOS 26.7.2 (runs 3 and 1) and 26.6.2 (run 2), Apple M1 (Virtual), 3 vCPU.
  - iPhone 17 Pro simulator, iOS 26.5.
  - Debug build of `ai.openclawfoundation.app.debug`, made with xcodegen and `xcodebuild build-for-testing`, then run with `test-without-building`.
- **Code under test:**
  - Base is `6b959f4ca63`, fetched from openclaw/openclaw.
  - Head is base plus `git diff --full-index 6b959f4ca63..98e6cbaee3d`. The head build checks that the resulting tree equals the head tree `446f8700623` (log: `head tree 446f8700623a... (expected 446f8700623a...)`).
- **Scripts:** fork branch `proof/chatui-perf-p2`. Run 3 used [`9dbd9aebf56`](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/tree/9dbd9aebf56f8180cf9461f4465cdc5da6217bd7) (`rig/ios/`, `rig/ChatPerfProbe.swift`, `rig/instrument.py`), run 1 used `7668b84d981` and run 2 used `5778d323150`. None of it is part of this PR.
- **Xcode 26.6 compatibility:**
  - Hosted runners only have Xcode 26.6. At this base the app references iOS 27.1-only SDK symbols at four sites: three `if #available(iOS 27.1, *)` branches (`ChatProTab.swift` twice, `OpenClawProComponents.swift` once) and one `@available(iOS 27.1, *)` private view modifier, `ChatToolbarStatusPopover` (`ChatProTab.swift`).
  - The scratch build wraps exactly those four sites in `#if compiler(>=6.4)`. An Xcode 27 build sees unchanged source, and on the iOS 26.5 simulator none of the iOS 27.1 code runs either way.
  - The scratch build also drops the SwiftFormat/SwiftLint pre-build phases so they don't lint the scratch code.

**Same scratch changes on both sides:**
- **Probes:** a call counter and a monotonic timer around `ChatSourcePreviewState.update` and `project`, with an `os_signpost` interval around each. The counters cover card builds and title and excerpt renders.
  - After each `update`, the probe writes a SHA-256 of each cited reply's cards whenever they change, plus one digest of all cards. It also records the cards handed to each rendered `ChatView` row.
  - A `CADisplayLink` records frame times.
- **Fixture:** a launch flag seeds the app's local demo chat store (`AppleReviewDemoChatTransport`, the store behind `--openclaw-screenshot-mode`) with 80 cited turns. Each turn is a question, a `web_search` result and a reply citing 4 sources on public example domains (`example0.com`, `example1.com`, ...).
- **UI test:** a scratch XCUITest case only launches the app on the chat tab, waits and takes screenshots. It does not type.

**Event script.** After the transcript loads, the demo store publishes these events through the app's normal chat transport path, so the work goes through the view model into `ChatSourcePreviewState.update` and `project`:
1. **Appends:** 21 `.sessionMessage` events, one persisted message each: 7 turns of question, `web_search` result and cited reply.
2. **History refreshes:** 10 `sessions.changed` events (phase `message`). Each makes the view model refresh history, which returns the same rows (same ids) plus one new row.
3. **Context refreshes:** 10 `.chatMetadataChanged` events. Each makes the view model reload the source context through `loadSourceContext`, alternating between a gateway context and none. Under the gateway context, one cited link per reply is a gateway chat route on a reserved `.invalid` host, so its card is hidden.

**Rounds:** 6 rounds per run, ordered ABBA (base, head, head, base, ...). One app launch per sample. All 18 samples per side (36 in total) across the three runs finished the full script (21 / 10 / 10 steps).

**Card builds per step** (median over all steps of all samples, base / head). These counts are the same in all three runs:

| Step | Cited replies | `update` calls | Card builds, base | Card builds, head | Title / excerpt renders, base | Title / excerpt renders, head |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| transcript load | 80 | 5 / 5 | 160 | 80 | 320 / 320 | 320 / 320 |
| append: user question | 80 to 86 | 1 / 1 | 83 | 0 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| append: `web_search` result | 80 to 86 | 1 / 1 | 83 | 0 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| append: cited reply | 80 to 87 | 1 / 1 | 84 | 1 | 4 / 4 | 4 / 4 |
| history refresh: first after the appends | 87 | 1 / 1 | 87 | 7 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| history refresh: later ones | 87 | 1 / 1 | 87 | 0 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| context refresh (2 `update` calls) | 87 | 2 / 2 | 174 | 87 | 43.5 / 43.5 | 43.5 / 43.5 |

Run 3 totals over all 6 samples per side, base -> head: append 10500 -> 42 card builds, history refresh 5220 -> 42, context refresh 10440 -> 5220, load 960 -> 480.

**Reading the counts:**
- **Appends:** base rebuilds every cited reply's cards on each persisted message. Head builds only the new cited reply.
- **First history refresh:** it replaces the 7 event-delivered replies with their history copies. The ids are the same, but the rows are not field-for-field equal, so head rebuilds those 7.
- **Context refresh:** head rebuilds every reply once, which is the expected invalidation. Base rebuilds every reply on both `update` calls.
- **Load:** both sides build all 80 replies in one call. Base builds them again when the source context loads at launch, which is the 160.
- **Timing at step edges:** in a few samples an append's `update` landed just after the next step began (`update` calls 0 to 3 per step). The step totals are unaffected.

**Time per `ChatSourcePreviewState.update` call** (in-process timer around the signposted interval, all calls of all 6 samples per side; median / p95, base -> head):

| Phase | Calls per side, per run | Run 3 | Run 1 | Run 2 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| append one persisted message | 126 | 9.83 / 19.43 -> 2.82 / 9.11 ms | 7.58 / 13.36 -> 1.57 / 6.14 ms | 9.21 / 16.90 -> 2.14 / 6.53 ms |
| history refresh, same ids + 1 row | 60 | 13.79 / 24.05 -> 4.74 / 12.85 ms | 9.62 / 15.83 -> 3.54 / 8.29 ms | 12.59 / 23.45 -> 4.10 / 8.44 ms |
| context refresh, per call | 120 | 16.29 / 45.05 -> 11.29 / 60.73 ms | 12.95 / 32.58 -> 8.47 / 35.50 ms | 16.93 / 51.60 -> 9.25 / 46.13 ms |
| cold load: the call that builds all 80 replies, median of 6 samples | 6 | 161.8 -> 165.2 ms | 126.4 -> 127.0 ms | 157.5 -> 159.9 ms |

**Signpost check:** run 3 also streamed the app's own os_signpost intervals (subsystem `ai.openclaw.chatperfproof` only) from the simulator's unified log during one extra run per side. That gives 56 `sourceStateUpdate` intervals per side: median 9.44 ms and p95 28.46 ms on base, against 4.38 ms and 34.24 ms on head.
- The `signposts-*.json` files and the last lines of `summary.md` show 0.23 and 0.11 ms. They subtract `machTimestamp` values as if they were nanoseconds, but one tick is 41.67 ns on this runner, which the events' wall-clock timestamps confirm.
- The figures above are recomputed from `signpost-stream-<side>.ndjson.gz` with that factor.

**Output unchanged:**
- **Card digests:** in all three runs, the all-cards digest at the end of each phase is the same on every base and head sample: load `fc84a30f3c849913`, then `fd28340aed816e45` after appends, history refreshes and context refreshes.
  - At the end, 87 of 87 cited replies have equal per-reply digests on all samples.
  - The cards handed to the rendered `ChatView` rows are the same on every sample.
- **Run 3 trace:** all 12 samples pass through the same sequence of 18 card states, including the gateway-context state (261 visible cards, digest `5d7d2f534905b3c5`).
- **Screenshots:** each sample takes three (`sources-loaded`, `sources-after-appends`, `sources-end`).
  - The cards are visible in `sources-loaded` and `sources-after-appends`. `sources-end` shows the end of the transcript (the follow-up rows and only the bottom edge of a card); it is byte-identical on every sample that took it: all 12 in runs 1 and 2, and 11 of 12 in run 3.
  - In run 3, base round 1 hit an XCUITest "Timed out while requesting screenshot" on that last screenshot after its script had finished. XCTest saved a screen recording of the failure in its place.
  - The earlier screenshots show cited replies with their Sources cards ("Result 0 for question 80", `example0.com`). Their timing depends on how far the script had run, so they are not compared byte for byte.

**The trace** (run 3, artifact `chatui-perf-proof-p2-ios`, `timeline/<side>-<round>.json`, 12 files of 42 steps each): a per-step timeline of the event script.
- Each step has its start and end time, every `update` call in it (time, ms, card builds, title and excerpt renders), every reply whose cards changed (reply id and card SHA-256), and the card count and all-cards digest after the step.
- Excerpt, head round 1 and base round 1 (card change lists shortened):

```
head-1 append 20   update 4.687 ms, cardBuilds 1, titles 4, excerpts 4; changed perf-run-86; cards 348, sha256 fd28340aed816e45...
base-1 append 20   update 13.174 ms, cardBuilds 87, titles 4, excerpts 4; changed perf-run-86; cards 348, sha256 fd28340aed816e45...
head-1 refresh 0   update 9.939 ms, cardBuilds 7; no card changes; cards 348, sha256 fd28340aed816e45...
base-1 refresh 0   update 22.789 ms, cardBuilds 87; no card changes; cards 348, sha256 fd28340aed816e45...
head-1 refresh 9   update 3.376 ms, cardBuilds 0; cards 348
base-1 refresh 9   update 12.014 ms, cardBuilds 87; cards 348
head-1 context 0   update 5.769 ms (0 builds) + 13.090 ms (87 builds); 87 replies changed; cards 261, sha256 5d7d2f534905b3c5...
base-1 context 0   update 15.626 ms (87 builds) + 16.404 ms (87 builds); 87 replies changed; cards 261, sha256 5d7d2f534905b3c5...
```

**Redaction:**
- The timeline holds only step names, times, durations, counts, fixture reply ids (`perf-run-N`) and SHA-256 digests. It contains no message text, no URLs, no file paths and no device identifiers; a scan for paths, URLs and token patterns over all 12 files finds nothing.
- The transcript is the fixture. Its links point to public example domains, and the gateway route uses a reserved `.invalid` host, so no real endpoint is involved. The app never connected to a gateway, and the job had no secrets.
- The raw files in the same artifact (probe logs, the signpost stream and xcodebuild logs) also contain no credentials or endpoints. They do contain the hosted runner's simulator paths (`/Users/runner/Library/Developer/CoreSimulator/...`) and simulator UUIDs.

**Frames:** the display link recorded hitches in every phase on both sides. The differences between sides go in both directions from run to run (for example, append hitches in run 1 were 163 on base and 145 on head, and in run 2 were 112 and 143), so I make no frame-rate claim from these runs.

#### Earlier native run (macOS)

The same probes, the real `OpenClawChatView` and `OpenClawChatViewModel` in an `NSHostingView`, and a local chat transport ran on the same Xcode 26.6 image: https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/42165891108, 7 interleaved rounds.
- **Measured head:** `41394d91dc1`, tree `3fd4b5ec20f`. Its production source is identical to `98e6cbaee3d`; the only difference is 8 lines in `ChatSourcePreviewTests.swift`.
- **Counts:** card builds per step match the iOS table: per append 83 -> 0 (cited reply 84 -> 1), refresh 87 -> 0, context change 174 -> 87. `update` per append was 5.385 -> 1.390 ms median.
- **Cold first projection:** pooled with https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/42164742047 (same production source), 30 interleaved rounds gave a median of 55.2 ms on base and 55.1 ms on head (-0.2%, sign test p = 0.86).
- **Full suite:** OpenClawKit passed on head (2533 tests in 226 suites) and on base (2532 in 226) in https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/42168510931.

#### Gaps

- **Build and device:** this is a Debug build on a simulator, on a shared 3-vCPU hosted VM, not a Release build on an iPhone.
- **Runner load:** the runner was heavily loaded, with load averages from 35 to 146 across the three runs, and absolute times differ noticeably between runs (head append median 1.57 to 2.82 ms). The counts are the claim; the times are supporting evidence and point the same way in every run.
- **Cold load and context p95:** the cold-load call (both sides build all 80 replies) is 0.5 to 2.1% slower on head in all three runs, well inside the spread between samples. A cost of about 2 ms on a fresh view in an already warm process cannot be ruled out. Context-refresh p95 per call is higher on head in two of the three runs, while its median is lower in all three; head does half the card builds per refresh.
- **Scratch code:** the fixture, probes and UI test are identical on both sides and not part of this PR. The Xcode 26.6 compatibility wrap above is the only change to app source outside the fixture.
- **macOS context change, pooled:** over the two macOS runs (14 rounds), the change as a whole was cheaper on head (median 19.3 ms on base and 15.7 ms on head, p95 33.2 and 30.5 ms), but the rebuild call that also renders titles and excerpts was slower on head in 11 of 14 rounds, by a median of 1.5 ms (sign test p = 0.06). A context refresh happens only when the session's source context reloads.
- **Unrelated test failures in earlier runs:** some earlier macOS runs of the same production source had one hosted-runner audio timing failure each (`RealtimeTalkRelaySessionReviewTests`, `TalkBufferedAudioPlayerTests`). These tests are not touched by this change, and the full suite run linked above is clean.

#### Tests

- New test `incremental projection matches a fresh projection and reuses unchanged replies` (in `ChatSourcePreviewTests`): 11 steps of appends, an edited search result, a removed fetch, a reordered run, context changes, a return to the original and a new cited run. At every step the incremental projection must equal a fresh one. It also checks which replies keep their recorded cards: both after an unrelated append; only the other run's reply after a search result in one run is edited; neither after a source-context change; both after a new cited run is appended. On base it fails 3 reuse checks; on head it passes.
- Mutation check, one change at a time: always rebuilding cards fails 3 reuse checks. Dropping the context check fails the identical-output check at 2 steps and 2 reuse checks. Dropping the earlier-row id check leaves stale cards: the identical-output check fails at 4 steps, and two existing tests (`refresh invalidates only changed transcript inputs and removes deleted sources`, `inline results and JSON result text retain invocation and canonical run ownership`) fail too. Restoring the fix passes 17/17.
- Three mutations of the shared rendered-text cache (skipping its rebuild, dropping reused replies' values, skipping the merge) never change a card, because a rendered value depends only on its source text. They only change how much text is kept. This is not observable through `project`, so no test asserts it. A temporary local count of the cache caught each of them (9, 4 and 1 steps).
- `ChatSourcePreviewTests`: 17/17 pass on head.

Acceptance rule (it applies to the Command Line Tools package benchmark in the collapsed section below, not to the native run above): median `ChatSourcePreviewState.update` after appending one message to a 500-message transcript with 100 cited replies, release, warm, 60 iterations per run, base and head interleaved over 5 rounds on one machine. A win needs head to be faster than base in every round with identical output; any bench row that gets slower counts as a regression. Head met it on the append row in every round with identical output. The cold first projection was unchanged within noise there too. That table was measured on the first commit; on the final head, 7 more interleaved rounds gave a cold projection of 143.0 ms on base and 142.1 ms on head, with the update rows unchanged from the first commit. The native run above reports its own counts and timings, and its weak spots are listed under Gaps.

Related: #193741 caches citation parsing for split rows in `ChatSourcePreviewState.previews(for:)`; this PR changes the projector underneath it. The two touch neighbouring code, merge cleanly and compose.

<details><summary>Earlier package benchmark (Command Line Tools)</summary>

Machine: Apple M3 Ultra (32 cores), macOS 27.2, Swift 6.4.2, shared host (load average recorded per round). Base is `6b959f4ca63` (`apps/shared/OpenClawKit` is identical to `9f3ed313782`, where base was first measured).

Each cell is the median of 5 round medians; each round median is over 60 samples, and the range is the lowest and highest round median. The harness records medians only, so there is no p95 column.

| 500 messages, median of 5 rounds (range) | base | head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update` after one appended message | 8.72 ms (8.46 to 14.00) | 2.39 ms (1.23 to 2.59) |
| `project` after one appended message | 9.68 ms (8.19 to 10.19) | 2.57 ms (1.36 to 3.70) |
| `project` with unchanged messages | 8.77 ms (8.10 to 11.58) | 1.22 ms (0.96 to 1.95) |
| history reload, same ids | 14.31 ms (12.63 to 17.92) | 6.78 ms (5.22 to 12.02) |
| cold projection (first load) | 296 ms (257 to 330) | 293 ms (239 to 369) |

The host was busy during these rounds (load average 36 to 48, and the cold row ran about 2x slower than in earlier runs on the same machine). An earlier run (cold projection about 140 ms instead of about 296 ms) of the same harness measured 6.5 to 8.6 ms on base and 0.84 to 0.93 ms on head for the append row. Head was faster in every round on every row except the cold projection, which is unchanged within noise. What is left on head (about 1 to 2.5 ms) is mostly comparing each message with its cached copy and rebuilding the dictionary, which this change does not touch.

Per agent turn: an agent turn with k tool calls updates `messages` about 2k + 3 times (streaming deltas do not). Using the medians above, that is 113 ms on base and 31 ms on head at k = 5, and 375 ms on base and 103 ms on head at k = 20.

Observation: the `previews` reassignment is not a second source of work. With identical previews the harness sees 0 of 5 observer notifications on base, because the observable setter already skips equal values.

#### Harness and command

The harness is a Swift Testing suite run locally and not included in this PR. It builds 100 turns of 5 messages (user, assistant with `web_search` and `web_fetch` calls, a search result with 8 rows, a fetch result with about 6 KB of text, a final answer of about 1.5 KB citing 3 result URLs): 500 messages and 1.49 MB of JSON. It times `project` and `ChatSourcePreviewState.update` for an append, an unchanged array and a history reload with the same ids, 60 iterations each, and reports the median.

```
swift test -c release -Xswiftc -enable-testing --filter ChatSourcePreviewProjectionBenchmarkTests
```

#### Local toolchain notes

Measured with Command Line Tools only (no Xcode). To build OpenClawChatUI there, a scratch copy expanded `@Entry`, disabled `#Preview` blocks and used the macOS 26.5 SDK, because the CLT install lacks the SwiftUI macro plugins. The 7 XCTest-based files could not run under CLT and were moved aside for the full-suite run; the benchmark and mutation runs used a test target reduced to the source preview suites to save build time. None of these local changes are part of this diff. The Xcode run above is the authoritative full-suite result.

</details>

prs.title: fix(apple): chat sends with large attachments time out on slow uplinks
prs.body:
Closes #194213

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a chat message with a large attachment is reported as failed after 30 seconds when the uplink is slow, while the upload is still running.

## User Impact

User impact: on weak signal or slow networks, sending a large file or a photo from the iOS or macOS app stays pending until the Gateway acknowledges it, instead of failing at 30 seconds and asking for a retry that uploads the whole frame again.

## Why This Change Was Made

URLSession reports a WebSocket send as done once the frame is buffered in the process, and the task exposes no upload progress (`countOfBytesSent` stays 0). So the client cannot start the deadline after the upload, and the fixed 30 s `chat.send` deadline also covered the upload. The deadline now adds upload time for the attachment bytes at 256 kbit/s on top of the existing 30 s. Text-only sends keep 30 s, audio sends keep the zero deadline, and explicit `requestTimeoutMs` values are unchanged.

A dead socket during the longer wait is still caught by the tick watchdog, which fails pending requests. The worst case is bounded by the 25 MB frame budget (about 14 minutes at the floor rate). Uplinks slower than 256 kbit/s can still hit the deadline: a 1.5 MB photo at 128 kbit/s needs about 94 s against a 77 s deadline. The outbox then reports the send as unconfirmed, as it does today. A resumable HTTP upload path would remove the frame size from the request deadline entirely; that is a separate change.

## Evidence

Local runs: macOS 27.2, Xcode 27.2 (27B52), Swift 6.4.2.

- Shipped request path: `GatewayNodeSession.request` with a real URLSession WebSocket sends one 8 MB file to the native Gateway test fixture, which reads at 160 KiB/s (observed about 141 to 152 KiB/s), sends ticks every 5 s, and ACKs `chat.send` after the whole frame. Base: fails with `gateway request timed out after 30000ms` after 30.1 s, while the fixture has read 4,685,824 of about 10,667,000 frame bytes. Head: the deadline is 363,333 ms, and the ACK (`status=started`) arrives after 73.7 s, once the fixture has read the whole frame (10,666,977 bytes). The harness (https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/blob/proof/ios-offline-send-timeout/rig/harness.diff) is not part of this PR because it runs for over a minute.
- Unit regression `attachment send deadline leaves admission time after a slow upload` (`ChatGatewayRequestTests`):
  - Red on base `cb73e59f935` with only the new test: it fails by assertion (`request(nil, [file])` is 30000.0, expected 363333; `30000.0 > 115333.0` is false). 2 issues, 57 tests in 2 suites.
  - Green on the exact head tree `6f6b08adf92`: the new test passes, and all 57 tests in 2 suites pass. That includes the existing small-attachment 30000 ms and audio zero-deadline tests.
  - Same red/green on a hosted macOS runner (Xcode 26.6, Swift 6.3.3): https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/42236963255/job/127956976025
- Full OpenClawKit `swift test --parallel` on the exact head tree: 2485 tests in 220 suites and 40 tests in 4 suites pass. The pasteboard suites were skipped, because the local test user has no GUI login session and `NSPasteboard` writes fail. Run one at a time, the two macOS pasteboard suites fail the same way on base and head: `ChatFileAdmissionTests` "file selection remains with the captured conversation", and `ChatComposerPasteSupportTests` "extracts image data from PNG clipboard payload", which then crashes the test process with an index out of range. (`ChatPasteboardTests` and `ChatComposerTextViewIOSTests` are iOS-only and run no tests on macOS.) The other tests in those suites pass when run one at a time, except the tests after the crash, which do not run on base or head.
- SwiftFormat 0.63.1 lint and SwiftLint 0.65.1 (`apps/ios/.swiftlint.yml`, strict) are clean on the changed source file; `git diff --check` is clean.
- Not covered: no run through a real Gateway on a throttled network, and no iOS device or simulator run. The changed code is a pure deadline calculation shared by iOS and macOS.

<details>
<summary>URLSession send completion probe (macOS 27.2, Swift 6.4.2)</summary>

A loopback WebSocket server throttled to at most 256 KiB/s (observed drain about 140 to 200 KiB/s):

- 8 MiB frame: the send callback fires at 0.01 s; the server has read 11 bytes at 0.3 s and 524,299 bytes at 3.6 s.
- 2 MiB frame: the send callback fires at 0.01 s; `countOfBytesSent` stays 0 for the 7 s polled, while the server reads 1,835,019 bytes by 9.7 s.

This is why the fix budgets the upload in the deadline instead of moving the timer in `GatewayChannelActor`.

</details>

prs.title: improve(chat): stop recompiling preview regexes while rendering native chat
prs.body:
Closes #193737

## What Problem This Solves

Native chat on iOS and macOS recompiles the same link and source preview regular expressions every time a message bubble is rendered or a preview page is parsed.

## User Impact

User impact: chat bubbles and link previews do less main-thread work. In the native macOS run, link detection over every bubble took about a third as long and Open Graph parsing about a quarter as long. There is no visible behavior change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The bare URL, HTML attribute, HTML title, HTML entity and external content frame patterns are constants, but each was compiled inside the function that used it, in some cases once per Markdown text node or once per `<meta>` tag. They are now load-once constants, like the existing `NSRegularExpression` constants in `ChatReactions.swift` and `ChatSessionSidebarModel+Titles.swift`. Patterns, options and the `try?` fallbacks are unchanged.

Left as is on purpose: patterns built from runtime input (progress card closing tag, session title prefix), the hover card `match(_:_:)` helper that takes its pattern as an argument, and `ChatProgressCardMarkdown`, which builds its expressions per call by design. Caching the link preview result per message would also skip the Markdown parse (about 78 us of the remaining cost), but that needs a cache with its own invalidation and belongs in a separate change.

## Evidence

### Native runtime proof

Run: https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/42144162080 (both jobs passed)
- `workload p3`: https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/42144162080/job/127651498957
- `focused suites p3`: https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/42144162080/job/127651499397

Artifacts (90 days): `chatui-perf-proof-p3` (summary.md, counts.json, per-sample JSON, transcript screenshots, probe placements, instrumentation diffs, build and test logs, os_signpost export) and `chatui-perf-proof-p3-focused` (focused suite logs).
Reproducible workload: fork branch `etzelm/openclaw:proof/chatui-perf-p3` at `9e25db1dd95` (README explains each phase). Nothing from it is part of this PR.

**Toolchain:** GitHub-hosted `macos-26` runner (image macos26 20261026.0455.2, Apple M1 virtual, 3 cores), Xcode 26.6 (17F113), Apple Swift 6.3.3, macOS 26.6.2. Real Xcode toolchain, no shims or macro stand-ins. Xcode 27 is not on the hosted image.

**Exact code:** the job fetches base `9f3ed313782` from openclaw/openclaw, applies this PR's diff and refuses to continue unless the tree equals the head `3b90189fde1` tree `e6c9e906`. Tree check passed: 2 files, +22 -14.

**Workload:** the real `OpenClawChatView` and `OpenClawChatViewModel` in an `NSHostingView` in an `NSWindow`. A 60-turn cited web_search transcript comes in through an `OpenClawChatTransport` (`requestHistory`), giving 210 rows, 140 user and assistant bubbles and 210 source cards. Each assistant answer is a multi-paragraph Markdown message with three cited links and one bare link. Phases:
- load
- scroll (64 positions)
- resize (4 widths)
- append (10 turns)
- stream (24 deltas)
- bubbleScan: 20 passes of `chatFirstPreviewURL` over every bubble's display text. This is the function `ChatMessageBubble.linkPreviewURL` calls from `body`.
- openGraphParse: 50 `parseChatOpenGraph` calls on fixture HTML, alternating a page with `og:title` and one that falls back to `<title>`. The parser is called directly; the tap and network fetch are unchanged and not driven.

Base and head are built in release with identical scratch call counters. The probe sets match apart from line numbers, and the added lines are identical on both sides. Samples are interleaved base, head, 5 rounds, with a fresh process per sample. NSRegularExpression compiles are counted per pattern family by swapping `-initWithPattern:options:error:` inside the test process only, so product code is not changed.

Rule: head compiles each pattern at most once per process, outputs (row fingerprints, Open Graph results, screenshot) are identical, and no phase is slower at equal work. Counts are the claim; times are reported with spread.

#### NSRegularExpression compiles per phase (median of 5, range if it varied)

| Phase | Pattern | Base | Head | Work in phase (base and head) |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| load | bare URL | 3569 (3459 to 3569) | 1 | same 3459 to 3569 text-node scans |
| load | external content frame | 360 | 1 | 360 frame strips |
| scroll | bare URL | 1912 (1802 to 2951) | 0 | same 1802 to 2951 text-node scans |
| append | bare URL | 3122 | 0 | 3122 text-node scans |
| append | external content frame | 60 | 0 | 60 frame strips |
| stream | bare URL | 220 | 0 | 220 text-node scans |
| bubbleScan | bare URL | 77000 | 0 | 77000 text-node scans |
| openGraphParse | HTML attribute | 125 | 1 | 50 parses, 125 meta tags |
| openGraphParse | HTML title | 25 | 1 | 25 title fallbacks |
| openGraphParse | HTML entity | 100 | 1 | 50 parses |

In every phase and sample, base compiles equal the work count: one bare URL compile per Markdown text node, one frame compile per wrapped title or snippet, one attribute compile per meta tag, and two entity compiles per parse. Head compiles each pattern once per process, on first use, and 0 times after that. Over the whole workload, per process: bare URL 85823 compiles on base vs 1 on head, external frame 420 vs 1, attribute 125 vs 1, title 25 vs 1, entity 100 vs 1. One unrelated pattern is compiled twice on both sides.

#### Output unchanged

- Per-row fingerprint (SHA-256 of the bubble's link preview URL, every preview URL in its text, and its source cards with title, domain, excerpt and cited URLs) for all 210 rows: one digest `4beda980...e168` on all 5 base and all 5 head samples.
- Open Graph results for both fixtures are identical on base and head (title, image URL, decoded entities).
- Transcript screenshot (960x720 `NSWindow`, user bubble with its link preview card, cited assistant answer): PNG bytes are identical on base and head, SHA-256 `e41500f1...8800`, in every sample.

#### Timings (bonus; counts are the claim)

Shared hosted runner, load average 19 to 26 on 3 cores. 5 samples per side.

| Measure | Base median | Base p95 | Head median | Head p95 | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `chatFirstPreviewURL` over all 140 bubbles, per pass (us, n=100) | 65521 | 77394 | 23623 | 32566 | -63.9% |
| `parseChatOpenGraph` per call (us, n=250) | 144.0 | 434.2 | 35.1 | 80.5 | -75.6% |
| load phase (ms) | 652 | 926 | 516 | 750 | -20.9% |
| append phase (ms) | 1543 | 1764 | 1424 | 1529 | -7.7% |
| stream phase (ms) | 131 | 187 | 105 | 144 | -19.9% |
| resize phase (ms) | 79 | 100 | 80 | 87 | +0.3% |
| scroll phase (ms) | 2587 | 3253 | 3161 | 3601 | +22.2% |

The scroll cell does not show a regression. How many bubbles SwiftUI materializes while scrolling is bimodal, about 1,900 or 2,951 text-node scans per sample, and head landed on the larger count in 4 of 5 samples (base in 1 of 5). At equal work the two sides overlap:

| Scans per sample | Base scroll (ms) | Head scroll (ms) |
|---:|---|---|
| about 1,900 | 2388 to 2597 (4 samples) | 2142 (1 sample) |
| 2,951 | 3253 (1 sample) | 2960 to 3601 (4 samples) |

Normalized per text-node scan (the two sides materialized different numbers of bubbles in load and scroll): load 0.183 vs 0.149 ms (-18.6%), scroll 1.327 vs 1.120 ms (-15.6%). The compiles avoided in scroll are a small part of that phase. The time saving shows clearly in the bubbleScan and openGraphParse measures, where head p95 is below base median.

#### Gaps

- macOS `NSHostingView` only; the iOS simulator was not run. Wall times come from a shared virtual runner and are not a device frame-time claim.
- The os_signpost recording is partial: the base trace kept 5 of the 7 phase intervals, and the head trace timed out while saving. No claim rests on it; the counts and timings above come from in-process measurements.
- No committed benchmark. OpenClaw has no committed native chat workload to extend. The change has no behavior to assert, and counting compiles needs the method swap shown above, which belongs in a proof harness, not in the test suite. The rig branch is the reproducible workload: it pins base, diff and head tree, holds the workload and counters as source, and reruns end to end with one push to a fork (about 33 minutes) or locally with `bash rig/run-lane.sh prepare|focused|build|workload 5|summary`.

### Tests

- Xcode 26.6, unmodified code: `swift test --filter 'ChatSourcePreviewTests|ChatLinkPreview'`, 44 tests in 12 suites passed on base and on head ([focused suites job](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/42144162080/job/127651499397)).
- Full OpenClawKit `swift test` on the same head tree (`e6c9e906`), same Xcode: 2532 tests in 226 suites passed ([job](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/actions/runs/42122411213/job/127577896743), from an earlier run of the proof branch).
- SwiftFormat 0.63.0 with `config/swiftformat`: 0 files need formatting.
- No new tests: behavior is unchanged, and compile counts are only observable through the method swap used in the proof above.

<details><summary>Earlier package benchmark (Command Line Tools)</summary>

Acceptance rule: same machine, release build, base and fixed code interleaved ABAB, 12 samples per side per run, 5 runs; the fix counts if `chatPreviewURLs` on a realistic message improves by more than run-to-run spread, no workload regresses, and outputs are identical.

Apple M3 Ultra, macOS 27.2, Swift 6.4.2 (Command Line Tools), host shared with other builds (load average 25 to 35 on 32 cores):

| Workload | Base median (us) | Fixed median (us) | Base p95 (us) | Fixed p95 (us) | Median change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `chatPreviewURLs`, 1.4k char message, 37 text nodes, 15 links | 288 to 299 | 146 to 152 | 298 to 448 | 150 to 178 | -48.5% to -49.3% |
| `chatPreviewURLs`, one-line reply | 11.3 to 11.9 | 7.2 to 7.6 | 12.0 to 12.1 | 7.6 to 8.4 | -35.6% to -36.3% |
| `parseChatOpenGraph`, page with 33 meta tags | 432 to 453 | 151 to 158 | 446 to 799 | 159 to 263 | -65.0% to -65.2% |

Ranges are across the 5 runs. The fixed p95 is below the base median in every run. The harness is a local package (base and head copies of the parsing section of `ChatLinkPreview.swift`), not committed.

- Compile cost per pattern: 3.6 us (bare URL, title), 5.5 us (entities), 7.4 us (attributes), 9.0 us (external content frame). For scale, `Document(parsing:)` of the same message is about 78 us.

</details>

prs.title: fix: old Git plugin folder remains after an update timeout
prs.body:
Closes #193497

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after a Git plugin update times out while older work is still running, the previous checkout stays on disk through recovery, restart, and the next successful update.

## User Impact

A failed activation no longer abandons the previous Git checkout. The checkout stays while that generation is still loaded or named by configuration, and `openclaw plugins reload`, the next Gateway startup, or retained-plugin cleanup removes it once nothing is using it. If administrator authority is revoked before the delete, the directory stays.

## Why This Change Was Made

The install saves the new Git record before activation. When activation throws, the immediate directory removal never runs, and Git checkouts are outside the npm retention markers. The install now records that checkout immediately after the record commits and before metadata refresh, so a later refresh or activation failure can still retire it.

Reload, startup, and background cleanup remove it only when the path is still the recorded directory, sits inside the managed Git directory, is not a loaded or configured install, and the synchronous authority guard still passes at the directory remover. Reload matches the package install owner as well as the runtime plugin id. Startup and reload use the same absolute and home-relative config protection as background cleanup. A Git marker alone is enough for background cleanup to run.

The obligation is a marker file under the managed Git directory, the same kind of record the npm retention owner already writes beside a managed install. Existing install records are unchanged. A checkout with no marker is left in place.

## Evidence

Node v24.22.2, pnpm 12.15.0, Vitest 5.0.5. Package `2026.11.1`. Branch base `ef1f35180125`. Head `11a66104cb56`.

Red, on the previous cleanup behavior (authority guard not forwarded, install owners ignored, Git markers absent from background candidate detection):

- Package owner `demo-package` with runtime id `demo-plugin-npm`: `removed` was `0`. Case 67ms. Vitest 7.65s. Shard wall 10.64s.
- Revoked administrator authority: cleanup resolved `{ removed: 1, warnings: [] }` instead of rejecting. Case 13ms. Same run.
- `cleanupGatewayRetiredPluginArtifacts` with only a Git marker: the checkout was still present (`existsSync` true). Case 523ms. Vitest 55.53s. Shard wall 59.37s, including about 44s of compiler preparation.

Green, head `11a66104cb56`:

- `src/plugins/retired-git-installs.test.ts`: 8 passed. In-use 33ms, replacement removal 12ms, inode mismatch 4ms, outside root 3ms, unmarked checkout 3ms, package owner 5ms, configured path 4ms, revoked authority 5ms. Vitest 43.04s. Shard wall 46.27s, including about 40s of compiler preparation.
- `src/plugins/install-persistence.test.ts` activation failure: 1 passed, 23 skipped. The case took 4890ms. Vitest 10.25s. Shard wall 17.09s.
- `src/gateway/server-retained-plugin-cleanup.test.ts`: configured startup path 1193ms, configured current path 1053ms, Git-only removal 724ms. Vitest 11.36s. Shard wall 14.52s.
- `src/plugins/management-service.test.ts`: 20 passed. Vitest 11.09s. Shard wall 17.55s.
- `src/gateway/server-startup-post-attach.test.ts` plugin attachment: 1 passed, 79 skipped. Case 214ms. Vitest 13.09s. Shard wall 15.83s.
- Assertion-safety ratchet passed against `ef1f35180125`.
- `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base ef1f35180125 --no-merge-base` passed. Slack 0. Net test-line delta +233. Allocation `config/test-lines-allocations/retired-git-plugin-checkout.txt` is 219.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on the touched files passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.

The install regression calls the production install owner with a thrown activation and keeps the previous checkout. The cleanup regression calls `cleanupGatewayRetiredPluginArtifacts` and removes that checkout when no npm retention or native capture is present. The authority regression rejects before the directory is deleted. An existing checkout with no marker is not deleted.

Previous head `e20bc468cc36` CI:

- Failed: assertion-safety, `src/plugins/retired-git-installs.ts` had 3 uncommented type assertions. Those assertions are gone.
- Failed: `checks-node-changed` shards exited 22 because `curl` received HTTP 504 while staging the pinned Bun fork, before tests ran.
- Failed: some `check-lint` shards could not stage that same Bun fork. `check-lint-core-2` and `check-lint-core-4` succeeded. The mkdtemp guard warning on the new test is replaced by `useAutoCleanupTempDirTracker`.

prs.title: feat(openai): generate animated GIFs with GPT Image 2.6
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Agents can't generate GIFs with OpenAI's new GPT Image 2.6 models. `image_generate` rejects `outputFormat: "gif"` at the schema, and `gpt-image-2.6-flare` / `gpt-image-2.6-sunburst` aren't registered OpenAI image models.

## User Impact

On the direct OpenAI Images API (API key), `image_generate` and `openclaw infer image generate` can now return animated GIFs from `openai/gpt-image-2.6-flare` or `openai/gpt-image-2.6-sunburst`. They also accept the GIF frame controls `openai.frameCount` (2-64) and `openai.frameDurationMs` (20-2000 ms). The 2.6 models also work for still images with the same sizes and qualities as 2.5.

Limits users should know about:

- **GIF is text-to-image only.** A GIF request with reference images fails before any request is sent.
- **The ChatGPT/Codex OAuth route can't make GIFs.** OpenAI's backend rejects it (live result below). The docs point users to the API-key route.
- **Oversized GIFs fail instead of being flattened.** A GIF over the media cap returns an error that suggests fewer frames, a smaller size, or a higher `agents.defaults.mediaMaxMb`. Before, it would have been silently re-encoded to a still JPEG.
- **Other models drop the format, not the request.** A GIF request to a model without GIF support reports `outputFormat: "gif"` as an ignored override and returns a still image, as with other unsupported hints.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Shared contract.** `outputFormat` gains `gif` in one shared list (`IMAGE_GENERATION_OUTPUT_FORMATS`), replacing three hardcoded copies in the type, the tool, and the CLI.
- **Provider support.** The OpenAI provider declares GIF only for the 2.6 models through `formatsByModel`, so the existing runtime filtering handles every other model. Frame fields are sent only with GIF output, because OpenAI rejects them otherwise.
- **Frame size.** GIF `size` defaults to `auto`, since the request sets each frame's size and the total pixel budget covers all frames. An explicit GIF size only needs dimensions divisible by 16.
- **GIF recognition.** MIME sniffing recognizes GIF signatures, so tool output reports the format and dimensions.
- **File-size cap.** The OpenAI image catalog and per-model request rules moved to `image-generation-model-rules.ts`. This lets the grandfathered provider file shrink (the line-cap ratchet allows no growth). The GIF tests live in sibling files for the same reason.

## Evidence

- **Reproduced on current `main` through a Gateway's real `image_generate` tool.** `{ model: "openai/gpt-image-2.6-flare", outputFormat: "gif" }` failed with `outputFormat: must be equal to one of the allowed values (allowed: "png", "jpeg", "webp")`.
- **Live check on the ChatGPT/Codex OAuth route** (`openclaw infer image generate --model openai/gpt-image-2.6-flare --output-format gif`). OpenAI returned `HTTP 400: GIF output is not enabled for the model 'gpt-image-2-codex'. [type=image_generation_user_error, code=invalid_value]`. That route maps image requests to `gpt-image-2-codex`, so the docs send GIF users to the API-key route.
- **End-to-end CLI check against a local fake Images API** (isolated state dir, `OPENCLAW_QA_ALLOW_LOCAL_IMAGE_PROVIDER=1`). The fake served OpenAI's published 2.6 sample GIF.
  - `POST /v1/images/generations` received `{"model":"gpt-image-2.6-flare","n":1,"size":"auto","output_format":"gif","frame_count":12,"frame_duration_ms":150,...}`.
  - The CLI wrote `image/gif`, 512x512, byte-identical to the served animation.
  - The same command with `gpt-image-2.5-flare` sent no format or frame fields and reported `ignoredOverrides: [{ key: "outputFormat", value: "gif" }]`.
- **Tests.** New provider GIF tests (capability declaration, request body, per-frame size, frame fields omitted for still images, edit rejection), new tool GIF tests (forwarding and reporting, frame bounds, oversized GIF), and GIF sniffing. Affected suites pass: `extensions/openai/`, `src/image-generation/`, `src/cli/capability-cli`, and the image tool tests.
- **Gates.** `pnpm check:changed` passes except two failures in files this PR doesn't touch, both also failing on `main`:
  - `changelog attributions`: `CHANGELOG/records/2026.11.1.md`
  - dead-export scan: `extensions/google/provider-policy.ts`, `scripts/e2e/lib/upgrade-survivor/config-recipe.mts`
- **Docs.** `docs:check-links` and `docs:check-mdx` pass.

**Gap:** no real API-key GIF generation yet. The test host has no OpenAI API key, so the direct Images API was proven against the documented contract with a fake server, not against OpenAI itself.

Follow-ups (not in this PR): 2.6 `output_format: "svg"` and `complexity`; fal 2.6 routes.

prs.title: fix(models): models scan prints only "fetch failed" when OpenRouter cannot be reached
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw models scan` prints only `fetch failed` when the OpenRouter `/models` catalog request cannot connect (offline, DNS failure, refused proxy). The same bare text is the `--json` error message. Nothing says which request failed or why.

## User Impact

User impact: the command now prints, for example, `OpenRouter /models request failed: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:9. Check your network connection and retry.` (or `getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND openrouter.ai` offline). Exit code, `--json` envelope shape, timeouts, and HTTP-status errors (`OpenRouter /models failed: HTTP 503`) are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Node's `fetch` rejects network failures with a bare `TypeError("fetch failed")` and puts the real reason in `cause`. The CLI shows only `error.message` outside `--debug`, so the reason was lost. `fetchOpenRouterModels` now wraps a non-abort `fetch` rejection with the existing `formatErrorMessage` of its cause, keeping the original error as `cause`. Aborts from the scan timeout are rethrown unchanged.

## Evidence

From source on `main` at f24a3f03cd, Linux, Node 24.22.2, fresh state directory, with the network made unreachable by pointing `HTTPS_PROXY`/`HTTP_PROXY` at a closed local port.

Before:
```
$ openclaw models scan --no-probe
fetch failed
$ openclaw models scan --no-probe --json
{ "ok": false, "error": { "type": "cli_error", "message": "fetch failed" } }
```

After:
```
$ openclaw models scan --no-probe
OpenRouter /models request failed: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:9. Check your network connection and retry.
```
Exit 1 in both cases, as before.

Tests:
- `pnpm test src/agents/model-scan.test.ts src/agents/model-scan.probes.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 15 passed.
- New test "names the network failure when the catalog request cannot connect" stubs `fetch` to reject like undici (`TypeError("fetch failed", { cause: ENOTFOUND })`). It fails on `main` (`got 'fetch failed'`) and passes with the fix.
- Test-line budget: 16 added lines, allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/models-scan-network-failure.txt`; `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --staged` passes.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint --type-aware` on both files: clean.

prs.title: fix(agents): forward toolOwnerPluginId and workspaceDir to before_tool_call hook ctx
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`before_tool_call` trusted tool policies and regular hooks receive a ctx built by `buildToolContext` (`src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.policy.ts`) that drops two facts the host already holds on `HookContext`:

1. **`toolOwnerPluginId`** — the wrapper computes it (`getPluginToolMeta(tool)?.pluginId`) and puts it into the policy args' ctx, but `buildToolContext` does not copy it, so plugins cannot tell their own tool's call from a client-hosted tool reusing the same name (policies match by tool name only).
2. **`workspaceDir`** — the run's host workspace, the same value plugin tool factories receive. Without it, a plugin whose tool keeps state under the workspace has to guess (e.g. `resolveAgentWorkspaceDir(config, agentId)` as `extensions/active-memory/recall-run.ts` does), which is wrong when a run has its own workspace.

Closes #194402

## User Impact

Plugin trusted policies and `before_tool_call` hooks can now read `ctx.toolOwnerPluginId` and `ctx.workspaceDir` to scope policy decisions to the registered tool owner and judge calls against the same workspace state the tool factory uses, instead of guessing by name or by `agentId`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both fields already exist on the host `HookContext` and both were dropped in exactly one place (`buildToolContext`). Adding them to the plugin-facing `PluginHookToolContext` plus forwarding them in `buildToolContext` is the minimal fix the issue pinpoints; trusted policies pass the ctx through unchanged (`...ctxWithoutToolIdentity`), so no policy-path change is needed.

## Evidence

- New unit test `forwards toolOwnerPluginId and workspaceDir to before_tool_call hook ctx` (`src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.approval-policy.test.ts`) fails on main (fields absent from the hook ctx) and passes with this change — red/green verified locally with vitest on latest main.
- Existing trigger/requester forwarding test still passes unchanged.
- Fields are documented as optional: `toolOwnerPluginId` absent for core and client-hosted tools; `workspaceDir` is a diagnostics-only path fact, not the execution cwd and not an authorization input (per the semantics discussion in #194402).

## AI Assistance

This PR was authored with AI assistance (issue analysis, patch, and test written by an automated contributor workflow), reviewed by the submitter.

prs.title: perf(android): evaluate release Gradle heap sizing
prs.body:
## Experiment

Measure whether a 4 GiB Gradle heap improves Android phone/Wear release builds over the current 3 GiB heap. Both variants retain Parallel GC, identical source, the same eight-vCPU release runner, task selection, lint, R8, and signature verification. Production release configuration is unchanged while this draft gathers evidence.

The temporary diagnostic operation is manual, fixed to source `22b1aacbc054c003f6a7762d78b7c49da855ef38`, and has read-only repository permissions and no release environment or credentials. It uses a disposable keystore and never uploads to Play or Firebase. The harness is adapted from the committed GC benchmark at `217355ed4605e4d3a7bb4541b6bb6a1e6cfe4c0e`.

## Acceptance rule, recorded before dispatch

Run five serial paired comparisons on one runner, alternating pair order. Before every sample, restore identical pristine source and dependency snapshots at the same paths and stop the previous Gradle/Kotlin JVMs. Keep build metadata fixed and task-output caching disabled. Report medians, nearest-rank p95/max, spread, process CPU, peak aggregate Java RSS, available memory, host load, and OOM counters.

A candidate qualifies only with:

- At least 5% and five seconds lower median bundle time, winning at least four of five pairs.
- No regression in bundle p95, complete signing/build/signature median, median Java CPU, or maximum aggregate Java RSS; no OOM.
- All ten builds and twenty individual bundle signature checks passing, with identical complete task/outcome inventories.
- No 20% regression in any measured performance cell. A memory tradeoff is not implicitly accepted.

Temporary workflow, test-option changes, and benchmark code will be removed from the final production diff after measurement. If the experiment fails, close this draft without changing production configuration. If it qualifies, replace the experiment diff with the focused heap change and documentation, complete review, mark ready, and watch CI.

## Result: rejected; production remains at 3 GiB

[Nonpublishing benchmark run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42327684936) completed successfully in 29m35s on the exact committed workload `7a764c59c5f8bbd9a0c5eafa401c3afcb54c347e`, measuring frozen source `22b1aacbc054c003f6a7762d78b7c49da855ef38`. The runner reported eight available CPUs and 30.95 GiB RAM. The artifact `android-release-gradle-heap-42327684936` contains the root result, ten sample receipts, build/signature logs, complete Gradle profiles, and one-second resource samples.

All ten signed phone/Wear builds and twenty individual signature checks passed. Each build had the same 163 task/outcome rows and `149 actionable tasks: 146 executed, 3 up-to-date`. Daemon startup commands confirm 3 GiB versus 4 GiB, with Parallel GC in both. No Play or Firebase upload occurred.

| Metric | 3 GiB median | 4 GiB median | 3 GiB p95/max | 4 GiB p95/max |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Bundle build | 148.421 s | 146.897 s | 160.657 s | 155.373 s |
| Signing preflight + build + signature checks | 155.956 s | 155.668 s | 168.985 s | 163.671 s |
| Java CPU | 943.430 CPU-s | 922.060 CPU-s | 999.220 CPU-s | 964.690 CPU-s |
| Aggregate Java peak RSS per sample | 6.792 GiB | 8.107 GiB | 6.907 GiB | 8.153 GiB |
| Minimum available host RAM per sample | 23.114 GiB | 21.808 GiB | 23.158 GiB | 22.599 GiB |
| Host CPU busy per sample | 75.347 % | 75.173 % | 77.012 % | 76.898 % |

Five samples per variant; nearest-rank p95 is the maximum with this sample count. Bundle ranges were 133.677–160.657s (3 GiB) and 140.529–155.373s (4 GiB). Complete-workload ranges were 141.274–168.985s and 148.908–163.671s. Resource values cover the signing preflight through final signature verification. CPU is sampled aggregate Java process time; RSS is sampled peak aggregate Java memory.

| Pair | Order | 3 GiB bundle | 4 GiB bundle | 4 GiB saving |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 01 | 3g → 4g | 160.657s | 155.373s | +5.284s (+3.29%) |
| 02 | 4g → 3g | 135.815s | 150.576s | -14.761s (-10.87%) |
| 03 | 3g → 4g | 133.677s | 146.624s | -12.947s (-9.69%) |
| 04 | 4g → 3g | 153.003s | 146.897s | +6.106s (+3.99%) |
| 05 | 3g → 4g | 148.421s | 140.529s | +7.892s (+5.32%) |

The candidate saves only 1.524s (1.03%) in median bundle time, wins only three of five pairs, and increases maximum aggregate Java RSS by 1.246 GiB (18.05%). It fails the preregistered 5%/five-second threshold, four-pair requirement, and memory condition. No production heap change will be proposed from this experiment. The median complete workload improves only 0.288s.

The runner did not expose the captured cgroup OOM counters, so independent zero-OOM-counter proof is unavailable. No build failed, and no OOM error appears in the build logs. This limitation does not affect rejection: the speed, paired-win, and memory requirements already fail.

The task profiles do not support increasing the heap to accelerate the main R8 task: median `:app:minifyPlayReleaseWithR8` was 64.980s versus 68.750s. These task durations overlap and must not be summed as wall time.

## Preparation proof and limits

Workflow lint/security checks, focused emulator diagnostic contract, JavaScript syntax, formatting, and whitespace passed. Independent AutoReview at P0–P2 found no actionable benchmark issues; the subsequent operation-name adjustment was mechanical. Local type-aware lint did not execute because it waited on shared artifact ownership; it is not claimed as passing proof. Hosted Workflow Sanity and the nonpublishing benchmark passed. All current PR checks are terminal, with no failures; broad CI was skipped for this draft.

The temporary workflow operation, script, and test-option changes remain only on this closed experiment branch. They are not part of production configuration. Both production heap and Parallel GC remain unchanged.

Maintainer-requested Android release performance campaign; continuation of #194382.

prs.title: fix(infer): cancel interrupted image describe requests
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Ctrl+C during `openclaw infer image describe` / `image describe-many` leaves the provider HTTP request pending until the CLI is force-killed, and a late result can still be published after the interrupt. The video path (`infer video describe`) was repaired in #194251 and audio in #193893 by forwarding the invocation's execution context; the image describe path dropped it.

## Why This Change Was Made

`describeImageFile` in `src/media-understanding/runtime.ts` still called `runMediaUnderstandingFile` without the `MediaExecutionContext`, so the cancellation signal never reached the provider request. #194251 moved audio/video to the shared `runFile` runner that consumes the execution context (guarded-fetch authority + owned command scope); image describe was the remaining caller on the old path.

This change makes `describeImageFile` structurally identical to the #194251-approved `describeVideoFile`: it accepts an optional `execution` parameter and routes through the shared `runFile`. The CLI `image.ts` describe/describe-many branch now calls `getAsyncWorkSignal()` (already imported for the generate/edit branches), builds the execution context, and forwards it; the explicit-model fallback path passes `abortSignal` to `runWithImageModelFallback` (already supported). The parameter stays optional, so plugin-facade and one-argument callers (`bindMediaUnderstandingRuntime`, `registry-runtime-facades`) keep their existing behavior. No public runtime type, SDK entrypoint, config, schema, or retry change.

Production LOC: `+17/-10`. Classification: `behavior-completing`.

## User Impact

Interrupting `openclaw infer image describe` (with or without `--model`) now aborts the pending provider request and suppresses the late result, instead of waiting out the timeout and printing after Ctrl+C. Uninterrupted runs and image generate/edit are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Discriminative regression (RED -> GREEN)

`it.each` in `src/media-understanding/runtime.test.ts` now covers `["image", describeImageFile]` alongside the existing audio/video entries for "refuses canceled %s before preparing media", reusing #194251's exact test shape.

| Build | Result |
|---|---|
| RED (base `d4d6fe725bf`, no `execution` on `describeImageFile`) | `refuses canceled image before preparing media` **fails**; audio/video pass |
| GREEN (this head) | **18/18 passed** in `runtime.test.ts`, including the new image case |

### Targeted suites

- `src/media-understanding/runtime.test.ts` — 18 passed (GREEN); 1 failed / 17 passed (RED base)
- `src/cli/capability-cli.test.ts` — 111 passed (image.ts CLI registration unchanged)

All runs were executed on the isolated remote test host (10.54.159.54, node 24.22.1, `--user 0:0`) with no production Gateway, session, channel, token, or config touched.

### Checks

- `git diff --check` — clean
- `run-format.mts --check` on the three touched files — all correct format
- `tsgo:core` — the touched files report **0 errors**. The remote host's offline dependency tree produces pre-existing `Cannot find module` errors in unrelated `packages/*` (mdast-util-from-markdown, micromark, libphonenumber-js, smol-toml, etc.); the identical error set appears on the unmodified base, confirming it is environmental, not introduced here.

### Scope and risk

- Production LOC: `+17/-10`
- Test LOC: `+1` (one `it.each` row; no new mock factory, no new file — `check:test-mock-exports` and `check:test-lines-ratchet` unaffected)
