prs.title: fix(providers): resolve saved profile bindings for provider usage
prs.body:
Fixes #188534

## What Problem This Solves

Saving a provider API key in the Control UI reports success and the config hot reload applies, but the provider usage panel keeps returning `HTTP 401`. The save path writes the saved **profile id** (for example `deepseek:manual`) into `cfg.models.providers.<provider>.apiKey`, and provider usage put configured candidates first and sent that id as the bearer token instead of the stored secret.

## Why This Change Was Made

`prepareProviderApiKeyCandidates()` builds `[configuredValue, ...]` and `resolveProviderApiKeyCandidatesFromConfigAndStore()` only appends resolved profile credentials afterwards, so DeepSeek's usage fetcher selects candidate zero — the profile id — and authenticates with it.

Binding classification now goes through the shared provider-entry owner (`resolveProviderEntryApiKeyProfileReference` / `resolveProviderEntryApiKeyBinding`), so a binding is only used for the provider that owns it: `models.providers.deepseek.apiKey = "openai:manual"` is treated as incompatible instead of sending the OpenAI secret to DeepSeek. The async path resolves the secret through `resolveApiKeyForProfile`; the legacy synchronous path stays on the profile order (`resolveAuthProfileOrder`), so expired, disabled, or unreachable profiles are dropped rather than returned as raw tokens. Literal configured keys and values that do not name a stored profile keep their previous behavior.

This replaces the earlier catalog-precedence approach (dropped from this branch): that direction would have let shared config overwrite intentionally authored per-agent keys and could have paired a shared credential with a different `baseUrl`, which the review correctly rejected. `models.json` publication behavior is unchanged by this PR.

## User Impact

A key saved through the Control UI or `openclaw models auth paste-api-key` now works for the provider usage panel, because usage resolves the same saved credential the request path uses. Nothing changes for operators who put a literal key in config or rely on generated per-agent catalogs.

## Evidence

Head `f26971911e`, Node 26.12.1.

```text
$ pnpm test src/infra/provider-usage.auth.plugin.test.ts \
    src/infra/provider-usage.auth.normalizes-keys.test.ts src/infra/provider-usage.load.test.ts
Test Files  3 passed (3)
Tests      28 passed (28)
  ✓ resolves a saved profile binding written into provider config
  ✓ keeps a literal config api key as the first usage candidate
  ✓ never resolves a binding owned by another provider
  ✓ does not return an ineligible legacy binding's raw token

# with provider-usage.auth.ts at upstream/main:
× resolves a saved profile binding written into provider config
  expected 'deepseek:manual' to be 'saved-deepseek-secret'

# with the previous naive binding resolution (af06d423f0):
× never resolves a binding owned by another provider
  expected [ 'openai-secret' ] to not include 'openai-secret'
× does not return an ineligible legacy binding's raw token
  expected 'expired-token' not to contain 'expired-token'
```

The cases cover: a stored `deepseek:manual` profile resolves to its secret for both the candidate list and the resulting usage token; a literal configured key stays candidate zero; a binding owned by another provider never contributes its secret; and an expired profile binding is not returned by the legacy synchronous path.

`oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` are clean on the two touched files.

### Runtime proof through the shipped Gateway (`usage.status`)

Real Gateway on an isolated state dir, the real `usage.status` RPC (the method the Control UI usage panel calls), and a local HTTP stand-in for MiniMax `GET /v1/token_plan/remains` that accepts only the stored secret. The credential was seeded through `upsertAuthProfileAsync` (`minimax:manual` → `local-secret`); config is the save flow’s shape (`models.providers.minimax.apiKey = "minimax:manual"`).

Before (`upstream/main` `provider-usage.auth.ts`):

```text
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/index.ts gateway --port 18790
$ callGatewayFromCli("usage.status", …)
{"providers":[{"provider":"minimax","windows":[],"error":"HTTP 401"}]}
provider: REQ GET /v1/token_plan/remains Authorization=Bearer minimax:manual -> 401
```

After (this head):

```text
$ callGatewayFromCli("usage.status", …)
{"providers":[{"provider":"minimax","windows":[{"label":"5h","usedPercent":2,"resetAt":…}],"plan":"Coding Plan · MiniMax-M2"}]}
provider: REQ GET /v1/token_plan/remains Authorization=Bearer local-secret -> 200
```
### Authority-chain controls (both P1 findings)

Candidates now carry their source (`envDirect` / `environment` / `config`). Only a value actually selected from that provider’s config is classified as a binding, environment and direct candidates pass through untouched, and an unusable binding drops only the config value instead of removing a working key. A fixed destination (usage/billing) also opts out of the shared-base-URL exception before any secret is resolved, because those endpoints ignore inference `baseUrl`s.

Unit regressions (red on `95c363e6c3`, green here) in `src/infra/provider-usage.auth.plugin.test.ts`:

- `keeps an environment candidate ahead of a config profile binding` — the env key stays candidate zero and the configured profile’s secret is not substituted.
- `does not release another provider’s secret to a fixed usage endpoint` — an `openai:manual` binding under `minimax` with a shared proxy `baseUrl` contributes nothing.

Same Gateway harness as above, one config per control (`usage.status` through the real gateway, provider stand-in logs the bearer):

```text
env override   (MINIMAX_API_KEY set, config apiKey=minimax:manual)
  provider: REQ GET /v1/token_plan/remains Authorization=Bearer working-env-key -> 200

proxy cross-provider (openai + minimax share https://proxy.example/v1, minimax.apiKey=openai:manual)
  provider: REQ GET /v1/token_plan/remains Authorization=Bearer local-secret -> 200
  # openai-secret is never transmitted; usage falls back to minimax own stored profile

expired profile (config apiKey=minimax:expired)
  provider: REQ GET /v1/token_plan/remains Authorization=Bearer local-secret -> 200
  # expired-token is never transmitted; usage falls back to the eligible profile
```
**Test cost:** `config/test-lines-allocations/provider-usage-saved-binding.txt` allocates the 196 added test lines. Both regressions fail only once a config-sourced candidate is classified as a binding, so a cheaper layer cannot prove them; the shared scalar is unchanged.

**Gap:** the provider endpoint is a local stand-in (no real MiniMax key on this host); the Gateway, the RPC surface, the credential store, the binding resolution, and the request the panel receives are the real ones.

## AI Assistance
This PR is AI-assisted. Followed the review's recommendation after confirming the profile-id candidate in `provider-usage.auth.ts`, resolved the binding in the existing credential owner, and pinned both the binding and the literal-key control. The implementer understands the code: config may hold a credential or a binding to one, and every consumer has to resolve the binding before using it as a token.

prs.title: fix: tool_call rejects quoted numbers and booleans that direct calls accept
prs.body:
Related: #166133

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a deferred tool call fails with `limit: expected integer; received "3" (string)` when the model quotes a number or boolean inside `tool_call` args, even though the same quoted value works when that tool is called directly.

## User Impact

User impact: models that quote scalars inside `tool_call` args now reach the tool instead of failing the call. One #166133 reporter logged this with MiniMax on `web_fetch`, `exec` and plugin tools. Numbers and booleans that were already typed correctly behave as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

Direct tool calls go through `validateToolArguments` in the agent loop, which coerces `"3"` to `3` and `"true"` to `true` against the tool's schema. `tool_call` declares its nested `args` as `Record<string, Unknown>`, so that same step only sees an opaque object and never coerces the fields inside. The catalog validator then rejects them with no coercion step of its own. The nested args also give the model no type to anchor on, which is probably why quoting shows up here specifically.

This runs the existing coercion for `tool_call` targets too, before the `before_tool_call` hook and before catalog validation. If coercion can't satisfy the schema, the original input goes on to the catalog validator, so the error text from #172453 doesn't change.

A few choices worth checking:

- Only trusted targets coerce, using the same `entry.source !== "openclaw"` check catalog validation already has. #114461 deliberately left MCP and client schemas to their own execution boundary and `docs/tools/tool-search.md` documents that, so this doesn't read or compile those schemas. A quoted value bound for an MCP or client tool arrives exactly as it did before.
- Only the `tool_call` control opts in. Code Mode and other `runtime.call` users stay strict, because guests there get typed signatures, and the #172453 test that pins `"10"` as rejected on `runtime.call` still passes untouched. #172453 said strict rejection stays, and that was about its diagnostics scope, so I'd rather you weigh in on this than assume. If you want strictness on `tool_call` too, this is easy to close.
- It reuses the direct-path rules on purpose rather than adding a narrower set, so `tool_call` now matches them exactly. That includes the odd ones: `null` and `false` become `0` for a numeric field unless the schema rejects `0`.
- #172329 fixed this for one tool's limits (`maxFires` on standing intents). This covers the rest of `tool_call`. I left that normalization alone.

I used `Related` rather than `Closes` because #166133 also reports MCP servers receiving strings, and this doesn't change what they receive.

## Evidence

Reproduced on main at 5bb4dfda334 through the real `Agent` loop, with a scripted model emitting `{ limit: "3", recursive: "true" }` for a tool with `integer` and `boolean` fields:

| route | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| direct tool call | tool runs with `{"limit":3,"recursive":true}` | unchanged |
| `tool_call` | tool never runs | tool runs with `{"limit":3,"recursive":true}` |

- The new test in `tool-search.agent-loop.test.ts` fails on main (`expected "vi.fn()" to be called once, but got 0 times`) and passes here.
- Passing: `tool-search.agent-loop`, `tool-search`, `tool-search-runtime` (plus `.output-variants` and `.refusal`), `tool-search.mcp-error`, `tool-search.discovery`, `tool-search.metadata`, `code-mode.mcp`.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` are clean.

Gateway trace: I also ran this through a real Gateway started with `startGatewayServer` in isolated state, with a `chat.send` turn and a scripted OpenAI Responses provider, using `tools.toolSearch: { mode: "tools" }`. `sessions_history` is deferred in that config, and `read` is offered directly. The model sees `tool_call` as `dispatch_action`, so that's the name the provider called. Same script both times, with only `tool-search.ts` and `tool-search-runtime.ts` swapped to 5bb4dfda334 for the main column:

| provider call | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `read` directly, `limit: "2"` | returns 2 lines | unchanged |
| `dispatch_action` to `sessions_history`, `limit: "1"`, `includeTools: "false"` | rejected: `limit: expected integer; received "1" (string); includeTools: expected boolean; received "false" (string)` | returns 1 message |
| `dispatch_action`, `limit: 1`, `includeTools: false` | returns 1 message | unchanged |
| `dispatch_action`, `limit: "abc"` | rejected: `limit: expected integer` | still rejected with the same error, before the tool runs |

That harness was a scratch test and isn't in this diff, because it needed a temporary entry in the forked test lane. It's the source-run Gateway rather than a built `dist`, since the full tsdown build gets killed for memory on this machine. On head 6aaa73fec75, `tool-search.agent-loop`, `tool-search` and `tool-search-runtime` pass (100 tests).

That entry is the provider's own earlier call read back from the transcript, which is why it still shows `"limit": "1"`. The transcript keeps what the provider sent. The log doesn't print from inside the tool, so the exact received object is pinned by the agent-loop test instead (`{"limit":3,"recursive":true}`). In the invalid case the `Invalid arguments` text comes from catalog validation, raised in the before-tool-call stage and wrapped as `BeforeToolCallFailureError`, so `sessions_history` never ran.

The logs above were captured on 6aaa73fec75, before three later commits. e4968bfc02c and f66cbe87d62 only merge `main`, to pick up its `test-lines` ceiling, and neither touches the files in this PR. eae41c55b16 adds the trusted-target check. `sessions_history` and `read` are core tools, so that check doesn't change the path those logs cover, but I didn't rerun the Gateway trace. On eae41c55b16, `tool-search`, `tool-search-runtime`, `tool-search.mcp-error` and `tool-search.agent-loop` pass. That last file now has a test that a client tool still receives `limit: "3"`, which failed before the check. `oxlint` is clean on the changed source and test files, and I left typechecking this commit to CI.

This adds 36 net test lines, recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/tool-call-quoted-scalars.txt`. I kept the test because this was a silent mismatch between two routes in a shared entry point, and it runs through the real agent loop so it checks what the tool actually receives.

Not run: a live MiniMax turn, since I don't have those credentials. The scripted model stands in for the provider, so this proves what happens once quoted values arrive, not why a given provider quotes them. @miluo-star's transcript on #166133 shows the same call succeeding unquoted and failing quoted, but it isn't the raw provider capture steipete asked for. The test typecheck lane (`tsgo:core:test`) wasn't run locally either, and I didn't measure the new test's `--maxWorkers=1` wall time or CI seconds.

---
I'm a college freshman and I worked on this with Claude Code. I read the code paths, ran the repro and checked the results myself, but tell me if I missed something about why this is strict.

prs.title: fix(ui): open the mobile Where picker above when space below is short
prs.body:
Related: mobile Control UI picker report from @vincentkoc; follows #194126 and #194139.

## Problem

On a phone, the new-session **Where** picker (This computer) always opened below its trigger, into the small space above the composer. Its list shrank to 77px at 393×852 and 48px at 393×500 against 129px of content, so the **Hosted workspaces / Agents API setup** section was hidden behind an inner scroll. It never flipped above, because its max height was a fraction of the space below, so that side always "fit".

## Solution

Add one `max-height` declaration inside the existing `.oc-popover.new-session-page__select` rule (`ui/src/styles/new-session.css`), mirroring the composer pickers' existing `@position-try --chat-picker-fit` budget: a side with less than 200px is rejected, so the popover flips above its trigger and shows its whole list.

No new stylesheet, rule block or selector, and no design change: the desktop layout and the "What" picker are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Regression folded into the existing mobile docking test in `ui/src/e2e/mobile-new-conversation.e2e.test.ts` (390×844, touch): opening Where must not leave its list scrolling (base: 48px inner scroll).
- **Red on base:** only the docking test fails (`expected 48 to be 0`); the other 8 pass. **Green with the fix:** 9/9. Test-lines ratchet within budget.
- oxfmt, stylelint, oxlint and `git diff --check` are clean.

| 393×852 before | 393×852 after | 393×500 after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![Where picker before 393x852](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/62a6fbf9-94d9-4399-b7b2-26a3aac580f2) | ![Where picker after 393x852](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/92fd584b-5a1f-4d86-a1bc-26f978f7d907) | ![Where picker after 393x500](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5adb9da0-01c0-4f6b-875d-28dc8e77caa8) |

Screenshots are Chromium with synthetic data. The audit measured the same clipping in WebKit (Safari 27.2) and the same fix behavior via injected CSS.

## Gaps

- Not verified on a real iPhone.
- No isolated WebKit run on the final source; WebKit evidence is from the audit's injected-CSS check.

Human credit: vincentkoc and vyctorbrzezowski.

## Worked on by

- @vincentkoc
- @vyctorbrzezowski

prs.title: feat: gate personal instructions on private session audience
prs.body:
Related: #186068, #186067, #186066, #186065; parent #186050.

## What Problem This Solves

Keeps automatically selected personal USER.md content and canonical personal-instructions chat operations out of shared or unverified initial audiences, without replacing the existing human-profile registry, Settings editor, or session profile-selection rules.

## User Impact

This review proposal contains three bounded improvements:

1. Group/channel, cron, and subagent bootstrap contexts do not open the selected personal file. The final common filter also withholds personal-marked/origin hook entries. Shared defaults and existing allowlists remain intact.
2. The personal-file handler refuses agent-tool get/set operations with known group/channel origins or execution targets. Both actions return content; both are checked before file access or mutation.
3. Initial delivery also requires committed host sharing facts: an existing creator-private **Draft**, no public share, and a canonical creator matching the selected profile (bootstrap) or authenticated editor (chat tool). Shared/read-only/suggest, foreign-creator, and unverified audiences withhold the overlay or direct chat operations to **Settings → Profile → Personal instructions**. Distinct delegated origin and execution sessions must both qualify. A direct label alone is insufficient.

**Authenticated Settings self-editing is unchanged.** Session selection remains assigned human owner, otherwise authenticated human creator; a new sender does not replace it. The authenticated editor remains separate from that selection. Canonical aliases and immutable creator stamps stay with their existing owners.

**Not full person-level privacy; does not close #186068.** These checks cover initial loader delivery and the canonical file handler's response/write boundary. Admission is not retained through every provider submission, tool-history append, or native thread. Widening an already-used private conversation can expose prior context or generated responses. Generic file/shell/native capabilities, inferred-to-file confinement, Knowledge/LCM audience admission, and retained history remain unqualified. Trusted administrators/host access are not hostile tenants. This is proposed narrowing for owner review, not upstream design acceptance. Nothing is merged or deployed.

## Why This Change Was Made

One small admission composes the existing profile catalog and retained session-sharing facts; no second registry, cache, SQL schema, configuration, public SDK contract, or model-supplied identity/audience argument is introduced. The existing public-share fact now participates in the internal sharing projection and its invalidation. Bootstrap checks after reads and hooks; the personal-file owner composes audience checks with its existing requester/role/agent and safe-writer pre-mutation assertion.

Author simplification retains the existing profile/file and session-facts owners. Against refreshed base `d4d6fe725bff2be867784d666e1d2118b9e2f41a`: production +180/−19 (net +161), tests +462/−21 (net +441). The documented per-change record `config/test-lines-allocations/186068-profile-audience-regressions.txt` allocates exactly those 441 regression lines; the shared baseline is unchanged. Real committed sharing facts and final-effect negative controls justify the regression growth. The wider proposal remains documentation, not new Knowledge/history implementation.

## Refreshed-base verification — 2026-11-07

The updated source is published at `46ad274fef2930e0a82263d885c0bbc1e45f2d2c`. Integration with main at `d4d6fe725bff2be867784d666e1d2118b9e2f41a` resolved one bootstrap conflict: setup/shared-file preparation remains parallel, while personal-file reads remain behind audience admission. The current source has 14 intended PR paths and preserves the requested human credit.

- **124 tests across eight files passed** in four shards (233.92s wrapper). The separate explicit agents-support carrier suite passed **7 tests** (45.12s Vitest). The first carrier attempt failed during compiler OS-thread setup; the unchanged serial rerun supplied the missing coverage, not evidence of a product repair.
- Core, Gateway-methods, agents-root and agents-other test typing passed. Bootstrap lint/format, docs lint (1,411 files), docs format (1,421), MDX (1,433) and exact-base whitespace passed. The documented allocation gate passed locally with nine lines slack. CI seconds for the new head are not represented as local wall time.
- Fresh bound independent review of all 14 candidate paths against that exact base was **scoped-clean, no P0–P2 findings**. It did not execute the tests and does not certify wider person isolation.
- Hosted **check-docs is now passing** on this head. Other CI is not green: the executed merge `ba668bdd15fa46031d58a1ea7e0deb45866a3ad7` combines this head with main `efb980423985b290f5c294ba7b13ad4c2bd074d8`. It reports TS2532 at `test/scripts/release-validation-waivers.test.ts:384` and a one-line test-budget deficit. The typing file is outside this PR; its baseline attribution is not yet independently reproduced here. Canonical upstream repair [#194386](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194386) explicitly targets that exact inherited budget deficit and remains separate. Do not increase this PR’s 441-line credit to conceal inherited debt or claim the failed run passed.

The original MD018 failure and the published merge conflict are repaired. Current CI, owner acceptance and hosted review remain separate gates. No merge or deployment is authorized.

## Documentation CI repair — 2026-11-07

The initial repair commit `f0815ff1` made a one-line prose correction in `docs/architecture/authenticated-profile-audience.md`. A line beginning with an issue number was parsed as a malformed heading (MD018); “evidence for #186065” retains the meaning without heading syntax.

- The exact `pnpm lint:docs` command reproduced the CI failure before the edit, then passed with zero issues across 1,402 files.
- `pnpm format:docs:check` passed across 1,412 files; `pnpm docs:check-mdx` passed across 1,424 files; whitespace checks passed.
- No runtime code changed. Runtime tests and independent review recorded below are retained evidence for the unchanged `aa13a00d` implementation, not a new runtime rerun.
- The PR remains ready for review, not a claim of merge readiness. New-head CI and current review remain separate gates; no merge or deployment is authorized.

## Evidence for this follow-up

Published head: `46ad274fef2930e0a82263d885c0bbc1e45f2d2c`; ready for review, with the broader privacy scenario still incomplete. Remote verification found all **14 expected changed paths**, without evidence files or dependency caches. The commit retains the requested human co-author credit.

- **Red → green:** the shared-web bootstrap regression originally exposed Alice's personal content after the session became shared. Committed Draft/sharing/public-link/creator facts now control delivery; no private overlay is admitted merely because chat type is direct. A public share added during a bootstrap hook invalidates the prepared release.
- **51 Gateway tests passed across two files**: 50 production tool → in-process dispatch → handler → guarded filesystem cases, plus the real isolated Gateway two-person Settings fixture. The tool suite uses synthetic admitted authority/mocked profile facts with real committed session rows. Shared web audiences, foreign creator, shared origin/private execution, and audience changes before read release or final write are denied. The real WebSocket fixture independently verifies each authenticated person's own file, other-file/shared-file denial, and final role/merge revocation. This is not a live-model/group-channel pass.
- **19/19 affected personal/remote bootstrap cases passed** in the final consumer rerun (13.36 s wrapper), including profile ordering, aliases, budgets, group/cron/subagent exclusion, metadata admission/revocation, and remote file provenance. The remote transport executes locally and does not qualify a remote-worker or native runtime.
- Other unchanged consumers passed in the broader invocation: memory provenance **4**, sharing-projection lifecycle **8**, collected-turn selection **2**, prompt-prefix stability **14**. That invocation executed eight files, with 96 passes and two fixture failures; it was not a clean whole-run pass. The fixtures were corrected at their owners: asynchronous cleanup drains SQLite borrowers before closing, and the remote provenance mock classifies the requested personal paths after supplying real session config. The affected 19-case rerun above is the repair proof; no second whole-flow rerun is claimed.
- An explicit **agents-support carrier run passed 5/5** via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-support.config.ts src/agents/harness/workspace-context.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`. The mixed-path invocation had not executed that suite. These are rendering/carrier tests with a mocked bootstrap producer, not native execution or audience-isolation E2E.
- Core, Gateway-methods, agents-root and remote/agents-other TypeScript checks passed. Scoped type-aware lint, targeted formatting, two-document MDX compilation, whitespace and exact-base staged test-line ratchet passed (24,614 lines of slack; no exception). Lint's missing braces were fixed, not suppressed.
- Retained bound Auto Review for runtime candidate `aa13a00d` inspected the full staged candidate and complete owner source context against the exact base: **scoped-clean, no P0–P2 findings**. It did not execute tests. The old hosted documentation review does not certify this runtime head. Current-head CI is separate and is not claimed green here.

## Dependencies and owner decisions still required

- **Knowledge:** #186455 is agent-private conversation access, not person isolation. Separate PR #189822 at `ce0ad0404b7b5cc3b21b4efb8bfccc17fef735f4` proposes person/agent grants selecting **one space**, not a private-plus-shared union; it disables bootstrap and excludes broad file/execution/history capabilities in its qualified profile. Do not duplicate that lane. Its current body reports an executed installed Knowledge–LosslessClaw 1.2.0 save/compact/restart/grep/evidence/replay fixture—new bounded #186065 evidence, not merely source. Those are its author's reported results, not this PR's execution; the shared-owner continuity fixture and separate P/Q cases do not prove the combined person-private/shared history scenario. It remains unmerged/proposed.
- **Host/profile owners:** accept or revise this Draft-only initial-delivery rule, then define run/provider/tool-history lifetime admission and safe handling when a conversation that already contains personal context is shared. Do not silently rewrite history or reassign personalization.
- **Knowledge/LCM owners:** settle private-plus-shared person/audience grants and supported explicit-ID/delegated expansion authority, with pinned installed-version proof. Knowledge remains the durable record/evidence owner; LosslessClaw remains history/compaction owner. No private LCM database reader is added.
- **File/sandbox/harness owners:** choose and qualify a capability profile where every enabled direct read/write/exec/native route respects personal roots and inferred records cannot overwrite user-authored instructions. Prompt filtering or a read-only mount is not that boundary.
- **Runtime qualification:** real-model embedded and generic CLI execution, native Codex, delegated history, ACP, realtime, remote-worker, and Windows E2E remain untested here. No Gateway, local remote-file adapter, carrier, or prefix pass transfers to those paths. Keep the complete two-person fixture open pending these contracts and proofs. No merge, auto-merge, or deployment is requested.

Implementation proposal and named owner map: [authenticated profile audience](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/46ad274fef2930e0a82263d885c0bbc1e45f2d2c/docs/architecture/authenticated-profile-audience.md).

<details>
<summary>Retained earlier-revision evidence and publication history (not current-head qualification)</summary>

Related: #186068, #186067, #186066, #186065; parent #186050.

## What Problem This Solves

Keeps personal USER.md content out of known group/channel bootstrap and personal-instructions tool results while preserving the authenticated person's Settings editor and stable session profile selection.

## User Impact

**This draft contains two bounded runtime improvements:**

1. Group/channel, cron, and subagent bootstrap contexts do not open the automatically selected personal file. The common post-hook filter also withholds personal-marked or personal-origin entries. Shared defaults and existing subagent/cron allowlists remain intact.
2. The canonical personal-file handler refuses agent-tool get/set calls whose host-captured origin or execution session is a known group/channel. Both operations return profile content, so both are checked before file access or mutation. A group-origin request cannot evade this check by executing in another session; a direct-origin request cannot use a group execution target. The error points to **Settings → Profile → Personal instructions**.

**Authenticated Settings self-editing is unchanged.** No new model-supplied audience/profile parameter, registry, SDK contract, configuration, or schema is introduced. Session-selected owner/creator and authenticated editor remain separate. Host-resolved direct chat type retains precedence over a same-session group-looking key. This deliberately narrows chat-tool availability in known groups/channels and remains a draft for owner review—not a claim of upstream design acceptance.

**Not full person-level privacy; does not close #186068.** Direct/unknown/shared-web audiences, generic filesystem/native paths, previously delivered history, person-private Knowledge grants, LCM expansion, and inference-to-file confinement remain unchanged or unqualified. #186455 grants agent-private conversation access, not person isolation. Nothing is merged or deployed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bootstrap classification now serves the pre-read decision and final file filter. The additional tool-result check belongs in the existing users.personalFile owner, where current requester/role/agent, hash conflict, cancellation and final-write assertions already run. It consumes the host's existing requester origin and execution key, not model arguments or another identity manager. The tool's description names the Settings fallback; its action schema is unchanged.

Production delta against refreshed base: +43/-11 (net +32). Regression delta: +167 lines across the two existing owner suites. Existing test-line budget passes without an allocation or baseline change. The wider architecture and implementation proposal stays clearly separated from these two implemented slices.

## Evidence

Base: `194b10349b12ee8480e3837b2c90f28803f362cd`. Current head: `7c4889ba5130d3bf074aab481e0aff0abc5b74f4`. All eight published file blobs match the validated local bytes; no task evidence or dependency caches are in the current diff.

### Current tool-result follow-up

- **Red → green:** new get/set regressions failed before the handler change: get returned Alice's private instructions, and set persisted and returned the replacement. Both pass after the fix. The final matrix covers authoritative group/channel origin, origin-key fallback, execution-key fallback, group-origin delegation, and direct-origin execution in a group; denied operations open no filesystem root and leave Alice, Bob, and shared files unchanged. A same-session authoritative direct override still succeeds.
- **60 tests passed across three files**: the 45-case personal-file/chat-tool suite, real isolated Gateway session-only self-edit fixture, and 14 prompt-prefix tests. The combined command took 59.13 s including compilation. A lint-required simplification of the test table preserved all cases; the final 45-case owner suite rerun passed in 12.00 s including compilation (about 0.9 s of test cases).
- The tool fixture uses the production tool → in-process dispatcher → handler → safe filesystem path, with synthetic admitted authority/profile state. Separately, the real isolated Gateway fixture confirms both authenticated people retain Settings self-edit access and role/merge revocation protection. It is not a live group-channel/model test, and captured-origin test cases are not a native delegation E2E pass.
- Core and Gateway-methods test TypeScript checks, scoped oxlint, targeted oxfmt, two-document MDX compilation, exact-base test-line ratchet, and diff whitespace checks pass. The first follow-up lint found an inefficient test-fixture map/spread; the fixture was simplified rather than suppressing the rule. Final lint and typing ran serially and exited 0.
- Fresh bound Auto Review over the full candidate against the exact base, with complete handler/tool/caller/origin/parser context: no P0–P2 findings, scoped-clean. It inspected source/tests but did not execute them. The subsequent fixture-table rewrite was mechanical and rerun green. The earlier hosted documentation review does not certify this runtime code.

### Retained bootstrap proof

The unchanged bootstrap slice previously passed 58 tests across seven files. Its three new owner regressions were red before the fix and green afterward; canonical Alice/Bob files, no personal opens, hook filtering, shared defaults, session selection, CLI transport, and prompt-prefix checks were covered. Those results remain scoped to that slice, not a second execution of the full combined feature. Its initial static run's preparation timeout/retained lock was recovered after process retirement, and serialized checks passed without bypassing a guard.

### Remaining qualification

No new real-model embedded, CLI executable, native Codex, delegated-history, ACP, realtime, remote-worker, or Windows E2E pass is claimed. Neither a common-loader pass nor a synthetic caller-origin case transfers to another harness. The complete two-person Knowledge–LosslessClaw save/compact/restart/recall/direct-file-denial scenario remains unqualified. Keep this draft pending owner review and the named live/harness proof; no merge/deploy is requested. Current-head CI is separate from the local checks above.

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/users-personal-file.test.ts src/gateway/server.personal-instructions.session-scopes.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.prefix-stability.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

prs.title: improve: reduce Android build GC overhead
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Android release builds spend substantial CPU time in R8 and garbage collection. Use Parallel GC for Gradle to reduce this overhead with the existing 3 GiB heap. The qualified comparison reduced median phone/Wear bundle time by **9.67 seconds (6.09%)**, while lowering CPU use and peak memory.

## User Impact

One JVM flag changes in the canonical Android Gradle configuration, shared by local builds and CI. Task selection, Kotlin's existing collector, heap limits, lint, R8, signing, release identity and uploads retain their existing behavior. No dependency or runner changes. No builds were published by this campaign.

## Why This Change Was Made

The [completed JFR diagnostic](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42319464302) found R8 in 10,868/14,708 Gradle Java execution samples, plus 12.426 seconds of G1 pauses and 79.12 CPU-seconds reported by GC CPU events. Native blocking samples are excluded from CPU attribution. Both recordings passed the sensitive-event audit: zero initial environment, initial system-property and process-list events. [Android's build guidance](https://developer.android.com/build/optimize-your-build#experiment-with-the-jvm-parallel-garbage-collector) recommends testing Parallel GC.

The resulting candidate passed the separate **unprofiled** acceptance campaign. Temporary recording and benchmark tooling is removed from the final diff: the whole production change is one JVM flag plus six documentation lines. Reproduce the measurement from the [committed benchmark](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/217355ed4605e4d3a7bb4541b6bb6a1e6cfe4c0e/scripts/bench-android-gradle-gc.mjs) and its [diagnostic workflow revision](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/217355ed4605e4d3a7bb4541b6bb6a1e6cfe4c0e/.github/workflows/android-emulator-diagnostic.yml).

## Evidence

[Unprofiled benchmark run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42320898370): ten serial builds, five interleaved pairs on one production-class eight-CPU runner, alternating the first variant by pair. Every sample restored the same pristine source and dependency-cache snapshots at the same paths, with fresh outputs and JVMs. Source was frozen at `d1be6e243ccd850329d93567cb3ffd71e0ff837d`; synthetic release metadata and disposable signing were fixed. Pinned production Java/SDK/Gradle, read-only dependency-cache setup, normal Wear-first task order and no task-output caching. **No JFR** during this comparison. This measures warm dependencies and cold build outputs, not empty dependency caches or an entire upload workflow.

| Metric | Baseline | Parallel GC | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Median bundle wall time | 158.780 s | 149.105 s | −6.09% |
| Bundle p95/max | 179.648 s | 154.290 s | −14.12% |
| Median preflight + build + signature checks | 166.539 s | 156.650 s | −5.94% |
| Full-stage p95/max | 190.005 s | 162.643 s | −14.40% |
| Median Java CPU | 1050.72 CPU-s | 926.26 CPU-s | −11.85% |
| Java CPU p95/max | 1159.38 CPU-s | 977.54 CPU-s | −15.68% |
| Median peak aggregate Java RSS | 7.099 GiB | 6.776 GiB | −4.55% |
| Worst peak aggregate Java RSS | 7.133 GiB | 6.950 GiB | −2.56% |

| Pair | First variant | Baseline bundle | Parallel GC bundle | Saving |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 01 | Baseline | 148.444 s | 149.105 s | −0.661 s |
| 02 | Parallel GC | 166.353 s | 145.800 s | +20.553 s |
| 03 | Baseline | 154.151 s | 140.477 s | +13.674 s |
| 04 | Parallel GC | 179.648 s | 154.290 s | +25.358 s |
| 05 | Baseline | 158.780 s | 149.358 s | +9.422 s |

**Every criterion recorded before dispatch passed:** at least 5% and five seconds lower median bundle time; wins in at least four of five pairs; bundle p95 within 5%; full-stage median within 2%; worst aggregate Java RSS within 10%; median Java CPU within 10%; no observed OOM/memory-pressure failure; and no 20% regression in measured performance metrics. Candidate won four pairs; pair 01 was 0.66 seconds slower.

All ten phone/Wear bundle builds and **twenty individual AAB signature checks passed**. Each build retained **149 actionable tasks: 146 executed, three up-to-date**, with the same **163 unique profile task/outcome rows** across all samples. Actual Gradle daemon command lines confirm the collector flag differs as intended; Kotlin retains Parallel GC and its 3 GiB heap in both variants.

Spread: baseline/candidate bundle ranges were 148.444–179.648 / 140.477–154.290 seconds; full-stage ranges 156.231–190.005 / 147.935–162.643 seconds; Java CPU ranges 972.68–1159.38 / 858.02–977.54 CPU-seconds; peak RSS ranges 7.020–7.133 / 6.745–6.950 GiB. Host CPU busy ranged 77.49–80.99% / 73.82–76.44%. Available memory stayed above 22.778 GiB. Resource sampling is once per second and can miss process-exit tails; cgroup OOM counters were not exposed. With five samples, nearest-rank p95 is the maximum. These are controlled release-build observations, not a universal speedup guarantee.

Focused script/parser/workflow checks passed before the measured revision. Final documentation sanity, formatting and diff checks pass. The existing manual, exact-SHA-bound, secretless Android diagnostic contract test also passes after removing temporary instrumentation. Fresh local AutoReview (Codex, P0–P2) of the final production diff is scoped-clean with no actionable findings.

[Final-head PR CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42324010362) passed at `4a6d579488df266cff899b264a96b21b22949462`: Play, third-party and Wear tests, Kotlin lint, both 4 KiB/16 KiB native Android lanes, documentation, security and the overall CI gate. No branch-related CI failures or repair commits were needed.

Unrelated source edits select the update-restart filesystem regression even though it evaluates a finite set of update modules.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194380

## Evidence

- All 168 tests in the three affected planner suites pass; scoped lint, root-tooling typecheck, formatting and diff checks pass.
- The regression reads both real VM input lists (91 distinct modules), checks native-worker/bootstrap inputs and rejects unrelated source selection. It fails on the original generic watch.
- Same-source planner replay at base `23c0328d39d8f45b63a69fd90669a2cb33be216f`, using the eight real paths from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194184: 86 -> 85 selected test files. Only `update-restart-module-outcome.test.ts` is removed; no additions. This is a common-revision replay, not a historical runtime measurement.
- Recorded run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42315120712/job/128226155444 spends 1.764s in this fixture body. Its containing job still runs; no observed billing saving is claimed.
- Independent source/input review: no findings. Local ClawSweeper reviewed the full committed range `23c0328d..05ef8fc9`: complete, no patch defect or actionable findings (0.93 correctness confidence).

The first broad validation caught over-selection of unrelated test-file edits. Restoring the original source-only behavior fixed all four failures; expected results were not weakened.

prs.title: feat: reload plugins across active native conversations
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An agent running `openclaw plugins reload <plugin> --wait` can wait on its own retained plugin generation. Multiple active conversations retaining the same generation make caller-only handoff insufficient.

## User Impact

`openclaw plugins reload <plugin> --force --wait --accept-capabilities --json` can hand off all supported retaining native conversations without asking the model to stop polling. The Gateway owns accepted maintenance independently of the CLI socket: an external CLI receives final JSON, while interrupted agent callers receive the actual outcome in the same conversation.

Force requires Gateway administration authority. It never discards live plugin leases or replays completed side effects. Ordinary Stop still cancels queued work; maintenance preserves durable queued inputs and their original requester. Failed activation or retirement keeps continuations fenced unless the lifecycle owner proves a healthy outcome.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Add the CLI/protocol force option through the existing reload reservation, publication and rollback owner. Non-force behavior and existing drain budgets remain unchanged.
- Capture exact retaining native-run continuations under each admitted original requester, with current-authority checks, session incarnation, queue custody and successor barriers. Unsupported runs fail before interruption.
- Give cooperative holders a short bounded grace, then use normal controller maintenance interruption and join subprocess plus actual plugin-call cleanup before allowing successors.
- Revalidate the maintenance administrator at physical interruption. Keep initiating-person and exact-run Stop ownership after the original RPC retires, retain private internal delivery, and preserve canonical Gateway binding for queued followups.
- Consume the canonical settled replacement outcome, including publication and recovery health. A committed activation failure must not resume conversations or claim rollback. Missing old rollback code must not block a successfully applied, healthy replacement.
- Scope is process-local only: no operation journal, startup recovery, schema migration, public operation observer or new queue. After a Gateway crash, inspect plugin state before retrying.

Designed and implemented from @jacobtomlinson’s approved multi-session reload plan.
## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @jacobtomlinson](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/85b7d33e-fd16-4ea2-85ee-46951f9ab0e2)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/353ee643-f438-4437-82e2-e5514304140f)

## Evidence

### Fresh dummy-plugin / real-Gateway proof

Conditions: isolated Linux Gateway launched through the normal `pnpm openclaw` guard, deterministic local Responses API fixture, real native and Code Mode tool execution, and actual CLI commands. The fixture never voluntarily completed retaining work before maintenance handoff. B/C held Node subprocesses with 200ms SIGTERM cleanup. In the force-control runs, D started while the target plugin was disabled, then the plugin was enabled before A/B/C started; D genuinely retained no selected instance. Merely hiding a tool does not establish that control. The non-force baseline instead had four retaining turns.

Sources: baseline `659d1c5bb3513f51b5ec0981a06909ed27c6bc15`; initial repair `bac8e5ac1103360717da35e449a8400f5da6ffab`; final repair `18661f5b89b35983eac9aa61d2862c10b55e8e9c` (same tree as this publication's metadata commit). Native/Code Mode and healthy-rollback rows ran on the initial repair; those unchanged paths are reused. The committed-activation fence and missing-old-source correction were exercised on final runtime bytes. Recorded runtime file hashes matched their corresponding committed source.

The dummy replacement registered this fault only in its new version:

```ts
api.on("gateway_start", async () => {
  throw new Error("POST_PUBLICATION_PROOF_REFUSAL");
});
```

Actual commands:

```text
openclaw plugins reload reload-proof --wait --accept-capabilities --json
openclaw plugins reload reload-proof --force --wait --accept-capabilities --json
```

| Observation | Result |
|---|---|
| Published non-force baseline, 12-second bounded observation | `phase=reloading`; 12 retained work items; A/B/C remained on original active runs; no continuation. Explicit Stop cleaned up afterward. This is not an infinite-time claim. |
| Native actual force CLI | A/B/C each gained exactly one maintenance continuation in the same conversation; append once; B inputs FIFO 1 then 2; pending=0. D stayed on its original active run without handoff or cleanup. B/C cleanup preceded the first handoff by 936ms. |
| Code Mode → exec actual force CLI | Same once-only A/B/C continuation, append and FIFO assertions; D unchanged. B/C cleanup preceded the first handoff by 670ms. |
| Published committed-activation RED | CLI exit=1: activation failed, replacement applied. `ready=false`, `pluginReload.phase=failed`. Nevertheless one continuation ran and its model received the false `rolled back` hint. |
| Final committed-activation GREEN | Same CLI error and failed readiness. Original subprocess cleanup recorded; successor count=0; handoffs=0; pending=0. Exact unhealthy-runtime fence warning observed; delivery error=false. |
| Pre-publication service-start failure | CLI exit=1: replacement not applied. Old healthy runtime `ready=true`; one legitimate `rolled back` continuation completed. |
| Review-found missing-old-source edge | Moved only the owned dummy capture root. Final CLI succeeded with the explicit old-source-unavailable warning; `ready=true`; one continuation completed. The preliminary repair had incorrectly fenced this same successful operation. Old rollback availability is not new-runtime health. |

Selected sanitized terminal facts:

```text
baseline: Plugin replacement queued behind 12 retained work item(s)
fault: Plugin operation failed during activate: [hooks] gateway_start handler
       from reload-proof failed: POST_PUBLICATION_PROOF_REFUSAL
fault: Gateway generation 7: replacement applied. (final-source repeat)
RED:   ready=false; handoff=rolled back; continuationCount=1
GREEN: ready=false; handoffCount=0; continuationCount=0; pendingCount=0
GREEN: Plugin maintenance left the runtime unhealthy; successor admission remains closed.
physical check after normal-flow proofs:
  originalHoldersStillAlive=[]; reloadCliProcessesRemaining=0
```

The before-publication case uses a throwing service start, not the `gateway_start` fault. Ordinary Stop was used for cleanup after recording each result. All participants and outputs are synthetic. No tokens, keys, signed authentication payloads, environment dumps, private paths or conversation transcripts are included.

### Retained real authority proof

**Historical runs, not fresh execution of head `23d9323`.** The revoked-admin RED control used `70c7b1d8e1c1259d759dbe23c5a539c1af6eb20b`. The GREEN authority/Stop candidate was subsequently committed in `7119ca645381680cfc64fc50ab8c5e47fefdd31a` and published in the `659d1c5` lineage, before the health-only repairs above. Minor typing/lint-only edits followed these runtime observations; no byte-for-byte rerun of later heads is claimed.

Conditions: isolated TLS Gateway and deterministic local inference fixture, with real Gateway admission, tool execution and continuation machinery. Revocation/Stop cases used configured synthetic trusted-proxy identities: Alice/Bob connections had `operator.read`/`operator.write` scopes, not `operator.admin`; the supervisor had administration scope. Bob was a member, not the original initiator. The revocation case used an actual signed, paired administrator device and `device.token.revoke`. The separate allowed native CLI control used a valid local-owner credential. No real IdP or channel credentials were used.

| Authority case | Recorded outcome |
|---|---|
| Current administrator allowed | Supervisor force retired Alice's original RPC before either Stop request below. Separately, the actual native force/wait CLI interrupted its original tool and completed exactly one successor in the same conversation. |
| Administrator revoked during capture/grace | Revocation completed after capture. Original run stayed active; no interruption was observed; the same two physical process identities remained alive. |
| Foreign writable member | Member addition returned `ok:true`; Gateway sharing role was `member`. Bob's exact-original-run Stop returned `unauthorized`. Write/membership did not become initiator rights. |
| Original initiator after RPC retirement | Alice on another connection received `aborted:true` for the original run. After the driver released the physical holder and reload succeeded, no continuation appeared. |

Normalized recorded terminal/client facts (UTC; identifiers are replaced per case, not shared across cases):

```text
2026-11-05T14:34:12.616Z allowed CLI: original toolResult.isError=true; abort observed
2026-11-05T14:34:13.471Z allowed CLI: successor completed in same conversation
allowed CLI: original+successor run count=2; completed replies=1; active=[]; pending=0

2026-11-05T14:30:54.318Z capture-complete: original-requester count=1
2026-11-05T14:30:54.327Z administrator device revocation recorded
2026-11-05T14:30:54.328Z revoke response received; reload client closed (4001): device removed
revoked-admin: originalInterrupted=false; originalRunActive=true
revoked-admin: samePhysicalProcessesBeforeAfter=true; live process count=2
revoked-admin: physical-interruption log count=0

2026-11-05T14:31:34.169Z Alice physical plugin holder started
2026-11-05T14:31:35.145Z allowed supervisor force: original RPC retirement observed
retirement gate: original aborted tool result AND no active original run
bobStop={"error":"unauthorized"}
aliceStop.value={"ok":true,"aborted":true,"runIds":["run-A"]}
then: physical holder released; reload.value.ok=true
then: retired capture disposed after successful reload
after reload + observation: runs=["run-A"]; resumed=false; active=[]; pending.total=0
```

The retirement timestamp records the real Gateway-history predicate shown above, not a fabricated internal-memory inspection. The final Stop observation followed physical-holder release, successful reload and the script's observation interval; failed runtime health was not what suppressed this wakeup. The allowed CLI control also shows ordinary caller interruption did not itself revoke accepted maintenance authority.

Captured runtime file SHA-256s:

```text
plugin-maintenance-continuation.ts a1b0d2ee93d5c7d0225d9f00b3d5f7ee9e177a32a96da58245531de20fb87789
server-plugin-force-reload.ts      0a5a395588a37d26b3f770db77e8dc86f3a622d5815f86735ab36fc4f4f755c8
chat-abort-exact-run.ts            2e55899b06296e3d006fb31b1f99d8bbb44963e80a8b96c5cde70e61f370e521
```

Only authorization metadata, synthetic labels and outcome facts are reproduced—not tokens, keys, signatures, recovery scopes, authentication payloads, environment data, protected paths or private conversation content. These earlier observations cover unchanged authority paths; the health-repair executions above have separate source chronology.

### Validation and review

- Focused owner/consumer regressions, 13 native-continuation tests, 5 coordinator tests, 6 after-publication activation variants, 14 prefix-stability tests, core/affected test types, targeted lint, formatting and line-cap checks passed. Existing non-force and omitted-force protocol coverage remains applicable.
- Fresh independent full-source precommit review and the shared helper completed. Complete-context committed-range review found an additional successful-replacement edge; it was fixed and proven red/green before publication. Final renewed complete-context review reported no actionable P0–P2. Static review does not independently verify execution claims.
- The prior `659d1c5` CI gate passed its selected families. This publication's CI and the next ClawSweeper review are separate checks; no new-head CI-green claim is made here.
- Released-driver compatibility was attempted using published `openclaw@2026.11.1` and pinned candidate `23d9323c4c15427fb7899ab322f6c29f96040d25` (tree `56e6a2a5ad0c5204d14e633a6119adab5a4089b7`) in a rootless isolated container, but package acquisition failed before installation because the required managed proxy was unreachable from the container network. No upgrade or pre/post plugin compatibility cell completed; that repository-required proof remains unverified pending a supported container-to-proxy route. This is an environment prerequisite failure, not a product-test pass or failure. No UI changes, real channel credentials, shared Gateway operation, merge or deployment. No crash-survival guarantee.

Test budget: exact dedicated allocation of 907 test/support lines. The frozen health repair used 904; strengthening the review-found success case added exactly 3 more. The shared scalar is unchanged; no baseline padding or ignored failure was introduced.

prs.title: feat(memory): let workspaces exclude generated files from search
prs.body:
Related: #101422 Supersedes #177868 by @CheekyHobson: their reviewed head `a2008ab09`, ported onto current main with co-author credit on the commit, plus the proof ClawSweeper asked for. ## What Problem This Solves Generated dreaming reports under `memory/dreaming/` are indexed like curated notes and crowd them out of memory search, and there is no setting to exclude paths inside the default memory folders. ## User Impact User impact: operators can set `memory.search.excludePaths` (globally or per agent), for example `["memory/dreaming/**", "memory/.dreams/**"]`, to keep matching workspace files out of memory search and file watching. - Unset or empty changes nothing. The index scope hash is identical to the one 2026.11.1 writes, so this setting adds no rebuild on upgrade. - Setting or changing the list is a scope change, like changing `extraPaths`: `openclaw memory status` reports it, vector search pauses, and `openclaw memory index` rebuilds and drops the excluded rows. - Search only: excluded files are not deleted, `memory_get` can still read them, `memory forget` still scrubs them, and short-term recall/promotion eligibility is unchanged. ## Why This Change Was Made One workspace-relative glob check, next to the existing `extraPaths` glob matcher in the memory host SDK, is applied where search scope is decided: file discovery (local and remote workspace providers), watcher eligibility, and the index scope hash. Shared watchers include the exclusions in their selection keys, so agents with different exclusions on one workspace rebaseline when one joins or leaves (the P2 ClawSweeper found on #177868). Changes compared with #177868 at `a2008ab09`: - Rebased onto main: the scope hash goes through the single `resolveConfiguredMemoryScopeHash()` owner, and the matcher is exported from `plugin-sdk/memory-core-host-engine-fs`, the subpath #181891 narrowed the file worker to, instead of `engine-storage`. Both are private local-only subpaths, so this adds no third-party SDK contract. - The matcher lives in `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts` beside `matchesExtraMemoryPathEntry` instead of core `src/memory/root-memory-files.ts`. - Added the config field label, corrected the docs about the rebuild step, and linked the setting from the dreaming docs. - Tests: replaced the 13 s CLI e2e case with a manager test of about 4 s that mirrors two unforced `openclaw memory index` runs (the real CLI run is below). Dropped a test that indexed an excluded file through a private method, a `selectionKeys` shape test covered by the join/leave behavior test, a worker integration test that still passed with the P2 fix reverted, and (after ClawSweeper's review) a test that only checked the worker request shape. Size against main: production +67/-8 in 15 files; tests +148/-3; docs +15/-4; generated baselines +3/-3. (#177868 was +439/-18 in 33 files.) ### Maintainer decision needed #101422 asks for both search exclusion and recall/promotion eligibility control. This PR is the narrow first stage: search discovery, watching, and index scope only, with defaults and promotion safeguards unchanged. ClawSweeper's review of #177868 recommended approving that narrow search stage and leaving recall inclusion and diagnostics to follow-up work; the alternative is one combined search+recall include/exclude design. An operator on #101422 said the search-only step covers their need. Config surface: `pnpm config:docs:gen` raises the core count by 4 (2638 -> 2642 on main `4c6f043`) for `memory.search.excludePaths` and `agents.entries.*.memory.search.excludePaths`, each with its `.*` item path. That is the new setting itself. ## Evidence Real runs on head `6d9ace7` (on main `cd20cf7`), starting from the latest stable release, `openclaw@2026.11.1` from npm (npm 11.20 skipped the package's install scripts by default; the CLI ran without them). The branch CLI on `6d9ace7` reported `2026.10.10` because main had not bumped its version string yet. An earlier run from 2026.10.10 on `b607675` showed the same behavior. Synthetic workspace: 3 curated files (`MEMORY.md`, `memory/backups.md`, `memory/garden.md`) and 7 generated reports (5 light, 2 REM, one REM report containing only "No strong patterns surfaced."). Isolated `OPENCLAW_HOME` under `env -i`, Node 26.12.1, and a local OpenAI-compatible embeddings stub on 127.0.0.1 (deterministic vectors, no provider calls). **Upgrade from 2026.11.1 and existing data:** 2026.11.1 builds the index (10 files, 10 chunks). After this branch's `doctor --fix` (main's agent-database migrations since 2026.11.1, v27 -> v40), the existing index loads clean (`Dirty: no`) and returns the same results and scores as 2026.11.1, before any re-index. With `excludePaths` unset, `memory index` keeps the stored scope hash, the chunking version and every stored chunk row (same count and same fingerprint over `id`, `path`, `hash`). This PR adds no database schema or stored fields; the scope hash changes only when `excludePaths` is set. **Opting in:** setting `excludePaths` marks the index dirty with a scope change and pauses vector search until a rebuild, both shown in `memory status`. `memory index` then drops the 7 reports and keeps the 3 curated files; the curated note ranks first, and an edit refreshes it.
Terminal output (paths redacted to $OPENCLAW_HOME) ```text $ openclaw --version # npm openclaw@2026.11.1 OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (4ffdd20) $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 10 files indexed. $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.449 memory/backups.md:1-5 0.318 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-28.md:1-5 0.310 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-27.md:1-5 0.303 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-26.md:1-5 0.296 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-25.md:1-5 0.290 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-24.md:1-5 # stored index identity (2026.11.1): {"scopeHash":"e861c1d291b583b9f4bf96233b72b9e6984cc92320671a0805e1063946e4b1a1","chunkingVersion":6} # stored rows (2026.11.1): {"chunks":10,"chunkIdsSha256":"e538aca49c37a70e"} $ openclaw --version # this branch OpenClaw 2026.10.10 (6d9ace7) $ openclaw doctor --fix --non-interactive # main's state migrations since 2026.11.1 Upgraded agent database schema in $OPENCLAW_HOME/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite: v27 -> v40 $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 10/10 files · 10 chunks Dirty: no $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main # existing 2026.11.1 index, before any re-index 0.449 memory/backups.md:1-5 0.318 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-28.md:1-5 0.310 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-27.md:1-5 0.303 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-26.md:1-5 0.296 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-25.md:1-5 0.290 memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-24.md:1-5 $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 10 files indexed. # stored index identity (this branch, no excludePaths): {"scopeHash":"e861c1d291b583b9f4bf96233b72b9e6984cc92320671a0805e1063946e4b1a1","chunkingVersion":6} # stored rows (this branch, no excludePaths): {"chunks":10,"chunkIdsSha256":"e538aca49c37a70e"} $ openclaw config set memory.search.excludePaths '["memory/dreaming/**","memory/.dreams/**"]' --strict-json Updated memory.search.excludePaths. Restart the gateway to apply. $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 10/3 files · 10 chunks Dirty: yes Index identity: index scope changed (owner: configuration, code: scope) Vector search: paused until memory is rebuilt $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw memory status --agent main Indexed: 3/3 files · 3 chunks Dirty: no # indexed rows by path: {"path":"MEMORY.md","chunks":1} {"path":"memory/backups.md","chunks":1} {"path":"memory/garden.md","chunks":1} $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.422 memory/backups.md:1-5 The nightly backup runs at 02:30 and copies the photo archive to the NAS. # edit memory/backups.md: 02:30 -> 03:15 $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw memory search "when does the nightly backup run" --agent main 0.422 memory/backups.md:1-5 The nightly backup runs at 03:15 and copies the photo archive to the NAS. ```
**Gateway watcher:** a throwaway loopback Gateway with `excludePaths` set. One agent turn opens the Gateway's default memory manager and its watcher: a local chat-completions stub calls `memory_search` once, through `dispatch_action`, because current main keeps `memory_search` behind Tool Search for this model. Then, with no further CLI calls, a new dreaming report is written and the curated note edited: the watcher refreshes the note within about 2 s and never indexes the report.
Terminal output ```text $ openclaw memory index --agent main Memory index updated (main): 3 files indexed. $ openclaw gateway run --bind loopback ... # throwaway Gateway [gateway] ready $ openclaw agent --agent main --message "When does the nightly backup run?" # stub model calls memory_search once via dispatch_action Done. tool call: dispatch_action {"id":"memory_search","args":{"query":"nightly backup"}} # memory_search result paths (from the stub log): memory/backups.md # indexed memory/ rows before edits: {"path":"memory/backups.md","text":"# Backups The nightly backup runs at 02:30 and copies the p"} {"path":"memory/garden.md","text":"# Garden Water the tomatoes every second evening in summer."} # wrote memory/dreaming/light/2026-10-29.md and edited memory/backups.md (02:30 -> 04:45); no CLI calls from here # after the Gateway watcher sync (~2s), plus 5s more: {"path":"memory/backups.md","text":"# Backups The nightly backup runs at 04:45 and copies the p"} {"path":"memory/garden.md","text":"# Garden Water the tomatoes every second evening in summer."} # dreaming rows: {"dreamingRows":0} ```
**Regressions fail without the fix:** - `file-watcher.lifecycle.test.ts` "rebaselines shared exclusions when a differently scoped agent joins and leaves" fails with `excludePaths` removed from `selectionKeys` ("expected setScopes to be called once, but got 0 times"). - `manager-workspace-files.test.ts` "drops generated Dream reports once excluded and keeps curated edits fresh" fails when the config resolver drops `excludePaths` (the report is still found). **Changed test files** (`pnpm test --maxWorkers=1` on `685db0c`, same test code as `8eb4b7b`, where they pass again; CI seconds to follow): | File | Result | Wall | Vitest duration | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `file-watcher.lifecycle.test.ts` | 29 passed | 48s | 41.65s | | `manager-reindex-state.test.ts` | 49 passed | 40s | 36.19s | | `manager-workspace-files.test.ts` | 11 passed | 71s | 64.91s | | `watch-policy.test.ts` | 6 passed | 47s | 41.51s | | `internal.test.ts` | 43 passed | 4s | 749ms | | `memory-search.test.ts` | 39 passed | 46s | 42.06s | Vitest time is mostly cold transform; the new manager case takes about 4 s and the other new cases take 1-24 ms. **Checks:** `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main` on `83eb31b` (main `200afde`, same code) passes typecheck (core, core tests, extensions, extension tests), lint, format, config docs baseline, Plugin SDK package exports, plugin boundaries and the other changed-file guards. Three lanes fail outside this PR: wrapper shadowing (`buildSkillWorkshopPromptSection`) and the public Plugin SDK surface budget (`agent-harness-runtime`) fail identically on clean main `200afde`, and the dead-export scan lists only auto-reply, gateway and UI exports this PR does not touch. The `pnpm check:docs` content checks pass. Test lines grow by a net +145, covered by `config/test-lines-allocations/memory-search-exclude-paths-188294.txt`: default scope-hash compatibility, the shared-watcher rebaseline, discovery and glob matching, and the exclusion rebuild. **PR CI:** earlier runs had failures inherited from main: `read-file.test.ts` after the fs-safe 0.26.14 bump (#188352) and `archive-restore.postgres.test.ts` from #155538, both fixed on main (#188531, `34a4e118dc1`), then `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` while main was over its test-line ceiling (main's own scheduled job logged the same overage with net delta 0). #188780 restored the headroom. The branch now merges main `4c6f043` at `fc34fcd`; earlier merges conflicted only on the generated config baseline, which was regenerated each time, and the PR diff is unchanged. The v2026.11.1 proof above ran on `6d9ace7`; the merge after it brought in main's changes and the regenerated baseline. Main's #139230 reworked dirty-index maintenance and the watcher's background sync in `manager-watch-ops.ts`, which this PR also edits; the merge keeps this PR's one `excludePaths` line there, and `file-watcher.lifecycle.test.ts`, `watch-policy.test.ts` and `manager.watcher-config.test.ts` pass on `fc34fcd`. Main's #191749 bounded the realpath deduplication at the end of `listMemoryFiles`; it merges cleanly because `excludePaths` filters files as they are collected, before that step. Main's #192488 moved the search manager types into `search-manager.types.ts`; this PR does not import them. Main's #193952 added provider name and icon help to `schema.help.models.ts`, which this PR also edits; both sets of entries merge cleanly. On `1cc43f3`, `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` (and so `ci-gate`) failed because main `bf10667` was over its own test-line ceiling by 137 lines; main's own scheduled job logged the same overage and passed only because that run added no test lines. Main `d1ffc39` got back under the ceiling, and the ratchet passes locally on `fc34fcd` (6,556,537 test lines, ceiling 6,556,548, with this PR's +145 lines covered by its 145-line allocation). On `df4f9e6`, `check-prompt-snapshots` failed on three JSON prompt snapshots this PR does not touch: main's #192596 stopped formatting JSON snapshots without regenerating the committed ones (the content was identical, only the layout differed). Main fixed it in #192628, `5d93337` merged that fix, and `prompt:snapshots:check` passes locally on `fc34fcd`. On `0a3aa17`, 19 CI jobs failed in setup before running any check because downloading the pinned Bun runtime from the `openclaw/bun` release returned HTTP 504; `pnpm test:ci-failed 188294` found no test failures, and CI on `5858e44` passed. `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions` and `config:docs:check` pass, and the touched tests plus `memory-files-worker.test.ts`, `workspace-memory-client.test.ts` and `manager-search-orchestration.test.ts` (files main also changed) pass. `checks-node-changed` on `a63b2b5` failed in `plugin-sdk-package-contract-guardrails.test.ts` after main's #188833 referenced an untyped SDK entrypoint in a guide; main fixed it in #188937, and that test passes locally on `fc34fcd`. On `5a03cd1`, `checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-3` (and so `ci-gate`) failed in `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-publication-admission.test.ts` because main's #189247 changed seal-less agent-database opens while that memory-core test still expected the synchronous integrity check; it failed the same way on main `f8e492f` without this PR. Main fixed the test in #189449, and it passes locally on `fc34fcd`. On `3bb1a2e`, `check-lint-core-5` failed on two `typescript(no-unnecessary-type-arguments)` errors in `src/skills/workshop/experience-review.test.ts` (lines 167-168, `createDeferred()`), which main's #190158 (`22c1060`) added; this PR does not touch that file. Main's push CI skips the full core lint stripes, so main did not flag it. Main removed the type arguments in #190292; `8866f78` merged that fix and its CI, including `check-lint-core-5` and `ci-gate`, passed. **Local review:** autoreview, Codex `gpt-6.1-sol`, branch mode against `upstream/main`, P0–P2: scoped-clean, "patch is correct" (0.87). It ran on `685db0c`, before the rebases onto `200afde` and `f980e01`, which changed only the base and the generated baseline files. Not covered: Windows paths (the matcher normalizes `path.sep`) and a live remote node workspace (the harness test checks that list and watch requests carry `excludePaths`).

prs.title: feat(ios): reconcile unread app-icon badges (WIP)
prs.body:
Related: #191489

## What Problem This Solves

iOS users have no app-icon unread reminder after dismissing a notification. **This is an explicitly partial/WIP draft, not a completed fix for #191489.**

## User Impact

This slice implements app-applied unread-session badge reconciliation on foreground, authenticated reconnect, session invalidations, accepted session mutations, and existing background wakes. It counts authorized unread conversations across agents, including manual unread, independently of sidebar pagination. Archived and execution-only subagent sessions are excluded; user-openable child conversations remain eligible.

**Automatic assistant-activity APNs wakes are still missing.** A disconnected phone is not yet woken by a newly completed assistant response. The accepted delivery limitation also remains: if iOS does not execute the app, its badge cannot update. Native compilation, simulator/device behavior, and real APNs acceptance are not verified.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Reuse `deriveSessionUnread` through an optional `sessions.list` `unreadOnly` filter and existing exact `totalCount`; no separate unread-message counter or new unread store.
- Keep the badge a replaceable, authenticated current-scope projection. Account/route changes invalidate pending reads; privacy resets do not mark sessions read.
- Serialize OS badge setters separately from network reads so a privacy reset need not wait for an offline request. Keep APNs payloads badge-free: custom scope/revision fields cannot stop iOS from applying delayed `aps.badge` values.
- Keep `push.test` a transport diagnostic. No durable registration or permission changes are included.

### Maintainer design acceptance needed for the remaining wake path

Native APNs registrations currently contain node/transport identity, but no durable authenticated operator-profile binding. Pairing scopes alone cannot select disconnected recipients without risking an unrelated-profile activity broadcast. The existing web-push recipient-authority path has a profile binding; native registrations do not.

Proposed next step: extend the **existing APNs registration owner** with a binding established only from the authenticated operator/device, revalidate current pairing/profile/role/session visibility at the actual send boundary, and clear or replace the binding on unregister, unpair, or identity replacement. Then wire real assistant activity into an authorized badge-free invalidation/wake path. Do not broadcast to all registered iPhones or infer a profile from a display name.

This durable-data/authority-lifecycle design still needs recorded maintainer acceptance under the [storage-change checkpoint](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/844d0222bd65e979eea562a3973ee8f83e90e26e/docs/reference/database-schemas/storage-changes.md#review-checkpoint-for-material-changes). This draft is the discussion and review checkpoint; it does not claim that acceptance has been granted.

## Evidence

Current published head: `75543e5e0e96265179d6da487b52d9402ffd24ac`; reviewed tree: `f9a10df3bfd3b139750c5a6e00e92975e5d25b5e`. The published tree matches the reviewed local candidate exactly. The exact PR merge base is `844d0222bd65e979eea562a3973ee8f83e90e26e`, confirmed by GitHub comparison. The target-main SHA / prior hosted-review base `c230ae5c3c4643476e5a6eddc3120260d043a86e` is distinct; it was not silently substituted for the local review base.

### Simplification and ownership

Applied **pr-simplify → cross-layer-pr-regression-review → Auto Review**. Scope stays with the existing authenticated operator connection and its authority generation. Removed the duplicate badge scope/route caches, gateway-identity and reaction-identity lookups, repeated cleanup/guard branches, and the private count-only response decoder. The canonical session-list response decoder is reused.

The small badge helper remains because it coalesces reads and serializes OS writes separately: a privacy reset must not wait for an offline network read, and an already-started OS setter must settle before the reset. Accepted-read transport invalidation and the existing foreground/reconnect/background hooks remain; no server-side unread counter or new registration state was introduced.

Compared with the full pre-simplification local candidate (tree `a0d763184e47f09d31f2cdbb669b75476ddb30bf`, including the retained roster test follow-up), production code is **59 lines smaller** and native tests are **one line smaller**, with an OS-setter failure case added. This is separate from the entire PR against its merge base: **381 added / 6 removed lines** across ten files. Excluding generated data/docs/allocation, production is +170/−4 lines and tests are +181/−0 lines. The necessary remaining growth implements the new query, native projection, and distinct boundary regressions.

### Executed checks and review

- The new real `sessions.list` handler regression was **red before implementation and green after canonical filtering and validator regeneration**. The retained follow-up also interleaves normal/unread queries and covers both ordinary and serialized/retained selection; canonical read/activity changes update totals without pagination or visibility leakage. This is Gateway boundary proof, not an icon demonstration.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.unread-count.test.ts src/gateway/session-utils.filters.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/index.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — **41 tests passed** across three files; 21.42 seconds total command time in the retained terminal-success log. The Gateway restarted after the run; its process exit receipt was lost, so no separate exit-code receipt is claimed for that run. CI seconds remain unavailable.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` — exit 0.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --type-aware packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/sessions-list.ts src/gateway/session-list-filters.ts src/gateway/server.sessions.unread-count.test.ts` — exit 0, three files clean.
- `pnpm gateway:validators:check`, `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base 844d0222bd65e979eea562a3973ee8f83e90e26e --staged`, and whitespace checks — exit 0. Targeted TypeScript/docs formatting is unchanged and passing. The isolated 93-line allocation covers the RPC regression; the shared baseline is unchanged.
- Read-only cross-layer review of the frozen candidate: no P0/P1 findings in the implemented Gateway → protocol → transport → connection lifecycle → OS-write path. Native execution gaps are retained below.
- Fresh independent **Auto Review**, local mode against the exact merge base, through P3: **scoped-clean**, exit 0, no findings across the complete simplified candidate. This is source review of the partial slice, not native compilation or completion of the original feature.

The [previous hosted ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193491#issuecomment-6659144709) reported zero actionable findings / `needs-human` for **old head `b925619e2bf9ade5186833d1c8162b0755395d94`**. It does not attest this new head. No duplicate hosted re-review was requested for this cleanup. At new-head verification, 30 attached CI checks were skipped; skipped checks are not passing build/test proof.

The broader prior `pnpm lint` invocation expanded beyond the requested files and failed six existing `max-lines` checks in untouched files: `extensions/anthropic/cli.runtime.ts`, `extensions/crabbox/src/crabbox-worker-node-enrollment.test.ts`, `extensions/oc-path/src/cli.test.ts`, `extensions/tlon/src/monitor/index.test.ts`, `src/agents/plugin-model-catalog.ts`, and `src/infra/sqlite-readonly-location.ts`. No lint exceptions were added; the bounded changed-file check passed.
