## What Problem This Solves

Personal skill imports require manual downloads and uploads even when a skill and its companion files already have an HTTPS source.

## User Impact

Import an HTTPS `SKILL.md` or archive bundle through **Plugins → Skills → My skills → Import skill**. Recognized GitHub, GitLab, and Gitea/Forgejo folder-link shapes are normalized without a browser hostname allowlist. Companion files, nested relative paths, and binary files use the existing bundle representation. File, folder, ZIP, and ClawHub imports remain available.

Operators can permit private-network downloads with `skills.library.import.allowedOrigins`: exact HTTPS scheme/host/port entries, absent or empty by default. Grants apply to everyone already authorized to import. An explicitly approved loopback-literal origin retains the shared guard's exception; metadata/link-local destinations and unrelated private origins remain protected. This grants network access, not repository authentication: the Gateway still needs corporate DNS/VPN and TLS trust, and browser login cookies or publishing credentials are not forwarded.

Repository archives must fit the existing download/extraction limits before directory selection, so a small skill inside a large repository can fail. Use a smaller direct bundle URL and selected directory in that case. Unknown forge webpages need the explicit archive fallback; ambiguous refs can use the ref/directory overrides.

## Why This Change Was Made

The replacement is a source adapter into the existing guarded HTTP, safe extraction, canonical bundle, scanning, install-policy, and personal-save owners—not a separate installer. The same import RPC gains a closed URL source alternative. Remote files/archives retain truthful third-party, mutable, network source facts rather than being classified as user-authored local files. Current write authority and private-origin grants are checked across awaited work.

The GitHub-only repository importer, chooser, and superseded policy/test plumbing are retired. There is no Git clone/sparse-checkout system, browser host-list expansion, or fetched-script execution. Canonical validator regeneration causes large numbering changes, but independent normalization isolated the semantic change to the import-parameter predicate.

## Evidence

**The complete candidate authority case passed in real CI. The required stable-upgrade case is still blocked; overall CI is partial/failed—not merge-ready.**

The [exact-head run 42318674850](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42318674850) tested head `4d595fe1b42a39c095203072d3a775432ebe7260`, tree `f7f608e7747663469ee5e76ac611b100e23b908a`; expected, observed and build commits match. Sanitized artifact `13551964748` contains only `report.json`, `imported-skill.png` and `companion-detail.png`. Its ZIP SHA-256 was verified as `13cb6b7dc0a3f54923d4c920416a9aa373d9044cf855eb34414094ee86735e62`.

Actual report: `status: partial`, `authorityStatus: passed`, `upgradeStatus: failed`. All nine authority assertions passed:
- Owned HTTPS source and alternate-host reachability.
- Strict private-network default and read-only access reject before any source request.
- Browser → authenticated Gateway → HTTPS → real policy/extraction → SQLite publication, with correct personal ownership and exact nested/text/binary/executable companion bytes.
- Exact-origin and redirect boundaries issue no next request to an ungranted target.
- Real install-policy denial creates no publication.
- Live role revocation during a held redirect: one initial request, zero next requests, no publication.
- Live role revocation during held publication: committed role change causes the exact canonical post-HELLO connection retirement; settled staging/immutable artifact and library-entry counts remain unchanged. Reconnection through the same profile, requesting the original full scopes, receives a genuine correlated server rejection for a fresh import and makes zero outbound requests. A generic close is not counted as an RPC denial.
- Live origin-grant revocation: effective config version changes while the same authenticated connection stays alive; the held request cannot follow the redirect or publish. One initial request, zero next requests; `connectionStable: true`.

The independent enabled watchOS/direct-node TLS consumer also passed both tests on this head. The proof file ran both required cases: candidate authority passed; stable preparation failed. No skip or continue-on-error masks the failure.

**Remaining required proof:** latest-stable settings/skills/two-revision upgrade survival has not run. prs.title: fix(discord): DM sends to bare usernames ending in digits fail as unknown channel
prs.body:
Closes #193478

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: sending a Discord DM to a bare username that ends in digits (e.g. `jane99`, `bob2k`, `alice_2023`) fails because the username is misrouted as a channel and the directory lookup that resolves usernames to user IDs is never attempted.

## User Impact

User impact: users can now send DMs by bare username even when the username ends in digits, matching the documented behavior for usernames without trailing digits (`jane` already worked). The fix is a one-character-class change; there is no breaking change and no new configuration.

## Why This Change Was Made

In `extensions/discord/src/target-resolver.ts` the username heuristic is:

```ts
const likelyUsername = !/^(user:|channel:|discord:|@|<@!?)|[\d]+$/.test(trimmed);
```

The `^` anchor only binds to the first alternative group, so the second alternative `[\d]+$` matches any string that merely *ends* in a digit. `test("jane99")` returns `true`, `likelyUsername` becomes `false`, and `resolveDiscordTarget("jane99", ...)` returns `{ kind: "channel", id: "jane99" }` without querying the directory.

The intent (see the doc comment on `resolveDiscordTarget`) is to exclude all-numeric IDs from the username lookup; that requires a full-string anchor `^\d+$`. This change aligns digit-suffixed usernames with the existing behavior of every other username (directory lookup first, channel fallback on miss), so digit-suffixed channel names like `general2` behave exactly like `general` already does today.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof (shipped outbound path, before/after)

Ran the shipped Discord plugin outbound path end to end — the real `sendMessageDiscord` → `parseAndResolveDiscordTarget` → directory lookup → DM channel creation → message POST — through the real `RequestClient` over real HTTP to a simulated Discord REST endpoint (the plugin's supported `DISCORD_API_URL` loopback override). The only faked dependency is Discord itself.

Environment: Windows 11, Node 24.16.0, tsx loader (`node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs`), repo main + this patch. Command: `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs proof-discord-username.mts` with a mock Discord REST server on `127.0.0.1` that returns guild `111` and a member `jane99 → user 999`.

**Before this patch** (pre-fix regex) — `jane99` is treated as a channel; the directory is never queried and no DM is created:

```text
=== REST requests the (simulated) Discord endpoint received ===
GET /api/v10/channels/jane99
POST /api/v10/channels/jane99/messages body={"content":"hello from proof","flags":4,...}
=== Proof summary ===
directory member search for "jane99": NO
DM channel created for recipient 999: NO
DM message delivered to recipient 999: NO
```

**After this patch** — `jane99` is looked up in the directory, resolved to user 999, and the DM is created and delivered:

```text
=== REST requests the (simulated) Discord endpoint received ===
GET /api/v10/users/@me/guilds
GET /api/v10/guilds/111/members/search?query=jane99&limit=1
POST /api/v10/users/@me/channels body={"recipient_id":"999"}
GET /api/v10/channels/dm-555
POST /api/v10/channels/dm-555/messages body={"content":"hello from proof","flags":4,...}
=== Proof summary ===
directory member search for "jane99": YES
DM channel created for recipient 999: YES
DM message delivered to recipient 999: YES
```

### Regression test, red on the old code then green

`extensions/discord/src/targets.test.ts`, new case `resolves a bare username ending in digits through the directory lookup`:

```text
× expected { kind: 'channel', id: 'jane99', …(2) } to match object { kind: 'user', id: '999', …(1) }   (red)
✓ resolves a bare username ending in digits through the directory lookup                              (green)
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  9 passed (9)
```

### Affected consumer suites green

`send.sends-basic-channel-messages`, `send.message-request`, `send.messages`, `send.permissions.authz`, `resolve-users`, `resolve-channels`:

```text
Test Files  6 passed (6)
     Tests  95 passed (95)
```

### Checks

- CI: `checks-node-changed` (incl. extension lanes), lint, boundaries, contracts, baseline ratchets, dependency review — all green on the reviewed head.
- Format (`run-format --check`) and `oxlint` clean on both changed files.
- `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` passes (slack 17).

## Root Cause

`resolveDiscordTarget` classifies a target as a "likely username" only when it has no known prefix and is not a bare numeric ID. The digit test `[\d]+$` is unanchored at the start, so it also classifies any string *ending* in a digit as non-username. The directory lookup — the only path that turns a bare username into a `user:<id>` target — is gated behind `shouldLookup`, which is `false` for those inputs. The result is a channel target that the Discord REST call rejects.

## Regression Test Plan

Coverage level: **unit** (owning boundary).

- Target file: `extensions/discord/src/targets.test.ts` — new case `resolves a bare username ending in digits through the directory lookup`, which mocks `listDiscordDirectoryPeersLive` and asserts `resolveDiscordTarget("jane99")` returns the user target and that the lookup was called with `query: "jane99"`.
- Why this is the minimal reliable guardrail: the resolution heuristic is a pure function of `trimmed` plus the directory result; this single case pins the exact regressed input class (bare username ending in digits) and fails red on the old regex while the existing cases (all-numeric IDs, explicit `user:`/`channel:` prefixes, non-digit usernames) keep it from over-rotating the heuristic.

## Scope Boundary

Only `extensions/discord/src/target-resolver.ts` (one regex) and its regression test were changed. No other channel, no shared/plugin-sdk surface, no gateway/core code. The `@username` prefixed lookup path (which sends the raw `@` as the directory query) and the voice/DM delivery layers were not modified.

## AI Assistance

This change was authored with AI assistance and is tested at the boundary unit level plus the affected consumer suites and the real-HTTP shipped-outbound-path proof above. What was **not** tested: a live Discord bot account / real Discord API (the external endpoint was simulated via the supported loopback override), and full CI extension matrix (covered by PR CI).

prs.title: fix(codex): redact credentials in dynamic tool error content
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Thrown and failed Codex dynamic-tool paths were putting raw `errorMessage` / failure `message` text into `contentItems` without running it through `sanitizeToolResult`. Successful and middleware-adjusted result paths already redacted credentials, so a thrown tool error that embedded a bearer token (or similar secret) could still surface the credential in the app-server tool-result content.

**Configuration-dependent gap:** `formatToolExecutionErrorMessage` → `redactSensitiveText` uses configured `logging.redactPatterns` **in place of** defaults. Model-visible `sanitizeToolResult` / `redactModelVisibleToolPayloadText` **combines** custom patterns with built-in tool payload patterns. So under a nonmatching custom `redactPatterns` config, diagnostic/error formatting alone still leaks an unregistered synthetic bearer, while catch-path `sanitizeToolResult` keeps built-in bearer protection.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the shared `sanitizeToolResult` helper from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime` on the two remaining failure content builders:

- `createCodexDynamicToolBridge` catch path in `dynamic-tools.ts` (thrown execution errors)
- `createFailedDynamicToolResponse` in `dynamic-tool-response-state.ts` (failed response factory)

Non-goals: no change to success-path redaction, budget truncation, or middleware ordering.

## User Impact

**Before:** A dynamic tool that threw (or failed via the shared failed-response helper) could return `contentItems` containing unsanitized credentials from the error text — especially when `logging.redactPatterns` replaced diagnostic defaults with patterns that do not cover bearer tokens.

**After:** Thrown/failed dynamic-tool error content is redacted with the same `sanitizeToolResult` used on successful result content (built-ins always apply for model-visible output).

## Evidence

- Production catch path: `extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tools.ts` now sets `text: sanitizeToolResult(errorMessage)`.

Mock restored in `finally`.
- Diagnostic harness: `scripts/codex-dynamic-tool-error-redact-proof.mts` prints the actual protocol response JSON.





### Custom-pattern regression (exact head `67505f4ca5c4`)

- **Canonical reachability path:** `createCodexDynamicToolBridge` → tool `execute` throws → `formatToolExecutionErrorMessage` → catch builds `contentItems` with `sanitizeToolResult(errorMessage)` → `toCodexDynamicToolProtocolResponse`.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
$ node --import tsx scripts/codex-dynamic-tool-error-redact-proof.mts
# writes /workspace/codex-runtime-proof.txt
```

- **Evidence after fix (diagnostic transcript):**

```text

# Generated: 2026-09-07T14:53:48.289Z (UTC)

#               → toCodexDynamicToolProtocolResponse (JSON contentItems)
# Live Codex binary: NOT used (unavailable / not required for this harness)

logging.redactPatterns = ["\\bunrelated-only-[A-Za-z0-9]+\\b"]
(nonmatching custom patterns replace diagnostic defaults;

## Before catch-path sanitizeToolResult
formatToolExecutionErrorMessage(...) under custom redactPatterns:
{
  "formatted": "Upstream failed: Authorization: Bearer bearer-model-visible-credential-1234567890"
}
contains synthetic credential: true

## After fix: protocol response returned toward Codex app-server

{
  "contentItems": [
    {
      "type": "inputText",
      "text": "Upstream failed: Authorization: Bearer bearer…7890"

success: false

## Summary
- Under custom nonmatching redactPatterns, diagnostic formatting LEAKS the synthetic bearer.

- This records the actual protocol response object, not Vitest expect() output.
```

prs.title: test(gateway): channel account routes keep serving after another plugin's config reload
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A channel account that serves inbound traffic over HTTP must keep its route when a different plugin's config is edited and the Gateway hot-reloads. Nothing tested that path end to end on a real Gateway. If it regresses, the account still reports as running, but its route returns 404 until a restart.

## User Impact

There is no user-visible change; this adds a test only. It protects channels that register an HTTP route when an account starts, such as webhook-style inbound routes.

## Why This Change Was Made

On reload, a retained plugin's routes are projected into the new registry. Today only unit tests in `src/gateway/server/plugins-http.ownership.test.ts` cover that projection. The real-Gateway channel lifecycle tests reload the route's own plugin, not an unrelated one.

The new test follows the existing `server-plugins.lifecycle.*` fixtures and helpers. It starts a channel account that registers a prefix route at `startAccount`. It then hot-reloads another plugin's config three times with `config.patch`. After each reload it checks four things:
- the other plugin really re-registered, with a new instance and a new active registry;
- the account's route still answers 200 from the current registry;
- the route set is unchanged;
- the account was started only once.

Finally, stopping the account still removes the route (404).

## Evidence

- `pnpm test src/gateway/server-plugins.lifecycle.channel-routes.test.ts` on current `main`: 1 passed (gateway-server project).
- **Mutation check.** The mutation removes the `target.httpRoutes.push(...)` line from `projectPluginHttpRoutes` in `src/plugins/http-route-owner.ts`.
  - The new test fails at the first reload: `status: 404`, expected 200.
  - Under the same mutation, `server-plugins.lifecycle.channels.test.ts` still passes 3/3 and `plugins-http.ownership.test.ts` fails 3/8.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the file: clean.
- `tsgo -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.gateway-server.json`: clean. A type error injected into the file makes it fail, so the file is in that project.
- `check:max-lines-ratchet`, `check:line-cap-ratchet`, `check:assertion-safety` and `check:database-worker-ratchet`, run against the parent commit: OK.

prs.title: fix(control-ui): avoid warm chat reload backtracking
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in warm reload of an active chat follows provisional appended-row heights, then moves backward when measured rows replace the estimates. A later tool completion repeats the correction. Campaign observations recorded repeated corrections over roughly 500 ms and CLS 0.11–0.12 on a signed-in active-chat reload.

On the active-chat fixture, retained-row movement is **278 → 202 px** and backtracking **76 → 0 px in 11/11 pairs**, confirmed by a planned second 11/11 block. History replacement followed by tool completion is **346 → 202 px**, with backtracking **144 → 0 px in 11/11**. Both reader variants have **0 px movement/excursion and no missing anchor frames in all 11 pairs**. End followers finish exactly at the end; the retained long reply stays 3706.65625 px high throughout the sampled active runs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Automatic end follow chooses its destination from the existing native measurement batch after mounted destination rows and virtual sizes agree. It removes the competing synchronous warm measurement pass. The measured window covers the full destination viewport, including multiple appended turns.

Warm reader restoration joins that batch. Real older-prefix insertion retains the existing synchronous before-paint anchor contract; deferring that boundary regressed continuous native reading. Arrival retires the scroll command through its existing owner. Retargeting also retains an already-issued smooth destination while preparing its measured replacement, so continuing native motion is not mistaken for reader input.

No store, configuration, protocol field, database or cache shape is introduced. Runtime growth above the earlier ~25-line candidate preserves those observed prefix/window/native-motion contracts, within the lane’s ~60-line ceiling.

## User Impact

Unchanged cached rows retain their height. Readers keep their anchored row fixed through live replacement. End followers move forward once for appended turns and once for actual tool completion, without reversing. A small tool-completion CLS remains; its painted source is documented below.

**Documented lead exception:** visible movement is the campaign’s primary harm. The lead accepted backtracking **76 → 0 px and two-round 144 → 0 px in 11/11**, with the painted reader excursion fixed, despite the historical cost of **+34 ms total blocking, +19 ms blocking and +21 ms forced style/layout in the 700–1300 ms replacement window, and +7 ms final rows**. The lead determined that this cost delays no visible content and accepted it under the same precedent as #190925. **This is an explicit lead exception, not a passing blocking secondary.** The new final-head measurements are reported separately; the exception does not silently waive a newly discovered cost.

## Evidence

**Candidate `1908fb8bd1fb5999d57f5c5edbea55d8aeee8058` on main `36a1c58e91dd9ae991edd76f9ccbfdcd056c5fa0`. Ready for lead review; do not merge.** All **158 focused checks pass**, production UI build succeeds, and exact-head [CI 42310136781](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42310136781) is **green**. The full UI suite is complete, with every red classified against pinned main. All 25 reviewed source files stayed identical through the required final fetch/rebase; the six transcript owners remain byte-identical to qualified `ab4ebed`.

**No cap changed.** All earlier L285 cap-only commits, including the later conditional raise, are removed. The entire performance-budget file, every pre-existing comment and all other caps/startup baseline included, matches pinned main byte-for-byte. Final [CI performance job 128210032762](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42310136781/job/128210032762) reports **`chat boot JS gzip vs base: 1288104 B -> 1288765 B (+661 B); requests 20 -> 20`**. Main's unchanged **1,289,030 B** Chat cap leaves **265 B headroom**; cap delta **0 B**.

The exact test allocation is **278 = 273 net regression-test LF +5 LF lead-approved inherited debt**, an exact **+19 LF** from this lane's original 259 record (14 new checker-boundary regression LF +5 base overage). Main is **6,555,799 LF / ceiling 6,555,794**; candidate is **6,556,072 LF / ceiling 6,556,072**, zero slack. Shared scalar, other owners' grants and tests are unchanged.

The **+3 LOC checker-owner correction** is necessary for that approved exact grant: the old credit<=own-growth guard rejects 278 for 273. The owner now permits net growth plus inherited base debt, floored at zero, while rejecting excess credit (including negative growth), overlapping/folded grants and unreconciled debt. The three parameterized real-Git cases fail on old code; all 14 owner cases pass with the correction. Canonical guidance requires explicit approval for above-own-growth reconciliation; there is no per-PR bypass or configuration option.

#194283 and #194284 are on this base; no Deep Research source belongs to this PR. Final-diff autoreview is **clean through P2**. The lead cost exception, CLS attribution, 132 pair tables and inspected synthetic strips below are unchanged. No new timing matrix is required under the explicit lead carry-over decision.

**Lead-approved carry-over:** The six transcript runtime files are byte-identical to the qualified prior head `ab4ebed`. The lead accepted the prior-head **132 pairs** because the main changes from `28d7bb6` to then-current main `d4ae77e` touched no transcript geometry: #194017 (sidebar rows), #193996 (provider failure text), #194008/#194068 (copy-button locale), #194118 (Models page), #194113 (plugin bindings). The lead explicitly requires **no new timing matrix**. The required rebases through current pinned main `36a1c58e91dd` still leave all six owned runtime files byte-identical to `ab4ebed`. The comparisons and timing tables below retain their original candidate/base labels.

Qualified comparison candidate `ab4ebedafa692b0e07315c7b74e5422074cebd85`; pinned main `28d7bb63a53ebf5b6e51a2e1b1592a87361c7f58`. All comparisons ran unprofiled on one quiet AWS **c7a.4xlarge**, lease `cbx_e6ce46b8e043` (observed 16 CPUs/~31 GiB RAM), repository Playwright Chromium, Team-scale fixture and `live-fast` latency. Both immediate CPU preflight samples were 100% idle. No diagnostic jobs or transfers ran during comparisons.

[Performance/native/full UI run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_37d13e3ca1d2c91ef1f3f27a5f45d0b5). All **132 interleaved pair deltas** are below: the required 88 plus dashboard A/A/repeat and a planned end-follow A/A/repeat. RPC count and payload deltas are zero in every pair. A/A preserves the baseline backtracking, while each candidate end block removes it in all 11 pairs.

Qualified-head paired medians, candidate − control:

| Scenario | Total blocking Δ | 700–1300 ms blocking Δ | Window forced style/layout Δ | Final rows DOM Δ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| One-round end | −11 ms | 0 ms | −8 ms | −2.8 ms |
| One-round end repeat | −20 ms | −10 ms | +9 ms | +16.7 ms |
| Two-round end | +4 ms | −2 ms | −1 ms | +3 ms |
| One-round reader | −20 ms | −10 ms | −28 ms | +11.2 ms |
| Two-round reader | −12 ms | −11 ms | +3 ms | −22.3 ms |

The end-repeat +16.7 ms final-row median has 7/11 worse pairs and overlapping IQRs; the reader +11.2 ms has 6/11 and overlap. These mixed signs remain visible. No block establishes an adverse hello-handled, FCP or first-painted-row result. The accepted blocking exception remains explicit.

Dashboard total blocking is −3 / −4 ms in its two candidate blocks; window forced style/layout is +6 / 0 ms, with mixed signs and overlapping IQRs. Its repeat has **+87.9 ms final rows DOM, 8/11 worse, overlapping IQRs**; the first block is −28.8 ms and A/A −12 ms, each 5/11 worse. This is inconclusive under the standing regression rule, not evidence of a consistent delay. Archived-chat results and every raw secondary/control remain in the tables.

### Reproduce the primary

Build pinned-main and candidate UI bundles, then run the committed shared fixture/probe:

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/bench-control-ui-cold-load.ts \
  --gateway-http --warm-reload --untraced --face chat \
  --pane-chrome-facts --details-session-facts --latency-profile live-fast \
  --capture-ms 3500 --runs 22 --transcript-witness \
  --active-transcript --active-transcript-two-round \
  --bundle-dir <main-ui> --compare-bundle-dir <candidate-ui> --output <new-dir>
```

Omit `--active-transcript-two-round` for one round; add `--active-transcript-reader` for a reader. A/A compares the main bundle with itself. The recorded timing runs additionally load the campaign’s LoAF/mutation and RPC-census init scripts with `--init-script`. The native regression is `pnpm test ui/src/e2e/chat-snapshot-text-fidelity.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`.

### CLS and painted frames

One-round end CLS is 0 in both arms. Two-round end remains **0 → 0.0013041388327 in all 11 pairs**. The candidate causes the residual through measurement/end-follow ordering around actual tool completion; it is not called an improvement.

The final-head capture shows the tool group growing **69.5 → 103.5 px** at DOM sample **1226.4 ms**. The following `div.chat-virtual-row` user row moves **y 895 → 929**, keeping its 97 px height; the assistant row moves **992 → 1026**, keeping its actual 71 px height (43 px remains visible). Chrome records the shift at **1231.1 ms**, delivered at 1233.6 ms. Candidate screencast **frame 31 at 1208.629 ms** precedes it; **frame 32 at 1233.549 ms** shows the displaced rows before the end write **20238 → 20272 at 1235.8 ms**. Frame 33 at 1258.788 ms is corrected; DOM geometry settles at 1259.1 ms. All three raw captures were inspected. This reaches a painted frame. Main has the same growth at 1191.7 ms, corrects at 1196.2 ms and records CLS 0. The earlier bounded small compensation attempt failed and was removed; the source is documented under the requested residual-CLS path.

One-round reader CLS is 0 in both arms. Raw two-round reader CLS is **0.000003789 → 0.005200725**. In all 11 affected candidate runs the extra 0.005196936 event precedes the fixture’s established reader anchor and live history; after reader anchoring, both arms are exactly 0.000003788858 in all 11 pairs. In the first candidate pair it occurs at 463.5 ms, before the anchor at 512 ms, hello at 549.9 ms and history response at 893.5 ms. The raw totals are not hidden or described as a passing whole-reload CLS result.

A final-head [matched-cache attribution control](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_ae44699efa06da512933c96a49071e23) removes only optional transcript row-height facts, after native priming, from both arms. Both loaded active records are exactly **87,089 B**. Both arms then record exactly **0.0052007247917 CLS**: the same retained-long-reply shift of **0.0051969359333** (main 459.0 ms, candidate 451.5 ms), plus the same later rail-marker shift. The fixture dispatches an untrusted −240 px wheel at 412.2 / 416.5 ms; native reader-resize compensation subsequently writes **19830 → 19807 (−23 px)** in both arms. The established anchors begin at 508.2 / 573.9 ms and never move. This isolates the raw reader difference to native priming with optional height facts present/absent; it is not a candidate-only live-history correction. This diagnostic is excluded from the timing comparisons and does not erase their raw CLS totals.

The common post-tool reader CLS is from the position rail; the transcript anchor stays fixed. Archived CLS is 0 in both arms; dashboard CLS is 0.0000140807755 in both arms.

### Reader excursion and native motion

The rejected earlier candidate had a **220 px reader excursion in 2/11 runs, versus 0/11 on main**. A separate capture reproduced it in 3/11 candidate runs and showed it in painted frames: this was the rejected candidate arm, not main. Commit-time prepend measurement and relative resize compensation competed with absolute restoration. Warm restoration now joins native receipts, while actual older-prefix insertion keeps its before-paint path. Both final-head reader variants are 0 px in every pair; no anchor disappears.

[Prior-head native controls](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_93199541e6236edd93633da641595fc1) also found a desktop-send reversal in the prior candidate: all three main controls passed 5/5, while all three candidate runs failed only desktop send. [The stack/one-line experiment](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_5d10f049535265c6bac71492ff84ec37) identifies native-offset reconciliation cancelling an unissued replacement command, then the reader anchor writing −28 px. Retaining the prior issued destination fixes that real path; the final native file passes **5/5**. Main independently landed the same prompt/caret readiness assertion, so main’s exact fixture is retained and our duplicate edit is removed.

### Snapshot and asset cost

Snapshot shape is unchanged. Active records are 87,465 → 87,462 B in the first end and two-round end blocks; the end repeat is 87,089 → 87,462 B (+373 B). A/A itself varies by 376 B under native priming. The largest observed growth is **+441 B archived** (57,023 → 57,464); dashboard is **+324 B** (56,031 → 56,355). All per-pair snapshot deltas are included below.

**Approved pinned-main asset evidence:** the owner's AWS measurement on `acb3aa6` against pinned main `7a2001f` was **1,288,362 → 1,289,193 B normalized gzip (+831 B)**, with **20 requests in both arms**. The lead approved that measurement plus 64 B independently of #193996's allowance; that other owner's allowance was never ours to consume. This is historical owner evidence, not the current authoritative CI value.

**Final CI cap evidence:** [CI 42310136781 / performance job 128210032762](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42310136781/job/128210032762) passes with **`chat boot JS gzip vs base: 1288104 B -> 1288765 B (+661 B); requests 20 -> 20`**. The entire budget file matches pinned main; Chat cap **1,289,030 B**, **0 B cap diff**, **265 B headroom**. No L285 comment or startup-baseline change remains. Earlier cap-only commits are removed; CI is authoritative for byte enforcement.

### Final-head validation and costs

Head `1908fb8bd1fb5999d57f5c5edbea55d8aeee8058`; pinned main `36a1c58e91dd9ae991edd76f9ccbfdcd056c5fa0`. [Focused/build run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_13b91d394f7dd5b95f601e5e961792fe) and [full UI / main-control run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_02ef5d5af595792e24c7ac3bc5339f60) use AWS **c7a.4xlarge `cbx_05fdc59b408f`**, observed 16 CPUs/~31 GiB RAM, exact fresh-PR source and no local patch. Source was verified clean before/after execution. Reports are saved; the lease is released with cleanup complete and no host/resources remaining.

| Focused command | Result | Wall time |
|---|---:|---:|
| End anchor, initial range, offset observer, prepend anchor, follow continuity | 43 passed / 5 files | 8.73 s |
| Native browser geometry updates | 28 passed / 1 files | 12.07 s |
| `pnpm test ui/src/e2e/chat-snapshot-text-fidelity.e2e.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | 6 passed / 1 files | 35.71 s |

| `pnpm test test/scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | 14 passed / 1 files | 6.50 s |

**158/158 focused checks pass.** Wall times here are validation costs, not performance comparisons. Actual whole-tree gate: **`Test lines OK: 6556072; ceiling: 6556072; slack: 0.`** Production UI build succeeds. The native regression was red on the recorded pre-fix control (**3 passed /3 intended failures**: one-round backtracking, two-round backtracking and final placement after eight appended pairs), versus **6/6** on qualified and rebased candidates. Checker-boundary proof is red on old code (**3 intended failures /11 pass**), green **14/14** on this head. No extra Gateway-per-case fixture or real timers were added.

**Full UI e2e:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner`. **946 files: 940 passed / 2 failed / 4 skipped. 3,599 tests: 3,591 passed / 3 failed / 5 skipped.** The command exits 1; this is not an all-green full suite. Every red reproduces on pinned main; no candidate-only red remains.

`extensions/qa-lab/src/control-ui-automation-management.real-gateway.e2e.test.ts`: The owner/admin/non-owner case fails during fixture provider readiness with `Private mutation boundary is writable by another POSIX principal.` The stack enters `createQaCrablineTransportAdapter` before the UI assertion; this PR changes no security boundary or expectation. [Every file pass/fail/skip result and main evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193217#issuecomment-6673979357). Native warm-transcript cases also pass in the full run. #194283 and #194284 resolve the earlier Deep Research and browser-panel reds on this base; no Deep Research source belongs to this PR.

Changed-test cost, each using `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` on the same final head:

|---|---:|---:|
| `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-transcript-controller.test.tsx` | 32 passed | 10.80 s |
| `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-transcript-follow-continuity.test.tsx` | 5 passed | 8.45 s |

The first geometry-cost command supplied a duplicate `--config` already selected by the root test router and exited before running tests. The corrected standard command above passes all 28 cases in a [separate cost-only run](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_42d187583497f517d7e4f70cf5f372d2) on the same source/lease; no product source or expectation changed. This corrects command-cost evidence and does not replace the full-suite execution.

**Exact-head [CI 42310136781](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42310136781) is green**, including the aggregate gate. [Performance job 128210032762](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42310136781/job/128210032762) reports **`chat boot JS gzip vs base: 1288104 B -> 1288765 B (+661 B); requests 20 -> 20`**. **No cap changed:** the entire performance-budget file matches pinned main, including every comment, all other caps and startup baseline. prs.title: fix(commands): refuse reset/uninstall while an unmanaged Gateway owns state
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw reset --scope full` (and `openclaw uninstall --all`) can silently destroy the state directory while a non-service Gateway is still running. `stopGatewayForCleanup` only stops a managed (launchd/systemd) service; when `service.isLoaded()` is false it returns `stopped = true` even though a foreground or container `openclaw gateway run` is still alive. The reset/uninstall call sites then trust that return value and proceed to delete `stateDir`, whose live Gateway recreates deleted paths (`agents/`, `sessions/`) and leaves a half-reset, broken install.

Concrete scenario: a user runs `openclaw gateway run` in a container or foreground shell, then (later, in another shell) runs `openclaw reset --scope full --yes`. The managed service is not loaded, so cleanup proceeds and wipes the state dir underneath the running Gateway.

- Problem: `stopGatewayForCleanup` assumed "no managed service" == "no Gateway", so destructive cleanup ran while an unmanaged Gateway still held the state directory.
- Solution: when no managed service is loaded, read the gateway owner lease (`readGatewayOwnerLease`) and refuse destructive cleanup while the Gateway is live, telling the user to stop it first.
- What changed: `src/commands/cleanup-service.ts` gains a second gate in the `loaded === false` branch; `src/commands/cleanup-command.test-support.ts` mocks `readGatewayOwnerLease`; `src/commands/reset.test.ts` and `src/commands/uninstall.test.ts` add regression tests.
- What did NOT change: the managed-service stop path is untouched; a state dir with no live Gateway still resets/uninstalls normally; we never auto-kill the Gateway (the operator must stop it).

## Why This Change Was Made

The teardown gate for destructive ops was incomplete: it only considered the managed service lifecycle, not a Gateway running outside it. The fix reuses the existing canonical owner (`readGatewayOwnerLease`, which already matches pid + startedAt and reports `state: "live"`) so reset/uninstall refuse when the real owner process is alive. Placing the guard in `stopGatewayForCleanup` keeps the single teardown gate the call sites already trust, instead of duplicating lock logic in `cleanup-plan.ts`.

- Best fix: reuse `readGatewayOwnerLease` (pid-aware) rather than a raw `kill(pid, 0)`; it is exactly the state the running Gateway publishes and is already exercised by existing tests.
- Alternative rejected: probing `gateway.lock`/pid with `kill(pid, 0)` — less precise than the lease's pid+startedAt check and already superseded by `readGatewayOwnerLease`.
- Risk: none for the common path; the only new behavior is refusing when a live unmanaged Gateway is detected, which is the intended safety improvement.

## User Impact

Operators who run `openclaw gateway run` outside the managed service (foreground/container) can no longer accidentally wipe their state directory mid-run via `reset`/`uninstall`. Instead they get a clear error naming the pid and the `openclaw gateway stop` command, and their data is preserved until the Gateway is stopped.

## Evidence

### Behavior matrix

```text
service.isLoaded()   live unmanaged Gateway (owner lease)   pre-fix reset          post-fix reset
true                 n/a                                   stopped + safe         stopped + safe
false                none                                  proceeds (unchanged)  proceeds (unchanged)
false                live                                   proceeds + deletes (BUG)  refused, exit 1, data preserved
```

The same matrix applies to `openclaw uninstall --all`.

### Pre-fix (source reverted via `git stash push -- src/commands/cleanup-service.ts`, tests kept)

The new regression test fails, proving reset proceeds despite a live unmanaged Gateway:

```console
$ node --import tsx scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit-fast.config.ts src/commands/reset.test.ts
× src/commands/reset.test.ts > refuses reset while an unmanaged Gateway holds the state directory 6ms
⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯ Failed Tests 1 ⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯
FAIL  src/commands/reset.test.ts > refuses reset while an unmanaged Gateway holds the state directory
AssertionError: promise resolved "undefined" instead of rejecting
Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  1 failed | 11 passed (12)
```

### Post-fix (real production paths: `stopGatewayForCleanup` + `readGatewayOwnerLease` + `resetCommand`/`uninstallCommand`)

```console
$ node --import tsx scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit-fast.config.ts src/commands/reset.test.ts
✓ src/commands/reset.test.ts > refuses reset while an unmanaged Gateway holds the state directory 1ms
✓ src/commands/reset.test.ts > proceeds with reset when no Gateway owns the state directory 1ms
```

prs.title: docs: add Wally provider guide
prs.body:
Closes #194394

## What Problem This Solves

Wally users have no OpenClaw guide for configuring it as a custom OpenAI-compatible provider, and two settings that matter for a custom remote endpoint (streamed usage and turning thinking off) are easy to miss.

## User Impact

Users can configure Wally, save its key, select a model, fill model entries from Wally's public catalog, and get token usage, cost, and `/think off` working. Runtime behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `docs/providers/wally.md` in the same shape as the Liquid Inference and Neon AI Gateway guides, plus one line each in the provider index and the "Chat and coding models" navigation group. The example sets `compat.supportsUsageInStreaming: true` because Wally returns usage when asked and OpenClaw does not ask a custom remote endpoint by default. It also maps `off` to `none`, which Wally's DeepSeek V4.1 Flash accepts to disable thinking. Model limits and prices come from `GET https://inference.runanywhere.ai/v1/models`. Docs only: no production or test code.

## Evidence

Docs checks on this head: `format:docs:check`, `docs:check-config-examples`, `docs:check-mdx`, `docs:check-links` (0 broken), `lint:docs` (0 issues) and `git diff --check` pass. `docs:spellcheck` reports hits only in files this PR does not touch.

Live, against `main` (2026.11.1) built from source, isolated state dir, with the guide's config:

- `openclaw config validate`: valid.
- `models auth paste-api-key --provider wally`: key stored as `wally:manual`; `models list --provider wally` shows `wally/deepseek-v4.1-flash` (text+image, 1049k ctx).
- `agent exec` on `wally/deepseek-v4.1-flash`, with `WALLY_API_KEY` unset so the stored key is used: plain reply; a tool turn (`write` then `read`, 0 failures) with usage recorded while streaming and cost `$0.003313`, matching catalog prices.
- `--thinking off`: 2 output tokens, no reasoning. `--thinking max`: reasoning tokens present.
- `wally/glm-5.3-flash` with `--thinking off`: still reasons, as the guide says for models whose catalog entry has `thinking_off: false`.
- Image input on `deepseek-v4.1-flash` checked directly against the API.

Local review: an independent Codex review found three issues, all fixed: `--agent main` assumed an agent with that id exists, the thinking paragraph implied the server default applies when OpenClaw sends its own level, and the guidance for models that cannot turn thinking off overpromised.

prs.title: fix(gateway): report closed connections as cancelled requests, not profile changes
prs.body:
[AI-assisted]

Fixes #193439

## What Problem This Solves

`prepareAuthenticatedProfile()` folded two unrelated conditions into one guard in `src/gateway/server-methods/users-profile-access.ts`: a requester identity/authority change **and** `client.connectionSignal.aborted`. Both threw `new Error("Gateway requester profile changed")`.

So when an iPhone goes to background and drops its socket while a profile-scoped read is still preparing, the gateway logged an authority event that never happened:

```text
request handler failed: Error: Gateway requester profile changed
```

for an ordinary `models.list` cancellation. The reporter saw five of these, each right after an iPhone reconnect/disconnect cycle. Nothing about the requester had changed; the transport had simply gone away. Operators cannot tell a real profile swap — a security-relevant event — from a routine background disconnect.

## Why This Change Was Made

Cancellation and authority drift are different outcomes and need to be reported separately:

- **New `GatewayRequestCancelledError`** (`src/gateway/server-methods/request-cancelled-error.ts`) owns the cancellation outcome: message `Gateway request cancelled: connection closed`, plus a `retryable` `UNAVAILABLE` error shape for direct callers.
- **`assertConnection()` checks the transport first.** An aborted `connectionSignal` throws the cancellation error; every identity, `connId`, role, scope, profile-binding and lifetime comparison stays exactly as before for genuine drift. The same normalization covers `assertLifetimeCurrent()`, which also reports an aborted transport.
- **The dispatcher settles cancellations quietly** (`authenticated-request-dispatch.ts`). A cancelled request logs a `cancelled` WS record instead of `request handler failed: ...` at error level, and writes no response to a socket that is already gone. `finally` still releases the entry, policy response and completion.
- **`users.self` and `chat.metadata` (`models.list`)** no longer translate cancellation into a profile failure: `chat-metadata-handler` now also treats a closed `connectionSignal` as cancellation rather than `PreparedModelRuntimePublicationSupersededError` ("Chat metadata access changed..."), and both hand the error to the dispatcher.

No identity, lifetime, role, scope, or mutation check is removed or relaxed. Only the classification of a closed transport changes.

## User Impact

- Background iOS reconnects stop logging false `Gateway requester profile changed` handler failures for requests the client already abandoned.
- Real requester-profile changes keep failing closed: the existing `users-enumeration.worker` cases for revoked and reassigned authority still pass unchanged.
- Clients still connected get the same responses as before; a client whose socket died gets no error frame on a dead socket, only the normal cancellation record.

## Evidence

Regression was written first and fails on the unpatched base (`d082771eb6`), then passes with the fix.

Baseline — the fix reverted, new tests only:

```text
 ×  gateway-methods  src/gateway/server-methods/users-profile-access.cancellation.test.ts > classifies a closed connection as a cancelled request, not a requester-profile change 57ms
   → expected 'Error' to be 'GatewayRequestCancelledError' // Object.is equality
 ✓  gateway-methods  src/gateway/server-methods/users-profile-access.cancellation.test.ts > still reports a real requester-profile change after the connection stays open 14ms
 ×  gateway-methods  src/gateway/server-methods/users-self.cancellation.test.ts > settles a closed-connection users.self request as cancelled instead of a profile-change failure 60ms
   → expected undefined to be 'GatewayRequestCancelledError' // Object.is equality
 Test Files  2 failed (2)
      Tests  2 failed | 1 passed (3)
```

The unpatched `users.self` case resolves as a settled request (the handler caught the mislabeled error and answered with it), which is exactly the reported behavior: the caller saw `Gateway requester profile changed` instead of a cancellation.

With the fix, new tests plus the existing authority-suite regression:

```text
 ✓  gateway-methods  src/gateway/server-methods/users-profile-access.cancellation.test.ts > classifies a closed connection as a cancelled request, not a requester-profile change
 ✓  gateway-methods  src/gateway/server-methods/users-profile-access.cancellation.test.ts > still reports a real requester-profile change after the connection stays open
 ✓  gateway-methods  src/gateway/server-methods/users-self.cancellation.test.ts > settles a closed-connection users.self request as cancelled instead of a profile-change failure
 ✓  gateway-methods  src/gateway/server-methods/users-enumeration.worker.test.ts > checks operator.sessions.read at the native profile commit after authority is unchanged
 ✓  gateway-methods  src/gateway/server-methods/users-enumeration.worker.test.ts > checks operator.sessions.read at the native profile commit after authority is revoked
 ✓  gateway-methods  src/gateway/server-methods/users-enumeration.worker.test.ts > checks operator.sessions.read at the native profile commit after authority is reassigned
 ✓  gateway-methods  src/gateway/server-methods/users-enumeration.worker.test.ts > checks operator.sessions.write at the native profile commit after authority is unchanged
 ✓  gateway-methods  src/gateway/server-methods/users-enumeration.worker.test.ts > checks operator.sessions.write at the native profile commit after authority is revoked
 ✓  gateway-methods  src/gateway/server-methods/users-enumeration.worker.test.ts > checks operator.sessions.write at the native profile commit after authority is reassigned
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  17 passed (17)
```

`chat.metadata` / `models.list` owner suite (Node 24.22.1, `vitest.gateway-methods.config.ts`):

```text
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  30 passed (30)
```

Lint and formatting on the touched files (`oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json`, `oxfmt --check`):

```text
Found 0 warnings and 0 errors.
Finished in 2.4s on 7 files with 259 rules using 6 threads.

Checking formatting...
All matched files use the correct format.
Finished in 460ms on 1302 files using 6 threads.
```

Line-cap ratchet on the changed sources:

```text

```

`tsc -p tsconfig.core.json --noEmit` reports no diagnostics in any touched file (the run still lists pre-existing unrelated `src/tui/*` errors from the local toolchain).

Not proven: the iOS-side reproduction. The reported failures are observation-only logs from a phone, so the fix is verified at the source-proven classification boundary and through the real `users.self` dispatch path, not against a live iOS background refresh.

`mcp doctor` reports working stdio commands as missing when their configured working directory or a PATH directory contains leading or trailing spaces.

## User Impact

Users can diagnose servers installed in literal whitespace-containing directories without a false command-not-found error. No configuration rewrite or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The launch/configuration path preserves literal paths, but doctor still trimmed cwd and each PATH entry. Doctor now uses the existing nonblank-string reader for cwd and preserves PATH entries, including the existing meaning of an empty entry.

## Evidence

- Registered real `mcp doctor --json` command, no mocks, synthetic on-disk configuration: before, both `/proof/bin /proof-mcp` (PATH lookup) and `/proof/app /proof-mcp` (relative command with cwd) reported command-not-found; after, both report `ok: true`, with no issues. Independently spawning the two actual executables completed MCP initialize and tools/list (`ping`) with exit 0.
- Regression before the fix: normal relative PATH passed; whitespace in cwd, a padded PATH entry, and a whitespace-only PATH entry each failed. Final focused regression: all four pass (33.49s Vitest / 168.03s wrapper, dominated by worker compilation and module setup). The regression extends an existing real-filesystem CLI test by 8 lines, with a matching allocation. The existing command-level harness is needed to exercise persisted configuration and filesystem executable discovery together. Windows keeps the original ordinary-path case; POSIX-only whitespace fixtures are excluded there.
- Simplification: removed destructive trimming at the existing diagnostic owner; production net -2 lines, test net +8. No new production helper, option, or state.

- Full touched CLI suite: 44 passed, 1 failed, 1 Windows-only test skipped (154.52s Vitest / 329.78s cold wrapper including worker compilation). The existing initialize-timeout probe test first exceeded its 1.5s timing assertion; focused reproduction reached a probe `ExitError`. Repeating it with the original base production module produced the same probe failure. That `mcp add` path does not call the changed doctor resolver. This known local failure is recorded, not counted as a passing suite.
- Targeted production/test typechecking, type-aware lint, formatting, whitespace checks, and test-line ratchet passed. Typechecking used the documented `OPENCLAW_TYPECHECKER=tsgo` fallback. Hosted checks for this unchanged head passed (CodeQL is neutral; a superseded auto-response was cancelled).

- An independent reviewer inspected the complete final diff at `def42739e70f0f41fb77e56b6a0cf156bea1027f`, its runtime consumers, red/green evidence, and the unrelated baseline probe failure; no actionable P0–P2 findings. Autoreview is unavailable in this environment because its provider preflight rejects the configured `stream_max_retries` field. This is an independent review, not a successful autoreview run.

### Normal CLI behavior proof (2026-11-06)

Ran the normal `pnpm openclaw mcp doctor --json` launcher at unchanged head `def42739e70f0f41fb77e56b6a0cf156bea1027f` on Linux, Node 24.22.1, pinned pnpm 12.15.0. The normal launcher built its runtime from this source tree; the actual doctor command then ran in a secretless container with `--network none`. No handler imports, Commander harness, mocked filesystem, edited source, or handwritten build stamps were used for this run.

Both the relative command with a literal trailing-space cwd and the command resolved through a literal trailing-space PATH directory return `ok: true` and no issues. Exit code: 0.

<details>
<summary>Literal paths, config, command, and raw output</summary>

Created executable files at these exact paths (the space before `/proof-mcp` is part of the parent directory name):

```text
/proof/app /proof-mcp
/proof/bin /proof-mcp
```

Each file is the existing synthetic MCP fixture with executable permissions and a Node shebang. The prior separate process proof completed initialize and tools/list for these fixtures; this new run verifies the normal shipped diagnostic entry point itself.

Config at `/proof/state/openclaw.json`:

```json
{
  "mcp": {
    "servers": {
      "path": {
        "command": "proof-mcp",
        "env": {
          "PATH": "/proof/bin "
        }
      },
      "cwd": {
        "command": "./proof-mcp",
        "cwd": "/proof/app "
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Command inside the isolated container:

```sh
OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/proof/state \
OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/proof/state/openclaw.json \
pnpm openclaw mcp doctor --json
```

Raw stdout:

```json
{
  "path": "/proof/state/openclaw.json",
  "ok": true,
  "servers": [
    {
      "name": "cwd",
      "ok": true,
      "issues": []
    },
    {
      "name": "path",
      "ok": true,
      "issues": []
    }
  ]
}
```

Raw stderr:

```text
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs mcp doctor --json
```

The launcher used the supported Node build runtime with `OPENCLAW_VITEST_RUNTIME=node`, `OPENCLAW_BUNDLED_PLUGIN_BUILD_IDS=memory-core`, and `OPENCLAW_INCLUDE_OPTIONAL_BUNDLED=0`. Build preparation used network access to obtain pinned native build dependencies. Its initial automatic heap preflight stopped; the normal build subsequently completed with the documented `OPENCLAW_TSDOWN_MAX_OLD_SPACE_MB=4352` setting. The doctor run above was offline.

</details>

The earlier registered-handler and MCP handshake evidence remains supporting evidence. The new run covers normal CLI startup and the changed static diagnostic. `mcp doctor --probe`, a Gateway, and a latest-stable upgrade were not exercised; this read-only diagnosis change neither writes nor migrates configuration.

prs.title: fix(ui): hide empty session status sidebars and stabilize People
prs.body:
Requested by @jacobtomlinson.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @jacobtomlinson](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/ddd84ad7-0adb-4c6b-bc33-4e8b13d321d9)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/94ee1611-f3b8-4c84-a08b-7f9d7b825344)
- [Review repairs and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/subagent/8350193e-d746-4c6e-8310-39f8033737aa)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an empty, slim status card remaining beside a conversation when there are no visible status sections, and the self-only People section flashing during identity and membership loading.

## User Impact

Empty status sidebars no longer occupy space. Self-only conversations stay quiet during loading. Known participants remain visible when viewer lookup fails, and populated sections keep their conversation gutter while Details hydrates. Cached Processes reserves space only when its actual open callback is available; live-empty or denied results can retire the section. Cached process rows do not gain live control actions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Section owners report presence and scoped availability instead of querying their own DOM. Rendering and pre-hydration reservation share admission policies for viewer identity, live/cached Outputs and Processes, Environment, Subagents, Automations, and published links. Lightweight Boolean selectors stay eager while rich projections and view rendering remain lazy. Existing scoped owner facts override initial cache forecasts without adding another inventory, identity owner, or process observer.

No migration or configuration changes are required.

## Evidence

- **192 tests passed across 15 focused suites**, preserving the prior regressions and adding cached-Processes pending→ready geometry, callback admission, and settled-empty/access retirement. The Processes regression was reproduced before the repair and passes afterward with the initial 313px gutter and unchanged conversation rectangle.
- Known live-empty/cached-zero precedence, unresolved self-only deferral, partial caches, deferred RPC denial, Gateway replacement, and same-key/new-session reset remain covered. The viewer adapter adds no `users.self` request.
- Strict UI typecheck, targeted lint, controller/test-lines guards, introduced-scope max-lines/line-cap checks, formatting, and whitespace checks passed. Exact scoped allocation includes fixtures; no shared scalar, primitive allowance, performance budget or threshold was raised.
- Independent code review found no actionable issues in the Processes and eager-boundary changes and audited the current cached-schema keys against actual desktop owners. Reviewed tree: `29ee45416dace6f4409ca29f6ccecaacc181a718`.
- The retained main integration was previously validated with four production UI controlled-Gateway E2Es and a hidden-host discovery probe. The matching viewer-failure captures remain below.
- This update is published in head `a5ec7ddc9bed84d092e9a80e081ad732abfd6476`. The hosted review and failing performance run for `881c1104a18f9f195f83394472640eab1a343bda` predate it. Current-head hosted review and CI remain required; no green hosted performance result is claimed here.

<details>
<summary>Performance evidence and validation limits</summary>

Local exported collector/evaluator APIs, pinned to the CI checker/config/normalizer with Node 24.22.1 and the authentic CI baseline report, returned no metric violations for the measured dist. This was **not a completed paired official-wrapper run or hosted-CI pass**. The failing head was not rebuilt as an isolated local control, product sources differed from CI's synthetic merge, and the evaluation receipt did not independently bind those assets to the final staged tree. These measurements are diagnostic evidence, not a substitute for the new hosted performance gate.

The browser proof uses the real built UI with controlled Gateway fixtures, not a real agent/model run. The isolated real-Gateway attempt timed out during runtime postbuild before Gateway assertions started. Local ClawSweeper/autoreview was unavailable; independent code review is not represented as those tools' output. Extra direct-base probes exposed unchanged baseline/Cron drift; these are not described as green global checks.

</details>

prs.title: fix: recover conversations after accidental session resets
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: accidentally choosing `/reset` clears the visible conversation with no recovery action in chat.

## User Impact

The latest recoverable manual reset now offers **Undo** in the existing Session reset divider, with confirmation. It restores earlier history and the next agent's context. Messages sent after the reset remain on another branch instead of being deleted or silently merged. Undo does not reverse tool actions or file changes.

Automatic or tail-preserving resets are not undoable. Active, queued, or unadopted input must settle before Undo; the operation does not cancel it.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing rewind, transcript, and mutation owners rather than adding a recovery store. A deliberate leaf selection opens the requested reset window while ordinary stale controls remain fenced. Validated navigation records exactly which reset IDs were reopened; the planner consumes those facts, and later resets revoke them.

History and model-context projections share one complete navigation-field contract, so restoring the UI also restores the actual model request. Authority and the latest boundary are revalidated before mutation. No database table or migration is added.

## Evidence

### Current published raw-source-hash inventory repair

- Published head: `591578e4a775106f83f791bbc8f3e8a3b165f3e6`, tree-identical to approved source commit `80dbcf7d60a78c3da9ef7ee46388d78031c304b8`, with the exact Jacob coauthor trailer verified. Managed publication completed as `roboclaw-bot`; no main integration or PR merge was performed for this update. Its only source delta from prior published `912b13e7d0597099a05bf0352347d766e790b069` is **one added entry**, `en-chat-reset-confirmation.ts`, in the authoritative `sourceFiles` inventory in `scripts/lib/control-ui-i18n-catalog.ts`.
- The exact prior-head CI failure was reproduced locally before editing: `ui/src/app/vite-config.node.test.ts` → **includes every English dependency in the raw source-hash input** failed with the same reset-confirmation assertion (**1 failed, 43 unselected skipped**). The fragment was already consumed by the catalog composition and its modal; its complete raw bytes were missing from the maintained hash-input inventory. No test, collector, hash contract, snapshot or missing-file guard was weakened.
- After the one-line owner fix, **111 full consumer tests pass**: all **44 Vite-config/source-hash tests**, all **30 catalog tests**, and **37 catalog-verification/deadcode tests**. Scripts and UI type lanes, scoped owner lint, formatting and whitespace pass. These are **implementation-owner-run** results, not independent reviewer-run tests. No test source growth was added; the **853-line allocation is unchanged**.
- The same retained independent reviewer approved the frozen one-line artifact with **no findings**. The committed diff matches reviewed SHA-256 `af632061bb367b63843e4a68510f44578853fefeec25cfda03d0095f21533a59`; whole-checkout/index checks confirmed only that intended path and entry. This approval is limited to the inventory repair, not overall readiness, a performance waiver or a new runtime repair.
- Managed inspection at this updated head reports **open, unmerged, mergeable: false / dirty**. This did not prohibit the authorized branch publication; it does prevent a conflict-free/readiness claim. The reviewed upstream pin remains `9d8bbfbbaf162cda2f5cd620816b6ac8a8bd5d00`. New-head CI must establish its own outcome; **the prior-head run and performance measurements below are not CI evidence for this new head**. No automatic moving-main integration, performance experiment, Android retry or denied upgrade attempt was used to publish this one-line fix.

### Prior 912-head CI and integrated proof — historical scope

- The prior `912b13e7` tree matched reviewed integration `17345dd8af2c24640941d50385244c93021573c5`. Its branch integration restored normal CI eligibility; this was not a PR merge. The single generated-predicate conflict was resolved through canonical generation/check, while source/UI changes auto-merged.
- Exact prior-head [CI run 42132165125](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42132165125) **completed with failure**. Its aggregate selected three failing lanes: [UI source-hash job 127611975030](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42132165125/job/127611975030), repaired locally above; [Android access job 127611975286](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42132165125/job/127611975286), which failed while preparing the Emulator SDK ZIP with **Error reading Zip content from a SeekableByteChannel**, before Gradle or tests; and [performance job 127611974700](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42132165125/job/127611974700). Android's setup failure is not product proof, a proven inherited defect or a passing run, and it was not retried. Baseline-ratchets job 127611974942 passed separately.
- The prior cloud performance annotation says **1264.7 KiB chat-boot gzip exceeds 1264.4 KiB**. These rounded values are not the exact local measurements below. A truncated check listing must not be interpreted as all green, and a Security Review target/workflow_run result is not a normal CI result for another head.
- Earlier integrated owner proof passed **368 core/tooling tests**, **90 affected UI tests**, **14 prefix-stability tests**, all five maintained type lanes, targeted core/scripts/root-test lint, formatting, source-line and whitespace gates. These retain their earlier source scope and were not all rerun for the one-line repair.
- The prior test-line checker passed **6,510,614 ≤ 6,510,672**, with **853** allocated regression lines. Earlier full core lint was not green: plugin-model-catalog (702) and supervisor (701) exceeded max-lines with files/config byte-identical to pinned upstream. No suppression or unrelated edit hid them. Complete integrated P2 autoreview returned two chunks with zero actionable findings; that review and the independent pipeline audit below are not passing CI or upgrade proof.

### Final symmetric local asset comparison — failing, independently audited

This measurement belongs to the **prior 912-source candidate**, compared with pinned 9d8; it was **not rerun after the one-line raw-source inventory repair**. Both source roots were prepared with their maintained native UI builders and metadata finalizers for the same **eight declared plugin UIs / 21 assets**, using **Node 26.12.1, Vite 8.3.5 and Pako 3.0.3**, the same installed/remapped dependencies and fixed comparison build identity. The actual performance checker and cap were unchanged.

| Local profile | Chat-boot gzip | Requests | Against the 1,294,735 B cap |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Pinned 9d8 baseline | 1,294,874 B | 20 | **139 B over** |
| Prior 912-source candidate | 1,295,475 B | 20 | **740 B over** |
| Candidate minus baseline | **+601 B** | 0 additional | Not a waiver |

Population records are byte-identical, including generations, normalized declarations and asset names; emitted plugin asset paths/revisions/printed sizes also match. Both have the same 1,751 mapped eager module IDs. The generated plugin-distribution carrier is **3,689 raw / 807 standalone-gzip bytes on both sides**. The preserved archive contains eight manifests, eight package identities and all 21 assets; the auditor verified all 21 recorded asset hashes. Individual module gzip estimates are not additive shipped-bundle attribution.

**Interpretation:** this is a failing symmetric **local** comparison: an independently over-cap local baseline plus a **601 B candidate increment**. It is neither wholly inherited nor a 740 B candidate-only regression. **It does not prove the cloud baseline failed**, identify the exact cloud byte gap, or establish a safe code cut. No asset cap, checker, integrity guard or inventory filter was relaxed.

#### Audit qualifications and recovery evidence

- Preparation used each root's maintained builder, real builder paths, ownership helper and metadata finalizer. The auditor found no argv impersonation or fabricated lease. **Per-root preparation ownership ends before population capture and direct Vite execution**; the adapter does not establish an uninterrupted lease through measurement. The implementation owner ran the recorded preparation/build stages serially, launched no intervening source/artifact writer, and retained clean-tree/diff-identity receipts. Equal emitted inventories corroborate this particular run, not a general concurrency guarantee.
- Baseline source came from the pinned Git archive with workspace-dependency remapping. Candidate measurement used the owned working checkout; its HEAD label alone is insufficient, so clean-tree receipts and equality with reviewed/published source are retained alongside the reports.
- The optional consumed-input signature failed because `ui/src/i18n/locales/en-chat-reset-confirmation.ts` is **absent in the pinned baseline** but present in candidate: **897 bytes**, SHA-256 `2bdf7a36a70c0778e7767528c84c0524922b469e0c06f815090cafafe2a77637`. This is explicitly recorded absence, **not a successful signature check or filtering of missing inputs**. Resume built the baseline normally and ran the unchanged checker; setup failures are not product verdicts.
- CSS normalization used the baseline's own authored CSS and rewrote compression sidecars, not CSS source. Original packaged generations, manifests, hashes, reports, source-tree receipts and the task-only preparation/resume adapters remain in the implementation worktree's recovery evidence. The retained audit was read-only; it did not rerun builds, tests or cloud access.

Two bounded lazy-Undo prototypes saved **152 B** and **76 B** relative to the same candidate profile; their plugin asset rows matched the control. Neither closed the gate, and their additional asynchronous/ordinary-reset coupling was not justified. **Both were restored exactly; neither was committed or published.** No further justified narrow production cut was identified. Larger boot-performance work needs explicitly agreed scope rather than speculative refactoring or a cap waiver. The unresolved performance gate and separate operator-only compatibility proof remain blockers to readiness.

### Superseded asymmetric and historical measurements

The first 9d8 pair reported candidate **1,295,475 B** versus baseline **1,294,201 B** (+1,274 B), but used **21 plugin assets/eight plugins versus seven assets/three plugins**. Settings-only preparation built a subset while the producer consumed all existing completed distributions. The extra distributions were **not shown stale or corrupt** and were not removed. Therefore the entire earlier +1,274 B must not be attributed solely to Undo; the symmetric 139/601/740 accounting above supersedes that attribution.

The [older c531 performance gate](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42104571414/job/127517378885) reported **1,294,739 B**, four bytes over the unchanged cap. Historical d999 before/after copy-only measurements reported **1,295,147 → 1,294,950 B** (197 B less), raw **4,152,210 → 4,151,855 B**, 20 requests unchanged, and an older 215 B local overage. Those are historical results, not cross-base comparisons, cloud-equivalent measurements or passing evidence for this head.

### Prior source repair and test-allocation rationale

- Source `142914988afb9621516ad0089f2e14c85611c8e6` moved five **unchanged** reset-confirmation strings into the already-lazy modal's English fragment. Before/after snapshots proved complete `chat.board` and `chat.sessionReset` key/value identity; explicit catalog merges preserve both namespaces. Modal props, markup, lifecycle, recovery controllers and authority checks were unchanged by that copy-only repair.
- The [test-lines failure](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42104571414/job/127517379831) reproduced locally: required regressions added **851 net lines**, plus two catalog-consumer lines. `config/test-lines-allocations/session-reset-undo.txt` therefore records exactly **853 justified net regression-test lines**, as the fix workflow permits. They cover state/Gateway/model-context fencing, retained-history/UI confirmation, real-Gateway/upgrade-fixture proof and catalog ownership. **The shared scalar and shrink rules are unchanged by this PR. Retain this rationale in the squash body.**
- On that earlier tree, 39 UI tests, full catalog/wrapper closure, types, lint, format and line gates passed. All 30 changed-catalog tests passed with one worker in **9.49 s Vitest / 10.46 s wrapper**. These are historical local costs, not current CI estimates. The copy-only delta received a complete P2 pass with zero actionable findings; other earlier reviews retain their stated scopes, not exhaustive independent reproduction.
- Both hosted P2 findings were repaired: generated locale/translation-memory changes were removed under publisher ownership, and the catalog owner preserves eager reset keys alongside lazy Undo copy. Canonical generation/keyless baseline were run, not hand translations. No generated locale/translation-memory changes are shipped by this source PR.
- Earlier pinned proof passed the three CI consumer guard suites (**234 tests**), selected catalog regression (**1 passed, 29 unselected skipped**), owner suites (**104 tests in three shards**) and UI suites (**39 tests in four files**). The interrupted earlier full catalog attempt is not green.
- The [serial-owner gap](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42095199598/job/127484325920) and [trusted wrapper import gap](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42095199598/job/127484325315) reproduced; repairs passed 219 full guard tests and scoped review. Later [E2E inventory assertions](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42098710378/job/127497159725) were repaired using independently declared expected sets, preserving inventory/sharding/phase/worker-cap/parallelism assertions and both provider-removal and reset-Undo cases. No ignore, snapshot waiver or guard weakening was introduced.
- An earlier broad changed-check exited 143 at its deadline amid repository I/O waits. Subsequent checks passed selected SQLite worker/dialect, line-cap, assertion-safety, timeout-race and mock-factory gates on their selected snapshots. Historical results do not replace current-head CI.

### Released-data upgrade proof — BLOCKED

The opt-in fixture uses genuinely installed **OpenClaw 2026.11.1** and its dependencies outside the source checkout, avoiding candidate tsconfig alias contamination. It is designed to create released settings/transcript, stop and snapshot state, replace only the executable, then verify continuity, Undo, reload, next provider request and branch switching.

**No successful upgrade run is established.** The standalone-prefix repair resolved initial source-alias setup failures. The released Gateway subsequently started and created the session, but baseline `chat.send` was explicitly refused by the agent/subagent attribution boundary. The fixture exposes stdout and stderr to make the refusal visible.

This is authority-blocked, not passing compatibility proof or demonstrated migration breakage. **No alternate CLI, WebSocket, browser or CI retry, marker stripping or guard weakening was used.** Human/operator invocation or a boundary-owner-approved attributed fixture route is still required. This separate blocker does not justify bypassing security or declaring source readiness.

### Earlier behavior evidence

Regressions reproduced automatic/tail-reset eligibility, queued/unadopted input preservation, lost model-context navigation and nested-reset fencing. Tree/worker, prefix-stability, model-context siblings, Gateway policy/storage/reader and UI suites passed; `pnpm build:ci-artifacts` passed on that earlier snapshot.

A real browser, isolated Gateway, actual agent execution and SQLite exercised reset → Undo/confirmation → reload → next provider request containing earlier but not later context → retained/restored branch round trips. Inference was deterministic/local, **not a live LLM**; actual provider input was inspected. The final scenario passed assertions but cleanup hit the infrastructure deadline; recorded child PIDs were later absent. An earlier complete harness run passed. Neither result replaces the blocked upgrade proof or establishes all-green current-head evidence.

Earlier inherited findings included a 701-line `chat-pane-render.ts` count on base and candidate against the 700-line rule, and four medium Zizmor action-pin/version-comment mismatches in unchanged workflows. No suppressions or timeout increases hid them.

### Visual proof

Inspected real Control UI captures with synthetic hiking-plan content and a mock Gateway. Real-Gateway persistence and actual agent-request verification are reported separately above. [Public proof comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193459#issuecomment-6657339349).

| Before | After: Undo in the existing divider |
| --- | --- |
| ![Session reset before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4f98a62a-705e-46a0-a13a-86763c5a7243) | ![Session reset with Undo](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7899f47d-0c16-4111-bc13-06a0783d088c) |

<details>
<summary>Confirmation and restored conversation</summary>

![Undo reset confirmation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/333e1768-8ea5-4cf6-bb4f-0014b4a3474c)

![Earlier hiking-plan conversation restored](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c84d46c0-e9fb-462b-ab73-f30284f39719)

</details>

Requested by @jacobtomlinson.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @jacobtomlinson](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/9f5e7c31-a154-400d-a554-d17f371a2b9e)
