## What Problem This Solves

`infer image describe` and `describe-many` leave provider work running after interruption; a failed primary can also start another model after cancellation.

Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194251

## User Impact

Interrupted image descriptions stop promptly, preserve the interruption exit status, and produce no late output. Normal descriptions and configured fallback behavior are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Carry the existing invocation execution context into image understanding and its existing model-fallback owner. The repair adds 19 net production lines. The four regressions reuse existing fixtures at the CLI, fallback and provider boundaries; a separate allocation funds exactly their 64 net test lines.

## Evidence

- Real public CLI, synthetic PNG, and a held loopback OpenAI-compatible request: the base ends in SIGKILL after 2,020.1 ms, with HTTP closing after 2,017.3 ms. The repaired tree exits 130 in 41.3 ms and closes HTTP after 1.0 ms. The harness never forced either process to exit. Uninterrupted controls succeed on both trees.
- Four regressions are red on base `d1be6e243ccd850329d93567cb3ffd71e0ff837d`, including an unwanted second fallback call. The complete CLI suite (114 tests) and media-runtime suite pass together in 52.77 s; the final four regressions plus normal fallback replay pass in 18.91 s.
- Focused TypeScript, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, whitespace and staged test-line checks pass. The final regression allocation is exactly 64 lines, with 19 lines of budget slack. Tested source tree `4d50a52b59d10803d80fedf2663b3f7ba6737367` matches signed head `c1e51e7d581717ef1be900c01d5a7a34c8238e82`.
- The base runtime build and repaired CLI build succeed. Fresh independent source review and complete local ClawSweeper review (high reasoning, full range `d1be6e243ccd850329d93567cb3ffd71e0ff837d..c1e51e7d581717ef1be900c01d5a7a34c8238e82`) found no actionable findings. These were source reviews; execution evidence comes from the separate runs above.

Wire evidence uses actual SIGINT and synthetic local I/O. It does not exercise an external provider. A separate held remote-image input probe still ends in forced exit after about 2.02 s, before any provider request. That unchanged cache/fetch cancellation defect is recorded as the next follow-up; this patch repairs provider work and model fallback.

CI run https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42321980326/attempts/1 completed with only the test-budget job and its aggregate gate failing. Closes #164557

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Settings → Notifications shows Safari Home Screen installation instructions when opened inside the native iOS app.

## User Impact

User impact: iPhone and iPad app users can see their native notification delivery and permission settings and open the existing device settings pages. Browser/PWA and macOS notification flows remain separate and unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The page already observes the native device-settings capability but did not pass its snapshot into the notification view. This repair uses that existing owner, shows a loading state while its snapshot is pending, and keeps missing status values unknown. Device links use application navigation so the native Back history is retained; modified clicks keep normal link behavior.

Upstream migrated the settings UI from Lit to Solid. This update keeps the current Solid renderer and ports the native-notification regression with it. Native notification presentation and capability-to-view props live in focused siblings to respect the existing file-size guards. No notification transport, native permission operation, configuration key, dependency, or generated translation memory changes.

prs.title: fix(gateway): avoid unnecessary cold-start initialization
prs.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/192547

## What Problem This Solves

Constrained ARM64 Gateways can pass health checks but run out of memory before completing a model turn because startup and request preparation initialize optional runtime code too early.

## User Impact

Headless Gateways with `gateway.controlUi.enabled: false` defer browser-oriented prewarming and initial full provider discovery until needed. Default Control UI startup stays eager, and request-time handlers remain available. Scoped refreshes, native-first discovery, provider authentication, tool authority and the public synchronous SDK contract are preserved.

Headless remote catalog updates preserve deferred discovery until inventory is requested. Once requested, pending and completed discovery survives catalog replacement.

Ordinary provider-filtered model-picker reads keep their provider scope. Providers first requested after startup retain their source identity, so a repeated settled read reuses discovery; later unfiltered demand can still acquire the full inventory.

Strict ARM64 acceptance remains unresolved; this PR does not yet establish that the constrained model workload succeeds. No migration or new configuration option is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Keep catalog discovery on captured inputs and lightweight provider/authentication metadata. Defer execution, OAuth, media and session-event delivery code until requested, preserving authority checks after asynchronous imports.
- Avoid ordinary tool construction and auxiliary MCP/LSP/client preparation under resolved global deny-all policy. Async preparation uses shared assembly without the synchronous SDK facade; host-owned tools, collectors and final policy enforcement remain intact.
- Reuse state/runtime snapshot owners, defer PostgreSQL migration construction in SQLite workers, and export the existing opaque session-event target type so plugin declarations can name it without changing its brand or redemption checks.
- Defer initial full catalog discovery only for explicit headless configuration. Picker demand uses the current owner and requested provider set. Native-only or scoped inventory cannot suppress the first complete acquisition, and later provider-local refreshes retain their scope.
- Preserve already-loaded provider and authentication registrations when composing lightweight discovery entries, without loading new plugins. Restore the byte-exact historical research client required by frozen main's existing panel imports; this repairs a missing build dependency without a UI redesign or new authentication scheme.

## Evidence

Candidate: `34bad692f2f41171db8a1435fb82874bd3edeaef`, integrated with frozen main `e27b909e49d33bd723a2cfc10e944845f00249b7`.

- Current 45 Node tests across four affected suites and 11 Bun tests passed. The headless adoption regression was red on the previous candidate; the held-first-request case also reproduced premature retirement before the attempt-owner fix. Core types, targeted typed lint and formatting passed. Earlier scope, freshness and provider-reuse evidence remains valid for unchanged code.
- Exact-candidate `sourcePerformance` build passed in 55 seconds, with its build stamp verified.
- Test-line ratchet remains red by the inherited 54 lines: 6,552,420 / 6,552,366 here versus 6,551,665 / 6,551,611 on frozen main. The PR adds 755 test lines and 755 allocation credit; the shared scalar baseline is unchanged.
- Prior full-PR and scoped ClawSweeper reviews are retained for unchanged code. The prior late-provider freshness P2 was reproduced and repaired. Final scoped `7df7bd42…34bad692` local review found no actionable correctness or security findings (confidence 0.89); runtime proof is separate.
- Current [CI run 42320379833](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42320379833), attempt 1, completed 145 jobs: 116 passed, 24 skipped and five failed. Four root failures were attributed: a one-line test-budget deficit also present on the exact merge parent; unchanged main tests for release-waiver typing and the private UI-server inventory; and a Docker daemon preflight timeout before its product lane started. The aggregate gate propagates those failures. All PostgreSQL jobs passed; other workflows completed without additional failures.
- **Final exact-package ARM64 acceptance is pending. R1 remains unresolved.** No ARM success is claimed.

The preceding `7df7bd42` canonical ARM64 package passed build/static gates and health, then its Gateway service was OOM-killed before a completed model reply or soak. Outer peak was 956,874,752 bytes; ancestor local OOM counters stayed zero while hierarchical counters recorded five OOM events and one kill. The conditional 512 MiB trial was skipped and owned resources were closed. The new source regression is proven; its effect on that OOM still needs the constrained runtime test.

R1 remains open until the final package produces the real `CARDPUTER_GATEWAY_OK` response, completes a 60-second soak, stays at or below 928 MiB peak and records zero OOM under unchanged 1 GiB outer / 768 MiB service limits. The conditional 512 MiB trial remains gated on primary PASS.

prs.title: feat(plugins): prepare automation tools and preserve runtime defaults
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An automation can be approved or saved without a configured default tool, then fail when its instructions need that tool. Plugins also need to prepare a selection against the creating turn's executable permissions before requesting approval.

`ctx.prepareCronToolSelection` prepares that concrete selection before approval. The submission callback preserves the original proposal and current creator authority through approval and native persistence. Embedded runs bind preparation to completed tool capture after policy filtering and schema quarantine; preparation before capture or after generation retirement is rejected. Incomplete configured MCP discovery remains incomplete when app discovery succeeds.

Configured `cron.defaultTools` extends nonempty effective selections during isolated agent-turn execution for existing and new jobs, without rewriting saved payloads, approvals, or run identity. Downstream permissions and execution-target checks still apply. Saved `toolsAllowMode: "exact"` opts out durably; `"defaults"` resets that choice. Explicit empty selections remain tool-less. Schedule/name-only edits preserve copied selections; a mode-only reset reloads the job, prepares its current tools before approval, and saves against its current configuration revision.

## Current status

**Draft; full acceptance remains incomplete.** Current signed head is `c7074a8eb01b7fc84661af7e0f6dfe9ca4d7df7b`, including captured canonical main `ec702e8338827dee1ef3ec28a931842c6be9826b` through that signed merge.

The supported nonrelease full run [42079940382](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42079940382) targets older source `ab781ec9549e6ae6c815549063a9f10fcd8254c8`, verified by its preflight. Its workflow revision `6869e37c69c3ac2a7ead000d3e866b3e994ae24a` is not the tested source. The run completed with failure. It is not active; its unresolved failures remain under investigation. It does not qualify this newer head. No new full run, retry, or cancellation was requested for this repair.

#187798 (configured defaults before approval) and #186306 (reader-enabled automation guidance) are merged. Those merges do not establish this broader runtime/defaults follow-up's acceptance.

Selected-model capability discovery and live consumer qualification remain open. A supported custom model may expose no shell while the native projection infers `read`/`exec`; a partial native bridge list is not proof of the complete callable surface. Session-target runtime default projection remains separate. This PR does not add a producer capability API or establish live scheduled `read` execution.

## CI repairs in this update

- Removed the unused `operator-recovery.test-support.ts` orphan and unnecessary exports reported by the dependency check. No Knip ignores or baselines changed.
- Updated the scheduled native-child fixture to distinguish the stored inherited ceiling from effective permissions. It resolves the actual accepted child's persisted session through `prepareConversationCapabilityProfile` and the canonical policy pipeline, requiring `read` to remain while `automations` and legacy `cron` are excluded. Hidden-child hard denials enforce this restriction; the test does not invent or claim inherited `selfJobId` authority. The parent scheduling facade is also absent.
- Integrated pinned main for verified existing owner repairs: [#193651](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193651), `7e93c1681b7cc68377dde0c75cb5d0845de8f024`, restores the Swift shared-chat inheritance expectations; [#193642](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193642), `566559c6bd3c2d39b53c2a468f50ca5fd0afefb1`, refreshes native locales; [#193671](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193671), `a7c42ae41d3b5c99ca273f0e7f6bdc6b462d12c4`, refreshes Control UI locales. Generated locale files come from those canonical owner commits. Their inclusion is source repair evidence, not a local Swift/i18n test-pass claim.


Latest integration also reuses canonical macOS fix #193686 (`54ed2bcc`) for the stable real Bun path and bundled identity assertion. The stronger scheduled-child policy test was preserved. No new full run has qualified this head. The older ingress loader failure occurred under Bun while its Node cases passed; a root cause or repaired result has not yet been established.
## Evidence

- Current repair: changed-file formatting, staged whitespace checks, normal commit hooks, and the canonical staged-index test-line ratchet pass. Latest staged ratchet at c7074a8 passed with 6,505,647 lines against a ceiling of 6,505,654.
- Test-budget policy: a separate 674-line allocation covers 665 previously unallocated follow-on regression lines for creator authority/lifecycle, MCP completeness, embedded tool capture, and durable defaults/opt-out, plus nine net lines for this child-policy assertion and orphan cleanup. Original allocations remain 361 and 27. Total credit growth is exactly 1,062, matching this PR's positive test-line delta against pinned main; main's three-line slack is preserved. The shared scalar is unchanged, with no inherited debt forgiven or duplicate credit.
- **Local focused tests did not execute.** The supported Vitest wrapper reached worker compilation, which failed on the existing dependency graph: unresolved `smol-toml`, `@noble/hashes`, and `libphonenumber-js`, then missing `@lancedb/lancedb` and `quickjs-wasi`. Sparse UI/extension source inputs were materialized, but no dependency install, relink, or test bypass was used, and the unchanged dependency failure was not retried. The new child-policy assertion still needs execution on a qualified host or CI.

Earlier canonical Gateway/config/prompt checks and Windows embedded proof passed on their respective previous heads; none qualifies this current repair head.
- Other inspected failures in the completed older-source full run remain unresolved unless explicitly covered above. Passing a retry or the other runtime is not evidence that a failing case was repaired.

Existing owner repairs retain original author/date and upstream provenance: #189072, #188955, #189702, #189794, #188986, #188998, #188936, #189236, #189731, #189707, and the paused-detail assertion from #188922. Their inclusion is not current-head test evidence.

prs.title: fix(daemon): keep launchd findings when inspection reaches its limit
prs.body:
Closes #183805
Related: #183825, the earlier partial-scan proposal.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Gateway status and Doctor lose all stray launchd job diagnostics on macOS when more than 64 jobs match OpenClaw's candidate labels.

## User Impact

User impact: status and Doctor report the jobs they could inspect and say how many they could not. Restart-storm warnings can still name a verified job from that partial scan. Doctor still re-inspects a job before any repair.

## Why This Change Was Made

The scanner threw before inspecting the first job when the candidate list exceeded its limit, and it discarded completed findings if it ran out of time. It now keeps verified findings within the existing limits and sends one incomplete-scan diagnostic to each caller. Native inspection failures and repair checks retain their existing behavior.

## Evidence

### Native CLI at the candidate limit

I built and ran `openclaw gateway status --no-probe --json` on macOS with an isolated OpenClaw config and inert temporary user LaunchAgents. The CLI queried the system `launchctl`. These excerpts show the number of `service.foreignLaunchdJobs` entries, the synthetic restart job's actions, and the inspection warning or error.

```text
Unpatched build, 65 candidates
{"found": 0, "lifecycle": null, "warning": null, "error": "Too many OpenClaw launchd jobs to inspect safely (65; limit 64)."}

PR build, 65 candidates
{"found": 64, "lifecycle": ["restart"], "warning": "Foreign launchd scan incomplete: 1 of 65 candidates not inspected.", "error": null}

PR build, 64 candidates
{"found": 64, "lifecycle": ["restart"], "warning": null, "error": null}
```

### Native status diagnostics at the time limit

I ran the production status diagnostic collector on the PR parent and branch with 24 temporary LaunchAgents. The test seam delayed each native `/bin/launchctl print` by 550 ms, so the real 10-second deadline fired below the 64-candidate cap. The collector classified the native results and produced these status fields.

```text
PR parent
{"nativePrints":18,"elapsedMs":10149,"found":0,"lifecycle":null,"warning":null,"error":"OpenClaw launchd job inspection exceeded its 10-second budget."}

PR branch
{"nativePrints":18,"elapsedMs":10139,"found":18,"lifecycle":["restart"],"warning":"Foreign launchd scan incomplete: 6 of 24 candidates not inspected.","error":null}
```

Native `launchctl` confirmed that all temporary jobs were unloaded after each run.

- 128 focused tests passed in six files, including two native launchd process tests. One Windows-only status-formatting test was skipped on macOS. Core and service-test types, targeted lint and format, and the runtime build passed.
- The per-file and test-line checks passed with a 24-line allocation. Independent Codex autoreview found no actionable P0–P2 issues. [Required CI passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42318323483/job/128239133693).

Closes #194223

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: after a reconnect, route change or sequence gap, the iOS and macOS chat send their model, composer, Swarm, question and source context refreshes alongside the transcript history read, and send them again on every back-to-back reconnect or health recovery.

## User Impact

User impact: on a weak or flapping connection, the transcript read is the first request after a reconnect, and the catalogs refresh once when recovery settles instead of once per reconnect.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reconnect handler still clears every stale value right away (model choices, source previews, agent roster, composer capabilities, Swarm state, progress card, run state, and the reaction/session metadata sync). Only the refreshes that repopulate those catalogs now wait for the history read. If a newer reconnect arrives first, it takes over and the older pass skips its refreshes. A health recovery while a reconnect pass is pending does not start its own set, because that pass will refresh the same catalogs. The session metadata sync stays immediate because queued sends wait on it. Questions missed while disconnected now load after the transcript instead of alongside it; live question events are unaffected. No Gateway protocol change.

Progress card: #125442 fetches the saved progress card after a successful history load and on health recovery. Both triggers still hold. A successful history read schedules the fetch as before. A reconnect pass whose history read fails (for example a transient `UNAVAILABLE`) now fetches the card itself once the read settles, whether or not a health recovery arrived during the pass. A health recovery during a pending pass no longer fetches separately, so a global conversation keeps its card either way.

Accepted edge cases:
- If the history read hangs, catalog refreshes (including a health recovery in that window) wait until it ends with success, failure or the 15 s request timeout, or until the next reconnect.
- If the socket drops while a history read is in flight, that read fails at once and its pass settles, so its refreshes go out once on the new socket ahead of the next transcript read. In the wire trace below this is the one `question.list` before the second `chat.history`; models and composer reads skip themselves while no route is current.

## Evidence

Xcode 27.2 (27B52), Swift 6.4.2, macOS 27.2 (26B123), Apple silicon Mac, 32 cores. Head `75b5fdd69e4` (tree `9abb6dd7fca`); the changed files on the test machine match the commit byte for byte.

**Real iOS transport, wire order.** A proof-only harness (not part of this PR) runs in the OpenClaw iOS test host on an iOS 27.2 simulator (iPhone 18 Pro). It drives `OpenClawChatViewModel` through the app's `IOSGatewayChatTransport` and `IOSSourceResourceLoader`, over `GatewayNodeSession` and a real `URLSession` WebSocket, to a local Gateway fixture (`NativeGatewayWebSocketFixture` with a chat mode added). The fixture answers each `chat.history` after 1.5 s, drops the socket, sends `health` false then true, and drops the socket again; each reconnect raises the same `seqGap` the app sees on a flapping link. The harness and its driver are `rig/harness.diff` and `rig/ios-sim.sh` on the fork at [`a946eb71977`](https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/tree/a946eb7197750d2d50a633939c4e27d4656e1ab1/rig). Loopback only; no credentials in the trace.

| 3 runs per side, same counts each time | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Catalog reads during the burst | 20 | 8 |
| Catalog reads before the first transcript answer | 20 | 1 |
| Most times one catalog was read before that answer | 5 | 1 |
| Harness test | fails | passes |

Catalog reads here are `models.list`, `chat.metadata`, `question.list`, `config.get` (composer and source context), `skills.status` and `tools.effective`. The `sessions.list` read for session metadata still goes out immediately on each reconnect, on purpose, and is not counted.

<details><summary>Wire trace, this branch (run 1, condensed: request/response pairs on one line)</summary>

```
+521ms  conn1 connected
+523ms  conn1 -> chat.history
+523ms  conn1 sessions.list
+527ms  conn1 event health {ok: false}

+1337ms conn2 health

+2850ms conn2 models.list, question.list, chat.metadata, config.get x2, tools.effective, skills.status
```

On main the same scenario sends these catalog reads with each reconnect and again with the health recovery: 20 catalog reads, all before the first `chat.history` answer.

</details>

**Focused tests.** `ChatViewModelReconnectBurstTests` uses a fake transport that records request order and holds history open.

| Test | main | previous head `6afa276f229` | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `flapping reconnects recover history before one catalog refresh` | fails (10 issues) | passes | passes |
| `health recovery during a failed transcript read still refetches the progress card` | passes | fails (card never refetched) | passes |

```

branch: RECONNECT_BURST requests= history,history.done,history,history.done,health,source,models,composer,swarm,questions
```

**Suites on this branch** (in apps/shared/OpenClawKit):
- `swift test --filter 'ChatViewModel|ChatModelSignIn|ChatStreamReplay|ChatQuestionCard|ChatSwarm|ChatSource|ChatComposer|ChatSessionCompletion|ChatProgress'`: 727 tests in 32 suites pass; 18 XCTest cases pass. On main the only failure is the burst test.
- `swift test --parallel`: 2491 tests in 222 suites pass; 40 tests in 4 suites and 61 XCTest cases pass. On main the only failure is the burst test.
- Both runs skip two clipboard tests, `ChatComposerPasteSupportTests` and `file selection remains with the captured conversation`. The test machine had no logged-in desktop session, so `NSPasteboard.writeObjects` returns false and the paste test then crashes the test process. prs.title: fix(ios): queued chat messages wait for the app to open instead of sending during background wakes
prs.body:
Closes #194253

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: chat messages queued offline on iOS stay unsent through background app refresh and silent push wakes, even when the wake reconnects to the Gateway.

## User Impact

User impact: a message sent while offline can now go out during a background wake once the Gateway is reachable, without the user opening the app. Sending can start an agent run while the app is in the background. A wake with queued messages can stay open up to 8 seconds longer; with nothing queued, or when the wake cannot reach the Gateway, wakes take no extra time.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both wakes reconnect, send one beacon, and report done, so iOS can suspend the app before the outbox replay that the reconnect starts gets to send. The wake now waits for the operator connection and then for the rows that were waiting to leave, up to 8 seconds and within a 25 second budget for the whole wake, since silent pushes have no expiration handler and iOS allows about 30 seconds. A slow reconnect leaves less of the 8 seconds, the health check inside the wait gets only the time that is left, and a wake whose node connection did not come up does not wait at all.

The wait never starts a flush itself. It only asks for a health check when Chat has not seen the reconnect yet; the healthy edge starts the outbox's normal replay. So order, retry backoff, the attempt limit and duplicate protection stay as they are: every replay keeps its original idempotency key, and a send whose outcome is unknown is never replayed automatically. Each wake logs whether the waiting rows were delivered, are still pending, failed, had no route, or why the wait was skipped.

Silent pushes report their result to UIKit. Since #129026 a throttled push (node still connected, last beacon under ten minutes ago) reports `.noData`, because that wake changed nothing. With the wait, the same wake can now send queued messages and refresh their history, so it reports `.newData` when the wait delivered messages and keeps `.noData` when it did not. An unhandled beacon stays unhandled, so the existing follow-up refresh for pushes that could not be applied still runs; UIKit then sees no data even if queued messages went out, because the beacon itself was not recorded.

<details><summary>Implementation notes</summary>

- `OpenClawChatViewModel.drainOutboxForBackgroundWake(timeoutMs:waitForRoute:)` returns `OpenClawChatOutboxWakeDrain` (`idle`, `delivered`, `failed`, `pending`, `noRoute`). It tracks only rows that were queued or sending when it started. `pollHealthIfNeeded` gains a `timeoutMs` parameter (default 5000, unchanged for other callers).
- `NodeAppModel` calls it after the beacon in `handleBackgroundRefreshWake` and `handleSilentPushWake` and gets back the outcome, or nil when the wait was skipped; `handleSilentPushWake` combines it with the beacon result as described above. `waitForRoute` returns at once without the node session, and otherwise waits for the operator session with the existing `waitForGatewayConnection(owner: .operator)`, because the beacon only waits for the node session.
- The BGTask expiration handler cancels the wake task, which ends the wait.
- Tests: `NativeGatewayWebSocketFixture` can now answer requests after connect and advertise hello capabilities, so iOS tests can drive the app's real Gateway client through a wake.

</details>

## Evidence

Mac Studio, Xcode 27.2 (Swift 6.4.2), iOS 27.2 simulator. Base 60a2e23d542, head 9216c3d60cb. The runs below used trees that differ from the head only in the wording of one test comment and, for the OpenClawKit runs, the imports of one iOS test file.

**Shipped app on the simulator, over the app's real network transport.** The app's own Gateway client (`GatewayNodeSession` on a `URLSession` WebSocket task, TLS with a pinned certificate fingerprint) connects to a WebSocket Gateway running inside the test process on 127.0.0.1. That Gateway is the repository's existing native WebSocket fixture, which this PR extends (tests only) to answer health, `node.event`, `agents.list`, `sessions.list`, `chat.send` and `chat.history`. It is not a full Gateway process, because pairing needs a signed device identity and approval that a headless simulator run cannot complete. The test connects the app, sends it to the background, ends the grace period so both connections close, sends a message while offline (Chat queues it), and then runs `handleBackgroundRefreshWake`, which has to reconnect:

| | wake returned | message sent before the wake returned | sends |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| base | 0.27 s | no, still queued | 0 |
| head | 0.39 s | yes, at 0.29 s, confirmed by history | 1 |

Harness, tests and runner (proof-only branch, not part of this PR): https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/tree/733d3db80cd6dfa0893f3a099d580dd8f81bb637/rig

<details><summary>Raw output</summary>

```
BG_OUTBOX_DELIVERY side=base handled=true wakeSeconds=0.27 sentBeforeReturn=false rowsAtReturn=queued firstSendSeconds=none sentWithin10sAfter=false sendCount=0 roles=node,operator,operator,node
BG_OUTBOX_DELIVERY side=head handled=true wakeSeconds=0.39 sentBeforeReturn=true rowsAtReturn= firstSendSeconds=0.29 sentWithin10sAfter=true sendCount=1 roles=operator,node,operator,node
```

</details>

- Wake time when both connections are up but the Gateway never answers chat health: with a queued message, base 0.00 s and head 8.07 s (the bound); with an empty outbox, base 0.00 s and head 0.03 s.
- Silent push result through the real application delegate (`didReceiveRemoteNotification:fetchCompletionHandler:`) with a throttled beacon: with a queued message the push sends it and reports `.newData`; with nothing queued it reports `.noData`. Red on the previous revision of this change: the message was sent but the push still reported `.noData`. The existing #129026 test (throttled push reports `.noData`, background refresh still succeeds) passes.
- A wake that cannot reach the Gateway returns in 0.09 s with the message still queued. On an earlier revision of this change that wake waited 8.28 s.
- Existing suites around the wake code on head (NodeAppModelInvokeTests, BackgroundAliveBeaconTests, RootTabsPresentationTests, ChatSendHydrationTests) together with the new and proof tests: 334 Swift Testing tests, including the 3 proof tests, and 3 XCTest tests pass.
- The simulator build leaves out the Watch app dependency in a local copy of the project spec, because the test Mac has no Rust toolchain for the Watch WebRTC library.

OpenClawKit, new suite `ChatViewModelOutboxBackgroundWakeTests` (6 tests):
- Red, base plus only the new test file: the build fails, `OpenClawChatViewModel` has no `drainOutboxForBackgroundWake`.
- Green, head: 6/6 pass. With the production retry delays, a Gateway rejection inside the wake leaves the message queued with one attempt spent, and the outbox's own 2 second retry then delivers it inside the next wait. A Gateway that answers health only after 5 seconds no longer holds a 0.8 second wait open: it ends in 0.97 s (5.50 s on the previous revision). The other tests cover delivery in order with the original idempotency keys when the health event was missed, a terminal rejection reported as `failed`, the deadline while offline, no route, and no resend of an unconfirmed send on a second wake.
- The retry case is the regression for an earlier revision, where the wait re-triggered the flush and spent all three attempts in 0.31 s (`failed:retry=3`); without the wait the same setup is `queued:retry=1`.
- Full OpenClawKit on head: 2490 tests in 221 suites, 40 tests in 4 suites, and 61 XCTest tests (2 skipped) pass. `ChatComposerPasteSupportTests` and `ChatFileAdmissionTests` were skipped because they need a system pasteboard, which the headless test session does not have.

Lint: SwiftFormat 0.63.1 reports 0/6 changed Swift files need formatting. SwiftLint 0.65.1 `--strict` with `config/swiftlint.yml` and `apps/ios/.swiftlint.yml` reports 0 violations on the changed files except `ChatViewModelOutboxTests.swift`, which keeps the same 12 violations it has on main, none on changed lines.

Real OS wakes on the simulator, attempted with the same queued message and local Gateway: the app was backgrounded by a real app switch, and its own logs show the 25 second grace starting and its timer disconnecting both sessions (`Background reconnect suppressed reason=background_grace_timer disconnect=true`). On base the message then went out only after the app returned to the foreground. The wake itself could not be delivered by the OS there: the iOS 27.2 simulator logs `BGTaskScheduler is not available on this platform.` when the app schedules its refresh task, and `xcrun simctl push` refuses a content-available-only push ("Notification has no user visible content"), while a push with an alert added was accepted ("Notification sent") but iOS did not call the app's remote-notification handler in the background.


**Physical device proof.** iPhone 14 Pro Max, iOS 27.2, built with Xcode 27.2 for base (60a2e23d542) and head (9216c3d60cb), with the same local signing setup on both. The app talked to an isolated test Gateway built from the base checkout (its own state directory, LAN, token auth). A message was typed on the phone while the test Gateway was paused, so Chat queued it. The app was then backgrounded by a real app switch; its own logs show the real 25 second grace and a real background refresh request being scheduled. The background refresh task was launched with Apple's documented debugger call `_simulateLaunchForTaskWithIdentifier:`, and expired with `_simulateExpirationForTaskWithIdentifier:`. Logs are the app's own `PushWake`, `BackgroundWake` and `GatewayDiag` lines.

| | Expiry (Gateway paused, task expired 4 s in) | Delivery (Gateway resumed 1 s after the task launched) |
|---|---|---|
| base | reconnect, then expired before the Gateway answered: `Background refresh wake outcome wakeId=BCC15811 ... reason=connect_timeout durationMs=4395`; message still queued | reconnect, then `Background refresh wake outcome wakeId=B27847B7 ... reason=beacon_failed durationMs=1458` and `Background wake refresh finished` at 14:03:11.654 with the message still queued; the Gateway stored it at 14:03:13.074 |
| head | reconnect, then expired before the Gateway answered: `Wake chat outbox skipped wakeId=12EC9A85 reason=cancelled`, `... reason=connect_timeout chat=skipped durationMs=4036`; message still queued | reconnect, then `Wake chat outbox wakeId=ABC9E19E result=delivered` and `... chat=delivered durationMs=1662`, before `Background wake refresh finished` |

Limits of this run:
- The trigger has to be issued while the app is still running in the background: once the grace ends, iOS suspends the debug app and the debugger expression cannot run. So the task was launched about 8 seconds into a real grace window. The wake still had to reconnect, because the Gateway had been unreachable, but iOS did not resume the app from suspension for it. For the same reason, base's message could still go out in the grace time left after its task finished, which a real background refresh wake would not have.
- The test Gateway rejected the presence beacon for this pairing ("node pairing changed while invocation was active"), so both sides report `beacon_failed` and the task finishes with `applied=false`. That is the same on both sides and unrelated to this change.
- The builds are local personal-team builds: no push notifications, no Watch, Share or Widget extensions, and an empty entitlements file. A real silent push was therefore not possible. Chat's databases live in the app's own storage, so the outbox is unaffected.
- The expiry arrived while the wake was still reconnecting, so the outbox wait was skipped (`reason=cancelled`) rather than cut short.
- The grace ends with `reason=expired` in the base trace and `reason=timer` in the head trace, both about 25 seconds after it started; that is OS timing between the background task's expiry and the app's own timer, not a base/head difference.
- Device times use the phone clock and Gateway times the laptop clock. The Gateway logged the beacon rejection at 14:03:11.643 and the phone logged the reply at 14:03:11.650, so the two clocks agree to within a few tens of milliseconds.

Device traces, run commands and the local build changes: https://github.com/etzelm/openclaw/tree/733d3db80cd6dfa0893f3a099d580dd8f81bb637/rig/device

prs.title: fix(codex): count Codex base instructions and confirm native AGENTS.md in the context report
prs.body: Fixes #193111 ## What Problem This Solves On Codex-backed sessions, the Dashboard context panel shows "—" for **Workspace files**, **System instructions** and **Messages**. This affects only the Codex harness (`extensions/codex`). The Codex context report marks `AGENTS.md` as `native_unverified` with `injectedChars: null`, because Codex loads and injects it itself. That one unknown file makes the files total unknown. System instructions and messages are both worked out by subtracting it, so they go blank too. The report also leaves out the base instructions Codex sends with every request. Depending on the model and configuration that's about 10–17k chars. ## Why this reads Codex's rollout file Codex has no API for the instructions it loaded into a thread yet: - The app-server accepts `baseInstructions` and `developerInstructions` on `thread/start`, `thread/resume` and `thread/fork`, but never returns them. - `thread/read` hides the AGENTS.md block Codex injects. The only record is Codex's local rollout file for the thread: - `session_meta.base_instructions` holds the base instructions. - The `agents_md` entry in `world_state` records holds the AGENTS.md text the model currently sees. This PR reads that file. It depends on Codex's on-disk format until Codex exposes a thread's loaded instructions through the app-server, and that API should replace this reader. The plugin already reads `session_meta` from the same file for its native tool catalog. Both now use one shared check that the rollout is on this machine. ## What changes **Reading the rollout** (`client-workspace-state.ts`, `native-model-context.ts`) - Reads only when Codex runs locally (stdio or unix transport) against the Codex home OpenClaw selected. Remote app-servers, and homes that don't match, keep today's `native_unverified`. - Reads only what was added since the last read, with progress cached per client and thread. - Follows Codex's own rebuild rules: compaction drops what is known about AGENTS.md, full snapshots replace it, and partial updates change only the fields they name. - **Rollback:** after a `thread_rolled_back` event, Codex rebuilds its state without the dropped turns' changes. Rather than copy that per-turn replay, the reader drops what it knows about AGENTS.md. AGENTS.md then shows as unverified, never as text Codex has discarded, until the next full snapshot. **The report** (`attempt-context.ts`) - `systemPrompt.chars` now covers OpenClaw's developer instructions, Codex's base instructions, and the AGENTS.md block exactly as Codex renders it (`# AGENTS.md instructions for ` … ``). The AGENTS.md block counts as project context. - AGENTS.md is confirmed when Codex's recorded text contains the workspace file. If Codex recorded no AGENTS.md, it is confirmed as 0 chars. Changed, truncated or unread content stays `native_unverified`. **Settlement** (`run-attempt-settlement.ts`) - The read starts beside the settlement drain and is never awaited, so a slow or stalled disk read can't delay the end of a turn or hold the session lane. That includes runs that were aborted or whose settlement deadline has passed. - Its result is applied only while settlement is still active, which is before the attempt result is built. The read is aborted when the drain grace expires or `closeSettlement()` runs, so a read that finishes late changes nothing. - The read checks the abort signal between chunks and keeps what it has already processed, so an interrupted first read of a large rollout continues on the next turn. ## Known gaps - **Messages is still overstated** by roughly 12k tokens on a real session. Codex also injects its own developer messages (permissions, collaboration mode, multi-agent, environment), about 4,300 chars, plus an `additional_tools` item that was about 46k chars on that session. Neither is counted yet, so both land in Messages. Follow-up. - If the read hasn't finished when settlement closes, that turn's report keeps AGENTS.md unverified and leaves out the base instructions. The next turn catches up. ## Evidence On a live Gateway running this branch, all 3 ordinary Codex turns saved a report that counted the base instructions (15,649 chars) and confirmed AGENTS.md (90 chars). On a real Codex session, the same report data gives (tokens, estimated as characters ÷ 4): | | Messages | Workspace files | Tools | Skills | System | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Before | — | — | 4,869 | 1,642 | — | | After | 21,908 | 2,642 | 4,869 | 1,642 | 4,967 | ## Tests - **New tests:** - `run-attempt-settlement.test.ts`: settlement returns and starts draining while the native read is held pending, for a normal run and for an aborted run with an expired deadline. A read that finishes late doesn't change the report, and one that finishes during settlement does. - `client-workspace-state.test.ts`: reading across appends, a half-written last line, compaction, rollback and an interrupted read. - `attempt-context.test.ts`: confirmed, absent and changed AGENTS.md, as cases of the existing run-report test. - **Before the fix:** the settlement and rollback tests fail on the previous commit. - **With the fix:** the targeted Codex suites (new tests, `attempt-context`, `run-attempt`, `run-attempt.settlement`, `run-attempt.steering-settlement`) pass with `--maxWorkers=1`: 153 tests. - `attempt-context`, `client-workspace-state` and `run-attempt-settlement` pass with `--maxWorkers=1` (18 tests). - Lint, format and the codex plugin typecheck pass. ## Test-line allocation `config/test-lines-allocations/codex-native-context-report-193151.txt` allocates 258 lines, the net test growth after the AGENTS.md report cases were folded into the existing run-report test. The remainder covers behavior no existing test reaches: the rollout reader (appends, half-written records, compaction, rollback, aborted reads) and settlement never waiting on the native read. - An independent review found no remaining defects.

The ClawRouter plugin now projects native fast eligibility and pricing from its catalog, honors explicit-null modifiers, and uses the router's exact reviewed legacy-card fallback rather than a model-family guess. prs.title: fix(imessage): expire cached chat snapshots on elapsed time
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveIMessageChat` (`extensions/imessage/src/chat-lookup.ts`) snapshots the Messages chat list for 30 s so consecutive chat-targeted actions reuse one `chats.list` RPC. Both ends of that window read the wall clock:

- freshness: `cached.expiresAt > Date.now()`
- snapshot write: `expiresAt: Date.now() + CHAT_LIST_CACHE_TTL_MS`

A backwards clock step on the Gateway host (NTP correction, VM resume, manual `date`) keeps a pre-step snapshot fresh for the length of the step. A chat created or renamed after the step is not in that snapshot, so a `chat_id`/`chat_guid` action resolves against the stale list until the step elapses.

## Why This Change Was Made

Expiry now runs on elapsed time (`performance.now()`). The TTL, cache key (`cliPath` + `dbPath` + `remoteHost`), snapshot contents, and the per-call client stop are unchanged; behavior without a clock step is identical.

The module is a bundled extension and may only import `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*`, so it reads `performance.now()` directly. Bundled extensions ship with the host, so no compatibility path is needed.

This is **behavior-completing** for the elapsed-clock family (#191606, #192700, #193147, #193306).

## User Impact

A clock correction no longer pins a stale chat snapshot. Without a clock step nothing changes: same TTL, same snapshot, same RPC count.

## Evidence

Regression test run through the repository's Vitest entry (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/imessage/src/actions.runtime.test.ts`) on Node v24.22.1:

| Test | BASE | HEAD |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `expires cached chat lists on elapsed time when the wall clock steps backwards` | **FAIL** — the second resolve reuses the cached snapshot (one `createIMessageRpcClient` call) | PASS |
| `isolates cached chat lists by resolved remote host` (existing) | PASS | PASS |

HEAD output:

```
 ✓ extensions/imessage/src/actions.runtime.test.ts (20 tests)
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  20 passed (20)
```

The test enters through the shipped `imessageActionsRuntime.resolveChatGuidForTarget` path with the RPC client mocked at the `createIMessageRpcClient` boundary, steps only the process-local clock, advances fake timers past the TTL, and asserts a second client was created.

### Impact surface

| File:line | Risk |
| --- | --- |
| `extensions/imessage/src/chat-lookup.ts:66` | Freshness read only |
| `extensions/imessage/src/chat-lookup.ts:88` | Snapshot write only; key and contents unchanged |

### Real-behavior proof ceiling (requesting maintainer help)

ClawSweeper asks for real behavior proof on the running Gateway path (a live `chats.list` RPC through `resolveIMessageChat`), and separately notes the clock-policy direction awaits its area owner (`Owner decision: Required`). That evidence is **structurally unreachable here** as a contributor:

- The iMessage extension talks to the `imsg` binary (macOS Messages.app AppleScript + private API) on a macOS host; this Linux contributor host has no macOS boundary to drive the shipped RPC client against.
- The committed regression asserts the chat snapshot is re-fetched after its 30-second TTL despite a backward wall-clock step (red on BASE, green on HEAD) using the process-local clock, but the shipped-path round-trip needs a Mac.

This is one of a family of identical elapsed-clock fixes (#193412, #193392, #193397, #193405); #193412 and #193392 carry real-boundary proof where the transport allowed it. Given ClawSweeper's `Owner decision: Required` flag, this PR is ultimately the area owner's call — if a maintainer with a Mac can run the shipped path under a backward clock step, or decides the elapsed direction on the family precedent, we will act on the result.

### Not tested

- No real clock step on a running Gateway; the test steps the process-local clock only.
- No live Messages Mac `chats.list` RPC; the client is mocked.
- Local `pnpm tsgo:core` cannot run on this contributor host (bundled `tsrs` needs GLIBC 2.29+); type checking is left to CI.

### Cleanup

Work happened in a detached worktree off `origin/main`; no production Gateway, session, token, or user config was touched.

### Maintainer options

<details>
<summary>Land-ready or alternatives</summary>

Narrow single-owner change in one extension module plus its test; land as-is if the elapsed-clock direction is what you want here.

Alternatives rejected: clamping instead of switching clocks (leaves existing snapshots frozen); shortening or removing the cache (adds an RPC per action).

Scope: `extensions/imessage/src/chat-lookup.ts` and an existing test file.

</details>

prs.title: feat(sessions): allow same-channel thread recall without agent-wide visibility
prs.body:
Closes #163256

## What Problem This Solves

Let an agent recall sibling threads in one verified channel without exposing every session owned by that agent.

## User Impact

Opt-in `tools.sessions.visibility: "channel"` enables same-channel retrieval while excluding other agents, channels, accounts and workspaces. Existing defaults and other visibility modes are unchanged. Sibling send, status/model changes and session mutations remain denied.

Cross-session list, history, search and transcript-backed recall require a Gateway-hosted owner and fail closed when that owner, route, incarnation, or policy is withdrawn. Ordinary memory/wiki results remain available.

## Implementation

- Require matching stored provider, explicit account, opaque channel destination, chat kind and workspace/space under the same agent.
- Recheck route, incarnation, aliases, physical owner, and policy at final disclosure.
- Carry query-local transcript-owner bindings through memory and direct Wiki consumers; filter final snippets, citations, and recall side effects synchronously.
- Preserve self-only reads, ordinary memory/wiki retrieval, and archived metadata-only inventory behavior.

prs.title: fix(macos): preserve the selected CLI when inspecting a managed install
prs.body:
Closes #140128

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes macOS CLI selection changing when the app inspects a ready managed CLI while an external CLI is selected.

## User Impact

Inspecting installations no longer changes the selected CLI. A successful managed install or update still selects the verified managed CLI.

## Why This Change Was Made

Managed inspection returns status without persisting selection. Discovery retains its existing selection behavior, while installation and update record the managed CLI only after their success checks. No preference keys or formats changed, and no CLI is removed.

## Evidence

Current product head: `6fc1559689dbe9b5a355901c2aae20524c25dc36`. The 2 November merge combines the published discovery-test follow-up `64bf55b81f6573a8c14313dfa51542d21071eba7` with main `c1b0fc1415a09138c48e3f81055aca0f8e4f12aa`. Evidence below is pinned to the revision actually checked; earlier runs are not current-head native execution.

- **Current PR CI:** [Run 41518373631](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41518373631) completed successfully at product `6fc1559`, including selected preflight, security-fast, native-i18n and the CI gate. The [combined gate 41518985777](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41518985777) and security/dependency review statuses also passed. Both macOS Swift entries and macOS Node were skipped, not executed. Periphery build and scan checks passed separately; neither is native test execution.
- **Published discovery regression:** [Commit `64bf55b`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/64bf55b81f6573a8c14313dfa51542d21071eba7) strengthens the existing selection test: it clears both selection keys, calls real discovery, asserts executable/version persistence before managed inspection, and removes the debug project-path shortcut before checking the resolver. The complete delta is one test file (+11/−1), with no production seam or weakened controls. Exact source-delta, patch-application and whitespace checks passed. Independent source review and scoped AutoReview (P0–P3, `openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, no findings) covered the prepared test change against `b3ee562`; native compilation/execution and baseline mutation proof were not run. Public source inspection confirms these assertions remain present at `6fc1559`.
- **Current-head review (2 November):** [ClawSweeper](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140131#issuecomment-5559521046) completed a review of exact head `6fc1559689dbe9b5a355901c2aae20524c25dc36` with no actionable code findings. Patch quality is 4/6; overall readiness and proof remain 2/6 because actual app-entry/install-update behavior, current native execution and released-state upgrade qualification are not established. [Review run 41547046623](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/41547046623) completed; this is source review, not execution proof. The generic existing-data checklist does not identify a concrete schema or data-model defect; the bounded upgrade/preservation proof remains outstanding.

- **Prior-head native-owner proof:** [Hosted macOS run 38597006067](https://github.com/TheAngryPit/openclaw/actions/runs/38597006067) passed with QA/workflow `4cf95ff77fae422b8b380f4a2c49c4101a8f38b1` and clean initial/final product `76ee71b`. macOS 27.0.1, Xcode 27.0, Swift 6.4 arm64: 56 Swift Testing declarations across four suites, expanding to 64 executed cases (50 single-case declarations plus 14 cases from six parameterized declarations). Selection, managed-update success/failure, and older/missing/revoked canonical-verification controls passed. These are executable fixtures, not real npm installations or signed-app proof.
- **Prior-head canonical CI:** [Run 38599555604](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38599555604) passed at exact product `76ee71b`, including `openclaw/ci-gate`. Its macOS Swift and macOS Node jobs were skipped, not executed; native proof comes from the separate owner run above.
- **Prior applicability:** Source review of then-current main `794d6500f382311cab58f5d474a9ef248598e5f2` still finds the ready `managedStatus` selection write. This is source evidence, not a new live reproduction.
- **Prior-head review (29 October):** [ClawSweeper Revision 14](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/140131#issuecomment-5559521046) reviewed `a2c6197` on 29 October. It reports no findings, patch quality 4/6, and overall/proof 2/6. App-entry inspection and verified installation/update evidence, plus an existing-state upgrade from `v2026.10.9` preserving settings and data, remain required. The completed review does not establish a data-model defect.

prs.body: Closes #141184 ## What Problem This Solves The iOS chat composer occupies a large fixed footer, preventing messages from flowing behind Liquid Glass. Connection and loading indicators compete with the conversation, and ordinary session actions look destructive. ## Why This Change Was Made Use a compact floating composer with measured trailing transcript space, native menus, and quieter navigation while preserving the existing red/gray palette, typography, attachments, and voice controls. The composer overlays the transcript instead of reducing its viewport. Upstream’s session-bound, one-shot scroll commands handle sending and jumping to the latest reply without retaining row-ID scroll constraints. Shared presentation helpers keep loading and connection chrome consistent. ## User Impact - Messages scroll behind the composer; multiline drafts grow naturally, and the latest reply remains reachable above the input. - Attachments come first in the options menu. Model, effort, context, and permission controls retain their capability restrictions and use catalog-compatible localized labels. - Selected model options remain visible to accessibility. The macOS model menu retains its sign-in action when no models are available. - Ordinary session actions use standard colors; Delete remains destructive. Unread indicators are neutral, and rows announce unread/pinned state. - Overview keeps its toolbar reachable, uses quieter counters, and opens Usage from Tokens. Small sidebar and onboarding controls meet 44-point touch targets. Reduce Motion is respected. - Upstream’s persistent iOS chat owner, gateway switcher, session attention controls, and desktop styling are preserved. ## Evidence October 12 update integrates upstream `a010ee5721f140f5da48c6c761273b5ebda4cd54`, retaining its live-reply deduplication, deferred menus, compact-width avatar treatment, session-bound scroll commands, and operator/node connection distinction. Removed the unused chat-layout parameter reported by shared dead-code CI. The previously blocked keyboard/history flow reproduced on the integrated candidate: after a multiline send, the app consumed a full CPU core in SwiftUI `LazySubviewPlacements`. Ungrouped transcript content now has one stable layout container per lazy-stack child, preserving row IDs and spacing. The unchanged keyboard/history test passes after this repair; assertions were not weakened. Local validation on iPhone 17 / iOS 26.2 with Xcode 27: - 106 iOS tests in six suites pass, including the latest upstream connection/reconnect regressions, sidebar, and typography. - 39 shared chat tests in five suites pass; shared macOS and iOS simulator builds pass. - The full keyboard/history test passes three times after the fix, covering keyboard opening, typing, sending, preserved history position, multiline anchored replies, and jumping back to the latest reply. - Composer/options sizing, restored session history, long-press actions, and Overview/Usage navigation UI tests pass. - Native lint/formatting, localization verification, and `git diff --check` pass (existing test-file length warnings remain). - Interaction proof used layout fix `5fc55fcc218`; the final `66f8e6bb317` integration adds only upstream’s connection-state changes to the native code, validated by the 106-test run. Shared transcript/composer code is identical. No new tests or CI jobs were added; the existing keyboard/history regression supplies the before/after proof. Independent reviews of the full integration and the focused layout repair found no actionable P0–P2 issues. Hosted CI on the pushed head remains separate from this local evidence. Current synthetic screenshots show keyboard-visible content and preservation of the reader’s position: | Typing | Reading older history | | --- | --- | | | | Original before/after layout comparison: | Before | After | | --- | --- | | | | These original layout captures use synthetic data on the same simulator. The baseline fixture’s model label was normalized for publication; its layout is unchanged. Physical-device, iPad, largest Dynamic Type, and macOS visual comparisons remain unverified. Shared macOS compilation and chat tests are covered. Maintainer product acceptance of the floating composer and placement of advanced controls is still pending.

prs.title: fix: keep dispatched agents’ MCP calls independent of sender completion
prs.body:
Closes #185303

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes configured MCP calls failing with `Tool call authorization expired` when a recipient agent continues after the agent that dispatched it finishes its loopback MCP tool call.

## User Impact

Agents can continue using configured MCP servers after accepting work from another agent. Recipient cancellation and revocation still stop calls, and direct calls still enforce the caller's grant. No configuration changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Start autonomous in-process agent execution outside the dispatching tool call's MCP authority store, at the same boundaries that already release the caller's operator-tool and transcript-writer context. This covers both ordinary agent dispatch and prepared sessionless execution.

The patch leaves request signals, admission checks, recipient authority, and configured-server failure backoff unchanged. Simplification kept one existing authority owner and two existing dispatch boundaries: production delta is 10 additions and 2 deletions, with no new state or retry mechanism. The 222-line regression and its matching test-line allocation are necessary to exercise both boundaries with real configured HTTP MCP I/O and cancellation/revocation controls.

## Evidence

- On base `bab51cf53226bd30303d43d1a50b73005b2ffcb5`, both recipient continuation and prepared sessionless execution fail on the expired sender grant. Three cancellation/revocation/direct-call controls pass.
- With the fix, all five regression cases pass through real loopback JSON-RPC handling, sessions_send delivery, in-process dispatch/internal facade, and a configured HTTP MCP server. Only model execution is substituted.
- Final regression: **5 passed**, 14.74 s Vitest / **17.91 s wall**; test execution itself is below one second.
- Affected authority, commit-guard, continuation, requester-continuation, plugin-subagent, and session-fork suites plus the regression: **111 passed across 7 files**, **113.44 s wall**.
- Production typecheck, owning Gateway test-graph typecheck, targeted type-aware lint, formatting, mock-export guard, test-line ratchet, and `git diff --check` passed on Node 24.22.1 with pinned pnpm 12.15.0. Remote proof bytes match this candidate.
- **Local review gap:** isolated Codex autoreview was attempted on the complete local change against the base above at P0-P2 coverage, but authentication failed (401); no assessment was produced. The CLI is not signed in and no configured recovery provider is available. No clean-review claim is made.
- **Live/CI gaps:** no live Claude-to-embedded model handoff was run. CI timing and broad-suite results are pending.

prs.title: fix(ui): surface native device setting edit failures on their row
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Native device and permission setting rows silently swallow write failures. `ui/src/app/native-device-settings.ts` makes the edit callback optional: when a generic row calls `set()` without one, a rejected native write only reaches `console.warn`, the control stays where the user left it, and the UI shows no error at all. GatewayHosting, cookie sync, and launch-at-login already surface failures via a completion-signal pattern; the generic rows never did.

## User Impact

Toggling Native experience, changing Appearance / icon style / computer control provider, switching location access mode, enabling precise location, or turning on active computer presence — while the native host rejects the write — leaves the control in a wrong or stale position with no feedback. The user believes the setting saved. After this change, the row that issued the edit renders the failure inline with `role="alert"`.

## Why

Every action needs a visible outcome or a recorded intentional non-outcome. `set()` reports failures through the settle callback, but these call sites never attached one, so the error had no path to the UI. Rendering it on the issuing row keeps the failure next to the control the user just touched, matching the existing launch-at-login treatment instead of inventing a new error channel.

## Evidence

- Red on base (`openclaw/main` at `01a5e160dab`): `ui/src/pages/device/device-pages.test.ts` → `5 failed | 18 passed` — the new role=alert assertions fail because generic rows show nothing on failure.
- Green with the fix: `23 passed (23)`.
- Static checks: `pnpm tsgo:ui` clean; test shard `tsconfig.core.test.ui-pages.json` clean; `oxlint ui/src/pages/device/` → 0 errors, 0 warnings (`device-page.tsx` 698/700 lines); max-lines ratchet OK; test-lines ratchet OK (`slack 28`, this change's +48 test lines recorded in `config/test-lines-allocations/native-edit-failure-feedback.txt`); `oxfmt --check` clean.
- Visual proof (mock Control UI + stub native bridge rejecting `set`, Chromium 1440×1000; temporary e2e harness, not committed). Rejected **select** edit — base is silent, fix shows the alert on the Appearance row; a successful retry clears it:

| Before (base, silent) | After (fix, alert on row) | Retry succeeded → cleared |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![select before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/193921-device-failure/select-before.png) | ![select after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/193921-device-failure/select-after.png) | ![retry clear](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/193921-device-failure/retry-clear-after.png) |

Rejected **toggle** edit (Native experience row) — base silent, fix alerts on the issuing row:

| Before (base, silent) | After (fix, alert on row) |
| --- | --- |
| ![toggle before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/193921-device-failure/toggle-before.png) | ![toggle after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/193921-device-failure/toggle-after.png) |

Rejected **permission** edit (Location access mode) — base silent, fix alerts on the issuing row:

| Before (base, silent) | After (fix, alert on row) |
| --- | --- |
| ![permission before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/193921-device-failure/permission-before.png) | ![permission after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/huwei-xydt/huwei-openclaw/proof/193921-device-failure/permission-after.png) |

All six frames inspected: alerts carry `role="alert"` with the exact rejection text on their issuing rows; baseline and base-failure frames show no inline error.

- **P3 separator (ClawSweeper):** `native-edit-feedback.tsx` now inserts a space between an existing row description and the `role="alert"` failure copy when a description is present, so copy reads `…here. The native host rejected…` instead of `here.The native…`. Covered by an extended assertion in `device-pages.test.ts` (`/here\.\s+The native host rejected/u`); file green `23 passed (23)`; test-lines ratchet OK (`slack 25`). Head `88cbaf173ac`.
- **Real native-app path:** still open. Review asks for screenshots through the running native app + real bridge. This environment has no Android emulator (no KVM; emulator capture is out of scope) and no macOS/iOS native host, so that item cannot be produced here; mock Control UI + stub bridge remains the strongest available runtime proof.

## Merge Danger

UI-only: two pages, one shared feedback helper (now with a description/alert separator), one test file, one allocation file. No schema, config, protocol, or gateway changes. `device-page.tsx` sits just under the 700-line max (698) — keep new rows in the shared helper rather than inlining. Test-line credit is fully accounted for. Duplicate search before opening (`file:device-page`, `file:permissions-page`, `edit failure in:title`) found no competing open PR.

prs.title: feat(pdf): add explicit OpenAI native document opt-in
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI Platform users cannot explicitly choose native PDF document input through the PDF tool while preserving existing upload and model-selection behavior.

## User Impact

`agents.defaults.pdfNativeOpenai: true` opts an already-selected OpenAI vision model into complete-document input. **Unset or false preserves extraction and the existing provider order**, including saved configurations upgraded from the latest stable release. Selecting an OpenAI model alone does not authorize complete-document upload.

Page selection, passwords, unknown completeness, page/text/image truncation, size-limit violations, custom endpoints, Codex/ChatGPT transports and text-only models retain bounded extraction. Completeness checks still require the configured extractor. Existing Anthropic and Google paths are unchanged.

## Implementation

This replaces the earlier automatic-upload/provider-preference proposal with one default-off core boolean at the existing PDF configuration owner. The bundled OpenAI provider implements a narrow optional media-understanding hook using the official [PDF input contract](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/file-inputs): inline `input_file`, official Platform HTTPS `/v1/responses`, `store: false`, each PDF under 50 MB and combined PDF input at most 50 MB. There is no persistent Files upload, automatic provider preference or new dependency. The official configuration generator records the single additional core leaf; channel/plugin surfaces are unchanged.

Prepared credentials, headers and symbol-attached request/auth overrides use the existing scoped egress helpers. The native branch also reuses the host-owned `withGuardedFetchRequestAuthority` scope with `assertModelCurrent`, the **original model's** credential authority and the retained provider-resource assertion. The existing HTTP guard rechecks these synchronously immediately before dispatch after asynchronous preparation and on redirects. This closes the assert-only operator/credential retirement gap across lazy provider and DNS awaits without adding an authorization abstraction or changing shared HTTP behavior.

Capability adoption and the proposed setting placement remain normal maintainer product decisions. This branch provides a concrete default-preserving candidate for that decision.

prs.title: fix(slack): stop untagged bot loops with opt-in explicit mentions
prs.body:
Related: #160750, #160752.

## What Problem This Solves

Operators cannot reject untagged bot thread replies without also making humans repeat mentions or changing existing bot handoffs on upgrade.

## User Impact

Slack operators can opt into `requireExplicitBotMention: true` alongside `allowBots: "mentions"` at the existing root/account/channel scopes. Strict mode rejects untagged bots that otherwise qualify through reply-to-bot or thread participation. Human follow-ups, explicit bot mentions, DMs, authorized commands, configured mention patterns, and `allowBots: true`/`false` retain their behavior.

Omitted or false preserves shipped implicit bot handoffs. This is an alternative to #160752's default change, not a downstream adoption decision. **Slack-owner acceptance of the new optional public setting remains required.**

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing bot-admission gate owns this choice. The unchanged mention classifier moves to the existing thread-mention sibling, keeping the oversized prepare module smaller. Existing no-restart reload metadata covers all four projections. No new admission mechanism, retroactive revocation, persistence schema, migration, private runtime patch, or distribution is added.

Integrated fixed official main `228b5e9e7df8b978a85a0f3f3aa249b705f383aa` with an ordinary merge to repair actual preparation-owner and generated-output conflicts. Main retains a single `prepareSlackMessage` owner; retired helper frames are not restored. Existing mention decision and unchanged source classification live together in the existing mention sibling to satisfy the shrink-only line-cap. Current canonical generators own the metadata/baselines. The schema regression uses main's direct `safeParse` assertions after its former test helpers were removed; all validity/default/type assertions remain.

## Adoption decision and fresh distribution evidence — 2026-11-02
