prs.title: fix(telegram): honor group mention activation for commands
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram currently treats an authorized bare slash command as an effective mention in groups. That lets `/steer` start an agent turn, or `/stop` / `/new` affect a session, even when the group's effective activation is `mention`.

This patch makes Telegram group and forum-topic commands follow the effective mention policy before native dispatch, text-command admission, media download, pending-text cancellation, or ingress supersede. It uses the existing `requireMention` / `/activation` contract; there is no new config surface.

| Context | Bare command | Command addressed to this bot |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Group/topic with effective `mention` activation | Ignored | Admitted if sender is authorized |
| Group/topic with effective `always` activation | Admitted if sender is authorized | Admitted if sender is authorized |
| DM, including direct-message topics | Admitted if sender is authorized | Admitted if sender is authorized |

Existing mention patterns and reply-to-bot implicit mentions remain recognized. A command addressed to another bot is not treated as addressed to this one. This intentionally changes the documented Telegram group command exception; the issue discusses the compatibility choice.

Fixes #164065.

## Evidence

- Frozen-base maintenance exact head `ca11b494906febdb43343c0cf356636530624027` is signed over immutable base `432ade6f500de6cdb0bcd4b0948a07bf466672f1`; clean merge tree `5be45911627da8853f95316bb4805a346e309b1a`. The deterministic preflight passes every selected lane, including full core/extension/test/script type graphs, Plugin SDK surface budgets, dead exports, touched lint/format, architecture/ratchet guards, import cycles, and `git diff --check`. A lockfile-frozen dependency refresh changed no tracked source or lockfile bytes.
- The latest exact-head review found media pre-download omitted configured participant mentions. This head now reuses the canonical group-thread mention facts there, preserves exclusive ACP binding behavior, and passes a registered-handler photo-caption regression addressed to a configured participant.
- Telegram command-gate and ingress-supersede tests: **26/26 passed**, including bare `/steer`, `/steer@bot`, other-bot addressing, DM, always-active group, and pre-adoption cancellation cases.
- The targeted native `/login` group test passed after updating its input to `/login@BotUsername`; it still proves that device codes are not sent publicly. The preceding hosted run had one failure because the old fixture expected a response to a bare command in a mention-gated group.
- Worker-backed Plugin SDK session read: the focused `session-store-runtime` read test passed. This replaces the new synchronous SQLite lookup flagged in the first PR review.
- Previous-head CI on `0afec71` found two branch-owned omissions: the new public async read exceeded the Plugin SDK export/callable budgets by one, and a bot-topic fixture still expected bare group `/status` to dispatch. Head `307710f` records that one-export expansion and tests both ignored bare `/status` and addressed `/status@openclaw_bot`. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37555349607) passed, including the SDK surface test and the Telegram extension shards; the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` also passed.
- The branch was rebased once onto upstream `b0c330d27df4` and force-pushed as signed head `0a0c63af2c3e`. A merge-tree check against current upstream `ae64a98a4eb1` is clean.
- The prior run also hit SQLite worker admission refusal in an ordinary channel-DM test, followed by a dependent zero-reply assertion. The command gate does not run for that non-command DM input. It did not recur in the exact-head full shard, but its root cause was not established; no code change is claimed as its fix.
- `oxfmt` on the two latest changed files through the repository's qualified tooling-owner pre-commit hook and `git diff --check`: passed. Earlier touched-code `oxlint` and assertion-safety checks passed on preceding heads; the latest changes add no assertions or casts.
- An isolated exact-head `check:changed` run passed the branch-owned gates, including formatting, policy ratchets, Plugin SDK exports/surface budget, plugin boundaries, core typecheck, all 27 core-test typecheck graphs, extension and extension-test typechecks, and script typecheck. The only nonzero gate was the full-tree Knip scan reporting two unused exports already present with identical references in the immutable base (`readSessionEntryCreationTransition` and `RESTART_CONTINUATION_CONTEXT_PREFIX`); neither file nor any reference to either symbol is changed by this PR.
- [Fresh hosted CI on `0a0c63a`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/37877199608) completed with 65 successful, 23 skipped, and 3 failed jobs. The two root failures are outside this PR's diff and byte-identical from the rebase base/current `main`: an existing two-file Madge cycle in `prepared-model-catalog-{fingerprints,worker}.ts`, and two `unbound-method` lint findings in `scripts/e2e/lib/upgrade-survivor/package-activation-fault.mjs`. The third failure is the aggregate gate reflecting those two. No branch-caused hosted failure was found.
- Repository-supported Crabline Telegram integration proof passed on the exact PR tree: the real Telegram plugin and an ephemeral Gateway ran against a local Bot API transport with a mock provider. In a mention-gated group, bare `/status` and `/steer` produced no outbound reply, zero provider requests, and no session mutation; `/status@crabline_bot` was admitted; another-bot addressing stayed quiet. Bare DM `/status` and bare `/status` in an always-active group remained admitted. This is transport-emulated integration evidence, not Telegram Test Server/TDLib proof.
- Real Telegram Test Server behavior proof is still pending. The exact-head repository doctor was attempted, but no existing Convex launcher could authenticate and no QA broker environment pair was available, so it stopped before acquiring a credential or starting a Gateway. A maintainer/credential-owner run of the group-capable `telegram-e2e-userbot` route is required; the automatic DM-only Mantis plan cannot prove this group-policy change. No live Gateway, Telegram account, or production configuration was changed.

## Review focus

Please confirm that making effective group/topic `mention` activation authoritative for commands is the desired compatibility contract, and review the one-function public Plugin SDK expansion required for the nonblocking session read. The patch keeps bare commands in DMs and `always` groups, and gates the early cancellation paths so an ignored command cannot still interrupt pending work.

prs.title: fix(android): keep realtime Talk alive through slow audio acknowledgments
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/182602

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Android realtime Talk over the Gateway relay ends with "Talk failed: request timeout" when the Gateway's answer to one audio append takes longer than 8 seconds, on the phone and through a paired Watch.

## User Impact

User impact: a short network stall or a busy Gateway no longer ends an Android realtime Talk call. Audio past about three seconds in flight is dropped, Talk says "Realtime audio input fell behind; repeat the last part", and "Microphone input recovered; repeat the last part" once the Gateway catches up. A paired Watch shows its own shorter text ("Audio fell behind. Repeat the last part.", "Audio recovered. Repeat the last part.") in place of the elapsed time; each notice stays until the next Talk state change, as on the phone. Talk still ends on an explicit Gateway error, a lost connection, or an append left unanswered for 30 seconds.

## Why This Change Was Made

The browser relay and the Apple apps already follow this contract (https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/155839, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180572, `docs/nodes/talk/realtime-sessions.md`); https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180572 did not reach Android. Both Android relays sent every frame with an 8 second deadline, no limit on audio in flight, and ended Talk on the first timeout.

A small `RealtimeInputAudioBudget` owns the three-second budget and the two notices, and both relays use it: the phone's append loop in `TalkModeManager` and the Watch relay in `WearRealtimeTalkController`. To release audio from the budget when the Gateway answers, `GatewaySession.sendRequestFrameForEndpoint` gains an optional success callback, and the Watch relay's send callback now reports success as well as errors. The append deadline is the 30 second liveness limit from the same contract. The Watch shows the notices from its own strings: the relay's snapshot gains an optional `notice` field (older watches ignore it), and the Watch Talk screen shows it in place of "Listening · 0:00" while listening. The notices are registered for translation; the docs page now says Android follows the same budget.

Trade-off: a Gateway that keeps the socket open but stops answering is now noticed after 30 seconds instead of 8, as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/180572 states for the Apple apps.

## Evidence

Tested at `170d5c59956` (base `upstream/main` `315fba74e12`). The Before/After runs below used a build of an earlier revision of this branch with the same phone-side code; the stall run was repeated on a build of this head (see "Re-run at this head").

Real app: the Android app (play debug build of each side) on an Android 16 emulator, paired with an isolated Gateway (empty state directory, loopback port, no outside traffic) whose realtime Talk provider is a local fake that only counts audio. The Gateway is an older source build (2026.9.6, `19afe35954`) on both sides; the bug and the fix are in the Android client. A local WebSocket proxy between the app and the Gateway sets the answer delay: while a stall is on, it holds each `talk.session.appendAudio` answer for a fixed time and logs every 50th held answer as `hold`. Same steps on both sides: open the chat, start realtime Talk, let audio flow, turn the stall on.

Proxy lines are UTC; logcat lines are the emulator's local time (UTC+9), whose clock runs about 1.06 s behind the proxy's. On the proxy clock, Talk closes 8.0 s after the stall starts on the base and 30.0 s after it in the 40 second run.

Before (base, 12 second stall per answer):

```text
11:58:35.244Z req   talk.session.create
12:00:20.447Z hold  held=1   stallMs=12000
12:00:25.441Z hold  held=51  stallMs=12000      (every frame still sent)
21:00:27.401 (UTC+9) W TalkMode: realtime appendAudio failed: request timeout
12:00:28.448Z req   talk.session.close
screen: dialog "Talk failed: request timeout"
```

After (this PR, same stall):

```text
12:17:39.337Z req   talk.session.create
12:17:48.405Z hold  held=1   stallMs=12000
screen: "Realtime audio input fell behind; repeat the last part"
screen: "Microphone input recovered; repeat the last part" (held answers start coming back, about 12 s in)
(stall turned off by the operator at about 12.7 s, not logged)
12:18:03.915Z append appends=151
12:18:13.912Z append appends=251
no talk.session.close, no append failure in logcat, Talk stays on

40 second stall per answer:
12:19:02.948Z hold  held=1   stallMs=40000
21:19:31.897 (UTC+9) W TalkMode: realtime appendAudio failed: request timeout
12:19:32.953Z req   talk.session.close
```

![Before: dialog "Talk failed: request timeout"](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/before.png)
![After: "Realtime audio input fell behind" notice during the stall](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/after-fell-behind.png)
![After: "Microphone input recovered" notice, Talk still on](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/after-recovered.png)

Re-run at this head (`170d5c59956`, same Gateway, fake provider and proxy, each held answer delayed 12 s; screenshot times are the host clock, which matches the proxy's):

```text
13:14:31.185Z req    talk.session.create
13:14:44.146Z hold   held=1   stallMs=12000
13:15:01.746Z append appends=301
13:15:08      screen: "Realtime audio input fell behind; repeat the last part"
13:15:15.876Z append appends=351      (14.1 s for 50 appends instead of 5 s: frames past the budget were dropped, not sent)
13:15:16      screen: "Microphone input recovered; repeat the last part", Talk still on
13:15:20.854Z append appends=401
...
13:17:30.856Z append appends=1701
13:17:57.360Z close  who=client code=1006 appends=1952 held=31   (held: running count of held answers; the operator closed the app)
no talk.session.close, no append failure in logcat
```

Watch display (rendered by `WearVoiceLayoutTest` under Robolectric, round 192 dp, not on a watch): before this commit the Watch shows "Listening · 0:00" while the relay reports the notice; now it shows each notice.

![Watch before: "Listening · 0:00" while input fell behind](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/watch-before.png)
![Watch after: "Audio fell behind. Repeat the last part."](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/watch-fell-behind.png)
![Watch after: "Audio recovered. Repeat the last part."](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261024-finding-android-talk-append-timeout/watch-recovered.png)

Mixed versions with the latest stable (`v2026.10.9`, `8b18b5578f6`): the new `notice` field crosses the phone-Watch protocol in both directions while one side still runs the stable release. A throwaway JUnit test (not committed) ran in `:wear-shared` of each tree and passed the real encoded bytes between them: this head's `WearProtocolCodec.encode` of a Talk event with each notice, decoded by the stable `WearProtocolCodec.decode` and `WearRealtimeTalkCodec.decode`, and the stable encoding of a listening event decoded by this head.

```text
head wrote    {"type":"event",...,"event":"talk","payload":{...,"status":"LISTENING",...,"notice":"INPUT_FELL_BEHIND"}}
stable read   WearRealtimeTalkSnapshot(attemptId=attempt-1, active=true, listening=true, speaking=false, status=LISTENING, statusText=Listening, conversation=[])
stable read   (same for INPUT_RECOVERED)
stable wrote  {"type":"event",...,"event":"talk","payload":{...,"status":"LISTENING",...,"conversation":[]}}
head read     WearRealtimeTalkSnapshot(..., status=LISTENING, statusText=Listening, conversation=[], notice=null)
```

An updated phone with a stable Watch keeps Talk working and the Watch shows its usual status text; a stable phone with an updated Watch sends no notice and the Watch shows "Listening · 0:00" as before. In the stable release both codecs already share `WearProtocolCodec.json`, which sets `ignoreUnknownKeys = true` and `explicitNulls = false`.

Upgrade from v2026.10.9 (same emulator, same isolated Gateway and proxy, no stall): the stable play debug build was installed on a wiped Android 16 emulator, paired with the Gateway (operator and node approved), and the Talk speaker set to "Muted" in Voice settings. This head's build was then installed over it with `adb install -r` (no uninstall; both builds are version code 2026080201, `firstInstallTime` unchanged, `lastUpdateTime` changed).

```text
14:57:11.572Z close  who=client code=1006   (the install stops the stable app)
14:57:14.909Z req    connect                (same device ID, no pairing request, no onboarding)
screen: Overview with Gateway "Online"; Voice settings still show "Enable speaker · Muted"
14:57:44.825Z req    talk.session.create
14:58:05.492Z append appends=201            (Talk "Listening")
```

After the upgrade the Overview's Nodes row shows "Review node access" instead of "1 online": `openclaw nodes list` on the same Gateway shows the node in `pending-reapproval` with the same 7 caps and 14 commands as approved and one changed permission, `microphone` false to true, because the microphone was granted after the node was approved and 14:57:14 was the first reconnect since; the stable build, installed back over this head, reconnects into the same `pending-reapproval` and shows the same row, so it does not come from this change.

Observed result: on the base, Talk ends 8 seconds into the stall; with this PR it drops audio past the budget with the notice, recovers when the answers arrive, and ends only after an append is unanswered for 30 seconds.

Regression tests: `TalkModeManagerTest.stalledAppendsDropInputPastThreeSecondsWithoutEndingTalk` feeds 31 frames while every append is unanswered, expects 30 appends, the fell-behind notice and Talk still on, then answers one append and expects the recovered notice and the next frame sent. It fails on the base (the 31st frame is sent) and passes with this PR. `WearRealtimeTalkControllerTest` has the same case for the Watch relay and also asserts the 30 second deadline on every append, which pins the deadline constant both relays share; it changes the relay's callback type, so it does not compile on the base. It also asserts the notice the relay sends to the Watch. `WearVoiceLayoutTest` has two new listening cases with each notice; they fail with the previous Watch screen code (the notice text is not on screen) and pass with this PR, and they check the text fits the round screen at font scale 1 and 1.3 in English and in the German locale (which shows the English text until the native locale refresh adds the translation).

Checks at this head: `./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.wear.*' --tests ai.openclaw.app.voice.TalkModeManagerTest --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.gateway.*' :wear:testDebugUnitTest :wear-shared:testDebugUnitTest :wear:lintDebug` (848 tests, 0 failures); `:app`, `:benchmark`, `:wear` and `:wear-shared` `ktlintCheck`; `node scripts/check-native-state-schema-version.mjs`; `pnpm native:i18n:verify`; `git diff --check`. `TalkModeManagerTest` was run again on the base with the test file carried over: the new test times out at 31 appends there, and the other 111 tests pass on both sides. The broad suites run in this PR's CI.

CI: the previous head failed `preflight` with "Native generated locale artifacts must be isolated from source changes", and `openclaw/ci-gate` failed because of it. That head carried English placeholders in 21 Watch `values-*/strings.xml` files. This head leaves those files unchanged, so the native locale refresh workflow fills them. `node scripts/ci-changed-scope.mjs --base 315fba74e12` exits 1 with that message on the previous head and exits 0 on this one.

CI at this head ([run 41094221772](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41094221772)): `preflight`, `android-test-play`, `android-test-third-party`, `android-test-wear`, `android-ktlint` and `android-access-native (16384, google_apis_ps16k)` passed. `android-access-native (4096, google_apis)` [failed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41094221772/job/124196671436) while installing the Android Emulator, before the emulator started or any test ran: `sdkmanager` reported "Error reading Zip content from a SeekableByteChannel" while preparing the Android Emulator package, and the job uploaded no test results. `openclaw/ci-gate` is red only because of that job. The same job passed on main in [run 41123124777](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41123124777/job/124295092007) (that run is red for unrelated Node and UI jobs). That job has not passed on this head; it needs a rerun.

The CI seconds below come from the JUnit reports of `android-test-play` (phone files) and `android-test-wear` (Watch file). CI tests the PR merged into main, where `TalkModeManagerTest` has 113 tests.

| Test file | Local wall (Gradle, this head) | CI seconds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `apps/android/app/src/test/java/ai/openclaw/app/voice/TalkModeManagerTest.kt` | 0.84 s for the new test (file 17.8 s, 112 tests, Gradle `--max-workers=4` with other modules running) | 0.77 s for the new test (file 14.8 s, 113 tests) |
| `apps/android/app/src/test/java/ai/openclaw/app/wear/WearRealtimeTalkControllerTest.kt` | 0.16 s for the new test (file 1.1 s, 26 tests) | 0.01 s for the new test (file 0.38 s, 26 tests) |
| `apps/android/wear/src/test/java/ai/openclaw/wear/WearVoiceLayoutTest.kt` | two more cases in the existing layout loop (file 7.9 s, 12 tests) | file 4.5 s, 12 tests |

Simplify pass: no change. One budget type serves both relays instead of two copies of the policy, and each new test covers a different relay. Against the merge base: production +147/−15 lines, tests +135/−6, docs +2, Watch English strings +2, translation source +4.

Not covered: no real phone and no real Watch. The phone runs used the Android 16 emulator. No Wear OS device is available, and no Wear OS emulator image is installed; pairing an emulator also needs the Play Store companion app and a Google sign-in. So there are no Watch screenshots or recordings with transport logs from a live call. The phone-side Watch relay is proven by its unit test, the Watch screen by Robolectric renders, and the phone-Watch payload against the latest stable by the codec run above. The device runs used an older Gateway build (see above); the change is client-only. Non-English locales show the English notices on both the phone and the Watch until the native locale refresh translates them.

Follow-up: the microphone transcription stream (`NodeRuntime` `appendTranscriptionAudio`, used by `MicCaptureManager`) also sends `talk.session.appendAudio` with an 8 second deadline. It is a separate feature outside the realtime Talk contract, so it is left for its own change.

prs.title: improve(ci): defer accelerated checkout startup on native Git
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Native Git PR provisioning loads the filesystem-acceleration implementation even when it will not use it. This adds startup work to every affected provisioning call, including the CI fixture suite.

## User Impact

Native provisioning avoids unnecessary module loading. Checkout behavior, ownership checks, hooks, sparse handling and accelerated provisioning remain unchanged. No application-facing change or operator action.

## Why This Change Was Made

Load the existing accelerated checkout owner only inside its current branch. A matched import-only replay reduces project modules from 747 to 723, with no added modules. This is a work-count result; runtime and billing savings are not measured.

Requested by @vincentkoc as part of the ongoing OpenClaw CI cost-reduction work. Production delta: +1/-1 line; existing test delta: +2/-2, with no additional test cases or fixture setup.

## Evidence

- The existing real `review-init` regression fails on base `38f68a10828da63adf76376ac974e92577b43f55` when its loader rejects eager acceleration imports, and passes with this change.
- Full provisioning suite: 16 passed, one platform skip, one existing APFS multi-checkout timeout (120s limit; case reported 139.95s). The identical case on unchanged base `38f68a10828d` also timed out (143.72s). The native-path regression and accelerated failure/retry case pass. No timeout or assertion was weakened.
- The PR wrapper runtime-import inventory passes (one targeted case). The APFS timeout remains an explicitly unresolved local fixture limitation; PR CI provides the applicable broader proof.
- Tooling-root typecheck, targeted lint, formatting and whitespace checks pass.
- Independent review and local ClawSweeper review of `38f68a10828d..d8571580ecc9` found no actionable correctness or security issues.
- Recorded normal CI run [42292321588](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42292321588) spent 301.73s in this fixture file. This motivates reducing repeated startup work; it does not quantify this patch's time saving.

prs.title: fix(matrix): stop treating unnamed two-member rooms as DMs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Before the Matrix `m.direct` cache has loaded, an unnamed room with exactly two members is classified as a direct message. Ingress no longer does that. A room is still a direct message when `is_direct` is set, when the room is stored in `m.direct`, when a recent invite was promoted, or when opted-in per-room recovery allows it.

## Evidence

On commit `567572f5adc51a` the direct-room tracker refuses an unnamed two-member room before the cache seeds, and it still accepts `is_direct` and `m.direct`. The QA harness sets the Matrix wildcard group to accept a reply without a mention, because those smoke rooms are groups now.

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/direct.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/crabline-transport.test.ts -t "does not treat an exact 2-member|still trusts is_direct|binds Matrix"
 ✓ createDirectRoomTracker > does not treat an exact 2-member room as a DM before the dm cache seeds 24ms
 ✓ createDirectRoomTracker > still trusts is_direct and m.direct before the dm cache seeds 1ms
 ✓ crabline transport > binds Matrix config and normalizes transport targets 3065ms
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
[test] passed 2 Vitest shards in 10.89s
```

QA smoke profile 6, which includes `matrix-restart-resume` and `matrix-restart-replay-dedupe`, passed on this head in CI: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41541733549/job/125608393398

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** An unnamed two-member Matrix room is not a direct message only because the direct-room cache has not seeded. Explicit direct signals still are.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS Darwin 27.0.0 arm64, Node v26.12.1, worktree at `567572f5adc51a` on `fix/matrix-dm-two-member-fallback`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/direct.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/crabline-transport.test.ts -t "does not treat an exact 2-member|still trusts is_direct|binds Matrix"`
- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output copied below.
```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/direct.test.ts extensions/qa-lab/src/crabline-transport.test.ts -t "does not treat an exact 2-member|still trusts is_direct|binds Matrix"
 ✓ does not treat an exact 2-member room as a DM before the dm cache seeds 24ms
 ✓ still trusts is_direct and m.direct before the dm cache seeds 1ms
 ✓ binds Matrix config and normalizes transport targets 3065ms
[test] passed 2 Vitest shards in 10.89s
```
- **Observed result after fix:** The unnamed room is not classified as a direct message, and `setAccountData` is not called. `is_direct` and `m.direct` still are direct before the cache seeds. The QA Matrix config sets `groups.*` to `requireMention: false`. CI smoke profile 6 passed.
- **What was not tested:** A live federated homeserver. Recent-invite promotion and opted-in per-room recovery are unchanged.

## Summary

Remove the pre-seed two-member fallback in `createDirectRoomTracker`. Recent-invite promotion, opted-in per-room recovery, and an explicit `is_direct` or `m.direct` signal are unchanged.

Crabline smoke rooms are ordinary groups. They only received replies because two members counted as a direct message. The harness sets the wildcard group so those rooms can reply without a mention pill. Product group rooms are unchanged.

prs.title: fix(imessage): group activation mode now controls replies
prs.body:
Related: #50490

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: iMessage groups keep replying to unmentioned messages after an owner runs `/activation mention`.

## User Impact

User impact: iMessage group owners can use `/activation mention` and `/activation always` to change reply behavior without editing channel config.

## Why This Change Was Made

The iMessage ingress gate only resolved `requireMention` from channel config and never consulted the routed session's persisted `groupActivation`. This change reads the activation mode from that exact session and gives it the same precedence over group config used by Telegram and WhatsApp. Authorized control commands still bypass mention gating so owners can switch modes.

## Evidence (exact head)

- Exact candidate head: `f1c66eb055618f0aa79505abd7bfacb1498445c8`; frozen base: `432ade6f500de6cdb0bcd4b0948a07bf466672f1`; clean merge tree: `de8299f6f3c4776fce1a0e00db9843f8289c8f7a`.
- Focused test command: `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/imessage/src/monitor/inbound-processing.activation.test.ts extensions/imessage/src/monitor.watch-subscribe-retry.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/session-store-runtime.test.ts src/plugins/runtime/runtime-agent.session-patch.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/commands-session.activation.test.ts` → 5 files, **43/43 passing** on the merged tree. Core and extension TypeScript gates and touched-file formatting pass under Node 26.7.0.
- Production path exercised by the mock-Gateway proof: `resolveIMessageInboundDecision` in `extensions/imessage/src/monitor/inbound-processing.ts` → `createIMessageGroupActivationResolver` in `group-activation.ts` → runtime `getSessionEntryInWorker` → SQLite worker-backed read; admission uses `createHostChannelIngressRuntime`. The test calls the production decision function with a routed group and real isolated SQLite store, not Apple's Messages transport.
- The proof harness writes persisted activation entries through `runtime.agent.session.upsertSessionEntry` (simulating the command's persistence), rather than issuing live `/activation` commands. Command owner-gating/persistence is separately covered by `commands-session.activation.test.ts`. This distinction matters: it is not a single end-to-end live Apple/command receipt.
- The exact frozen-base deterministic preflight is green after a lockfile-frozen dependency refresh. It passes extension production/test type graphs, touched-file formatting/lint, dead exports, architecture/ratchet guards, import cycles, and `git diff --check`. The refresh exposed and the branch repaired a strict session-entry test fixture that lacked required identity/timestamp fields and literal activation typing.
- Earlier sanitized behavior receipt (the production behavior path is unchanged by the frozen-base replay):

```json
{ "verdict": "PASS", "base": "9bb171bf39b98a6965a47ab4f636e35a5701b409", "head": "68a07b52e5881bc9294ec1ddaa548a605ad7a433", "harness": "real SQLite session store + worker-backed read + mock Gateway iMessage admission", "sessionKey": "agent:main:imessage:group:99", "decisions": { "mention": "drop", "always": "dispatch", "restoredMention": "drop" } }
```

- Reviewer follow-ups: no-mention diagnostic now explains `/activation always` precedence, covered by the monitor test; the public asynchronous worker-read API has a narrowed, documented parameter/store-selection contract. The monitor test fixture now provides its required session runtime and locally passes the hosted-red shard.
- Hosted CI and maintainer proof/compatibility review on this new head remain authoritative; this evidence does not claim their acceptance.

prs.title: fix: personal memory hooks miss authenticated webchat users
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes personal-memory hooks receiving no user identity for authenticated Control UI turns, causing integrations such as Honcho to fall back to an owner peer even when the transcript identifies a different person.

## User Impact

Hooks can observe the verified initiating user for each accepted UI turn, including successive turns by different people in one shared session. This does not add command, tool, or MCP permissions. Expired personal bindings skip hook dispatch or discard returned enrichment instead of becoming anonymous owner turns.

Attribution remains per accepted initiating turn; this does not add separate authorship for every coauthor merged through steering. No configuration or data migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Control UI intentionally omits the legacy transport sender to preserve authority boundaries. The fix carries a live, host-bound profile observation through the existing run projections solely for hook context. Dispatch rechecks it before invoking a plugin and before accepting returned results, including cached contexts and delegated ingress. The private observer reads in the captured ingress async context, so a later agent tool context does not misclassify the original human request. Live grant checks still run on every read; plugin callbacks never run in that captured context. Existing channel senders retain precedence, and the private resolver is removed before plugin delivery.

An existing pure finalize-result merger is moved unchanged to keep the edited hook runner within the repository line-cap ratchet.

## Evidence

- Regression reproduced against the original Gateway turn preparation path: an authenticated profile was recorded, but the hook sender was undefined.

prs.title: fix: OpenClaw ID sign-out and sign-in asks to re-approve an already-approved browser
prs.body:
Related: Linear OCF-495

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: signing out of OpenClaw ID and back in on an already-approved browser asks the Gateway owner to re-approve that browser, under the title "Approve the new role", even though it asks for the same role and scopes as before.

## User Impact

User impact: an OpenClaw ID browser that signs out and back in reconnects with the access it was already approved for, without a prompt. A new role, added scopes, or a different device still needs owner approval. When a prompt is needed, the Control UI now says what is being requested instead of always saying "new role".

## Why This Change Was Made

OpenClaw ID remote sign-out revokes the browser's Gateway tokens but intentionally keeps its device approved. Effective roles only count active tokens, so the next connect reported the approved `operator` role as a `role-upgrade`. No auto-approval lane accepts a repair with that reason, so it fell through to a manual prompt. This is the generic re-pair path, triggered by OpenClaw ID sign-out. It is not specific to the tunnel, and it is not caused by the `trusted-proxy` approval provenance.

- **Gateway:** on the OpenClaw ID lane only, a same-key reconnect for a role that the device row already approves gets that role's token back. The scopes are first capped by membership and connection, and the token is issued only when they fit inside the row's approved scopes. Anything broader stays a manual owner decision. Generic trusted-proxy `deviceAutoApprove`, remote-ingress, local and node lanes are unchanged.
- **Approval kernel:** a revoked token's old scopes no longer set the scopes of its replacement when the request names scopes. The new token gets what the request asked for, so a narrower reconnect after sign-out is not blocked by the old grant.
- **Connect error details:** these now describe the merged pending request that approval would grant. If the request carries an earlier role the device doesn't have, that role is reported.
- **Control UI:** the login gate titles the prompt by what approval adds. "Approve this browser again" means the same access as before. A scope prompt names the added scopes. "Approve the new role" names the role.

Accepted edge case: an owner's explicit `devices revoke` of an OpenClaw ID browser is also restored on that browser's next connect. A fresh key from the same admitted principal is already auto-paired on this lane, so revocation was never a lasting block there. Removing the OpenClaw ID membership still refuses admission.

## Evidence

- Reproduced first through the real WebSocket connect path over the OpenClaw ID tunnel test harness. The owner reconnected after token revocation and got `reason: "role-upgrade"`, the same role and the same six scopes. That test now passes.
- `src/gateway/server.auth.openclaw-id-tunnel.test.ts`: owner and operator-member restores; fewer scopes (only those are issued); more than approved still pending; a merged pending `node` role is named and stays pending. The last two cases from review fail without the repair.
- `src/gateway/server.auth.trusted-proxy-device-autoapprove.test.ts`: on the non-OpenClaw ID trusted-proxy lane, a revoked token's reconnect with the same access still waits for the owner (flag-off guard).
- `ui/src/components/login-gate.test.ts`: restore, added-scope and new-role titles.
- `pnpm check:changed`: everything passes (core/UI typecheck, core lint, dead-export scan, ratchets, i18n catalog) except `changelog attributions`, which fails identically on main (`CHANGELOG/records/2026.11.1.md`, untouched here).
- `check:test-lines-ratchet`: this PR adds 140 test lines with a matching allocation (`config/test-lines-allocations/openclaw-id-signout-restore.txt`). The tree stays 5 over the ceiling, which main already is on its own.
- UI oxlint on the changed UI files: clean. Scoped suites on HEAD: tunnel, trusted-proxy auto-approve, Control UI auth, device pairing, ingress approval, local/trusted-CIDR node pairing, remote sign-out, login gate, connect-error, gateway-store auth/retention. All pass.
- Independent security review (isolated, read-only) found two P2s: a narrower reconnect was refused by the revoked token's scopes, and "nothing new" copy could hide a merged role. Both are fixed and covered by tests. Re-review: clean, with no P0–P2 findings.

Login gate before and after, using the same `role-upgrade` request (same role and same six scopes as in the issue):

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Same role, same six scopes (the OCF-495 case) | ![before: Approve the new role](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/da1daa69-ea38-495b-9bea-15735b2e1bc5) | ![after: Approve this browser again](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2f939eb9-b0b4-4819-af8a-5aec6429833c) |
| Role not yet approved (a real new role) | ![before: Approve the new role](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7f65aeb5-3781-4ba4-99da-c3e5dc59877c) | ![after: Approve the new role, naming operator](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bad753c2-7703-4bcc-b185-275e7d890f4c) |

Captured from the production Control UI build with a mocked Gateway connect rejection (`role-upgrade`, request `7f6e33d0…`), on main `936f38793bab` and on this branch.

Not done: a live sign-out/sign-in cycle on staging gateway3. The tunnel tests use the canonical token revocation that sign-out performs.

prs.title: fix: Talk consults fail with unsupported thinking preferences
prs.body:
Closes #194183

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: chat-backed Talk consultations fail before agent execution when the configured thinking preference is unsupported by the consult target model.

## User Impact

Talk can consult the selected agent without requiring one global thinking setting to fit every model. Supported choices and ordinary explicit user-command validation remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The internal Talk setting is a machine-selected preference, not a user command targeting a particular model. Keep the normalization switch internal, outside the public plugin options. Mark only trusted internal Talk requests with an explicit preference for normalization, then use the existing thinking policy after the actual execution model and runtime are resolved.

Keep the original preference for per-candidate fallback normalization; do not persist the normalized value or clamp inherited session preferences.

## Evidence

- Stock admission source: **1 failed, 5 passed**. The new unsupported-`off` case returns before the agent executes.
- Patched admission: **6 passed**. Covers unsupported `off` → `low`, supported `low`/`high`, retained original preference, inherited preferences, and ordinary explicit rejection. Command: `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts --maxWorkers=2 -t 'resolves Talk preference|validates .* thinking|does not clamp inherited thinking'`.
- Trusted request policy: **4 passed**, covering explicit Talk, absent preference, unrelated internal tool, and ordinary input.
- Chat dispatch integration: **1 passed**, verifying ordinary thinking metadata stays out of command text and does not opt into normalization.
- Scoped lint and `git diff --check` pass.
AI-assisted implementation.


The 72-line allocation matches the added regression coverage. Merged current main without rewriting branch history (head `69543ab3ced6`). Full Git-index test-line check passes: **6,556,085 lines / 6,556,093 ceiling** (8 spare). Admission regressions rerun on this head: **6 passed**. Exact-head CI is running.

**Real shipped Talk consultation: stock rejects, patched returns the agent result.** Both isolated Gateways used `consultThinkingLevel: off`, the same authorized `opencode-go/grok-4.7` target and the same question. Its current live-advertised ladder excludes `off`; both overlays pin that same ladder to align provider metadata across builds.

- **Stock:** final rejection `Thinking level "off" is not supported for opencode-go/grok-4.7`, zero model tokens.
- **Patched:** real Grok agent lifecycle, streamed output, and final reply **`TALK_CONSULT_OK_194184`**.
- [Live proof, exact builds, requests, and redacted event excerpts](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/pr-evidence-talk-thinking-194184/LIVE-PROOF.md). This uses the shipped legacy Talk tool-call ingress without an audio session; it proves consultation dispatch and returned result, not audio playback. The four changed production files in the tested candidate are byte-identical to this PR head.
- The normalization switch is now in `InternalReplySessionOptions`, not the public plugin contract. The low-value manual fallback-helper test was removed.

Report provenance: the original report was the November 6 task brief recording three rejections of `off` for `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`. No production log excerpt was captured. The stock-versus-patched admission results above independently reproduce the rejection.

prs.title: fix(codex): preserve one-shot client shutdown grace
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A one-shot Codex run can finish its native turn and then fail during client cleanup. Releasing the caller-owned client lease invokes `close()` first, starting memoized transport shutdown with the default one-second grace. The later `closeAndWait()` requests the existing five-second grace but joins the shutdown already in progress.

## User Impact

A native process that exits cleanly after three seconds now receives the intended five-second grace instead of being escalated after one second. Cleanup still fails if termination cannot be confirmed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Start and await the caller-owned client's existing bounded close policy before releasing its lease; release exactly once in `finally`, including rejected close and uncertain receipts. The authorized sandbox lease still closes first, and shared-client retirement retains its existing completion and rejection behavior. No deadlines, process-containment checks, persistence, authentication, or permissions change.

The related client-selection fix in #193461 is already on the base. This addresses ordering after a caller-owned client has been selected.

## Evidence

Exact reviewed source: `3cfc255a4bbbe891823d20f1ea4467f0b6248156`, based on `36a1c58e91dd9ae991edd76f9ccbfdcd056c5fa0`.

[Focused hosted proof](https://github.com/moonlitnayeem-p/openclaw/actions/runs/42314153758) passed in 551 job seconds on a standard Ubuntu runner with Node 24.22.2. The workflow verifies the checked-out source SHA, direct parent, exactly three changed paths, and their content hashes. Its separate fork-only workflow commit is not part of this PR.

- **Red/green:** restoring only the original production file makes the named delayed-exit case fail because process inspection occurs before the intended grace ends. The patched owning cleanup suite passes **14/14 cases, zero skips**. The new cases cover delayed clean exit and exactly-once lease release after rejected or uncertain cleanup. The synthetic PID has both process inspection and OS signalling stubbed. Original-source command: 98.11 seconds; patched suite: 89.45 seconds, including worker preparation.
- **Types and lint:** selected SDK declaration preparation; semantic typechecking of the official generated Codex production entry graph; a focused projection of the official extension-test graph; exact compiler file-list inclusion checks for both changed files; normal type-aware lint using `extensions/tsconfig.json`; CI formatter parity; and `git diff --check` all pass. The semantic checks do not claim the separate boundary worker's dependency/admission receipt.
- **Build:** the official single-package runtime check reports one publishable Codex plugin and one npm runtime built successfully. This is targeted Codex package proof, not a full repository or release build.
- **Live evidence:** the equivalent change on a task-owned OpenClaw 2026.11.1 installation completed a native Codex response and a subsequent installed MCP tool read with exit code 0 and no cleanup warning. This is separate from the current-source build above. The change does not claim to resolve independent catalog-startup or transcript-worker delays.

The [proof artifact](https://github.com/moonlitnayeem-p/openclaw/actions/runs/42314153758/artifacts/13549998762) contains synthetic test reports, timings, type/lint/build logs, and the verified source manifest. Its SHA-256 is `6738de4a47742ce49c5a0b04c0cdd5ccb27d5f2ea26ba36d2e83686b7fc68cb5`.

Independent source/fixture review passed. The production owner remains within its existing line limit; a separate allocation records exactly 88 added regression lines. Broader upstream PR CI and maintainer review remain the landing gates.

prs.title: improve: evaluate phone-first Android release builds
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

**Experiment concluded: candidate rejected.** The candidate and temporary workflow have been removed. This PR is closed without a production change.

Android release bundle builds spend most of their final work compiling, linting and shrinking the phone app. This experiment tested whether requesting the phone bundle before Wear reduces the complete build time.

## User Impact

No published behavior changes during this experiment. The candidate changes only the order of the two existing Gradle bundle tasks; production signing, checks, versioning, atomic Play upload and Wear-first Firebase distribution remain unchanged. No uploads are performed by the benchmark.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both bundles already share one Gradle invocation and compile `wear-shared` once. Reordering the existing work is a smaller experiment than adding parallelism, workers or caches. The temporary manual diagnostic job and script were removed with the rejected candidate. The [committed workload](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/5f277672c243119089857e02dcf6ce41fc920d06/scripts/bench-android-bundle-order.mjs) remains available at the measured revision.

## Evidence

Acceptance rule recorded before measurements:

- Workload: signing preflight, the real phone/Wear release bundle tasks, and verification of both AAB signatures. Source is frozen at `f99d785d2ac6269b37a1c88eb8d5ef2283b76b99`. Both orders use identical synthetic version/build metadata and one disposable signing key per pair, with no production credentials or uploads.
- Environment: the current release runner (`blacksmith-8vcpu-ubuntu-2404`), pinned Java/SDK/Gradle, production read-only Gradle dependency cache setup, task-output caching disabled. Five serial pairs, alternating which order runs first. Each sample starts at the same filesystem paths from pristine source/dependency-cache snapshots with no previous outputs or live Java processes. Cache download/setup and resetting seeds are outside the measured bundle window. This measures dependency-warm, output-cold builds; no claim about an empty dependency cache.
- Metrics: bundle wall time and full preflight/build/signature-check time; median, nearest-rank p95 (the maximum with five samples), spread and paired deltas. Record one-second CPU, Java RSS, available memory, pressure and cgroup events. Retain standard Gradle profiles and exact executed task/outcome inventories.
- Keep only if all ten samples pass, task coverage/cache outcomes match, the candidate improves median bundle time by at least **5% and five seconds**, and wins at least **four of five pairs**. Candidate p95 may not exceed baseline by more than **5%**; full measured-stage median may not regress by more than **2%**. Peak aggregate Java RSS and Java CPU time may not regress by more than **10%**, and no OOM or memory-pressure failure is acceptable. Any metric worsening by **20%** stops the change. Otherwise reject the production reorder.

Pre-measurement checks: 11 focused release-artifact/Fastlane gate tests passed; workflow actionlint/zizmor, focused lint, formatting, syntax and diff checks passed. Local AutoReview (Codex, P0–P2) reviewed the complete candidate against `f99d785d2ac6269b37a1c88eb8d5ef2283b76b99`: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. The release helper dry run selects exactly the phone and Wear AAB tasks. Measured results follow; this experiment will not be marked ready.

**Measured results**

[Benchmark run 42312349744](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42312349744), measured tooling `5f277672c243119089857e02dcf6ce41fc920d06`; all five serial pairs completed. No builds were uploaded.

| Pair | First order | Wear-first bundle | Phone-first bundle | Phone-first saving |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 01 | wear | 243.402s | 190.146s | +53.256s (+21.88%) |
| 02 | phone | 162.876s | 168.754s | -5.878s (-3.61%) |
| 03 | wear | 159.592s | 158.389s | +1.203s (+0.75%) |
| 04 | phone | 145.386s | 139.559s | +5.827s (+4.01%) |
| 05 | wear | 152.731s | 154.439s | -1.708s (-1.12%) |

| Metric (five samples per order) | Wear-first | Phone-first |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Bundle median / p95 | 159.592s / 243.402s | 158.389s / 190.146s |
| Preflight + build + signatures median / p95 | 167.538s / 255.849s | 167.132s / 199.799s |
| Peak Java RSS median / maximum | 7.057 GiB / 7.166 GiB | 7.011 GiB / 7.078 GiB |
| Sampled Java CPU median / p95 | 1057.520s / 1587.510s | 1080.460s / 1283.660s |

Bundle ranges: 145.386–243.402s Wear-first; 139.559–190.146s phone-first. With five samples, nearest-rank p95 is the maximum; the first baseline remains included. Median paired saving was 1.203s.

**Decision:** reject the reorder. Median bundle time improved only **1.203s (0.75%)**, below the predeclared 5% and five-second requirements, and phone-first won **three of five pairs**, below four. The complete measured-stage median improved only 0.406s (0.24%). Peak memory stayed similar; sampled Java CPU median increased 2.17%. The large first-pair saving did not repeat consistently. No runner, heap, parallelism, task, cache or upload behavior changes are being shipped.

**Build and resource proof:** all ten bundle invocations and all twenty individual AAB signature checks passed. Every build reported 149 actionable tasks (146 executed, three up-to-date). The authoritative Gradle profiles have identical 163 task/outcome rows across all ten samples, including non-actionable tasks. Every pair restored the same exact dependency-cache key, and every host exposed eight usable CPUs. The minimum observed available host memory was 22.760 GiB; no build reported an OOM. Cgroup memory-event files were unavailable, so no cgroup OOM-counter claim is made. One-second Java CPU/RSS samples can miss process-exit tails.

**Harness failure disclosed:** the workflow conclusion is `failure`: pairs 02–05 failed only after both builds, both signature checks and daemon cleanup passed. The temporary guard compared repeated `--info` console task headings, whose repetition varies with interleaved logging. Direct comparison of the full Gradle profile task/outcome inventories proves the selected work and cache outcomes were identical. These are successful build measurements with a failed log-parser assertion, not a green workflow or a repaired product failure. No job was rerun to obtain green status. The discarded temporary workflow and parser will not be deployed. Raw logs, resource samples and profiles are in the run's five benchmark artifacts (seven-day retention).

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway administrators currently have no Profile UI for explicitly associating a channel sender with a personal OpenClaw Profile.

## User Impact

A connected administrator with the negotiated `operator.admin` scope can view, add, and remove exact channel/account/sender identity links for their currently authenticated personal Profile. The Shared Gateway Owner is not a link target. A link is an administrator-entered association; it does not verify control of the external account.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Profile page now exposes the Gateway's existing list/link/unlink methods. It adds no backend method, identity store, or automatic name/email matching. Failed writes preserve entered identifiers, and stale results cannot update a replaced Profile or connection. Linking does not merge people, rewrite transcript attribution, assign session ownership, or change session visibility.

Fixes #194330

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Android shows an unexplained total-refresh warning when model discovery fails but a populated model catalog remains available.

<!--

## User Impact

User impact: users keep their model choices and see a bounded provider or native-discovery warning when that scope is known, with an honest partial-catalog fallback when it is not. Genuine refresh failures remain visible.

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."

## Why This Change Was Made

The catalog attempt owner records provider/native failures, including an unknown scope, but previously published only an aggregate flag. This draft derives live `refreshFailures` from that owner, carries the facts through the decision adapter and RPC projection, and updates Android to consume them without changing authentication outcomes or model eligibility. Partial recovery now publishes a status change even while another acquisition remains failed.

The public projection omits raw errors, credentials, endpoint/profile-shaped labels, and provider identities outside the requested view. Android honors these sanitized scopes rather than recovering hidden labels from legacy outcomes; legacy fallback labels must be present in the returned catalog.

**Related work:** #194338 overlaps the same producer and proposes synthesizing `providerOutcomes`. This is an alternative, not a parallel auth-state fix: it retains ready/auth outcomes, distinguishes native and unknown acquisition scopes, and includes Android handling. Reconcile the two approaches before either is readied. #159670 was also inspected; its catalog-auth retention change is not copied here.

- **Red/green regression:** the final Gateway regression file on unchanged base `36a1c58e91dd9ae991edd76f9ccbfdcd056c5fa0` fails 3 assertions for missing diagnostics (6 existing cases pass), including the real `models.list` handler with synthetic context. Restoring the exact fixed source was SHA-256 verified. The fixed server owner/adapter/result/handler/native-lifecycle fixture suites pass **49 tests across 5 files**. These are synthetic server proofs, not Android-device or live-deployment proof.

prs.title: fix(deepinfra): honor thinking off for Nemotron 3.5 Super VL
prs.body:
Closes #192978

## What Problem This Solves

Explicit thinking `off` for DeepInfra `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3.5-Super-VL` was lost before request serialization. The default-on model received neither a disabled-reasoning selector nor an equivalent off request.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing DeepInfra wrapper now sends `reasoning: { enabled: false }` only for explicit off, the exact Nemotron model, and the existing OpenAI Completions API. [The model-specific vendor documentation](https://deepinfra.com/blog/nvidia-nemotron-3-5-super-vl-release) supports `reasoning_effort: "none"`; [DeepInfra's reasoning documentation](https://docs.deepinfra.com/chat/reasoning) explicitly equates it to `reasoning.enabled: false`.

Enabled thinking, unspecified thinking, other model dialects, Anthropic caching, API routing, shared reasoning normalization and model/default policy are unchanged. No new SDK API, config, schema, auth or retry behavior. Both original ooiuuii commits and credit are preserved.

## Evidence

[Maintainer current-main/built-Gateway HTTP proof, request hashes and runnable collector](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192979#issuecomment-6699033090)

Secretless Docker `node:24.22.1`; independently installed/built current main `f99d785d2ac6269b37a1c88eb8d5ef2283b76b99` and candidate. The shipped CLI runs `infer model run --gateway` through an actual built Gateway/embedded raw agent turn and the actual DeepInfra plugin against a faithful local OpenAI-compatible SSE fixture.

- Main twice, explicit off: outgoing request omits the off selector.
- Candidate twice: outgoing request adds exactly `reasoning: { enabled: false }`, with no scalar `reasoning_effort`. No other off-payload field changes.
- Explicit high, CLI default and another DeepInfra model (DeepSeek off): **full request bodies byte-identical** across main/candidate.
- All ten runs exit 0, send one local HTTP request, consume a valid SSE reply and return the expected final CLI text.
- Exact binary config/SQLite resolution, explicit isolated profiles/HOME/state/config/workspace, unique ports and unchanged config bytes are recorded.

This is a serialization/response-consumption proof, **not a live-vendor inference, token, entitlement or billing claim**. The omitted CLI flag retains the Gateway's existing medium default; wrapper-level undefined-thinking coverage separately preserves the provider-default selector behavior.

## Checks and simplification

The 106-line new reasoning suite and allocation file are removed. All six reasoning/compatibility scenarios now share the existing cache/request wrapper fixtures. Existing useful cache-retention, TTL, system-block, native-API passthrough and managed string-only controls remain; no unrelated tests were cut to buy budget.

- Final cache-wrapper/index/provider-contract suite: **31 passed**.
- Same final wrapper suite on frozen main: **13 passed, 1 failed**—only Nemotron off, expected disabled reasoning but received undefined.
- Scoped touched-test/provider typecheck: passed.
- Canonical extension typed lint and formatting: passed.
- Against merge base `e629e2a6eaceb7b62fa935177967687847b5d669`: production **+11/-0**, tests **+111/-112 (net -1)**, docs **+9**. No allocation.

The final follow-up only changes tests/allocation metadata relative to the runtime exercised above. Fresh exact-head review and CI are requested after push. The lead maintainer merges, not this worker.

prs.title: fix(ui): Control UI breaks under browser auto-translate
prs.body:
Closes #191961

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Control UI shows a "panel failed to load" error in Edge when browser auto-translate is on.

## User Impact

The Control UI no longer breaks under auto-translate. It already localizes itself. Browser translate of chat text is off for the page.

## Why This Change Was Made

Auto-translate rewrites text nodes under the Solid renderer, so `insertBefore` throws. The shell now sets `translate="no"` and `notranslate`.

## Evidence

- New test fails on main, passes here.
- Not tried in Edge: headless can't run its translate. Two reporters on the issue confirmed translate as the cause.

## Proof (partial)

Built Control UI (Sessions page) in real headless Chrome through the UI e2e harness, with a simulated translator that wraps every text node the browser reports as translatable in `<font>`, like a page translator:

```
            html translate attr   html.translate   text nodes replaced
main        null                  true             109
this PR     "no"                  false            0
```

Not shown: Edge's own translator, and the original `insertBefore` crash. Neither reproduces in headless, and the simulation did not trigger it on main either. This only shows the opt-out reaches the built page.

<details>
<summary>Agent transcript (trimmed)</summary>

**User:** Pick the open issue you can fix most confidently with no PR yet, and open a PR.

**Agent:** Checked open bug issues for linked PRs. #192031, #186832, #173611 already have PRs. #191043 and #193262 need maintainer decisions or Windows repro. #191961 has a confirmed cause in the thread: Edge translate rewrites text nodes while `<html lang="en">` is hardcoded.

**Agent:** `translate.ts` already sets `lang` at runtime, but Edge decides at load. Chose `translate="no"` plus `<meta name="google" content="notranslate">` in `ui/index.html`. Tradeoff: no browser translation of chat text.

**Agent:** Added a test beside the `index.html` boot test. Red on main, green with the change. `oxfmt` clean.

</details>

prs.title: fix(ios): sidebar rows jump when sessions arrive above the viewport
prs.body:
Closes #194322

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: iOS sidebar sessions jump when new pinned sessions arrive above a scrolled viewport.

## User Impact

Users keep their place while new sessions arrive. Layout, typography, appearance, and session actions stay unchanged. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve the visible session position by compensating for row movement above the viewport. Do not compensate at the top or during active scrolling. The independent session-button memoization and equality suite were removed after review; the original in-place button is restored.

Known limitation: deleting the chosen anchor row is not corrected.

## Evidence

- **Running app, stock:** real onboarding, sidebar drag, and three pinned-session insertions through a synthetic loopback Gateway. Same-row accessibility Y **94.333 → 232.333**, a **138 pt** jump; the <2pt assertion fails.
- **Running app, anchoring only:** identical runner and scenario; Y **94.333 → 94.333**, effectively **zero drift**. **1 XCTest passes, 0 failures.** No screenshot-mode roster injection or product instrumentation.
- The tracked Work33 frame starts clipped beneath the header. The screenshots independently show visible Work32–19 staying put with the fix and moving down on stock.
- **24 focused tests in 2 suites pass**: insertion compensation and typography.
- Pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.1: **0/3 files require formatting**. Strict SwiftLint 0.65.1: **0 violations in 2 production files**, using repository configurations. Simulator lint phases bypass baseline violations; scoped checks ran separately.
- Stock XCTest restarted after its assertion failure and printed an empty suite; the wrapper incorrectly counted zero tests. The executed failure and screenshots establish the regression.

These are running-app simulator captures, not physical-phone or deleted-anchor proof. Prior-head CI passed; new-head CI is pending.

AI-assisted implementation and testing. [Sanitized validation record](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/blob/5ede717fce3/EVIDENCE.md).

prs.title: feat: watch a running command automation's output live in the Control UI
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a long-running command automation shows nothing in Automations, Run history until it finishes, so an operator cannot tell what a multi-hour job is doing. Only Settings, Logs is live, and it does not contain the script's output.

## User Impact

User impact: while a command automation runs, its Run history shows a **Live output** panel that follows the combined stdout and stderr like `tail -f`. It auto-scrolls, pauses when you scroll up (with a **Jump to latest** button), and stops polling while the browser tab is hidden. When the run ends the panel goes away and the recorded run appears in the list as before. Gateway clients can read the same tail with `cron.liveOutput`.

Risks and limits:
- Live text is redacted with the tool-payload policy, so it can be masked more strictly than the recorded summary of the same run. The recorded summary is unchanged. A private key is masked across polls; one whose start was already dropped from a full tail is masked only while its end line is still held.
- Only the most recent output is kept: at most 256 KiB, or `payload.outputMaxBytes` when that is smaller. The panel keeps the last 2000 lines.
- Agent-turn runs have no live panel. Their transcript is still available only after the run is recorded (see Evidence).

## Why This Change Was Made

The Gateway keeps a fixed-size in-memory ring for the active run. The command runner owns it and discards it in its existing `finally`, so exit, timeout, abort and spawn failure all clean up through one path. `cron.liveOutput` (`operator.read`, same job visibility checks as `cron.get`) returns complete lines from a byte cursor, so a reconnect neither loses nor repeats lines. The panel reuses the existing visible-poll and stream-auto-follow helpers. Cursor polling, like `logs.tail`, keeps the Gateway free of timers and per-chunk broadcasts when nobody is watching. No config key, schema or migration; `cron.history` and `cron.runs` are unchanged.

Size: about 360 lines of new production code across 3 modules, about 560 lines of tests, small edits to existing files, plus regenerated validator files.

## Evidence

Before and after screenshots (Run history of a running command job; Live output panel; paused with **Jump to latest**; hand-off when the run ends) are in the first comment below. The extra Error row in the before shot is from restarting the throwaway Gateway while testing.


- Throwaway Gateway (own state dir, port 28789, loopback, throwaway token) and a real headless Chrome against the built Control UI. A command job printed a line per second for 60 to 90 s. Follow reads returned only new lines, replaying a cursor was idempotent, stderr was interleaved in order, a fake `token=sk-...` was masked, and `active` flipped to `false` exactly when `state.runningAtMs` cleared, including after a job timeout. The recorded run was unchanged.
- Tests: buffer bounds and fixed memory, cursor, drop-oldest, UTF-8 safety, redaction (including a private key across polls) and escape stripping, cleanup on exit, timeout, abort and spawn failure; the gateway method (follow, inactive, validation, visibility, access closed mid-read); the UI line bound and panel (follow, hidden tab, hand-off, still polling before the command starts, jump to latest).
- Review round: fixes covered by focused tests and typecheck only; the throwaway Gateway run above predates them. `check:changed` passes except the dead export scan, which flags `flattenRun` in `scripts/lib/catalog-compare-released-diff.mts` (already on main, not in this PR).
- Checks run: `pnpm gateway:validators:check`, `pnpm protocol-registry:check`, the protocol since-guard (new method vintage `2026.10`), the native protocol check, scoped core and UI tests (including the existing `command-runner`, `cron.history` and `cron.runs` suites), `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `pnpm ui:i18n:verify`, and `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base upstream/main` (all lanes passed). I re-ran the validators, registry and new tests after the work finished.
- Agent-turn runs: not changed. Run history rows, including the transcript binding `cron.history` needs, are written when the run completes, so an in-flight run has no row and **View transcript** is unavailable. Live agent transcripts need an early binding row from the run owner and a follow protocol for transcript pages, which is a separate change.
- Local review: autoreview and local ClawSweeper were not run. The author read the full diff against the simplify checklist before opening.

prs.title: feat(mattermost): add allowBots mention policy
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Mattermost has no equivalent of Slack's `allowBots` policy. When thread participation is enabled, implicit activation also applies to other bot authors, so an allowlisted bot can trigger a turn in an engaged thread without a new explicit mention.

## Solution

- Add `allowBots: true | false | "mentions"` at account and group scope.
- Identify bot authors through the post's `from_bot` property (both boolean and Mattermost's string form) or the Mattermost user's `is_bot` field.
- In `"mentions"` mode, require explicit activation for bot authors even when thread participation would admit a human follow-up. Authorized control-command behavior is preserved.
- Keep `allowBots: false` for disabling bot-triggered turns and the default `true` for existing behavior.
- Avoid a new sender lookup in the default mode when Mattermost already supplies `sender_name`.
- Document the setting and regenerate channel config metadata.

Human thread participation and existing sender/channel restrictions remain unchanged.

The intentional `+4` channel config-surface entries are the root/account and group variants of the new `allowBots` policy (including account-scoped group overrides). This is required for Slack-compatible policy precedence, not an unrelated budget increase; the generated config docs baseline is refreshed with `pnpm config:docs:gen`.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test extensions/mattermost/src/config-schema.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 19/19 passed on the fixed tree; the same regression test fails on the pre-fix schema (1 failed / 18 passed), then passes after restoration.
- `pnpm config:channels:check` — passed.
- `node scripts/run-format.mts --check <changed files>` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Independent read-only review (xai/grok-4.7) found two P1 issues; both were fixed and covered with regressions for string/boolean `from_bot`, failed sender lookup, and group precedence. No post-fix independent re-review is claimed.
- Live Mattermost API contract check: the tested bot account returns `is_bot: true`; the tested human account omits the flag, which the `=== true` check handles.

## Local environment gaps / CI-required proof

- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/monitor-posts.bot-threads.test.ts` includes the behavioral regressions, but the local suite did not start: its compiled worker was killed with exit 137 twice on the 8 GiB host, including with a 2 GiB heap cap. No passing behavioral result is claimed locally.

prs.title: fix(discord): preserve fenced code after marker lines with trailing text
prs.body:
Closes #127656

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

Allow edits from maintainers is enabled.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users receiving long Discord code blocks would see later code rendered as prose when the block contained a fence-like line with trailing text, such as ` ```not-a-close`. The same defect affects ordinary channel messages and webhook replies.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discord's chunker closed a block after checking only the fence marker and its length. Its closing rule now matches the existing shared Markdown contract: the marker must match, be at least as long as the opener, and have only spaces or tabs after it. CRLF fence lines are recognized, while backtick-containing info strings are not misclassified as block openers. The outer reasoning italic marker is separated before scanning, and generated closing italics are placed on a separate line after code fences with space reserved in the transport budget.

The repair stays in the Discord chunk owner; no SDK, dependency, or configuration changes. Separating the existing reasoning wrapper preserves its formatting contract while enforcing actual fence endings. Wrapper restoration also runs when only one nonempty message survives, placing the closing delimiter before trailing whitespace.

## User Impact

Code remains fenced across Discord message boundaries, including code that looks like a Markdown heading. Actual closing fences still return following text to prose, and outgoing messages remain within the transport limit.

## Evidence

- September 12 integration: rebased onto main `366335ad9cd6`, preserving the allocation improvements from #142447 and all upstream webhook tests. The only manual conflict joined independent test additions; `git range-diff` confirms unchanged repair logic. **237 tests passed across four suites**, covering chunking, ordinary sends, webhooks, and native-command replies. Targeted formatting, typed lint, `git diff --check`, and a fresh independent branch review passed for the rebased candidate `e211bb56f01b`. [GitHub CI passed on this head](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34673184167).

- Before the repair: the three affected suites reported **9 failed, 193 passed**. The new failures cover false closers, CRLF, channel HTTP payloads, and webhook HTTP payloads.
- At the previously reviewed head `8a07c53835eb`: three suites reported **207 passed** under Vitest 5.0.0, including an additional regression for reasoning markers after synthetic closing fences. The tests use `mdast-util-from-markdown` as an independent semantic oracle and capture requests through local HTTP servers using the real Discord send paths.
- Review follow-up: the single-surviving-chunk regression failed for both `Reasoning:` and `Thinking...` before correction (**2 failed, 103 passed** in the chunk suite). Both now parse as actual emphasis, including when trailing blank lines are discarded. A further pair of cases for `__hello__` also failed before correction (**2 failed, 105 passed**) and now preserve strong emphasis rather than losing a content-adjacent underscore. The final 207-test run covers this correction.
- The initial repair passed full Discord plugin validation with isolated fork workers: **246 files, 3,343 tests passed**. A subsequent review found the synthetic-fence reasoning edge case; its new test failed before correction, and the final focused run above includes the correction. The default worker run previously exited unexpectedly after 2,812 passing tests; the isolated rerun completed without failures.
- Before the September 12 rebase, changed-scope formatting, lint, production/test typechecks, plugin boundaries, dead-export checks, and runtime import-cycle checks passed; that head also passed [GitHub CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/34071825635).
- Independent `autoreview --mode branch --base origin/main --max-priority P2`: **scoped-clean**, with no actionable findings.

```sh
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.sends-basic-channel-messages.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.webhook.chunk-limit.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/native-command-reply.test.ts
pnpm test:extension discord --pool=forks --isolate --maxWorkers=1
node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- extensions/discord/src/chunk.ts extensions/discord/src/chunk.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.sends-basic-channel-messages.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.webhook.chunk-limit.test.ts
git diff --check
```

Validation used Node 24.19.0 on macOS arm64. Live Discord client screenshots were not captured: this environment has no dedicated test bot/channel credentials. Local HTTP payload evidence does not claim a live Discord round trip.

Related follow-up: the shared `hasBalancedFences` test helper still uses the old marker-only closing rule. These regressions deliberately use the independent Markdown parser instead of that helper.
