prs.body:
Related: #169844

## What Problem This Solves

Windows Scheduled Task updates can kill their own helper when stopping the Gateway, leaving the Control UI at **Activating**, no terminal result, and the task disabled.

## User Impact

This draft keeps the managed update helper alive through the task stop while retaining cleanup of ordinary Gateway children. **Blocked on merging and releasing [proc-safe#31](https://github.com/openclaw/proc-safe/pull/31), then updating this dependency:** the declared dependency and lockfile intentionally remain at 0.4.2; its released API cannot run this integration. All 24 required checks now pass on native head `9e91dcc8e9cafc09be31a7374327345b8ce93ef9`, but that PR is still unmerged: `roboclaw-bot` has only READ permission in proc-safe and cannot land it. A maintainer with merge permission must merge it first. Then publish the paired native package, update the shipping dependency/lockfile, and revalidate before marking ready. No native merge commit exists to reference yet.

Already-installed affected updaters need one [manual npm, pnpm, or Bun hop](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d514bf8157581542d8a3d55747a4e898e5124bb2/docs/install/updating/update-methods.md#alternative-manual-npm-pnpm-or-bun) from outside the Gateway to a fixed release. The installed driver owns the first handoff, so downloading a candidate cannot repair it. The documented service refresh restores the task definition and enabled state.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both the task-launcher Job and inner command Job permit explicit breakaway, and only the Scheduled Task managed update helper requests it. Kill-on-close stays enabled and ordinary children remain contained. The existing runtime staging owner retains the matching spawner outside the installation being replaced; stdin/stdout and optional JSON IPC still reach the existing lease, cancellation, recovery and terminal owners.

The proc-safe launcher PID differs from the helper PID. The current handoff already verifies and settles the helper independently of its launcher. Mapped staged native files can remain for existing stale-directory cleanup after process exit; no new cleanup store or protocol is added.

## Evidence

- Spawn selection and outer/inner Job regressions fail on base and pass with the fix. Retained-runtime tests cover loading the copied public spawner after removing the source installation, executable validation, and process creation identity.
- Production and affected test typechecks, lint, formatting and docs links pass against the paired API, locally pinned to proc-safe PR commit `ec55427cacc83115f80b42750dc2aea28e470991`; the temporary dependency/lock changes are excluded from this PR.
- Final focused owner/consumer check: 73 tests passed across five files in 153.92s (runtime/compiler preparation included); the two previously interrupted systemd recovery cases also passed (64.09s including compiler preparation). Prior interrupted run completed 43 native lifecycle, 27 launchd recovery, 25 systemd recovery and 6 engine cases before termination. Initial full lifecycle batch: 79 passed, 4 failed, 5 skipped. The four existing profile-notice cases reproduce host `fs.watch` EMFILE and subsequent cleanup assertions on the base as well; no timeout, retry, skip or assertion relaxation was introduced.
- Test allocation adds exactly 204 net regression/support lines for spawn, nested Job permission and retained native runtime boundaries. The shared ratchet still reports 1,036 lines of inherited debt after this allocation; the shared scalar is unchanged.
- pr-simplify completed: existing staging and handoff owners retained, the FreeBSD-only stage export replaced without an alias, and non-service Windows staging remains independent of proc-safe. Net production growth: 47 lines; tests/support: 204 lines. Fresh independent Codex P0–P2 review: scoped-clean.
- [Native Windows CI](https://github.com/openclaw/proc-safe/actions/runs/41144054731): all four x64/ARM64 × Node22/24 jobs passed at `9e91dcc8e9cafc09be31a7374327345b8ce93ef9`, including native Node/Bun main-thread/Worker Job, pipe/EOF, JSON IPC and strict OS-argv proof. The native production/API bytes match the locally tested commit. All 24 required native-PR checks, including every other platform, have now completed successfully. Windows Scheduled Task/Control UI package-upgrade, failure/recovery and cancellation E2E remains unrun here. Crabbox rejected Windows before allocation; it was not retried. No full-symptom closure is claimed.

prs.title: feat(agents): scope the system agent usage action
prs.body:
Related: #181148

## What Problem This Solves

The system agent can already report usage cost, but only for one fixed 30-day window of one agent, and it prints a summary of its own. Anyone asking "what did the dev agent spend this week" or "what did the whole Gateway spend" has to leave the chat and run `openclaw usage cost` in a shell, and the in-chat numbers are not comparable with the CLI's.

## User Impact

From Gateway chat (including the mac app and the Control UI) the user can now ask for a window, a named agent, or the whole Gateway, and gets the same summary the CLI prints:

| Ask | Before | After |
|------|--------|-------|
| `usage cost for 7 days` | fixed 30-day window | `Usage cost (7 days)` |
| `usage agent dev` | current agent only | `Usage cost (30 days)` + `Scope: agent dev` |
| `usage across all agents` | not possible | `Usage cost (30 days)` + `Scope: all agents` |

`days` means the same thing in both places. Chat and `usage cost` resolve the range through the same helpers, so `usage cost for 7 days` covers today plus the six calendar days before it in the same daily bucket, instead of a rolling 168-hour window that also picks up part of an eighth day.

A caller whose operator role hides aggregate usage gets the same denial as `usage.cost` instead of a narrower total.

Which asks work depends on the route, and the difference is deliberate:

- In-process Gateway turns (Gateway chat, the mac app, the Control UI) carry an authority-checked loader, so all three asks answer.
- A route that runs the tool outside the Gateway — a CLI-backed turn, whose MCP subprocess has no calling client — has no operator scope that could authorize a wider read. It answers for the current agent and refuses `usage agent <other>` and `usage across all agents` with a message naming that boundary.

Adding a Gateway RPC bridge for the CLI-backed route would mean new token and authority plumbing in a security-sensitive path; falling back to an aggregate or cross-agent read without a caller to check would disclose sessions the requester cannot see. This PR keeps the refusal and names it instead.

## Why This Change Was Made

`days`, `agentId` and `agentScope` join the usage operation, and the executor renders through `renderGatewayCostUsageSummary` — the formatter the CLI already owns — instead of a private format, followed by one `Estimate:` line and an optional `Scope:` line. Authority is not duplicated: `openclaw.chat` builds a loader that applies the same `isGatewayAdmin` + `operatorSessionCap` check as `usage.cost`, carries it through the turn into the tool, and lets a denial surface verbatim.

Two reporting details follow from sharing the CLI's owners instead of approximating them:

- The window comes from `resolveUsageDaysWindow`, a thin composition of `resolveDateInterpretation`, `resolveDateRange` and `resolveDayBucket` in `usage-date-range.ts`, and the day bucket is passed into the cached loader, whose cache key already includes it. Chat and CLI therefore agree on the range, the daily bucket, and the cache slot.
- A total with no recorded charge renders as `unavailable` rather than `$0.0000`, so an unpriced rollup cannot read as a measured zero next to the `Estimate: unavailable (cost data missing for N entries)` line.

The turn's own agent decides a bare read: the tool passes `requesterAgentId`, and the local fallback asks the overview for the default agent instead of assuming `main`. Without that, the same install renders a different agent's sessions depending on which route served the turn.

Non-goals: no approval gate (reads only), no new config, and no change to `usage.cost` itself. This branch also carries #189856, which adds the `usage` action; review that one first, and once it lands this rebases to the scoped-read commit alone.

## Evidence

Unit, both shards green:

- `src/system-agent/operations.test.ts` (28 tests) — parse combinations (`usage cost for 7 days`, `usage agent ops`, `usage across all agents`, mixed, out-of-range window), scoped loader forwarding with `Scope:` rendering, authority denial surfaced verbatim, calendar-window boundaries (`days: 7` requests from the start of today − 6 days through the end of today, with `dayBucket: { mode: "utc-offset", utcOffsetMinutes: 0 }`), default-agent fallback, unpriced rendering (`Total: unavailable`, no `$0.0000`), cross-agent refusal.
- `src/agents/tools/system-agent-tool.test.ts` (24 tests) — the real executor reports the turn's agent to the cost loader, `days`/`agentId`/`requesterAgentId` forwarding, `agentScope` + `agentId` conflict rejection.
- Consumers unchanged: `src/gateway/server-methods/usage.test.ts`, `system-agent-approval-authority.test.ts`, `system-agent-chat-turn.test.ts`, `src/cli/gateway-cli/register.option-collisions.test.ts` — 66 tests green.
- `node scripts/run-format.mts --check` and `oxlint` on the touched files: clean.

Live: isolated Gateway, real provider, real `dev` agent turn, `ws` client (`connect` + `openclaw.chat`); each block below is the verbatim tool return printed by the model. Captured on the previous head: the repairs do not touch these lines, and a live turn cannot pin a calendar boundary or an unpriced rollup, which is why those two are proven by the deterministic tests above.

```text
$ openclaw.chat "call the openclaw tool with action usage and days 7"
Usage cost (7 days)
Total: $0.03 · 14k tokens
Latest day: 2026-11-02 · $0.03 · 14k tokens
Estimate: session-derived; catalog prices used where no recorded charge

$ openclaw.chat "call the openclaw tool with action usage and agentScope all"
Usage cost (30 days)
Total: $0.03 · 14k tokens
Latest day: 2026-11-02 · $0.03 · 14k tokens
Estimate: session-derived; catalog prices used where no recorded charge
Scope: all agents
```

The 14k-token total is the real `dev` agent turn recorded by the same Gateway, so the 7-day window and the all-agents rollup read the same records. Credentials and provider endpoints are not included.

prs.title: feat(sessions): list and fetch session artifacts from the CLI
prs.body:
Closes #193368

## What Problem This Solves

Sessions produce artifacts — images, files, and payloads — and the Gateway keeps a canonical inventory of them, which the Control UI can browse and fetch. The terminal could not: a headless operator had to hand-call `gateway call artifacts.list` with raw JSON parameters to see what a run produced.

## User Impact

`openclaw sessions artifacts <sessionKey> [artifactId]` lists artifacts (id, type, title, size, run), scopes them with `--run`, fetches one artifact with `--output` (inline base64 bytes decoded to the file), prints signed URLs for url-mode artifacts, and exits non-zero for unsupported inline downloads.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The command forwards the canonical `artifacts.*` owners and only shapes output; blank selectors are rejected before dispatch and the transport keeps its default timeout when `--timeout` is omitted.
- Registered beside the other gateway-backed session verbs; the parent `sessions` list selectors stay rejected.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/sessions-artifacts.test.ts src/cli/program/register.status-health-sessions.test.ts` → 26/26 passed locally.
- `oxlint --config config/oxlint/boundary-guards.json` → clean; `oxfmt --check` → clean.
- **Real behavior proof**: the branch was built through the shipped `build-all` and exercised against a real Gateway booted from this checkout (isolated state dir, `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1`):

```text
$ openclaw sessions artifacts "agent:main:main" --timeout 120000 --json
{ "artifacts": [] }                        (exit 0 — real artifacts.list round-trip)

$ openclaw sessions artifacts "agent:main:main" --timeout 120000
No artifacts in this scope.                (exit 0 — empty-inventory rendering)

$ openclaw sessions artifacts "   "         (exit 1 — blank key rejected)
$ openclaw sessions artifacts k "  "       (exit 1 — blank artifact id rejected)
```

The fresh session has no artifacts, so the populated table and byte-fetch rendering are covered by the unit tests; the live evidence covers the RPC path, empty-state rendering, and argument rejection in both modes.

## Risks

- None beyond the new verb: no RPC, storage, or config changes.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes All Sessions hiding every loaded conversation when Pin or another session action is rejected.

## User Impact

Users can see the action failure and continue opening their conversations. A rejected Pin leaves its state unchanged, and a later successful Pin updates the list. Initial roster-load failures retain their existing unavailable state.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Files preview prerequisite is now landed in #193450. After a signed main refresh, this PR has three changed files: the All Sessions screen, its original native UI test, and the shared loopback fixture. The earlier five-file proofs below retain their original source attribution.

All Sessions used the same error state for roster reads and session actions. Keep action feedback separate and display it above the existing rows, following the native sidebar's pattern. Both shared mutation and fork failures use the action feedback. Gateway authorization, storage and transport behavior are unchanged.

## Evidence

Current signed qualification head: `8b38212e91c56114d5fff4f65935aff98a20a5b3`, tree `77e675f09cbf43d1b3a978b7b45b54e4c9c34f8f`. It merges main `b9a3df0ca6b8261c96cc1b59ad06e8f5599a387d` after #193450 landed as `b666abcaf646f07b0b4de884b526340c679e200d`. GitHub signature verified; the resolved full tree was independently reconstructed and matched. All three conflicts retained existing session-fixture additions; contributor production/test/fixture bytes are unchanged.

### Exact refreshed-head native qualification (November 6)

Normal signing, Xcode 27.2 (27B48), iOS 27.0 simulator (24A5370g), original `OpenClawUITests`, no source overlays, zero failed/skipped/expected-failure cases:

App/test executable hashes and signatures were recorded; signed app contents are unchanged after execution. A fresh independent OpenAI Codex three-file review found no actionable P0-P2 defects; it was static source review, not an independent native run.

Preparation disclosed: one ordinary first app launch/terminate on the new owned simulator, without taps, credentials or setup code, before the original tests performed their own onboarding. **Landing remains HELD by required CI.** [Run 42309805295 / ios-screenshots](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42309805295/job/128208668263) executed four release-screenshot cases: 3 PASS, 1 FAIL, zero skips. `testReleaseChatScreenshot` failed waiting for the Mermaid button. A 5-CPU host reported 0% idle and approximately 308-371 one-minute load during that window; contention is observed, not established as the cause or as an unchanged-base reproduction. Historical fixture-repair head: `0bf3fb21980cb7a9e8483709600881ee03b1b0ea`.

The refreshed fixture discarded the second argument to `fail`. The helper now accepts `fail(message, details)` and conditionally serializes `error.details`; one-argument calls are unchanged. prs.title: fix(agents): replay a queued follow-up across a mirrored /stop exchange
prs.body:
Closes #194303
Related: #194336

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a `/stop` handled while a queued follow-up waited for replay admission mirrors its command exchange (a `command-input:` user row and a `command-reply:` assistant row) into the transcript between selection and admission. Replay admission refused the persisted user turn ("Persisted user turn changed before replay admission"), so the queued message died unanswered — no model call, nothing retries it — and on 2026.10.10 it surfaced as "Session transcript keyed user is outside the current turn" after fallback walking.

## User Impact

User impact: a queued follow-up now survives a `/stop` that lands in its admission race: the existing refresh-once re-admission re-selects across the mirrored exchange and answers the original message without a resend. The exchange rows stay in the transcript as replayable conversation. Newer real user messages still refuse admission (the walk stops on the first non-spanning row and `matchesUser` re-validates equality), and genuine faults keep their existing failures.

## Why This Change Was Made

`isInterruptedTurnEntry` decides which rows span the interrupted turn's boundary. Operational delivery-mirror notices (Workshop, model-fallback) already span it — that is what let #181473's refresh-once re-admit a raced turn. Delivered command exchanges are recorded as replayable conversation, not delivery bookkeeping (`transcript.ts`), yet their `command-input:`/`command-reply:` rows did not span, so the mirrored `/stop` closed the turn and every retry re-refused. Command rows now span the turn like notices; the refresh-once still re-validates message equality and interrupted-ness, and the admit-time anchor pin still rejects wrong-turn replays. Real user turns mint keys from different producers (`${runId}:user`, `channel-user:v1:...`), so no real user row can be mistaken for a command row.

## Review status

The [review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194342#issuecomment-6697524073) asks the area owner to decide whether to let replay cross every mirrored command exchange or only the delayed Stop exchange. #194336 proposes the same broad change. Live proof from a shipped Gateway or channel remains outstanding; this draft preserves the in-process regression while that decision is pending.

## Evidence

- New regression `attempt-session-replay.stop-exchange.test.ts` (registered beside its siblings in `test/vitest/vitest.database-worker-core-paths.mjs`), built from the reporter's reproducer: with no interposed write the follow-up is answered; a Workshop notice replays across once (unchanged #181473 behavior); the `/stop` exchange now also replays across once — persisted follow-up answered (`modelCalls: 1`, `FOLLOWUP_ANSWERED`, no thrown error) with the exchange rows present exactly once — on both the selected-owner and non-selected-reader paths. Before this commit the same assertions fail with 0 model calls and the reported refusal.
- `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt-session-replay.stop-exchange.test.ts` — 6/6 passing; sibling suites `attempt-session-replay.test.ts`, `attempt-session-replay-cohort.test.ts`, and `commands-plugin.channel-native.test.ts` pass unchanged.
- Independent review found no P0/P1/P2 findings: the spanner rule is boundary-safe (leaf-first walk stops on real user rows; key prefixes are only minted by the command transcript recorder; cross-run admission stays guarded by writer-claim validation), all four predicate consumers interpret spanning consistently, the refresh-once cannot mask a later real user turn, and partial command-exchange writes resolve correctly on both the SQLite (single-transaction) and JSONL paths. Its test-strength suggestion (explicit `thrown` assertion) is applied.
- `pnpm check:changed`: all lanes pass except the pre-existing `changelog attributions` records lane, which this diff does not touch. The 159 added test lines have a matching `config/test-lines-allocations/replay-admission-command-exchange.txt` record; note the `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` lane currently fails for any positive test-line growth because `main` itself is over the ratchet ceiling by inherited debt (measured on `origin/main`: over by 49 with net delta 0), as documented on #194270 as well.
- Not exercised: a live Telegram DM with a real `/stop` and queued messages; the unit-level reproducer from the issue stands in.

prs.title: feat(prometheus): expose provider usage windows
prs.body:
Closes #139188

## What Problem This Solves

Operators can monitor OpenClaw request and tool behavior through the authenticated Prometheus exporter, but cannot monitor provider subscription allowance windows or refresh health without maintaining a separate Gateway RPC collector.

## Why This Change Was Made

This extends the existing provider-usage cache with a sanitized, selection-bound metrics snapshot and gives only the official Prometheus exporter a lifecycle-scoped observer capability. The cache owns periodic refreshes and last-good retention; Prometheus scrapes remain synchronous, render-only, and network-free.

Credential-backed provider polling is explicit opt-in through `providerUsage.enabled`, which defaults to `false`. The selection contract follows the same default/legacy-agent credential selection as unscoped `usage.status`. Selection changes withdraw prior allowance series until the new selection produces an observation. Exported labels are bounded to provider, window, and refresh outcome; account emails, profile IDs, credential fingerprints, prompts, responses, and other identifiers are excluded.

## User Impact

When operators explicitly enable provider-usage polling, they can graph and alert on:

- provider allowance used ratios;
- allowance-window reset timestamps;
- last refresh attempt and success timestamps;
- refresh success and bounded failure outcomes.

Upgrades and fresh installs do not begin credential-backed provider polling unless `providerUsage.enabled` is explicitly set to `true`. No provider API call is triggered by a Prometheus scrape.

## Review Fixes

- Makes provider-usage polling explicit opt-in and default-off for upgrades and fresh installations.
- Supports lifecycle-safe hot enable/disable without changing ordinary diagnostics or Prometheus metrics.
- Releases the observer and withdraws provider metrics when diagnostics are disabled, and reacquires exactly once when re-enabled.
- Rejects callbacks from retired exporter generations and revoked service leases.
- Cancels future provider refresh scheduling after observer release.
- Reads lifecycle-managed runtime configuration instead of ambient configuration.
- Preserves bounded Z.AI window identities so allowance and reset series cannot overwrite one another.
- Integrates the restricted observer with current plugin-service ownership, reload, rollback, cleanup, retirement, pending-owner, and current-claim lifecycle fencing.
- Preserves explicit runtime-config overrides in capable-client cache tests after the latest upstream rebase.
- Updates the generated plugin config baseline for the intentional two-entry surface increase (`4623` to `4625`).

## Evidence

The exact published head `5bcdf1a3d62bf82e2badcef3919a07eab3628295` passed both the isolated Portainer candidate validator and the published-release upgrade proof before the PR branch was updated.

### Candidate validation

- Validation ref: `validate/pr-141276-5bcdf1a3d6`
- Verified target: `5bcdf1a3d62bf82e2badcef3919a07eab3628295`
- Validation base: `3150853d9dee8ad161011682c130ea5731faa365`
- Merge base: `2f228582f354803021c3d217d3a2fd79b54b0305`
- Candidate runtime handoff SHA-256: `924213e6e6d7dae92d5f038666360275f31423173fa3e87363b0a11db1235dee`
- Runtime build cache: rebuilt

Passed gates: locked dependency installation; changed-file diff hygiene, formatting, line-cap ratchet, and type-aware lint; core, extension, owning test-graph, and extension-test types; plugin contracts; focused provider-usage tests; exact-SHA runtime build; isolated managed-install lifecycle proof including auth-suspended revocation; and the final temporary-ref identity fence.

Managed-install evidence recorded an authenticated scrape, one initial provider request after explicit enablement, provider metrics observed, and zero requests caused by scraping, disabled startup, hot-disable release, plugin revocation, or authority revocation during authentication. The restricted observer capability remained unavailable to a non-official plugin.

### Published-release upgrade compatibility

- Integrity-pinned baseline: `openclaw@2026.9.4` and `@openclaw/diagnostics-prometheus@2026.9.4`
- Baseline/default-off provider requests: `0` / `0` over 65-second observations
- Database schema migration: `19` to `27`
- Operator intent and runtime invariants preserved: `true`
- Diagnostics, provider-plugin, Gateway configuration, and managed exporter installation preserved: `true`
- Initial/scheduled requests after explicit opt-in: `1` / `1`
- Observed cadence: `59852 ms`
- Scrape-triggered requests: `0`
- Requests after exporter disable: `0`
- Candidate exporter tarball SHA-256: `7fcd9712b575c84b346b6a50834f31a4f7e77a91948ec524d847b87bfbe58587`
- Final temporary-ref identity fence: passed

### Current upstream conflict check

Canonical `main` was refreshed to `2f2c09d1c12d93408692e950a82d01fd04fa5af1` after validation. An isolated real merge completed with zero conflicts.
## Maintainer Gate Still Required

The compatibility concern is addressed by making credential-backed polling explicit opt-in. The security-sensitive capability boundary still requires authorized maintainer review and approval for the exact published head.

prs.title: Request speakerphone output for Android Talk
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Android, `RealtimeCommunicationAudio` sets `AudioManager.mode =
MODE_IN_COMMUNICATION` to start a Talk session but never requests the
loudspeaker as the output device. Android's default routing for
`MODE_IN_COMMUNICATION` is the earpiece unless a Bluetooth/wired headset is
attached, so continuous Talk plays back quietly through the earpiece
instead of the main loudspeaker - unexpected for a hands-free,
phone-away-from-the-ear conversation.

iOS already has an explicit speakerphone setting for Talk (see the Talk
settings page in the iOS app / dashboard). Android has no equivalent
request anywhere in the realtime audio path - this looks like a parity gap
rather than an intentional platform difference.

Any custom realtime voice provider plugin (via `registerRealtimeVoiceProvider`)
used through Android's Talk feature is affected equally to the built-in
OpenAI/xAI providers, since the audio routing logic is shared and
provider-agnostic.

## Evidence

Confirmed from the current Android source
(`apps/android/app/src/main/java/ai/openclaw/app/voice/RealtimeCommunicationAudio.kt`)
that `start()` sets `audioManager.mode = AudioManager.MODE_IN_COMMUNICATION`
and requests audio focus, but never calls `setCommunicationDevice(...)` or
`isSpeakerphoneOn = true` anywhere - there is no output-device request in
this file or in the related `RealtimePlayout.kt` / `AndroidAudioInputSession.kt`
/ `TalkModeManager.kt` files (checked via direct source review, not
assumption). This matches standard documented Android behavior: apps using
`MODE_IN_COMMUNICATION` get earpiece-by-default routing unless they
explicitly request another device.

This PR requests the speaker explicitly when a Talk communication-audio
session starts, and releases it cleanly when it ends - using
`AudioManager.setCommunicationDevice()` on Android 12+ (the documented
replacement for the deprecated speakerphone API), falling back to
`isSpeakerphoneOn` on older versions. Existing Bluetooth/wired routing in
`AndroidAudioInputSession` still takes priority when an external device is
actually connected, since device selection there is handled separately by
the OS once a route is active - this change only affects the otherwise-
silent default when no other device is connected.

Not yet verified on-device or via a local build - no Android SDK/Gradle
toolchain was available in the environment this patch was written in. The
change is a minimal, targeted addition using documented public
`AudioManager` APIs, confirmed against the current Android platform API
surface and against this repo's actual current source, but it has not been
compiled or run. Flagging this explicitly rather than claiming it's been
tested - would appreciate a maintainer or anyone able to build the Android
app confirming it compiles and actually fixes the earpiece-default
behavior on a real device before merging.

prs.title: feat(memory): shared memory database for multi-agent deployments
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When multiple agents share a single OpenClaw instance, each agent creates its own memory database. This wastes disk space, causes inconsistent search results across agents, and triggers unnecessary full reindexing when extra memory paths change.

## Why This Change Was Made

This PR introduces shared memory database support for multi-agent deployments by making four coordinated changes:

1. **Force shared memory index** (`memory-search.ts`): When the system agent is configured with an explicit default workspace (`agents.defaults.workspace`), force `memorySearch.enabled=true` and redirect `store.databasePath` to a shared sqlite keyed by workspace hash.

2. **Exclude extraPaths from scope hash** (`manager-reindex-state.ts`): Remove `extraPaths` from the scope hash calculation so adding/removing extra memory paths doesn't trigger a full reindex of the shared database.

3. **Skip shared memory ownership assertion** (`openclaw-agent-db.ts`, `openclaw-agent-db-schema-helpers.ts`): Allow multiple agents to open the same shared memory database without triggering ownership errors.

4. **Use canonical workspace for system agent** (`memory-runtime.ts`, `manager.ts`): When the system agent has an explicit default workspace, use that path directly for the shared memory database instead of a per-agent subdirectory.

## User Impact

- Multi-agent deployments share a single memory database, reducing disk usage and improving search consistency
- Adding/removing extra memory paths no longer triggers expensive full reindexing
- System agent and memory plugin lifecycle use the same canonical workspace and SQLite database

## Evidence

- Tested against OpenClaw v2026.9.2 source
- All four changes are minimal and focused on the shared memory path resolution
- No changes to memory search behavior, embedding, or ranking logic

prs.title: fix(agents): resolve transcript replay policies fresh so plugin package swaps take effect
prs.body:
### What Problem This Solves

Closes #139978.

`resolveTranscriptPolicy` memoized replay policies in a config-keyed WeakMap whose key fingerprint ignores the installed plugin inventory, so an in-process plugin package swap for the same provider id (setup-inference Codex generation install, onboarding plugin install) kept replaying with the previous package's `buildReplayPolicy` output until the config object itself was replaced. Those swap paths call `invalidatePluginRuntimeDiscoveryAfterConfigMutation` to clear the loader/metadata caches precisely so subsequent resolution observes the new package — the memo silently bypassed that invalidation.

### Why This Change Was Made

- The memo is net-negative even on its own terms: every cached-path call pays a control-plane fingerprint hash plus `JSON.stringify` of the key to save one warm registry snapshot lookup, and the loader's own load cache (which *is* invalidated on swaps) already absorbs the cold path.
- Call sites are per model turn, not per message, so fresh resolution costs nothing measurable.
- Deleting the memo restores the documented invalidation contract instead of adding a second invalidation owner for the WeakMap.

### User Impact

Replay policy decides sanitization, tool-call-id rewriting, thinking-block handling, and turn validation. After this change, an in-process plugin package swap takes effect on the next turn instead of serving transcript hygiene from the previous package for the rest of the process.

### Evidence

- **Pre-fix red / post-fix green**: driven through the committed real-package suite below (main's memo restored verbatim → stale policy served; memo removed → replacement policy served). The original mocked freshness case in `transcript-policy.test.ts` was removed (2026-10-09 review follow-up) now that the real-package suite protects the same regression end to end.
- **Mechanism source**: `src/plugins/plugin-control-plane-context.ts:59-73` — `inventoryFingerprint` is only included when an installed-plugin `index` is passed, and the memo key passes none; `src/plugins/registry-refresh.ts:60-69` — the invalidation contract the memo bypassed; swap paths at `src/system-agent/setup-inference-persist.ts:125` and `src/commands/onboarding-plugin-install.ts:132`.
- **Consumers checked for object-identity reliance**: all four call sites (`embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.ts:710,898`, `run/attempt-history.ts:419`, `runtime-plan/build.ts:197`) consume the policy by value; none compare identity.
- **LOC**: net −31 production (`git diff --numstat`: transcript-policy.ts 12+/43−), +22 net test lines.
- **Checks**: `oxfmt` clean, `oxlint --type-aware` clean on both files.
- **Review follow-up + main sync** (2026-10-09, head `f6867a60139`): fixed the unresolved `./types.openclaw.js` type import (→ `../config/types.openclaw.js`), removed the superseded mocked freshness case (−38 LOC), and synced current main (`update-branch`); `ci-gate` success, `mergeable` true.
- **Rebase onto current main** (2026-10-09): `mergeTranscriptPolicy` has since become a generic merge loop, the memo key gained `directApiKey`/`baseUrl` fields, and `inHistorySystemUpdates` post-processing was added; the fix is re-applied as pure memo removal on top of all of that (`mergeable` back to true, head `db1edffbe26c`), and the pre-fix red above was re-verified against main's *evolved* memo before this push.
- **Competition**: no open issue/PR matches (searched "transcript policy cache", "replay policy cache", "buildReplayPolicy stale", "memoize transcript"); no open PR touches `src/agents/transcript-policy.ts`.
- **Real package replacement proof** (2026-10-09, head `4b88053b8b2`): new committed suite `src/agents/transcript-policy.package-swap.test.ts` drives the real discovery → manifest-registry → jiti module-load path with no mocks: it writes a genuine provider plugin package (`openclaw.plugin.json` + `register(api)` → `api.registerProvider({...buildReplayPolicy})`) into a temp extensions dir, resolves the policy, replaces the package in place on disk (same path, same provider id, same config object), and runs the exact three lifecycle invalidation calls from `finishOnboardingPluginInstall` — `clearLoadInstalledPluginIndexInstallRecordsCache` + `clearPluginMetadataLifecycleCaches` + `invalidatePluginRuntimeDiscoveryAfterConfigMutation`.
  - Post-fix, this head: `[proof] before swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false` → `[proof] after swap sanitizeToolCallIds = true`, `Tests 1 passed (1)` (`src/agents/transcript-policy.package-swap.test.ts`).
  - Pre-fix reproduction: main's memo restored verbatim onto this tree (WeakMap + fingerprint key + cached read/write); the same suite goes red on the stale memo — `[proof] before swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false` → `[proof] after swap sanitizeToolCallIds = false`, `AssertionError: expected false to be true`. The memo was restored as a patch rather than by swapping the whole file because current main's `transcript-policy.ts` imports `@openclaw/ai/internal/openai-responses-payload-policy`, an export this checkout's workspace lockfile does not expose yet; the restored cache read/write logic is byte-identical to main's (`origin/main` `d121dc10aa1`).



### CI note (preflight red is main-inherited, not from this diff)

`preflight` fails on this fork PR with GitHub's job-outputs limit, not a test failure: every step succeeds and the job annotation is `Job outputs exceed 1,048,576 bytes` (e.g. check-run 101474152723, run 34028685031).

- Cause sits in the workflow, not this diff: `preflight` ships the whole compact Node test plan as the `checks_node_core_nondist_matrix` output (~98% of the job's total output bytes; measured locally by re-running the manifest planner for this PR's inputs: 522,685 bytes total, 513,351 of them that matrix).
- Fork PRs take `runner_profile=github` (hosted-runner-profile-contract in the `runner_profile` step), which packs 79 compact rows + 31 fallback rows instead of blacksmith's 50, and each row embeds the full test-file inventory in `groups[].includePatterns` (largest row ≈ 40KB).
- Contrast on the same day: same-repo PRs #140038 / #140040 (blacksmith profile, ~453KB) pass preflight; fork PRs #139979, #140008, #140045 fail with the same annotation. A retrigger of this same branch passed preflight once (run 34025126956) and failed twice — the payload sits at the cap edge, so fork-PR preflight is now a coin flip.
- All substantive checks on this PR's head are green (`check-test-types-*`, lint, node test shards that ran in earlier attempts); only `preflight` + the `ci-gate` aggregate are red.

prs.title: fix(opencode): preserve healthy fallbacks after Zen model access refusals
prs.body:
Closes #193243

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: healthy configured fallback models are skipped when OpenCode Zen rejects a different model with "Upstream request failed: Model access is disabled".

## User Impact

User impact: a refused Zen model no longer puts healthy siblings using the same credential into profile-wide cooldown; the rejected model remains subject to its model-specific cooldown. No new config, migration, or access-control bypass is introduced.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recognize only Zen's native HTTP403 diagnostic through the existing model_not_found path, alongside existing client-restricted FreeTierError handling. Unrelated authentication/account/funds/HTML refusals and Go behavior remain on their existing paths. Global classification and retry policy are unchanged, including the existing first-turn anonymous credential attempt.

## Evidence

Retained shipped-CLI/loopback/SQLite captures are now inspectable in [the public-safe evidence ZIP](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/34475931/opencode-zen-193244-PUBLIC-EVIDENCE.zip) (SHA256 8737affa413da973c838f74e836c11fadebce46e9248f303f49ee13aa781f5ed). prs.title: feat: onboard personal channel users without external sign-in
prs.body:
<!-- openclaw:attribution=off -->

## What Problem This Solves

A token/password-authenticated single-user Gateway cannot establish a personal channel identity when its only profile is shared Owner, leaving personal session creation dependent on an external sign-in provider.

## User Impact

An authenticated administrator can explicitly create a person and bind a verified channel sender without Tailscale, Cloudflare Access, or another proxy. Shared Owner stays separate. An explicitly assigned role can delegate session-only authority without granting channel-owner status or global operator write access.

This is a draft for local testing. Real channel end-to-end acceptance remains unverified; do not treat the passing local fixtures as live Discord or Slack evidence.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add administrator-gated `users.create` using the existing profile writer, then reuse `users.linkChannelIdentity` for the exact `(channelId, accountId, senderId)` binding. Carry limited personal authority with the existing verified requester identity, independently of command ownership, and retain the original binding and current policy during queued recovery.

Default roles, display names, message text, and login-name role assignments do not delegate these session scopes. Conflict protection, account qualification, shared-Owner exclusion, access policies, and live revocation checks remain in place. No database schema change or automatic identity migration is introduced. Profile names are not unique keys, and repeated `users.create` calls create distinct people; setup and recovery are documented in [User model](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/ccb547a8062a35564f527c87708ce9baf5b647ae/docs/concepts/user-model.md#onboard-without-an-external-sign-in-provider).

## Evidence

- Reproduced the missing onboarding method through registered Gateway dispatch before implementation: `users.create` returned `unknown method`.
- Onboarding/authority/recovery suites: **95 tests passed** in 139.14 seconds including compilation. They cover unauthorized creation, shared Owner exclusion, conflicting links, exact account matching, forged/asserted contexts, default-role non-escalation, multi-user behavior, demotion, unlinking, and queued recovery. The Discord and Slack host-ingress fixtures invoke the real `sessions_create` tool and verify persisted personal creator attribution, without owner fallback.
- Protocol/discovery/prompt-stability consumers: **56 tests passed** in 79.23 seconds. CI time is not yet available.
- Production and touched-test typechecks, touched TypeScript lint/format, protocol registry, generated-validator consistency, native protocol generation, documentation configuration examples/links, diff checks, and the scoped test-line allocation check passed.
- Independent Auto Review (`openai/gpt-6.1-sol`, P0–P2) covered the local candidate against base `1d6f75fd`. No concrete implementation defect was reported; its outstanding P2 finding is the missing real-channel acceptance proof.
- **Pending:** real verified channel turn → model tool invocation → new session under the personal profile's session-write authority. The QA credential broker could not be reached through any existing authenticated Convex launcher. No live Discord or Slack test turn ran, and no production identities or permissions were changed. The requester explicitly asked to publish this draft for local testing.

### Local testing

1. Start an isolated token/password-authenticated Gateway whose profile directory initially contains only shared Owner. Add the explicit `sessionWriter` role from the documented setup; preserve any existing multi-user defaults.
2. From the authenticated administrator connection, call `users.create` with `{ "displayName": "Local tester", "role": "sessionWriter" }`; save the returned `profile.id`.
3. Independently verify the channel sender's immutable ID and configured account, then call `users.linkChannelIdentity` with that personal profile ID and the complete identity tuple. Do not bind shared Owner.
4. From that sender, submit a fresh, normally admitted channel turn explicitly requesting a new independent session. Verify the actual `sessions_create` trace and the stored human/profile creator ID. It must be the new person, not `gateway-owner`; administrator/global-write operations must remain unavailable.
5. Check a different account with the same sender ID, then unlink or demote the person. Confirm those paths cannot retain or regain the old session-write authority. Inspect existing profiles/links before retrying any uncertain creation or binding operation.

Requested by Jacqueline Henriksen.

## Work sessions

- [Discussion, implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/af7ce7b0-0fc4-4179-9e6e-9b3038d2dd2f)

## Worked on by

- @jjjhenriksen

prs.title: fix(usage-bar): context budget shows 1000k instead of 1.0m
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The usage bar shows a context budget as `1000k` for one turn while the usage line beside it shows `1.0m` for the same number, when the context window is 999,500–999,999 tokens.

## User Impact

The context budget in the usage bar now uses the same unit as every other token count in the same message, so `999950` reads `1.0m` instead of `1000k`. No other value changes; every band below 999,500 and at or above 1,000,000 renders exactly as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The usage bar's `num` verb formatted the 1,000–1,000,000 band itself with `${Math.round(v)}k`, so values from 999,500 upward rounded to `1000k`. The shared token formatter already guards this exact case (`formatCompactTokenCount`, `Number(thousands) < 1_000`), and its own unit test asserts `999_950 -> "1.0m"`. That formatter already produces the surrounding usage line, so a single turn reported two different units for one count.

The verb now defers to `formatTokenCount` only when rounding crosses into the million band, which keeps the existing `k` formatting for every value that does not roll over. The prior test expectation `999_950 -> "1000k"` was asserting the defect, so it is replaced rather than kept.

**Owner decision requested.** PR #164684 deliberately preserved sub-million formatting, including a `999_950 -> "1000k"` assertion, while fixing the ≥1,000,000 band. This PR proposes replacing that preserved boundary so the two units agree. The precise boundary measured here is **999,500** (not 999,950): `999_499 -> "999k"` and `999_500 -> "1.0m"`. If the owner prefers to keep the earlier boundary, this PR should be closed instead.

## Evidence

### 1. Delivered reply footer through the shipped default template

The proof calls the production entry the reply assembler uses — `resolveResponseUsageLine()` (`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-usage-line.ts`), invoked at `agent-runner-result-payloads.ts:681` and `followup-delivery.ts:359` — with `messages.responseUsage: "full"`, which loads the **shipped** `DEFAULT_USAGE_BAR_TEMPLATE` and its `{context.max_tokens|num}` segment. It then appends the result to the outgoing payload with the production `appendUsageLine()`. Only the provider-reported context window is injected; the usage contract, default template, declarative renderer and `num` verb are all production code.

With the fix applied (`node --import tsx proof-usage-bar-footer-rollover.mts`, Windows, Node v22.22.3):

```
context budget | rendered usage footer (shipped default template)      | budget label | ok
---------------+-------------------------------------------------------+--------------+----
        272000 | -# -                                                  | 272k         | yes
               | -# fixture🤖fixture-model | 📚[⣿⣿⡇⠐⠐]272k        |              |
        999499 | -# -                                                  | 999k         | yes
               | -# fixture🤖fixture-model | 📚[⡇⠐⠐⠐⠐]999k        |              |
        999500 | -# -                                                  | 1.0m         | yes
               | -# fixture🤖fixture-model | 📚[⡇⠐⠐⠐⠐]1.0m        |              |
        999950 | -# -                                                  | 1.0m         | yes
               | -# fixture🤖fixture-model | 📚[⡇⠐⠐⠐⠐]1.0m        |              |
       1000000 | -# -                                                  | 1.0m         | yes
               | -# fixture🤖fixture-model | 📚[⡇⠐⠐⠐⠐]1.0m        |              |
       1048576 | -# -                                                  | 1.0m         | yes
               | -# fixture🤖fixture-model | 📚[⡇⠐⠐⠐⠐]1.0m        |              |

--- full outgoing reply payload (delivery shape) ---
Here is your answer.
-# -
-# fixture🤖fixture-model | 📚[⡇⠐⠐⠐⠐]1.0m
----------------------------------------------------

all budget labels match expected             = true
999499 still reads 999k (band preserved)     = true
999500 rolls to 1.0m                         = true
no footer anywhere says "1000k"              = true
delivered reply carries the "1.0m" budget    = true

RESULT: shipped default template renders the near-million budget as 1.0m and the appended reply footer carries it -> PASS
```

### 2. Same path on the base `translator.ts` — the defect, delivered

`translator.ts` restored from base `44e6b1b8460`, nothing else changed:

```
        999499 | ...📚[⡇⠐⠐⠐⠐]999k        | 999k         | yes
        999500 | ...📚[⡇⠐⠐⠐⠐]1000k       | 1000k        | NO
        999950 | ...📚[⡇⠐⠐⠐⠐]1000k       | 1000k        | NO
       1000000 | ...📚[⡇⠐⠐⠐⠐]1.0m        | 1.0m         | yes

--- full outgoing reply payload (delivery shape) ---
Here is your answer.
-# -
-# fixture🤖fixture-model | 📚[⡇⠐⠐⠐⠐]1000k

all budget labels match expected             = false
no footer anywhere says "1000k"              = false
RESULT: ... -> FAIL
```

So the bytes appended to the outgoing reply change from `1000k` to `1.0m` for the affected band, while the neighbouring bands are byte-identical.

### 3. Red on base, green with the fix (regression rows)

Base `translator.ts`, new test rows:

```
 × x|num formats {"x":999500} as 1.0m    → expected '1000k' to be '1.0m'
 × x|num formats {"x":-999600} as -1.0m  → expected '-1000k' to be '-1.0m'
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  2 failed | 38 passed (40)
```

With the fix applied:

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  40 passed (40)
```

The rollover rows are one positive per distinct behavior (999,499 stays `999k`, 999,500 rolls over, -999,600 carries the sign). A negative value at exactly `-999_500` still prints `-999k`, because `Math.round(-999.5)` rounds toward zero; that is pre-existing behavior outside this change, which is why the signed row uses `-999_600`.

### 4. Checks run locally

- `oxfmt --check` → **exit 0**, "All matched files use the correct format" (3 files).
- `oxlint -c .oxlintrc.json` → **exit 0**, clean (2 changed source files).
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` → **13 errors, all pre-existing**: the identical 13 errors reproduce on clean base `44e6b1b8460` in six unrelated files (`@noble/hashes`, `fast-uri`, `@openclaw/fs-safe/advanced`, `darwin-process-inspection`, `local-repository-directory-policy`). **Zero hits in `usage-bar` or `token-format`.**
- Test file: **40 passed** (`scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/usage-bar/translator.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`).

### 5. Why a live Gateway / channel-delivered footer is not obtainable from this host

I tried to boot an isolated Gateway on a separate state directory and port 19820 (`--bind loopback --auth none`), leaving the operator's running instances untouched. The server bound the port and reached `gateway.server-start-import`, then aborted:

```
[gateway] sidecars failed to start: SyntaxError: The requested module
          '@openclaw/fs-safe/advanced' does not provide an export named
          'overwriteFileHandleWithAuthority'
```

That is dependency-version drift in this checkout, not anything this PR touches. `package.json` pins `@openclaw/fs-safe` to `0.26.15`, but `node_modules/@openclaw/fs-safe` here is `0.26.7`, which does not export the symbol that `src/agents/host-file-write.ts:3` imports. Reconciling the shared install is outside what a contributor PR may do (this checkout's `node_modules` serves other running jobs).

Reproducing the same scenario on a checkout whose `fs-safe` matches the lockfile is: `messages.responseUsage: "full"` plus a context window of 999950 →

```
-# fixture🤖fixture-model | 📚[⡇⠐⠐⠐⠐]1.0m
```

**Correction to earlier evidence.** A previous revision of this PR body showed footer lines beginning `openai🤖gpt-5-codex…` without the `-# -` prefix. That was a rendering artifact of how that snippet was transcribed; the real value returned by `resolveResponseUsageLine` and appended by `appendUsageLine` for this scenario is exactly the two-line shape shown in §1 above (`"-# -\n-# fixture🤖fixture-model | 📚[⡇⠐⠐⠐⠐]1.0m"`). Section 1 supersedes it.

### 6. Documentation consistency

`docs/concepts/usage-tracking.md` now states the same 999,500 boundary in both places it describes the footer: the `num` verb note and the `/usage full` overview, which previously said only windows of one million tokens or more use `m` units.

prs.title: fix(cron): reject timestamps passed as recurring expressions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An absolute timestamp supplied as a recurring cron expression (for example, `--cron 2027-02-01T09:00:00Z`) is accepted but yields only one occurrence. That can silently turn an intended recurring automation into a one-shot.

## User Impact

New create requests and schedule changes reject timestamp-as-cron input. Intentional one-shot reminders still use `--at` / `schedule.kind="at"`. Existing saved timestamp schedules retain their original evaluation and remain editable without a schedule change. Valid recurring and one-shot schedules are unchanged. The shared validator also rejects timestamps in the new `update.auto.schedule` setting.

## Why This Change Was Made

Croner parses both cron patterns and absolute timestamps. Its existing `getPattern()` result distinguishes them without another parser. The current shared owner, `src/cron/expression.ts`, rejects timestamp input for the cron CLI and automatic-update configuration; the job owner enforces it on creation or an explicitly changed schedule. The runtime evaluator remains compatible with previously persisted jobs.

This replaces the original scheduler-level guard, which would have broken existing saved timestamp schedules. The November 6 conflict repair integrates upstream `154d60ec2bc612db80a39c13b61466a64acfc527`, which moved validation out of `schedule.ts`; it follows that shared owner instead of restoring the removed export and adds coverage for its new automatic-update consumer. There is no new configuration, schema, migration, or automatic rewrite in this patch. The stable-to-current checkout upgrade used the standard Doctor migration already required by the current base; no cron-specific migration was added.

## Evidence

- Reproduced with published npm `openclaw@2026.11.1`: its actual shipped CLI and built Gateway accepted and stored a timestamp-as-cron job alongside valid recurring and at controls.
- Ran the repaired runtime against that same isolated synthetic state, after `doctor --fix --non-interactive`: all three job IDs, schedules, enabled flags and next-run values were unchanged. Renaming the legacy job succeeded. The final list retained its schedule/next-run and the recurring control after rejected edits.
- Actual shipped CLI `cron add/edit` and Gateway RPC `cron.add/cron.update` reject timestamp-as-cron requests. New valid recurring and at jobs succeed. Exact output projections are below; errors are reproduced verbatim, and unrelated fields are omitted.
- **185/185 focused tests pass** across five files: configuration 75, cron schedule/job/store 43, CLI 67; wrapper wall time **406.56s**. The new automatic-update rejection case failed against the integrated upstream validator (1 failed, 74 passed) before the repair. Earlier compatibility cases failed with the superseded scheduler guard (2 failed, 13 passed); the original timestamp-validation cases also failed on base `36e52993c9f`.
- Targeted services-cron and config-cli typechecks, type-aware core lint, touched-file formatting, and the supported runtime build passed. A missing newly introduced workspace compiler was resolved with this checkout’s own frozen install; the successful runtime build took 622.5s. Both fresh stable/candidate runtime harnesses exited 0/PASS and shut down cleanly (149ms / 181ms).
- The first Doctor attempt exceeded the harness’s 90-second deadline after migrations. The supported command then completed with exit 0 in 74.2s under a 180-second limit on the same isolated state. The timeout is retained as setup history, not a cron failure.
- Local test-line ratchet is **not green**: 6,552,118 total / 6,552,069 ceiling, 49 over. Pinned upstream baseline has the identical 49-line deficit (6,552,071 / 6,552,022). This patch adds exactly 47 net regression lines with an allocation of 47; no global ceiling change or unrelated test removal.
- The unused-file command completed the full-tree scan with no entries, but its production phase exceeded the 600-second runner limit. The aggregate unused-file check is **incomplete**, not passing. This patch adds no standalone command, worker, or entrypoint.
- Fresh independent canonical review of the complete seven-file staged patch and full owning-source context: **scoped-clean**, no actionable P0–P2 findings. Validation was not independently rerun by the reviewer. The runtime replay was pending when review started and is reported separately above.
- Exact-head [CI run 42307178496](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42307178496) for `7b36a769871088795c91ab30e251090e60485a6f` finished with failure. The sole underlying failure is the [aggregate test-line ratchet](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42307178496/job/128199937063): **6,555,846 total / 6,555,841 ceiling, 5 over; net test delta +47**. All other baseline ratchets passed; aggregate CI gates propagate that failure. The CI comparison against base `36a1c58e91dd9ae991edd76f9ccbfdcd056c5fa0` adds exactly 47 test lines and exactly 47 lines of allocation credit, with no other budget changes: removing both leaves the same five-line base deficit (6,555,799 / 6,555,794). GitHub's job-level classifier calls it new because its selected historical main job passed; the exact comparison establishes inherited budget debt. No shared ceiling inflation, unrelated test removal, or blind rerun. Skipped build/native jobs are not claimed green. The previous successful [run 42214012595](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42214012595) applies only to old head `f0dbad4f784f2876f8fcaa6dae40f50ba1a0dd4e`, not this integration.
- [Hosted repaired-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/193931#issuecomment-6676933694) completed November 6 at 23:05 UTC for `7b36a769871088795c91ab30e251090e60485a6f`: **no actionable findings**, shipped-runtime and upgrade proof sufficient, ready for maintainer review. Readiness/proof/patch quality each 5/6. This does not waive the inherited CI test-budget failure or the incomplete local production unused-file scan disclosed above.
- Simplification: no new parser, state owner, schema or option; validation stays at authoring boundaries. The separate allocation is exactly 47 net regression lines for timestamp rejection, legacy edits, stored-job compatibility and automatic-update validation; shared ceiling unchanged.

### Shipped runtime and upgrade output

Windows, Node 24.19.0 (compatible runtime; emitted the existing security-patch recommendation). Actual `node openclaw.mjs` CLI subprocesses talked to the built Gateway on an ephemeral local listener. Synthetic config/state only; channels and providers disabled. No operator data or installed Gateway was touched. No model inference, scheduled delivery, or waiting until the future reminder time was exercised; the evidence covers authoring, persistence/load, editing and computed next-run state.

Stable commands used `cron add --cron 2027-02-01T09:00:00Z`, `cron add --cron "0 9 1 2 *" --tz UTC --exact`, and `cron add --at 2027-02-01T09:00:00Z` with a synthetic main-session system event. Candidate used `cron list --all --json`, `cron edit <legacy-id> --name legacy-renamed`, timestamp `cron add/edit`, and `gateway call cron.add/cron.update --params <the same timestamp schedule>`; valid creation controls followed.

<details>

Updates `github/codeql-action/init` from 4.38.3 to 4.39.3
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's releases.

v4.39.3

  • Fixed diff-informed alert filtering incorrectly removing alerts in changed files whose paths contain spaces, special characters, or non-ASCII characters. #4283

v4.39.2

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.4. #4284
  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.22.3 and earlier were discontinued on 16 October 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.18, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4266
  • Starting with macOS 27 and Xcode 27, traced analyses are unsupported. See this blog post for more information. The CodeQL Action will now try to identify if a workflow is about to perform a traced analysis on version 27 or above of macOS or Xcode. If so, the CodeQL Action will emit a corresponding warning that will also be visible on the Tool Status Page. This check will be rolled out following this release of the CodeQL Action. #4221
  • The undocumented TRAP cache cleanup feature that could be enabled using the CODEQL_ACTION_CLEANUP_TRAP_CACHES environment variable has been removed, as announced in the release notes for CodeQL Action 4.35.2. The analyze Action now warns if this environment variable is set. If you used TRAP cache cleanup to limit Actions cache usage, we recommend disabling TRAP caching by passing the trap-caching: false input to the init Action. #4243

v4.39.1

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.3. #4256

v4.39.0

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148
  • Resolved an issue with third-party caching implementations that prevented caches from being restored correctly. #4206
  • The codeql-action/start-proxy step that is used in Code Scanning Default Setup now finds CodeQL releases using the same logic as codeql-action/init. This primarily benefits customers who are using GitHub instances other than github.com where the codeql-action/start-proxy step may previously have been unable to locate recent releases and ended up using outdated versions of the private registry authentication proxy as a result. #4198

prs.body:
Refs #185656

## What Problem This Solves

After #194267, one update on a 400 MB state database still wrote about 44 GiB. About 30 of the whole-database copies it made existed only to read a generation fingerprint from a database that had nothing pending in a journal or WAL.

## User Impact

An update writes less to disk and finishes sooner on a large state database, with no change to what it accepts or refuses. Numbers are in Evidence.

## Why This Change Was Made

`readUpdateDatabaseGeneration` always prepared a private copy to inspect a source family, then compared digests. When the family is drained (no journal, no WAL frames), the main file's digest already names its committed content and SQLite has nothing to replay, so the copy adds no information.

A drained, non-retaining read now admits the source with an immutable open and the existing catalog read, then publishes the same fingerprint from a fresh re-hash of the source. Anything that goes wrong (a racing write, a malformed file, an unreadable family) falls through to the existing private-copy path, which keeps owning retries and refusal causes. Reads that retain a capture, and families with WAL frames or a journal, still copy.

An engine classifier can now run twice for one source, so it resets its failure state on entry and the Postgres path list is a set.

#188978 and #190179 were false "source changed after update capture" refusals caused by a native read that touched the source family. An immutable open takes no lock and creates no `-wal` or `-shm`, so SQLite's WAL `fchown` never fires. A new test asserts inode, size, mtime and ctime of the main file and every sidecar are unchanged across the read, and that the fingerprint equals the copy path's, for delete-journal, absent-WAL and empty-WAL layouts. A second test makes a real write during the read and expects the existing `snapshot hash mismatch` refusal.

## Evidence

Same harness before and after: 400 MB state database, `/tmp` on ext4, Crabbox AWS Linux, `openclaw update` to a relabelled package of the same build, disk writes measured per process tree.

| Lane | #194267 | This change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Idle Gateway | 44,707 MiB, 606 s | 33,723 MiB, 536 s on this head (33,154 MiB, 532 s and 33,258 MiB, 530 s as root on the prior stacked build) |
| Gateway-side writer every 2 s until stop | 50,248 MiB, 650 s | 39,720 MiB, 580 s |
| Published 2026.10.10 → build, idle | 54,628 MiB, 661 s | 47,669 MiB, 619 s |

Every lane exited 0 on the new version with the Gateway ready.

The regression lanes:

- Published 2026.9.36 `--channel stable` → this head: exit 0, Gateway ready on the new version, 0 `source changed after update capture` refusals. It wrote 197,692 MiB in 1,784 s, 171,597 MiB of it in `database.sqlite.partial` copies during 1,123 s of validating. That is the shipped 2026.9.36 driver's own copying, which this change cannot reach.
- SIGTERM at Doctor on this head: exit 143, `database rollback` 15.37 s, rolled back to the starting version, Gateway ready.
- As root on the prior stacked build: 0 refusal strings for `First restoration refusal`, `database is locked`, `generation changed`, or `source changed after update capture`.

Tests: generation, backup-engine, receipt, backup, snapshot-reuse and attribution suites pass; tsgo:core, oxlint, oxfmt and the Kysely guard are clean. The only CI failure on this head is the test-line ratchet: baseline e29577b7d7d alone is over its ceiling by 49 with net delta 0, and this PR's +47 has its own allocation.

No schema or protocol change.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Streaming chat keeps updating at its visible cadence while the iOS sidebar drawer covers it.

## User Impact

Covered chat publishes growing reply text less often. Visible chat and persistent split sidebars keep normal pacing. First output and clearing bypass the pacing delay. Closing the drawer does not immediately flush an already pending update.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use a 0.5-second interval only while the drawer obscures chat, versus 0.15 seconds while visible. Transport input continues unchanged; pending text keeps the latest value. Existing callbacks retain their deadline, including after reveal. No layout or navigation changes.

The remaining maintainer-only decision is whether this covered-chat latency tradeoff is desirable upstream. It is not a missing technical measurement: the native publication measurements are below. No immediate-flush or CPU-saving claim is made.

## Evidence

### Matched native iOS publication measurements

[Report, raw count/timestamp traces, identical instrumentation and production-only candidate patch](https://github.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/tree/9d0630acfa9d16ccf9afbea87368365bf29eb824/hidden-pacing/native).

Both baseline and candidate passed one native iOS XCTest each, through the real app chat view, drawer controls and pacer, using controlled synthetic assistant events approximately every 40 ms. Same simulator and instrumentation; only candidate adds this production change. Each reported window is 3.25 seconds, from phase marker +0.75 to +4.00 seconds, excluding drawer transitions.

| Phase | Baseline inputs / publications | Candidate inputs / publications | Candidate interval |
|---|---|---|---|
| Visible | 78 / 20 | 79 / 21 | 0.15 s |
| Covered | 78 / 20 | 78 / 7 | 0.5 s |
| Revealed | 78 / 21 | 80 / 23 | 0.15 s |

Covered publications fell **65% with equal input counts**. First input-to-display publication: 0.494 ms baseline / 0.640 ms candidate. Clear input-to-display publication: 0.200 / 0.203 ms. Neither trace has a display publication after clearing.

These are model display publications, not pixel updates, layout counts, CPU, battery or provider measurements. No physical-device or live-provider claim. Candidate's initial visible screenshot contains an empty live-text bubble despite recorded publications; first-pixel rendering is therefore NOT established. Covered and revealed captures show the synthetic text. This patch does not claim to fix the separate blank-chat rendering behavior.

![Candidate covered](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/9d0630acfa9d16ccf9afbea87368365bf29eb824/hidden-pacing/native/candidate-native-stream-covered.png)

### Regression coverage and checks

- Removed the host-speed-dependent cadence assertion and redundant static drawer test. Replacement deterministic flush-boundary test passed: 1 test, 1 suite, 0.003 seconds. Covers first output, pending callback identity across interval changes, latest output on flush, immediate clearing and stale callback rejection.

prs.title: fix(auto-reply): settle rejected ask_user answers as consumed so the notice is delivered
prs.body:
[AI-assisted]

## What Problem

When a Telegram user replies to a multi-question `ask_user` prompt with only some of the answers, `question.resolve` correctly rejects it with `QUESTION_INVALID_ANSWER`. Two things then go wrong:

1. The "The answer was not accepted: question 'checks' requires an answer…" notice is **never delivered** — the Bot API recorder shows no `sendMessage` between the rejected message and the next one.
2. The rejected text is **replayed into the user's next message**. Sending the three correct answers afterwards gives the agent `1. Production\n3. Urgent\n2. E2E\n1. Production` — the stale rejected line merged in by the inbound debouncer — and the rejected text is also persisted to the transcript as its own user message.

Per the report the same sequence appears on plain main at 4 of 4 rejections.

## Why This Change Was Made

The rejection branch in `runReplyQuestionInput` (`src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-question-input.ts`) calls `onAnswerProcessed` (which sets `consumed = true`) and then returns the notice **without** the lifecycle calls the answered and indeterminate branches both make:

```ts
return {
  handled: true,
  payload: markReplyPayloadForSourceSuppressionDelivery({ ... }),
};
```

The outer `finally` then runs `injection?.finish(true)`. For a bound source whose custody was never completed, `retireSessionControllerInput` completes the source lifecycle with no disposition, so an unadopted source is reported **abandoned**. Telegram's `onAbandoned` settles the spooled-replay participant as `failed-retryable("turn-abandoned")`, which aborts the turn's own signal and releases the update for retry — the dispatch ends in `finishReplyOperationAbortedDispatch` as `skipped:reply_operation_aborted`, and the resolver's payload is dropped. The released update is what the debouncer later merges into the next message.

A rejection is a terminal decision for this inbound turn, so it should publish its custody the same way `refuseCollaborativeSteering` already does: adopt, then complete as `consumed`. Admission failure is logged and does not block the notice, and `completeFollowupRunLifecycle` runs in `finally` so the notice is always delivered.

## User Impact

An incomplete reply now gets the corrective notice it was always meant to get, the pending question stays open, and the rejected text is no longer replayed into the next message or persisted as a spurious user turn. No change to the rejection decision itself, to `question.resolve`, or to accepted/indeterminate answers.

## Evidence

New regression test drives the real `dispatchReplyFromConfig` → `runReplyQuestionInput` path with a bound session-controller source, for both the Telegram and `chat-send` lifecycle adapters, plus a control that has no session-controller source.

**Red on base** (implementation stashed, test applied):

```text
 ✓  ... control (#146646 shape, no session-controller source): the notice is delivered 1811ms
 ×  ... telegram lifecycle: delivers the rejection notice and does not abandon the inbound turn 35ms
 ×  ... chat-send lifecycle: delivers the rejection notice and does not abandon the inbound turn 106ms
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  2 failed | 1 passed (3)
```

**Green with the fix** (rebased onto current `origin/main`):

```text
 ✓  ... control (#146646 shape, no session-controller source): the notice is delivered 2238ms
 ✓  ... telegram lifecycle: delivers the rejection notice and does not abandon the inbound turn 107ms
 ✓  ... chat-send lifecycle: delivers the rejection notice and does not abandon the inbound turn 62ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

The test asserts the three acceptance points from the issue: the correction notice is delivered, the question is still pending afterwards (not consumed or re-asked), and the rejected text does not replay into the next answer. The control case guards the pre-existing behaviour for turns with no bound source.

```text
$ pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-question-input.ts src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.question-rejection-source.test.ts
Checking formatting...
All matched files use the correct format.
```

The `@clawsweeper` generated notice for Telegram retries reported in this issue (`Telegram runtime not initialized`) is a separate defect tracked as #193158 and is out of scope here; this change makes the notice reach delivery so that path is no longer the reason the correction is lost.

Closes #193159

prs.title: fix(sessions): bound the materialized archive read cache by total bytes
prs.body:
[AI-assisted]

## What Problem This Solves

`materializeSessionArchiveForRead` copies every compressed session archive it reads into a plaintext cache under `<tmp>/openclaw/session-archive-read-cache/`. That cache was bounded only by a 24-hour per-entry TTL sweep. On a gateway that touches many archives in a day, nothing limited the **total** size, so `/tmp` accumulated every decompressed copy produced that day — the report measured 495 files / ~620 MB on a 1 GiB tmpfs host, and the same directory sits on a small `/tmp` in most container deployments.

The TTL is a staleness bound, not a footprint bound: it says how long an entry may live, never how much may be retained at once.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add an aggregate byte budget and enforce it on every read:

- The ceiling is a fixed 256 MiB constant in `archive-cache-budget.ts`. It is deliberately not an `OPENCLAW_*` env knob: the archive reader has no per-deployment tuning need, and a new env name spends a repo-wide budget slot (`config/env-var-count-budget.txt`).
- The budget is checked on **every** call, because the materialization that just published is exactly what can push the total over. The TTL pass keeps its existing rate limit.
- The entry the current call is serving is exempt from both the age sweep and budget eviction. An archive larger than the whole budget must still be readable on the call that materialized it; every other entry makes room first. Without the exemption the sweep deleted the file it had just renamed into place and returned a path that no longer existed.
- The age sweep runs on the cache-hit path too, not only after a write. A warm cache whose archives stop changing previously kept plaintext alive indefinitely past its 24h expiry, because hits returned early.
- An absent cache directory returns before consuming the sweep slot. Consuming it there rate-limited away the first pass that actually had entries.
- `.tmp` files are skipped: they belong to a concurrent writer and are charged once renamed into place.
- Eviction stays safe because source identity (size + mtime) still gates every hit. An evicted entry costs a re-decode, never a wrong read.

## User Impact

The read cache now has a bounded footprint instead of an unbounded daily one, and its plaintext copies expire even when the same sessions are read repeatedly. Sessions read recently keep a warm cache; quiet archives are dropped first. No behavior change for callers — `materializeSessionArchiveForRead` still returns a readable path, and evicted archives transparently re-materialize.

## Evidence

Three regression tests in `src/config/sessions/archive-compression.cache-budget.test.ts`. Each new case was confirmed red with the corresponding fix reverted, then green with it in place.

**Red — with the P1 fixes reverted** (`keepName` not honored by eviction, no sweep on the hit path):

```text
 ✓ src/config/sessions/archive-compression.cache-budget.test.ts > materialized archive cache aggregate budget > evicts least-recently-materialized entries once total cache bytes exceed the budget
 × src/config/sessions/archive-compression.cache-budget.test.ts > materialized archive cache aggregate budget > keeps a materialized archive readable when it alone exceeds the budget
   → expected false to be true // Object.is equality
 × src/config/sessions/archive-compression.cache-budget.test.ts > materialized archive cache aggregate budget > expires aged entries while still serving the archive being read
   → expected true to be false // Object.is equality
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
```

**Green — current head `cffb5b82e7`**, both archive suites in one parallel run (Node v24.16.0):

```text
 ✓ archive-compression.cache-budget.test.ts > evicts least-recently-materialized entries once total cache bytes exceed the budget  118ms
 ✓ archive-compression.cache-budget.test.ts > keeps a materialized archive readable when it alone exceeds the budget  14ms
```
