prs.title: fix: honor trusted admin authority for eligible Access programs
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

An authenticated administrator assigned a named operator role cannot use an otherwise permitted and entitled Access program when that role omits `accessPrograms`.

## User Impact

Administrators can use eligible Access programs without enumerating each mode. An explicit `accessPrograms.cyber` list, including `[]` for Standard only, remains a ceiling for administrators too. Operators without admitted `operator.admin` authority still require explicit nonstandard grants.

This intentionally changes omission semantics for named administrator roles. Set an explicit list when a narrower ceiling is intended. Model and agent permissions, account ownership, provider entitlement, tools, sandbox rules, external-action controls, and live revocation remain enforced. There is no new configuration option or migration.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing Access policy owner now uses the initiating operator's admitted scopes together with the role ceiling. Model presentation and requester catalogs consume that same authority, including through child runs and internal adapters; synthetic administrator RPC scopes cannot elevate the original requester. The rule applies to supported Access programs rather than one program exception.

The simplified change retains the existing authority and policy owners: no parallel permission system, state manager, or compatibility reader. Against base `e29577b7d7df`, production code is +12 net lines, tests +121, docs +8, and the allocation record +2. The 121-line allocation covers distinct execution, adapter, ceiling, recovery, and retained-requester boundaries; it does not raise the shared baseline.

## Evidence

**Real isolated Gateway and provider replay (November 6):** authenticated named roles used the production child-spawn path, with actual provider-discovered Blue eligibility.

| Original requester | Child result | Child provider requests |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Admitted administrator, omitted ceiling | Blue saved; child completed; parent final result present in operator `chat.history` | 1 |
| Administrator, explicit `cyber: []` | Recorded authorization failure | 0 |
| Read/write requester, omitted ceiling | Recorded authorization failure through the same internal child adapter | 0 |

**Retained/revoked authority:** the committed production-boundary case closes the foreground admission and parent owner, confirms the child retains current requester custody, then revokes that requester inside asynchronous payload preparation. The child aborts with zero physical provider submissions; the neighboring allowed case submits and completes. Existing account-revocation/reassignment cases separately inspect physical OpenClaw fetch or native runtime submission. Restricted-adapter, explicit-ceiling, and scheduled-recovery tests remain covered.

prs.title: fix(ui): long answers hide prompts from input recall
prs.body:
Closes #194327

## What Problem This Solves

ArrowUp can miss even the latest loaded user prompt after a long answer produces 100 or more assistant/tool transcript entries. Limit recall by the latest 100 nonempty user inputs, rather than the last 100 raw rows.

## User Impact

Recent loaded prompts remain recallable after long runs, and ArrowDown restores the unsent draft. Existing caret guards, per-traversal snapshot, ordering and local-command merge remain unchanged. No extra history fetch, retention, storage, configuration or Gateway change.

## Evidence

[Built Gateway + built Control UI Chromium proof, inspected before/after screenshots and exact measurements](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194332#issuecomment-6697788637) on `771a9b4e1743da518d1b39d1a0ea5ffe3cf6851c`, compared with main `936f38793bab7199ea2cbe11fb5ef559062254a1`.

Main misses a loaded prompt behind 106 assistant rows; the candidate recalls it. Both restore drafts and pass the short-session control; recall adds no history reads. Ordinary pagination loads the older prompt before either recall attempt. Three focused unit files (13 tests), the local-command control and the existing bundled Chromium recall E2E pass. The updated unit and E2E regressions both fail on main. Tests are consolidated into existing cases with net zero test lines; no allocation added.

Real served gzip: startup −13 B, chat boot +31 B, combined +18 B against merge-base. The original commit by @AmelioMansour is preserved; the documentation clarifies that only loaded inputs count.

## Merge Risk

Two-way door: reverting fully restores previous behavior, with no persisted-state or public-contract changes. Blast radius is Control UI composer history traversal over already-loaded chat messages; the first traversal may scan more loaded rows, while subsequent movement reuses the existing snapshot.

prs.title: fix(cli): publish CoreDNS config atomically with preserved permissions
prs.body:
Closes #184888

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes: `openclaw dns setup --apply` rewrites an existing CoreDNS `Corefile` (and its `.server` files) by truncating in place, so a crash or ENOSPC mid-write destroys the operator's DNS configuration with no backup and no recovery copy (the file lives outside OpenClaw's state dir).

## User Impact
A failed write no longer destroys the previous Corefile or `.server` contents. Existing file and parent-directory permissions are preserved (the previous code kept them by writing directly); newly created files keep `writeFileSync`'s umask-respecting permissions instead of the helper's restrictive defaults; CoreDNS setups that use a symlinked `Corefile` or a symlinked `conf.d` keep working and now also publish atomically.

## Why This Change Was Made
`writeFileSudoIfNeeded` called `fs.writeFileSync` on the final path (and `sudo tee` as fallback), which truncates before any content is written. It now uses `@openclaw/fs-safe`'s `replaceFileAtomicSync` (temp-file + rename): a failed publication leaves the previous bytes exactly as they were, verified by a regression that injects a `renameSync` failure. Options chosen deliberately: `preserveExistingMode: true` so existing rwx bits survive, `dirMode` pinned to the immediate parent's current mode so helper defaults cannot tighten existing directories, and `mode: 0o666 & ~process.umask()` for new files. Symlinked Corefiles publish to their real target (dangling links resolve the link target, normalizing its real parent when the target does not exist yet). The `sudo tee` fallback is unchanged.

## Evidence
Level A (real CLI entry `dns setup --apply` driven by the repo's test harness with synthetic paths and no operator files touched):
- Rename failure injected: the pre-existing Corefile is byte-identical afterward. Red on base (the truncate path left it partial), green with this change.
- Existing Corefile and parent directory modes preserved after a successful rewrite (0755/0644 fixtures); a newly created Corefile gets `0o666 & ~umask` rather than fs-safe's 0600.
- Real symlinked Corefile, a dangling link, and a symlinked `conf.d` directory all publish correctly and preserve the link itself; a nested dangling case whose target sits inside a symlinked directory also passes.
- All 12 cases in `src/cli/dns-cli.test.ts` pass (node 24.19, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <file> --run`).
- Independent Codex review of the final diff found four findings, all addressed and re-verified (restrictive default modes, new-file umask mode, symlink handling, dangling-link parent normalization).
- Known boundary disclosed deliberately: fs-safe's `applyDirectoryMode` chmods the parent directory even when its mode already matches and does not restore it on failure; the privilege-escalation fallback (`sudo tee`) is unchanged and out of this fix's scope.
- Not run locally: tsgo/extension-boundary lanes and a live CoreDNS installation (CI covers the type lanes).

prs.title: fix(sms): preserve callback capacity across upload sources [AI]
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Concurrent slow SMS uploads can prevent callbacks from other sources from reaching ingress.

## User Impact

Callbacks from unrelated client addresses retain reader capacity during a burst from one source. Pending reads are limited to eight per resolved client address within the existing 64-reader account-route limit. Callbacks sharing a provider egress address share that eight-reader budget; reverse proxies must use the existing trusted-proxy configuration for accurate attribution.

## Why This Change Was Made

The SMS plugin now applies the existing keyed limiter to client addresses before reading bodies. Route admission happens first so active client keys remain bounded. Both slots are released on completion and failure. Signature verification, durable acceptance, body size/time limits, and validated-sender quotas retain their existing behavior. Enough distinct sources can still reach the aggregate ceiling.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/sms/src/webhook.boundary.test.ts extensions/sms/src/webhook.test.ts extensions/sms/src/webhook.delivery-admission.test.ts extensions/sms/src/gateway.test.ts extensions/sms/src/ingress-spool.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 49 tests passed across five files, 53.62 seconds wall time. The boundary scenario completes in about one second; CI timing is pending.
- The new registered-route HTTP regression failed before the patch: a signed callback received 429 during held uploads. It passes with the patch, including aggregate overload, connection closure, and recovery controls.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p extensions/sms/tsconfig.json --noEmit`: passed after SDK declaration preparation.

## What Problem This Solves

Teams tests duplicated parts of the inbound runner and attachment policy, while the test isolation guard treated SQLite file URIs as literal paths.

## User Impact

No user-visible production change. This strengthens internal tests and private test support; production LOC delta is zero. The test-line ratchet remains unresolved, so this is not ready to land.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fixtures now use the real public inbound runner and isolated session persistence, with dispatch injected at its existing per-turn boundary. Cleanup joins session work and canonical SQLite cleanup before deleting owned roots, while explicit runtime-config reload snapshots remain intact.

Attachment checks assert ordered saved results and adapter forwarding without duplicating media policy or replacing the existing real SharePoint storage path. The SQLite guard checks NUL before canonical decoding and retains physical containment and original opener arguments. Superseded suites and the retired SQLite coordinator remain removed.

The correction is integrated on frozen base 91d08c31d14cd85be17e5ecb4d8a0ec075ef53bb. Final head is f7a21e31e0976f3ea1de083cede24f7965fd8200: 15 test/private-support source files, +500/-197 lines, plus the exact test-line allocation.

Passing D core lint/core types/core-test types/plugin production types are retained for unchanged applicable source. E changes only truthful core-managed generic typing, Promise collection typing/equivalent iterable use, braces and a dead initializer; the 181-case run remains D evidence.
- **Final source review:** one complete review of E and its whole owner/caller context found no actionable findings. This was source-only, not another runtime or CI run.
- **Environment:** Darwin arm64, pinned Bun 1.4.4-canary.1+191755ec1, Node 26.12.1 launcher. The remote backend stopped before receiver/tests; normal trusted-source local fallback supplied these results. No Linux, native Windows or live Teams proof is claimed.

**Budget and remaining gates:** the actual pre-grant counter ran on staged candidate source before C was signed: 6,442,408 lines against 6,441,800, +253 counted test lines, exit 1. prs.title: improve: avoid dependency scans during Android release cache setup
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Android Store and Internal releases spend about 12 seconds computing a Gradle cache key after mobile dependencies are installed.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. Release setup avoids about 10.4 seconds of unnecessary dependency-tree hashing in the controlled benchmark. The cache key, restore-only authority, signing, builds, and uploads retain their existing behavior. No build was published for this experiment.

## Why This Change Was Made

Move Android toolchain setup before the existing mobile dependency installation. The pinned Gradle action's broad globs otherwise traverse node_modules even though none of those files contributes to this cache key. Node/pnpm/Bun setup remains first; dependencies remain installed before release preparation.

The final change adds no helper, cache, input, job, test, or test-budget allocation. Temporary measurement controls and the benchmark script are removed from the final diff. Production workflow delta: three lines moved; documentation: two lines added.

## Evidence

[Nonpublishing benchmark run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42306718244) succeeded. Qualification and upload jobs were skipped. [Raw results and CPU profiles](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42306718244/artifacts/13545524520) are retained for seven days.

**Acceptance rule was declared in this PR before dispatch:** same seven hashed files and exact cache key in every sample; median saving at least 1,000 ms; observed p95 (maximum of five) no worse; peak RSS within 20%; dependency-tree filesystem calls zero for the candidate and nonzero for the baseline. Every condition passed.

| Hashing metric | After dependency install | Before dependency install |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Filesystem calls per sample | 505,300 | 72,667 |
| Calls under node_modules | 432,583 | 0 |
| Median wall time | 12.147 s | 1.723 s |
| Observed p95 / maximum | 12.462 s | 1.839 s |
| Wall range | 12.016–12.462 s | 1.686–1.839 s |
| Median CPU time | 13.526 s | 2.064 s |
| Maximum peak RSS | 223.30 MiB | 168.72 MiB |

Five serial, interleaved after/before pairs used fresh Node processes after one filesystem priming pair, identical source `36a1c58e91dd9ae991edd76f9ccbfdcd056c5fa0`, Node 24.22.1, eight reported Linux x64 CPUs, and 30.95 GiB RAM. Only the baseline received the actual filtered mobile release install. Samples used the pinned provider's real `@actions/glob@0.7.0` and hash patterns. Both trees always hashed the same seven Gradle files to `setup-java-Linux-x64-gradle-194efd598202594ca8e871c54cebb3f156984f9bfacda95bdca1f69575a0ab65`.

Separate excluded CPU-profile samples show the removed work in filesystem stat and glob/minimatch traversal. This is an 85.8% reduction in measured hashing time, not an independently measured cache-service lookup or whole-release improvement.

[Committed reproducible workload and preparation](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/56487800784106e1d731b407d7ecc5766fb8c566): at that proof revision the workflow prepares clean/installed source worktrees and runs `node scripts/perf/android-gradle-cache-key.mjs campaign <clean-source> <installed-source> <glob-package> <pinned-provider-source> <output-dir>`. The temporary operation is intentionally absent from the final workflow.

Final checks passed: workflow validation, 194 focused routing/guard tests (8 skipped), documentation inventory, formatting, and whitespace. Fresh local AutoReview against base `36a1c58e91dd9ae991edd76f9ccbfdcd056c5fa0` completed for the final candidate with no findings through P2. Local ClawSweeper is unavailable; AutoReview is the selected local fallback, with hosted ClawSweeper review requested when ready. [Final-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42307452620) settled with 45 passing checks, 51 intentional skips, and no failures on `873a0b67710d15087bb05b167b2939682b3070a3`. No merge or further build publication is part of this task.

prs.title: fix(ui): recover focused Gateway desktops when Host Desktop is off
prs.body:
Continues #178405 from the original RoboClaw contribution, at Vítor's request. This personal-fork PR starts from the original PR's exact published head `83ac2b2d3763fb005304fc2e3eb32256f69b19b6`, preserving its commit ancestry, authorship and recorded evidence. Review and CI results below retain their original revision and do not imply a fresh qualification of this PR.

Follow-up to #177888. Related: #174368 (already closed).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: focused Gateway Desktop windows show an unavailable notice and empty picker when Host Desktop is disabled, instead of the setup recovery already available in chat.

## User Impact

Explicit Gateway desktops and focused sessions targeting that Gateway now reuse setup guidance, authorized enablement, and same-host retry. Back is available during setup/sign-in and other nonconnected focused states, including the unselected picker.

Desktop remains admin-only. Enablement requires the existing config authority and explicit action; OpenClaw does not change OS sharing permissions. No new settings, schema, migration, or setup owner.

## Why This Change Was Made

#177888 fixed chat recovery but deliberately left focused windows unchanged. This follow-up wires those missing entry points into the same setup and runtime-config owners rather than introducing another Systems-navigation flow.

The quality follow-up adds only a small admission regression: an advertised Desktop method must still reject a non-admin connection, offer no Enable action, dispatch no config patch/desktop observation, and retain Back. Production code is unchanged by that follow-up.

## Evidence

**Latest CI repair:** `83ac2b2d3763fb005304fc2e3eb32256f69b19b6`, tree `9cb472af62e872681ee6ade63f6a12201ebac5b3`, a normal child of the approved copy head `b467669acd42a56213f54a91675e88ea5b60f680`. Complete remote tree, parent, four-file delta and human co-author credit were verified.

- **Attachment defect reproduced and repaired:** a pending original-file download was cancelled when a same-session metadata refresh recreated its destination callbacks. The download resolver and attachment-input callbacks now retain identity within their existing host/read lifetime. Snapshot fields still refresh normally; no cancellation, destination, policy, authentication or live-connection guard was removed.
- **Deterministic regression:** the existing file-navigation scenario holds the original HTTP bytes, publishes a same-session title change and commits that frame before releasing the download. It fails at the same missing `Remove notes.md` chip on the pre-repair production code and passes after the producer repair. A plain focused replay had passed before this ordering was controlled; that replay was not counted as a fix.
- **Context test corrected to the actual contract:** the production shell intentionally warms lazy code at idle. The scenario now explicitly waits for that real code preload, then verifies that opening Details still performs **zero context-report RPCs**. It retains the later exactly-one report request and displayed breakdown checks. No idle warmup was disabled and no timeout, retry or skip was added.
- **25/25 browser cases passed** across both failed files and the original Desktop document flow. **71/71 existing consumer tests passed**, including real destination/connection/policy/auth changes, hidden/unmounted readers and pending-read handoff/retirement. Both scoped type graphs, typed lint, formatting and whitespace passed.
- **Fresh independent four-file P0–P3 review: scoped-clean**, with the complete patch and unchanged authority/idle-owner context supplied intact. The review was static; it is separate from the executed tests and earlier review scopes.
- **Published-head CI is not green:** [run 40975725218](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40975725218) completed with failures in [UI shard 1/3](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40975725218/job/123803629647) (split-diff scroll geometry) and [UI E2E shard 5/7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40975725218/job/123803629671) (new-session permission persistence). The checkout was GitHub merge candidate `8f4e3b0e47be4c1f940abdd785a4094403f07f6c`, combining this head with main `878e682ecc3228e7bb9a535254e0bddaa4d97e7f`. Passing branch-only proof does not resolve these failures. Main has since added a committed-draft wait for the permission scenario; integrating it and upstream attachment ownership still needs qualified publication on this PR. The split-diff failure remains unexplained; a later focused replay is not a claimed fix. No manual CI rerun or dispatch was used. Prior CI outcomes remain bound to their original heads.
- **Current readiness:** not merge-ready. Reconcile the overlapping attachment implementation with main and publish the qualified refreshed candidate. New real-Gateway source/session acceptance for the unpublished candidate is recorded below; it does not qualify the unchanged published head by itself. Earlier Gateway proof remains bound to its recorded source. No refreshed local candidate has been published here.

The approved Desktop copy, buttons, layout, styles, setup behavior and earlier source history are unchanged by this repair. There is no new public API, config option, permission rule or state owner. The production growth retains operation bindings at the existing producers instead of weakening the consumer's cancellation guards.

<details>
<summary>Unpublished refreshed candidate acceptance — not published-head CI</summary>

**Local source tree:** `5f2043107c70cc67a516683176258f743fce4614`, against selected main `3effbc5ae15d9d7b4f670d8e2d561277bab99f65`. This candidate is **not published on this PR**. Canonical PR source preparation has now succeeded in a clean managed checkout at the existing published head. Integrating the selected main source remains incomplete; successful preparation is not a source publication or proof of actual push permission. The existing published head and its failed CI remain unchanged.

**New real-Gateway acceptance: 2/2 passed**, focused source and session routes, using the built Control UI, a real non-minimal in-process Linux Gateway and native WebSockets. Gateway RPC responses were not mocked. The session was created through real `sessions.create` with a genuinely generated and paired disposable fixture identity; no operator credential or real session was borrowed. Both Gateways closed cleanly, and the temporary probe was removed without changing the recorded source tree.

Sanitized observations, independently checked for both selectors:

| Boundary | Source route | Session route |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Before explicit Enable | 0 config patches, 0 observations | 0 config patches, 0 observations |
| Authorized config write | exactly 1 successful `config.patch` | exactly 1 successful `config.patch` |
| Submitted patch | `{ "desktop": { "host": { "enabled": true } } }` | same minimal patch |
| Persistence and application | independent disk readback; real hot reload | independent disk readback; real hot reload |
| Observation target | every request used `{ "kind": "host" }` | every request used `{ "kind": "host" }` |
| Account boundary | actual `DESKTOP_CREDENTIALS_REQUIRED`; sign-in form | actual `DESKTOP_CREDENTIALS_REQUIRED`; sign-in form |
| Back | returned to preceding dashboards route | returned to preceding dashboards route |

Built entry asset SHA-256: `d61840dcf646e99b65164ea7caf130c394acefe832b93009582717deb69d979a`. The peer supplied a **synthetic TCP RFB 3.8 ARD security offer**: this is real Gateway/config/transport proof, **not** physical macOS permission, actual account authentication, desktop pixels or model inference. No account password was submitted. Current inventory can replace Check again with readiness before a manual click settles; explicit retest remains covered by the committed synthetic-Gateway browser case, not this live trace.

**Other fresh candidate checks:** attachment browser file **4/4 passed with clean terminal exit**; Desktop/Systems and attachment owner/consumer tests **95/95 passed across 7 files**; production and focused-test type graphs passed through repository wrappers; typed lint passed on **7 production + 4 test files**, with no problems; formatting on all 12 contribution files and whitespace passed. Source-equivalent unaffected earlier browser proof is reused, not relabeled as fresh: Desktop 19, context 2, prompt attachments 11 and split-diff layout 7. The original split-diff CI failure remains unexplained.

**Fresh independent AutoReview: all 12 contribution files and critical unchanged owners, P0–P3 scoped-clean, no findings.** Static review is separate from runtime acceptance. Upstream now owns the stable attachment callback/download implementation; this candidate uses those main implementations byte-for-byte instead of maintaining a second producer repair. The existing file scenario retains upstream pending-RPC/resize coverage and the HTTP-pending metadata-publication regression.

Fixture recovery is not counted as product repair: an obsolete heartbeat config was rejected before startup; a null-identity CLI was refused and replaced by normal disposable identity/pairing without widening scope; an obsolete Check again wait targeted an already replaced control. The earlier attachment run that printed passes but timed out during enclosing cleanup is not terminal proof; the final recovered-runtime file run exited zero. Initial review preparation rejected generated Bun cache files before reviewing; only verified task-generated cache was separated from authored inputs, then the unchanged complete candidate was reviewed successfully.

The requester received a sanitized 24-member source/proof package, SHA-256 `43b927dfeb6f48c96f218a15542b6a4e8a0371b81c5ea7293585eba5ec239a67`. This is self-reported local-candidate evidence, not a remote commit or a claim that a private chat attachment is publicly accessible. Normal canonical publication, resulting-source equivalence, automatic CI and final mergeability remain outstanding. No manual CI rerun, branch push, force-push, merge or deployment was performed.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Failure evidence and exact verification scope</summary>

- Original file failure: [UI E2E shard 1/7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40915872088/job/123596744832), `chat-workspace-files.e2e.test.ts:175`, timed out waiting for `Remove notes.md` after Attach to session.
- Original context failure: [UI E2E shard 3/7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40915872088/job/123596744823), expected no breakdown-module request but observed one. That code-load assertion conflicted with `warmWhenIdle(ChatContextBreakdown.preload)` and the existing shell idle owner; it was replaced by the independent report-I/O condition, not merely deleted.
- The narrow unmodified replay passed six cases. A held download alone also passed. Holding it across a real same-session metadata publication exposed the attachment defect; an earlier probe that waited for a hidden mobile title to become visible was a fixture error, not product evidence.
- Correct pre-repair control: **1 failed / 3 name-filtered**, at the missing attachment chip after metadata publication. Same controlled scenario after repair: **1 passed / 3 name-filtered**. Final owning-boundary batch: **3 files, 25 passed**, 38.65s Vitest / 41.14s enclosing command.
- Consumer batch: **4 files / 49 passed** plus the existing handoff file **22 passed**; 14.88s wrapper time across two assigned Vitest shards. The attachment consumer and its adverse-case assertions are unchanged.
- Cache identity: attachment bindings are per host and renew for a changed read owner or abort signal. The per-host download delegate still reads live host state inside the unchanged download authority owner; it does not capture credentials or connection epochs as cached answers.
- Production delta: **+41 / −13** lines; test delta: **+34 / −11** lines. Existing fixtures were extended rather than adding a new server, production test seam or duplicate regression suite.
- The initial review collection split path-only metadata away from the patch. Those context-only partitions were not counted as complete patch reviews. The completed review supplied the full patch and critical source context intact to every partition; no actionable findings remained.
- Proof remains synthetic Control UI/Gateway boundary evidence, not a new physical macOS permission, real desktop login/pixels or model-inference qualification. No visual component or style changed in this repair; the approved copy comparisons remain below at their recorded source.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Approved copy update and earlier recovery evidence</summary>

**Copy predecessor:** `b467669acd42a56213f54a91675e88ea5b60f680`, tree `585e5710e592dfa95ccf38d49c785999f80ea829`, a normal child of `907c72360abab85c9880ae14640fc61fb6bc7467`. The complete published tree and the three-file delta were read back and verified.

- Shorter explanatory text names the Gateway host without assuming the browser runs on another device, and identifies the macOS account used to sign in. Network exposure, account credentials and OS permissions remain explicit.
- **Unchanged:** Enable desktop access in OpenClaw, Check again, Back, all other action labels, component structure, alignment, spacing, typography, styling, setup-state conditions, disabled actions, explicit config authority, error rendering and same-host retry. No runtime, JSX, CSS or owner code changed in this copy commit.
- The shared administrator explanation is used only by the Desktop setup notice and Systems setup surface; both uses were reviewed. Existing i18n keys and locale coverage are preserved. No foreign catalog, translation-memory or fallback-metadata edits were made.

Localization baseline/verification, the scoped production type graph, typed lint on both catalogs and the changed existing test, formatting and whitespace passed. Existing copy expectations were updated; no action/authorization assertion was removed or weakened.
- **Copy-predecessor CI failed:** [CI 40915872088](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40915872088) failed its file-attachment and context-breakdown browser scenarios. The subsequent four-file repair is documented above; this record remains bound to the copy predecessor.

<details>

prs.title: fix(gateway): scope the JSONL transcript usage estimate to the live window across boundaries
prs.body:
Refs #150579

## What Problem This Solves

A compacted session's transcript usage report (the JSONL artifact seam behind diagnostic reads) counted the whole append-only archive as live context. Content superseded by a compaction or reset stays in the file, and the chars-based estimate summed every user/assistant message ever written, so the reported total kept growing across clean compactions while the model's actual context stayed small.

A second gap sat next to it: once the estimate restarted at a boundary, eligibility was re-derived only from model-tagged assistant entries in the retained window. A summary-only window (the cut names an entry outside the message window) or a retained-user-only window (overflow compaction with a pending user message as its tail) lost the estimate until the next assistant reply, even though the summary and retained text were sitting in the model context.

## Root cause

`aggregateSessionTranscriptUsage` fills `totalTokens` from a chars estimate when no per-call usage snapshot provides one. `readLatestSessionUsageFromTranscriptFileAsync` feeds it the full JSONL transcript, and the estimate accumulated `estimatedTranscriptChars` over the whole scanned set with no notion of boundary markers or the retained window they name. The boundary restart also reset `sawEstimateModelIdentity` from the retained entries alone, while `finish()` requires that flag, so any window without a surviving model-tagged assistant reported no estimate at all.

## Fix

- The JSONL reader passes `compaction`/`reset` boundary records through with their `summary`/`firstKeptEntryId` fields, and forwards each entry's id, instead of skipping markers.
- The accumulator keeps per-entry char counts for the current window. At a boundary it keeps the retained tail named by `firstKeptEntryId` plus the compaction summary, matching the model-context contract (compactionSummary + retained entries + post-boundary messages) and the transcript tree selector's fallback (an unknown kept target drops the pre-boundary window). The previous revision restarted the estimate at zero, which undercounts a compacted session that retains a large summary or window.
- A boundary leaves the window estimate-eligible whenever it holds counted text. A compaction or reset marker is only written by a live model session, so requiring a model-tagged assistant to survive the cut only masked reads taken between the boundary and the next reply.
- Usage snapshots (input/output/cache/cost) still aggregate over the whole record, and a fresh per-call `totalTokens` snapshot still wins over any estimate, unchanged.

## Scope

This change lives entirely in the JSONL artifact seam: `readLatestSessionUsageFromTranscriptFileAsync` reads bounded transcript artifacts and its callers are diagnostic paths. The live budget-preflight path from #150579 reads the SQLite seam, which already scopes to the active context and is untouched here; that preflight symptom stays with #150579 and the PRs addressing it directly. This branch does not close the issue.

## Evidence

- New regressions in `session-usage-estimate.test.ts`: a compaction keeps its 500-char summary plus the 2000-char retained message named by `firstKeptEntryId` while dropping the 4000-char superseded prefix; a reset keeps its named retained tail; an unknown kept target drops the pre-boundary window but still counts the summary. Three further regressions end the transcript right at the boundary (summary-only window, compaction retaining only user messages, reset retaining only user text), covering the read between the boundary and the next assistant reply; earlier versions of these tests appended that reply, which masked the eligibility drop.
- Red/green: the boundary-terminal three fail on the previous head (no estimate reported). The consolidated table preserves all 10 independent scenarios, including snapshot precedence, reset boundaries, retained-user-only windows and the structural anchor.
- Runtime proof on a real compacted session (regenerated after the earlier /tmp artifact expired): isolated Gateway plus embedded agent against the scripted provider; a real injected 400 `context_length_exceeded`, one committed auto-compaction, then one more turn. The committed marker carries a 464-char summary and names a retained 91-char user message as `firstKeptEntryId`, so the boundary leaves a summary-plus-retained-user window. The artifact is the session's real settled transcript events serialized back to legacy JSONL, with redacted variants that drop usage fields and the model-snapshot entry so the chars estimate is what gets measured. The after-fix reader reports `totalTokens: 139` on the redacted prefix ending at the boundary (ceil((464 + 91) / 4), the summary plus the retained user text) and `176` on the full redacted artifact (ceil((464 + 91 + 56 + 90) / 4), adding the post-boundary assistant and user text). On the usage-carrying artifact the reader still reports the real provider aggregates (input 105 / output 25, latest context snapshot 120 total and available), so the estimate path and the snapshot path stay separate.
- Current head `591ef68b2e9`: `node scripts/test-projects.mts src/gateway/session-usage-estimate.test.ts src/gateway/session-transcript-derived-readers.usage.test.ts src/gateway/session-utils.fs.test.ts src/gateway/session-utils.transcript-usage.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passes 4 files and 50 tests. oxfmt and type-aware oxlint pass on the consolidated test; `git diff --check` is clean.
- Shipped diagnostic proof on `591ef68b2e9`: the real settled Gateway compaction events drive the production `buildReplyDiagnosticsPayload` raw diagnostic path through `readLatestSessionUsageFromTranscriptAsync`, not just a direct reader call. With usage fields removed, the boundary-terminal artifact emits `total=139` and the full artifact emits `total=176`. The measured control emits `input=105`, `output=25`, `cacheRead=0`, `cacheWrite=0`, `total=120`. The probe prints only the session usage block, with no transcript text, credentials or endpoints.
- Test budget: `config/test-lines-allocations/session-usage-active-window.txt` allocates the exact 157 lines retained by the consolidated test. An earlier non-staged sparse-worktree run omitted 566 tracked test lines and its slack 561 claim is withdrawn. The full-index ratchet against current main `936f38793bab`, matching hosted CI, reports `6555915 / 6555910`, over 5 with net delta +157. Current main still carries that 5-line debt after #194326; the shared scalar is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(release): verify post-publication container registry readback
prs.body:
## Problem

RRI-352 identified that release verification could treat successful publication workflows as sufficient evidence without reading the published container manifests back from every registry. Missing architecture tags, stale moving aliases, or cross-registry descriptor drift could therefore escape verification.

## Solution

- add a bounded, retrying registry-v2 readback verifier for GHCR, Docker Hub, and Vercel Container Registry
- verify immutable default/slim/browser indexes and amd64/arm64 tags, cross-registry digests and descriptor sets, and policy-owned moving aliases
- run readback after Vercel mirroring and include its outcome in the workflow summary
- update release verification guidance for regular and extended-stable releases
- authorize credential-bearing Bearer challenges only for HTTPS registry-owned token realms (plus Docker Hub's explicit auth realm)
- compare complete normalized Vercel platform descriptors while ignoring JSON property insertion order
- retain distinct workflow contracts for recovery authorization, secret-safe handoff, concurrency, and copy → smoke → promotion ordering

## Tests

- 32 focused registry-readback and Vercel-publication tests pass
- script and tooling test typechecks pass
- targeted Oxlint and Oxfmt checks pass
- test-line ratchet passes exactly
- local workflow validation is unavailable because the host lacks Python `venv`/pre-commit support; hosted CI owns that remaining gate

## Review remediation

- rejected insecure or unrelated Bearer realms before any credential-bearing request
- restored full descriptor metadata validation and canonicalized nested platform metadata
- restored the distinct release-safety tests that had been consolidated away
- added final-effect tests for allowed/rejected credential flows, descriptor drift, and equivalent reordered metadata

## Limitations

This repair verifies published manifests and alias/descriptor consistency. It does not replace the separate attestation checks. Live reads of a private Vercel registry require existing Docker credential state; when unavailable, release verification must report that live-readback gap explicitly rather than infer success from the workflow conclusion.

## Worked on by

- @RomneyDa

prs.title: fix(gateway): session observer drops run digests when agent events are emitted inside a database write
prs.body:
Related: #181660, #182744 (same guard message from a different path, the Control UI `chat.send`; not closed by this PR)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Gateway log repeats `Session observer event failed` with `Session read batch cannot reenter an active SQLite writer admission` and the Control UI session observer drops that run's digest when an agent event is emitted while its producer still holds the agent database writer (for example from a worker write reservation).

## User Impact

User impact: operators stop seeing the recurring `Session observer event failed` warning, and Control UI observer digests (preamble headlines, progress) keep arriving for runs whose events are published from inside a database write. No configuration or protocol change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The observer subscription in `startGatewayEventSubscriptions` called `sessionObserver.handleEventAsync(evt)` directly from the agent-event listener, so the observer's queued work inherited the producer's async context. When the producer was an active store writer or admission turn, the observer's ordered session read was treated as a nested read of that writer and refused by the write-admission guard.

Every other entry into the observer already runs detached: the deprecated `handleEvent`, the `background` helper, and the lifecycle-error retry path (`work.background(() => work.handleEventAsync(...))`). The subscriber now uses the same `runInDetachedAsyncContext`. The reader still captures config, routing and env synchronously before detaching (`captureSessionObserverRead`), the work stays tracked by the observer's own `acceptedWork` scope, and `disposeAsync` drains it at shutdown, so only the inherited context changes; ownership, ordering and shutdown behavior are unchanged.

## Evidence

- New regression test `src/gateway/server-runtime-subscriptions.observer-context.test.ts` uses a real session store (`withOpenClawTestState`), the real observer and the real ordered read path. A preamble event is emitted from inside `runOpenClawAgentWorkerWrite` while the writer is held until the observer's read has either queued behind it or failed.
  - On `main` without the fix: fails with `Session observer event failed` and `Session read batch cannot reenter an active SQLite writer admission: {"database":".../agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite","operation":"worker",...}`.
  - With the fix: passes, and the `session.observer` digest reaches the subscribed connection.
- `pnpm test src/gateway/server-runtime-subscriptions.test.ts src/gateway/session-observer.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: 2 files, 79 tests passed.
- `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint --type-aware` on the changed files; assertion-safety, line-cap and test-lines ratchets against `upstream/main`: OK.
- Cost: the new file runs in about 3.7 s of test time (gateway-server project); the single-file wall time of about 90 s is module-graph transform, not the test.
- Not run locally: `tsgo` typecheck and the broad suites (left to PR CI).

<details>
<summary>Red run on main (without the fix)</summary>

```
×  gateway-server  src/gateway/server-runtime-subscriptions.observer-context.test.ts > publishes the observer preamble for events emitted inside a writer admission
AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times
  "Session observer event failed",
  { "error": [Error: Session read batch cannot reenter an active SQLite writer admission: {"database":"$OPENCLAW_HOME/.openclaw/agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite","operation":"worker","workerOperations":[],"threadId":0,"isMainThread":true,"ageMs":630}] }
```

</details>

## Revision 2 (rebased on `d2db8ded`)

- Added `config/test-lines-allocations/session-observer-detached-context.txt` (87 lines) for the new regression file; the shared scalar is unchanged. prs.title: fix(whatsapp): judge group metadata cache expiry on elapsed time
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

WhatsApp group titles and member lists are cached for five minutes, and both cache layers measured that five minutes with `Date.now()` — the wall clock. A backward wall-clock step (NTP correction after a laptop wake, a container time sync) moves the stored deadline into the future by the same amount, so an entry written before the step keeps being served until the wall clock catches up. A member added after the step is missing from the cached roster, so an outbound `@mention` for that person goes out as plain text, and the same roster feeds Baileys sender-key recipients; the title stays stale for the same window.

Reads moved: `baileys-cache.ts:29` stored `expiresAt: Date.now() + ttlMs`, `:43` compared `entry.expiresAt <= Date.now()`; `group-metadata-cache.ts:62` compared `entry.expires <= Date.now()` and five write sites seeded `Date.now() + GROUP_META_TTL_MS` (`:98`, `:104`, `:126`, `:145`, `:172`). They are one cache: `group-metadata-cache.ts:152` copies `hydratedEntry.expiresAt` into `entry.expires`.

## User Impact

After the machine's clock moves backward, group titles and member lists refresh on time again, so an `@mention` for someone added after the change resolves instead of silently turning into plain text, and the agent's group context stops serving a pre-change roster. The failure is silent — the message still sends, only the mention is dropped.

## Why This Change Was Made

The deadline is a duration, and the repository already fixes this class by measuring durations on the process-local elapsed clock.

- Both caches are process-local `Map`s, never serialized, persisted, or compared by another process, so the deadline can move to `performance.now()` with no second clock domain. `groupMetadataCache`/`baileysGroupMetaCache`/`recentMessageKeys` are constructed in `inbound/monitor.ts:107-109` and `auto-reply/monitor.ts:119-121` and only reach the two helpers.
- Accepted shape from #193147 (`2f183b38629`): change the read and the seed at each site, no new helper, drive the existing tests from the elapsed clock. `performance.now()` rather than `monotonicNow()` because extensions may only import `openclaw/plugin-sdk/*`, and bundled plugins already call it directly (`extensions/telegram/src/polling-liveness.ts:114`).
- Both files in one commit: a half-migrated pair compares monotonic values against a wall-clock read and every hydrated entry expires on first read.
- Left alone: TTL, the 500-entry cap, the `cacheRevision` guard, and `reconnectCache` serving across reconnects within one process (a restart clears all three maps).

## Evidence

Base (`origin/main` @ `ee8f4da1d7e`) with only the test changes applied — the cache stores a wall-clock deadline and still serves the entry after five elapsed minutes; with this change the same file is green:

```
AssertionError: expected 1793882969205 to be 300000 // Object.is equality
 Tests  2 failed | 12 passed (14)        <- base
 Tests  14 passed (14)                  <- this branch
```

The suites over the same caches pass too (`monitor-inbox.*`, `inbound.send-api`, `auto-reply.monitor-state`): 137 passed, 10 files.

End to end on the shipped path: the shipped Gateway runs the bundled WhatsApp plugin, its group metadata cache owner, the inbound monitor and the outbound send; the shipped `openclaw message send` CLI performs the send. With no WhatsApp account here, the channel's real `makeWASocket` client talks to a local WhatsApp Web endpoint through the shipped `OPENCLAW_WHATSAPP_WEB_SOCKET_URL` override. That endpoint speaks the real framing and `Noise_XX` handshake, answers the group IQs on the wire, and hosts a second real Signal device that decrypts the delivered stanza (`pkmsg` + `skmsg`) and reports the mention list the client sent. The only task-local change is the Noise trust anchor the client pins (`node_modules/baileys/lib/Defaults/index.js`), restored after the run; no product file is patched. A runner that stalls the Gateway's main thread after the step can keep the unresolved text in the prepared payload, so the harness repeats the send once.

Once the roster is hydrated over that transport, the peer adds `15550000333` to the group **without a group event** and the Gateway's wall clock steps back 30 s (`Date.now` only; `performance.now` keeps running). The mention is sent after 301 s of real elapsed time, so the 300 s TTL has elapsed for real:

```
GREEN — this branch, first send, performance.now=445870ms at the step:
PROOF clock step back 30000ms (Date.now only): wall 2026-11-05T12:26:12.172Z -> 2026-11-05T12:25:42.172Z
PEER roster refreshed ... participants=15550000001@...,15550000222@...,15550000333@s.whatsapp.net
PEER iq xmlns=w:g2 type=get to=120363000000000001@g.us child=query request=interactive
PEER group metadata served (#1) ... participants=15550000001@...,15550000222@...,15550000333@...
PEER message participants=15550000001@...,15550000222@...,15550000333@... group_enc=[skmsg:187B]
PEER delivery decrypted enc=[pkmsg,skmsg] text="handoff ping @15550000333" mentionedJid=["15550000333@s.whatsapp.net"]
RED — both cache files at origin/main, same harness, first send:
PROOF clock step back 30000ms (Date.now only): wall 2026-11-05T12:10:59.379Z -> 2026-11-05T12:10:29.379Z
PEER roster refreshed ... (the same silent roster change)
PEER message participants=15550000001@...,15550000222@... group_enc=[skmsg:155B]
PEER delivery decrypted enc=[pkmsg,skmsg] text="handoff ping @15550000333" mentionedJid=[]
```

The base never asks the peer for the roster (no `w:g2 … query` on the wire), so the new member is missing from both the mention resolution and the sender-key recipients; this change expires the entry on elapsed time, refetches once over the transport, and the mention reaches the group. Harness: [proofs/193311](https://github.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-winproof/tree/main/proofs/193311), both arms rerun in [this workflow](https://github.com/SunnyShu0925/oc-winproof/actions/runs/42031059101).

Not tested: a live WhatsApp account and a real OS clock change; the peer is local and the step applies to the Gateway process only.

prs.title: Ignore retired config keys that supervisors rewrite at boot
prs.body:
Fixes #193171

## What Problem This Solves

A supervisor that rewrites retired keys into `openclaw.json` on every boot can prevent Gateway startup with InvalidConfigError until someone runs `openclaw doctor --fix`.

## User Impact

Gateway startup accepts the retired `meta.lastTouchedAt`, `gateway.controlUi.allowInsecureAuth`, and empty `plugins.installs` shapes without requiring a manual Doctor run after each supervisor restart.

## Why This Change Was Made

Load drops those keys in memory before schema validation, matching the cleanup Doctor already performs. Other settings under the same objects stay. `dangerouslyDisableDeviceAuth` stays because the schema still accepts it. The file is not rewritten; the next boot strips the keys again if the supervisor puts them back.

## Evidence

Source validation for `41e46c630` (the following allocation-only commit leaves these source files unchanged):
- The focused retired-key regression passes. It preserves unrelated sibling settings and checks removal of containers left empty by cleanup (4 ms test time; 7.59 s wrapper wall time).
- All 36 eager-import-closure tests pass, including the PR wrapper inventory and extracted dependency-context checks (212.48 s wrapper wall time).
- The disabled-acceleration provisioning regression passes (1 selected test, 17 unrelated cases skipped; 58.16 s test duration, 151.21 s wrapper wall time including cold compilation).
- Shared-coercion guard, the test-line budget, scoped source-backed core lint, formatting, and whitespace checks pass. The regression was consolidated to 20 lines. Its unique `retired-startup-keys` allocation accounts for that genuine regression growth, as required by the documented test-line budget policy; the shared scalar and CI checks are unchanged.
- Fresh independent review of the scoped repair found no actionable findings.

The initial full provisioning attempt hit its existing 120 s timeout while cold compiler jobs were running; its symlink-preservation case passed, and the focused failed case passed after those jobs ended. The full provisioning suite was stopped rather than counted as passing. Generic lint preparation hit a 300 s plugin-SDK declaration timeout; the supported source-backed core lint passed. The additional broad type run was stopped. Full build/test, production types on this repaired head, isolated Gateway startup, and stable-version upgrade replay remain unverified locally. Helper-level checks do not establish those outcomes.

The first repaired-head CI merged newer main changes and found only 10 lines of remaining budget for the 20-line regression. The allocation-only follow-up was checked against that exact CI merge tree and comparison base: 6,484,529 test lines fit the 6,484,539-line ceiling with 10 lines of slack. This keeps the sibling-preservation and empty-container regression coverage without depending on incidental upstream slack.

CI on `252c054cd8aafac9d514f9098b3631b2c0ba5f91` is green: 67 successful checks, 58 skipped, and one neutral check, with no failures or running checks at verification. The main CI run and separate native Darwin job both completed successfully. The local validation gaps above remain explicit.

prs.title: fix: stop Windows services when PATH omits System32
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Windows, stopping a local model-service process could leave the owned child running when the parent PATH omitted System32. The shared tree-termination owner launched bare `taskkill`, so the OS helper was never found.

## User Impact

Owned local-service shutdown works without depending on CLI PATH initialization. The same existing tree-signal owner serves forced/graceful shutdown and downstream process consumers. Unix behavior, public APIs, signal arguments, grace periods and helper-completion deadlines are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve `System32/taskkill.exe` beneath a drive-absolute `SystemRoot`, then `WINDIR`, with the conventional Windows-directory fallback, directly in the existing producer. This avoids another execution owner, registry lookup, existence probe, setting or dependency. Explicit PATH-provided taskkill shims are intentionally no longer selected.

## Evidence

Native Windows, inherited Node **24.19.0**, repository-pinned pnpm **12.15.0**, normal frozen dependencies, base `526371eefd46fafe813250493e4a056ec32ec720`. Current upstream admits this runtime; no engine/PATH execution override was used. The restricted PATH below is the isolated reproducer inside the test, not a toolchain workaround.

```text
Original owner: native service-stop regression FAILS
  expected process.kill(ownedPid, 0) to throw; owned process was still alive
Fixed owner: 36 unit tests + 1 real Windows owned-service regression PASS
Real stopLocalServiceProcess, normal PATH: closed=true, alive=false, error=null (2519ms)
Real stopLocalServiceProcess, restricted PATH: closed=true, alive=false, error=null (2899ms)
```

The native regression starts an actual Node child, waits for IPC readiness, calls the production local-service owner, joins helper completion, checks OS PID extinction, then joins the child. Its emergency cleanup cannot turn the baseline failure into a pass. Alternate-drive/spaced-root and invalid-root/WINDIR controls extend the existing unit suite.

- Affected process/reaping/service-shutdown/monotonic consumer suites pass; one existing platform skip is retained.

prs.title: fix(feishu): streaming cards repeat the reply so far when preview and block streaming are both on
prs.body:
Related: #192446, #192482

## What Problem This Solves

With `channels.feishu.streaming` set to `{ mode: "partial", block: { enabled: true } }`, every card after an idle close restarts the reply and repeats earlier paragraphs. Replays on main `06e3bb94b2d1` confirmed this after #192482, which documented but did not fix it.

## User Impact

Ordinary continuation cards start after accepted text. The fix stays Feishu-only with no configuration or public API change.

Recovery credit belongs to its first covering preview occurrence. Block-only recovery grants no credit. Partial receipts must cover the frozen earlier base before crediting the current message. A start during a held close freezes earlier text without provisional credit.

An old block uses its source's accepted remainder only with unused current-preview coverage. A frozen open-card copy survives previews and text-free starts. A matching old block advances that copy. Suppression needs a known cursor and current preview coverage. Without a cursor, the first matching block appends. Suppression grants no recovery credit.

When no earlier message has shown preview or block text, a covered lower index prompts the dispatcher to re-learn its source offset. The same callbacks can describe a restarted subscription or a previewless earlier message's late block. That trade matches main.

## Why This Change Was Made

Core idles before delivery finalization. Feishu closes the card and corrects provisional coverage at settlement. Recovery cannot cross a failed gap. Rewritten prefixes keep the whole snapshot. Final text prevents rebuilding. Late settlement keeps appended blocks, but later snapshots can replace them.

Continuation cards reopen unfinished fences. A cut after the marker or inside the info string completes the opening line from the extending snapshot and keeps the code. With no code yet, the completed opener stands alone. A cut after the complete opening line reuses the original opener. A matching closing-fence remainder and following blank lines drop. A completed non-opener stays literal. The scanner uses CR, LF and CRLF endings and treats Unicode line separators as data. The old card gets no synthetic closer. Continuations drop leading separator whitespace and keep indentation.

Accepted limits remain.

- The unlearned index gap can lose text with rejected closes. No built-in route was established.
- Measured text-free restarts now match main's count except `u4-block-first-next`, `u11-nomatch` and the selective-prefix case. Restarts after the failed attempt or any earlier message showed preview or block text still repeat. A first block arriving before its preview or not covered by it can leave later blocks repeating too. The selective-prefix replay closes `[P] C.[P] C.` where main closes `[P] C.`. This PR introduced those above-main repeats.
- A fresh subscription creates the index gap only after an earlier counted assistant start. Pre-start failures add no epoch. Retry evidence combines source traces and synthetic core-subscriber replays. No complete provider retry loop was run. The configured-prefix replay uses the core dispatcher, so that case reaches a built-in formatting route.
- Rejected CardKit writes recover the whole block, including already shown text. Main sends the same static. Gaps, non-prefix receipts, recovered tails and preview catch-up can repeat accepted text. A lagging preview can add a copy. A successful held close after a new message starts repeats its frozen earlier preview, as on main. Eleven recorded core pipelines kept preview delivery before blocks.
- Eight direct plain-index orders still exceed main and round 17. They are `f22-1512`, `f22-0767`, `f22-1889`, `f21-1582`, `f21-0555`, `f22-0378`, `f21-2129` and `f21-2032`. They combine accepted-rest consumption, starts, held closes or partial receipts. No safer Feishu-only replacement was established.
- An unmatched old block appends after current text. A later snapshot can replace it and an accepted close suppresses recovery, as on main. In `f22-2327`, the final behavior and main show no `Y.`. In `f61-1644`, the final behavior shows two `X.` copies against three at round 18 and main. Main replaces the same old occurrence, then masks its loss with another repeat.
- A held close rejected before any later preview can lose its unaccepted text, as on main. A later rejected close can lose an earlier frozen base, as on main. A restarted twin can coalesce with an in-flight close. These complete routes remain unproven.
- Core collapses identical consecutive paragraphs in previews but not blocks. A removed preview copy can arrive later as a block or share recovery with a separately authored copy. The latter gets credit once. Normal response prefixes decorate blocks but not previews, so unmatched text appends on main too.
- Block chunks, including reopened fences, glue to the preview without a separator, as on main. Covered blocks can open empty cards. Finals during an earlier close show the whole message. Mid-word cuts remain.
- Only fenced code reopens. Tables, lists, block quotes, HTML and fences inside quotes or four-space indentation do not. Cuts inside markers, content lines including inner fences, continuation indentation or inline backticks can render wrong. Separator-only U+2028 or U+2029 extensions can lose that info-line separator, as before this change.
- An unfinished closer-looking line extended into code can lose one `~` after an empty-answer reasoning update. A final then preview before late settlement can lose `X.`. These and close-before-card-start lack an established complete core route.

A full fix needs core to pass the new message's index to `onAssistantMessageStart`, which this PR does not change.

Candidate b and the empty-preview relaxation pass all committed rows. Candidate b removes the `u4` and `u11` repeats, while the relaxation removes only `u4`. Both add `f22-2350` above main with four `X.` copies against three. A prefix-metadata repair also introduced other repeats and losses in probes. Older open-copy and recovery-credit variants lack final-file reruns. Removing the nonblank-opener-tail guard passes the fence rows but changes the separator-only Unicode probes.

Tests remove 88 blank separators and join mock calls, a comment and an assertion with a local rename to keep net test lines at 0. Existing assertions remain. The support file equals main. Against `06e3bb94`, production is +282/-5 and tests +152/-152. Counted lines grow from 1,314 to 1,557 against cap 700 and 1,783 to 1,868 against cap 1,000. Removing blanks does not reduce those counts.

The Gateway proof comment reports runs on `5f153378`, before rounds 20 to 22.

## Evidence

Final head is `4478d6d39fef6d4fae9a0c29de7cd01a85637bc0`, with 31 commits after `031a06e6`. These are local results, with no hosted CI result claimed for this head.

Hash-restored swaps select 79 of 156 tests and skip 77.

| Production | Result |
| --- | --- |
| main `06e3bb94` | 36 failed, 43 passed |
| previous head `5f153378` | 7 failed, 72 passed |
| final `4478d6d3` | 79 passed |
| candidate b | 79 passed |
| empty-preview relaxation | 79 passed |
| exactly-one-behind | `retry gap` fails, 78 passed |
| preview-only earlier text | `block guard` fails, 78 passed |

Four fence rows cover tilde and backtick openers, partial info strings, bare markers and indentation. `retry` checks that the learned offset carries to the next message. `retry gap` covers multiple text-free starts. `trade` pins the ambiguous late-block reading. `block guard` deliberately pins the documented repeat `A.\n\nX.X.` while main shows `A.\n\nX.`.

The corpus ran on `40430f95`. Round 22 changes only comments and tests. Of 1,197 saved cases, 1,189 are identical and eight change. Of 119 final controls, 117 are identical and two change. All 119 matched-main controls are identical. Of 1,470 recordings, 1,460 are identical and ten change. Those changes are the split-fence repairs. All 117 source-order and 87 accepted-receipt comparisons stay unchanged from rounds 19 and 20.

Against round 20, 17 corpus records change to main's text-free restart count. Fourteen of 5,000 fuzz orders change, with no newly changed marker below both main and its authored count. Four orders reach main's count below the authored count, `f21-0135`, `f21-2107`, `f22-0093` and `f22-2309`. Other inherited losses remain. The callbacks cannot identify both histories. Six replays remain field-identical at the final head.

The Gateway proof uses a local HTTPS fixture and no real tenant. At `5f153378`, cross-card output retained 1,722 of 1,728 answer characters without repeating non-whitespace text. Rejection still repeated 55 accepted characters. The indented control retained its extra fenced rendering. That matrix does not establish the later recovery and fence repairs. No Gateway, provider or tenant run was made at `4478d6d3`.

Gates at `4478d6d3` against `06e3bb94`.

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| full Feishu, one worker | 89 files, 1,003 tests, exit 0 |
| all ten baseline checks, `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true` | exit 0, net test lines 0, total 6,452,171 against 6,452,151 |
| extensions, extensions-test and scripts types | each cold 0, live `TS2322` probe 2, restored 0 |
| typed lint with `--deny-warnings` and format checks, production, test and support | exit 0 |
| diff checks against main, `40430f95`, `5f153378` and worktree | exit 0 |
| six replays | exit 0 |

Net 0 permits the inherited 20-line excess. CI treats line-cap growth as advisory.

prs.title: fix(agents): hand delegated failures back to their parent
prs.body:
## Summary
- Return failed subagents' cause and saved progress to their owning parent without waiting on the failed root's descendants.
- Quiet inherited error attention only after durable input/result custody, while preserving child diagnostics, collector ownership and genuine native human questions.
- Keep failure diagnostics in the committed handoff, preserve ready unconsumed failed-collector findings, and count handed-off failures correctly.
- Acknowledge failure custody only for children represented in the committed input. A bounded batch keeps omitted failures unacknowledged and recoverable.
- Collector results: acknowledge only failures whose diagnostics survive in the final persisted tool result, after transcript truncation and detail reduction, and only for the expected host completion. Failures dropped from the stored result stay unacknowledged and recoverable.
- Bind private settle retries to the findings they replay: a retry that reuses the retained message acknowledges only failed runs whose diagnostics are in those exact bytes and that are still in the current cohort. A legacy retained message without that record adds no acknowledgement, and a new run generation under the same ID does not inherit it.
- Keep the 160,000-character findings budget, with its truncation markers, per-result floors, stable order and overflow summary.
- Keep the receipt in cold reads: the compact SQL session-list projection now selects the four `failureHandoff` fields, including the `parentCompletion` mirror. No schema, writer, codec, migration or retention change.
- Leave ordinary session rows unchanged on the wire: `failureHandedOff` is sent only when true.

## Delivery contracts
- Settle (`subagent_settle`): the complete bounded cohort message, including healthy children's findings, is stored as the hidden replay input, exactly as on `main`. Private retries keep their own retained input and failure IDs.
- Direct completion (`subagent_announce`): a healthy child's result stays in runtime context only; a failed child's diagnostics are saved with the handoff.
- Collector: results remain an ordinary durable tool result; failure custody follows what was actually stored.

## Integration with `main`
- This branch merges `main` at `68fbe4a` (#188180) with no conflicts and no resolution edits. All 96 feature files are byte-identical to the pre-merge commit `46ab0a0`.
- Against `main`, the PR changes 96 files, +4189/−392. The larger first-parent diff of that merge is upstream `main`, not new feature code.
- Earlier merges brought in `315380c` (#188047) without conflicts and `445e566` with a conflict in the three Control UI end-to-end test inventory files, resolved by keeping both sides' entries.
- Test repairs merged on `main` and included through the merge: #188178 (widget retention fixture), #188156 (empty-leaf admission), #188195 (thinking-claim ordering) and #188180 (keyed commentary in refreshed history). Earlier: #188047, #187979, #187933 and #188056. None is copied as a separate patch.
- `main` has moved since `68fbe4a`. The Copy-feedback repair landed on `main` as #188311; #188299, which overlapped it, was closed without merging. Separate test-only corrections for the new-session draft and quota tests are being prepared and are not yet published. This branch has not yet integrated the newer `main`.

## Stream-budget test readiness
- `chat-stream-runtime-budgets.e2e.test.ts` ("commits a streamed delta burst in frame-bound transcript batches") could count native pane commits caused by lazily loaded menu translation catalogs. Those landed after the measurement reset but before the first measured delta.
- The test now waits until the menu modules already requested by the page, and their dependencies, have loaded and the active pane has finished updating, before it measures. The original assertion, thresholds, timers and production code are unchanged. A new line allocation of 136 covers this test-only code.
- On `53ee37c`, Linux CI passed all six tests in that file.

## Verification
- Independent QA of the current source (`d70644f`): PASS with notes, no findings or blockers.
  - One fresh private Gateway build and matching Control UI (build `2026.10.9-d70644fb5c3c-2026-10-30T10-03-19.128Z`) ran a real Gateway and browser test through all four modes: default, parent-target, yielded and collector.
  - Each mode asked a native question, survived a reload, accepted a suggested choice or free text, kept durable custody, delivered the final reply in the same run as the answer, and showed no failed-child attention. Each mode verified that the served UI asset matched the build byte for byte.
  - In default mode, a descendant that finished late did not revive the failed child.
  - Five new test cases in four files ran: the four-mode Gateway case, three native legacy and cold-read cases, and one historical import case. The author's 215 tests and 6 boundary checks were not rerun; the two sets overlap and are not added together.
  - The provider was scripted locally, not a hosted model. Screenshots were inspected locally; none are attached.
- Independent review of the `main` integration effects on `d70644f`: PASS with notes, no integration defect or new missing context. All 96 feature files are unchanged, and `main`'s 522 changed paths do not overlap them. The `main` changes to outer authorization, the QuickJS namespace copy, collector inputs and attention inputs leave the delivery, persistence and custody paths unchanged. This is a source assessment, not a new canonical review or tests.
- Current source (`d70644f`, author): 215 tests across 15 files plus 6 targeted boundary checks pass, along with core and UI type checks, four test type graphs, inventory types, lint, format, mock, line-allocation and whitespace checks. Four UI lint warnings are unchanged from `main` and outside the feature's changes.
- Persisted-collector fix (`46ab0a0`): scoped canonical and independent reviews of that change. They do not cover the whole PR.
- Hosted review of `cb024b5` (current head): no findings; the earlier `53ee37c` collector P2 is addressed. It held the PR for data-model compatibility proof, which is added below. That hold stands until a fresh hosted review of a later head.
- Earlier proof is tied to its own source and does not cover `d70644f`:
  - Independent QA of `3a82cc7`: PASS with notes, including the stream-budget mutation checks and a Gateway runtime proof reused from `ad5a535` (build `2026.10.9-ad5a5354de4a-2026-10-30T05-25-28.209Z`).
  - Independent shipping verification of `43ddaef`: PASS with notes, 110 native tests and four Gateway and Control UI modes (build `2026.10.9-43ddaef1f7a6-2026-10-30T04-25-21.835Z`).
  - Scoped reviews: readiness fix (`ad5a535..3a82cc7`, two passes, zero findings), diagnostic step (`4bf61ee..ad5a535`), private-retry fix (`a296cbe..801b1a4`, eight passes, zero findings), `315380c` integration (PASS with notes).
  - Review of `f27f807..a296cbe` (36 passes): incomplete; no clean result is claimed for that range.
  - Baseline review (source `4599951`): eight passes, scoped-clean.
- CI on earlier published heads found missing mocks, test inventory gaps, an unconditional wire field, unbounded findings, a lint miss, the dropped settle findings and the stream-budget failure. Those failed runs remain history.
- Pending, not approval: a fresh whole-PR hosted review of the next head, and passing CI.

## Data compatibility
- This PR changes no schema, writer or retention.
- **Upgrade from the latest stable release (independent, PASS with notes):** data written by the published `openclaw@2026.10.9` package was opened and upgraded by this PR's source (`d70644f`).
  - Stable artifact: npm `openclaw-2026.10.9.tgz` (published 2026-10-29), tarball SHA-256 `43c61a00ef2c73416a072a7216cb3be80555d6740199f07194da2714283b04ab`; npm SHA-512 and SHA-1 integrity checked; signed tag `v2026.10.9` at build commit `8b18b55`. The npm provenance and signature chain was not separately audited.
  - The unmodified published compiled code, with its exact 66 production dependencies and no modules from this PR, wrote 6 sessions, 4 subagent runs and a 7-row transcript (header, 6 events, 4 model messages). The data included a retained private settle input and a collector's structured result and usage.
  - This PR's Doctor command then migrated the stores (shared schema 20→36, agent schema 25→38). Every original registry and transcript column and payload byte was preserved. The migration added the expected transcript navigation-index columns with their default values (for example `navigation_valid` = 1 and `navigation_display` = 0). Existing session-entry fields were preserved, and one expected display title was added. No represented-failure IDs or failure custody were invented.
  - Fresh processes then read the data through the production paths: the full and bounded registry readers, the session manager, Gateway row projection and presentation, and the Control UI attention and tree aggregation. Old failed children without a receipt still show failed-child attention (3 failed children, attention "error").
  - A new native write after migration, then a separate cold reopen, kept both the old and new bytes (7 events, 5 messages, 4 runs).
- **Historical import:** a frozen schema-v24 SQLite fixture went through the current Doctor import and a fresh read-only read. All three rows kept their full payload, IDs, keys, run ID and recovery data; the only changes were `main`'s existing queued→interrupted rule and a new empty `consumed_event_id`.
- A legacy retained settle message, replayed with its original run and idempotency IDs but without a record of represented failures, adds no new acknowledgement.
- Scope: this proves stored-data and schema activation. It does not cover a stable Gateway daemon boot, managed package replacement, service cutover or restart, a full packaged install of this PR, or live user data. Doctor completed both migrations, but its overall health check is not green in this isolated setup (plugin and model setup warnings, unset gateway mode). The stable data had no pending-input mailbox rows, so that path rests on the v24 import proof.

## Limits
- Runtime proof uses a scripted local model on macOS arm64/headless Chromium, not Linux or hosted-model compliance. Active-steering failure timing was not separately exercised. No latest-stable service activation (daemon boot, package replacement or restart) and no PostgreSQL run is claimed.
- The required `openclaw/ci-gate` check is not waived. No live Odin update, restart or deployment. CI and landing remain separate gates.
