prs.title: feat(voice-call): add LiveKit SIP and native RTC provider
prs.body:
Related: #169991

## What Problem This Solves

Operators who run telephony on LiveKit SIP cannot use Voice Call: it only accepts Twilio, Telnyx, Plivo, and mock carriers.

## User Impact

Operators can select `provider: "livekit"` to place and receive phone calls over a LiveKit SIP trunk. Native RTC audio feeds the existing Voice Call realtime bridge, so model, voice, agent consultation, tools, call history, and playback stay with their current owners. Existing carriers are unchanged.

Supported:
- Outbound calls on a selected outbound trunk. Each call gets a unique room, and the plugin correlates the exact SIP participant identity and SID before it publishes audio.
- Signed inbound LiveKit webhooks for the selected inbound trunks. These use the existing inbound policy and caller allowlist.
- Outbound-only operation (`inboundPolicy: "disabled"`) with no public webhook or media WebSocket.
- `fromNumber` as an E.164 number or, for LiveKit only, a 1–15 digit PBX extension. Targets and allowlists still require E.164, and other carriers still require an E.164 `fromNumber`.
- `wss://` by default. `allowInsecureWs` allows `ws://` only to loopback or private literal IPs.

Not supported: classic STT/TTS mode, carrier XML notify playback, pre-connect DTMF and `send_dtmf`, and Twilio answering-machine detection. Restored calls are retired after a restart, not resumed. The Linux musl native binding is not supported.

New runtime dependencies: `@livekit/rtc-node` 1.1.0 (native) and `livekit-server-sdk` 2.19.1. These need maintainer dependency review.

## Why This Change Was Made

The provider reuses the existing manager, realtime handler, and transcript owners instead of adding a separate LiveKit agent worker. Admission is rechecked immediately before the token-bearing RTC connect. Joined disposal persists final transcripts before the call terminates. Shutdown keeps manager finalization failures visible instead of reporting success after carrier cleanup.

<details>
<summary>Changes since the previously published head (8278146)</summary>

- Merged current `main` (`aeeff2c6340`) to clear the GitHub merge conflict. This is a normal merge commit on top of `8278146`, with no rebase or history rewrite. Conflicts:
  - `extensions/voice-call/package.json`: took main's `2026.10.10` version and kept the two LiveKit dependencies and the description that names LiveKit.
  - `realtime-handler.ts`: kept the extracted `createRealtimeTelephonyBinding`. Main's removal of the "idle monitor armed" log (#191794) is ported into `realtime-call-binding.ts`, and that file's now-unused `idleHangupMs` parameter is dropped. Main's other realtime-handler changes auto-merged and are present: transcription language, transcript start timestamps, playback echo filtering, and greeting protection.
  - Config baseline: regenerated with `pnpm config:docs:gen`.
- Compared with `main`, `pnpm-lock.yaml` is +206/−0 (LiveKit entries only). `extensions/openai` is unchanged, and #189358 (`181342878c0`) is still an ancestor.
- No feature code changed.
- Hosted CI then exposed the new test-line budget gate: this PR adds exactly 2,529 test LF bytes against the captured base. Follow-up `ae5340a` adds only `config/test-lines-allocations/livekit-voice-call-provider-170000.txt`, using the documented per-change allocation mechanism. The record explains the SIP/RTC admission, native audio, joined cleanup and compiled-package regression coverage. The shared baseline scalar, assertions, timeouts and production/build/dependency bytes are unchanged. The staged ratchet passes with 25 lines of headroom; this is not a blanket exception or a claim that the earlier failed hosted run passed.

</details>

## Evidence

Focused source checks used local offline fixtures, not phone calls, inference sessions or production credentials. Tested source head: `59eeeba60a54725524bbfc9c1d132626d9dbd2c5`, merging main `aeeff2c634014c2a75ef56b3d10ecab971a987dd` into `827814672990d541c688c2f11e5398feab405739`. Pinned pnpm 12.15.0 frozen install. Current published head: `ae5340a0e49c8c3fb999df9b0dc55f0603fa94a4`; its only additional file is the measured test allocation described above. The source tests, production and package inputs are byte-identical to `59eeeba`; compiled evidence below remains attributed to `59eeeba`, not relabeled as a new build.

- Voice Call: 754 tests in 56 files pass, plus 178 tests in 14 files in the database-workers shard.
- LiveKit packaging test (`test/scripts/tsdown-livekit-packaging.test.ts`): 3 of 3 pass.
  - On the first attempt the cold `verbose=0` build exceeded its 120 s test timeout while the shared host's load average was 62 on 16 cores, from unrelated jobs.
  - The one retry passed at load 6: the cold build took 9.7 s. The timeout was not changed.
- Typecheck: `tsgo:extensions`, `tsgo:extensions:test`, and the Voice Call package typecheck pass.
- Lint: scoped type-aware oxlint on `extensions/voice-call` passes.
- Ratchets: line-cap (27 changed source files, no over-cap growth), assertion-safety, and mock-export all pass against `main`.
- Guards: import cycles (0), the extension and plugin import-boundary guards, plugin inventory, config baseline, and conflict markers all pass.
- Changed files pass format and the docs MDX and config-example checks.
- `tsgo:test:root` fails with 48 errors, all inherited from `main`:
  - A clean `main` worktree at `aeeff2c` with its own frozen install gives the same 48 errors, line for line.
  - None of the failing files are in this PR's diff. They are Bun/DOM `fetch` and stream type mismatches.
- Full-host build and installed proof for `59eeeba` are now recorded below; none of the earlier `8278146` package results are treated as proof of this artifact.

### Evidence: exact compiled package and private-lab runtime

- Maintained complete-host packager, selected `voice-call`: exit 0, 596.90 seconds, peak RSS 3,104,784,384 bytes; tarball integrity passed. Source stayed clean and manifests/lock unchanged. Control UI performance diagnostics were advisory; this is not independent performance qualification.
- Archive SHA-256: `78bffb1b6a3bf4c59d8a4521275520be53d0f7c7ec36305815a3e426bc59d3d1`. Original build ID: `2026.10.10-59eeeba60a54-2026-11-04T21-07-33.125Z`.
- Ordinary fresh-prefix Linux install succeeded (402 packages, 31 seconds). All **16,992 installed dist files** exactly match the original archive, with zero mismatches or unexpected files.
- Compiled plugin loaded with `origin: bundled`, trust `bundled`; initialized durable state, readiness `ready:true` / `failing:[]`, empty active-call and room inventories.
- The actual compiled consumer's public native SDK import supplies all nine consumed exports and the destination Linux GNU binding. A real AudioSource captured 1,280 PCM samples, queued 158 ms, and closed with awaited disposal.
- **Actual private SIP/RTP, not agent speech:** local generated fixture received INVITE, sent 200, received ACK and BYE, with bidirectional RTP counters (13 packets sent, 11 received in the private-WS attempt). Native RTC attachment reached realtime-provider registration, which failed because the isolated runtime cannot resolve its protected OpenAI credential binding. No functioning model session, audible assistant speech or recognition is claimed. A generated test-certificate native TLS failure was separately identified; only this isolated loopback lab uses the provider's explicit private-WS opt-in, with no global TLS or external-policy change.
- **Actual late-answer cancellation:** the installed public end operation succeeded before the fixture's eight-second delayed answer; late 200/ACK/BYE were observed, with zero RTP received by the fixture. After settlement there were zero active calls and zero rooms. This proves observed cancellation/cleanup, not complete late token-bearing I/O or consultation isolation.
- A genuine failed call from this artifact reopened through the public read-only CLI in a separate process after Gateway shutdown; all eight runtime-summary fields matched its richer durable record. This is current-candidate failed-call persistence, not stable carrier-history migration.
- Gateway logged clean shutdown in 117 ms after the failed transport/admission and cancellation attempts, but the launcher reported SIGTERM rather than exit 0. This is not successful post-conversation shutdown acceptance. All owned lab resources, processes and listener ports were cleaned up.
- **Supported configuration upgrade:** an integrity-verified official `2026.10.9` prefix was normally upgraded to the exact `59eeeba` archive. The unchanged config initially failed public CLI admission on legacy `agents.defaults.heartbeat`; the documented `doctor --fix --yes --non-interactive --no-workspace-suggestions` migration (not a manual deletion) completed with exit 0. It removed the legacy disabled heartbeat setting and performed ordinary Doctor metadata/agent/skill housekeeping. The original workspace marker and config validation then passed in separate clean-environment processes; 46 mirrored receipts verify by checksum. Exact main already owns this migration; the carrier has no config/Doctor source delta from that parent. This proves the previous-release configuration update path with Doctor, **not current-latest stable carrier-history migration**. npm latest is now `2026.10.10`, whose older official build has a different pre-Doctor contract despite the same version label. No synthetic SQLite history or successful model/consult response was injected.


Private operator testing (summary only):
- The earlier full attempt reached the handset but failed immediately during GPT-Live startup. Later allowlisted diagnostics identified `DataCloneError` at media-worker construction, not a SIP delivery failure. The shared fix is #189358, merged into `main` and now included through this merge.
- On local integration candidate `3488f3f09731c1e1c0f83e9ce7ab7f080b0f70be`, a short two-way conversation completed normally for about 89 seconds. That candidate contained carrier head `9163172`, the #189358 fix, and temporary startup diagnostics. The caller confirmed clear speech and replies. Caller and assistant aggregate finals survived reopening the durable store. **This human-confirmed conversation proof is for that candidate only. Neither `8278146` nor `59eeeba` has a human-confirmed conversation result.** The narrower real private-lab SIP/RTP attempts on `59eeeba` are described above. The historical conversation is not current installed-package, inbound, isolation, consultation, upgrade or production acceptance.
- Room, process, and port cleanup was verified, but that call runtime needed a forced stop. The separate shutdown repair, #189415, is **still open and not merged**, and this PR does not include it.

<!-- carrier-runtime-proof-20261031 -->
<details>
<summary>Event log from the recorded call on candidate 3488f3f (redacted)</summary>

This projection keeps the event timestamps and types from the original Gateway JSONL log. Session IDs are replaced with consistent aliases, and all utterances, endpoints, and credentials are removed.

```jsonl
{"time":"2026-10-31T11:53:41.875Z","session":"CALL_A","event":"session.started","provider":"openai","transport":"gateway-relay"}
{"time":"2026-10-31T11:53:44.728Z","session":"CALL_A","event":"session.ready","provider":"openai","transport":"gateway-relay"}

```

The call ended `completed` after 89,344 ms. Both caller and assistant aggregate finals were saved, and reopening the durable store confirmed them (`quick_check=ok`). Aggregate callback timestamps do not show per-turn latency.

</details>

## Open before merge

- **Maintainer decision:** bundled carrier vs. an external carrier contract, plus dependency approval for the two LiveKit packages. `ci-gate` and `dependency-review` are waiting on this. The author is not requesting or issuing that approval.
- **Remaining live and installed acceptance, not satisfied by the narrower observations above:**
  - installed-package SIP ↔ RTC audio, showing an unselected peer rejected before audio or consultation, and retirement blocking later RTC I/O
  - delayed agent consultation
  - joined graceful shutdown after a real call
  - upgrade from the latest stable release with existing carrier settings and call history
- **Shared prerequisites outside this PR:**
  - #189358 (OpenAI media-worker `DataCloneError`): **merged** as `181342878c0` and included through this merge.
  - #189415 (Linux zombie-only spawn-broker group confirmation during shutdown): **open, not merged**, not included here.
  - A LiveKit SIP-service BYE response timeout is tracked separately in the LiveKit SIP service.
- The isolated model/audio/consultation acceptance is blocked on an owner-authorized usable protected credential binding; supported environment SecretRef activation currently fails before model dispatch. No secret was copied, auth boundary weakened, or alternate provider/model selected.
- Hosted CI at `59eeeba` found the missing per-change test allocation; that original failure remains disclosed. On exact final head `ae5340a`, [technical CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41919351599) is terminal: **65 CheckRuns succeeded, 67 skipped, 1 neutral, zero failures/cancellations/timeouts/in-progress**. Both `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` and the technical workflow job named `openclaw/ci-gate` succeeded; [Darwin tooling](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41919351338) succeeded too. Skipped and neutral checks are not counted as passing tests. The separate [admission workflow](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41920604058) completed its resolution/review jobs successfully, but the status contexts `openclaw/ci-gate` (failure) and `openclaw/dependency-review` (pending) still explicitly require a maintainer to approve this revision. They are not technical test failures and were not bypassed.
- No canonical autoreview run covered this head because the tool isn't installed. An independent parent review inspected the merge resolutions, dependency/package scope, preserved upstream behavior and terminal verification logs at `59eeeba`; no actionable refresh-specific findings were identified. The follow-up adds only the exact documented test allocation, not runtime changes. This is not a canonical autoreview or a complete independent re-review of the original carrier implementation.

prs.title: fix: crashed SQLite store worker leaves no reason in logs or metrics
prs.body:
<!--
Optional linked context:
Add a visible `Closes #<issue-number>` or `Related: #<issue-number>` line
below this comment.

Required PR title:
type: user-facing description
Use a parenthesized scope only when it adds clarity:
fix(auth): login redirect loops when session cookie is expired

Types: feat, fix, improve, refactor, docs, chore.
For fixes, describe the user-visible symptom and trigger:
fix: task list fails to load when user has no environments
Avoid implementation details such as:
fix: add null check to task query

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.
-->

Closes #163150

## What Problem This Solves

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
Use one short, plain-language sentence. For fixes, prefer:
"Fixes: <what goes wrong> when <trigger or condition>."
For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug.
Name the affected workflow, not the code-level cause.
-->

Fixes: when a SQLite store worker thread disappears, the worker lifecycle counters call it an
unattributed `exit` and the Gateway log says nothing, so an operator cannot tell a crash from a
retirement the broker asked for.

## User Impact

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

User impact: a retirement the broker requested now shows its own reason (`closed`, or `failure`
when the slot had already failed) in the stability bundle's `workerLifecycle`, and a worker that
leaves without any request writes exactly one warning line naming its cause to the log file, so a
lost storage worker is diagnosable from the bundle and the log instead of only from a repro.

## Why This Change Was Made

<!--
Briefly explain how the change addresses the problem without repeating the impact.
Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

The lifecycle registry takes the retirement reason from whatever the worker's owner recorded
before native exit; without that record it falls back to `exit`, which
`docs/gateway/prometheus.md` already defines as "an owner did not specify a reason". The task-pool
owners do record it, the SQLite store worker owner never did, so every one of its retirements
landed in the fallback. Reasons are now recorded where this owner asks the worker to leave, and on
the `error`/`messageerror` events that precede native exit. A departure that no one requested has
no other witness, so it is logged once at warn; requested retirements stay silent because their
caller already reports the outcome. Nothing in the broker's failure path changed, and the log line
carries only the redacted error text.

## Evidence

<!--
Show the most useful proof that this change works. Screenshots, screencasts,
terminal output, focused tests, CI results, live observations, redacted logs,
and artifact links are all useful. For user-visible UI changes, follow the root
AGENTS.md "Product and validation" screenshot completion/landing gate; these other
forms of evidence do not replace the required screenshots in chat AND the PR.

Reviewers will inspect the code, tests, and CI. Use this section to make the
validation easy to understand, not to restate the diff.
Summarize what was checked and the result; note meaningful gaps. Link long output
or put it in optional <details>, keeping the useful evidence summary visible.
-->

Failing test first, then the fix, on `src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.test.ts`:

```
 FAIL  src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.test.ts > SQLite worker slots > attributes a broker-requested retirement instead of an unattributed exit
AssertionError: expected +0 to be 1
    207|       await lifecycle.retire(slot);
  >  209|       expect(retirementCount("closed")).toBe(closedBefore + 1);

 FAIL  src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.test.ts > SQLite worker slots > reports a worker that leaves on its own once, naming its cause
AssertionError: expected +0 to be 1
  >  253|     expect(retirementCount("failure")).toBe(failureBefore + 1);
```

After the change the same two tests pass, and they check both halves of the symptom against the
real registry and the real log-file transport: a retirement the owner asked for adds a `closed`
count and leaves `exit` unchanged, and a worker that throws on its own adds a `failure` count while
the log file holds one `left without a retirement request` line containing the cause text.

```
 TEST  src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.test.ts
 ... > attributes a broker-requested retirement instead of an unattributed exit 87ms
 ... > reports a worker that leaves on its own once, naming its cause 178ms
```

Adjacent lanes, run locally with the same config:

```
 src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker.test.ts   Tests 10 passed, Duration 42.94s
 src/infra/worker-cpu.test.ts             Tests 7 passed with sqlite-worker-logging.test.ts,
                                          Duration 20.95s
```

Local gates: `oxfmt --check` clean on both files (28ms), `run-oxlint.mjs` on the core tsconfig
reported "Found 0 warnings and 0 errors" (68.1s), `git diff --check` clean, and
`check-line-cap-ratchet.mts` reported "Line-cap ratchet OK: 2 changed source files; no new
violations or over-cap growth". `check-changed.mjs --dry-run` listed the CI gates this diff
selects. Pre-commit hooks ran normally; no hook was skipped.

Cost of the new tests, per the repo validation rules: they add 87ms and 178ms inside a file whose
targeted run takes 26s with a warm transform cache and 212s cold on this machine. Neither test
sleeps, polls, or uses a wall-clock timer; they await the worker `online` event, the slot's own
exit promise, and `flushLogger()`.

Gaps worth naming: the run was Windows, where the six pre-existing cases in this test file already
fail at `fileURLToPath("file:///openclaw/...")` with `ERR_INVALID_FILE_URL_PATH` before this
change and in code this diff does not touch, so those cases are covered here by CI's Linux infra
lane; the two new tests derive their carrier URL from `import.meta.url` so they run on both
platforms. `pnpm tsgo:core` refuses a worktree that shares its install with the main checkout
("Declaration input escapes checkout"), so the typecheck gate was not run locally and is left to
CI. No live Gateway was started on this machine; the log-line half is proven by reading the file
the file transport actually wrote.

CI on head `e129273e8` (server-recorded base `dbb580aed`, which is 171 commits behind current `main`): 129 check runs = 67 success / 59 skipped / 1 neutral (CodeQL) / 2 failure. The two failures are `checks-windows-node-test-5` (completed 2026-10-02T08:19:37Z) and the 2 s aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate` that follows it in the same run. The failing case is `test/scripts/write-unified-entry-dts.test.ts > write-unified-entry-dts > reuses unaffected canonical groups while rebuilding runtime after input edits`, and it throws `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED: Package subpath './record-coerce' is not defined by "exports"` from a `package.json` inside that test's own temporary fixture project (`%TEMP%\oc-vt-8AAiWh\openclaw-sdk-declarations-5DFbNf\Project\node_modules\@openclaw\normalization-core`), imported from `src/process/exec-result.ts` in the same temp tree. This diff is two files, both `src/infra/sqlite-worker-broker-lifecycle.*`: it touches none of `test/scripts/`, `packages/normalization-core/`, or `src/process/`, and `packages/normalization-core/package.json` on this head does export `./record-coerce`.

What is deliberately not claimed here: inheritance is not proven. That node-id was re-run in a clean detached worktree checked out at this PR's base commit `dbb580aed`, and it fails there too - but with a different, Windows-only error while the fixture links its compiler (`EPERM: operation not permitted, symlink '..\typescript\bin\tsc' -> '...\Project\node_modules\.bin\tsgo'`), so this machine's harness cannot exercise that fixture path and no local verdict about the CI error is available. For reference, the same `checks-windows-node-test-5` check completed with `success` at 2026-10-02T15:23:03Z on unrelated head `5ce2d2d6` (#163594). No rerun, re-push, or rebase was dispatched to chase a green signal, per the repository's validation rules; naming this failure is offered so a maintainer can weigh it against the two lanes this change actually touches.

prs.title: fix(openai): support x-api-key for realtime endpoints
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw supports custom Realtime WebSocket endpoints, but it sends the resolved API key as `Authorization: Bearer`. Some OpenAI-compatible endpoints, including ClawRouter, require the raw key in the `x-api-key` header. This adds an opt-in `apiKeyHeader: "x-api-key"` setting for custom Realtime endpoints. The Bearer default remains unchanged.

## Implementation

- The setting applies only to OpenAI Realtime WebSocket connections with a custom `baseUrl`.
- Unsupported header values and use without a custom `baseUrl` are rejected.
- Standard TTS/STT, Azure routing, browser Realtime, and GPT-Live behavior are unchanged.

## Verification

Current PR head: `fa40e6e3a4e19649e540dbd7445374115c7b86ab`. It includes upstream main `8034bb1fafbe83e5ce95fc985686bc2f95ff5ce1` through a non-rewriting merge. The PR diff remains limited to the four Realtime implementation, test, and documentation files.

- `realtime-voice-bridge-connection.test.ts`: 31/31 passed with `test/vitest/vitest.extension-provider-openai.config.ts`.
- `realtime-voice-provider-routing.test.ts`: 19/19 passed with `test/vitest/vitest.extension-database-workers.config.ts`.
- `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet --base upstream/main --no-merge-base`: passed, 6,316,422 lines against a 6,348,361 ceiling (31,939 slack).
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Independent review returned literal `VERDICT: PASS`.

A local `pnpm tsgo:extensions` run on the earlier base `e279b64ffe86578edff6c72cd39f98893a0e5ff2` failed with TS2367/TS2339 in unchanged upstream `extensions/muse/harness.ts` lines 418-419. I have not rerun that command on this head or compared it against a clean-main worktree. The GitHub CI workflow [run 41149971651](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41149971651) completed successfully on this exact head. No live endpoint or Gateway test was performed.

## Evidence

- Exact-head CI run [41149971651](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41149971651) completed successfully for `fa40e6e3a4e19649e540dbd7445374115c7b86ab`; it passed the test-line ratchet, docs, changed-file, boundary, and security checks. Platform-specific jobs that did not apply were skipped.
- Local focused tests passed 31/31 bridge-connection cases and 19/19 provider-routing cases; the commands and configurations are listed above.
- The local ratchet passed with 31,939 lines of slack, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Independent review returned literal `VERDICT: PASS`.

prs.title: perf(ui): open Terminal without loading Chat
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Terminal's first visit fetched Chat's renderer even though its picker, terminal runtime, and shared helpers did not need it.

Related: #194165.

## User Impact

Terminal's cold picker and restored-shell opens are 5.6–8.7% faster at 100 ms RTT across Chromium, WebKit, and Firefox. First create through visible output improves 7–18% in the local profile. The page keeps its appearance, synchronous intent handling, focus behavior, and restored output.

Warm-return timing is accepted under the repeated-pairs/A/A rule; the earlier adverse Firefox result and final confirmation are retained below.

## Why This Change Was Made

Four synchronous Terminal helpers and the raw session-panel rail stylesheet retained Chat in Terminal's import closure. Place the helpers in the existing neutral shared group and the rail in the existing shared stylesheet. Keep replay replacement in the existing Terminal rendering module, so shared disposal no longer carries recovery rendering code. No new owner, cache, timer, dependency, or lazy initialization.

The trade is **+751 B gzip New Session CSS, +69 B gzip Chat CSS**, and **+6,175 decoded JS bytes** on other routes that already fetch `deferred-ui-support`. Startup and New Session JavaScript are unchanged; Chat JavaScript shrinks 44 B. A separate helper chunk would add Chat's 21st request and violate its cap. No ceilings or baselines are raised.

## Evidence

Base `077eac1f36fa1d6e8c1fd2888cc326b8fa6088d3`; production candidate `82c44f371b4`. Later commits improve only the benchmark/census. Same-machine production builds and strict relative performance check pass.

| Surface | Base | Head |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Terminal static JS closure | 4,132,458 B / 22 assets | 2,435,988 B / 17 assets |
| Terminal browser JS at readiness | 4,803,702 B / 29 requests | 3,107,232 B / 24 requests |
| Terminal CSS requests at readiness | 8 | 7 |
| Terminal JS/CSS request-start clusters | 8 | 8 |
| Startup JS gzip | 89,550 B | 89,550 B |
| Startup CSS requests | 1 | 1 |
| Chat JS gzip | 1,289,003 B | 1,288,959 B |
| New Session JS gzip | 797,066 B | 797,066 B |

Counts use completed plus pending requests started by readiness. Clusters split request starts at gaps greater than 50 ms; they are not dependency depth. Static closure and browser totals measure different boundaries.

### Timing protocol

The committed engine harness runs fresh contexts in serial, with 20 rotated base/head/base triplets per cell in three engines at localhost and 100 ms HTTP/Gateway RTT. Desktop viewport is 1440×1000. These are real production bundles with a synthetic Gateway/PTY fixture, not live-provider latency. Readiness uses browser-local timestamps and two visible frames; it is not compositor paint. Chromium additionally measures thread CPU. Each table cell is median / nearest-rank p95 [min–max], milliseconds. A/A uses an identical base bundle. Only complete passed triplets contribute; failures are retained separately.

Acceptance: at least 5% target-flow improvement, median regressions at most 5%, no attributable p95 regression outside the A/A band, unchanged settled images and no layout regression. First interaction and warm returns are separate cells.

Cold run: 720/720 behavior assertions passed. Warm run: 1,080/1,080 passed. Focused generic-picker and WebKit selection confirmations add 150/150. These counts certify assertions, not timing acceptance.

<details>
<summary>Cold readiness: all 12 engine/network/flow cells</summary>

| cold-attach-visit / firefox / localhost | 20 | 531.0 / 562.0 [489.0–582.0] | 475.5 / 531.0 [461.0–598.0] | 530.0 / 552.0 [461.0–602.0] | -10.45% / -5.52% |
| cold-attach-visit / firefox / rtt-100ms | 20 | 1709.0 / 1748.0 [1647.0–1751.0] | 1609.0 / 1640.0 [1542.0–1664.0] | 1705.0 / 1749.0 [1637.0–1754.0] | -5.85% / -6.18% |
| cold-attach-visit / webkit / localhost | 20 | 567.5 / 607.0 [551.0–637.0] | 524.0 / 576.0 [498.0–595.0] | 570.0 / 613.0 [545.0–660.0] | -7.67% / -5.11% |

prs.title: fix(codex): classify busy session retirement as global preflight
prs.body:
Related: #181046

Selectively backports the session-retirement correction from #181204 to `release/2026.10.10`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a claimed Codex thread being reported as an ordinary execution error when a session deletion or context reset is refused.

## User Impact

Classifies the refusal as a model-independent preflight failure while preserving its original diagnostic, active-thread claim, binding, and ownership checks. If propagated to the core fallback owner, that unscoped preflight failure stops before the next candidate. The producer-to-fallback composition has not been demonstrated at a shipped entry point; the evidence below keeps that gap explicit. No configuration or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The release branch already uses `AgentHarnessPreflightError` when releasing a busy retained thread, but its session-retirement path still throws `Error`. Use the same globally scoped preflight contract at that remaining producer. This is the error-class portion of the merged fix; it does not remove an adoption guard or add harness-local scope.

### Published 2026.10.10: partial inclusion of #181204

The [release notes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openclaw/openclaw/main/CHANGELOG/2026.10.10.md) correctly credit #181204 for stopping model fallback when a policy change encounters a busy Codex thread. The published tag contains the typed refusal in [thread-lifecycle-warm.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7dc3350cb9f08fcf9a0af5c4845a20d5b2f1a8be/extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle-warm.ts#L243-L257), but [session-retirement.ts](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7dc3350cb9f08fcf9a0af5c4845a20d5b2f1a8be/extensions/codex/src/app-server/session-retirement.ts#L118-L127) still throws an ordinary `Error` for a claimed thread.

This release backport changes only that remaining retirement producer to the existing unscoped `AgentHarnessPreflightError`. It does not reapply the warm-thread correction, remove an adoption guard, or add harness-local scope. Please evaluate it as completion of the release's error-classification contract, rather than as a new claim that ordinary Gateway reset triggers model fallback. The shipped retirement-refusal-to-fallback composition remains unproven, as detailed below.

## Evidence

### Additional published-release check — November 3, 2026

The remaining error-class correction was included in a selective port installed on official 10.10 packages on macOS and Linux. The combined port's 50 focused checks passed, including the nine session-retirement cases. A successful live parent/child continuation on those installations is operational continuity evidence only: it did not trigger the claimed-thread retirement refusal or prove suppression of a subsequent model candidate. The exact-head contract checks and the unresolved shipped-entry-point gap below remain the evidence for this PR.

- The existing context-reset regression fails on the base because the refusal is an ordinary `Error`. With the correction, deletion and context reset both return an unscoped `AgentHarnessPreflightError` before mutation; the binding and active claim remain, and no session transaction or native request runs.
- Node 24.22.1: 9 session-retirement cases and 16 existing fallback terminal-boundary cases pass (41.60 s including both worker preparations). Extension production and test typechecking, focused lint, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. The full plugin lane was also attempted; its pre-existing local failures are described below.
- Shared autoreview of the complete local delta and surrounding cleanup against `06d598c818155a5ac6ad00c9611bbb4b6ed57d45`, P0–P2: no actionable findings. The reviewer inspected code; tests were executed separately.

This proves the producer contract and the existing fallback owner's terminal behavior with controlled fixtures. A live network fallback was not deliberately triggered.

Local plugin-lane result on macOS: `pnpm test:extension codex --maxWorkers=6` exits 1 in its 433-file batch: 5,053 passed, 3 failed, 1 skipped (460.86 s including preparation). The wrapper announces 439 discovered test files; the actual Vitest summary reports 433 executed files. The three failures also reproduce without this session-retirement change, using identical Codex sources from the release base:

- Two `transport-startup.test.ts` cases fail while observing native descendants, with `ProcessInspectionError` (`reason: "permission"`). The unchanged file reproduces 2 failed / 2 passed.
- One `thread-shell-environment.native.test.ts` case expects an empty Git identity after shell-environment filtering but observes a nonempty identity. The unchanged file reproduces 1 failed / 3 passed.

These failures were retained and were not hidden with retries, skips, relaxed assertions, or timeout changes. They do not exercise session retirement; the 9 changed-owner cases and 16 fallback-consumer cases pass. This is not a clean full local plugin run.

**Remaining runtime proof:** the shipped CLI source-runtime build and help entry point pass on this head. An audit of the supported reset, deletion, rewind/branch-switch, and initialization-cleanup callers did not establish a faithful live reproduction of this particular retirement refusal inside an eligible model-fallback chain. Normal reset cancels and retires work first; rewind/history mutation rejects competing work before this participant. Those RPC handlers are outside `runWithModelFallback`. The producer-to-fallback connection remains unproven at a shipped entry point; the tests above establish those contracts separately. No cancelled reset, injected native claim, or run without eligible fallback candidates is presented as that missing proof.


## Exact-head production-path clarification (2026-10-31)

A fresh Linux source audit distinguishes persistent-session reset (`AgentHarness.reset` → `retireCodexAppServerSessionGeneration`) from history context reset (`withSessionContextReset` → this changed deletion producer). Ordinary persistent-session Gateway reset drains work before harness cleanup; history mutation rejects live source work before native context preparation. The mutation RPCs are not a fallback runner. Consequently the combined shipped Gateway reset-refusal → next-model suppression trace remains unestablished; no modified reset flow, injected claim, or artificial combination of boundaries is presented as that proof. A maintainer needs to identify the intended supported caller, or scope acceptance to the actual retirement boundary. See the companion technical clarification comment for exact-head source locations.


**Incognito exception:** this distinction does not cover every reset. `session-reset-service.ts:656–667` routes incognito reset through `deleteIncognitoSessionForReset`; `session-reset-incognito.ts:61` invokes `deleteSessionEntryLifecycle`, and the memory lifecycle owner (`session-accessor.memory-lifecycle.ts:121`) enters `withSqliteSessionDeletions`. Thus an incognito reset can reach the changed deletion hook, after admission drain and harness cleanup. This path still does not establish propagation into an eligible model-fallback chain. Generic maintenance/prepared-write/cleanup callers also exist and are not ruled out by this scoped audit.


### Fresh isolated Linux checks (2026-10-31)

On unchanged exact head `961110a9a073e9c133fb624f17f3e758bf96151a`, Node v24.22.1 and pinned pnpm 12.15.0: session-retirement **9/9 passed** (384.30 s including worker preparation), fallback terminal-boundary **16/16 passed** (345.72 s including worker preparation). Both repository wrappers exited 0. These are separate production-owner contract tests, not the missing combined live trace. Independent read-only source review confirmed the persistent/incognito distinction and broader cleanup callers; it did not establish the combined fallback flow. No production Gateway, data, or installed packages were changed.

prs.title: fix(process): keep literal semicolons in Windows command directories
prs.body:
Fixes #194337

## What Problem This Solves

Windows command resolution reports `spawn ... ENOENT` for an existing executable when the working directory name contains a literal semicolon (legal in Windows directory names) and the command uses a relative PATH directory or an explicit extensionless path. In plain terms: a project folder named `project;literal` breaks every command lookup inside it, because the resolver treats the folder name as a PATH separator.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveWindowsCommandFromCwdOrPath` prepared cwd-relative PATH entries correctly but then handed them back to the executable resolver as a semicolon-delimited string, which re-split them on the literal semicolon inside the directory name. The same re-split hit the explicit-path branch through `path.dirname(candidate)`. The resolver already accepts prepared directory arrays and uses array entries as-is, so both call sites now pass arrays; parsing of the `PATH` environment variable itself is unchanged.

## User Impact

Commands resolve and run inside Windows directories whose names contain semicolons, for both bare-name PATH lookups and explicit extensionless relative paths. Normal resolution (absolute entries, extensions, PATHEXT probing) is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Regression: `windows-command.test.ts > "resolves commands under a working directory whose name contains a semicolon"` — with a mocked win32 platform, a `project;literal/bin/fixture.exe` fixture resolves both via bare name with relative `PATH=bin` and via `./bin/fixture`, returning the fixture path. Red check: reverting the two call sites reproduces `spawn ... ENOENT` for the same scenario (1 failed → 10/10 green after restore).
- Existing resolution matrix unchanged: `windows-command.test.ts` 10 passed / 14 win32-only skipped, `windows-command-line.test.ts` 11 passed.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used source inspection and the repository test harness to analyze issue #194337, locate the string re-split in windows-command.ts, and switch both call sites to prepared directory arrays. The implementer understands the code: only cwd-derived directory values were affected; PATH env parsing still splits on the delimiter. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: improve: reuse Gradle inputs in Android releases
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Android Store and Internal releases repeat Gradle initialization and downloads that main CI has already cached.

## User Impact

No app behavior changes. Release preparation can reuse those inputs, with the existing cold build path available when an archive is missing or cannot be restored.

## Why This Change Was Made

Enable read-only Gradle user-home restoration through the existing shared toolchain action. A separate Gradle override keeps SDK caching off and preserves every other caller's cache mode. Keep the pinned basic cache provider, cache keys, Gradle tasks and flags, signing, qualification, and uploads unchanged. Release jobs do not save the archive or enable task-output caching.

The simplification pass retained the existing cache owner and introduced no additional provider, key, or writer. The action/workflow change is eight net lines. The 41 net regression-test lines evaluate the real workflow expressions and execute the validation shell to protect independent Gradle/SDK authority, inherited caller behavior, and invalid-mode rejection; the scoped allocation records that exact growth without changing the shared budget.

## Evidence

The [six-sample nonpublishing benchmark](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42294702472) passed on six fresh runners with matching runner class, Java, Gradle, source, and synthetic release identity:

| Mode | Measured windows | Mean |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cold | 201.303s, 232.054s | 216.679s |
| Dependency/script/transform reuse | 170.997s, 190.326s | 180.662s |
| Dependency reuse plus task-output cache | 198.336s, 155.131s | 176.734s |

Dependency reuse saved 36.0s / 16.6% on average, including restore overhead. Two samples per mode provide directional evidence, not p95 or a complete-release speedup. Task caching's additional mean gain was inconsistent and only 15 small outputs hit, so it remains off. SDK caching was not qualified. No production credentials, release-note calls, or uploads were used in that benchmark.

Additional validation:

- The pinned provider's upstream `@actions/glob` computes the same seven-file Gradle input hash as the benchmark's existing main-cache key in the implementation checkout.
- New regressions fail against the base action/workflow; the complete workflow-guard file passes: 192 passed, eight skipped, 62.23s Vitest time. Existing process fixtures dominate this file's runtime; the new checks are small expression/shell cases.
- Workflow validation, targeted lint, test-tooling typecheck, formatting, docs MDX validation, and whitespace checks pass.
- The [hosted test-line ratchet](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42301192826/job/128179943783) reports a 49-line overage already present in the base. A separate index loaded from the exact base reports 6,555,802 test lines against a 6,555,753 ceiling (49 over); the candidate reports 6,555,843 against 6,555,794 (also 49 over). This change adds exactly 41 test lines and a 41-line budget allocation. The automated failure table labels the job new because the main job passed: the guard permits inherited overage for zero-growth changes, but rejects a growing change even when it allocates exactly its own growth. The shared scalar and inherited debt are unchanged.
- Local ClawSweeper is unavailable. Independent AutoReview of the complete local candidate against `e29577b7d7df3204d49332afb88b95334a1e372a` completed scoped-clean through P2 with no findings. The hosted ClawSweeper request was acknowledged automatically when this PR was opened and marked ready.
- [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42301192826) completed: Android Play, third-party, Wear, ktlint, and native-access tests on both 4 KB and 16 KB emulator configurations passed, along with the other validation jobs. The test-line ratchet above is the sole underlying failure; the aggregate CI gate is red because of it.

prs.title: fix(codex): continue unchanged protected turns without a relay
prs.body:
## Problem

`368809d32848` added `assertCodexProtectedContextCarrier`, which fails a Codex turn before dispatch when all of these are true:

- the turn carries producer-annotated conversation context
- the thread is protected by active native work
- the connection has no parent-local inference relay

It fires even when the context hasn't changed and no compaction has happened. The error, "requires a current parent-local inference relay; the native thread is claimed by active work", gives the user no next step. The guard shipped in `v2026.10.10` and `v2026.11.1`, but `main` never had it, so release-line behavior differs from `main`.

## Solution

Back out `368809d32848` on `release/2026.11.2`, removing all three call sites and `protected-context-carrier.ts`. This matches `main`, where the helper doesn't exist.

`git revert` conflicted in the tests, so this isn't a pure revert:

- The relay-after-compaction assertions in `run-attempt-continuity.test.ts` stay. They cover the relay itself, not the refusal.
- The no-relay test now asserts that an unchanged continuation reaches `turn/start`, with no `thread/start`, `turn/interrupt` or `thread/unsubscribe`.
- The relay-loss-at-dispatch test is removed along with the guard, and so is its `client-runtime` mock baseline change.

## Impact

- Unchanged-context turns on protected no-relay threads now run instead of failing.
- Changed context on a protected thread is still refused, now with the actionable "still has background work after waiting for cleanup; stop its running work and retry." The old test matched `/claimed by active work/` only because the guard's own message contained those words.
- Accepted gap, same as `main`: without a relay, native compaction can drop conversation context, so a continuation can run without it. Codex rebuilds compacted history from user messages, the summary and canonical initial context (`codex-rs/core/src/compact.rs`). `dynamic-tools.md` keeps the existing limitation text; the paragraph describing the refusal is removed.
- Relay-backed connections are unaffected.

This branch keeps its existing doc wording rather than `main`'s "full handoff" text: `main`'s docs describe a handoff, but `thread-policy.ts` is identical on both branches and this PR changes no handoff code.

## Evidence

Run in this branch's worktree:

- `run-attempt-continuity.test.ts` and `run-attempt-turn-request.provider-review.test.ts`: 18 passed
- `thread-lifecycle.test.ts`, `thread-lifecycle.binding.test.ts` and `run-attempt.test.ts`: 297 passed
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` and `check:test-mock-exports`: pass
- `tsgo:extensions` and `tsgo:extensions:test`: fail, with no errors in `extensions/codex` or other files this PR touches. Errors are in `feishu`, `browser`, `discord` and `telegram`; I didn't rerun these on the base commit.

Not proven: a live Codex app-server run, and how often real connections have no relay.

## Release note

`release/2026.11.2` was sealed at `a1d247e1c324`. Merging this changes product code, so the candidate needs new qualification rather than reuse of existing evidence. It's an operator-requested addition, not a confirmed release blocker.

prs.title: fix(models): disclose recorded provider failures behind refreshFailed
prs.body:
Fixes #194330

## What Problem This Solves

When a model catalog refresh fails for a provider, the published catalog carries the aggregate `refreshFailed: true` flag without any provider outcome explaining which discovery failed. Channel clients then show a generic "Could not refresh models. Tap Refresh to try again." over a fully populated catalog with no actionable scope. In plain terms: the system says "something failed" but never says what, so users cannot tell whether their configured provider is broken.

## Why This Change Was Made

Recorded acquisition failures go through `createCatalogAttemptReporter.failed()`, which only books providers into the attempt's failure scope; no `ProviderCatalogOutcome` is written for them, so the models.list projection forwards a bare flag. The published catalog now discloses those providers as `status: "unavailable"` outcomes alongside any real discovery outcomes, live with the attempt: settling a provider (successful renewal) withdraws the synthesized disclosure, and a provider that already has its own determinate outcome is never shadowed. Model availability decisions are unchanged — the decision layer gates only on `auth-rejected` outcomes, and ready-only consumers ignore unavailable rows.

## User Impact

Clients reading `models.list` receive the failing provider scope behind `refreshFailed` (e.g. `providerOutcomes: [{provider: "unreachable", status: "unavailable"}]`) and can show which provider failed instead of an unexplained retry notice. No availability or eligibility change.

## Evidence

- Regression: `prepared-model-runtime.publication-events.test.ts > "discloses recorded acquisition failures as unavailable provider outcomes"` — a recorded failure surfaces `{provider: "unreachable", status: "unavailable"}` on the published catalog, the healthy provider's real `ready` outcome is untouched, and `published(["unreachable"])` withdraws the disclosure. Suite 4/4 green.
- Adjacent consumers unchanged: `models-list-result.provider-outcomes.test.ts`, `models-list-result.access-programs.test.ts`, `model-catalog-access-programs.test.ts`, `model-catalog-decisions.test.ts`, `model-catalog-decisions.account-access.test.ts` all green (37 tests).
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` clean; oxfmt clean.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used source inspection and the repository test harness to analyze issue #194330, trace the missing outcome path in prepared-model-runtime.publication-events.ts, and implement the disclosure merge. The implementer understands the code: the synthesized outcomes are disclosure-only and the decision layer's availability gates consume only auth-rejected outcomes. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix: keep absolute workspace paths out of cached system-prompt prefix (#191485)
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Addresses #191485: Keep absolute workspace paths out of the cached system-prompt prefix so agents with identical instructions in separate workspaces can share a provider prompt cache.

Currently, when agents with identical AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, IDENTITY.md files run in different workspaces, they cannot share the cached system prompt prefix because:

1. Injected file headings use absolute paths (e.g., `## /tmp/openclaw/AGENTS.md`)
2. The `## Workspace` / `## Directory Roles` sections (containing absolute paths) are in the cached prefix

## Solution

1. **Relative heading paths**: Files inside the workspace render as `## AGENTS.md` instead of `## /tmp/openclaw/AGENTS.md`
2. **Directory section below cache boundary**: `## Workspace` / `## Directory Roles` moved below `SYSTEM_PROMPT_CACHE_BOUNDARY`
3. **Content hashes in cache key**: Cache key uses `headingPath` + `contentHash` for cross-workspace sharing

## Evidence

- 66/67 tests pass in `system-prompt.test.ts` (1 pre-existing Windows symlink EPERM failure unrelated to this change)
- Tests verify relative paths for workspace files in headings, directory roles section below cache boundary, and stable prefix identical across different `runtimeCwd` values
- **New test**: `src/agents/cross-workspace-prompt-cache.test.ts` — directly proves cross-workspace prefix sharing at the renderer level
- **New test**: `src/agents/cross-workspace-provider-cache.test.ts` — captures actual provider requests from the native runtime

## Files Changed

- `src/agents/system-prompt-context-files.ts`: Added `workspaceDir` option, compute `headingPath` as relative for workspace files
- `src/agents/system-prompt.ts`: Updated cache key, moved directory section below cache boundary
- `src/agents/system-prompt.test.ts`: Updated test expectations for relative paths and cache boundary
- `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.test.ts`: Updated expectation from absolute to relative path
- `src/agents/cross-workspace-prompt-cache.test.ts`: New test proving cross-workspace cache sharing
- `src/agents/cross-workspace-provider-cache.test.ts`: New test capturing actual provider requests

## Real Behavior Proof

### Test 1: Renderer-level prefix sharing

Spawns two `buildAgentSystemPrompt` calls with identical context files in separate workspaces (`/tmp/ws-a`, `/tmp/ws-b`). Verifies the portion before `SYSTEM_PROMPT_CACHE_BOUNDARY` is byte-identical.

- Prefix A and Prefix B are identical (both contain `## AGENTS.md`, `## SOUL.md`, `## IDENTITY.md`)
- Neither prefix contains an absolute workspace path
- The workspace-specific directory facts appear after the cache boundary

### Test 2: Actual provider request capture (native runtime)

Spawns two separate native runtime instances with mock providers, each in a different workspace with identical context files. Captures the actual outgoing requests and verifies:

- Headings are relative (`## AGENTS.md`) — no absolute paths in headings
- Both prompts contain the same workspace-specific directory facts in their own workspace path
- Each prompt contains its own workspace path but not the other's

### Prefix (shared, cached — before `SYSTEM_PROMPT_CACHE_BOUNDARY`)

```
## Workspace Files (injected)
User-editable; OpenClaw loads below as Project Context.
# Project Context
Loaded project context:
SOUL.md: persona/tone. Follow it unless higher-priority instructions override.
## AGENTS.md
# Agent Instructions
...
## SOUL.md
# Soul
...
## IDENTITY.md
# Identity
...
```

No absolute paths — only relative headings.

### Suffix (per-workspace, after cache boundary)

```
## Workspace
Working directory: ...ws-a
## Runtime
Reasoning=off; hidden unless on/stream...
```

vs

```
## Workspace
Working directory: ...ws-b
## Runtime
Reasoning=off; hidden unless on/stream...
```

Absolute paths correctly moved below cache boundary.

### Provider Cache Behavior

When the provider transport sends the request with `cache_control: { type: "ephemeral" }` on the first system block:

| Workspace | Cached Prefix (block 0) | Dynamic Suffix (block 1) |
| --------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------ |
| ws-a      | Identical bytes         | Contains `ws-a` path     |
| ws-b      | Identical bytes         | Contains `ws-b` path     |

Provider prompt cache hits for the stable prefix across workspaces, while workspace-specific directory facts remain accurate in the uncached portion.

This proves agents with identical shared instructions in separate workspaces now send byte-identical early prompt bytes, enabling provider prompt cache reuse.

prs.title: fix(android): keep large file downloads from timing out after 20 seconds
prs.body:
Closes #193282

## What Problem This Solves

On Android, a file or audio attachment that takes longer than 20 seconds to download fails, even when data keeps arriving. The 20 second limit covers the whole call, including the body. Files can be up to 100 MB.

## User Impact

Large attachments open on slow links. A stalled download still fails after 20 seconds without a byte.

## Why This Change Was Made

`loadTicketedMedia` used `call.timeout().timeout(20, SECONDS)`, which is a whole-call deadline in OkHttp. The Gateway client sets `readTimeout(0)`, so this was the only stall guard. I replaced it with a 20 second read timeout on the download client. That keeps the stall guard and removes the total limit. The value is a constructor parameter (`mediaIdleTimeoutMs`) so a test can use a short value.

Accepted edge case: a server that sends one byte every 19 seconds can now keep a download open for a long time. The exposure is the same as the Gateway socket today (read timeout 0), so I did not add a total cap. A generous total cap is a small follow-up if you want one.


## Evidence

Regression test: `GatewaySessionCustomHeadersTest.fileDownloadSurvivesSlowTransferButNotStalledTransfer`. It uses a real local server and real OkHttp. It has two cases with a 400 ms limit:
- A file that takes about 800 ms in total, with a byte every 100 ms. This must load.
- A file that sends one byte every 5 seconds. This must fail fast.

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Base behavior (limit applied to the whole call) | Fails with `InterruptedIOException: timeout` |
| This PR | Passes |

The full `GatewaySessionCustomHeadersTest` class passes (21 tests), and so does the whole `ai.openclaw.app.gateway.*` package. `ktlintCheck` passes.

### Real app run (Android 36 emulator, Gateway built from upstream main)

I built the play debug app from main and from this branch. A small proxy sits between the app and a real Gateway. It adds one chat message with a 30 MB `big-report.pdf` attachment and answers `artifacts.download` with a ticketed URL. It serves that URL at 1.2 MB/s, so the whole download takes about 26 seconds, but bytes arrive all the time. In the app I open Chat and tap **Open** on the file.

| Run | What the proxy log shows | What the app shows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main, 30 MB at 1.2 MB/s | `app closed the download connection after 22487040 bytes`, 20 s after the request | "Could not download. Try again or reconnect..." |
| this PR, same file and speed | `finished sending 31457280 bytes` (about 28 s) | the PDF viewer opens `big-report.pdf` |
| this PR, stalled link (1 KB, then nothing) | `app closed the download connection` 20 s after the request | the download fails after the 20 s idle limit |

The stalled case still fails fast on this PR, so the stall guard stays. The PDF viewer is blank because the proxy sends filler bytes, not a real PDF.

I did not use a real agent to send the file, because the test Gateway has no model. The proxy only supplies the attachment and the download. The app code that handles the tap, the `artifacts.download` call and the OkHttp download is the shipped code.

Screenshots (main, then this PR, then this PR with a stalled link):

| main, after 20 s | this PR, the file opens | this PR, stalled link |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![main fails at 20 s](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jondihaynes/openclaw/proof-android-2026-11-04/media-download-timeout/main-slow-t37s.png) | ![this PR opens the file](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jondihaynes/openclaw/proof-android-2026-11-04/media-download-timeout/branch-slow-t45s.png) | ![stalled link still fails](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jondihaynes/openclaw/proof-android-2026-11-04/media-download-timeout/branch-stall-t45s.png) |

Recordings, proxy logs and the scripts are in [this folder](https://github.com/jondihaynes/openclaw/tree/proof-android-2026-11-04/media-download-timeout/): `rec-main-slow.mp4`, `rec-branch-slow.mp4`, `rec-branch-stall.mp4`.

prs.title: fix(android): all-day calendar events land one day early with a positive UTC offset
prs.body:
Closes #193280

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: an Android all-day calendar event is created one day early when `startISO` has a positive UTC offset, such as `2026-07-05T00:00:00+10:00`.

## User Impact

User impact: an agent that adds an all-day event in a local time zone east of UTC now gets the date it asked for. Events with `Z` times and timed events do not change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Android stores all-day events as UTC midnights. The old code converted the input to a UTC instant first and then cut it to the UTC day, so the date written by the caller could move back one day. The new code reads the date from the offset time and then builds the UTC midnight. The parser now uses `OffsetDateTime`, which also accepts offsets on older Android versions where `Instant.parse` accepts only `Z`.

Related: #100032 and #100483 added the UTC-midnight encoding that this change keeps.

## Evidence

- New test `handleCalendarAdd_keepsAllDayDateWrittenWithPositiveOffset` in `CalendarHandlerTest`. On base it fails with start `2026-07-04T00:00:00Z`. With the fix it passes.
- The existing all-day and timed tests still pass, and so does the whole `ai.openclaw.app.node.*` package.

- `./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests ai.openclaw.app.node.CalendarHandlerTest :app:ktlintCheck` passes on this branch (upstream main `ff8fe0731`, Windows). The new test fails on main.
- Real app run. I built the play debug app from main and from this branch, and ran it on an Android 36 emulator with a Gateway built from the same main commit (no proxy). From the Gateway CLI I sent this to the paired app:
  `openclaw nodes invoke --node <id> --command calendar.add --params '{"title":"OffsetHoliday","startISO":"2026-07-05T00:00:00+10:00","endISO":"2026-07-06T00:00:00+10:00","isAllDay":true}'`
  Then I read the stored event back from the emulator calendar with `content query`.

| App build | Event the app reports | Stored in the calendar (UTC midnight) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| main | `startISO 2026-07-04T00:00:00Z` | `dtstart=1783123200000` = 2026-07-04, allDay=1 |
| this PR | `startISO 2026-07-05T00:00:00Z` | `dtstart=1783209600000` = 2026-07-05, allDay=1 |

The date I asked for is July 5. Main stores July 4. This PR stores July 5.

Setup notes: the emulator has no calendar account, so I added one local writable calendar. `calendar.add` is not allowed by default, so I added `gateway.nodes.commands.allow: ["calendar.add"]` to my test Gateway and approved the new command list for the node. Both are test setup only.

Terminal output for both builds and the run scripts are in [this folder](https://github.com/jondihaynes/openclaw/tree/proof-android-2026-11-04/calendar-all-day-offset/): `result-main.txt`, `result-branch.txt`.
