prs.title: fix(agents): keep a local Codex owner refusal from cooling the shared credential
prs.body:
Closes #191473

## Needs from a maintainer (nothing is waiting on the author)

Two one-line actions, neither of which CODEOWNERS routes to anybody — which is the mechanical reason they have been waiting since Nov 3:

1. **`/allow-security-sensitive-change`** for head `a8f1213f25098dfefe1dca1078037f6b6276bd96` — this is the conflict-resolved head the re-derived review now names; `e960518954b` is one merge behind it, and approving a stale SHA does not clear the gate. This is maintainer-tier, not SecOps: matched against the repo's own security policy, the gate covers **one** non-test production file (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-profile-failure-policy.ts`) and **3 lines** in it. The gate is live and correctly keyed, verified from the shipped logic: `scripts/github/security-review-rollout.mjs` returns mode `enforced` for this PR (rollout pull 152415 merged 2026-09-19, this PR created 2026-11-03), and `.github/workflows/security-review.yml` triggers on `issue_comment` created/edited plus a ten-minute reconcile schedule — so posting the command is picked up on its own, with no push or re-run needed from anyone. The exact acceptance predicate is `scripts/github/guard-review.mjs:525-552`, with the command grammar at `scripts/github/guard-shared.mjs:128-138`, and four of its clauses fail silently - worth quoting before anyone posts, so the first attempt sticks: (i) the comment must be created **after** the guard's current approval request, because any push re-keys it; (ii) **every** non-empty trimmed line must be one bare command from the closed set (`/allow-security-sensitive-change` or `/allow-dependencies-change`) - `lines.every(...)` means prose wrapped around the command makes the parser return nothing at all; (iii) the comment must **never have been edited**, since `updated_at !== created_at` disqualifies it, so tacking a clarifying note onto an already-posted command silently revokes that approval; (iv) the author's own comment is ignored and the poster must hold `maintain` or `admin`. Two intuitive choices that do **not** work: a GitHub Review - Approve satisfies nothing here (no review state is read anywhere in these files), and re-editing the command comment is equivalent to deleting it. The same function also closes the loop on the #193250 comparison quoted above: when the PR author's own repository role is `maintain` or `admin`, `findMaintainerApproval` returns an author-kind approval immediately and no command is required at all.
2. **A yes/no on the `Decision needed`**: whether `session_authority` joins the closed failover vocabulary. The review's own recommendation is to approve it; the measured alternative is that a refused scheduled run's cause is dropped to `undefined` by the run-history reader's own enum (`z.enum(FAILOVER_REASONS)`), because the writer already emits the value. Who can answer: the repo requires explicit approval for protocol changes (`AGENTS.md` — “Protocol/version bumps … need explicit approval; fix/ship authority ≠ release authority”) but names no owner for them — `CODEOWNERS` is 23 lines covering only `openclaw-secops` and `openclaw-release-managers`, has no catch-all, and lists nothing for `packages/gateway-protocol/**`; searching `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `docs/` for a protocol/vocabulary owner returns nothing. So this is waiting for any maintainer, not for a specific team that has been silent. Measured so the decision is framed correctly: `packages/gateway-protocol/src/failover-reasons.ts` has **exactly two commits in its entire history** — created whole by #121334 (2026-08-10, `3d5f916523d`) after duplicated reason lists had drifted and worker live events were rejecting `tls_certificate` payloads, and touched once since by #158222 (2026-09-26, `3c449bd35be`), a refactor that preserves the contract. **That framing was accurate when written and is now obsolete — and the correction is the most useful paragraph in this body.** `6f69195cd6b` (#193250, landed 07:24:45Z the same day) added `route_unavailable` to this very list, so `main` is at 17 members and this PR would make 18. That commit is the precedent the reviewer said did not exist, and it is nearly line-for-line the same change: it touched `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-profile-failure-policy.ts` with a **one-line addition to the same no-cooldown-write list** (`main` now reads `params.failoverReason === "route_unavailable" ||` at line 35, immediately beside this PR's line 41), updated the same formatter files (`user-copy.ts`, `assistant-request-failure-copy.ts`, `probe-status.ts`, `failover-error.ts`), regenerated the same predicate (`+3187/−3185` — the ordinal shift described above), added its own `config/test-lines-allocations/clawrouter-credit-immediate-fallback.txt`, and merged. Its final state: **`rating: 🦐 gold shrimp` (3/6)** — the same rung this PR sits on — with **`status: 👀 ready for maintainer look`**, carrying `security-sensitive-changed`, and **zero** `/allow-security-sensitive-change` comments anywhere in its comments or timeline. Two consequences stated plainly: the vocabulary is extendable by exactly the mechanism used here, so a yes points at an in-repo template rather than setting a precedent; and a 3/6 rating has never been this repo's merge bar. (Verified 15:14:10Z against `main`; the gate asymmetry recorded here as unexplained **is now explained, from source**. #193250's guard comment states verbatim: "No secops approval is required. This comment is informational because the PR author has Maintain or Admin access.", names `Repository role: admin` for its author, and matches **the same file** this PR does (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-profile-failure-policy.ts`). The shipped predicate is `scripts/github/security-review-event.mjs:309`, which drops a PR from the review queue when the author's repository role is `maintain` or `admin` — so the exemption keys on the author's permission on the repository, not on the scope of the change. Both PRs do report `author_association=CONTRIBUTOR` in REST, which is exactly the field that misled the earlier version of this paragraph: the workflow does not read it. Two consequences, stated separately so neither overreaches: this PR cannot borrow that zero-approval path, because the command is genuinely required for a contributor-author change; and the rating argument is unaffected, because #193250 still merged at 🦐 3/6, which is why 3/6 is not this repo's merge bar. The `status:` difference is explained by the same mechanism plus the review's own definition - it labels `👀 ready for maintainer look` when it has no contributor-facing blocker left, and `⏳ waiting on maintainer` when an explicit approval or decision is outstanding, which is precisely the state the enforced gate plus the recorded vocabulary decision create here.) The two options, and their costs, both quotable from shipped code. **Option A** is this PR: name the state (`session_authority`) so every consumer that already keys on the vocabulary says the same thing - the 403 mapping (`src/agents/failover-error.ts:191`), the cron run-history cause (`src/cron/run-history-detail.ts:77`), and the four exhaustive copy maps. **Option B** is the narrower alternative the question implies: keep classifying the refusal as `auth` and only suppress the profile-health write, so no public member is added. Its cost is user-visible and specific: under `auth`, the shipped copy at `src/agents/failover/user-copy.ts:621-622` reads "Couldn't sign in to ${provider}. Your saved login looks expired or no longer works.", and `auth` additionally carries cooldown copy (`:652` → `AUTH_PROFILE_COOLDOWN_COPY.auth`) - so a local relay that never spoke to the credential would still tell the user their saved login is broken, which is the false statement these reports are about (#162119's own diagnostics log `reason=auth` for exactly these 403s). Option A's copy instead reads "refused this request before sending it. Start a fresh request with /new." (`:625-626`), true whether or not the credential works. `VISION.md:99` states the repo's preference for this shape of change - "Once several independent PRs or requests wire in the same kind of capability, the right response is a contract, not a queue of merges" - and three independent P1 reports (#162119, #165739, #191473) wire this one. VISION does not decide enum membership, so this remains a human ask rather than a citation that answers itself.

Head moved twice since the last review: `main` regenerated the one colliding generated path, first in 513c12703ad and again in d0e78b07144, each time flipping this PR to CONFLICTING and stopping CI, so the branch was re-integrated and the predicate regenerated — `e960518954b` (main `9cb29007ed1`, 56 commits) was the head to approve at that point (superseded twice since; item 1 names today's); `a58d99c1fbc` is one merge behind it, the durable review quotes `83e1c7e1d1b`, two merges behind, and the historical notes below still name `23ba4def295`. Re-verified on the newest merge: all five validator checks; the protocol registry, generation, native `--check` and since guards; the core test typecheck; the seven touched suites (45, 25, 13 and 72 passed across four shards); and the test-line ratchet with 15 lines of slack. On the previous merge the same set passed with the touched suites at 72, 13, 42 and 25. One environment caveat carried forward: `codex-app-server:protocol:check` cannot run here because it wants a sibling `openai/codex` checkout at `rust-v0.164.0`, and no workflow references it, so it is a dev-time sync check rather than a gate. One measured caveat: on that earlier merge `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` reported the tree 7 lines over the ceiling, and the identical 7 is `main`’s own overage (same checker, same throwaway-index method: `Test lines: 6467640; ceiling: 6467633; over by: 7; net delta: 0`), while this change still contributes exactly its allocated 292. Nothing was trimmed to hide it; the shared scalar is untouched.

Current state (03:08:18Z, head `a8f1213f25098dfefe1dca1078037f6b6276bd96`): **mergeable, and CI is red-free** — the run is **complete and red-free** (re-read 12:07Z): 111 succeeded / 72 skipped / 1 neutral (`CodeQL`), zero failures, zero cancellations, nothing in progress, and 3 checks that never report. `mergeable` is **MERGEABLE**, with `mergeStateStatus=BLOCKED` only on the two approvals above. Drift is measured as one full sweep plus hourly increments: the full head-to-`main` sweep at 07:07Z (66 `main` commits, 680 distinct changed paths) and every hourly window since (this round: 8 commits, 95 paths against `main` @ `9f5e8175577`) intersect this PR's 21 files in **0** paths, and `packages/gateway-protocol/src/compiled/protocol.generated/predicates.js` is still blob `c5df64e150ac` on that tip, identical to this branch's merge base - so no regeneration is pending and `a8f1213f25098dfefe1dca1078037f6b6276bd96` is a head that can be approved and merged as-is today. Concretely: `check-lint-core-1..5` all green, `checks-ui-e2e (1/4)`, `(2/4)` and `(3/4)` green, both `android-access-native` matrix cells green, `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` green, the `openclaw/ci-gate` mirror green, and all 20 `checks-node-changed-*` shards — the family that runs the Gateway product proof — green. That clause is now a citation rather than an inference: in job `127671424815` (`checks-node-changed`, log fetched 21:20Z) the shard log shows `[shard:bun:test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/codex-local-refusal-profile-health.e2e.test.ts] begin` at 02:30:35Z, then `[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 77.48s` and `end (exit 0)` at 02:31:53Z, and the neighbouring `gateway-codex-refusal-product-proof.e2e.test.ts` reports `Test Files 1 passed (1)` at 02:33:21Z. So both refusal-proof e2e files execute in CI on this head - the first is this PR's own, and the second predates it (same blob `50f493f86ad9` on `main`, first added by #136194 on 2026-09-04), which also means this PR does not disturb the lane that already covers the sibling refusal shape. Proof confidence 🦞 5/6 ("Sufficient (terminal)"), patch quality 🦞 5/6, zero open findings, no remaining rank-up moves, and the reviewer's `Before merge` has collapsed from two items to one. The two lanes that *were* red on earlier heads cleared exactly as attributed below (upstream repaired both), so what follows is kept as a measurement trail, not as open work:

- `checks-ui-e2e (1/4)`, `(2/4)`, `(3/4)` — Control UI copy assertions broken by upstream `f1a317d4674` ("chore(ui): refresh control ui locales", landed 17:50Z, i.e. after this branch's previous integration). All seven failing spec files (`cron-search`, `cron-filters`, `cron-run-completion`, `cron-run-suppression`, `boot-module-boundaries`, `settings-layout`, `new-session-page.workspace-memory`) are byte-identical to `main` here — `git diff 77c263b9fa1 HEAD -- <file>` is empty for each — and none is in this change's surface.
- `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` — the tree is 7 lines over the test-line ceiling, and `main`'s own tree is over by the same 7 under the same checker and method (`Test lines: 6467640; ceiling: 6467633; over by: 7; net delta: 0`); this change still contributes exactly its allocated 292.

Head `a58d99c1fbc` then merged main past `9938e65a609`, the upstream commit that realigned those e2e expectations with the refreshed locales, and past the test-line reconciliation: on this merge the ratchet measures 25 lines of slack rather than 7 over, and the seven UI spec files are byte-identical to a `main` that contains its own repair. Measured on this merge: `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` and `checks-ui-e2e (3/4)` turned green, exactly as those two upstream reconciliations predict. Two lanes stayed red there for a **different** copy drift that the e2e-alignment commit did not cover: `ui/src/e2e/new-session-page.device-dispatch.e2e.test.ts` still expects `No worker slots are available` while the UI renders `No session slots are available. Wait for a slot or pick another device.`, and `boot-module-boundaries` / `cron-filters` still expect `to the selected runner` where the UI now renders `to the selected device`. Concretely, on this tree `ui/src/i18n/locales/en-new-session-setup.ts:243` renders `deviceNoSlots: "No session slots are available…"` and `:96` renders `placementSyncsFolder: "Syncs {folder} to the selected device"`, while `ui/src/e2e` still holds 3 expectations for the retired `No worker slots are available` and 1 for `… selected runner`. The paired unit tests already assert the new wording (`ui/src/pages/new-session/device-placement.test.ts:43`, `checkout-chip.test.ts:245`), so the rename was deliberate and only the browser layer lags — a one-line alignment in those specs, not a product change. 
All three spec files are byte-identical to `main` on this branch (`git diff a58d99c1fbc^2 -- <file>` is empty for each), none is in this change's surface, and the alignment belongs to whoever owns that rename — not patched quietly inside a credential-health PR. Superseded — by 05:04:27Z `main` had completed that alignment; the commit-level closure is recorded once in the CI section below rather than three times here. Those strings still appear on this head only because the branch cannot be re-integrated from the contributor's machine right now: `git fetch` of this repository negotiates (the server announces the object count) but no pack data ever arrives, and it has stalled that way across every round since, while a small repository on the same SSH connection round-trips in 4 seconds — so it is specific to this repository's transfer, not a general network outage. Nothing in this list needs a decision anymore; it needs a merge.

Mergeability, stated plainly so nobody re-derives it: `main` regenerated that same generated predicate **again** at 00:44:29Z (`730b60991ee`, #186073), which is twenty minutes after the head above, so this PR went back to `CONFLICTING`. **That is now closed**: a fourth integration, `a8f1213f25098dfefe1dca1078037f6b6276bd96`, resolved it — preserving **both** `session_authority` and main's `route_unavailable` in the canonical tuple (18 members) and regenerating the Gateway predicate against the integrated schema, which is exactly what the reviewer's `Before merge` had begun to ask the contributor for — and the PR now reports `MERGEABLE`. The collision is one generated file and the resolution is mechanical — corrected at 15:14:10Z, because the earlier version of this sentence was wrong: it claimed *one* intersecting file, read from the `compare` API, whose `files` array silently caps at 300 entries — and `main` had changed exactly 300 files in the window, so the list was truncated rather than complete. Counting per file instead (`commits?path=<file>&since=<base date>` for each of this PR's 21 files) gives **12** overlapping paths: the generated predicate plus 11 source and test files — and **all 12 come from that single #193250 commit** (26 files in total), each as a one-line list addition at a different offset. Most are one-line additions at different offsets in the same lists, so the merge is expected to auto-resolve with only the predicate conflicting as it always does, but I cannot prove that from this machine (the fetch needed to test it fails — see below), so what is claimed here is a measured overlap count with an unverified merge outcome, which is strictly better than the false precision it replaces — take main's version of `packages/gateway-protocol/src/compiled/protocol.generated/predicates.js`, run `pnpm gateway:validators:gen`, commit the generator output (then re-`git add` it, because a merge commit records the index) — and it recurs on roughly every protocol-touching merge. One thing worth knowing before you merge, measured 13:07Z: two **open** PRs edit the same lists this change touches - #193752 edits `src/agents/failover/classify-core.ts` and `failover-error.ts` (this PR's priority-classifier slot and its 403 status mapping), and #148275 edits `src/agents/failover/message-patterns.ts` (this PR's refusal matcher). Neither one is a competing repair of this bug; the point is only that whichever of them lands first will make this branch need one more mechanical integration, so the approval should key to the head you actually merge rather than to a SHA read earlier. `main` as of `b4c2c8f9e43` still has `session_authority` at 0 occurrences in `failover-reasons.ts` (344 B), `message-patterns.ts` (18,768 B) and `auth-profile-failure-policy.ts` (3,543 B), so nothing has landed ahead of this.

 every push re-keys `/allow-security-sensitive-change` to a fresh SHA and re-runs ~30 minutes of shared CI while changing no verdict. The order of operations that actually ends this is *final integration first, then the approval on whatever head lands*. Two artifacts can mislead whoever picks this up, so both are named rather than left to be rediscovered:

- *Resolved at 02:31:07Z.* The hosted review's `Before merge` checkbox had been asking for `/allow-security-sensitive-change` for `83e1c7e1d1b`, two merges dead — approving a stale SHA does not clear the gate. Re-requesting the review **with new dated facts attached** is what fixed it: the re-derived review is pinned to `a8f1213f25098dfefe1dca1078037f6b6276bd96` and its `Before merge` collapsed from two items to one. The artifact that tracks the live head automatically remains the pinned `openclaw:security-sensitive-guard` comment (it re-keyed to `e960518954b` at 00:37:32Z and re-listed the same single sensitive file, which is the entire scope of what is being approved).
- The inherited reds are tracked to commits, not described vaguely — and **both are now closed upstream**. `8168f831574` (01:39:19Z, #193097) gave the promise executors block bodies, and `9edb1d3e633` (05:04:27Z, #193160, sub-commit `test(ui): align placement expectations with device copy`) aligned `ui/src/e2e/session-placement-module-boundaries.test-support.ts:250` (`:262` had already been using the new wording, which is how the miss was visible). **CI on `e960518954b`** — tally re-read at 13:08:37Z on the unchanged head — bot lanes keep re-reporting on a static head, so this is a snapshot, not a final count: 145 succeeded / 154 skipped / 4 red / 1 neutral (`CodeQL`) with 3 checks never reporting when re-read at 18:07:12Z, and **the red set identical across both reads**, which is the part that matters, and none of the four red comes from this diff (`check-lint-core-1..5` are four successes plus this one failure; `checks-ui-e2e (2/4)` and `(3/4)` are green). `build-artifacts` was green on the previous head, which is the lane that proves the regenerated predicate matches a moving `main`, and the Android disk failure did not recur there. Everything below is the evidence and the reasoning behind those two asks.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a local Codex owner refusal (HTTP 403 produced by the in-process inference relay, before any provider request) was classified as a provider authentication failure, which cooled down the shared OpenAI OAuth profile and interrupted every other agent using that credential.

## User Impact

User impact: one refused run no longer logs an entire profile out. Sibling agents on the same credential keep working, the model fallback chain is not consumed for a refusal that says nothing about the model, API clients receive a permission rejection instead of a retryable server error, and the message no longer tells operators to sign in again — it tells them to start a fresh request.

## Why This Change Was Made

The refusal is generated locally, so the credential answered nothing; the 401/403 rule in `src/agents/failover/classification-rules.ts` could not tell the two apart. The fix preserves the local refusal's identity instead of exempting HTTP 403 or the `model_permission_denied` code globally, so genuine provider permission errors keep their exact current handling.

- The local relay's own refusal copy is the identity carrier. Codex's transport drops the relay's JSON body and renders only `error.message` as `unexpected status {status}: {message}, url: {url}` (`codex-rs/protocol/src/error.rs`, `UnexpectedResponseError::display_body` / `Display`), so the copy is the part that survives to the runner.
- A new run-scoped `session_authority` failover reason carries it: `src/agents/auth-profiles` and `run/auth-profile-failure-policy.ts` record profile health only for `auth`, `auth_permanent`, and `billing`, so the shared credential is never cooled.
- The reason resolves to `coordination` in `resolveModelFallbackError`, the owner that already stops the chain when "changing models cannot repair" the failure. Another model cannot re-establish the refused run's owner, so the chain surfaces the refusal instead of blaming a candidate, which is what the issue's "should not consume the model fallback chain" requirement asks for.
- `FAILOVER_STATUS` projects the reason as `403` with `permission_error`, so OpenAI-compatible clients stop seeing an unmapped reason fall through to a retryable `500`.
- Operator-facing copy for the reason avoids sign-in advice on both the assistant and auth-profile surfaces.

## Evidence

The runner regression pins the shape the transport actually produces (prose only, no `model_permission_denied` token), so a repair keyed on the discarded JSON code cannot pass it. Red first, then green, same command:

```
node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.infra.config.ts \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.harness-auth-failover.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

- Before the repair (test-only commit `8c80e28397b`, production code unchanged): `× keeps a healthy auth profile untouched when the local Codex owner refuses → expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 2 times` — the shared profile was marked **and** the run rotated to a second profile (`1 failed | 12 passed`).
- With the production-shaped fixture on this head: `Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 13 passed (13)`.
- Same run, now also proving the sibling turn: after the refusal the next run on the same credential resolves with its payloads and the recorded attempt profile list stays `[openai:failed, openai:failed]` with `markAuthProfileFailure` never called — the refusal consumed neither the profile nor the fallback chain.
- Model fallback chain, at its owner (`src/agents/model-fallback.chain-stop.test.ts`), with a configured second candidate `fixture-next/fixture-model`: `stops the chain for a local Codex authority refusal without blaming a candidate model` → the error surfaces unchanged, `run` is called once, and neither `onError` nor `onFallbackStep` fires. Red without the coordination routing: `FAIL … stops the chain for a local Codex authority refusal …`.
- HTTP projection for the pinned prose error (`src/gateway/openai-compatible-agent-run.test.ts`): `projects a local Codex authority refusal as a permission rejection` asserts `{ status: 403, error: { type: "permission_error" } }`. Reverting only the status mapping reproduces the reported defect exactly — `AssertionError: expected { status: 500, … } to deeply equal { status: 403, … }` — and restoring it returns `Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 25 passed (25)`.
- Why the prose fixture still has teeth, probed against the shipped classifier rather than a mock: the same message still matches the generic credential-auth pattern list (`isAuthErrorMessage(prose) === true`, through its `forbidden` and `status 403` patterns), so `session_authority` is carried by the new priority matcher alone — remove it and this input lands on the `auth` path that marks the profile.

```
PASS | local prose -> reason | actual="session_authority"
PASS | local prose hits generic auth pattern | actual=true
PASS | local envelope -> reason | actual="session_authority"
PASS | provider model_permission_denied -> reason | actual="auth"
PASS | provider bad api key 403 -> reason | actual="auth"
PASS | signal model-policy 403 -> reason | actual="session_authority"
PASS | signal 401 invalid key -> reason | actual="auth"
PASS | session_authority copy has no re-login hint | actual=false
PASS | auth copy does carry the re-login hint | actual=true

The `16384/ps16k` variant is **skipped** on other recently landed PRs and never reports on `main` push commits, and `openclaw/ci-gate` is not a required status check either — PR #192499 landed with `openclaw/ci-gate` red on its merge commit. So this lane needs a re-run by someone with write access to be green, not a code change from me; nothing about it reflects the tree.

The latest review marks this explanation as contributor-supplied because its own log download was redirected to a blocked host, so here are the two lines verbatim from `gh api repos/openclaw/openclaw/actions/jobs/126253990114/logs` (re-fetched just now, both still present): `##[warning]You are running out of disk space. The runner will stop working when the machine runs out of disk space. Free space left: 0 MB` at `22:42:12`, then `Warning: An error occurred while preparing SDK package 16 KB Page Size Google APIs Intel x86_64 Atom System Image: No space left on device.` at `22:42:20`. The job died inside SDK/emulator provisioning — the only earlier steps were Java setup and that `sdkmanager` download, and no Gradle build or instrumentation task had run yet — so the lane cannot be reporting anything about this diff. GitHub’s own record corroborates it without the log CDN: the annotations endpoint for that check run reports `No files were found with the provided path: apps/android/app/build/outputs/androidTest-results/connected/**`, i.e. the job produced no Android test results at all, which is only possible if it stopped before instrumentation.
4. **Optional** — `pnpm test:docker:published-upgrade-survivor` to cover the packaged update lifecycle, which the host-side checks deliberately do not claim.

As of the latest recorded review (re-keyed to `23ba4def295`), evidence is not the constraint and neither is code: proof confidence is graded 🦞 diamond lobster ("Sufficient (terminal)"), patch quality 🦞 diamond lobster with **no actionable findings and no remaining rank-up moves**, and overall readiness is held at 🦐 only by owner direction on the public vocabulary — the review states that in two places, so the sub-scores cannot lift it on their own. The two items that remain are maintainer-only: the security-sensitive approval for `23ba4def295` (any push resets it) and the recorded `Decision needed` on adding a member to the closed failover vocabulary, for which the review's own recommendation is to approve the additive reason. This section is kept as a record of what was produced locally and what a container would still add, not as a claim that more evidence is required.

Currency check, re-run at 10:04:12Z against today's `main` @ `43654d5fcea` (09:56:52Z) — still no competing repair. `session_authority` occurs **0** times, on that tip, in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/failover-reasons.ts` (344 B), `src/agents/failover/message-patterns.ts` (18,768 B), `src/agents/failover/classify-core.ts` (16,997 B) and `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/auth-profile-failure-policy.ts` (3,543 B); the byte counts are quoted because a truncated or empty read would print the same zero. `auth-profile-failure-policy.ts` on `main` already carries the `route_unavailable` exclusion (1 occurrence) and not this one, and a repo-wide code search for `owner of this model request` on `main` returns **exactly one path** — `extensions/codex/src/app-server/inference-dispatch.ts`, the relay that emits the refusal — so nothing on the classification side mentions it. Earlier reads (at `be881a7f8b1`, then `8209e020b8c`) said the same; today's is the one that matters. So the misclassification is live on `main` as of now, and this PR remains the only fix.

Hook integrity was checked pre-merge against `df9d3240e52` because CI could not run while the branch was unmerged; the merge makes that reasoning moot and the live code is now the evidence. Between the old base and `be881a7f8b1` exactly one commit touched the classifier files this repair hangs off (`7e4bdf2f607`, provider deadline timeouts reported as auth failures), and after the merge the classification still resolves the refusal prose to `session_authority` (`classify.test.ts`), the profile policy still skips the health write (`run.harness-auth-failover.test.ts`), and the Gateway proof still shows the shared profile serving the next turn.

The one stronger form not reproducible on this host:

- **Latest-stable upgrade with existing state** — `pnpm test:docker:published-upgrade-survivor` with `OPENCLAW_UPGRADE_SURVIVOR_BASELINE_SPECS="openclaw@2026.10.10 openclaw@2026.9.36"` (current `latest` and `extended-stable` from the registry) against this PR's candidate package; Package Acceptance resolves the same lane from `source=ref`, and the QA Lab scenario id is `docker-upgrade-survivor` (`qa/scenarios/runtime/docker-upgrade-survivor.yaml`, script `test/e2e/qa-lab/runtime/docker-e2e-lane.ts`). Checked before writing this: every existing-state upgrade scenario the repo ships (`docker-upgrade-survivor`, `docker-release-upgrade-user-journey`, `docker-update-channel-switch`, `docker-update-migration`, `docker-update-restart-auth`) routes through `docker-e2e-lane.ts`, so there is no host-runner equivalent to substitute — this is the one gate that genuinely needs a container or a runner rather than more local evidence. That is the check that a pre-existing install still loads its stored cron, auth-profile and session state after moving onto this build. The additive-vocabulary probe above shows existing reason values still validate, but it is not the upgrade run the review asked for.

Correction worth recording: the Gateway-turn gate did **not** need a container. It runs on the host through the shipped QA product harness (`test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts`, `--runner host` semantics), and the earlier claim that this sandbox could not exercise a Gateway turn was wrong. The survivor lane genuinely is container-only (`scripts/e2e/upgrade-survivor-docker.sh` hands off to `scripts/e2e/lib/upgrade-survivor/run.sh` inside the harness image) and this machine has no running Docker daemon; starting one, or using a credentialed remote runner, is a host-level action that needs the operator's go-ahead, and remote execution is maintainer-authorized. I still tried the host route today, and it stops on a guard that should not be bypassed: published `openclaw@2026.10.10`, run in an isolated `HOME` on its own port, created real durable state (a seeded cron row, canonical `state/openclaw.sqlite`, per-agent SQLite, config journal), and this branch's CLI then refuses to load it with `UpdatePreMutationError: Runtime artifacts changed, but the affected Gateway is running or its offline state could not be verified`, because the machine has a LaunchAgent-managed Gateway. That refusal is correct behavior on a live install, so the existing-state upgrade check needs a container or a runner without a live service rather than a workaround. One ordering detail matters for whoever runs it: until `main` is integrated, this branch's own version reads `2026.10.9`, which predates the `2026.10.10` stable baseline, so a meaningful upgrade run has to follow the merge rather than precede it. Integration is complete, and the blocker was local configuration rather than the link: this machine's global `http.lowSpeedLimit=1` aborted the fetch during the v0 full-ref advertisement ("expected flush after ref listing"), which is what the earlier failures looked like. `git -c protocol.version=2 -c http.lowSpeedLimit=0 fetch` pulled the whole pack at 9-11 MB/s. The merge itself was one generated file plus `pnpm gateway:validators:gen`, and the branch version now reads `2026.10.10`, so a survivor run pairs a published `openclaw@2026.9.36` baseline against this build rather than treating `2026.10.10` as the newer side.

prs.title: improve: clarify prompt delivery and request intent
prs.body:
Related: #188740

## What Problem This Solves

Clarifies advisory prompt wording that can refuse a separately configured integration, turn a requested plan into implementation, treat compatibility wording as ACP execution intent, count retries as recurring work, or delegate despite excessive handoff overhead.

## User Impact

Follows the requested operation and delivery target more precisely while preserving identity, credential, enforced approval, tool-policy, sandbox, channel-isolation, and ACP boundaries. No runtime enforcement, configuration, or credential behavior changes.

## Scope and Review Follow-up

- Distinguish managed channel transport from separately configured services such as email; native-tool equivalence includes operation, destination, sender identity, attachments, and delivery semantics.
- Deliver the requested planning/audit/review/report artifact without unrequested implementation; change/build requests continue beyond a plan.
- Preserve stronger prefer-mode delegation for responsiveness, with small/tightly coupled work and excessive handoff cost as bounded exceptions. Preserve explicit user/model choices.
- Distinguish explicit ACP execution intent from compatibility/artifact-target wording.
- Exclude retries, corrections, and failed/incomplete follow-ups from recurring-job promotion.
- Treat explicit current-turn authorization as confirmation only within its bounded target/content/scope; runtime policy, enforced approvals, and missing safety decisions still govern.

Rebased on `71ab715e24240d9ae8e31efeed76f376f891fc6d`; candidate `41bc8f2a3d87fbd2b2b69091d6173d27f7133825`. Resolved snapshot conflicts by regeneration. Fixed attributable formatting and line-budget growth; removed a redundant negative assertion and unnecessary line allocation. The source diff retains prefer-mode responsiveness rather than flattening it into general delegation guidance.

## Evidence

Verification on exact candidate `41bc8f2a3d87fbd2b2b69091d6173d27f7133825`:

- Five affected test files: **108/108 passed** (43 unit-fast + 65 agents-core), pinned Vitest 5.0.5 and repository-selected configs.

- Changed-file formatting and `git diff --check`: pass.
- Max-lines, test-lines, and line-cap ratchets against the stated base: pass; no baseline weakening or new allocation.
- All six generated prompt snapshots: current.
- Clean isolated worktree; no installed OpenClaw/Gateway changes.

These are text-contract/unit and generated-prompt checks, **not real-model behavior proof**. Before/after shipped-agent scenario evidence requested by review remains outstanding; no full build or broad test-suite result is claimed. Prior setup failures were resolved with an isolated frozen-lockfile root-only dependency install; lifecycle scripts were disabled and shared dependencies were not modified. Remote source CI and the repository `openclaw/ci-gate` passed for this exact head ([CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41160400891)). prs.title: fix(session): let replay admission cross mirrored command exchanges
prs.body:
Fixes #194303

## What Problem This Solves

A `/stop` sent while a queued follow-up turn was replaying could invalidate that turn: the stop's mirrored command exchange landed in the transcript between the follow-up's persisted user row and its replay admission, and admission refused the turn with "Persisted user turn changed before replay admission" — the queued message was persisted but never answered and nothing retried it. In plain terms: a stop command that arrived while a waiting message was starting should not make that waiting message fail; the stop is bookkeeping, not a new conversation turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replay admission walks the transcript back from the turn tail and only crosses entries that cannot start foreground work (context metadata, compaction, operational notices per #181473). Mirrored command exchanges (`command-input:` / `command-reply:` rows written by `recordDeliveredCommandExchange`) are operational history in the same sense — they never carry agent turn input — but the walk treated them as turn changes. This change lets the interrupted-turn walk cross them; the turn's identity is still pinned by the exact idempotency-key/user-row match, so a genuinely newer conversation user row still invalidates admission as before.

## User Impact

A queued follow-up survives a `/stop` that raced its admission and gets answered instead of failing with a generic error. The transcript still records the stop exchange; no cleanup or retry machinery changes.

## Evidence

- Regression (adapted from the issue's repro): `attempt-session-replay.stop-exchange.test.ts` (registered in `vitest.database-worker-core-paths.mjs` next to `attempt-session-replay.test.ts`). With the stop exchange appended after replay selection and before admission, the follow-up now makes 1 model call and answers ("FOLLOWUP_ANSWERED"); the persisted user turn is written once and the stop exchange once. Red check: reverting the walk change makes the same scenario fail with `Persisted user turn changed before replay admission` and 0 model calls (6/6 pre-fix assertions green, post-fix 6/6 green).
- Controls unchanged: no interposed write and a Workshop notice interposed both still answer across both replay windows (selected reader on/off).
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on changed files.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used source inspection and the repository test harness to analyze issue #194303, adapt the issue's repro into a regression test, and extend the existing interrupted-turn walk predicate in pre-persisted-user-turn.ts. The implementer understands the code: command exchange rows are operational mirrors whose identity checks stay keyed to the exact idempotency match. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix(kubernetes): Gateway refuses to start after an fsGroup volume remount widens its private stores
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Closes #192959.

A Kubernetes `fsGroup` volume broadens the permissions of every directory and file on the volume each time it is mounted, and Linux propagates the volume's setgid bit into directories created under it. OpenClaw's private-storage owners then refuse to open state this installation already owns, and the Gateway cannot start.

`fsGroupChangePolicy: OnRootMismatch` (#193010) only narrows *when* kubelet performs that walk. It does not restore permissions that have already been broadened, so an established deployment stays down.

## User Impact

A Gateway on an `fsGroup` PVC starts again after a remount that widened its stores, instead of refusing with `Client credential directory is unsafe` and leaving the container unavailable across restarts. Existing PVC contents and installation identity are preserved.

Reported from three independent deployments: OpenShift with the AWS EBS CSI driver, k3s with a local-path PVC, and OpenClaw Enterprise running OpenClaw through OpenShell, which currently carries an external workaround for it.

## Why This Change Was Made

`ensureOpenClawStatePermissions` already restores the shared state database's directory and files on every Gateway start, and it already runs before credential admission. It simply did not cover the sibling private stores. The parked reproduction volume showed exactly that asymmetry — `state/` private at `0700` while every sibling was left broadened:

```
2770  uid=1000830000  d  /home/node/.openclaw
2770  uid=1000830000  d  /home/node/.openclaw.update-captures
2770  uid=1000830000  d  /home/node/.openclaw/client
0660  uid=1000830000  -  /home/node/.openclaw/client/credentials.sqlite
2770  uid=1000830000  d  /home/node/.openclaw/control
0660  uid=1000830000  -  /home/node/.openclaw/control/services.sqlite
0700  uid=1000830000  d  /home/node/.openclaw/state
```

So this extends that existing owner to the stores beside it rather than adding a new mechanism, and **no admission check is modified**. Every runtime refusal stays exactly as strict as before; the repair simply runs before the owners read their stores.

The restore is deliberately narrow:

- an **enumerated** path list — the client credential store, the daemon runtime pin store, their SQLite sidecars, and the `<stateDir>.update-captures` sibling — never a recursive walk of the state tree
- the **state root itself is left as found**, because a shared, group-accessible state root is a supported layout that config publication deliberately preserves; only the private stores under and beside it are restored
- **no ownership changes**; restoring a mode is not ownership transfer
- **symlinks are skipped**, not followed
- paths owned by **another UID are left alone**
- paths carrying **world permission bits are left for their owner to refuse**, because `fsGroup` never sets those, so the existing refusal of a world-accessible credential directory is preserved
- an already-private path is untouched, so its ctime stays stable
- group membership still grants no credential authority

It is also wired into Doctor's earliest startup phase, because Doctor's recovery capture reads these paths before database preflight (`maintenance begin → Preserve original state → database preflight`), so without that the pre-repair recovery copy was still skipped on the same boot.

## Evidence

**Red on the base.** `src/state/openclaw-state-db-permissions.test.ts` fails on the unfixed tree with the reported error, using only APIs the base already has:

```
× lets the credential owner admit a remounted installation
  → Client credential directory is unsafe.
```

With the fix: 7 passed. Unit sweep across the affected owners — `client-credential-store`, `private-store-file`, `openclaw-state-db-open`, `openclaw-state-db.permissions`, `openclaw-agent-db.permissions`, `runtime-pin` — all green.

**Cluster A/B, same PVC, no init-container chmod.** OpenShift 4.21.16 / Kubernetes v1.34.7, RHCOS 9.6, `ebs.csi.aws.com` (`gp3`, `fsGroupPolicy: File`), `fsGroup: 1000830000`, `fsGroupChangePolicy: Always`, Gateway running as the namespace's arbitrary UID. Starting state: directories `2770`, store files `0660`.

Unfixed image:

```
Failing check state-schema (step-refused): Failed migrating shared state database
  schema: Error: Client credential directory is unsafe.
- Pre-repair recovery copy was unavailable: Private SQLite staging root must be
  owned by the current user and not writable by other users:
  /home/node/.openclaw.update-captures.
Failing check config-machine-state (blocked-by-prior-refusal)
→ exitCode 1, container restarting, never Ready
```

Fixed image, same volume, kubelet still leaving the volume broadened at each mount:

```
→ Doctor complete.  ready=true  restarts=0

0700  uid=1000830000  d  /home/node/.openclaw
0700  uid=1000830000  d  /home/node/.openclaw.update-captures
0700  uid=1000830000  d  /home/node/.openclaw/client
0600  uid=1000830000  -  /home/node/.openclaw/client/credentials.sqlite
0700  uid=1000830000  d  /home/node/.openclaw/control
0600  uid=1000830000  -  /home/node/.openclaw/control/services.sqlite
0700  uid=1000830000  d  /home/node/.openclaw/state
0600  uid=1000830000  -  /home/node/.openclaw/state/openclaw.sqlite
```

`openclaw.json already present (preserved)` throughout; no reseed, no empty-subpath switch, no relocation.

## Review feedback already applied

CI caught two things, both now fixed and both worth stating plainly:

- **A real regression.** Restoring the state root to `0700` broke `src/config/io.write-config.test.ts`, "preserves a shared state root when publishing private config" — a deliberate contract where the state root may stay group-accessible while the files inside remain private. The reported refusals were all on the stores under and beside the root rather than the root itself, so the root is no longer restored, and the regression suite now asserts a shared root is preserved. The fix is strictly smaller as a result.
- **A type error.** The private-store path list was typed as `readonly string[]` rather than tuples, so destructuring produced `string | undefined` under strict index checking and `tsgo` rejected the core and core-test projects. That accounted for the typecheck and lint failures on the first run.

## Scope and Limitations

- **Not fixed here, by design:** the group-writable temp-ancestor failure (#156985), which the reporters and the issue both treat as separate.
- **Still operator work, and structurally so:** Doctor's pre-repair recovery copy refuses a staging ancestor another user could replace, and it walks the whole ancestor chain to the kubelet-created mount point, which `fsGroup` leaves group-writable (`/home/node`, `2775 owner=0`). I tested moving the state directory one level deeper under the mount; the check still names the mount point, so layout depth does not help. `fsGroup` is both the enabler and the blocker here: it is what makes the volume writable by an arbitrary UID, and it is what makes the mount point an untrusted ancestor. Recovery capture therefore needs a mount point provisioned with the Gateway's ownership before startup (OpenShell #5047; OpenClaw Enterprise does this with a preparation Deployment). Restoring modes is not ownership transfer and an unprivileged container cannot chown a foreign-owned mount point. The Gateway starts and Doctor completes either way; only the pre-repair recovery copy is unavailable.
- **Declared unsupported rather than accommodated:** a state volume shared between workloads by group membership. The Gateway requires its stores private to its own UID, so there is no supported configuration for group-sharing the state volume. `docs/install/kubernetes.md` now says so explicitly instead of weakening validation to allow it.
- **Newly created directories** inheriting setgid already normalize correctly on current `main` (#188464); verified across parent modes `02700`, `02770`, `02775` and `0770`, each yielding `0700`/`0600`. No change was needed for that half.
- **Checks.** The first CI run went red and one cause was mine: the private-store path list was typed as `readonly string[]` rather than tuples, so destructuring produced `string | undefined` under strict index checking and `tsgo` rejected the core and core-test projects. Fixed in the follow-up commit. `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` and `run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs` now both exit 0 locally, alongside file-scoped `oxlint` (0 errors, 0 warnings), format, docs-format, docs-MDX and the import-cycle check. I had been relying on file-scoped lint plus vitest, neither of which type checks, which is why this reached CI.
- **`checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` cannot pass on this merge base.** With my test file removed entirely the ratchet still reports `over by: 34; net delta: 0. Tree is over the ceiling; this change does not add test lines.` The credit cap limits any allocation to the lines a change itself adds, so the pre-existing 34 cannot be allocated away from here; it needs a baseline bump or a prune on `main`. My own 172 lines are fully accounted for in `config/test-lines-allocations/194307-fsgroup-remount.txt`, which brings the report down to exactly that pre-existing 34.
- The other first-run failures came from the merge base rather than this branch: `plugins:assets:build` could not resolve `./client.js` from `extensions/deep-research/browser/index.tsx`. That module is present on `main` now, so those jobs should pass on re-run. `doctor-config-preflight.recovery.test.ts` fails identically with and without this change in my environment.
- The in-cluster validation used a patched image rather than a staged init container, because this environment's policy blocks chmod-bearing manifests.

## Docs

`docs/install/kubernetes.md` records what the Gateway now restores, the narrowing rules, the validated driver and policy, and the two cases that still require the storage owner.

prs.title: fix(discord): thread replies and bindings stop working when a slow channel stop overlaps a restart
prs.body:
Related to #177691. Reviewed snapshots through `206f11bc8903`.

## What Problem This Solves

Discord thread replies and bindings can stop working when a restart overtakes an older task that is still stopping. Each start gets its own binding manager, so the old task's late stop cannot tear down the replacement's manager.

Two paths reproduced on main snapshot `7e81872cbbc`. In round 1, a startup held at `/gateway/bot` resumed late, failed with `Plugin service scheduler is closed`, and stopped the shared manager from its `finally`. In round 2, a slow bind made two replacement starts wait on the old stop. Read-only logpoints observed the mechanism in one run. An aborted start's cleanup stopped the manager that the other start had reused. The account broke in 3 of 4 main runs, including holds before and during the create. Of the three broken runs, only the logpoints run had the inspector attached. The other two match it by symptom only.

Only the narrow config-reload race was exercised. Recovery on a later provider start and other restart entries are read from code, not tested.

## User Impact

A late stop leaves replies working in old bound, newly bound and unbound guild threads. New binds are approved and written to SQLite.

- The old adapter is unregistered at handover. It cannot resurface after the newest owner stops and block session listings for other channels.
- Both native creates check ownership before sending, including direct subagent auto-bind. No built Gateway run measured the subagent path. A bind caught before its create is refused, and no webhook create POST is sent. Built Gateways measured this at `3fe8a885`, `2ae50585` and `206f11bc8903`, the last against real Discord, but not at `900208f1`. In round 2 the approver saw only the deferred update at both snapshots, with the approval prompt unchanged and no error text.
- An accepted thread or webhook create is still published. No built Gateway accepted a thread create. An accepted thread gets no follow-up webhook from the retired manager, so replies use bot sends without the persona. The retired manager sends no intro. This fallback has test and driver coverage, not real Discord proof. No run has shown a webhook-delivered reply.
- A bind settled by the replaced manager keeps that manager's idle timeout, max age and persist flag. The replacement's limits apply only to binds it creates.
- A replaced manager clears its sweep timer at its next tick, even if provider cleanup hangs, so it stops scanning.

A replacement registers without waiting for the old provider to stop. Binding work the old manager already queued, such as an accepted create, settles before queued work on the replacement runs. This includes async session-wide unbinds, idle timeout and max-age updates, inbound activity touches, startup cleanup of stale ACP bindings, and the replacement's own stop. It does not wait for the old manager's stop or the rest of its sweep. Each REST attempt keeps its 15 s timeout and a rate limited request is retried at most three times. Queueing, rate limit delays and persistence mean the total wait has no fixed cap. Deprecated synchronous unbind and duration setters skip the queue and can still overtake the create.

## Why This Change Was Made

`2ae50585` removes manager reuse across starts. Stop removes the account entry and token only for the current manager. #169226 merged the same reuse removal for Feishu.

- `68fb31d6` retires the predecessor's adapter by identity across loaders and guards both native creates.
- `3fe8a885` publishes a native create accepted before replacement, while still refusing new creates by a retired manager. This preserves #153508's accepted-write settlement without granting permission for later sends.
- `900208f1` copies the predecessor's queued-work promise without awaiting it at registration. Async session mutations and replacement stop wait for it, restoring #156627's ordering without joining the old stop.
- `206f11bc8903` makes retired sweepers clear themselves before checking pending work. Cancellation lags at most one 120 s interval.

## Evidence

### Tests

For reviewed snapshots through `206f11bc8903`, all 12 required gates passed. The 19 Discord monitor files passed 182 tests and the 7 binding-consumer files passed 145. Type checks, formatting, typed lint and four ratchets passed.

- The original 3 restart cases fail with main's manager. Creation cases catch old-stop token cleanup and stale adapters resurfacing. The latter fails at `2ae50585` and passes with main's manager and the fix.
- The direct-create cases fail at `2ae50585`. Accepted thread and webhook settlement cases fail with that manager and `68fb31d6`, then pass at `3fe8a885` and `900208f1`.
- The session-wide unbind, idle and max-age cases hold a create across two replacements. All 3 fail with `3fe8a885` and pass at `900208f1`. Wrong-fix controls catch partial inheritance and waiting at registration.
- Two new restart cases hold voice cleanup across two replacements, idle and pending. Both fail at `900208f1`. Guards that skip scans but keep the timer, or check pending work first, fail.

### Built Gateway proof

Rounds 1 to 3 used isolated built Gateways, a Discord stand-in, fake credentials and a local mock response server, not real Discord or model services. Synthesized interactions went only to the newest connected socket at injection time. SQLite rows were checked during runs, not across Gateway restarts. These runs predate the timer commit.

Round 1 compared main `7e81872cbbc` with `2ae50585`. Two `channels.discord.historyLimit` edits about 3 s apart, with one `/gateway/bot` response held about 10 s, overran the 5 s stop grace. The shared edge shim rewrote the gateway URL in `/gateway/bot` and `resume_gateway_url` in READY, renumbered dispatch sequence numbers, and answered interaction callbacks itself. The exact scheduler throw site is inferred.

Main failed in all 4 runs. All 3 guild-thread turns tried after the late stop in the primary run got no reply and logged `SessionWorkStartChangedError`. New binds failed with a binding-owner error.

Round 2 built `3fe8a885` and passed the unchanged late-stop sequence. It also compared main and `2ae50585` on the slow-bind path. At both fix snapshots, refused creates wrote no row, replies kept working, and the pre-create hold sent no webhook create POST. Accepted settlement was unproven because the stand-in returned 404 to every native create.

Round 3 built `900208f1`. Its late-stop run matched round 2 in its outcome rows, but its first replacement start exited with `Skills discovery was retired before publication` and was auto-restarted. The hold lasted 16.1 s, against 10.1 s in round 2, because the harness waited for the usable replacement. The stand-in lacks the webhook create and execution routes, so the edge synthesized four HTTP 200 webhook-create responses with fake IDs and tokens. There was one in each accepted-create run, plus one in a no-reload control at `900208f1`. No webhook-execution response was used. By the edge code, other native REST calls passed unchanged, and the edge answered interaction calls as in round 1.

Each build had one run of this case. At `900208f1`, under a synthetic webhook-create success, the held bind was approved and its webhook ID and token were stored, with no simulated orphan. At `2ae50585`, the same synthetic success was refused, leaving no row and a simulated orphan. Main stored the row but stopped replying and logged 27 ownership-change errors.

Round 3 is PARTIAL for webhook replies. In the bound reply of the accepted run at `900208f1`, a bot send was used despite the stored webhook. The no-reload control, run at `900208f1` only, also used a bot send. The cause of that bot send is read from code, not measured. The reply's agent session key finds no binding row, so no thread id reaches the webhook path. Persona delivery and webhook reply POSTs remain unproven. The optional session-wide probe stopped before its held create, with a Gateway error that begins `Session key does not contain an agent id`. That probe was not run on main or `2ae50585`, so it is not known whether the failure predates this change. Those waits have regression-test coverage only. The separate predecessor socket leak repeated and is not fixed here.

### Live Discord proof

At `206f11bc8903` I ran a built Gateway with real Discord via a TLS proxy and real `gpt-5.6-luna`. A retired manager refused a bind before any webhook create request. A webhook create Discord accepted across a handover was stored by the original bind. L1 was inconclusive, and both attempts needed SIGKILL after a clean-shutdown log. The no-hold control, L2 and L3 each ran once. I ran no base. Details and limits are in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178931#issuecomment-6509058680. L3 receipts are in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178931#issuecomment-6512844287.

### Driver proof

At `206f11bc8903` I ran a scripted driver over the built modules, with a loopback Discord REST stand-in and no Gateway. A retired manager sent no create or intro. Limits are in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178931#issuecomment-6511023964, and redacted receipts in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178931#issuecomment-6511604213.

A second driver added a loopback Gateway stand-in and ran the built channel manager restart over the built provider. Two runs per case were reproduced twice by an independent rerun. After the replacement registered, the older task's startup `finally` stopped only its own manager, and the replacement then took a driver-issued bind and send. The Gateway lifecycle `finally` and a running provider's late stop are unproven. See https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178931#issuecomment-6512196949.

prs.title: fix(discord): native slash commands fail in a plugin-bound thread
prs.body:
## What problem this solves

Native slash commands in a plugin-bound Discord thread fail with `Command failed. Check the Gateway logs for details.` The log says `Session key does not contain an agent id; resolve it with the configured default agent.` I saw `/status` and `/codex binding` fail on main at da60d41, and `/codex detach` on earlier main 572cb278b243. Plain messages work. DMs, top level guild channels and ACP or subagent-bound threads do not hit it.

## User impact

Commands now use the thread's normal routed session and agent, and plugin commands receive the thread and parent ids that find their binding. No config change is needed.

At earlier head 59a4746d, an in-process non-default-agent run got a status card, but `/codex binding` failed before its handler because the binding record named another agent, which this change also fixes.

With `match: { channel: "discord", accountId: "*" }` and no narrower scope, bound-thread `/new` and `/reset` under a disabled parent crashed on main with the session-key error and now reach the existing `binding.channel` recovery exception, as unbound threads do. That crash was no disabled-parent rule to keep. Without that route binding, a test still pins `/new` to `This channel is disabled.`

Source at v2026.8.1-beta.1, sampled stable tags through v2026.10.5 and main has this failure. I did not run those releases. v2026.7.35 resolved the key to the default agent.

## Why this change was made

The native route feeds an opaque `plugin-binding:codex:...` key into `resolveDiscordEffectiveRoute`, then `resolveAgentIdFromSessionKey`, which requires an agent id. The message path has skipped plugin-owned records since #45318 at `message-handler.routing-preflight.ts:57-59`. This change gives `native-command-route.ts` the same ownership guard, and plugin commands find their binding from the conversation.

The guard returns `undefined`. The message path's empty string would become the native command session key at `src/channels/native-command-session-targets.ts:13` and pass `boundSessionKey != null` in the `/new` and `/reset` guard bypass, skipping a disabled-parent denial.

Plugin bind metadata supplies no agent id, so the stored agent can differ from the channel route. For plugin-owned records, `native-command.ts` now takes the agent for session lookup, plugin dispatch and reply recording from `effectiveRoute.agentId`. Other records and configured bindings keep their precedence. Otherwise the shared plugin runtime at `src/plugins/plugin-command-execution.ts:58` rejects the mismatched agent/session pair before its handler.

Telegram and Slack already classify plugin-owned records through core runtime binding routes, so this fix is Discord only. #146898 overlaps only on the call chain and edits free ACP keys in `route-resolution.ts`, untouched here.

## Evidence

Focused tests fail on main and pass with the fix.

`extensions/discord/src/monitor/native-command.interaction-boundary.test.ts` adds a five-case `plugin-bound thread` group to main eb8fa7d's 16, 21 in all. It drives the real internal Discord client with REST, session lookup, status construction, the agent turn, reply recording and the `codex` handler stubbed. Parsing, access policy, routing and plugin dispatch are real.

- Three main-route cases pin status to `agent:main:discord:channel:<thread id>`, `/codex binding` to that key, `args: "binding"` and thread/parent ids, and disabled-parent `/new` denial with no context build or agent turn.
- The work-route case gives the record `main` and the route `work`. Status, session lookup, handler execution and reply recording must all use `agent:work:discord:channel:<thread id>` and `work`.
- An agent-owned record naming `main` with `agent:work:subagent:bound` must still refuse before its handler with `⚠️ Command failed. Please try again later.` Since #180173 the shared runtime catches this mismatch instead of throwing, and drops the error text.
- At 8ffec518, all 17 passed. Reverting only the route file to da60d41 failed the work case and three main cases on the session-key error, 13 passed. Reverting only `native-command.ts` to 59a4746d failed the work case with `The agent-scoped session key belongs to "work", not "main".`, 16 passed. Always choosing the effective agent failed the refusal case, 16 passed. Recording replies on the record agent failed the work case, 16 passed.
- At 99f07dc0, all 21 passed. Reverting both source files to eb8fa7d failed the same four cases, 17 passed. Always choosing the effective agent failed the refusal case, 20 passed. Each listed variant ran once.
- At 59a4746d, defaulting the agent in `session-key.ts` failed three main cases and returning an empty string failed two. Dropping every bound key passed this file but failed `loads model picker data from the effective bound route`. Keeping the configured-binding fallback passed all 15 and is equivalent, since `native-command-route.ts:53-65` skips that resolver when a thread record exists.
- At 2b6df40b, production-equivalent to 8ffec518, `native-command.status-direct`, `message-handler.preflight.acp-bindings`, `acp-bind-here.integration`, `native-command.model-picker` and `native-command.plugin-dispatch` passed 6, 2, 1, 31 and 25 tests. The full Discord project passed at 99f07dc0, 257 files and 2627 tests.
- Test cost, per `docs/help/testing/writing-tests.md:30-36`. At 2b6df40b the 17-case file took 16.28, 19.62 and 20.39 s. At 59a4746d the 15-case file took 19.15, 26.91 and 27.86 s, with tests at 9 to 16 percent of that, under the 5 s target. Back to back, da60d41's 12 cases took 15.75 s and the 15 cases 17.48 s. No CI seconds recorded here.
- At 8ffec518, `tsgo:extensions:test` passed, and `oxfmt --check` and the type-aware extensions lint passed on the test file. At 2b6df40b with `--base da60d41 --no-merge-base`, the line-cap, assertion-safety and mock-export checks passed, and the database-worker, database-dialect and timeout-race checks, `config:docs:check` and `plugins:inventory:check` passed on the same production code with an earlier fixture. `check:max-lines-ratchet` failed with `New max-lines suppressions are forbidden` for three UI files that are byte-identical to da60d41, as is the baseline, and a da60d41 tree fails the same way.

The default-route Gateway runs at da60d41 and 915f97d used isolated homes/state, fake tokens, a loopback mock model and a Discord stand-in, with a local shim injecting native commands and Allow once as `INTERACTION_CREATE` events. Native `/codex bind` plus Allow once persisted one `plugin-binding:codex:` row with `pluginBindingOwner: plugin` on both builds.

| Native command | Main da60d41 | Fix 915f97d |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/status` | `Command failed. Check the Gateway logs for details.` | Card naming `Session: agent:main:discord:channel:<thread id>` |
| `/codex binding` | Same failure | `Codex conversation binding:` block naming the workspace |

Main logged two session-key errors, one per command, the fix none. The binding row was unchanged on both. The route file at 8ffec518 is byte-identical to 915f97d. `/codex detach` and the other native commands share it but did not run on that build.

## Additional Evidence

Built Gateway through mocked Discord gateway/REST: main twice fails /status and plugin /proofprobe after plugin binding approval; candidate twice returns status and matching agent/session context. Default-route controls pass on both. https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177850#issuecomment-6432527783

### Not fixed here

Unrelated slash-command failures are outside this fix. This additional transport proof covers the default-agent route, not non-default-agent or unauthorized-user behavior.

## Authority proof

On real Discord at `99f07dc0` with `gpt-5.6-luna`, bound-thread `/status` showed the `work` session while the record still named `main`. A sender on no allowlist was refused with no binding change or model request. All observed checks passed, but the run is inconclusive against my evidence plan. Limits are in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177850#issuecomment-6494748481.

The local runs below, detailed in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177850#issuecomment-6491720075, used built Gateways at `9b7db694` and `99f07dc0`, a loopback Discord stand-in, fake tokens and mock models.

A2 binds with only `main`, then fully restarts with a `work` route. Head's `/status` and both probes use `agent:work:discord:channel:<thread>`, and its one model request hit the work mock with `Bearer fake-work-key`. Base fails all three with the session-key error. The binding row stays byte-identical and names `main`.

B's six denied commands in the bound thread got `You are not authorized to use this command.` before any plugin handler or model call, in the single-agent fixture.

With `accountId: "*"` and no `commands.allowFrom` or `commands.ownerAllowFrom`, B2's denied `/new` and `/reset` fail on base with the session-key error and reach core refusal on head, which B2-U also finds on main unbound threads and plain channels. No final reply, reset or model call, but session metadata is written.

C's local unit test, outside this PR, defers the session lookup and revokes `commands.allowFrom` during it. The handler never runs. Removing only post-lookup `authority.assertActive()` at `native-command.ts:538` makes it fail. Source shows no Discord-observable step inside that window, so a Gateway run cannot hold it.

Main's unbound work-routed thread already selected `work` and sent `fake-work-key`, so routed-agent credential selection pre-exists. On both revisions the sender gate at head `native-command.ts:383-385` rejects before route state at 391, except in the `/new` and `/reset` bypass. This PR adds no await and moves no authorization check.

prs.title: fix(discord): codex detach and rebind are lost after a Gateway restart
prs.body:
Fixes #178330. Related to #175379.

## What Problem This Solves

A Discord thread detached with a typed `/codex detach` can become bound again after the Gateway restarts. A typed `/codex bind` that moves a bound thread to a new workspace can also be undone by a restart.

## User impact

Detached threads stay detached, rebinds keep their new workspace, and later binding changes remain durable. A write refused by a retired runtime or a closing Gateway no longer disables persistence, and a refused binding change reports a failure, not success. A replacement Discord provider that starts after its predecessor retires gets its own thread binding manager, so its bind, idle timeout and detach writes persist. No config change or migration is needed.

A row left behind by an earlier detach is still loaded at startup. That thread needs one more `/codex detach` on this build.

The repair reaches core runtime-owned state stores, so the Telegram, ClickClack and `/codex` caller suites are included below. Matrix's separate no-instance repair is #177372.

## Cause and repair

Discord looked up its plugin runtime in the slot of the plugin instance currently running, and a typed detach starts in the `/codex` instance, where the Discord slot is empty. The write threw `Discord runtime not initialized`, the manager changed memory and disabled persistence for the process, and the command appeared to succeed until restart.

Each Discord manager now retains its creating runtime and passes it into async and synchronous store opens, and session-wide idle timeout, max age and unbind helpers read the same runtime from a private WeakMap through the account registry. Core now checks a runtime-owned synchronous store at open and before all seven mutators, update and deleteIf also after their callback. Already-open handle reads are unchanged.

The state runtime marks its authority refusal with `PLUGIN_STATE_RUNTIME_INACTIVE`, and the worker client preserves it. Discord tells it from a storage failure through the SDK facade it already imports, drops the uncommitted write and leaves persistence on. For a retired runtime, async unbind, bind, detach and the session-wide idle timeout, max age and unbind updates reject with it, send no unbound notification and publish no record. The check runs before every shared-memory publication, including a touch inside the 15 s persist interval and a manager with persistence off or latched off. It opens a data-only V2 handle with no store operation before the operation module source is captured. Synchronous compatibility calls still return null or an empty array, a retired owner's touches resolve null, and a deleted thread still closes its sessions after a refused unbind. Real storage failures still disable persistence and apply the change in memory.

`createThreadBindingManager` used to return the account's cached manager even after its owner retired, so a replacement provider's own bind, idle timeout and detach were refused, and after the old stop removed the adapter nothing recovered until a later acquisition. Now, when the cached manager's runtime is inactive, acquisition checks that the caller's runtime is active, starts the old stop without waiting for it, and registers a new manager that retains the caller's runtime. The old manager's runtime is never reassigned, and its late stop clears the slot and adapter only while it owns them. A live owner's manager is still reused, an inactive caller still gets the typed refusal, and a reference taken while its owner was live stays refused after retirement.

Reviewed through `5388ada4c289`, manager method signatures, account queues and the runtime lookup for managers without a retained runtime are unchanged.

Public SDK semantics change for retired runtimes. Typed and plain runtime refusals now count as closed admission for SDK retries and tool outcomes. New synchronous opens and writes through retained synchronous handles now refuse work, and async binding changes through a retired Discord manager now reject. An October 19 usage query found no resolved references to this member but covered only 2,047 of 2,432 eligible artifacts, so third-party impact is unknown. `createThreadBindingManager`, exported from the Discord runtime API, now also replaces the cached manager of a retired owner, and in that case it throws the typed refusal if the caller's runtime is inactive or missing.

## Evidence

At `857edb7316cf`, six PR test files passed 218 tests, 15 plugin-state files passed 193 with one skipped, and ten baseline checks passed. My real Discord/model checks at `d1e4495644c5` are in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177691#issuecomment-6505159776. The checks passed, but the full runbook evidence remains inconclusive. Typed detach and rebind persisted across restart. These runs cover only the first half of the authority-chain item. Retirement and replacement writes ran in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/177691#issuecomment-6507291299, a scripted driver over the built production modules at `d1e4495644c5` and not a Gateway reload. A checker's revoke run there covers revocation. Other results below ran at earlier heads.

### Tests at `22ea62d`

Head `857edb7316cf` merges `5388ada4c289`, uses upstream's `publicationEffect` helper and adds six cases. Commit `22ea62d` adds `src/plugins/conversation-binding.discord-handoff.test.ts` with three cases. A live owner's retained manager refuses a candidate's writes after retirement until an explicit acquisition hands off. A replacement started after retirement gets a distinct manager whose bind, idle timeout, touch and detach persist, and the old manager's late stop leaves it registered. An inactive candidate cannot replace a retired owner. All three fail with the two production files from `56cd59f` and pass at `22ea62d`. Wrong versions that borrow the caller's runtime at call time, fall back to memory on the typed refusal, hand off over a live owner, or skip the candidate's activity check each fail one of them.

On a mocked clock, an uncommitted diagnostic found that at `56cd59f`, after the owner retired, the candidate's idle timeout write was refused at five points from +1 s to +1 h. At main `e2da41f` the idle writes, bind, touch and detach all succeeded before the old stop. A probe then stopped the old instance from accepting calls, started the replacement with the old manager unstopped, and ran each operation in the replacement.

| Operation | `56cd59f` production files | `22ea62d` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bind | Refused | Persisted |
| `/session idle` | Refused | Persisted |
| Touch | Null, no write | Row updated |
| `/codex detach` | Refused | Removed |
| After the late old stop | `BINDING_ADAPTER_UNAVAILABLE` | Bind persisted |

At `22ea62d` the 14 Discord binding, listener and manager caller files passed 206 tests and the 7 conversation binding and contract files passed 128. The extensions type check, the core plugin-platform test type check, formatting and typed lint on the three files it changes, and the mock-exports and line-cap ratchets also passed. At `22ea62d`, max-lines, the other ratchets, the SDK exports check, plugin inventory and config documentation were not rerun. At the `56cd59f` production code they passed except max-lines, which flagged three unchanged UI files, and 17 Telegram, ClickClack and `/codex` caller files passed 310 tests.

The 19 retired Discord cases fail at `d5f8321`, and the bound-source and core open cases fail at `ed59bdf`. Real SQLite trigger failures verify the memory fallback. The `/codex detach` command file checks the failure reply and the restored native binding. A 30-cell guard matrix from `95d9afe` through `ed59bdf`, a 45-cell probe and an uncommitted 153-cell probe of earlier heads found no durable difference and were not rerun.

### Prior-head Gateway evidence, not rerun

The earlier local Gateway record used a Discord stand-in and mock model. It compares main `89e77376ccb` with local merge `3a4095bc93d`, the earlier `de7639b` repair. It was not rerun on a later head, and its typed detach reply predates the refusal path above. After detach, stop and a fresh start, main held 1, 1, 1 rows and the old binding returned after restart, while the merge held 0, 0, 0. A typed rebind run kept the new workspace through restart on the merge, not on main.

### Remaining limits

The live runs did not cover a base build, a DM, Always allow or registry retirement, which the scripted driver ran. The full Discord extension project passed at `67b59f2ef60e` and was not rerun after main changed 96 Discord extension files through `5388ada4c289`. #178330 holds its author's pre-fix reproduction on a real Discord bot, which was not rerun on this branch.

The typed detach failure reply and the real store's refusal were measured separately, not together in a Gateway. The reload ordering, with the old instance's calls stopped before the replacement provider starts, was read from source and modeled with an instance that no longer accepts calls. The time from retirement to the replacement's acquisition was not measured, and writes in it are still refused. The handoff for a caller with no runtime has no test. A channel restart inside the same plugin instance after a timed-out stop still shares one manager, so the old task's late stop removes its adapter until the next provider start, as on main. A session-wide call while no manager is registered still uses the ambient runtime lookup, whose failure still turns persistence off, as on main. A session-wide update across two accounts stops at the first refused row without rolling back earlier rows, startup reconciliation does not catch a refused stale unbind, and a refused thread-delete unbind leaves its row for the replacement owner's sweeper.
