prs.title: fix(feishu): accept the documented markdown table mode
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Feishu `markdown.tables` validation at startup and applies the setting to sends, replies, presentations and previews.

## User impact

Channel and account table settings are accepted, including the delivering/default account. Ordinary `off` table messages settle as authored rich-text posts. In `off`, presentations keep controls and show literal rows in card text and live previews. When idle close reuses a posted answer, reasoning stays with opening prose on the preview card when both fit, and otherwise follows the answer once. With block and preview streaming on, quoted and list-opened `block` tables after prose post once in tested batches. A fenced example of the table no longer splits the card.

With tables off, a partly accepted fallback or recovery prose card lets later text send without replaying its content. A final whose remainder is rejected whole reports accepted receipts and sends its attachment. Only the idle close keeps that failure bare, so the matching final still sends only the remainder. A thrown close can leave a stale preview visible and unreported. The unchanged post renderer draws authored Markdown tables as grids.

In `block`, the table post names retained prose and tail at close. A later extension, final, block or retry sends only what follows an accepted prose tail, and a later final or block that repeats it names it. A preview that ends the run with no later final or block reports its late post to no caller. Block post receipts carry their image. A recovery card carries only added prose. Receipts list IDs in creation order. After settlement, a new message keeps its equal tail and repeated prefix. An overlapping message boundary can lose or interleave preview text. A retry after a rejected late chunk keeps prose accepted before a soft line break. An accepted converted table repeats on retry. A new row checks the following sentence arrives once. With tables off, idle does not retry the rest. Plain-table early drains repeat preview text. Main's #192482 owns the double tail of a completed card, and this PR keeps that behavior. With tables off, preview-only closes still omit receipts.

## Why this change was made

Feishu's strict schema gains the shared table option and keeps the legacy `markdown.mode` and `markdown.tableMode`. Formatting-aware delivery converts whole logical tables before chunking. Core calls the channel's `beforeSendAttempt` hook before recording a formatted send as started, so recovery can resend after a stop during Feishu's first runtime load. Presentations and reasoning degrade undrawable block-mode tables to readable lists. For `off`, display-only delimiter escaping leaves authored fallback and deduplication text alone. It declares `block` as Feishu's table default.

The generated channel baseline gains two entries, `channels.feishu.markdown.tables` and `channels.feishu.accounts.*.markdown.tables`. The core and plugin counts are main's. This exception is not maintainer approval. The allocation covers 7,153 net test lines for table conversion, chunking, receipts and recovery. The PR leaves the shared scalar alone. Baseline cuts consume headroom.

## Evidence

### Upgrade proof

Published stable `2026.10.2` at `b8952d477f0c` seeded channel `markdown.mode: native` and `markdown.tableMode: ascii`, an account's `mode: escape` and `tableMode: simple`, and two accounts without Markdown settings. Proof head `effbf8c7a8ab` used that state and main `29fc232d40be` a copy, in fresh worktrees with separately packed Feishu plugins.

| Check | Stable | Proof head | Upstream main |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Legacy config validates, keys and overrides read back unchanged | Yes | Yes, before and after migration | Yes, before and after migration |
| Feishu config object on disk | Seed | Byte-identical | Byte-identical |
| Stored session loads with the same key and ID, and a label update survives restart | Created and patched here | Yes | Yes |
| Documented `markdown.tables` at channel and account scope | Rejected, exit 1 | Accepted, all four values | Rejected, exit 1 |
| Account override wins, unset accounts inherit the channel value | Key rejected | Yes | Key rejected |

Both Gateways exit 78 on the schema 24 agent database until `openclaw doctor --fix` migrates it to 26. Repair and shutdown then exit 1 with `ERR_SPAWN_BROKER_UNAVAILABLE`. Both databases stay readable. The cause is undiagnosed. This proves compatibility, not a clean upgrade. Credentials were synthetic, with Feishu accounts and transports disabled. Only the Feishu config object stays byte-identical. Maintenance changed other config. The diff adds no `src/state` change or migration.

### Table default

Upgrade proof at stable `b8952d477f0c` and main `29fc232d40be` resolves `code` for unconfigured and legacy-only accounts, but `auto` routes pipe-bordered tables to raw cards with native grids. Legacy keys do not select the mode. Proof head `effbf8c7a8ab` resolves `block`, retaining those grids. Other modes convert before routing.

Standalone pipe-less and one-sided-pipe tables get cards on `auto` sends and non-streamed replies. In chat text, quoted and list-opened tables take posts. Messages needing multiple static cards also take posts, using `code` unless fences cannot survive the cut. The five-table limit excludes streams. Direct post sends and edits still resolve `code`. Comments convert raw rows to `code`.

A `code` default fences those grids in cards, shown at `outbound.markdown-tables.test.ts:662` in `948b2088919`. `block` also drops "Avoid Markdown tables." from Feishu group prompts, even with account `code` or `bullets`, because `src/auto-reply/reply/groups.ts:126-131` reads the plugin default. Telegram and Matrix already declare `block`. Maintainers decide the default.

### Current repair verification

Hosted CI on `d56ccf17129e` merged with main `0cc3586362cb` passed 79 checks, with 52 skipped and neutral CodeQL. No hosted CI result is claimed for `f1acbc1dfb87`.

Local runs passed 1,533 Feishu tests and the extension type lanes at `d56ccf17129e`, and 272 Feishu database-worker tests and 179 core delivery tests at `cea11348420c`. The generated-file checks passed on `f1acbc1dfb87` with the matching install. Typed lint, formatting and `tsgo:scripts` last passed at `ff39b7bb3adc`. All ten ratchets against `c50ff4fbe541` passed, test-lines with 163 lines of slack. The PR adds 7,153 lines and matching credit. Main's seven #192482 rows pass. Five upstream rows fail with old test setups. Updated rows preserve their assertions.

### Lark before/after rendering

[Comparison and limits](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147886#issuecomment-6093982920) cover four byte-identical synthetic fixture pairs through production send, reply and streaming components with the real SDK. They compare plugin source `e7f29073f4dc` with rendering files published at `34f132a1bb49` and were not retaken at `effbf8c7a8ab`. Later merges retain those rendering files and the off-mode projection. The idle row's settlement bookkeeping changed, so that row rests on regression tests rather than these captures.

| State | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Off-mode presentation | ![Native table despite off mode](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff00b807-a9e6-465b-9f63-5829ea331710) | ![Literal rows and retained button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/96bf5ced-1f4e-4375-985f-cf0a9ab4132f) |
| Off-mode answer preview | ![Native answer-preview table](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e54aec3f-9a7c-41a7-886d-145522b8feed) | ![Literal answer-preview rows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/02c9e642-b5dd-4203-a3cf-87be4de7f7aa) |
| Off-mode reasoning preview | ![Reasoning-table rows missing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/325f6680-67b2-4de6-99f7-a93a0eb9afb1) | ![Reasoning-table rows visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c07ea2c4-df53-4628-9793-8e1946bbf661) |
| Idle reuse of accepted answer | ![Reasoning disappears after idle](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4087a562-8abe-4253-8517-ac947981a16c) | ![One answer and separate reasoning](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/430c18ca-2774-45cc-9055-44da9e169007) |

Both runs exited 0. Idle settlement adds one reasoning-only post and keeps two receipts without replaying the accepted answer. All three dispatcher cases keep byte-identical authored final-post payloads. The captures used no Gateway or mainland Feishu client. Lark still joins adjacent quoted paragraphs in the reasoning preview, not addressed here.

### Historical evidence

Results apply to the named commits.

- CLI at `dbb422c85a5` rejected `tables` with exit 1 and refused Gateway startup with exit 78. At `08c0c469de4`, validation passed, the Gateway reached ready and shut down with child exit 0, and Doctor kept the Markdown keys.
- Gateway send RPC at `314ddb95`, HTTPS Feishu stub, real SDK, `renderMode` unset. Accounts resolved `code`, `bullets` and `off` as configured across full, reply and default-account sends, all exit 0.
- Authority proof at `c311d8a5d53` [comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147886#issuecomment-5707888042), real SDK. Allowed sent four of four with every receipt. Revoked after one of four was accepted, kept its receipt and exact content in the partial-delivery envelope, and the claim guard refused the pending terminal rather than replay it.
- Lark client round at `9d52663f11b` and `d0f6e3a3ba0` [comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/147886#issuecomment-5689525610), real SDK, 62 captures. Blockquote and list-opened tables became readable fenced posts, and a mixed message kept both tables.

prs.title: fix(slack): inherit root action gates in account overrides
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes partial Slack account-level `actions` overrides discarding channel-level restrictions for gates the account did not name.

With this configuration

```json
{
  "channels": {
    "slack": {
      "actions": { "messages": false, "pins": false },
      "accounts": {
        "work": { "botToken": "xoxb-...", "actions": { "reactions": true } }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

`work` resolved to `{ "reactions": true }`. Missing gates default to enabled, so discovery advertised disabled message and pin actions, and the runtime gate let them proceed to later checks. Target policy and API authorization still apply.

## User Impact

Account overrides now change only named gates. `actions: {}` previously reset every gate to enabled and now inherits channel-level gates. Anyone relying on replacement must explicitly enable the desired account gates. Root-only and account-only settings resolve as before.

## Why This Change Was Made

The five-file delta adds `actions` to the nested merge list in `extensions/slack/src/accounts.ts`, three tests and one sentence in `docs/channels/slack/access-control.md`. The schema already accepts partial objects. Both consumers are unchanged.

The docs add a previously undocumented contract. Replacement predates refactor `ff759f991e6f`, but the inspected history establishes neither its introduction nor an intended reset contract. Earlier introduction-date and affected-release-range claims are withdrawn.

## Decision Needed

A maintainer must decide whether partial or empty account `actions` should inherit unset keys or replace the whole block. Acceptance remains pending.

## Evidence

On October 18, head `ec516390d97512019f058caafcda267b35d00317` merged cleanly against main `55ce16b61cd5822f98be360d8297aca7de4353f3` in a merge check. No code changed and no tests were rerun.

Prior evidence records main `2d6f7a3052a0` merged with upstream test deletions retained, 28 tests in 74.17 seconds, changed-file checks in 1103.52 seconds and no actionable review findings through P2. Those records were not independently reconstructed today. [CI 38024921612](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38024921612) passed at the earlier head `ec516390d975`, including `openclaw/ci-gate` and `security-fast`. Its published-driver job was skipped.

### Historical behavior checks

Earlier published results compare `fbae6ae9573f54f1504f40476ee2c9af0a5c635a` with baseline `cf0f8f90a7b6317a5a618ac5d5a7e69e01c050d2`. They were not rerun or independently reconstructed today.

- The account regression expects `work` to resolve to `{ messages: false, pins: false, reactions: true }` and the default account to retain the root object.
- With all root gates false and only account reactions enabled, discovery lists exactly `send`, `react`, and `reactions`.
- The runtime regression rejects `listPins` with "Slack pins are disabled" before any API call, while a `react` control runs.

The recorded baseline failed all three regressions. A discovery-only change left account and runtime checks failing. The runtime test uses a sibling file to respect the line limit.

Built CLI results with the example config and placeholder tokens were

| Check for account `work` | Baseline | Fixed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Capability discovery | exit 0, all 15 actions | exit 0, `send`, `broadcast`, `react`, `reactions`, `member-info`, `emoji-list` |
| `message pins --channel slack --account work` | exit 1, "Slack read target channel is not allowed." | exit 1, "Slack pins are disabled." |
| `message react --channel slack --account work` | exit 1, "Slack read target channel is not allowed." | same exit and error |

The unchanged reaction error proves gate passage, not delivery. The recorded default-account control without an override failed at the pins gate on both builds.

Historical records report 165 focused tests, 170 files/3124 extension tests, 145 files/2739 source tests, and passing type, lint, format, docs and assertion-safety checks, not current-head reruns.

### Supplementary forward upgrade on October 11

At head `ec516390d975` the PR declared `2026.9.9`. October 11's stable baseline was `2026.10.1`. Candidate [`b682ad79204c`](https://github.com/marmar9615-cloud/openclaw/commit/b682ad79204c585b345e1628746679812df81a00) applies the exact five-file delta to published [`2026.10.5-beta.1`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.10.5-beta.1), parent `f283c3c71226c2e1d9ca06b11972f8bdb3969bd8`. This proves release-line integration, not an exact-head forward upgrade. No release or extra PR was published.

[Run 38155906533](https://github.com/marmar9615-cloud/openclaw/actions/runs/38155906533), harness [`53f5600b88877`](https://github.com/marmar9615-cloud/openclaw/blob/53f5600b88877ac7d81610cd5f0b4773a7b6ed0c/proof.mjs), passed 47 checks, 28 tests in 52.040 seconds and changed-file checks in 918.444 seconds. Packaging passed. Source and harness reviews found no actionable P0 through P2 findings.

Both fixtures used published core and official Slack `2026.10.1`, all root gates false, and `work` set to `{ reactions: true }` or `{}`. Normal core plus external Slack retained the `@openclaw/slack@latest` selector. A sealed local registry supplied the matching companion without fabricated ownership.

Captured command and result excerpts are

```text
$ openclaw update --channel beta --tag /app/package/candidate.tgz --yes --no-restart --json
both fixtures exit=0, status="ok", run.status="succeeded"
before.version="2026.10.1", after.version="2026.10.5-beta.1"
slack plugin status="updated", sync.errors=[], integrityDrifts=[]

$ openclaw channels capabilities --channel slack --account work --json --timeout 1000
before update, both fixtures exit=0, all 15 actions
after update, partial exit=0, ["send","broadcast","react","reactions"]
after update, empty exit=0, ["send","broadcast"]
```

Installed core matched `b682ad79204c585b345e1628746679812df81a00`. External Slack loaded at `2026.10.5-beta.1` with matching SHA-512 integrity in both install records. Account actions, `channels.slack`, `gateway` and `plugins` were unchanged. Whole-file equality is false. Only empty webhook migration arrays for `telegram`, `feishu` and `nextcloud-talk`, `agents.entries.main`, `meta.lastTouchedVersion`, `wizard.lastRun*` and requested `update.channel` changed.

No live actions were sent. Offline probes returned expected connection-refused errors. These checks cover update completion and discovery, not live delivery or managed Gateway activation. Restart was skipped. Dummy plaintext credentials caused plugin status `warning`. Automatic database restoration was unavailable because an unknown writer changed databases after capture. Snapshots remained and cleanup was deferred. Rollback, complete data-resource recovery and production health were not proven.

Recorded SHA-256 identities follow. The [transcript, command records, plugin indexes and config snapshots](https://github.com/MarMarLabs/openclaw/actions/runs/38155906533/artifacts/11709788486) expire November 10, 2026.

| Item | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| Exact source delta | `40103994e51b960236893dbede3245cadbc168172524a9dfee6390e2664c80a9` |
| Candidate core | `f4c232fab8b16189ecea85d24fef545bdaab14ec70fba4a0704b646dbb4e76aa` |
| External Slack | `b82815544cd80c9aaa14b87590fb6f33c20419d4632ba11cb607ca839202bc2b` |
| Registry manifest | `ef974ec5c6325aeb58cbd015c71dd45cb6cfdd90f4acca7727dc6910b53e9d80` |

Earlier attempts [38155267259](https://github.com/marmar9615-cloud/openclaw/actions/runs/38155267259) and [38155468679](https://github.com/marmar9615-cloud/openclaw/actions/runs/38155468679) stopped on harness environment problems before updater fixtures ran. The latter had passed the 28 focused tests.

### Exact-head downgrade failed

[Run 38151741290](https://github.com/marmar9615-cloud/openclaw/actions/runs/38151741290) built and installed `ec516390d975`, the PR head on October 11, with `--bundle-plugin slack`. This custom `2026.9.9` package contained matching Slack source, unlike stock core. Its SHA-256 was `8f59b0067b4f6d39b4cf780f9e41c34bab27da713f3644525984357cc290e8d2`.

The baseline used published core `2026.10.1`, commit `e178c39e9aae3fa440735217f9aef9574f286677`, and official Slack `2026.10.1`. Action configs matched the cases above. The update command omitted `--channel beta`. Candidate action lists matched the forward results. Explicit account actions and the Slack, Gateway and plugin sections were preserved.

Both updater fixtures failed with exit 1. This was a downgrade/replacement from `2026.10.1` to `2026.9.9`, not forward-upgrade proof. Installation, candidate checks, startup canary, swap and configuration repair succeeded, but plugin handling reported `Plugin "slack" has no authoritative package-owner metadata`. Backup retention and recovery were unverified, the updater returned `state-migrated-no-rollback`, and a later cleanup import failed. The internal plugin index was not captured, so the deeper cause remains unestablished. Whole-file configuration preservation is not claimed.

These package proofs ran in isolated CI containers without repository or environment secrets or live Slack actions. The [transcript, commands, identities and configs](https://github.com/marmar9615-cloud/openclaw/actions/runs/38151741290/artifacts/11707372026) expire November 10, 2026. The forward result neither erases this failure nor establishes its cause.

prs.title: fix(cli): reject blank channels capabilities selectors
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes `openclaw channels capabilities` treating an explicitly blank selector as omitted, which could widen a channel report or skip a target permission audit.

## User impact

Blank or whitespace-only `--channel`, `--agent`, and `--target` values are rejected with a message naming the flag, consistent with the existing `--account` guard. Omitting selectors preserves the existing defaults. Scripts that pass empty variables must omit those flags when they want the default scope. No configuration migration is required.

Maintainer acceptance of this behavior change remains pending.

## Why this change was made

Capabilities reuses `parseChannelSelector`. Account validation remains at its option parser. The channel, agent and target guards run after config validation and before config persistence, secret resolution, discovery and probes. The selector matrix stays at the command boundary, with one process smoke test for exit 1 and JSON rendering.

Related PRs are #133781 and #136412.

## Evidence

- Merge `6d8c78877700` brings upstream main `8ba4604bb7f2` into `1bc25613973a`. Its only conflict was an import line in `capabilities.test.ts`, after upstream #189993 moved `ExpectedCliError`. The merge removes that unused test import and retains upstream's test trims and fixture changes from #184882. The PR's added and removed lines remain intact, with the production error import updated to upstream's new module.
- At `6d8c78877700`, `capabilities.test.ts` passes 25 of 25 tests, the process file passes 12 of 12, and the existing account-selector boundary file passes 3 of 3. Removing only the production fix makes exactly five blank-selector rows and the blank-channel process case fail. Both omission controls still pass. The process case observes exit 1 and the expected JSON error with the fix, and exit 0 without it.
- Local formatting, typed lint, production types and CI's test type route pass at `6d8c78877700`. Deliberate type errors in the production file and both changed test files fail their checks, which pass again after restoring the files with matching hashes. All 10 baseline ratchets pass against `8ba4604bb7f2`. Three isolated doctor test files still fail, each on the same case and assertion on both the merge and plain `8ba4604bb7f2`. The full commands project was not rerun. These are local results, not hosted CI results for this merge.
- The [built-CLI transcript](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/137233#issuecomment-6111025779) records ten blank or whitespace rejection cases and four omission controls passing on the installed `2026.9.9` package built from `451a32c657fb1ac7f2fc167294f364c93819decf`. It covers channel, agent, target with and without a channel, and the existing account guard. Slack and Discord came from the same source commit. This transcript was not recorded again at `6d8c78877700`.
- The [secretless selector job](https://github.com/MarMarLabs/openclaw/actions/runs/38151741290/job/114506439272) passed using product source `451a32c657fb` and workflow commit `4097d60eff0f`. The transcript links the [artifact](https://github.com/MarMarLabs/openclaw/actions/runs/38151741290/artifacts/11707550779) for the recorded commands, outputs and package identities. Capability commands ran offline. Expected health-probe errors do not prove live connectivity. The workflow's separate PR #137250 job failed.
- [Upstream CI run 38031072863](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38031072863) succeeded at `451a32c657fb`. It is historical evidence for that commit. No hosted CI result is claimed for the merge `6d8c78877700`.

Earlier merges and validation are historical. The October 18 merge `283fe6fdedb` brought in main `55ce16b61cd`. Earlier published validation records seven failing command regressions on `cf0f8f90a7b6317a5a618ac5d5a7e69e01c050d2`, followed by 26 passes at `19d8f01de3a0f3d1d1f57306dce151485defad29`. The earlier description also reported a local environment-variable budget failure of 456 versus 455. Those older measurements were not rerun or independently reconstructed for this update.

prs.title: fix(update): keep restored npm packages readable by non-root services
prs.body:
Related: #175423, #175449, #170032. cc @steipete for information.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a failed update makes a root-owned global npm installation unreadable to a non-root systemd service, preventing the old version from starting after rollback.

## User Impact

Rollback preserves npm package read/execute permissions (0755 directories and executables, 0644 regular files), so a service running as another OS user can still launch the restored package. Private activation anchors, controls, helpers, and journals remain owner-only. This does not change service lifecycle or state ownership.

## Why This Change Was Made

#175423 targeted private activation objects affected by recursive POSIX ACLs. #175449 extended permission repair to retained package trees; its body explicitly notes that the copy path preserves npm's original public modes. The #170032 diagnosis also explicitly preserves another account's read access to the installed package. Applying the private-object `0o077` rule to package content turned normal 0755/0644 npm files into 0700/0600.

The integrity owner now repairs only group/other WRITE (`0o022`), including write grants controlled by POSIX ACL masks, preserving read/execute. Package fingerprint encoding and historical receipt matching are unchanged: permission-only drift still permits recovery; changed bytes, identity, ownership, owner permissions, and symlink targets still refuse it. The existing no-follow, descriptor-checked repair and private-object permission rule are unchanged. Old full-mode-only receipts retain their existing compatibility behavior.

## Evidence

- Focused retain → restore regression is red with main's original permission policy: observed `[0700,0700,0600,0700]` instead of `[0755,0755,0644,0755]` on the retained package. It passes with this fix (846 ms test time).
- Focused permission/publication/private-object tests: **16 passed**, one Linux ACL test platform-skipped on macOS (19 unrelated boundary cases deselected). Private anchors/controls repair to 0700; journals/helpers to 0600. Includes write-only drift, shared-inode deduplication, old public-mode receipts, changed-content refusal, and filesystem-repair warnings. Wrapper wall time 36.34 s, mostly existing worker preparation; CI seconds not yet available.
- Targeted oxfmt and oxlint passed. Test growth is 38 lines, allocated for the retain/restore regression and revised write-only permission assertions. Production growth is two lines; no new permission owner or repair path.
- Initial CI found one stale legacy-consumer expectation that ordinary public package modes emit a repair warning. That expectation is corrected; its focused three-case link-count run passed (213 ms test time; 46.72 s wrapper wall time including compilation).
- Retained real-systemd baseline: main predecessor `d755a99495e79c0b98ae1ad612511889097b259f` → frozen target `c84048f70d1deea59736c030584708e38ea57b10`, root-owned global npm install, umask 022, `User=openclaw`. Natural post-activation Doctor failure rolled back the old package; all five sampled objects changed 755 → 700 root:root. `runuser -u openclaw -- node .../openclaw.mjs --version` exited 1, and an actual systemd restart ended `ActiveState=failed`, `MainPID=0`, `Result=exit-code`, `/readyz=false`. This is retained production-path evidence, not a new execution of today's main.

- Fixed real-systemd run: built this branch's fixed source on main base `b99ed97b8f8f` with `pnpm build:package` and the canonical self-contained Docker packer through pueue. The build began before the commit, so embedded build metadata names that base; the source is the production patch in this PR. Package SHA-256: `521332c51f5c51e9b14ab08c4665bbe2de5b9ba02964792fb653ea1b74351d9e`. Reused the same frozen target and existing systemd harness, umask 022, a root-owned global install, and `User=openclaw`; no product tracing or permission intervention.
  - A real `openclaw update --tag /inputs/target.tgz --yes --json --timeout 600` staged and swapped successfully, then returned `doctor-failed` because the existing Gateway lease prevented post-activation maintenance. `package-rollback` exited 0 and restored 2026.10.10.
  - Post-rollback `runuser -u openclaw -- node .../openclaw.mjs --version` exited **0**. An actual systemd restart became **active/running**, `Result=success`, `/readyz=true`. Readiness was false before that explicit restart: this proves restartability, not a service-lifecycle fix or automatic recovery.
  - One task-owned container ran, then was removed. No daemon restart or unrelated container changes.

`stat -c '%a %U:%G %n'` at the package boundaries:

| Object under `/usr/local/lib/node_modules/openclaw` | Main predecessor: before → rollback | Fixed source: before → rollback |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.` | 755 → **700** root:root | 755 → **755** root:root |
| `dist/` | 755 → **700** root:root | 755 → **755** root:root |
| `openclaw.mjs` | 755 → **700** root:root | 755 → **755** root:root |
| `node_modules/` | 755 → **700** root:root | 755 → **755** root:root |
| `dist/index.js` | 755 → **700** root:root | 755 → **755** root:root |

The retained main baseline failed later at `Client credential directory is unsafe`; today's fixed-source run refused the still-live owner lease earlier in Doctor. Both executed real publication and successful package rollback. These are intentionally not claims that the lifecycle/ownership defects are fixed here.

### CI baseline limitation

The [initial exact-head CI run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41985858481) failed its [test-lines ratchet](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41985858481/job/127106899231): total 6,481,936, ceiling 6,481,907, net +42. The PR allocated precisely those 42 lines; removing the PR delta and allocation gives base total 6,481,894 versus base ceiling 6,481,865, an inherited **29-line deficit**. The corrected consumer test reduces this PR's net growth and allocation together to +38; it does not pay unrelated baseline debt or raise the shared scalar.

prs.title: fix(android): show Claude CLI history tools under their OpenClaw names
prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/193267

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: in the Android chat, a Claude CLI session reloaded from history shows OpenClaw tool calls under their raw loopback MCP bridge names, so an `exec` call is a generic plugin row titled "Mcp Openclaw Exec · ls docs" instead of the exec command row. This is the Android side of https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/192360, which https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192361 fixed for the Control UI and the Gateway's CLI runner.

## User Impact

User impact: on Android, OpenClaw tools that a Claude CLI backend called through the MCP bridge show in history under their OpenClaw names, with their own rows (for `exec`, the terminal row `$ ls docs`), as in the Control UI.

## Why This Change Was Made

`chat.history` keeps the tool name Claude CLI recorded, `mcp__openclaw__exec`. The Gateway's prepared activity summary already says `exec`, but the Android app builds the expanded tool rows from the message's tool call, and `unwrapToolCallForDisplay` in `ToolDisplayCall.kt` passed the name through, so the row matched no known tool and was titled from the raw name.

`unwrapToolCallForDisplay` now strips the two OpenClaw bridge prefixes (`mcp__openclaw__`, and Gemini CLI's `mcp_openclaw_`) before its dispatcher unwrap, the same rule and order as `stripOpenClawMcpToolPrefix` in `src/agents/tool-display-call.ts` from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192361. Both Android callers (message parsing in `ChatController` and the timeline's tool projection) go through it. Tools of other MCP servers keep their names, as in that TypeScript rule. Display only: the call's identity and results are unchanged. The browser-tab and web source-preview checks still read the raw name, as the Control UI's do after that fix.

## Evidence

Tested at `6e962adefd5` (base `upstream/main` `94bea34ae99`); the device run used an APK built just before a wording change to one code comment, with the same code.

Both sides ran the Android debug app (play flavor) on an Android 16 emulator, paired with an isolated Gateway: own home, state and config, a loopback port, no provider variable (so no provider calls), its runtime started from this branch's checkout, which changes only `apps/android`. Its main session is bound to a synthetic Claude CLI transcript with one `mcp__openclaw__exec` call (`ls docs`) and its result. One script drove both sides; only the installed APK differed. It opens the session, expands "Worked for 3s", then "Tool activity". Nothing was mocked.

| Expect | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| the Claude CLI turn is open (control) | met | met |
| the activity summary says Exec (control, from the Gateway) | met | met |
| no expanded row shows the raw bridge name | **not met** ("Mcp Openclaw Exec · ls docs") | met |
| the expanded row is the exec command row (`$ ls docs`) | **not met** | met |

![Tool activity expanded. Before: a generic plugin row titled Mcp Openclaw Exec · ls docs. After: the exec command row $ ls docs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/masatohoshino/openclaw/proof-assets/20261105-192361-android-mcp-bridge-tool-names/2-rows.png)

Observed result: on the base the expanded row is titled from the raw bridge name with a generic icon; with the fix it is the exec command row.

"1 tool outcome unknown" shows on both sides: the Gateway's prepared activity reports the CLI result without an exit status. That is Gateway behavior, outside this change.

Checks, through Gradle: the new test `ChatMessageContentParsingTest.claudeCliHistoryShowsBridgedOpenClawToolsAsTheCalledTool` (Claude and Gemini prefixes, a prefixed `tool_call` dispatcher, and another MCP server's tool that keeps its name) fails on the base (`expected:<[]exec> but was:<[mcp__openclaw__]exec>`) and passes with the fix; it is a plain JUnit test of the parser (about 1 ms, no Robolectric). `./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.chat.*' --tests 'ai.openclaw.app.ui.chat.*'`: 1483 passed, 0 failed; `./gradlew :app:ktlintCheck` passes. The test-lines ratchet passes (it counts TypeScript tests only; main is at its ceiling with no slack).

Not covered: an emulator and a synthetic transcript only; no live Claude CLI or Gemini CLI run. The Gemini prefix is covered by the unit test, not on a device.

prs.title: feat(cli): create the shared state database before the first Gateway start
prs.body:
Related: #167545

Draft proposal awaiting the design answer in the linked issue. It adds a public CLI contract on the state database and should not merge before that answer. I am happy to rework it toward the preferred interface.

## What Problem This Solves

A container image that provisions the operator's own devices before first start has no command that only creates the shared state database. Doctor against the retired `devices/paired.json` format covers the approval workflow today, but also repairs config and other state.

## User Impact

Operators can run `openclaw database init --json` to initialize absent, empty, or recognized native-bootstrap state and get its path, schema version, and `created`/`found` status. Repeating the command preserves current database contents. Older, newer, or incompatible mature state is refused with repair/version guidance and exit status 1.

The command only creates storage. It does not make direct approval-row writes a supported interface; `devices approve` still needs a pending request. Doctor remains the supported offline import route. The design question is whether storage initialization alone is useful enough to add, or whether a supported offline approval command is preferable.

Leave the database path absent for a new installation. A file that already exists, even empty or partly initialized, follows the Gateway's existing-state policy and lacks the Doctor-owned deletion-history table. State selection uses the process environment and `--profile`; the database command does not load dotenv files.

## Why This Change Was Made

`database` already owns the schema and write-ownership commands, so the subcommand lives there and loads the state module only in its action. It goes through the opener the Gateway uses, with one new internal flag: when the file already holds mature state, the opener validates it and returns before the writable setup and schema convergence an ordinary open performs. Fresh state takes the existing bootstrap path, so the result is the database an ordinary open would have created. The command closes its own handle and does not record migration completion, change config or workspaces, issue credentials, or start a Gateway or plugin runtime.

I did not build it on `withOpenClawStateStartupMigrationCheckpointDatabase`, which also creates a fresh database: on older state that path can add its checkpoint tables or indexes before the caller sees anything, and this command has to refuse older state untouched. With schema version 19 and the lease-owner index removed:

```text
[checkpoint-connection] bytes identical: false; idx_state_leases_owner present after: 1; user_version: 19
[init] bytes identical: true; idx_state_leases_owner present after: 0; user_version: 19
```

The verb follows `openclaw storage init`: create when absent, verify when present. Two simultaneous initializers may both return `created`; schema changes remain serialized by the existing maintenance owner.

No schema or version bump, dependency, SDK export, Gateway startup change, or changelog edit. The main risk is the new public operator contract on database admission, which awaits the linked design decision. Updates retain the existing Doctor migration path; this command refuses mature state that needs migration.

## Evidence

A real Gateway built from this change accepted the synthetic approved device on its first connection after either Doctor or initialization plus a direct test insert. All scenarios used the same signed `cli`/`cli` client, `operator.read`, loopback token authentication, and `autoApproveLocal: false`.

The initializer scenario inserts one approval row directly after `init`, because `devices approve` needs a pending request. That insert is test setup, not something this PR proposes to support. Today's behaviour on main uses the same build with unchanged Gateway and pairing code, a legacy file, and no Doctor or initializer. It differs in two inputs, so it does not isolate the command.

<details>
<summary>First connections and shutdowns, verbatim</summary>

```text
{"scenario":"doctor","firstConnection":{"accepted":true,"protocol":4,"scopes":["operator.read"],"attempts":1}}
{"scenario":"doctor","gatewayExit":0}
{"scenario":"init","firstConnection":{"accepted":true,"protocol":4,"scopes":["operator.read"],"attempts":1}}
{"scenario":"init","gatewayExit":0}
{"scenario":"todays-behaviour-on-main","firstConnection":{"accepted":false,"name":"GatewayClientRequestError","code":"NOT_PAIRED","message":"device pairing required (requestId: ef385870-402e-444f-9705-f22f5ca98d7a)","attempts":1}}
{"scenario":"todays-behaviour-on-main","gatewayExit":0}
```

All three Gateway logs show `startup.maintenance.pairing` completing:

```text
2026-10-09T03:54:01.706+03:00 [gateway] startup trace: startup.maintenance.pairing 8.5ms total=7101.1ms eventLoopMax=0.0ms
2026-10-09T03:54:09.115+03:00 [gateway] startup trace: startup.maintenance.pairing 9.4ms total=5778.4ms eventLoopMax=0.0ms
2026-10-09T03:54:14.884+03:00 [gateway] startup trace: startup.maintenance.pairing 5.5ms total=4953.9ms eventLoopMax=0.0ms
```

</details>

The initializer created 101 tables, with only the `primary` row in `schema_meta`. A second run returned `found` and preserved database and config bytes. Also run through the built CLI: zero-byte initialization; `--profile` path selection; older, newer, incompatible, and externally owned database refusal with exit 1 and byte-identical preserved databases.

The supported alternative was measured on the same fresh directory, reset to the same inputs before each command:

| Command | Run | Wall | User CPU | System CPU | Total CPU |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `doctor --fix --non-interactive` | 1 | 6.58 s | 4.88 s | 1.38 s | 6.26 s |
| `database init --json` | 1 | 0.63 s | 0.67 s | 0.13 s | 0.80 s |
| `doctor --fix --non-interactive` | 2 | 5.85 s | 4.93 s | 1.50 s | 6.43 s |
| `database init --json` | 2 | 0.58 s | 0.68 s | 0.13 s | 0.81 s |
| `doctor --fix --non-interactive` | 3 | 4.70 s | 4.29 s | 1.16 s | 5.45 s |
| `database init --json` | 3 | 0.60 s | 0.68 s | 0.13 s | 0.81 s |

Doctor's five-to-seven-second cost is modest. It imported the approval, archived the retired file, changed config, created backups and a recovery capture, and left rows in nine tables plus temporary lease activity. The initializer took about 0.6 seconds, created only the database file, and left config and the legacy file unchanged. It does not import or approve the device. Neither route left `state-migrations` or `startup-migrations` rows; Doctor additionally wrote its shared-auth migration ledger. The official container entrypoint already runs Doctor, which weakens the case for another command solely for this workflow.

Bundled plugins were disabled. Doctor exited 0, but this structured-health warning limits the health-check evidence:

```text
│  doctor:structured-health-repairs run failed: Unable to resolve bundled  │
│  plugin public surface memory-core/doctor-health-api.js                  │
```

Focused tests exercise real database admission, native-bootstrap row preservation, ordinary-opener equivalence, and refusal without changing existing bytes. They cannot pass on `b2d00be5`, where the new function does not exist.

| Test file | Tests | Sum of case durations | `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` wall time |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `src/state/openclaw-state-db-init.test.ts` | 8 | 0.373 s | 8.40 s |

The file uses one template for five mature-state cases, reducing full schema creations to four including native-bootstrap coverage. The 0.373-second sum is below the under-five-second target. Byte-preservation assertions use byte equality instead of deep object comparison. About 3.8 seconds of wall time was compiled-worker preparation and cache validation. No Gateway boots, timers, polling, or worker configuration were added. CI seconds are pending.

The unchanged startup-preflight availability suite also passed: 5 tests, 9.260 seconds summed case time, 28.85 seconds wall time.

- `pnpm build` exited 0; the Gateway runs used that build. It printed an existing startup-JavaScript size advisory.
- `pnpm check:docs`, lint on the changed files, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Broader checks are not green. The last `pnpm check` passed guards and typechecks, then stopped at ten `max-lines` errors in untouched files; those same ten reproduce on `b2d00be5` without this change.
- The last `pnpm check:changed` passed formatting, guards, and typechecks, then failed the unused-export scan on `ClientVoiceToolEffect` in `src/talk/client-voice-session-store.ts`, also reproduced on `b2d00be5`. These broader checks have not been rerun for this final revision.
- Independent review of the final revision and CI are pending before this draft is ready to merge.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Turning on OpenClaw ID currently leaves service configuration incomplete, while accounts outside the private preview receive generic setup failures.

## User Impact

Enabling the Labs switch supplies the staging services, and accounts that Discovery has not enabled see a clear message with their email and a sign-out option instead of starting setup. Existing claws and invited members retain their access. Explicit service settings still win; the flag remains off by default and inert while off.

**Stacked on #192352. Keep this draft unmerged until the Gateway stack has landed and the Discovery preview gate has been deployed.** No live Gateway or staging configuration was changed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Discovery remains the policy owner. The Gateway checks `/v1/access` before recording the signed-in account, preserves `preview_access_required` from gated calls, and retains the explicitly supported 404 behavior for older Discovery. The UI consumes that result and labels the built-in environment as staging. Name checks use the freshly acquired enrollment code directly rather than reading a deferred Solid signal. If access is removed after local ownership commits, the dialog preserves that linked result, explains that remote registration failed, and documents how to retry registration with the saved binding after access is restored.

## Evidence

### Rebased checkpoint — November 6

- Head `2e75ab86bc67b0955afb38ecce051e638cb9b883` is rebased onto #192352 at `9977465a40a99ccc7ea11fa7b8a8c7d80c32e9ba`. The stack was rewritten again during validation, so the candidate was rebased a second time and checked again. The **Access** sidebar label, **Remote access** title, `access` page ID, and existing internal People names are preserved.
- The first rebase conflicted in three files: experimental-features docs now combine staging-default instructions with upstream Access copy; config baseline hashes were regenerated; the setup dialog combines preview-refusal handling with upstream feature-lifetime, signer-custody, and single-preparation guards. The second rebase conflicted only in the config hashes, which were regenerated again.
- Range-diff inspection found **identical added/removed source and test lines** in the preview patch before and after rebasing. Only documentation context and regenerated hashes differ. No new behavior was introduced during conflict resolution, so no additional independent review was needed.
- Scoped Gateway, config, UI, Access/People, and browser-form suites: **375 passed / 10 skipped** in 152.5s. The skips are unchanged native-iroh-dependent tunnel-child cases.

- `tsgo:ui`, i18n baseline/verification, test-line and source-line ratchets, config-doc generation/check, docs config examples, docs links, changed-doc MDX, focused lint on all 21 source files, formatting and whitespace checks passed. Focused lint retains one non-failing warning on the existing `queueMicrotask` initialization pattern.
- The full changed-file gate was not repeated for this source-patch-identical rebase; its older results and original review scope are retained below, not asserted as fresh checks of the new base.

### Original implementation evidence (before rebase)

- Scoped Gateway, configuration, Control UI, People, and browser-form suites: **362 passed**, with **8 existing tunnel-child tests skipped**.
- Real Chromium account-menu E2E: **2 passed**. The denied fixture has no link action or authority request. Synthetic before/after screenshots were inspected.
- Test-line and source-line ratchets pass; no lint suppressions or dependency changes were added.
- The full changed-file gate completed: core/UI/test typechecks, formatting, docs, i18n, controller checks, and most guards passed. New test-lint violations were repaired; all **21 changed source files now pass focused lint** and the **28 affected tests pass again**. The initial post-commit denial finding was fixed and verified by the second review. Its only remaining finding—a missing `claws.` prefix in the recovery documentation—was corrected against the canonical URL builder; runtime source and tests are unchanged from that second review. prs.title: feat(openclaw-id): define accountless node enrollment
prs.body:
Related: #192352

## What Problem This Solves

Headless nodes need an accountless, owner-approved identity and bootstrap contract before they can reach a claw through the OpenClaw ID relay and tunnel.

## User Impact

This draft defines the protocol layer only; it does not yet enable node connectivity in the running product. Nodes get a separate W-only key class, never owner or member privileges. All changes revise the unshipped v1-draft in place.

**Stack dependency:** this targets `openclaw-id/pr-ui-people`. Gateway, Discovery and node-host consumers follow in the implementation stack. A minimal existing Gateway consumer repair refuses accountless member-redemption mail with `audience_mismatch` through the normal settlement/acknowledgment path; valid member handling is unchanged. Test fixtures initialize the new empty draft state and preserve their concrete human-sender types. Full node dispatch, persisted-state initialization and snapshot re-signing remain in the following stack, without adding legacy compatibility readers here.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Owner-signed `NodeInviteCap` plus a proof key registers directly at the Gateway. W-signed `NodeRedemption` proves the invite and becomes pending, admitting nothing.
- Owner/R-signed `add_node` and `remove_node`, denial and peer revocation use the existing membership authority. Nodes have listing seqs, limits, inactivity clocks and pairing-cleanup events; snapshots carry `node_peer_keys`.
- W-signed bearerless Discovery requests can only mail a node redemption before admission; verified admitted nodes can read the descriptor and snapshot. Relay admission includes the new snapshot list.
- Strict fragment-only join links contain only the invite and claw pin/routing fields. `--discovery-url` (or deployment configuration) supplies the separate Discovery origin; clients never infer it from the hostname/relay and never weaken pin verification.

The simplification pass reused owner verification, sequences, invite proof-key derivation, retention, strict schema combinators and signature transport. Node-specific lifetime enforcement leaves member policy unchanged. This remains a protocol stage: Gateway/UI/runtime enforcement follows in the stack.

The owner-reviewed flow now includes a shared six-digit `nodeVerificationCode` bound to the claw, invite, W and signed `NodeDescription`. The terminal and dialog show the same code; the owner compares it and explicitly clicks Approve. Opening the dialog never approves automatically. The signed description declares display name, platform, commands and caps under strict size/count limits; it is retained with pending and approved nodes, but is not standalone authority. First-connect command/capability auto-approval is bounded to subsets of what the owner approved; additions use normal capability approval. Node invite creators default to 10 minutes; registration enforces a strict one-hour maximum.

## Evidence

- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`: independent physical worktree install passed; donor checkout unchanged.
- `pnpm test packages/openclaw-id-protocol --maxWorkers=1`: **169 tests / 25 files passed** after the owner-approval UX additions (4.03s Vitest, 7.38s wrapper).
- Targeted strict tsgo of the protocol public barrel and affected protocol tests, plus canonical `pnpm tsgo:core`: passed.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json packages/openclaw-id-protocol/src`: passed, 67 files.
- Package-config boundary lint also passed (66 files) after successful declaration emission; the original Gateway consumer type error is resolved.
- Package format check, docs MDX check, changed-source line-cap ratchet and staged whitespace check: passed.
- Test-line allocation: 565 = original 436 + exactly 40 mailbox regression lines + exactly 89 net description/code/lifetime test lines. Two fixture initialization lines use existing slack; the shared scalar is unchanged. The allocation protects forgery/class-separation and bootstrap boundaries, not test-volume growth for its own sake.
- Existing claw-store and member-profile persistence tests: 8 tests / 2 files passed (89.99s Vitest including 67.5s one-time worker preparation; 96.21s wrapper).
- Mailbox reader: 6 tests passed; new regression failed before the guard and passed after it. Existing callback/acknowledgment tests remain green. Final run: 86.19s Vitest including 80.55s one-time worker preparation, 94.02s wrapper; regression itself 7ms. CI timing is not yet available.
- Deterministic v1-draft JSON regenerated from the vector builder; fixtures test byte-for-byte agreement.
- Independent read-only review found one P2 (Discovery origin absent from link bootstrap). Verified and resolved through the explicit configured-origin/default-and-override contract, preserving the requested link fields. No other verified P0–P2 findings in the original review. A follow-up review of the small consumer repair completed but its result was unavailable; publication proceeds with coordinator approval on the original review and passing affected checks.

Fresh independent read-only review of the UX delta found no verified P0–P2 findings and independently reproduced code vector `168017`. Canonical production types and strict package types (including tests), lint, format, MDX, line caps, test allocation and whitespace checks passed.

Protocol boundary coverage includes forged/wrong-key and mailbox approval refusal, pending-only redemption, owner capability/sequence checks, node/human key separation in both directions, limits, denial, removal events, revocation replay, inactivity, strict links and W-signed request path binding. Deployed Gateway/Discovery enforcement and real tunnel traffic remain named integration gates for the following stack, not claims made by these tests.

Stack conflict repair: rebased onto `90a2c765e10799dce65c5cffc2539b878a46f71a`, preserving both the base’s signed `protocols` and this change’s `node_peer_keys` snapshot fields. Regenerated deterministic vectors; protocol suite, canonical production typecheck, test-line ratchet and whitespace checks passed again. The range-diff contains only the combined snapshot schema context and regenerated signatures.


Combined independent Astra review at `30d3f15ac8bec96419d9641ffb76a587de3ded41`: **no verified P0–P2 findings**. This closes the earlier missing-review gap by covering the accountless member-mail refusal together with all UX additions. Source inspection traced refusal settlement, subsequent-message processing, acknowledgment and cursor persistence; human redemption behavior is unchanged. The reviewer also independently reproduced code `168017`. Existing passing test/type/lint evidence was reused, not rerun by the reviewer. No code changes were required.


Vendor portability follow-up at `84d94f697987e0ed145f7edb3be0edd257080d59`: replaced `URLSearchParams.keys()` iteration with `forEach` pair counting; the existing exactly-once known-field checks still reject duplicates and unknown keys. Added `tsconfig.portable.json` and its documented command, checking package source with ES2023 + DOM and no Node ambient types or DOM.Iterable. ES2022 alone fails on pre-existing Array.toSorted usage; no unrelated array behavior was changed. The local compiler includes iterable DOM declarations, so Discovery/loader vendor builds remain the final consumer-compiler gate. All 169 protocol tests, portable types, focused lint, 7-file MDX check, format, source line cap and whitespace checks passed. Independent Astra review found no verified P0–P2 findings and confirmed equivalent parser guards across 43 cases. Test allocation remains 565 (no new test lines).


### November 6 stack rebase

Replayed only the three owned protocol/UX/portability commits onto rewritten base `8f6b45814afd1a3aa6b241a4908ec6c0d7b6504a`. New head: `5eb5e40cdfa31e691fae575a1bd792bc3d9c1758`. Retained the base RootReset types, strict validation, verifier and vectors alongside the node contracts; snapshots retain both protocols and node_peer_keys. Regenerated signed fixtures with buildStatementVectors. Protocol suite: **187 tests / 26 files passed**; portable typecheck and `pnpm tsgo:core` passed. Focused lint, seven-file MDX check, formatting and whitespace checks passed. Independent Astra conflict-resolution review found no verified P0–P2 findings and verified preservation of base reset/pin vectors and original feature vectors. Pushed using an exact expected-head lease on `84d94f697987e0ed145f7edb3be0edd257080d59`. No downstream branches changed.

prs.title: feat(openclaw-id): add the Control UI account menu, linking dialogs and the Access page
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

With the Gateway parts in place, an owner still needs a way to use OpenClaw ID from the Control UI: sign in, turn on remote access for a claw, keep the recovery kit, approve their other browsers, and invite and manage people. This PR adds those Control UI surfaces and the bundled Access plugin.

## User Impact

No user-visible change while the `gateway.openclawId.enabled` Labs switch is off (the default): the account menu, dialogs, the Labs entry's dependent surfaces, the `gateway.openclawId` settings, the Access page and its plugin catalog entry, grants and asset routes are all absent.

With the switch on, owners get:

- **Account menu** (sidebar avatar): Sign in with OpenClaw ID, Turn on remote access, Your devices, Copy claw link, Sign out of OpenClaw ID, depending on the connection and setup state. Members see their own account and role, and no Access or setup actions.
- **Turn on remote access**: choose a claw name, create and save the recovery kit (download, print, or save to 1Password), then link. Each linking step reports its own progress and failure.
- **Owner approval**: approve a new owner browser from an existing one with a short authentication string (SAS) check.
- **Your devices**: list approved owner browsers and remove one; the confirmation names that device and any devices removed with it.
- **Access** page (bundled `openclaw-id-access` plugin, under Pages, titled Remote access): who may reach this claw through OpenClaw ID. Its People section invites by email, approves or denies requests, shows members' devices and activity, and removes members. A one-line pointer sends readers to Settings → Devices for devices paired with the Gateway.

There is no owner reset in this version; the docs say so.

## Why This Change Was Made

Builds on the Gateway core PR (#192335) and the tunnel and sign-in PR (#192345), both merged. It is the last PR of the Gateway split of the OpenClaw ID stack.

- `ui/src/lib/openclaw-id/**`: browser-side account storage and sign-in popup, link ceremony steps, recovery-kit export, owner device keys (non-extractable WebCrypto Ed25519 in IndexedDB), owner-approval SAS, device mail and remote sign-out.
- Your devices signs each revocation with the claw id and the seq it last read (#193146), so it covers only the listing on screen; a device approved again since is refused as a concurrent change, and the dialog refreshes.
- `ui/src/components/openclaw-id/**`: the account menu, Make reachable, recovery kit, owner approval and Your devices dialogs, with the Control UI's existing menu and modal components.
- Sidebar and settings: an optional, feature-owned extension of the identity menu (`app-sidebar-identity-menu.tsx`), the Labs registry entry, and `gateway.openclawId` hidden from settings search and the config form while the switch is off.
- `extensions/openclaw-id-access/**`: the Access page (display name "OpenClaw ID remote access"), a bundled plugin enabled by default whose Control UI module loads only while the switch is on.
- Gateway: the Control UI document carries a public `data-openclaw-id-enabled` attribute only when the switch is on; the plugin catalog, tab grants, asset routes and managed-plugin list hide `openclaw-id-access` while it is off, and a switch change broadcasts `plugins.controlUi.changed`.
- New dependency: `@1password/save-button` 1.3.0 in `ui` (the recovery kit's Save in 1Password button).
- Config surface: the plugin config baseline grows from 4,997 to 5,018 entries for the new bundled plugin (`docs/.generated/config-baseline.counts.json`). The `gateway.openclawId` core keys landed with the earlier PRs.
- Docs: `docs/concepts/experimental-features.md` (OpenClaw ID remote access) and the plugin reference and inventory.

<details><summary>Notes for review</summary>

- The account menu conflicted with `main`'s fix that keeps the profile avatar element stable (#189747). The OpenClaw ID initial is rendered inside that stable avatar instead of replacing it.
- Type assertions in the new browser code either carry `// SAFETY:` comments or were removed (`stepOfKind` in the Make reachable dialog, the role select on the Access page).
- Exports that focused tests use but production does not import have Knip production-scan entries; the full-tree scan still checks them.

</details>

## Review

An independent review (GPT-6 Astra) found three issues; all are fixed here:

- Two overlapping "Create recovery kit" requests could show one kit while another root signed the link, leaving a kit that cannot recover the claw. Overlapping requests now share one kit (regression test in `link.test.ts`).
- The config editor removed the `gateway.openclawId` settings even with the switch on, because it filtered the schema a second time without the flag.
- The owner-approval toast could open its dialog after the switch turned off. It now checks whether the feature is still on.

Later changes on this branch:

- `people-error.test.ts` builds its credentialed-URL fixture at runtime (`new URL` with `username`/`password`), so the diff holds no `user:password@` literal for secret scanners. The test still checks that such a URL is stripped from diagnostics.
- `docs/concepts/experimental-features.md`: `clientId` is listed with the settings needed to turn on remote access, not as optional. The account menu offers Turn on remote access only after OpenClaw ID sign-in, which needs `clientId` (ClawSweeper P3).
- Access page actions reach the Gateway authority from #192335, which decides access; the page grants nothing itself. Invites must be signed by a current owner device (`service.invites.test.ts`: registration is refused over the mailbox or from an unidentified client); `openclawId.people` and the authority actions refuse viewers, operators, LAN clients and expired owner devices (`people-access.test.ts`).
- Rebased onto #192345 and `main` at `258d034391a`. `main` dropped per-row Documentation links from Labs (#191418), so the OpenClaw ID Labs row no longer has one and the off-state e2e no longer expects it.

- Rebased onto `main` at `49f8a60f227`. `main` now requires an explicit toast `severity` (#192453), so the OpenClaw ID toasts set one: errors are `error`, sign-in and link copy are `success`, the reachability offer and approval notice are `info`, and partial sign-out is `warning`. Labs labels follow `main`'s renames.
- The raw config editor's schema filter is now a named helper, `omitEditorOwnedConfigLeaves`, so `config/view.tsx` stays within the 700-line cap.


A second independent review (GPT-6 Astra) found one P1 and three P2s; all are fixed here. Each fix has a regression test, and each test fails with its fix reverted:

- **One recovery kit per preparation (P1).** Pressing Continue twice in Turn on remote access could start two preparations, save one recovery kit and link with the other. A second press now does nothing while one preparation runs, and a late answer cannot send the dialog back to a step that makes another kit (`make-reachable-dialog.tsx`).
- **The first owner device key is stored before linking (P2).** The browser now keeps its non-extractable owner key before the link is committed, so a link never names a device key the browser has lost. If two tabs race, the first key stored wins (`make-reachable-dialog.tsx`, `device-key.ts`).
- **Key storage is reported only after IndexedDB commits (P2).** Success waits for the transaction's `complete` event, so an aborted write is reported as a failure (`device-key.ts`).
- **Dialogs close when the Labs switch turns off (P2).** Turn on remote access, owner approval, Your devices and their notifications close when the switch turns off, and the recovery kit is discarded on close (`feature-lifetime.ts`).

Repository guards found three more issues, also fixed: sign-in and recovery-kit print windows now open through the Control UI's opener-free window helpers, the owner-approval handoff is typed as JSON instead of using a chained type assertion, and a device-key test mock documents why it does not keep the module's real exports.

- Screenshots for this PR showed the claw name title and hint in Turn on remote access running together: `SettingsRow`'s styles load only with the Settings pages, and the dialog opens from the account menu on any page. The dialog now imports them (`make-reachable-dialog.tsx`).
- Rebased onto `main` at `5310c71fb32` (now `9977465`), because `main` changed the config baseline and the PR conflicted on its generated hash file. That hash was regenerated; every other file's change is unchanged.
- **People page renamed to Access** (`9977465`, first pushed as `761915c`, at Josh's request): the sidebar entry is **Access**, and the page title and heading are **Remote access**. The page and route id is now `access` (`plugin?plugin=openclaw-id-access&id=access`) and the plugin display name is "OpenClaw ID remote access". Nodes will join this page, the sidebar already has Users, and chat details already has a People section. Invites, approvals and members stay under a **People** section heading. The plugin id `openclaw-id-access` and the `openclawId.people` RPC are unchanged. Labs copy, docs, the plugin inventory and reference page, config-baseline hashes and tests follow the rename. Checks on the Studio: the Access plugin tests, the OpenClaw ID UI tests, the Labs-off and account-menu e2e suites, `tsgo:ui`, `tsgo:test:ui`, `tsgo:extensions`, changed-file oxlint and oxfmt, `lint:ui:i18n`, `check:docs`, the plugin inventory check and `config:docs:check` all pass. The test-line allocation is now 3,662.
- After the rebase, CI found two docs issues, fixed in `0080431`: `docs/concepts/experimental-features.md` had two "OpenClaw ID remote access" headings, because #192335 had added a short section. This PR's section now carries that section's off-state and configuration-key details, and the page has one heading. The plugin inventory and reference index now count the bundled `openclaw-id-access` plugin.
- Rebased onto `main` at `2394bff0c01` after #192345 merged (`59b8a114bf6`). Only the generated files conflicted: the config baseline counts and hashes and the Control UI raw-copy baseline were regenerated on the new base. Every other file's change is identical to the previous head (`8f6b458`).
- Rebased onto `main` at `0a6590652dc` (head `9cbe690`). Earlier, only the performance budgets conflicted, because `main` lowered its boot JS ceilings (#194241); the budgets below are measured on the current base.
- **CI fixes.** Core lint's new `typescript(unbound-method)` rule flagged `device-key.test.ts`; the test now calls the real `IDBObjectStore.add` through `Reflect`. The Control UI performance check found larger Chat and New Session boot graphs: `config-sections.ts` is in them, and its new `visibleConfigSchema` helper imported `view-schema.tsx`, which pulled the config form analyzer into boot (+6 KiB gzip and two more Chat requests). The helper now lives in `config-page-state.ts`, which only Settings loads.
- **Performance budgets (approved by Josh Lehman).** `main` at `0a6590652dc` already exceeds its own Chat, New Session and largest-chunk ceilings. On it, this branch measures Chat boot JS at 1,288,774 B, New Session boot JS at 797,124 B (Linux CI) and the largest shared chunk at 560,277 B gzip; those ceilings are now the measurement plus 256 B for `main`'s concurrent growth. Total CSS measures 325,045 B gzip / 1,675,690 B raw; its ceilings are the measurement plus 64 B. What this PR adds is the lazy OpenClaw ID sidebar mounts, the sign-in callback check in `main.ts` and the account menu styles. Request counts stay within their existing limits.
- **Your devices copy.** Remove access is offered only for other devices, but its confirmation said "This browser loses access now". It now names the device being removed (`owner-devices-dialog.test.tsx`; the test fails with the fix reverted).
- **Default name check (ClawSweeper P3).** Turn on remote access fills the link code from the signed-in account, then checks the default claw name. Solid settles the code signal later, so the check read an empty code and never asked the Gateway; it now receives the acquired code directly (`make-reachable-dialog.test.tsx` expects the `check_name` request and fails without the fix).
- `kit-export.test.ts` only repeated the helper's text and is removed (ClawSweeper); `recoveryKitLines` is now module-private and its Knip entry is gone.

## Live proof on a staging Gateway

The studio lab Gateway, one of the four testnet Gateways, runs this PR's head `9977465` against staging Discovery and the claw loader on `main`'s protocol (discovery#4 and claw-loader#4, then their #5 preview-access changes). The later commits (from the lint fix to `608a551`) change tests, the config page's import graph, one confirmation string, the initial name check and the performance budgets; none touches the Access page's signing or the Gateway. Hostnames, invite secrets and the request location are redacted.

- **Upgrade.** This build requires the agent database at schema v40; `openclaw doctor --fix` migrated it from v39. Afterwards the claw's link, root, owner devices with their approvers, members and invites matched a copy taken before the upgrade, and the new Discovery accepted its snapshot with `protocols` `{"statement":[1],"descriptor":[1]}`.
- **Owner, over the tunnel, on Access.** Created an invite (an InviteCap signed by this browser's owner device). The member's request appeared on Access 840 ms after it was sent, with no refresh. Approve (a MembershipChange `add`) admitted the member, who reached the Control UI 5 s later. Remove closed the member's tunnel connection.
- **Member, over the tunnel.** No Access page. `GET /_openclaw-id/v1/membership` returned 403 `not_owner_device`; `POST /_openclaw-id/v1/statements` with an `add_owner_device` change signed by the member's own key returned 403 `not_an_owner`. The seq did not change.
- **Signers.** The Access page's InviteCap and MembershipChange statements were sent to the same authority from four signers. A root-listed owner device S1 registered an invite and approved device S2, which the Gateway recorded as approved by S1. A key that was never listed, S2 after the root revoked it, and S3 after its certificate expired were each refused with `not_an_owner`, for the invite and for the change; S3's invite had been accepted before it expired. After every refusal the seq, owner devices and invites were unchanged.
- **Your devices and device approval.** Browser A enrolled with the recovery kit and approved browser B by matching codes. Your devices showed B as approved by A and, on Remove access for A, named B as removed with it. The removal closed both tunnels; both browsers were refused on reconnect; Discovery's relay admission refused both keys and still admitted the owner's and the claw's; Discovery's snapshot verified and lists only current devices.

**Access page: a pending request with Approve and Deny.**

![Access page with a pending request](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9d068ba3-8ff0-475e-8a38-8172e9f0a911)

**After Approve: the member is listed with Remove.**

![Access page with the approved member](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7b26f48d-c85a-4eeb-be4c-ca3f15a7fee1)

**Approving a new browser: the code the owner compares (claw loader).**

![Approval code on the approving browser](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/91fbc8b3-f09c-441a-951e-dda7850525ab)

**Your devices: the removal preview.** Taken at `9977465`, before the copy fix above, so it still says "This browser loses access now".

![Your devices removal preview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/150c72ff-670d-4ee9-9728-1aec14bdcba6)

**A removed browser is refused.**

![A removed browser is refused](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26ff70e0-2ae5-4cfb-b775-78a7817c2104)

## Evidence

- On `608a551`, on a macOS arm64 host through Crabbox: the OpenClaw ID UI tests (17 files), `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `tsgo:test:ui`, changed-file oxlint and oxfmt and `pnpm deadcode:exports` pass, and the name-check test fails with its fix reverted. On `8751edc`, `pnpm ui:check-performance:base fc53c551f5e` measured the budgets above. On the same commits rebased on `6f3cd220d44`: the OpenClaw ID UI and config page tests (74 files), the Labs-off and account-menu e2e suites, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `tsgo:test:ui`, changed-file oxlint and oxfmt, `lint:ui:i18n`, `ui:i18n:verify`, `config:docs:check`, `check:docs`, the plugin inventory check, mock exports, the performance script tests and the base performance check pass. With the Your devices copy fix reverted, its test fails.
- On `0080431`, on the same host: `pnpm check:docs` (formatting, markdownlint, MDX, links, config examples) and the plugin inventory check pass.
- On `25d1354` (the styles fix above), on the same host: the Labs-off and account-menu e2e suites, the OpenClaw ID dialog tests and `pnpm tsgo:ui` pass.
- On `3da34a9`, on a macOS arm64 host through Crabbox: the OpenClaw ID UI tests (18 files), the Access plugin and the Gateway Control UI bootstrap, document and plugin-asset tests pass. `pnpm tsgo:ui`, `tsgo:test:ui` and `tsgo:core` pass, as do oxlint and oxfmt on the 108 changed code files, the mock-export, raw-`window.open`, chained-assertion, Control UI i18n, config-docs, unused-export and Madge checks. On the previous head, each of the four review fixes above was reverted in turn and its regression test failed.
- `pnpm test` over the 34 test files this PR adds or changes (UI unit, browser and e2e suites, the People plugin, and the Gateway Control UI bootstrap, document and plugin-asset tests): 37 files, 316 tests passed (with `management-service.test.ts`).
- **Labs switch off:** `openclaw-id-off.e2e.test.ts` drives the built Control UI in Chromium with the switch absent and with it `false`. Across the shell, Pages, the account menu, Settings, Labs and the command palette it finds no OpenClaw ID copy or elements, loads no OpenClaw ID, recovery-kit or 1Password assets, and sends no config writes or chat requests; an unsent draft survives; `control-ui-plugin-assets.test.ts` checks that the plugin catalog, grants and asset routes disappear at once when the switch turns off; the bootstrap tests check the document attribute is absent.
- `pnpm tsgo:core`, `pnpm tsgo:ui` and `pnpm tsgo:extensions` passed. `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` passed after regenerating the raw-copy baseline (two recovery-kit strings). `pnpm check:changed`: see the comment below for the run on the published head.
- Test-line ratchet: `config/test-lines-allocations/openclaw-id-ui-people.txt` allocates exactly the 3,667 test lines this PR adds (new tests for new surface).
- Staging: see the live proof above.

## CI failures inherited from `main`

These fail on `main` itself and are not caused by this PR (which touches none of the inputs):

- **`deep-research` plugin build.** On `main`, `extensions/deep-research/browser/index.tsx` and `pane.tsx` import `./client.js`, which `097f990` ("retire unused research browser client") deleted before #177232 added the imports. The plugin asset build, `tsgo:extensions` and the deep-research e2e fail with `Could not resolve "./client.js"` / `TS2307`: `build-artifacts`, `check-prod-types`, `checks-node-changed`, `checks-node-changed-compact-small-*`, `checks-ui-e2e` (deep-research shard) and PostgreSQL conformance (its build step).
- **Test-line ratchet.** `main` at `0a6590652dc` alone reports `over by: 52; net delta: 0. Tree is over the ceiling; this change does not add test lines` (`main`'s CI skips this job). This PR's allocation equals the test lines it adds.
- **`chat-goal-replace.e2e.test.ts`** fails on `main` `0a6590652dc` on a macOS arm64 host as well.
- On the previous head, `chat-composer-overflow.browser.test.tsx`, `chat-composer-display-snapshot.e2e.test.ts` and `settings-layout.e2e.test.ts` failed in CI; all three pass on both `main` and this branch on a macOS arm64 host, and `main` fixed the settings-layout locator in #194277.

`control-ui-performance` was this PR's and is fixed by the approved budgets above.

## Screenshots

Taken from the built Control UI in Chromium on a macOS arm64 host, with a mocked Gateway and a synthetic account (`owner@example.test`, `claws.example.test`). The menu shots are from `3da34a9`; the Turn on remote access shots include the styles fix in `25d1354`.

**Before: Labs switch off (the default).** The account menu has no OpenClaw ID section; `openclaw-id-off.e2e.test.ts` checks this across the shell.

![Account menu with the Labs switch off](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0333298d-9996-494b-9610-57257f2440f3)

**After: switch on, signed out, then signed in on this computer.**

![Account menu offering Sign in with OpenClaw ID](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bbc69568-6de7-4c3f-b87c-a57aa5203836)

![Account menu signed in, offering Turn on remote access](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/663ae03e-4bd2-4a0f-a55a-86c0f4993b43)

**Turn on remote access, name step (light and dark).**

![Turn on remote access dialog, light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/296e1c44-e78d-4b07-83c1-c9f48e662823)

![Turn on remote access dialog, dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5f3a4102-c3f2-47a2-b5d3-161ddcc74158)

**Remote access on: desktop (dark) and phone width.**

![Account menu with remote access on, dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4db2138e-c3f0-41a3-a587-e3beeede4e6c)

![Account menu with remote access on, phone width](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/21b210a8-8a88-44d7-90f2-2b99b75e7b2c)

Not shown here: the recovery kit step (it displays a generated secret). The Access page, approval and Your devices are in the live proof above.
