prs.title: fix: prevent duplicate Claude answers in session history
prs.body:
## October 10 contributor update

The replacement-message defect is fixed at the CLI producer. After an accepted hook or preparer returns, producer receipts are restored only when the final authored text still equals the accepted aggregate. Rewritten content loses stale receipt correspondence; blocked writes remain blocked. Regression controls cover a fresh hook object without metadata, a preparer dropping metadata, rewritten text, and blocked persistence.

Integrated current upstream main `ff1303e4e8` to resolve the parser conflict. The combined upstream assistant/commentary flush retains buffered receipt selection for accepted assistant text and discards commentary correspondence.

Current contributor head: `14e879642b19e3f04bc1ff5c337a979f5bb4a9bd`. Exact-head GitHub CI has a failed UI E2E job; no full CI pass is claimed for this head. Current Railway source gates (Linux, Node 24.21.0, pinned pnpm 12.9.0): frozen-lock install passed (32.9s); parser, native history, and history paging suites passed 88 assertions in the four-file qualification run (209.74s overall). Final persistence-only replay passed 9/9 (64.96s), covering both original coordination/run-ID assertions and the separate replacement/rewrite/block/preparer controls. All three touched files passed final type-aware lint with zero warnings/errors (24.4s); the final test-only adjustment renames a shadowed local variable without changing the green test behavior. Local and Railway source digests match; `git diff --check` passed. Fresh independent review found no blocking code findings.

The subsequent `check-test-types-core-2` failure was confined to the new hook fixture. The fixture now narrows assistant messages, returns a fresh spread preserving mandatory provider/runtime fields, explicitly removes `__openclaw`, and assigns rewritten content through the typed assistant object. This preserves the receipt-loss discriminator without incomplete-message union typing. On a new disposable Railway sandbox: frozen-lock install passed (30.3s), the exact previously failing `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.agents-other.json` leaf passed, one-file type-aware lint passed with zero warnings/errors (31.0s), and the existing persistence suite passed 9/9 through the native agents-support config (190.27s including cold worker compilation). Source digests match. Initial default-workspace scanning encountered upload-generated AppleDouble sidecars; those were removed from the disposable source. Unit/core launcher attempts collected no tests and are not qualification. No production code changed in this final correction.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Cloudflare Access-protected portals show a blank iframe until the operator manually opens the private portal URL in a top-level tab.

## User Impact

User impact: the Portals page now detects the Access login redirect, shows a clear **Sign in to portal** action, and mounts the preview automatically after the operator returns. Cloudflare Access and the portal bearer check remain enabled.

## Why This Change Was Made

The browser's no-CORS reachability check treats an Access redirect as a successful response, so it cannot distinguish the login page from the application. A new read-only Gateway inspection checks only the token-free `publicUrl` with redirects disabled and reports a recognized Cloudflare Access login route. The authenticated bearer URL remains available only to write-capable operators.

The documentation also records the longer-term architecture decision: keep portals on isolated wildcard origins with one private wildcard Access policy. A same-origin Control UI proxy is intentionally rejected because arbitrary development applications would inherit the Control UI's browser authority.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/portals.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — 3 tests passed; 15 seconds wall time (CI time not measured).
- Combined focused run — all 5 new `portal-access-probe.test.ts` cases passed before the host killed the larger Gateway worker build with exit 137; 99 seconds wall time. The Gateway method suite did not start its tests.
- Mocked browser flow — reproduced the blank iframe, rendered the Access sign-in state without mounting an iframe, verified repeated top-level sign-in returns replace the iframe, and verified selecting another Access portal and returning preserves the recovered preview.
- `pnpm ui:build` — passed (4,120 modules; 419 assets precompressed).
- `pnpm ui:i18n:verify` — passed.
- `pnpm docs:check-links` — 14,932 internal links checked, 0 broken.

Known local gaps: `pnpm tsgo:ui` and type-aware Oxlint exceeded this host's memory limit (exit 137/SIGKILL). The UI Vitest harness also failed before test discovery with the existing `No such built-in module: node:` loader error. Independent AutoReview was attempted but unavailable because the isolated Codex route returned HTTP 401 and no Claude executable was installed. This development-only agent has no Cloudflare or production access, so it cannot supply a real Access login capture; the Gateway redirect classifier and browser recovery lifecycle are covered at deterministic protocol, unit, build, and mocked-browser boundaries.

prs.title: fix(android): only admit chat attachments whose chat.send frame fits one WebSocket message
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #193810: Android accepts videos up to 20 MiB, but `chat.send` carries attachment content as inline Base64 in one OkHttp WebSocket message, and the pinned OkHttp rejects any single frame over its 16 MiB outgoing-queue bound even when the queue is empty (it closes with 1001 and returns `false`, which `GatewaySession` maps to `GatewayRequestNotEnqueued`). A 13 MiB MP4 is 18,175,320 Base64 bytes, so it is admitted by the composer, fails to enqueue, is returned to `Queued` as a transient connection problem, closes the connection, and blocks later sends in the same session while reconnects replay the same untransportable bytes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Size admission must be about the frame that actually goes on the wire, not only the decoded payload.

- `ChatSendTransportLimit.kt` (new) owns that arithmetic: `chatSendBase64Length`, the complete-frame check `chatSendAttachmentsFitWebSocketFrame` (Base64 payload + a small JSON envelope per attachment and per command) against the pinned 16 MiB bound, and `CHAT_COMPOSER_MAX_VIDEO_SEND_DECODED_BYTES` — the largest video whose full `chat.send` frame still fits.
- `admitChatAttachments` keeps every existing per-kind and Base64 ceiling and adds the frame check, so a 13 MiB video is refused at pick time (the draft is not cleared) while the 8 MiB control and all 8 MiB audio/document limits still pass.
- `outboxCommandAttachmentsWithinByteLimits` applies the same frame check to the bytes an outbox row already captured, so a row journaled before this repair can never be replayed as an unenqueueable frame.
- When a claimed outbox row's frame cannot be sent, `ChatController` settles it as a permanent `Failed` row (`OUTBOX_TOO_LARGE_TO_SEND_ERROR`, "remove some and try again") instead of `Queued`, so later sends in the same session/branch proceed through the existing failed-row handling and reconnecting no longer re-breaks the socket. Transient failures keep their existing `Queued` path.

Trade-off made explicit: only video was ever able to exceed the frame (images 6 MiB, audio/documents 8 MiB), so the new video ceiling lands at ~12 MiB and no other kind changes. A real 13 MiB frame is not executed here — no Android SDK is available in this environment — so the wire-level claim rests on the pinned OkHttp contract cited in the issue plus the executable arithmetic below.

## User Impact

- An oversize video is refused in the composer with the existing "too large" feedback before the draft is cleared, instead of a queued bubble that closes the connection.
- A video already queued from an older build fails immediately, visibly, and actionably; messages sent afterwards in the same session are delivered instead of waiting behind it.
- No change for text, images, audio, documents, or videos that fit one frame.

## Evidence

Real Kotlin executed with the Gradle-cached Kotlin 2.4.21 compiler on JDK 21. Both gates are verbatim copies of `outboxCommandAttachmentsWithinByteLimits` (pre-repair from main `ba33925801`, post-repair from this branch) plus the new `ChatSendTransportLimit.kt` arithmetic:

```text
$ java -cp out2:$KOTLIN_STDLIB fixture.ProofGateKt
13 MiB video  before=true after=false
 8 MiB video  before=true after=true
 8 MiB audio  before=true after=true
```

The candidate helper reproduces the issue's own arithmetic and boundary behaviour:

```text
$ java -cp out:$KOTLIN_STDLIB ai.openclaw.app.chat.LimitHarnessKt
chatSendBase64Length(repro)      = 18175320  (issue arithmetic: 18175320)
chatSendBase64Length(control)    = 11184812  (issue arithmetic: 11184812)
frame bound                      = 16777216
frame fits (repro)               = false
frame fits (8 MiB control)       = true
composer admits BEFORE repair    = true
composer admits AFTER repair     = false
control AFTER repair             = true
actual Base64 string length      = 18175320 ; exceeds bound alone = true
frame fits at ceiling            = true
frame fits at ceiling + 1 byte   = false
8 MiB non-video still admissible = true
```

Unit tests added: `ChatSendTransportLimitTest` (5 cases: repro arithmetic, 8 MiB control, ceiling boundary, unchanged non-video ceiling, envelope counted per attachment), `ComposerCeilingContractTest` (ceiling contract + replayed-row gate), and one outbox case in `ChatControllerOutboxTest` that asserts the oversize row is refused by the base gate and that a frame-fitting FIFO head is still dispatched and retired. These were **not executed**: this host has no Android SDK or Robolectric runtime (`./gradlew :app:testPlayDebugUnitTest` fails with `SDK location not found`; the SDK is not installed and the network is unavailable to fetch it), so CI is the first executor of those files. The production Kotlin files in this branch are byte-identical to the variant whose helpers were executed above.

[AI-assisted: drafted with Hermes/Codex; producer ordering and outbox states were traced in source by the implementer.]

prs.title: feat(web-fetch): assess unusable pages with opt-in Decision model
prs.body:
Related: #166688

## What Problem This Solves

`web_fetch` can return a successful-looking login, access-denied, bot-check, or navigation shell that provides no source material for the user's question.

## User Impact

Default behavior is unchanged. Operators who enable Decision assistance, select a Decision model, and set `tools.web.fetch.decisionQuality: "shadow"` get a page-quality judgment while retaining content. `"apply"` can withhold text at an unusable-page probability of at least 0.90, only when both the fetched result and evaluated excerpt are complete. Unavailable or uncertain judgments retain the page.

A hosted Decision provider may receive a bounded page excerpt and charge for each evaluation. The five-second evaluation deadline is unchanged. The threshold is experimental, not calibrated for production false-drop rates.

## Why This Change Was Made

Uses the existing Decision runtime after direct/fallback extraction and outside the shared fetch cache. Evaluation includes at most 6,000 characters of wrapped extracted text plus bounded metadata, not request URL/headers or generated private spill locators. The original result remains cached. The owning agent's consent, selected model, mode and invocation authority are checked around inference; cancellation/source loss remains terminal, and accepted usage is completed only for retained judgments. This does not promise cancellation of already-admitted work or exactly-once final tool delivery.

Real opt-in apply and shadow are both preserved. The one additional core config path is intentional; core placement, page-data transfer/cost and experimental withholding policy remain upstream maintainer decisions. `web_search`, page-change monitoring, provider/dependency changes and production activation are out of scope.

## Evidence

### October 26 integration refresh — `a85c0ff8907832ff0138f007f03560130e5f8c63`

Rebased onto `09104d524ce1a89968716367b8691c4081f7397b` for demonstrated conflicts. Preserves upstream #183797's execution-owned fetch/cache/spill closures rather than restoring the retired request parameter bags. Regenerated config baseline is current-main core +1; channel/plugin counts are unchanged. Fourteen other feature files are byte-identical to the previously reviewed head. Pre-publication main `31c6d5440b24b91929e9d472d17f652901e7c133` advanced 163 paths with no overlap in the 17 PR paths; merge preview is clean.

- **83 selected tests passed; one unchanged macOS sandbox fixture failed** because it invokes GNU `stat -c` on BSD/macOS. This includes quality/accepted-usage, config, assembly, fallback and prompt-prefix checks. No skip, command shim or weaker assertion; Linux CI remains the platform gate.
- Production and agents-tools test types, scoped type-aware lint, changed-file formatting, generated-config, line-cap and whitespace checks passed.
- **Independent clean-context native integration review: PASS**, no actionable P0–P2 findings; previous full 17-file review remains applicable to unchanged feature bytes. Local AutoReview CLI is unavailable and is not counted as completed review.
- **Exact clean-head runtime build passed** (runtime profile, 1m28.8s), including bundles, built plugin closures and UI. Both runtime stamps identify this clean head.
- **Built Gateway + built CLI agent proof passed all four strict cases**, using actual registered local TypeSafe/Clef inference. A credential-free scripted local agent transport selected the real registered `web_fetch`; this was not `--local` or a helper-only call. Each CLI turn exited 0 and took 4.3–4.7 seconds after Gateway startup.

| Scenario | Unusable probability | Result | CLI exit |
|---|---:|---|---:|
| default-off-junk | not evaluated | original text retained | 0 |
| shadow-junk | 0.9482 | original text retained | 0 |
| apply-junk-short | 0.9515 | withheld; complete marked 200-character recovery notice | 0 |
| apply-useful | 0.0481 | original text retained | 0 |

These are warmed synthetic integration observations, not classifier-accuracy or universal latency measurements. A separate real local model warmup took 6.3s, outside the unchanged five-second evaluation deadline. No credentials, hosted/paid inference, new dependencies or production service/config changes. Isolated proof listeners were stopped.

- Supplemental source registered-provider controls: consent removal and model reassignment retain the page; invocation revocation rejects. Actual transport observations counted **zero provider requests** for all three pre-admission controls. This is source-boundary proof, not built-Gateway capture-stall proof.
- **Current-head hosted CI and ClawSweeper review: pending after publication.** Previous head `20e7790a` completed CI without failures and final hosted review with zero findings/sufficient shipped-entry proof; those results are historical, not coverage of this head.

Author simplification retained the existing schema/assembly seams to bound oversized owners and reused upstream's local character-budget value. Full diff: 17 files; source +348/-96 including mechanical moves, tests +479, docs +41, generated +3/-3. No new policy owner, manager or framework. The full apply contract and distinct consent, truncation, cache, cancellation and accepted-usage regressions remain coherent as one optional consumer.

### Acceptance / rollback

Maintainer acceptance is still required for the core setting, page-data transfer/privacy/cost and experimental 0.90 withholding policy; no merge is implied. A broader independently labelled corpus showing useful-page drops would falsify the threshold's suitability. Historical small development/held-out sets are not a rerun corpus on this refresh.

Unset `tools.web.fetch.decisionQuality` to disable the feature. Original content remains in the fetch cache. AI-assisted implementation/review: yes.

prs.title: fix(update): stop chat /update asking owners to retry a running update
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: every chat `/update` tells the owner to ask again while the update is still running. Right after the acknowledgement, the same chat receives `No answer was returned. Ask again if you still need one.` Published 2026.11.1 and earlier send the older wording, `OpenClaw couldn't produce or deliver a reply. Please try again.`

## User Impact

User impact: after this ships, a chat `/update` shows the acknowledgement, progress and outcome, with no prompt to retry. It helps from the first release that contains it, because the installed Gateway handles `/update`. Real failures still reach the requester.

## Why This Change Was Made

`update.run` delivers its own acknowledgement, or hands it to the durable update notice owner, so `/update` correctly returns no reply. Reply tracking only saw an empty command result, so it sent the missing-reply notice. #170534 changed the notice text but kept that path.

`/update` now records the turn as `delivered` when the Gateway delivered the acknowledgement, and as `pending` when the durable notice owner holds it. A `blocked` outcome is preserved. `/restart` replies through the turn, and plugin commands already have `suppressReply`, so neither changes.

## Evidence

Native on Crabbox AWS Linux with a systemd Gateway, an owner listed only in `commands.ownerAllowFrom`, and a real `/update` through a fake Telegram Bot API:

| Installed | Chat messages |
|---|---|
| main `fc53c551f5e` | ack, `No answer was returned. Ask again if you still need one.`, restarting, ready, updated |
| this fix | ack, restarting, ready, updated |
| published 2026.11.1 | ack, `couldn't produce or deliver a reply. Please try again`, `Couldn't sign in to the AI service`, restarting, ready, updated |

All three updates completed.

- `commands-update.test.ts`: three new cases fail on base (`outcome: missing`) and pass with the fix; 15/15 pass, 36 s wall with `--maxWorkers=1`.
- 17 test lines are allocated in `config/test-lines-allocations/chat-update-ack-completion.txt`; the regression needs them.
- `$autoreview` is scoped-clean at P2. The independent Codex review found nothing.
- Gap: the `pending` path (`ackQueued`) has a unit test only; the native runs delivered the acknowledgement directly.

prs.title: fix(process): keep commands available with retained MCP servers
prs.body:
Closes #166017

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes command startup failures when retained session-owned stdio MCP servers fill the Gateway's shared 256-child spawn broker limit.

## User Impact

Commands keep bounded headroom while MCP servers remain alive between turns. Capacity errors identify whether to close unused MCP sessions or running processes before retrying. Session idle eviction remains opt-in; no config or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Separate the 256 concurrent startup/file-read budget and 256 native-resource budget from retained process custody. Host and worker enforce 512 pending/retained children total, with at most 448 MCP children, reserving 64 slots for commands. The MCP transport carries its admission class through asynchronous process preparation.

Confirmed local IPC refusal releases its reservation and settles raw, execa, and file-output requests. Uncertain delivery retains custody until native completion or cleanup is confirmed, including across broker restart. Unknown launch outcomes can conservatively retain capacity until Gateway restart. These are broker-owned process-root limits, not an OS quota on descendants.

Rebased onto main `fc53c551f5e5`, preserving GodBlf's three commit authorships. Current command/resource owners, Docker custody, file reads/output and process-group cleanup remain in place. No changelog changes.

## Evidence

Current head: `e8ec12e6058cc3aa5a6f5ec990d4e4bdca33be3b`.

- **One added regression:** `reserves command capacity while MCP children retain cleanup custody` proves MCP 448 refusal, command 64 headroom, total 512 refusal, slot reuse and cleanup custody. With only `host.ts` replaced by its exact main `fc53c551f5e5` version, the named test fails at the old 256-child guard (`Spawn broker is unavailable`); the candidate passes.
- **18 focused tests passed:** `timeout 120 pnpm test src/process/spawn-broker/host-scope-settlement.test.ts src/process/spawn-broker/worker-admission-settlement.test.ts src/process/spawn-broker/ipc.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` (2.05s command wall). The changed host file alone: 13 tests, 1.76s wall. [Exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42268614047) passed: 59 successful jobs, 28 skipped, zero failures; baseline ratchets, Docker seed E2E, lint, types and all selected test shards passed.
- **Net test lines −2 versus main:** host fixture 338→336 LF; worker tests restored exactly to main; IPC tests unchanged. Existing raw-spawn refusal assertions now share the existing failure table. All original host scenarios remain. Removed redundant added cases and their 379-line allocation; no allocation or ceiling change remains in the PR. Git diff confirms the only changed test file has 88 additions/90 removals.
- **Static checks passed:** timeout-bounded typecheck with nine touched TypeScript roots plus the existing worker test and ambient declarations; scoped oxlint on the nine touched TypeScript files; targeted formatting; `git diff --check`.
- **Independent autoreview:** complete final candidate versus `fc53c551f5e5`, with full lifecycle context, scoped-clean through P2; no actionable findings. The previous ClawSweeper IPC pre-send-refusal finding remains repaired.

Native/build proof relies on exact-head PR CI. No broad local suites, container workloads, real-process saturation, packaging or live Gateway changes were run on the production host. Native review and preparation completed for this head; the fresh local autoreview is the selected review route. Do not merge; landing stays with the lead.

prs.title: fix(gateway): strip __controlUiReconnectResume from chat.send params before validation
prs.body:
<!--
Closes: #165433
-->

## What Problem This Solves
Fixes: `chat.send` requests from non-Operator-UI clients (e.g. webchat on a browser reconnect with a preserved `sessionId`) are rejected with `invalid chat.send params: at root: unexpected property '__controlUiReconnectResume'`. `resolveControlUiReconnectResumeParams` only strips the internal `__controlUiReconnectResume` marker when both `value === true` AND `isOperatorUiClient(clientInfo)` returns true; in every other case the `__`-prefixed marker leaks into the AJV-strict `chat.send` schema and the request is dropped before dispatch.

## User Impact
User impact: Webchat and other browser-based reconnect paths that emit the internal `__controlUiReconnectResume` marker now have their messages admitted and dispatched normally on reconnect. No user-visible change for Control UI clients — their behavior is preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made
`__controlUiReconnectResume` is an internal `__`-prefixed wire field added by the Control UI to signal "treat this as a reconnect resume, not a fresh run." Such fields should never reach the public `chat.send` schema. The patch decouples "strip the field before validation" from "record that a resume was requested" — the field is now stripped whenever it is present on the input record, and the `resumeRequested` flag is still gated by both the strict-value check and the Operator UI client check, preserving the downstream semantics. The strict-value check is unchanged on purpose so a non-true value (e.g. `false`, `1`, the wrong type) still does not mark a resume even from an Operator UI client.

## Evidence
- Six focused unit tests added in `src/gateway/server-methods/chat-server-timing.test.ts` (new file) cover the regression and the surrounding cases: field absent, non-object input, true value with operator UI client, true value with non-operator UI client (the regression), true value with missing `clientInfo`, non-true values with operator UI client, and input-record immutability.
- A local reproduction on the bundled `dist/chat-server-timing-soo795Of.mjs` (the same logic, minified) confirmed the bug and the fix: pre-patch, a `webchat` clientInfo with `__controlUiReconnectResume: true` returned the marker in the result params; post-patch, the marker is stripped and `resumeRequested` is `false`.
- `diff -u` of the patched file vs. upstream main shows changes confined to the `resolveControlUiReconnectResumeParams` function body; no other exports, signatures, or unrelated fields are touched.

prs.title: improve(ios): run simulator tests with pnpm ios:test
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Running iOS app tests from a terminal needs a long, hand-built `xcodebuild` command, and a mistyped suite name in `-only-testing` silently runs nothing and still exits 0.

## User Impact

No app change. Developers and agents get one command, `pnpm ios:test`, that runs the iOS app tests on a simulator with the same flags as CI and reports a short, trustworthy result.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `pnpm ios:test` runs the `OpenClaw` scheme (`OpenClawTests` and `OpenClawLogicTests`). `pnpm ios:test TalkModeManagerTests` or `Target/Suite[/test]` selectors run fewer; `OpenClawUITests` selectors use their own scheme. `IOS_SIM` picks a simulator by name or UDID; otherwise a booted iPhone, then the first available one.
- It runs the same project preparation as `ios:gen`, then `xcodebuild test` with CI's flags (`-parallel-testing-enabled NO`, `-collect-test-diagnostics never`) and the `apps/ios/build/DerivedData` path `ios:run` already uses. Output goes to a log file, as in CI, so simulator log forwarding cannot stall timed tests.
- It prints each failure (test ID and the first lines of the message), the pass/fail/skip counts, and the log and `.xcresult` paths in `apps/ios/build/TestResults`. When the build fails, it prints the compiler errors instead of "0 tests".
- `xcodebuild` ignores `-only-testing` selectors that match no test. `findUnmatchedSelectors` in `scripts/lib/ios-test-results.mjs` (the existing xcresult parser) compares the selectors with the result tree, and `ios:test` fails when a selector ran nothing. It matches on node URLs, so Swift Testing suites with display names still match their type name.
- `apps/ios/README.md` documents the command.

## Evidence

- `pnpm ios:test` (whole `OpenClaw` scheme) on an iPhone 17 simulator: 3m19s, 1343 passed, 3 skipped, 2 failed. Both failures are existing source-text tests that are red on `main` and not in any CI list (`RootTabsSidebarRegressionTests` "sidebar has one agent selector…", `WatchApprovalTransportSourceGuardTests` "retry reset matches the exact active attempt"); this PR does not touch them.
- Misspelled suite plus real selectors (a Swift Testing suite, a Logic target suite, an XCTest test method): the real ones ran (21 passed), then `no tests ran for OpenClawTests/NoSuchSuiteTests` and exit 1. The same plain `xcodebuild` command exits 0.
- A throwaway failing test printed its full test ID (`OpenClawTests/ZZThrowawayTests/…`) and expectation text, exit 1. A throwaway compile error printed the compiler error line and `xcodebuild exited 65 before running tests`, exit 1.
- `pnpm ios:test OpenClawUITests/ShareExtensionUITests`: passed through the `OpenClawUITests` scheme.
- `pnpm tsgo:scripts` (red with TS2345 before the selector-target fix, green after), `tsconfig.test.root.scripts.json`, oxlint, oxfmt, `check:script-erasability` and the existing `test/scripts/ios-test-results.test.ts` (20 passed) are clean.
- No new Vitest test: `main` is 49 lines over the test-line ceiling, and the ratchet fails any PR with positive test-line growth while that debt stands (allocations do not forgive it). The unmatched-selector behavior is proven by the real `ios:test` runs above and below; `pnpm check:test-lines-ratchet` reports net delta 0.
- Rebased onto `main` to pick up #194283 (the first CI run merged with a `main` that failed `tsgo:extensions` in `extensions/deep-research`). Smoke on the rebased head:

<details>
<summary>pnpm ios:test GatewayStatusBuilderTests NoSuchSuiteTests OpenClawLogicTests/WatchChatStatusLocalizationTests</summary>

```text
ios:test: OpenClawTests/GatewayStatusBuilderTests OpenClawTests/NoSuchSuiteTests OpenClawLogicTests/WatchChatStatusLocalizationTests on iPhone 17 (<simulator-udid>)
ios:test: log apps/ios/build/TestResults/2026-11-06T20-29-54-025Z.log
ios:test: Passed: 20 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped
ios:test: results apps/ios/build/TestResults/2026-11-06T20-29-54-025Z.xcresult
ios:test: no tests ran for OpenClawTests/NoSuchSuiteTests; check the target, suite and test names.
[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 1.
```

</details>

- Review: hosted ClawSweeper on this PR.

Merge danger: two-way door. Developer tooling only; no app, CI workflow, state or config changes.

[Built Linux CLI / real PTY before-and-after capture and controls](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194310#issuecomment-6695751985).

prs.title: fix(mcp): retire stdio servers decisively on host loss
prs.body:
Fixes #194078

## What Problem This Solves

MCP servers launched over stdio were not enrolled in host-loss termination: if the Gateway host process disappeared abruptly, the subprocess custody anchor could wait for a lineage-close receipt instead of retiring the server decisively, leaving orphaned MCP server processes behind. In plain terms: when the manager dies suddenly, the helpers it started should be shut down right away, not left waiting for a goodbye message that never arrives.

## Why This Change Was Made

`OpenClawStdioClientTransport` calls `createOwnedStdioProcess` without `terminateOnHostLoss`, so the stdio path only gets best-effort host-loss handling. The Claude CLI owner path (`extensions/anthropic/cli-process.ts`) already arms `terminateOnHostLoss: true` on the same owned-stdio custody. Normal transport `close()` ends stdin explicitly, which is exactly the contract the flag requires, so the stdio MCP path can adopt the stronger behavior without changing graceful shutdown.

## User Impact

MCP stdio servers are killed decisively when their host is lost, matching the Claude CLI owner behavior. Normal connect/close flows are unchanged.

## Evidence

- Real-runtime custody behavior behind the flag (shipped machinery, unmodified): `service-child-group-anchor.input-lifetime.test.ts > "host-loss distinguishes protocol EOF from host loss"` — 4/4 pass; host-loss mode ends the child with SIGKILL while EOF modes exit cleanly (code 0).
- Wiring regression: `mcp-stdio-transport.test.ts > "arms host-loss termination for owned stdio custody"` asserts the transport passes `terminateOnHostLoss: true` into owned stdio custody; the suite passes 26/26.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` clean; oxlint reports 0 warnings and 0 errors on the changed files.

## AI Assistance

This PR is AI-assisted. Used source inspection and the repository test harness to analyze issue #194078, locate the missing flag in mcp-stdio-transport.ts, and mirror the existing Claude CLI owner path. The implementer understands the code: normal close ends stdin explicitly, and the flag makes host loss kill the child instead of waiting for lineage-close confirmation. All evidence above is from real local runtime execution.

prs.title: fix(codex): keep parents on the same thread after native child completion
prs.body:
Related: #153354

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a native Codex parent switching threads and losing access to its existing child when the last child's completion resumes the parent.

## User Impact

A parent can receive its child's completion and send a follow-up to that same child without replacing the native parent thread or rebuilding its accepted tool catalog. No configuration or migration is required. This change does not address duplicate visible completion replies.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing catalog recovery path depends on live-child execution protection. That protection is correctly released before the last child's completion is delivered, leaving the automatic continuation exposed to a newly generated catalog.

Use the existing completion-delivery owner to identify an exact, currently in-flight completion for the same parent, child, requester session, run, and physical client. Only that delivery can recover the native thread's accepted catalog. Its authority is checked again after metadata is read. Runtime, home, transport, catalog fingerprints, and current tool-execution checks remain enforced; ordinary turns retain their existing behavior. No additional registry or SDK surface is introduced.

Codex's native contract was checked against `rust-v0.164.0` (`6aaac694803004a63c6f393d153c96d22521a6b9`): `thread/start` accepts dynamic tools, while `thread/resume` does not replace them. A small existing parent-release loop moves to the existing parent owner without changing its behavior, keeping the monitor within the repository's source-size gate.

### Published 2026.10.10: what is already fixed and what remains

The [release notes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openclaw/openclaw/main/CHANGELOG/2026.10.10.md) credit #174900 for native catalog continuity. That is the upstream foundation this PR extends: protected parents can reuse their accepted declarations while current tool permissions remain enforced. It does not cover every completion lifetime. In the [published tag's catalog guard](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7dc3350cb9f08fcf9a0af5c4845a20d5b2f1a8be/extensions/codex/src/app-server/native-tool-catalog.ts#L28-L70), recovery still requires live-thread protection. The last child's completion releases that protection before delivery, so this automatic continuation can still miss catalog recovery and replace its parent thread.

This PR addresses that remaining completion-delivery interval through the existing owner, without weakening runtime fingerprints or granting execution rights from retained declarations. #188526 carries the corresponding release-branch change together with its WebChat-origin repair. The release notes therefore do not make this PR redundant.

## Evidence

### Additional published-release check — November 3, 2026

A selective port of this catalog change, the release-specific WebChat fix, and the remaining retirement error-class fix was applied to official 10.10 packages. On both macOS and Linux, a real-model authenticated WebChat run completed parent → child → automatic completion → same parent → follow-up to the same child. The parent and physical client stayed the same; the child returned its remembered marker. Shipped CLI history confirmed settlement. On Linux, an actual `session_status` call also succeeded after completion. These were observations of the combined installed port, not a new exact-head run of this PR or proof of all fallback paths.

The port's 50 focused tests passed, including composed checks for wrong-requester catalog denial, custody revoked during an awaited metadata read, and current executor restrictions after catalog recovery. The downstream native-dispatch denial and custody-reassignment trace requested in review is still missing. These checks do not clear that security/proof request. Accepted native metadata was inspected after each live run; no independent before-run catalog snapshot was taken. The exact-candidate evidence and its limits remain below.

- Regression cases fail before the fix at the completion owner and catalog loader, then pass with it. The final changed suites pass 19 tests; related availability, execution-authority, and continuation suites pass 26 tests. The existing two parent-retention cases also pass after the owner extraction.
- Codex production and test typechecks, targeted lint/format, `git diff --check`, source-size and test-line gates pass. The separate allocation grants exactly the change's 126 net regression-test lines; no shared ceiling or source-size baseline is raised.
- Shared autoreview of the final range `f3009a56907e34a42d0d453dddff8adb13de4f20..417d7e2113f065fb147bd458584dc72d9538b43f`, including complete affected owners and authority context, found no actionable P0–P2 findings. Tests were executed separately, not by the reviewer.
- `pnpm build:runtime` passes on `417d7e2` (82.3 s). A real-model, authenticated WebChat run on that exact source/build completes parent → child → automatic completion → parent continuation → follow-up to the same child. All three parent-ready events identify the same native parent and physical client; the child's follow-up returns its remembered marker. All 48 originally accepted functions match the final retained binding. The shipped CLI confirms the visible result and settled session.
- Full local `pnpm test:extension codex --maxWorkers=6`: **5,368 passed, 3 failed, 17 skipped**, across 441 executed files (481.57 s). Two failures are macOS process-inspection permission errors in unchanged `transport-startup.test.ts`; the third is the validation-watcher assertion in unchanged `transcript-mirror-cleanup.test.ts`. For the watcher failure, temporarily reversing this entire patch, verifying the parent-tree source bytes, and running the exact file through the supported Node 24 wrapper reproduces the same assertion on base `f3009a5` (1 failed, 12.77 s). The patch was then restored and all changed-file hashes and clean HEAD verified. The process-permission signatures were also reproduced during the release baseline investigation; they have not been repaired here. Watcher root cause/order sensitivity remains undiagnosed. This full lane is not claimed as passing. No assertion, timeout, retry, skip, or expected-failure setting was weakened.

The live run used the pinned OpenClaw Bun 1.4.4 and Codex 0.164.0, isolated synthetic state, internal routing, and disabled model fallbacks. It produced two identical visible final replies, one for each child completion. It qualifies thread/catalog/child continuity, not exactly-once delivery, stale external routing, or general fallback behavior. The original accepted metadata was inspected after the run; no independent before-run catalog snapshot was taken.

<details>
<summary>Sanitized exact-candidate runtime proof</summary>

```text
Exact-candidate main catalog-continuity proof
Source/build commit: 417d7e2113f065fb147bd458584dc72d9538b43f
Gateway runtime: pinned OpenClaw Bun 1.4.4 (openclaw-v1.4.4-20261026-191755ec11-webkit-b82bc917e9); identified from the running Gateway executable. Native runtime: workspace-pinned Codex 0.164.0.
Environment: authenticated WebChat client, isolated synthetic session, internal route, no external channels. Model fallbacks were disabled to fail closed.

One chat.send request was accepted; no manual continuation or model retry was sent.
Parent: 01a18e92-c25a-7e02-939a-b7ae5127109f
Child: 01a18e92-ef88-75d2-b7e3-14ee747f42e4 (native agent target /root/catalog_child)
Parent thread_ready: started, resumed, resumed; same parent and physical client throughout.
Parent native transcript: exactly one spawn_agent and one followup_task to that same child.
Child terminal results: FIRST_READY; FOLLOWUP_OK CATALOG_MEMORY_110.
Original accepted native catalog: 10 top-level declarations / 48 functions.
Accepted catalog fingerprint: sha256:a41950488f43f4dca21fd13f8e67488f888f443e901a80e45b2502112c1e9661
The final retained binding identifies the same parent and client and matches that accepted catalog fingerprint. The accepted session_meta record was inspected after the run; no separate before-run snapshot exists, so this is not a before/after digest comparison.

Shipped CLI read after settlement:
  OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=<isolated-state> OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=<isolated-config> pnpm openclaw gateway call chat.history --params '{"sessionKey":"agent:main:catalog-chain-proof","limit":100}' --json
Result: logical session catalog-chain-proof; visible CATALOG_CHAIN_OK 01a18e92-ef88-75d2-b7e3-14ee747f42e4; hasActiveRun=false; pendingInputs.total=0.

Observed limitation: two identical visible final replies, corresponding to the two child completion announcements. This run proves catalog/thread/child continuity; it does not prove exactly-once visible delivery, general fallback behavior, or stale external routing. The inherited spawn record in the child's rollout was not counted as a second spawn.

Cleanup: the proof client finished; the task-owned Gateway stopped cleanly after settlement and its listening port is closed. No production state or services were used. Private fixtures remain only until this sanitized evidence is published.
```

</details>

prs.title: fix(update): update and Doctor still copy the state database for most reads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Refs #185656: after #194042, one update on a 400 MB state database still writes about 62 GiB. Whole-database snapshot copies, one per read, are most of it, and each copy extends the update.

## User Impact

On a 400 MB state database, an update writes about 28% less and finishes about 2.5 minutes sooner (idle Gateway: 62,409 → 44,707 MiB, 749 → 606 s). An update from published 2026.10.10 improves too, because the candidate's own processes do this work (65,990 → 54,628 MiB, 755 → 661 s). This does not solve #185656: a 400 MB update still writes about 45 GiB. What remains is listed under Evidence.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Root cause

#194042 lets read-only callers share one private image, but only producers that leave no child behind could seed it, and only Doctor one-shots had the scope. So in those scopes the most common reads, which go through the retained producer, could borrow an image but never leave one. The update driver, `update admit`, post-core, and the automatic cleanup worker had no scope at all. A source written under 2 s before a read was also never retained, so every commit cost two copies: one that could not be kept, then one that could.

### Fix

- Inside a reuse scope, awaited readers prepare through a one-shot child (`prepareSqliteReadOnlyLocationAwaited` → `prepareSqliteReadOnlyLocation`). It seeds the image and leaves no process behind, so Doctor's process-group settlement sees nothing extra. The earlier attempt to keep retained children alive failed exactly there. Outside a scope nothing changes, and the sync `lazy` path keeps its retained producer because it must advance without an event loop.
- The scope now covers `openclaw update`, `update admit`, the delegated post-core step, and the automatic cleanup worker's task. The Gateway process itself still never holds an image.
- `prepareArtifactPreservingSqliteRead` opts in: its readers open the image read-only.
- The retention delay follows the file's clock. A whole-second timestamp can come from a clock as coarse as FAT's 2 s, so it still waits 2 s. Any other timestamp comes from a fine clock, where 50 ms clears a tick.

### Rejected alternatives

- Keeping retained children alive for the image's lifetime: the earlier revision of #194042 did this and Doctor refused with `data-at-risk`.
- Hardlinking a retained child's image out at release: more moving parts for the same hits.

### Accepted edge cases

- A filesystem with sub-second timestamps coarser than 50 ms could hide a write inside the window. Real sub-second clocks (ext4, APFS, NTFS, exFAT at 10 ms) do not. A whole-second clock still waits 2 s.
- An image in the update driver holds its database's size of disk for longer. Each new copy retires the stale image first, so this is one extra copy per database at peak.

## Evidence

Native on Crabbox AWS Linux: systemd Gateway, 400 MB state database, `/tmp` on ext4, disk writes during the update, all rc=0 and healthy unless noted. A fresh install of each build updates to the same build relabelled. Base is main `2a2cd293145`.

| Lane | Base | This PR (`54e28ace133`) |
|---|---|---|
| Idle Gateway | 62,409 MiB, 749 s | 44,707 MiB, 606 s |
| Gateway-side writer every 2 s until stop | 63,367 MiB, 757 s | 50,248 MiB, 650 s |

prs.title: feat(telegram): offer each configured model runtime as its own /model picker button
prs.body: Supersedes #163908, which the inactivity bot closed. Same change, now merged with current `main`. The review history on #163908 still applies, and the points it left open are covered below. Related: `pickerRuntimes` (2026.9.5 release notes, `docs/concepts/models.md` › "Choose the same model with different runtimes") ## What Problem This Solves In the Telegram `/model` picker, a model with several configured runtimes (`agents.defaults.models["/"].pickerRuntimes`, for example API and Claude CLI) appears as a single button, and that button carries only the default route label. The Control UI and the Discord picker already offer each runtime as its own choice. On Telegram, the other runtime is only reachable by typing `/model --runtime `. ## User Impact Telegram shows one button per offered runtime, labelled with the existing route prefix (`API · Claude Opus 5.5`, `Claude CLI · Claude Opus 5.5`). Tapping one selects the model and pins that runtime for the session, and ✓ marks the active model/runtime pair. Models with a single runtime look exactly as before. Picking the configured runtime of the agent's default model still resets the session to its default. ## Why This Change Was Made The picker data already carries `runtimeChoicesByModel`; the Telegram list did not use it. - `model-buttons.ts` expands a model into one entry per runtime variant. The new callback is `mdl_rt_{runtime}_{provider/model}`. When that does not fit Telegram's 64 bytes, an opaque `mdl1~r:{sha256}` is used instead. Runtime selections resolve only against the variants the picker offered. - `model-runtime-variants.ts` (new) builds the variants per model, with the configured runtime first. - `bot-handlers.callback-router.ts`: pagination counts entries, and a runtime button applies `applySessionModelSelection` with `runtime: { kind: "set" }`. - `commands-models-catalog.ts` exposes `modelRuntimeIds`. This is the runtime each multi-runtime model uses with no session pin, resolved from config and auth for any provider. It is optional and absent for single-runtime models. - `commands-models.ts` / `command-ui.ts`: the direct `/models ` reply pages over the same runtime rows as the callbacks. - `ChannelCommandAdapter.buildModelsListChannelData` gains five optional inputs. Adapters that ignore them keep one row per model. No config, storage or protocol changes, and existing `mdl_sel_*` / `mdl1~m:` callbacks keep working. ## Revision on current `main` This revision merges current main. The one real conflict is main's role-policy filter for CLI alias twins in `loadModelsProviderData`. It now runs after `modelRuntimeIds` is filled and also drops the runtime id of a model it filters out. Behaviour and callbacks are otherwise unchanged from the last reviewed head `abb6c39d7bb`. ## Evidence **Before / after (live Telegram, `pickerRuntimes` set on the Anthropic models):** | Before | After | |---|---| | | | **Real behavior proof.** ClawSweeper asked for this as "Add real behavior proof". Since 2026-10-18 the change has been running in a production installation: first on a 2026.10.4 build, and since 2026-11-05 on a 2026.10.10 build with this exact port. It serves three daily-use Telegram bots, and selecting a runtime from the picker moves subsequent turns to that runtime. A logged CLI↔API switch is shown below. ``` cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 trigger=user useResume=false cli turn: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 durationMs=17379 cli exec: provider=claude-cli model=claude-opus-5-5 trigger=user useResume=true session=present [model-fetch] response provider=anthropic api=anthropic-messages model=claude-opus-5-5 status=200 ``` Session entry afterwards: `modelOverride: "claude-opus-5-5"`, `agentRuntimeOverride: "openclaw"`. Still open from the review: Telegram **Test Server userbot** evidence via the repository `telegram-e2e-userbot` skill, covering revised selection, the configured-default reset, and direct-reply/callback pagination. It needs Convex-leased team credentials that I do not have. If a maintainer can run that lane, or lease me the credentials, I'll add the recording. **Owner decision.** The five optional `ChannelCommandAdapter` inputs are additive, and adapters that ignore them are unaffected. They still need a maintainer's yes or no. **Tests** (`pnpm test --maxWorkers=1`, merged base `d189a554154`, wall time on a shared host): - `extensions/telegram/src/model-buttons.test.ts`: 13 passed (11 s); `model-runtime-variants.test.ts`: 5 passed (9 s); `command-ui.test.ts`: 5 passed (64 s) - `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-models.test.ts`: 19 passed (70 s, includes "reports each model's configured runtime regardless of the session runtime pin"); `commands-models-order.test.ts`: 1 passed; `commands-models.catalog-recovery.test.ts`: 6 passed - `extensions/telegram/src/bot.test.ts -t model`: 5 passed - `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:extensions`: clean. `oxlint` (core + extensions tsconfig) and `oxfmt --check` on the changed files: clean. No real timers, sleeps, or Gateway boots in the new tests.

prs.title: fix(ui): Control UI checks flake on slow CI shards
prs.body:
Related: #190824 (CI run 41451247788, jobs 125297564171 and 125297564323) ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: Control UI checks fail intermittently on contended CI runners when a test's real-time wait also pays for loading a lazy module or for opening dozens of unrelated sections of the complete Settings form. ## User Impact No user-visible change. PRs stop picking up these unrelated `checks-ui` and `checks-ui-e2e` failures, and a future test that hides the same costs fails deterministically on a fast machine instead of only on a slow CI shard. ## Why This Change Was Made All three failures on #190824's head are timing contracts, not leaked state. Each test's real-time budget included work the assertion is not about: - **`chat-details-session.test.ts`, "groups every direct subagent…"** polled for the lazy live-activity element inside `waitForSolid`'s 1 s budget, so the first, cold import of `chat-subagent-activity-live.tsx` counted against it. The test now settles that import with `vi.dynamicImportSettled()` (the file already does this at three other lazy boundaries) and asserts synchronously, leaving no import-speed-dependent wait. - **`config-form-integrity.e2e.test.ts`, "round-trips Agent List model overrides…"** used `revealControl`, which opened closed config sections in document order until the target rendered. Against the complete Gateway schema that meant 48 unrelated sections before reaching the agent's `Tools` section. Callers now name the closed sections that hold a nested control, and the helper fails with that instruction if the control is not rendered. The two other callers never opened a section. - **`plugins-page.test.ts`** failed on that head only because the head predates #191157, which already preloads `settings-view.tsx` before the fake-timer test. Test 2's failure was a cascade from test 1's still-pending import. Main needs no change here.
Why not change waitForSolid itself Settling imports inside the shared helper would add a real macrotask to ~4,000 waits, and it would deadlock tests such as `chat-question-card-loading.test.ts` that deliberately hold a lazy import pending with `vi.doMock` to assert loading states.
## Evidence Reconstructed from the failing job's `[vitest:module]` records: one Bun fork (concurrency slot 2, one environment batch) ran `app-sidebar-rail` → `agents/view` → `session-hovercard` → `widget-card` → `desktop-panel` → **`plugins-page`** → `session-pull-requests` → **`chat-details-session`**. I replayed that exact order in a single Bun fork (`unit` project, `isolate: false` with the cleanup runner) through a scratch sequencer: - On a fast Mac without emulation it passes, matching the green single-file controls. - With cold lazy modules emulated by a 2.5 s real-time top-level await in `settings-view.tsx` and `chat-subagent-activity-live.tsx`, **before** reproduces exactly the three CI unit failures: plugins tests 1 and 2 with `No plugin action matching …`, and the subagent test with `expected null not to be null`. 219 other tests pass. **After** (main with this PR): 222/222. - Without the new settle line, the subagent test now fails 3/3 locally with the CI message (56–74 ms), not just under load. - E2E under 20x Chromium CPU throttle (`Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate`): **before** times out at 120 000 ms, the CI error, with 73.5 s spent in the section walk. **After** it passes in 94.3 s with a 9.3 s reveal. Unthrottled locally, the reveal drops from 5.1 s to 0.8 s and the test from 14.7–17.2 s to 11.0–15.0 s. - The original unnamed `revealControl(rawOnly)` call fails under the new helper with `Pass the closed sections that hold this control`. - `check:changed` passes. The test-line ratchet net delta is 0. The three `revealControl` e2e files pass 7/7. - Cost (`--maxWorkers=1`, local): `chat-details-session.test.ts` 18/18 in 8.6 s wall (tests ≈0.7 s); `config-form-integrity.e2e.test.ts` 3/3 in 22.1 s test time (69 s wall with bundled-UI setup). CI seconds will follow from this PR's run.

prs.title: fix(llama-cpp): restore managed Windows runtime downloads
prs.body:
Fixes #192366.

## What Problem This Solves

Managed llama.cpp setup fails on Windows because the pinned b10809 CPU archives and CUDA runtime dependency are served with different, much shorter bytes than their published SHA-256 digests describe.

## User Impact

This proposes restoring managed Windows downloads by refreshing the runtime from **b10809 to b11977**. **Draft: the runtime refresh still requires explicit maintainer approval.** Native Windows setup has not been exercised on this Mac.

## Why This Change Was Made

b11977 is the newest complete binary release that had seven days of soak at the selection cutoff (2026-11-05 04:47:32 UTC). The newer `v0.9.0` release contains a nightly-tag marker, not the platform archives; upstream still publishes binaries under `b` tags.

Refresh the build/commit, published hashes and sizes, and authenticated library aliases together. Increase only the CUDA archive's extraction budgets to fit its measured 657,155,869-byte expanded contents and 594,121,728-byte largest DLL. SHA-256 enforcement, CUDA driver requirements, and installed-runtime validation remain unchanged.

## Evidence

Complete GETs and the production installer reproduce the b10809 failures:

| Archive | Published bytes | Served bytes |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Windows CPU x64 | 18,407,457 | 507 |
| Windows CPU arm64 | 11,974,499 | 371 |
| CUDA 12.4 runtime | 391,443,627 | 6,491 |

All eight selected b11977 release archives were fully downloaded and matched the upstream published sizes and SHA-256 digests. Both unchanged Visual C++ redistributables also matched their pinned sizes and hashes. All manifest aliases and CUDA extraction budgets match the inspected archive members. The macOS 13.3 and Linux glibc 2.34/x64 and 2.38/arm64 floors are unchanged. The actual executable reports `build 11977, commit 7ac5727d6`.

The Mac managed installer completed in 6.1 seconds. CLI embedding-only onboarding completed in 28.3 seconds. A real `openclaw agent --local` turn using Qwen 2.5 7B returned exactly `PIN_REFRESH_OK` (20.4 seconds in the agent, 46.4 seconds wall time). Local memory indexing completed in 11.3 seconds, and a real embedding-backed search returned the synthetic note with vector score 0.635 in 7.4 seconds. These ran in isolated state on port 20447; no operator Gateway was used.

`pnpm build`, scoped production/test typechecking, scoped lint/format, and all baseline ratchets passed. Full build phase time was 14m46s; ratchets took 306.4 seconds. The build logged non-fatal Control UI bundle-budget warnings. The first lint invocation needed the existing pinned `@openclaw/solid-lint` workspace installed after gateway-only preparation; its rerun passed.

The updated archive fixture fails against the original manifest at the stale SONAME source (13.2 seconds wall time). All **136 focused tests across eight suites passed** in 140.2 seconds, including first-use worker-cache compilation. Suites cover installer integrity and extraction, managed server and recovery, setup and non-interactive setup, presets, and managed media. Production line delta is 0; test line delta is -1. The fixture uses independent upstream library filenames and retains the unsafe-symlink check in the same fixture.

Final Codex autoreview of base `2270152d224ae48de9a10f3fe26b4c594ac9e87d` through head `c05d61847840c7e7c95f38337ad7b7c4866dc6b2` is **scoped-clean through P2**. Its earlier stale-test-digest finding was fixed.

Remaining platform proof: native managed setup on Windows x64 CPU, arm64 CPU, and NVIDIA CUDA, followed by inference. The existing Windows CI suites exercise platform contracts; they do not prove native runtime downloads and GPU startup.

CI: [corrected exact-target run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41974945586) dispatched with `target_ref=c05d61847840c7e7c95f38337ad7b7c4866dc6b2`; preflight passed and its log confirms the exact checkout SHA. Broad results are pending. The [first dispatch](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41974663833) checked out that exact head but rejected my `validation_tier=main` argument, which is reserved for same-revision main validation. The corrected run uses the supported default tier. The PR remains draft pending approval of the runtime refresh.

prs.title: feat(sessions): list and read session workspace files from the CLI
prs.body:
Closes #193221

## What Problem This Solves

The Gateway knows every file in a session's workspace — the Control UI file view renders that inventory — but the terminal could not read it. An operator on a headless host had to hand-call `gateway call sessions.files.list` with raw JSON parameters.

## User Impact

`openclaw sessions files <sessionKey> [path]` lists the workspace files (name, kind, size, update time) with `--search` name filtering; `--get` prints one file's content; `--output` writes it to disk. `--json` returns the raw `sessions.files.list` / `sessions.files.get` response.

## Why This Change Was Made

- The command forwards the canonical owners and only shapes output: blank selectors and `--output` without `--get` are rejected before dispatch, transport failures exit non-zero, and the transport keeps its default timeout when `--timeout` is omitted.
- Registered beside the other gateway-backed session verbs; the parent `sessions` list selectors stay rejected.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/commands/sessions-files.test.ts src/cli/program/register.status-health-sessions.test.ts` → 27/27 passed locally.
- `oxlint --config config/oxlint/boundary-guards.json` → clean; `oxfmt --check` → clean.
- **Real behavior proof**: the branch was built through the shipped `build-all` (after refreshing the pinned `@openclaw/fs-safe` dependency the moved `main` requires) and exercised against a real Gateway booted from this checkout (isolated state dir, `OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1`):

```text
$ openclaw sessions files "agent:main:main" --timeout 120000 --json
{ "sessionKey": "agent:main:main", "files": [] }        (exit 0 — real sessions.files.list round-trip)

$ openclaw sessions files "agent:main:main" --timeout 120000
Session files agent:main:main
No files in this session workspace.                       (exit 0 — empty-inventory rendering)

$ openclaw sessions files x --output f.txt                (exit 1 — --output requires --get)
$ openclaw sessions files "   "                           (exit 1 — blank key rejected)
```

The fresh session workspace has no files, so the populated table rendering is covered by the unit tests; the live evidence covers the RPC path, empty-state rendering, and argument rejection in both modes.

## Risks

- None beyond the new verbs: no RPC, workspace, or config changes.

prs.body:

Related: #153678

## What Problem This Solves

Telegram mentions from chats where the bot is not a member currently have no native OpenClaw guest-request lifecycle. This adds an explicitly enabled, caller-allowlisted text reply path using Telegram’s guest API.

<!--
Describe the concrete user, product, or operational problem.
Use one short, plain-language sentence. For fixes, prefer:
"Fixes: <what goes wrong> when <trigger or condition>."
For other changes, describe the need without inventing a bug.
Name the affected workflow, not the code-level cause.
-->

## User Impact

- Disabled by default; each account has a numeric `guestMode.allowFrom` policy, independent of private DM/pairing grants.
- Account/channel bindings select the agent. Each guest interaction has a distinct public/group-like session, with tools and workspace bootstrap context disabled in this MVP.
- One final text answer through `answerGuestQuery`, with no ordinary chat-send fallback, streaming, media, or callbacks. Long text is safely truncated.
- Reuses polling/webhook ingress, duplicate tracking, durable adoption, account throttling, and live authority checks. Ambiguous delivery is not blindly retried.

The five-minute update-age cutoff and 60-second turn budget are local OpenClaw resource bounds, **not a documented Telegram query TTL or guarantee of query validity**. The public-context prompt is explanatory, not the security boundary: runtime tool restrictions and bootstrap filtering enforce the built-in path. Configured prompt/memory hooks and the actual model request still require separate acceptance evidence.

**Draft / not production-ready:** live Telegram acceptance is incomplete. This version is deliberately tool-free. Configured prompt extensions still need a public-context/memory-canary audit on the actual test Gateway. No production configuration, BotFather setting, deployment, or merge is part of this change.

<!--
"User impact: <what users, operators, or developers can now do or expect>."
Lead with the concrete outcome in plain language, usually one sentence.
For internal-only changes, say there is no user-visible change; do not invent a benefit.
Keep important risks, breaking changes, migrations, and required user actions visible here.
-->

## Why This Change Was Made

Unlike #83632, this is strict opt-in rather than `auto`, keeps account routing, and respects the SDK’s `SentGuestMessage` result. Unlike #95673, it adds no broad raw-ingress plugin hook. Guest delivery has a separate transport owner and cannot fall through to ordinary Telegram sends.

The code remains additive: no SDK/dependency update or runtime dist patch. A dedicated public-safe agent configuration is recommended.

<!--

Keep the body short. Leave file lists, internal acronyms, and root-cause walkthroughs
in the diff or optional <details>; include technical detail only when it explains
behavior or a material tradeoff. Do not hide risks or required actions in <details>.
-->

## Evidence

Base: `9651d6347b1ab99453e8e6b5105d10d7800d82dc` (managed fresh-main refresh, clean initial worktree and existing dependency cache).

- Guest/lane/account-throttle tests: **54 passed** across 3 files.
- Existing bot, webhook, and durable-ingress tests: **170 passed** across 3 files.
- New real bot-registration regression: **fails on the base, passes with this change**.
- Tool-prefix stability: **14 passed**.
- Supplemental production-owner enforcement tests: **30 passed** (tool construction, auxiliary-tool non-widening, and native execution restrictions).
- Real bootstrap resolver probe on a default user turn: full-context positive controls loaded synthetic USER/MEMORY sentinels; guest lightweight/group context produced **zero bootstrap files and zero prompt context files**, with no sentinels. This is prepared-context proof, not a captured model request or installed-plugin proof.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --noEmit`: **passed**.
- Changed-file Oxlint and formatting, `git diff --check`: **passed**.

The broader source-extension typecheck fails only in the untouched `deep-research/browser/index.tsx` and `pane.tsx` (missing `./client.js` and consequent type errors); targeted extension test typechecking is green. No authorized Telegram test bot/chat was available, so external group/private-chat round trips, live duplicate/restart behavior, and installed memory-plugin privacy canaries remain unverified. The handoff ZIP records reproducible commands and the remaining scenario matrix; mocked API tests are not presented as live proof.

prs.title: feat(automations): preview impact before changing default models
prs.body:
Related: #188761

## What Problem This Solves

Changing a default model can leave existing automations blocked by model policy or account/runtime compatibility, with no warning at the point of change.

## User Impact

Models and Agents settings show automation impact before changing the primary model, and ask for confirmation when enabled jobs have blockers or unknown compatibility. CLI and agent callers can inspect the same read-only result. Existing model overrides, account ownership, permissions, schedules, and expired work are not changed.

This is an advisory metadata preview, not proof that upstream inference, fallback attempts, tools, or delivery will succeed. Missing personal/native observations remain explicitly unknown. CLI `models set` reports unavailable assessment as unknown and preserves its existing offline save behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

One cron-owned assessment reuses scheduled model selection, account-route availability, and runtime checks. UI callers use it before autosave/config writes; `automations model-impact` and the model-facing `model_impact` action expose the same result and recovery guidance. This is the agreed preview-and-guidance first stage; bulk editing automation overrides is intentionally deferred. No migration or new configuration option is required.

## Evidence

### Current repair head `1c754b4c7b99b38aa0bee6b42a2a0941fb6db3c0`

Integrated pinned main `9651d6347b1ab99453e8e6b5105d10d7800d82dc` to resolve the existing integration/validation failures. The sole new-main conflict was reproduced and resolved by using main’s shared `InlineAlert` owner while retaining multiline status formatting; incoming main already mapped warning tone correctly. The repair rechecks execution-session visibility immediately before disclosure, separates agent-specific preview/dispatch admission from connection-owned settlement of already-dispatched global saves, breaks the static model-impact type cycle, regenerates the affected prompt fixtures, and updates the offline advisory assertion.

- **Authority boundary:** 3/3 registered-Gateway-dispatch tests pass. Real profiles, CronService, session storage and visibility projection prove that deleting execution session B during an awaited assessment withholds its payload while owner session A remains accessible. Both target modes fail against the original handler and pass with the repair. Catalog/read I/O is deterministic; this is not a separate WebSocket/live-model run. Wall time approximately 6½ minutes including red/green replay.
- **UI admission and settlement:** the repair passed 86/86 owner tests (6.08s wall) and 4/4 browser tests (36.05s). After the required current-main integration, fresh status/view/model-provider owners pass 84/84 (6.06s), and recovery + automation-impact + chat-session-diff browser suites pass 12/12 (37.55s). UI typecheck passes (4.75s), scoped lint exits 0 (5.53s; three warnings on unchanged helper lines 83–84), and formatting passes (0.07s). The exact stale-agent admission regression was red before the repair (2.93s). Agent page state is within its line limit without suppression. Production UI build passed.
- **CLI/tool/prompt consumers:** 197 tests across 7 files pass (132.01s). Models-set source-command replay passes 10 tests (54.71s) using `OPENCLAW_E2E_SKIP_BUILD=1`; this is source-contract proof, not full-runtime proof.
- **Domain/catalog:** 6 domain and 48 catalog contract tests pass (413.85s). The introduced dependency cycle was reproduced and eliminated; final cycle check reports zero. Core/selected Gateway typechecks, scoped lint/format and generated validator/prompt checks pass.
- **Historical CI reproduction:** chat-session-diff passed 8/8 (40.61s) and passes again as part of the current 12-test browser replay. The old failure did not reproduce; its historical cause is not claimed fixed.
- **Follow-up CI repairs:** `cron.modelImpact` now declares the actual current introduction train, `2026.11`; no global protocol/version was bumped. The exact failing since guard was reproduced red using CI base `19dd9d010911f689624776248c6ecbf19453603c`, then the full `pnpm protocol:check` passed (2.49s), including registry and Swift/Kotlin determinism checks. The Agents channel-read projection now explicitly exposes its original four-field contract, derived from canonical `ChannelsState`; there are no casts, copied state, runtime wrappers or padded fixtures. The exact UI-pages test-type gate failed before the fix (18.31s) and passes after (1.28s); production UI types pass (1.56s), and 98 tests across nine affected owner/view files pass (3.97s). Final three-file format, type-aware lint and whitespace checks pass (0 warnings/errors, 2.36s lint), without line packing. Test growth is unchanged.
- **Tool line-cap repair:** a later hosted pass reported the unchanged automation tool at 707 counted lines against its 700-line cap. The actual `check:line-cap-ratchet` reproduced the violation. The existing typed Gateway parameter-rejection classifier was moved unchanged into the existing Gateway adapter owner; all callers and authority handling remain unchanged. No wrapper, new module, cap raise, suppression, or test deletion was introduced. The full line-cap gate now passes (0.46s), scoped type-aware lint has 0 warnings/errors (2.7s), and all 66 automation-tool plus 14 prompt-prefix tests pass (51.36s total wall). The committed source passed the line-cap gate again before push.
- **Test cost:** exact feature-only growth is 1,426 LF lines with a matching separate allocation. Shared scalar is unchanged. The ratchet still reports 51 inherited base lines over the ceiling (6,553,451 lines versus 6,553,400); no unrelated debt was hidden. New-head CI seconds are not yet available.
- **Open proof limits:** ordinary full-runtime preparation fails before tests because the unrelated deep-research browser entry imports missing `./client.js` (also absent in pinned main and the inspected newer main). A fresh read-only invocation of the actual strict isolation fence now confirms separation from managed Gateway artifacts (`refuse:false`); the earlier isolation refusal is historical, not a current blocker. The supported isolated `qaRuntime` preparation still requires plugin assets, so it cannot omit the missing client source. Head-pinned CI on `84b7f294` reproduced this same unrelated failure before tests in a [39-second job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42284471202/job/128122526468), and extension typechecking reports the missing module as well. These are separate from the two attributable CI failures repaired above. This is not a product pass; no stale-dist replay, guard bypass, unrelated plugin repair, or current full-dist/real-Gateway pass is claimed.
- **Independent local review:** the full integrated feature completed 3/3 P0–P2 passes with no actionable findings. The complete CI-repair delta against `84b7f294` and the subsequent line-cap delta against `025356df` each received fresh independent review, exit 0, with no actionable P0–P2 findings and final source verification. The completed hosted reviews of `84b7f294` confirmed the five prior findings resolved, then requested the release-train and line-cap corrections now included here. Hosted review receipts are tracked in the PR discussion; local checks are not a readiness verdict. The existing re-review command is followed without duplicate submissions.

No upstream inference, credential acceptance, live scheduled-run, or WebKit claim. The original before/after and real-Gateway screenshots are retained as historical evidence; the current fixture captures below are not live-Gateway qualification.

<details><summary>Scope and simplification</summary>

One shared read-only assessment serves the UI/CLI/tool callers. Existing account/runtime mismatch and catalog auth-ref decisions are shared with execution/catalog consumers instead of copied. No new persisted state, migrations, fallback engine, or bulk-edit workflow. Most generated churn is validator renumbering. prs.body:
**Draft — patched candidate still lacks passing rendered completion proof.** The earlier patched run lost Jump after a 14-point departure. A fixture-only stock control now reproduces Jump disappearing at completion after the same 14-point departure, with visible text movement. This symptom predates the patch. The fresh patched variant did not run: its build failed on missing `sodium/version.h`. No passing paired comparison or complete fix is claimed.

Closes #194281

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the iOS live-edge policy treating a deliberate 15–40-point upward departure during a reply as still following the latest content.

## User Impact

On iOS, departures beyond 12 points release following and expose Jump to latest sooner (13–48 points now count as away). Bottom overscroll remains at the live edge. macOS keeps its existing 48-point tolerance. No migration is needed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use a 12-point iOS tolerance in the existing geometry owner. The predicate is extracted for focused tests; no new scroll state, positioning command, or renderer is added. New-turn keyboard behavior is unchanged.

Simplification pass: removed the old threshold owner and an earlier synthetic follow-state simulation. The final diff is 28 added and 2 removed lines, including independent threshold and bottom-bounce boundary assertions.

## Evidence

Native red/green proof against caaff17579aa55617ab207fb74ed1653dbe9c856, Xcode 27.2, iOS simulator:

- Stock policy: two Swift Testing tests ran; four expected assertion failures, exit 65.
- Patched policy: both tests passed, exit 0.
- git diff --check passed. Simulator compilation passed; lint was bypassed. macOS was not separately compiled.

**Rendered same-reply retention and Jump proof are pending.** These threshold tests do not prove reply-finalization viewport retention or rendered interaction. [Sanitized r1–r3 harness evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/194281) records the compile failure, pre-gesture fixture failure, and out-of-band 135-point gesture. None is presented as a product pass or failure. The final controlled-gesture attempt (r4) compiled and ran one UI test, measured a 14-point departure (inside the 12–48-point guard), then failed at reply completion: `XCTAssertTrue(jump.exists, "Completion restored following")`. This is a failing rendered test on the patched candidate, not successful retention proof. Jump restoration and the stock rendered control remain unproven. No further rendered attempt is planned; no phone result is claimed.

AI-assisted implementation and review. [Sanitized investigation record](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/194281) contains the test results and evidence limitations.
