prs.body:
Related: #183625

## What Problem This Solves

Verified personal Gateway profiles pass command allowlists but fail elevated profile-ID lists, and direct bash drops the admitted caller's cancellation before handing background work to exec.

## User Impact

Operators can list a verified profile ID, plain or `id:`-prefixed, in the global WebChat elevated list and any configured per-agent list. Direct bash retains the same live caller authority through preparation and background execution. Existing execution approval policy still applies.

**Shared `gateway-owner` attribution remains unsupported for personal-profile entries.** This does not resolve the reporter's shared-owner configuration, grant authority to client labels/synthetic callers, or narrow existing `*` behavior. No new configuration, migration, dependencies, protocol, or public SDK authority field.

## Why This Change Was Made

The elevated matcher now consumes the existing private live profile resolver through its normal identity-token owner, rather than a separate plain-ID shortcut. Command authorization already uses this principal. Mutable-name, From/E.164, application-ID, and configured global/per-agent boundaries remain separate.

Direct bash passes the already-issued reply authority and startup abort signal to the existing exec lifetime owner through a core-only adapter. The public exec API stays unchanged; no partial Gateway caller identity is fabricated. The public fixture consolidation is preserved, and overlapping new tests were combined without dropping preparation, approval, channel-owner, or retained-process controls.

## Evidence

**Head: `4ab8b17e93db7d9e256154777c2fb6a0c3005836`. [Exact-head CI 40714331943](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40714331943) and the [external aggregate 40721371642](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40721371642) passed; both required checks are green.** CI at `388cbb342d94` exposed a stale Talk test import; the exact CI base was integrated and the test migrated to the current owner. No compatibility export was restored. Prior-head CI is not admission for this head.

- **Real built Gateway + Control UI:** normal trusted-proxy login produced a personal profile through `users.self`; no seeded rows, forged authority, private handlers, or auth/device bypass. Exact global/configured-agent profile lists allowed harmless `/bash printf`; a configured agent mismatch denied at the agent gate. Pre-fix `e642` production denied at the global gate; restoring the repair and rebuilding passed.
- **Real retained-process comparison:** public `ec5` production allowed foreground execution but left the harmless background process alive for a bounded 20 seconds after actual current-device removal/disconnect. Restored repaired production cancelled it at the first observation. Both used the same setup. Browser reconnect was blocked only after loading Devices to observe the removed state; ordinary trusted-proxy login otherwise auto-pairs again. This is cancellation evidence, not a latency SLA or permanent login-revocation claim.
- **Source identities:** live proof used `c597020c` production, identical to the authored production at `388cbb34`. It is prior-base evidence, **not a current-head UI/build claim** after main integration. The `ec5` comparison overlaid its five production blobs at `c597` HEAD, not an `ec5` checkout; build metadata correctly remained `c597`. The authored permission/lifetime repair is retained after integration.
- **Committed regression shape red/green:** restoring only the original public bash caller made all three preparation-revocation rows incorrectly execute with `Exit: code 0`. Restoring the repair passed all 19 exec tests. After exact CI-base integration, eight affected files passed **116 tests in five shards, 70.56s wrapper**, including retained-process/approval/revocation, identity/Talk, and all 14 current prompt-prefix controls.
- The formerly failing Talk tests and test-type leaf now pass against the current authority owner. Targeted type-aware lint, canonical format, native staged-content/freshness guard, and diff checks pass. Independent full-candidate review found no P0–P2 findings before mechanical base integration; its three minor coverage concerns were addressed. The canonical autoreview CLI was not rerun for this head.
- **Budget:** the authored diff changes neither the upstream ceiling nor counting rules. Against integrated exact CI base `903394cc`, the unchanged staged checker passed **6,302,366 / 6,310,000**. Earlier lower-ceiling replays remain recorded historical failures; no baseline exception was added. The base was integrated for named import/type failures, not to chase main advancement.

Before — `e642` production rejects the verified profile:

![Before: verified profile denied at the global elevated gate](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f7c8c434-34df-46df-b617-0d4cd93b06c8)

After — prior-base repaired production executes the harmless command (not a new-head capture):

### Limits and required review

Security/execution-owner review remains required before merge; neither tests nor an advisory score grants that approval. Live proof used `security: full`, `ask: off`; approval registration/decision routing is covered by real exec integration with only network transport mocked, **not** a live approval-network roundtrip. No live shared-owner, Talk/audio, or node-host proof is claimed.

prs.title: fix(agents): preserve sandbox skills during concurrent runs
prs.body:
Closes #122554

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes sandboxed agents reading another run's skill instructions, or losing advertised skills, when concurrent runs refresh a shared skills directory.

## User Impact

An active run keeps its advertised instructions and companion files until its tools and asynchronous cleanup finish. Eligible copies remain readable by a non-host container user without changing source permissions. No configuration changes or migration are required. Sandbox owner/security review is appropriate for this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

Publish a retained catalog below the existing mounted directory and prepare the prompt from that exact catalog. Reuse the existing disposable sandbox result and asynchronous work owner; native staging locks preserve live catalogs and permit cleanup after a process dies. Settled turns keep their session's prompt locations. An ordinary copy failure omits that skill with a warning; required library selections still fail. Preparation copies each run's catalog rather than relying on mutable shared copies.

This builds on the investigation and unmerged implementation in #122679 by @eightHundreds, including its unresolved copy-failure, SDK-lifetime and abandoned-directory findings.

## Evidence

- [Exact reviewed PR head: full build and shipped CLI/Docker proof](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/actions/runs/39999276007) passed on `4b85835fc16692ebc86b491913b1f6f989df7a79`, checked out directly without applying a patch. Four real agent turns completed through the built CLI and Gateway with actual Docker reads. The [pinned workflow and controlled fixture](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/blob/17d181be4e9249a229235619ef1a833932c37d51/.github/workflows/pr-maintenance-proof.yml) reproduce the run; the HTTP model is synthetic and isolated to loopback.
- [Real baseline reproduction](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/actions/runs/39919765190): the first sandbox's advertised path reads the later run's replacement instructions.
- [Shipped Gateway/CLI and Docker comparison](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/actions/runs/39938841384): B and C finish while A is paused. Baseline A reads C's instructions and companion; repaired A retains its originals. Independent Docker UID 65534 probes read all four catalogs, including copies of a 0700/0600 source whose permissions stay unchanged. The model transport is synthetic, loopback-only, with no paid provider calls.
- [163 focused regressions and four type graphs](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/actions/runs/39938784366): context, publication, killed-process recovery, delayed cleanup, prompt stability, native dispatch and CLI controls pass; production/test types and changed-file lint/format pass. That run stops on six stale mock baseline rows, removed and verified in the next evidence link.
- [Final mock and line-cap guards](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/actions/runs/39940175612): pass, with exactly six obsolete baseline rows deleted. Its other 17 file patches are byte-identical to the validated candidate.
- [Generated-file Git discovery regression](https://github.com/yinx65588-boop/openclaw/actions/runs/39940988282): the existing Git-discovery test first exposes generated ownership files; the runtime-owned ignore fix passes 24 materializer/custody tests, targeted types, lint and guards.
- Independent Codex review of the final patch and coupled source modules completed in two passes with no actionable P0–P2 findings; source-consistency checks passed. This was source review, separate from the execution evidence above.

Exact-head result, verified against the downloaded artifact and source stamp:

```text
Source: 4b85835fc16692ebc86b491913b1f6f989df7a79
A pauses; B and C finish; A resumes: OriginalAlpha retained
B: ReplacementBeta; C: ReplacementGamma; D: PrivateDelta
Independent Docker UID 65534: all four instructions and companions readable
Original private source: directory 0700, SKILL.md 0600, unchanged
Model requests: 8; fixture failures: 0; paid provider calls: 0
Production build and shipped proof: success
```

The final change retains the existing mount, SDK disposer and async-work owner. The additional catalog publication/custody code is necessary to keep both instructions and companion files alive; production +394/-10, tests +362/-3, docs +6, and six obsolete mock-baseline rows removed.

Linux/Docker is exercised. Live SSH/OpenShell transport concurrency and Windows execution are not covered by this proof.

Repository automation note: [Auto response on this PR](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39999173725) fails in the unchanged Barnacle `isPrivilegedActor` code (`Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'owner')`). The [same failure on an unrelated PR](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40000071573) confirms it also occurs outside this change; it is separate from the sandbox validation above.

prs.title: fix: Muse requests stall or lose approval authority after reuse
prs.body:
Closes #183672
Related: #183282 (independent compaction fallback repair).

## What Problem This Solves

Muse requests can time out behind retained native work, replay an earlier answer into a new reply, or fail with `missing scope: operator.approvals` after reusing a process created by a narrower caller.

## User Impact

Status requests can join native work and receive its current answer. Approval requests use the current admitted caller while preserving genuine System scope limits and revoked-owner checks. Stopping an observation of earlier work detaches that observation; turns started by the current request retain normal cancellation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use `ifBusy: "steer"` and the SDK's authoritative started/joined identity. Observe real native tool progress, keep historical items out of the current reply, and fence publication after asynchronous transcript append.

Install approvals before resume traffic and bind each new handler to its prepared attempt context. Pooled stdio callbacks otherwise inherit the process creator's async context. Keep authority checks before host approval and native decisions, cancel pending approval UI when observation ends, and retire a failed SDK projection so a fresh owner can recover the same native session and approval stage.

This keeps approval handling in the harness and transcript/result projection in its existing event owner. No provider, dependency, configuration, permission-policy, or transcript-schema changes.

## Evidence

Validation ran on an isolated macOS arm64 host with Node 24.22.1, task-owned state, and the package-pinned SDK. Tested and committed source files were verified byte for byte.

Current head `da67db5d0bfc054fddaf142d884afd2af5209c13` integrates main `d4ae3a73118767a3f9bf80625a91733d19055393`. Its only conflict was the controlled MSP test helper; the resolution preserves both the native approval-effect controls and upstream helper simplifications. The Muse production harness, event owner, and process pool remain byte-identical to the native-tested parent `15457a3a`. All 60,327 tracked candidate blobs matched the isolated Gronk checkout. The 73 controlled tests, focused source and package-boundary typechecks, typed lint, formatting, and independent conflict-resolution review passed again against the integrated source and frozen current-main lockfile. The maintained lint owner prepared the SDK boundary declarations; no core/app build or additional real-model run was performed.

Parent and integrated-head evidence:

- **73 canonical tests passed:** the four non-live Muse suites (71) plus two real-SDK pooled-context regressions. These cover reply/history isolation, joined abort/timeout, native settlement lifetime, resume-time approval replay, deferred transcript publication, offered refusal safety, and completed-first history.
- The pooled-context regression failed before the fix with the exact missing-scope error. After the fix, one physical peer serves both attempts, approval dispatch carries the current run identity, and exactly one offered approval decision produces the native filesystem effect. The inverse control keeps full admitted authority under a genuinely narrow current System frame and verifies denial with no effect.
- Existing real-SDK controls verify that detached or revoked observations cannot make a native approval decision or effect, and that a fresh owner recovers the same pending stage. Their late-request barrier is causal. Tool-progress fixtures likewise wait for production observation rather than a fixed sleep.
- Package and focused regression typechecks, changed-file typed lint, formatting, and diff checks passed.
- Independent P0–P2 source review and structured autoreview found no blocking defects. The final equivalent factory capture location received a focused caller-chain review; review did not substitute for test execution.

Captured controlled-fixture results:

```text
uses the current full approval owner after reusing a pooled native peer: PASS
uses the current narrow approval owner after reusing a pooled native peer: PASS
Tests  2 passed (2)
Test Files  4 passed (4)
Tests  71 passed (71)
```

A matching operator compatibility port also passed a real isolated public Gateway approval-manager flow using SDK 1.4.2 and a controlled MSP peer: narrow warmup → full approval produced a final reply through the same physical host; full warmup → narrow caller remained denied. Its 28 regression controls passed. This is compatibility-port acceptance, not canonical SDK 1.4.10 native-provider/busy-turn qualification.

Real native-provider authority evidence was also captured on exact head `15457a3aebf4124de78ade51d6d478e31ee3e95c`: SDK 1.4.10, official Muse 1.4.13-R6996.1, Meta provider, Node 24.22.1/macOS arm64, and the published declared-compatible OpenClaw 2026.10.10-beta.3 host. The selected Muse target was built without changing minHost/compatibility metadata; this was not an all-main Gateway build. Native permissions used task-only `:ask-me`, with exact prehashed effects confined to the owned sandbox workspace.

- A genuine narrow warmup followed by a full current owner reused the same physical native host. One public plugin approval and one offered allow decision produced the exact owned effect after resolution.
- A separate native conversation on that same pool was warmed by a full owner, then resumed by a client negotiated with only `operator.read` and `operator.write`. Its real native approval request failed closed: one offered abort decision, zero allow decisions, zero plugin approval events, and no effect after all owned processes ended. The missing-scope Gateway diagnostic was fenced to that admitted run.
- The inverse runner's original **FAIL remains preserved**: `agent.wait` returned `error: "agent run failed"` without the detailed scope string its assertion required. Independent scoped adjudication accepted the authority behavior from the matched wire, run, diagnostic, and filesystem evidence; the runner was not relabeled green.

Captured redacted native result:

```json
{
  "head": "15457a3a",
  "sdk": "1.4.10",
  "samePhysicalPooledHost": true,
  "fullOwnerApprovedEffect": true,
  "narrowOwner": {
    "nativeAbort": 1,
    "nativeAllow": 0,
    "pluginApprovalEvents": 0,
    "effectAbsent": true
  },
  "originalInverseRunnerPassed": false,
  "scopedAuthorityAdjudication": "accepted"
}
```

prs.title: fix(discord): voice autoJoin flaps in and out when joining keeps failing
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a Discord bot with `voice.autoJoin[].whenOccupied` flaps in and out of the voice channel about once a second when joining keeps failing (for example, the realtime provider is down or the bot lost access to the channel).

## User Impact

User impact: when an occupied auto-join fails, the bot stays out of the channel and retries after a growing wait (5 seconds, doubling up to 10 minutes) instead of rejoining on every voice-state change. Discord `Missing Access`/`Missing Permissions` failures stop auto-join for that channel with one warning that says to restore the bot's View Channel and Connect permissions, then run `/vc join` or reload the config. A successful `/vc join` or a config reload clears the wait.

## Why This Change Was Made

Occupied auto-join reconciles on every guild voice-state update, including the bot's own leave after a failed start. Only credential-like errors were suppressed, so any other failure rejoined immediately and the bot's own leave scheduled the next attempt. In the reported incident this produced 119 join/leave cycles in under three minutes, then 140+ `Missing Access` lookups, and a voice-state queue backlog of 30–45 seconds per event.

The auto-join owner in `voice-runtime.ts` now keeps one failure record per guild/channel: fatal failures (the existing credential set plus Discord access errors) stay suppressed until a successful join or manager rebuild; other failures get bounded exponential backoff. Voice-state events during the wait return early without a join attempt, and a one-shot scheduler job rechecks the room when the wait expires so an idle room still recovers. Each failure logs one warning naming the next retry; skipped events log nothing. Cancelled joins and shutdown are not counted as failures.

Not changed here: GPT-Live error redaction (separate follow-up), and plain (non-`whenOccupied`) auto-join still retries only on gateway Ready/Resumed, now subject to the same backoff.

## Evidence

- New regression tests in `extensions/discord/src/voice/voice-auto-join.test.ts` use fake timers through the plugin scheduler:
  - transient realtime startup failure: the bot's own leave and another member's update do not rejoin; retry happens at exactly 5 s, then 10 s, and the third attempt connects.
  - Discord `Missing Access` on channel lookup: no further lookups across voice-state updates and an hour of time; an explicit `join` afterwards succeeds.
- Red on base `364c0d4` (runtime file reverted, tests kept): both new tests fail (`joinVoiceChannel` called 3 times instead of 1; `fetchChannel` called 3 times instead of once).
- Green with the fix: `pnpm test extensions/discord/src/voice/voice-auto-join.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` → 10/10 passed; wall time 41 s cold (Vitest duration 38.1 s, mostly transform; tests themselves ~20 ms), 9 s warm.
- Sibling voice/autoJoin consumers: `manager.ready-listener`, `transcripts-capture`, `transcripts-readiness`, `transcripts-target`, `voice-following`, `voice-receive`, `voice-runtime.e2e`, `voice-runtime.secret-owner.e2e`, `voice-session.lifecycle`, `voice-session.promotion`, `voice-occupancy`, `monitor/provider.lifecycle` → 12 files, 217 tests passed.
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` clean; `tsgo -p extensions/discord/tsconfig.json` reports no errors in changed files (its only error is an existing test-support import outside that config's scope); `run-oxlint` on both changed files clean, `oxfmt --check` on all changed files clean.
- Local autoreview (helper `source-sha256:d2b2d03f…`, default Codex engine), branch mode `origin/main` `364c0d4` → `f6afb3d`, max priority P1, with `voice-runtime.ts`, `listeners.ts`, and the scheduler sources as context: scoped-clean, no findings. The reviewer did not execute tests.
- Not run: live Discord e2e against a real guild. The live Team Gateway and its config were intentionally left untouched; the incident timeline above comes from its logs.

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @jalehman](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/7f538e07-7436-4691-aa09-77db4d1d11f9)
- [Implementation and verification](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/~key/dashboard/eef0742d-1019-47a6-b670-e6f8990c6b99)

## Worked on by

- @jalehman

prs.title: fix: chat inputs do not capitalize sentence starts on mobile keyboards
prs.body:
Closes #194304

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: chat inputs never auto-capitalize sentence starts when typing from mobile keyboards (Firefox for Android and any browser that honors the `autocapitalize` hint strictly), unlike every mainstream messaging app.

## User Impact

Mobile users get automatic sentence capitalization in all Control UI chat fields, matching Signal/Telegram/Messages behavior. Desktop browsers ignore the hint; no visible change there.

## Why This Change Was Made

Chrome defaults text inputs to sentence capitalization when the page says nothing, but Firefox for Android requires an explicit `autocapitalize="sentences"` opt-in. None of the eight chat free-text inputs requested it (the side-rail composer also sets `autocomplete="off"`, which further suppresses keyboard assistance). This adds the standard hint to each chat input: main composer, side-rail composer, new-session message, queued-message edit, custodian chat, question-answer multiline field, annotation comment, and goal objective. Intentionally untouched: password/secret fields, command palette, code/config editors, and remote-desktop keystroke passthrough inputs, which already opt out deliberately. Attribute-only, no logic change.

## Evidence

- Built the Control UI from this branch and grepped the shipped bundle — all eight inputs now render the hint, e.g.:
  `<textarea class=chat-session-rail__input rows=1 maxlength=400 autocomplete=off autocapitalize=sentences enterkeyhint=enter aria-autocomplete=list`
  (8/8 `autocapitalize=sentences` occurrences in `dist/control-ui/assets/`.)
- Existing suites for the touched components pass locally: `chat-composer-dom`, `chat-details-goal`, `chat-composer-content`, `chat-async-question`, `chat-annotations.browser`, `custodian-page` (3 files passed / 1 env-skipped, plus 3/3 in composer-content).
- Gap noted: no mobile-browser screenshot since the change is an invisible DOM hint; the bundle grep above is the direct before/after proof (before: zero occurrences).
- Same one-line fix accepted upstream in MeshMonitor: https://github.com/Yeraze/meshmonitor/pull/6217

prs.title: fix(telegram): keep progress and final replies after delegation
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Telegram can lose its progress card and final reply after an agent delegates work. A later user message can suppress an already accepted result, and retained cards can show an outdated plan. A yielded requester can also incorrectly treat consumed child input as fulfillment of its own final answer.

## User Impact

The conversation keeps one progress card while delegated work runs and the requester processes its results. A requester that yields while it still owes an answer must deliver its own final or a visible failure outcome. Ordinary child completion events can remain quiet, as intended by [#185388](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185388). Plan changes replace outdated steps; finished work disappears and explicit failures remain visible. Meaningful acknowledgments and streaming preferences are preserved.

Use `sessions_yield` with an acknowledgment for a waiting update when a final is still owed. A normal final “started” acknowledgment alone does not register a pending final. Progress remains process-local and is not restored after Gateway restart. Stop/reset and revoked authority prevent follow-up delivery; private child input is not automatically forwarded.

## Why This Change Was Made

The repair follows the existing completion and delivery owners:

- Accepted results retain their original caller, conversation and session. A new message retires old automation privileges without discarding a still-authorized result or borrowing the new turn's privileges.
- Progress follows the pending result through waiting and requester processing. Updated plans replace old steps; closed owners retire their rows.
- Telegram confirms initial card delivery before taking it over. The additive `adoptProgressDraftWithReply` contract preserves a normal reply alongside the card; optional `updatePlan` keeps retained cards accurate.
- A yielded requester's final obligation remains until its own visible-final receipt is recorded. Silent/empty settled output uses the existing bounded tool-free finalizer; exhausted recovery uses the existing missing-answer notice. Completed actions are not replayed. Ordinary quiet child processing and Peter's later [visible-unsent fallback coverage (#185840)](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/185840) are both preserved.

No new queue, job store, polling loop, permission model or generic blocked-notice producer is introduced.

## Evidence

### Current integration and remaining gates — 6 November

Published head: c3de6f290ad6dae7072b9f39eab354aaa12ac155, normally merging pinned main cddc5ee4baa2e466a27ff76d5243d6a7372b1ced into prior head 6a3462e75dffa9c9a1e98630ffb5d846728751c5. Four generated prompt conflicts were resolved with the canonical generator; all six snapshots are current. No upstream policy file changed.

Six canonical snapshots and whitespace against pinned main pass. These are bounded source/mock checks, not packaged Gateway, Bun E2E or live Telegram acceptance. No fresh full build, lint/typecheck or substantive independent review is claimed; this checkpoint resolves generated conflicts mechanically. Previous reviews retain their original revisions.

Direct Git-blob LF counts independently confirm historical CI: base 206d54934a3d0764cad0ea59a31d43f74bec0fa0 has 6,444,088 lines / ceiling 6,444,035; merge 29a067e728d57117565faddfb8e422daf4bcaf4a has 6,445,888 /6,445,835. Both are 53 over. On new pinned main the native exact-base check remains red: base 6,551,900 /6,551,849; candidate 6,553,700 /6,553,649, both 51 over. PR growth and existing allocation remain exactly 1,800. No scalar, allocation, assertion or counting rule was raised or weakened. Historical 291-line accounting below belongs to its older base.

The other historical failure was the Bun kill/restart test expecting no requests after SIGKILL but receiving two restart-resume requests. Included upstream [5b0e4e8c0c9](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/5b0e4e8c0c934c3d75b92bdbf66bb815dbc1fd95) already aligns this exact test with the crash-resume contract. The candidate test is byte-identical to pinned main and that repair; historical CI base and merge share the old test blob. This establishes source repair inclusion, not a new same-base Bun reproduction. The local E2E launcher consumes dist/index.js, whose build identity is f5f912cf17a4, not either comparison base or this candidate. prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A cold managed-worktree preparation can report `missReason=commit-changed` after incremental refresh was rejected, leaving operators unable to distinguish validation failure from refresh refusal.

## User Impact

The existing preparation record adds bounded `refreshRejectReason` and boolean `refreshAttempted`. The new fields contain fixed categories only, with no paths, session IDs, SQL, or raw errors. Workspace selection, leases, reader custody, retirement, fallback, and error propagation retain their existing behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

Record the actual eligibility, validation, attribute/policy, and Git-advance decision in `templateDetails`, preserving it when a fallback cold build later reports ready. Successful reuse clears the rejection reason. This attributes future observations; it does not identify the historical production rejection or claim a latency improvement.

## Evidence

- **Remote red/green on Node and Bun:** baseline production plus the regression (`405412aa1c305`) fails because both new fields are absent in [baseline job 127074071637](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41975550579/job/127074071637). The regression itself took 2734 ms on Node and 1699 ms on Bun in the candidate CI batch. Timing-contract tests also pass on both runtimes.

The existing integration file retains its worker-backed custody/clone coverage; its summed case times were 9.791 s Node / 5.280 s Bun, not standalone process wall times.
- Exact-head production/test types, regular core lint, pinned oxfmt on the four touched files, and `git diff --check` pass. Fresh independent Codex autoreview with complete owner context is **scoped-clean through P2**. No worker tests/builds or broad checks ran on the production Gateway host.
- [Exact-head CI 41973639627](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41973639627) has a **verified inherited** Knip failure for unused `scripts/bench-template-detail.mts`, matching scheduled main [41967849929, job 127049161515](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41967849929/job/127049161515). prs.title: fix(gateway): report retryable session work-start conflicts from OpenAI-compatible endpoints
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `/v1/responses` and the other OpenAI-compatible endpoints report `SessionWorkStartChangedError` ("changed while starting work. Retry.") as a generic HTTP 500 / `response.failed` with type `api_error` and message `internal error`, so clients cannot tell the request is safe to retry.

Closes #192465.

## User Impact

User impact: a client that overlaps two requests on the same session key now receives a 409 with a stable `code` (`SESSION_WORK_START_CHANGED` / `SESSION_WORK_START_INVALIDATED`) and the original "Retry." message instead of a hard 500 internal error, so retry logic can act on it exactly like the archived-session case.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveOpenAiCompatError` in `src/gateway/openai-compat-errors.ts` handles `SessionWorkStartError` with reason `archived` (409, added in #170029) and failover reasons, but has no branch for `SessionWorkStartChangedError` / `SessionWorkStartInvalidatedError` from `src/config/sessions/work-start-error.ts`. Those fall through to `describeFailoverError`, stay unclassified, and the caller (`openai-compatible-agent-run.ts`) emits the fallback 500 `internal error`. Both error classes carry stable `code` fields specifically so wrappers can classify them, and both are retryable conflicts like the archived case.

The fix adds one branch that maps `isSessionWorkStartInvalidatedError(err)` (which recognizes both classes and wrapped errors carrying the stable codes) to 409 `invalid_request_error` with the error's own message and stable code — mirroring the #170029 precedent.

## What Was Changed

- `src/gateway/openai-compat-errors.ts`: new branch mapping session work-start changed/invalidated errors (including wrapped errors that only carry the stable code) to 409 + stable code.
- `src/gateway/openai-http.test.ts`: three regression cases in a self-contained describe — changed error, invalidated error, and a wrapped error carrying only the stable code.

Not changed: the archived-session branch, tool-authorization and failover mappings, retry behavior inside the gateway, and the error classes themselves.

## Evidence

Real before/after through `resolveOpenAiCompatError` (the exact production mapping for these endpoints), run as part of the registered `openai-http.test.ts` suite:

```text
before (fix stashed): Tests 3 failed | 112 skipped — the mapping returns
  undefined, so the caller emits 500 {"type":"api_error","message":"internal error"}
  (matches the issue's production log)
after:                Tests 3 passed | 112 skipped — each error maps to
  409 invalid_request_error with its stable code and "Retry." message
```

- Focused suite: `scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway-server.config.ts src/gateway/openai-http.test.ts -t "session work-start conflicts"` — 3/3 passed.
- Full-file run for reference: 111/115 passed; the 4 failures are pre-existing environment-sensitive SSE/disconnect e2e tests in this heavy suite (15s streaming timeouts on a loaded local Windows machine), unrelated to this change and not touched by it.
- Format check (after formatter write) and scoped oxlint on both changed files: pass.
- Latest-main re-check at `3816bcb3dea1`: `openai-compat-errors.ts` still has no work-start-conflict branch, so the fix is not already upstream.
- Local full-repo typecheck was not runnable in this environment (it needs the generated `packages/plugin-sdk/dist` declarations, which the local build pipeline does not emit on Windows); the change reuses the existing error-class guards and mapping shape, and CI type coverage applies.

## Risks / Notes for Reviewers

- Status/type choice follows the archived precedent (409 + `invalid_request_error`); the stable `code` field lets clients branch precisely.
- Wrappers that only forward the stable `code` are recognized by the same guard the sessions layer already ships.

prs.title: perf(control-ui): render cached Subagents without awaiting live activity
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A signed-in warm reload with cached ordinary child activity holds every Details section until the live observer module loads. The cached display receipt already has the row geometry. This removes that admission wait and unblocks #194142's synchronous Details composition; that lane owns co-framing integration.

## Why This Change Was Made

Delete the composition-wide `prepared()` memo/Show and the unused activity preload import/export. Reuse the existing static `SubagentActivity` as the existing lazy boundary's fallback. The fallback receives receipt rows, or current query rows if the receipt retires before the module resolves, strictly as noninteractive presentation. The live observer remains behind the existing `createIdleImport` and dynamic import. Error containment and localized Reload recovery are unchanged.

There is still one receipt/projection owner. Empty/denied retirement, scope, caps, protocol and cache shape are unchanged. Cached rows confer no open/stop actions. Emitted source maps put the static row and live observer in separate deferred activity chunks, not startup/shared chunks.

## User Impact

Cached Subagents and the other Details sections render without waiting for live activity. Outputs and Automations remain stationary through the static-to-live handoff. Native first populated Details is earlier in 10/11 pairs: paired median **−32.3 ms**, just over half of the prior 60.4 ms admission. Unpaired medians are 1,394.3 → 1,328.8 ms, with separated IQRs. Team-scale improves by a paired median 8.8 ms, descriptive only.

Open follow-up, deliberately outside this change: four-or-more ordinary rows in the default expanded desktop section still exceed the bounded cached preview.

## Evidence

### Before/after (synthetic fixture)

Base `e27b909e49d3`: with two ordinary children already cached, the activity chunk held and connect deferred, the open Details panel still has no populated sections.

![Base held chunk; Details empty](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4e4288db-0eeb-4994-b953-7d589b01b5dc)

Candidate after the module and connect resolve: both live rows retain exactly the same Subagents, Outputs and Automations bounds as the first populated held frame (0 px maximum difference).

![Candidate live rows; unchanged Details geometry](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cd102e56-272f-4a49-bf99-5b0f9a746656)

Base `e27b909e49d33bd723a2cfc10e944845f00249b7`; candidate `e3b66a3a94b2c50dc5ddff763e8f2a7b5da4b2cb`. One dedicated AWS **c7a.4xlarge**, lease `cbx_267469c1ce10`, observed 16 vCPUs / 32 GiB, repository Playwright Chromium 156.0.8078.4. Native RTT 80 ms and Team-scale `live-capped`, 240 messages / 12 widgets, seeded ordinary children, warm cache, open Details, no persistent-children owner-filter override. Existing committed native and Team-scale workloads; unprofiled, eight-second windows, standing LoAF/mutation and RPC probes. Native alternates pair order; Team interleaves ABAB. Acceptance was recorded on this draft before capture.

The compared UI directories are frozen clean-source `pnpm ui:build` outputs. The Gateway uses `node scripts/prepare-native-protocol.mjs`, `OPENCLAW_BUILD_PRIVATE_QA=1 OPENCLAW_RUN_NODE_SKIP_DTS_BUILD=1 node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/build-all.mts gatewayWatch`, then `node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/write-build-info.ts`. Build/fixture preparation is outside capture. `BASE_UI` / `CANDIDATE_UI` name those frozen directories; `PROBE_DIR` contains the unchanged standing init probes. A/A replaces `CANDIDATE_UI` with `BASE_UI` in both commands.

```sh
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/warm-reload-proof.ts \
  --dist dist --ui-root "$CANDIDATE_UI" --base "$BASE_UI" --candidate "$CANDIDATE_UI" \
  --output .local/l295-sync/proof/native-ab --transcript-late-paint --details-session-facts \
  --active-targets --route chat --reloads 11 --rtt-ms 80 --capture-ms 8000 \
  --init-script "$PROBE_DIR/loaf-mutation.init.js" --init-script "$PROBE_DIR/ws-rpc-census.init.js"

  --bundle-dir "$BASE_UI" --compare-bundle-dir "$CANDIDATE_UI" --runs 22 \
  --warm-reload --untraced --latency-profile live-capped --gateway-http --port 19670 --sandbox-port 19671 \
  --row-facts --pane-chrome-facts --details-session-facts --details-subagent-activity \
  --sidebar-presentation --sidebar-cached-parity --full-uuid-route --face chat \
  --init-script "$PROBE_DIR/loaf-mutation.init.js" --init-script "$PROBE_DIR/ws-rpc-census.init.js" \
  --capture-ms 8000 --output .local/l295-sync/proof/bench-ab
```

First post-hello RPC send means the first serialized non-connect request on the authenticated WebSocket. Hello-handled is the application microtask completion mark; a request sent during handling can precede that mark.

Each harness has 11 A/B pairs plus 11 A/A pairs. **All 88 scored captures valid**; no discarded/replayed samples, missing hard metrics, truncated buffers or censored tails. At least 6.05 s native / 5.52 s Team quiet tail remains after final rows, last Details sample and visual/layout/mutation activity. Native A/A and Team A/A use identical frozen baseline bundles. Per-file hashes bind each bundle to its pinned clean source; native quiet-host idle samples were 81.0% and 75.9% on the dedicated 16-vCPU box.

Primary A passes **11/11** on both harnesses: first populated Subagents is already at final height (native **112→112 px**, Team **142→142 px**); Outputs/Automations movement is **0/0 px on every base and candidate capture**, including A/A, with no later section insertions/removals. prs.title: fix(research): restore the native pane browser client
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the native Deep Research plugin failing to build because its browser client was deleted before the pane that consumes it landed.

## User Impact

The native research pane can load its existing progress, evidence, cancellation and safe pending-start recovery behavior again.

## Why This Change Was Made

Restores the exact `client.ts` blob from #177231 (`d5a2338a9ade9f50c7bc090fb3661fc8d497080b`). The cleanup in `097f990aa24` removed it while it had no production caller; #177232 subsequently added the native pane and its imports. There is one client implementation, and the current caller and server contracts still match it. No dependencies, budgets, recovery rules, or UI markup change. Thanks @vincentkoc for the original implementation.

## Evidence

All green checks below ran against `3d436d5e3bb5bd2a049f440931bdf5f3b24ed258`; the [dispatch preflight](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42280171441/job/128106824344) confirms that checkout explicitly.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Plugin/runtime build | [Passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42280171441/job/128107842593). |
| Production extension types | [Passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42280171441/job/128107845306). |
| Native research account recovery | [Passed](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42280171441/job/128107843523): `restores uncertain starts only for the same account after a native remount`. |
| Native research pane behavior | [Passed in the same job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42280171441/job/128107843523): `opens native pane, safely navigates citations, handles cancellation/offline/reconnect and clears denied data`. |
| Red baseline | [Scheduled main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42279537309/job/128105175561) fails both native research cases with `Could not resolve "./client.js"`; its [build](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42279537309/job/128105174683) and [extension types](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42279537309/job/128105178895) fail for the same missing module. |
| Independent review | Codex autoreview, P0–P2, complete candidate against `077eac1f36f`: scoped-clean, no actionable findings. |
| Diff | Exact prior blob verified; `git diff --check` passed. Production +410/−0; tests +0/−0. |

Local builds, typechecks and tests were deferred to CI while this Mac runs a separately pinned timing census. The native tests use the actual built plugin and synthetic Gateway data. No rendering markup or styles changed, so there is no new visual diff.

The full manual run is not green: its package-boundary, dead-code and Goal replacement failures match completed jobs on scheduled main; broad Node-only unit checks also fail and are not claimed as passing or attributed by this evidence.

The ready PR's normal [`ci:full` run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42283614860) completed. Its only two non-aggregate failing jobs match the completed [scheduled-main baseline](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42279537309) exactly:

- [UI unit job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42283614860/job/128119443735): `Browser panel > renders async page loads and retains the page and focus through successful and failed refreshes`, same null-versus-`false` assertion as [main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42279537309/job/128105175133).
- [Goal E2E job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42283614860/job/128119443808): `Control UI goal replacement > confirms replacement from the literal command and Goal picker without restarting the goal` and `Control UI goal replacement > confirms a running goal without stopping on Cancel and adopts its resumed turn`, same missing `/goal ` prefix after Cancel as [main](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42279537309/job/128105175667).

The affected UI source and test objects are byte-identical on this PR's base, the scheduled baseline, and the actual tested merge. Hosted Codex review completed with no findings. Every other selected job passed or was intentionally skipped, including security-fast and both real-Gateway shards. Native landing uses the inherited-failure route with these exact names and unchanged source objects; no ignores, tests or budgets were relaxed.

The first draft dispatch ([42278556102](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42278556102)) stopped in preflight because `validation_tier=main` requires the workflow and target revisions to match. No payload check ran. The replacement dispatch used the documented default tier with the same target SHA.

prs.title: feat(agents): hide picker-hidden agents from user-facing pickers
prs.body: Related: #166678 ## What Problem This Solves Internal worker agents must be configured as full `agents.entries` entries to stay spawnable as `sessions_spawn` targets, so every user-facing agent picker (sidebar roster, agent switcher, New Session target picker) lists agents that are never meant to be chatted with directly. The only way to remove one from the picker today is to delete its entry, which breaks spawning. ## User Impact Operators can set `agents.entries..picker.hidden: true` to keep those agents out of user-facing pickers and switchers. Hidden agents remain valid `sessions_spawn` targets and stay listed by `openclaw agents list`, marked `(hidden)`, so an internal roster can stay out of the way without losing capability. Agents settings pages still show and manage them. ## Why This Change Was Made This is the config flag proposed in #166678. It rides the existing selectable-agent filter (`listSelectableAgents`), the same helper that already excludes system rows, so pickers, switchers, and the New Session target picker stay consistent with one rule while diagnostic and settings surfaces keep seeing every configured agent. The Gateway keeps returning hidden agents in `agents.list`; only presentation filters them. ## Evidence **PR CI** (first run, analyzed via `pnpm test:ci-failed 194280` + job logs): - `checks-ui (3/3)`: `browser-panel.test.ts` failed in CI and passes locally on this branch (33/33) — flaky, unrelated file. - `build-artifacts` (`Build dist`) and `check-prod-types`: both fail resolving generated `extensions/deep-research/browser/index.tsx -> ./client.js`; not reproducible here — `pnpm build` exits 0 and typecheck/lint are green on this branch, and the same files are untouched by this diff. - `checks-node-changed` (+ shards): failed in `Setup pinned Bun test runtime` / `Build Node test runtime` setup steps — infra. - `checks-fast-baseline-ratchets` (`test-lines`): `main` itself is over the ceiling by 32 lines (clean `main` worktree: `over by: 32; net delta: 0`, passes only as a non-growing notice). This PR adds +81 test lines and records exactly that in `config/test-lines-allocations/194280-picker-hidden.txt` (the maximum the checker allows: allocation credit may not exceed added lines). The residual 32-line inherited debt needs a maintainer `--prune`/offset; this PR does not touch unrelated tests to pay it down. No failure in this run points at the changed contract; the focused tests and targeted gates for the change are green. **Visual proof** (mocked Control UI via `pnpm dev:ui:mock`, Chromium, switcher menu open): - Before: `Show all / Molty / Forge / Scout / Bloom` — capture `picker-before.png` - After (`picker.hidden: true` on Scout): `Show all / Molty / Forge / Bloom`, Scout gone — capture `picker-after.png` Both inspected. Captures are retained as local artifacts (not committed) at `/tmp/opencode/picker-before.png` and `/tmp/opencode/picker-after.png`; the GitHub API cannot attach images, so they still need a manual upload into this PR — that is the one open evidence gap. **Focused tests**, all green: - `src/config/zod-schema.agents.test.ts` (25 pass) — accepts `picker.hidden`, rejects unknown picker keys and non-boolean values - `src/gateway/session-utils.picker-hidden.test.ts` (1 pass) — projection carries `hidden: true` for hidden agents and omits it for visible ones - `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/agents-models-skills.test.ts` (16 pass) — `AgentSummarySchema` accepts `hidden`, rejects a non-boolean flag - `src/commands/agents.commands.list.test.ts` (11 pass, 1 skipped) — text output marks `- worker (hidden)` while JSON keeps the row - `ui/src/lib/agents/display.test.ts` (25 pass) — `listSelectableAgents` / `findSelectableAgent` exclude picker-hidden rows **Targeted gates** (`pnpm check:changed`): typecheck core, typecheck core tests, typecheck UI, lint core changed files, format changed files, config docs baseline, mock-export ratchet, and all architecture/ratchet checks pass. The config surface deliberately grew by 2 (the new key), so `docs/.generated/config-baseline.{counts.json,sha256}` are regenerated in this PR per the config-surface bar. Two `check:changed` checks fail, both pre-existing on clean `origin/main` and unrelated to this diff (each reproduced in a clean `main` worktree): `changelog attributions` (`CHANGELOG/records/2026.11.1.md`) and the dead export scan (`extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-prompt.ts`).

prs.title: feat(gateway): echo resolved session key on chat completion responses
prs.body:
Related: openclaw/openclaw#183497

## What Problem This Solves

Callers of `/v1/chat/completions` cannot discover the generated session key for a request, so they cannot use that key to continue the conversation later.

## User Impact

- Authorized JSON and streaming responses return the resolved session key in `x-openclaw-session-key` when it is representable as an HTTP header value.
- If a key contains characters HTTP headers cannot represent (for example a Unicode `user` value such as `张三`), the header is omitted and the request continues normally. Existing session identity and routing are unchanged; callers can continue using their stable `user` value.
- The OpenAI response body is unchanged; its `id` remains the run ID (`chatcmpl_...`). Callers that need explicit continuation can send a returned header value as `x-openclaw-session-key` on the next request.

## Why This Change Was Made

The endpoint already supports explicit `x-openclaw-session-key` routing and stable `user`-derived sessions, but its default per-request key is random and was not disclosed in the response. Echoing the resolved, header-safe key closes that discovery gap without changing the OpenAI response body or existing routing behavior.

## Evidence

- `corepack pnpm test src/gateway/openai-http.session-key-echo.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` — passed. The real Gateway HTTP server test covers generated, `user`-derived, and explicit keys; streaming; rejected session targets; and a Unicode `user` request that still succeeds without the unrepresentable response header.
- `node scripts/run-format.mts --check` and `git diff --check` — passed.
- The focused HTTP test uses a mocked agent command; it proves the response and request behavior at the Gateway HTTP boundary, but it is not a real-model conversation/resume trace. The ClawSweeper review requested that live trace, and the related issue also asks maintainers to accept the standalone echo contract. Neither is represented as completed evidence here.

## Scope

This PR implements session-key echo only. Ephemeral storage and per-request TTL remain out of scope until their lifecycle semantics are agreed in #183497.

prs.title: fix(config): preserve malformed UTF-8 sources before writing
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `config set` can silently replace malformed UTF-8 in unrelated root/include text with U+FFFD and rotate lossy copies through recovery backups while reporting success.

## User Impact

Normal writes refuse malformed original sources before staging backups, preserving source and recovery bytes. Valid Unicode, emoji, intentional U+FFFD and BOM-prefixed sources remain accepted. Best-effort loading, recovery and explicit destructive-write authority keep their existing paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse `decodeUtf8Input` at the canonical publication guard's actual root/include reread, before backup staging. Both ordinary writers opt in. The decoder receives the bare source path, retaining its existing `<file path> must be valid UTF-8.` message. Existing path/hash/lock/authority/compensation checks remain. The existing decoder leaf is added to extraction inventory; no schema, permission, dependency or public API changes. @Alix-007's original commits are retained.

The review's short-write finding is repaired: only the already-owned `raw === null` copy-fallback destination uses the legacy read while a multibyte character is incomplete. Original sources and unchanged includes remain strictly decoded. The existing partial-write regression now splits a UTF-8 character and checks final bytes plus the original backup.

Duplicate root/include backup-warning setup is consolidated without dropping assertions. Whole PR tests are **+46/-48 (net −2)**, no allocation; production +16/-2, docs +3, inventory +1.

## Evidence

[Built CLI, short-write regression and released-version compatibility proof](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194181#issuecomment-6693776736) on `5bedaad0dac4`; [current-main integration and fresh focused tests](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194181#issuecomment-6694158188) on `bfe7ebc2a928`. Affected implementation/tests are unchanged across integration; all main inventory entries are preserved and the existing decoder leaf remains required.

- Pinned main twice and final built candidate twice, each covering real root/include malformed sources and valid controls. Main's four malformed writes succeed and corrupt recovery bytes; candidate refuses with every hash unchanged across 48 source/recovery file comparisons.
- Valid controls succeed with exact original backups and normal five-slot rotation. Best-effort reads are unchanged. CJK, emoji, intentional U+FFFD and BOM backup bytes remain legal.
- Actual latest stable **2026.11.1** published CLI writes valid Unicode root/include configurations. Final candidate reads and sets those same files using the same HOME/state, preserving values, recovery bytes and exact stable-source backups.
- The strengthened short-write case fails on the previous head and passes after repair. Five focused files: **177 passed, 5 skipped**; changed-file format/lint pass. Physical Windows/macOS execution is not claimed.

The earlier test-lines red was ours and is corrected without a ceiling change or allocation ([correction](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194181#issuecomment-6692406881)). Inherited deep-research browser/build failures have [an exact-main-parent reproduction receipt](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194266#issuecomment-6693087256); no unrelated repair or job rerun is included.

## Merge Danger

Two-way door for the guard: a revert restores lossy normal writes; no migration or schema change. Previously lost bytes cannot be recovered by reverting. Blast radius is ordinary root/include config publication and backup preparation, including copy fallback. Strict-original-source, valid Unicode/BOM, short-write, backup preservation and released-config controls cover false refusals; existing recovery and explicit destructive authority remain available.

prs.title: test(ui): measure repeated provider artwork loads
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The standard performance fixtures use built-in provider icons and do not exercise custom provider artwork. A picker can therefore repeat authenticated image work for every visible row and every filter update without appearing in the existing census.

## Change

Add an opt-in `provider-model-picker-artwork-cycles` scenario to the existing engines harness. It supplies 1,000 models sharing one synthetic image and counts image requests, response blob reads, and object URL creation/revocation while opening, filtering, closing, and reopening the real picker. It checks decoded row artwork, the exact filtered choice, restored focus, unchanged selection, and no configuration writes. Document the command and its diagnostic-only timing boundary.

There is no production UI change. The scenario deliberately reports the current repeated work rather than asserting that it is acceptable or establishing a latency regression.

## Evidence

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm tsgo:scripts` | Passed |
| `pnpm tsgo:ui` | Passed |
| Focused scenario, Chromium/WebKit/Firefox, desktop/mobile | Six cells passed; selection and focus preserved, no saves |
| Typed lint and formatting | Passed |
| Suppression inventory test | 14 passed; no new suppression |
| `git diff --check` | Passed |

With one shared image, the six cells read 190–259 response blobs and create/revoke 44–140 object URLs. These are work counts from an instrumented diagnostic, not latency measurements. One pre-existing selected/control image remains live before and after the cycle; all URLs created during the cycle are released.

The first probe attempt incorrectly expected the empty selection option to contain artwork. The readiness selector now checks actual model choices. The corrected scenario passes in all six cells.

Production delta: 0 lines. Harness/documentation delta: +196 lines (harness 240→423). The growth supplies the missing fixture, lifecycle counters, and user-visible assertions; no new dependency or runtime abstraction.

CI caught shadowed local names, captured method receivers, and then the suppression inventory guard. The final probe binds methods to their real receivers and instruments only matching fetch responses. Both targeted lint and the unchanged suppression guard pass; all six browser/viewport cells were rerun successfully on that final implementation.

### CI attribution

Final head `73bbdbb8` has passing lint and test-type checks. Its primary run [42276267907](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42276267907) fails extension production types because the newer main merge imports a deleted `deep-research/browser/client.ts`. The separate artifact build fails resolving that same import. Completed scheduled main [42279537309](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42279537309) has the exact same four type diagnostics and build failure. This PR changes neither Research imports nor their configuration. The native inherited-failure route retains those failures; it does not claim green CI. Research restoration is tracked separately in #194283.

prs.title: fix(backup): backups and updates fail on slow storage when a header probe batch misses its deadline
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw backup create` and update backup discovery still fail with `SQLite header probe timed out` on slow or cold storage, because 4,096 paths can miss the 10-second deadline even after #187197 batched them.

Refs #193962, #187150

## User Impact

Backups and updates now finish on slow disks instead of refusing. A path that can't answer on its own still refuses the backup, and how long that takes is bounded. This needs a release containing it as the updater; it does not repair an installed 2026.10.10 or 2026.11.1 updater.

The docs also gain the recovery for those installed updaters, which we ran end to end: warm the file cache and retry, or take the manual hop using `openclaw backup create --no-include-workspace --verify`.

## Why This Change Was Made

#187197 gives each 4,096-path batch its own 10 s deadline, which works down to about 410 paths per second. Cold reads on spinning disks, NAS volumes and SD cards can be slower than that, and then the backup fails even though every file is readable.

When a child reports `ETIMEDOUT`, `probeSqliteHeaderBatch` now splits that batch in half and retries each half with the same deadline. A batch that does finish still answers every path it was given, and results are validated as before. Only a single path that can't answer in 10 s rethrows, which keeps the existing refusal, its message, and the link to the manual procedure.

Rejected: raising the deadline, because a hung mount would then block for longer before anything is refused. Rejected: treating a timed-out path as non-SQLite, because that would fail open.

Accepted cost: on a filesystem where one path hangs, the refusal now comes after up to 13 timeouts (about 130 s) instead of 10 s, since the batch has to split down to that path.

## Evidence

Real CLI `backup create` on Crabbox (AWS Linux, Node 24.22.1), with a cold cache, on a dm-delay device adding 10 ms to reads, 20,150 paths:

| Build | Result |
|---|---|
| main `2a2cd29` | rc=1 in 20 s, `SQLite header probe timed out after 10000 ms while checking 20150 backup paths` |
| this branch `02c7477` | rc=0 in 241 s; `backup verify` scanned 20,154 entries and verified the SQLite inventory |

Later commits on this branch change only docs and the test file, plus a merge of main. The test file nets zero added lines.

Regression test: the new case in `src/infra/sqlite-header-probe.test.ts` fails on base and passes with the fix. The existing timeout-refusal case and `backup-create.sqlite-header-probe.test.ts` pass. Lint and the core and core-test typechecks pass locally. `$autoreview` is scoped-clean at P2 and an independent Codex review returned NO FINDINGS.

The docs claims come from native runs on published builds, 320,000 small files under `~/.openclaw/workspace`, 4 vCPU, EBS, cold cache:

| Path | Result |
|---|---|
| 10.10 → 11.1 `openclaw update` | rc=1, `spawnSync node ETIMEDOUT`, Gateway stays healthy on 10.10 |
| Warm the cache, then the same update | rc=0 in 959 s, healthy on 11.1 |
| 10.10 full `backup create --verify` | rc=1 in 33 s |
| 10.10 `backup create --no-include-workspace --verify` | rc=0 in 6 s |
| Manual hop to `@latest`, and to `2026.11.5-beta.1` | healthy on the target, all files present |
| main `2a2cd29` updater → relabelled main | rc=0 in 342 s, healthy; worst batch 3.65 s of 79 |

The warmed retry isn't guaranteed: one warmed full backup timed out while a heavy build saturated the box, and the docs say it depends on the host. Not run on Windows or macOS.

No schema, protocol or config change.

prs.title: fix(ui): catalog dashboard e2e stalls in reconnect on loaded runners
prs.body:
Related: openclaw/openclaw#190824 (CI run 41404623180, job `checks-ui-e2e` 6/7, failed on an unrelated head)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: the Control UI model catalog dashboard e2e test (`ui/src/e2e/model-catalog-dashboard.e2e.test.ts`) intermittently times out in its `reconnect` step on loaded CI runners, with the UI stuck in `reconnecting`, failing unrelated PRs.

## User Impact

No user-visible change. The test no longer flakes in its reconnect step, so unrelated PRs stop failing `checks-ui-e2e` on it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The compact replay pauses Playwright's virtual clock and drives each action by polling `page.clock.runFor(50)` inside a 15 s real-time `expect.poll` budget. The `reconnect` step calls `reconnectMockGateway`, whose offline → new socket attempt → online → connected transitions are awaited in real time with `page.waitForFunction`. That couples two clocks:

- The step needs about 1 s of virtual time, the transport's first reconnect delay (800–960 ms), so about 20 polls. When polls are slow, the 15 s budget runs out first and the UI is left in `reconnecting`, which is the CI signature.
- When polls are fast and the host lags, virtual time passes the browser socket's 30 s opening deadline. The offline attempt closes and backoff grows (observed: a second attempt after a 1.4–1.6 s backoff).

The reconnect step now runs with the clock ticking, the way boot already does, then pauses it again. That matches the other suites, which call `page.clock.resume()` before `reconnectMockGateway`. The helper now documents that it expects a ticking clock. Assertions, timeouts, and row attribution are unchanged; the reconnect row still waits for its post-reconnect catalog read.

## Evidence

- **Mechanism, instrumented locally:** a probe logged virtual time, socket states and `connect` counts on every poll.
  - Normal run: the new socket appears after ~0.9–1.0 s virtual (~20 polls). The offline socket stays CONNECTING (the mock never fails it), so backoff does not grow in normal timing.
  - Host held 30 s before `setOnline(true)`: the offline socket closed at ~31 s virtual, and the next attempt came after the grown backoff.
  - No local timing reproduced the CI failure unthrottled: 6 parallel copies, 6× page CPU throttle, and 8 s host lag all passed.
- **Throttled variant (900 ms real host delay per virtual-time poll), same harness applied to both:**
  - base `0809cf31e693`: 2/2 failed at `reconnect` with `expected false to deeply equal true`, readiness `{gatewayPhase: "reconnecting", rosterReady: false, ready: true}` (identical to the CI dump).
  - this branch: 2/2 passed all 24 rows.
- **Bounded loop, 20 runs each of base and this branch, unthrottled, two parallel workers on a host at load average 110–143:**
  - base: 19/20. The failure was organic: it stopped at `reconnect` with the CI signature above, after the 15 s poll budget.
  - this branch: 20/20.
- **Checks:** `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` clean on the changed files. The local oxlint wrapper timed out preparing plugin-sdk boundary types under host load; CI lint covers it.
- **Review:** Codex autoreview (local diff vs `0809cf31e693`, P0–P1): scoped-clean, no findings.

Gap: the CI failure dump has no transport state, so which of the two modes the CI runner hit is not proven. The fix removes the coupling behind both.

prs.title: fix(security): isolate install-policy tests from host temp permissions
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes 18 install-policy test failures when `TMPDIR` has a non-sticky, group-writable ancestor. Found while validating #186817.

## User Impact

No product behavior change. Developers can run the install-policy suite when their checkout or temp directory lives below a 0775 volume or directory; policy commands under writable parents remain rejected.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fixture at `src/security/install-policy.test.ts:119` on base `2270152d224ae48de9a10f3fe26b4c594ac9e87d` called `tempDirs.make()` without an explicit root. `test/helpers/temp-dir.ts:14` selects `os.tmpdir()`, so even a private 0700 fixture inherited unsafe ancestors. The production guard correctly rejects these at `src/security/install-policy.ts:178`, before the command can run.

Create each POSIX fixture under canonical `/tmp`, whose root-owned sticky directory is accepted by the existing policy. The shared tracker still creates private 0700 directories and owns cleanup. Windows retains the existing temp-directory selection. Reuse the per-test fixture for the writable-parent and symlink cases instead of allocating redundant roots; the explicit 0777 child and all assertions remain intact. Production delta: 0 lines; test delta: -1 line. Completed the pr-simplify pass; no new helpers or policy exceptions are needed.

## Evidence

Reproduced before any source edit on unmodified `origin/main` at `2270152d224ae48de9a10f3fe26b4c594ac9e87d` after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`:

```sh
mkdir -p .artifacts/install-policy-proof/group-writable
chmod 775 .artifacts/install-policy-proof/group-writable
TMPDIR="$PWD/.artifacts/install-policy-proof/group-writable" node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/security/install-policy.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

Before (exit 1; absolute fixture path abbreviated):

```text
AssertionError: expected { blocked: { …(2) } } to deeply equal {}
"reason": "install policy failed closed: security.installPolicy.exec.command parent directory permissions are too open: <worktree>/.artifacts/install-policy-proof/group-writable"
Test Files  1 failed (1)
     Tests  18 failed | 8 passed (26)
Duration 268.43s
[test] failed 1 Vitest shard in 286.05s
```

After, the identical command and 0775 parent (exit 0):

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  26 passed (26)
Duration 34.83s
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 48.69s
```

This includes the writable-parent negative controls and the real forked-child timeout test. The first run built the repository's compiled-worker artifacts; the second reused them. CI timing is pending; CI was not waited for.

Validation:

```sh
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.config-cli.json --incremental
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.core.json src/security/install-policy.test.ts
pnpm format:check src/security/install-policy.test.ts
git diff --check
node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/check-test-lines-ratchet.mts --base origin/main
```

Ratchet (exit 0):

```text
Test lines: 6479092; ceiling: 6479000; over by: 92; net delta: -1. Tree is over the ceiling; this change does not add test lines.
```

All validation commands above passed. Independent Codex autoreview covered the complete local diff against `2270152d224ae48de9a10f3fe26b4c594ac9e87d` at P2 coverage and returned `scoped-clean`, with no accepted/actionable findings. It also inspected the unchanged production policy and temp-dir tracker. The measured post-fix case durations total 2.379 seconds; the longer command wall time includes worker preparation and cleanup.

prs.body:
Related: #191974

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: `openclaw agent --config-override` errors show a blank path when the bad key is at the top level, so `{"sessions":{"allowThreadTargets":true}}` gives `Invalid --config-override: : Unrecognized key: "sessions"`.

## User Impact

User impact: that error now reads `<root>: Unrecognized key: "sessions"`, so a key put at the top level by mistake says where it is. Paths into arrays change too, from `agents.list.0.id` to `agents.list[0].id`, which is how the reload log and the other config errors already print them.

## Why This Change Was Made

Same gap #191974 closed for the reload log. The message goes through the shared issue formatter with the root label on, rather than building each line itself.

## Evidence

The new row in the rejected-override table in `agent-exec.test.ts` fails on `main` (it gets `: Unrecognized key`) and passes with the change. 

Here's the real CLI from a fresh checkout of this branch:

```
$ node --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs src/entry.ts agent exec hi --isolated --config-override '{"sessions":{"allowThreadTargets":true}}'
Invalid --config-override: <root>: Unrecognized key: "sessions"
```

Same command with `src/commands/agent-exec-input.ts` put back to main's version:

```
Invalid --config-override: : Unrecognized key: "sessions"
```

The committed test row fails on main and passes with the change. That's `vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts src/commands/agent-exec.test.ts -t 'rejects invalid override'`, which gives 1 failed and 5 passed on main, and 6 passed here.

@clawsweeper re-review

---

`/config set` builds the same line by hand in `config-mutations.ts`, so a top-level typo there probably shows the blank path as well. I haven't tried it, so it's not in here.
