prs.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/180602

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a `--session main` automation with no delivery config fails every run with `plugin delivery capability is no longer active`, before the model is called, when the main session is used from a channel DM with the default `session.dmScope`.

## User Impact

User impact: scheduled check-ins that continue the main conversation run again for people who talk to their agent in a DM. Before this change, every run failed silently, and each failed run was carried into later turns as interrupted input.

## Why This Change Was Made

Scheduled session turns minted their message-action turn capability under the execution session key (`agent:main:main`). Plugin tool delivery and the message tool look the capability up under the run's runtime policy key, which is peer-scoped for a DM-routed main session (`agent:main:<channel>:default:direct:<peer>`). The lookup missed, so the scheduled branch in plugin tool delivery was skipped, and tool construction threw.

The scheduled mint now binds the same key as ordinary replies: the turn's runtime policy key, falling back to the session key. The fix is at the producer, so every consumer keeps its single lookup key.

The scheduled path started minting this capability in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/178764.

## Evidence

Tested at `69e2e6951b7`, which merges `upstream/main` `5ed4aa230f8` into this branch; the PR's own diff is unchanged. The checks and the authority-chain run below used the same tree as this head, built at `3c1257965ef` (the diff between the two commits is empty). The fail-to-pass run (base `5ed4aa230f8`) ran at this head. The Before/After and control runs are from the earlier head: base `b0d3cd303a0`, after-side build `7d1723c57be`. At the new head, the authority-chain run's first job shows the same After behavior: its scheduled send reached the provider and Alice's DM.

An isolated Gateway (Linux, Node 24.18.0), built from each side, ran in a loopback-only network namespace with its own state directory and no provider keys. It used a local IRC server for the DM (default `dmScope`) and a local OpenAI-compatible stub provider that records each request. The automation was created and run through the built CLI: `openclaw automations create --name checkin-main --every 1h --session main --message "…"` (no delivery config), then `openclaw automations run <id>` twice, with an ordinary DM before and after. The output below is the Gateway's error lines, the stub provider's request count per step, and the stored job state.

Before (base `b0d3cd303a0`):

```text
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=cron-nested error="plugin delivery capability is no longer active" errorName=Error taskKind=cron sessionKey=agent:main:main runId=<run>
Embedded agent failed before reply: plugin delivery capability is no longer active
[session-events] session event execution failed source=cron agentId=main sessionKey=agent:main:main eventId=<event> error="Session event execution failed"
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=cron-nested error="plugin delivery capability is no longer active" errorName=Error taskKind=cron sessionKey=agent:main:main runId=<run>
Embedded agent failed before reply: plugin delivery capability is no longer active
[session-events] session event execution failed source=cron agentId=main sessionKey=agent:main:main eventId=<event> error="Session event execution failed"
provider requests: 4 (alice 4)
job checkin-main: lastStatus=error lastError="Session event execution failed" consecutiveErrors=2
```

After (this PR):

```text
provider requests: 6 (alice 4, run-main 2)
job checkin-main: lastStatus=ok consecutiveErrors=0
```

Observed result: on the base both scheduled runs failed before the model call and only the DM turns reached the provider; with this PR both scheduled runs reached the provider, no errors were logged, and the job is `ok`.

Controls, unchanged on both sides: a main session started with `chat.send` (`provider requests: 5 (chat-1 1, chat-2 1, run-main 2, chat-3 1)`, job `ok`), and an owner-announce job on the DM-routed main session (`provider requests: 6 (alice 4, run-proactive 2)`, job `ok`).

Authority chain, with this PR, same isolated Gateway and IRC DM. The roster has two agents, `main` (bound to IRC) and `spare`. Two `--session main` jobs for `main` have no delivery config. The stub provider answers each job's turn at once with a `message` tool call (`action: "send"`, `channel: "irc"`, `target: "alice"`).

A proof-only plugin, loaded from a local path and not part of this change, registers a `before_tool_call` hook on `message`. The hook holds the second job's send after the model returned it and before the tool runs. While the send is held, the job's owner is retired through the built CLI: `openclaw config patch` removes `main` from `agents.entries` and moves the IRC binding and the system agent to `spare`. The Gateway applies this as a hot reload: no Gateway restart, no cron restart, and no cancellation of the run. Then the hook lets the call through unchanged. The hook only waits; it never blocks or edits the call.

The run key stays split from the policy key: the hook sees the run under `agent:main:main`, while the send's capability is bound to Alice's DM policy key, which is the only key the first send can redeem under.

The output below is:

- the stub's request log;
- the hook's lines;
- the CLI result;
- the Gateway's reload and tool lines;
- the two jobs' run receipts from the state database;
- every line the bot sent on IRC.

```text
provider request 1: alice DM, stub reply text
provider request 2: alice DM, stub reply text
provider request 3: send job run, stub reply tool:message
provider request 4: hook-held job run, stub reply tool:message-hook-held
hook: hold message send "HOOK_HELD_SEND 4" sessionKey=agent:main:main runId=<run>
hook: release message send "HOOK_HELD_SEND 4" (released, tool call aborted=false)
cli: openclaw config patch --file retire-main.patch.json -> Applied 3 config update(s). Change will apply without restarting the gateway.
[reload] config hot reload applied (agents.defaults.systemAgent.agentId, agents.defaults.authInheritance, agents.entries.main, agents.entries.spare.workspace)
[tools] message failed:
[diagnostic] lane task error: lane=cron-nested error="Session target preparation outlived its attempt: Error: admitted run authority is no longer active | cron job agent is unavailable: main" errorName=Error taskKind=cron sessionKey=agent:main:main runId=<run> modelFallbackCandidate=true
cron_run_receipts send job: status=ok delivery_attempt_state=started
cron_run_receipts hook-held job: status=error error_text="Session event execution failed" delivery_attempt_state=not-started
IRC bot -> alice: <ordinary reply>
IRC bot -> alice: <ordinary reply>
IRC bot -> alice: SCHEDULED_SEND 3
```

Observed result:

- The scheduled turn's `message` send reached Alice's DM (`SCHEDULED_SEND 3`). Its receipt shows the delivery attempt started.
- For the second job, the model had already returned the send when the owner was retired. The run was not cancelled: the hook released the call with `aborted=false`. The `message` tool then failed, and the run's admitted authority was refused (`cron job agent is unavailable: main`).
- The second job's receipt shows the delivery attempt was never started, and no `HOOK_HELD_SEND` line reached IRC.
- This scenario was run on the PR build only; on the base the same job shape fails before the model call, as in the Before run above.

Revocation does not depend on the key this PR changes. Closing the scheduled admission revokes the capability token from the store, and the capability's active check reads the store before each delivery attempt, so a revoked token is refused whatever session key it was bound to. This PR changes only the key used at mint.

Cross-peer redemption (Alice's grant under Bob's runtime identity) is not proven through a real transport client, because no product path produces it. A turn's capability token is carried only in its own run's signed runtime identity, and the Gateway redeems it under that run's id and session key: the `turnCapabilitySessionKey` lookup in `src/agents/tools/gateway.ts:535-541` and the identity check in `src/gateway/server-methods/message-action-context.ts:168-180`. Presenting Bob's identity with Alice's token would mean forging that signed identity, which no product path does, and a forged identity would not prove the real owners. So the regression test in `agent-runner-execution-session-events.test.ts` pins this at the owner instead, and this point is left to maintainer judgement. The scheduled grant redeems under the turn's own runtime policy key (`agent:main:irc:default:direct:alice`). It does not redeem under another peer's key (`…:direct:bob`), and it does not redeem under the shared execution key that the base used. The redeeming checks are unchanged: one lookup by agent, run, session key and session id, then the delivery-attempt fence before outbound I/O, which `src/agents/tools/message-tool.scheduled-lifetime.test.ts` covers for revocation during send.

Checks: the touched test (`pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1`, wall time in the table below); the nearby scheduled-turn and message-capability suites (`session-event-config-readmission`, `session-event-handoff`, `agent-runner-execution-message-authority`, `message-tool.scheduled-lifetime`; 87 passed together with the touched test); `tsgo` on `test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.messaging.json`; `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on the changed files. The new test (`agent-runner-execution-session-events.test.ts:204-236`) fails on the base (`expected undefined to be defined` at line 233) and passes with the fix. The broad suites run in this PR's CI.

| Test file | `--maxWorkers=1` wall | CI seconds |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-execution-session-events.test.ts` | 17.2s on this head's tree (Vitest duration; 70.9s with a cold worker compile) | 14.6s at `ac947109e97` ([`checks-node-changed-1`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/39785814621/job/119849515354)); the new head's CI runs after this push |

Not covered: real Telegram, Discord or Slack DMs (the trigger is any direct chat route under the default `dmScope`; IRC was used here), live model providers, other owner retirements that leave the run alive (the run above retires the agent; job removal and cron config changes also cancel the run), cross-peer redemption through a real transport client (see above), and automations created by the agent's own cron tool.

prs.title: fix(fetch): retain response metadata when releasing request ownership
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: official plugins lose a fetched response's URL, redirect status, and response type when `responseWithRelease` retains request ownership, including when cloning that response.

## User Impact

Official plugin consumers can inspect the actual final URL and redirect status while retaining the existing body-release behavior. `fetch-runtime` is a private-local JavaScript host export for official plugins, as documented in the SDK subpath catalog. This is a response-metadata correction with no API, configuration, or dependency changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the metadata/recursive-clone handling already used by the abort wrapper. Keep the release wrapper's copied Headers and native clone isolation; preserve the abort wrapper's existing header behavior. Body ownership, cancellation, and exactly-once release remain with the existing owner.

This is the same boundary/lifecycle defect class as the externally contributed, maintainer-merged #181655; it fixes a separate metadata-loss bug.

## Evidence

- Real loopback HTTP server, native `fetch`, and built `openclaw/plugin-sdk/fetch-runtime`, without mocked responses: a 302 to `/final` originally gives the native response a final URL, `redirected=true`, and `type=basic`. Before the fix, the release wrapper, its clone, and its clone-of-clone report `url=""`, `redirected=false`, and `type=default`. After the fix, all three retain the native metadata. Direct responses are also checked; every payload stays `complete`, and each request releases exactly once.
- Red regression: six existing SDK checks pass; both new HTTP metadata cases fail on the base. Final focused tests at `81e393e872429d0c737fc6a83e62046a87d0cd62`: **16 pass on Node; 15 pass and 1 existing Node-specific test skips on the pinned Bun**. Both direct/redirected HTTP cases and mutable-header isolation pass in each runtime.
- Canonical `tsdown-build.mts` SDK/runtime compilation, owner and changed-test typechecks, targeted lint and format check passed. The earlier sparse working-tree test-line check passed; the full-index baseline failure has since been repaired by the upstream synchronization described below. The broader `cliStartup` build compiled successfully but its subsequent plugin-assets stage stopped at an absent unrelated `@discord/embedded-app-sdk`; no full startup-build pass is claimed. The built SDK HTTP reproduction passed again after this build. All repository execution used an isolated, secretless container with independent dependencies and the pinned Node/pnpm toolchain. Typechecking used the lock-integrity-verified musl build of the same pinned tsrs version through its supported binary override to accommodate the container libc.
- Simplification: one existing metadata/clone decorator now serves both wrappers; no new exported abstraction or finalizer. Production delta +32/-20; tests +66 lines. Those lines cover real direct/redirected HTTP and the distinct mutable-header compatibility boundary (explicit test allocation: 66).
- Independent full-diff review found and resolved an initial header-sharing regression, then passed the final three-file change at `bbb49031459ee4fae4086baf39b873d79de59d4a`. After the CI portability repair, the complete three-file diff was independently reviewed again at `81e393e872429d0c737fc6a83e62046a87d0cd62`. The complete rebased diff was independently reviewed at `424490831ce4f039e323f70e8ab5ed9a765afdfd`, including unchanged patch identity and the repaired full-index gate. Local `autoreview` could not start because the configured provider contains unsupported `stream_max_retries`; no autoreview pass is claimed.

- **CI runtime repair:** pinned Bun returns native `Response.type="default"`, while Node returns `"basic"`. The test now compares with `original.type`, preserving the metadata invariant rather than hardcoding Node semantics. The production fix is unchanged. Native HTTP assertions through the owner supplement the earlier unchanged built-SDK proof on both runtimes; this test-only repair does not claim a new whole-SDK build.
- **CI baseline repair:** the previous failing merge snapshot reported 6,479,568 test lines against a 6,479,548 ceiling (20 over), despite exactly +66 test lines and +66 allocation in this PR. The original branch snapshot separately reproduced 86 inherited lines over its ceiling. Rebased onto `34e607682be52d3a35419daf8ba923ac10c49a1e`, which includes the maintainer-approved inherited-debt repairs (#193183 and #188338). The complete three-file PR patch is byte-identical before and after rebase; no product code, tests, allocation, or checker policy was changed for this CI repair. The canonical full-index check now passes at `424490831ce4f039e323f70e8ab5ed9a765afdfd`: **6,493,587 lines / 6,493,616 ceiling / 29 spare**. Whitespace and exact-patch equivalence checks passed. Earlier test/build/lint evidence remains tied to its stated prior head; fresh current-head [CI run 42030060124](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42030060124) passed, including the formerly failing [baseline ratchet](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42030060124/job/127254542586), all selected tests/typechecks/lint, and the aggregate CI gate. Hosted ratchet output exactly matches the local full-index result: 6,493,587 / 6,493,616, slack 29.

Scope: this proves the built SDK runtime boundary and lifecycle on Linux/Node, with current native-owner and committed-regression validation on the repository-pinned Bun; it does not claim full release, other-platform, or live-provider validation. Broader coverage is left to PR CI.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the observable boundary</summary>

After installing and building the checkout, run:

```sh
pnpm test src/plugin-sdk/fetch-runtime.test.ts src/infra/net/guarded-body-stream.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
```

The committed regression uses a real HTTP redirect and direct response. The independent built-SDK check imports `openclaw/plugin-sdk/fetch-runtime`, fetches a loopback `/redirect` → `/final`, calls `responseWithRelease`, then clones twice and drains all bodies. Its observed output was:

```text
Before: native   /final  redirected=true   type=basic
        wrapped  ""      redirected=false  type=default
        clone    ""      redirected=false  type=default
        grandclone ""    redirected=false  type=default
After:  native, wrapped, clone, grandclone all /final redirected=true type=basic
Both:   bodies=[complete,complete,complete]; release=1
PASS: shipped SDK preserves fetched metadata, cloned payloads, and exactly-once release
```

</details>

prs.title: fix(agents): private CLI completions lose delivery under restrictive profiles
prs.body:
Related: #121661

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: a private subagent result can fail to reach the user when the requester uses a restrictive tool profile such as `coding`, or a CLI backend that does not retain the full requester tool surface.

## User Impact

User impact: a verified private completion can relay its result to the requesting conversation through `message`, while its final answer stays private. Explicit tool denies, frozen policies, channel action gates, and grant revocation remain authoritative.

An additional completion messaging grant is restricted to sends in the original channel, account, conversation, and thread, and cannot become general messaging authority for spawned children or cron jobs. Existing requester permissions are preserved.

## Why This Change Was Made

Current main already restores the normal Claude CLI requester tool surface. The remaining repair uses the explicit `privateCompletion` flag, carries source restriction independently of automatic final-reply delivery, and keeps the admitted completion allowance through the actual Gateway tool projection. The same policy merge helper preserves explicit denies and frozen allowlists at both stages.

The earlier destination-scope rationale in this PR was incorrect. This revision uses the existing source-reply guard for the additional grant. It also follows the current media contract: #176594 permits source-conversation photos and attachments through normal media validation; this PR does not restore the obsolete text-only restriction.

Integrated main at `650091daacdc10aa374e82a6327e8beffe136072` to resolve the stale branch conflicts and preserve current runtime selection and requester-tool retention.

## Evidence

At `bed203a26ff9c7aac301f0bff632b97d23895318` (tree `30b8d9d69f3d1a9983b45bc4f12f445b877763dc`):

- Production typecheck passed (`tsconfig.core.json`).
- Focused typecheck of all four changed test entrypoints, extending the repository root-test configuration, passed. It caught and fixed the current-main MCP startup API change.
- Type-aware lint passed for changed production files, tests/support, and the CI inventory; formatting, `git diff --check`, and the line-cap ratchet passed.
- The test-line ratchet still reports **51 inherited lines over budget**. At the integrated base the measured total is 6,551,687 and the effective ceiling is 6,551,636. This change adds exactly 663 test/support lines and a separate 663-line allocation, preserving that pre-existing difference. No shared baseline increase is included.

The complete Gateway → private parent completion → CLI runner → minted MCP grant → message tool → Telegram transport fixture passed **5/5** in [CI job 128116367053](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42282734165/job/128116367053). Only model decisions and external Bot API responses are synthetic. CI checked merge `328504c21532c5402858ade03a23c749cf1aa84e`, combining this head with main `9651d6347b1ab99453e8e6b5105d10d7800d82dc`.

| Scenario | Verified result |
| --- | --- |
| Ordinary private completion | Exactly one send containing the child result |
| Coding profile | Exactly one allowed send; other chat/thread and non-send probes rejected |
| Explicit operator deny | No completion message tool or child-result send |
| Disabled Telegram send action | Tool error and zero child-result sends |
| Revoked grant | HTTP 401 and zero child-result sends |

The five reported case durations total 122.7 seconds. This expensive composition stays in the release-only tier except for changed-file CI because admission-only tests miss authority lost between projection and dispatch.

The [CLI attempt suite](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42282734165/job/128116366616), including the new private/coding/other-CLI cases, and [MCP grant-context suite](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42282734165/job/128116366918) also passed. CI lint and all five core test-type stripes passed.

Full CI is red on an unrelated current-main defect: [production type checking](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42282734165/job/128116569548) and some asset-building jobs cannot resolve `extensions/deep-research/browser/client.js`. The browser directory has identical filenames and blob SHAs in main `9651d634` and the tested merge; both lack that module. This PR does not change those files.

The [CI baseline-ratchet job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42282734165/job/128116365654) also confirms the same inherited test-line debt on main `9651d634`: total 6,552,688, ceiling 6,552,637, over by 51, PR net delta +663. The separate allocation covers exactly the PR's +663; all other ratchets passed.

Local runtime attempts did not start tests: the worker compiler exceeded a 3 GiB cgroup limit, including a retry with a smaller Node heap; a narrow unit selection needed the same compiler and was stopped. The CI run supplies current-head GREEN proof. A fresh full-flow RED control, a real Gemini process, and Telegram Test Server were not run; the older-head live trace is not treated as evidence for this implementation.
Independent Codex source review covered the production and regression changes against `650091daacdc`: no actionable findings. This was an independent source review, not an autoreview or ClawSweeper execution. The existing private-delivery owner cases cover suppression of nonempty private final text; the new integration fixture itself returns `NO_REPLY`.

Simplification retained the existing runtime-selection and policy owners and removed unused photo/document assertions. Against the integrated base: production +38 net lines, regression tests/support +663. The exact 663-line test allocation is justified by the end-to-end authority boundary: admission-only tests miss a grant lost during CLI projection. The expensive integration is release-only except when selected by changed-file CI; the shared test baseline is unchanged.

prs.title: fix(macos): open session logs without the code shell command
prs.body:
Closes #190151

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the macOS session menu's "Open Session Log" action doing nothing when VS Code is installed without its `code` command on the GUI search path.

## User Impact

Session logs open in the installed VS Code app, or appear in Finder when the editor is unavailable or cannot open them.

## Why This Change Was Made

Resolve VS Code through macOS Launch Services and observe the open result through the existing app-activation owner. This preserves the activation policy and Finder fallback.

## Evidence

### Attached production-menu screenshots

These are saved, unedited window captures from a repeat of the same production-menu checks on November 1 at 4:54–4:55 PM ET. Brian clicked the native menu and saved the Screen Sharing window; I inspected both PNG files before uploading them. They contain only the disposable guest and synthetic fixture.

The native executable is still at reviewed head `4a375b5278d01e90346e586b7ebf0020e85e968a`, SHA-256 `d1442816618c18cf3643d8a0af3a7dfeaad0c98ebb939ded1796ffdeba3eacd6`. The exact transcript is `fd4be50b-93c8-40db-a31b-e225c5087b60.jsonl`, with SHA-256 `fceff4d1096421809122302f0342d1c71dcd735f1fd0c4b175e685675da50e11`.

**VS Code outcome.** After choosing OpenClaw → Session log proof → Open Session Log, real Microsoft VS Code displays the transcript tab, full task-state breadcrumb path, and synthetic marker. The native app launch PATH still has no `code` command.

![Real Microsoft VS Code displaying the exact synthetic session transcript after the production menu action](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6e77da68-2348-454c-b0e7-37ab15c2e638)

**Finder outcome.** After making the task-installed editor unavailable to Launch Services, the same menu action brings Finder forward with the JSONL selected in its `agent` folder. Finder abbreviates the selected icon label; the full matching filename remains visible in the editor tab behind it. This was the menu's reveal action, not a separate manual Finder selection.

![Finder selecting the synthetic JSONL after the same production menu action with the editor unavailable](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/834a0670-ef43-4949-8cc2-10ca8336edba)

The read-only Launch Services query returned `resolvedEditorPath: null` before the Finder capture at 21:54:58 UTC and afterward at 21:57:01 UTC. The reviewed native process was PID 828. The already-running Code process, PID 393, remained behind Finder but was unavailable to bundle lookup. The app and transcript hashes above were rechecked afterward. The editor bundle and registration were then restored, and its signature and lookup were verified.

### Native menu with real Microsoft VS Code and Finder

Validated November 1 on an isolated macOS 27.0 guest, build `26A428`, at unchanged PR head `4a375b5278d01e90346e586b7ebf0020e85e968a`.

Built and launched the full native development executable with its SwiftPM resources. prs.title: fix(macos): keep attach-only save failures visible
prs.body:
Closes #190153

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the macOS Debug "Attach only" toggle silently failing when it cannot save the setting.

## User Impact

The toggle reports a failed save and returns to its saved value. A permission problem can be corrected and retried without the rollback erasing the error.

## Why This Change Was Made

The marker write now throws on failure. A user-action binding owns persistence, so updating the displayed value after a failed save cannot trigger another write that clears the error. There are no new settings or storage formats.

## Evidence

- On unchanged main `c8f87b2e516`, a non-root disposable macOS 27.0 guest exercised the real marker setter against a task-owned read-only directory. The new creation regression failed because the setter returned nil even though the marker did not exist. The complete owner suite finished with 24 tests and this one expected failure, 0.062 seconds.
- With the repair, all 111 tests in GatewayLaunchAgentManagerTests, GatewayProcessManagerTests, and GatewayAutostartPolicyTests pass in the guest, 17.267 seconds. The new table covers both write directions, unchanged saved state after failure, successful retry, and idempotency.
- The native app and test bundle compile with `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests --disable-automatic-resolution`, 101.86 seconds.
- Pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.1, SwiftLint 0.65.1, and `git diff --check` pass. Fresh independent source review found no actionable P1/P2 findings.

The full macOS formatting check passes. The full lint script reports two inherited file-length violations in unchanged DashboardManager.swift and GatewayConnection.swift; both files are byte-identical to the base. The local sandbox also prevented SwiftLint cache writes. Lint of every changed file passes without a cache.

Actual-app before/after proof was captured in the disposable guest on November 2. With the task-owned state directory at mode 0500, the baseline app's failed removal returned the toggle to on and erased the error. The fixed app kept the saved on state and displayed the permission error. Restoring mode 0700 and retrying turned the control off, removed the marker, and cleared the error. Failed creation likewise kept the control off and showed an error; a writable retry recreated the marker. The test directory is back at mode 0700. This was a new offline profile with no running Gateway, operator credentials, or live account data.

![Before: failed-removal rollback silently clears the save error](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5e1dabea-74b4-4fbd-ac50-8d2a48392281)

![After: failed removal retains the saved state and permission error](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8e917158-e598-4700-bfd2-df8d0d93211a)

![After: failed creation reports the save error and stays off](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/70a7209b-cdb0-4005-a941-2a93b63bc54f)

![After: restoring write access lets the retry succeed and clears the error](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d38548c9-6e09-4350-9228-ed8fedbf563a)

The production change removes one net line; the regression adds 23 Swift test lines. Release-note context: macOS attach-only preference save failures remain visible and can be retried.

AI-assisted. Thanks to @anmol0b for reporting both failure paths.

prs.title: fix(macos): use recognition language for Talk pause timing
prs.body:
Closes #190154

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes macOS Talk submitting Japanese speech too soon, or delaying English turns, when Talk's recognition language differs from Voice Wake's language.

## User Impact

Native Talk applies its existing two-second CJK minimum pause to the language actually selected by Apple Speech, including fallback from an unsupported language. Longer configured pauses remain unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Native recognition startup owns both the selected recognizer and its pause window. Configuration no longer infers recognition timing from Voice Wake. Realtime-to-native fallback uses the same configuration and recognition path.

## Evidence

### Full signed-app turns through a real Gateway, agent, and model

On November 2, 2026, the signed production macOS app completed real microphone turns on a Mac Studio through a separate real Gateway, isolated agent/workspace, and existing local model via the vLLM-compatible provider. These were actual `OpenClaw` main-executable launches, not XCTest entry points. Recognition, native lifecycle, Gateway submission, model inference, and system playback were live. The launcher only selected test configuration and started/stopped the app; it supplied no recognition, transport, model, or playback mocks.

The app and its genuinely staged matching runtime were built from `aaecc05b7d9375eeccf6f4e91c14b72ac833a25b`, version 2026.10.9, and signed through the normal macOS signing script. Strict bundle verification passed. Current head `88f4d2b2f57` changes only the tests from that production build; the production source is identical. The separate Gateway was release 2026.10.9, commit `8b18b55`.

| Apple recognition | Voice Wake | Actual startup path | Gateway/model outcome | Playback |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| en-US | ko-KR | Native | Recognized `Hello`; real `chat.send`, model HTTP 200, completed assistant reply | System speech completed; user heard reply |
| ja-JP | en-US | Native | Recognized `こんにちは`; real `chat.send`, model HTTP 200, completed assistant reply | System speech completed; user heard reply |
| ja-JP | en-US | Realtime opted in, incompatible Gateway bootstrap configuration, native fallback | Recognized `こんにちは`; real `chat.send`, model HTTP 200, completed assistant reply | System speech completed; user heard reply |

Sanitized log excerpts below use ET. Request/device identifiers, model identity, endpoints, and credentials are omitted. Transcript checks used only the requested synthetic greeting and its associated assistant reply.

```text
English, native:
15:34:37.967 talk.runtime speechLocale=en-US silenceTimeoutMs=700 macOSRealtimeOptIn=false
15:34:44.654 Gateway chat.send accepted
15:34:49.714 model response provider=vllm status=200
15:34:50.132 Gateway agent.wait completed with assistant reply
15:34:50.448 talk.tts talk system voice start chars=46
15:34:54.879 talk.tts talk system voice done

Japanese recognition, native:
15:40:40.230 talk.runtime speechLocale=ja-JP silenceTimeoutMs=700 macOSRealtimeOptIn=false
15:40:50.438 Gateway chat.send accepted
15:40:53.541 model response provider=vllm status=200
15:40:54.158 Gateway agent.wait completed with assistant reply
15:40:54.461 talk.tts talk system voice start chars=51
15:40:58.894 talk.tts talk system voice done

Japanese recognition after actual fallback:
15:51:16.229 talk.runtime speechLocale=ja-JP silenceTimeoutMs=700 macOSRealtimeOptIn=true
15:51:16.229 talk macOS realtime relay opted in but Gateway tuple is incompatible:
                 mode=missing transport=missing brain=missing; using native fallback
15:51:16.238 talk realtime unavailable; using native fallback:
                 Gateway realtime Talk configuration changed before startup
15:51:28.107 Gateway chat.send accepted
15:51:31.820 model response provider=vllm status=200
15:51:32.244 Gateway agent.wait completed with assistant reply
15:51:32.666 talk.tts talk system voice start chars=46
15:51:37.103 talk.tts talk system voice done
```

The fallback is a real app transition after the real Gateway's native-only configuration lacks a compatible realtime tuple. No exception or bootstrap dependency was injected in this full-app run. This does not claim a live realtime-provider outage or reconnection test. The complete full-app turns establish product flow; exact silence duration was not instrumented in these runs. These captures establish turn completion, not normal application shutdown; the fallback fixture was forcibly stopped after its audible reply and TTS completion.

For audible Japanese-recognition checks, the isolated agent was instructed to answer in English while recognition stayed ja-JP and Voice Wake stayed en-US. An earlier run produced a Japanese model reply and logged system playback completion, but the user heard no speech. That result is not counted as audible proof. The unchanged macOS system-playback path uses Voice Wake's language when the response has no explicit language directive; Japanese-language playback remains outside this timing repair. Realtime opt-in in the final fallback run is confirmed by the actual app log.

The Gateway used isolated state, synthetic conversations, disabled tools/discovery, and a separate loopback port. Only the existing local-model provider credential was used with explicit permission. No normal operator Gateway or normal app profile was modified. Raw microphone audio, private configuration, credentials, device identifiers, non-public endpoints, and unrelated captured input are not published.

### Runtime regression replacing the helper table

The helper-composition table is removed. `TalkModeRuntimeNativeLocaleProofTests` applies real configuration, enters actual `startRecognition`, and observes the selected Apple recognizer and applied pause window. Identical test source was compiled against base `c8f87b2e5163870671510659745f4167239ff50e` and the fix.

| Runtime startup | Base | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ja-JP recognition, en-US Voice Wake, 700 ms configured | Fails: 0.7 s, expected 2.0 s | Pass: 2.0 s |
| en-US recognition, ko-KR Voice Wake, 700 ms configured | Fails: 2.0 s, expected 0.7 s | Pass: 0.7 s |

The fixed run passes both argument cases in 0.035 seconds with no issues. The base run reports exactly the two expected window assertion failures. Separately, 50 current tests in `TalkModeRuntimeSpeechTests`, `TalkModeConfigParsingTests`, and `TalkModeRuntimeReplyTests` pass in 1.816 seconds.

The opt-in startup regression requires `OPENCLAW_TALK_NATIVE_SETUP_PROOF=1`, available Apple Speech services, and no usable input device. It ran in the disposable macOS guest with a process-only audio-service denial. It reads the runtime's private recognizer and applied window through reflection, so private field renames require updating the test. Unused playback cleanup is stubbed; recognition startup and cleanup are real. This tests the applied startup state before missing-input rejection, not microphone timing or full-app completion. The real microphone runs above cover the latter boundary separately.

### Earlier isolated microphone timing measurements

At the same production source `aaecc05b7d93`, signed native-capture test-app runs exercised real Apple recognition, silence monitoring, finalization, and submission to an in-memory Gateway. These measurements exclude agent/model execution and playback; they are supplementary timing evidence, not the full-product proof above.

| Recognition | Voice Wake | Startup | Configured effective pause | Observed last-activity-to-submission |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| en-US | ko-KR | Native | 0.7 s | 1.298 s |
| ja-JP | en-US | Native | 2.0 s | 2.483 s |
| ja-JP | en-US | Injected realtime-startup failure to native | 2.0 s | 2.508 s |

Observed submission time includes recognition shutdown and dispatch overhead. Each measured run captured real speech, received a nonempty Apple transcription, submitted it, exited 0, and completed its Swift Testing event stream without issues or skips. The injected failure applies only to this earlier harness row.

### Other checks and review

- The native app and test bundle compile with `swift build --package-path apps/macos --build-system native --build-tests --disable-automatic-resolution`.
- The unchanged shared `OpenClawKitTests/TalkConfigParsingTests.swift` also passed: 11 tests in 0.002 seconds in the guest. Its exact source was temporarily compiled into the native test bundle and filtered by suite name; this was not a separate shared-package `swift test` invocation.
- Pinned SwiftFormat 0.63.1 and SwiftLint 0.65.1 pass for the changed test files. `git diff --check` passes. The earlier full lint found two inherited file-length violations in unchanged DashboardManager.swift and GatewayConnection.swift; no claim is made that those were repaired.
- A fresh independent Codex source review of the runtime regression replacement found no actionable likely or high-impact findings. The opt-in environment and reflection limitations above remain explicit. This is source review, not maintainer approval or proof of a ClawSweeper rating.

AI-assisted. Thanks to @anmol0b for reporting the mismatch.

prs.title: fix: reach the configured owner on project-parent sessions_spawn preflight
prs.body:
Closes #182467

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: project-attached `sessions_spawn` rejects a plugin-resolved child model (`deepseek/*`, native `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5`) as `Unknown model` or `selected account or native runtime is unavailable`, even though the agent's configured owner knows the model and a normal session on the same installation accepts it.

## User Impact

User impact: a Child spawned from a project-parent session resolves provider-plugin and native-runtime models the agent's configured owner already knows, without the operator having to detach the project or `/reset` the session.

## Why This Change Was Made

A project-parent read supplies the project workspace to `withPreparedModelCatalogOwner({ readOnly: true })`. `resolveReadOnlyPublishedModelCatalogOwner` builds two candidates (`full`, `activationFull`); both carry the explicit project workspace, so the resolver's exact-key lookup misses the single configured owner published at the agent's workspace. The configured-workspace fallback inside `resolvePublishedOwner` is also gated on strict workspace equality, so it misses too. The code then falls through to `acquireReadOnlyPreparedModelRuntime`, which builds a runtime-free ephemeral catalog without the provider plugin registry — the plugin's `resolveDynamicModel` hook is never invoked and the model is reported as unknown.

This change narrows the preflight to a third read-only candidate that probes at the agent's **known configured workspace** (resolved via `resolveAgentWorkspaceDir`, not any arbitrary workspace) with every other identity dimension carried from the caller and `env` bound to the effective process environment so the resolver's env match stays exact instead of degrading to the wildcard branch. If the configured workspace is not resolvable, the fallback is suppressed and the existing ephemeral read-only path takes over, preserving the prior behavior for that shape.

Agent, agent-directory, inherited-auth, environment, and generation isolation are preserved exactly. Writable publications and non-read-only paths are unchanged.

## Evidence

- New unit coverage in `src/agents/prepared-model-catalog.test.ts`:
  - Positive: project-parent read falls back to the configured workspace with agent, agent-dir, env, and workspace identity verified in the fallback input; the fallback carries a plugin-provider model that is absent from the ephemeral read-only snapshot.
  - Negative: when a competing publication matches by workspace but diverges on agent / agent-dir / env, the fallback rejects it and the ephemeral read-only path takes over.
  - Suppression: a workspace-less caller does not synthesize a second workspace-less probe.
  - Guard: when the agent's configured workspace is unknown, the preflight skips the project-parent fallback and lands on the ephemeral read-only build.
- Full targeted test suite (6 files, 119 tests) passes locally:
  - `src/agents/prepared-model-catalog.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/prepared-model-runtime.owner-selection.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/model-runtime-choice.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/model-runtime-choice.native.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/subagents/spawn/subagent-spawn.workspace.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/openclaw-tools.subagents.sessions-spawn.plan.test.ts`

<details>
<summary>Review notes</summary>

Marked draft pending maintainer sign-off on scope. ATX reviews surfaced a residual architectural suggestion to gate configured-workspace reuse behind an explicit, validated project-parent predicate; introducing such a predicate expands scope beyond the acceptance criteria recorded in the issue's Codex review ("preserve agent, account, environment, and generation isolation"; "a focused inventory-owner correction"), so it is deferred.

</details>

prs.title: fix(clawrouter): stop sending Claude to Responses after catalog loss
prs.body:
Closes #188562

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Claude inference and compaction being sent through OpenAI Responses when a selected ClawRouter model disappears from discovery after a restart.

## User Impact

An unresolved ClawRouter selection now fails before dispatch with an actionable refresh/model-selection message. Valid retained routes and explicitly configured model APIs remain supported. Temporary upstream unavailability still needs to recover; this change does not bypass router grants or rate limits.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawRouter owns its upstream protocol choice. Its dynamic model preparation now rejects a catalog miss unless a known catalog route or explicit model-level API exists, rather than falling through to the facade's provider-wide Responses default. Generic custom-provider fallbacks are unchanged. No new cache, configuration option, or migration is introduced; production growth is nine lines.

## Evidence

- The restart-resolution regression fails on base `20310449b39ca71c0d9b3ce93677d046620db39b` with Claude incorrectly resolved as `openai-responses`, and passes with this fix. prs.title: fix(chat-ui): keep a budget-rejected voice note recoverable
prs.body:
Closes #193813

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: finishing a voice note in a nearly full attachment draft destroys the recording. `addVoiceNoteAttachment` deleted the capture file in an unconditional `defer`, the aggregate-budget rejection from `stageAttachment` was ignored, and the recorder returned to idle — so removing another attachment could not recover the note, and the only copy of the recording was gone.

## User Impact

User impact: a capture the aggregate budget rejects is now retained with its file and surfaced in the composer as a retry/discard row. Removing an attachment retries it automatically (the issue's recovery case), the Retry button re-stages against the current budget, and Discard deletes the file explicitly. Successful staging still removes the temporary file, and the upload limit itself is unchanged. Recordings over the per-note 5 MB limit or unreadable files are still discarded, since no amount of freed budget can admit them.

## Why This Change Was Made

The recorder handoff now retains a capture the draft cannot admit instead of destroying it. The retained note (`OpenClawRetainedVoiceNote`, module-internal: recording URL, duration, and the exact localized rejection message captured at retention time) belongs to the draft that recorded it:

- The draft pins its owner (`isAttachmentOwnerPinned`, send paths, and programmatic `send()`) until the note is staged or discarded, so a pending session switch cannot strand it; `syncSession` completes after the note resolves.
- Removing an attachment retries staging synchronously through the MainActor retry guard; the voice-note button is disabled while a note is retained, so there is never more than one retained capture and no supersession races.
- Retry validity is identity-based (`retainedVoiceNote?.recording == recording` re-checked after every await), so a discarded note's bytes cannot reappear; the rejection banner is cleared by exact message match, which is locale-safe.
- Discard deletes the file explicitly; staged transfers delete it; a fresh `readAndStageVoiceNote` failure with a superseded or cleared retention leaves the draft untouched.

## Evidence

- Regression tests in `ChatFileAdmissionTests.swift`: the retained note keeps the draft pinned ("Keep this recording with the draft" scenario — pending session switch waits, auto-retry after removal admits the note into the original draft, then the switch completes) and a short-budget retry keeps the note until discard. The parametrized `all staging paths count existing attachment bytes` voice branch pins retention plus explicit-discard deletion; aggregate enforcement stays pinned; the success/oversize/malformed-duration tests pass against the retained signature.
- Two independent review rounds drove the implementation (a compile-level setter visibility defect, a locale-dependent error-prefix match, and lifecycle/concurrency gaps including discard-retry resurrection and duplicate staging); the final design replaces the generation counter with draft ownership plus identity re-validation, reviewed to confirmation.
- Local gates on this commit: `swiftc -parse` clean on all nine touched Swift files, `scripts/format-swift.sh ios` reports 0/514 files needing formatting, `pnpm native:i18n:verify` passes (inventory carries the new apple-surface strings). This host has Command Line Tools only — no full Xcode — so the SwiftUI SDK macro plugins cannot load and the native build/test gate is the iOS/macOS CI on this PR, consistent with `docs/platforms/mac/dev-setup.md`.

## Current review status

Draft: the repair for the published revision's build failure is pushed as the current head. Remaining before ready, per the review plan: hosted iOS/macOS build lanes on this head, the focused regression suites in CI, and isolated iOS simulator evidence covering recording, rejection, retry, and discard.

## What Problem This Solves

Opening split view or forking a conversation mounted the destination transcript in one task, delaying paint and input. This change paints the pane shell and composer first, then prepares and mounts rows after two turns of the existing frame scheduler. It reuses the transcript owner's initial-range path, cancels pending mounts on hide/disposal, and retains revealed content. Restored snapshots still render in the first frame; the placeholder preserves the loaded transcript annotation inset.

The campaign coordinator accepted the disclosed WebKit single-key movement and authorized the native pre-existing-failure route for the inherited test-line debt. The original fixture type error is repaired; the focused test-type leaf passes.

## User Impact and Measured Trade

The split-view longest task falls from **76 → 56 ms at 1×** and **391 → 304.5 ms at 4×**. Fork's 4× longest task falls from **233.5 → 187 ms**. Both preserve native typing and composer geometry. Edit/resubmit remains accepted as done from the earlier 174–199 ms evidence; this change does not alter composer geometry.

The campaign coordinator accepted the byte trade after comparing raw, served and normalized sizes. Both complete builds contain **all eight native UI plugin distributions / 41 inputs**. The measured base is `07ef5b84fd1b1bf29c069cf7d3b92686cf5a1f1f`; the runtime build is `4b9b85c65b5e9ed861970dedaf83dec363e3c0be`. Subsequent commits change only the cap and test fixture. Current source head: `877ffc8d32338f1d61777af13d7a2a6007ffb51b`.

No code moved across chunk boundaries: identifier mangling makes normalized gzip price this small change differently. **The trade was accepted by the campaign coordinator because the normalized delta is minifier noise, not comparable real growth.** Real whole-Chat served growth is 111 B. Whole-Chat served Brotli decreases 66 B. Only `chatBootJsGzipBytes` changes, to **1,287,669 B = measured head +64 B**. Strict performance check: zero violations. The Solid performance guide now records the normalization caveat in two lines.

The committed engines harness ran 20 rotated base/head/A-A triplets per cell, with bounded confirmations of the cells whose tails needed review. **1,260 observations, zero behavior failures.** Chromium ran at 1× and 4×. ## What Problem This Solves

The path CLI reference puts invalid mutation options under exit status 2. A script that omits `--dry-run` when using `path set --diff` receives exit status 1 and a result on stdout.

## User Impact

Scripts can distinguish an invalid preview invocation from a malformed path and read the failure from the correct stream.

## Why This Change Was Made

Document the existing exit statuses and output shapes for `set --diff`, `validate`, and errors such as an unparseable `resolve` address. Only the reference changes.

## Evidence

On macOS with Node 24.22.1, I ran the repository's production `path` Commander registration in isolated processes against a temporary JSONC fixture.

| Invocation | Exit | Observation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `set ... --diff --json` | 1 | stdout contained `{"ok":false,"reason":"--diff requires --dry-run"}` |
| `set ... --diff --human` | 1 | stdout contained `set failed: --diff requires --dry-run` |
| `set ... --diff --dry-run --json` | 0 | stdout contained a preview diff |
| `validate not-an-oc-path --human` | 1 | stdout contained `INVALID: OC_PATH_MISSING_SCHEME` |
| `resolve not-an-oc-path --human` | 2 | stderr contained `OC_PATH_MISSING_SCHEME` |

prs.title: feat(codex): bind native goal pursuit to admitted run ownership
prs.body:
Related: #192988. Depends on #193136, #193103 and #193024.

## What Problem This Solves

Codex can schedule native Goal turns after its initial host turn, but the adapter currently disables that engine. Treating those turns as ordinary host reprompts also loses the native thread's continuation and budget semantics.

## User Impact

An admitted OpenClaw Goal can use Codex's native continuation engine while retaining the original host permissions, model/process/hook ownership, cancellation and final-response accounting. Resume reconciles remaining allowance against native lifetime usage instead of resetting it. A committed host complete/blocked verdict stops further native pursuit without discarding the current answer.

This dependent draft is not live-qualified or ready to merge. It includes unchanged prerequisites; [the stage-only comparison](https://github.com/GoatInAHat/openclaw/compare/41f1d1aab017a0ec0268621ec01d11d873347ee1...e301de4feec686a1a50b080ee5fd7d3eece860d3) isolates this change. Required-human-decision durability is not implemented by this change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing attempt, route, inference, process and cleanup owners remain responsible. Native turn receipts bind each successor before HTTP model requests or tool dispatch can proceed. A narrow notification on the existing host Goal capability lets the Codex adapter join native suspension after an actual terminal-tool transaction. Uncertain native cleanup retains its resources until exit is confirmed; it does not report success from an attempted shutdown.

The native loop, receipt admission, model/process/hook rotation, terminal suspension, budget reconciliation and their consumers form one complete stage. Enabling the scheduler without any of these would admit successors without the current execution contract. No new host scheduler, polling timer, state store, provider or configuration option is introduced. Mechanical helper extractions keep existing owning modules within their size bounds.

## Evidence

Checked Codex commit: `e301de4feec686a1a50b080ee5fd7d3eece860d3`.

- 202 owning-boundary tests across 6 files and 473 affected-consumer tests across 22 files pass (675 total).
- Six canonical production/test type projects, scoped source and test-registration lint, formatting (42 files), SDK exports, both plugin-boundary checks, Goal MDX and the exact incremental test-line allocation (1,666 LF) pass.
- Full committed-revision SDK API comparison (`41f1d1aab017` → `e301de4feec6`) completed on an idle macOS arm64 host with the canonical checker (exit 0; both revision snapshots rendered and temporary worktrees cleaned). It reports one added `AgentHarnessNativeGoal` export and 167 reachable-export changes from the optional `subscribeToolStatus` capability and its re-export, with no entrypoint/export removals or direct export-signature changes. Report digest: `eb7bb834`. This closes the comparison-execution gap, not live qualification or maintainer API acceptance.

- Independent review of all 43 selected source paths found no actionable findings. Every integrated postimage and 14 preserved precursor paths match the reviewed manifest.
- Earlier R1/R2 regressions reproduced terminal-tool successors and sticky native budgetLimited readback; final selective-head checks are being run separately.
- The native-attempt tests use production attempt/router/inference/host owners with a controlled native transport. They are not real-binary inference proof.
- The opt-in Gateway smoke checks multiple native completions and same-thread Resume. It does not prove private HTTP/receipt ordering, synchronized active/idle cancellation, terminal-tool suspension, native budget persistence or physical descendant cleanup.
- Real configured-provider multi-turn pursuit, final external effect/delivery and physical restart remain outstanding. No live qualification or deployment is claimed.

prs.title: improve(ci): defer unused assertion scope analysis
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Boundary checks load binding scopes for files that have no identifier assertion to analyze.

## User Impact

This is an internal CI optimization. Product behavior, configuration, guard selection, and diagnostics stay unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Load scopes on the first relevant assertion in each file instead of at the start of every file. Keep the existing binding resolver and all six boundary rules.

## Evidence

- Full-command instrumentation covered the same 48,765 distinct file paths on both versions. Scope requests fell from every file to 4,814 files (90.13% fewer); the candidate loaded scopes at most once per file. Both count runs exited successfully with Oxlint 1.89.0.
- The existing boundary-guard suite passed all 25 tests on the frozen dependency set; syntax and formatting passed.
- Fresh independent review and the completed local ClawSweeper review found no actionable correctness issues. All timing runs also passed with identical complete diagnostics and inventories.
- Frozen base: `5dcee9e55291a354a7541a0b1130875dfd9db7c6`. No tests, coverage, worker limits, retries, or runner sizes change.

### Performance acceptance rule — recorded before timing

Run the committed `pnpm lint:no-chained-type-assertions --format json` command on the same task-owned Linux Testbox, serially, with the baseline and candidate guard bytes verified before every run and restored afterward. Use warm filesystem/tool caches and fresh subprocesses: one untimed warm-up per variant, then five interleaved baseline/candidate pairs. Record available CPU/memory, host load, wall time, CPU time, peak RSS, status, and complete diagnostics. Compare medians, p95, and spread.

Accept at least a 10% reduction in median wall time with identical status and diagnostics, fewer scope requests, and no material p95, CPU, or peak-memory regression; a 20% worsening in any metric stops the change. This measures this guard on the recorded host. It does not establish a cold-run improvement, explain the entire historical nine-minute hosted tail, or claim invoice savings.

### Measured result

Five interleaved pairs of the full command, after one warm-up each, on the same Blacksmith Testbox:

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median wall time | 31.55s | 26.80s (15.1% lower) |
| Observed p95 wall time | 33.10s | 27.86s |
| Wall-time range | 30.78–33.10s | 26.24–27.86s |
| Median CPU time | 83.12s | 70.76s (14.9% lower) |
| Median peak RSS | 907.8 MiB | 891.9 MiB |
| Maximum peak RSS | 914.3 MiB | 914.9 MiB |

Observed resources: 16 CPUs in process affinity, 62.0 GiB total RAM (60.7 GiB available initially), Node 24.22.1, Oxlint 1.89.0. CPU and memory cgroup limits were not exposed at the inspected paths. Initial host load was 0.16; sample-start one-minute load ranged 0.16–4.62. Every run returned exit 0, zero diagnostics, 48,783 reported files, and six rules. The separate scope probe counts the 48,765 distinct paths entering the rule; its coverage is identical before and after. Candidate bytes were restored after measurement.

The declared acceptance rule passed. Five samples give a bounded host measurement, not a reliable fleet percentile or billing result. Broad PR CI remains the final gate.

prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Cloud-worker startup repeats repository admission, prepared-content scans, and worker-code prewarm that the same dispatch or freshly forked snapshot has already completed.

## User Impact

Fresh snapshot workers can reuse prepared content and runtime work while private-computer preparation overlaps node connection and bundle installation. Installation acknowledgement, private-computer use, and cleanup still wait for readiness. Ordinary starts and older peers retain verification.

Depends on #193872, included at `e45cfac4d439cec7ef2e75542fa5967fa9643849` as explicitly requested. This PR targets `main`; the prerequisite remains open and should land first. No cherry-picks were used for this lane.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reimplements the final behavior of `564936d5ffc`, `06b2f065757`, and `668001f302a` against main's owners. Reuses one dispatch's admitted repository facts while preserving live caller, identity, attachment, and cancellation checks. Explicit REST revalidation retains its repository-instance checks.

Fresh snapshot facts travel through the existing preparation and intent owners and are consumed once. Reuse requires the original enrollment connection and negotiated support; code invocation closes both content and runtime freshness. Reconnects cannot mint new freshness. Matching dedicated runtime forks can reuse producer prewarm with setup disabled even when hooks are configured; omitted execution mode uses `worker-turn`.

Necessary prerequisite integration repairs project canonical registration fields instead of sending a rejected extra field, and disambiguate a shared receipt export. Existing lifecycle functions were extracted only to keep owning modules within repository size limits. No new durable freshness store or protocol-version bump.

## Evidence

- Admission/access boundary suites: 66 passed. Pinned GraphQL revalidation metadata requests **2 → 1**; private pack metadata requests **4 → 0** and identity preparations **2 → 0**; binding extra remote revalidations **1 → 0**. Revocation, cancellation, REST fallback, and source/recipe mismatch coverage retained.
- Node and Gateway bundle installers: 70 passed, including producer prewarm, zero-scan/zero-child fresh consumption, mutation fallback, original-connection guard, and older-node behavior.
- Prepared workspace and enrollment suites: **68 passed**, including process-boundary hash memo reuse/fallback, private-edit replay, and capture of the first node connection (164 seconds combined; process and SQLite/transport ownership are the contracts).
- Private-computer/invocation suites: **62 passed**. Remaining consumers: **42 passed, one 120-second timeout** in `runtime.worker-supervisor.test.ts` (claimed worker across cancellation/reconnect). This remains an unresolved proof gap, not a passing run. Combined batch: 104 passed, one failed; infra shard 171 seconds.
- Full `build-all.mts`: **passed**, 3m16s. It emitted a Control UI boot-size budget warning (778.2 KiB versus 778.1 KiB); this lane has no UI source changes.
- Independent local autoreview (Codex, P0–P2), full local diff against `8662f3bf78dc7d644d207c8afb6f2f8b8f5750b0`: one P2 finding, an inverted shared-host test fixture, corrected before publication. No other P0–P2 defects established. Static diff review; unchanged source and execution were not available to the reviewer. Subsequent changes were that fixture correction, a mechanical test-fixture extraction, documentation clarification, and test-budget accounting.
- Core typecheck, bundle/workspace/provisioning scoped lint, and touched-file formatting passed. The private-runtime lint batch reports three outstanding findings: test-file max-lines, a Promise executor return in a test, and missing `cause` on the preparation cleanup AggregateError. These remain documented follow-up work. Provisioning eligibility suite: **21 passed** (47 seconds wrapper, including compilation), covering dedicated/shared hosts, setup-disabled hooks, default mode, and runtime/provenance mismatches.
- Added a separate **993-line** test allocation for this lane's connection/provenance, invalidation, readiness-order, and eligibility regressions. The shared scalar is unchanged. The full staged test-line check still reports **121 lines over budget**, inherited from main (51) and the included prerequisite's 416 net test lines versus its 346-line allocation (70); this task does not inflate its allocation to hide that debt. CI seconds are unavailable; no CI run was monitored.

Simplification: redundant revalidation and consumer-side prewarm disappear from eligible startup; existing intent and runtime owners retain the facts. The prerequisite is the smallest independent stage and should land first. Combined main-target delta: production/docs/config +1,809/−759; tests +1,710/−301. The new lane needs added connection/custody and readiness lifecycle handling because generic node code execution and reconnects invalidate freshness.

prs.title: fix(telegram): render authored tg-time dates in rich messages instead of raw markup
prs.body: Closes #192158 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes: an agent-authored `` date shows up as raw markup instead of a Telegram date when rich messages are on, while the same tag already renders with rich messages off (#112911). ## User Impact User impact: with `richMessages: true`, an authored `` now reaches Telegram as a native date instead of visible markup, as it already does with rich messages off. The Bot API lets the client format that date from `unix` and `format` (relative, weekday, short or long date, short or long time); Telegram for Android 13.1.1 shows the tag's own text, styled as a date (see Live). A tag with a missing or invalid `unix` or `format` now shows only its text, with no visible markup, and the rest of the message is still sent. Rich-off delivery is unchanged. ## Why This Change Was Made The rich HTML-island mapper now turns `` into a Bot API `RichTextDateTime` node (`date_time`). The tag is accepted under the same rule as on the classic HTML path: the attribute pattern moved from `format.ts` to `format-html.ts`, so the classic sanitizer and the rich mapper share it (`unix` is a positive integer, `format` matches Telegram's `r|w?[dD]?[tT]?`). The rich mapper also requires a `unix` that fits Telegram's 32-bit time, so millisecond timestamps and dates after 2038-01-19 keep only their text. Without `format`, `date_time_format` is `""`, which Telegram documents as "text as-is". The node text stays plain, because it is what clients that cannot format the date and the plain-text fallback show. Formatting inside the tag is dropped, and formatting around it (`**…**`) is kept. The rich splitter treats `date_time` as an atomic leaf, like custom emoji and formulas, so a long message never shows one date in two chunks. The rich authoring rules get one line about the tag, limited to an exact Unix time in seconds, because a client that applies the format shows the date from `unix` rather than the text. `docs/channels/telegram/rich-messages.md` documents the tag. Verified edge case: - A `` inside a link is sent as is (`url{date_time}`). The Bot API accepts it and normalizes it to `date_time{url}`, so the link is kept; an MTProto client on layer 227 received `textDate` wrapping `textUrl`. Known limitations: - Telegram for Android 13.1.1 shows the tag's own text, styled as a date, instead of formatting it (see Live), so the text should name its time zone, as the authoring rule's example does (`Thu, Mar 17 2022, 15:45 UTC`). - Telegram rejects dates more than about three years ahead of the send time with `RICH_MESSAGE_DATE_INVALID`. The existing rich-to-plain fallback then sends the whole message as plain text, so nothing is lost, but its rich formatting is. The mapper only enforces the 32-bit cap: the server limit is undocumented and was measured in one session, so it is not hard-coded. ## Evidence ### Date-label entity fix (2026-11-06) Current head: [`4251ee9ededb`](https://github.com/aspalagin/openclaw/commit/4251ee9ededb3909503b1ba97389cf5a6fdb0d10). Addresses the [P2 review finding](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/192161#issuecomment-6612231241): `A & B` must retain `A & B` in the date label and plain fallback. The Markdown IR has already decoded the text once. The date mapper now uses the existing plain-text walker without a second decode; other callers retain their previous behavior. - Red: the strengthened existing HTML-island test fails on `068873df3d53` with received `A & B`; the other 49 cases pass. - Green: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/telegram/src/rich-blocks-html.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/format.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/rich-blocks.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` passes **163/163**. - The existing HTTP regression now checks the escaped date label in both `sendRichMessage` and the plain `sendMessage` fallback. Its local run was stopped during compiled-worker preparation when the 2 GiB memory cap was reached; **no new local HTTP pass is claimed**. That regression and broader type checks remain for CI on this head. - Scoped `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint --threads=1`, and `git diff --check` pass. Independent read-only review of the patch and all walker callers found no actionable findings. - Existing test cases were strengthened with zero net additional test lines; the 85-line allocation is unchanged. No fresh full build or Telegram client run was performed for this fix. Earlier live evidence below is historical. The successful CI and review evidence below covers earlier revisions, not this new head. ### Historical base refresh and exact-head CI (2026-11-05) Refreshed this branch onto [main `3df082cf325b`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3df082cf325b7105fbf6833faed7f96d04f68bc8) with an ordinary merge at [`068873df3d53`](https://github.com/aspalagin/openclaw/commit/068873df3d530c2dc40d21e8374623a1cbb5e783). This incorporates the upstream UI typecheck repair (#192868) and test-budget reconciliation (#192905), rather than changing contributor-side UI, allocations, or CI checks to hide inherited failures. All 10 original PR files are byte-identical to the previous head, and the effective patch and exact +85 test-line allocation are unchanged. There were no merge conflicts or manual resolutions. Scoped formatting and boundary lint, patch parity, ancestry, and diff checks pass. An independent parent check repeated file equality and merge verification. **CI on previous head `068873df3d53`: SUCCESS.** [Run 41915225093](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41915225093) explicitly checked out this PR head merged into the pinned base above. Logs confirm **168 target/sibling passing cases** (55 direct cases in the two changed test files, plus 113 sibling cases). All 5 selected test shards, all seven type-check jobs, six QA Smoke profiles, and baseline ratchets pass. The executed test-line check has 30 lines of slack. Published `openclaw/ci-gate`, dependency-review, and security-sensitive-review contexts are successful; there are no pending checks. The previous inherited UI/test-budget failures no longer reproduce on this tested merge. `build-artifacts` was **SKIPPED** by scope selection, not a verified full build. Runtime results are hosted test/HTTP-harness proof, not a fresh Telegram client demonstration. Earlier live evidence and hosted reviews below concern earlier heads; they are not presented as new exact-head hosted reviews or maintainer approval. The historical failure sections explain why the base was refreshed and do not describe the current gate result. A separate **independent read-only model code review** of this exact head against `3df082cf325b` found no confirmed actionable findings in the effective patch and inspected integration paths. It checked converter/capability callers or date parsing/splitting/transport as applicable, including the intervening upstream changes. Historical live behavior proof remains applicable within its recorded client/version limits; it is not a new live run. This is not a new hosted ClawSweeper review or human approval. ### Historical budget audit (2026-11-04, before upstream reconciliation) The [failed CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/41710128075/job/126177106601) tests head `c313d9b2407c` on main base `2780c3f62240`. The PR adds exactly 85 test LF (+57 HTML-island, +28 HTTP-boundary) and already has an exact 85-line allocation. Subtracting both gives the same 359-line deficit on that tested base; this PR does not add to the inherited deficit. The unchanged branch passes the canonical ratchet against its original base with 153 lines of slack. A pinned-source LF audit of [main `7c2ff8f775ac`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/7c2ff8f775acca3e5c93c9c22b6247e37df29bae) still finds 191 inherited lines (6,466,021 / 6,465,830). This is an arithmetic source audit, **not** a new canonical checker run on main. The existing debt is tracked in #191738. The allocation, shared scalar/checker, and coverage have not been changed to hide it. This documented the pre-reconciliation state; upstream repairs are now integrated by the current base refresh above, pending fresh CI. Fresh focused verification on the unchanged head: `rich-blocks-html.test.ts` passes 50/50. The HTTP-suite rerun exceeded the local 3 GiB test-worker preparation limit; it is not reported as a new pass. Earlier HTTP and live evidence below is unchanged. - Regression tests: - `rich-blocks-html.test.ts`, "tg-time inline islands": - valid tags with `wDT`, with `r` inside bold, and without `format` become `date_time` nodes, and the plain text keeps the fallback text; - 9 invalid attribute forms keep only their text, without `date_time` or `22:45 tomorrow, ` and the wire block is `"text": "Call at 22:45"`. After the fix: 55/55 pass in those two files. With only the 32-bit check replaced by a safe-integer check, exactly the `2147483648` and millisecond cases fail (they would reach the API as `date_time`); `unix="2147483648"` and a millisecond value keep only their text with the fix. With only the splitter change reverted, the split case fails with two `date_time` nodes. - Neighbor suites, all green: `format.test.ts` (the existing classic `` keep/escape cases are unchanged), `rich-blocks.test.ts`, `rich-plain-fallback.test.ts` (135 passed); `rich-blocks.span-work.test.ts`, `rich-blocks-table-segments.test.ts`, `channel-actions.contract.test.ts` (24 passed); `send.telegram-http.test.ts` (45 passed); `outbound-adapter.telegram-http.test.ts` (34 passed). - `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` on the touched files, `git diff --check`, `pnpm lint:docs`: clean. Line-cap ratchet passes. A full typecheck was not run locally; CI covers it. A scoped check confirmed that the local `RichText`/`InputRichBlock` still assign to grammY's types, and that a non-Bot-API `date_time_format` fails to compile. - Test lines: allocation `config/test-lines-allocations/telegram-rich-date-time.txt` (85, the net added lines): new focused tg-time cases (valid/invalid tag table, atomic split, sendRichMessage wire + plain fallback). - Historical CI on `c313d9b2407c`: `assertion-safety` now passes (the first run flagged the date-format assertion; `c313d9b2407c` adds its `SAFETY:` note). The remaining red check is `test-lines`, inherited from `main`: "Test lines: 6442180; ceiling: 6441821; over by: 359; net delta: +85". This PR's +85 lines are covered by its own allocation of 85, so `main` alone is 359 over its ceiling (the debt tracked in #191738). - Live Bot API check (`sendRichMessage`, 2026-11-03; rich blocks built by a backport of this mapping to a release build and posted in the request shape OpenClaw uses; the range probes vary only `unix_time` of the mapped node): `date_time` was accepted in a paragraph and inside bold; an MTProto client on layer 227 (Telethon 1.44) received `textDate` with the requested flags (`wDT`: long date, long time, day of week; `t`: short time). - A date inside a link (`[…](url)` and `…`, sent as `url{date_time}`) was accepted; the server normalized it to `date_time{url}`, and the layer 227 client received `textDate` wrapping `textUrl`, so the link is kept. - `unix_time` 2147483648 and the millisecond value 1793793600000 (sent without the int32 cap) were rejected with `Bad Request: can't parse InputRichBlock: Field "unix_time" must be a valid Number`; 2147483647 and dates more than about three years after the send time were rejected with `Bad Request: RICH_MESSAGE_DATE_INVALID`; past values down to `unix_time` 1 were accepted. Both error texts match the existing rich-to-plain fallback (`can't parse InputRichBlock`, `RICH_MESSAGE_*_INVALID`), so such a message degrades to plain text instead of being lost; with the int32 cap, values above 2147483647 keep only their text and never reach the API. - **Live.** Before and after on the same 2026.10.9 gateway. Before (2026-11-03 13:47 UTC) ran without this change. After ran with the same change as a local patch, along with the companion expandable-quote and compact-table patches; gateway restarted at 2026-11-03 16:30 UTC.
