issues.title: [WebUI] Scroll-to-bottom button flickers: it reappears for most of the smooth navigation after being clicked
issues.body:
### Bug Description

Clicking the "Scroll to bottom" button makes it flicker: it disappears on click, reappears for most of the smooth scroll down, and disappears again on arrival. The button genuinely unmounts and remounts, with its `animate-in fade-in-0 zoom-in-95` entrance.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a conversation longer than one viewport.
2. Scroll up so the "Scroll to bottom" button appears.
3. Click it: hidden on click → visible again during the scroll → hidden on arrival.

In code: park `ThreadViewport` at `maxScrollTop`, take the camera with `wheel`, move `scrollTop` far from the tail so the button mounts, click it, then step the animation and emit a `scroll` event per frame. The clock must be controlled (`requestAnimationFrame` into a queue, `performance.now` into a counter): [`thread-camera.ts`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/3404fe83/webui/src/components/thread/thread-camera.ts#L1) animates over `NAVIGATION_DURATION_MS = 220`, so on an unloaded machine the trip settles within one real frame and a test driven by real frames never observes the flicker.

### Expected Behavior

Once clicked, the button stays hidden for the whole trip to the tail.

### Actual Behavior / Code Evidence

At upstream revision [`3404fe83`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/commit/3404fe83):

- [`scrollToBottomNow()`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/3404fe83/webui/src/components/thread/ThreadViewport.tsx#L536-L552) starts the trip with `navigateLatestTo(top)` (mode `navigating-latest`) and hides the button optimistically with `setAtBottom(true)`.
- [`onScroll()`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/3404fe83/webui/src/components/thread/ThreadViewport.tsx#L933) then recomputes the state from geometry alone: `logicallyAtBottom = !historyWindow && (owner === "automatic" || (owner === "navigation" && near))`.
- While the camera is still travelling, [`observeScroll()`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/3404fe83/webui/src/components/thread/thread-motion.ts#L348-L381) returns `owner === "navigation"` and `near` is false until the trip enters the [`NEAR_BOTTOM_PX = 48`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/3404fe83/webui/src/components/thread/ThreadViewport.tsx#L80) band, so the state flips back and the button remounts — measured over a frame clock, visible for 9 of 13 sampled frames (~150 ms of the trip).
- Also in the released build: [`v0.4.0`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/releases/tag/v0.4.0) already has [`setAtBottom(true)`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/v0.4.0/webui/src/components/thread/ThreadViewport.tsx#L537) in `scrollToBottomNow` and [`(owner === "navigation" && near)`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/v0.4.0/webui/src/components/thread/ThreadViewport.tsx#L917) in `onScroll`.

issues.title: [WebUI] Middle-click autoscroll at the live tail is snapped back; the viewport fights the user (wheel works)
issues.body:
### Bug Description

With a conversation longer than one viewport and the view resting at the bottom, **middle-click autoscroll does not move the page**: the viewport is snapped back to the bottom every frame and jitters while autoscroll is armed. The wheel, touchpad, scrollbar thumb and keyboard are unaffected. In a freshly opened thread the same defect appears as a hard jump instead of an animated pull.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a conversation longer than one viewport and let it finish streaming so the view sits at the bottom.
2. Press the middle mouse button in the message area, then drag slightly up or down.
3. The viewport keeps resetting to the bottom; repeating the same gesture with the wheel scrolls away normally.

In code: dispatch `pointerdown` with `button: 1`, then move `scrollTop` up and fire `scroll` — the camera reclaims the viewport on the next geometry frame. The same sequence driven by `wheel` does not.

### Expected Behavior

Autoscroll keeps the reading position, like any other user scroll.

### Actual Behavior / Code Evidence

At upstream revision [`3404fe83`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/commit/3404fe83):

- [`thread-motion.ts`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/3404fe83/webui/src/components/thread/thread-motion.ts#L341-L348) — scroll events are treated as geometry, not intent; ownership changes hands only through an explicit input handler.
- [`ThreadViewport.tsx`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/3404fe83/webui/src/components/thread/ThreadViewport.tsx#L1120-L1127) registers `wheel`, `touch*`, `keydown`, `pointerdown`, and [`handlePointerDown`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/3404fe83/webui/src/components/thread/ThreadViewport.tsx#L1012-L1019) accepts only `event.button === 0`.
- Autoscroll emits no `wheel`, only `scroll`. Each step therefore reaches [`observeScroll(nearLiveTail = false)`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/3404fe83/webui/src/components/thread/thread-motion.ts#L348-L381) in an automatic mode → `invalidateGeometry()` → the next frame re-targets the tail, via [`followTo(maxScrollTop)`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/3404fe83/webui/src/components/thread/thread-motion.ts#L431-L440) or [`jumpTo(maxScrollTop)`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/3404fe83/webui/src/components/thread/thread-motion.ts#L476-L484). User and camera alternate every frame.
- [`atBottom`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/3404fe83/webui/src/components/thread/ThreadViewport.tsx#L932-L933) comes from the same owner, so the "Scroll to bottom" button never appears either.
- Also in the released build: [`v0.4.0`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/releases/tag/v0.4.0) ships the identical predicate in `nanobot/web/dist/assets/ThreadShell-*.js` (`le.button===0&&…`) — a build artifact, so the nearest source anchor is [`ThreadViewport.tsx#L993`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/v0.4.0/webui/src/components/thread/ThreadViewport.tsx#L993).

### Possible Fix

An automatic mode only drives the camera *toward* the tail, and layout churn moves the boundary with the offset (the scroller sets `overflow-anchor: none`), so an upward displacement at an unchanged boundary outside history/navigation modes can only be the user. In `onScroll`, before `observeScroll()`:

```ts
const frame = { top: el.scrollTop, max: el.scrollHeight - el.clientHeight };
const previousFrame = lastScrollFrameRef.current;
lastScrollFrameRef.current = frame;
if (
  previousFrame
  && frame.top < previousFrame.top - SCROLL_INTENT_EPSILON_PX
  && Math.abs(frame.max - previousFrame.max) <= SCROLL_INTENT_EPSILON_PX
  && !threadMotionRef.current?.isAutoFollowPaused()
) {
  yieldCameraToUser();
}
```

Accepting `button === 1` instead would not work: the same handler also gates on `event.target === el`, and autoscroll is armed over message content.

issues.title: [WebUI] Language defaults to English instead of following the browser, and the first visit pins it
issues.body:
### Bug Description

The WebUI never reads the browser language when resolving the initial locale, so a first-time visitor whose browser is set to a supported non-English locale (e.g. `zh-CN`) gets an English UI.

The inline preboot script in `webui/index.html` **does** probe `navigator.languages`, so the two disagree and the mismatch is visible: the splash screen comes up in the browser's language, then the whole UI turns English when React mounts, and `<html lang>` is rewritten to `en`.

A second effect compounds it: the boot-time locale sync writes the resolved value to `localStorage`, so the very first visit pins the language. From then on, changing the browser language has no effect even though the user never picked anything.

Source at `main` (`f5c35947`):

- `webui/src/i18n/config.ts:18-19` — `defaultLocale = "en"`, `fallbackLocale = "en"`
- `webui/src/i18n/config.ts:64-66` — `resolveInitialLocale()` returns `readStoredLocale() ?? defaultLocale`; no `navigator` lookup anywhere
- `webui/index.html:183-188` — preboot resolves `stored || (navigator.languages && navigator.languages[0]) || navigator.language || "en"`
- `webui/src/i18n/index.ts:108` — `syncLocaleSideEffects(currentLocale())` runs during initialization, and `syncLocaleSideEffects` (`:127-131`) calls `persistLocale(locale)`

For contrast, the theme resolves the same shape of problem correctly: `webui/src/hooks/useTheme.ts:21-26` defaults to `"system"` and only explicit choices are persisted, so locale is the outlier here.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Fresh browser profile (nothing stored under `nanobot.locale`), browser UI language `zh-CN`.
2. Start the gateway and open the WebUI.
3. Watch the startup splash, then the loaded app.
   - splash: Chinese copy, `<html lang="zh-CN">` (set by the preboot script)
   - after mount: English UI, `<html lang="en">`
4. DevTools → `localStorage.getItem("nanobot.locale")` returns `"en"`, although no language was ever selected.
5. Change the browser UI language to `zh-CN` and reload → still English, because the value written in step 4 now outranks the browser.

Static equivalent, no browser needed:

```shell
# artifacts shipped in the 0.4.0 wheel
grep -c 'navigator.languages' nanobot/web/dist/index.html     # 2   (preboot script)
grep -rho 'navigator.languages' nanobot/web/dist/assets | wc -l   # 0   (app bundle never consults it)
```

### Expected Behavior

On a first visit with no stored choice, the app should resolve to the browser's language — the same value the splash screen already used — and nothing should be written to `localStorage` until the user actually picks a language in the switcher, which is the rule the theme already follows with `"system"`.

### Relevant Logs

```shell
$ grep -o 'navigator\.languages' nanobot/web/dist/index.html | wc -l
2
$ grep -rho 'navigator\.languages' nanobot/web/dist/assets | wc -l
0

$ grep -n -A3 'export function resolveInitialLocale' webui/src/i18n/config.ts
export function resolveInitialLocale(): SupportedLocale {
  return readStoredLocale() ?? defaultLocale;
}

$ grep -n -A5 'function syncLocaleSideEffects' webui/src/i18n/index.ts
function syncLocaleSideEffects(language: string) {
  const locale = normalizeLocale(language);
  applyDocumentLocale(locale);
  persistLocale(locale);
}
```

### nanobot Version

0.4.0 (`nanobot --version` → `🐈 nanobot v0.4.0`); still present at `main` (`f5c35947`).

### Python Version

3.11.2

### Operating System

Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm), gateway running as a systemd service

### Channel / Platform

WebSocket (WebUI)

### LLM Provider

Not applicable — client-side locale resolution, no provider call involved.

### Model

Not applicable

### Browser

Chromium-based desktop browser with UI language `zh-CN`. The app bundle never consults a browser API, so this is not browser-specific.

### Connection

Remote host (WebUI served over HTTPS behind a reverse proxy)

### Configuration (Optional)

```yaml
# no gateway configuration affects this behaviour
```

### Additional Context

- `webui/src/tests/i18n.test.tsx:481` codifies the current behaviour: `it("defaults to English until the user chooses another language")`.
- The two resolvers do agree on the supported set today — the preboot `copy` keys and `supportedLocales` both list `en es fr id ja ko pt-BR vi zh-CN zh-TW` — so the divergence is only about consulting the browser and about persisting a boot-time resolution.
- Findings come from reading `main` and the artifacts shipped in the 0.4.0 wheel; no automated browser test was run.

issues.title: DeepSeek Chat Completions: image tool results are sent in an unsupported message role
issues.body:
Checked main at `3a37269f3f4b1f81c316a341b9dd2c5040ecf033`.

## Contract and mismatch

DeepSeek's [vision guide](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/zh-cn/guides/vision#使用限制) states that images are supported **only in `user` messages** for Chat Completions. In contrast, its [Responses guide](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/zh-cn/guides/responses_api#image-input) explicitly supports images in `function_call_output.output`.

With `deepseek-flash` and an explicit Chat Completions preset, reading an image through `read_file` produces this next-request shape:

```json
{
  "role": "tool",
  "tool_call_id": "call_image",
  "name": "read_file",
  "content": [
    {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "data:image/png;base64,..."}},
    {"type": "text", "text": "(Image file: ...)"}
  ]
}
```

The image remains in the unsupported `tool` role rather than being adapted to the Chat contract. This also reaches the same request builder after a Responses-to-Chat fallback; it is not a claim that the default Responses path is broken.

## Verification and impact

Offline reproduction used the actual `AgentRunner`, `ReadFileTool`, OpenAI SDK and `httpx.MockTransport`, with a locally generated 1×1 PNG and `ModelAPICapabilities(("chat_completions",), "chat_completions")`:

1. The first mocked model response calls `read_file`.
2. The captured second HTTP request contains the image under `role="tool"`, as above.
3. When the mock rejects that request with HTTP 400 according to the documented role restriction, nanobot retries with **no images** and can finish normally without the requested visual input.

As a control, converting the same history through the Responses builder retains the image as `function_call_output.output[input_image]`.

No live DeepSeek request was made. The unsupported request shape and local fallback behavior are verified; the actual service's response/error wording was not tested.

## Source

- [nanobot/agent/tools/filesystem.py:319–325](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/3a37269f3f4b1f81c316a341b9dd2c5040ecf033/nanobot/agent/tools/filesystem.py#L319-L325): image reads return native image blocks.
- [nanobot/agent/runner.py:543–565](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/3a37269f3f4b1f81c316a341b9dd2c5040ecf033/nanobot/agent/runner.py#L543-L565): tool results are appended with the `tool` role.
- [nanobot/providers/openai_compat_provider.py:589–682](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/3a37269f3f4b1f81c316a341b9dd2c5040ecf033/nanobot/providers/openai_compat_provider.py#L589-L682): the Flash image-capable path preserves that content without moving images to a supported role.
- [nanobot/providers/base.py:1750–1794](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/3a37269f3f4b1f81c316a341b9dd2c5040ecf033/nanobot/providers/base.py#L1750-L1794): error recovery retries after removing image input.

Could you adapt image tool results to the selected API's supported shape rather than relying on image-stripping recovery?

prs.title: fix(webui): follow browser language on first visit
prs.body:
## Why

On a first visit, the splash follows the browser language but the app switches to English and saves that choice even though the user never made it. This keeps the startup and app language consistent and reserves saved preferences for explicit choices.

Closes #6583

## What changed

- Resolve the initial language from the browser when no saved preference exists, using the same first-language and fallback rules as the splash.

## Scope

This does not migrate existing saved preferences: a previously auto-saved value cannot be distinguished from an explicit choice. Browser language changes apply on the next load when no preference is saved, not live.

## Blast Radius

prs.title: fix(providers): keep parallel tool calls apart when the stream omits index
prs.body:
Gemini's OpenAI-compatible API streams parallel tool calls without `tool_calls[].index`: each call arrives whole (id, name and arguments) in its own chunk, and the turn ends with `finish_reason: "stop"`. `_parse_chunks` falls back to the call's position inside its chunk when `index` is missing. That's 0 for every one of these chunks, so all the calls of a turn land in one buffer: the id and name of the last call win, and the arguments are concatenated.

Replaying a captured `gemini-3.5-flash` stream with two parallel `get_weather` calls through the `openai` client and `_parse_chunks`:

```
before: call_4234487 get_weather '{"city":"Paris"}{"city":"Tokyo"}'
after:  call_4234484 get_weather {'city': 'Paris'}
        call_4234487 get_weather {'city': 'Tokyo'}
```

### Change

A delta without `index` now starts a new call when it carries an id different from the current call's id, or a name on an id-less call that already has one. Anything else is appended to the current call, so providers that stream unindexed argument fragments keep working. Deltas that do carry `index` are handled as before.

### Tests

- `test_parse_chunks_keeps_parallel_calls_without_index_apart`: the two-call Gemini shape from the capture (thought signature shortened). It fails on `main` and passes with the fix.
- `test_parse_chunks_appends_unindexed_fragments_to_the_last_call`: id-less argument fragments still join the current call.
- `tests/providers` plus `tests/agent/test_gemini_thought_signature.py`: 1464 passed.
- `ruff check nanobot/`: clean.

This change was made with Claude Code; the tests above were run on the branch to check it.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

prs.title: fix(webui): preserve oversized turn history with record pagination
prs.body:
## Summary

A single WebUI turn could exceed the replay budget while still fitting in SQLite. The old selector retained selected records and silently omitted the rest, with no cursor to retrieve the missing answers, reasoning, or tool activity. This changes oversized turns to contiguous record-level pages instead of sampling them.

Resolves NAN-418

## Changes

- Add bidirectional record-position cursors, stable record identities, and history generations. Keep the existing 4,000-record / 20 MiB selected-source page budgets, including context-graph expansion accounting, without rewriting existing history.
- Reassemble adjacent fragments in the bundled WebUI, deduplicate overlapping refreshes, continue through invisible telemetry pages, and preserve both prompt navigation and the reader's scroll anchor.
- Preserve live contributions while a fragment gap is pending. Once the complete turn is assembled, use the existing authoritative cumulative stream snapshot semantics, including signed media, without adding a per-delta receipt tracker or duplicating raw text in storage.
- Separate fragment lifecycle settlement from content fencing so reconnect does not discard unconsumed live output or tool activity. Reuse the existing bounded completion ledger and retain genuine Temporary Chat behavior.
- Preserve incomplete-turn canonical answer recovery and legacy missing-user backfill on fragmented history. Recovery reads are separately accounted for; existing exceptional canonical/navigation recovery can exceed the normal selected-source budget.

Client and gateway ship together; no old-client compatibility branch or database migration is added.

## Verification

- Focused Python transcript/page/snapshot and WebSocket tests: **341 passed**.
- Focused transcript, hydration, prompt navigation, reconnect, and client tests on the final head: **316 passed**.
- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run build`, focused Ruff, and `git diff --check`: passed. CI caught a missing test-only type import after the finishing commit; the follow-up imports it and passes typecheck.
- Final focused Chromium history regressions: **4 passed**, including fragment prepend reading position and cached live-output handoff.
- Real isolated gateway + production WebUI build: **4,205-record** and **1,455-record / 26.76 MiB** synthetic turns both replayed through contiguous pages. Verified older scrolling, prompt navigation followed by newer scrolling, both user inputs, a single cumulative answer, expanded reasoning/tool activity, and reload. Every observed source slice stayed within the default page budgets. No production conversation was modified.
- [Full remote CI for the final head](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/42202188989): **passed**. WebUI has **3,625 passing unit tests** and **439 passing browser tests**; Python 3.11, Python 3.14 + coverage, Windows 3.14, Windows process compatibility, both TUI jobs, Docker, and the required gates passed. The scope selector skipped native-package and Windows-installer acceptance for this change.

## Scope notes

The earlier draft's receipt-cap / 8 MiB metadata problem was removed structurally: there is no new persisted receipt tracker and no outbound delivery lifecycle change. The signed-media restart-key and anonymous recovery-ownership behaviors were reproduced on the exact original base `f5c359476`; they are not introduced or changed by this PR. The browser acceptance above uses isolated synthetic conversations, not the user's original conversation.

prs.title: fix(providers): report DeepSeek generation interruptions
prs.body:
## Why

DeepSeek Chat Completions can end with `insufficient_system_resource` or `aborted`. These interruptions were treated as successful completions, so a partial answer could be saved as a normal reply.

## What changed

- Report both DeepSeek interruption reasons as model errors for streaming and non-streaming Chat Completions, including Responses-to-Chat fallback.

- Preserve prior Responses state when a stateless Chat fallback is interrupted.
- Propagate model errors through budget finalization and message delivery, preserving earlier completed length segments.
- Report structured model failures through the OpenAI-compatible API and Python SDK.

## Scope and tradeoffs

Successful Responses requests and ordinary Chat completions are unchanged. Interrupted output that was not streamed is not saved as a completed answer.

- `git diff --check` passed.
- Earlier PR head: 51 offline focused DeepSeek interruption, Runner, parser, and retry tests passed using simulated SDK HTTP responses; new regression cases reproduced the original failure before the fix.
- Focused agent, provider, API, and SDK tests: 405 passed (pytest 8.4.2; the project requires pytest 9).

prs.title: feat(heartbeat): add heartbeat-specific model override
prs.body:
## Problem

The heartbeat cron job runs on the main agent model for both the execution turn and the post-run notification evaluation. Heartbeat can run frequently (default every 30 minutes) and usually only makes a lightweight decision, so deployments using a premium or auto-routed model pay that cost for routine background checks. `agents.defaults.dream.modelOverride` already lets Dream run on a different model, but heartbeat has no equivalent setting.

## Solution

Add an optional `gateway.heartbeat.modelOverride`. For each heartbeat run, resolve an immutable runtime via `runtime_resolver.resolve_override(model=..., config=...)` (which also resolves the correct provider for the requested model); when the override is unset, snapshot the current default via `runtime_resolver.current()`. The same resolved provider/model is used for both the heartbeat turn and the notification evaluation. The main agent model and provider are never mutated, and unsetting the field keeps today's behaviour exactly.

## Changes

- `nanobot/config/schema.py` — add `model_override` to `HeartbeatConfig` with `modelOverride` / `model` aliases.
- `nanobot/cli/gateway_runtime.py` — resolve the heartbeat runtime and pass it to `process_direct`; use its provider/model for `evaluate_response`; startup output shows the effective heartbeat model.
- `docs/configuration.md` — document the new option with an example.
- Tests: config alias/serialization cases and a runtime case (default + override) asserting both the execution and evaluation use the resolved model while the main agent model is unchanged.

## Testing

**Environment**
- Runtime: Python 3.13.16
- OS: Windows NT 10.0.26200.0
- Arch: AMD64

**Test Commands & Results**
1. `pytest tests/cli/test_commands.py tests/config/test_gateway_config.py -k heartbeat`
   -> 20 passed, 150 deselected
2. `pytest tests/config tests/cli tests/agent`
   -> 2781 passed, 30 skipped, 0 failed (baseline: 2776 passed, 30 skipped, 1 flaky timing failure; the 4 added tests account for the count difference)
3. `ruff check nanobot tests`
   -> all checks passed
4. `basedpyright nanobot/config/schema.py nanobot/cli/gateway_runtime.py`
   -> 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes

**Pre-existing Failures**

It passes in isolation and passed in the post-change full run; it has no file intersection with this PR and is a pre-existing flaky timing test.

## Notes for Reviewer

- The earlier attempt #4549 was withdrawn without the feature landing; this re-implements the same requested behaviour against the current code, using the side-effect-free `runtime_resolver.current()` for the default case.

prs.title: fix(tools): read SVG files as text instead of image blocks
prs.body:
## Problem

`read_file` decides whether a file is an image with `detect_image_mime(raw) or mimetypes.guess_type(path)[0]`. `detect_image_mime` recognises PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP from their bytes; for anything else the file extension decides. So `logo.svg` comes back as an `image_url` block holding `data:image/svg+xml;base64,...` instead of its source.

That block is not usable. Neither Anthropic nor OpenAI accepts SVG as image input (both take JPEG, PNG, GIF and WebP), and the Anthropic converter's `data:(image/\w+);base64` pattern does not match `svg+xml`, so the block is sent as a `url` source with a `data:` URL. The model never gets the SVG markup it asked to read or edit. Binary `.bmp`, `.ico` and `.tiff` files took the same path.

## Fix

Treat a file as an image only when `detect_image_mime` recognises its bytes. That is the same set `utils/artifacts.py` maps to extensions. SVG then goes through the UTF-8 text path like any other XML file, and returns line-numbered source.

Behaviour change: binary files that are none of those four formats (`.bmp`, `.ico`, `.tiff`, `.avif`, `.heic`/`.heif`, gzip `.svgz`) now get the existing `Cannot read binary file ... (MIME: image/bmp)` error instead of an image block. Anthropic, OpenAI and Bedrock reject those blocks anyway. Gemini accepts HEIC/HEIF, so a `.heic` read on Gemini loses its image block; this PR keeps nanobot's existing image set (`detect_image_mime`, also used by `utils/artifacts.py` and the CLI's inline artifacts) rather than adding HEIC detection here. An SVG that is neither UTF-8 nor BOM-marked gets the same error, because `.svg` is not in `_is_text_extension`.

The second image check in the undecodable branch used the same inputs as the first one, so it could never match; it now only looks up the MIME type for that error message.

## Tests

- New `TestReadFileTool::test_svg_file_returns_numbered_source`. On main it fails because the result is `[{'type': 'image_url', 'image_url': {'url': 'data:image/svg+xml;base64,...'}}, ...]`; with the fix it returns `1| <svg xmlns=...`.
- `tests/tools/`: 1170 passed, 6 skipped.
- `ruff check` is clean. `basedpyright` reports 0 errors in `filesystem.py`.

Not changed here: inbound attachments (`utils/document.py` `is_image_file` and `agent/context.py`) use the same extension fallback, so an SVG a user uploads still becomes an image block. That can be a separate PR.

prs.title: perf(session): accelerate canonical history search with FTS5
prs.body:
## What

`search_sessions` loads complete canonical histories when titles do not fill the requested results. With many sessions and long histories, an older body match or a no-match query must load every candidate session.

Add a per-workspace SQLite FTS5 candidate cache to `SessionHistoryReader` so body candidates are selected before the existing reader verifies matches and returns excerpts. This preserves title priority, result order, archived messages, public-history filtering, original message indexes and current-session exclusion.

Related to #5509. This PR covers the agent's canonical `search_sessions` path. The current WebUI search filters loaded titles/previews in the browser; its API/UI is outside this change.

## How

- Index only visible canonical user/assistant text, obtained through the existing reader. Python `casefold()` and a quoted trigram query preserve literal substring semantics. Queries shorter than three folded characters, including two-character CJK queries, keep the canonical scan.
- Invalidate from committed `(generation, revision)` identities through one bulk session-version read. This replaces the JSONL file signatures and locks after #5943 moved session state into SQLite. Sessions changed during indexing are returned as candidates for direct verification; the cache never blocks session writes.
- Keep the cache in a separate sidecar file under the workspace session directory. Rebuild a corrupt cache under its own lock; unavailable/busy caches fall back to canonical reads and can recover on a later query. The session database remains the source of truth.
- Read session headers in one `list_metadata()` snapshot instead of one SQLite read per session.
- No new dependency or configuration setting is introduced.

Merged `main` at `d617b723`; the earlier JSONL signature/locking integration was replaced by session-version invalidation. Diff against `main` `d617b723`: **5 files, +399/−15**.

## Performance

Windows 10 / Python 3.13.6 / SQLite 3.50.4; synthetic canonical histories; a body match in the oldest session forces the canonical path to load all histories. Single local runs, warm OS cache.

| Workload | Canonical scan | First index + query | Warm indexed query | Warm no-match |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 200 sessions × 20 messages | 328.00 ms | 612.15 ms | 9.34 ms | 7.85 ms |
| 300 sessions × 500 messages | 1448.09 ms | 2503.79 ms | 13.97 ms | 8.10 ms |

Warm body reads fall from 200/300 to **one**. First construction has an upfront cost, and metadata enumeration remains linear in session count. These are local synthetic measurements, not CI numbers.

## Testing

- `python -m pytest tests/session tests/agent/tools/test_sessions.py tests/webui/test_session_mentions.py -q`: **209 passed, 3 skipped**.
- `python -m scripts.check_import_boundaries`: passed.
- `python -m ruff check` on the five changed files: passed.
- Strict BasedPyright on all four changed production modules: **0 errors, 0 warnings**.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Regression coverage includes Unicode/CJK and literal queries, cache reuse, equal-timestamp rewrites, add/delete/recreate, cache failure/recovery, corruption rebuild without modifying history, writes during SQLite lookup, workspace isolation and threaded searches. Existing session-tool tests cover ranking, visibility, transcript exclusion, archived/compacted history and current-session exclusion.

Cross-platform CI for this merge commit passed on Python 3.11, Python 3.14, Windows 3.14 and the Windows process-compatibility job: [run 39565108320](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/39565108320).

Implemented and tested with Codex assistance.

prs.title: perf: reduce memory copies across files, sessions, and model requests
prs.body:
## Why

Large file reads, session searches and model requests retain or construct complete copies when only a range or incremental result is needed. This reduces those peaks without truncating the searchable history or the returned file range.

## What changed

- Stream text-file range extraction while computing the full-file hash and line count. A still-visible read receipt is checked before reparsing an unchanged file; changed files are re-detected and parsed on the same open handle.
- Project session messages in reverse within per-session read snapshots, stopping once enough visible matches are found. Unmatched searches still scan the complete history. The history reader owns handle lookup, invalidated-match refill and final generation/visibility/handle validation, advancing one ordered candidate list rather than a multi-field cursor coordinated by the tool. A cancelled history scan cooperatively exits and releases its read transaction.
- Aggregate Chat Completions chunks incrementally while preserving live callbacks and deferring parser failures until stream completion. Explicit stream cleanup preserves an existing primary error; callback and cleanup failures cannot be mistaken for image incompatibility and retried without the images.
- For valid Responses replay state, extract instructions and convert pending messages without first converting the complete fallback transcript. The original full fallback remains for unavailable or incompatible state.

## Scope

Contributes to NAN-416. [Issue details](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-416/降低文件读取会话检索与模型请求中的多余复制和内存峰值). This covers its four measured Python paths; WebUI history, token estimation and image batching are not included.

## Tradeoffs and boundaries

Session search runs only when explicitly requested by a tool call; its frequency has not been profiled as a product hot path. Its retained benefit is bounded long-history allocation, not a claim of gateway-wide throughput improvement.

A history read that finds enough matches no longer decodes older, unvisited records. A malformed unvisited database record is therefore reported only when an operation actually scans it. Search ranks initially captured headers and uses separate per-session snapshots rather than one global snapshot; a concurrent rename may still be represented by the earlier title. Generation, visibility and handle are rechecked before returning, but a later concurrent change can still occur after validation. A normal long unmatched scan holds its session snapshot until that scan completes and can delay a WAL checkpoint; cancellation of a started scan waits for it to exit, and existing session-owner barriers in handle lookup have their own cancellation behavior.

A changed file with a still-visible receipt requires a hash pass followed by a second pass for decoding; force reads and reads without an applicable receipt use one pass. File reads are not atomic snapshots of concurrent writes, though the returned text and recorded hash come from the same parsing pass. A file that grows past the existing size limit during reading is now rejected.

This fixes errors masked by nanobot's own explicit stream cleanup. OpenAI SDK 2.24 can itself mask an iterator error or cancellation if its internal response close also fails, before control returns to nanobot; a controlled reproduction also fails on the pre-PR baseline. The PR does not modify that SDK behavior. Langfuse's OpenAI instrumentation independently retains streamed chunks, so the Chat stream memory figures below do not establish the same reduction when that instrumentation is enabled.

A separate warm-cache comparison of a 41,800-byte, 1,900-line UTF-8 Markdown file found higher small-file latency: the median of seven alternating 100-call batch averages was 2.71 ms before versus 7.04 ms after (batch-average ranges 1.64–3.42 versus 5.01–9.95 ms). Both sides used the same synthetic media-directory lookup stub and returned identical output. This is a memory optimization, not a general file-read speedup.

## Verification

**Windows synthetic comparison:** Python 3.14.6, base `11f738f0` versus `642bca7b`, five fresh-process runs per side in alternating order. These measurements predate the search-coordination simplification in `051aaab57`. File reading, single-session reads and provider production paths are unchanged; the two search rows describe the earlier implementation and have not been remeasured after simplification. Values are absolute process peaks in MiB and elapsed milliseconds, shown as median [min–max]. Private Working Set and Private Bytes were sampled approximately every 1 ms. The very short Responses replay had only 3–4 samples, so its peak may be underestimated. Outputs were checked for matching digests, and changed-file content hashes were verified. These are isolated synthetic workloads, not gateway, browser, or real-model end-to-end measurements.

| Workload | Private Working Set, before → after (MiB) | Private Bytes, before → after (MiB) | Time, before → after (ms) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 16,384,000-byte ASCII file, first line, `force=True` | 92.32 [90.64–92.43] → 33.15 [33.04–33.88] | 95.00 [93.36–95.22] → 36.10 [35.63–36.44] | 55 [53–65] → 34 [32–35] |
| Same file, visible unchanged receipt | 51.12 [50.36–53.49] → 33.06 [32.95–33.87] | 53.74 [52.84–56.15] → 35.45 [35.27–36.39] | 19 [17–23] → 15 [15–16] |
| Same file, changed outside selected range | 93.63 [92.00–95.91] → 33.26 [33.21–33.74] | 97.20 [93.82–97.94] → 36.00 [35.64–36.37] | 52 [51–60] → 47 [42–50] |
| Session: 4,000 × ~4,101-character messages, latest 8 | 54.41 [54.23–54.54] → 34.44 [34.40–34.73] | 57.39 [57.19–57.55] → 37.10 [36.77–38.02] | 70 [59–115] → 17 [17–26] |
| Same session, no query match | 54.14 [53.96–54.74] → 35.88 [35.65–35.94] | 57.50 [57.00–57.66] → 38.61 [38.36–38.78] | 82 [79–84] → 87 [76–90] |
| Search: 101 sessions, one 4,000-message history, one match | 53.48 [53.32–53.81] → 37.18 [36.84–37.63] | 56.47 [56.32–56.72] → 39.68 [39.06–39.87] | 537 [486–587] → 112 [104–116] |
| Same search, no match | 53.71 [53.50–53.88] → 35.88 [35.84–36.19] | 56.88 [56.38–57.28] → 38.57 [38.37–39.08] | 512 [476–576] → 79 [73–88] |
| Chat stream: 6,000 SDK chunks, 180,000 text characters | 71.96 [71.24–73.06] → 57.46 [57.16–59.09] | 75.55 [74.68–75.95] → 60.44 [60.07–61.73] | 97 [88–102] → 80 [77–92] |
| Chat stream: ~6,000 tool-argument chunks, 180,000 characters | 79.29 [78.77–79.46] → 57.73 [57.24–59.61] | 82.26 [81.46–82.92] → 59.89 [59.70–61.87] | 193 [181–199] → 144 [140–150] |
| Responses replay: 1,500 tool calls, ~2 KiB arguments each | 43.12 [42.96–43.48] → 40.51 [40.20–40.77] | 44.84 [44.62–45.24] → 42.80 [42.06–43.07] | 22 [21–24] → 3 [2–3] |

The missed session query shows a 5 ms higher median and a 6 ms higher maximum in this run; ranges overlap. Further five-per-side file comparisons were run at `a892f9f8`; file-reading production code has not changed since those comparisons. A 16,384,000-byte UTF-8 CJK file measured PWS 85.91 [82.62–86.60] → 33.13 [33.07–33.68] MiB, Private Bytes 88.74 [85.66–89.50] → 35.93 [35.61–36.15] MiB, and 60 [56–76] → 60 [57–61] ms. A dense 16 MiB one-character-per-line file measured PWS 184.33 [181.70–185.99] → 34.73 [34.18–35.38] MiB, Private Bytes 196.39 [194.02–197.96] → 37.72 [36.69–37.88] MiB, and 271 [237–295] → 153 [150–183] ms. A synthetic 16.9 MiB PNG measured PWS 92.57 [91.09–95.45] → 94.38 [92.23–95.69] MiB, Private Bytes 98.38 [97.32–98.70] → 97.83 [97.33–98.43] MiB, and 74 [73–87] → 79 [72–85] ms; the ranges overlap, but the higher image PWS and elapsed medians are disclosed rather than treated as zero cost.

- Earlier-head focused tests on Windows/Python 3.14: file and session suites **296 passed, 11 skipped**; provider and Responses suites with OpenAI SDK 2.24.0 **497 passed, 6 skipped**; the same provider suites with minimum SDK 2.8.0 **503 passed**. Those file/session results predate the search-coordination simplification; its focused results are listed separately below. Six local file skips lacked `pymupdf`/`fitz`, five require `/dev`, and six provider cases specifically target SDK 2.8's caller-owned close behavior.
- Synthetic OpenAI SDK `httpx.MockTransport` checks cover stream callbacks, malformed chunks, cancellation, errors, retries, cleanup, image preservation and chunk release. Langfuse 4.7/OpenAI 2.8 and Langfuse 4.18/OpenAI 2.24 were exercised with synthetic streams and an in-memory trace exporter; outbound sockets were disabled and no real user or model data was used.
- The prior CI run on `642bca7b` failed its Python 3.11 job because an existing idle-timeout test's fake stream lacked the SDK's `close()` method (**1 failed, 11,631 passed, 86 skipped**). The fixture now implements and verifies that method; its focused suite passed **6 tests** locally. The old result is not evidence for the new head.
- `ruff check --no-cache` on changed Python files, changed-source `basedpyright`, and `git diff --check`: passed.
- [Prior-head CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/42187667688): **CI required passed**. Its actual checkout was the synthetic merge of head `31289cb4` into target `f5c35947`. Python 3.11: **11,632 passed, 86 skipped**; Python 3.14 with coverage: **11,632 passed, 86 skipped**, with lint and full-project typecheck passing; Windows 3.14: **11,284 passed, 166 skipped**. WebUI, TUI, Docker and Windows process compatibility jobs also passed; installer and native package jobs were skipped by scope.

- Simplification at `051aaab57`: **59 session tests passed**; the consolidated SDK chunk-release cases passed **2 tests each on OpenAI 2.8 and 2.24**. Changed-file lint, changed-source typecheck and `git diff --check` passed. The follow-up removes 60 net lines while retaining privacy, reset, cancellation, refill, callback, output and usage coverage.

prs.title: refactor(webui): unify code and diff highlighting
prs.body:
## Why

Replace the WebUI's separate Prism code/preview/diff paths with shared highlighting while preserving the existing reading and file-change workflows. This also restores the earlier single-conversation preview layout: messages and Composer stay together in the left column, with the file preview filling the right column.

## What changed

- Replace `react-syntax-highlighter`/Prism with shared Highlights tokens and CSS-variable colors. Load Shiki only for grammars absent from Highlights; render source through React text/spans and preserve complete preview text, native find/selection, copy, ANSI, streaming settlement, wrapping, line numbers, themes and reading sizes.
- Render each complete read-only file diff through one Pierre instance, with bounded metadata/AST caches and a render window read from the existing chat scroller. Preserve file summaries, line limits, expansion/collapse, hunk gaps, truncation notices and local previews.
- Keep the single-conversation Composer inside its conversation column. Actual multi-pane tabs retain the shared footer, including compact rendering. Update both lockfiles, lazy-chunk guards, dependency notices and behavioral tests.

## Scope

WebUI only. No backend, TUI, provider, protocol or persistence-format changes; no patch editing/applying, new scroller ownership or bottom-mask removal. Uses pinned `@pierre/diffs` 1.6.1, `@pierre/highlights` 0.2.0 and Shiki 4.5.0.

## Tracking

Related: [NAN-343 — 统一 WebUI 代码与只读 diff 高亮，保留源码操作及侧栏布局](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-343).

## Tradeoffs

**Draft: large-diff scrolling and first-use transfer tradeoffs have not been remeasured after the fixes below.** This is not presented as a blanket performance improvement.

Five interleaved original-Prism/new-renderer trials on equivalent synthetic production fixtures, taken **before the final preview-layout follow-up**, found:

| Workload | Prism → replacement |
| --- | --- |
| 600-line code block, warm topic return | 316.6 → 190.0 ms |
| 600-row diff, warm expanded viewport | 189.5 → 30.7 ms |
| Code-block browser Private Working Set increment | 203.6 → 120.0 MiB |
| Diff browser Private Working Set increment | 217.8 → 171.6 MiB |
| Large-diff scroll p99, normal / Chromium 4× CPU throttle | 16.8 → 33.4 ms / 33.4 → 183.4 ms |
| Whole JS/CSS/WASM first-use transfer, code / diff | 708.8 → 797.1 KiB / 706.9 → 887.8 KiB |

Memory subtracts each independent browser's blank-host baseline; private commit was measured separately. Transfer is actual negotiated response-body bytes, not decoded size. Diff viewport readiness is separate from a complete source-coordinate traversal. The 600-row diff is a stress fixture above the ordinary default 500-row native output cap; 4× throttling is not a real low-end device. These figures are retained evidence for that earlier snapshot, **not a performance claim for this repaired head**.

## Blast Radius

Shared Markdown/code rendering, source-file previews, read-only file activity and single/multiple-pane Composer placement. Main review risks are grammar-loading failures and resource ownership, source/line-ending integrity, virtual-diff geometry and scrolling tails, and draft/attachment retention when changing pane ownership.

## Verification

The repaired source/build passed locally: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, `bun run check:imports`, `bun run test:imports`, `bun run test:coverage --maxWorkers=2 --minWorkers=2` (**3297 tests**), `bun run test:browser` (**246 cases**), `bun run build --outDir <isolated-output>` and `git diff --check`. The source inventory, normalized staged blobs/Git tree and frozen production assets were checked against the repair commit; no source change intervened after those checks.

A new isolated production gateway passed **32 normal black-box cases** on desktop/light and narrow/dark: code blocks including INI, PowerShell, C#, Docker and literal unknown-language HTML; exact clipboard content; themes; full previews/native find and selection; long-line plain-text budgets; six kinds of diff including the INI Worker path; complete retained coordinates, line limits, expansion, truncation and close/reopen. No browser or HTTP errors occurred in these normal cases. Preview open/close retained the same Composer DOM instance and its draft.

The targeted production regression checks also passed: a real failed INI grammar request in the direct source-file preview retained complete plain source, the same Composer and draft, working theme/close controls, and local diagnostics. The normal → blocked → normal controls each used a fresh browser context in the same Service-Worker-blocked interception mode; this is not a claim of automatic same-page module retry. Ordinary black-box cases used the normal Service Worker path. A real mouse drag plus native wheel across the original virtual-window boundary retained the exact selection; further scrolling kept both the selected rows and current viewport, native Copy matched the selection, and clearing it released the pinned rows without changing total scroll height.

The full browser suite additionally covers forward/backward selection and multi-hunk missing-context coordinates, native clipboard content and 26px localized gaps. Earlier built-gateway single → multiple → single pane checks with text and browser-File drafts remain recorded against the initial review commit; pane/Composer ownership source was unchanged by this repair, and the full current unit/browser checks were rerun.

## Review results

The initial review of `48e7177e9669f86f2f50ae462871ad296a19abd1` independently confirmed two P2 defects in the production UI. Both are repaired in [`d4469e316`](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/commit/d4469e316ce26a9169d911d7ebd33ff765d51049):

1. **Contain grammar/highlighter failure in CodeBlock.** Optional syntax enhancement can fail without clearing the source-file preview or the app. Keep the full plain source and Copy control outside the failed child; discard failed cached resources after the fallback commits, while retaining diagnostics.

Chromium's retargeted document `Selection.isCollapsed` is not used to reject a real shadow selection.

## Summary

Start a lighter release process without adding a second build system.

- Keep one Stable preparation path for feature releases and patches. Patches need generated change notes and affected documentation, not a full wiki and promotional refresh.
- Add opt-in daily Preview candidate preparation to the existing workflow. It stays disabled unless maintainers enable the repository variable. Require successful latest push CI for the exact source and skip an already accepted source/base pair.

- Preserve existing dispatch inputs, Preview numbering, five-platform acceptance and artifact-ID handoffs. Daily runs cannot replace pending manual runs.

This is the preparation step, not a complete automatic publisher. It creates no tags, GitHub Releases, PyPI uploads or catalogue updates. No release workflow was dispatched for this PR.

No application, configuration, session, package-layout or model-request behavior changes. Existing manual inputs remain supported. Website deployment and public channel announcements are outside this PR.

prs.title: test: stabilize timing-sensitive CI checks
prs.body:
## Problem

The cron reschedule regression test shares one two-second timeout across callback entry, two durable schedule writes and callback completion. On a Windows CI worker, those writes can consume the timeout while the job still completes correctly. The main run failed this case after 2.7 seconds.

A separate restart-notice test requires two send attempts within 100 milliseconds. Linux CI recorded a 142-millisecond delay between attempts, so the production deadline correctly refused the second attempt. That case tests retry behavior, not a 100-millisecond delivery requirement.

Windows also timed out while starting a real gateway during the parallel full suite. The log stopped before AgentLoop started. This cold-start test checks cooperative shutdown and lease release; it does not need to compete with package-building and session-index fixtures.

The ephemeral-delegation test passed every privacy and persistence assertion, then exceeded its two-second cleanup limit while closing real storage threads. That test does not define a two-second shutdown requirement.

## Change

- Wait separately for callback entry and job completion, with the same two-second asynchronous progress guards.
- Keep schedule edits outside the shared timeout and check completed task results directly.
- Cancel and drain both owned tasks on failure.
- Preserve the real writes, reload, saved schedule/history and next-occurrence assertions.
- Use the normal restart-notice deadline with a bounded test wait. Keep the exact attempt count and delivered-content assertions.
- Run the Windows update-stop suite in the existing serial coordination step, instead of the parallel full suite. Preserve the startup timeout and all shutdown/lease assertions. A workflow regression checks that the suite still runs exactly once on Windows and remains in the Linux full suite.
- Give the ephemeral-delegation test the same bounded cleanup allowance as the adjacent real-runtime test. Always remove its log listener and finish resource cleanup, even if waiting for the consumer fails. Keep every privacy and persistence assertion.

Only tests and CI scheduling change. Production behavior, persisted data, prompts, cache, and dependencies are unchanged. This branch includes the independent runtime fix for idle scans blocking `/stop`, which merged in #6565.

## Verification

- All 210 cron tests pass locally; Ruff and diff checks pass.
- Injecting 1.1 seconds into each of the two real schedule writes reproduces the timeout on the old test. The revised test passes with the same delay and real persistence.
- Removing the production schedule-preservation guard makes the revised test fail, so it still detects the original functional regression.
- A 150-millisecond pause before the restart-notice retry reproduces the original failure; the revised retry test passes with the same pause. Deadline-specific behavior remains covered by the send-retry policy tests.
- Removing the deadline-based retry path makes the revised notice test fail.
- Delaying each real storage executor shutdown by 1.1 seconds reproduces the old cleanup timeout. All four revised ephemeral-delegation cases pass with that delay. Forcing ephemeral execution to persist still fails the privacy assertions.
- 524 related cron, channel, update-stop, runtime-maintenance, subagent and CI-contract tests pass locally after the rebase and cleanup repair.
- Current-head CI is required before merge.

Assistant text containing `<tool_call>` markup could become an executable tool call, including quoted examples. Remove the plaintext extraction introduced in #4662 and require the API's structured tool-call fields. Preserve assistant text verbatim in streamed and final output.

The existing image retry policy is retained, including switching to Chat with images when Responses explicitly rejects `input_image`. Required Codex compaction still fails the request if compaction cannot succeed.

## Compatibility and limits

This intentionally removes plaintext tool execution. Services that return tool markup only in assistant text must expose structured tool calls. Provider documentation includes recovery guidance for self-hosted and hosted endpoints.

This does not hide XML, infer execution from text, or repair malformed model output. Legitimate code examples remain visible. Structured arguments still reach the existing tool validation boundary. prs.title: fix(webui): avoid remounting outgoing conversations
prs.body:
## Why

Switching away from a conversation with file diffs can block the main thread by rebuilding the conversation being left. The session-keyed results wrapper introduced in #6443 remounts `ThreadMessages` before the stream hook hands over its messages, so the outgoing diff DOM and synchronous layout measurements run again.

## What changed

- Retain the outgoing transcript until its messages actually hand over. Derive `messagesKey` from the stream's existing message scope and key only the transcript subtree on that owner, leaving the viewport/composer and selection-time scroll behavior intact.
- Reset all transcript-local state on real ownership changes, including activity overrides, message menus and nested disclosures. Keep the independent session-owned subtask disclosure reset.
- Cover outgoing diff reinsertion, cached A → fork → A isolation with shared turn IDs, direct subtask disclosure resets and the history-only consumer.

## Scope

This fixes redundant work when leaving a conversation. It does not change history loading, cache/replay policy, transport contracts, diff highlighting, or offscreen rendering.

## Verification

- The original baseline fails outgoing-node identity and diff reinsertion checks. The initial PR revision also reproduced an activity disclosure leaking into a cached fork with shared history IDs; that regression now passes alongside the original performance regression.
- Focused unit suites for viewport, subtask disclosures, stream/history hooks and temporary-chat navigation: **259 passed**.
- History browser verification: **10 passed**, covering outgoing diff retention, cached fork state reset, live/history reconciliation, desktop/mobile pagination and canceling an in-progress history pull.
- `git diff --check`: passed. Full-project validation is delegated to remote CI.

### Controlled performance comparison

Production-built real `ThreadShell`, synthetic HTTP/WebSocket data, Windows Chrome 156 headless, 1440 × 800, no CPU throttling. Heavy conversation: 20 file diffs × 120 lines (about 68,000 live DOM nodes); target: a short conversation. Three interleaved batches per build, one warm-up round trip excluded per batch, **12 measured switches per direction per build**. No other task-owned test/build ran during the reported comparison.

| Heavy → short | Baseline | Fix |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Click interaction median | 772 ms | 248 ms |
| Click interaction range | 688–848 ms | 224–328 ms |
| Processing median | 692 ms | 206 ms |
| Outgoing diffs reinserted per switch | 20 | 0 |

The median click interaction fell by **68%** in this workload. Rendering an incoming heavy conversation remains expensive: automation-observed content-ready medians were 1.401 s / 1.528 s, with maxima 1.714 s / 1.767 s (baseline / fix). That incoming-content median was about 9% higher in these runs; the PR does not claim parity for heavy entry or that every switch is below 200 ms. These numbers were remeasured after the ownership-isolation fix. The original private recording is not included.

prs.title: fix(webui): update usage and tool progress during active turns
prs.body:
## Summary

Resolves NAN-401

Long-running goals now keep the existing context meter and recent-round chart current before the whole task finishes. Existing run indicators and controls are reused; no separate model-status text is added. Individual tool results are published when each call settles, rather than waiting for slower siblings.

## Changes

- Emit typed logical model-call lifecycle snapshots at the provider invocation boundary, including failure/cancellation. Reuse reported usage and measured streaming telemetry; snapshots contain cumulative usage and at most eight runner-visible rounds. Recovery requests update the current round, matching terminal aggregation rather than changing the chart when the turn closes.
- Reuse existing routed delivery and durable display history. Update active-turn usage independently of answer streaming; final snapshots replace rather than duplicate live statistics. Fence duplicate/stale events and reject late usage snapshots after Stop/end.
- Publish per-call tool start/result events, including rejected calls and cancellation, without duplicate batch-end results. This does not change background shell-process observation semantics or absorb the closed, unmerged #6524.
- Preserve context-meter invalidation after successful compaction until a newer request reports context usage.
- Keep protocol v1 compatible: new clients opt into model-request history via `include_model_requests=1`; default history omits the optional event for older clients, with separate ETags. Older hosts still provide end-of-task statistics. Other channels do not receive model-request UI traffic.

## Verification

- Focused runner, hook, progress, WebSocket, transcript, and frontend regression suites cover live updates, bounded snapshots, cancellation/failure, fast tools with blocked siblings, deduplication, history replay, and compatibility.
- Latest UI-only verification: 247 focused frontend tests, TypeScript, targeted ESLint, and production build. Retired the extra status-label test along with its component, helper, unused projected phase, and ten locale strings; kept coverage for live usage, Stop, and stale-snapshot rejection.
- Follow-up integration verification: 126 focused Python tests; two real isolated Gateway/HTTP/WebSocket goal scenarios (normal finish beyond the former continuation limit, and Stop with independent follow-up). The live scenario verifies persisted usage before closure and old-client history/ETag separation.
- Real Gateway + local synthetic OpenAI-compatible model + Chromium: the fourth model call was held while the goal remained active. The desktop UI showed 107K context and three recent calls; reload preserved both. Checked desktop and 390px layout, then released the call and verified normal completion, with zero browser page errors.
- Follow-up browser acceptance includes malformed-call recovery: three reported requests produce two live rounds, guidance and reload retain the existing run controls and context meter, and the final model-request and turn-end round arrays for the same turn match. Desktop and 390px Chromium checks completed with no page errors.
- Rechecked the previous-head CI failures: updated event/hook/transcript test doubles and exact history URLs to the changed contract. The four affected UI test files pass, as do 26 focused history-boundary/prompt-rail browser tests; no tests were skipped to address failures.
- Ruff, targeted strict BasedPyright, TypeScript, client/server import boundaries, targeted ESLint, and production WebUI build checked locally.

No user documentation expansion, main-instance changes, external LLM calls, or deployment. Browser acceptance uses a synthetic model, not proof of every provider's usage reporting. Missing provider usage is not invented by the live feed; existing terminal estimation remains distinct. Windows execution is left to CI.

The previous CI coverage job also reported a coverage-database error. That tooling issue is not claimed fixed here; a new remote CI pass is still required.

prs.title: feat(webui): inspect file context in a live graph sidebar
prs.body:
The context control opens a persistent file graph beside the conversation. Users can see files used since the latest compaction, open them in the shared preview sidebar, and replay the graph's growth without interrupting chat.

## Behavior

- Show supplied prompt files, explicit skills, successful text-file reads, and discovered local Markdown references. A loaded node records use during this phase; it does not claim that all of the original text remains in the current model request. File-size indicators estimate the content actually read.
- Start a new replay phase after successful compaction. The next actual request supplies the new graph; existing historical snapshots remain readable. Missing historical snapshots are not recreated from today's files.
- Support node dragging, zoom, click-to-open details, transient labels for newly loaded files, adaptive replay, and smooth whole-panel expansion. Share sidebar surfaces and transitions with file previews, keeping the composer usable in split panes and on narrow screens.
- Move preview/source controls into the file header and simplify related navigation and session panels.

## Ownership and compatibility

- A WebUI observer consumes the ordered tool progress stream. It parses successful `read_file` results in a worker, stores compact read facts in display history, and restores observations across turns and restarts. It never rereads source files or linked targets; parsing failures preserve tool results.
- Prompt builders record raw file-use facts in a turn-local capture scope. A composed observer publishes those facts at the prepared-request boundary, before request lifecycle events. Parsing and token estimation run in the delivery worker, outside model execution. Parallel turns and cancellation keep capture scopes isolated.
- The runner exposes a generic `before_model_request` hook and reports individual request usage separately from accumulated usage. It does not read graph metadata. `loop.py`, context governance, runtime context blocks, file-read tools, session message persistence, and memory consolidation have no changes against the PR base.
- Skill loading shares its existing discovery snapshot and records the resolved source, including aliases. Rebuilding prompt files does not multiply their token estimates. Tool working directories belong to individual progress records, rather than the surrounding batch.
- Successful compaction starts a new phase; failed compaction preserves observations. Shell-command file-read inference is out of scope.
- Optional graph wire fields and compressed, self-contained history records remain supported. Compact history responses retain the `webui.context-graph.references.v1` capability; ordinary inline responses remain supported. No database migration or history rewrite is required.
- Canvas rendering retains keyboard/touch access, reduced-motion support, and suspension while hidden.

## Validation

Current head `355c3b720`: [all CI checks passed](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/41994720141), including `CI required`, WebUI checks/build, 3,551 WebUI unit tests, 408 browser tests, Python 3.11/3.14/Windows, Windows installer/process compatibility, both native-package acceptance jobs, Terminal UI and Docker.

CI follow-up fixes: await the lazy graph scene before replay timing assertions; update browser request expectations for graph encoding and the single preview toggle; verify wide tables remain scrollable; match the narrow-screen preview skeleton button to the real 44px control, eliminating a 12px loading shift. Local verification additionally passed all 63 affected browser cases, browser TypeScript and touched-file lint.

The first Windows Python run hit an unchanged shell test's one-second output wait before its first startup output. Both local Windows wait/timeout tests passed, and the failed CI job passed on one rerun without code or timeout changes. Other successful checks were retained; the final required aggregate is green. This CI result does not remove the mobile graph performance limitations documented below.

## Production performance retest — 2026-11-05

One round per scenario, as requested. Main: `e6127aa32`; PR performance implementation: `8a2a58c7f`. Cache thrashing and large Python-preview overhead improved substantially. Large mobile graphs and continuous graph growth remain slow; this is not a blanket performance sign-off.

### Shared paths (main → PR)

| Scenario | Main | PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Desktop input to next RAF, P95 | 15.1 ms | 15.4 ms |
| Desktop input during streaming, P95 | 15.0 ms | 13.1 ms |
| Mobile input to next RAF, P95 | 18.7 ms | 21.4 ms |
| Mobile input during streaming, P95 | 22.8 ms | 20.6 ms |
| Mobile streaming frame interval, P95 | 116.7 ms | 116.7 ms |
| Mobile scrolling frame interval, P95 | 33.2 ms | 33.3 ms |
| Desktop large Python preview, main-thread task total | 131 ms | 121 ms |
| Mobile large Python preview, main-thread task total | 480 ms | 514 ms |
| Mobile large Markdown preview, main-thread task total | 711 ms | 642 ms |

Preview numbers use the corrected mobile overlay fixture. Python highlighting limits now match main (100,000 characters / 2,000 lines); both show this 120 KB / 4,200-line file as full plain text. Mobile Python-preview longest tasks were 214/229 ms, so main itself is not free of preview jank. The former PR result was roughly 1,512 ms total with highlighting enabled; that historical comparison spans the newer main typography change as well.

### PR-only graph and analysis

Main has no graph: these are absolute PR costs, with older PR diagnostics used only as historical references.

- Mobile graph cessation: 100 nodes 2.53 s, 500 nodes 14.51 s (historical PR: 12.14 / 27.18 s). Both settle without timing out, and restore the full DPR-3 canvas afterward. This is time from opening until the final draw, not time until first interaction.
- Mobile opening frame-interval P95: 33.4 ms at 100 nodes; 116.7 ms at 500 nodes. The 500-node opening sample still contains 40 long tasks, up to 228 ms.
- Twelve-snapshot replay: 2.64 s, frame-interval P95 50 ms. Continuous growth every 200 ms remains poor: frame-interval P95 200 ms. These remain performance limitations.
- Repeated analysis of twenty approximately 8 KB prompt files: median 13.10 ms, P95 13.66 ms (historical PR median 158.54 ms). Six files: median 5.10 ms. First-use/warm-up tails remain; caching does not make initial parsing free.
- New-content 120 KB Markdown analysis still costs median 51.49 ms in the ordered delivery worker. Repeated content: median 1.66 ms. Non-file observation: about 0.4 microseconds. Closing the UI does not disable backend observation.

### Resources and lifecycle

- Full production entry JS/CSS gzip: 275,943 → 279,220 bytes (+3.2 KiB).
- Entry plus chat static JS/CSS closure: 449,060 → 480,053 bytes (+30.3 KiB). The historical increment was about 41.1 KiB. Graph layout and scene loading are deferred, but other feature code remains eager. Font assets are not included in these JS/CSS totals.
- Read 120 KB: median 3.65 → 3.53 ms; ordinary history write 1.07 → 1.10 ms; history read 1.04 → 1.02 ms.
- Three warm-up opens followed by twelve open/close cycles: stable DOM/listener counts; desktop heap 13.42 → 13.94 MiB, mobile 14.09 → 14.70 MiB, flattening toward the end. Closed-panel draws: zero. No page errors. This does not establish a long-term no-leak guarantee.

### Method and evidence

Windows / i5-13400 / headless Chromium / production builds. Desktop 1440×900 DPR 1; mobile emulation 393×852 DPR 3 with 4× CPU slowdown. Real ThreadViewport, ThreadComposer and preview components, 300 messages, stream updates every 50 ms. No model requests, full authenticated-app latency, real-phone measurement, Lighthouse score or official INP claim. Samples run serially; single-run differences can be noise. No traces were captured during this timing pass.

The primary round has 34 samples. A 14-sample targeted follow-up replaced preview samples with the correct overlay fixture and checked chat input/stream/scroll after adding the message shadow; mobile PR input P95 was 17.4 ms and streaming input 21.1 ms. The final user-requested change restores only the original background utility; that last color correction was visually checked and unit-tested, not performance-rerun. Bundle measurements include the shadow change before that final color-only correction.

Raw results and scripts: `C:/Users/HR/AppData/Local/nanobot-context-graph/perf-retest-20261105`: `frontend.json`, `frontend-followup.json`, `backend-main.json`, `backend-pr.json`, `backend-extra.json`, `settlement.json`, `memory.json`, `bundles.json`. Older comparison values come from the previously recorded report and summaries, not a fresh before-optimization control on the new base.

Tracks [NAN-407](https://linear.app/nanobot-ai/issue/NAN-407).

### Mobile CPU-only control

Same production fixture/artifact, 393×852 viewport, DPR 3 and touch input; only CPU throttle changed. One run at 1× and one at 4×, serially, with no source changes.

| Metric | CPU 1× | CPU 4× |
|---|---:|---:|
| Opening 100 nodes, frame interval P95 | 16.8 ms | 49.9 ms |
| Opening 500 nodes, frame interval P95 | 33.3 ms | 199.9 ms |
| Replay, frame interval P95 | 16.8 ms | 50.0 ms |
| Continuous growth, frame interval P95 | 33.3 ms | 216.7 ms |
| 100 nodes, last draw after opening | 1.68 s | 2.71 s |
| 500 nodes, last draw after opening | 1.80 s | 19.67 s |

At 1×, the 500-node opening and continuous-growth samples have no tasks over 50 ms, but their P95 frame intervals still indicate dropped frames. The 100-node opening contains one 54 ms task. Both configurations stop drawing once settled and restore the full DPR-3 canvas. Severe sustained jank was observed at 4×; it is inaccurate to claim there is no jank at 1×. This remains desktop mobile emulation, not evidence about real-phone hardware. The 4× result varies from the earlier 14.5 s measurement, illustrating single-run variability.

Artifacts in the same evidence directory: `cpu-control.json`, `cpu-settlement.json` and matching scripts/logs. No production code was changed for this comparison.

prs.title: refactor(commands): own trusted Shell completion outside agent loop
prs.body:
## User and maintenance scenario

A model's shell tool should return a bounded observation and keep the same long-running command available for later checks. A trusted user `!command` should instead wait for its full literal result. Those existing behaviors remain; changing how trusted commands wait or construct their replies should not require the model execution loop to know the concrete Shell implementation.

Resolves NAN-330

## Change

- Make the existing command route directly own trusted user Shell execution, scope setup and full-result handling in `command/user_shell.py`.
- Remove the Loop's Shell-specific callback and concrete ExecTool dependency. This is not a new generic tool/plugin capability or a duplicate execution service: both paths still use the configured Shell tool and existing process/session owner.
- Keep trusted-source checks, workspace/access policy, temporary/log-content scope, turn scopes, literal rendering, model bounded observations and existing timeout/cleanup rules.

The narrow internal `AgentLoop.execute_user_shell_command` method is removed; use the existing command route. No new public SDK/API behavior is promised. This is a concrete maintenance boundary, not a faster shell command, memory optimization or claim that every client/Loop coupling is gone.

## Verification

- **199 Python tests passed**: commands, exec session isolation/tools and task cancellation; real model-observation yield vs user full-result coverage, scope unwinding, existing restricted paths and literal output.
- Touched strict Python types, Ruff, import boundaries and diff checks passed.
- Actual isolated authenticated Gateway + WebSocket user Shell + HTTP saved history: full stdout/stderr/exit status, Markdown preserved literally, restricted traversal rejected. No model request, real credentials, production sessions or daily services. Owned Gateway exited cleanly.

Limits: real process probe on Linux; cross-platform execution is covered only by the selected CI matrix. No merge, deployment or formal review.


## Verified delivery

Head `148289350f6bd1faa693d3c54763960c4fd0e89f`. Final exact-head required gate and every selected check succeeded, including Windows. Out-of-scope WebUI/native/installer jobs were skipped, not run. The initial Windows failure was an unchanged prompt-responsiveness timeout; one bounded rerun passed without modifying the test or relaxing a gate. Its original cause remains unconfirmed.

Ready transition was executed and REST readback confirms OPEN, non-Draft, the same exact head, base main and mergeable. Linear is In Review, not Done; Ready is not approval or merge.

prs.title: fix(webui): stabilize context usage and session switching
prs.body:
## Why

The live context meter becomes empty (`—`) whenever a new model request advances the graph before reporting usage. Switching sessions also closes the graph, disrupting the single-pane layout. Simply keeping it open leaves the panel tied to a session-keyed composer and its detached alignment target.

## What changed

- Select live usage independently from the displayed graph, keeping the latest known measurement until a new one arrives. Replay stays frame-local, and compaction starts a new measurement baseline.
- Move sidebar ownership out of the keyed composer into the stable pane layout. The composer receives only its usage control; session changes reset graph, replay, and selection without replacing the open sidebar.
- Keep an already-open graph on single-pane session switches and show the target session's context. Loading or unmeasured sessions remain empty/unknown rather than showing the previous session's data. Closed panels stay closed.
- Use the workbench's actual visible pane count: multiple visible panes do not automatically carry the graph into another session. Manual opening remains available.
- Rebind sidebar alignment to the current composer surface when the session-keyed input changes. The viewport reports grid-row movement as well as size changes, so empty/history transitions cannot leave a stale bottom inset.
- Extend existing unit coverage and the history-hydration browser fixture for session switching, deferred history, sidebar identity, geometry, replay reset, and single/multiple visible panes. Update existing composer callers to the new control slot.

## Scope

Frontend presentation and ownership only; no provider accounting, event protocol, persistence, graph physics, or animation timing changes.

## Verification

- `git diff --check` and `bun run build` passed for the current source. The local build was requested to provide an isolated manual-test instance; full automated checks remain on remote CI.
- A real-provider smoke request successfully read two synthetic workspace files and returned their titles through the built WebUI.
- In the real gateway preview, empty/existing-session switches retain the sidebar. A controlled comparison with and without layout animation exposed a position-only alignment gap in the intermediate revision (161.5px); the final implementation aligns the sidebar and current composer bottoms in all four checked cases (0px difference).
- The latest published head awaits remote CI results. The intermediate revision passed WebUI checks/build and Docker; its browser job had not completed at the last bounded status check.
- The [earlier revision's CI](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/42154675129) passed WebUI checks/build and Docker, but the browser job had 415 passes and one failure: the mobile placeholder tooltip remained visible after Escape (`composer-action.spec.ts:189`). That failure has not been reproduced or repaired in this PR; no assertion, retry, or timeout was weakened.

prs.title: perf(ci): reduce WebUI browser test overhead
prs.body:
## Why

The WebUI browser job slows the development feedback loop. Marketplace and model-catalog skeleton checks loaded the same fixture twice per scenario, while CI used only two Playwright workers.

## What changed

- Capture skeleton geometry on a cold page, release its intercepted request, and compare the loaded geometry on that same page.
- Preserve the viewport, touch, language, provider, row-count, visibility, geometry, and overflow checks, along with individual test isolation and zero retries.
- Try up to three CI workers, bounded by available parallelism; local runs retain two. The runner's Ubuntu mirror and Playwright dependency installation are unchanged in the final diff.

## Scope and tradeoffs

The affected loaded states now follow a deliberately blocked request instead of a separate immediately fulfilled page; the skeleton is still checked on a cold load. More CI workers increase contention: in the runs below, individual case p95 increased from 7.1s to 8.8s, and the slowest case increased from 13.6s to 19.0s. No test deadline or assertion was weakened.

## Verification

- `git diff --check`: passed.
- [Final PR run](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/42175812824) passed all 419 browser cases with three workers and all selected WebUI and Docker checks. On the [matching base run](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/42170513010), the same 419 cases used two workers. The browser test step was 11m10s → 9m57s and the whole browser job was 11m36s → 10m23s. Each side has one run, so these numbers do not establish repeatable improvement or stability.
- A [two-worker PR run](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/42174218581) passed all 419 browser cases; its changed cases were shorter, but the whole job was 11m40s. This suggests reducing navigations alone was not enough in that comparison.
- An [earlier full PR run](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/actions/runs/42171661286) passed the browser cases but failed Python coverage (gateway process did not exit within 30s) and Windows native acceptance (packaged upgrade verification). Their causes remain unconfirmed; these lanes were skipped by normal path selection in later test-only runs, not revalidated.
