prs.title: fix(webui): distinguish unknown history from exhaustion
prs.body:
## Why

Live messages can arrive before the first history response. Pulling upward at the start of that partial transcript could show “No earlier messages” because an unknown history boundary shared the same `false` value as confirmed exhaustion. A failed first request left the same misleading state and no retry action above the live messages.

## What changed

- Keep the transcript's oldest boundary unknown until a history response establishes it; retain that distinction through live delivery, failed reads, and cached restoration.
- Show initial-history loading or retry feedback alongside live messages. Only confirmed boundaries enter the older-history spring/exhaustion flow, while backward input still gives the user control of the reading position.
- Match the boundary fixture's readiness to production and cover live-first loading, failure, retry, pagination, and genuine exhaustion with wheel and touch input.

## Scope

WebUI history state and presentation only. Local conversations still have a known start. HTTP/WebSocket contracts, persistence, backend behavior, and independent client/host upgrade requirements are unchanged.

## Blast Radius

Initial history hydration and the viewport's top-boundary feedback. Existing older-page loading, detached history navigation, and scroll ownership must remain intact.

## Verification

- Reproduced the pending-request and HTTP 503 counterexamples in Chromium with the real `ThreadShell` and synthetic HTTP/WebSocket delivery; delivering the same valid history first avoided the false exhaustion.
- Added regressions failed before the fix and passed afterward.
- `bun run test src/tests/thread-transcript.test.ts`: 30 passed.
- `bun run test src/tests/thread-viewport.test.tsx src/tests/useSessions.test.tsx`: 116 passed.
- `bun x playwright test browser/history-hydration.spec.ts -g 'unresolved history' --workers=1`: 2 passed using installed Chrome, covering wheel and CDP touch input.
- `git diff --check`: passed. Full validation is delegated to remote CI; it has not run locally.

The original recording's exact request ordering remains unknown; the controlled reproduction establishes this reachable defect, not that uncaptured ordering.

Resolves NAN-417

prs.title: refactor(webui): improve task navigation and isolate workflow ownership
prs.body:
## Why

Small edits should start at the behavior's owner and its existing tests, rather than require a tour of the repository or a large shared component. Add a progressive task index and isolate two concrete WebUI workflows without imposing a file-length limit or rewriting the application.

Resolves NAN-413

## What changed

- Link the root agent instructions to task-to-source/test navigation, with a more focused WebUI change map and a state-ownership guideline.
- Move channel pairing requests, subscriptions, polling, snooze and approval into `ChannelPairing`, with the existing popup/input in `PairingCodePopup`. `App` only mounts the feature.
- Move waiting-prompt storage, shared delivery ownership and turn-completion policy behind `useQueuedPrompt`. Keep draft input and UI feedback in `ThreadComposer`, preserving its application-level regression coverage.

## Scope

One independent change based on `main`. No AgentLoop/TUI rewrite, dependency change, API/wire change, storage migration, security-policy change, or intentional UI/copy change.

## Tradeoffs

The new boundaries own state and lifecycle, rather than just moving helpers. Existing broad App and Composer integration suites remain in place; this does not introduce a new test harness or claim measured development-time savings.

| Typical change | Before | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pairing refresh, approval retry, or snooze | State, effects, actions and popup spread through `App.tsx` | `ChannelPairing.tsx` owns the lifecycle; open `PairingCodePopup.tsx` only for input/display changes |
| Waiting-message persistence or completion gating | Store, authorization, turn effects and send logic mixed into `ThreadComposer.tsx` | `useQueuedPrompt.ts` owns queue state and execution; Composer supplies draft content and UI feedback |

The task maps link these owners directly to their retained regression and integration tests. This reduces the unrelated code needed for these tasks, not the repository's total line count.

## Blast Radius

WebUI channel pairing and waiting-prompt execution. The important retained contracts are visibility-aware notification/poll refresh, late approval replies and retry, same-page queue ownership, exact-turn completion, session switching, and draft/attachment retention after rejected sends.

## Verification

- Local source/diff review and `git diff --check`: passed. Checked 125 local Markdown link targets and their heading fragments; none missing. Runtime validation is delegated to remote CI.
- Pairing popup/helper text matches the baseline apart from its export/import boundary. Original App integration assertions and the desktop/mobile `pairing-refresh.spec.ts` browser scenarios remain; a focused snooze-expiry case is added.
- Queue persistence/delivery helpers and store remain text-identical apart from exports and the internal key argument type. Existing `queued-guidance`, `thread-composer`, `thread-shell`, `turn-completion` and queued-guidance browser test files are unchanged.
- Full remote lint, typecheck, tests, browser tests and production build: pending the PR's CI run. No local lint/typecheck/tests/build/browser checks were run.

releases.name: v0.4.1
releases.body:
## Changes

- Fix TLS certificate verification, sandboxed shell execution and workspace permissions for queued inputs.
- Keep idle maintenance from blocking active work or incorrectly refusing an update. Improve retry, reconnection and recovery behavior, and preserve native provider state through compaction.
- Add a file-context graph with file previews, local Markdown links and recent context snapshots. Switching topics keeps each conversation's context separate.
- Share syntax highlighting across code, source previews and read-only diffs, with complete source copying and plain-text fallbacks.
- Reduce unnecessary memory copies in file reads, session history and provider requests. Improve navigation, context-usage display, history loading and skill-source identification.
- Retain legacy history and proxy migration throughout 0.4.x, including original workspace ownership for unmigrated conversations.

## Upgrade notes

- Stop affected processes and back up configuration and conversations before an external upgrade. Use the original installer, package manager or container workflow, then verify the running version, old conversations, a new message and another restart. See [Updating nanobot](https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/blob/v0.4.1/docs/updating.md).
- **0.3.5 can upgrade directly to 0.4.1 through its original installation method.** No intermediate 0.4.0 installation is required. Legacy JSONL and proxy importers remain available throughout 0.4.x and are scheduled for removal in 0.5.0; retain original files and migration backups.
- **0.4.1 is the final release accepting the temporary OpenAI `apiType` / `api_type` conversion introduced in 0.4.0.** Save the migrated `api` configuration and replace old environment variables before a later upgrade; saving configuration does not rewrite the process environment.
- Managed program recovery is conditional and does not restore old chats over current data. Changed data can prevent safe program rollback; other installation owners retain their repair route.
- **In-app automatic installation is not enabled for this version.** Publishing packages does not enable release approval proof, change update subscriptions or activate a public Preview feed.
- Large or growing graphs and very large diffs can still be less responsive on slower devices. The memory changes are not a general latency guarantee; missing historical graph snapshots are not reconstructed from current files.

## Packages and verification

The platform wheels include the built WebUI and matching native TUI. Native installation, terminal and update/recovery checks passed on macOS arm64/x64, Linux arm64/x64 and Windows x64. Original public 0.3.5 and 0.4.0 upgrade paths were additionally tested on macOS with disposable data; this is not a guarantee for every environment.

Packages are attached below and available on [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/nanobot-ai/0.4.1/).

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/HKUDS/nanobot/compare/v0.4.0...v0.4.1

issues.body:
[Feature]: Optional response header showing model + thinking level in gateway replies

Problem or Use Case
Today, when Hermes is used through the messaging gateway (especially Telegram), it is hard to tell at a glance which model produced a given reply and what thinking/reasoning level was active for that turn.

This is especially useful when:
- comparing behavior across providers or model variants
- validating that a config change actually took effect in messaging sessions
- debugging reports like “the thread says it is one model but config says another”
- understanding whether a reply was produced with low / medium / high / none reasoning

Right now there are adjacent pieces, but not the actual user-facing reply header:
- #5892 is about show_reasoning not surfacing Anthropic thinking blocks correctly
- #4568 is about the CLI status bar showing the wrong model under routing
- #3710 is about model-picker UX in the gateway

This feature request is different: it is about optionally prepending a compact model/thinking header to the actual gateway-delivered reply text.

Proposed Solution
Add an optional gateway-facing response header that prepends a compact plain-text line before the assistant’s reply, for example:

Model: gpt-5.4 | Thinking: high

<actual reply follows>

Suggested behavior:
- Controlled by a config option, for example `display.response_header: true|false`
- Off by default (or defaulted conservatively if maintainers prefer)
- Applied in gateway/messaging replies, where users do not have the CLI status bar
- Uses the resolved runtime model for that turn, not just the configured default
- Uses the effective reasoning setting for that turn (`none`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, etc.)
- Plain text preferred so it renders safely across Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp without requiring rich formatting

Nice-to-have extension:
- support a shorter form, e.g. `gpt-5.4 · high`
- optionally expose provider too when useful, e.g. `Model: gpt-5.4 | Provider: openai-codex | Thinking: high`

Alternatives Considered
1. Rely only on `/model`, `/reasoning`, `/status`, or config inspection
   - This is weaker in messaging because it adds extra steps and does not tag the actual reply that was just produced.

2. Use `display.show_reasoning`
   - That surfaces reasoning content itself, not a compact summary of model + thinking level.
   - It is also much noisier than a one-line header.

3. Put this only in the CLI status bar
   - Messaging users do not get the CLI status bar, so that does not solve the gateway use case.

Feature Type
Gateway / messaging improvement

Scope
Small (single file, < 50 lines)

Contribution
I’m not volunteering a PR in this issue yet; this request is mainly for upstream product/UX consideration.

issues.title: hermes update restarts gateways from the old service file and rewrites it afterwards
issues.body:
`hermes update` restarts gateways from the service files the previous release wrote. On Linux the systemd user unit is rewritten only by the new gateway at boot, after systemd has already started it with the old unit's environment, and nothing restarts it afterwards. That boot-time rewrite also runs before the update's Node dependency step recreates `node_modules/.bin`, so right after a successful update `hermes gateway status` reports the unit as outdated.

Reproduced end to end: v0.23.0 installed with `install.sh`, gateway as a systemd user service, `hermes update --branch main --yes`. The journal shows the gateway started at the old unit, then `Updated gateway user service definition` from the new gateway five seconds later; with a stale unit on disk, the running gateway kept systemd's default `PATH`.

Today this costs an environment mismatch. Once module paths change, an old unit that names an internal module would start a process that fails on import, and the boot-time rewrite would never run.

Plan: rewrite every profile's launch file (systemd user and system units with a daemon-reload, the plists of stopped launchd jobs, the Windows `.cmd`/`.vbs` launchers compared by content) once the dependencies are prepared and before the first gateway start. Generators stay unchanged.

The explainer is attached as an artifact.

issues.title: Self-repo guard suggests clones into a scratch folder nothing prunes

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
When the terminal tool blocks a git command that would rewrite Hermes's own running checkout, its message suggests cloning into `<HERMES_HOME or ~/.hermes>/scratch/<task>`. Nothing prunes that folder: the idle prune covers only `<home>/cache/scratch` (`hermes_constants.get_scratch_dir`). Clones the agent makes there, often several GB with installed dependencies, stay on disk. The line also builds the home path by hand with a hard-coded `~/.hermes` fallback.

Plan: build the suggested path with `get_scratch_dir()`, so it names the active profile's pruned scratch folder.

The explainer is attached as an artifact.

issues.body:
**What changed.** On 14 October, #106742 (the unified gateway) moved every local conversation into one gateway process. The CLI, the terminal UI, the local Desktop app, the API server, editors, messaging bots, cron jobs, Kanban cards and Group Chats now hand their turns to that one process, instead of each running its own copy of the agent on the same session database. Updates also move installs with several profiles onto one shared gateway that serves them all. **Progress (7 Nov):** Since this issue opened on 23 Oct, 79 of its 305 problems are fixed on `main` (DB-11 by #141864; CMD-10 by #142166; CMD-11 by #142183; RT-85 by #143105; MSG-8, MSG-28, MSG-29, MSG-30, MSG-31 and MSG-32 by #143590; LC-31, LC-45 and LC-47 by #143591; LC-33 by #143592; MP-19, MP-20 and MP-28 by #143593; MP-24 by #143594; CLI-50 and GW-10 by #143595; HR-11 and HR-14 by #143596; RT-71 and RT-80 by #143597; RT-72 and RT-75 by #143598; TUI-29 by #143599; ACP-23 and ACP-24 by #143600; RT-30b, RT-48, RT-49, RT-54 and RT-56 by #143601; HR-15, HR-16, HR-20 and HR-23 by #143607; LC-35, LC-36 and LC-37 by #143626; MP-23 and MP-25 by #143660; GW-76 by #144534; CRON-11, KB-22 and RT-90 by #144591; GW-27 by #144592; KB-11 and KB-12 by #144593; RT-59 by #144594; MSG-34, MSG-35 and MSG-44 by #144595; DB-15 by #144596; CLI-54 and GW-60 by #144597; W11 and W13 by #144598; RT-52 by #144708; GW-42 by #144788; RT-89 and RT-92 by #144840; GW-39 by #144894; GW-81 and GW-82 by #144911; RT-30c by #145598; HR-9 by #145642; KB-16 by #145952; MSG-49 by #146249; DB-9 by #148219; HR-24 and HR-25 by #148418; HR-21 and HR-26 by #148422; HR-17 by #148436; HR-27 by #148877; RT-60 by #149419; HR-7 by #150240). 1 more have a fix in review in 1 PR, and 225 have no fix yet. **Status (25 Oct):** maintainers checked every row against `main` (`cb757fac59c9`) and ran [Wave 1](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/143547#issuecomment-6366610804). All 14 of its PRs are merged (#143590 to #143601, #143607 and #143626; their rows are marked 🟢 below, [summary](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/143547#issuecomment-6399704986)). MP-23 and MP-25 were fixed on `main` by #143660 (@yoniebans). MSG-29 isn't covered by a Wave 1 PR yet (still 🟠), and four rows stay deferred until the `hermes serve` cutover (🔵).
What broke for people, and how serious it is (by area and severity; click to open) **What broke for people.** 305 problems found on `main`, grouped by what people were doing (each problem is counted once): - **Opening and resuming chats (21):** Desktop can't reopen many stored chats: sessions cleaned up at a restart, chats from the API server, cron, subagents, the WebUI, Claude Code imports and bot handoffs, and a root profile's bot chat. A credential rewritten in config strands older sessions, and some large or compressed sessions fail to resume or come back out of order. - **Turns stuck, lost or never stopping (18):** A prompt can wait forever behind a paused session, a finished reply can miss the screen, queued messages can sit until a restart, and a turn keeps running after its window closes. One busy chat can freeze the gateway for everyone, and any local process can silently stop it from saving. - **Several profiles, renames and moves (51):** Renaming a profile or moving to the shared gateway strands old chats. Secrets, settings, ports and fallbacks are read from the wrong profile or not found. Desktop sends requests and lists to the wrong profile, parked or standalone profiles stay offline, and hosts with many profiles stall or restart. - **Messaging bots (26):** Background-task results never reach Discord threads, Slack DMs and relay chats. Progress updates, cron results and webhooks go out through the wrong profile's bot or not at all. Images, files and relay messages are dropped, and a stop or new conversation doesn't fence a command that is already running. - **Scheduled and background work (26):** Kanban cards fail for whole classes of models and providers, die or hang at start, hide why they failed, and never wake the chat that made them. Cron jobs stop their own gateway, are booked as failed during updates, pause while still running, or create an empty session on every tick. - **Desktop and the terminal UI (47):** Desktop doesn't reconnect after the gateway drops, forwarded turns lose their prompts and Stop, pasted screenshots vanish from history, and the context, queue, voice and dictation views show nothing or the wrong thing. Dashboard bulk actions and some remote connections are refused. - **Group Chats, including rooms across computers (23):** In gateway-hosted Group Chats a message or a Stop can be lost, rooms can't be renamed or ended, retries make duplicate rooms, and mention suggestions, file sends and rooms with Bots on two computers are gone. - **Windows and WSL (15):** A Desktop or CLI run under another account never attaches, stale Task Scheduler entries or a non-ASCII install path block start-up, updates start the gateway twice, and editor sessions in per-task homes time out. On WSL2 every Kanban card, cron run and subagent dies. - **Starting and updating the gateway (17):** Every client now needs one supervised gateway, so one start-up refusal blocks the CLI, terminal UI and Desktop together: an unpaired WhatsApp adapter, a symlinked database, a root-owned unit file, or a systemd, launchd, Home Manager, Docker or s6 mismatch. Desktop's update dialog fails without saying why. - **The terminal CLI, scripts, editors and API clients (34):** Scripts that pass their own session source, and old sessions resumed with flags, fail at start. The CLI's session lists miss recent chats. Editors lose their environment, MCP servers and session lists, and API clients get stuck sessions, ignored session names and lost messages after a stop. Several commands still start a second copy of Hermes. - **Model and provider picks (14):** Named custom endpoints collapse to a bare provider and fail, model switches crash on chats that follow their profile, picks and fallbacks land on the wrong provider, and reasoning and Fast changes are dropped. - **Tools and plugins (13):** Terminal commands run with the environment and API keys of whichever client started the shared gateway, or lose the client's own variables. Workspace containers are killed mid-run or pile up, and plugin shell calls and some hooks stop working. **How serious it is.** Of the 305 problems, 156 are broken (something fails or gives a wrong result), 120 degraded (silently does less), 9 security and 20 cosmetic. 37 of these are older multiplexing bugs that #106742's update made everyone with several profiles hit. 228 are confirmed still present on current `main`, by a live run or a code read; 124 were reproduced live on a build that has the gateway. The worst: - Terminal commands can run with the environment and API keys of whichever client started the shared gateway, so later runs and other profiles inherit them. - Any local process that opens the session database can silently stop the running gateway from saving anything until it restarts. - On a gateway serving several bots, one profile's progress updates and review notices arrive in another bot's chat. - Desktop can't reopen many stored chats, and several of these failures came back on builds that contain the earlier fix. - Background-task results never arrive in Discord threads or Slack DMs, and Kanban cards fail for whole classes of models and on WSL2. - A single start-up refusal, such as an unpaired WhatsApp adapter, blocks every local client at once. Hit hardest: installs with several profiles (51 problems) and Desktop and the terminal UI (47). Data loss shows up as messages, replies and background results that never arrive, and as pasted screenshots that vanish from history.
**What this issue is.** #134889 closed on 21 October with rows still open, and reports kept arriving after it closed. This issue gathers what is still open on `main`, from anyone: #134889's leftover rows, its package issues, and reports filed after it closed. Only problems that #106742 or its cutover caused are counted; the rest are listed for a second look in the [housekeeping comment](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/143547#issuecomment-6365457974). Everything is grouped into lanes that can be fixed in parallel, as the packages were. Maintainers: edit this description freely; it's meant to be maintained like #134889. ## Found a problem on `main`? Report here **Report anything you hit with the unified gateway as a comment on this issue**, or link your issue here. Each report is checked on current `main` and triaged into a lane below, and the fix PR is linked back on your comment so you can retest. Include, where you can: - **Build:** the `main` SHA (`git rev-parse --short HEAD`) or `hermes --version`, plus Desktop's version from Settings → About if Desktop is involved. v0.22.2 has no gateway runtime, so retest a v0.22.2-only problem on v0.22.3 or later first. - **Surface and setup:** CLI / TUI / Desktop (local) / API / ACP / bot / cron / Kanban / Group Chat; OS; native, container or WSL; one profile or several on one gateway - **Steps, expected, actual** - **Evidence:** the relevant lines from `~/.hermes/logs/gateway.log`, `errors.log` and Desktop's `desktop.log`; for a stuck or lost turn, its `session_admissions` row (`intent`, `status`, `outcome`, `owner_epoch`) - **Redact** tokens, API keys, cookies, tickets and session URLs before posting Fixing an item? Name its ID (for example `RT-30a`) in the PR so it can be ticked off here. ## Contract under test From [#134889](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/134889), unchanged: - Queued admissions survive an owner restart and run FIFO, exactly once. - A started admission that loses its owner becomes interrupted and is never replayed automatically. - A retry reuses the original admission identity and committed payload. - Clients read and submit; the gateway is the only canonical writer. - Profile, provider, generation and revision boundaries hold on every transport. Deliberate limits (not bugs), as in #134889: the served profile set is a start-time snapshot (adding a profile needs `hermes gateway restart`), and hosted-room execution across two profiles on one gateway is not live-certified. ## Direction: follow #106742 Every fix here must keep the direction of [#106742](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/106742). Put this section in the brief of every sub-agent you start. - One gateway owns every local session: one FIFO, one durable queue, one writer. Fix the gateway path. Don't bring back a client-side agent, a local fallback or a second writer to `state.db`. - Clients only read and submit. A missing capability gets a gateway handler or a named refusal, not client-side state. - Keep the contract above, and profile boundaries on every transport. - Design calls are yours. Pick the option that best fits this design and write the choice and the reason in the PR body. Ask here only when every option would break a rule above. ## Working rules - Branch from current `main`. Reproduce 🟡 rows on `main` first. A row that doesn't reproduce gets no commit: post the evidence (`file:line`, the probe test) here. - Lanes touch different code, so they can run in parallel. Open one PR per lane (split it if it grows), each with a failing test first. - Name the row ID in the PR and reference this issue, as the packages did (`Refs #134889 (GW-19)`). Use `Fixes` only for the row's own report (`Fixes #142942`), never for this issue or #134889. - **An open PR from an outside contributor doesn't cover a row.** Review it. If it's right, finish it on the contributor's branch, or salvage it with `git cherry-pick -x` so they stay its author and add your work on top; use `Co-authored-by` only for code you rebuilt. If it's wrong or stale, fix the row fresh, say why on that PR, and close it with a credit note. - A fix not run against what it targets (Desktop, a gateway serving several profiles, native Windows, an install upgraded from an older version) uses `Refs`, not `Fixes`, and says what still needs a live retest. - 🔵 rows wait for a maintainer decision. Record it here, then fix. ## Lanes Each lane is one kind of fix in one part of the code, so lanes can run in parallel. Lanes are ordered by how many broken and security rows they hold. Rows within a lane: security and broken first. | Lane | What it fixes | Rows (broken / degraded / security / cosmetic) | Start with | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | [1. Opening stored chats](#lane-1-opening-stored-chats) | Resume, adoption and history controls for rows the gateway did not create live | 14 (13 / 1 / 0 / 0) | RT-30a, RT-30b | | [2. Group Chats (#97681)](#lane-2-group-chats-97681) | Gateway-hosted Group Chats: send, Stop, gates, files, and rooms across computers | 23 (11 / 8 / 1 / 3) | HR-8, HR-12 | | [3. Starting, restarting and updating the gateway](#lane-3-starting-restarting-and-updating-the-gateway) | `hermes gateway ensure`, service-manager discovery and identity checks, start-up refusals, restart and update hand-offs | 16 (11 / 4 / 0 / 1) | GW-27, GW-30 | | [4. Profile scope inside the shared gateway](#lane-4-profile-scope-inside-the-shared-gateway) | Code that reads `os.environ`, a module global or the launch profile instead of the served profile's scope | 19 (8 / 8 / 2 / 1) | GW-41, GW-42 | | [5. Kanban and managed workers](#lane-5-kanban-and-managed-workers) | `agent/managed_worker.py`, `gateway/session_kanban.py` and the worker client | 13 (7 / 5 / 1 / 0) | KB-10, KB-11 | | [6. Background results that never arrive](#lane-6-background-results-that-never-arrive) | Automation, completion and notify wakes refused `admission_conflict` or never admitted | 13 (12 / 1 / 0 / 0) | MSG-8, KB-22 | | [7. issues.body:
Hermes bots are personal agents. Each one runs where its owner chooses, with its own models, tools, memory and credentials. This issue builds the foundation that lets them work together: across machines now, and across owners next, without anyone giving up control of their bots.

[Current review queue and version-specific evidence](#user-content-current-disposition)

Teknium set the bar on [31 Aug](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/97681#issuecomment-5472640342): a group chat must survive **any** gateway going down, including the authority host, and must keep going when one or more bots become unavailable.

That includes continuously persisting the **full ordered event log on every participant gateway**, so a surviving participant holds the conversation’s history. Surviving-participant epoch takeover is a stated design goal; automatic promotion can land later, once split brain can be prevented. The storage schema and replay contract must be shaped for that now. Replication targets and permission to become the writer are separate: a copy alone grants no authority, and an offline participant must not impose a unanimity barrier on healthy participants.

![Bots on a laptop, home server and VPS collaborating in one group chat, with Desktop and phone access](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dokterdok/hermes-agent/653a19574bd6b5de7fa0cbb1ce67a057446b6c51/docs/issue-assets/bot-group-chats-concept.png)

## Seven layers

These are the complete layer contracts, not a claim that every guarantee is already on `main`. The dated [implementation status](#user-content-implementation-status) below is the canonical PR-state map.

![Seven-layer group chat architecture. Merged foundations: 1 durable identity and replay, 2 gateway-owned execution, 3 cross-gateway collaboration (foundation on main), on the unified gateway runtime, now on main. Parallel tracks: 4 Desktop, 5 shared files, 6 messaging. 7 host-loss resilience spans every layer: every member computer keeps the full history, and a group moves on its own to a computer its owner allowed, with no cloud in the middle. Future directions build on the whole stack. Review order: 1, the fixes since #106742, led by #149775 (Layer 4 landed as #148877); 2, shared files; 3, cross-gateway group chats, whose gateway half is open as #149655 (the maintainer's salvage of #148466).](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dokterdok/hermes-agent/b14a47c0f201ec279fe49a8ecda4f77eee8c3d8e/docs/issue-assets/bot-group-chat-layers-20261106.png)

| Layer | What it guarantees | PRs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **1. Durable identity & replay** | One ordered conversation you can return to. Work already accepted is recognized. | Merged foundation: #99007. Safety owner: #99107 (closed and retained). |
| **2. Gateway-owned execution** | Rounds run on the gateway instead of in the Desktop window. | merged #99099 |
| **3. Cross-gateway collaboration** | Bots on different gateways request work and exchange results, even after a lost reply. | Merged foundation: #99244, with which a gateway kept a group chat with bots on other gateways running with Desktop closed, until #106742 turned it off. Slice 1's gateway half, #149655 (the maintainer's salvage of #148466), brought that back on `main` on 6 November; its Desktop half is the draft #149702 (#141178, #142248, #142926, #144634). |
| **4. Desktop** | Create hosted groups that keep running when Desktop closes. Follow progress, reconnect and send follow-ups. | Landed on 5 November as #148877, the maintainer's salvage of #143218 (which continues #97846). Merged maintainer PRs #148418 (group chats with bots on several computers, Desktop-driven while Desktop is open) and #148422 (the native chat look and each bot's live state) build on the same client. |
| **5. Shared files** | Retain accepted inputs, retrieve published outputs and share bounded files/PDFs across gateways. | Rebuilt on `main` from #98072, #99159 and #104199: open as #150450, bots sharing files next. Input custody (#111362) is on `main`. Files across gateways (#131022, #131353) wait for Layer 3 · #104198 is parked classic-only work |
| **6. Messaging** | List, send to, approve and stop a group's work from an authorized private or shared chat, including "always allow in this chat". | #111939, absorbing #98073's canonical part; its slice 1 (read-only `/group`) is queued |
| **7. Host-loss resilience** | Every member computer keeps the full ordered history unless its operator opts out. When the host goes away, the group can continue on a computer its owner allowed: automatically by majority with three or more always-on voters; Ask me first by default with exactly two; or a deliberate manual move. Two-computer careful automatic recovery requires separate risk consent because both sides of a network split may keep working. Moves reconcile accepted work; uncertain work never reruns by itself. A returning host rejoins as a copy. | #99107 (copy-integrity fixes posted as #143380, #143381, #143382 and #143383), #104601, #105079, #105197 · UX: #130790, #97846, #111939 (closed, retained sources below) |
| Runtime pieces | Contracts the layers consume from the unified runtime (#106742), and fixes found while reviewing it. | Mostly on `main` now: #111216, #116137, #116477 and #130016 are superseded, #120652 was absorbed and #109338 is partly on `main` · #116466 is parked |

Supporting fixes, to include where the affected workflow needs them: #100755, #105467, #93224 (#109644 and #109647 are superseded on `main`). #105984 merged on 6 October and #105985 merged on 3 October. #103638 and #97273 are closed, because `main` fixed both differently. The optional UI companions #93903 and #93993 are parked: they render only in classic groups, which no current gateway runs.

**How it lands.** Each PR names its prerequisites and owns a defined behavior. Shared runtime changes are carried or composed where needed, with exact provenance stated by each owner. Some independent owners also touch the same call sites; their descriptions document the resolutions exercised in local composition tests. This is not a claim that every branch merges automatically or that the entire stack has passed native-app or hosted-CI acceptance. PRs land as their prerequisites land. #98307 (closed, kept for testing) is an integration branch and is never merged.

Shared-file history and byte availability are separate. The full ordered log retains shared-file references; bytes stay on the computer that stored them. After host loss, verified references remain visible as unavailable. This does not add byte replication or promise that an old file becomes downloadable when its original host rejoins.

## Cross-layer lifecycle contracts

The aim is simple: keep accepted files available while work is unresolved, prevent an uncertain retry from silently starting another task, and stop a replacement bot from acting as the original one.

**Readiness:** these contracts do not establish full-stack, public-only, native or hosted-CI acceptance.

<details>
<summary>Technical contracts and dependencies</summary>

```text
Accepted attachment work
  |-- Viewer disconnects: accepted work and input obligations remain owned
  `-- Authorized Stop: refuse new work within its scope, retain obligations
          |
          v
      Execution settles / cancellation is acknowledged
          |
          v
      Output settles its publication / ACK / discard obligations
          |
          v
      Input releases only when applicable holders and evidence permit
```

*Intended lifecycle, not a literal call graph or proof of every path. The current Input and Output owners have separate durable obligations and scoped composition checks. The older stopped-output acknowledgment/retained-input donor is preserved in #111362's recovery map; it is not claimed as implemented by the current standalone branches. Ordinary successful completion keeps its applicable release rules.*

- **[Input — #111362](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/111362):** retain/reconstruct the exact accepted inputs; require identity-matched release evidence. An apparently completed Output record is not an acknowledgment of an outstanding obligation. `main` now provides this with its own design (`e217e102ab2` and follow-ups), so #111362 is not needed.
- **[Route — #100016](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/100016):** preserve the selected bot/route and accepted-work identity across reconnects and replacements; closing admission does not erase authorized settlement obligations or grant new execution authority.
- **[Output — #99159](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/99159):** own publication, attempt identity and pending acknowledgment/discard obligations. Repeated observations reconcile the same attempt; uncertain external outcomes do not establish exactly-once delivery.

**One Gateway compatibility:** the [entry-point/session-ownership proposal](https://gist.github.com/unsupportedpastels/765f9d551ce88ee01630c18367763e75) moves callers to the canonical profile authority; it does not turn local session ownership into group chat authority. Group chat epochs, independent participant gateways and passive-history restrictions remain intact. On `main`, automatic takeover remains off; the retained Layer 7 implementation and its revision-specific tests are separate, nor does it make the whole Layers stack a prerequisite of the caller cutover. Exact source, dependency tuples, decisive regressions and open public-only/native/full-composition gates stay in the owning PRs.

</details>

## Decisions

1. **One owner per group chat.** One gateway owns each group chat's authority and ordered log, with an epoch that only increases and no leaderless replication. ([31 Aug](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/97681#issuecomment-5472640342))
2. **Durable beyond the authority host.** This is a design goal, and takeover waits until split brain can be prevented (same decision). On `main`, copies on other gateways stay passive and automatic takeover is off. A successor must be provably the only one, including during a network partition and when the old host rejoins. Layer 7's proposal (#105197) meets this with a majority lease for groups with three or more always-on computers; two-computer groups ask by default. Careful automatic recovery is available only after separate explicit risk consent, and a manual Continue anyway also depends on the owner correctly judging that the old host is offline.
3. **Clients don't coordinate.** Desktop and messaging apps are views and controls, never hidden coordinators.
4. **Uncertainty is surfaced, not retried.** A missing receipt never authorizes running work again, and missing evidence never proves that work didn't run.
5. **History isn't authority.** A replicated copy of history gives no authority to execute. Files, secrets and OAuth identities stay with their host, and resources on a host that is unavailable stay visibly unavailable.
6. **Owners, not tenants.** Group chats connect separate owners' instances. Multi-tenancy is a different problem (#34352).
7. **Reachability.** Behind NAT, put authority on the host that every participant can reach. Reverse-dial and relays come later.

## Done when

On a released build, with bots on at least two gateways:
1. A group created in Desktop keeps running after Desktop closes, and reopening it on another device shows the same history.
2. Bots on different gateways hand work and files to each other, and the user retrieves the exact version that was produced.
3. An authorized messaging chat, private or shared, can list a group's work, send to it, approve or deny its requests (once, or always in that chat) and stop it.
4. When the authority host is lost mid-conversation, accepted work is reconciled and exactly one successor continues the same conversation. This must hold when both hosts are alive on either side of a partition, when successors compete, and when the old host rejoins. (Two-computer careful automatic recovery is a separately accepted exception: during a cut it can run on both sides until a device bridges them or they reconnect. It is off by default; the owner is warned and can choose which history to keep.)

## Terms

- **Bot:** a Hermes profile, shown in Desktop's Bot Mode.
- **Gateway:** the long-running Hermes process on a machine (`hermes gateway run` or `hermes serve`).
- **Hosted group:** a group chat whose rounds a gateway drives. A **classic** group is one that Desktop drives.
- **Authority:** the one gateway that orders a group's history. Its **epoch** goes up each time authority moves to another gateway.

## What this unlocks

<details>
<summary>Future product directions enabled by these foundations</summary>

Think of a team where everyone brings their own computer, accounts and tools. They collaborate through conversations, requests and files they deliberately share, and joining the team doesn't give anyone access to anyone else's laptop. That is the model here: **personal agents that work together without their owners giving up control.** It extends Hermes' [personal-agent model](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/) from one agent to many.

Every direction below depends on what the seven layers provide: durable identity, a single authority for each group chat, safe dispatch across gateways, custody of shared files, authorized control, and recovery when a host is lost. That's why the foundation is built as contracts rather than as a Desktop feature.

1. **Scoped collaboration identities.** Owners choose which tools, files and knowledge a bot may use or disclose in each group, with enforced approval and revocation. Related: [per-tool allow/ask/deny rules (#80993)](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/80993) and [per-chat memory scoping (#28279)](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/28279). Neither is enough for complete isolation on its own.
2. **Invite other people's bots safely.** Revocable roles, explicit access to earlier files and history, and joining or leaving without breaking the conversation ([#102253](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/102253)). Documented API and messaging flows for creating groups, so Desktop is optional from the start.
3. **Limits on cost and autonomy.** Per-bot and per-group limits on spending, time and delegation, with clear approvals and a record of who did what. [Per-session token budgets (#91713)](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/91713) are a starting point, not a complete group budget.
4. **Reusable specialist teams.** Save roles and handoffs for recurring research, review or implementation, with a record of where each result came from and checkpoints where a human signs off.
5. **Community contribution campaigns.** Maintainers invite community-owned bots to help resolve an issue, matching bounded tasks to each bot's specialty, model and owner-approved budget. Contributors keep control and credit, and maintainers coordinate review. Bots from other frameworks could take part through an open collaboration protocol built on existing standards.
6. **A discoverable bot ecosystem.** Owners offer specialists for bounded jobs through trusted directories, without handing over credentials or private memory. Verifying capabilities and preventing abuse need their own design, because a listing is not trust.
7. **Broader reach.** Relay or reverse-dial connections would remove the requirement that hosts can reach each other directly. A relay could also hold a content-free vote, so two-computer groups get the same safe automatic moves as groups with three always-on computers (Layer 7 leaves room for it).
8. **A bots-first mobile app.** A familiar chat experience without plumbing or jargon, bringing bot collaboration to people who aren't technical. The initial native-app API slice below is smaller than this broader product direction.

These are follow-on directions, not requirements for closing this issue.

</details>

## Bot Mode in a native Hermes app

<details>
<summary>How a native app could reuse the group chat contracts</summary>

With #106742 and the changes proposed in the [One Gateway gist](https://gist.github.com/unsupportedpastels/765f9d551ce88ee01630c18367763e75) in place, a native Hermes app could let users pick up their existing conversations on another device.

For group chats, the expectation would be familiar: open the app, find the groups you already belong to, catch up on messages, talk to the bots and send commands, just as you would in any chat app. You should be able to leave and return later without recreating the group, losing progress or keeping Desktop open.

The groundwork in this issue can support that experience: shared group history and live updates, conversations that keep running while the app is closed, reliable follow-up messages, approvals and Stop with the right permissions, and file sharing. That includes groups whose bots run on different machines.

A native app could reuse this group behavior: The existing `groups.*` API and the layer PRs are starting points for the integration, not a finished native-app feature:

| App needs | Relevant work |
| --- | --- |
| Find the right group, load its history and catch up after reconnecting | Durable identity/replay in merged #99007; the Desktop consumer and reconnect cases in #143218 |
| Keep the conversation running while the app is closed | Gateway execution in merged #99099; client integration on `main`, completed in #143218 |
| Send follow-ups and avoid duplicate work after a lost reply, including across gateways | Merged transport #99244; route and retry contracts from #100016 and #99960, rebuilt on `main` as slice 1 (a new PR when a slot frees) |
| Approve, deny or stop the intended work under explicit permissions | Canonical runtime controls in #106742, admission/lifetime guards on `main` (superseding #111216) and participant controls in #105079. Messaging #98073/#111939 is a separate consumer with its own consent rules, not a required native-app transport |
| Share an input and retrieve the exact result later | Input custody on `main`; Layer 5's file catalog and bot output, rebuilt on `main` (#150450, bots sharing files next). Its Desktop Files is a consumer, not a native UI implementation |

**Proposed first app/API slice:** hosted-group discovery and creation, history/live progress, follow-up submission and scoped controls. File exchange can follow the app's requirements. Full authority-host recovery is a separate milestone; the whole seven-layer roadmap need not block an initial app integration. This does not change the programme's completion criteria above.

This work builds on the one-gateway runtime in #106742. It does not replace that PR or its staged remote-client cutover. The native-app API still needs agreement on authenticated access, gateway/profile discovery, replay after connection gaps, command/receipt identities and version compatibility. No new REST routes or fast-follow landing commitments are specified here.

Some foundations have merged; the remaining owners have revision-specific implementation and tests. They are not a finished native-app API or a fully accepted app/backend combination. The useful next step is to compare the app's API sketch with these contracts and choose the first supported journey.

</details>

### What is on main

`main` already has the foundations:
- **Gateway-owned group chats:** durable identity and ordered replay (#99007), a gateway round driver (#99099) and cross-gateway dispatch (#99244). They are reachable through the gateway's `groups.*` API.
- **Bot-to-bot messages across machines without Desktop:** [`hermes peer`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/website/docs/user-guide/bot-mode.md#bot-initiated-dms-across-machines-hermes-peer).
- **Manual authority transfer:** an [operator procedure](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/website/docs/user-guide/bot-mode.md#transferring-hosted-room-authority) that requires fencing the old host first. Automatic takeover is off.

The first gap users hit was that Desktop didn't use those foundations and drove rounds itself. Even when every bot lived on an always-on server, a group chat stopped when the laptop running Desktop slept ([field report, 23 Sep](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/95163#issuecomment-5803548558)). The docs described that behavior as shipped ([bot-mode.md:158](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/130b8f2c5dbc/website/docs/user-guide/bot-mode.md?plain=1#L158)). Since #106742 landed on 14 October, `main` runs new Desktop groups on the gateway; Layer 4 (#148877, merged on 5 November) completes the client. The other layers deliver the rest of the bar.

<summary>Layer 7 copy, continuation and authority boundaries</summary>

#### Layer 7: host-loss resilience

**Reviewed audit contract.** Built to Teknium's [31 Aug bar](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/97681#issuecomment-5472640342) and [follow-up](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/issues/97681#issuecomment-5473401238). The full design, with diagrams, is at the top of #105197.

- **Full copies.**
  - Every member computer keeps the full ordered history by default, with an explicit opt-out. The owner can add backup computers that hold a copy without a bot.
  - An opted-out computer (`groups.peer.invite` with `replication: false`) holds no copy and can't host the group. If no other computer holds a copy, the group waits for its host, and its status shows how much history only the host holds (`at_risk`). The opt-out is the one operator-chosen exception to the every-participant history bar.
  - A copy grants no authority. It follows the group only through verified, marked transitions.
- **Who may host next is owner-controlled:** the computer's operator allowed it, and the owner designated it. Always-on computers among them vote; laptops can continue a group on request but never vote.
- **How a group moves when its host goes away:**
  - **Majority mode, 3+ voters:** the host runs only while a majority grants its lease. A standby takes over automatically only after the lease ends, so an automatic move never leaves two hosts; an owner's "Continue anyway" can override this.
  - **Ask by default with exactly 2 voters. Careful mode is an explicit opt-in:** the standby moves after 3 minutes of silence in both directions, if its own online check passes (public endpoints only). The owner is warned with Keep going, Go back or Ask me first.
    - This mode doesn't prevent split brain, and it's the one place the layer goes past the bar, only after separate risk acceptance.
    - If both computers stay online but can't reach each other, both run until a device that reaches both passes on the move, or they reconnect. The host at the higher epoch then keeps running.
  - **Ask mode:** the owner taps "Continue on <best computer>".
  - **Planned stops and sleep:** the old host hands over itself.
- **Accepted work is reconciled** as completed, re-attached, unknown (shown, never rerun) or waiting for a host.
  - In majority mode, tasks are dispatched only after a majority stores them.
  - In the other modes, work dispatched in the old host's last seconds can be unknown to the successor, and the owner can send again.
- **No cloud in the middle.** A content-free referee vote (relay, or opt-in hosted) is a designed extension point, not built.
- **It fits the planned one-gateway-per-installation entry point:**
  - a restart through Hermes is announced and isn't treated as host loss (in majority mode the voters extend the host's lease);
  - copies and keys are per installation;
  - group chat authority stays separate from each bot's session authority.

issues.title: A sleeping group chat member stalls other chats on the same connection
issues.body:
When a bot's computer stops responding, using Stop or Disband in its group chat can also freeze reads and controls in other chats on the same Desktop connection.

Steps on main (`6b21d0564d`):

1. Create a gateway-owned group chat with a bot on another computer. Keep another group chat and an ordinary session available on the same gateway connection.
2. Pause the member gateway process, or put its computer to sleep while keeping the group chat's gateway awake.
3. Choose Disband in the group chat. For the Stop case, first leave a peer turn running or uncertain, then choose Stop.
4. Refresh the group chat, switch to another group chat and use Stop or answer an approval, or submit a prompt or interrupt in the ordinary session.

Expected: reads and unrelated chats keep working while this group chat waits for its member. The group chat stays available when safe deletion can't finish.

Actual: the shared socket waits for the slow operation before dispatching later requests. Desktop uses a 30-second request deadline, so requests can fail with messages such as `request timed out after 30s: groups.state`. The connection can still answer heartbeats. A timed-out control may execute later after the wait clears.

I saw this live on real Electron with a second gateway paused: pressing Disband showed `request timed out after 30s: groups.state`. From the code, a socket runs nearly every request in order, and each call to the other computer can take 30 seconds.

Regression: `tests/tui_gateway/test_ws_group_controls.py` drives the real socket dispatcher. The peer-wait cases use the real canonical group service and a gated peer HTTP boundary. On main, group reads and unrelated controls fail to answer while that boundary is held. The Stop case also checks that uncertain admission recovery makes two attempts before returning.

A fix with those tests is open as #150486.

Refs #97681

issues.title: Observed group messages are persisted with a substituted timestamp: adapters write an ISO string the write path rejects (one WARNING per message)

labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

issues.body:
### What happens

Every group message recorded by an observe path is persisted with a **substituted** timestamp and
logs one WARNING per message:

```
WARNING hermes_cli.timefmt: Ignoring corrupt message timestamp '2026-09-21T09:59:17.532760+00:00'
```

On a Telegram group running `observe_unmentioned_group_messages: true` this is **222 warnings in a
single day** in one deployment's `errors.log` — one per observed message. `errors.log` is the
WARNING+ channel operators actually read, so a genuine warning is now a needle in a haystack.

### Root cause

The observe paths stamp the transcript entry with an **ISO string**, while the write path only
trusts epoch numbers.

`plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py::_observe_unmentioned_group_message`:

```python
entry = {
    "role": "user", "content": self._telegram_group_observe_attributed_text(event),
    "timestamp": datetime.now(tz=timezone.utc).isoformat(), "observed": True}
...
store.append_to_transcript(session_entry.session_id, entry)
```

`gateway/session_transcript.py::_append_transcript_message` passes that value straight to
`append_message(timestamp=...)`, which runs it through
`hermes_state_messages.py::_coerce_timestamp` → `hermes_cli/timefmt.py::coerce_epoch`:

```python
try:
    ts = float(value.timestamp()) if isinstance(value, datetime) else float(value)
except (TypeError, ValueError):
    ts = math.nan
if not (EPOCH_MIN <= ts <= EPOCH_MAX):  # also False for nan
    logger.warning("Ignoring corrupt %s %r%s", field, value, ...)
    return None
```

A `datetime` is accepted, a **string spelling of one is not** — so the row silently falls back to
the write-time default and the warning fires. `EPOCH_MIN..EPOCH_MAX` exists to catch garbage
doubles from damaged pages (#102399, #102352, #99959); here it is a writer handing the reader
a format it never accepted.

### Same bug class, three sites

`grep`ping the other `append_to_transcript` callers:

- `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py` — `_observe_unmentioned_group_message` (observed group chatter)
- `gateway/platforms/yuanbao.py` — `GroupAtGuardMiddleware._observe_group_message` (observed group chatter)
- `gateway/platforms/yuanbao.py` — the recall system note (`[recall] message_id=... has been recalled`)

Every caller in `gateway/run_turn.py` already passes `time.time()` and is unaffected.
`gateway/mirror.py` builds an ISO `timestamp` key too, but `_append_to_sqlite` never forwards it to
`append_message`, so it is a dead field rather than a corrupt write — excluded here.

### Impact

Not data loss: the fallback is the write instant, microseconds from the intended value. The cost is
the log flood and the fact that `messages.timestamp` no longer comes from the adapter that observed
the message — a deferred or replayed observe write would silently record the wrong instant.

### Reproduce

Any Telegram group with `observe_unmentioned_group_messages: true`; every unmentioned message emits
the warning. In-tree, `SessionDB.append_message(timestamp=datetime.now(tz=timezone.utc).isoformat())`
followed by reading the row back shows the stored value is the fallback, not the one passed.

### Fix

Stamp `time.time()` at all three sites, matching every other transcript writer. PR incoming with a
parametrized regression test covering both adapters, proven to fail on current `main`.

### Environment

Hermes `0.21.3 (2026.9.14)`, Python 3.13, Telegram adapter, Linux.

issues.body:
### Pre-flight

- [x] Searched existing issues and PRs by split-resume (control: #123913, #123947, #124295, #124294, #126399), "qqbot split", `_send_chunk`, "yuanbao chunk", `send_text_chunk`, "feishu chunk", "feishu last_response", `_feishu_send_with_retry`, "feishu middle chunk". #8966 (@qwertysc, open, stranded on the removed `gateway/platforms/feishu.py`) skips a failed chunk and reports success; #46361 (@zmlgit, open) adds per-chunk uuid5 server-side dedupe, a different approach.
- [x] Confirmed on current `main`
- [ ] `hermes debug share`: N/A. Reproduced with the real code paths against a temp `HERMES_HOME` (fakes on 127.0.0.1 only).

### Bug Description

The same split-reply bug #124295 fixes for eight other adapters, on three more:

- **QQBot:** `_send_chunk` retries each chunk internally and returns only a `SendResult`, so a failure on chunk 2+ comes back `retryable=True` with no partial mark and the base retry sends the whole reply again.
- **Feishu:** `send` only checks the LAST chunk's response (`_finalize_send_result(last_response)`), so a middle chunk that got an error response is silently missing while the send reports success.
- **Yuanbao:** `MessageSender.send_text` returns a plain failure after earlier chunks landed, and the base plain-text fallback sends the whole reply again.

### Steps to Reproduce

```
Fake QQ REST server on 127.0.0.1; all three attempts at chunk 2 fail:

| | 502 | 429 |
|---|---|---|
| before | success=True, 4 messages on screen, 569 of 1400 words duplicated | same |
| after | success=False, partial_overflow=True, 1 message, 0 duplicated | success=True, 3 messages, 1400/1400 words, 0 duplicated |
```

### Expected Behavior

A chunk that already landed is never sent again, and a failed middle chunk is never reported as success.

### Actual Behavior

As shown under Steps to Reproduce.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform

QQBot, Feishu, Yuanbao

### Debug Report

N/A: reproduced against a temp `HERMES_HOME` with fake credentials; `hermes debug share` uploads to a public paste service, so it was not run.

### Operating System

macOS 26 (host independent)

### Python Version

3.14

### Hermes Version

main

### Root Cause Analysis

`gateway/platforms/qqbot/adapter.py` `send` / `_send_chunk`, `plugins/platforms/feishu/adapter.py` `send`, `gateway/platforms/yuanbao.py` `MessageSender.send_text`.

### Proposed Fix

Route mid-split failures through the split-resume helpers from #124295.

issues.body:
### Problem or Use Case

In Yuanbao group chats, common Hermes slash commands such as `/stop` and `/new` are currently ignored or unavailable.

This creates a major UX inconsistency between direct chats and group chats:

- Users cannot interrupt long-running tasks with `/stop`
- Users cannot reset conversation context with `/new`
- Failed or looping tasks continue running until completion
- Group chat sessions become difficult to recover without restarting the bot/session

For multi-user environments, command-based interruption and context reset are essential operational controls.

### Proposed Solution

Add support for standard Hermes slash commands in Yuanbao group chats, including:

- `/stop`
- `/new`
- `/background`
- `/queue`

Suggested behavior:

- Commands should only affect the current group session/thread
- `/stop` should cancel active agent execution for the current session
- `/new` should clear conversation context and start a fresh session state
- Commands should behave consistently with other supported platforms


### Alternatives Considered

No practical workaround currently exists for Yuanbao group chats.

Gateway / messaging improvement

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.description: Tool registry, model_tools, toolsets

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

issues.body:
## 现象

在 Yuanbao 平台创建 cronjob 时用 `deliver=origin`，投递时好时坏。看日志基本就是两种结果：

1. 正常投递（live adapter 路径命中）
2. 报错 `Yuanbao adapter is not running`，然后就没有然后了

## 复现方式

Yuanbao WebSocket 偶尔会断连重连（02:14、02:19、02:23、02:36 都断过），断连窗口期里 cron ticker 触发 delivery 就会挂。频率不高但很烦。

## 根因分析

两个地方有问题：

### 1. `_send_yuanbao` 没有重试

`tools/send_message_tool.py` 里 `_send_yuanbao()` 直接调 `get_active_adapter()`，返回 None 就立刻报错退出。但 WS 断连重连通常就几秒的事，等一下多半就好了。

### 2. `_deliver_result` standalone 路径缺 Yuanbao fallback

`cron/scheduler.py` 的 `_deliver_result()` 在 live adapter 路径失败后走 standalone，standalone 又调 `_send_yuanbao`，还是同样的问题。WS 重连期间两层都打不通。

## 修复

- `_send_yuanbao`: adapter 不可用时重试 3 次，间隔 2s
- `_deliver_result` standalone 路径: 检测到 Yuanbao adapter 报错时，递增延迟重试 3 次（3s/5s/8s）
- 清理 `__pycache__` 确保新代码被加载

修完跑了一遍相关测试（`test_scheduler.py` 207 项 + yuanbao 相关 140 项 + send_message 13 项），全过。

## 临时绕过

在等正式修复的话，用 explicit delivery target 替代 `deliver=origin` 可以 100% 投递：

```python
cronjob(
  action="create",
  name="my-task",
  schedule="every 1h",
  prompt="...",
  deliver="yuanbao:direct:<account_id>"
)
```

## 环境

- Windows 10, Hermes Agent latest
- Yuanbao adapter (WS persistent connection)

issues.title: Yuanbao forwarded-records loading heartbeat is never sent (coroutine not awaited)

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/gateway
labels.description: Gateway runner, session dispatch, delivery

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low — cosmetic, nice to have

issues.body:
### What happens

When a Yuanbao message carries forwarded records, the "loading bubble" (RUNNING heartbeat) is never shown, and Python logs `RuntimeWarning: coroutine 'ForwardedRecordsParseMiddleware._send_loading_heartbeat' was never awaited` on every such message.

### Where

`gateway/platforms/yuanbao.py`, `ForwardedRecordsParseMiddleware.handle`:

```python
async def handle(self, ctx, next_fn):
    try:
        if ctx.forwarded_records:
            self._send_loading_heartbeat(ctx)        # missing await
            ctx.raw_text = self.build_forward_text(...)
```

`_send_loading_heartbeat` is `async` and awaits `ctx.adapter._outbound.heartbeat.send_heartbeat_once(...)`. Without `await` at the call site, the coroutine is created and immediately discarded, so the heartbeat send never runs.

### Expected

The loading heartbeat should actually be sent while forwarded records are parsed — i.e. the call must be awaited (`await self._send_loading_heartbeat(ctx)`), and no "never awaited" warning should be emitted.

A fix with a regression test is in #55782.

issues.body:
## Bug Description

In **Yuanbao group chats**, an @-mention sent while the agent is busy processing a previous message is **queued** and only handled after the current task finishes — it never interrupts the running task. In **private DMs** the same @-mention (or any new message) interrupts the active turn immediately. This makes it impossible to stop/redirect a long-running task from a group chat, which is a common need (e.g. correcting a direction, aborting a bad loop, issuing a quick urgent command).

`display.busy_input_mode: interrupt` (the default) and `HERMES_GATEWAY_BUSY_INPUT_MODE` have **no effect** on group chats.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Join a Yuanbao group with the Hermes bot, DM the bot too.
2. From the DM: send a message that starts a long-running task (e.g. `run a 5-minute task`), then immediately send a second short message (e.g. `stop` or any text).
3. Observe: the second DM message **interrupts** the running task (busy ack "⚡ Interrupting current task" appears, agent pivots).
4. Repeat the same from the **group chat** with an @-mention: send the long task, then @-mention the bot with `stop`.
5. Observe: the @-mention is **queued silently** — the running task continues to completion, and only afterwards is the follow-up processed.

## Expected Behavior

An @-mention to the bot in a group chat should behave like a DM: if the session is busy, the new message should interrupt the active turn (subject to the same `busy_input_mode` policy as DMs).

## Actual Behavior

Group-chat @-mentions never reach the interrupt path — they are serialized behind the current turn.

## Root Cause

`gateway/platforms/yuanbao.py`, `DispatchMiddleware.handle()` (~line 2993) routes group vs DM messages through **two different paths**:

```python
if ctx.chat_type == "group":
    is_new = _sk not in adapter._group_queues
    queue = adapter._group_queues.setdefault(_sk, asyncio.Queue())
    queue.put_nowait(_dispatch_inbound_event)      # ← group: enqueue
    if is_new:
        consumer = asyncio.create_task(self._consume_group_queue(adapter, _sk), ...)
else:
    task = asyncio.create_task(_dispatch_inbound_event(), ...)  # ← DM: dispatch immediately
```

The group consumer (`_consume_group_queue`, ~line 3019) waits for the current turn to fully finish before dispatching the next message:

```python
await dispatch_fn()
while session_key in adapter._active_sessions:
    await asyncio.sleep(0.1)   # ← blocks until current turn completes
```

Because the follow-up message is stuck in the per-session queue, it never reaches `BasePlatformAdapter.handle_message()` → the busy-path logic in `GatewayRunner._handle_active_session_busy_message()` (gateway/run.py ~8350) that implements interrupt/steer/queue modes is never invoked. The `_group_queues` serialization is hardcoded — there is no config/env switch to disable it.

## Proposed Fix

In `DispatchMiddleware`, dispatch **@-mention messages to the bot** (and owner commands) in group chats the same way as DMs: directly via `asyncio.create_task(_dispatch_inbound_event())`, so they enter `handle_message()` and honor `busy_input_mode` (interrupt/steer). Keep the serial per-session queue only for **non-@-mention** group traffic (e.g. other members' messages that were observed but not addressed to the bot), preserving the current anti-concurrency behavior for general group noise.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20), upstream b4f8c491
- Platform: Yuanbao (yuanbao adapter)
- OS: Linux (WSL2), Python 3.12.3

## Related

- #64289 — Per-scope / per-chat `busy_input_mode` override (DM vs group, per-group-chat)
- #29065 — Support session control commands in Yuanbao group chats
- #54370 — `require_mention` gate bypassed when message arrives during active group session

issues.title: Yuanbao GIF MIME parameters lose image_format

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/gateway
labels.description: Gateway runner, session dispatch, delivery

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Low — cosmetic, nice to have

issues.body:
## Summary

Yuanbao image message construction treats parameterized GIF MIME values as unknown image format `255` instead of TIM GIF format `2`.

## Environment

- Repo: `NousResearch/hermes-agent`
- Branch tested: `main` at `d577408f3`
- Affected path: `gateway/platforms/yuanbao_media.py`

## Actual Behavior

`get_image_format()` lowercases the raw MIME string and looks it up directly:

```text
get_image_format("image/gif; charset=binary") -> 255
```

That value flows into `build_image_msg_body(..., mime_type=...)` as `msg_content.image_format`, so a GIF response/header with common MIME parameters is sent as an unknown image format instead of GIF.

`is_image()` has the same narrow raw-prefix check, so MIME values with surrounding whitespace or uppercase can also miss image classification.

## Expected Behavior

MIME classification should trim whitespace, lower-case, and remove parameters before comparing or looking up media types:

```text
get_image_format("image/gif; charset=binary") -> 2
get_image_format(" IMAGE/GIF ") -> 2
```

Non-image MIME types should remain non-image.

## Why This Matters

HTTP `Content-Type` values often include parameters. If Yuanbao receives or is passed `image/gif; charset=binary`, the outbound TIM image payload loses the GIF-specific format number even though Hermes has enough information to classify it correctly.

## Duplicate Search

Checked existing issues/PRs with:

- `Yuanbao image/gif mime parameter`
- `Yuanbao GIF image_format content-type`
- `get_image_format image/gif charset`

I did not find an existing report or PR for this exact Yuanbao MIME normalization issue.

## Proposed Fix

Add a small MIME normalization helper for classification (`split(";", 1)[0].strip().lower()`) and use it in `is_image()` and `get_image_format()`.

issues.title: [Bug]: Yuanbao silently reports successful delivery for rejected long replies; smaller chunks restore delivery

labels.name: type/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: comp/gateway
labels.description: Gateway runner, session dispatch, delivery

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Medium — degraded but workaround exists

labels.name: sweeper:risk-message-delivery
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may drop, duplicate, misroute, or suppress messages

issues.body:
### Bug Description

Long Chinese replies appear in the Hermes Dashboard/session but are not delivered to the Yuanbao app.

Two related problems were observed:

1. The Yuanbao adapter reports success after receiving a WebSocket response without checking the protocol status or business response code.
2. The default 4000-character chunk target allows a tested reply to be sent as one message that the service rejects. Reducing the chunk target restores delivery.

After adding local response decoding, the service returned:

head.status = 0
business code = 999
business message = {"code":9992501,"message":"请求云 IM 服务返回失败"}

The tested full payload was 2491 Python characters / 6619 UTF-8 bytes. Changing MAX_TEXT_CHUNK to 1200 restored delivery, confirmed in the app. A subsequent target of 1800 produced two chunks, both acknowledged successfully by the service.

The exact upstream size limit is not established. This report does not claim that code 999 or 9992501 always means an oversized message.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure Hermes with Yuanbao direct-message delivery.
2. Keep YuanbaoAdapter.MAX_TEXT_CHUNK = 4000 in gateway/platforms/yuanbao.py.
3. Generate a mostly Chinese reply below 4000 characters but relatively large in UTF-8 bytes.
   - Observed sample: 2491 Python characters / 6619 UTF-8 bytes.
   - It contains Markdown headings, lists and a table.
   - Python len() and JavaScript UTF-16 .length are identical for this sample.
4. Observe that the reply appears in the Dashboard/session but does not reach the Yuanbao app.
5. Add temporary diagnostics to decode the outbound business response rather than treating any response as success.
6. Resend the payload. Observe head.status=0 but business code=999, with an inner error code of 9992501.
7. Set MAX_TEXT_CHUNK = 1200, restart the gateway externally, and resend the same original payload.
8. Observe successful delivery in multiple chunks.
9. Optionally set the target to 1800 and repeat. The tested payload was split into two chunks, both acknowledged successfully.

Additional testing:
- Plain-text fallback also failed for the tested full-length reply.
- Varying payload length produced the following observed boundary:
  - 2330 characters / 6188 UTF-8 bytes: received.
  - 2331 characters / 6191 UTF-8 bytes: received.
  - 2332 characters / 6194 UTF-8 bytes: not received.

These observations concern one tested payload. They do not establish a universal byte limit. The original payload is not included; a public synthetic reproducer still needs validation.

### Expected Behavior

- Decode both protocol-level status and business-level response codes.
- Report business rejection as a delivery failure instead of success.
- Log bounded, sanitized error details without credentials, recipient identifiers or message bodies.
- Split long replies within the effective transport size limit.
- Preserve complete, ordered content across chunks.
- Ensure oversized tables or code blocks cannot silently bypass a hard size limit.
- Do not treat receipt of a WebSocket response/ACK as proof of successful business delivery or client display.

### Actual Behavior

The original MessageSender._dispatch_encoded() effectively does:

response = await adapter._connection.send_biz_request(encoded, req_id=req_id)
return {"success": True, "msg_key": response.get("msg_id", "")}

However, the Response branch of _handle_frame() resolves the pending future with:

{"head": head, "data": business_payload_bytes}

The adapter does not check head.status or decode the business response's code/message. Therefore, a rejected message can be reported as successfully sent.

Additionally, msg_id is nested under head on this response path, rather than at the top level. Its meaning should be checked against the SendResult contract before treating it as a platform message identifier.

With the original 4000-character target, the tested 2491-character reply is sent without splitting and is rejected.

After adding response parsing:
- The service returns outer business code 999.
- The error message contains inner code 9992501: 请求云 IM 服务返回失败.
- All three attempts fail.
- Plain-text fallback also fails.

Reducing the target to 1200 restores delivery of the tested payload.

### Affected Component

Gateway (Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp)

### Messaging Platform (if gateway-related)

_No response_

### Debug Report

```shell
Installation:
- Hermes running in a Linux container.
- Yuanbao direct messages.
- Adapter: gateway/platforms/yuanbao.py.
- The unmodified adapter matched the official repository main file byte-for-byte when checked during investigation.
- No commit ID is available because the installation directory is not a Git checkout.
- Exact Hermes release/image tag: not established in this investigation.

Original file SHA-256:
yuanbao.py:
99d623a688834a17268e70ac08851b5b89e88a9f19095368a2d9cf7bfbd382cb

yuanbao_proto.py:
973465cff3c10907bc8facf61a37a34e833f91effd6c3fb67bd5f0e8e2c723cc

Sanitized failure logs after adding diagnostics:
[yuanbao-send-ack] rejected: request=<id> status=0 code=999
message='{"code":9992501,"message":"请求云 IM 服务返回失败"}'
send_text_chunk attempt 1/3 failed
send_text_chunk attempt 2/3 failed
send_text_chunk attempt 3/3 failed
Send failed — trying plain-text fallback
Fallback send also failed: status=0, code=999

Verified workaround:
Set YuanbaoAdapter.MAX_TEXT_CHUNK to a smaller value.

Target 1200:
input=2491 chars, max=1200, output=3 chunk(s)
sizes=[1200, 1157, 130]
All three chunks acknowledged successfully.
Receipt was explicitly confirmed in the Yuanbao app.

Target 1800:
input=2491 chars, max=1800, output=2 chunk(s)
sizes=[1774, 715]
Both chunks acknowledged successfully.
A separate explicit full-text receipt confirmation was not captured for this target.

The slight differences between the original length and chunk-size sums have not been verified character by character.

Existing call chain:
send_text()
  -> truncate_message(content, adapter.MAX_TEXT_CHUNK)
  -> MarkdownProcessor.chunk_markdown_text(content, max_length, ...)

The explicit target therefore overrides the methods' default arguments of 4000 on this path.

Local diagnostic change:
- Read head.status.
- Decode the business response:
  - field 1: int32 code
  - field 2: string message
- Return success=False when either status or code is nonzero.
- Log bounded, sanitized error information.

Protocol field definitions were verified against:
openclaw-plugin-yuanbao@2.18.3
dist/src/access/ws/proto/biz.json

Useful npm reference:
- business/pipeline/middlewares/dispatch-reply.js:
  DELIVER_TEXT_CHUNK_LIMIT = 1200 for final delivery when no partial reply was received.
- business/outbound/streaming-output-session.js:
  Separate streaming defaults minChars=2000, maxChars=3000, with a 1000 ms minimum interval in its serialized streaming send queue.
- access/ws/biz-codec.js:
  Decodes outbound response code/message.
- access/ws/client.js:
  Propagates business response and protocol status.

The npm values are implementation choices, not proof of a universal platform limit. Its guard-send-access.js checks inbound ctx.rawBody.length; that 4000 value should not be cited as an outbound limit.

Suggested upstream fix:
1. Add strict outbound response decoding and check both protocol status and business code.
2. Handle malformed responses explicitly rather than silently accepting them.
3. Confirm the actual Yuanbao/cloud IM size limit; use a conservative configurable chunk target in the interim.
4. Enforce the final size budget after code-fence repair, including oversized tables/code blocks.
5. Avoid unchanged retries for confirmed deterministic size rejections, but do not classify generic code 999 as a size error without evidence.

Offline diagnostic tests:
- Valid success: passed.
- Business rejection: passed.
- Protocol header rejection: passed.
- Timeout: passed.
- Truncated protobuf fixture b'\x08\x80': failed; the existing permissive parser still accepts it as success.

The local patch is diagnostic, not a merge-ready strict decoder.

Restart behavior:
After failures became visible, the gateway persisted failed delivery obligations. Restarting after lowering the chunk target caused previous failed replies to be redelivered, as shown by "Redelivered recovered final response" logs. This should not be confused with the splitter duplicating a single reply.

Uncertainties:
- Exact upstream size limit.
- Whether the limit applies to raw UTF-8 or an encoded envelope.
- General meaning of inner code 9992501.
- No claim that the underlying size-limit cause is fully fixed.
```

### Operating System

Linux (Docker container)

### Python Version

_No response_

### Hermes Version

_No response_

### Additional Logs / Traceback (optional)

```shell

```

### Root Cause Analysis (optional)

_No response_

### Proposed Fix (optional)

_No response_
