prs.title: fix(yuanbao): block redirect-based SSRF in download_url
prs.body:
## What does this PR do?

`gateway/platforms/yuanbao_media.py::download_url` fetches model-supplied and inbound URLs server-side. It has an `is_safe_url()` pre-flight, but its per-hop redirect guard was inert:

```python
async def _redirect_guard(response: httpx.Response) -> None:
    if response.is_redirect and response.next_request:   # <- next_request is None here
        ...
```

Inside an `httpx.AsyncClient` **response event hook**, `response.next_request` is `None` even for a genuine 302 (it is populated later by the redirect-following machinery). So the guard condition was always falsy and **never validated the redirect target**. A public URL that passes the pre-flight check can therefore 302-redirect to `http://169.254.169.254/` (cloud metadata / IMDS) or any private address, and httpx (`follow_redirects=True`) follows it — a redirect-based SSRF.

This is the same class that **#56160 (merged)** fixed across the other httpx download hooks by resolving the hop from the `Location` header via `redirect_target_from_response`; `yuanbao_media.py` was the one path that migration missed. (The broken `next_request` guard here was introduced by #54470.)

## Related Issue

No open issue — found while auditing the httpx redirect guards after #56160. N/A.

## Type of Change

- [x] 🔒 Security fix

## Changes Made

- `gateway/platforms/yuanbao_media.py`: `_redirect_guard` now resolves the redirect target with `redirect_target_from_response(response)` (reads the `Location` header, `urljoin`-resolving relative Locations) instead of the always-`None` `response.next_request`, then rejects it with `is_safe_url`. This mirrors `gateway/platforms/base.py::_ssrf_redirect_guard`.
- `tests/gateway/test_yuanbao_media_ssrf.py`: added `test_redirect_to_metadata_blocked` — drives a 302 whose `Location` points at `169.254.169.254` with `next_request=None` (the real in-hook shape) through the registered guard and asserts `ValueError`. Fails on the old guard, passes on the fix.

## How to Test

```
$ python -m pytest tests/gateway/test_yuanbao_media_ssrf.py -q
6 passed
```

The new test reproduces the bug: with the previous `next_request`-based guard, a 302 to the metadata endpoint (with `next_request=None`, as httpx leaves it inside the hook) is **not** blocked; with the fix it raises `ValueError: Blocked redirect to private/internal address`.

prs.title: [security] fix(gateway): harden Yuanbao URL downloads
prs.body:
## Summary

This PR hardens the Yuanbao media URL downloader so user-supplied HTTP(S) media URLs are checked with Hermes' existing SSRF protections before any network request is created, and so redirects are re-checked during the HTTPX redirect chain.

The change is intentionally narrow:

- validate the original URL with `tools.url_safety.is_safe_url()` before `HEAD` or `GET`
- attach the shared `_ssrf_redirect_guard` response hook while following redirects
- add focused regression coverage that proves unsafe URLs are rejected before HTTP client creation and that the redirect guard is installed

## Security issues covered

- Issue: Yuanbao media URL download SSRF guard bypass
- Impact: a user-controlled Yuanbao media URL could be fetched by the gateway without the SSRF admission checks already used by other platform download paths
- Fix: enforce initial URL validation and redirect-time validation in `gateway/platforms/yuanbao_media.py`

## Before this PR

- `download_url()` accepted a caller-provided URL and immediately created an `httpx.AsyncClient` with `follow_redirects=True`.
- No initial `url_safety.is_safe_url()` check was applied before the `HEAD` or streamed `GET` request.
- Redirect targets were followed by HTTPX without the shared response hook that blocks unsafe redirect destinations.

## After this PR

- Unsafe URLs are rejected before any HTTP client is created.
- Redirect-following remains enabled for normal Yuanbao media use, but each redirect response is passed through the existing SSRF redirect guard.
- Regression tests cover both the pre-network rejection path and the redirect hook wiring.

## Why this matters

Yuanbao media sending can cause the gateway host to fetch a URL selected by a message/tool caller. Without the same SSRF boundary used elsewhere in Hermes, a malicious or compromised caller could try to make the gateway connect to loopback, private-network, metadata, or other host-local services. Redirects are especially important because an apparently public URL can later redirect to an internal address.

## Attack flow

1. A caller supplies a Yuanbao media URL for delivery.
2. The Yuanbao media helper calls `download_url()`.
3. Vulnerable code creates an HTTPX client and issues `HEAD` / `GET` requests to the supplied URL.
4. With redirects enabled and no SSRF guard, the gateway can be steered toward an internal or otherwise blocked destination.

## Affected code

- `gateway/platforms/yuanbao_media.py`
  - `download_url()` URL admission and redirect behavior

## Root cause

- The Yuanbao media downloader implemented its own HTTP fetch path instead of reusing the SSRF validation pattern already present in shared platform code.
- Redirects were enabled without a response hook that validates redirect destinations.

## CVSS assessment

- CVSS v3.1: 6.5 Medium
- Vector: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N`
- Rationale: exploitation requires access to a Hermes message/tool path that can request Yuanbao media delivery, but the vulnerable fetch is network-reachable from the gateway host and may expose sensitive local/internal HTTP responses depending on deployment topology.

## Safe reproduction steps

On vulnerable code, inspect `gateway/platforms/yuanbao_media.py` and observe that `download_url()` creates an HTTPX client with `follow_redirects=True` before any `url_safety.is_safe_url()` check and without the shared `_ssrf_redirect_guard` response hook.

This PR adds safe unit coverage instead of connecting to real internal services:

```bash
python3 -m pytest tests/test_yuanbao_media_security.py -q
```

The tests monkeypatch the URL safety checker and HTTP client so they verify the vulnerable boundary without performing real network requests.

## Expected vulnerable behavior

- An unsafe URL is not rejected before HTTP client creation.
- Redirect-following is configured without the shared SSRF response hook.

## Changes in this PR

- Import the shared SSRF redirect guard and safe URL log helper from `gateway.platforms.base`.
- Import the existing URL safety checker from `tools.url_safety`.
- Reject unsafe Yuanbao media URLs before creating an HTTP client.
- Install `_ssrf_redirect_guard` as an HTTPX response hook while preserving redirect-following behavior.
- Add focused async regression tests for both security boundaries.

## Files changed

- `gateway/platforms/yuanbao_media.py`
  - Adds initial URL validation and redirect-time SSRF guard wiring.
- `tests/test_yuanbao_media_security.py`
  - Adds regression tests for unsafe URL rejection and redirect guard installation.

## Maintainer impact

- Normal public HTTP(S) Yuanbao media URLs continue to work.
- URLs that Hermes' shared SSRF policy already considers unsafe are blocked consistently with other guarded download paths.
- No Yuanbao COS upload behavior is changed.

## Fix rationale

The gateway should enforce the same SSRF policy at both relevant boundaries: before the first outbound request and during redirect traversal. Validating only the initial URL would still leave redirect-to-internal bypasses; relying only on redirect hooks would still create unnecessary HTTP client/request activity for obviously unsafe inputs. This patch applies both checks with the existing shared helpers.

## Type of change

- [x] Security hardening
- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Regression tests
- [ ] Documentation-only change

## Test plan

Run locally:

```bash
python3 -m pytest tests/test_yuanbao_media_security.py -q
python3 -m ruff check gateway/platforms/yuanbao_media.py tests/test_yuanbao_media_security.py
git diff --check
```

Results:

- `2 passed`
- `All checks passed!`
- `git diff --check` passed

Note: `ruff format --check gateway/platforms/yuanbao_media.py ...` reports pre-existing formatting churn across the legacy Yuanbao media file, so I avoided whole-file formatting changes and kept this PR's diff focused on the security boundary.

## Disclosure notes

This PR is bounded to the Yuanbao media URL download path. It does not claim to audit every URL-fetching surface in Hermes, nor does it change the global SSRF policy itself.

issues.title: skills install fails with "registry archive is not a valid skill" when another skill shares the frontmatter name
issues.body:
## Summary

`picoclaw skills install` (and the agent's `install_skill` tool) fail with:

```
failed to install "<slug>": registry archive is not a valid skill
```

whenever another already-installed skill uses the same `name` in its
`SKILL.md` frontmatter — even when the two skills are completely different
(different directories, authors and content).

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install a skill whose frontmatter `name` is `weather`:
   ```bash
   picoclaw skills install --registry=clawhub weather-zhouli
   ```
2. Install a second, different skill that also declares `name: weather`:
   ```bash
   picoclaw skills install --registry=clawhub weather23
   ```
   → fails with `registry archive is not a valid skill`.
3. Remove the first skill and retry → the install succeeds.

Both ClawHub ZIPs contain a byte-identical `SKILL.md`
(md5 `107ea6b0f12a145071ba29153699aa67`), so the failure is caused purely by the
shared `name`.

## Root cause

`pkg/skills/loader.go` → `ListSkills()` deduplicates globally by the frontmatter
`name`:

```go
if seen[info.Name] {
    continue
}
seen[info.Name] = true
```

The install validation re-scans the workspace through `ListSkills()` and then
looks for the newly installed directory:

- `workspaceHasValidInstalledSkill` in `pkg/tools/integration/skills_install.go`
- `workspaceHasValidSkillDirectory` in `cmd/picoclaw/internal/skills/helpers.go`

Because the new skill is deduplicated away (same `name` as an already-installed
skill), the lookup never finds it and the install is reported as invalid.

## Impact

- Two skills sharing a frontmatter `name` cannot be installed together.
- The second skill is also invisible to the agent (not listed, not loadable).
- Reproduced on `v0.3.1` and on `main`.

## Proposed fix

Deduplicate per root instead of globally by name: shadow a `name` only when it
appears in a **higher-priority** root (workspace > global > builtin), and list
distinct directories within the same root:

```go
firstRoot := make(map[string]int)

addSkills := func(dir, source string, rootIdx int) {
    // ... same as before ...
    if r, ok := firstRoot[info.Name]; ok && r != rootIdx {
        continue
    }
    firstRoot[info.Name] = rootIdx
    skills = append(skills, info)
}

// Priority: workspace > global > builtin
addSkills(sl.workspaceSkills, "workspace", 0)
addSkills(sl.globalSkills, "global", 1)
addSkills(sl.builtinSkills, "builtin", 2)
```

Verified locally against `v0.3.1`: with the patch, both `weather` skills install
and are listed, and `install_skill` works.

## Environment

- picoclaw v0.3.1 (git `2cf030d2`), Go 1.25.11
- Linux amd64

Happy to open a PR if the fix looks good.

prs.title: fix(skills): deduplicate installed skills per root, not by frontmatter name
prs.body:
## Problem

Fixes #3462.

`picoclaw skills install` (and the agent's `install_skill` tool) fail with
`registry archive is not a valid skill` whenever another installed skill shares
the same frontmatter `name`, even when the two skills are completely different
(different directories, authors and content).

Reproduction:

```bash
picoclaw skills install --registry=clawhub weather-zhouli   # ok
picoclaw skills install --registry=clawhub weather23        # fails
```

Both ClawHub ZIPs contain a byte-identical `SKILL.md` (`name: weather`, md5
`107ea6b0f12a145071ba29153699aa67`), so the second install is rejected purely
because of the shared name.

## Root cause

`pkg/skills/loader.go` → `ListSkills()` deduplicated globally by the frontmatter
`name`. The install validation re-scans the workspace through `ListSkills()` and
looks for the newly installed directory
(`workspaceHasValidInstalledSkill` / `workspaceHasValidSkillDirectory`); since
the new skill was deduplicated away, it was never found and the install was
reported as invalid.

## Fix

Deduplicate per root: a `name` is shadowed only when it appears in a
**higher-priority** root (workspace > global > builtin); distinct directories
within the same root are all listed.

## Testing

- Built `v0.3.1` with the patch: both `weather` skills now install and are

issues.title: [bug] Recurring task fires resume the previous fire's conversation, re-paying its whole history every fire
issues.body:
### Affected NanoClaw version or commit

v2026.10.0 (install); code paths below re-checked on `main` @ 79deb707

### Host platform

WSL2

### What happened?

Every fire of a recurring task resumes the **previous fire's conversation**. Each task series gets one long-lived system session (`resolveTaskSession` → `findSystemSession`, `src/session-manager.ts:180`), and that session's `continuation:claude` survives between fires (`poll-loop.ts:100`). So fire N runs on top of the full transcript of fires 1…N‑1: their prompts, their tool calls, and their tool *output*. The history is bounded only by auto-compaction (`CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_COMPACT_WINDOW`, default 165k) and by the size/age rotation, which runs only at a cold start (see #3732).

For a recurring task this history is almost never useful. A well-written recurring task keeps its state in files (a last-checked marker, a list of open items) precisely because each fire should stand on its own. What the resumed history mostly carries is stale tool output, such as the raw API responses from earlier fires.

The cost shows up as prompt-cache writes. Fires are usually spaced further apart than the cache TTL, so the first request of every fire re-writes the whole accumulated history to the cache. Measured on one real series (an inbox digest, 3 fires per weekday, 49 fires so far, transcript 3.4 MB), from the `usage` fields of the SDK transcript:

| | first request of a fire |
|---|---|
| read from cache (shared system/tool prefix) | ~9.4k tokens, constant |
| **written to cache (carried-over history)** | **45k–122k tokens**, growing through the day until compaction |

Only the ~9k stable prefix is warm. Everything else on that first request is history from earlier fires, paid at the cache-write rate on every fire, and then re-read on every later request in the same fire.

The impact scales with the very pattern the scheduler encourages. `enforceRecurrenceLimit` lets scripted tasks poll faster because "a skipped fire costs no agent tokens" (`src/modules/scheduling/create.ts:83`). That holds for skipped fires, but every fire that does wake pays for the whole accumulated history of the series. A monitor that wakes a few times a day, or a task whose tools return large payloads, carries far more than our example. The docs also set a different expectation: "Each task runs in its own isolated session" (`scheduling.instructions.md`). The session is isolated from chat, but the fires are not isolated from each other.

### What did you expect?

Each fire of a recurring task starts with a fresh agent conversation, while the session (mailbox, workspace, run log, destinations) stays the same. In practice that means clearing the continuation before a task fire, the same way `/clear` does (`clearContinuation`), but on the task path and before the query starts.

If some tasks genuinely want memory across fires, that could be an opt-in per series (e.g. `ncl tasks create --keep-context`). The default should be fresh, because files and the run log are already the supported way to carry state, and the run log already records each fire's outcome.

This would also make #3732 moot for task sessions, since there would be no long-lived task transcript left to rotate.

### How can we reproduce it?

1. `ncl tasks create --name probe --recurrence "0 */2 * * *" --prompt "Run 'ls -la /workspace/agent' and reply with the file count."`
2. Let it fire 3–4 times.
3. Find the transcript for the session's `continuation:claude` (in its `outbound.db` → `session_state`) under `data/v2-sessions/<ag>/.claude-shared/projects/-workspace-agent/<id>.jsonl`.
4. The `usage` of the first assistant entry of each fire shows `cache_creation_input_tokens` growing with every fire, and the transcript contains the earlier fires' prompts and `ls` output.

### Optional context

Related: #3732 (rotation never runs for tasks that keep their container alive), the same root cause from the size side; #4173 (agent-initiated session reset), which covers similar continuation-clearing mechanics but is triggered by the agent.

Things I tried without core changes, none of which work: a `/clear` in the task prompt (the runner only honours `/clear` on chat messages); deleting `continuation:claude` from a pre-task script (the poll loop already holds it in memory, and the next fire writes it back); moving the transcript aside (the resume then fails with a stale-session error and that fire's batch is acked as completed, so the run is lost).

prs.title: fix: stage inbound attachments that expose only a url (Discord)
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Makes Discord attachments (images, and pasted text Discord turns into `message.txt`) readable by the agent.
- **Problem**: the chat-sdk bridge only downloads bytes via `att.fetchData()`. The Discord adapter exposes a CDN `url` instead, and the bridge drops `url` when serializing. The entry reaches the host with no `data`, `extractAttachmentFiles` skips it, and the agent sees a path-less `[file: message.txt]` it can never open.
- **Fix**: move enrichment into `enrichAttachments()`. Always keep `url` on the entry. When there is no `fetchData` but there is a `url`, download from the url so the bytes stage to the inbox like any `fetchData` attachment.
- **Cap**: both download paths bound inlined bytes by `MAX_INBOUND_ATTACHMENT_BYTES` (default 10 MB). Checks run cheapest first: declared `att.size`, then `Content-Length` (url path only), then actual byte length. Oversized attachments keep `url` as a reference and carry no bytes.
- **Out of scope**: rate-limiting repeated uploads. That belongs at the session/rate layer.

## Related work

Closes #2426. Supersedes #2427, which preserved `url` but never fetched the bytes, so url-only adapters still produced no readable file.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/channels/chat-sdk-bridge.test.ts` → new `enrichAttachments` suite passes: url-only download, `fetchData` preferred over `url`, url kept and no `data` on download failure, metadata-only when neither is present, and the cap on both paths (declared size, oversized body without size metadata, within-cap still staged).
- `pnpm exec vitest run` on this branch merged with current `main` → 213 files / 2532 tests pass.
- `pnpm exec tsc --noEmit` → clean.
- Manual: running in production on a Discord install since June; pasted text and images reach the agent as files in the inbox.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Discord attachments (images and pasted text) now reach the agent as readable files instead of a bare placeholder. Inbound attachment downloads on every chat-sdk channel are capped at 10 MB, overridable with MAX_INBOUND_ATTACHMENT_BYTES.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

Untrusted input: anyone who can message the bot controls attachment contents and size. The host now fetches the adapter-supplied attachment `url` (the Discord CDN link from the platform payload, not user message text). Bytes are inlined only within the cap, so a large upload cannot inflate the POST body or prompt context. The same cap now also applies to the existing `fetchData` path (Slack et al.), which previously had none.

## Skill delivery

- [x] Not a skill
- [ ] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

## AI assistance

- [x] AI tools or agents helped produce this change

## Related work

None. Additive skills and docs only.

- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

`LLMMAN_API_KEY` is forwarded via `contributedEnv`; `LLMMAN_API_KEYS` never is. `llmman_generate` cannot trigger a model download unless `LLMMAN_ADMIN_TOOLS=true`.

prs.title: fix(container-config): never write container.json through a symlink
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Makes the host's `container.json` rewrite safe when the file is not mounted read-only in the session.

- **Problem**: `materializeContainerJson` rewrote `groups/<folder>/container.json` with a plain `writeFileSync`, which follows a symlink at that path and blocks on a FIFO. Docker mounts the file read-only, so this only matters for a driver that doesn't (the Apple container skill in #3503 drops that mount).
- **Fix**: open with `O_NOFOLLOW|O_NONBLOCK` and rewrite in place only when it is a regular file; otherwise unlink the entry and create a new file with `O_EXCL`.
- **Why in place, not temp + rename**: a rename gives the file a new inode, which detaches the read-only mount held by a running session of the same group. Reproduced on Docker Desktop's Linux kernel: after a rename the running session could write the file; after an in-place rewrite it could not.

Out of scope: the composed `CLAUDE.md` still uses temp + rename and has the same detach issue; separate follow-up.

## Related work

Related to #3503: should land before it, since that driver drops the read-only `container.json` mount.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [x] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- 4 new tests in `src/container-config.test.ts`: symlink, FIFO with a reader, FIFO with no reader, in-place rewrite keeps the inode. The symlink and FIFO tests fail on main; without `O_NONBLOCK` the no-reader test fails in about 3 s instead of hanging.
- `pnpm test` on base d61af17b: 3553 passed, 15 skipped. `typecheck` and Prettier clean. The branch merges cleanly with current main.

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Setup now says why a background Slack install failed, and verify passes again once a later Slack run has connected and wired a chat.

- **Problem**: a failed background Slack job saved only `install_needs_attention` and dropped the reason. After a good manual re-run, the saved job stayed failed, so verify stayed red.
- **Fix**:
  - The worker saves the failure reason (one line, tokens removed). Verify prints it as `SLACK_INSTALL_REASON`, and the wizard shows it. A companion failure names the companion and its first error line.
  - Verify sets a failed or expired job aside when Slack is set up and a chat on its default instance was wired after the job began. Only the welcome runs after wiring. A same-app retry keeps the wiring it finds and the first job's start time, so a job that failed at the welcome also clears once its chat is wired, even after a retry. The saved job is not rewritten. The wizard's closing note follows verify, so it doesn't call Slack broken after verify passed; a job that fails after verify still shows.
- **Out of scope**: the `OWNER` line and counting a webhook Slack as set up, now separate PRs (#4287, #4288). A same-app retry that fails before it applies (say the app was deleted) is also set aside once an earlier run wired the chat; verify doesn't check Slack's tokens live, so a deleted app after a good install already passes it.

## Related work

No issue; found in an OSS user's WSL setup report (Slack job stuck after a missing jq).

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`

## Validation

- `vitest run setup/verify setup/central-db-inspection setup/slack-worker setup/channels/run-channel-skill setup/auto src/community-portal/slack-job`: 78 pass. prs.title: fix(container-config): write container.json without following a symlink
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

`materializeContainerJson` writes a group's `container.json` on every spawn, by path. While a container runs, `container.json` is mounted read-only over the group folder, so the agent cannot swap that leaf then; the reachable window is before the mount exists — an old or legacy group folder, between runs, or a second mount of the group folder without that read-only layer. This is defense in depth for that window.

- **Problem**: the write used `fs.writeFileSync(path, …)`, which follows a symlink at the leaf and blocks on a reader-less FIFO.
- **Fix**: open the leaf with a no-follow, non-blocking open. A regular file is truncated in place (same inode, so a running container's read-only mount still sees the config live, as before); a symlink or FIFO is unlinked and replaced with a fresh regular file; a planted directory is left in place and the spawn fails, as it did before, rather than being removed.
- **Out of scope / residuals**: the startup backfill read (separate PR); the unlink/create window on the replace path (a sibling replacing the name between operations); and the bind-source resolution — Docker resolves `container.json` as a mount source later, at container-create time, and follows a symlink itself, with other steps (`initGroupFilesystem`, project-doc compose) in between, so this writer does not close that path. All tracked with the other mount-source residuals.

## Related work

No linked issue. Maintainer hardening; the diff and its tests are the review surface.

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`

## Validation

- `pnpm exec vitest run src/container-config-materialize.test.ts` -> 5 passed: fresh create; in-place rewrite keeps the same inode; a planted symlink is replaced without touching its target; a planted FIFO is replaced without blocking; a planted directory fails the spawn and deletes nothing outside the group.
- Full `vitest run`, `tsc --noEmit`, `lint` (0 errors), `format:check` -> clean apart from load-dependent integration timeouts that pass in isolation.
- Behavior confirmed on Linux + Docker: an in-place truncate keeps a running container's bind-mounted config live; a no-follow open refuses a planted symlink.

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

The startup backfill reads a legacy group's `container.json` with a no-follow open instead of by path. The group folder is a host-owned mount source the container cannot swap, so only the `container.json` leaf is container-controlled.

- **Problem**: the one-time backfill for groups without a `container_configs` row read `container.json` by path, so a symlink or special file at that name was followed, a bad file's text reached the log, and `null` JSON stopped startup.

- **Out of scope**: the spawn-time writer `materializeContainerJson` (it also writes `container.json` by path — tracked as a separate follow-up, see note) and other readers of the group folder.

prs.title: fix(onecli): warn when a remote gateway points agents at their own machine
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Setup now shows a warning, with the line to set, when a OneCLI gateway on another machine would send agents to their own machine.

- **Problem**: OneCLI tells agents to use the proxy at `GATEWAY_BASE_URL`, default `host.docker.internal:10255`. With a remote gateway that's the agent's own host, so every model call retries forever and the agent never replies, with no error.
- **Fix**: a check at the end of `/add-onecli` reads the proxy OneCLI hands the seeded `default` agent (`/v1/container-config?agent=default`; a named lookup never creates an agent). It only reads the gateway when setup was pointed at a remote one (`NANOCLAW_ONECLI_API_HOST`). If the proxy is `host.docker.internal`, a loopback address or a wildcard (`0.0.0.0`, `::`), a `nc:operator` note shows the exact `GATEWAY_BASE_URL=<host>:<port>` line to set on the gateway host. The wizard shows operator notes on screen; `setup.ts` output only reaches `logs/setup.log`, so the check is its own step. The hint also names `ONECLI_GATEWAY_PORT`, since OneCLI hands out its default port even when another one is published. It says nothing when the gateway URL itself is on this machine, where `host.docker.internal` is right. It never fails the install, and a rerun without the token uses the key saved in `.env`. `docs/onecli-upgrades.md` gets a short "Remote gateway" section: the `.env` line, a recreate of the `onecli` container alone (`--no-deps`, with an exported `GATEWAY_BASE_URL` unset), and a check.
- **Out of scope**: no warning for a gateway without a `default` agent, or one that hands out another address of the NanoClaw host (such as its docker bridge). Setup's older `GATEWAY_HINT` still reaches only the log. The docs.nanoclaw.dev pages (separate docs PR).

## Related work

No issue; found in the OneCLI 1.45 two-machine test (gateway and NanoClaw on separate LXCs). Both new sections sit at the end of their files, clear of #4199's edits to the same two files.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `vitest run .claude/skills/add-onecli scripts/onecli-upgrade-guide.test.ts scripts/skill-conformance.test.ts`: 531 pass. New `remote-proxy.test.ts` (27): the hint names the exact line for `host.docker.internal`, `127.x`, `localhost`, `::1`, `::ffff:127.x`, `0.0.0.0` and `::`, says nothing for a gateway URL on this machine (loopback, `localhost`, `0.0.0.0`, `::`; these fail without the fix), keeps the port the gateway hands out, never contains the agent token, and stays quiet for a real address or an unreadable answer. The read sends the API key and gives nothing back on a refused, empty, malformed or unreachable answer. The real SKILL.md section shows the hint as a note, with no pause, only when the check warns (fails on the old SKILL.md); the check never fails (fails without its catch), prints its JSON from a checkout path with a space (fails with a run-directly guard), and reads nothing without a remote gateway.
- Full `vitest run` (without `setup/gateways/onecli-detection.test.ts`): 4324 pass. 6 tests in 4 files (`transaction.e2e`, `add-dial-tool-scope`, `onecli-grants-gate`, `mattermost-discovery`) hit the 5 s timeout under load; the 4 files pass alone with a 30 s timeout (135/135).
- Ran the check against a fake gateway on this Mac's LAN address: it warns with the exact line, is quiet with no remote gateway, and exits 0 quietly when the gateway is down. The two-machine 1.45 test that found the hang still shows the problem.

prs.title: fix(agent-runner): answer each message in its own thread after /clear
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

After `/clear`, or once a message arrives while the agent is still answering, replies in a threaded chat could land one thread behind for the rest of the query.

- **Problem**: a batch holding `/clear` and the next message took its reply route from the `/clear` row. Also, the Claude CLI folds a message pushed mid-turn into the running turn, and Codex steers it into the running turn. Either way one result answers both, but the turn queue expected one result per push, so it stayed one entry behind until the query ended.
- **Fix**: commands reply on their own route, and a turn routes from the message that woke it. Providers now report a result that answered folded inputs (`answeredInputs`). Claude reads it from `user_message_uuids`; `add-codex` counts its accepted steers and fails one it never heard back about on its own thread. The poll loop then retires the folded turns and sends a failed turn's notice to each folded thread.
- **Out of scope**: OpenCode answers each push with its own result and needs no change. Context rows beside a command still start a turn by themselves, as on `main`; that moves to its own PR.

<details><summary>Behavior notes for reviewers</summary>

- Accumulated (`trigger=0`) rows no longer pick the reply thread when they sort first. This applies to every accumulate batch, not only `/clear`.
- Codex keeps inputs in push order. It steers only when nothing is queued and no steer is awaiting its reply, and a rejected steer runs ahead of the inputs queued after it. A turn's result waits up to 5 s for its steer replies, or less if the query is aborted. A steer still unanswered then fails on its own result: its thread gets a "please send it again" notice, it never runs a second time, and a late reply is ignored. Running it again could repeat what it asked for if the server had taken it after all.
- Claude's `user_message_uuids` keeps only the first 64 entries, so a turn that folds more than 64 inputs is undercounted and later answers stay behind until the query ends. That has not been seen in use. The CLI lists only inputs this query sent it, each once (its restart rescue turn could list an older one, but that needs `CLAUDE_CODE_RESUME_INTERRUPTED_TURN`, which NanoClaw never sets). A result that listed none of ours would count as one, as on `main`.

</details>

## Related work

No issue: found by a staging release check (`/clear` in a Slack DM, then answers one thread behind for up to ~30 min). No host, schema, or channel change.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `cd container/agent-runner && bun test --isolate` → 643 pass, 4 skip, 0 fail. With the `add-codex` container payload copied in and its barrels wired: 701 pass, 3 skip, 0 fail. `tsc -p container/agent-runner/tsconfig.json` is clean both ways. The new tests are red on `main`.
- Real Claude Code CLI 2.1.300 (Haiku) drove the real poll loop and provider against a test session DB. On `main`: q → the `/clear` thread, m4 → m3's thread, m5 → m4's thread. On this branch, each answer landed in its own thread.
- Codex (`CodexProvider` with a fake app-server, real poll loop): a steered follow-up sent the next answer to the previous thread on `main`'s loop, and to its own thread here. With B's steer reply held past the wait and C, D, E sent after it, the answers went to threads A, C, D, E, E at 596b81ff; here B gets the resend notice in its own thread and C, D, E are answered in theirs.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Replies in threaded chats (like Slack DMs) no longer drift one thread behind for the rest of the conversation after `/clear`, or after a message arrives while the agent (Claude or Codex) is still working; a message folded into an answer already in progress is answered in that answer's thread. Unaddressed messages that arrived before `/clear` still reach the fresh session. With Codex, a message that can't be confirmed while an answer is finishing gets a short "please send it again" reply in its own thread.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

None. Routing still uses only the session's own inbound rows.

prs.title: fix(delivery): one stuck channel send no longer silences a session until restart
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

A hung send no longer silences its session until restart. Other sessions keep their pace while up to 8 are hung.

- **Problem**: sends were awaited with no limit. One hung send blocked its session silently, and the shared poll tick waited on it.
- **Fix**: after 60 s a send is parked and logged (`Message delivery passed its deadline`). A parked message is never sent again while it might still land: a late success marks it delivered, a late failure is retried, and no answer 60 min later marks it failed. A tick waits at most 5 s on a session and leaves slower drains in the background, up to 8 at once.
- **Limits**:
  - Past 8 background drains a tick waits on each drain again, so other sessions can wait for the 60 s deadline. In a test, a healthy session behind 16 hung ones waited 65 s (behind 24, 70 s).
  - A session parks at most 3 sends at once. A send given up on frees its slot while it may still be out, so this does not cap sends in flight.
  - A parked message can arrive after later ones. If the session's first replies are parked, more than one reply can carry `firstDelivery`.
  - A send that lands after the give-up stays marked failed. A mailbox error at the give-up leaves the message to be sent again.

## Related work

Refs #2665 (instance A). Overlaps #3059. Not covered: backoff (#4227), idempotency keys, and the Discord click timeouts (inbound click path, left to the card stack: #4168).

prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Setup accepts a display name of any length: the agent's folder name is cut to fit, instead of setup failing.

- **Problem**: the terminal agent's folder is `cli-with-<name>` and the DM agent's is `dm-with-<name>`, capped at 63 characters. Since #4148, a name of 55+ characters makes "create terminal agent" fail with "Couldn't create …'s Terminal", and the reason is only in `logs/setup-steps/`. Before #4148, the agent was created and could never start.
- **Fix**: `src/operator-agent-folders.ts` derives both folders for the two init scripts and cuts the name part to fit 63 characters, never ending on a `-`. A cut name ends with `_` and 12 hex characters of a hash of the whole name, so two long names that start the same don't share a folder by chance. Normalized names never contain `_`, so a name that fits can never equal a cut one. Names that fit are unchanged. The display name itself stays as typed; only the folder, which the user never sees, is shorter.

## Related work

Follow-up to #4148 (its verify note 4: "the setup wizard still gives no reason").

New: two long names that start the same get different folders, and a second user with such a name gets their own agent (both fail without the hash); Copilot's pair that shared a 6-hex hash gets two folders (fails with 6 hex); a name that fits is unchanged and can never equal a cut one (fails with `-` before the hash); one pinned folder fixes the hash input, so an existing cut folder can't move later. `vitest run scripts/init-cli-agent.test.ts scripts/init-first-agent.test.ts src/operator-agent-folders.test.ts setup/templates.test.ts src/channels/cli.test.ts src/group-folder`: 43 pass.

<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stored context no longer starts a turn just because a runner command shares its batch.

- **Problem**: when `/clear` or `/upload-trace` reached the runner in a batch whose other rows were all accumulated context (`trigger=0`), the runner ran the command, then started a turn on the context rows alone. The agent answered messages it was only meant to store, and the command replied in the first context row's thread.
- **Fix**: a batch with no waking non-command row now takes only its waking commands. The context rows stay pending and ride along with the next message that wakes a turn, as the accumulate gate already does for context-only batches.
- **Out of scope**: a context row that itself reads as a command (an admin's `/clear` not addressed to the agent) still runs as a command, as on `main`; whether it should is a separate question. Which thread a turn replies to when context sorts first is https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4159.

## Related work

Split out of https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4159 at review, as a separate behavior change. No issue. Both PRs touch the runner's command block in `poll-loop.ts`, so the second to merge needs a small rebase.

prs.title: fix(setup): count a webhook Slack as set up in verify
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Verify now counts Slack as set up in webhook mode, not only in Socket Mode.

- **Problem**: `/add-slack`'s webhook mode saves `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` and `SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET` and no app token, but verify required `SLACK_APP_TOKEN`. So a webhook Slack was missing from `CONFIGURED_CHANNELS`. The wizard could suggest adding Slack to someone who already has it. With Teams also set up and no groups yet, verify passed as "wiring pending" while Slack had no wired chat.
- **Fix**: Slack counts as set up with the bot token plus either the app token or the signing secret.
- **Out of scope**: nothing else in setup checks Slack's tokens.

## Related work

Split out of https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4204 after review, which asked whether this is a real webhook fix. It is: see Problem.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `vitest run setup/verify`: 24 pass. Two new `verify-slack` cases fail without the change: a webhook Slack is in `CONFIGURED_CHANNELS` (a bot token alone is not), and Teams plus an unwired webhook Slack fails verify.
- Full `vitest run` (without `setup/gateways/onecli-detection.test.ts`): 4300 pass. A few `scripts/update/transaction.e2e.test.ts` tests hit the 5 s timeout under load; that file passes alone with a 30 s timeout (29/29).
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Setup's verify step now recognizes a Slack set up in webhook mode, so it no longer suggests adding Slack again, or passes while that Slack has no wired chat.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

None. Verify only checks that the signing secret is present; it never prints it.

- [x] Not a skill
- [ ] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

prs.title: fix(telegram): update Chat SDK for rich messages
prs.body:
<!-- contributing-guide: v1 -->
## Type of Change

- [ ] **Feature skill** - adds a channel or integration (source code changes + SKILL.md)
- [ ] **Utility skill** - adds a standalone tool (code files in `.claude/skills/<name>/`, no source changes)
- [ ] **Operational/container skill** - adds a workflow or agent skill (SKILL.md only, no source changes)
- [x] **Fix** - bug fix or security fix to source code
- [ ] **Simplification** - reduces or simplifies source code
- [ ] **Documentation** - docs, README, or CONTRIBUTING changes only

## Description

Closes #3151.

Updates the Chat SDK core and channel adapter pins from `4.29.0` to `4.35.0`. Telegram adapter `4.35.0` converts Bot API 10.1 `rich_message` blocks into text and media instead of producing an empty inbound message.

All channel skill pins move together because each adapter depends on the exact matching `chat` version and NanoClaw validates that lockstep contract. The changelog includes the existing-install migration: re-run every installed `/add-<channel>` skill, then rebuild and restart.

## Testing

- `corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
- `corepack pnpm run build`
- `corepack pnpm run format:check`
- `corepack pnpm exec vitest run scripts/skill-directives.test.ts` — 56 passed
- Parsed all 8 changed channel skills with `scripts/skill-directives.ts` — no problems or warnings
- `bash -n setup/install-github.sh`
- Inspected the published `@chat-adapter/telegram@4.35.0` tarball and confirmed its inbound parser calls `richMessageToText` and `richMessageMedia`

No live Telegram bot credential was used.

prs.title: fix(setup): restart the host after provider-auth installs a provider
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

`setup --step provider-auth <provider>` now restarts the running host after it installs a provider, so the first chat on the new provider works.

- **Problem**: provider-auth installed the payload and rebuilt the image, but the service kept running the `dist/` it loaded at start. The payload adds host code (provider contracts and registrations under `src/`), so the first Codex turn failed until a manual rebuild and restart. Found in the OneCLI 1.45 e2e matrix for #4094 (row P3); main behaves the same.
- **Fix**: when `applyProviderSkill` reports `changed` (the same signal that already triggers the image rebuild), provider-auth runs `pnpm run build` and `setup/lib/restart.sh` right after the image build. That is before auth, because a failed sign-in exits the process and a re-run only re-authenticates. It never restarts onto a failed build: `tsc` can write `dist/` despite errors, so restarting then could load broken output.
- **Failure paths**: no service installed → nothing restarted, one line names the service step, exit 0. Restart failed → auth still runs, one line prints `pnpm run build && bash setup/lib/restart.sh`, exit 1. `restart.sh` now exits 2 only for "nothing installed", on Linux too, matching macOS. Any other failure that returns 2 (launchctl, systemctl) exits 1, and so does a unit file that systemctl can't see (no user bus).
- **Out of scope**: no restart follows settings that auth saves. OpenCode saves its endpoint during auth and the host reads it only at start, so an OpenCode install or re-auth that sets a new endpoint needs one more `bash setup/lib/restart.sh`.

## Related work

Found while testing https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4094; no issue filed. Safe to review directly: setup-only, the full setup flow (`setup/auto.ts`) is unchanged.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `vitest run setup/provider-auth.test.ts setup/lib/host-restart.test.ts setup/lib/restart*.test.ts` → 38 pass. They cover: one restart on install and `--refresh`, none when the apply changed nothing, no service (one message, exit 0), a failed restart (auth still runs, exit 1), no restart onto a failed build, and `restart.sh` exit 2. A launchctl or systemctl `restart`/`show` that exits 2, and an installed unit systemctl can't see, all exit 1 (these fail without the fix); other launchctl codes still pass through.
- Full `vitest run` (without `setup/gateways/onecli-detection.test.ts`): 4307 pass. 7 tests in `scripts/update/transaction.e2e.test.ts` and `scripts/registry-copy.integration.test.ts` hit the 5 s timeout under load; both files pass alone with a 30 s timeout (47/47).
- `tsc` over `src/` and `setup/`: no new errors.
- Live (2026-10-21, exe.dev, the install path, unchanged by the cut): `provider-auth codex` with an API key rebuilt and restarted the host (PID 9436 → 14696) right after the payload install, and a Codex agent answered.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
`setup --step provider-auth <provider>` now restarts NanoClaw after installing a provider, so Codex, Cursor and OpenCode work without a manual host restart.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

None. No credential handling changes; the restart uses the existing `setup/lib/restart.sh`.

## Skill delivery

- [x] Not a skill (prose-only edits to the add-codex, add-cursor and add-opencode SKILL.md files; no directives changed)
- [ ] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

prs.title: fix(setup): keep user text out of setup diagnostics
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Stops setup diagnostics from sending text the user typed or wrote.

- **Problem**: `setup_aborted.reason` sent the failure message, which can hold the user's name, agent names, timezone and local paths. `channel_other_named` sent whatever the operator typed. Provider names come from local skill files, so a private provider skill sent its own name.
- **Fix**: `fail()` now takes a fixed `reason_code` for each failure branch, and the message stays local. A bounced channel install sends the directive kind and SKILL.md line, and a kind the engine does not handle is sent as `unknown_directive`. A typed channel name or a provider name is sent only if it is on a fixed public list; anything else is `unknown` (a failed provider install reports step `add-unknown`). A test fails when a shipped provider skill is missing from the provider list.
- **Out of scope**: version, channel and run-id props and a sturdier sender. They move to a separate PR, opened once something reads them.

## Related work

No issue. Found in a review of setup diagnostics; only setup telemetry and its tests change.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `vitest run` (all suites but `setup/gateways/onecli-detection.test.ts`) → 4,222 pass. 15 tests in 6 files this PR does not touch hit the 5 s timeout on a loaded machine; those files pass 146/146 alone with `--testTimeout=30000`.
- New: `initial-setup.test.ts` (channel list), `provider-diagnostic.test.ts` (every shipped provider skill is on the list; it sits outside `setup/providers` so the install verifier never runs it in a user's install), the `reason_code` and `diagnosticStep` checks in `runner.failure.test.ts`, and `bounceReasonCode` tests in `run-channel-skill.test.ts` (custom `nc:hand-wire` → `unknown_directive:L5`).
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
Setup diagnostics no longer send failure messages, typed channel names, custom skill step names or private provider names; they send fixed codes instead. NANOCLAW_NO_DIAGNOSTICS=1 still turns them off.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

Less data leaves the machine: free text and local skill names in three events are replaced by fixed codes. No new transport or permission.

## Skill delivery

- [x] Not a skill
- [ ] Skill: apply/remove footprint and fresh-clone verification are described above

- [x] AI tools or agents helped produce this change

prs.title: ci: add Dependabot for Actions, pnpm, bun, docker and skill pins; remove the inert Renovate config
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

Turns on Dependabot version updates for every manifest it can read, behind a release-age cooldown, and removes the Renovate config that never ran.

- **Problem**: main has no `dependabot.yml`. Alerts are on but security-update PRs are off, so a fixed version reaches us only when someone bumps it by hand, as with this week's Node.js base image. On 2026-10-21 LiteLLM 1.107.0 shipped a credential stealer to PyPI and Docker Hub for about two hours ([incident](https://docs.litellm.ai/blog/security-incident-oct-21-2026)); a cooldown keeps a release like that out.
- **Fix**: weekly entries for GitHub Actions, the root pnpm project, `container/agent-runner` (bun), the `container/Dockerfile` base image, and the skill pins. Cooldown is 7 days, 14 for majors and agent-runner minors (its 0.x SDKs break on a minor), 3 for the base image; never below pnpm's 3-day gate. Minor/patch bumps are grouped, except root production and agent-runner runtime deps (one PR each, per CLAUDE.md), so the agent SDK and `claude-code` (skill pins) move in separate PRs. Majors come alone; nothing merges itself. `chat` moves only with its `@chat-adapter/*` pins; Node and `@types/node` majors wait for a deliberate Node move.
- **Out of scope**: turning on security-update PRs (a repo setting); the Dockerfile's `BUN_VERSION`, `PNPM_VERSION` and `NPM_VERSION` args and `# syntax` line; skill Dockerfiles and `go.mod` (listed in `not-covered.json`).

## Related work

No issue. Follows https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/3968 (actions pinned by SHA) and https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4007 (skill-pins manifest, merged).

## Change kind

- [ ] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [x] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- Validates against SchemaStore's `dependabot-2.0` schema (ajv); a copy with a typo'd key fails.
- Checked against dependabot-core: it parses this `bun.lock` format, and with `pnpm@10.34.5` it applies the larger of the cooldown and our 4320-minute gate to transitive versions too. Bun has no such transitive gate.
- Renovate: no PRs, `renovate/*` branches or dashboard issue since the file landed 2026-07-29.
- Docker tracks only a pinned `FROM`; a floating `node:22-slim` gets no PRs. https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/pull/4183 pinned `node:22.23.4-slim@sha256:…` on main, so the first run moves tag and digest together.

- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not): config-only; the first Monday run after merge is the real test (parse errors show under Insights → Dependency graph → Dependabot).

## User and release impact

```release-note
NONE
```

## Security and trust boundaries

Repo config only. Dependabot PRs get a read-only token and no Actions secrets, and need the same CI and review as any PR. A bun bump moves the lockfile the pinned agent image was built from, so `pull.sh` warns about lock drift until the next release image.

prs.title: fix(setup): reach Docker from the user service when the docker group was just added
prs.body:
<!-- nanoclaw-pr-template:v2 -->

## Summary

When setup has just added the user to the docker group, the background user service can now reach Docker on the first run.

- **Problem**: the systemd user manager keeps the groups it had at login, and setup's linger keeps it alive, so logging out doesn't help. Setup's `setfacl` workaround needs the `acl` package, which stock Ubuntu and WSL lack. The service crash-loops on `docker.sock`, the first chat is skipped, and the printed fix (`sudo setfacl …`) can't run.
- **Fix**: in the service step, install `acl` non-interactively (`sudo -n`, apt only) when `setfacl` is missing, then apply the socket ACL. After that repair, setup stops the service, clears this checkout's crash counter (`data/circuit-breaker.json`) and starts it. A service that crash-looped without Docker would otherwise wait out its crash backoff, up to 15 minutes. When the repair can't run, the wizard prints commands that work: the acl install only when needed, the setfacl line, clearing the crash counter, and `systemctl --user restart <unit>`, plus that a reboot (on WSL, `wsl --shutdown`) makes the group stick.
- **Out of scope**: the ACL resets when Docker restarts; the reboot note covers the lasting fix.

## Related work

Refs #2006
Builds on #4200 (merged): the repair's `sudo -n` reuses its up-front sudo ask.

## Change kind

- [x] `kind/bug`
- [ ] `kind/feature`
- [ ] `kind/documentation`
- [ ] `kind/cleanup`
- [ ] `kind/hardening`

## Validation

- `vitest run setup/service setup/lib/docker-access-hint.test.ts setup/auto`: 74 pass (14 Linux-only skipped on macOS). New: a service with an existing crash counter is stopped, the counter cleared, then started (this test fails without the fix), and a counter that can't be removed still gets the restart. Also covered: acl install before the ACL, no cached sudo ticket, setfacl failing, no apt, group not stale, and a `'` in the checkout path kept literal in the hint's commands.
- Live, with a user whose sudo needs a password and no Docker or acl:
  - On exe.dev, the first run without this fix reproduced the crash loop. With it, the log says `Installing acl for the socket workaround` → `Applied temporary ACL…`, and the agent replies.
  - Same on Windows 11 WSL / Ubuntu 24.04 with Docker Engine.
  - Crash counter, same exe.dev user: stale docker group, service stopped, counter at attempt 6 from a crash, then the real service step. Before: `attempt=7 delaySec=900` and `chat ping` exits 2. After: `NanoClaw running` 2 s after the start, and `chat ping` gets a reply.
- [x] Tests cover the changed behavior (or Validation says why not)

## User and release impact

- [ ] No user-visible behavior change
- [x] User-visible change — release note below
- [ ] Breaking change — release note below covers detect, why, fix/migration, rollback

```release-note
When setup has just added you to the docker group, it now gives NanoClaw's background service access to Docker itself and starts it right away. Otherwise it prints commands that work; before, the first chat failed and the suggested fix needed a tool that isn't installed.
```

## Security and trust boundaries

Installs the `acl` package with `sudo -n` (no prompt) and grants the current user read/write on `docker.sock` by ACL, the same access the docker group membership setup just added.

prs.title: fix(auth): avoid double gateway restart after login
prs.body:
## Problem

After logging in with a subscribed account, the OpenClaw gateway restarted twice (~24s apart, the first taking ~20s).

Log evidence from a real login:

1. `media-entitlement-changed` sync → `lobsterai-model-compat` plugin **removed**, `plugins,models` changed → `restartImpact=restart` → hard restart #1
2. `server-models-updated` sync (queued at login, waited `queueWaitMs=23079`) → plugin **re-added** → hard restart #2

## Root cause

The `auth:exchange` handler calls `clearServerModelMetadata()` and then `syncOpenClawConfigIfAuthQuotaGateChanged()`. With tokens present but the metadata empty, config sync renders a full config without the plan catalog or the model-compat plugin, so the gateway restarts. The renderer's post-login `loadServerModels()` then restores them and restarts again.

The entitlement no longer affects the rendered config (`canUseMediaGeneration()` result is discarded in `openclawConfigSync.ts`), so this login-time sync only produced a transient incomplete config. `10220caf` stopped forcing the restart but did not address that the rendered config itself was incomplete. Free accounts were unaffected because their gate does not change at login.

## Fix

Drop the quota-gate sync from the exchange path. The renderer's post-login model load performs the single sync (metadata was just cleared, so `metadataChanged=true` guarantees it runs) and reads the current gate. Logout and mid-session GetUser/GetQuota gate syncs are unchanged.

## Behavior change

OpenClaw config/restart: login no longer triggers a `media-entitlement-changed` config sync. Expected result is at most one gateway restart after login, usually none when re-logging into the same account (model-only changes hot-reload).

## Verification

- `npx eslint` on `src/main/main.ts`: clean
- `npm run compile:electron`: passes
- Vitest (config delivery / agent models / config sync runtime / shared auth): 245 passed, 3 skipped (on the original branch)
- Manual: log out, log back in with a subscribed account; `main-*.log` should show no `reason=media-entitlement-changed` and at most one `HARD RESTART EXECUTING`

prs.title: chore(deps-dev): bump the docx-editor group with 2 updates
prs.body:
Bumps the docx-editor group with 2 updates: [@docx-editor.dev/core](https://github.com/eigenpal/docx-editor/tree/HEAD/packages/core) and [@docx-editor.dev/i18n](https://github.com/eigenpal/docx-editor/tree/HEAD/packages/i18n). Updates `@docx-editor.dev/core` from 2.22.0 to 2.34.0
Release notes

Sourced from @​docx-editor.dev/core's releases.

@​docx-editor.dev/core@2.34.0

Minor Changes

  • 3934f6a: Inline equations place n-ary limits to the right of the operator as a subscript and superscript, display equations follow m:limLoc, and an n-ary with an m:limLoc of subSup displays as math; EquationExpression n-ary structures carry it as limitLocation. Fixes #1543.
  • 3934f6a: Equation scripts and bars take their size from the structure's control properties, or from the text around the equation, and a tall subscript drops until its top meets the subscript limit; EquationExpression structures carry the control size as controlFontSizePt. Fixes #1539.
  • f182c70: Close the link panel when another participant strikes its selected words in suggesting mode, and add hyperlinks.selectionIsPendingDeletion() to tell whether a selection is a pending deletion. Fixes #1643.
  • 4e4d44d: Remove a generated table of contents from its context menu or with the removeToc command. Fixes #1223.
  • bb84b35: A handle at a table's top-left corner selects the whole table, and dragging it moves the table between the blocks around it; selectTableRegion supports region: 'table'. Suggesting mode no longer deletes a whole table untracked. Fixes #1567, fixes #1568
  • 9c02206: Equations render border boxes, text boxes that fit their shape to their text take the text height, paragraphs that name a missing or character style take the default paragraph style, and page borders held only in tracked section properties draw. PDF export uses fonts installed on the system, and Segoe UI resolves to a metric-compatible packaged substitute.

Patch Changes

  • ae0ccce: Backspace at the start of an indented paragraph now removes the indent before it joins the paragraph to the previous one, and keeps the right indent. Fixes #1690.
  • 8671251: Backspace at the start of a list item now removes its bullet or number and keeps the text in place, and a second Backspace joins it to the previous paragraph. In suggesting mode, list changes are now tracked as suggestions. Fixes #1594.
  • 5abd50f: In a legacy compatibility mode that compresses punctuation, a document that balances single-byte and double-byte widths now shrinks inter-word spaces down to a quarter of the font size to keep one more word on a line. Fixes #1667.
  • 2b3abe6: Text inside w:bdo and w:dir wrappers now displays in the direction that the wrapper declares, and the caret, clicks, and arrow keys follow that order. Fixes #714.
  • 6a8141c: Page number, page count, and section page count fields in the document body now show the page they are on, instead of the result saved in the file.
  • 93fbd9b: Data-bound content controls open showing the current value of their custom XML or document property node instead of the saved text. Fixes #1684.
  • f5cdd00: Paragraph formatting, such as indents, spacing, alignment, styles, and lists, now applies inside data-bound block content controls, and the bound text stays unchanged. In suggesting mode, indents, spacing, alignment, and styles become a suggestion that can be accepted or rejected. Fixes #1661.
  • 98f3186: Text no longer disappears from runs, paragraphs, and tables whose markup is out of order, repeated, or nested, and repeated run, paragraph, and table properties now combine instead of only the first applying. Text in w:t without xml:space="preserve" now drops its leading and trailing spaces.
  • 398963c: Formatting or clearing formatting at a caret inside a word applies to the whole word as one undo step, and a format painter click on a word with a tracked replacement paints the whole visible word.
  • 5186d17: Replacing a checkbox content control's glyph with its checked or unchecked glyph now changes the checkbox state inside the control, and other replacement text is refused instead of emptying the control. Fixes #1144.
  • 752d5fb: A long word with no break opportunity keeps its final period on the line, hanging past the margin, instead of moving it alone to a new line. Fixes #1639.
  • 9e7a1ac: Justified and distributed lines with East Asian text give every character the same gap, including gaps next to punctuation, and spaces and automatic gaps between scripts take only a bounded share of the slack. Fixes #1542.
  • a343e05: Lines drawn in a Chinese, Japanese, or Korean face that is taller than one em now take 1.3 times the height of that face, so documents that use such faces paginate correctly. A character in a run with the East Asian font hint that the East Asian face cannot draw now keeps the Latin face.
  • 74b3b0e: In a collaboration session, moving a block toward the start of its container, or formatting text whose properties are stored out of order, no longer removes a neighboring block or property for every participant. A table moved after concurrent moves of the same table keeps the empty paragraph between it and the next table. Fixes #1572. Fixes #1606.
  • f5cdd00: The Decrease Indent button state updates quickly when a long selection, such as a select-all in a long document, has no indented paragraph. Fixes #1660.
  • d460053: Formatting stored on the default character style no longer changes text, so text keeps the size and color of its paragraph style.
  • 3e928db: Distributed paragraphs stretch their final line, including table cells and passages beside floating objects. Fixes #1361.
  • 9622f77: Distributed paragraphs spread their lines across every character in legacy compatibility modes and when the styles part defines run defaults, keep the letters of kerned runs together in modern modes, and center a line that has nothing to stretch.
  • 752d5fb: A distributed line keeps the next word only when its spaces would lose at most a third of the stretch the shorter line takes, and hangs a final comma or period beside spaces at their limit. Fixes #1637.
  • a990507: A distributed line with a tab stretches the text after its last tab from a left stop to the line end, and centers when that tab reaches a right, center, or decimal stop. Fixes #1541.
  • b3f007c: Punctuation compression, kana compression, and hanging punctuation now turn on for documents whose default East Asian font is Osaka, Nanum Gothic, Klee Medium, Klee One, or a font named in East Asian characters, and turn off for Hiragino, PingFang, and Heiti unless the font table marks them as East Asian. Picking Osaka in the font menu now also sets the East Asian font. Fixes #1725.
  • a4a765d: Documents whose default East Asian font is Noto Sans CJK JP now compress punctuation and shrink justified spaces like other Japanese defaults, also when the face is not installed and the font table has no entry for it. Fixes #1663.
  • 00044e7: East Asian line-end punctuation hangs only where the line-start rules forbid it, at every alignment in legacy compatibility modes and in distributed paragraphs, kana compress to fit a line-start-prohibited character, and pair kerning leaves full-width East Asian text unkerned. Fixes #1574, #1575, #1577, #1578, #1581.
  • fca265a: In documents with an East Asian language, a justified line shrinks its spaces to keep a line-end comma or period inside the margin, and hangs the mark only when the spaces cannot make room for it. Fixes #1605.
  • 9e7a1ac: East Asian text on justified lines no longer spreads between its characters, and automatic spacing between East Asian and Latin text no longer opens, when the document's run defaults name no East Asian font. Fixes #1556.
  • 677252d: Formatting at the caret of an empty paragraph applies to its paragraph mark as a document change with its own undo step, so Bold and other toggles turn off a format the mark already has. Fixes #1626.
  • 7760eb5: When two participants type at the same place, each caret now stays after its own text, and later typing no longer lands inside text that was already typed. Fixes #1710.
  • 598631e: Use authored text fonts for equation digits, except in bold math styles, and the paragraph font for unstyled normal text. Fixes #1307.
  • f7baed2: An equation overline or underline keeps a fixed gap from the glyphs that it covers, and its stroke follows the rule thickness of the math font.
  • f7baed2: Equation runs whose font slots name different faces render as math with their face, size, and math style instead of a text fallback.
  • f7baed2: Inline equation fractions center their rule on the math axis, place their numerator and denominator by the math font constants, and add no side padding, so a line with a fraction is no taller than it needs to be; fractions in display equations keep their padded placement.
  • 4d616ff: An equation whose runs differ in size no longer makes its line too tall: the first run keeps its full height, and a later, larger run adds only the height of its glyphs. Fixes #1540.
  • 6505457: Equations space relations, binary operators, punctuation, fractions, and n-ary operators by their operator class, and a sign at the start of an argument or after another operator stays unspaced; a hyphen draws as the minus sign and * as the asterisk operator, and the saved text does not change. Fixes #1533.
  • f7baed2: Equation runs that name a language render as math at their own size instead of a text fallback, and save keeps the language.
  • f7baed2: Equation scripts draw at 73 percent of the run size in whole half points, or 60 percent inside another script, and superscripts rise a fixed share of the size, or higher over a tall base.
  • 7e0a75f: Equation lines with scripts and fractions now take the height of their glyphs, later scripts and fractions take their offsets from the size of the first run, and multiple line spacing adds its share of the text height below an equation instead of keeping the equation as a minimum. Fixes #1591.
  • f7baed2: Equation subscripts sit a fifth of an em below the baseline and keep a gap below a superscript on the same base, so a line with a subscript no longer gains extra height.
  • 6505457: Equations with spaced operators paint each source run as one text span, and PDF export writes one text object per face and baseline, so pages with many operators paint faster and export smaller. Fixes #1560.

... (truncated)

prs.body:
Bumps [@univerjs/find-replace](https://github.com/dream-num/univer) from 1.0.2 to 1.3.1.
Release notes

Sourced from @​univerjs/find-replace's releases.

🕶️ Release v1.3.1

Full changelog: v1.3.0…v1.3.1

🎃 Release v1.3.0

👻 Halloween is around the corner, and Univer 1.3.0 comes with a few treats 🎃 This release adds slicers, timelines, and expanded pivot grouping, alongside improvements to document editing, rendering performance, and everyday interactions.

New features

Slicers and timelines (Pro)

Filter tables and pivot reports with interactive slicers. Timelines provide date-range filtering for pivot tables and pivot charts, with year, quarter, month, and day views.

Three new packages provide the feature:

Package Purpose
@univerjs-pro/slicer Shared slicer and timeline models, rendering, and themes.
@univerjs-pro/sheets-slicer Worksheet integration, data-source connections, commands, and Facade APIs.
@univerjs-pro/sheets-slicer-ui Interactive controls, insertion menus, settings, and connection dialogs.

These plugins and the slicer Facade API are included in UniverSheetsAdvancedPreset. For direct plugin integrations, register the Sheets Slicer and Sheets Slicer UI plugins and load the corresponding styles and locales.

Expanded pivot grouping (Pro)

Group selected items manually, organize numbers into ranges, and group dates by calendar units. These capabilities work with connected slicers and timelines for interactive report filtering.

Code block fonts and table alignment (Pro)

Code blocks now support built-in and custom monospaced fonts on desktop and mobile. Fonts registered with FontCategory.MONOSPACE are available in the code block font picker.

Traditional documents also gain left, center, and right table alignment controls in the Ribbon.

Conditional formatting: Stop If True

Use “Stop If True” to prevent lower-priority formatting rules from applying when a rule matches. The rule editor and rule list now expose this setting.

Improvements and fixes

  • UI: Move overflowing Ribbon groups into a compact More menu, improve the color picker, and support resetting sheet tab colors.
  • Sheets: Preserve text values during formatting, correct number-format colors, and retain table borders after filtering.
  • Sheets: Improve mobile editing and row/column resizing, and support Format Painter on row and column headers.
  • Docs: Improve block dragging, pasting, and focus handling across embedded editors and multiple instances.
  • Bases (Pro): Improve view tabs, hierarchical rows, and selection interactions.
  • Performance (Pro): Improve PDF scrolling and zooming, and reduce rendering work for 3D charts.
  • Collaboration and export (Pro): Provide clearer license errors, expose server rejection reasons through CollaborationConflict.message, and fix formatting loss in generated collaboration snapshots.

Breaking changes and upgrading

Keep all @univerjs/* and @univerjs-pro/* packages on the same version.

prs.title: chore(deps): bump mermaid from 10.9.8 to 12.2.0
prs.body:
Bumps [mermaid](https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid) from 10.9.8 to 12.2.0.
Release notes

Sourced from mermaid's releases.

mermaid@12.2.0

Minor Changes

  • #8394 6ac38cb Thanks @​jackroberts236! - feat: Add opt-in mindmap coloring by hierarchy depth using mindmap.colorBy: depth and the existing theme palette.

Patch Changes

  • #8409 419ee68 Thanks @​ashishjain0512! - fix: size circle and double-circle nodes from their label instead of minNodeWidth, and trim neo circle padding

  • #8395 2fb3ff1 Thanks @​ashishjain0512! - fix: ELK no longer straightens an edge terminal when that would put a label over another edge, or an edge through a label

  • #8394 cbf89ab Thanks @​jackroberts236! - fix: Keep mindmap HTML labels readable in the neo look on themes that repaint node backgrounds

  • #8390 430ac9b Thanks @​ashishjain0512! - fix: Centre mindmap node labels when htmlLabels is false

  • #8161 d7532ed Thanks @​filipsajdak! - fix: scope a swimlane cluster's DOM id like every other cluster, so two diagrams on one page do not collide

  • #8270 ad8d61a Thanks @​filipsajdak! - fix(rendering): clip an edge for the layout engine that drew it, so a diagram pinning its own engine (bpmn, swimlanes) still renders when the configured default is another one

  • #8383 9d41c0f Thanks @​filipsajdak! - fix(swimlanes): split shared terminal lanes again after crossing cleanup, so an edge that detours around another lane no longer ends on the same attachment point as a neighbouring edge

  • #8384 6c67397 Thanks @​filipsajdak! - fix(swimlanes): move a lane's title band clear of an edge that crosses it, in LR diagrams whose lanes carry no direction of their own and when the edge runs along the band's border

  • #8366 40124c3 Thanks @​SwastikTripathi! - fix: swimlane nodes with no edges keep their source order inside a lane instead of being sorted by ID

mermaid@12.1.0

Minor Changes

  • #8303 9140716 Thanks @​filipsajdak! - feat: add the elk.orientFeedbackEdges option, enabled by default. With the ELK layout, an edge from a node that a subgraph feeds back into that subgraph is now routed downstream instead of around the subgraph. This changes the layout of existing ELK diagrams that contain such edges; set elk.orientFeedbackEdges: false to keep the previous routing.

  • #8250 fd4f5f2 Thanks @​kartben! - feat: add a bitOrder option to packet diagrams. It defaults to ascending, which is the current behaviour, and descending mirrors every row so it reads from that row's highest bit down to its lowest. Fields are still declared lowest bit first and keep their width, so switching a diagram between the two conventions only means changing bitOrder.

Patch Changes
