prs.body:
Bumps [eslint-plugin-react-hooks](https://github.com/facebook/react/tree/HEAD/packages/eslint-plugin-react-hooks) from 5.2.0 to 7.1.1.
Release notes

Sourced from eslint-plugin-react-hooks's releases.

eslint-plugin-react-hooks@7.1.1 (April 17, 2026)

Note: 7.1.0 accidentally removed the component-hook-factories rule, causing errors for users who referenced it in their ESLint config. This is now fixed.

  • Add deprecated no-op component-hook-factories rule for backwards compatibility. (@​mofeiZ in #36307)

eslint-plugin-react-hooks@7.1.0 (April 16, 2026)

This release adds ESLint v10 support, improves performance by skipping compilation for non-React files, and includes compiler lint improvements including better set-state-in-effect detection, improved ref validation, and more helpful error reporting.

  • Add ESLint v10 support. (@​azat-io in #35720)
  • Skip compilation for non-React files to improve performance. (@​josephsavona in #35589)
  • Fix exhaustive deps bug with Flow type casting. (@​jorge-cab in #35691)
  • Fix useEffectEvent checks in component syntax. (@​jbrown215 in #35041)
  • Improved set-state-in-effect validation with fewer false negatives. (@​jorge-cab in #35134, @​josephsavona in #35147, @​jackpope in #35214, @​chesnokov-tony in #35419, @​jsleitor in #36107)
  • Improved ref validation for non-mutating functions and event handler props. (@​josephsavona in #35893, @​kolvian in #35062)
  • Compiler now reports all errors instead of stopping at the first. (@​josephsavona in #35873–#35884)
  • Improved source locations and error display in compiler diagnostics. (@​nathanmarks in #35348, @​josephsavona in #34963)
Changelog

Sourced from eslint-plugin-react-hooks's changelog.

7.1.1

Note: 7.1.0 accidentally removed the component-hook-factories rule, causing errors for users who referenced it in their ESLint config. This is now fixed.

  • Add deprecated no-op component-hook-factories rule for backwards compatibility. (@​mofeiZ in #36307)

7.1.0

This release adds ESLint v10 support, improves performance by skipping compilation for non-React files, and includes compiler lint improvements including better set-state-in-effect detection, improved ref validation, and more helpful error reporting.

  • Add ESLint v10 support. (@​azat-io in #35720)
  • Skip compilation for non-React files to improve performance. (@​josephsavona in #35589)
  • Fix exhaustive deps bug with Flow type casting. (@​jorge-cab in #35691)
  • Fix useEffectEvent checks in component syntax. (@​jbrown215 in #35041)
  • Improved set-state-in-effect validation with fewer false negatives. (@​jorge-cab in #35134, @​josephsavona in #35147, @​jackpope in #35214, @​chesnokov-tony in #35419, @​jsleitor in #36107)
  • Improved ref validation for non-mutating functions and event handler props. (@​josephsavona in #35893, @​kolvian in #35062)
  • Compiler now reports all errors instead of stopping at the first. (@​josephsavona in #35873–#35884)
  • Improved source locations and error display in compiler diagnostics. (@​nathanmarks in #35348, @​josephsavona in #34963)

7.0.1

  • Disallowed passing inline useEffectEvent values as JSX props to guard against accidental propagation. (#34820 by @​jf-eirinha)
  • Switch to export = so eslint-plugin-react-hooks emits correct types for consumers in Node16 ESM projects. (#34949 by @​karlhorky)
  • Tightened the typing of configs.flat so the configs export is always defined. (#34950 by @​poteto)
  • Fix named import runtime errors. (#34951, #34953 by @​karlhorky)

7.0.0

This release slims down presets to just 2 configurations (recommended and recommended-latest), and all compiler rules are enabled by default.

  • Breaking: Removed recommended-latest-legacy and flat/recommended configs. The plugin now provides recommended (legacy and flat configs with all recommended rules), and recommended-latest (legacy and flat configs with all recommended rules plus new bleeding edge experimental compiler rules). (@​poteto in #34757)

6.1.1

Note: 6.1.0 accidentally allowed use of recommended without flat config, causing errors when used with ESLint v9's defineConfig() helper. This has been fixed in 6.1.1.

  • Fix recommended config for flat config compatibility. The recommended config has been converted to flat config format. Non-flat config users should use recommended-legacy instead. (@​poteto in #34700)
  • Add recommended-latest and recommended-latest-legacy configs that include React Compiler rules. (@​poteto in #34675)
  • Remove unused NoUnusedOptOutDirectives rule. (@​poteto in #34703)
  • Remove hermes-parser and dependency. (@​poteto in #34719)
  • Remove @babel/plugin-proposal-private-methods dependency. (@​ArnaudBarre and @​josephsavona in #34715)
  • Update for Zod v3/v4 compatibility. (@​kolian and @​josephsavona in #34717)

6.1.0

Note: Version 6.0.0 was mistakenly released and immediately deprecated and untagged on npm. This is the first official 6.x major release and includes breaking changes.

  • Breaking: Require Node.js 18 or newer. (@​michaelfaith in #32458)
  • Breaking: Flat config is now the default recommended preset. Legacy config moved to recommended-legacy. (@​michaelfaith in #32457)
  • New Violations: Disallow calling use within try/catch blocks. (@​poteto in #34040)

prs.title: fix(cowork): request macOS image thumbnails in points so QuickLook stops returning the file icon
prs.body:
## Problem

On macOS, generated images in the conversation could show the generic PNG file icon instead of the image.

`nativeImage.createThumbnailFromPath` takes **points**, and QuickLook renders them at the screen scale. `LocalImageThumbnails` passed device pixels, so on Retina a 1536×1008 request became 3072×2016 px. When the request is larger than what QuickLook renders for a big image (reproduced with a 2560×1680 chart), it returns the file-type icon padded to the requested box. The icon passed the size check and was cached on disk for 30 days. In one local cache, all 23 PNG thumbnails were this icon.

## Changes

- **Request points on macOS:** `createScreenScaleThumbnail` asks QuickLook for `size / scaleFactor` and reads back the screen-scale bitmap. Electron's 1x copy is not used because it is blurry. QuickLook now renders exactly the pixels needed, which is also 4× less work.
- **Reject the icon:** a thumbnail whose four corners are fully transparent is treated as the file-type icon, and the original is served. Side effect: images with transparent corners (cut-outs, logos) get the original, as all images did before thumbnails existed.
- **Cache version:** the cache key now includes a version, so icons already on disk are never served again. They are removed by the normal 30-day prune.
- Windows wiring is unchanged.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run src/main/libs/localImageThumbnails.test.ts src/main/artifactLocalFileProtocol.test.ts`: pass. New tests cover the points request, the icon guard and the cache version.
- ESLint on changed files and `npm run compile:electron`: pass.
- Ran the compiled module in Electron 43 against a fresh 2560×1680 chart:
  - the new wiring returns a real 1536×1008 JPEG, as sharp as a direct high-quality downscale;
  - the old wiring is now caught by the icon guard.
- Manually tested in the app on macOS.

## Electron-specific notes

- Main process only. The `localfile://` thumbnail resolution now uses `screen.getPrimaryDisplay().scaleFactor` on macOS.
- No IPC, storage schema or OpenClaw changes.

prs.title: fix(desktop-companion): prevent unintended selection answer cancellation
prs.body:
## Summary

Selection quick answers use independent HTTP requests, but their availability was tied to the OpenClaw gateway. Restarting the gateway could therefore hide an active answer card and cancel its request.

A rapid second click on **Regenerate** could also cancel the answer: the first click removed the previous answer and shrank the window, leaving the original button position outside the card.

## Changes Made

- Keep selection tools available during gateway transitions, with foreground monitoring active while selection remains available. Continue honoring the companion switch, selection preference, snooze, and screenshot state.
- Preserve the card's current minimum height when regenerating, bounded by the available maximum height. Reset it when the selection or action changes, or the card closes, so the second click stays inside the card.
- Add regression coverage for gateway transitions, selection before gateway readiness, foreground changes, and disabling selection.

## Electron-Specific Changes

Updates selection availability and foreground monitoring in the main process, and answer-card sizing in the renderer. Agent task entry retains its gateway readiness checks; clicks outside the card still dismiss it.

releases.name: LobsterAI 2026.11.6
releases.body:
## 2026.11.2

A release focused on reliability: chat streams now survive mid-reply drops, oversized contexts recover with visible compaction progress, the image pipeline is cheaper and less chatty, and installers ship a lot less dead weight.

## Highlights

1. Model streams reconnect automatically when they drop mid-reply instead of leaving the message truncated (#2974).
2. Oversized conversations now recover instead of failing, with compaction progress surfaced in the UI (#2982, #3014, #2988).
3. One image confirmation can now approve the rest of a turn's images, and delivery recovery is more robust (#2995, #2980, #2994).
4. Installer and runtime bundles are significantly slimmer: no source maps, no tsc output, no debug-only files (#2976, #2985, #2996).
5. DeepSeek Harness runtime moved to 0.2.2-rc.1 with cleaner shutdown and leftover reclamation (#2989, #3007, #3008).

## New Features

1. 
2. Desktop companion: selection requests continue after sign-in instead of being dropped (#3005).
3. Sidebar: login benefits now shown in a promo bubble (#3015).
4. Release: added the codown SVN publish workflow (#2966).
5. DSH: bumped DeepSeek Harness runtime to 0.2.1-rc.5, then 0.2.2-rc.1 with bundled pnpm plugin installs (#2989, #3007).

## Performance

1. OpenClaw ships only allowlisted bundled skills (#2996).
2. Windows process start times are read natively (#2997).
3. Windows registry roots and code page are read natively (#3002).
4. Gateway client connects sooner after startup (#3000).
5. The dreaming startup scrub is skipped when dreaming is off (#3001).
6. `build-info.json` ships beside the gateway bundle instead of being generated at runtime (#3011).
7. Media intent recovery no longer blocks the main thread (#2965).
8. Memory search no longer launches a second app instance (#3013).

## Bug Fixes

**Chat and Cowork**

1. Restored truncated `chat.history` replies and fixed composer popover clipping (#2981).
2. Model selection is preserved in scheduled-task conversations (#2986).
3. Generated images are no longer stored inline in message metadata (#2999).
4. Images are kept when copying a user message (#3009).
5. macOS image thumbnails are requested in points so QuickLook stops returning the file icon (#3017).

**Media**

1. Image confirmation is preserved and image delivery recovers after interruptions (#2980).
2. Visible subagents can generate images again (#2994).

**Desktop Companion**

1. The orb stays under the pointer while dragging (#2979).
2. Selections the hook skips are now shown over the pointer shape and in AppKit apps (#2984, #2992).
3. Task card stays above full-screen apps, and hidden surfaces no longer jump on open (#3003).
4. Reopened panels get key focus back on macOS (#3006).
5. Unintended selection answer cancellation is prevented (#3016).

**OpenClaw Runtime**

1. `sessions_spawn` children stay off model-picked models (#2975).
2. Windows plugins load natively, and plugin realpaths are cached (#2987).
3. Byte-bounded history is compacted instead of slid (#2988).
4. Integrity checks are skipped for cleanly closed agent databases (#2990).
5. Install paths are re-rendered in the no-model config sync (#3010).
6. Sign-out config shrink is applied without a gateway restart (#3012).

**Packaging and Build**

1. Source maps, tsc output and unused runtime files are no longer shipped (#2976).
2. Bundled and debug-only files are excluded from the installer (#2985).

**Web Search**

1. Bundled dist stays usable after copying, and npm repairs that cannot work are no longer attempted (#2977).
2. Node runs without the env found on `PATH` (#2983).

**DSH**

1. Plugins install with bundled pnpm (#3007).
2. The runtime stops on quit and leftovers are reclaimed on restart (#3008).

**Account**

1. Account menu opens without waiting on the daily check-in (#2991).

## CI and Docs

1. Dependabot no longer opens unmergeable dependency PRs (#2978).
2. Documented stacked post-ready measurement for the registry/code page patch (#3004).

## Contributors

Thanks to @fisherdaddy, @btc69m979y-dotcom, @Mind-Hand and @liuzhq1986 for this release.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/netease-youdata/LobsterAI/compare/2026.10.30...2026.11.6

issues.title: [Tests]: Fix unawaited coroutine warnings caused by scheduling mocks and loop context
issues.body:
## Summary
Six unawaited-coroutine warning occurrences originate from test scheduling mocks or an incorrect execution context. They obscure real async lifecycle defects (for example #7857) even though the tests pass.

## Environment / scope
macOS arm64, Python 3.11.15. Investigated during local validation of #5992; the listed tests and corresponding implementation files are unchanged relative to upstream commit `77576f6dd88982af134fe8ff9315d65ada3b4c1d`. No clean full-main test run is claimed.

## Identified sources
| Test | Cause |
| --- | --- |
| `tests/unit/agents/memory/test_proactive_trigger_logic.py::TestEnableDisable::test_enable_stores_config_and_workspace` | Mocked `asyncio.create_task` returns a fake task without executing or closing the supplied `_run_trigger_loop` coroutine. |
| `tests/unit/agents/skill_system/test_hub.py::TestClientLifecycle::test_aclose_hub_client_drain_timeout_warns` | Fake `wait_for` raises TimeoutError without consuming/closing the supplied `Event.wait` coroutine. |
| `tests/unit/channels/test_dingtalk.py::TestDingTalkStreamMode::test_run_stream_forever` | Async test directly calls a synchronous thread entry point that uses `asyncio.run`. It fails inside the already-running test loop; production starts this entry point in a separate thread. |
| `tests/unit/channels/test_qq.py::TestDownloadAttachmentSync::test_download_attachment_exception` | Test configures `qq_channel._loop.run_coroutine_threadsafe`, but production uses module-level `asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe`. The fake loop never schedules the real download coroutine; the test does not exercise the intended exception as designed. |
| `tests/unit/channels/test_telegram.py::TestTelegramTypingIndicators::test_start_typing_creates_task` | Mocked `create_task` does not consume the typing coroutine. |
| `tests/unit/channels/test_telegram.py::TestTelegramTypingIndicators::test_start_typing_replaces_existing` | Same scheduling-mock cleanup omission. |

Warning attribution can appear under a later test because garbage collection is delayed. Allocation tracing was used to locate the originating calls.

## Reproduction
```sh
python -X tracemalloc=5 -m pytest -q \
  tests/unit/agents/acp/test_acp_service.py \
  tests/unit/agents/memory/test_proactive_trigger_logic.py \
  tests/unit/agents/skill_system/test_hub.py \
  tests/unit/channels/test_dingtalk.py \
  tests/unit/channels/test_qq.py \
  tests/unit/channels/test_telegram.py
```

Local result: 726 passed, 38 warnings. Seven warning occurrences were unawaited coroutines: the six above plus the separate ACP defect in #7857. The remaining warnings include asyncio marks on synchronous tests; the total is environment/order dependent.

## Suggested acceptance criteria
- Scheduling mocks explicitly consume/close coroutine arguments when intentionally not scheduling them, or use real tasks and await their cleanup.
- Exercise the DingTalk thread entry point in its intended execution context and assert the stream routine actually ran.
- Patch the actual module-level QQ scheduling function and verify its exception path.
- Assert behavior, rather than merely suppressing RuntimeWarning.
- Re-run these tests with no unawaited-coroutine warnings after the ACP issue is addressed separately.

This issue concerns test correctness; it does not claim these six warning occurrences demonstrate production download/typing failures.

issues.title: [Bug]: ACP shutdown fallback can silently skip session cleanup and leak its event loop
issues.body:
## Summary
The synchronous fallback in `_shutdown_acp_services()` can clear the service registry without executing session cleanup, and leave its newly created event loop unclosed.

## Environment / scope
Reproduced on macOS arm64, Python 3.11.15 during local validation of #5992. The affected ACP source and test are unchanged relative to upstream commit `77576f6dd88982af134fe8ff9315d65ada3b4c1d`. This is a separate lifecycle issue, not a session-model feature change.

## Minimal reproduction
Run in a separate Python process from an installed source environment; no real ACP subprocess is needed:

```python
import asyncio
from qwenpaw.agents.acp import service

calls = []

class FakeService:
    async def close_all_sessions(self):
        calls.append("closed")

asyncio.set_event_loop(None)
service._acp_services["test-agent"] = FakeService()
service._shutdown_acp_services()
print("cleanup calls:", calls)
print("registry:", service._acp_services)
```

With warnings enabled, observed:
```text
RuntimeWarning: coroutine 'FakeService.close_all_sessions' was never awaited
cleanup calls: []
registry: {}
ResourceWarning: unclosed event loop
```

Expected: cleanup is executed and any event loop created by this fallback is closed.

## Cause
In `src/qwenpaw/agents/acp/service.py`, the fallback creates a new loop but evaluates `asyncio.gather(...)` before entering that loop. With no current loop, construction fails; with a different current loop, the gathered future can belong to the wrong loop. The broad exception handler silently discards the failure. `loop.close()` is not protected by a finally block.

The existing `TestServiceRegistry.test_shutdown_clears_registry` only asserts an empty registry, so it does not prove cleanup occurred.

## Suggested acceptance criteria
- Create/await the cleanup aggregation inside the intended loop.
- Reliably close a loop owned by this fallback, including on error.
- Do not silently hide cleanup failures.
- Add regression tests asserting cleanup was awaited with no current loop and with a different non-running current loop; retain coverage for the running-loop branch.
- Review existing ACP resource loop affinity before choosing the implementation.

The reproduction establishes skipped cleanup, not confirmed real subprocess leakage.

issues.title: feat: add tool_call_format config for compact tool call display in IM channels
issues.body:
## Feature Request: Add `tool_call_format` config to control tool call display format

### Problem

Currently, tool call messages in channels (Feishu, DingTalk, etc.) always render with the full format:

```
🔧 **execute_shell_command**
```
{"command": "cd ~/.qwenpaw && python3 -c \"import json; ...\""}
```
```

This is **3 lines per tool call**, which becomes very noisy in IM channels where users want a lightweight progress trace — "I want to know you're alive, not see every argument."

The existing config fields (`show_tool_calls`, `show_tool_details`, `tool_call_max_length`) only control **visibility** and **truncation**, not the **format** itself. There's no way to get a compact single-line output like `🔧 **execute_shell_command**` without patching source code.

### Proposed Solution

Add a new config field `tool_call_format` to `ChannelDisplayConfig`:

```python
@dataclass
class ChannelDisplayConfig:
    show_tool_details: bool = True
    show_thinking: bool = True
    show_tool_calls: bool = True
    show_tool_results: bool = True
    tool_call_max_length: int = 200
    tool_result_max_length: int = 500
    tool_call_format: str = "full"  # NEW: "full" | "name_only" | "compact"
```

**Format modes:**

| Mode | Output | Use case |
|------|--------|----------|
| `"full"` (default) | `🔧 **name**` + code fence + args | Current behavior, no breaking change |
| `"name_only"` | `🔧 **name**` (single line, no args) | IM channels: lightweight progress trace |
| `"compact"` | `🔧 **name**: {first 80 chars}` | Balance between info and brevity |

**Implementation sketch** (in `renderer.py`):

```python
def _fmt_tool_call(
    name: str,
    args_preview: str,
    style: RenderStyle,
) -> str:
    fmt = getattr(style.display_config, "tool_call_format", "full")

    if fmt == "name_only":
        if style.use_emoji:
            return f"🔧 **{name}**"
        return f"**{name}**"

    if fmt == "compact":
        truncated = args_preview[:80] + ("..." if len(args_preview) > 80 else "")
        if style.supports_markdown and style.use_emoji:
            return f"🔧 **{name}**: `{truncated}`"
        if style.supports_markdown:
            return f"**{name}**: `{truncated}`"
        return f"{name}: {truncated}"

    # Default: "full" (current behavior)
    if style.supports_markdown and style.use_emoji:
        return f"🔧 **{name}**\n```\n{args_preview}\n```"
    if style.supports_markdown:
        return f"**{name}**\n```\n{args_preview}\n```"
    if style.supports_code_fence:
        return f"{name}\n```\n{args_preview}\n```"
    return f"{name}: {args_preview}"
```

### Why not just `show_tool_details=false`?

I tried that approach. When `show_tool_details=false`, `args_preview` becomes `"..."`, but the code fence is still emitted:

```
🔧 **execute_shell_command**
```
...
```
```

That's still 3 lines with no information gain. The user wants **just the name** — a single line per tool call.

### Config usage

Per-channel config (e.g. `agent.json` → `channels.feishu`):

```json
{
  "channels": {
    "feishu": {
      "tool_call_format": "name_only"
    }
  }
}
```

### Impact

- **Backward compatible**: Default is `"full"` (current behavior unchanged)
- **Per-channel**: Each channel can choose its own format
- **No global side effects**: Unlike `show_tool_details=false` which affects all channels

### Context

- QwenPaw version: v2.1.0 (installed via pip)
- Affected file: `src/qwenpaw/app/channels/renderer.py`, function `_fmt_tool_call`
- Related config: `ChannelDisplayConfig` in same file
- User scenario: Feishu (Lark) channel where tool call noise degrades mobile UX

issues.title: [Feature]: Quote/Reference text from responses for follow-up context

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

issues.body:
---
name: Feature Request
about: Suggest a new feature or enhancement
title: "[Feature]: Quote/Reference text from responses for follow-up context (like Perplexity)"
labels: ["enhancement", "triage"]
assignees: []
---

## Summary

Add a "Quote to follow-up" feature that allows users to select text from agent responses and automatically include it as quoted context in their next message, similar to Perplexity AI's "Add to follow-up" functionality.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Console (frontend web UI)
- [x] Core / Backend (message handling, context injection)

## Problem / Motivation

When working with AI agents on complex topics, users often need to reference specific parts of previous responses to ask follow-up questions. Currently, users must:

1. Manually copy text from responses
2. Paste it into their next message
3. Format it to indicate it's a quote

This is tedious and disrupts the conversation flow, especially when:
- Discussing technical details with multiple code snippets
- Asking clarifying questions about specific parts of long responses
- Building on previous context in multi-turn conversations

The Perplexity AI model demonstrates this feature effectively, allowing users to highlight text and click "Add to follow-up" to seamlessly include quoted context.

## Proposed Solution

### User Experience

1. **Text Selection**: User selects/highlights text within an agent response
2. **Floating Action**: A floating "Quote" or "Add to follow-up" button appears above the selection (similar to the copy button)
3. **Quote Display**: Selected text appears as a quoted block in the chat input area (styled differently from regular input)
4. **Context Injection**: When user sends their follow-up message, the quoted text is automatically included as context

### Technical Implementation

**Frontend (Console):**
- Add text selection detection in message components
- Implement floating action button for selected text
- Add quote display component in chat input area
- Style quoted text with distinct visual treatment (e.g., border-left, italic, or blockquote styling)

**Backend:**
- Add API endpoint to handle quote context
- Modify message handling to accept optional `quoted_context` field
- Include quoted text in system prompt or message context for the next turn

**Example UI Flow:**
```
[Agent Response with long explanation...]
User selects: "The key difference between X and Y is..."
↓
[Floating button: "Quote to follow-up"]
↓
[Chat input shows:]
> The key difference between X and Y is...

[User types:] What about Z?
↓
[Message sent with quoted context included]
```

### Benefits

- **Improved UX**: Reduces friction in multi-turn conversations
- **Better Context**: Ensures AI understands exactly what the user is referencing
- **Consistency**: Standardizes how users reference previous content
- **Competitive**: Matches functionality available in other AI assistants

## Alternatives Considered

1. **Manual Copy-Paste**: Current workaround, but tedious and error-prone
2. **Reference by Line Number**: Less intuitive, requires users to count lines
3. **Plugin System**: Investigated, but current plugin architecture doesn't support modifying existing chat components (only adding new routes/pages)

## Additional Context

**Reference Implementation:**
- Perplexity AI: Users can highlight text and click "Add to follow-up" button

**Technical Notes:**
- The `@agentscope-ai/chat` package handles message rendering
- The plugin system supports adding routes but not modifying existing components
- This feature requires changes to core chat components

---

**Priority:** Medium-High
**Complexity:** Medium (requires frontend + backend changes)
**Impact:** High (improves core chat UX for all users)

issues.title: [Bug] Default agent edit button is disabled in console although the PUT API allows editing
issues.body:
### Environment

- QwenPaw **2.3.0b2** (console assets built 2026-10-30)
- Linux x86_64, self-hosted
- Not browser-specific: the restriction is compiled into the served React bundle (no CSS / cache / third-party plugin involved)

### Description

The built-in `default` agent cannot be edited from the console at all. Every edit entry point is hard-disabled, so single-agent setups cannot configure per-agent features (mail, model routing, approval level, system prompt files, tools, channels) through the UI.

Related: #7644 (same request, still open).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the QwenPaw console → Agents page
2. Locate the built-in agent with `id = "default"`
3. Hover the card: the Edit action is disabled
4. Open the agent detail drawer: the Edit button is also disabled

### Expected

The `default` agent's configuration should be editable like any other agent. `delete`, `pin` and `reorder` may reasonably remain blocked, since `default` is the root profile and fixed at the top of the list.

### Actual

All editing entry points for `id === "default"` are disabled.

### Root cause (frontend only)

In `console/assets/AgentGallery-C3HV5hg2.js` (loaded through `index-BAoMMfzG.js`):

```js
// card: edit
disabled: d || n.id === "default"
// card: pin
disabled: n.id === "default"
// card: drag handle
disabled: d || n.id === "default"
// detail drawer: edit
disabled: s.id === "default"
```

### The backend does allow it

`app/routers/agents.py`:

- `PUT /api/agents/{agentId}` (around L1175) validates existence, workspace canonicalization, mail/backend compatibility and memory config — **no `default` special case**.
- `DELETE /api/agents/{agentId}` (around L1865) is the only endpoint that explicitly protects it:

```python
if agentId == "default":
    raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail="Cannot delete the default agent")
```

So the update path is a supported API contract; the restriction exists only in the UI layer.

### Docs are inconsistent with the UI

`docs/multi-agent.en.md` / `docs/cli.en.md` only state that the default agent **cannot be deleted**. Neither says it cannot be edited.

### Workaround

Calling the API directly works:

```bash
curl -X PUT http://127.0.0.1:8088/api/agents/default \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"id":"default","name":"<current name>","description":"..."}'
```

`id` and `name` are required; `exclude_unset` semantics mean only supplied fields are updated; `workspace_dir` is ignored. Authentication is required when not on loopback.

But there is no visual feedback in the console, and the change cannot be reviewed or adjusted from the UI.

### Suggested fix

Keep `delete` / `pin` / `reorder` protected for `default`, but allow `edit`.

If the read-only behavior is intentional, then:

1. document it explicitly (docs currently mention only deletion), and
2. provide a supported UI path for the per-agent settings that single-agent users need.

issues.title: Memory tag index never rebuilds: /memory/tags returns 503 "Memory tag index is unavailable" (tags are generated but unreadable)
issues.body:
**Environment**
- QwenPaw Desktop UI: v2.3.0b2; backend package `qwenpaw` PKG-INFO: 2.4; `reme_ai` 0.4.2.0; Windows 10 (AMD64).
- Config: `running.reme_light_memory_config.auto_memory_generate_tags = true` (set through `PUT /api/agents/{id}`, read-back verified; on-disk `agent.json` diff = exactly 2 lines).

**Observed**
1. After enabling the switch, auto-memory saves DO generate tags. The log shows `[FrontmatterUpdateStep] path=memory/... keys=['memory_tags']` on 2/2 post-enable cycles, and the note frontmatter contains `memory_tags:` with values.
2. But both read endpoints fail permanently:
   - `GET /api/agents/{id}/memory/tags?page=1` -> HTTP 503 `{"detail":"Memory tag index is unavailable"}`
   - `GET /api/agents/{id}/memory/tag-files?tag=<t>&page=1` -> HTTP 503, same detail
   - The Console file panel "tags" tab therefore stays empty.
3. `GET /api/agents/{id}/memory/status` -> 200; `runtime.auto_memory = {enabled: true, interval: 5}`; worker idle; embedding_store / file_graph / file_store / keyword_index components all present.

**Root-cause evidence (from qwenpaw.log)**
- Tag index rebuild fails on historical file paths that contain backslashes: the log carries 159 index entries whose `path` field contains a backslash, and rebuild attempts since 2026-10-28 error out on them.
- There are 18 successful `Rebuilt tag index: files=0, tags=0` lines, all dated 2026-10-28; zero successes afterwards. So the failure predates enabling the switch (the toggle is not the cause).

**Expected**
After enabling `auto_memory_generate_tags` and at least one successful auto-memory save, `/memory/tags` should return 200 with the generated tags; the Console "tags" tab should list them; `memory_search` should accept a `tags` filter.

**Actual**
503 always; tags exist only inside note frontmatter; no error is surfaced in the UI (silent 503).

**Repro**
1. `PUT /api/agents/{id}` with `running.reme_light_memory_config.auto_memory_generate_tags=true`.
2. Wait for an auto-memory save (interval 5 min) or trigger one; confirm the note frontmatter gains `memory_tags`.
3. `GET /api/agents/{id}/memory/tags?page=1` -> 503.

**Impact**
The feature is half-working: write path OK, read path dead. Users see an enabled toggle and an empty tags tab with no explanation.

**Suggested fix**
- Normalize stored paths (backslash -> forward slash) during tag-index rebuild, or skip/quarantine malformed path entries instead of aborting the whole rebuild.
- Surface the rebuild failure in `/memory/status` (e.g. `tag_index: {healthy: false, last_error}`) and in the Console tab instead of a bare 503.

issues.title: [Bug]: Model config write path bypasses field validation — invalid thinking_budget / max_input_length are persisted and the provider silently disappears after restart
issues.body:
## Summary

`ModelInfo` declares `thinking_budget >= 1` and `max_input_length >= 1000`, but the per-model config write path never enforces those bounds, so an out-of-range value is accepted, persisted to disk, and then breaks every read path — after a restart the provider fails to load and silently disappears.

## The chain

1. `Provider.update_model_config` (`src/qwenpaw/providers/provider.py`) handles `thinking_budget` and `max_input_length` with a bare `int(...)` assignment. Pydantic does not validate plain attribute assignment (`validate_assignment` is not enabled), so the declared `ge` bounds in `src/qwenpaw/providers/model_info.py` are never checked on this path.
2. The HTTP layer has the same gap: `ModelConfigRequest.thinking_budget` (`src/qwenpaw/app/routers/providers.py`) is the only numeric field in that model without a bound — `max_input_length` carries `ge=1000` and `generate_kwargs.max_tokens` has an explicit `>= 1` validator.
3. The invalid value is stored and persisted by `ProviderManager.update_model_config`.
4. Read paths re-validate: `resolve_model_info` runs `ModelInfo.model_validate(model.model_dump())` and raises `ValidationError`. After a restart, `load_provider` catches the validation failure and returns `None` — a custom provider silently disappears, and a built-in provider loses all persisted configuration, with no error pointing at the value that caused it.

## Reproduction (against current main)

```python
provider.update_model_config("m1", {"thinking_budget": 1024})  # baseline OK
provider.update_model_config("m1", {"thinking_budget": -5})
# -> returns True, stores -5 (declared ge=1)
provider.resolve_model_info("m1")
# -> ValidationError: thinking_budget Input should be greater than or equal to 1
OpenAIProvider.model_validate(provider.model_dump())
# -> ValidationError (1 error) -> load_provider returns None after restart
```

## Related: `thinking_budget_range` has no shape validation

`ModelInfo(thinking_budget_range=[8000])` constructs fine, but `Provider.thinking_control()` unpacks `low, high = info.thinking_budget_range` and raises `ValueError: not enough values to unpack`. The newer `ThinkingControl` model (`src/qwenpaw/providers/thinking.py`) already validates that a budget range is complete and ordered; the legacy `List[int]` field has no equivalent check. A malformed range also poisons `list_provider_info`, which aggregates providers without isolating per-provider failures.

## Expected behavior

- Out-of-range `thinking_budget` / `max_input_length` values are rejected at write time (HTTP request validation and `update_model_config`), consistent with how `update_model_config` already rejects an invalid `model_type` or non-boolean `supports_*` values with `ValueError`, instead of being persisted.
- `thinking_budget_range` only accepts a complete, ordered `[min, max]` pair.

I have a fix and regression tests ready and would like to work on this.

issues.title: [Bug]: Matrix channel logs in with password on every start and never re-uploads E2EE keys after the server drops the device

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.2.2

## Description

With the Matrix channel configured with `user_id` + `password` (no `access_token`), QwenPaw performs a **fresh password login on every process start**, which creates a new authentication session each time. On homeservers where device lists are reconciled against active sessions (Element's **MAS / matrix-authentication-service** with `matrix-authentication-service` + Synapse's `/_synapse/mas/sync_devices`), a restart produces a short window in which the bot account appears to have **zero** devices, and the homeserver deletes the bot's device — **together with its E2EE device keys and one-time keys**.

After that, QwenPaw never recovers on its own:

- `matrix-nio`'s `should_upload_keys()` returns `False` once the local `accounts.shared == 1`, even though the server holds **0** device keys, so `keys_upload()` is never called again (`channel.py` gates the upload on that property).
- The channel's `health_check()` only verifies that an access token exists, so it keeps reporting `healthy`.
- The only signal is a `WARNING` per undecryptable event (`MatrixChannel: could not decrypt event …`), which is easy to miss.

Result: the bot silently loses the ability to decrypt new messages (new Megolm sessions) for an unbounded time, until an operator manually rewrites the local crypto store.

**Security considerations:** affects E2EE availability (silent decryption failure), not confidentiality of already-decrypted content.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.2
- **OS:** Ubuntu (server), Python 3.12.14
- **Install method:** pip / venv
- **E2EE stack:** `matrix-nio 0.26.0`, `vodozemac` backend enabled
- **Homeserver:** Synapse `v1.158.0` + Element MAS `1.23.0` (`enable-mcp` irrelevant; device sync is the MAS default)
- **Channel config:** `homeserver`, `user_id`, `password`, `device_name=qwenpaw-worker`; `access_token` **not** configured; `encryption` enabled

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a Matrix channel with `user_id` + `password` and a fixed `device_name`; enable encryption. Confirm `MatrixChannel: E2E keys uploaded` appears and the homeserver has 1 device key + 50 one-time keys for that device.
2. Restart the Synapse + MAS stack (e.g. reboot the homeserver host), then let QwenPaw start.
3. Observe (timings from an actual occurrence, local time):

```
17:14:53  homeserver host booted
17:16:08  synapse / mas containers started
17:18:53  synapse: "Syncing 0 devices for user @bot:… will delete 1 devices"   <-- device + E2EE keys deleted
17:19:17  QwenPaw: "logged in as @bot:… (password, device=qwenpaw-worker)"     <-- 24s later
```

4. Check the server: `e2e_device_keys_json` / `e2e_one_time_keys_json` for the bot device are **0 / 0**.
5. Send a new encrypted message from another device. QwenPaw logs `could not decrypt event …` and never uploads keys again, regardless of how many times it is restarted.
6. Inspect the local store: `accounts.shared == 1` — the deadlock condition.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** keys are never re-uploaded; decryption stays broken until someone manually runs `UPDATE accounts SET shared=0` in `matrix_crypto_store/<user_id>_qwenpaw-worker.db` and restarts the process. `health_check()` reports `healthy` throughout.
- **Expected:** QwenPaw detects that its device/keys are missing server-side and re-uploads them; at minimum the channel should report itself unhealthy and log at `ERROR` rather than degrade silently.

## Logs / Screenshots

```
# QwenPaw (app log) — login uses password on every start
MatrixChannel: logged in as @bot:example.org (password, device=qwenpaw-worker, device_name=qwenpaw-worker)

# QwenPaw — only warning, once per broken event
MatrixChannel: could not decrypt event $… in !…:example.org (session_id=…)

# Synapse — MAS device reconciliation right after homeserver start
synapse.rest.synapse.mas.devices - Syncing 0 devices for user @bot:example.org will delete 1 devices
```

## Additional Notes

### Root cause chain (three independent defects)

1. **Password auth mode never reuses the cached session.**
   `_restore_auth_state_before_start()` calls `_load_auth_state(restore_token=False, …)` whenever explicit password credentials are configured, with the comment *"otherwise we may accidentally bypass the intended auth path"*. So the `access_token` that `_save_auth_state()` happily persists (`channel.py:956`) is written but never used, and every start creates a new session/device login.

2. **Key upload is gated on a purely local flag.**
   `channel.py` does `if self._client.should_upload_keys: await self._client.keys_upload()`, and `matrix-nio` (`nio/crypto/olm_machine.py:269`) returns `False` as soon as `account.shared` is truthy. Local state says "already uploaded"; the server says "0 keys". Nothing ever reconciles the two, so the failure is permanent and survives any number of restarts.

3. **No health signal.**
   `health_check()` returns `healthy` if `self._client.access_token` is set. It cannot tell "connected" from "connected but cryptographically mute", so operators learn about the outage from users.

### Suggested fixes

- **Reuse before re-login:** in password mode, try the persisted `access_token` first (`whoami`), and fall back to a password login only on `M_UNKNOWN_TOKEN`. This alone removes the repeated device churn.
- **Verify, don't trust, the upload flag:** on startup, query the server for the current device's key counts (or handle `M_UNKNOWN_DEVICE`), and force `keys_upload()` when the device or its keys are missing.
- **Surface the state:** make `health_check()` report `unhealthy` when device keys are absent, and log the first missing-session event at `ERROR` with a hint about re-uploading keys.

### Workaround

Configure the channel with `access_token` instead of `user_id`/`password` (e.g. a MAS personal access token). The token path restores the session rather than logging in again, so the device identity stays stable across restarts.

### Related issues (checked 2026-10-22)

- **#2393** *(open, tracking)* — "Expand Matrix channel (E2EE, sync token, history, allowlists, mentions)": covers auth modes and sync persistence, but not session reuse or key-state reconciliation.
- **#6486** *(closed)* — vodozemac backend probing; fixed the "E2EE unavailable" class of failures. Different root cause.
- **#7109** *(closed)* — retry login on transient homeserver failures; this is the correct behaviour we rely on during startup, and it is what makes the 24-second race visible.

### Frequency

Observed three times on the same deployment (2026-10-01, 2026-10-06, 2026-10-21), each time within ~3 minutes of a homeserver restart, on four bot accounts sharing one homeserver (three affected, one unaffected because it keeps a single long-lived session).

issues.title: [Feature] 浏览器标签页标题跟随当前会话名，便于多标签页区分
issues.body:
## 需求背景

同时打开多个控制台标签页、分别停在不同会话时，**所有标签页标题完全相同**（如「聊天 · QwenPaw」），无法通过标签页标题分辨是哪个会话。

## 现状（代码定位）

控制台通过 `KB` 组件设置标题，标题源是**页面路由名**（如 `core.chat`），不包含会话名：

```js
function KB({ title }) {
  document.title = title === "QwenPaw" ? title : `${title} · QwenPaw`;
  document.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent("qwenpaw:document-title-change", { detail: ... }));
}
```

代码里已有完整的标题变更事件机制（`qwenpaw:document-title-change`）以及未读/审批时 `•` 前缀闪烁，说明基础设施已具备。

## 建议方案

1. 在聊天页（`core.chat`）时，`document.title` 使用当前会话名：`${chat.name} · QwenPaw`，未命名会话回退默认标题；
2. 切换/重命名会话时同步更新（复用现有事件）；
3. 其他页面保持现有行为。

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Console (frontend web UI)

## Environment

- QwenPaw version: 2.2.2
- OS: macOS 15.3
- Browser: Chrome / Safari
- Install method: pip

issues.title: [Bug]: Codex/Qoder 后端的定时任务将非空请求误判为空
issues.body:
### 现象

智能体使用 `codex`（或其他第三方后端）时，包含完整文本指令的 `agent` 类型定时任务会立即失败：

```text
ValueError: Third-party agent requests require text or attachments
```

失败发生在交给第三方智能体之前。

### 复现步骤

1. 为智能体选择 Codex 后端。
2. 创建一条包含非空文本指令的 `agent` 类型定时任务。
3. 手动执行或等待调度触发。
4. 观察执行记录中的上述异常。

已在当前 `main`（`c26d31c0688aa9cce9bc1aef688177d2e14e25df`）通过单元测试复现；原问题也出现在 `2.2.2`。

### 原因和预期行为

`CronExecutor.execute()` 将 `job.request.model_dump(mode="json")` 得到的字典传入 `Workspace.stream_query()`。内置 `Runtime` 会将字典转换为 `AgentRequest`，但第三方后端直接进入 `HarnessRuntime`，其中通过 `getattr(request, "input", None)` 读取输入，因此把非空字典请求误判为空。

预期在共享请求入口统一转换字典，再选择后端；已有请求对象保持原样。文本、附件、`session_id`、`user_id`、`channel` 和 `request_context` 都应保留。

### 修复验证

准备的最小修复仅在 `Workspace.stream_query()` 中增加字典到 `AgentRequest` 的转换，并增加 Codex/Qoder、字典/已有对象、附件和执行上下文的回归测试。

```text
修复前：3 failed, 4 passed
修复后（Harness 和 cron 相关单元测试）：249 passed, 3 skipped
```

将提交对应的修复 PR。

issues.title: [Bug]: Reopening a chat after /clear shows the /clear message and hides the empty-state greeting
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

2.2.2.post1 (latest release). The same code path is still present on `main` (checked at `c84ff8d`, 2026-11-05).

## Description

After running `/clear` in an existing chat, the live view is cleared correctly. But when the user switches to another chat and comes back (or reloads the page), the chat shows a single user bubble whose text is the literal `/clear`, and the empty-state greeting (`chat.greeting`, e.g. “你好，我今天能帮你做什么？”) is not displayed. The conversation should be empty after `/clear`.

Cause, from reading the shipped console bundle (2.2.2.post1) and the source at the tag and on `main`:

1. The console persists every submitted user text in `localStorage` under `qwenpaw_pending_user_msg_<chatId>` so an in-flight message survives a refresh — `savePendingUserMessage`, called from `console/src/pages/Chat/index.tsx` (`sessionApi.setLastUserMessage(...)` in the send path). Slash commands go through the same path, so `/clear` is cached too.
2. `/clear` intentionally erases that turn from the backend context: `_process_clear` → `_persist_and_clear()` in `src/qwenpaw/agents/command_handler.py`. The runtime skips the agent for slash commands (`src/qwenpaw/runtime/runtime.py`, `skip_agent = True`), so no turn is persisted, and `GET /chats/{id}` (`src/qwenpaw/app/chats/api.py`, reads `agent.state.context`) returns `messages: []`.
3. On reopening the chat, `patchLastUserMessage` (`console/src/pages/Chat/sessionApi/index.ts`) tries to reconcile the cached text with the fetched history. When the chat is idle it only drops the cache if the last user message in history equals the cached text. For `/clear` that can never happen — history is empty by design — so it falls through and re-injects the cached text as a user card.
4. Nothing clears the cache when the server signals `clear_history`: `scheduleHistoryClear` (`console/src/pages/Chat/index.tsx`) only calls `messages.removeAllMessages()` and resets the turn-usage snapshot.

Net effect: empty history + one synthetic `/clear` card. The welcome/greeting block is only rendered for an empty message list (SDK behavior), so the re-injected card suppresses it. The state also survives a full page reload, because the cache lives in `localStorage`.

**Related PR(s):** none found

**Security considerations:** none (text is user's own input, local browser storage only)

## Component(s) Affected

- [ ] Core / Backend (app, agents, config, providers, utils, local_models)
- [x] Console (frontend web UI)
- [ ] Channels (DingTalk, Feishu, QQ, Discord, iMessage, etc.)
- [ ] Skills
- [ ] CLI
- [ ] Documentation (website)
- [ ] Tests
- [ ] CI/CD
- [ ] Scripts / Deploy

## Environment

- **QwenPaw version:** 2.2.2.post1
- **OS:** OS-independent (browser-side `localStorage`); observed on Linux
- **Install method:** pip
- **Python version (if applicable):** 3.11

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open an existing chat that has some history, send `/clear`.
2. The live chat becomes empty (correct).
3. Switch to another chat and back — or simply reload the page.
4. A single user bubble `/clear` is shown, and the greeting is missing.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** after reopening a cleared chat, the console renders one user message `/clear` (no assistant reply) and hides the empty-state greeting.
- **Expected:** the chat renders as empty, with the greeting shown.

## Logs / Screenshots

No backend errors. The mechanism can be confirmed in DevTools → Application → Local Storage: the key `qwenpaw_pending_user_msg_<chatId>` still holds `{"text":"/clear",...}` after the clear. (Diagnosis is from code reading of the shipped bundle and `main`; I have not run the UI with the key removed.)

## Additional Notes

**Likely also affects `/new`:** `/new` is submitted through the same console path and its backend handler also wipes the turn (`_process_new` → `_persist_and_clear()`), so it should show the same symptom. Not verified.

**Suggested fix (not implemented here):**

- In `scheduleHistoryClear`, drop the pending cache for the affected session ids (`sessionApi.discardLastUserMessage([...])`) before/after `removeAllMessages()`. The same needs to be done in the queued-item execution path, since a queued `/clear` never goes through the live response handler.
- Optional defensive check in `patchLastUserMessage`: if the fetched history is empty and the cached text is a control command (`/clear`, `/new`), clear the cache instead of patching it in.

**Workaround:** remove the `qwenpaw_pending_user_msg_<chatId>` key from `localStorage`, or send a new message in that chat (which overwrites the cache).

**Related issue:** #3297 (closed) fixed the live view not clearing after `/clear`; this report is the follow-up on reopening the chat.

issues.title: [Bug] recall_history broken on Windows: workspace_dir canonicalized to `\\?\` extended-length path breaks SQLite read-only URI
issues.body:
## Environment
- QwenPaw Desktop **2.3.0-beta.1** (backend: `qwenpaw-backend.exe`, PyInstaller-packaged), Windows 10 x64
- Workspace path: `C:\Users\lxm\.copaw\workspaces\<agent>\`
- **Cross-version**: the failure also occurs on the previously installed 2.2.x build — earliest failure log entry is 2026-10-26 23:28, ~19h **before** the 2.3.0-beta.1 upgrade (2026-10-27 18:27). So this is not a 2.3 regression; it has persisted across at least two major versions.

## Symptom
`recall_history` fails on **every call** since at least 2026-10-26 (verified across 4 rotated log files, dozens of `recall_history failed` warnings per day), while the **write path works fine** (WAL file actively growing, session persistence OK).

Error:
```
OperationalError: unable to open database: file:\\?\C:\Users\<user>\.copaw\workspaces\orchestrator\history.db?mode=ro
```

## Root cause
1. `config.json` stores every agent's `workspace_dir` as a Windows extended-length path, e.g. `"\\\\?\\C:\\Users\\...\\workspaces\\default"`. This appears to be produced by the backend itself (likely `Path.resolve()` on Windows, which returns `\\?\`-prefixed form) — editing the config to a plain path is silently rewritten back to the `\\?\` form on restart (observed: 19 config entries + 19 agent.json files all reverted after manual fix + restart).
2. The recall tool builds a SQLite URI by concatenating this path verbatim: `file:\\?\C:\...history.db?mode=ro`. SQLite's URI parser cannot handle the `\\?\` prefix → `unable to open database`.
3. The write path uses a plain (non-URI) connection, where `\\?\` is a valid Windows path — hence "writes succeed, reads fail".

## Evidence (isolated repro, Python 3.14)
```python
import sqlite3
plain = r'C:\...\history.db'
ext   = r'\\?\C:\...\history.db'

sqlite3.connect('file:' + plain.replace('\\', '/') + '?mode=ro', uri=True)
# -> OK, PRAGMA quick_check returns "ok"  (DB itself is healthy, 740MB)

sqlite3.connect('file:\\\\?\\C:/.../history.db?mode=ro', uri=True)
# -> sqlite3.OperationalError: unable to open database file
```

## Suggested fix
Strip the extended-length prefix before building the URI, e.g.:
```python
path = str(path)
if path.startswith("\\\\?\\"):
    path = path[4:]
uri = "file:" + path.replace("\\", "/") + "?mode=ro"
```
(or normalize via `os.path.normpath` / avoid `Path.resolve()` when persisting `workspace_dir`).

## Impact
Cross-session raw-history recall is unavailable for all agents on Windows; agents silently degrade (workarounds via memory notes / external APIs). Not fatal — writes, sessions, and semantic memory search are unaffected — but it defeats the purpose of the durable history log.

issues.title: [Bug]: Hub Docker runtime fails to start with Permission denied on working/config.json when Hub runs as non-root
issues.body:
## QwenPaw Version

The deployed package version and Docker image tag/digest were not captured in the available report.

Source analysis below was checked against upstream commit [c26d31c0688aa9cce9bc1aef688177d2e14e25df](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/commit/c26d31c0688aa9cce9bc1aef688177d2e14e25df). This is the reviewed source revision, not a claim that the affected server runs that exact revision.

## Description

A QwenPaw Hub running as a regular Ubuntu user starts successfully, but starting an existing personal Docker runtime fails with:

```text
[Errno 13] Permission denied: '/data/qwenpaw/hub/runtimes/<runtime-id>/working/config.json'
```

The observed failure is a host-side access failure on a runtime's shared configuration. Source review suggests an ownership mismatch between the non-root Hub and the root application in the Docker image. Actual file ownership/mode and Docker user-namespace settings on the affected server have not yet been collected, so this cause still needs runtime verification.

**Security considerations:** A fix should preserve restrictive configuration/secret permissions and avoid requiring the Hub itself to run as root.

## Component(s) Affected

- [x] Core / Backend (Hub runtime lifecycle, configuration persistence)
- [x] Scripts / Deploy (Docker entrypoint and Supervisor)

## Environment

- **OS:** Ubuntu server; release not captured
- **Hub process user:** Non-root user `ubuntu`
- **Python:** 3.12, according to the installed-package log path
- **Install method:** Hub runs from a Python environment on the host; managed runtime uses the Docker backend
- **Docker image tag/digest, Engine version, rootless/userns mode:** Not captured

## Steps to Reproduce

Observed trigger:

1. Run the Hub as the regular `ubuntu` user with an existing personal Docker runtime.
2. Start the Hub with:

   ```bash
   qwenpaw hub \
     --host 0.0.0.0 \
     --port 8080 \
     --force-public \
     --config hub.yaml
   ```

3. A runtime start operation fails while accessing that runtime's `working/config.json`.

Suggested focused reproduction to verify the suspected cause (not yet independently executed):

1. Use a non-root Hub with a standard Linux Docker Engine and the current runtime image.
2. Initialize a Docker runtime, then cause the container application to save configuration in the bind-mounted working directory.
3. Record ownership and mode of `config.json` and `workspaces/*/agent.json`, then stop/start the runtime.
4. Check whether host-side configuration preparation fails after the container has written root-owned, owner-only files.

## Actual vs Expected

- **Actual:** The Hub HTTP server starts, but the personal runtime start operation fails with `EACCES` on its shared configuration.
- **Expected:** Runtime initialization and later configuration writes remain accessible to the Hub across runtime and Hub restarts, while keeping sensitive files private.

## Logs / Screenshots

Relevant output from the affected Ubuntu host; the runtime ID has been redacted:

```text
INFO:     Application startup complete.
INFO:     Uvicorn running on http://0.0.0.0:8080 (Press CTRL+C to quit)
WARNING lib/python3.12/site-packages/qwenpaw/hub/service.py:531 | 2026-10-30 20:37:56 | Runtime <runtime-id> start operation failed: [Errno 13] Permission denied: '/data/qwenpaw/hub/runtimes/<runtime-id>/working/config.json'
```

## Additional Notes

### Source evidence and suspected failure mechanism

All links below refer to the same upstream revision, `c26d31c0688aa9cce9bc1aef688177d2e14e25df`:

- [DockerRuntimeProvisioner.start](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/c26d31c0688aa9cce9bc1aef688177d2e14e25df/src/qwenpaw/hub/docker_provisioner.py#L219-L245) creates read/write bind mounts for working, secrets, and backups without specifying a container user.
- [entrypoint.sh](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/c26d31c0688aa9cce9bc1aef688177d2e14e25df/deploy/entrypoint.sh) runs `qwenpaw init` before starting Supervisor, without dropping privileges.
- [Supervisor configuration](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/c26d31c0688aa9cce9bc1aef688177d2e14e25df/deploy/config/supervisord.conf.template) sets `[supervisord] user=root`; the application has no separate `user=`.
- [RuntimeService._start_locked](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/c26d31c0688aa9cce9bc1aef688177d2e14e25df/src/qwenpaw/hub/service.py#L266-L270) calls `prepare_workspace_paths` before `provisioner.start`.
- [prepare_workspace_paths](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/c26d31c0688aa9cce9bc1aef688177d2e14e25df/src/qwenpaw/hub/runtime_paths.py#L58-L68) reads `config.json` and workspace `agent.json` files on the host.
- [write_text_atomic](https://github.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/blob/c26d31c0688aa9cce9bc1aef688177d2e14e25df/src/qwenpaw/utils/io_utils.py#L280-L320) defaults new internal files to `0600` and uses a sibling temporary file plus `os.replace`. Existing permission bits are preserved, but ownership is not explicitly preserved. A root writer can therefore replace a Hub-owned configuration with a root-owned inode.

### Possible fix direction

Align the host-visible identity used for runtime initialization and subsequent application writes with the Hub's shared-data access requirements.

Simply adding a hard-coded `user="1000:1000"` to the provisioner is insufficient for the current image: Supervisor configuration generation, logs/PID/socket paths, system D-Bus, and desktop processes also need appropriate handling. A smaller approach could retain a privileged bootstrap/Supervisor while dropping initialization and application processes to the intended identity, with explicit HOME/environment setup.

Rootless Docker, userns-remap, and Docker Desktop require platform-aware identity handling rather than blindly copying the host UID/GID.

Existing root-owned data also needs a controlled one-time ownership migration while the affected runtime is stopped. Changing the image alone will not repair a file the Hub cannot read before container startup.

### Workaround and validation status

A targeted ownership repair on the affected instance has been suggested, but success has not yet been confirmed. No deployed code fix or independent reproduction is claimed here.

Useful regression coverage would include first initialization, subsequent application configuration writes, runtime stop/start, Hub restart, and continued Hub access to configuration without weakening file permissions.

### Duplicate search

Searched open and closed issues for Hub/config.json permission failures, Docker permissions, UID, and Hub root ownership. #7612 concerns CLI authentication inside local sandboxes and appears to be a different issue.

issues.title: `run_code` is invoked with empty arguments on custom OpenAI-compatible providers (`'code' is a required property`)
issues.body:
## Summary

When agent `default` runs on a **user-defined OpenAI-compatible provider** (`kimi`, `kimi-codingplan`) with model `k3.1-pro`, **every** `run_code` tool call is emitted with an empty arguments object `{}` and is rejected at the execution entry point:

```
Input validation failed for tool 'run_code': 'code' is a required property (at $)
```

Python never executes — the call fails before the interpreter starts. Switching **only the provider** to a built-in one on the same session, same agent, same tool set works immediately.

## Environment

- QwenPaw Desktop, package metadata reports `qwenpaw` **2.3.0b2** (`_internal/qwenpaw.egg-info/PKG-INFO`)
- Windows 10 (AMD64), single local user
- Agent `default`; build log reports `tools=1`
- Affected providers: custom provider `kimi` (model `k3.1-pro`), provider `kimi-codingplan` (model `k3.1-pro`)
- Control (unaffected) providers: built-in `dashscope` (models `kimi-k3`, `kimi-k3.1-pro`), built-in `deepseek` (`deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp`)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a custom OpenAI-compatible provider (e.g. `kimi`) pointing at a Kimi endpoint serving `k3.1-pro`.
2. Select it as the model of agent `default`.
3. Ask the agent to perform any action that requires `run_code` (e.g. "run this Python snippet").
4. Observe: a `run_code` tool-call card appears in the UI (so the call *is* emitted), but the call is rejected with the message above. Every retry reproduces it identically.

## Evidence

### A. 22 occurrences, all on the non-built-in providers

From `desktop.log`, the exact string `Input validation failed for tool 'run_code': 'code' is a required property (at $)` occurs **22 times** between `13:57:05` and `14:29:32` local time (same day):

| time | session | provider/model |
|---|---|---|
| 13:57:05 – 14:01:54 (13x), 14:07:54 (1x) | `1793896025942-navdv2q` | `kimi/k3.1-pro` |
| 14:24:37, 14:24:48, 14:24:56, 14:25:08 (4x) | `1793945790243-fkjq6d5` | `kimi/k3.1-pro` |
| 14:29:09, 14:29:18, 14:29:32 (3x) | `1793944680105-15238vw` | `kimi/k3.1-pro` |

(The file contains one duplicated marker at the end of the log; occurrence count above excludes the duplicate.)

### B. Controlled comparison — same session, only the provider changed

From `qwenpaw.log`, agent build records for one and the same session:

```
14:16:30  built agent session=1793945790243-fkjq6d5 agent=default model=dashscope/kimi-k3                   tools=1
14:20:28  built agent session=1793945790243-fkjq6d5 agent=default model=dashscope/kimi-k3.1-pro             tools=1
14:24:19  built agent session=1793945790243-fkjq6d5 agent=default model=kimi/k3.1-pro                       tools=1
14:31:39  built agent session=1793945790243-fkjq6d5 agent=default model=deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp tools=1
```

And the `run_code` outcomes on that same session:

| provider | `run_code` outcome |
|---|---|
| `dashscope/kimi-k3` | executed Python, produced output |
| `dashscope/kimi-k3.1-pro` | executed Python, produced output |
| `kimi/k3.1-pro` (custom) | 4x empty-arguments rejection |
| `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp` | executed Python, produced output |

This is the key point: **the same model family (`k3.1-pro`) works when served through a built-in provider and fails when served through a custom OpenAI-compatible provider.** That argues against "the model cannot emit tool arguments".

### C. Provider identity

`desktop.log` records the custom provider lifecycle:

```
POST   /api/models/custom-providers               201 Created
DELETE /api/models/custom-providers/kimi          200 OK   (14:34:02)
```

## Analysis (hypothesis — not yet proven)

The most plausible mechanism is that the `code` property is missing or stripped from the tool definition that reaches the model, so the model correctly emits an empty arguments object for what it believes is a zero-parameter function.

**What we could NOT verify** (stated explicitly to avoid over-claiming):

1. We do not have the outgoing request body / tool JSON Schema — QwenPaw logs record the tool-call outcome but not the request payload. We therefore **cannot** tell whether the schema is already wrong when rendered by QwenPaw, or gets lost inside the custom-provider adapter hop.
2. The build-log counter `tools=1` (agent `default`) vs `tools=13` (another agent on the same build) — the meaning of this counter is unverified; we list it only as a lead.
3. We did not capture a raw provider response showing what the model claimed to receive.

## Impact

- Any agent that depends on tools can be **functionally crippled** on a custom OpenAI-compatible provider, while the UI still shows a tool-call card — so it looks like the tool was "sent" and silently failed.
- The failure message (`'code' is a required property`) points at the tool contract, not at the provider configuration, so users are likely to conclude "this model can't call tools" and switch models instead of reporting a platform defect.
- Cost: repeated retries burn tokens; in our case 22 failed calls before the custom provider was removed.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Normalize and pre-flight the tool schema** on the adapter hop: assert that every function named in the outgoing request has a non-empty `parameters.properties` map containing its required keys; if not, fail loudly *with the provider name* instead of letting the model produce `{}`.
2. **Distinguish this failure class**: when a tool call arrives with an empty arguments object for a tool that has required parameters, emit a diagnostic such as `provider returned empty arguments — tool schema may have been lost in the adapter` rather than a generic schema-validation error.
3. **Debug-level logging of the outgoing `tools` payload structure** (names + parameter keys, redacted) so this class of bug is diagnosable from logs alone.

## Notes

- Happy to provide a minimal reproduction config or a request-level capture if maintainers want one.
- We are **not** claiming this affects built-in providers — in our environment they are unaffected.
- We are also not claiming the custom provider's endpoint itself is faulty; the same model works through a built-in provider.

prs.title: fix(tools): decode GBK/CP936 in read/edit/grep instead of dropping bytes
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`read_file_safe` (used by `read_file` / `edit_file`) and `grep_search` decoded files as UTF-8 with `errors="ignore"`. On Chinese Windows, Notepad/legacy `.txt` / `.csv` / `.md` notes are often GBK/CP936. Every non-UTF-8 byte was deleted with no log line, so:

- `read_file` returned ASCII leftovers (e.g. `姓名: 张三` → `: `)
- `grep_search` for Chinese terms missed the file
- `edit_file` could still report success and persist the damaged snapshot as UTF-8

Markdown/skill loaders already use `decode_text_bytes_with_encoding_fallback` (utf-8 → gbk/cp936 → …). This PR routes the tool read path through the same helper.

## Changes

- `src/qwenpaw/agents/tools/utils.py`: `_read_file_safe_sync` uses the shared encoding fallback
- `src/qwenpaw/agents/tools/file_search.py`: `_walk_and_grep` reads bytes and decodes with the same fallback (files already capped at 2MB)
- Regression tests for GBK read, GBK `edit_file`, and GBK grep

## How to reproduce (before)

```python
from pathlib import Path
path = Path("note.txt")
```

## Description

Automatic memory recall was represented as an assistant-authored thinking/tool-call/tool-result sequence. Models could imitate that synthetic trajectory and call `memory_search` again in the same turn.

prs.title: fix(ollama): size context window from num_ctx instead of 128k default
prs.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Ollama already opts out of the static cloud context catalog (`_context_catalog_enabled → False`), which is correct: a local `qwen3-coder:30b` truncates at `num_ctx`, not at the family's cloud window.

But discovery never filled that gap. `fetch_models` reused the OpenAI `/v1/models` parser, whose rows do not carry `context_length` / `num_ctx`, so every Ollama model stayed at the **128k placeholder**. Compaction then compared against `0.8 × 131072` while the server often serves a few thousand to a few tens of thousands of tokens.

This is **independent of #7979** (and of open PR #7986):

| | #7979 / #7986 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Provider | custom / llama.cpp OpenAI-compatible | built-in **Ollama** |
| Failure mode | cloud catalog matches alias → **1M** | catalog already skipped → **128k default** |
| Fix | skip pattern catalog for custom endpoints | read native Ollama context into `max_input_length_auto_detected` |

A fix for #7979 does not call `/api/show` or `/api/ps`, and does not change Ollama.

## Changes

`OllamaProvider.fetch_models` lists models with `/v1/models`, then sets `max_input_length_auto_detected` from native Ollama signals. Precedence:

1. `GET /api/ps` served `context_length` when the model is loaded (reflects `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH` and the load-time window). A hit skips `/api/show`.
2. Modelfile `num_ctx` from a successful `POST /api/show`.
3. If neither is available, leave the value unset (do **not** invent a 4096 or other fallback). The 128k default remains until a later successful probe reports a real window.

GGUF `*.context_length` is **not** used. That field is the model's maximum supported context, not the window Ollama is serving.

Failed native probes (`None`, 401, 403, timeout, or an invalid payload) leave the model **unchanged**, so merge keeps any previous auto-detected window. A successful `/api/show` that omits `num_ctx` clears a stale auto-detected value **only when `/api/ps` also succeeded** (and reported no served window). A failed `/api/ps` followed by an unknown show does not clear. Non-string `parameters` are treated as malformed (retain the old value), not as “successful but unknown”.

`check_model_connection` uses the lightweight `/v1/models` list (`super().fetch_models`). It only checks that the model id exists and does not call `/api/show` per model.

Native `/api/ps` and `/api/show` probes reuse `_build_default_headers()` and add `Authorization: Bearer` when an API key is set and Authorization is not already configured. Explicit user `max_input_length` still wins over auto-detection, and the cloud catalog stays disabled for Ollama. `ModelInfo.max_input_length_auto_detected` allows `ge=1` so a small explicit `num_ctx` (for example 512) is kept.

Model id aliases parse the tag only in the final path segment, so `registry.example.com:5000/team/qwen3` still matches `/api/ps` rows tagged `:latest`.

## Testing

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest \
  tests/unit/providers/test_ollama_provider.py \
  tests/unit/providers/test_context_windows.py -q
# 101 passed
```

`black --line-length=79` is clean on the touched files.

Coverage includes precedence (served `/api/ps` → Modelfile `num_ctx` → unset when unknown), GGUF `*.context_length` ignored, 401/403 and timeout on `/api/show` leaving `max_input_length_auto_detected` unset, failed `/api/ps` + unknown show retaining a prior window, malformed `parameters` retaining a prior window, registry:port `:latest` alias matching, `check_model_connection` not calling `/api/show`, authenticated native probes, the catalog still skipped without detection, and explicit `max_input_length` still winning over auto-detected values.

prs.title: feat(memory): add reranker model center with service test, multi-query precision history and auto-verify
prs.body:
## Description

**What this PR does:** Adds a reranker model center to the reranker settings (Runtime Config → Memory & Retrieval), mirroring the existing Embedding model center, and upgrades the ranking-precision verification from a single binary smoke test into a multi-query, persisted, and optionally scheduled metric.

**Why:** A misconfigured reranker is currently invisible until retrieval quality degrades. The new center surfaces configuration status, current model, service verification (connectivity + latency) and a meaningful ranking-precision figure (`correct/total`, 10-run rolling average, sparkline) so a bad model is visible at a glance and its trend can be tracked across restarts.

The overview shows four slots: configuration status, current model, service verification and ranking precision.

### Changes

- **Reranker model center**: `RerankerModelCenter` overview on the same 4-column grid and status styles as the embedding card; session-scoped `rerankerVerificationStore` keyed by agent + service fingerprint, invalidated when the service config changes or the agent switches.
- **Service verification**: `POST /workspace/reranker/test` sends a real rerank request with sample documents (one clearly relevant plus two distractors) and returns latency, relevance scores mapped back to request order, and whether the expected most-relevant document ranked first. The outbound call runs under a hard `asyncio.wait_for` deadline, upstream HTML error pages are stripped to plain text, and the API key is masked in returned messages.
- **Multi-query precision**: runs a 5-case multi-domain suite (password / checkout / unit conversion / planet / subscription) and reports `total`, `correct_count`, `precision` and per-case `scores`/`correct`, instead of a single boolean.
- **Persistent history**: new `reranker_history.py` appends each verification to `WORKING_DIR/reranker_history.json`, keyed by a service fingerprint; new endpoint `GET /workspace/reranker/history?fingerprint=`.
- **Trend UI**: the precision slot shows `correct/total = NN%`, a 10-run rolling average and a mini SVG sparkline; history survives restarts and refreshes.
- **Scheduled auto-verification**: `RerankerConfig.auto_verify_interval_hours` (0 = off) plus a background sweep task in the app lifespan that probes due services.
- **i18n**: strings for the overview, verification and precision slots across all 7 locales.

prs.title: fix(providers): keep boolean additionalProperties in tool schemas
prs.body:
## Description

`_sanitize_boolean_schemas` expands every boolean schema value into a nested `not` schema, including keyword values such as `additionalProperties`. A tool schema that declares

```json
"additionalProperties": false
```

was therefore sent as

```json
"additionalProperties": {"not": {}}
```

`false` is the native JSON Schema keyword spelling and the form OpenAI strict-mode tool definitions use. `{"not": {}}` is semantically equivalent, but several OpenAI-compatible servers do not implement `not`: they either reject the schema or silently drop the surrounding `properties` map. When the parameter map is lost the model sees a zero-parameter function and returns `{}`, so a tool whose schema has required properties fails validation before it runs (see #8603, where `run_code` fails on custom OpenAI-compatible providers while the same model works through a built-in provider that only applies the nullable pass).

This change keeps the native boolean spelling for the `additional*` / `unevaluated*` keywords and still converts standalone boolean schemas at positions where an object schema is expected.

## Evidence

Sanitizing the `run_code` tool schema (`{"properties": {"code": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["code"], "additionalProperties": false}`):

prs.title: fix(providers): reject out-of-range model config values on the write path
prs.body:
Fixes #8549

## What Problem This Solves

`ModelInfo` declares `thinking_budget >= 1` and `max_input_length >= 1000`, but the write path never enforced those bounds: `Provider.update_model_config` assigned `int(...)` results directly (Pydantic does not validate plain attribute assignment), and `ModelConfigRequest.thinking_budget` was the only numeric field in its model without a bound. An invalid value was accepted and persisted, then failed re-validation on every read — after a restart `load_provider` returned `None` and the provider silently disappeared.

## What changed

- `app/routers/providers.py`: add `ge=1` to `ModelConfigRequest.thinking_budget`, matching the existing `ge=1000` on `max_input_length`.
- `providers/provider.py`: `update_model_config` now raises `ValueError` for `thinking_budget < 1` and `max_input_length < 1000` before assigning, consistent with the existing `model_type` / `supports_*` validation in the same method.
- `providers/model_info.py`: `thinking_budget_range` gains a model validator requiring a complete, ordered `[min, max]` pair (mirroring `ThinkingControl` in `providers/thinking.py`); previously `[8000]` constructed fine and `thinking_control()` crashed unpacking it.

## Evidence

New regression tests (10):

- `tests/unit/providers/test_provider_config_validation.py` — `thinking_budget` of -5 / 0 and `max_input_length` of 500 are rejected and not stored; valid values round-trip and clearing with `None` still works; `thinking_budget_range` of length 1 / 3 or `low > high` is rejected, an ordered pair still drives `thinking_control`.
- `tests/unit/app/routers/test_provider_config_request_validation.py` — `ModelConfigRequest(thinking_budget=-5 / 0)` fails request validation, `1` is accepted.

Red/green: with the fix reverted, the 8 rejection tests fail (the 2 valid-value guards pass both ways); with the fix, all 10 pass. The reproduction script that previously showed `update_model_config(..., -5)` returning `True` and poisoning reads now raises `ValueError: thinking_budget must be at least 1` at write time.

Broader subset `tests/unit/providers/` + the provider router tests: 1008 passed; the single failure (`test_typesafe_evaluation.py::test_as_model_injects_same_instance_and_preserves_host_headers`) fails identically on the unmodified baseline in this environment because the optional `reme` package is not installed.
