prs.title: fix(gateway): limit and cap OIDC bearer verification on the config route group
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - The config/onboarding route group verified every OIDC bearer with nothing in front of it: no attempt ledger and no cap on verifications in flight, while with `validation = "introspection"` each verification is an authenticated round trip to the identity provider under the daemon's own client credentials. Anyone who could reach the gateway could make it call the provider once per request, get the daemon's client throttled there, and, through session re-verification, end every dashboard session.
  - `config_route_auth` now takes a `ConfigRouteAuth` state carrying `BearerVerificationLimits`: a per-client attempt ledger (the shared thresholds: 10 refused credentials in a minute, then a 5-minute lockout, loopback exempt) on a ledger of its own, and a process-wide 16-permit cap on verifications in flight, held for the verification alone and refused (503, `Retry-After: 5`) rather than queued, loopback included.
  - Only `AUTH_REQUIRED` denials are booked. A `FORBIDDEN` denial is a verified identity the policy grants nothing, or the provider unreachable, throttling or misconfigured; neither says anything about the caller.
  - The client key is `client_key_from_request`, the same derivation every other rate-limited gateway surface uses, so this composes with #12114 unchanged.
  - Docs: the limits are recorded in `security/authentication.md` beside the route-layer description, and `auth_rate_limit.rs` names the three ledgers built from it.
- **Scope boundary:** The config route group's OIDC bearer path only. Not changed: the native pairing-bearer branch (its legacy 401 shape stays byte-for-byte), the enrollment relay and its own three limits, dashboard session classification and re-verification (#12096), the pending-flow store (#12049), forwarded-header keying (#12114), any runtime crate. No negative token cache (recorded as a follow-up option on the issue).
- **Blast radius:** Scripted clients that present an OIDC bearer per request to `/api/config/*`, `/api/quickstart/*`, `/api/channels/bind`: a client refused ten times in a minute gets 429 for five minutes; more than 16 verifications in flight at once get 503 with `Retry-After: 5`. Valid tokens are never booked. Native bearers and dashboard sessions see no change. Test constructors that build the route group now pass a `ConfigRouteAuth`.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12047. Related #8289, #12052, #12096.

### What this does, simply

When a client sends the gateway an OIDC token, the gateway checks it, and in one common setup that check is a network call to the identity provider using the daemon's own client secret. Pairing, webhooks and the browser sign-in relay all limit how often one client can make the gateway do that kind of work; the token check did not. A remote client could send junk tokens in a loop, every one costing a call to the provider, until the provider throttled or locked the daemon's client, at which point every real OIDC user was refused and every signed-in dashboard user was signed out at their next check.

Now a client whose tokens keep being refused is locked out for five minutes after ten refusals in a minute, on a ledger of its own so a stale-token loop never locks anyone out of pairing, and at most sixteen token checks are in flight at once across all clients, so a burst cannot hold many connections to the provider. A provider outage is not held against the caller, and a valid token is never counted. Dashboard sessions are checked by their own layer and never wait behind these limits.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes: an A/B against a provider with `validation = "introspection"` makes the delta visible in the provider's own logs.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=web`, the gateway's config route group over HTTP. No messaging channel.
- **Setup / preconditions:** One `[oidc.<alias>]` with `validation = "introspection"` and a reachable introspection endpoint; the gateway listening beyond loopback.
- **Steps to run:** From a remote host, send 12 requests of `GET /api/config/list` with `Authorization: Bearer junk` and `X-ZeroClaw-Auth-Provider: oidc.<alias>`. Then, from 17 addresses at once (or 17 concurrent connections behind a proxy with `trust_forwarded_headers` off), send the same request while the provider is slow to answer.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The first 10 return 401 and show as 10 introspection calls at the provider; the 11th and 12th return 429 with `Retry-After: 300` and produce no provider call. Of the 17 concurrent ones, 16 reach the provider and one returns 503 with `Retry-After: 5`.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** All 12 return 401 and all 12 reach the provider; all 17 concurrent requests reach it, and the loop can continue at any rate.

### How I tested

#### Current fixture validation (2026-11-04)

Revision `462c8f38eca5158193b36fe18f9a6201d1241060`, tree `01f4f9ac2747973b514cdde47099a6c379118bf9`; macOS ARM64 / Rust 1.97.1.

The live forwarded-header test started its true-to-false case with a forwarded loopback address. #12114 correctly bills that request to its remote peer, so the first request already consumes one of the ten attempts; the test then expects an extra allowed request. I reproduced the combined failure at attempt 9 (429 instead of 401). The fixture now starts with a different non-loopback forwarded address, then confirms that publishing the opposite trust setting bills the peer’s fresh ledger. All assertions remain, including both policy directions and the provider-call count. Production behavior is unchanged.

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
# passed on 462c8f38eca5158193b36fe18f9a6201d1241060
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib
# 784 passed on 462c8f38eca5158193b36fe18f9a6201d1241060
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets -- -D warnings
# passed on 462c8f38eca5158193b36fe18f9a6201d1241060

# Temporary local combination with #12114 at 16a4015b010e3638295d5a289e43885db9ad90b3:
git merge --no-commit --no-ff 16a4015b010e3638295d5a289e43885db9ad90b3
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib
# 788 passed, combined tree 479d12a6fe6b279e7310e4e6666de585db279b4b
git merge --abort
# restored the clean candidate; no dependency merge is published
```

The original fixture was also run in an unmodified `3c1c664ca2b8d88fa78ee830e9b658194f7831ec` plus #12114 combination with `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib principal_gate::tests::bearer_client_keys_follow_persisted_forwarded_header_trust -- --exact`: it failed with the expected 429/401 mismatch. The repaired combined suite passes. The final change and evidence were independently checked. Apple’s large `__eh_frame` linker warning appeared during tests; tests and strict Clippy passed.

**Remaining validation:** Full-workspace tests, native Windows execution, and a real identity-provider/reverse-proxy run were not performed in this fixture-only repair. The HTTP regressions use the real route group and mock provider. Hosted CI and required human review must run on the new head. #12114 still needs its own review and landing; this test fix does not deliver its proxy behavior.

Hosted validation update (2026-11-05T04:55:43.427584+00:00): the [required CI gate](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41969394376/job/127057541060) passed, with 52 successful checks, eight skipped and no failures or pending checks. The [Linux workspace job](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41969394376/job/127053849403) passed `cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop`: 20,066 passed and 43 skipped (one slow, two leaky), including the repaired regression. CI tested merge `0bf2242631a25a61475df8076c9b449a5234a590` / tree `dc1888086aa8b40b8df098194f23fb82c2690269` with master `65f8eb3c9284e396d9de7872c3df6dba993b7093`; this includes two master advances beyond the published candidate and is not a whole-tree match. The repaired `principal_gate.rs` is byte-identical. Native Windows bearer-test execution, a real provider/proxy run, #12114 landing, and required human review remain separate gates.

#### Earlier validation at `f0a3d81`

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Lint` (fmt, clippy `-D warnings`) and `Test` cover the gateway crate, where every changed line lives; `Docs Style` covers the changed Markdown.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No live-provider run; the provider is a wiremock in every test. The 2-second delayed-introspection test depends on wall-clock timing within one process and is sized with ample margin.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```text
cargo fmt --all -- --check
exit 0
cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --all-targets -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized] target(s) in 26.26s
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib principal_gate::
test result: ok. 29 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 752 filtered out; finished in 5.19s
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib -- api_pairing:: api_oidc:: dashboard_session::
test result: ok. 117 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 664 filtered out; finished in 43.14s
cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway
test result: FAILED. 780 passed; 1 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 78.97s
  # the one failure, api_config::tests::unreadable_existing_config_survives_failed_save_rollback,
  # chmods a file to 0o000 and expects the read to fail; the build box runs as root, and the
  # same test fails identically on unpatched master there (git stash; rerun; stash pop)
DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/security/authentication.md scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
Summary: 0 error(s)
DOCS_FILES=docs/book/src/security/authentication.md scripts/ci/docs_links_gate.sh
No added links detected in changed docs lines.

# Negative controls, each restored afterwards:
# 1. `record_attempt` call removed:
test principal_gate::tests::ten_failed_bearers_lock_the_client_out ... FAILED   (left: 401, right: 429)
test principal_gate::tests::forwarded_headers_key_the_ledger_when_trusted ... FAILED   (left: 401, right: 429)
# 2. permit bound at function scope so it outlives `next.run`:
test principal_gate::tests::the_permit_is_held_only_for_the_verification ... FAILED
  assertion `left == right` failed: every permit was released before its handler ran  (left: 0, right: 16)
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source-traced that the permit scope ends before `method_floor` and `next.run`; that the dashboard-session branch runs before the bearer branch and touches neither limit; that `authenticate_native` is untouched. Not verified: a real identity provider, or a reverse proxy.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A — no user-visible interface state changed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `f0a3d81` on `fix/12047-bearer-verification-limits` (master `683d101`), Rust 1.97.0 on Linux x86_64 with 2 cores; gateway unit tests over the real route group with a wiremock identity provider.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** The full workspace `cargo test` was not run; the change is confined to `zeroclaw-gateway`, whose complete test target was run.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? (`No`)
- New external network calls? (`No`)
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? (`No`) — the ledger stores client keys and timestamps, never tokens.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? (`No`) — test addresses are RFC 5737 documentation ranges.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? (`No`)

## Compatibility (required)

prs.title: fix(gateway): key rate limits on the proxy-appended XFF hop
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - `forwarded_client_ip` now prefers the rightmost parseable non-loopback `X-Forwarded-For` entry instead of the leftmost client-supplied value. It decodes each hop separately so an opaque prefix cannot hide the proxy-appended suffix.
  - For a loopback-only forwarded value, `client_key_from_request` uses a non-loopback peer or the non-exempt `unknown` key, so remote clients cannot inherit a loopback peer's limiter exemption.
  - Docs note the nginx directives operators should use and the loopback-forwarded behavior.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not add a trusted-proxy CIDR list or change limiter thresholds; only how the client key is derived when `trust_forwarded_headers` is on.
- **Blast radius:** Pairing lockout, webhook auth limits, and OIDC enrollment per-client budgets that key through `client_key_from_request`.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #12052

### What this does, simply

When the gateway sits behind a reverse proxy with `trust_forwarded_headers`, it used the first address in `X-Forwarded-For`. Most proxies append the real client after any client-supplied value, so a remote caller could put `127.0.0.1` first and skip pairing lockouts and enrollment budgets. This PR takes the rightmost usable non-loopback address, and never treats a forwarded loopback value as the local exemption.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A — covered by focused unit tests; no user-visible UI change.

- **Setup / preconditions:** N/A
- **Steps to run:** N/A
- **Expected on this branch (after):** N/A
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** N/A

- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Full pairing integration against a real appending proxy not run locally

```sh
# client_key_ignores_spoofed_loopback_forwarded_header ... ok
# client_key_falls_back_to_peer_when_forwarded_header_invalid ... ok
# test result: ok. 4 passed
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Source review of callers of `client_key_from_request`; did not spin a live nginx proxy.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A — no user-visible interface state changed

- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** see command output above

## Compatibility (required)

prs.title: feat(web): add paired-device voice settings and chat controls
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- Add opt-in dictation and speech playback controls to web chat, with a localized usage guide in Config → Other → Browser Voice and Audio.
- Store voice preferences on the existing paired-device record in the gateway's SQLite registry. The chat resolves its own device through the authenticated paired token. Config lists paired devices so operators can load and save preferences for the selected device. Select or preview installed voices in that browser itself. No voice preferences are persisted in browser storage or HTTP caches.
- Default dictation to on-device processing, require explicit download of missing language packs, and expose browser-service processing only as an explicit choice. The speaker supports one-time, stopped, and continuous reading with a temporary per-chat override.
- **Scope boundary:** Browser speech APIs and paired-device preferences only. No server STT/TTS provider, agent configuration schema, pairing lifecycle, or audio upload endpoint is added.
- **Blast radius:** Web Config/chat, device-registry schema migration, and gateway Permissions Policy. Microphone and on-device recognition become permitted for the same origin; user microphone permission is still required.
- **Linked issue(s):** None.

### What this does, simply

A paired browser can enable a microphone and speaker next to the chat composer. Dictation fills the draft without sending it. Clicking the speaker reads the latest assistant reply; another click stops it. Holding the speaker enables continuous reading of new completed replies, and a short click disables it even if the saved automatic default is enabled. Shift+Enter provides a keyboard equivalent.

Preferences are saved by ZeroClaw for that paired device and survive reloads and daemon restarts. This uses the existing device identity rather than introducing a client-chosen browser ID. A new pairing receives its own defaults. Settings refresh across tabs of the same device, and automatic reading skips restored chat history. Config includes instructions explaining setup, exactly where to click, all speaker states, local versus online processing, permissions, and preference storage.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=web`, web chat.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Pair a browser with a gateway built from this branch; use HTTPS or localhost. Voice availability depends on browser/OS support. Select an available voice before testing playback.
- **Steps to run:**
  1. Open Config → Other → Browser Voice and Audio → How to use dictation and reading. Enable microphone/speaker, select language and voice, then use Test voice.
  2. Reload Config: selections remain. Pair a second independent browser: its settings start disabled. Use the device list to switch between the two records and verify that each keeps its own settings. Inspect browser storage: this feature adds no preference key.
  3. Open an agent chat. Click the microphone, grant permission, dictate, and confirm the text enters the draft without being submitted. Click again to stop.
  4. Click the speaker to read the latest reply, and click again to stop. Hold to highlight continuous mode, receive a new completed reply, then click once to turn it off. Repeat with Shift+Enter.
  5. Switch conversation or hide the chat/tab during capture/playback. Confirm it stops and stale recognition results do not populate the new conversation. Reloading history must not read it aloud.
  6. Try unavailable local recognition: it must not fall back to a remote service. Browser-service mode requires explicitly selecting that mode. Revoke the device: its preference API must refuse access.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Documented opt-in voice controls and isolated, durable paired-device preferences.
- **Prior behavior on master (before):** These settings, help, device-preference routes and chat controls are absent; Permissions Policy blocks microphone access.

### How I tested

![Paired-device selector](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/6338a726b3297bd18fa3d3a3cc06f5b6a7d109ae/.pr-evidence/web-voice-devices-other-desktop.png)

- **CI checks relied on and why:** Local focused checks below; GitHub CI results will be reported by the PR checks. The master base now supplies vodozemac 0.11.2, including the upstream secret-zeroization fixes. Local cargo deny check and the hosted Security check pass.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** Real microphone hardware, actual OS speech output, language-pack installation, and browser-provider network behavior require reviewer/device testing. Automated UI checks use synthetic speech APIs and gateway responses.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  - `cargo web check`: generated the API TypeScript from this source and completed `npx tsc -b`.
  - `npm run build`: production bundle built successfully (existing large-chunk warnings remain).
  - `npm test`: completed successfully, including chat/session regressions and the 16 voice tests.
  - `npm run test:auth`: completed successfully, including paired/OIDC flows and read-only Config.
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib api_pairing::tests --no-default-features`: `14 passed; 0 failed`.
  - `cargo test -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib security_headers::tests --no-default-features`: `5 passed; 0 failed`.
  - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and `git diff --check`: clean.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Automated interaction with the actual WebUI in installed Chrome at desktop and mobile sizes using synthetic data: settings writes/reload, no voice preference storage keys, voice sample, held speaker/highlight, short-click disable, and dictation into the draft. No page errors. Reviewed the English and Portuguese guide screenshots. This did not exercise real microphone capture or real voice output.
- **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshots of the actual WebUI, with synthetic data only.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `6338a726b3297bd18fa3d3a3cc06f5b6a7d109ae`, web, `.pr-evidence/web-voice-*.png`; desktop 1440×1050 and mobile 390×844.
- **Screenshot evidence:**

![Config and voice settings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/6338a726b3297bd18fa3d3a3cc06f5b6a7d109ae/.pr-evidence/web-voice-settings-desktop.png)

![Integrated usage guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/6338a726b3297bd18fa3d3a3cc06f5b6a7d109ae/.pr-evidence/web-voice-guide-desktop.png)

![Mobile chat controls](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/6338a726b3297bd18fa3d3a3cc06f5b6a7d109ae/.pr-evidence/web-voice-chat-mobile.png)

[Mobile settings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/6338a726b3297bd18fa3d3a3cc06f5b6a7d109ae/.pr-evidence/web-voice-settings-mobile.png) · [Desktop chat, continuous enabled](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/6338a726b3297bd18fa3d3a3cc06f5b6a7d109ae/.pr-evidence/web-voice-chat-desktop.png) · [Portuguese usage guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CastelloBrancoTecnologia/zeroclaw/6338a726b3297bd18fa3d3a3cc06f5b6a7d109ae/.pr-evidence/web-voice-guide-pt.png)

- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Enabling controls saved three preference writes; reloading recovered server-side choices; holding highlighted the speaker; clicking disabled it; final dictation entered the draft without sending; browser voice preference keys remained empty.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No full-workspace Rust suite or workspace-wide clippy; gateway tests and the canonical WebUI check cover the changed modules. Real speech-engine behavior remains the device-testing gap described above.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes.** Same-origin microphone/on-device recognition is allowed by Permissions Policy. Both voice features default disabled, and microphone use requires a user action and browser consent.
- New external network calls? **Yes, opt-in.** Downloading local language packs uses the browser implementation; explicitly selected browser recognition or an online synthesis voice may contact its provider. Local recognition never silently falls back online, and online choices are labeled. The gateway receives no microphone audio.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes.** New own-device routes resolve the existing paired bearer token under a held live pairing guard, without accepting arbitrary device IDs. The own-device route requires the paired bearer. Managing other devices uses the existing operator authorization for listing and revoking devices. No bearer is returned or logged.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.** All fixture and screenshot content is synthetic.
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No.** Dictated text follows the existing user draft/send path.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **HTTP/config: yes.** The database adds a nullable column and existing devices receive disabled defaults. Rust callers of DeviceRegistry::new now handle its Result, because initialization and migration failures propagate.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes:** new device-scoped web preferences and `GET/PUT /api/devices/me/voice` and `GET/PUT /api/devices/{id}/voice`; no TOML/env/CLI keys.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**
- **Upgrade steps:** None beyond building the matching gateway/WebUI. Enable voice explicitly in Config. Cookie-only OIDC sessions have no paired-device identity and see an explanation instead of editable device voice preferences.

## Rollback

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert 6338a726b3297bd18fa3d3a3cc06f5b6a7d109ae` and rebuild/restart the gateway. The extra nullable database column can remain; the previous binary ignores it.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** Disable microphone, speaker and automatic reading in Voice and audio.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** WebUI save/capture/playback errors, `Failed to persist device voice preferences` / `Failed to read device voice preferences` logs, or a paired-device preference API refusal. Browser support issues are surfaced without automatic remote fallback.



### Voice localization

All 55 browser voice/audio strings, including device selection, the usage guide, privacy notices and errors, have translations in English, Simplified Chinese, Portuguese, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Russian, Japanese and Arabic. Existing locale codes and the English fallback for other locales are preserved.

Validated complete key coverage with no duplicate voice keys, rendered the settings and guide in all ten locales, and passed typecheck, 16 voice tests and the production build. These checks validate coverage and rendering. Native-speaker editorial review is welcome.

### Review follow-up

Continuous reading preserves waiting assistant replies in arrival order and only marks a reply consumed once playback starts. A regression queues two replies while another is speaking, checks ordered playback and excludes history-trim notices. The branch is rebased onto master at b98b67bed4e0316d298e112d8b9187d50bc84f16, which already supplies vodozemac 0.11.2 and its zeroization fix.

Validation on this head includes cargo deny check, locked Cargo metadata, TypeScript checks, 16 voice tests, the WebUI test suite, authentication tests and the production build. Hosted CI is tracked in the PR checks.

prs.title: fix(providers): accept complete SSE sentinel at EOF
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`, extracted directly on `a66cc98a4`.
- **What changed and why:** A complete `data: [DONE]` sentinel at EOF now finishes a compatible-provider stream even when its final newline is missing.
- Preserve already parsed text and usage. Partial sentinels, unfinished JSON and incomplete trailing UTF-8 still report truncation.
- **Scope boundary:** Compatible SSE completion handling and regressions; no retries, session storage, routing or configuration changes.
- **Blast radius:** OpenAI-compatible streamed responses.
- **Linked issue(s):** None; this extraction does not depend on the proposed session-history foundation.

The branch is synchronized with upstream master at `b98b67bed` using a merge; original topic commits remain intact. Its PR diff contains only the feature/fix files, with no Cargo.lock change relative to the updated base.

### What this does, simply

Some compatible endpoints close immediately after the final sentinel. Previously a response without a finish_reason could display its content and then fail as truncated. This accepts that complete terminal marker without treating arbitrary partial response data as success.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes; the regression is deterministic.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** Provider stream adapter used by `surface=web` and `surface=cli`.
- **Setup / preconditions:** No account, network service or credentials needed.
- **Steps to run:** `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers --lib eof_`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Text and usage survive and exactly the completed stream ends successfully; incomplete terminal data still fails.
- **Prior behavior on master (before):** The new no-newline sentinel case fails with truncation.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Local focused adapter tests; upstream CI is pending, not claimed as passed.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** Synthetic byte streams replace a live vendor endpoint. Upstream accepted #12273, and this branch now includes that base with fresh required CI requested.
- **Commands run and tail output:** `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-providers --lib eof_`: 8 passed, 0 failed. Formatting, changed-line Markdown and added local-link gates passed. `cargo +1.98.0 clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-providers --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed. Full provider library suite: 1,982 passed, 4 ignored with `--test-threads=1`. The default parallel harness had three failures in existing process-global proxy fixtures; a serial run of the same compiled test binary passed. Required upstream CI isolates tests with nextest.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The success fixture deliberately omits finish_reason so it exercises the previously failing path.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; wire completion behavior only, no presentation change.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `7861b80f6`; EOF tests in compatible.rs. The raw-byte incomplete UTF-8 regression passes; temporarily removing the UTF-8 completion guard makes it fail by emitting Final.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** `test result: ok. 8 passed; 0 failed`.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** Complete terminal sentinel at EOF yields Final; partial sentinel/JSON yields error.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No real provider request was needed for this deterministic wire-format case; optional external documentation link validation needs lychee.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No.**
- New external network calls? **No.**
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No.**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No; synthetic payloads only.**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **No.**
- If any Yes, describe the risk and mitigation: N/A.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? **Yes.**
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? **No.**
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.**
- Exact upgrade steps: None.

## Rollback

Revert the fix commit. Observable regression would be a complete no-newline sentinel reported as a truncated response. There is no feature flag.

## Supersede Attribution

N/A.

## Summary

Base branch: `master`.

Add explicit per-alias opt-in for OpenRouter balance reporting and fixed-mask editing of saved secrets. Depends on #11845.

### What this does, simply

Balance reporting defaults off. Disabling it preserves credentials. Saved secrets show a constant mask; replacement starts with an empty draft.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

Run the hosted Web Permission Tests and gateway/config regressions, then exercise opt-in, save/cancel and secret replacement in the authenticated dashboard.

### How I tested

Current-head CI Required Gate passes at 72b345ba975a64316d9c77da4438449abf803467, including the hosted Web Permission Tests. This refresh integrates master and resolves the package.json conflict by retaining both the SecretField regression and the new authentication suite. Local navigation/secret-field tests passed; the first local authentication-suite run lacked generated API descriptions, so it is not cited as passing evidence. Hosted current-head checks supply the integrated coverage.

Visual interface evidence: this follow-up changes integration, lifecycle or tests; prior feature UI evidence remains linked in the review discussion. No new presentation claim is made from source inspection. Remaining platform/integration gaps are those not covered by current-head hosted CI and the named local checks.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

No new permissions or network destinations in this refresh. The feature adds authenticated balance reporting through the configured provider/proxy; provider credentials remain server-side. Stored secret values and lengths are not returned to the browser.

- New permissions/capabilities/filesystem scope: No
- New external network calls: Yes — inherited authenticated OpenRouter balance requests from #11845; configured proxy routing remains enforced.
- Secrets/credentials handling changed: Yes — fixed-mask replacement editing preserves saved secret values until an explicit replacement.
- PII, real identities or private messages in the diff/tests/docs: No.
- Untrusted model-visible content changed: No

## Compatibility (required)

Backward compatible. The feature adds the documented opt-in setting, default false. No toolchain-floor change. Merge #11845 first, then reconcile the stacked branch against master.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Revert the feature commits. Reporting can be disabled through its opt-in setting while preserving saved credentials. Verify that the dashboard hides unavailable balances and stored secrets remain masked.

prs.title: feat(plugins): support multiple plugin registry origins
prs.body: ## Summary - **Base branch:** master - **What changed and why:** - Accept a JSON array in ZEROCLAW_PLUGIN_REGISTRY_URL so private and public registries can be used together. - Preserve fetched-origin identity through search, caching and selection in install, update and Quickstart so same-name packages cannot silently switch publishers. This does not add durable origin metadata to installed packages. - Carry origin information into suggestions and the web catalog without exposing credential-bearing URLs in catalog responses or display labels. - **Scope boundary:** No changes to plugin execution permissions or package layout. Fork-only validation tooling is not included. - **Blast radius:** Registry/cache consumers, CLI/Quickstart, runtime suggestions, gateway API types and the web Plugins page. - **Linked issue(s):** Related #12109 ### What this does, simply Use multiple plugin registries without losing track of which publisher a package belongs to. Existing single-URL configuration still works. Custom lists replace the default registry rather than automatically adding it. Only one package per name can be installed. ## Testing (required) ### How you can test (when useful) - **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. - **Interface(s) exercised:** cli and web; Quickstart interaction remains unverified. - **Setup / preconditions:** Two reachable registry indexes containing a package named demo. Replace the example URLs below. Use the same fixtures on master and this branch. - **Steps to run:** ~~~sh ZEROCLAW_PLUGIN_REGISTRY_URL='["https://registry-a.example/registry.json","https://registry-b.example/registry.json"]' zeroclaw plugin search demo ~~~ - **Expected on this branch (after):** Results from both registries with distinct publisher labels. - **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The single-registry implementation does not support the JSON list or combined results. Manual A/B confirmation is still pending. ### How I tested - **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Previously recorded focused fork-hosted Linux checks cover registry behavior, compatibility and affected consumers. These are the existing results recorded for revision `645a9ae5fdba6ae9e6026d7d057dfbdfc49ac0d4`, not a fresh CI result for the current head: | Check | Result | |---|---| | [Shared registry](https://github.com/ggettert/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41557780235) | 10 passed | | [CLI](https://github.com/ggettert/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41564605521) | 16 passed | | [Runtime suggestions](https://github.com/ggettert/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41673545578) | 1 passed | | [Gateway catalog/compatibility](https://github.com/ggettert/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41676472684) | 6 unique tests passed; 7 executions (nonadditive) | | [Frontend helpers](https://github.com/ggettert/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41682990141) | 4 passed | | [Schema/typecheck](https://github.com/ggettert/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41683862525) | Export, contract guards and typecheck passed | - **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Current-head required CI is not established by the links above. Standard lint/docs gates, full workspace/default-feature test suites, Windows, MSRV and the full release/feature matrix remain outside the evidence here. The sandbox checks below add actual Linux release CLI/gateway and web coverage, but not Quickstart interaction. - **Commands run and tail output:** The linked historical logs contain the focused CI commands. Frontend output: ~~~sh node --experimental-strip-types --test-reporter=tap --test web/src/pages/pluginCatalog.test.ts ~~~ ~~~text # tests 4 # pass 4 # fail 0 # cancelled 0 # skipped 0 # todo 0 ~~~ The historical schema check ran `cargo run --locked -p xtask --bin web -- gen-api` and `npm run typecheck`, including the generated-file check and `tsc -b`. Three new DTOs passed presence checks in both generated contracts. For the current-head sandbox run, the actual CLI commands included `plugin install tool-fixture@0.0.0 --registry http://127.0.0.1:18281/b.json`, `plugin list --verify` and `plugin info tool-fixture`, using the release binary and an isolated `--config-dir`. Each exited 0; selected output lines: ~~~text Installed plugin tool-fixture v0.0.0 tool-fixture v0.0.0 — (no description) [loads] Loads: yes. The component instantiates against this host's WIT world. ~~~ - **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** On 2026-11-03, exercised the real CLI and paired dashboard/API in an isolated Linux sandbox (Rust 1.98, Node 24.22.2). The PR release CLI/gateway used default features plus `plugins-wasm-cranelift`; the dashboard used the separately built canonical web dist. No source changes were made during validation. - Legacy single-URL search and dashboard/API returned the two expected entries. Two registries returned four rows, including two same-name packages with distinct authoritative origin IDs; publisher-supplied spoof origin metadata was ignored. - Both unpinned and version-pinned duplicate installs rejected ambiguity and required `--registry`. Explicit selection of an origin rejected versions available only from the other origin; request logs showed only the selected index was fetched. - Malformed JSON and connection refusal failed without partial search results or cache publication. Cache bytes, inode and restrictive permissions survived failures; initial mode was `0600`, and a successful refresh preserved deliberately narrowed `0400`. Matching offline cache remained usable; a mismatched explicit source set excluded it. This is failure atomicity and separate offline reuse, not successful-search fallback. - Built the repository's harmless `tool-fixture@0.0.0` for `wasm32-wasip2` and installed it from registry B with normal archive/digest, manifest and host-load checks enabled. B-only index/package requests and matching installed component/manifest hashes proved the selected download. `list --verify` reported `[loads]`; `info` reported `Loads: yes`. Installed metadata does not retain an origin field; this is not a durable installed-origin or signature-authenticity claim. - **Visual interface evidence:** Screenshot of the actual paired web Plugins page with all four registry rows and distinct origin IDs. Quickstart screenshots remain unprovided. - **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `342cf3c12683365ee3d1b7f68f9da6fdea86a88f`; actual cli, paired web Plugins page and authenticated catalog API. Current-head evidence is summarized above, with exact CLI output above; the captured dashboard screenshot will be attached separately. Earlier automated evidence is linked separately. - **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** CLI output above. The actual multi-registry dashboard screenshot has been captured; - **Action or changed state and observed result:** Switching the web catalog to Installed hid the uninstalled registry entries; All restored all four rows. The authenticated catalog stayed HTTP 200 with the same four rows after both failed refreshes; unauthenticated access returned 401. The later CLI installation succeeded and the host loaded the fixture; that installation was not a web install flow. - **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Tool invocation/execution was explicitly skipped; no supported safe direct non-provider invocation surface was established. Install/load is not execution. Interactive approval, provider/production integration, Quickstart interaction, an unpatched-master comparison, signature authenticity, timeout behavior and concurrent/crash cache stress were not tested. This was bounded sandbox validation, not a full test/lint or platform matrix. A Google Fonts request blocked by dashboard CSP was observed but did not affect catalog behavior; it was treated as nonblocking for this acceptance run and was not attributed to this PR without a baseline comparison. ## Security & Privacy Impact (required) - New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **No.** Existing cache location; more restrictive cache writes. - New external network calls? **Yes.** Up to eight configured HTTP(S) indexes, with bounded requests and no partial cache publication. - Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **Yes.** Catalog responses/display labels use opaque origin IDs; cache writes are private. This is not blanket URL redaction for errors or executable commands. - PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.** - Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes.** Registry-backed suggestions retain the fetched origin rather than publisher-declared provenance. Registry metadata remains untrusted. - If any Yes, describe the risk and mitigation: Additional registries expand the publisher trust surface. Ambiguous installs and multi-origin updates require an explicit registry. Source validation and all-or-nothing cache publication prevent silently mixing incomplete results. ## Compatibility (required) - Backward compatible? **Yes**, for existing single-registry configuration and public Rust struct literals. - Config / env / CLI surface changed? **Yes.** The existing variable also accepts a JSON array. Ambiguous installs and multi-origin updates require `--registry `. - Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? **No.** - If backward compatibility is No or either surface/floor question is Yes: exact upgrade steps for existing users: No change for single-registry users. To opt in, set ZEROCLAW_PLUGIN_REGISTRY_URL to a JSON array of one to eight HTTP(S) URLs. Include the public registry explicitly if wanted. ## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs) - **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert `. Restore a single registry URL and discard/regenerate the union cache at plugin-registry/registry.json before using the old reader. Installed packages are unchanged. - **Feature flags or config toggles:** No feature flag. A single URL or explicit `--registry ` selects one registry. - **Observable failure symptoms:** Missing catalog entries, unexpected origin-selection errors, cache-source mismatches or failed registry refreshes. ## Supersede Attribution (required only when Supersedes # is used) Not applicable; this PR does not supersede another PR.

prs.title: test(runtime): isolate trim attribution capture from concurrent agents
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`, extracted directly on `b98b67bed`; no history-foundation dependency.
- **What changed and why:** Scope the trim-attribution test's broadcast subscription to its own agent before asserting model and provider fields. Other tests can emit a history-trim event concurrently; the old selector accepted the first such event from any agent.
- Reuse the fixture's attribution object as the selection source. Keep all model, provider and inherited-agent assertions.
- **Scope boundary:** One test function; no logger, runtime behavior, configuration, authority or dependency change.
- **Blast radius:** Reliability of shared-process runtime test runs.
- **Linked issue(s):** None.

### What this does, simply

The test should inspect the log record produced by its own loop. A valid record from another simultaneous test must not cause a false model-attribution failure.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** Structured log broadcast from the real ToolLoop fixture.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Local Rust test fixtures; no account or network service.
- **Steps to run:** `cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib trim_record_carries_model_attribution`; for concurrency coverage run `scripts/ci/parallel_runtime_test_gate.sh`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Only the fixture's agent record is selected, and all existing attribution assertions pass.
- **Prior behavior on master (before):** Concurrent history trims can select a different model's valid record and fail the test.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Local focused upstream test plus the identical patch in the fork's repeated runtime/channel gate.
- **Known CI coverage gap:** Upstream required CI is pending; this is not a claim that CI has already passed on the new upstream head.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Focused upstream Rust 1.98 test: `1 passed; 0 failed`. Identical patch in the fork passed the complete parallel gate: runtime 5,844 passed per run and channels 1,984 passed per run, three runs each at 16 threads. Formatting and diff checks passed.
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The observed failure selected an unrelated `mock-model` record without the fixture's agent alias. The new selector does not filter on either model or provider, so their assertions remain independent.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; test isolation only.

prs.title: docs(runtime): record the relay-served dashboard placement exception
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - #12270 adds the daemon side of the relay-served dashboard to the relay bridge, which already lives in `zeroclaw-runtime`:
    - the bridge's `gateway` route target in `src/relay.rs`;
    - the in-process handoff to the gateway in `src/relay_dashboard.rs`;
    - the module's export in `src/lib.rs`.
  - `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md` and ADR-016 require a recorded, Core Team-approved exception before that merges, and a feature pull request can't grant itself one. A review comment on #12270 raised exactly this.
  - Moving the relay bridge out of the runtime is the planned daemon extraction, not something to start inside #12270. So this records a bounded exception for the paths #12270 touches and names where they go.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - One row in the active-exceptions table of `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`. No code, tests or other files change.
  - The row doesn't approve #12270's implementation. It doesn't cover any other peer hint, transport, listener or local service, the gateway's or relay's own changes, or HTTP/2 or path-prefixed dashboards.
- **Blast radius:** a placement record only. It applies to the listed runtime paths, as #12270 changes them.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #12270 (the feature; this record must land before it merges). Related #10315.

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw's runtime crate is a temporary holding area, and new features shouldn't go there without a written, Core Team-approved exception. #12270, which lets a ZeroRelay serve a daemon's web dashboard, has to add a piece to the relay code that already lives there. This PR writes down that permission, how far it goes, and where the code moves when the runtime is split up. It doesn't change what ZeroClaw does.

### The row

| Column | Content |
| --- | --- |
| Scope | `src/relay.rs` and `src/relay_dashboard.rs`, plus the `src/lib.rs` export, limited to #12270. That covers the `[relay.dashboard]` opt-in in `Hello`, the dashboard label derived from the registration key, and the `gateway` route target. The route target refuses loopback and unspecified client addresses and hands connections to the in-process gateway through the bounded `DashboardIngress` queue. Focused tests and fixture updates are included. Admission, origin and sign-in stay in `zeroclaw-gateway`, and the relay side stays in `apps/zerorelay`. |
| Destination | The relay bridge moves with `src/relay.rs` in the planned daemon extraction. `DashboardIngress` and its connection types move with the gateway's connection intake in the planned `zeroclaw-gw` extraction. |
| Approved by | **Pending Core Team review**, the same wording other rows used before approval. The approver replaces it with their handle and a link to their approving review, as in #11628. |
| Expires or reviewed | A review condition, not an expiry. Review comes at the daemon or gateway process-extraction design review, whichever is first. It also comes earlier if the bridge would hand any other peer hint to an in-process service, or the relay-served dashboard would accept HTTP/2 or a path-prefixed gateway. |

@Audacity88, I opened #12270, so this needs another Core Team member's approval. Would you review the row, or pass it to another Core member? On approval, the approver cell becomes your handle and a link to your review.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: no behavior changes. Review is of the row's scope, destination and review condition against #12270's diff.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** none claimed. `Docs Style` skips this scoped `AGENTS.md` under its default path selection, so I ran its gates on the file directly.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** `Docs Style`'s default selection excludes `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`; the explicit run is below.
- **Commands run and tail output** (Linux, at `bb4ff0300d` on `a66cc98a47`):

  ```text
  git diff --check a66cc98a47 HEAD
  (exit 0; no output)

  BASE_SHA=a66cc98a47 bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
  No docs files detected; skipping docs quality gate.

  BASE_SHA=a66cc98a47 DOCS_FILES=crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md bash scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
  Linting: 1 file(s)
  Summary: 0 error(s)

  Collected 0 added link(s) from 1 docs file(s).
  No added links detected in changed docs lines.

  python3 scripts/ci/check_internal_docs_links.py
  Checked authored Markdown links in 219 file(s); no broken local targets.
  ```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - The row is one line, contiguous with the active-exceptions table, with the table's four columns.
  - The scope matches #12270's runtime diff:
    - `src/lib.rs` +1;
    - `src/relay.rs`;
    - the new `src/relay_dashboard.rs`;
    - the new `tests/relay_dashboard_path.rs`;
    - the new protocol and bridge-config fields in three existing relay test fixtures.
  - The pending-review wording matches what earlier rows carried before approval (#11628).
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A; no user-visible interface state changed.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `bb4ff0300d`, repository documentation, `crates/zeroclaw-runtime/AGENTS.md`.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** the diff adds one exception row and changes no other file.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** no Rust build or tests, because nothing executable changes.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No runtime permissions. The row records only a code-placement exception.
- New external network calls? No.

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: fix(security): enforce cron approval and authority at the write across RPC, tools and token revocation
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`. Merged with master 50e01f55e4, which includes #12232, and merges cleanly with master eca7edf9b4. Head a149bec611.
- **What changed and why:**
  - **The approval fix.** `cron/add` passed `approved = true` ("RPC calls are pre-approved") into `add_shell_job_with_approval`. That skipped the supervised-autonomy gate that the CLI (`cron::add_shell_job`) and the gateway (`POST /api/cron`, `approved = false`) both apply. An RPC request is not an operator approval, so `cron/add` now passes `false`. `cron/patch` validated a replacement command with `approved = true` for the same reason, and now also passes `false`. Two regression tests show that a medium-risk command is refused by `cron/add` and `cron/patch` and never stored, and that a low-risk command still succeeds. The test command is `touch`: allowlisted, but medium-risk under a supervised profile with `require_approval_for_medium_risk`.
  - **Authority is rechecked at the write.** The cron store writes synchronously and can wait out SQLite's five-second busy timeout, so a revocation published during that wait used to be ignored. After the agent selector passes:
    - `cron/add` takes the agent lifecycle reservation first, then the config writer gate (`lock_config_writer()`, the mutex every config commit takes), and rechecks the caller against the current policy. This is the order `config/set` uses. It holds both through the insert, so neither a lifecycle delete or rename of the alias nor a grant publication can land between the recheck and the row.
    - Once SQLite grants the store's writer, `cron/add` takes the authority lease (`hold_authority()`), checks the caller's credential and grants under it, and holds the lease through the insert and commit. The gate already fences policy changes; this check catches a credential that expires or reaches its revalidation deadline while SQLite waits. A refused add inserts nothing. This is IftekharUddin's repair.
    - `cron/patch` takes the writer gate, rechecks the caller, and runs #12232's agent-job check (`authorize_cron_agent_execution`) under it. It then runs #12232's checks of the row and the caller's authority under the store's writer, and validates a replacement command there without an approval. The gate is held through the store's writer wait, so a grant change published meanwhile waits behind the patch. If the store stays busy, the patch gives up with nothing written and the change publishes after it.
  - **Wrappers no longer carry approval.** The runtime writes a tool's `approved` argument only on the call it dispatched, under that call's own name. A `pipeline` step and a skill alias each call their child tool directly, and the model supplied that child's `approved: true`. Both wrappers now clear `approved` on a child that takes runtime approval, so a nested medium-risk command meets the supervised gate. The list of such tools moved to `zeroclaw_api::tool::takes_runtime_approval`, so the runtime's own sanitizer and the wrappers share it.
  - **Token revocation is ordered against these writes.** The gateway's device revoke, token rotation, admin single-device revoke and revoke-all used to remove the token from the live set first. They took the config write lock only to persist, so a cron write that had checked the token could commit after the token was gone. They now admit `begin_config_commit()` first, and nothing changes until that commit holds the writer mutex. Under it, one synchronous step removes the device row (or clears the registry) and the live token together, and the token set is then persisted under the same commit. Revoke-all goes through `PairingGuard::revoke_under_config_write_lock`. The three per-device paths share `revoke_device_credential`, which deletes the row in a `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction on the device database and checks the caller again once SQLite grants that writer. As a result:
    - a write that checked the token first commits before the revocation lands, and one that checks after sees the token gone;
    - a request dropped while it waits has changed nothing and can be retried, and a commit refused because the daemon generation is closing changes nothing at all (503);
    - the requesting caller is checked again under the commit and under the device database's writer, before anything is deleted, so a device revoked while its own request was queued is refused. Device registration and capability updates write that database without the config writer, which is why the second check is there;
    - a dashboard session is checked against its live grants at both points, not the grants it signed in with. A session demoted from administrator while its request waited is refused with 403 `operator_required`, and one whose sign-in provider is no longer offered with 401 `session_invalid`; neither changes anything. A rotation checks a session once more just before it mints the new pairing code. A native device can still rotate its own credential. This is IftekharUddin's repair;
    - rotation keeps the commit until its new pairing code is issued.
  - **Docs.** `docs/book/src/security/authentication.md` describes the approval rule for RPC cron writes, the recheck at the write, and wrappers never carrying an approval.
- **What #12232 now covers:**
  - This PR used to mark `cron_add`, `cron_update`, `cron_run`, `schedule` and `send_message_to_peer` as tools a principal-bound session must not keep. It also refused agent-job patch and trigger to every principal but the shared operator.
  - #12232 marks the same tools and withholds them from every non-admin principal, through one posture function for prompts, rehydration and steering. It also refuses non-admin agent-job patch and trigger.
  - This PR now keeps #12232's rule: administrators keep the tools, and a non-admin with wildcard tools and agents keeps a bound `delegate`.
  - Dropped here: the markers, the shared-operator posture, the steering rule and their tests. The `cron_update` and peer-agent tests stay, worded for non-admin principals.
- **Scope boundary:**
  - Scheduled and manual execution are unchanged; they already re-validate with `approved = false`.
  - Agent-job support in `cron/add` is unchanged.
  - The gateway's cron routes and the CLI are unchanged; only the gateway's token revocation paths change.
  - **Not changed here, and needs a design decision:** a job keeps running after whoever installed it loses their grants. Two cases remain: shell jobs a non-admin adds through RPC `cron/add` with its cron grant, and jobs installed before this change. Closing it means storing the submitter's authority with the job and re-resolving it on every run. That is the cron site of the authority-recheck work, not a guard this PR can add.
- **Blast radius:**
  - RPC clients (zerocode/TUI, and a future external gateway) that add or patch shell cron jobs.
  - Under `autonomy = supervised`, a medium-risk (when `require_approval_for_medium_risk`) or high-risk command is now refused at creation with `requires explicit approval`, instead of being stored.
  - Full-autonomy profiles are unaffected.
  - `cron/add` and `cron/patch` now queue on the config writer gate, as config writes and `session/new` already do. The store write runs while the gate is held, so a busy `jobs.db` delays config publications and revocations for up to the busy timeout.
  - Under supervised autonomy, a medium- or high-risk command inside a `pipeline` step or a skill alias is refused unless it is called directly, where the runtime's approval applies.
  - Gateway device revoke, rotation and revoke-all wait for any in-flight config write before deleting the device or removing the token. A request dropped while it waits leaves both in place. A device revoke or rotation whose caller was revoked while it waited is refused with 401 and changes nothing; a dashboard session demoted from administrator meanwhile gets 403.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12260. Related #12232, #7432, #12046, #11225, #11176, #11182, #11286.
- **Labels:** `bug`, `agent`, `config`, `gateway`, `runtime`, `tool`, `tool:cron`, `security:pairing`, `domain:security`, `risk:high`, `size:XL`, `release:v0.9.0`.

### What this does, simply

A cron job scheduled over the RPC socket (zerocode/TUI) was treated as though a human had already approved its shell command. The CLI and the web dashboard both ask for approval under supervised autonomy. With this change the RPC path follows the same rule.

Related gaps are also closed:
- A permission removed, or a device revoked, while a cron write was waiting on the database now stops that write or waits for it to finish.
- A tool run inside a `pipeline` or a skill alias can no longer claim an approval nobody gave.

In practice the old behavior did not let the command *run*: every scheduled run re-checks the command without approval and refuses it. What it did was store a job the policy would not accept, which then failed on every tick. After this change the job is refused up front with the policy reason.

### Present in v0.8.5?

Partly.
- `git show v0.8.5:crates/zeroclaw-runtime/src/rpc/dispatch.rs` has the same `true, // RPC calls are pre-approved` in `handle_cron_add` (line 3143). It was introduced in #6848.
- v0.8.5 has no command validation in `handle_cron_patch` (no `validate_shell_command` call), so the patch half is master-only.

Because execution re-validates with `approved = false` in both v0.8.5 and master (`cron/scheduler.rs`, `execute_and_persist_job`), I do not think this alone justifies a v0.8.5 security patch. It is an approval-gate inconsistency that stores unrunnable jobs; it does not bypass execution.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The RPC tests drive the real handlers or `process_line`, and the tool tests go through the production tool dispatch. The revocation and lock-order tests use deterministic pauses rather than sleeps: they hold a competing SQLite writer or the config writer gate, and poll the waiting future once, before the change they race.

### How I tested

- **Tested revision:** the head's tree, 7f458a55b8. Linux x86_64, Rust 1.98.0, with CI's own commands from `ci.yml` at master 2341ab56c3 (unchanged since 50e01f55e4).
- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `CI Required Gate` runs the lib tests of every changed crate.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

```
# tree 7f458a55b8 (head a149bec611, merging master 50e01f55e4); Linux x86_64, Rust 1.98.0
$ cargo fetch --locked                                  # exit 0
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check                            # exit 0
$ bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.test.sh && bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh   # exit 0
$ git diff --check 50e01f55e4 HEAD                      # no output
$ cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets   # exit 0
$ bash scripts/ci/run_clippy.sh --scope workspace --summary-title "Lint diagnostics" \
    --log-name cargo-clippy.log                         # exit 0 (workspace, --all-targets, --features ci-all)
$ cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-api -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-gateway \
    -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings   # exit 0
$ cargo nextest run --locked --no-fail-fast --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop
     Summary 20111 tests run: 20106 passed, 5 failed, 43 skipped
# the 5 are outside this change; see "skipped" below
$ cargo nextest run --locked --no-fail-fast -p zeroclaw -p zeroclaw-config -p zeroclaw-tools \
    -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-gateway --features tools-compat \
    --lib --test integration -E 'not binary(integration) or test(/^report_template_tool_test::/)'

$ cargo deny check                                      # cargo-deny 0.19.9, fresh advisory DB
advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok
$ cargo audit                                           # cargo-audit 0.22.2: exit 0, 8 allowed warnings

# this branch's tests, with #12232's agent-job and delegate tests that it touches;
# three runs in a row, every run:
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- rpc::dispatch::tests::cron_ \
    rpc::dispatch::tests::a_token_revocation rpc::dispatch::tests::a_cron_write_queued \

    rpc::dispatch::tests::principal_headless:: rpc::dispatch::tests::principal_delegation_bounded \

test result: ok. 85 passed; 0 failed
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib -- api::tests::device_ api::tests::revoke \
    api::tests::rotate api::tests::a_device_request tests::admin_paircode
test result: ok. 19 passed; 0 failed
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib -- --exact \
    api_pairing::tests::device_revoke_checks_authority_while_holding_the_sqlite_writer \
    dashboard_session::tests::device_delete_rechecks_cookie_operator_after_the_writer_wait \
    dashboard_session::tests::device_rotate_rechecks_cookie_operator_after_the_writer_wait
test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-tools --lib -- pipeline
test result: ok. 24 passed; 0 failed
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib -- pairing
test result: ok. 109 passed; 0 failed

# the merge with master eca7edf9b4 (no conflicts), same commands:
$ cargo check --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop --all-targets   # exit 0
$ bash scripts/ci/run_clippy.sh --scope workspace --summary-title "Lint diagnostics" \
    --log-name cargo-clippy.log                         # exit 0
$ cargo nextest run --locked --no-fail-fast --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop
     Summary 20146 tests run: 20141 passed, 5 failed, 43 skipped
# the same 5
```

- **Revert checks,** run at aaccc4656b, whose code is the head's without the clippy allow: each change below touches one functional line, or moves one line. The named tests fail, and the branch's other tests in that crate pass unless noted.

  - `cron/add` back to `approved = true`: `cron_add_does_not_pre_approve_a_medium_risk_shell_job`.
  - `cron/patch` validation back to `true`: `cron_patch_does_not_pre_approve_a_medium_risk_command`.
  - The recheck under the gate reads the connection's stamped grants instead of current authority:
    - fails `cron_add_revoked_while_queued_is_refused` and `cron_add_holds_the_publication_lock_while_the_store_is_busy`;
    - the two token-revocation tests still pass, because `cron/add`'s check under the store's writer now refuses a revoked token on its own. `cron/patch`'s revocation test passes for the same reason.
  - `cron/add` without its check under the store's writer, or with that check moved back before the writer wait: `cron_add_rechecks_credential_deadlines_after_the_sqlite_writer_wait`.
  - `cron/patch` skips the agent-job check under the gate: `cron_patch_refuses_an_agent_job_change_before_waiting_on_the_store`.
  - `cron/patch` releases the gate before the store write: `cron_patch_rechecks_authority_and_row_after_sqlite_writer_wait`.
  - `cron/add` releases the gate before the insert: `cron_add_holds_the_publication_lock_while_the_store_is_busy`, `a_token_revocation_waits_for_a_cron_write_blocked_on_a_busy_store` and `cron_add_reserves_the_alias_before_the_writer_gate_and_holds_both_through_the_insert`.
  - `cron/add` takes the gate before the reservation, or releases the reservation before the insert: `cron_add_reserves_the_alias_before_the_writer_gate_and_holds_both_through_the_insert`.
  - **Wrapper approval clears:**
    - either pipeline clear removed (sequential or parallel): `steps_never_carry_approval_to_tools_that_take_runtime_approval`;
    - the skill-alias clear removed: `skill_builtin_tool_never_forwards_approval_to_its_target`.
  - **Device revocation:**
    - the device row and token removed before the gate is held: `device_revoke_and_rotate_remove_the_live_token_only_under_the_config_write_lock` and `device_revoke_and_rotate_dropped_while_waiting_can_be_retried`. Every test that expects the gated delete to still find the device fails with them. For revoke-all, the same change in `revoke_under_config_write_lock` fails `admin_paircode_rotate_dropped_while_waiting_can_be_retried`;
    - a bearer caller not checked again under the device database's writer: `a_device_request_queued_behind_its_callers_revocation_is_refused`;
    - the device delete opened as a deferred transaction instead of taking that writer: `device_revoke_checks_authority_while_holding_the_sqlite_writer`;
    - a dashboard session not checked against its live grants: `device_delete_rechecks_cookie_operator_after_the_writer_wait` and `device_rotate_rechecks_cookie_operator_after_the_writer_wait`. Either session check alone, under the commit or under the writer, refuses a demotion published before the request reaches the writer, so removing just one of them fails nothing.
  - **Not pinned by any test:**
    - a rotation keeping the commit until its new pairing code is issued, and checking a session again just before the mint. Removing either fails nothing; the second was checked in the code;
    - `cron/add` holding the lease through the insert and commit. Releasing it right after the check fails nothing.

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - Scheduled runs (`execute_and_persist_job`) and `cron/trigger` (`run_manual_job_with_selection`) already validate with `approved = false`, so no execution path changes.
  - In the daemon, the RPC context and the gateway admit config commits through the same live-config authority, whose writer mutex is the process-wide `shared_config_write_lock()`. A gateway revocation holding a commit is therefore ordered against an RPC cron write holding `lock_config_writer()`.
  - **Lock order:** the cron handlers take the config writer gate first, then the store's writer, and no production path takes them the other way round.
    - Every cron store write is a synchronous SQLite call. The callbacks inside it are `cron/patch`'s recheck, which takes the config read lock and then the authority lease, and `cron/add`'s, which takes the authority lease alone. Neither takes the writer gate.
    - The config commit's publish does not touch the cron store.
  - The gateway's per-device recheck runs under the commit and inside the device database's `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`. It is synchronous: a bearer goes through `require_auth` (or `require_gateway_admin_token`), a session through the session store, the live config's read lock and the RPC auth state. None of these opens the device database or takes the config writer. The delete commits before the registry's cache lock is taken, because reconciliation takes the cache first and then writes that table.
  - I did not run a live daemon.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Nothing was skipped. My test machine has no `mold`, `clang` or `expect` and runs Node 18, so CI's linker settings were left out, and five workspace tests failed for reasons outside this change: four `zerorelay` front-door page tests need Node's global `crypto` (Node 19 and later), and `daemon_feedback_follows_foreground_job_control_transitions` needs `expect`. They fail the same way on master 50e01f55e4 on the same machine, every run. None of these crates is touched here, and master's own CI Test job passed them at 50e01f55e4.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No. This narrows them.
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes. Paired-token revocation (device revoke, rotation, admin revoke and revoke-all) now waits for the config writer gate and removes the device row and the live token in one step under it. A per-device revoke or rotation checks its caller again under that gate and under the device database's writer, and a dashboard session is checked against its live grants. What a revocation removes is unchanged; only its ordering against in-flight writes, and who may still perform it, changes.
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation:
  - The revocation change only orders an existing removal against in-flight cron writes. A request dropped or refused before it holds the gate changes nothing.
  - The rest tightens an approval gate to match the CLI and gateway, rechecks authority at the cron write, and removes a model-controlled approval path through wrappers.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes for full-autonomy and low-risk commands. The following changes:
  - Under supervised autonomy, RPC `cron/add` and `cron/patch` now refuse medium- and high-risk commands that were previously stored and then failed at run time.
  - Wrappers no longer pass `approved` to a child.
  - A device request whose caller was revoked, or whose dashboard session was demoted, while it waited is refused.
- **Jobs already stored:** there is no migration.
  - Under supervised autonomy, a medium- or high-risk shell job added over RPC before this change is still in the store and keeps failing on every tick with `requires explicit approval`.
  - `cron list` and the run history show which ones. Remove or patch them, or approve a `cron_run` call for one.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No. `zeroclaw_api::tool` gains `takes_runtime_approval` and `clear_runtime_approval`, and `PairingGuard` gains `revoke_under_config_write_lock` and `revoke_token_hash_ordered`; nothing existing is removed.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** `git revert <sha>`
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** None
- **Observable failure symptoms:**
  - RPC `cron/add` returns `Cron add failed: blocked by security policy: Command requires explicit approval` for a command a client expects to schedule.
  - A nested medium-risk command in a pipeline or skill alias fails with `requires explicit approval`.
  - A device revoke or rotation during a daemon reload returns 503 with `Revocation refused without any change`.

milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.
