prs.title: fix(deps): update vodozemac to 0.11.2 for RUSTSEC-2026-0445 and -0451
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - `Cargo.lock` only: vodozemac 0.11.0 → 0.11.2. `cargo deny check` fails on two vodozemac advisories published on 2026-11-06, so `Security`, and with it `CI Required Gate`, fails on every PR. 0.11.2 fixes both:
    - **RUSTSEC-2026-0445** (GHSA-mxcm-mrw6-c446): 0.11.0 and 0.11.1 build aes, cbc, hmac, sha2, chacha20poly1305 and cipher without their `zeroize` feature, so those crates don't wipe expanded keys and cipher state on drop.
    - **RUSTSEC-2026-0451** (GHSA-v27v-f96q-qhjq): up to 0.11.1, each Olm root key ratchet step leaves the new root key and chain key in freed heap memory.
  - The lockfile is cargo's own output for `cargo update -p vodozemac --precise 0.11.2` (Rust 1.98.0). Plain `cargo update -p vodozemac` gives the identical file. Besides vodozemac's version and checksum:
    - aes 0.9.3, block-buffer 0.12.0, chacha20 0.10.2, chacha20poly1305 0.11.0, cipher 0.5.2, digest 0.11.3 and hybrid-array 0.4.15 gain a `zeroize` dependency. That is the fix: 0.11.2 turns on their `zeroize` feature.
    - cargo points three range requirements at the other version already in the lock: tempfile 3.27.0's getrandom (`>=0.3.0, <0.5`) from 0.4.3 to 0.3.4, prost-derive 0.14.4's itertools (`>=0.10.1, <=0.14`) from 0.14.0 to 0.13.0, and num_enum_derive 0.7.6's proc-macro-crate (`>= 1, <= 3`) from 3.5.0 to 1.3.1.
    - No crate is added, removed or changes version.
  - It is a fix, not an exception: `deny.toml` and `.cargo/audit.toml` are unchanged.
- **Scope boundary:** No `Cargo.toml` change, no matrix-sdk bump, no advisory exception, no code change.
- **Blast radius:**
  - The Matrix channel's end-to-end encryption, through matrix-sdk 0.19.1 and matrix-sdk-crypto 0.19.1. `channel-matrix` is off in Cargo's `default` features and on in the release builds (`dist_extra_features`).
  - tempfile's getrandom edge reaches everything that makes temp files. Both getrandom versions were already in the build, and both use the operating system's random number generator.
  - The itertools and proc-macro-crate edges are build-time only (prost-derive and num_enum_derive are proc macros).
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #12272

### What this does, simply

ZeroClaw's Matrix channel uses vodozemac, the Matrix project's encryption library, to talk in encrypted rooms. Two problems were reported in it this week. In both, encryption keys could stay in memory after they were done with, rather than being wiped. Getting at them would take a separate way to read the process's memory, but it weakens a safety margin that encrypted chat relies on. vodozemac 0.11.2 fixes both. This PR moves the lockfile to it.

The project's dependency scan in CI fails whenever a known advisory is in the lockfile. Right now it fails for every pull request, whatever the pull request changes. Once this lands, the scan passes again.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A: a lockfile-only patch release; `Security` on this PR is the A/B (it fails on master and should pass here).

### How I tested

On Linux x86_64 with Rust 1.98.0, using the commands from `.github/workflows/ci.yml` at master a66cc98a47. The tested tree is 3b00954fe7, the same as the head.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:**
  - `Security` (cargo-deny 0.19.9, cargo-audit 0.22.2) is the check this fixes.
  - `Lint` (workspace clippy under `ci-all`, which includes `channel-matrix`) and the workspace test jobs build the new lockfile.
  - `Test (channel Matrix)` runs the Matrix channel's tests against vodozemac 0.11.2.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No test sends real encrypted Matrix traffic. The channel tests use matrix-sdk's mocks.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  The Security commands on master and on this branch, against the same advisory database (309392b18f, RustSec `main` at 15:34:32Z on 2026-11-06; fetched on the master run and reused offline on the branch run):

  | step | master a66cc98a47 | this branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | `python3 scripts/ci/lru_advisory_scope_test.py` | rc=0 | rc=0 |
  | `cargo deny check` | **rc=1**: `advisories FAILED, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok`; `error[vulnerability]` RUSTSEC-2026-0445 and RUSTSEC-2026-0451 for vodozemac 0.11.0 | **rc=0**: `advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok` |
  | `cargo verify-project && cargo fetch --locked` | rc=0 | rc=0 |
  | `cargo audit` | **rc=1**: `Loaded 1422 security advisories`, `error: 2 vulnerabilities found!` (the same two), `8 allowed warnings` | **rc=0**: `Loaded 1422 security advisories`, `8 allowed warnings` |

  `cargo deny`'s eight warnings (six `unmatched-skip`, two `unused-wrapper`) and `cargo audit`'s eight allowed warnings are the same on both sides. They come from master's existing skips, seven unmaintained crates and a yanked async-executor 1.14.0.

  On this branch:

  ```text
  cargo fetch --locked                                                          rc=0
  cargo fmt --all -- --check                                                    rc=0
  bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.test.sh && bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh   rc=0
  bash scripts/ci/run_clippy.sh --scope workspace                               rc=0 (rebuilt vodozemac 0.11.2, matrix-sdk-crypto, matrix-sdk, zeroclaw-channels)
  cargo nextest run --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --no-default-features --features channel-matrix --lib matrix::
      Summary [  10.936s] 260 tests run: 260 passed, 929 skipped
  cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --exclude zeroclaw-desktop
      Summary [  73.769s] 20131 tests run: 20126 passed (2 leaky), 5 failed, 43 skipped
  ```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?**
  - I read vodozemac's 0.11.0 → 0.11.2 changes in the published crates. `Cargo.toml` only adds `features = ["zeroize"]` to its RustCrypto dependencies. The source changes are the two fixes above, plus #447 (per-message keys are expanded straight onto the heap) and #453 (`Ed25519PublicKey::from_base64` and `Ed25519SecretKey::from_base64` return an error for 31- or 33-byte input instead of panicking). No public API changes, and the pickle formats are unchanged.
  - 0.11.1 also changed the HPKE check code for QR-code login (MSC4388); its codes don't match 0.11.0's. ZeroClaw's Matrix channel signs in with `matrix_auth().login_username` or `restore_session` and never starts a QR login, so this doesn't reach us.
  - `cargo fetch --locked` accepts the lockfile, and an unlocked `cargo fetch` leaves it unchanged.
  - Not verified: a live Matrix homeserver with encrypted rooms, and macOS or Windows builds.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A, no interface change.
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** tree 3b00954fe7 (head 5f16a31f06); CI's commands above.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:** N/A.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** none skipped. The five workspace nextest failures are environment-only: four `zerorelay` `frontdoor_assets` page tests need a newer Node than the test machine's v18.19.1 (`ReferenceError: crypto is not defined`), and `daemon_feedback_follows_foreground_job_control_transitions` needs `expect`, which wasn't installed. The same five fail on that machine at earlier master heads, CI installs what they need, and `zerorelay` has no path to vodozemac in `Cargo.lock`. CI's mold and clang linker settings were left out; they don't change what is tested.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? Yes
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: the Matrix channel's encryption keys are now wiped from memory after use, inside vodozemac and the RustCrypto crates it uses. That is the upstream fix for both advisories. Nothing in ZeroClaw's own key handling changes.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes. A patch release with no API or pickle format change, so existing Matrix sessions and crypto stores keep working.
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No. vodozemac 0.11.2 keeps 0.11.0's `rust-version`, and `zeroize` was already in the dependency graph.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: N/A

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low risk: `git revert <sha>`. Reverting brings both advisories back, and `Security` fails again.

prs.title: fix(runtime): emit single SBPL backslash for home-dotfile regex
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions)
- **What changed and why:**
  - The macOS Seatbelt "home dotfiles for tool configs" rule was emitted as `regex #"^/Users/[^/]+/\\."`, so `sandbox-exec` never matched `~/.cargo`, `~/.nvm` and similar (#12137). The grant is now a literal `(allow file-read* (prefix "<HOME>/."))` built through the existing SBPL string-literal escaper, so the `/` boundary is fixed and quotes/backslashes in `HOME` cannot break the profile.
  - The grant is scoped to the current account's absolute `HOME` only. There is no `/Users/[^/]+` fallback, and no grant at all when `HOME` is unset or relative.
  - After the grant, `deny file-read*`/`file-write*` subpath rules close `~/.ssh`, `~/.gnupg`, `~/.aws`, `~/.config` (the home entries of `default_forbidden_paths()`) plus `~/.netrc` and `~/.git-credentials`. Seatbelt is last-match, so these stay closed.
  - `SeatbeltSandbox::with_roots` resolves `HOME` once and delegates to a private `with_roots_for_home`, so tests inject a synthetic home instead of mutating process-global `HOME`.
- **Scope boundary:** Does not change the workspace/tier root rules, the system path rules, Linux sandboxes, or user-configured `forbidden_paths` (those still apply through the existing policy layer, not this profile).
- **Blast radius:** Shell/tool commands run under the macOS Seatbelt sandbox.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #12137

### What this does, simply

On macOS, sandboxed tool commands were supposed to be able to read tool settings in hidden folders in your home directory (for example Cargo or Node version manager config), but a doubled backslash meant the rule never matched. This PR makes that rule work for your own home folder only and explicitly keeps the folders and files that commonly hold keys and saved passwords closed.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `Yes` (macOS only; the module is `cfg(target_os = "macos")`)
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `cli` (sandboxed shell tool)
- **Setup / preconditions:** macOS with `/usr/bin/sandbox-exec`
- **Steps to run:** `cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib security::seatbelt`
- **Expected on this branch (after):** `seatbelt_home_dotfile_allows_tools_and_denies_credentials` passes: the synthetic `.cargo/config.toml` is readable; `Documents/private.txt`, `.ssh/id_test`, `.aws/credentials`, `.config/gh/hosts.yml`, `.netrc` and `.git-credentials` are denied.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** `~/.cargo/config.toml` is denied inside the sandbox.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** Format, Lint, and the aarch64-apple-darwin `cargo check` cover formatting and compilation. They do not run this module's tests.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** No CI lane runs `cargo test` for the macOS-only Seatbelt module, so the native test below is not exercised by required CI.
- **Commands run and tail output:**
  - The three new pure policy-string tests (`generate_policy_home_dotfile_grant_is_scoped_to_home_with_path_boundary`, `generate_policy_home_dotfile_grant_escapes_home_literal`, `generate_policy_without_absolute_home_omits_home_dotfile_grant`) were compiled standalone with the policy functions extracted from this head and run on Linux: `test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed`.
  - The exact profile generated by this head for a synthetic home `.../zc-sbx-probe/o"brien.smith` was run under `/usr/bin/sandbox-exec -f profile.sb` on macOS 27.0.1 (arm64):
    ```
    .cargo/config.toml        rc=0  tool-ok
    Documents/private.txt     rc=1  Operation not permitted
    .ssh/id_test              rc=1  Operation not permitted
    .aws/credentials          rc=1  Operation not permitted
    .config/gh/hosts.yml      rc=1  Operation not permitted
    .netrc                    rc=1  Operation not permitted
    .git-credentials          rc=1  Operation not permitted
    workspace write + read    rc=0
    ```

prs.title: fix(cron): persist --agent reassignment on cron update
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `zeroclaw cron update <id> --agent <alias>` validated the alias and printed success, but never stored the new owner (#12228). The CLI now reassigns jobs through a dedicated operator-only entry point (`update_shell_job_with_approval_reassigning` → `update_job_reassigning_owner`).
  - Reassignment is deliberately **not** a `CronJobPatch` field. That struct is deserialized from model input by the agent-facing `cron_update` tool, so an owner field there would let an agent move its own job into another agent's execution context. `cron_update` now rejects a patch that names `agent_alias` (or `agent`) instead of silently dropping it.
  - Unrelated updates (gateway edits, pause/resume, scoped tool updates) bind `NULL` for the owner, and the `UPDATE` keeps the row's current alias via `COALESCE`. This runs inside master's existing `IMMEDIATE` transaction, so a stale caller copy can never restore a previous owner.
  - Naming the current owner is a no-op for ownership, so the required `--agent` no longer breaks same-owner edits to declarative jobs. Actually transferring a declarative job is still refused because its owner comes from `[agents.<alias>].cron_jobs`.
  - The new errors use Fluent keys (`cli-cron-owner-empty`, `cli-cron-owner-declarative`, `cli-cron-update-owner-forbidden`) in all five runtime catalogues.
- **Scope boundary:** Gateway `PATCH /api/cron/:id` and RPC updates keep treating `agent` as the shell risk-profile alias only; they cannot reassign. No change to declarative sync or the agent rename cascade.
- **Blast radius:** Cron store update path, the `cron_update` tool's patch parsing, and the `zeroclaw cron update` CLI.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #12228

### What this does, simply

Every scheduled job belongs to one agent, and that agent's tools, memory and policy are what the job runs with. The CLI let an operator name a different agent on `cron update`, said it worked, and then silently kept the old owner. This PR makes the CLI actually move the job, but only the CLI. Agents editing their own jobs through the `cron_update` tool still can't hand them to another agent, and ordinary edits keep whatever owner the row already has. Jobs defined in `config.toml` keep getting their owner from config.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** N/A. The CLI, tool and store paths are each covered by focused tests at the real entry point (listed below).

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** `Lint`, `Format`, `Test` (runs the `zeroclaw-runtime` cron/tool tests and the root CLI cron tests).
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None for this surface.
- **Commands run and tail output:** (macOS arm64, on head `ae8f1491c28f5bd58ac9a49327850744de50ab24`)

```text
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
(clean)
$ cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized] target(s)
$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib -- cron:: tools::cron_ i18n::
test tools::cron_update::tests::rejects_owner_change_and_keeps_stored_owner ... ok
test cron::store::tests::update_job_reassigning_owner_persists_new_owner ... ok
test cron::store::tests::update_job_reassigning_owner_rejects_empty_alias ... ok
test cron::store::tests::unrelated_patch_keeps_current_owner ... ok
test cron::store::tests::update_job_reassigning_owner_rejects_declarative_transfer ... ok
test cron::store::tests::update_job_reassigning_owner_allows_same_owner_declarative_edit ... ok
test result: ok. 354 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 5803 filtered out
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** Traced every `CronJobPatch` consumer (CLI, gateway, RPC, `cron_update`) to confirm only the CLI can reach `update_job_reassigning_owner`. Not run: a live daemon.
- **Visual interface evidence:** N/A (no rendered-interface change).
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** `ae8f1491c`, `cli` and the `cron_update` tool, via the tests named below.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** N/A
- **Action or changed state and observed result:**
  - `cron_update` with `patch.agent_alias` (object and stringified JSON) → rejected with the localized `cli-cron-update-owner-forbidden` message; owner and name unchanged (`rejects_owner_change_and_keeps_stored_owner`).
  - Operator reassignment persists (`update_job_reassigning_owner_persists_new_owner`, `cli_update_agent_reassigns_imperative_job`); an empty alias is refused (`update_job_reassigning_owner_rejects_empty_alias`).
  - An unrelated patch from a stale copy keeps the newer stored owner (`unrelated_patch_keeps_current_owner`).
  - Declarative jobs: same-owner edits succeed and transfers are refused, both in the store and through the real CLI path (`update_job_reassigning_owner_allows_same_owner_declarative_edit`, `update_job_reassigning_owner_rejects_declarative_transfer`, `cli_update_same_owner_edits_declarative_job`, `cli_update_rejects_declarative_owner_transfer`).
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** Full workspace `cargo test`; the focused crates cover the changed paths and CI runs the rest.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: `cron_update` now returns one new localized error when model input tries to set `agent_alias`. The field has no effect on the store; ownership changes are reachable only from the operator CLI.

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? Yes. `cron update --agent` now reassigns imperative jobs to the named agent (it was documented as doing so but did not).
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No
- Upgrade steps: none; existing jobs keep their owners until an operator runs `cron update --agent`.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low-risk: `git revert` of this PR's commits. Rolling back returns `cron update --agent` to validating the alias without persisting it.

prs.title: feat(sessions): add persistent session prompt attachments
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds an opt-in SQLite collection of four bounded prompts owned by one durable Chat session. Restart preserves them; whole-session reset, deletion and TTL cleanup remove them transactionally with their owner. Schema initialization, legacy prompt binding and ownership reconciliation migrate in one immediate transaction, including rollback on failure.
  - Adds current-session `session_prompt_list`, `session_prompt_set` and `session_prompt_delete`. Mutations require exact one-time approval by default. Global/per-risk-profile `session_prompt_approval = "disabled"` is an explicit operator choice. The tools are direct-only, not skill aliases, pipeline children or inherited auxiliary capabilities. Memory-free RPC Chat retains these tools independently of long-term memory exclusion; ACP remains unsupported.
  - Injects a deterministic next-primary-turn section after immutable host context. Provider context, explicit list and dedicated approval previews retain content; ordinary events, progress and retained/export history mask it without rewriting provider working history. Modifying LLM hooks are skipped for private requests rather than receiving a masked mutable copy. Independent child transcripts do not inherit attachment-bearing parent prompt scope; same-agent SOP continuation retains its existing primary transcript without prompt-tool capability. Its scoped tool-protocol rebuilds preserve complete approved context and refuse overflow before dispatch. Unsupported prompt-tool calls are rejected before approval, and their arguments/results are excluded from SOP step audit capture.
  - Binds primary work to the admitted durable incarnation. Chat deletion now coordinates RPC and gateway work: cancel the captured generation, serialize deletion, commit durable alias removal atomically in SQLite, and invalidate the gateway generation only after commit. SQLite rollback preserves the durable owner and leaves an idle WebSocket usable; already-cancelled work cannot be restored. Each overlapping delete retains its own generation-bound cancellation claim until it finishes, so an early failure cannot clear another waiter’s signal. This also protects late or replacement token registration without cancelling a successor generation. Non-transactional backends delete aliases sequentially and can partially delete them before reporting an error. Gateway cancellation binds the exact admitted queue key and generation, preventing deletion of an underscore session from cancelling a distinct dotted WebSocket session.
  - Merges official master through `a66cc98a47d7`. The early undispatchable-call path omits session-prompt arguments from observer and stream events, and abandons a hook only when it entered the hook pipeline. Orphan retirement compares the same redacted history projection used by RPC persistence, while refusing retirement when the stored history is incomplete.
  - The previous sync through `65f8eb3c9284` keeps the tool assembly’s upstream owned-session memory routing and the feature’s direct-only prompt-tool boundary. One existing SOP test fixture supplies the new optional owner field with `None`, preserving the unowned case.
  - The prior `c54e002a836e` sync retains upstream dashboard sign-in lifetimes and delegated principal-memory ownership. Initial Chat construction uses the same sign-out-aware session-permit helper as later turns, preserving the deletion fence while closing a waiting signed-out viewer. Current authority is resolved again after session/storage waits and held through cancellation or durable mutation; the admitted attachment owner survives execution-time preparation. Guarded JSONL alias cleanup preserves ordinary prompt-disabled session deletion while SQLite remains atomic. Preserves supplied-only registries, native recipes, memory provenance and child capability/principal wiring while retaining Chat-only prompt admission. Prompt-tool exclusion now runs after registry sealing so it cannot misclassify a supplied tool as a deferred built-in. Request-only tool-context retention preserves the full required prompt section and working transcript. Executed-result privacy now survives typed history and native/text request replay even when a hook rewrites an ordinary call into a prompt tool. Earlier literal strict Signal-preview and independent-child isolation fixes remain intact.
- **Scope boundary:** Channel and gateway-RPC Chat sessions, including Web and ZeroCode Chat. No ACP prompt support, JSONL prompt support, cron/SOP/delegate/subagent/one-shot/auxiliary capability, arbitrary-session management, REST collection management or new slash commands. Ordinary ACP lifecycle handling remains isolated from Chat aliases. No deployment, WIT/WASM ABI change, new lockfile package or workflow-permission expansion. `zeroclaw-infra` adds a direct dependency on the already-locked `tokio-util`.
- **Blast radius:** 131 files changed, 23843 insertions(+), 1944 deletions(-) against official `a66cc98a47d72dbf008679190f2443d413f473ca` at `ccd943de8b070ac98e9c4effbd340e91c95ff434`: storage/lifecycle, daemon coordination, approvals/redaction, channels/RPC, configuration/localization, Web/ZeroCode and prompt budgeting; CI also adds a WhatsApp gateway feature-test lane. Private-request hook exclusion affects programmatic hook transforms, cancellation and model selection.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #9998, the accepted contract; Related #10405, the Chat/ACP tracker. ACP remains a separate follow-up. Related #10412 is parallel session-contract work, not a dependency or supersession.
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/9998
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10405
  https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/10412

### What this does, simply

A chat can keep a small reminder attached to itself rather than relying on remaining conversation history. A later primary turn receives it after restart, but another session and auxiliary workers do not. Successful whole-session reset starts without the attachments. The feature is off by default.

Operators normally approve the exact proposed mutation once. Unsupported confirmation surfaces refuse it; ordinary approvals still work. Prompt text grants no permissions and cannot override immutable safety/host instructions. If the complete collection and required tool-protocol framing cannot fit, provider dispatch fails instead of silently dropping content.

There are at most four attachments, each at most 2 KiB and 8 KiB collectively. Symbolic IDs follow `[a-z][a-z0-9_.-]{0,63}`. Changes take effect on the next top-level turn, not during the already-running turn.

The deletion fix prevents an open WebSocket from recreating a session that RPC just deleted. A same-ID successor is a new owner, not permission for the old connection or queued work to continue. Deleting `team_alpha` does not cancel an unrelated active `team.alpha` WebSocket queue; HTTP/SSE still uses its actual normalized queue and raw abort ID.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, on disposable sessions.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface: web` and `surface: tui` (ZeroCode Chat/Dashboard); messaging channels `matrix`, `slack`, `telegram`, `signal`, plus CLI confirmation. Other adapters have negative strict-capability coverage, not enabled-feature claims.
- **Setup / preconditions:** SQLite Chat persistence, `[channels].session_prompts_enabled = true`, global `session_prompt_approval = "required"`, matching clients. Default full tool selection includes the tools; a minimal configuration must name `session_prompt_list`, `session_prompt_set` and `session_prompt_delete` in `[tools].optional`, then reload. Selection grants no execution permission and does not gate injection of stored attachments into an enabled primary Chat turn. WebSocket Chat additionally requires `[gateway].session_persistence = true`; restart after enabling that prerequisite. Matrix-only configurations need not enable gateway persistence.
- **Steps to run:** Ask the agent to set `{"id":"task","content":"Keep this chat focused on the synthetic inventory task."}`; inspect the literal preview and approve once. List the collection, send another turn, restart and ask again. Check another session, then reset the original and list again. Inspect and reject a 2 KiB synthetic proposal after scrolling to its end. Separately keep a WebSocket open, delete its Chat session through RPC and try another prompt through that old connection; reconnect to create or use the intended successor.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Next-turn injection and restart persistence are current-session-only; successful reset clears the collection. Strict approval has one-time allow/reject, no Always, and rejection changes nothing. After committed deletion the old WebSocket reports `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`; it cannot recreate or adopt the successor. Durable deletion failure is reported without claiming success and preserves the durable state.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** The prompt collection/configuration/tools do not exist. The independent RPC/gateway deletion paths can leave an open gateway connection able to recreate deleted durable Chat state.

### How I tested

Current candidate `ccd943de8b070ac98e9c4effbd340e91c95ff434`, tree `afcf3f0e014cb82a269422a73f42c6fb57844012`, against official master `a66cc98a47d72dbf008679190f2443d413f473ca`. ## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? **Yes.** Opt-in durable metadata and current-session tools. Admission/transactional ownership checks prevent stale or cross-session mutations.
- New external network calls? **No.** Session-prompt approval previews use existing transports without marker expansion/upload. Matrix clients may independently fetch URL previews; disable those in the reviewing client when appropriate.
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? **No.**
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? **No.**
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? **Yes.** Opaque bounded text intentionally enters the system prompt, beneath immutable host/safety authority.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Exact default-required single-use approval, current-session incarnation ownership, direct-only dispatch, complete prompt-budget checks and output masking contain the risk. `disabled` relaxes additional content-bound confirmation, not ordinary authorization, and can permit auto-approved writes without operator preview. Hooks cannot read sensitive bodies/results. Content hashes can permit low-entropy guessing; masking is not secrecy. Sensitive text-mode exchanges omit unrepresentable media declarations; ordinary rounds/native carriers retain upstream behavior. Previously stored opaque transcripts are not retroactively scrubbed.

Custom adapters must override it with the literal-preview and operator-confirmation contract to support these mutations. The channel prompt-building compatibility helpers are now test-only, but were already crate-private on master and create no external Rust migration.
- Add `TurnAttribution.session_id: Option<String>` for caller-visible identity separately from durable `session_key`. Both `rpc::turn::execute_turn` and `execute_turn_prepared` take `session_prompts: Option<SessionPromptAdmission>` after `cost_context`; capture `{ backend, owner }` at primary Chat admission, never resolve a fresh owner after asynchronous preparation. Direct constructors use the registry instead of a plain map; entries are `GatewayCancellationEntry { session_key, generation, token }`. Registration and deletion helpers carry the actual admitted queue key and lifecycle generation, not a queue reconstructed from a normalized abort ID. Wire/configuration/SQLite formats are unchanged by this correction. Do not invent generations outside the lifecycle.

**Observable changes, including with attachments disabled:**

- `sessions_reset` invokes whole-session reset, clearing attachments and rotating incarnation atomically in SQLite. Its "already empty" wording still counts removed messages, not attachment removal. Message-only clear preserves attachments.
- Durable `/new` deletion failure keeps existing history and reports `channel-runtime-new-session-failed` instead of claiming success. Without a durable backend, ordinary ephemeral behavior remains.
- Chat RPC deletion attempts `<id>`, `rpc_<id>` and `gw_<id>` aliases, even without metadata, and coordinates live gateway cancellation/invalidation. Alias deletion is atomic in SQLite; non-transactional backends delete aliases sequentially and can partially delete them on failure. Existing SQLite aliases must match the admitted principal for the complete deletion, including for unscoped callers. Mixed-owner IDs are refused as ambiguous before deletion. ACP deletion stays in its own recorded domain. Scoped callers receive `FORBIDDEN` for foreign, legacy-unowned or ambiguous records. A custom backend that has not implemented guarded RPC deletion refuses that effect, including with prompt injection disabled. With the backend unavailable after its failed-open retry, scoped callers skip optional gateway cancellation because its owner cannot be verified, then receive `FORBIDDEN` from finalization. This refusal already existed at `ceff7651864b` but differs from official master, which removed the owned live session in that state. A running RPC turn can already have been cancelled while the session remains; `session/close`, administrator deletion, or repairing storage and restarting are recovery paths. Healthy Chat/ACP creation writes its durable owner row before returning, so this particular degraded state is not a normal fresh-session path. Queue admission can report `SESSION_BUSY`; old deleted WebSockets report `SESSION_NOT_FOUND` and must reconnect. Already-cancelled work is not resumed on rollback. Gateway deletion cancels only entries bound to the deleted queue and generation; a distinct dotted WebSocket queue survives an underscore-session deletion. RPC Kill captures the queue generation before waiting and prevents prompts queued behind that killed generation from entering the provider; it does not cancel a same-ID successor.
- Current-session views, strict previews, turn spans and delegate forensic principal identity use the canonical storage key. Public RPC/cost/OpenCode/shell identity remains separate; `ZEROCLAW_SESSION_ID` prefers caller-visible identity. ACP identity is unchanged.
- The three session-prompt tool names are reserved for plugins/skills even when disabled, including prepared-skill registration. Rename conflicts. They also follow master's built-in selection: default full includes eligible prompt tools; minimal requires their explicit names in `[tools].optional` and a reload. This selection changes availability, not authorization or injection of already-stored prompts into an enabled primary Chat turn. Deferred MCP tools must use full `server__tool` names rather than conflicting bare suffixes. Indirect `unfiltered_tool_arcs` excludes prompt tools; use canonical direct calls.
- Native tool framing changes from 42 to 36 characters ("Use tools when this request needs it") for exact budget substitution, including feature-off turns. Native prompt fingerprints consequently change. Complete native/XML prompt framing is paired; nonempty attachment overflow fails closed without truncating host context.
- Strict mutation previews visibly encode Unicode 17 format/default-ignorable characters, including legitimate joiners and variation selectors. This can change how joined text and emoji look in the preview; stored text, content hashes and provider context keep the original bytes. This is display encoding, not a new restriction on valid prompt text.
- Channel retention preserves upstream selection after the last user-role row, including synthetic text-tool results. Text-protocol call/result exchanges are omitted from retained history; native-tool retention remains unchanged. Privacy projection scans the complete exchange before selection so host-marked results can identify sensitive calls. Provider working history is unchanged.
- Export recovery separately recognizes malformed JSON/XML/MiniMax prompt-tool material before ordinary diagnostic output; shared streamed detection retains master's name-based behavior. Recovery is best-effort, not approval or execution. Unrepresentable text media carriers are omitted only for marked sensitive rounds; ordinary media behavior remains upstream.
- Programmatic `HookHandler::before_llm_call` is skipped when the request or active scope carries private session-prompt content, including max-iteration summaries. Its transforms, cancellation and model selection do not apply to these requests; ordinary requests retain them. The classifier is deliberately conservative: parseable `session_prompt_*` envelopes can skip the hook even with the feature disabled. The feature guide documents this caveat; the short API rustdoc does not enumerate it. Observational input masking remains separate, and provider working history is never replaced with a masked hook projection.
- With single-tool rounds enabled, the host instruction is inserted before the private Session Prompts suffix. Diagnostic exports retain that instruction, and host protocol replacement leaves opaque attachment bytes unchanged. Trim reconstruction preserves the canonical host prompt before reapplying the transient instruction. Ordinary no-attachment and no-system behavior is preserved. The guide documents a reserved-heading limitation: host text (workspace files, skill/tool descriptions) with a standalone `## Session Prompts` after a blank line can be mistaken for the private suffix, leaving later tool-format/framing instructions unchanged and masking later host text in diagnostic/export views. Dispatch still rejects disallowed multi-tool calls; a failed turn may need a client retry. Use another heading in host text. This sync documents the limitation without changing runtime behavior.
- Independent child transcripts withhold attachment-bearing parent protocol scope, while same-agent inline SOP continues the primary transcript without attachment tools. Ordinary non-attachment child protocol inheritance is pre-existing and intentionally unchanged by this repair; this is not general child-context isolation.

The additive incarnation migration adopts valid unbound legacy attachments and removes mismatches/orphans. Historical legacy ownership cannot be proved retroactively; reset questionable old sessions. Feature-off does not delete stored attachments or scrub old histories. Downgrading and clearing history with an older binary can leave attachments that reappear after re-upgrade; reset affected sessions before downgrade and retain the backup.

`ToolResultMessage` adds the public `session_prompt_tool_result: bool` field.
Out-of-tree Rust struct literals must initialize it: use `false` for ordinary
results and preserve the host-derived value when replaying existing results.
Exhaustive patterns must bind the new field or use `..`; forwarding code must
preserve the flag.
The reserved key is exported as
`zeroclaw_api::model_provider::SESSION_PROMPT_HISTORY_RESULT_KEY`. Absent
serialized fields default to `false`; ordinary serialized results omit the
field. Marked results retain the existing native host key or text privacy
marker through Chat replay, including when a tool hook changed the original
call name. This is privacy provenance, not a capability or ACP prompt support.

The legacy public `SessionBackend::delete_session_owned` SQLite implementation retains master's two-autocommit deletion behavior. Runtime Chat now uses the guarded transactional `delete_session_key_set_authorized` replacement; external Rust consumers needing atomic owner/message/attachment deletion should use `delete_session_key_set_owned`. Retiring or transactionally repairing the legacy method is deferred to a separate follow-up.

The runtime loop facade additionally exposes `scope_required_session_prompt_section` for channel orchestration. This is an additive Rust API; it grants no tool capability or wire access.

A stalled, non-reading dashboard client can delay sign-out close processing while the server sends the rejection of a forbidden Always approval. The existing SOP-frame reply path has the same timing limitation. Later input is still checked against current authority; this integration leaves that broader transport hardening for follow-up.

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

- **Fast rollback command/path:** Reset/delete affected sessions with this version first when stored attachments must be removed; back up SQLite and restore the previous known-good binary/client pair. Reverting this feature restores previous source behavior but does not retroactively clean stored data. Keep the backup for migration recovery.
- **Feature flags or config toggles:** Set `[channels].session_prompts_enabled = false` and restart. This stops injection/tools, not attachment persistence, redaction of previously marked history or the feature-off lifecycle/retention changes described above. Reset/delete is required to remove attachments.
- **Observable failure symptoms:** `SESSION_PROMPT_LOAD_FAILED`, `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`, `SESSION_BUSY`, `FORBIDDEN`, `channel-runtime-new-session-failed`, strict-preview refusal or prompt-budget errors before provider dispatch. Modifying-hook callbacks not firing for classified private requests is intentional; deployments relying on hook transforms/cancellation/model selection must account for this exclusion and conservative feature-off cases. Inspect lifecycle/approval metadata without dumping prompt bodies. An idle old WebSocket refusing after committed deletion is expected behavior, not a reason to bypass the owner fence.

milestone.title: v0.9.0
milestone.description:
v0.9.0 prioritizes opt-in OIDC dashboard sign-in, principal isolation, schema V4 and a CLI-only build option.

The standard build keeps the working in-process dashboard. Sign-in stays off by default, preserving the existing pairing flow. Release gates are real-provider sign-in evidence; the five principal-isolation repairs (#11234, #11220, #11225, #11230, #11266, with #11198 tracked); schema V4 (#11218); and a build-time CLI-only option that omits gateway/web assets and directs dashboard users to the standard build.

Scoped dashboard chat has a November 3 go/no-go, with sign-in alone as the fallback. November 10 is the earliest target, subject to the gates, not a committed date.

Standalone zeroclaw-gw, full gateway IPC route/parity work, cross-process webhook handling and two-process desktop packaging move to v0.9.x. Channel listeners remain in core under existing documented exceptions. These deferrals do not complete the remaining gateway roadmap.

Source of truth: #7432 (https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/7432), current release allocation. Existing implementation trackers keep their detailed work. Feature acceptance, current-head review/CI, recorded placement decisions and the v0.8.7-tag hold on breaking work remain in force.

prs.title: fix(config)!: forbid /mnt,/media,/run/media and Windows drive/UNC defaults
prs.body:
## Summary
Fixes #12134.

Under Full autonomy (`workspace_only = false`), the default denylist stopped at OS directories and left WSL DrvFs (`/mnt/c/...`), `/media`, `/run/media`, non-system Windows drives, and UNC shares open while the matching Linux/Windows system homes were refused.

- **Unix defaults:** add `/mnt`, `/media`, `/run/media`.
- **Windows defaults:** deny every drive-letter root (`A:\`…`Z:\`) in addition to the existing `C:\Windows` / Program Files spellings; refuse UNC shares in the path checkers when no allow entry matched.
- **Most-specific-match unchanged:** a workspace or `allowed_roots` entry under those trees (common WSL layout) still wins by depth.
- **Filesystem channel:** reject single-letter `/mnt/<x>` watches unless `allow_broad_roots = true`; named binds such as `/mnt/inbox` stay allowed.
- **Docs:** `docs/book/src/security/model.md` lists the new defaults.

This is a deliberate behavior change for operators who relied on Full autonomy to roam those trees; `allowed_roots` remains the opt-in.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --test mnt_forbidden_paths`
- [x] `cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib checklist_default_forbidden`
- [x] `cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib filesystem_validate_rejects_drvfs`
- [x] `cargo test -p zeroclaw-config --lib filesystem_validate_allows_named_mnt`

## AI disclosure
Prepared with AI assistance. I reviewed the diff, ran the tests listed above, and take responsibility for the change.

prs.title: fix(web): return focus to the chat message box when a turn ends
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - `handleSend` focuses the message box, but the textarea is `disabled={!connected || typing || !hydrated}` for the whole turn. Disabling it drops that focus, and nothing focused it again when `typing` went back to false. `AgentChatInner` now arms a refocus when a turn starts. When the turn ends and the box is enabled again, it focuses the box.
  - It only does that when nothing else has focus (`document.activeElement` is the body, missing, or the box itself, which covers Firefox leaving focus on the disabled control) and when the pane is rendered (`getClientRects().length > 0`). That way a turn ending in a hidden chat tab, or after the user moved to another tab, the model picker or a dialog, doesn't steal focus. If the turn ends while the box is still disabled (disconnected or not hydrated), the refocus stays armed until the box is enabled.
  - Pressing Stop leaves focus on the composer's own Stop button, which turns into Send when the turn ends. `chatInputFocusOwner` treats that button as part of the composer, so a stopped turn also gives focus back to the box (found in the browser run below, fixed in 03b7786).
  - The decision is a small pure function in `web/src/pages/chatInputRefocus.logic.ts`, with node tests. A component-level regression test in `sessionLifecycle.test.ts` runs a real `AgentChatInner` turn: send, `done` from the socket, then check the composer's focus calls.
- **Scope boundary:** The input lock during a turn from #6220 stays in place. No other focus behavior changes (the image upload and slash-command focus calls are untouched), and there's no new UI.
- **Blast radius:** The web dashboard agent chat only. The worst case is focus moving to the message box at the end of a turn when nothing else had focus.
- **Linked issue(s):** Fixes #11658

### What this does, simply

In the dashboard chat, the message box used to lose the cursor while the agent replied and didn't get it back, so every follow-up needed a click. Now the cursor goes back into the box when the reply finishes, unless you clicked somewhere else in the meantime or the chat is in a background tab.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Optional. I ran the cases below in headless Chromium; a check in another browser (Firefox/Safari) would still be useful.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `web`
- **Setup / preconditions:** A running gateway with a working provider; open an agent chat in the dashboard.
- **Steps to run:** Type a message and press Enter. Wait for the reply to finish, then start typing without clicking. Also try clicking the model picker (or another chat tab) during a reply.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The text goes into the message box. If you moved focus during the reply, it stays where you put it.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Nothing is typed until you click the message box.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The web dashboard checks (`tsc -b` and the `test:contexts` suite) run the new logic tests and the `AgentChatInner` regression test.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** None of the CI suites runs a real browser, so CI checks focus against a mocked textarea node (react-test-renderer `createNodeMock`). The browser run below covers real DOM focus.
- **Commands run and tail output** (Node 24.21.0, in `web/`):
  - `JITI_JSX=1 JITI_TSCONFIG_PATHS=1 npx jiti src/contexts/sessionLifecycle.test.ts` → `ℹ pass 20` / `ℹ fail 0`. With `AgentChat.tsx` reverted to `master`, the new test fails:
    ```
    ✖ the composer takes focus back when a turn ends, unless hidden or focus moved
      AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: focus returns to the composer
        actual: 0,
        expected: 1,
    ```
  - `node --experimental-strip-types --test src/pages/chatInputRefocus.logic.test.ts` → `ℹ tests 8` / `ℹ pass 8` / `ℹ fail 0` (with `chatInputRefocus.logic.ts` from ae47552 the new Stop test fails: `actual: 'other'`, `expected: 'nothing'`)
  - `npm test` → all suites `fail 0`
  - `npm run test:contexts` (run by web CI; the new logic test lives here since ae47552) → all suites `fail 0`, including the node suite `ℹ tests 40` / `ℹ pass 40` (at 03b7786)
  - `cargo web check` (generates the API files, then `npx tsc -b`) → passed
  - `bash scripts/ci/comment_hygiene_gate.sh` → `Comment hygiene gate passed.`
- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** A Playwright 1.64.0 run in headless Chromium (Playwright's chromium-1248 build) on Debian 13, 1280×800, English locale, against the dashboard from this branch at 03b7786 (`npm run dev` in `web/`, proxying to a local `zeroclaw` gateway built from the same tree, one agent `local` on a mock OpenAI-compatible provider that answers after ~3 s). Script, full log and screenshots: [proof/11661-chat-focus](https://github.com/ump45nose/zeroclaw/tree/2063f26868c632e5ff962f1717a9f27eb6a43092).
- **Visual interface evidence:** [normal completion](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ump45nose/zeroclaw/2063f26868c632e5ff962f1717a9f27eb6a43092/v2-A-normal-completion.png), [focus moved](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ump45nose/zeroclaw/2063f26868c632e5ff962f1717a9f27eb6a43092/v2-B-focus-moved.png), [Stop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ump45nose/zeroclaw/2063f26868c632e5ff962f1717a9f27eb6a43092/v2-C-stop.png), [hidden pane](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ump45nose/zeroclaw/2063f26868c632e5ff962f1717a9f27eb6a43092/v2-D-hidden-pane.png), [offline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ump45nose/zeroclaw/2063f26868c632e5ff962f1717a9f27eb6a43092/v2-E2-offline.png), [reconnected](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ump45nose/zeroclaw/2063f26868c632e5ff962f1717a9f27eb6a43092/v2-E2-reconnected.png).
- **Tested revision, interface, and evidence path:** 03b7786, web dashboard agent chat (Vite dev server, not the gateway-embedded production bundle), screenshots and log linked above.
- **Screenshot or exact-output evidence:** see the screenshots above and the results in the next item.
- **Action or changed state and observed result:**
  - Normal completion: after the reply, `document.activeElement` is the visible textarea; typing with no click puts `typed without clicking` in it.
  - Focus moved to the conversation picker during the turn: after the turn, focus stays on the picker button.
  - Stop: right after clicking Stop focus is on the Stop button; after the turn ends it is on the textarea and `after stop` types into it. (At ae47552 it stayed on the button; fixed in 03b7786.)
  - Hidden pane: during the turn I opened a second chat tab; when the hidden tab's turn ended, its composer did not take focus (`hiddenComposerFocused: false`, active element is the body).
  - Disconnected: browser context set offline mid-turn; the composer stayed disabled (`Running…`) and unfocused while offline, including after the mock turn would have finished. After going back online and the composer being re-enabled, focus was on the textarea and `after reconnect` typed into it.
- **If any command was intentionally skipped, why:** No Rust code changed, so I didn't run `cargo test` / `cargo clippy`.

## Security & Privacy Impact (required)

- New permissions, capabilities, or file system access scope? No
- New external network calls? No
- Secrets / tokens / credentials handling changed? No
- PII, real identities, or personal data in diff, tests, fixtures, or docs? No
- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? No

## Compatibility (required)

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config / env / CLI surface changed? No
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No

## Rollback (required for medium/high-risk PRs)

Low risk: `git revert <sha>`.

prs.title: fix(zerocode): show temporary local file-write diffs
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master` (all contributions).
- **What changed and why:**
  - Eligible local ZeroCode `file_write` calls show red removed lines and green added lines from a bounded observation before a successful write. Overwrite cards show `Overwrote existing file`, and six-row previews offer Show all when rows are omitted.
  - Previous text uses a private local notification outside ordinary tool results, model messages and saved history. The private inbox and view share a five-minute deadline. The runtime drops the entire pair if `scrub_credentials` changes either the previous or written text, so ZeroCode falls back to the labelled preview.
  - Direct ACP clients stop constructing creation diffs from write input across live events, restored history and approval requests. Capture admission uses the executor's canonical live resolver, native provenance, exclusions and read-approval policy.
- **Scope boundary:** Capture requires existing native read authority, workspace containment and supported readable text. It adds no durable diff history or remote/direct-ACP diff transport. The pre-write observation cannot guarantee the exact inode contents replaced by a concurrent external writer. ACP separation, Unicode format-character handling and tab presentation are outside this revision.
- **Blast radius:** File-write observation, transient native RPC events, local ZeroCode Chat/Code cards and ACP write presentation. File authorization and atomic replacement remain in force. No new dependency, configuration or durable schema is introduced. Runtime adapters stay in the owners covered by the temporary file-write diff exception approved in [#11436](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11436#pullrequestreview-5474715854).
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10294. Remote and direct ACP diffs remain unavailable, so this PR does not close the issue.
- **Release notes:** ZeroCode can show temporary local file-write diffs when existing read authority permits capture and credential scrubbing leaves both sides unchanged. ACP clients, including Zed, no longer get a `file_write` creation-diff preview. Base64 writes now put raw base64 in `rawInput.content`, with `rawInput.encoding` preserved.

### What this does, simply

An agent can replace an existing file with `file_write`. Showing only the new text as green additions makes a replacement look like a creation. ZeroCode can now show what was removed and added when the agent already has permission to read that workspace file. Old text disappears from this view after five minutes and is not saved with the conversation. Reopening shows the saved write summary. If private evidence is unavailable or would require credential redaction, the card uses the supplied-content preview instead of a diff. Recognized overwrite results still have an overwrite heading.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes, with disposable synthetic files.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=tui`, local native ZeroCode Chat and Code through RPC (`channel=rpc`). Direct ACP presentation also has adapter-level automated coverage; interactive ACP client verification remains pending.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Build daemon and client from the same revision. Use an agent with native `file_write` and `file_read`, no read exclusion and no pending read approval. Use an English tool-result catalog for compact-summary recognition. Start a fresh conversation with a disposable workspace file. A write-only profile intentionally receives the fallback preview.
- **Steps to run:** On both `master` and this branch, ask the agent to use `file_write` to create `write-demo.txt` with eight numbered lines, then overwrite it with three different numbered lines. Inspect the six-row preview, choose Show all, then wait five minutes or disconnect and reopen the conversation. Repeat with read authority disabled or an allowed path outside the workspace. Rewrite a file with identical content. For the scrub cases, put a synthetic labelled credential in the previous file, then separately in the written content. Check `file_edit` independently for its existing diff behavior.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** Eligible overwrites show `Overwrote existing file`, red removals, green additions, `Changes · temporary local view` and Show all when rows are omitted. An identical rewrite says `Content unchanged`. Expired, restored, unsupported or credential-scrubbed overwrites show the recorded size summary and `Content preview · diff unavailable`. Pending and unknown calls acquire no success claims. Direct ACP preserves original write arguments without synthesizing a creation diff.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Results report bytes written and path. Write previews look like additions regardless of previous contents, without execution-time overwrite evidence.

### How I tested

The new focused runtime regressions are `agent::tool_execution::tests::local_file_diff_executor_drops_previous_credentials` and `agent::tool_execution::tests::local_file_diff_executor_drops_written_credentials`. Each drives a real filesystem overwrite through the production executor with admitted native read authority and synthetic `token=supersecretvalue` on one side. They assert a successful write, the ordinary correlated result and no `LocalFileDiff` event. Both pass on the current head (results below).

The earlier PR body reported 79 selected API/tools/runtime/ZeroCode tests and a matched daemon/client build. Those reports predate this revision and are not validation of the merge resolution or scrub gate. Existing coverage includes read exclusion and approval, foreign and write-only roots, binary/control text, credential filenames, hard links, size limits, failed writes, nonlocal transport, revoked grants, full queues, inbox retirement, expiry, reused IDs and restored history.

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** [`CI Required Gate`](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/40996117315) passed on `b06b42f8b`, including Format, Lint, Test, Docs Style and platform/feature checks. CI on the current head `9fccb917a` (master merge `4f3ca7c38`) is running. Historical [CI run 39022116522](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/39022116522) also passed at the earlier head `a95e2d235f11`.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** Local results for the current head are below. The master merge `9fccb917a` resolved one conflict in `crates/zeroclaw-api/src/jsonrpc.rs`, keeping this PR's `try_send_raw` next to master's `reserve_frame`.
- **Commands run and tail output:**

  Run on head `9fccb917a` (master merge `4f3ca7c38` into `b06b42f8b`), `zc-cargo-narrow`, `-j2`:

  ```text
  cargo fmt --all -- --check                                   ok
  cargo clippy -p zeroclaw-api -p zerocode -p zeroclaw-tools -p zeroclaw-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings   ok
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-api                  324 passed; 0 failed
  cargo test -p zerocode                      lib 54 passed; bin 1614 passed; 1 failed; 2 ignored
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-tools --lib          1390 passed; 0 failed; 3 ignored
  cargo test -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib        6036 passed; 2 failed; 10 ignored
  ```

  Both new regressions pass: `agent::tool_execution::tests::local_file_diff_executor_drops_previous_credentials` and `agent::tool_execution::tests::local_file_diff_executor_drops_written_credentials`. The three failures also fail on clean master `5a51398dd` on this machine and are not touched by this PR: `connection_tests::insecure_tls_prompt_preserves_default_sigint` (zerocode), and `relay::local_dial_tests::a_closed_route_releases_a_dial_parked_on_a_stalled_listener` / `a_dial_that_never_connects_ends_on_its_own_budget` (macOS loopback backlog never fills).

Standalone Rust formatting and the docs quality and links gates passed. A live ZeroCode run on `b06b42f8b` captured the new-file and overwrite views (see Visual interface evidence).
- **Visual interface evidence:** Real screenshots of the `file_write` diff view are in [this comment](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11463#issuecomment-6537009304): a new file, then an overwrite of the same file.

Yes, an authorized write can make a bounded previous-text observation for local display using existing native read authority, readable-path policy and workspace containment. Tool names or model arguments grant no native trust or new read permission.
- New external network calls? No. Private evidence goes only to the trusted local native RPC connection. Remote RPC, direct ACP, gateway and channel adapters do not receive it.

- Prompt injection or untrusted model-visible text introduced/changed? Yes. Successful results gain pre-write existence and byte counts. Captured previous text stays outside ordinary output, model messages, hooks, observers, receipts, checkpoints and saved history. Rendering escapes terminal controls.
- If any `Yes`, describe the risk and mitigation: Each snapshot is limited to 16 KiB and 1,024 lines. Capture rejects unsupported text, listed credential filenames/key extensions and Unix files with multiple hard links. Capture is a read that does not count toward the `file_read` rate limit and emits no observer or audit read event. Existing written-content exposure through `ToolCall` arguments is unchanged by the scrub gate.

The inbox and view each cap raw pairs at 64 KiB and 16 entries per session. The inbox tracks at most 16 sessions and each pane at most eight. The generic notification ring holds only opaque tokens. - Config / env / CLI surface changed? No.
- Rust/MSRV/toolchain floor changed? No.
- If backward compatibility is `No` or either surface/floor question is `Yes`: exact upgrade steps for existing users: Build daemon and ZeroCode together. ACP clients must read original `rawInput.path`, `rawInput.content` and optional `rawInput.encoding`; base64 content remains raw base64. They must not treat write input as a creation diff. No configuration migration is needed. Compact summaries recognize saved English results with a matching argument path. Unknown or localized results keep their original display. Historical results without pre-write evidence remain unknown.

prs.title: feat(channels): add passive Telegram group context
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`
- **What changed and why:**
  - Adds opt-in `passive_group_context` for Telegram group chats, defaulting to `false`, so authorized unaddressed group text becomes silent context instead of being dropped by the `mention_only` gate. In a multi-bot group the bot can then follow the discussion and answer with full context the moment it is @-mentioned.
  - Marks those messages `passive_context = true` and keeps them out of every active path: the acknowledgement reaction and typing indicator in `dispatch_incoming_message`, the SOP gate and worker SOP ingress, the `/stop` fast path, and the debouncer, so passive chatter cannot swallow another member's addressed turn.
  - Leaves input-driven voice mode alone for passive messages. The text parser clears `voice_chats` when the addressed participant switches back to typing; an observation is not that participant, so without the guard unaddressed chatter could downgrade a pending voice answer to text.
  - Reuses the passive channel fields from the WhatsApp Web work in #8389 (`ChannelMessage::passive_context`), so there is no new API surface.
  - Rebased onto the `per_user_session` work in #9772 and adapted to it, which removed this PR's own scope, scheduling and attribution helpers in favor of the native `conversation_scope_for`, `message_debounce_key` and `attributed_channel_user_turn`. That rebase was contributed by @RO-mix from production use of this branch.
- **Scope boundary:** No change to default Telegram behavior, and no change to any other channel. Passive recording covers text only; unaddressed media keeps the existing `mention_only` drop. Shared-room rendering does not distinguish an observation from an addressed turn, which is left as a follow-up on #9772's rendering.
- **Blast radius:** Medium. Enabling `passive_group_context` selects shared group/topic history, including shared session controls such as `/new`, regardless of `mention_only` or `per_user_session`. With `mention_only = true`, authorized unaddressed group text is also admitted, persisted and later model-visible in that history. DMs are unchanged, and `ChannelMessage` gains no fields.
- **Linked issue(s):** Closes #10715. Related #8379 and #8389 for the WhatsApp Web equivalent, Related #9772 for the session machinery this now builds on, Related #8362 for channel parity.
- **Labels:** `enhancement`, `channel`, `config`, `daemon`, `integration`, `runtime`, `experienced contributor`, `channel:core`, `channel:telegram`, `risk:medium`, `size:L`.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** `Yes`. The feature is only observable through a real group chat with more than one participant.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `channel` (`telegram`).
- **Setup / preconditions:** A Telegram bot in a group with two authorized members. Set `mention_only = true` and `passive_group_context = true` on the Telegram channel. The first leaves unaddressed messages for this feature to record; the second admits them and puts the group on one shared history.
- **Steps to run:** Member A sends an ordinary group message that does not mention the bot, for example `deploying the gateway myself tonight`. Member B then mentions the bot and asks about it, for example `@yourbot who is deploying the gateway?`.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The bot stays completely silent on A's message, with no acknowledgement reaction and no typing indicator, and answers B's question naming A.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** A's message is dropped at the mention gate, so the bot answers B without it and cannot name A.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** The required `Quality Gate` covers the changed Rust surface, including `Test`, format and clippy, the feature-matrix checks and the cross-target builds. On current head `5c08e0af2` it passes, `CI Required Gate` included. The `Parallel Runtime Test` abort on the previous head came from `master`, was fixed there by #10965, and this branch now carries that fix through a merge of `master` at `757db6c35`; that job passes on this head.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** CI does not exercise a live Telegram group. The author-reported two-member live check below covers that gap.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Author-reported macOS aarch64 runs on current head `5c08e0af2`.

```sh
$ cargo fmt --all -- --check
$ cargo clippy --locked -p zeroclaw-channels -p zeroclaw-config --all-targets -- -D warnings
    Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s) in 2m 25s

$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --lib 'telegram::'
test result: ok. 320 passed; 0 failed; 2 ignored; 0 measured; 1452 filtered out

$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-channels --lib passive
test result: ok. 8 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1736 filtered out

$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-config --lib passive_group_context
test result: ok. 4 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 1612 filtered out

$ cargo test --locked -p zeroclaw-runtime --lib send_message_to_peer
test result: ok. 7 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 4494 filtered out
```

- **Beyond CI, what did you manually verify?** The earlier author-reported checks showed that the voice regression fails without `!passive_context`, and that the scope regression fails without flag-alone room selection. - **What changed and why:**
  - Some channel image attachments, especially WhatsApp stickers, arrive as `image/webp`.

  - Add a narrow `image-normalization` feature that enables WebP support in the existing `image` dependency for channel builds that already use image normalization.

prs.title: feat(session): implement append-only session event history
prs.body:
## Summary

- **Base branch:** `master`.
- **What changed and why:**
  - Replace separate transcript writers with a shared, append-only session history. Record accepted inputs, model attempts and reasoning, tool execution, approvals, failures, model changes, context compression, and child-agent activity so recovery can reconstruct what actually happened.
  - Separate typed contracts and replay (`zeroclaw-api`), storage and migration (`zeroclaw-infra`), execution and authorization (`zeroclaw-kernel`), and application wiring (`zeroclaw-session-host`). CLI, RPC, ACP, channels, gateway, Web, and ZeroCode consume the standard session model.
  - Use one canonical `session_id`, with protocol source recorded only as creation metadata. Add a rebuildable session index, persistent titles and workspace metadata, same-session branches, copied sessions with shared frozen history, child sessions, and disposable temporary sessions.
  - Support SQLite and JSONL, resumable migration from master's stores, source-file backups, backend switching, and interrupted-execution recovery. Keep message, reasoning, tool, and multimodal content typed through the internal pipeline; convert protocols at provider/channel boundaries and parse legacy attachment markers only during import.
  - Store the cost ledger in the selected backend, attributed to actual session IDs where available. Preserve reported input/output tokens, cache reads and cache creation separately, and pricing evidence. Historical provider references remain unchanged when configuration aliases are renamed or deleted.
- **Scope boundary:** Full attachment/blob lifecycle work remains under #9488. This does not add history-content credential filtering, new at-rest encryption, a tamper-detection hash chain, automatic replay of external effects, a dashboard redesign, or a complete runtime extraction. Existing config-reference, authorization, and ownership rules still apply to provider edits.
- **Blast radius:** Session creation, listing, history queries, persistence, resume and TTL handling; provider/tool dispatch and approvals; compression and delegation; CLI/RPC/ACP/channel/gateway adapters; Web/ZeroCode session consumers; cost persistence and legacy migration.
- **Linked issue(s):** Related #10526. Related #9600. Related #9487. Related #9488. These broader contracts and coordination issues are not automatically closed.

### Crate boundary changes

- **`zeroclaw-runtime → zeroclaw-kernel`:** The runtime calls the extracted session execution, recovery, authorization, approval, context-maintenance, and model-selection code through the kernel's ports. This dependency keeps those decisions in one owner instead of copying them into each entrance or back into the runtime holding crate. Kernel has no production dependency on runtime, providers, or channels, so this does not create a dependency cycle or move concrete model adapters into the kernel.
- **`zeroclaw-runtime → zeroclaw-session-host`:** The shared host wires the configured SQLite/JSONL backend, installation migration, repository, and kernel coordinator for all entrances. Retaining this dependency replaces the old direct ACP/transcript-store construction with one standard session implementation. Its runtime use is transitional: application composition already injects a session source, but daemon startup retains a native fallback and some lifecycle operations still open the repository directly. Those calls can later move behind narrow injected session-management ports; the boundary is not a new independent persistence owner or a claim that runtime extraction is complete. The runtime dependency ratchet also needs these new edges and their owners to be reconciled; adding manifest entries alone does not establish the architectural justification.

### What this does, simply

A transcript records messages, but does not reliably explain which model ran, what a tool did before an interruption, or which context survived compression. This PR records those observations as ordered events and rebuilds conversation views and working context from them.

With persistence enabled, reopening after a restart or TTL expiration restores the same logical session and its retained context. Recovery preserves partial execution and diagnostics; an unproven tool outcome stays unknown rather than being reported as successful or silently executed again. Historical permissions and approvals never grant current access.

SQLite and JSONL share the same logical format. Existing histories are imported into the configured backend and the old files are renamed as backups. ACP no longer owns a separate execution-history database. A session index provides discovery metadata; the event history remains authoritative. A copy gets a new session ID and references a frozen source prefix, while a fork creates a branch inside the same session. Temporary sessions are hidden and removed on close or cleanup after restart.

## Testing (required)

### How you can test (when useful)

- **Reviewer testing requested?** Yes. Use separate disposable installations for `master` and this branch; migration changes the on-disk writer format.
- **Interface(s) exercised:** `surface=cli`; automated coverage also exercises RPC, ACP and messaging-channel boundaries.
- **Setup / preconditions:** Configure an agent named `fixture` with a working provider and a harmless permitted tool. Stop other writers. Repeat with `channels.session_backend` set to `sqlite` and `jsonl`.
- **Steps to run:** Run `zeroclaw agent -a fixture --session-state-file /tmp/session-events-review.json`, exchange messages and request a harmless tool action, exit, then reopen with the same command. Repeat against a disposable copy of an installation containing legacy session/ACP history. Inspect `<data-dir>/sessions/` and its backups after import.
- **Expected on this branch (after):** The standard event store and installation manifest contain execution observations and retained context. Reopening retains the conversation; imported source files become backups. Reading history does not repeat the tool. Renaming a provider alias does not rewrite its old historical references; select an available model manually if an old reference no longer resolves.
- **Prior behavior on `master` (before):** Separate transcript stores retain conversation messages, but do not provide this common execution-event history, shared session index, or installation-wide cutover.

### How I tested

- **CI checks relied on and why they cover this change:** No claim that required CI is fully green. The latest pushed revision is `2fac551de5`; its [CI run](https://github.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/actions/runs/41801200397) reports failures, including default-stack tests, the CLI cost fixtures, and the runtime dependency boundary check. These are not claimed as resolved on that pushed revision. Local evidence below covers the latest functional change and the subsequent master merge.
- **Known CI coverage gap, if any:** The full workspace/all-features, platform/MSRV, million-event performance, and VM power-loss matrices were not repeated locally for the latest revision. Runtime tests below used a 16 MiB test-thread stack; they do not prove the default-stack gateway issue is resolved. Search currently builds a disposable authorized FTS view per query; no persistent full-text-index performance claim is made.
- **Commands run and tail output:** Linux, Rust 1.99.0, locked dependencies. Provider-edit checks ran on `ad2c3060d0`'s source; the subsequent `2fac551de5` merge only added master's desktop release workflow, smoke script, documentation and architecture tests.

```sh
TMPDIR=/tmp RUST_MIN_STACK=16777216 cargo +1.99.0 test --locked \
  -p zeroclaw-runtime -p zeroclaw-gateway --lib provider_alias_ -- --test-threads=4
# gateway: test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed
# runtime: test result: ok. 6 passed; 0 failed

TMPDIR=/tmp RUST_MIN_STACK=16777216 cargo +1.99.0 test --locked \
  -p zeroclaw --test component provider_rename_cli -- --test-threads=1
# test result: ok. 4 passed; 0 failed

TMPDIR=/tmp cargo +1.99.0 test --locked \
  -p zeroclaw --test architecture desktop_release -- --test-threads=4
# test result: ok. 6 passed; 0 failed

TMPDIR=/tmp cargo +1.99.0 test --locked \
  -p zeroclaw --test architecture release_workflow -- --test-threads=4
# test result: ok. 26 passed; 0 failed

cargo +1.99.0 fmt --all -- --check
# exit 0
bash -n scripts/desktop/smoke-dashboard.sh scripts/desktop/prepare-kernel.sh
# exit 0

  scripts/ci/docs_quality_gate.sh
```
